docs.title: §9 item 395 — 2026-10-12 (chain T37, daily provisional under §9 rule (6); chain step (solve))
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-12 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

Licence. §9 rule (6) (PROJECT_PLAN.md :3813–3823): the 03:00 review writes T37 as the next numbered step of live §10 chain T, tagged (daily, 2026-10-12 — provisional). This is chain T's third and last provisional step between weeklies, after T35 and T36, and the weekly ratifies or reverts it. T37 is T26 (§10 chain T, PROJECT_PLAN.md :4649–4653, quoted, not changed: "the in-model zero at C_in(r) at 64.000 MHz within T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION, circuit = field at REDUCTION_BAND; printed Q(r)/Q_0 against 1/Q = 1/Q_0 + 1/Q_C, Q_C = 1/(ωC_in r). Target: identities.") run on T28's h = 0.01 exact-rectangle rung (item 310, ANS-7 step 12): item 214's five Cu nodes, T28's C_in(h) and z64(h), and item 311's construction. It serves chain T's open question, Q's h-statement (T30 / F31; the weekly's Phase 6 paragraph, PROJECT_PLAN.md :4905–4907). With ESR, the tuned coil's Q is dominated by capacitor loss, so this step measures whether Q(r) moves with h less than Q_0 does.

The rulings that apply: - the ESR ruling (§9 :3792–3811): r = 0.2 Ω on every capacitor, both sides at once; lossless records stay, labelled lossless; - the sheets ruling (:3790): exact rectangles, κ None.

The zero band on this rung. T26's band is T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION, registered from the ×1 grid's node residuals. Item 310 found that no band exists for the h = 0.01 rung: its node files carry no identity residuals (field_solve false). Ruling 310-Q1 therefore asserted only the crossing inside the bracket. It printed the offset beside T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION for scale only (20261008T112649Z_ANS-7-item310-W5-assemble.log:138), and 365-Q1 repeated this at 127.74 MHz. No weekly has registered a rung band since. Rule (6) never sets a band, so T37 takes 310-Q1's form: the zero half of T26's target is the crossing, and the offset is printed. No band, tolerance, Done-when or target is set or moved; every band is imported by name.

Feasibility (checked 2026-10-12 against the code and the disk). The two paths combine with a tests-only edit and no new node solve: - The h-path inputs are all on disk (logs/ans7_exact/): - item 214's five node_{62.0,63.2,64.5,65.8,67.0}_p2_h0.01_cu.json; - item 310's tune_p2_h0.01.json: c_in 6.364316664701229e-11 F, c_mode["cu"], z64["cu"], tie, cells 140 270, resolution 0.01, c_in_h_rel 8.346525677918049e-4; - item 310's assembled lossless tune_inmodel_cin_p2_h0.01.json: rows_a Q 964.432729560342, R_in 18 592.58100053142 Ω, c_in and cells. - ESR's C_in(r, h) is pure. It is _c_in_esr (test_ans7_exact_strip.py:2215) applied to that z64, so no 4×4 is re-solved. - What costs compute is three degree-2 Route A drives on the rung, plus the (W) wiring drive. - Five literals and guards in the current code would block the h path or misread it (code steps 1–6 below): - _esr_ohm() (:2178–2194) refuses RESOLUTION; - _tune_point() (:1090–1109) raises on the h inmodel path when TUNE_POINT is unset; - tune_esr builds the ×1 tie and mesh (:2312, :2314), reads the ×1 lossless Q_0 (:2280) and writes the ×1 ESR file names (:2457–2466); - test_t26_inmodel_zero_esr (:2494) asserts _zero_resolution(), which is T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION when TUNE_MHZ is unset. - Price: one ESR window on the rung is three ≈ 100 s drives (item 310's per-drive measurement), so it fits one window under 590 s at -n 12, and the whole item fits one ≤ 1 h slot. No a / b split is needed (see the price and the kill contingency below).

ANS-7 step 11c: tune the exact-sheet F-small birdcage on C_in with r = 0.2 Ω on both sides, at 64.000 MHz, on the h = 0.01 rung (140 270 cells, degree 2, κ off, Cu). - Executor: implementer. Spawn sentence: "The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped." - Edits: tests only, tests/validation/test_ans7_exact_strip.py. No src/, ans:7, test_ans7_sparse_route_b.py or test_ans7_t30_rin_q_sequence.py edit. - Tier: heavy. W1 runs at -n 12, the rung's measured width (items 214 / 310 / 365): summed ru_maxrss 33.8–36.7 GiB, and h = 0.01 is unpriced at -n 8. The re-gates run at their records' widths (-n 8 / -n 2). Complex build. Class: chain step (solve). - Time: ≈ 13 measured (chain-solve class median, 18:00 restock table, PROJECT_PLAN.md :4002) / ≈ 50 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 15 code + W0 ≈ 4.5 + W0b ≈ 1.5 + W1 ≈ 7 + ≈ 7 spare. - Depends on nothing open. Items 310 and 311 have landed (outcomes above). If any input file named above is absent, stop and mark BLOCKED. Never re-create one.

Code (tests/validation/test_ans7_exact_strip.py). Every knob-unset path stays behaviourally identical. Item 311's ×1 64 MHz ESR path is shown unchanged by W0, item 387's 127.74 ESR path is untouched by construction (the edits branch on h37 only), and item 310's h lossless path is shown unchanged by W0b. 1. _esr_ohm() (:2186–2193) gains a third legal set: _tune_mhz() is None, _resolution() == H_RES and _cols() == ("cu",). TUNE_POINT must still be unset in every set. Any other RESOLUTION raises ValueError, and the message names all three legal sets. 2. _tune_point() (:1093–1096): the "unset on the h rung" ValueError fires only when _esr_ohm() is None. Under the ESR knob, unset returns None. There is no recursion: _esr_ohm() reads TUNE_POINT_ENV directly. 3. tune_h (:2025–2031): if _esr_ohm() is not None: pytest.skip(...) before pt = _tune_point(). Otherwise pt * 1e6 fails on None. 4. tune_esr (:2264–2469): h37 = _h_tune(). _active(), _tune_json() and _stored_active() already return the T28 set under these knobs, giving tune_p2_h0.01.json and the five checked _h0.01_cu nodes. Then, on the h path only: - Q_0 comparand: jl = act["out"] / f"tune_inmodel_cin_p{deg}{act.get('sfx', '')}.json". That is tune_inmodel_cin_p2_h0.01.json on the h path, and the name is unchanged on the other two paths (their act has no sfx). - (F-Q0), asserted on the h path: lossless["c_in"] == tj["c_in"] and lossless["cells"] == recs[0]["cells"]. A Q_0 taken from the wrong rung fails here, not silently. - Tie without a mesh: tie = _tie_from_json(tj["tie"]) in place of _fixture_tie(). The ×1 call builds an extra ×1 mesh and asserts the ×1 record. - (W) first, on the ×1 mesh. Run _exact_geo(th14, comm, GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION), then _route_a_solve(…, TUNE_TARGET_HZ, "cu"), then del the ×1 geo, as tune_h does (:2066–2085). - Then build the rung: geo, specs, cells = _exact_geo(th14, comm, GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION, res=H_RES). The three drives are _route_a_solve_esr unchanged. - Outputs: rank 0 writes tune_p2_h0.01_esr0.2.json and tune_inmodel_cin_esr0.2_p2_h0.01.json, the ×1 payloads plus "resolution": H_RES. It never writes item 311's tune_p2_esr0.2.json / tune_inmodel_cin_esr0.2_p2.json, any lossless file, or any node file. - The return dict gains "h": h37 and "hres": H_RES if h37 else None. The key "res" already holds the residuals. - Prints: tag T37, with the 64 MHz text. Every PREDICTED clause is from Predictions below, and no ×1 or 127.74 prediction is inherited (item 365b C1's two inherited "NOT met" lines). The ×1 and 127.74 print strings stay byte-identical. 5. Record literals, printed on the h path only and never asserted, each with its provenance comment: - T26_C_IN_R_X1 = 6.359301781809668e-11 (20261011T094028Z_ANS-7-item311-W2-cin64-esr.log:359); - T26_Q_R_X1 = 164.5434331710199 (…094028Z…:2130); - T26_Q_CLOSED_EXCESS_X1 = 1.0996e-2 (…094028Z…:2133); - T21P_Q0_X1 = 971.0667834101893 (Q_0 at the ×1 C_in, …094028Z…:2133); - T30_Q_H_REL_CF = -6.9811e-3 (Q at C_F, h = 0.01 against ×1, 20261011T094910Z_ANS-7-item364-T30.log:76). - The C_in(h) move uses the existing T28_C_IN_H_REL_64 (:1068). - These are literals because W0 rewrites item 311's ×1 ESR JSONs in this slot. A literal from the registered log cannot drift with the run-to-run round-off. 6. Tests: - test_t26_ab_circuit_equals_field_esr (:2473–2481): _assert_tie(cells, tie, res=tune_esr["hres"]). - test_t26_inmodel_zero_esr (:2485–2494): on the h path it asserts exactly one up-crossing, no down-crossing (rows_a["crossings_down_hz"] == []) and lo < f₀,A < hi. It skips the band line, and its docstring says why (310-Q1). The ×1 and 127.74 paths are unchanged.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported by name), at 64.000 MHz on the rung: - (AB-rh) circuit = field at C_in(r, h): |S11_A − S11_B|/|S11_B| ≤ REDUCTION_BAND (1e-3, tests/validation/test_port_lumped_rlc_termination.py:88, imported through test_port_circuit_layer_field at test_ans7_exact_strip.py:81) at 63.9 / 64.0 / 64.1 MHz. Route B is the five-node h grid through bary_interp and _route_b_z_esr. - (T2-rh) the in-model zero (310-Q1's form): Im Y_in,A changes sign − → + exactly once, and never + → −, in (63.9, 64.1) MHz, with f₀,A inside the bracket. - |f₀,A/64 MHz − 1| is printed beside T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION (1.287e-5, test_ans7_exact_strip.py:1018) for scale only, never asserted. - (F) the rung: - the drive-mesh cells equal the stored node cells (140 270) and tune_p2_h0.01.json's; - _assert_tie(…, res=H_RES) passes; - its (N-wire) clause holds: the cells are off the ×1 record by > CELL_COUNT_BAND (0.01, tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheet_prerequisite.py:57). - (F-Q0): the lossless comparand's c_in and cells are the rung's. - (W): unchanged; ≤ NODE_S_RTOL (1e-9, tests/validation/test_ans7_sparse_route_b.py:87) against item 195's stored point.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (W): asserted. Same degree-1 ×1 64 MHz drive, same comparison. Backed by: - item 310 W3, on an h-rung window at -n 12: 1.720e-13 (20261008T111904Z_ANS-7-item310-W3-p64.0.log:1430); - item 311 W2: 3.927e-14 (…094028Z…:2126); - item 387 W1: 7.091e-14 (20261012T003929Z_ANS-7-item387-W1-esr64.log:2126). - The residual is not digit-stable across windows. It must only stay ≤ NODE_S_RTOL. - (N-wire): asserted inside _assert_tie(res=H_RES). The same comparison on the same rung was green in item 310 W2–W4 (test_t28_rung_and_wiring, 140 270 cells) and item 365's nodes. - (N2-rh): predicted, printed. The circuit at 0.5·C_in(r, h) against the in-model at C_in(r, h) is ≥ 10 × REDUCTION_BAND. On this rung the lossless reading was 493.62× (…112649Z…:143), and ×1 ESR read 494.39× (…094028Z…:2136). It has never been measured with r on this rung. - (N-Lh): predicted, printed — predicted NOT to separate at 10×. The lossless circuit at C_in(0, h) against the in-model at (r, C_in(r, h)), on the bare S11, is predicted in [3, 7] × REDUCTION_BAND. - At ×1 it read 4.97× against a ≥ 10× prediction (item 311, a recorded negative). - The Z_in form |dZ|/|Z| is predicted ≈ Q_0/Q_closed − 1 = 4.94, in [4.6, 5.2]. The ×1 reading was 4.878. - (N-r0h): predicted, printed. _c_in_esr(z64(h), 64 MHz, C_mode(h), 0) equals tune_p2_h0.01.json's c_in bit for bit. That was bit-equal at ×1 and 127.74, but never run on the rung's z64. - (N-h): predicted, printed. |C_in(r, h)/C_in(r, ×1) − 1| ≥ 10 × the secant tolerance (|g| ≤ 1e-15 S → ≈ 1e-12 relative). This is the step's reading, so it is not gated.

Predictions (written first, printed, never asserted; drafter's arithmetic from the stored JSONs). - C_in(r, h)/C_in(0, h) − 1 in [+3e-5, +6e-5], central +4.610e-5. The ×1 value +4.602610e-5 scales as C² (1/Q_C²) by (1 + 8.35e-4)². - C_in(r, h)/C_in(r, ×1) − 1 in [+8.0e-4, +8.7e-4], central +8.3473e-4, printed beside T28_C_IN_H_REL_64 +8.346526e-4. r moves the lossless h-move only at ≈ 8e-8. - Q_C(h) = 1/(ωC_in(r, h)·r) ≈ 195.36 (×1 195.524). With Q_0(h) = 964.4327 (item 310 W5), the closed form 1/Q = 1/Q_0 + 1/Q_C gives Q ≈ 162.454, ratio 0.16844. - Q(r, h) in [161, 167], central 164.24, which is the closed form carrying ×1's +1.10 % excess. - Q(r, h)/Q_0(h) in [0.166, 0.174]. - Q(r, h)/closed form − 1 in [+0.7 %, +1.5 %] (×1 +1.0996 %; 127.74 MHz +3.5494 %). - The step's reading: Q(r, h)/Q(r, ×1) − 1 is predicted in [−4e-3, 0], central −1.84e-3, printed beside two references: - Q_0's h-move at C_in: Q_0(h)/Q_0(×1) − 1 = −6.832e-3, from the two stored lossless rows; - T30's move at C_F: −6.981e-3. - The ratio of the Q(r) move to Q_0's is predicted ≈ 0.27, in [0, 0.6]. In the closed form, Q(r)'s relative h-move is 0.168 × Q_0's plus 0.832 × Q_C's (−8.34e-4, the C_in move). - R_in(r, h) ≈ 3 166 Ω. R_in(r, h)/R_in(r, ×1) − 1 is predicted in [−6e-3, −1e-3] (×1 R_in(r) 3 175.98 Ω; lossless R_in h-move −0.78 %). - (AB-rh) in [5e-6, 3e-5] at each point (lossless h 1.239 / 1.262 / 1.289e-5; ESR at ×1 moved them −0.3 %). - |f₀,A/64 − 1| ≈ 2.59e-6, about 0.20 × T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION, printed (lossless h 2.545621e-6; ESR at ×1 moved +1.9 %). - f₀,B(C_in(r, h))/64 MHz − 1 within ±1e-9, by construction. r_AB = f₀,A/f₀,B − 1 in [−5e-6, −1e-6]. - W1 in 330–450 s at -n 12 (≈ 560 s on a ×1.4-slow box); cells 140 270.

Two premises the drafter settled from the code (the review checks them). 1. "Accepted power" is the SPEC's, not item 361's. SPEC v3 says P_acc = incident − reflected at the two feeds, at the 50 Ω line. In our model each feed is a 50 Ω source in parallel with its own gap's r + C, reduced to a Thevenin pair (w_i, Z_th = 50 Ω ∥ Z_RC) (tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root.py:76–83). The line's accepted power therefore includes the feed gaps' ESR loss: P_acc,SPEC = ½ Re Σ_feeds V_port,i · conj(I_line,i), with V_port,i = w_i − Z_th·I_i and I_line,i = I_i + V_port,i / Z_RC. Item 361's P_acc excludes that term (its "caveat, printed", MAT-15.md item 361). Drafter's arithmetic from the node JSON (unlogged): P_acc,SPEC ≈ 2.906e-2 + 1.265e-3 ≈ 3.032e-2 W at |w| = 1 V. 2. Row 2 on our side is the in-model field's sheet currents, not the circuit reduction of the stored 32×32. SPEC row 2 says "step 1's row 2b algebra on the 32-port S at this C". On our copper fixture the circuit ↔ field identity with local loads is red at 1.58 (H12c, the pre-registered red; printed on every H17 node, e.g. 20261010T093200Z_WF-10-step1e2-W1a.log:6324). Our row 2 is therefore ring_modes.k_spectrum applied to the builder's cur["ccw"], which 358's (Lin) tied to the field to ≤ 6.6e-16. It comes with one Status checkbox and one revision-history line. - The slot returns a W2 text of 4 lines or fewer for the review to paste. - It does not edit docs/status/dashboard.md: moving W2 to the top of Waiting-on-you is the review's job (flag 4).

Executor and cost. - Executor: implementer, or the slot directly (item 400's precedent for a writer-only change). - Tier: standard (container timeout -k 30 180), no MPI (-n 1), complex build, because the script's import pulls in dolfinx. - Class: lane 1 (median 6). - Cost: ≈ 6 measured / ≈ 30 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 10 for the writer, SPEC and test + ≈ 3 for windows + spare. The window times come from item 386's W0, 33 passed in 75 s (20261011T170500Z_ANS-8-v3b-W0.log), and item 400's render-only W1 at 3 s. - Depends on nothing. - Inputs, all tracked: metrics.json rows_v3. It carries power_w.p_acc_spec / p_acc_wave and gap.rel_line_cut (0.008317), gap.rel_field_net and gap.mechanism.{P17,P21}.cs_over_x. Read on the host while drafting.

Edit 1: the writer (_v3_section only). - Replace the intro clause "Per-W / per-√W figures are per W of P_acc = incident − reflected at the two 50 Ω feed lines (… W at unit Thevenin drive)" with a definition paragraph in the SPEC's terms. It states five things: - What P_acc is. P_acc is the sum over the two feed ports of the accepted power at the 50 Ω lumped port: incident − reflected at the port plane, HFSS's default per-port accepted power. - How our side computes it. Ours is the line cut ½ Re Σ_feeds V_port·conj(I_line), rendered from power_w["p_acc_spec"]. Beside it goes its relative difference from power_w["p_acc_wave"], computed from the two stored floats and never typed. - The feed-gap load. The feed gaps' capacitor and 0.2 Ω ESR are load inside P_acc; they appear as row 5's ESR fraction. - The field partition. The field's feed-sheet partition exceeds the line cut by gap["rel_line_cut"], rendered as a percentage to two decimals. That excess is the discrete feed sheet's Cauchy–Schwarz excess. Render CS/X from cs_over_x on both sheets. It is a documented sheet property (weekly ruling 2026-10-12; known-issues 2026-10-11), not a defect, and not a quantity the AED column is asked for. - The per-partition values stay printed beside each row, as now. - Re-label row 5's residual line as "residual = feed-sheet Cauchy–Schwarz excess (documented sheet property, weekly 2026-10-12; known-issues 2026-10-11)". The 0.991683 / 0.008317 values do not change. - Nothing else changes: - not a v1 / v2 line; - not comparison_text's other branches; - no stage logic; - not metrics.json (its stored gap.label and spec strings stay as written).

Edit 2: SPEC.md, insertions only. - Status list: - [ ] Operator replication in AED, **v3 column** (step 2, one session — see "Operator session brief"). - Revision history: - **v3.1 (2026-10-13, §9 item 411):** operator session brief added; no row, readout, fixture value or definition changed. - New subsection ### Operator session brief (step 2 — one AED session). Each bullet points to the SPEC line it executes. Only C, R_p, the port pair and the order / frequency are written out. - Project. Open the operator's existing F-human project and copy the step-1 design to a new design. Never overwrite a step-1 design. - Conductor. Copper: Finite Conductivity σ = 5.8e7 S/m, Solve Inside off (SPEC.md:98–99, :266–268). - Gaps. All 32 gaps carry C = 118.2437 pF in parallel with R_p = 2 212 Ω (SPEC.md:268–271). Enter C with all its digits and its unit, 118.2437pF (step 1's Route A lesson, :128). - The 30 non-feed gaps are Lumped RLC sheets. - The two feed gaps (P17 at 0°, P21 at 90°) are 50 Ω lumped ports. The same R_p ‖ C must be present across each feed gap in the solved field. Rows 3–5 need it, because the feed capacitor's dissipation is inside P_acc (:285–287). A capacitor added "in post", as step 1's Route A did (:127–130), does not change the field. - The realisation is the operator's choice; state it in the results file. - Drive. Equal magnitudes, P21 lagging P17 by 90° (ccw = (1, −1j), :272–273). Row 6 is the sense check (:319–320). - Solve. 64 MHz only, First Order. Adaptive as in "Frequency and mesh" (:134–137). No re-tune; say so in the results file (:275–277). - Export. Rows 1–6 with all printed digits (:279–304), per the accepted-power note (:282–295), plus the solve metadata (:165). Results go only to the gitignored aed_results/. No AED number ever enters a tracked file.

Anchors (asserted). They live in a new tests/unit/test_ans8_v3_definition.py, which loads the script by importlib, as tests/unit/test_ans8_v3_rows.py:40–45 does. Every comparison runs on tmp copies. - (R) Byte-for-byte regeneration. comparison_text(json.loads(committed metrics.json)) equals the committed COMPARISON.md, bytes for bytes. - (P) Unchanged prefix. Everything up to the ## Step 2 (SPEC v3) heading equals the pinned pre-change writer's render up to that heading, byte for byte. The edit is confined to the v3 section. - (D) The definition landed once. The v3 section contains the definition paragraph exactly once: the substrings "accepted power at the 50 Ω lumped port", "Cauchy–Schwarz" and the rendered rel_line_cut ("0.83 %"). It no longer contains "incident − reflected at the two 50 Ω feed lines". Every v3 table row still ends | |, so the AED cells are empty. - (Rp) The operator subsection's arithmetic. Take ω = 2π·64e6, C = C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF·1e-12 (tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:68) and r = ESR_OHM (tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root.py:53), all imported. Then: - round(1/(ω²C²r)) == 2212 and round(1/(ωCr)) == 105, the values SPEC.md:270–271 prints; - the new subsection contains "118.2437" and "2 212". - Printed only: the series-vs-parallel admittance factor 1/(1 + Q_C⁻²) − 1. The drafter's unlogged arithmetic gives −9.0e-5, ≈ 0.11 of the 0.10 pF root grid, so it is inside row 1's resolution. - (R0) The test touches no repo file. The repo's COMPARISON.md, metrics.json and SPEC.md bytes are unchanged by the test.

Negative controls (rule (e); all asserted, all by construction). - (N-digit). Make a tmp copy of the committed COMPARISON.md and change one digit inside the v3 section (row 5's 0.268112 → 0.268113). The copy must differ from the render. Assert the inequality and print the first differing line. - (N-old). Copy the pre-change script to logs/ans8_writer_8f50751e/<the script's repo-relative path> with a host git show 8f50751e:<script> before W1. 8f50751e is the script's last commit at drafting; the slot re-reads git log -1 --format=%h -- <script> before its edit, uses that value and types it into the test as a literal, never HEAD:. The mirrored depth is item 400's deviation (parents[3]). That writer's render must differ from the committed file, and its v3 section must lack "Cauchy–Schwarz". - (N-Rp). Setting r = 0.02 Ω (one digit changed) gives round(R_p) ≠ 2212.

Windows. Foreground, bare, repo-relative, Bash timeout: 660000, -s, FEM_EM_ANS_SKIP_PRIVATE=1 in every ANS-8 window. The steps run in this order: 1. Pin copy (host). 2. Edits. 3. W-regen. Use the Write tool to create the gitignored helper logs/ans8_regen_comparison.py. It loads the script by importlib, reads the committed metrics.json, and writes only COMPARISON.md, from comparison_text. Then run: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-8-item411-regen "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_ANS_SKIP_PRIVATE=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 python3 logs/ans8_regen_comparison.py'" Afterwards, host git diff --stat on the case directory must show COMPARISON.md changed and metrics.json untouched. 4. W1. The script changed, so its unit modules re-run in the same window (rule (c)): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-8-item411-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_ANS_SKIP_PRIVATE=1 timeout -k 30 180 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/unit/test_ring_mode_rows.py tests/unit/test_ans8_private_comparison.py tests/unit/test_ans8_v3_rows.py tests/unit/test_ans8_v3_definition.py -s -v --tb=short'" This is item 386's W0 shape (33 passed there) plus the new module. 5. Wdoc. Gate on dead = 0 and exit ≠ 1; exit 2 on the stale report is the standing state (20261012T170143Z_ANS-7-item400-docrefs.log:130): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-8-item411-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" 6. Commit: script, new test, COMPARISON.md, SPEC.md and the logs.

Traps already paid for. - The synthetic rows_v3 in test_v3_comparison_text (tests/unit/test_ans8_v3_rows.py:91–103) has no gap key and no power_w["p_acc_wave"]. Stage R rewrites metrics.json; on 10-11 it moved the v1 / v2 floats by up to 1.4e-10 (item 386, D1 reading). - COMPARISON.md and metrics.json are owned by nobody (written by the container). Only a container window rewrites them, and never a host hand-edit. - The private side is never touched. The private writer is never called. No Palace figure is ever set against an AED one. - SPEC.md:319's row-6 readout says "ours 21.5". That is item 358's centre-sample purity (item 369's brief, above). Our row 6 at O reads 20.7092 (COMPARISON.md:94). Do not edit the readout. Return it as a flag for the review / weekly; the SPEC is the weekly's. - SPEC.md:270's R_p ‖ C is the high-Q equivalent. The exact parallel C is lower by 1/Q_C² ≈ 9e-5. Printed by (Rp) and never changed. - Pinned copies: the mirrored path, never HEAD: (OPS-43). - The pre-commit leak hook: a refusal is a stop. Never use --no-verify. - Formatting: ≈, never a tilde. No -k, no pipe, never delete a log, no edit after W1 (rule (i)).

Scope. Text only: one writer paragraph, one relabel, one SPEC subsection.

Not claimed: - any AED value or step-2 verdict; - the degree-2 v3 column (xl entry 35); - any change to a SPEC row, readout, definition or fixture value; - the dashboard edit (the review's); - the retirement of known-issues 2026-10-11. It retires when entry 35 prints the excess at degree 2.

This is a coding error: fix it in-slot, then re-run W-regen and W1. - (R) red after W-regen: the helper did not use the committed writer, or metrics.json moved. Restore nothing by hand, and park. - A pre-existing ANS-8 unit module red in W1: check known-issues first. If it is new, park. - A leak-hook refusal: unstage and park. Report the location only.

It is validated on h12c-cu-s32.npz, where both slot_k / slot_sign and names exist (anchor (Syn)). - Record constants (comparands, not bands; the 361-3 precedent), each with its log:line: - CLASS_MEAN_CU_D2_RECORD and CLASS_MEAN_CU_D1_RECORD: the 18 d2 and d1 means at 20261018T070008Z_WF-12-step5-H16c.log:8038–8055, 10 digits, in item 366's (same_ring, steps) dict shape; - SIGMA_MAX_CU_D2_RECORD = 0.999983227022 (:8036); - S1717_CU_D2_RECORD = 0.402723 + 0.391780j (:8057, printed beside); - C_MODE_CU_D1_RECORD_F = 1.181185799070e-10 and OFF_BLOCK_CU_D1_RECORD = 4.195925e-03 (…step3-a2-W1.log.gz:6366); - P17_2B_CU_D1_RECORD = (0.993012, 0.005612, 0.998482) (:6382) and CW_2B_CU_D1_RECORD = (0.993217, 0.998703, 0.005618, 0.000013) (:6387); - C_MODE_S800_RECORD_F = {2: 1.082287732e-10, 1: 1.131081186e-10} (20261011T123443Z_ANS-8-step1c-W1.log:116). - Predictions written first (printed, never asserted): - PRED_CMODE_CU_D2_PF_WINDOW = (114.37, 116.68), within 1 % of the root (the step's); - point predictions printed beside it: - 115.399 pF (the degree-1 C_mode / root offset 118.1186 / 118.2437 carried to the d2 root); - 113.023 pF (σ = 800's order move −4.314 %, item 366, applied to 118.1186; this one falls outside the 1 % window); - anti ≥ 0.99; - 2b ccw feed-ring share ≥ 0.99, with leak in [0.002, 0.02]; - PRED_D2_COLUMN_CONTROL = (2.0e-4, 4.0e-4) (the ≈ 0.01/32 ceiling); - the planted-ESR miss ≈ 3e-2 (PORT-24's (P) order, on σ = 800).

The same comparison read 1.776e-15 at :6367. - |c_own_f·1e12 − C_MODE_CU_PF| ≤ 5e-5 pF (the constant's 4-decimal resolution); - off-block vs OFF_BLOCK_CU_D1_RECORD ≤ OFF_BLOCK_RTOL; - the p17_alone and cw 2b shares and leaks vs their records ≤ SHARE_ATOL (6-digit prints). - (G1′) d2: reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND, printed beside 9.964981e-14 (:8035), and σ_max ≤ MATRIX_PASSIVITY_CEILING. - (L-d2) the H25 anchor: - σ_max recomputed vs SIGMA_MAX_CU_D2_RECORD ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL; - all 18 class means vs CLASS_MEAN_CU_D2_RECORD, each ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (predicted ≤ 1e-9); - S17,17 printed beside its record. - (L-σ) σ = 800 reproduction. rows_v2 on the two logs/wf7/ files reproduces C_MODE_S800_RECORD_F ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (10-digit prints; item 366 computed them from the same files with the same function). - The identities the share and leak are printed at: - (B0) own-C wiring: on d2 copper, own_c_mode's c_f is bitwise fixed_c["c_mode_f"], and c_own_f is bitwise the same (ring_modes.py:252–264). This is item 161's B0, the wiring that makes 2b each matrix's own resonance. - (Σk) the k-fractions: for every drive and control at own C, on each ring, Σ fractions = 1 to ≤ 1e-12. share_k1 == fractions[1] + fractions[15] and leak_k0 == fractions[0] bitwise (ring_modes.py:100–112). - (S) the ESR uniform shift, on the d2 copper matrix: - ring_mode_rows(…, esr_ohm=ESR_OHM) against esr_ohm=0 gives |ΔRe λ_k − r| / r ≤ SHIFT_RTOL for k = 0…8; - |ΔIm λ_k| / |Im λ_k| ≤ SHIFT_RTOL, and |ΔC_mode| / C_mode ≤ SHIFT_RTOL. - This is the ESR ruling's (i) ("uniform r adds r to every mode's eigen-impedance, so C_mode is unchanged", PROJECT_PLAN.md:3853–3854), which PORT-24 asserted on σ = 800 at 2.889e-15 / 4.571e-16 (tests/unit/test_port24_esr_circuit.py:276). - It is what licenses quoting the lossless C_mode beside the ESR root.

Each ≥ SAVE_CONTROL_FACTOR × REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL, with the factor printed beside PRED_D2_COLUMN_CONTROL. - Asserted against the floor, factor predicted: (P) a planted 0.4 Ω on P17 (the rest 0.2 Ω) misses (S)'s Re shift by ≥ SAVE_CONTROL_FACTOR × SHIFT_RTOL on at least one k. Predicted ≈ 3e-2, printed. PORT-24 asserted this on σ = 800, a different fixture. - Printed only: - the C₂ control, rows_v2(…, c_spec_f=<d2 Cu c_k2_f>) p17_alone feed-ring share, predicted < NEGATIVE_CONTROL_CEILING. H12c's degree-1 circuit read 0.105707 (…a2-W1.log.gz:6397), but through the Thevenin route, so it is not the same comparison. - the 2c controls' k = 0 leak at own C, predicted ≤ CONTROL_LEAK_BAR.

Printed (the record). Four columns, Cu d2 | Cu d1 (a2) | σ800 d2 κ off | σ800 d1 κ off, through item 366's _summary and line format: - row 1: c_mode_f, c_k2_f, off-block, anti; - row 4a: f₀ one-point against SPEC C, and also 64 MHz·√(C_mode / C_in(d2)); - row 2b at own C, for p17_alone, ccw and cw: feed / other share and leak, plus the |k| folds; - row 2c, both controls; - the order moves d2 − d1 on copper and on σ = 800, side by side. - The H25 lines: - C_mode(d2, Cu) in pF, beside 118.1186 (C_MODE_CU_PF) and 115.5209 (C_IN_F_HUMAN_D2_PF); - (C_mode − root) / root; - the window PRED_CMODE_CU_D2_PF_WINDOW hit or missed, and both point predictions; - beside them, the degree-1 offset (118.1186 − 118.2437) / 118.2437 = −1.058e-3. - The 2b rows again at r = ESR_OHM (ring_mode_rows_v2(…, esr_ohm=ESR_OHM)), labelled "ESR (production convention)", beside the lossless ones. - Every 2b share and leak is labelled "circuit route (Norton feeds); on copper the circuit ↔ field identity at C_mode is the pre-registered H12c record (1.581167); not the in-model row". Item 369's premise 2 applies: our SPEC row 2 is the field route, which H30 prints at degree 2. H12c's d1 in-model share was 0.998860 against the circuit's 0.993012 (:6382).

Windows. Each runs in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, with -s, and with FEM_EM_ANS_SKIP_PRIVATE=1 set (nothing here writes a private file, but the knob is set in every ANS-8 window). No module edit after W0 starts (rule (i)).

Traps already paid for. - Two orders. The d2 file is ordered with P17 first; the d1 files carry their own orders. Read every comparison by name (test_wf12_f_human_copper_s32_degree2.py:380–389) and never by index. - No slot keys on the d2 file. _slot_port_map raises KeyError on it. Use the names map, validated by (Syn). - κ. Both copper files and both wf7 files are κ off. The tracked metrics.json rows_v2 are degree 1 κ on σ = 800 (item 366's trap). They are not a column here, and never differenced against κ-off rows. - SPEC C ≠ any matrix's C_mode (item 161 trap 1). 2b is at each matrix's own C_mode, wired inside ring_mode_rows_v2, and one matrix's C_mode is never passed to another. - The circuit route on copper is not our row 2 (item 369 premise 2; H12c 1.581167). - ESR. rows_v2 is lossless. The root 115.5209 pF carries r = 0.2 Ω; C_mode does not, which (S) licenses. Never compare a lossless share with the ESR in-model share as if both were one quantity. - Sense: ccw = (1, −1j) (SPEC_DRIVES). H26's root is the P17 (1, +1j) reading (ruling (2)). - The h12c files are refused by the step-5 writer (REFUSED, :55). Opening them read-only is safe. Never write under logs/wf12/. - Gzipped logs: cite …a2-W1.log.gz line numbers of the decompressed text. Never decompress in place. - Never import a test_* name; never -k; no pipe; never delete a log; -s; do not import or run aed/.

Scope. Rows from four saved 32×32 matrices (copper d2 / d1 on the hole mesh, σ = 800 d2 / d1 boxed), κ off, 64 MHz, circuit route, no solve. Not claimed: - any AED value, verdict or level; - the in-model (field-route) row 2 at degree 2 (H30); - f₀, Q, match or tuning accuracy; - that C_mode(d2, Cu) is the root (it is printed beside the root, never asserted); - the WF-12 glyph; - an h-statement.

Negative result. Report and stop. Park on attempt/ANS-8-H25-* and mark item 516 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). - (F) red: the d2 file is not what entry 36 wrote. Stop; the review compares it with :8032. - (Syn) red: the names synthesis is wrong. Read no d2 class mean. - (L-d1) red with (Syn) green: the d1 records do not reproduce. Print the table and park. - (L-d2) red with (L-d1) green: the saved d2 matrix does not reproduce its window. File a known-issues entry, and H30 / the weekly do not read it. - (G1′) red: a passivity or reciprocity finding. File a known-issues entry. - (B0) / (Σk) red: a ring_modes regression. Stop. - (S) red: the ESR identity fails on copper. That is a PORT-24 finding: known-issues, and the weekly rules. - A floor-asserted negative control below its floor: report the factor; the review rules. - Every row, move, prediction and printed control is a reading, never a red. A C_mode(d2, Cu) outside the 1 % window is a reading for the weekly.

There is no PREDICTED RED: line, so a red anywhere stops the slot.

Status it can move. No glyph; rule (j) does not bind. - ANS-8 (✅ on step 1; step 2 open) gains one record sentence: C_mode(d2, Cu) beside 118.1186 / 115.5209 pF, and the circuit-route 2b ccw share / leak, labelled. - §10 H25 gains a DONE line. - docs/testing/xl-pending.md entry 36's readout clause "ring_mode_rows_v2 on the saved matrix" is marked met by this item (a status line, the review's edit; never the command). - The record feeds the 10-19 weekly's reading of whether the degree-2 copper C_mode sits with the root (H30's comparand context). It moves no known-issues entry unless a red files one.

Windows. Each harness call is bare and whole. Run foreground with Bash timeout: 660000. - Pre-censuses: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-9-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-9-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - Run both with the new script not yet in the tree (ANS-8's superseded-census trap). - W0, the re-gate after the additive keys (predicted 206 s, 20261002T112729Z_EX-79-mat15-regate.log): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-9-step1a-mat15-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 480 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py -s -v --tb=short'" - Dry run: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-9-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e ans:9 -n 2 -t 480 --dry-run". Traps already paid for. - Name every Function before the XDMF write. Unnamed θ / q_h Functions collided in HDF5 and hung EX-79's first run to Status 124 (20261002T113202Z_EX-79.log). - No dots in the XDMF basename. write_xdmf_with_tags treats the text after the last dot as a suffix (02_…py:210–211). - Snapshot indices are full steps only, and index 1 lands after two BE half-steps (transient.py:325). θ^{½} needs its own run. docs.title: §7 row text moved here verbatim — 2026-10-04 03:00 daily review (row near 2 KB)
docs.text: Progression (steps written now, placed by the weekly): 1 — one-way, gel: HFSS drives an existing four-leg fixture (ANS-2's 10 MHz loaded birdcage or ANS-7's tuned coil at 64 MHz — the weekly picks), its SAR maps into the thermal solve as the volumetric source; transient conduction in the gel with a stated outer boundary (Robin, as MAT-9/MAT-12) for a stated duration. Compared: temperature rise at pre-registered probe points and times, the initial slope dT/dt|₀ = SAR/c (the calorimetry quantity, MAT-12's anchor), and the volume-averaged rise; our side is MAT-10 ✅ (FEM SAR as the heat source) + MAT-12 ✅ (transient). 2 — two-way, gel: temperature fed back into σ(T) and the EM re-solved to the coupled fixed point (AEDT's HFSS ↔ thermal iteration; ours MAT-5 step 2's fixed point). 3 — perfusion (Pennes), tissue: only if the Ansys thermal solver carries a perfusion term natively or by a stated temperature-dependent sink — confirm on the Ansys side before the SPEC promises it; ours MAT-11 ✅. AED/Ansys numbers private as every ANS case (§5.4); relative agreement levels public (operator ruling 2026-09-24). Independent of ANS-8 — it needs only the four-leg fixture and landed Phase 8 chunks, so it may be commissioned before the human-scale case. Solve resources on the Ansys side: 12 cores, 1 TB (operator 2026-09-29).

docs.text:
The 2026-10-10 weekly adjudicated step 1 (§10 "Benchmarks, 2026-10-10 (step 5)"). It found DISAGREE at probe D: ours is 11 % below, against a 10 % band. The numbers are in docs/private/t13-t29-ans9-adjudication-2026-10-10.md. ANS-9 holds 🟡.

The known-issues entry the weekly filed is "2026-10-10 — 🟡 OPEN (ANS-9 step 1 adjudication, weekly review; §10 chain P21) — the coil-driven gel phantom's far-side probe D is 11 % colder in our thermal solve than in AED's (band 10 %), while the integral rows and the near-feed probes agree within 2 %" (docs/testing/known-issues.md, the last open entry before "Retired entries"). Diagnosis is step 1b (§10 P21), below.

ANS-2's SAR at r = 0.015 m reads +x 5.878e-7 > −x 6.558e-8 > +y 1.045e-8 W/kg per drive (ans2…/metrics.json pointwise["0"]), so D/C ≈ 6.3 and B/D ≈ 9.0. - Question for the review: if it intended "the d1 θ₄₀ reproduces ROW4_POINT_K's ordering" instead, that is the printed θ line, predicted equal to ≈ 1e-9. - (F0), d2x and d1x: the fixture is item 192's. - d2x: the rung's 10 MHz S against ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["10"] within STEP3A_RECORD_RTOL, ‖ΔS‖/‖S‖. - d1x: against ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P1_RECORDS["10"], same band. - Backing for the same comparison on this family: item 192's (X) read 8.9e-13 at -n 8 (ANS-4.md, item 192 outcome), and ANS-4 step 4 W1 reproduced the 2a″ digits to 7.1e-11 across widths at -n 8.

It re-records nothing: under the first branch the re-record at degree 2 exact is (b) plus a later step (see 371b's scope). - D/A is printed beside, not used. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-9-step1b-W2-d2x "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && mkdir -p /workspace/logs/ans9_1b && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_ANS9_1B_COLUMN=d2x PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_ans9_far_side_sar.py -s -v --tb=short > /workspace/logs/ans9-step1b-w2-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/ans9-step1b-w2-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/ans9-step1b-w2-raw.log; exit \$rc'"

Do not pass width_correction_kappa: κ stays off (the 2026-10-02 sheets-and-κ ruling). - Degree 2 is set on the rung (degree=2), and _solve_driven takes rung["degree"] (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:161–165). docs.title: §9 item 396 — 2026-10-12 (chain P23, daily provisional under §9 rule (6); chain step (solve))
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-12 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

Licence. §10 chain P, step P23, written by the 2026-10-12 03:00 daily under §9 rule (6) as a provisional next step on a live chain. The weekly ratifies or strikes it. It re-runs P21 (a) + (b)'s d2x window (371a / 371b, above) with the phantom refined. No band, tolerance, Done-when, decision rule or target is set or moved. Every band is imported by name. Our values only: no slot opens docs/private/, aed_results/, aed/ or COMPARISON_private.md.

Why this step. P21 left the weekly two readings of the far-side finding, and P21's own data cannot separate them: 1. 371b's θ₄₀ at D moved +16.6 % with the order (d1x → d2x) on the same thermal mesh, while 371a's point SAR_D moved −1.0 % (20261011T185145Z_ANS-9-step1b-W2b-d2x-thermal.log:2053, :1981, :2038). The 2026-10-11 18:00 review read this as the coarse phantom's cell-averaged source near D. Item 192's mesh has 537 tag-3 cells, ≈ 15 mm across (:2041). On that reading, the order sensitivity is an artefact of the DG0 source on 15 mm cells (the hypothesis line of 371b's journal entry, docs/testing/attempts.md:1554). 2. The other reading: the degree-2 source really is different near D, and a refined phantom keeps the θ_D order effect.

A refined phantom tells them apart. Under (1), θ_D's order effect falls toward the point-SAR order effect as h_p falls. Under (2), it stays. That is a reading for the weekly, not a decision rule this item applies.

Precondition finding: the knob. GEO-27 step 2's knob does not reach the ANS-9 fixture builder as it stands. - 371a / 371b build d2x through _four_port_rung (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_leg_offset_sweep.py:199). That calls tests/mesh/test_birdcage_leg_offset._build (:107–171), which takes leg_sheet_strip_fraction but no phantom_resolution. 371b's Scope already flagged this. - GEO-27 step 2 (item 377) builds through tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets._build(True, phantom_resolution=h_p, leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION) (:80–177). Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-13 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain P, step P24 (the 2026-10-12 weekly), executed as written.   • Why one window holds it. Item 396's W3 measured the whole EM half at this fixture: build 40.87 s, degree-2 sweep 261.47 s, thermal 10.16 s, body 328.91 s, 46.50 GiB summed, harness 333 s (20261012T100436Z_ANS-9-step1c-W3-h0025.log:2054, :2109).   • Gitignored inputs: none.

Precondition findings (read before coding). 1. The writer deletes the weekly's verdict. The script rewrites COMPARISON.md wholesale (examples/ansys_benchmarks/ans9_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz/09_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz.py:426). This is item 400's ans:7 defect in another file, and the same fix applies (below). 2. Two of the script's degree-1 anchors do not transfer. (R0) compares the re-run against MAT-15's gated T_star (09_…py:246–252), which exists only on the ragged fixture. The V_sub check is against V_SUB_RECORD_M3, the 58 866-cell phantom's record (tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:96, V_BAND 1e-10 at :98). Route B's phantom has 58 960 cells. On the new column both are printed: (R0) becomes a reproduction print against W3, and V_sub is printed to 13 digits beside the record. 3. The script is imported by path elsewhere. MAT-19's _load_spec_probes (tests/validation/test_mat19_probe_coil_phantom.py:96–105) executes the script as a module, and so do item 371a's and item 396's modules through _column_readout (tests/validation/test_ans9_far_side_sar.py:133). Code (script edit, a disclosed rule (c) change to an example; no src/ edit; no edit to any test module). - The EM half is route B, imported and never restated. Item 396's body steps 1–4 (tests/validation/test_ans9_far_side_sar_refined.py:161–200): - _build(True, phantom_resolution=RUNGS["h0025"], leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION); - build_four_port_sweep(built=…, build_only=True, degree=2); - _sweep(case, 2) (…refined.py:138), with _recip (:149); - _column_readout("h0025-d2x", f.e_complex, f.sigma_field, case["cell_tags"], comm) (test_ans9_far_side_sar.py:125) for G and (P1W); - _tag_submesh + _robin_tags, then q_h exactly as _thermal_readout builds it (test_ans9_far_side_sar.py:151–153): _to_sub(*_cell_average_dg0_tag(msh, ct, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, G·½σ·inner(e, e)), sub, parent_ids). - Imports by name: RUNGS (tests/validation/test_geo27_one_gram_rung_degree2.py:86), _build, build_four_port_sweep, GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION, _sweep, _recip, _column_readout, _to_sub, _robin_tags, _tag_submesh, _cell_average_dg0_tag, and the bands below. - Rows on the new column. That gives rows 1–6, (R1), (R3), (R6), (d6) and (s6) with the same snapshot, half-step and BE schedule. - Row 7 uses ANS-2's own arithmetic. Printed (predicted, never asserted). - Rows (predictions from W3's h0025-d2x lines, the same fixture and route): - row 1: 1 W; - row 2 ⟨θ⟩: 0.318123 / 0.614370 / 0.892184 / 1.153415 K (:1994); - row 3: slope 1.058563e-3 K/s, beside 1 W/(ρcV) = 1.058569e-3; - row 4 θ₄₀: A 0.889137, B 3.514465, C 0.683153, D 0.756873, E 0.959953 K (:1997); - row 5: max ≈ 4.3–4.5 K at r ∈ [0.020, 0.030] m, |az| ≤ 30° (1a: 4.457206); - row 6: 1254 − ρcV·⟨θ⟩₄₀ = 164.40 J (surface fraction 0.1311); - row 7: G·2.5e-3 W = 45 844.81 W at G = 1.833792433645e7 (:1986; +0.92 % from the degree-1 45 428.08), with supplied and accepted beside. - Reproduction against W3 (G, rows 2 / 3 / 4, SAR at A–E): predicted equal to ≤ 1e-6 relative. Item 396's x1 reproduced 371b's θ₄₀ to ≤ 6.5e-7, which is the thermal solver's digit floor; MUMPS at -n 8 is not bitwise. - Beside each row: the degree-1 value and the ratio degree 2 / degree 1. - Also: V_sub to 13 digits against V_SUB_RECORD_M3, κ_s, the first half-step deficit, and the PRICE line (build / sweep / thermal / body s, _peak_rss_gib(), ranks).

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (F0-ctl), x1 (W1), asserted > STEP3A_RECORD_RTOL; the factor is asserted. The same comparison on the same fixture read 1.020e-2 (…W1-x1.log:2039), ≈ 1e4× the band. - (d6), W2, the doubled source. (R6) against T·∫q_h misses by predicted 1.000 (the ceiling is exactly 1, by linearity). It is asserted only > D_CONTROL_FLOOR (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:102; 1a's sign-only form). - The factor is predicted. The nearest measurement on this fixture is (d6′), the (E′) form, at 1.000000 (…W3-h0025.log:1998), which is a different comparison. - (s6), W2, surface term dropped. Windows. Foreground. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Bash timeout: 660000. Two heavy windows never run at once. - First: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Then the any-orphan cache sweep as one bare call, label ANS-9-step1d-cache-sweep (daily-review.md rubric item 4). - Pre-censuses (with item 218's commands): ANS-9-step1d-pre-figures and ANS-9-step1d-pre-docrefs. - W0 (smoke, -n 1), before W2:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-9-step1d-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/unit/test_ans9_comparison_writer.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W1 (heavy, -n 8, the x1 route tie). It must print (complex build) and the 09_…py path. - W2 (heavy, -n 8, the column). Predicted harness 330–400 s, RSS ≤ 46.5 GiB summed. It is the runner's line in durable capture:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ANS-9-step1d-W2-h0025 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 examples/ansys_benchmarks/ans9_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz/09_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz.py > /workspace/logs/ans9-step1d-w2-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/ans9-step1d-w2-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/ans9-step1d-w2-raw.log; exit \$rc'"

The entry stays runnable, so rule (d) is met without BLOCKED (item 396's Q3 form).

Traps already paid for. - COMPARISON.md overwrite (finding 1). Never run W2 before W0's (R-keep) is green. - _four_port_rung has no phantom_resolution, and build_four_port_sweep(built=…) ignores sizing keywords, so h_p goes to _build only. Pass degree=2 on both the build and the sweep. Never pass width_correction_kappa: κ is off (2026-10-02 ruling). - Never call _solve_driven at h0025, degree 2. One extra factorisation costs ≈ 230–260 s and breaks 590 s. P1's field and current come from the one-factorisation sweep with keep_fields=True. - Free the sweep before the thermal runs. After taking q_h and row 7's current: del r2, gc.collect(). - Point reads. The N1curl point read uses owner="lowest_original_cell" on the parent (inside _column_readout). θ on the create_submesh mesh uses the default owner: lowest_original_cell raises "Mixed topology unsupported" there (item 218). Points are identical on every rank. - Snapshots and row 6. _transient snapshot 1 lands after two half-steps, and θ^{½} needs its own run. Never reconstruct row 6 from the balance itself (rule (h)). - XDMF. Name every Function before the write. No dots in the basename. write_xdmf_with_tags returns None off rank 0. - Reductions. Every one takes np.real and is allreduced on every rank; no collective sits inside rank == 0. Cell counts come from size_global / _global_tag_cell_count. - Imports. Import no test_* name and no pytest fixture. The 1c module's import-time knob read is inert with FEM_EM_ANS9_1C_RUNG unset (W2 leaves it unset). - Wrong rank count. Do not run ans:9 at -n 2: the degree-2 h0025 solve was priced at -n 8 only (46.5 GiB summed). The guide's old -n 2 -t 480 would not fit. - The pin test reads git ls-files. Stage metrics.json first. - Durable capture is copied verbatim, trailing ; exit $rc included. Use -k 30. No pipe inside the quoted command. - After a kill: run pgrep -c python3, then the cache sweep, then park. Status 124 is a price record, not a retry. Never raise the timeout or -n. - Rule (i): no script or test edit after its last window. An edit after W2 re-runs W0 → W2.

As posed (degree 2 on P24's h0025 fixture), P27 does not fit heavy. - The contraction identity re-solves E at every Picard iterate and power-iteration step: N = 8 + M = 5 = 13 _solve_driven calls (:99–100, :327–390), plus 3 at α = 0. - A degree-2 factorisation at h0025 costs ≈ 230–260 s at -n 8: the four-port sweep took 261.47 s with one factorisation (20261012T100436Z_ANS-9-step1c-W3-h0025.log:2054). σ(T) changes the matrix, so no factorisation can be held. - That is ≈ 16 × 245 ≈ 65 min, against a 590 s window and the 1200 s heavy ceiling. Item 410's degree-2 one-way column is printed beside. 3. solve_transient_conduction cannot restart from a field. It takes only a uniform scalar t_init (src/fem_em_solver/thermal/transient.py:103, :123). A staggered transient two-way (σ updated at the report times) is therefore built by superposition over source_schedule (:112, :136–143). The scheme is linear in q with θ(0) = 0 (t_init = T∞), so a run with source q_j switched on only in segment j, summed over j, is the staggered run. docs.title: ARCH-1 — The MRI-safety layer becomes solver-agnostic
docs.text: The MRI-safety layer becomes solver-agnostic — SAR averaging, B₁⁺ maps, loss partition, the thermal solve, the benchmark cases and their gates take fields and S-parameters from any field solver (ours, Palace's output, an HFSS field export) through one interface; the FEniCSx engine stays the in-house backend and the multiphysics home (operator directive 2026-09-20). EMBARGOED: not before the weekly of 2026-10-17 — four weeks out by the operator's instruction, so that PORT-21, OPS-61 (Palace) and the first human-scale physics land first and the interface is designed against two real backends, not one | ⬜ Not queueable by a daily review (outside §9 rule (4): it is architecture, not an enumerated chain step) and not to be scheduled by the weeklies of 09-26, 10-03 or 10-10 — those may only annotate this row with what they learn. Why: the project's replaceable part is the curl-curl solve; its hard-to-replace parts are the verification culture, the MRI-safety layer and the multiphysics reach. Today the safety layer is written against DolfinX function spaces, so it can only judge our own fields; decoupled, it is an evidence toolkit that works with the field solver a user already has — the wider audience arrives through "works with Palace / HFSS output", not through replacing the engine — and it is also what lets the engine be dropped later without losing anything else, should the target narrow. Shape (for the 10-17 weekly to write at execution grain): (1) a FieldSolution interface — an unstructured mesh with cell tags plus E (complex, cell- or edge-based) and the material map, read from XDMF/VTU or from a dolfinx function directly; and a PortSolution — a Touchstone file plus port metadata; (2) post/sar.py, post/b1.py, the loss partition and thermal/ consume only those; (3) two backends gated identically: the DolfinX one reproduces every existing MAT-4 / WF-6 / TH-14 record to the digit (the refactor moves no number), the Palace one reproduces OPS-61's S and the phantom power on the ANS-4 fixture; (4) the benchmark cases' runnable halves dispatch on the backend. Gate of record: digit-identical reproduction of every imported band and record on the DolfinX backend before any second backend is wired — a refactor that moves a record is a defect. Not in scope: a GUI, a new solver, changing any physics. Prerequisites the embargo waits on: OPS-61 step 1 (a second backend's fields to design against), PORT-21 (so the port interface is not frozen around a known offset), one F-human physics step (so the interface sees a human-scale field once).

docs.title: §9 item 517 — 2026-10-18 (§10 U16, ARCH-1 step 1; chain step, solve)
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-18 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. U16 is drafted as two items, 517 (U16a, the Study-side backend, the case writer and the read path, no Palace run) and 517b (U16b, the Palace runs and the S read-back, no code edit): the whole step does not fit one 1-hour slot (≈ 25 min of src/ + test code, four re-gate / build windows ≈ 10 min, two Palace windows ≈ 5 min, fixed + commit ≈ 21 min). This is a split on price and on a hard architectural fact (below), not a re-target. Four rulings are asked for at the end.

Licence. §10 chain U, U16 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4864–4870), weekly-enumerated (§9 rule (4)), quoted, not reworded: "Study.solve(backend="palace") and femem run --backend palace on the F-small four-port exact fixture: the Study writes the Palace config and mesh through OPS-61's writer, runs the fem-em-palace service, reads S back; target: equality with OPS-61 F26's recorded Palace read at ≤ 1e-9 (same input, same answer) and the tie to our degree-2 record at the recorded (T5) ≤ 1.9e-10 per class; the DolfinX path bitwise unchanged." The 2026-10-17 weekly lifted ARCH-1's embargo and named U16 its first step, glyph 🟡 when U16 lands (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4705–4709); the row's precondition (digit-identical DolfinX reproduction) is met by WF-16 step 1 and WF-14's snapshot (same lines). The Palace directive (§5.4 (i)–(v), PROJECT_PLAN.md:1176–1197), the sheets-and-κ ruling (exact rectangles, κ off), the 2026-10-13 03:00 rulings (1) and (4) (docs/planning/chunks/OPS-61.md:1208–1213) and the 2026-10-15 03:00 ruling on item 476 (docs/planning/chunks/ANS-4.md:651–653) bind. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved.

Finding that shapes the design: the solver container cannot run Palace. The fem-em-solver service mounts only ..:/workspace and the fem-em-cache volume (docker/docker-compose.yml:8–10); there is no docker socket inside it, and Palace lives only in its own image (fem-em-palace:0.18.1, docker/palace.Dockerfile), which has no DolfinX and no fem_em_solver. Every OPS-61 Palace window was a separate host-side harness call, docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/ops61 && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 <config>.json' (e.g. 20261003T110249Z_OPS-61-item194-W4-palace-o2.log:12), between two solver-container windows (write, then read). Mounting the socket is a mount change, which the §9 compose constraint forbids (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3946–3965: a blocked finding for the operator); putting Palace into the solver image is a Dockerfile change and also the operator's. So Study.solve(backend="palace") cannot literally "run the fem-em-palace service". The honest design, drafted here for the review to rule on (Ruling R2), is a three-stage backend: 1. Write. Study.solve(backend="palace", case_dir=D) builds the Study's mesh, writes D/case.json + D/mesh.msh + D/case.sha256 (a manifest of both files), or verifies byte-equality if they already exist. If D/postpro/port-S.csv is absent it raises PalaceRunRequired, whose .argv == ["palace", "-np", "8", "case.json"] and .cwd == D. femem run --backend palace prints the command and returns 3 (proposed new exit code, "external run pending"; R4). 2. Run. A separate harness window runs that command in fem-em-palace (host-side, exactly the OPS-61 shape). 3. Read. The same call again rebuilds and verifies the case byte for byte against the manifest, then reads D/postpro/port-S.csv through the lifted OPS-61 reader and returns a result carrying s_matrix. femem run --backend palace writes summary.json and returns 0.

The chain of custody (manifest checked at read time) is what makes "same input, same answer" a statement about the Study's own input, not about whatever sits in the directory.

Defects in the step text (for the review). - "OPS-61 F26's recorded Palace read" names no Palace read. F26 is ANS-6's copper h-rung, xl entry 31 (docs/planning/chunks/ANS-6.md:509, :620); the Palace read on that rung is F37 (§9 item 454: h = 0.0075 hole mesh, Boundaries.Conductivity on 401, four single-excitation windows of 142.9–144.9 s, docs/planning/chunks/OPS-61.md:2076). That is not the Study's F-small default (FourPortBirdcageGeometry.f_small() is the ×1 strip route, σ = 800 S/m volume conductor, src/fem_em_solver/study.py:225–269), and writing it would need a conductivity-boundary writer, as_hole and a resolution knob — three features beyond U16. Drafted on the fixture that is the Study's f_small() verbatim and that OPS-61 did read: the ×1 exact strip, logs/ops61/ops61_ans4_x1_strip.msh (117 206 tets, F10a), Palace v0.18.1 order 2 at 64 MHz, f05x_o2.json → postpro_f05x_o2/ (F17, §9 item 194, 20261003T110249Z_OPS-61-item194-W4-palace-o2.log; read 20261003T110728Z_OPS-61-item194-W5-read.log:49–56). Ruling R1. - "≤ 1.9e-10 per class" is the figure the 2026-10-15 03:00 review already ruled false (item 476: the bought maximum is 2.542e-10; the public ceiling is 2.6e-10, docs/planning/chunks/ANS-4.md:613, :653; 20261015T112551Z_ANS-4-item476-ties.log). On the drafted rung the recorded tie is 2.464e-10 / 9.668e-11 / 9.883e-11 (self / adjacent / opposite, 20261004T214342Z_OPS-61-item229-W4-read.log:41), so "≤ 1.9e-10" would fail the self class on Palace's own recorded output. Also, no cross-solver band constant exists and ties have been printed, never asserted (2026-10-13 ruling (1), OPS-61.md:1210). Ruling R3. - "through OPS-61's writer" cannot be an import. The writer is export() in a 5 410-line probe under scripts/ that imports tests/ (scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py:106–136), and src/ may not import either (WF-13's rule, as WF-16 step 1 applied it, docs/planning/chunks/WF-16.md, item 244). U16a lifts the writer and reader verbatim into src/ — the Gmsh 2.2 writer :213–302, the config dict :315–361, the reader _read_port_s :400–425 — and pins the copies with equality anchors against the probe's own files and functions (the WF-16 step 1 precedent). The probe is not edited. - §5.4 still says "nothing in src/ is built on Palace" (PROJECT_PLAN.md:1180–1181), and both Palace files say "Never the solver — nothing in src/ uses it" (docker/docker-compose.yml:107, docker/palace.Dockerfile:2). U8 (operator directive 2026-10-05, Palace as an opt-in backend behind the Study) supersedes that sentence in part, but it was never amended. U16 adds a Palace writer and reader to src/: it never imports or links Palace, and the default path never touches it. The plan sentence is the review's / weekly's to amend (Ruling R4). The compose comment is operator-owned (only environment: keys may be edited); flag it, do not edit it. - The ARCH-1 row still reads "EMBARGOED … Not queueable by a daily review" (this file :3 and the §7 row). The review amends it when it queues 517. - No Touchstone and no z_matrix on the Palace path. Palace's z_matrix_ohm is a terminated transimpedance (2026-09-29 ruling, never read), and PortStudyResult.write_touchstone needs an SParameterSweepResult (study.py:597–613). U16's summary carries s_matrix only; a Palace Touchstone is a follow-on, not U16.

ARCH-1 step 1a / U16a: the palace backend's write and read stages on the F-small ×1 exact strip, the written case proven equal to OPS-61's, the read path proven on OPS-61's recorded output, and the DolfinX path re-gated. - Executor: implementer. Additive src/ (a new private subpackage plus one dispatch branch each in Study.solve, run_study_file and cli.main), disclosed under ruling (c). One new test module. No probe, gate module, record, registry or generated page is edited. - Tier: - W0 smoke (-n 1, no mesh); - W1 heavy by ceiling (-n 1, mesh-only builds, no solve; ≈ 6 builds at ≈ 26–31 s each, F10a W3 31 s / mesh 26.4 s, 20261001T220353Z_OPS-61-F10a-W3-export.log; predicted 200–330 s); - W2 standard → heavy by ceiling (-n 2; 138 s measured, 20261005T202623Z_WF-16-W1-deg1.log); - W3 standard → heavy by ceiling (-n 2; 164 s measured, 20261007T051729Z_WF-1-s3-W3-wf1-w2.log); - W4 smoke (-n 1; 17 s measured, 20261015T214657Z_WF-17-s6-Wapi.log). - Class: chain step (solve; the DolfinX re-gates solve). Cost: ≈ 18 measured / ≈ 55 predicted slot-minutes: 15 fixed + ≈ 25 code + windows ≈ 10 (10 + 270 + 138 + 164 + 17 s) + commit and journal ≈ 6. Tight. If W1 is not green by minute 40, park (rule (d)). - Depends on: - nothing in §9; - on disk (gitignored, all present 2026-10-18, checked): logs/ops61/ops61_ans4_x1_strip.msh (Oct 1), logs/ops61/ops61_ans4_x1.msh (Sep 29, the ragged control), logs/ops61/f05x.json, logs/ops61/f05x_o2.json, logs/ops61/postpro_f05x/port-S.csv, logs/ops61/postpro_f05x_o2/port-S.csv, logs/ops61/postpro_f05x_o2_f10/port-S.csv. - If any is absent: the test that needs it skips with BLOCKED: <file> absent, and the item lands as BLOCKED with that line. Never re-export or overwrite an OPS-61 file (their traps: OPS-61.md:20, :98, :244). - Family: ARCH-1 step 1 (U16); attempt 1 of 4.

What the code is today. - Study.solve(self, comm=MPI.COMM_WORLD) (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:170–197) has no backend: a port geometry dispatches to _solve_ports (:173–174 → _study_solve_ports, :616, bound at :687). No palace / backend string exists anywhere in src/. - FourPortBirdcageGeometry.build (study.py:271–392) returns the mesh, cell tags, the narrowed sheet tags and per-sheet records; the full-sheet tags from _sheet_areas (:317–325) are reassigned and not returned. The writer needs F_i ∖ N_i (attributes 30 + i) to reproduce OPS-61's file, so it recomputes _sheet_areas from ports/_sheet_geometry.py:93 with the geometry's sheet_iface / port_lower / port_upper. build is not edited. - run_study_file (src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py:1354) calls study.solve(comm) at :1383; the four-port branch writes the Touchstone and s_matrix / z_matrix (:1412–1426). - cli.main (src/fem_em_solver/cli.py:120–181) maps StudyConfigError to rc 2 (:178–181); the run parser is :35–48. - The probe's writer runs serial only (assert comm.size == 1, ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py:139).

Code (additive; disclosed under ruling (c)). - New src/fem_em_solver/backends/__init__.py (empty) and src/fem_em_solver/backends/palace.py (found by [tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = ["src"], pyproject.toml:73–74). that log's :12 verbatim, relabelled; 138 s measured): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ARCH-1-U16a-W2-regate-wf16 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_WF16_DEGREE=1 timeout -k 30 400 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/package/test_wf16_study_four_port.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W3 (the WF-1 F-small CLI re-gate; Fix once; otherwise park. - W2 / W3 red: the dispatch moved the default path. Revert the src/ diff on the branch; BLOCKED. - W4 red: a public-surface or docstring leak. Fix in-letter (remove the leak) and re-run W0–W4. - Status 124 is not a result; park with the measured time.

docs.text:
Drafted with item 517; the review reviews both. No code edit.

ARCH-1 step 1b / U16b: Palace runs on the two cases the Study and femem wrote, and the Study reads S back — equal to OPS-61's recorded read on the same input, tied to our degree-2 record. - Executor: implementer. No edit to any file except the commit's record lines. - Tier: - W1 heavy (Palace -np 8, order 2, 64 MHz; 268 s measured on the same config, 20261003T110249Z_OPS-61-item194-W4-palace-o2.log — Total 265.6 s :351, 4 × 37 GMRES iterations :164–320, peak 6.1 G :368; predicted 240–400 s on today's box); - W2 smoke → standard (Palace -np 8, order 1; 26 s measured, 20261002T021838Z_OPS-61-F10b-W2-palace-f05x.log, Palace 23.35 s, 1.8 G); - W3 standard (-n 1, two mesh rebuilds and reads; predicted 70–120 s). - Class: chain step (solve). Cost: ≈ 18 measured / ≈ 30 predicted slot-minutes: 15 fixed + windows ≈ 7 (≈ 300 + 26 + 100 s) + pre-checks ≈ 2 + commit and journal ≈ 6. Start only before minute 30; W1 not started by minute 35 ⇒ do not start it (the slot rule; the Palace window may not cross the timebox). - Depends on: - item 517 DONE on main — skip otherwise; - on disk: logs/u16/f_small_d2_64/{case.json, mesh.msh, case.sha256} and logs/u16/f_small_d1_64_cli/palace_case/{…} with no postpro/; and logs/ops61/postpro_f05x_o2/port-S.csv, logs/ops61/postpro_f05x/port-S.csv. - If a logs/u16 case is absent, re-run item 517's W1 verbatim relabelled ARCH-1-U16b-W0-rewrite first (it writes them). If a postpro/ is already there, stop and report: never overwrite a Palace output. If an OPS-61 CSV is absent: BLOCKED ("comparand absent"); never re-run OPS-61's config to make one. - Family: ARCH-1 step 1 (U16); attempt 1 of 4.

Anchors (asserted, in W3, by T4 / T5 as committed in item 517). - (E2) same input, same answer, degree 2: ‖S_study − S_ops61‖_F / ‖S_ops61‖_F ≤ LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:165; the weekly's "≤ 1e-9"), S_study from Study.solve(backend="palace", case_dir=D2_CASE) and S_ops61 from read_port_s("logs/ops61/postpro_f05x_o2/port-S.csv") — one reader on both sides. Predicted ≤ 1e-11 (the CSV prints 13 significant digits; MUMPS / GMRES can drift by an ULP across processes, the OPS-43 observation, docs/testing/known-issues.md:79). Entry-wise max printed. - (E1) the CLI, degree 1: the same against postpro_f05x/port-S.csv, from summary.json after cli.main([... "--backend", "palace"]) returns 0. - (P) on Study and S_cli: (P-rec)'s set, bands iorted as in item 517. - (Tie2) the tie to our degree-2 record:** per classklzzwxh:0633meantudy −ean2| / |mean_P2zzwxh:0636 against ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["64"] (tests/validation/test_ans4_exact_strip_records.py:233), printed in e-notation beside the recorded 2.464e-10 / 9.668e-11 / 9.883e-11 (20261004T214342Z_OPS-61-item229-W4-read.log:41). Asserted ≤ 2.6e-10 only if the review rules R3 (a); otherwise printed, never asserted (2026-10-13 ruling (1)). Never against 1.9e-10. - (Tie1) per class against ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P1_RECORDS["64"] (:141): printed only (item 159's "0.0000 %", 20261002T022338Z_OPS-61-F10b-W6-ours-p1.log:1975). - Palace log check (executor, journalled). W1 / W2 each show 117 206 elements, Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on attributes 21–24, ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz, four GMRES solver converged lines, and ND (p = 2): 753062 (W1) / ND (p = 1): 140460 (W2) — item 194's numbers (OPS-61.md:275).

Negative controls. - Asserted (backed on the same fixture and comparison): (c-order) S_study's class means against Palace order 1 (postpro_f05x/port-S.csv) differ by > 1e-6 in every class. Measured 6.6674 / 2.5442 / 4.5224 % (20261003T110728Z_OPS-61-item194-W5-read.log:55); the weakest class clears the bar by ≈ 2.5e4×. The ceiling is the order move itself. A reader blind to the case (reading a stale or wrong-order file) fails it. - Predicted, printed: (c-freq) S_study against the 10 MHz order-2 read (postpro_f05x_o2_f10/port-S.csv): predicted O(1e-2 … 1e-1) Frobenius-relative (the 10 → 64 MHz change); not measured as a comparison, so never asserted.

Windows. Foreground, bare, timeout: 660000; -np ≤ 12; Palace v0.18.1, image fem-em-palace:0.18.1, profile palace. - Pre-check (not harness calls): docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps shows fem-em-solver Up; ls logs/u16/f_small_d2_64/ logs/u16/f_small_d1_64_cli/palace_case/ as above. A missing Palace image is a stop (2026-10-13 ruling (4)). - W1 (Palace, the Study's degree-2 case): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ARCH-1-U16b-W1-palace-d2 "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/u16/f_small_d2_64 && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 case.json'" - W2 (Palace, the CLI's degree-1 case): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ARCH-1-U16b-W2-palace-d1 "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/u16/f_small_d1_64_cli/palace_case && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 case.json'" - After any kill: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps for a lingering fem-em-palace container before W3. - W3 (the read-back, -n 1, knob on, T4 and T5 only): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh ARCH-1-U16b-W3-read "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_U16_PALACE_READ=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 400 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/package/test_arch1_palace_backend.py::test_u16_palace_read_back tests/package/test_arch1_palace_backend.py::test_u16_cli_palace_read_back -v -s --tb=short'"

Traps already paid for. - "Same input" includes -np 8. Item 194 ran -np 8; a different width changes Palace's partition and GMRES path. Never change -np, Order, Tol or MaxIts in-slot. - A GMRES … did not converge line is a finding, not a retry; that run's S is "not measured". - An abort on the port set (axis alignment) is a finding: never change Direction. - Palace writes postpro/ relative to its cwd; the window must cd into the case directory, as above. - The test module is used as committed by item 517 (rule (i)): no edit, not even a comment. - Compare S classes only; never read Palace's z_matrix_ohm. Record row and journal carry Palace's numbers in full (version, config, mesh cited) and our-vs-Palace gaps; no AED figure and no Palace figure set against an AED one in any tracked file (§5.4 (iv)). - Status 124 on W1 is the price finding: record it; never lengthen the timeout.

Scope. One fixture (×1 exact strip, κ off), one frequency (64 MHz), orders 1 and 2, S only. Not claimed: any other rung or frequency, copper / hole / F-human, fields from Palace (SAR, B₁⁺, the loss partition, thermal — ARCH-1 (1)–(2)), the benchmark dispatch (ARCH-1 (4)), an in-container Palace launch, accuracy (a cross-solver identity on our discretisation, not an accuracy level), GPU / AMR.

Negative result. docs.text:

How to analyze it, step by step) plus ## Setup figure and ## Related; - the setup PNG examples/materials/figures/materials_16_probe_readouts_in_coil_phantom_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

What the script does: 1. It builds MAT-19 step 2's fixture: MAT-15 P1's coil-driven gel phantom, 58 866 tag-3 cells, G = 1 W / P₁, CN + Rannacher, N = 40 to t* = 1254 s. 2. It reads the a = 5 mm ball-averaged probe series at ANS-9's SPEC centres A–E, plus C′, Ω and B⁺. 3. It re-asserts step 2's identities at their imported bands. 4. It prints what a probe log reports: the rise at the SPEC times, ball against point, a placement shift, and the probe-volume dependence at B.

Numbering: mat:14 and mat:15 belong to sibling items drafted the same day. This item writes mat:16 only and depends on neither. The runner selects by the zero-padded prefix 16_, so no registry edit is needed.

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents.
  • Tier: heavy, complex. The flagged run of record is at -n 2, and the control window at -n 4 (see "Why two widths"). Runner -t 590; container timeout -k 30 590.
  • Cost: ≈ 7 measured (example class median, as handed to this draft) / ≈ 55 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 25 script and guide + ≈ 13 windows.
  • Depends on: nothing. MAT-19 step 2's module is on main (item 258, landed 2026-10-06), and so is MAT-15 step 1's _run_heated (EX-79's lift).
  • Spawn prompt. The slot puts the first five sentences in verbatim, in the 03:00 review's EX-96 form, then the sixth:
  • "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-100, §9 item 301 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-100.md, heading §9 item 301). Do not spawn agents. Run every harness window in the foreground (Bash timeout: 660000) and never background one; do not end the turn while a window runs. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window."
  • Added for this item: "The control window runs at -n 4 and asserts (W) against the flagged run's npz; never recompute or delete that npz by hand."

Why two widths (the width identity's second width). MAT-19 step 2 asserted (W) at -n 4 and -n 1 against a -n 2 npz written by the gate module. The partition reading also ran at -n 4, the only width where the phantom submesh is split (O_4 = 2, G_4 = 1 378, docs/planning/chunks/MAT-19.md:459; at -n 2 it is owned by one rank, :462).
