docs.title: EX-101 — A sheet drawn inside a box becomes an integration surface: native interior facet tags and dS on a ghosted mesh (history)
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened 2026-10-07 by the 10:30 daily review (step 5, §5.4 ramp). §10 U11 (GEO-37 step 2, §9 item 267, GREEN 2026-10-06): a CAD-drawn interior face reaches DolfinX's facet tags on 0.11, and dS over it meets closed forms at STRIP_BAND on a shared_facet-ghosted mesh. No example shows an interior facet tag. Group: examples/meshing/ (real build, no solve; mesh:1 … mesh:12 exist).

Proposed §7 row (the review adds it in the same commit as item 302, rule (j)):

| EX-101 | A sheet drawn inside a box becomes an integration surface: native interior facet tags and dS on a ghosted mesh (history and §9 briefs: docs/planning/chunks/EX-101.md) (mesh:13; example-runner; opened 2026-10-07 by the 10:30 daily review, §5.4 ramp; angle: geometry/mesh input for the Phase 9 (9b) external-CAD user; base step §10 U11) Done-when: examples/meshing/13_interior_sheet_surface_integral.py + same-stem guide; real build, shared_facet ghosts, -n 2 and -n 4; imports GEO-37's fixture, closed forms and STRIP_BAND, restates none; asserted in-script: the reduced owned tag-201 count equals gmsh's triangle count, and ∫1, ∫g('+'), ∫(u⁺ + u⁻) over dS(201) and ∫1 ds(101) meet their closed forms at STRIP_BAND; controls: dS(999) assembles to 0.0 while validate_required_port_tags_exist raises on 999, and one planted dropped facet leaves the band; the combined XDMF (planted fields, rank, facet tags) is written; census +1, docrefs green; elapsed recorded ⇒ ✅. Not claimed: a port, a STEP import (U12 BLOCKED), an unghosted multi-rank run. | ⬜ Open: the brief is §9 item 302; no example shows an interior facet tag yet. | standard (smoke by prediction) |

docs.title: §9 item 302 — 2026-10-07 (§5.4 example; example-runner)
docs.text:
Outcome (2026-10-07 17:23Z, ✅): mesh:13 green at -n 2 (flagged, 20261007T172140Z_EX-101.log, 6 s wall) and -n 4 (20261007T172154Z_EX-101-control-n4.log, 3 s wall). (G) ghost cells 592 / 1162; (T) tags [101, 201], owned 192 = N_gmsh 192; (A) +8.9e-16 / +2.2e-16; (F) I2 +2.2e-16 / +2.2e-16, I3 +8.9e-16 / +2.2e-16; (I) +2.0e-15 / +1.1e-15; (V) raised; (c1) 0.0; (c2) −4.48e-3 / −5.07e-3; (c3) 0.9747 / 1.0695 printed; unfiltered tag-201 sum 210 / 247 vs 192. All equal the GEO-37 step-2 records. Census figures 93 → 94 broken=0, docrefs 93 → 94 dead=0 guide=0 exit 2 (predicted; stale 56 unchanged). No band, src/ or probe/gate edit.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-07 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §5.4 example ramp on a closed gate (§10 U11, PROJECT_PLAN.md:4709–4717). No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved; every band and closed form is imported by name.

EX-101 (mesh:13) adds examples/meshing/13_interior_sheet_surface_integral.py and a same-stem guide 13_interior_sheet_surface_integral.md. The guide carries the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step) plus ## Setup figure and ## Related. The setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB (scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py:124).

What the script does, for the Phase 9 (9b) user who will draw a port as a literal 2D sheet in an external CAD tool (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4294, "Ports as literal 2D sheets"): - It builds GEO-37's fixture by importing it: a unit box with one 0.8 × 0.6 rectangle embedded at z = 0.47 by occ.fragment, tagged as dim-2 physical group 201, the box faces 101, h = 0.08. - It reads the model through the project shim _model_to_mesh (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:13–28) with an explicit shared_facet cell partitioner, as step 2's probe does (tests/mesh/probe_geo37_interior_dS.py:87–94). - It shows the sheet arriving as facet tag 201, then integrates over it with dS(201): area, a planted linear field, a planted two-sided DG0 field, and the exterior ds(101) instrument. Every integral is allreduced. - It shows the two traps a sheet user meets: an absent tag assembles silently to zero (so tags are validated first), and ('+') is a cell-order side, not a geometric one.

Numbering and independence: - examples/meshing/ holds 01_ … 12_; this item writes 13_ only. run_examples.sh auto-discovers meshing examples by number (.claude/agents/example-runner.md:88–89), so no registry edit is needed. Items 298–301 may open other examples in the same queue; if one of them has already taken mesh:13 when this slot starts, use the next free number and note it. - It imports nothing from examples/ and depends on no other open item.

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents.
  • Build: real (the meshing group runs in the default real build, scripts/run_examples.sh:50–55, 273–281; GEO-37 step 2's windows ran real: PETSC_ARCH='linux-gnu-real64-32' ScalarType=float64, 20261006T185157Z_GEO-37-s2-W2.log:86). Never source complex mode.
  • Tier: standard ceiling (runner -t 180; container timeout -k 30 180), smoke by prediction. Ranks -n 2 (run of record) and -n 4 (control run, see (3)).
  • Cost: ≈ 7 measured (the example class median from today's five example items: 7 / 6 / 7 / 15 / 7 min, docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-07-daily-1030.md:12–16) / ≈ 40 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 script and guide + ≈ 5 for eight windows of under a minute each).
  • Depends on: nothing open. GEO-37 step 2 is recorded on main (docs/planning/chunks/GEO-37.md:161–176).
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-101, §9 item 302 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-101.md, heading §9 item 302). Do not spawn agents. Run every harness window in the foreground (Bash timeout: 660000) and never background one; do not end the turn while a window runs. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window."

Imports (never restated). - From tests.mesh.test_geo37_interior_dS (the gate module): STRIP_BAND (its import at :26, defined tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58), I1_CF (:34), I2_CF (:35), I3_CF (:36), I4_CF (:37). Importing the module is safe with GEO37_DS_RECORD_DIR unset: its pytestmark skip (:29–31) acts only under pytest collection. - From tests.mesh.probe_geo37_interior_facet (step 1's fixture, the one step 2 imports verbatim, probe_geo37_interior_dS.py:41–50): _build_model (:36), RECT (:30), H (:32), TAG_RECT, TAG_BOX (:33). The module's main() is guarded by if __name__ == "__main__", so the import runs nothing. - From tests.mesh.probe_geo37_interior_dS: _assemble (:55, the allreduced scalar that returns (value, error_text)), QD (:52, quadrature degree 2), TAG_ABSENT (:51). The script asserts each returned error_text is None before reading the value. - From src: - fem_em_solver.io.mesh: _model_to_mesh, _raise_geometry_failure_on_every_rank; - fem_em_solver.ports.definitions: PortDefinition, validate_required_port_tags_exist (:82), used only as a tag-presence check — the guide says so and claims no port; - fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils: write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership; - fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure.write_setup_figure. - No new number. The script states no area, closed form, band, tag, mesh size, triangle count or cell count as a literal. The planted field g = 2 + 3x + 5y and the DG0 side values 1 / 3 are the gate's (probe_geo37_interior_dS.py:114, 120, encoded in I2_CF / I3_CF); the script writes them exactly as the probe does and the guide says the closed forms come from I2_CF / I3_CF. If the review prefers, rule (a) allows one additive change: factor the probe's g and u construction into a helper in probe_geo37_interior_dS.py and import it; that edit requires the step-2 gate window re-run green in the same slot (see (3) step 6) and disclosure. Default: no helper edit; probe and gate files are imported unedited.

Order of calls in the script. gmsh.initialize() on every rank → rank 0 _build_model() inside try / except BaseException → _raise_geometry_failure_on_every_rank → N_gmsh = comm.bcast(...) → _model_to_mesh(gmsh.model, comm, 0, gdim=3, partitioner=dolfinx.mesh.create_cell_partitioner(dolfinx.mesh.GhostMode.shared_facet, 2)) → gmsh.finalize() → (G) → (T) → (V) → the integrals (A), (F), (I) → controls → XDMF → setup figure → prints → asserts.

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script, at every width the example runs). - (G) The mesh is ghosted before any dS is assembled: comm.size == 1 or the reduced index_map(3).num_ghosts > 0. Checked collectively (one allreduce), raising on every rank if false. Record 592 at -n 2, 1162 at -n 4 (20261006T185157Z_GEO-37-s2-W2.log:48, :55; printed beside the reading). This guard is the example's protection against ever assembling dS unghosted at more than one rank. - (T) The sheet arrives as a tag, complete and unduplicated: - the globally reduced facet-tag set equals [TAG_BOX, TAG_RECT] (record [101, 201], …s2-W2.log:48, :55); - the owned tag-201 count (local facets < index_map(2).size_local, allreduced) equals N_gmsh — an integer identity against gmsh's own triangle count on the same run (step 1's (A2), GEO-37.md:46). Record 192 at every width (…s2-W2.log:48, :55; GEO-37.md:97–99). - (A) Area: |I1 / I1_CF − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND, I1 = ∫ 1 dS(TAG_RECT). Records +8.9e-16 (-n 2) / +2.2e-16 (-n 4) (GEO-37.md:168–169). - (F) Planted fields: |I2 / I2_CF − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND with I2 = ∫ g('+') dS(TAG_RECT); |I3 / I3_CF − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND with I3 = ∫ (u('+') + u('-')) dS(TAG_RECT). Records I2 +2.2e-16 / +2.2e-16, I3 +8.9e-16 / +2.2e-16 (GEO-37.md:168–169). - (I) Instrument: |I4 / I4_CF − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND, I4 = ∫ 1 ds(TAG_BOX). Records +2.0e-15 / +1.1e-15 (GEO-37.md:168–169). - (V) A missing tag raises: validate_required_port_tags_exist([PortDefinition("P1", TAG_RECT, TAG_BOX, ...)], tag_set) passes; the same call with TAG_ABSENT raises ValueError matching missing required port tags: [999] — deterministic on every rank because tag_set is the reduced set (the test's form, test_geo37_interior_dS.py:131–139). Catch on every rank, never under rank == 0.

Printed, not asserted: - cells (record 10 150, GEO-37.md:93; …s2-W2.log:48), N_gmsh, per-rank owned and local tag-201 counts, per-rank one-sided count; - the unfiltered rank-local tag-201 sum beside the owned sum — what a user who sums facet_tags without the owned filter would report. Predicted from the same comparison on the same fixture: 210 vs 192 at -n 2, 247 vs 192 at -n 4 (sums of per_rank_local_201 [100, 110] / [49, 68, 34, 96], …s2-W2.log:48, :55). Printed, not asserted: no gate asserts it on a ghosted mesh; - seconds for mesh, import and assembly (records per width: 0.31–0.34 / 0.11–0.12 / 0.31–0.34 s, …s2-W2.log JSON seconds_* at :48, :55).

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) asserted — an absent tag assembles silently to zero: _assemble(comm, 1 * dS(TAG_ABSENT)) returns exactly 0.0 with no error. Backing, the same comparison on the same fixture at -n 1 / 2 / 4: 0.0 (GEO-37.md:167–169, 174; asserted at test_geo37_interior_dS.py:147). Ceiling: the miss against I1_CF is 100 % relative (1.0 ≈ 10⁹ × STRIP_BAND); a blind integrator cannot do worse. This is why (V) exists: the assembly does not raise, the validator does. - (c2) asserted — one dropped facet leaves the band: re-tag 201 with the first owned facet of the lowest owning rank removed (the probe's construction, probe_geo37_interior_dS.py:161–176: a new meshtags built on every rank); assert |I1′ / I1_CF − 1| > STRIP_BAND. Backing on the same fixture: −4.48e-3 (-n 2), −5.07e-3 (-n 4) (GEO-37.md:168–169). Ceiling: one facet's share of the area, ≈ 1 / N_gmsh = 1/192 ≈ 5.2e-3, ≈ 4.5 × 10⁶ × the band at the smaller reading; every facet has positive area, so the miss is certain. Print 1 / N_gmsh beside it. Build the reduced meshtags with sorted, unique int32 indices (the probe's mask keeps the original order). - (c3) printed, predicted, never asserted — ('+') is not a geometric side: ∫ u('+') dS(TAG_RECT). Records 0.9747 (-n 2), 1.0695 (-n 4) (GEO-37.md:168–169); predicted inside [I1_CF × 1, I1_CF × 3] = [0.48, 1.44] at any width and different between the two runs. The guide uses it to say a sheet's orientation must come from the user (an integration line, the (9b) convention), not from DolfinX's '+' side. - No unghosted leg. The example never constructs GhostMode.none and offers no option to.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. Nothing is chained or piped. 0. Orphan check: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Then the rubric's cache sweep (daily-review.md:426) as one bare call labelled EX-101-cache-sweep. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-101-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-101-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - Census at drafting: 93 (EX-97's outcome, docs/planning/chunks/EX-97.md:195). Use whatever the pre-census reads; items 298–301 may land first. 2. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-101-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mesh:13 -n 2 -t 180 --dry-run". It must not print (complex build) (run_examples.sh:281). 3. Run of record (flagged), -n 2, predicted [10, 60] s. - Basis: step 2's five completed probe legs plus pytest fit in ≈ 11 s of the 56 s window, the rest being the killed unghosted -n 4 leg's 45 s ceiling (…s2-W2.log:135–136; GEO-37.md:175); step 1's three widths plus pytest ran 5 s (GEO-37.md:93). The example adds ≈ 15 s for the setup figure and ≈ 5 s for the XDMF, plus a possible cold FFCx compile of the interpolation / XDMF forms. - Command: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-101 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/meshing/13_interior_sheet_surface_integral.py"' - PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace because the script imports from tests.*; the dry run emits /workspace/src only (run_examples.sh:279; the EX-93 / EX-96 disclosure). Note any other difference. 4. Control run, -n 4, without the figure flag: git add the PNG, then the same line with mpiexec -n 4 and no -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-101-control-n4, predicted [5, 40] s. The control changes the width on purpose — -n 4 is the width whose partition runs along the sheet (step 1: 9 facets of local-copy excess, GEO-37.md:99, 101), where ghosting is load-bearing. Compare at the band, never bitwise (the EX-91 ruling): - integers equal: N_gmsh, owned count, tag set, cells; - (A) / (F) / (I) each inside STRIP_BAND of its closed form at both widths; - (c3), cells_ghost, per-rank counts and the unfiltered sum differ by design; printed only. 5. Post-censuses: EX-101-post-figures / EX-101-post-docrefs, the step 1 commands with those labels. Write the prediction first: - figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0; - docrefs: runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1. 6. Only if rule (a) was used: re-run the gate window green in the same slot, scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-101-gate-geo37-s2 with step 2's W2 command verbatim (GEO-37.md:136, with tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py as W2's environment path, GEO-37.md:162), -s kept. It contains the deliberate unghosted -n 4 leg, which is killed at 45 s by design; the footer is pytest's. pgrep -c python3 reads 0 afterwards.

No pytest window is needed otherwise: the gates are re-read in-script. Any pytest window runs with -s (rule (g)).

Output. - Combined XDMF examples/meshing/paraview_output/meshing_13_interior_sheet_surface_integral_combined.xdmf, written with write_xdmf_with_tags(..., facet_tags=facet_tags) so tags 201 and 101 are a facet block in the same file. Fields (the example has planted fields, so the combined file is required): - g_planted: P1, g interpolated (exact for a linear g); - u_side: DG0, 1 below / 3 above the sheet plane (the (F) / (c3) field); - rank: DG0, each owned cell's MPI rank (x.array[:n_owned] = comm.rank, then scatter_forward()), so a reader can see where the partition cuts the sheet. - adopt_host_ownership after the write, as the precedents do. - Setup figure examples/meshing/figures/meshing_13_interior_sheet_surface_integral_setup.png. write_setup_figure draws cell regions only (src/fem_em_solver/post/setup_figure.py:180–195; mesh:4 titles its sheets "not drawn"), so build a display-only cell meshtags: tag 2 = local cells with a facet in tag 201 (both sides, via facet-to-cell connectivity), tag 1 = the rest; sorted unique int32 indices. Region names "air box (faces: facet tag 101)" and "tets touching the drawn sheet (facet tag 201)", tag 1 translucent, slice_normal=(0, 1, 0). Title ≤ 130 characters (MAX_TITLE_CHARS, setup_figure.py:65), e.g. mesh:13 -- a sheet drawn inside a box becomes facet tag 201; tets touching it shown (GEO-37). The display tags never enter an integral. - Guide. - The CAD recipe in words and code: draw the face, occ.fragment the box with it so the face is embedded, one dim-2 physical group per sheet, mesh, import. Say that occ.fragment is what makes the face part of the volume mesh (step 1's trap: an unembedded face's triangles are not tet facets, GEO-37.md:66). - The one line a multi-rank user must not miss: build the mesh with GhostMode.shared_facet; the unghosted -n 4 assembly hung on this fixture (GEO-37.md:175) — stated as a record, not reproduced. - Three reading rules: reduce owned facets before counting (the printed unfiltered sum shows why); an absent tag integrates to zero silently, so validate tags first; ('+') is a cell-order side, so a one-sided integral depends on the partition (the (c3) readings differ between the two runs). - Scope sentences (below), including that the face here is drawn in gmsh in-process, not imported from a STEP file. - ParaView recipe: open the combined XDMF, select the facet block and Threshold on tag 201 to see the sheet; colour the cell block by rank, then by u_side with a slice through y = 0.5. - ## Related lists mesh:4 (the cut / sliver-pair sheet route this replaces for drawn sheets), tests/mesh/test_geo37_interior_dS.py, tests/mesh/probe_geo37_interior_dS.py, tests/mesh/probe_geo37_interior_facet.py and src/fem_em_solver/ports/definitions.py. Every artifact by full filename (rule (b)).

(4) Traps already paid for. - dS on an unghosted mesh hangs at the width whose partition runs along the sheet (PORT-1 3b-iv on 0.7, 20260805T034007Z_PORT-1-step3biv-hang-localise-fine.log; reproduced on 0.11 at -n 4, killed at 45 s in both step-2 windows, not localised, GEO-37.md:175). The example passes the shared_facet partitioner, asserts (G) before assembling, and runs no unghosted leg at any width. - If a window hangs anyway (no footer before the 180 s container timeout): it is killed by timeout -k 30 180; then docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0 before anything else; clear leaked /dev/shm/mpich_shm_* segments (known-issues; GEO-37.md:68); sweep orphan .c only at pgrep 0. Then park and stop (see (6)). Never retry with a longer timeout, never drop to fewer ranks to get a green, never switch ghost mode. - Rank-0 gmsh throw must be broadcast before the collective import (GEO-23; _raise_geometry_failure_on_every_rank). _build_model already classifies the face at 1e-6 because OCC bounding boxes are padded (GEO-37.md:92). - FFCx compile on a SpatialCoordinate facet integral without a pinned quadrature degree ran > 9 min and poisoned the cache (POST-5 step 1): use the imported QD on every measure. - Interior facets need ('+') / ('-'); an unrestricted coefficient in dS does not compile. - Rank-local quantities: assemble_scalar, facet_tags.values and local counts are rank-local; _assemble allreduces; counts use the owned filter and allreduce; cells use size_global. - Collectives on every rank: the import, _assemble, the meshtags builds, write_xdmf_with_tags and write_setup_figure are collective. Prints go under rank == 0 with no collective inside (item 227's deadlock). (V)'s ValueError is caught on every rank. - Docrefs: name no scratch path or JSON record in guide prose (EX-93's first post-docrefs exited 1 on a bare filename, EX-97.md:149); write artifacts by full repo-relative filename. - Bare harness calls only, repo-relative, nothing chained (cd … &&, ; date, | tail and redirects are denied by bash_guard.py); -k 30 on every container timeout; executors foreground, never nested; Bash timeout: 660000; never delete a log, including a red or footerless one. - Rule (i): no edit to the script or guide after its last window. Write ≈, never ~.

(5) Scope. - Covered: one planar rectangle drawn in gmsh in-process, embedded by occ.fragment, h = 0.08, the default partitioner with shared_facet ghosts, real build, -n 2 and -n 4: tag arrival, a facet area, a linear and a two-sided piecewise-constant integrand, the exterior instrument, an absent-tag control. - Not claimed: - a port: no port operator, voltage functional, S-parameter or orientation (the PortDefinition call checks tag presence only); - a STEP import: U12 (GEO-34 step 1d, the STEP with a named port face) is BLOCKED — Gmsh's STEP writer drops the names and the embedded face (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3936); - an unghosted multi-rank run, or why the unghosted leg hangs; - complex-build forms, curved or multi-face sheets, a sheet on a material interface or touching the boundary, other partitioners, xl widths; - anything GEO-37 steps 1–2 do not claim.

(6) Negative result. If (G), (T), (A), (F), (I), (V), (c1) or (c2) misses, or a window hangs: - report the measurement and stop; - journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-101, and mark item 302 BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)); - leave EX-101 ⬜ and never widen a band or edit src/ or the probe / gate files (rule (a) aside, as above).

What each miss means: - (A) / (F) red with (I) green, or a ghosted window that hangs: contradicts U11's GREEN record at that width — a GEO-37 step-2 finding for the review (§7 annotation on GEO-37, a known-issues 9 line), not an example fix. - (T) red: the owned count ≠ N_gmsh — a facet-distribution defect on the ghosted import, step 1's red branch (the sliver-pair importer, GEO-37.md:77); to the review. - (I), (c1) or (c2) red: the instrument is wrong; fix the example once before the record window, disclose; still red ⇒ park as above. - (V) does not raise: a ports/definitions.py regression; stop and report (§6). - Cells or N_gmsh differ from the printed records with every assertion green: a mesher-version event (rule (1*)), reported for record-reconciler; not a stop, since nothing asserts them.

A run killed at 180 s is not a result: check orphans and stop. The fallback is a re-queue, never a longer timeout and never an unghosted or narrower substitute.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-101 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). Census examples +1 with broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1. The review adds the §7 row in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). This is the first example of a CAD-drawn interior sheet used as an integration surface, so Phase 9 (9b)'s "ports as literal 2D sheets" and (9d)'s "tutorials drawn from examples/" gain a runnable demonstration of the native-tag half; the port half waits for U12.

Review rulings (2026-10-07 10:30 daily review, item 302). (1) mesh:13: no collision with items 298–301 (those are mat:14 … mat:16 and a generator knob). (2) The control window runs at -n 4 (ghosted), where the partition crosses the sheet: accepted. No unghosted multi-rank leg runs, in either window. (3) The planted fields' literals (g = 2 + 3x + 5y, DG0 values 1 / 3) are inputs, not bands or records. They are imported from the probe by name if it exposes them; otherwise they are restated with a comment citing probe_geo37_interior_dS.py:114, 120. The closed forms I2_CF / I3_CF and STRIP_BAND are always imported. (4) The cell and triangle counts are printed beside their log records, never asserted. (T) asserts the owned count against the same run's N_gmsh. (5) The floor counts it at the example median (7).

docs.title: EX-102 — Refine the mesh at an implant tip: the CAD does not move, the cap-ball cells grow as (r/4 ÷ h)³ (history)
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened 2026-10-07 by the 18:00 daily review (step 5, §5.4 ramp). The base is GEO-36 step 4 (§9 item 298, commit a49f997c, DONE 2026-10-07; docs/planning/chunks/GEO-36.md:211–236). It added the knob implant_rod["tip_size"] (the cap-Ball VIn, metres; unset = r/4) to the rod generator, gated by tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py.

No example shows local mesh refinement at an implant tip. Checked at drafting: no examples/meshing/*.md or examples/implants/*.md names tip_size, and no example script passes it. imp:3 (examples/implants/03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.py) solves on the default r/4 tip only. mesh:3 / mesh:5 grade conductors and regions, not an implant.

Group: examples/meshing/, not examples/implants/. The implants group always runs in the complex build: run_examples.sh sources complex mode for imp: (scripts/run_examples.sh:273–275, labelled at :176). The knob is a mesh-only feature, and its gate ran in the real build (20261007T170700Z_GEO-36-step4-W2-rungs.log:50: PETSC_ARCH='linux-gnu-real64-32' ScalarType=float64). This example runs no solve. So it belongs with the real-build, no-solve meshing group, beside mesh:3 (graded conductors) and mesh:5 (region resolution policy). mesh:1 … mesh:13 exist.

Proposed §7 row (the review adds it in the same commit as item 304, rule (j)):

| EX-102 | Refine the mesh at an implant tip: the CAD does not move, the cap-ball cells grow as (r/4 ÷ h)³ (history and §9 briefs: docs/planning/chunks/EX-102.md) (mesh:14; example-runner; opened 2026-10-07 by the 18:00 daily review, §5.4 ramp; angle: the implant_rod["tip_size"] knob for the Phase 7 user who refines at a lead tip; base GEO-36 step 4, §9 item 298) Done-when: examples/meshing/14_implant_tip_refinement.py + same-stem guide; real build, no solve, -n 2 (flagged) and -n 4 (control); imports GEO-36 step 4's fixture, rungs, record and bands, restates none; asserted in-script per rung (unset, r/(4√2), r/8): (A0) CAD masses, wall area and centroid bitwise equal to the unset build's, tip_size_m = request; (A1) / (A3) at CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND, (A4) in TERMINAL_AREA_BAND, (A5) census, (A6) at EXACT·l; (D) N1curl d2 = 2E + 2F, d1 = E; (G) N_ball strictly increasing; unset cells against ROD_1G_RUNG_CELL_RECORD at CELL_COUNT_BAND; control (c1): two out-of-range tip_size values refused before gmsh; three combined XDMFs and the setup figure written; census +1, docrefs green; elapsed recorded ⇒ ✅. Not claimed: a solve, η_rod or tip SAR, an h-convergence statement, I15's solve windows, a ball-radius knob, the kept-cells build. | ⬜ Open: the brief is §9 item 304; no example refines at an implant tip yet. | heavy (by measurement) |

docs.title: §9 item 304 — 2026-10-07 (§5.4 example; example-runner)
docs.text:
Outcome (2026-10-08 00:43Z, ✅): mesh:14 green at -n 2 (flagged, 20261008T003337Z_EX-102.log, 239 s wall) and -n 4 (20261008T003809Z_EX-102-control-n4.log, 242 s wall). (N) 252 118 / record = 1.000000; (A0) True at all three rungs; (A1) 1.110e-16, (A3) 0 at every rung; (A4) 0.996254 / 0.996674 / 0.996934; (A5) True, tag 402 4 958 / 6 256 / 8 790; (A6) 1.735e-18; (D) d2 1 620 748 / 1 775 954 / 2 200 500, d1 302 002 / 331 014 / 410 054; (G) N_ball 11 938 / 32 826 / 93 132 strictly increasing; (c1) both refused, gmsh untouched. Printed: N_ball ×2.7497 / ×7.8013 vs cubic 2.828 / 8.000; cells 252 118 / 276 088 / 342 072; (c2) air 99 975 / 99 849 / 99 881, phantom 109 724 / 133 796 / 199 748; near-T1 11 / 19 / 26 cells. Every integer equal at -n 2 and -n 4 and to the GEO-36 step 4 W2 records. Census figures 97 → 98 broken=0, docrefs 97 → 98 dead=0 guide=0 exit 2 (predicted; stale 56 unchanged). Deviations: the orphan check needed -f docker/docker-compose.yml (read 0, unlogged); the script adds a local _ball_mask for the in_tip_ball field, asserted equal to _summarise's N_ball; the guide was written between the -n 2 and -n 4 windows (no edit after the last window). No band, src/ or gate edit.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-07 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §5.4 example ramp on a closed step (GEO-36 step 4, DONE 2026-10-07, GEO-36.md:211). No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved. Every band, record and constant is imported by name.

EX-102 (mesh:14) adds examples/meshing/14_implant_tip_refinement.py and a same-stem guide 14_implant_tip_refinement.md. The guide carries the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step) plus ## Setup figure and ## Related. The setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB (scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py:124).

What the script does, for the Phase 7 user who wants a finer mesh at a lead or rod tip without touching the geometry: - It builds GEO-36 step 4's fixture by importing it: the four-port F-small birdcage with a 1 mm-radius, 32 mm tip-to-tip capped rod cut from the phantom, at the 1 g phantom rung. It builds three times, at tip_size unset (= r/4), r/(4√2) and r/8, coarse to fine. - It shows that the knob is sizing only: the CAD masses, the OCC wall area and the wall centroid are bitwise identical at every rung. - It shows the refinement landing where it was asked for: the phantom cells inside the 2r cap balls grow ≈ as the cube of the size ratio (2.75× and 7.80× against the cubic model's 2.83× and 8×, 20261007T170700Z_GEO-36-step4-W2-rungs.log:7516–7517). The air count barely moves. - It shows what the refinement costs: cells, edges, faces and the N1curl degree-1 / degree-2 dof counts per rung. The guide reads them as the price a solve would pay.

Numbering and independence: - examples/meshing/ holds 01_ … 13_; this item writes 14_ only. run_examples.sh auto-discovers meshing examples by number (.claude/agents/example-runner.md:82–83), so no registry edit is needed. If another item has taken mesh:14 when this slot starts, use the next free number and note it. - It imports nothing from examples/ and depends on no other open item.

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents.
  • Build: real. The meshing group runs in the default real build (scripts/run_examples.sh:273–275: mesh is not in the complex-prefix list). GEO-36 step 4's three windows ran real (20261007T170700Z_GEO-36-step4-W2-rungs.log:50; 20261007T170256Z_GEO-36-step4-W1-noop.log:50). Never source complex mode, and never set FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX.
  • Tier: heavy, by measurement. The fixture's own windows ran 238 s (W1, three builds, …W1-noop.log:5748) and 330 s (W2, four builds, …W2-rungs.log:7674), both above the standard 180 s ceiling. Runner -t 590; container timeout -k 30 590. Ranks -n 2 (run of record) and -n 4 (control, see (3)). Each window is predicted ≈ 5–6 min, well under the ≈ 10 min durable-capture threshold.
  • Cost: ≈ 7 measured (the example class median, as handed to EX-101: 7 / 6 / 7 / 15 / 7 min, docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-07-daily-1030.md:12–16) / ≈ 55 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 25 script and guide + ≈ 15 windows (two heavy windows of ≈ 5–6 min each, plus ≈ 3 min of small windows).
  • Depends on: nothing open. GEO-36 step 4 is recorded on main (GEO-36.md:211–236, commit a49f997c).
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-102, §9 item 304 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-102.md, heading §9 item 304). Do not spawn agents. Run every harness window in the foreground (Bash timeout: 660000) and never background one; do not end the turn while a window runs. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window."

Imports (never restated). - From tests.mesh.test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip (the gate module): - records and rungs: ROD_1G_RUNG_CELL_RECORD (:90), ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2_PRINTED (:96), RUNAWAY_CELL_GUARD (:98), TIP_R4, TIP_R4S2, TIP_R8 (:112–114), PLANS (:116–119; the script iterates PLANS["rungs"]), FIXTURE_KW (:131–134); - probe point and tags: T1 (:84), T1_RADIUS (:100), AIR_CELL_TAG, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG (:122–123); - helpers: _summarise (:199, which calls _ball_and_t1 :158, _dofs :186 and _facet_check), _cell_geometry (:142) and _mean_edge (:150), for the XDMF field. - Importing the module is safe with FEM_EM_GEO36_STEP4 unset. KNOB (:111) is read but only gates pytest.mark.skipif marks. The module-level _load of scripts/probes/imp3_step4_palace_fields.py (:83–84) ran in the real build in W1 / W2. - From the gate module's own imports (re-imported by name from their defining modules, as the gate does at :49–71): - bands: CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_conductor_hole.py:123), EXACT (:117), TERMINAL_AREA_BAND (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_leg_gaps.py:73), CELL_COUNT_BAND (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheet_prerequisite.py:57); - fixture: ROD, ROD_RADIUS, ROD_LENGTH, ROD_CENTRE, _build_rod, _rod_area, _phantom_minus_rod (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py:93–97, 117–125), PORT_LOWER, PORT_UPPER (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets.py:73, 77), LEG_COUNT (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_tags.py:22). - From src: - fem_em_solver.io.mesh.BIRDCAGE_IMPLANT_SURFACE_TAG (:272); - fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils: write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership; - fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure.write_setup_figure. - Never import tests/validation/test_imp3_* in the real build (GEO-36 item 298 trap, GEO-36.md:195). ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 is read through the gate module's ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2_PRINTED. - No new number. The script states no cell count, N_ball, edge length, band or size as a literal. Two inputs are restated, each with a comment citing its source: - (c1)'s two refusal inputs, ROD_RADIUS / 3.0 and 0.0, the gate's own (test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:265); - the conductor cell tag 1 in the expected tag set, built exactly as the gate does (:318–320).

These are inputs, not bands or records (the EX-101 ruling (3) precedent). Default: no gate-module edit; every module above is imported unedited.

Order of calls in the script. (c1) refusals, on every rank, before any build → assert not gmsh.isInitialized() → for each (label, tip) in PLANS["rungs"] (unset, r/(4√2), r/8; coarse to fine, GEO-23): 1. out = _build_rod(implant_rod=ROD if tip is None else dict(ROD, tip_size=tip), **FIXTURE_KW); 2. s = _summarise(label, tip, out, comm). It prints the gate's own [GEO-36 step 4] lines and raises at RUNAWAY_CELL_GUARD. It drops only its local names; the caller's out still holds the mesh; 3. the per-rung combined XDMF; 4. keep out only for the last rung (r/8); drop the others.

Then: setup figure on the r/8 mesh → prints → asserts. Asserts run on every rank, from reduced values only.

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script, at every width the example runs). Each reading is from W2 (-n 2), the closing window of GEO-36 step 4. - (N) Record: |cells(unset) / ROD_1G_RUNG_CELL_RECORD − 1| < CELL_COUNT_BAND. The ratio is printed to 6 d.p. Record 252 118 at -n 1, -n 2 and -n 8 (…W2-rungs.log:3752; test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:86–90). Unset = explicit r/4 as integers is W1's (N0) (…W1-noop.log:5588). It is cited in the guide, not re-run: that would be a fourth build. - (A0) The knob is sizing only: at every rung, diag["cad_mass_by_group"], implant_rod_cad["wall_area_m2"] and ["wall_centroid_m"] are == the unset build's. tip_size_m == the request, or TIP_R4 when unset. Record: True at all three rungs, wall area 2.0106192982974677e-4 m² (…W2-rungs.log:7502–7504). - (A1) / (A3) / (A4) / (A5) / (A6) per rung, the gate's expressions (test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:333–364) with its imported bands: - (A1) |cad_mass_by_group["phantom"] / _phantom_minus_rod() − 1| < CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND; - (A3) |wall_area_m2 / _rod_area() − 1| < CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND; - (A4) area402 / _rod_area() inside TERMINAL_AREA_BAND; - (A5) census set = the expected set, census sum = cells, tag 402 > 0, all exterior and all on PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, 0 interior; - (A6) wall centroid |x − ROD_CENTRE[0]|, |y|, |z| ≤ EXACT * ROD_LENGTH. - Records (…W2-rungs.log:7507–7509): (A1) 1.110e-16 and (A3) 0 at every rung; (A4) 0.996254 / 0.996674 / 0.996934; tag 402 4 958 / 6 256 / 8 790; (A6) 1.7e-18. - (D) Dof identities, per rung: N1curl size_global * bs at degree 2 = 2E + 2F, and at degree 1 = E, exactly (_summarise's _dofs). Records (…W2-rungs.log:7512–7514): d2 1 620 748 / 1 775 954 / 2 200 500; d1 302 002 / 331 014 / 410 054. - (G) The refinement reaches gmsh: N_ball(r/(4√2)) > N_ball(unset) and N_ball(r/8) > N_ball(r/(4√2)), with N_ball from _summarise (owned tag-3 cells with centroid within tip_ball_radius_m of either cap centre, allreduced). Records 11 938 / 32 826 / 93 132 (…W2-rungs.log:3753, 5613, 7501). - Runaway guard: every rung < RUNAWAY_CELL_GUARD, raised inside _summarise before (D) on every rank.

Printed, not asserted (each beside its log record; no gate band exists for these, rule (e)): - The headline: N_ball ÷ N_ball(unset) beside the cubic model (TIP_R4 / h)³, computed from the imported TIP_*. Records 2.7497 vs 2.828 and 7.8013 vs 8.000 (…W2-rungs.log:7516–7517). Predicted to repeat to the printed digits, since the mesh is serial gmsh on rank 0 and identical at every width. Not asserted: no band for the ratio exists, and this item sets none. - Cells per rung, 252 118 / 276 088 / 342 072 (…:3752, 5612, 7500), and cells ÷ unset, 1.0951 / 1.3568 (…:7516–7517). r/8 is printed against ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2_PRINTED: 342 072 > 320 000 (GEO-36.md:227), so a test_imp3_*-style guard would trip at r/8. - Mean ball-cell edge ÷ tip_size_m: 1.3590 / 1.3765 / 1.3779 (…:3753, 5613, 7501). - Near-T1 (T1_RADIUS) mean edge and cell count: 6.983e-4 / 6.422e-4 / 5.082e-4 m on 11 / 19 / 26 cells (…:3753, 5613, 7501). The step-4 brief predicted these unchanged; they moved −8 % / −27 % (GEO-36.md:227). The guide states this as the measured fact that the Ball field grades past its 2r radius. - E, F, per-tag census, build seconds (61.65 / 71.40 / 86.71 s, …:3752, 5612, 7500).

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) asserted — an out-of-range tip_size is refused before gmsh starts: - _build_rod(implant_rod=dict(ROD, tip_size=v), **FIXTURE_KW) raises ValueError matching implant_rod for v = ROD_RADIUS / 3.0 (coarser than the r/4 cap) and v = 0.0; - gmsh.isInitialized() is False afterwards; - caught on every rank, never under rank == 0.

Backing, the same comparison on the same fixture at -n 2: both refused in 0.000 s (…W2-rungs.log:77, 85; asserted at test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:268–273). Ceiling: a deterministic raise with no factor; a knob without validation would mesh instead, which (A0)'s tip_size_m read-back would expose. - (G) doubles as the blind-knob control, asserted. A knob that never reaches the Ball field leaves N_ball flat: floor 1×, separation measured 2.75× / 7.80×. A strict inequality is all that is asserted, so no factor is set. Ceiling: the cubic model, 2.83× / 8×; the measured growth sits 3 % and 2.5 % under it. - (c2) printed, predicted, never asserted — the refinement is local. AIR_CELL_TAG's count moves by ≤ 126 cells across the rungs, while PHANTOM_CELL_TAG's grows +22 % / +82 %. Records: air 99 975 / 99 849 / 99 881, phantom 109 724 / 133 796 / 199 748 (census dicts …W2-rungs.log:3752, 5612, 7500). Predicted to repeat as integers. Printed only: no gate asserts locality. - (c3) printed — what a user who forgot the knob would see. The unset build is the r/4 build: (A0)'s tip_size_m == TIP_R4, and W1's integer equality (…W1-noop.log:5588, cited). The guide says so; nothing beyond (A0) is asserted.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. Nothing is chained or piped. Never beside another heavy window.

  1. Orphan check: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Then the rubric's cache sweep (docs/automation/daily-review.md:426) as one bare call labelled EX-102-cache-sweep. The 18:00 review's EX-100 ruling (1) keeps the sweep as written (EX-100.md:261).
  2. Pre-censuses, before any file is written:
  3. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-102-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'"
  4. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-102-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'"
  5. Census at drafting: 97 (EX-100's outcome, docs/planning/chunks/EX-100.md:259). Use whatever the pre-census reads.
  6. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-102-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mesh:14 -n 2 -t 590 --dry-run". It must not print (complex build) (run_examples.sh:281).
  7. Run of record (flagged), -n 2, predicted ≈ 315 s, range [260, 430].
  8. Basis: the three rod builds took 61.65 + 71.40 + 86.71 = 219.8 s (…W2-rungs.log:3752, 5612, 7500). W1 and W2 each spent ≈ 70 s beyond their builds on summaries, dofs and startup (238 − 167.7 s, …W1-noop.log:1915, 3750, 5586, 5748; 330 − 260.9 s, …W2-rungs.log:1917, 7674); that is taken whole. Add ≈ 10 s for the setup figure on a ≈ 250 k-cell mesh: imp:3's flagged -n 4 window ran 223 s and its unflagged control 214 s on the 250 866-cell rod mesh (20261003T051229Z_EX-83.log:3851, 20261003T051642Z_EX-83-control.log:3844). Add ≈ 15 s for three XDMF writes and the display submesh. The off build is not run (see (5)), so ≈ 41 s of W2 is absent.
  9. Margin to the 590 s container timeout: ≥ 160 s at the top of the range.
  10. Command: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-102 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/meshing/14_implant_tip_refinement.py"'
  11. PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace because the script imports from tests.*; the dry run emits /workspace/src only (run_examples.sh:279; the EX-93 / EX-96 / EX-101 disclosure). Note any other difference.
  12. Control run, -n 4, without the figure flag: git add the PNG first. Then run the same line with mpiexec -n 4 and no -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-102-control-n4, predicted ≈ 300 s, range [250, 420].
  13. The control changes the width on purpose. gmsh meshes serially on rank 0 (io/mesh.py:3998, 4480, per GEO-36.md:182), so every reduced integer must be width-invariant. At -n 4 the cap balls are more likely split across ranks, so a missing reduction in the owned-cell counts would show. Backing for width invariance on this fixture: the unset build read 252 118 at -n 1, -n 2 and -n 8 (test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:87–89).
  14. The executor compares the two logs as a reading (the EX-101 pattern):
    • integers equal: cells, census, tag-402 count, N_ball, E, F, d1, d2 at every rung;
    • (A1) / (A3) / (A4) / (A6) each inside its band at both widths, compared at the band, never bitwise (the EX-91 ruling): (A4)'s facet-area sum is reduced in a different order;
    • near-T1 counts are integers and predicted equal;
    • build seconds differ; they are printed only.
  15. Post-censuses: EX-102-post-figures / EX-102-post-docrefs, the step 1 commands with those labels. Write the prediction first:
  16. figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0;
  17. docrefs: runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1.

No pytest window is needed: the gate's assertions are re-run in-script on the same fixture. If the review requires the gate re-run, use W2's command verbatim (GEO-36.md:185), with -s kept (rule (g)), ≈ 330 s.

Output. - Three combined XDMFs, one per rung, written right after each build with write_xdmf_with_tags(..., facet_tags=facet_tags). Tag 402 (the rod wall) and the port sheets form the facet block. Full filenames: - examples/meshing/paraview_output/meshing_14_implant_tip_refinement_unset_combined.xdmf - examples/meshing/paraview_output/meshing_14_implant_tip_refinement_r4rt2_combined.xdmf - examples/meshing/paraview_output/meshing_14_implant_tip_refinement_r8_combined.xdmf

The labels are mapped from PLANS["rungs"]'s unset / r/(4rt2) / r/8 because / and ( cannot go in a filename. Fields: - mean_edge: DG0, each owned cell's mean edge length, from the imported _cell_geometry + _mean_edge. This is the h a reader colours by. Set x.array[:n_owned], then scatter_forward(); - in_tip_ball: DG0, 1 on the N_ball set (owned tag-3 cells with centroid within tip_ball_radius_m of a cap centre, the _ball_and_t1 definition :170–176), else 0.

Call adopt_host_ownership after the writes, as the precedents do. - Setup figure examples/meshing/figures/meshing_14_implant_tip_refinement_setup.png, from the r/8 build. At the full domain (≈ 0.2 m across) the 4 mm cap balls would be a few pixels. So the figure is drawn on a display-only phantom submesh: dolfinx.mesh.create_submesh(msh, 3, cell_tags.find(PHANTOM_CELL_TAG)), which returns four values on 0.11 (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:689). - Its display meshtags (sorted unique int32): tag 2 = submesh cells whose centroid is within tip_ball_radius_m of a cap centre, tag 1 = the rest. - Region names: "phantom (gel), outside the tip balls" (tag 1, translucent; the name picks the blue phantom class) and "tip-ball cells, tip_size r/8" (tag 2; no class keyword, so a fallback colour, setup_figure.py:93–126). - slice_normal=(0, 1, 0), slice_origin=ROD_CENTRE, edges on the slice. - Title ≤ 130 characters (MAX_TITLE_CHARS), e.g. mesh:14 -- rod tip refinement: phantom cells within 2r of the caps at tip_size r/8 (GEO-36 step 4). - The display tags and submesh never enter an assertion. - Guide. - The recipe in one call: implant_rod={"radius": …, "length": …, "centre": …, "axis": …, "tip_size": h}, h in metres, 0 < h ≤ r/4, unset = r/4. Say that h is the Ball field's VIn inside a 2r ball round each cap centre; the radius 2r is fixed, and there is no ball-radius knob. - Three reading rules: - the CAD is identical at every rung, so a volume or area change between rungs is a meshing effect, never a geometry one ((A0)); - N_ball grows ≈ as (r/4 ÷ h)³, and so do the dofs a solve would pay (the printed d2 per rung); - the refinement grades past the 2r radius: T1, 2.5 mm from a cap centre, refines too (printed, GEO-36.md:227). - The cost table per rung (cells, N_ball, E, F, d1, d2, build s), printed by the script and quoted from the run's own log. It names no solve time. I15's solve pricing is the weekly's (GEO-36.md:228–236), cited, not reproduced. - Scope sentences (below). - ParaView recipe: open …_unset_combined.xdmf and …_r8_combined.xdmf side by side. Threshold in_tip_ball = 1, colour by mean_edge on a log scale, and slice through y = 0. Select the facet block and Threshold on tag 402 to see the rod wall. - ## Related lists, every artifact by full filename (rule (b)): - examples/implants/03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.md (the solve on this fixture at the default r/4 tip); - examples/meshing/03_birdcage_graded_conductors.md and examples/meshing/05_region_resolution_policy.md; - tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py and tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py; - src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Real build only. No source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode. Never import tests/validation/test_imp3_* (GEO-36.md:195). - Coarse to fine (GEO-23). gmsh builds serially on rank 0 and broadcasts a build error to every rank (io/mesh.py:4513–4525 per GEO-36.md:182). A gmsh FAIL is recorded verbatim with its surface pairs and never retried. - (c1) before any build. The gate's (R) asserts not gmsh.isInitialized(), and that only holds before a build has run in the process. The refusal raises on every rank; catch it on every rank. - Rank-local quantities: cell_tags.values, assemble_scalar and the ball / edge sums are rank-local. _summarise reduces over owned cells. The script's own mean_edge / in_tip_ball fields are set on owned cells only, then scattered. Cells use the reduced size_local sum. - Collectives on every rank: _build_rod, _summarise (with its _dofs and _exterior_facet_area), create_submesh, write_xdmf_with_tags and write_setup_figure are collective. Prints go under rank == 0 with no collective inside (item 227's deadlock). - _summarise deletes only its local names. Keep the caller's out tuple alive while the XDMF (and, for r/8, the figure) is written. Drop the unset and r/(4√2) meshes before the next build. - If a window hangs or hits 590 s: it is killed by timeout -k 30 590. Then docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0 before anything else. Clear leaked /dev/shm/mpich_shm_* segments (known-issues), and sweep orphan .c only at pgrep 0. Then park and stop (see (6)). Never retry with a longer timeout, never drop a rung to get a green, never narrow the width. - Docrefs: name no scratch path in guide prose (EX-93's first post-docrefs exited 1 on a bare filename, EX-97.md:149). Write artifacts by full repo-relative filename. - Bare harness calls only, repo-relative, nothing chained: cd … &&, ; date, | tail and redirects are denied by bash_guard.py. -k 30 goes on every container timeout. Executors run foreground, never nested; Bash timeout: 660000. Never delete a log, including a red or footerless one. - Rule (i): no edit to the script or guide after its last window. Write ≈, never a tilde.

(5) Scope. - Covered: the hole build of GEO-36 step 4's fixture at the 1 g phantom rung, three tip_size rungs (unset = r/4, r/(4√2), r/8), real build, -n 2 and -n 4. Covered per rung: CAD invariance, the CAD identities A1 / A3–A6 at imported bands, the N1curl dof identities, the strict growth of the cap-ball cell count, and the refusal of out-of-range values. - Not claimed: - any solve: no η_rod, tip SAR or E-field. The I15 solve windows (heavy or xl, the rung set) stay the weekly's to commission (GEO-36.md:203; PROJECT_PLAN.md:4606–4613); - an h-convergence statement of any quantity. The ratio against (r/4 ÷ h)³ is a printed cell-count reading, not a rate; - (A2) and A5's flag-off leg. Both need the off build (≈ 41 s, …W2-rungs.log:1917), which this example does not run. They remain the gate's, cited; - W1's unset = explicit r/4 integer equality (cited, not re-run); - the kept-cells build (WF-9's), a ball-radius knob, r/16, F-human, complex-build forms, xl widths; - anything GEO-36 step 4 does not claim.

(6) Negative result. If (N), (A0), (A1), (A3)–(A6), (D), (G) or (c1) misses, the runaway guard trips, gmsh fails, or a window hangs: - report the measurement and stop; - journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-102, and mark item 304 BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)); - leave EX-102 ⬜. Never widen a band, edit src/ or the gate modules, or drop a rung.

What each miss means: - (N), (A0), (A1), (A3)–(A6), (D) or (G) red through the example path: contradicts GEO-36 step 4's GREEN W2 at the same width. That is an example / test divergence finding: a known-issues entry and a §7 annotation on GEO-36 for the review, not an example fix (example-runner.md:24–27). - (c1) does not raise, or gmsh is initialised after it: an io/mesh.py _normalise_implant_rod regression; stop and report. - Cells differ from 252 118 inside CELL_COUNT_BAND, or 276 088 / 342 072 / N_ball differ from their records, with every assertion green: a mesher-version event (rule (1*)), reported for record-reconciler. Not a stop, since only (N) asserts a record. - The -n 4 integers differ from -n 2's with both windows green: a width-dependence finding (a missing reduction or a non-deterministic mesh) for the review, a known-issues entry; EX-102 stays ⬜.

A run killed at 590 s is not a result: check orphans and stop. The fallback is a re-queue, never a longer timeout and never a dropped rung.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-102 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). Census examples +1 (97 → 98 at drafting) with broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1. The review adds the §7 row in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). This is the first example of local refinement at an implant. Phase 7 (7b) gains a runnable demonstration of the tip knob that I15 will use, and Phase 9 (9d)'s "tutorials drawn from examples/" gains a mesh-sizing tutorial. GEO-36 and IMP-3 stay ✅; I15 is not advanced.

Review rulings (2026-10-07 18:00 daily review, item 304). (1) The off build stays dropped: A2 and the off half of A5 are the gate's, cited, not reproduced; the example's angle is the rod rungs. (2) The setup figure on a display-only phantom submesh is accepted: nothing is read from it, and the cap balls must be visible. (3) The refusal inputs ROD_RADIUS / 3.0 and 0.0 and the conductor tag 1 may appear as cited literals (EX-101 ruling (3) precedent): they are inputs, not records or bands. (4) Importing the gate's private _summarise is accepted so the run prints the gate's own [GEO-36 step 4] lines, comparable with W2 digit for digit; if that helper changes, the example fails loudly, which is the right failure. (5) The -n 4 control keeps all three rungs (≈ 300 s, inside the window), so every integer is compared at both widths. (6) Cost counts at the example class median for the floor (9 since this review); the ≈ 55 min prediction sets the timebox — a slot starts it only before minute 30, and two heavy windows of ≈ 5 min each are the expected wall clock.

docs.title: EX-103 — th:16, the absorbing boundary on the two-torus box
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened 2026-10-08 by the 18:00 daily review (§5.4 example ramp). The base is TH-5 ✅ (step 2c, §9 item 320, commit 5a637e89, DONE 2026-10-08; docs/planning/chunks/TH-5.md:355). Its gates are tests/validation/test_th5_abc_two_torus.py ((P0), (E), (S); (R) retired, r(W) printed) and tests/validation/test_th5_mixed_wall_two_torus.py ((P0), (E), (S), (M), (c1), (c2)). The closing windows are docs/testing/logs/20261008T183105Z_TH-5-step2c-W1.log (7 passed, 225 s, -n 2) and docs/testing/logs/20261008T183455Z_TH-5-step2c-W2.log (8 passed, 169 s, -n 2).

No example uses an absorbing boundary. Checked at drafting: no script under examples/ names first_order_abc_term, "abc" or "absorbing". The two-torus fixture appears in ports:1 (examples/ports/01_two_torus_port_pair.py, PEC box) and the meshing examples, never with an open-boundary term. th:1 … th:15 exist, so this item writes th:16.

Proposed §7 row (the review adds it in the same commit as item 337, rule (j)):

| EX-103 | The absorbing boundary on a small box: at 10 MHz the first-order ABC is a magnetic wall, not an open boundary (history and §9 briefs: docs/planning/chunks/EX-103.md) (th:16; example-runner; opened 2026-10-08 by the 18:00 daily review, §5.4 ramp; angle: the ABC against the PEC and natural walls on PORT-1's two-torus box, and the box term B^ABC against padding; base TH-5 step 2c, §9 item 320) Done-when: examples/time_harmonic/16_abc_two_torus.py + same-stem guide; complex build, -n 2 (flagged) and -n 4 (control); imports both TH-5 gate modules' solver, constants and bands, restates none; one rule (a) lift (additive return keys on _solve_z_column) re-gated green at -n 2; asserted in-script: (P0) at P0_BAND_PP, (E) Re Z₁₁^ABC > 0 and PEC |Re Z₂₁| ≤ IDENTITY_TOLERANCE·|Z₂₁|, (S) B^ABC > 0 > B^PEC at 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.12 m, (c1) and (M) / (c2) at MIX_BAR_DIVISOR; r(W) printed as a record, never asserted; printed rows equal the step 2c logs to their printed digits; three combined XDMFs and the setup figure written; census +1, no new dead docref; elapsed recorded ⇒ ✅. Not claimed: an open boundary at k₀R < π, the 64 / 128 MHz birdcage box, a user-settable mixed wall, second-order ABC or PML, why r(W) falls. | ⬜ Open: the brief is §9 item 337; no example uses an ABC. | heavy |

docs.title: §9 item 337 — 2026-10-08 (example; §5.4 ramp from TH-5)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §5.4 example ramp on a closed chunk (TH-5 ✅ 2026-10-08). No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved. Every band, constant and helper is imported by name. Record digits appear only in a cited RECORD dict that is printed beside the run and never asserted (the th:12 precedent).

EX-103 (th:16) adds examples/time_harmonic/16_abc_two_torus.py and a same-stem guide 16_abc_two_torus.md. The guide carries the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step) plus ## Setup figure and ## Related. The setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB (scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py).

The angle, for the user who reaches for HFSS's Radiation boundary on a coil-sized box. The script solves PORT-1's two tori (tag 1 driven, 10 MHz, degree 1) in an air box whose outer wall (facet tag 1) is PEC, natural, or the first-order ABC (Jin 3e §9.2 (9.44), s = 1, fem_em_solver.core.boundary_terms.first_order_abc_term, through TimeHarmonicSolver.solve(extra_bilinear_terms=…)). It shows three things: - The ABC is in the matrix and it absorbs. Re Z₁₁^ABC > 0 at every padding, and Re Z₁₁·I₁² equals ∮|n × E|²/η₀ over the wall. The PEC wall carries no tangential E (∮ 4.17e-37 W) and no Re Z. The natural wall carries a large tangential E (0.258 W of ∮|n × E|²/η₀) and still has Re Z₁₁ = 0: tangential E on the wall is not absorption. - At k₀·half-width ≈ 0.02–0.04 the ABC is a reflector. It acts as the natural (magnetic) wall: its box term B^ABC = d^ABC − D∞^PEC is positive where PEC's is negative, +4.7133 / +2.3965 / +1.1256 pp at W = 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.12 m. Its deficit differs from the natural wall's by 0.224 pp at 0.08 m. Padding still matters under an ABC on this box. - The ⅓ PEC + ⅔ natural post-solve mix cancels the box term to −0.2520 pp against |B^PEC|/5 = 1.9468 pp, and swapped weights miss by 2.5647×. It is computed from the same window's PEC and natural solves. It is a combination of two solves, not a boundary condition.

r(W) = |B^ABC|/|B^PEC| = 0.4846 / 0.3567 / 0.2266 is printed as a record beside the sphere model's 0.5. It is never asserted: (R) was retired by the 2026-10-07 weekly.

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents.
  • Build: complex. The th: group sources complex mode automatically (scripts/run_examples.sh:13, 167; the dry run prints (complex build), :281). The script refuses a real default_scalar_type with the th:12 message (examples/time_harmonic/12_symmetry_plane_quarter_box.py:141–146). The gates ran complex (W1 :12).
  • Tier: heavy, by measurement. The gate window took 225 s (20261008T183105Z_TH-5-step2c-W1.log, footer), over standard's 180 s, and the example runs the same five solves. Ranks: -n 2 (the gate's width; flagged run of record and re-gate) and -n 4 (unflagged control).
  • Cost: ≈ 13 measured (example class median) / ≈ 55 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 20 script and guide + ≈ 15 windows (re-gate ≈ 4 min, flagged ≈ 4.5 min, control ≈ 4 min, ≈ 2 min of small windows) + ≈ 5 docs. If the flagged run has not started by minute 40, park (rule (d)).
  • Depends on: nothing open. Both gate modules are on main (TH-5 step 2c).
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-103, §9 item 337 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-103.md, heading §9 item 337). You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The only code edit outside examples/ is the rule (a) lift of _solve_z_column's return dict in tests/validation/test_th5_abc_two_torus.py (additive keys only), re-gated green before the example is written. Make no edit to the module, script or guide after its last window. Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record, the census before / after, and the disclosed lift diff."

Code (rule (a), additive, disclosed). 1. tests/validation/test_th5_abc_two_torus.py, _solve_z_column (:89–170): the return dict (:163–170) gains five keys and nothing else changes: - "omega_m12": omega_m12 (already a local at :154), which lets 2b's _mix_deficit read 2a's runs; - "e": fields.e_complex, the Function only, never the fields object (so no solver or factorisation is kept alive); - "msh": msh, "cell_tags": cell_tags, "facet_tags": facet_tags.

No print, assertion, constant, keyword or test changes. The module-scoped runs fixture now holds five meshes and five degree-1 fields (≤ 154 k cells each), which is a small memory cost and changes no number. No other module is edited (not 2b's, not test_port_reaction_impedance.py, not test_geo4_box_padding_heuristic.py, not src/). 2. The module is re-gated green at -n 2 before the example is written (windows 2–3).

Imports (never restated). - From tests.validation.test_th5_abc_two_torus (the 2a / 2c gate): _solve_z_column, _d_inf_pec, _b_pec, ABC_PADDINGS, PREMISE_PADDING, OUTER_BOUNDARY_TAG, ORIGINAL_FALL_FACTOR (:71–74, 84–89, 182–184). - From tests.validation.test_th5_mixed_wall_two_torus (the 2b gate): W_PEC, W_NAT, MIX_BAR_DIVISOR (:74–76) and _mix_deficit (:194–197). Import nothing else: its _solve_z_column has a different signature, and its fixture is not called. - From their defining modules, as the gates import them: P0_BAND_PP, P0_RUNG_PP (tests/validation/test_geo4_box_padding_heuristic.py); IDENTITY_TOLERANCE, TORUS_TAGS, FREQUENCY_HZ, SEPARATION, MAJOR_RADIUS (tests/validation/test_port_reaction_impedance.py:108–142, 192); PORT1_PADDING_RUNGS_M (fem_em_solver.io.mesh). Assert test_th5_abc_two_torus.P0_BAND_PP is test_th5_mixed_wall_two_torus.P0_BAND_PP: one band object, two importers. - From src: fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils (write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership) and fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure.write_setup_figure. - The script inserts the repo root on sys.path as th:12 does (:52–54), so the dry-run line runs verbatim with PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src. Never import another example's module. th:12's _export (CG1 E_real / E_imag, ≈ 12 lines) is re-written locally. - No new number. Paddings, tags, weights, divisor and bands are all imported. The RECORD dict (below) is the only digit block. Each entry carries its log:line comment and is printed beside the run, a difference reported and never asserted.

Order of calls in the script. It uses the same solve sequence as the gate's runs fixture (:174–179), with the imported constants: 1. PEC at PREMISE_PADDING; 2. ABC at each of ABC_PADDINGS; 3. natural at PREMISE_PADDING.

After each 0.08 m solve (PEC, ABC, natural), write its combined XDMF. After the ABC 0.08 m solve, also write the setup figure. Drop the "e" / "msh" / tag keys of the 0.10 and 0.12 m runs once read. Asserts and prints follow, on every rank, from the returned scalars. _reaction and the boundary integral are already allreduced inside _solve_z_column (:142–152).

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script at every width it runs; the gates' expressions, imported bands). - (P0) Premise: |d^PEC(0.08) − P0_RUNG_PP| ≤ P0_BAND_PP. Record −8.0404 pp, |Δ| 0.0080 (W1 :928; W2 :597). - (E) The ABC term is in the matrix: - Re Z₁₁^ABC > 0 at each of ABC_PADDINGS. Records +3.784205e-03 / +2.620085e-03 / +1.923719e-03 Ω (W1 :932–934). - PEC |Re Z₂₁|/|Z₂₁| ≤ IDENTITY_TOLERANCE. Record 0.000e+00 (W1 :931). - (S) Sign: _b_pec(w) < 0, and B^ABC(w) = d^ABC(w) − _d_inf_pec() > 0, at all three paddings. Records B^ABC +4.7133 / +2.3965 / +1.1256 pp, B^PEC −9.7258 / −6.7190 / −4.9667 pp, d^ABC +6.4067 / +4.0899 / +2.8190 pp (W1 :938–940). - (M) The mixed wall, on this window's PEC and natural 0.08 m runs: with d_inf = _d_inf_pec(), B^PEC = d^PEC − d_inf (the solve-referenced form, 2b's :255), B^mix = _mix_deficit(pec, nat, W_PEC, W_NAT) − d_inf. Assert |B^mix| ≤ |B^PEC| / MIX_BAR_DIVISOR. Records B^PEC −9.7338, B^NAT +4.4889, r_NAT 0.4612 (W2 :604); d^mix +1.4414, B^mix −0.2520 against the bar 1.9468 pp (W2 :606). - Why the 2a runs suffice: 2a builds a mesh per call and 2b builds one mesh for both walls. The two windows print the same cells (119 533) and the same Z₂₁ to seven digits under both walls (PEC W1 :232 = W2 :238; natural W1 :927 = W2 :239). So (M) is predicted to reproduce W2's digits. It is compared at the bar, never bitwise.

Printed, not asserted (each beside its RECORD entry; no gate band exists for these, rule (e)): - The headline table, one row per padding: cells; d^ABC; B^ABC; B^PEC; and r(W) = |B^ABC|/|B^PEC| labelled "(record; (R) retired, weekly 2026-10-07; sphere model 0.5)". Records 0.4846 / 0.3567 / 0.2266 (W1 :938–940). The original ≥ ORIGINAL_FALL_FACTOR× bar is printed False at every padding, as the banked negative. - Power per wall at 0.08 m: - Re Z₁₁·I₁² against ∮|n × E|²/η₀ on OUTER_BOUNDARY_TAG. ABC: 3.553290e-03 W both sides, residual 1.216e-11 (W1 :932); predicted ≤ 1e-6 in the gate and printed only. - The same integral under PEC, 4.171602e-37 W (W1 :232), and natural, 2.581840e-01 W with Re Z₁₁ = 0 (W1 :927, :935). - The guide reads these three as "absorbing, pinned, reflecting". - (c3) |d^ABC − d^NAT| at 0.08 m: 0.224456 pp (W1 :942). - The ABC free-exponent fit: the script calls _free_exponent_fit(ABC_PADDINGS, <the three d^ABC>) (imported from fem_em_solver.io.mesh, as the gate does at :248–256) and prints its result. Predicted to fail, as W1 :943 records; a fit that succeeds is printed and reported, never asserted. - 2b's printed rows that need only 0.08 m: B^swap −4.9929 and B^half −2.6225 pp with their ratios (W2 :607), and w_PEC* 0.3156 (W2 :608). The 0.10 / 0.12 m natural rungs are not re-solved (see Scope). - The complex Z₁₁ and Z₂₁ per run, and mesh / solve seconds. These come from the gate's own [TH-5 2a] lines, which _solve_z_column prints (W1 :232, 402, 574, 757, 927).

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) PEC in the ABC's place — asserted through (S) and (P0), as in the gate. A broken run that leaves the Dirichlet set on returns d^PEC, so B^ABC < 0 and (S) is red. Separation |B^ABC − B^PEC| at 0.08 m: 14.4391 pp (W1 :941), printed, against a rung precision of ≈ 5e-5 pp. Also asserted, 2b's form: |d^NAT − d^PEC| > P0_BAND_PP (record 14.2227 pp, W2 :605). - Conjugated γ — asserted via (E)'s sign. γ = −jk₀ makes the wall a source and Re Z₁₁ < 0 (boundary_terms.py:10–11; TH-5.md:175). The script never re-derives γ. - (c2) Swapped weights — asserted, conditional on (M): |B^swap| > |B^PEC| / MIX_BAR_DIVISOR, with B^swap = _mix_deficit(pec, nat, W_NAT, W_PEC) − d_inf. Record 2.5647× (W2 :607). Ceiling computed in item 290: 5(⅔ − ⅓r) = 2.0–3.0 for r ∈ [0.2, 0.8] (TH-5.md:243). No factor is asserted. - Control run (-n 4, unflagged), compared at the band and never bitwise: - integers equal: cells 119 533 / 135 685 / 153 952; - every deficit within P0_BAND_PP of the -n 2 run; - every sign the same; - (M) and (c2) green; - the power residual printed.

The width change is deliberate: MUMPS ordering and the owned-cell split change, so a missing reduction in _reaction or the boundary integral would show. gmsh meshes serially on rank 0, so the integers must be width-invariant.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. Nothing is chained or piped. Never beside another heavy window. Every window is under 10 min, so no durable capture is needed.

  1. Orphan check: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0.
  2. Pre-censuses, before any file is written (the EX-89 item 332 commands, 20261008T172115Z_EX-89-item332-pre-figures.log:12, …172117Z…pre-docrefs.log:12):
  3. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-103-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'"
  4. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-103-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'"
  5. At drafting: figures examples=98 ok=98 missing=0 broken=0; docrefs dead=2 guide=0 stale=56 exit=1. The two dead references come from an unrelated known-issues entry (2026-10-08, ans9 SPEC). Use whatever the pre-census reads.
  6. Edit 1, then the re-gate W1 (heavy; predicted ≈ 225 s, range [190, 330]; 7 passed). (5) Scope. - Covered: PORT-1's two-torus box, d = 0.04 m, 10 MHz, degree 1, at paddings 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.12 m (k₀·half-width ≈ 0.02–0.04), under the PEC, natural and first-order ABC walls (natural at 0.08 m only), at -n 2 and -n 4, and the ⅓ / ⅔ post-solve mix at 0.08 m. - Not claimed: - an open boundary at k₀R < π; - the band k₀R ∈ (0.04, π), which holds the 64 / 128 MHz birdcage box (TH-5 entry step 3's question stays open); - any birdcage, SAR or Radiation-parity figure; - a user-settable mixed wall; - a second-order ABC or PML; - 2b's printed natural rungs at 0.10 / 0.12 m (cited from W2 :611 and the 0.12 m row, not re-solved); - why r(W) falls (2a's hypothesis stays untested); - anything TH-5 does not claim.
