docs.title: EX-104 — mat:17, thermal dose and the six-minute average on closed-form histories
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-104 (mat:17) was opened 2026-10-08 by the 18:00 daily review under daily-review.md step 5 (§5.4 ramp). Its base is MAT-20 steps 1 and 2, closed-form half, both landed 2026-10-08: - Step 1 (§9 item 318): thermal/dose.py cem43, exact on the piecewise-linear interpolant. (A1) three ramps ≤ 6.3e-16 against the analytic (R^(43−a) − R^(43−a−bτ))/(b ln R); (A2) MAT-9's step response at N = 2¹⁸, 8.98e-12; (Rc) the planted R swap misses by ≥ 0.194. Log docs/testing/logs/20261008T171434Z_MAT-20-step1.log, test tests/validation/test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py. - Step 2 (§9 item 319): running_average. (B1) the integer-period window mean equals D × θ_ss(0) on MAT-17 case A's closed form to ≤ 1.03e-14; (B2) the window maximum lies within 0.40 sample of the brentq phase; (Wc) the control misses. Log docs/testing/logs/20261008T171843Z_MAT-20-step2.log, test tests/validation/test_mat20_running_average.py.

MAT-20 is 🟡. The FEM clause of step 2 (D_BAND on MAT-17 step 3's history) is the weekly's under ruling 319-3 and is not gated. This example therefore uses closed-form histories only: MAT-17's duty-cycled closed form, linear ramps, and MAT-9's step response. It never uses an FEM history.

Gap. No example computes a thermal dose or a six-minute average. - grep -rnlE 'cem43|running_average|thermal\.dose|CEM43' examples --include=*.py returns nothing. - mat:11 (EX-85) switches the same source on the same ball and says in its guide "Not claimed: … any pulse-sequence, 6-minute-averaging, IEC 60601-2-33 or other regulatory statement". mat:15 (EX-99, duty-cycled coil heating) reads θ, not dose.

docs.title: §9 item 338 — 2026-10-08 (example; §5.4 ramp from MAT-20 steps 1–2)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, record, Done-when or target. Every band is imported from the two MAT-20 gate modules.

EX-104 (mat:17) adds three tracked files: - examples/materials/17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle.py; - the same-stem guide examples/materials/17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle.md, with the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step) plus ## Setup figure and ## Related; - examples/materials/figures/materials_17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

The angle: a gel-phantom exposure story. The 10 cm Robin gel ball of MAT-9 / MAT-17 is switched 0/1 with P = 1200 s and D = 0.5 (case A). The example asks what two regulatory post-processors report on this history, and checks each against a closed form: 1. The six-minute average of the power. The source schedule χ(t) is on for 600 s, and 600 s exceeds the 360 s window. The six-minute mean of χ therefore peaks at 1, full power, while its whole-period mean is exactly D = 0.5. A six-minute SAR-style average reads twice the period average on this schedule. 2. The six-minute average of the temperature. The thermal mass (τ₁ = 1.9155e4 s ≫ P) flattens this. The six-minute mean of θ at the centre peaks only ≈ +0.8 % above D·θ_ss(0), at t ≈ 780 s (MAT-20 (B2)). A window of a whole number of periods sees D·θ_ss exactly ((B1)). 3. CEM43 of the same history. The temperatures are re-based to 37 °C, as MAT-20 (A2) did: θ is unchanged and only the additive base moves. The centre's periodic state then sits at 43.04–43.18 °C. Because 2^(T−43) is convex, the duty-cycled history's dose per period exceeds that of the average-power stand-in (θ ≡ D·θ_ss) by ≈ 4e-4 relative (Jensen). That holds only where T stays on one side of 43 °C. CEM43's R switch makes the integrand concave at 43 °C (slope 2 ln 2 below against ln 2 above), so the reading flips sign near the mean-43 °C isotherm (r ≈ 20 mm). The map shows this. 4. The same dose for a bench gel. On a 20 °C base the centre dose per period is ≈ 1e-7 s. CEM43 is a tissue metric. The 37 °C base is the gate's re-basing, not a claim about any phantom.

The gated operator anchors (A1), (A2), (Rc), (B1), (B2) and (Wc) are recomputed through imported helpers. Their printed values equal the gate logs' records.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: standard, -n 2, complex build (the mat: group sources it; nothing here needs complex numbers).
  • Cost: ≈ 13 measured (example class median, 03:00 restock table) / ≈ 40 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 code and guide + ≈ 5 windows). Price basis:
  • MAT-20 step 1's whole module took 12 s at -n 2 (20261008T171434Z_MAT-20-step1.log:145–146; 8 passed in 11.03 s, :139), and the A2 test is most of it. Step 2's two modules took 19 s (20261008T171843Z_MAT-20-step2.log:160–167).
  • The ball mesh at res 0.02 has 2 571 cells (20260929T112146Z_MAT-9-step2.log:87) and builds in under 1 s.
  • The closed-form map is evaluated at ≈ 600 P1 vertices × 2 049 times × 400 terms ≈ 5e8 multiply-adds, split over the owned vertices, ≈ 5–15 s.
  • The setup figure adds ≈ 15 s (EX-89 item 238's example overhead with the figure).
  • The example window: predicted [30, 120] s; runner -t 180, container timeout -k 30 180.
  • Dry run plus four census windows: ≈ 1.5 min together.
  • Smoke would be under-priced, so the tier is standard.
  • Depends on: nothing open. MAT-20 steps 1 and 2 are on main. The 17_ prefix is free (examples/materials/ holds 01–16).
  • Shared files. This item adds only the three paths above. It edits no gate module, nothing under src/, and not thermal/__init__.py (dose.py stays unexported; import fem_em_solver.thermal.dose directly). No rule (a) lift is needed.

Imports (never restated). Import the modules under aliases, never their names bare: both gate modules define BAR, R, K, Q, H and _p with different values. - import tests.validation.test_mat20_cem43_closed_form as s1: s1.BAR, s1.RAMPS, s1.SAMPLINGS, s1.ramp_dose, s1._side, s1._ramp, s1._rect_sum, s1._rel, s1._T_centre, s1.PHYS, s1.T_BASE, s1.T_END. - import tests.validation.test_mat20_running_average as s2: s2.BAR, s2.P, s2.D, s2.TH_SS0, s2.M_SEQ, s2.W_B2, s2._theta, s2._series, and s2.R, s2.K, s2.RHO_C, s2.Q, s2.H. - import tests.validation.test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form as m17cf: CASES, TH_SS0, TAU1, _modal, and the left-limit idiom of mat:11's _periodic (11_duty_cycled_gel_ball.py:98–102) for the peak and trough. - from tests.validation.test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem import _chi. It is the schedule's own definition, a scalar callable; apply it with np.fromiter. - from tests.validation.test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere import _ball (MeshGenerator.ball_domain, as mat:11 uses through m17._ball). - From src: cem43, running_average (fem_em_solver.thermal.dose), robin_sphere_duty_cycle_temperature, robin_sphere_steady_temperature (utils.analytical), write_setup_figure, write_xdmf_with_tags, write_xdmf_time_series, adopt_host_ownership. - Structural asserts at start-up (mat:11 precedent, :117–122): - (s2.P, s2.D) == m17cf.CASES["A"]; - s2.TH_SS0 == m17cf.TH_SS0; - (s2.R, s2.K, s2.RHO_C, s2.Q, s2.H) == (m17cf.R, m17cf.K, m17cf.RHO_C, m17cf.Q, m17cf.H); - (s1.PHYS["radius"], s1.PHYS["k"], s1.PHYS["rho_c"], s1.PHYS["q"], s1.PHYS["h"]) == (m17cf.R, m17cf.K, m17cf.RHO_C, m17cf.Q, m17cf.H).

One ball, three gate modules. - Numerical settings copied verbatim, with line citations, not bands: - A2's brentq(..., xtol=1e-12, rtol=4*eps) and its two quad(..., epsabs=1e-13, epsrel=1e-13, limit=2000) split at t₄₃ (test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py:142–149); - B2's bracket D·P + 1, D·P + W − 1 and brentq (test_mat20_running_average.py:106–109).

The record digits depend on them. - Nothing else carries a number. The 37 °C base is s1.T_BASE. The 20 °C bench base is m17cf.T_INF.

(1) Anchor. Part A recomputes the gated operator identities. Each printed value must equal its gate-log record at the gate's print format; copy the gate's format specs. The example prints once, on rank 0. The gate logs print the step 1 lines twice, one copy per rank, so compare values, not line counts. - (A1) three ramps × s1.SAMPLINGS. rel = s1._rel(cem43(t, T), s1.ramp_dose(...)) ≤ s1.BAR. Print ref and op at .15e, rel at .3e, and rect_sum at .10e. - Records: rise :51–53, shallow :59–61, fall :67–69 of 20261008T171434Z_MAT-20-step1.log. - ref and rect_sum must match to every printed digit. op and rel are round-off readings, asserted at the band only. - (A2) MAT-9's step response re-based to 37 °C. Build t_fine = np.linspace(0, s1.T_END, 2**19 + 1) and T_fine = s1._T_centre(t_fine) exactly as the gate does (:157–158). N = 2¹⁷ and N = 2¹⁸ are the strides 4 and 2. - Reference: brentq t₄₃ and quad, as above. - Asserted: rel(N = 2¹⁸) ≤ s1.BAR. - Printed beside the records: bracket :113; t₄₃ = 14087.0956163533 and quad = 1.708516120835631e+05 (:114); op = 1.708516120774260e+05 at N = 131 072 (:122); op = 1.708516120820288e+05, rel 8.980e-12 and pred 8.980e-12 at N = 262 144 (:123–124). - N = 2¹⁸ is the gate's recorded selection (:124). The example does not re-run the selection loop. - (B1) integer-period mean, k ∈ {1, 2} × s2.M_SEQ, through s2._series(M, k + 1) and running_average(..., window=k*s2.P). Assert max |mean − s2.D·s2.TH_SS0| / (s2.D·s2.TH_SS0) ≤ s2.BAR. Print the window count and the residual at .3e. Records: 20261008T171843Z_MAT-20-step2.log:144, :146, :148, :150 (5.959e-15 / 8.139e-15 / 1.032e-14 / 9.011e-15; window counts 4097 / 8193). - (B2) window-maximum phase, W = s2.W_B2, restricted to the second period, as :110–122 does. Assert |t_max − root| ≤ Δt. Print root and t_max at .6f and the offset in samples at +.3f. Records :154, :156: root 779.999309 s; t_max 779.882812 / 780.029297 s; offsets −0.398 / +0.205 samples.

Part B adds example-side assertions. Each is exact on its stated premise, and all use the imported s2.BAR. - (S1) the power's six-minute maximum. On χ sampled on s2._series's grid (t = arange × P/M, switch times on the grid, M = s2.M_SEQ[0], two periods), running_average(t, χ, window=s2.W_B2) has maximum 1 within s2.BAR. Every window that ends at or before D·P − Δt lies wholly in the on phase. - (S2) the power's whole-period mean. The same χ with window=s2.P gives every window mean equal to D within s2.BAR·D. The interpolant's two switch segments lose and gain Δt/2 each, so each period integrates to exactly D·P. This is the same kink cancellation that makes (B1) hold. - (J) Jensen at the centre, on the periodic θ of case A at r = 0 and M = s2.M_SEQ[0], re-based to s1.T_BASE, over the second period. - Precondition, asserted first: min T > 43, so a single R branch applies. Trough predicted 43.039341 °C (37 + 6.039341, mat:11 guide step 1 / MAT-17 step 1 S1 log :144). - Asserted: cem43(t, T) over the period > cem43([0, P], [T̄, T̄]), with T̄ = s1.T_BASE + s2.D·s2.TH_SS0. The stand-in's dose is taken through the operator on a two-sample constant series, so the R rule is not restated. - The margin is predicted [2e-4, 8e-4] relative: (ln 2)²/2 · Var θ, with a triangular ripple of 0.1435 K p-p giving ≈ 4.1e-4. That is ≥ 10⁸ × the interpolant's discretisation error and the (B1) mean residual, so the strict inequality is decisive.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (Rc), asserted. cem43(..., r_above=0.25, r_below=0.5) misses (A1) by > s1.BAR on every ramp and sampling. Records 1.3784 / 0.1937 / 1.3982 (step1.log:83–91), printed at .4f. The shallow ramp is the binding case, at ≈ 2 × 10⁹ × the bar. - (Wc), asserted. W = kP + P/2 misses (B1) by > s2.BAR. Records 1.957e-3 (k = 1) and 1.174e-3 (k = 2) at both M (step2.log:145, :147, :149, :152), each with its printed O(ripple) ceiling 3.915e-3 / 2.349e-3. - (Sc), printed only. No split at 43 °C: 1.2973 / 0.1292 / 0.1096 (step1.log:103–105), through s1._side. - (S1c), asserted. The power's whole-period-mean control: window = s2.P + s2.P/2 on χ misses D by > s2.BAR·D. Predicted max miss 1/3 (window means between 1/3 and 2/3). The ceiling is exactly 1/3, from (D·P + 0)/(1.5 P) against D, so no factor is asserted. - (Jc), printed only. The Jensen premise control: the map's minimum per-vertex excess (dose_duty / dose_stand-in − 1) over all vertices. - It is predicted negative, in [−3e-2, −1e-4], at vertices whose mean T straddles 43 °C (r ≈ 20 mm; D·θ_ss(r) = 6 K ⇔ r = 0.0200 m from the steady closed form). - It shows the concave kink of the R switch. A non-negative minimum is reported, not asserted.

Printed (no band; predicted beside measured). - τ₁ = m17cf.TAU1 (1.915501e4 s) and P/τ₁ = 0.0626 (mat:11's records). - Centre periodic peak / trough / mean: 6.182881 / 6.039341 / 6.111111 K, through m17cf._modal and mat:11's left-limit idiom. As °C on the 37 base: 43.182881 / 43.039341 / 43.111111. - Power: the six-minute max of χ = 1, the period mean = 0.5, so the six-minute average reads 2.000 × the period average. - Temperature: the six-minute max of θ at the centre is predicted 6.1614 K [6.150, 6.172], +0.82 % [+0.6, +1.0] % over D·θ_ss(0), at t_max ≈ 780 s (the (B2) record). - Dose, centre, 37 °C base, periodic state, per period: - stand-in P·2^(D·θ_ss(0) − 6) = 1296.07 s = 21.601 min (arithmetic, printed beside); - duty ≈ 1296.6 s [1296.3, 1297.2]; - dose per minute of exposure ≈ 1.080. - Dose at the surface (r = R, D·θ_ss(R) = 3.333 K, T ≈ 40.33 °C, R = 0.25 branch) per period: ≈ 30 s [20, 45]. - Bench gel, 20 °C base (m17cf.T_INF), centre per period: ≈ 8e-8 s [1e-8, 1e-6]. - Continuous heating from rest ((A2)'s history): 1.708516e5 s = 2847.5 min over 10 h (the :123 record ÷ 60). The ten-hour exposure is the gate's T_END, chosen to cross 43 °C, and is not a protocol. - (Pc) one-sample-short windows: step2.log:155, :157.

Output. - Setup figure examples/materials/figures/materials_17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle_setup.png, through write_setup_figure, called right after _ball(0.02): - region_names={1: "gel ball R = 0.1 m (Robin h = 10; closed-form histories only, no FEM solve)"}; - translucent_tags=(1,), slice z = 0 through the origin; - title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. "mat:17 -- 10 cm Robin gel ball (MAT-9 / MAT-17 fixture): CEM43 and six-minute average from closed forms". - If the PNG is over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Why a mesh at all. The harness (scripts/run_examples.sh) runs any script and does not look at outputs. But the setup-figure census (scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py:82–110) counts an example whose guide lacks a ## Setup figure PNG under figures/ as missing. All 98 current examples build a mesh and call write_setup_figure (20261008T172115Z_EX-89-item332-pre-figures.log:35–134, ok=98 missing=0). There is no no-mesh precedent. A closed-form-only example without a mesh would therefore leave the census at missing=1. - The example builds the ball the closed form describes, at res 0.02 (2 571 cells). It uses it for the figure and as the support of a closed-form field map: the radial closed form evaluated at each owned P1 dof's radius |x|. This is not an FEM solve and not an FEM history; nothing is assembled or solved. - Map XDMF examples/materials/paraview_output/materials_17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle_map_combined.xdmf, through write_xdmf_with_tags(…, msh, cell_tags, fields, comm=comm) + adopt_host_ownership. - Every field is P1 and named, with the 37 °C base, the periodic case A, M_map = 2¹⁰ per period, and two periods: - theta_mean_K = D·θ_ss(r); - T_six_min_max_C; - six_min_excess_pct; - cem43_duty_per_period_min; - cem43_stand_in_per_period_min; - jensen_excess (the (Jc) reading); - above_43_mean (1 where 37 + D·θ_ss(r) ≥ 43). - Use the operators' 2-D (n_t, n_vertices) call. Its column-wise equality is gated (step1.log:75–77; step 2 ramp test :69–75). - Time series …_period_combined.xdmf (write_xdmf_time_series): 17 frames, t = P + 75 j s for j = 0…16 (64 samples at M_map = 2¹⁰, on the grid), with fields T_C and T_six_min_mean_C. - CSV …_centre_history.csv: one row per sample over the second period at M = s2.M_SEQ[0], with columns t_s, theta_K, T37_C, chi, chi_six_min_mean, theta_six_min_mean_K, cumulative_cem43_min. - The XDMF / H5 / CSV are under the gitignored paraview_output/. Only the PNG is tracked; window 6 confirms this. - Guide. The three required headings, ## Setup figure and ## Related. Related lists mat:11 first, then mat:15, then the two gate modules and tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py by full filename (rule (b)). The guide explains: - why the six-minute average of the power reads full power on this schedule, while the temperature's barely moves (τ₁ ≫ P); - why a whole-period window hides the ripple exactly ((B1), (S2)); - CEM43 as the exact integral of the interpolant (ruling 318-1), and why the Σ R^(43−Tᵢ)Δtᵢ rectangle sum is printed only (37.5 against 750.65 on the rise at 2 samples, :51); - Jensen at the centre, and its failure across 43 °C; - that the 37 °C base is the gate's re-basing and that a 20 °C bench gel accumulates ≈ 0; - a ParaView recipe: open the map, colour by cem43_duty_per_period_min on Slice z = 0, Contour above_43_mean = 0.5 for the r ≈ 20 mm isotherm, colour by jensen_excess to see the sign flip; open the period series and Play; open the CSV in ParaView (CSV reader, Line Chart View) and plot chi_six_min_mean against theta_six_min_mean_K. - Write ≈, never ~.

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare harness call. Before window 1, docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written (the commands of 20261008T172115Z_EX-89-item332-pre-figures.log:12 and 20261008T172117Z_EX-89-item332-pre-docrefs.log:12, relabelled): - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-104-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-104-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - Record N, ok, missing and broken, and the docrefs dead= list. It read examples=98 ok=98 missing=0 broken=0 and dead=2 guide=0 stale=56 exit=1 at 17:21 UTC (:134 / :98). The two dead references are ans9_aed_results.json and ans9_corrected_rows.json from examples/ansys_benchmarks/ans9_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz/SPEC.md:36, :38, unrelated to this item. Take N fresh, since another example may land first. 2. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-104-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:17 -n 2 -t 180 --dry-run". It must print (complex build) and the line below, apart from -T. 3. Flagged run (predicted [30, 120] s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-104 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/materials/17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle.py"' - Pass: Status 0, every assertion green, and every recomputed row equal to its record as in (1). 4. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-104-control. The readings must be unchanged; every closed-form number is computed redundantly per rank and is deterministic, so they are predicted bitwise. 5. Post-censuses EX-104-post-figures / EX-104-post-docrefs (window 1's commands with those labels), run after the guide is final. - Write the prediction first: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, missing unchanged, broken=0. - Docrefs: no new dead reference. The dead= list is identical to window 1's (today the two ans9 SPEC entries, dead=2), with guide=0. exit=1 is expected for that unrelated reason and is not this item's failure. Any dead reference naming a materials_17_* file or 17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle.md fails the item. 6. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists exactly the three new tracked paths. No other code path is modified.

(3) Tier. Standard, -n 2, complex build (group-sourced). The predicted example window is [30, 120] s. The heaviest measured analogue is MAT-20 step 2's 19 s two-module window. There is no -n 4 window: nothing reduces except the collective mesh, figure and XDMF calls, and the scalar readings are rank-redundant.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Harness shape. Every harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, no cd … &&, no ; date / | tail, no redirect (bash_guard rule 3). ./scripts/run_examples.sh is host-side: emit it with --dry-run, then pass the string to the harness. Never wrap it in docker compose exec (the Status-127 trap). A docker-socket denial means stop and report. - Timeouts. Bash timeout: 660000 on every window, and container timeout -k 30 180. Status 124 is a finding, never a retry; never raise the timeout. - Blocked closed-form evaluation. robin_sphere_* broadcast to (n_points × 400 terms). An unblocked 2¹⁹ + 1 call is ≈ 1.7 GB per temporary. Use s1._T_centre (8192-point blocks) for (A2), and evaluate the map in ≤ 8192-point blocks of (vertex, time) pairs. - (A2) digit equality needs the gate's grid. Stride a 2¹⁹ + 1 linspace; never build a fresh 2¹⁸ + 1 linspace, whose last ulp can differ. - Switch times on the grid. robin_sphere_duty_cycle_temperature's docstring warns against evaluating within a few 1/s_N of a switch. The gate's grid s2._series puts samples exactly on switches and held (B1) to 1e-14. Use only that grid (t = arange × P/M) for every asserted quantity and for χ. Frame times must be grid samples. - NaN head. running_average returns NaN where t − W < t₀. Use np.nanargmax or the gate's np.where(sel, means, -np.inf) idiom, and restrict to the second period for (B2) and the map. - The complex build. P1 Function arrays are complex. Build every history as a real numpy array from the closed form, and never feed .x.array to cem43 / running_average (they raise on a non-zero imaginary part by design). Assign real values into the Functions and scatter_forward. - Rank safety. Mesh build, write_setup_figure, both XDMF writes and adopt_host_ownership are collective. Call them on every rank, never inside rank == 0. The map is evaluated on owned dofs only. Print on rank 0. - Name every Function. EX-79's HDF5 name collision cost a window. - Import collisions. Use module aliases (s1, s2, m17cf). Never import another example's module. Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (11_duty_cycled_gel_ball.py:55–57). - Units. cem43 returns equivalent seconds; divide by 60 for minutes and label every printed dose with its unit. - No FEM history, no D_BAND. Do not import test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py or test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem's runners (_run, _run_duty). The FEM clause is the weekly's (ruling 319-3). _chi is the only name taken from test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem. - The Jensen premise. Assert min T > 43 before (J). The R switch makes the integrand concave at 43 °C, and the map's (Jc) reading is expected to be negative there. - PNG ≤ 600 KiB (ans:8's first was 631 KiB). - Rule (i) freeze. The script is frozen once window 3 starts, and the guide before window 5.

(5) Scope. Closed-form histories only: linear ramps, MAT-9's step response re-based to 37 °C, and MAT-17 case A's periodic closed form on MAT-9's ball. cem43 and running_average are gated against closed forms; the map is the radial closed form at vertex radii. - Not claimed: - a CEM43 limit, damage threshold, or IEC 60601-2-33 / six-minute SAR compliance statement; - tissue, perfusion, or the 37 °C base as a phantom temperature; - any FEM history or MAT-20's FEM clause (D_BAND, weekly); - MAT-17 case B, a coil-driven or SAR-shaped source, or a pulse sequence. - MAT-20 and MAT-17 do not move.

(6) Negative result. - A recomputed record off its log digits ((A1) ref / rect_sum, (A2) t₄₃ / quad / op, (B1), (B2), (Rc), (Wc)), or an anchor red: an example/test divergence. Print the first differing value. Write a known-issues entry, park on attempt/EX-104-<UTC>, and mark item 338 BLOCKED (rule (d)). Never re-record from the example side and never loosen s1.BAR / s2.BAR. - (S1) / (S2) red: χ is off the grid or a switch sample has the wrong phase. Print χ around D·P, fix it once in-slot and re-run window 3; otherwise park. - (J) red with its premise green: a strict convexity inequality has failed. That is an operator finding. Stop, write a known-issues entry, and report; do not drop the assertion. - (J) premise red (min T ≤ 43): the re-basing or the closed form moved. Stop and report. - (S1c) inside the bar: the window did not reach the operator. Stop and report. - Over 180 s, Status 124, or the slot at minute 50 before window 4: park on attempt/EX-104-<UTC> with the last printed line and journal it; the review re-tiers. - A printed value outside its prediction (six-minute θ excess, duty dose, surface or bench dose, (Jc) sign): report it. It has no status effect. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

(7) Status it can move. EX-104 ⬜ → ✅ under its §7 Done-when, and the census N → N + 1. MAT-20 stays 🟡; this example neither executes nor substitutes for its FEM clause. No §2 sentence moves.

Executor prompt (verbatim, for the example-runner spawn):

Execute EX-104 (§9 item 338) exactly as briefed in docs/planning/chunks/EX-104.md#§9-item-338; you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The harness call is the whole Bash command — nothing piped or redirected. Add only the three examples/materials/ paths; edit no gate module, nothing under src/, and not thermal/__init__.py. Use closed-form histories only, never an FEM history. Make no edit to the script after window 3 starts or to the guide after window 5 starts. Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record (log:line) or prediction, and the census before / after with the docrefs dead= list.

Review rulings (2026-10-08 18:00 review) on item 338 — these outrank the brief above. (1) The figure mesh carrying a closed-form P1 map is accepted, labelled in the guide and XDMF as "closed form evaluated at vertex radii — not an FEM history". (2) (S1), (S2) are exact premises and are asserted at s2.BAR; (J) is asserted as a strict inequality only behind its asserted min T > 43 °C premise; (S1c) asserted. (3) Copied quad / brentq settings with citations are settings, not bands — accepted; no lift. (4) Asserting (A2) at the recorded N = 2¹⁸ without the selection loop is accepted. (5) No -n 4 control; the usual flagged + unflagged -n 2 pair (EX-57 convention) is the control, compared at the bands.

Outcome (item 338, 2026-10-08, 22:30 slot, take-next): DONE, EX-104 ✅. No lift, no gate or src/ edit. Dry run 20261009T034920Z_EX-104-dryrun.log (complex build). Two unflagged shake-down windows ran before the run of record (20261009T034925Z_EX-104-shakedown.log, exit 1 on an XDMF frame-padding bug in the script; 20261009T035022Z_EX-104-shakedown2.log, exit 0); the script was frozen before the flagged run (mtime 22:50:18 < 22:51:11). Run of record 20261009T035111Z_EX-104.log: Status 0, 45 s -n 2 (predicted [30, 120]). (A1) ref = rect_sum to every digit, rel ≤ 6.268e-16; (A2) t₄₃ 14087.0956163533 s, quad 1.708516120835631e+05, op rel 8.980e-12 at N = 2¹⁸; (B1) 5.959e-15 / 8.139e-15 / 1.032e-14 / 9.011e-15; (B2) root 779.999309 s, t_max −0.398 / +0.205 samples; (Rc) 1.3784 / 0.1937 / 1.3982; (Wc) 1.957e-03 / 1.174e-03 under their ceilings — all equal the step 1 / 2 logs. (S1) six-minute max of χ = 1 exactly; (S2) period-window mean = D, deviation 0 over 4097 windows; (S1c) 0.333171 miss; (J) premise min T 43.039341 °C, margin +4.125e-04 in [2e-4, 8e-4]; (Jc) −3.698e-03 in its predicted range. Six-minute θ max 6.1614 K at 779.883 s, +0.82 %. Control 20261009T035203Z_EX-104-control.log 45 s, identical apart from the figure line. Census figures 99 → 100, broken=0; docrefs dead=0 guide=0 stale=56 exit=2 before and after (the brief's dead=2 was retired by item 336). PNG 227 KiB. Both XDMFs carry a provenance Information element with ruling (1)'s label.

docs.title: EX-105 — ports:21, the capacitor ESR sheet on the copper birdcage
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened 2026-10-08 by the 18:00 daily review (step 5, §5.4 ramp). The base is PORT-24 step 2 (§9 item 309, gated 2026-10-08, commit 91254c5a; outcome and price in docs/planning/chunks/PORT-24.md:47–53). That step put a 0.2 Ω ESR in the model as a series-RC lumped sheet, series_rlc_impedance(f, r_ohm=r, l_h=0, c_f=C) (src/fem_em_solver/ports/lumped.py:138), on F-small's exact-rectangle hole mesh. The operator's binding ruling (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3762–3783, 2026-10-06) says every lumped capacitor carries r = 0.2 Ω and lossless records stay labelled lossless.

No example models capacitor ESR. Checked at drafting: no examples/**/*.py passes a non-zero r_ohm to a capacitor sheet. ports:17 (examples/ports/17_birdcage_tuned_circuit.py) terminates in a lossless series C. ports:18 (examples/ports/18_birdcage_copper_leontovich.py) has copper but no capacitor. ports:1 … ports:20 exist, and no open item claims ports:21.

docs.title: §9 item 339 — 2026-10-08 (example; §5.4 ramp from PORT-24 step 2)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §5.4 example ramp on a gated step (PORT-24 step 2, item 309, GREEN on all three arms). No band, tolerance, record, Done-when or validation target is set or moved. Every band, helper and fixture is imported by name.

The angle. What a 0.2 Ω ESR does to a copper birdcage's Q. On F-small at 64 MHz, the three capacitor sheets take 70.8 % of the non-port loss, and the loss-partition ratio Q(r)/Q(0) prints 0.2923 with Q_C = 1/(ωCr) = 187.57 (20261008T170256Z_PORT-24-step2-r02.log:946–947). That is the ruling's reason made visible: copper's own loss is small enough that the capacitor ESR dominates it. Asserted: the series-RC sheet is its circuit element. Printed as a record: the Q reading.

EX-105 (ports:21) adds examples/ports/21_capacitor_esr_sheet.py and a same-stem guide examples/ports/21_capacitor_esr_sheet.md. The guide carries the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step; scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py:110–113), plus ## Setup figure and ## Related. The setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Build: complex (ports: is in run_examples.sh's complex-prefix list, scripts/run_examples.sh:273–275). The script checks default_scalar_type and raises in the real build (the ports:18 pattern, :190–195).
  • Tier: heavy, -n 2, by measurement. The three gate arms took 94 / 91 / 140 s wall each at -n 2. The example runs all three in one process, ≈ 335 s, which is above the standard 180 s ceiling. Runner -t 590; container timeout -k 30 590. Every window is under the ≈ 10 min durable-capture threshold.
  • Cost: ≈ 13 measured (example class median, as for item 332) / ≈ 55 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 20 lift, script and guide + ≈ 13 windows (three re-gates ≈ 5.4 min, the example ≈ 5.6 min, dry run and four censuses ≈ 1.5 min) + ≈ 7 spare. A slot starts it only before minute 30.
  • Depends on: nothing open. PORT-24 step 2 is on main (91254c5a). Item 308 (step 1, BLOCKED for the 10-10 weekly) is not a dependency, and none of its code is used (see Traps).
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-105, §9 item 339 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-105.md, heading §9 item 339). You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window; do not end the turn while a window runs. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. Make no edit to the gate module after its first re-gate window starts, and none to the script after the example window starts."

Code (rule (a), additive, disclosed). 1. tests/validation/test_port24_series_rc_sheet.py: lift the port24 fixture body into a module-level _run_port24_arm(arm). The lift covers :130 (the th14 import) and :135–224, verbatim, prints included. The fixture becomes three statements: arm = _arm(), the existing pytest.skip when it is None, and return _run_port24_arm(arm). The test function test_port24_series_rc_sheet (:227–250) is untouched: no assertion is added, removed or re-banded. The diff is disclosed in the commit message. Only two additive changes are allowed: - Initialise q_ratio = None and q_rest = None before the if p_rc > 0.0: branch (:214). Inside it, assign q_ratio = p_rest / (p_rest + p_rc) and q_rest = q_rest_over_qc * q_c, the same expressions its print already evaluates. The print strings stay unchanged. - Extend the return dict (:223–224), keeping the existing keys, with: cells, t_mesh, omega, p_src, p_sheet (the per-port dict), p_vol, p_surf, p_rest, share, q_c, q_ratio, q_rest; and, for the example's figure and XDMF, msh, cell_tags, facet_tags, specs and e (fields.e_complex). - No new keyword, no src/ edit, and no edit to any other module. Every [PORT-24 s2] print stays byte-identical except its seconds. 2. examples/ports/21_capacitor_esr_sheet.py (new). It calls _run_port24_arm("r02"), then "r0", then "plant". It re-asserts on each returned dict, writes the figure and XDMF from the r02 result, and prints an [ESR on the copper birdcage] summary. Repo root goes on sys.path as ports:18 does (:86–88), so the runner's PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src suffices. After each arm's asserts, drop that arm's field keys (msh, e and the rest) before the next arm, except r02's until its XDMF is written. 3. examples/ports/21_capacitor_esr_sheet.md (new), written after the example window and before the post-censuses.

Imports (never restated). - From tests.validation.test_port24_series_rc_sheet (the gate module): _run_port24_arm, ESR_OHM, PLANT_OHM, PLANT_INDEX, FREQUENCY_HZ, DEGREE, POWER_DRIVEN, _rc. - From the modules the gate imports them from, re-imported by name as the gate does (:48–63), with an is check against the gate module's attribute for each band: - REDUCTION_BAND (tests/validation/test_port_lumped_rlc_termination.py:88, 1e-3); - LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:165, 1e-9); - DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (tests/validation/test_birdcage_power_identity.py:227, 1e-6); - C_F (tests/validation/test_ans7_exact_strip.py:91); - REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM; - PHANTOM_CELL_TAG (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:101, for the figure only). - From src: fem_em_solver.ports.lumped.series_rlc_impedance (for the printed Z column only, which must equal _rc(r)); fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils (write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership); fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure.write_setup_figure. - No literal record. The script states no residual, power, share or Q as a number. The only literals are the air cell tag 2 in the figure's region_names and hide_tags, cited to ports:18 :222, :230 (a display input, not a record; the EX-101 ruling (3) precedent). - Never import fem_em_solver.ports.ring_modes' esr_ohm path, tests/unit/test_port24_esr_circuit.py, anything on attempt/PORT-24-step1-*, or another example's module.

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script, at the gate's bands, on every rank). These are the test function's own assertions (:231–250), re-made on the returned dicts. - (I) The sheet is its circuit element. For every sheet P1–P4, in the r02 and r0 arms, ident[i]["res"] ≤ REDUCTION_BAND. Here res is ‖S′_meas − S′_pred‖_F / ‖S′_pred‖_F, with S′_pred = reduce_terminated_ports(S₄, 50, {i: series_rlc_impedance(f, r_ohm=r, l_h=0, c_f=C_F)}) (PORT-14's identity). - r02 records: 3.049022e-05 / 3.036163e-05 / 3.040555e-05 / 3.003774e-05 (…170256Z_PORT-24-step2-r02.log:941–944). - r0 records: 3.096783e-05 / 3.083764e-05 / 3.088213e-05 / 3.050839e-05 (…170618Z_PORT-24-step2-r0.log:941–944). - (Z) r = 0 is the capacitor-only sheet. In the r0 arm, every ident[i]["cap_res"] ≤ LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. Records 5.174213e-16 / 7.566631e-16 / 2.467983e-16 / 2.766926e-16 (…r0.log:941–944). These are round-off and are compared at the band only, never as digits. - (P) Exact power identity, the RC sheets' own dissipation counted. In every arm, resid ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. Records 1.011e-12 / 1.017e-12 / 1.012e-12 (…r02.log:945, …r0.log:945, …170439Z_PORT-24-step2-plant.log:945). Compared at the band only. - (R0) r = 0 sheets are lossless. In the r0 arm, p_rc == 0.0 (record: P2–P4 0.000000000e+00 W, …r0.log:945). This is the gate's printed fact. It is asserted here only because the lossless-record label of the ruling rests on it. The review rules whether to keep it (Q3). If struck, it is printed only. - Width: -n 2 only, the gate's width.

Printed rows equal the gate log records (a reading the executor reports; the script restates no record). The example log carries each arm's [PORT-24 s2] block from the lifted body. Compare these lines, digit for digit, except seconds and the round-off columns ((Z), (P), reciprocity): - the mesh line, 80 798 cells (:910 in each gate log); - the 4×4 line (:940); - the four (I) lines (:941–944); - the (P) power line (:945); - the (Dz) line (:946); - the Q line (:947).

All gate logs are under docs/testing/logs/. The executor reports any line that differs outside those exceptions.

Then the script's own [ESR on the copper birdcage] block. It is arithmetic on the returned values, printed only, each item beside its source line: - ESR loss share: share = P_RC / (P_RC + P_vol + P_surf) = 7.077045e-01 (…r02.log:946). The guide says 70.8 %. - Where the ESR loss sits. P2 3.438672404e-10 W, P3 2.544472427e-05 W, P4 6.634945767e-09 W (…r02.log:945). Under the P1 drive, the opposite sheet P3 carries ≈ 99.97 % of P_RC. The guide reads this as the drive's mode content, not as a per-capacitor Q. - The rest of the loss. P_vol (the phantom; σ is zero outside it) 6.276138116e-06 W and P_surf (copper, Leontovich on tag 401) 4.235904194e-06 W, so the copper share of P_rest is ≈ 40.3 % (…r02.log:945). - The Q reading. Q(r)/Q(0) = q_ratio = 2.922955e-01; Q_C = 1/(ωCr) = 1.875695e+02; Q_rest = 4.541422e+02 (…r02.log:947). It is printed beside its closed form, 1/Q = 1/Q_rest + 1/Q_C, evaluated from those two numbers: Q(r) ≈ 132.7, and Q(r)/Q_rest reproduces q_ratio. - This agreement is true by construction. Q_rest is inferred from the same partition, so the example prints it and never asserts it. The guide says so in one sentence. - The PORT-24 Done-when's "Q_Cu" is this fixture's Q_rest = copper + phantom (see Q2). - The size of the "fixed stored energy" assumption. P_rest(r = 0.2) / P_rest(r = 0) = 1.051204231e-05 / 1.057979998e-05 ≈ 0.9936 on the same drive (…r02.log:945, …r0.log:945). This is printed from the r02 and r0 dicts. PORT-24.md:52 rounds the move to 0.7 %. - (Dz), with the RC dissipation omitted: 7.031342e-03 of P_src, against 1.017e-12 at r = 0 (…r02.log:946, …r0.log:946). The guide explains why this is not the 70.8 %: P_src is dominated by P1's own 50 Ω sheet, 3.583786649e-03 of 3.619750395e-03 W (…r02.log:945).

(2) Negative control (rule (e)). - (Pl) asserted: a 0.4 Ω plant on P2 breaks the 0.2 Ω identity, and only there. In the plant arm, ident[PLANT_INDEX]["res"] > REDUCTION_BAND, and the three unplanted sheets stay ≤ REDUCTION_BAND. Asserted at the band, never bitwise. - Record 1.095344e-02 = 10.95× the band, unplanted max 3.049022e-05 (…plant.log:942, :949). - Ceiling: none is asserted. Item 309's predicted ceiling (≈ 5.3e-3, the terminal-impedance level) was exceeded ≈ 2×, through the (I − S_bb Γ)⁻¹ factor at |Γ| ≈ 1 (PORT-24.md:50). So no factor is asserted, only the direction. The 10.95× is printed. - The script prints its own (Pl) line, because the gate's :949 line comes from the test function, which the example does not call. - (Dz), printed only: omitting the RC dissipation moves the power residual from 1.011e-12 to 7.031e-03, ≈ 7e9× (…r02.log:945–946). The gate never asserts this, and neither does the example.

Output. - Combined XDMF examples/ports/paraview_output/ports_21_capacitor_esr_sheet_combined.xdmf, from the r02 arm (P1 at 50 Ω, P2–P4 series-RC at r = 0.2 Ω). Script: and Gate: lines name both files in full. - Section 1: the ruling in one sentence, the recipe LumpedSheetPortSpec(port_impedance_ohm=series_rlc_impedance(f, r_ohm=0.2, l_h=0, c_f=C)) on exact rectangles with width_correction_kappa=None, and the angle. - Section 2: ./run_examples.sh -e ports:21 -n 2 -t 590, the measured wall time, emit-then-harness, and the figure flag. - Section 3, the reading steps: - (I) per sheet, in both arms; - (Z) at r = 0; - (P); - the (Pl) control and why no ceiling is asserted; - the ESR block: the 70.8 % share, P3's dominance, the copper/phantom split, and Q(r)/Q(0) beside 1/Q = 1/Q_rest + 1/Q_C (true by construction, and the ≈ 0.64 % stored-energy move); - the ParaView recipe. - A table of this run's readings beside the gate log lines, quoted from the example's own log. - The scope sentences below. - ## Related, every artifact by full filename (rule (b)): examples/ports/17_birdcage_tuned_circuit.md (lossless series C, circuit side), examples/ports/18_birdcage_copper_leontovich.md (copper loss, no capacitor), tests/validation/test_port24_series_rc_sheet.py, tests/validation/test_port_lumped_rlc_termination.py, src/fem_em_solver/ports/lumped.py, docs/planning/chunks/PORT-24.md. - Name no scratch path in prose. (4) Traps already paid for. - Complex build. The runner sources it for ports:. The re-gates carry FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 and tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py first. No ufl.max_value and no ordering comparison on complex operands; the |E| helper takes sqrt of a real NumPy array. - Exact rectangles, κ off. The fixture is _exact_geo with GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION, and the lifted body already asserts width_correction_kappa is None on every spec (:139). Never build a sub-sheet out of a box (binding ruling 2026-10-02). - Step 1 is parked. Use no esr_ohm keyword (it does not exist on main) and nothing from attempt/PORT-24-step1-*. The ESR enters only through series_rlc_impedance's r_ohm, in the sheet impedance. Lossless records (ports:17, ans:7) are never re-read with r. - The fixture is a pytest fixture. Calling port24 directly raises, which is why the lift exists. The env var FEM_EM_PORT24_ARM is unset in the example window, and the lift takes the arm as an argument. - Collectives on every rank. _run_port24_arm, write_setup_figure, write_xdmf_with_tags and the |E| interpolation are collective. Prints go under rank == 0 with nothing collective inside (item 227's deadlock). Assertions run on every rank on the returned (already reduced) values. - Returned fields. If a re-gate hangs at teardown after 5 passed, the new field keys are the suspect. Kill at the timeout, check orphans, and stop (see (6)). Never retry with a longer timeout. - pytest needs -s for the printed rows (rule (g)). Never use -k a or b inside the quoted command, since the arm is the env var. - ./run_examples.sh is host-side. Emit with --dry-run, then pass the string to the harness as its own call; never wrap the runner in docker compose exec. - Harness shape. Bare, whole, repo-relative calls only: no cd … &&, no ; date, no | tail, no redirect (bash_guard.py). Use -k 30 on every container timeout. A docker-socket denial means stop and report. - After a killed window: pgrep -c python3 reads 0 first; then, only at 0, the rubric's orphan-stem sweep (docs/automation/daily-review.md:426) as one bare call with <ID> = EX-105. Never clear the cache wholesale. - Freeze order (rule (i)). The gate module is frozen from re-gate 1, the script from window 4, and the guide before window 5. Check file mtimes against the logs before committing.

(5) Scope. - Covered: the series-RC sheet identity (I) on every sheet at r = 0.2 and r = 0; the r = 0 reproduction (Z); the exact power identity (P); and the planted-sheet control (Pl). All on F-small's exact-rectangle hole mesh, 80 798 cells, 64 MHz, degree 1, κ off, copper Leontovich, C = C_F = 6.629e-11 F, -n 2. - Not claimed: - an absolute Q, f₀, S₁₁, Z_in or tuning figure (§2; no such figure is licensed until the h-rungs land, §10 F18 / T12′). The coil is not tuned here: P1 at 50 Ω absorbs ≈ 99 % of P_src; - a measured Q. Q(r)/Q(0) is a loss-partition ratio at assumed fixed stored energy on one drive, and Q_rest is inferred from it; - Q_Cu alone. Q_rest is copper + phantom; - a measured ESR, frequency dependence, degree 2, h-convergence, F-human, or any AED or Palace comparison; - PORT-24 step 1 (circuit layer). The example does not move PORT-24.

(6) Negative result. Report the measurement and stop. Journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-105-<UTC>, and mark item 339 BLOCKED with its unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)). EX-105 stays ⬜. Never widen a band, edit src/, or drop an arm. - A re-gate red, or its digits off item 309's logs: revert the lift and write a known-issues entry (the fixture moved under a green record). - An anchor red in the example with all three re-gates green, or printed rows off the gate logs: an example/test divergence finding (example-runner.md:24–27), for example in-process arm order or reuse of a JIT'd form across three mesh builds. Print the first differing line and write a known-issues entry. Never re-record from the example side. - (Pl) planted residual ≤ band: contradicts item 309's GREEN plant arm on the same fixture; stop. - Over 590 s or Status 124: check orphans, park, and stop. The fallback is the review's: for example, one arm per window through an env switch. Never a longer timeout. - There is no PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-105 §7 row goes ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). The review adds the row in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). Questions for the review. - (Q1) The lift returns field objects (msh, e and the rest) from a module-scoped fixture, so the XDMF and figure need no second solve. Accept, or require the figure and XDMF dropped (census then +1 without an XDMF) rather than a restated field solve? - (Q2) Q_Cu vs Q_rest. The PORT-24 Done-when says "1/Q = 1/Q_Cu + 1/Q_C". The gate measures Q_rest = copper + phantom (P_surf 4.236e-6 W, P_vol 6.276e-6 W). The example labels it Q_rest and prints the copper share (≈ 40.3 %). Confirm the wording, and whether the §7 row's phrase should be annotated (the weekly's, not this item's). - (Q3) (R0) p_rc == 0.0 exactly at r = 0. This is an assertion the gate does not make (it prints it). Keep it, or print only, per "the item adds no assertion the step does not make"? - (Q4) One flagged window at -n 2, no control run. Accept? A -n 4 control would add ≈ 6 min and test width invariance the gate never claimed. - (Q5) A two-function lift (build the mesh, 4×4 and problem once; run the arms on it) would save ≈ 60 s but is a larger diff with a changed construction order. EX-106 (mri:14) adds examples/mri/14_study_sar_and_b1.py and the same-stem guide 14_study_sar_and_b1.md: one Study, one field-keeping solve, two results. - The script builds WF-16's Study(FourPortBirdcageGeometry.f_small(), phantom, LumpedPortDrive(), frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_64_HZ, degree=1) (exact rectangles, κ off), as mri:8 does. - It asks the Study for |B₁⁺| (Study.b1_plus() / b1_plus_at) and for the 10 g mass-averaged SAR (Study.sar(mass_g=10.0)) on the four single drives. - It re-asserts both gated C4 identities at the imported C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, and shows that the second result reuses the first one's solve. - The angle is the Phase 9 (9a) user's question: "how do I get B₁⁺ and 10 g SAR out of my Study?" mri:8 answers it for S only.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: standard by prediction, heavy by ceiling (as mri:8). -n 2, complex, degree 1. Runner -t 300; container timeout -k 30 300.
  • Cost: ≈ 13 measured (example class median) / ≈ 45 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 script and guide + ≈ 10 windows). The price basis is under (3).
  • Depends on: nothing. Items 321 and 322 are on main. mri:8 (EX-92) is ✅, and this item does not edit it.
  • Shared files. The item adds only the three example paths (script, guide, PNG). It edits nothing in src/ or tests/, and imports from them. There is no rule (a) lift: the gate modules keep their fixtures private (case), so the script composes the same calls through the public Study methods.
  • Gap. grep -rnlE '\.sar\(|b1_plus_at|\.b1_plus\(' examples --include=*.py returns nothing. The existing SAR and B₁⁺ examples (mri:3 MAT-4's 10 g on the birdcage; ports:6 / ports:7 / ports:16 WF-6's B₁⁺ maps) build by hand on the older sheet fixtures, not through the Study. mri:7 – mri:13 compute S, mean SAR, temperature or an estimate, and none of them computes 10 g SAR or B₁⁺.

Degree: 1 at -n 2. Why. - It is the gate's cheapest leg. The degree-1 SAR window (field-keeping solve 36.41 s, 9 operator calls 21.00 s) took 114 s at -n 2 with 1.92 GiB summed RSS (20261008T184215Z_WF-16-s4-W1-deg1.log:1881–1882, :3821). The B₁⁺ window took 43 s (20261008T185141Z_WF-16-s5-W1-deg1.log:1877–1878, :1903). - Degree 2 is held at -n 8 (DEGREE2_RECORD_WIDTH). It needs ≈ 18 GiB summed (…184556Z_WF-16-s4-W2-deg2.log:1966, …185400Z_WF-16-s5-W2-deg2.log:1956) and carries the degree-2, quadrature-16 JIT compile. - -n 2 is also the width at which a missing reduction shows, and the width that item 192's P1 record holds at (OPS-41). The script asserts it. - The price of that choice is a thin margin. Degree 1's worst 10 g pair (3→0) reads 4.5024 %, which is 0.90× the band (…184215Z_WF-16-s4-W1-deg1.log:1897). Degree 2 reads 0.5961 % worst (…184556Z_WF-16-s4-W2-deg2.log:2002). The guide says so, and says why: a_10g / h = 0.891 on the 0.015 m phantom, 537 phantom cells, and a mesh that is not C4-congruent (WF-16.md item 321 traps). See (6) for what a reading above 5 % means.

Imports (never restated). - From fem_em_solver: Study, FourPortBirdcageGeometry, LumpedPortDrive. From fem_em_solver.materials: GelledSalinePhantomMaterial. From fem_em_solver.post.sar: averaging_ball_radius, mean_sar. From fem_em_solver.study: SAR_QUADRATURE_DEGREE (printed). From fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils: write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership. From fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure: write_setup_figure. From fem_em_solver.utils.instrumentation: report_peak_rss. - From tests.package.test_wf16_study_four_port: _record, _rel. - From tests.validation.test_ans4_exact_strip_records: ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH. - From tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_four_port: LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. - From tests.validation.test_birdcage_b1_plus_map: C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (:120), PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, _sample_points (:246), _rotate_z (:283), _relative_l2 (:600). - From tests.validation.test_birdcage_sar_mass_averaged: CENTRE_RADIUS_M, WHOLE_PHANTOM_BALL_RADIUS_M, EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, CONTROL_PREDICTED, CONTROL_CEILING (:149–170). - From tests.validation.test_birdcage_b1_quadrature: QUADRATURE_STEP_DEG, _port_index. - From tests.validation.test_mass_averaged_sar_standard_masses: TEN_GRAM_KG. - From tests.validation.test_lossy_sphere_fullwave: FREQUENCY_64_HZ, SALINE_SIGMA, SALINE_EPSILON_R. - From tests.mesh.test_birdcage_implant_rod: _cell_values_with_ghosts (:171), for the figure-only tags and the ball mask only. - No new number. mass_g=10.0 is the API argument, the same literal as the gate (test_wf16_study_sar.py:166). The script states no σ, εᵣ, frequency, radius, band or record of its own. The gate modules export no SAR or B₁⁺ record constant, so the record digits are compared by the executor against the gate logs (below) and not asserted in-script; the review rules on that under Q2.

The API sequence (public methods only; the private _solve_port_fields is never called). 1. study = Study(..., degree=1), then maps = study.b1_plus(comm=comm). This triggers the one field-keeping solve and caches it on study.fields_result. Keep fr = study.fields_result and time the call. 2. Read the sheets off fr.sheets, port id f"P{s['tag'] - study.geometry.sheet_iface}". Get the azimuths, Δ = (az["P2"] − az["P1"]) mod 360, and the indices k = _port_index(az[p], az["P1"], QUADRATURE_STEP_DEG) (it asserts the 90° grid). Then by_k and the centres c_k = CENTRE_RADIUS_M·(cos az, sin az, 0) for drive by_k[k], exactly as test_wf16_study_sar.py:150–162. 3. points = _sample_points({"mesh": fr.mesh, "cell_tags": fr.cell_tags}), then study.b1_plus_at(...) on the five images of test_wf16_study_b1.py:114–125 (P1@0, P2@+Δ, P4@−Δ, P3@2Δ, P2@−Δ control) and at the origin per drive. 4. study.sar(mass_g=10.0, centres=[c_k], drives=[by_k[k]], comm=comm) for k = 0…3 (the diagonal), the same at c_{k+2} (the control), and study.sar(radius_m=WHOLE_PHANTOM_BALL_RADIUS_M, centres=[(0, 0, 0)], drives=["P1"]): 9 operator calls, as the gate (:164–182). 5. mean_sar(fr.fields["P1"].e_complex, sigma=…sigma_field, rho=study.density_kg_m3, cell_tags=fr.cell_tags, subdomain_ids=study.geometry.phantom_tag, comm=comm) for (i), as :206–213.

(1) Anchor (asserted in-script; every band imported). Each line is printed in the gate's format beside its gate-log record, and the executor compares the printed rows with the cited lines. - (W) comm.size == ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, before anything else. - (R) same fixture: _rel(fr.s_matrix, _record(1)) ≤ LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. Record 9.557e-11 (…184215Z_WF-16-s4-W1-deg1.log:1884). - (One) one solve feeds both results: after step 4, study.fields_result is fr, and study.result is None (solve() was never called; the gate asserts the same at test_wf16_study_sar.py:147). This is the example's own check. A second solve would show as a changed object and a doubled wall time. - (ii) the 10 g C4 quadrant identity, the SAR gate: the four cyclic pairs |SAR(c_{k+1}; k+1) − SAR(c_k; k)| / SAR(c_k; k) ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. Records 0.8702 / 3.5284 / 2.0337 / 4.5024 % (…184215Z…:1897). The diagonal SAR_10g and masses are printed at .9e beside :1893–1896, and the max over the four evaluated centres (2.073991516e-05 W/kg, P4, :1898) carries the gate's own label: "at 1 V drive, NOT a spatial search, NOT a C95.3 compliance figure". - (i) whole-phantom coverage: the ball's power against mean_sar's, and its mass against ρ·V, each ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. Records 1.210e-14 / 3.997e-15 (:1888, round-off: asserted at the band only). Power 1.585977541981e-06 W and mass 2.195294683148e-01 kg are printed beside :1888. - (iv) containment on study.geometry's fields, as test_wf16_study_sar.py:118–132: CENTRE_RADIUS_M + a_10g < phantom_radius, and circumradius < WHOLE_PHANTOM_BALL_RADIUS_M < nearest conductor. Record line …184215Z…:66. Here a_10g = averaging_ball_radius(mass_kg=TEN_GRAM_KG, rho=study.density_kg_m3), printed 13.3650 mm (:1881). - (B1) the |B₁⁺| C4 covariance identity, the B₁⁺ gate: _relative_l2 of P2@+Δ, P4@−Δ and P3@2Δ against P1 on the common valid mask, each ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. Records 1.8695 / 1.9494 / 1.6405 % (…185141Z_WF-16-s5-W1-deg1.log:1884). The drive rotation is printed (90.000000°, :1877). - (B3) valid-point floor: every image is valid on all points.shape[0] points, and that count is > 0. Record 51 of 51 on each image (:1880). - (T) tag: PHANTOM_CELL_TAG == study.geometry.phantom_tag, the precondition of _sample_points. - Printed beside its record, not asserted: |B₁⁺| at the phantom centre per 1 V drive, 1.667281487e-08 / 1.700738851e-08 / 1.665270745e-08 / 1.674331925e-08 T (:1885), labelled "a record, not absolute, not homogeneity". Also printed: cells (117 206, version-tagged), phantom cells (537, …184215Z…:1881, the global count from an allreduce of owned tag-3 cells), a_10g / h (0.8910), times and summed RSS. - Digit equality is part of the Done-when. The printed rows (R), (ii) pairs and diagonal, (B1), (B3), the centre values and the controls must equal the cited gate lines at the gate's printed digits. The degree, width, mesh and calls are the gate's, at the same -n 2. A last-digit difference in a .9e / .12e field is reported, not a failure. A difference in a .4f % pair is an example/test divergence finding (see (6)).

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). Both cost no solve, and both are the gate's own controls re-asserted through the example's calls. - (c1) the mis-paired far-side ball: SAR(c_{k+2}; k) against SAR(c_k; k). The sign is asserted, > C4_COVARIANCE_BAND at every k. The size is printed beside its record, 88.1162 / 87.9366 / 88.6600 / 88.9315 % (…184215Z…:1906). It is predicted ≈ CONTROL_PREDICTED (90 %), and CONTROL_CEILING (100 %) bounds it (a non-negative SAR cannot fall more than 100 %), so the measured ≈ 88 % is 0.88 of the ceiling and no factor is asserted. Separation from the band is ≈ 17.6×. - (cB) the mis-rotation: P2 read at the counter-rotated points (−Δ) against P1. The sign is asserted, > C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. Its record is 35.0040 % (…185141Z…:1892). Item 322's 80–100 % prediction missed and was reported (WF-16.md item 322 outcome; this control is a 180° mis-rotation of P2's map, not step 2's pairing). The example prints 35.0040 % as the record and must not reprint the 80–100 % prediction. ‖a − b‖/‖b‖ of two non-negative maps has no tight ceiling below 2, so no factor is asserted.

(3) Windows (each the whole Bash command, Bash timeout: 660000, foreground, one bare repo-relative harness call, nothing chained or piped). 0. Orphan check from a bare shell: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. The cache sweep (rubric (4), label EX-106-cache-sweep) runs only after a killed window, and only when that check reads 0. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written (the commands of 20261008T172115Z_EX-89-item332-pre-figures.log:12 and 20261008T172117Z_EX-89-item332-pre-docrefs.log:12, relabelled): - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-106-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-106-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - Last readings: examples=98 ok=98 missing=0 broken=0 (20261008T173602Z_EX-89-item332-post-figures.log:134); docrefs 119 guides, dead=2 guide=0 stale=56 exit=1 (20261008T173603Z_EX-89-item332-post-docrefs.log:35, :98). Both dead references are unrelated to this item: ans9_aed_results.json and ans9_corrected_rows.json, cited from examples/ansys_benchmarks/ans9_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz/SPEC.md:36, :38 (:37–38). Take N and the dead list fresh from window 1, since other examples may have landed. 2. Dry run: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-106-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:14 -n 2 -t 300 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 3. Flagged run of record, predicted [70, 180] s. The basis: - the field-keeping solve is 36.41 s (mesh 27.25, sweep 8.65) and the 9 operator calls 21.00 s (…184215Z…:1881); - the 4 CG1 projections take 2.69 s and the evaluations 0.89 s (…185141Z…:1877); - mean_sar ≈ 1 s; the XDMF interpolations and write ≈ 10 s; the setup figure ≈ 15 s; startup ≈ 10 s. That sums to ≈ 95 s. - mri:8's flagged run took 51 s for a 36.8 s Study (20261007T094132Z_EX-92.log). Summed RSS is predicted ≤ 2.5 GiB (gate 1.92 GiB). - The command, which is mri:8's run of record with the path changed (-T added, PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src as emitted). If the dry run emits a string that differs in any other way, use the emitted one and note it: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-106 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/14_study_sar_and_b1.py"' 4. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-106-control. Every assertion must be green again, and the readings must match the flagged run at the band, never bitwise: (ii), (B1) and the controls on the same side of C4_COVARIANCE_BAND; (R), (i) and (One) at their bands. A digit difference between the two runs is reported. 5. Post-censuses EX-106-post-figures / EX-106-post-docrefs (window 1's commands under those labels), after the guide is final. Write the prediction first: - figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, missing unchanged, broken=0; - docrefs: guides scanned +1, guide=0, and no new dead reference: the dead list is identical to window 1's (today the two ans9 SPEC entries). exit=1 is acceptable only for that pre-existing reason; it is not this item's to fix. 6. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new paths (script, guide, PNG). No other tracked path is modified.

Output. - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_14_study_sar_and_b1_combined.xdmf, through write_xdmf_with_tags(…, fr.mesh, fr.cell_tags, fields, comm=comm) + adopt_host_ownership (mri:8's call). Every field is real and named: - B1plus_abs_P1 … _P4: P1 Lagrange scalars, built as array arithmetic on each CG1 vector from study.b1_plus(), np.abs(v[:, 0] + 1j*v[:, 1]) / 2 with v = fn.x.array.reshape(-1, 3) (the same blocked P1 node layout). They are the nodal values of the formula b1_plus_at applies; they are visual and not asserted; - E_abs_P1: |E| for the P1 drive, interpolated into P1 Lagrange, as mri:8 (08_study_four_port_birdcage.py:213–219); - power_density_P1: ½σ|E|² in DG0 (W/m³ per 1 V). It is not divided by ρ, which is 0 outside the phantom; - sigma (DG0); - ball10g_mask (DG0): k + 1 in the 10 g ball at c_k and 0 elsewhere, from numpy cell midpoints over owned + ghost cells with squared distances. Print each ball's owned-cell count (allreduced). A ball's mesh cells are not its quadrature mass: the operator integrates the ball exactly at quadrature degree 16, and the mask is only a picture. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_14_study_sar_and_b1_setup.png, on fr.mesh, called right after step 2 (the centres exist by then): - use a figure-only meshtags that is never passed to a solve: the values from _cell_values_with_ghosts(fr.mesh, fr.cell_tags), with the four balls' cells set to four new tag values. Assert first that those values are absent from the global tag set (allgather); - region_names as mri:8 (:129–136), plus "10 g ball at P1 … P4 centre"; - hide_tags = the air tags, translucent_tags=(phantom_tag,), slice_normal=(0, 0, 1) through the origin (it cuts all four balls), title ≤ 130 characters; - if the PNG is over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Guide examples/mri/14_study_sar_and_b1.md, with the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step), ## Setup figure and ## Related, in mri:8's pattern. It contains: - a readings table: the anchor, the reference (the gate log line), the reading and the band; - the API in four lines (b1_plus, b1_plus_at, sar, fields_result), and why b1_plus() returns a CG1 vector rather than |B₁⁺| (\|·\| is not linear; WF-16.md item 322 disclosure); - the 10 g default and the radius_m alternative, which is refused together with an explicit mass_g; - the margin paragraph: degree 1's worst pair at 0.90× the band, why (a_10g / h = 0.891, 537 phantom cells, a non-C4-congruent mesh), degree 2's 0.5961 % on the same mesh at -n 8, and that both are symmetry identities, not accuracy; - a ParaView recipe: Threshold CellTags = 3 and colour by B1plus_abs_P1; Slice z = 0 on power_density_P1; Threshold ball10g_mask ≥ 1 to see the four balls; compare B1plus_abs_P2 with B1plus_abs_P1 rotated by 90° (Transform filter); - ## Related: mri:8 first, then mri:3 (the hand-built MAT-4 10 g on the birdcage), ports:6 (the hand-built WF-6 B₁⁺ map), mri:7, tests/package/test_wf16_study_sar.py and tests/package/test_wf16_study_b1.py (full filenames, rule (b)), docs/guide/api/Study.md and docs/guide/first_study.md. - The XDMF / H5 are gitignored; only the new PNG is tracked.

Complex build. The script checks default_scalar_type and raises in a real build (the imp:3 guard, 03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.py:197; mri:8 has none). The mri: group sources source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode automatically and registers mri:14 from the 14_ prefix, with no registry edit.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Rank width. The gate asserts degree 1 at -n 2 only, and the P1 record holds there only (OPS-41). Assert (W) first and never run at another width. - κ / ragged refusal. FourPortBirdcageGeometry refuses κ and ragged sheets. Pass no strip_fraction or κ keyword (operator ruling 2026-10-02). - No phantom_resolution. Do not add one to widen the (ii) margin: it changes the fixture away from item 192 and is the review's call (WF-16.md item 321 traps). - The DG0 curl is not the gated estimator, and post.faraday.b1_plus is a DG0 operator. Use only Study.b1_plus / b1_plus_at (CG1, then |·| after evaluation). - Point evaluation goes through b1_plus_at (evaluate_vector_field_parallel inside). Never f.eval(points, np.arange(n)). points must be identical on every rank, which _sample_points and _rotate_z guarantee. - Collectives. sar, b1_plus, b1_plus_at, mean_sar, every allreduce and report_peak_rss stay outside any rank == 0 branch (WF-7 step 0e, item 227: a rank-0-only collective deadlocked a window). Print on rank 0 only. - Rank-local tags. cell_tags.values is rank-local: build the air-tag list and the figure's free-tag check from an allgather (mri:8 :127–128), and the phantom-cell count from an allreduce. - Complex operands. Use no UFL comparison and no sqrt comparison on complex operands (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). The ball mask is numpy on midpoints with squared distances; take np.real / np.abs in numpy. Interpolate E_abs exactly as mri:8 does. - Quadrature. Study.sar pins SAR_QUADRATURE_DEGREE (16); never pass another quadrature_degree, because an unpinned SpatialCoordinate integral can compile for > 9 min (POST-5). The degree-1, quadrature-16 form is already cached by item 321's W1. A killed compile leaves an orphan .c: check orphans, then sweep. - Name every Function (EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window). - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (mri:8 :56–58). Never import another example's module. - ./run_examples.sh runs host-side: emit with --dry-run, then pass the string to the harness as its own call. - Harness shape. Every harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, no cd … && prefix, no ; date / | tail suffix, no redirect (bash_guard rule 3; EX-89 item 332 lost a post-figures log to a chained call, 20261008T173553Z). A docker-socket denial means stop and report. - Timeouts. Bash timeout: 660000 on every window; container timeout -k 30 300. Status 124 is a finding, never a retry, and the timeout is never lengthened. - Rule (i). The script is frozen once window 3 starts, and the guide before window 5. Make no edit after the last window. - PNG ≤ 600 KiB (ans:8's first was 631 KiB). - Write ≈, never ~, in the guide.

(5) Scope. Two symmetry identities of WF-16's API at one frequency on one fixture at fixed h, degree 1, per 1 V single-port drives. - Not claimed: an absolute SAR, a C95.3 / IEC compliance figure or limit, a spatial-peak search, 1 g SAR, B₁⁺ homogeneity or CV, an absolute or closed-form B₁⁺, a quadrature drive, tuning or resonance, degree 2, h-convergence, copper, human scale, or anything WF-16 does not claim. - The printed SAR maximum is "max over 4 evaluated centres at 1 V drive", verbatim from the gate.

(6) Negative result. There is no PREDICTED RED: line. Any red stops the slot: report the measurement, journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-106-<UTC>, and leave EX-106 ⬜. Never widen a band. - (ii) above 5 % (the thin-margin case). At a fixed mesh, width and degree the pair is deterministic up to round-off (≈ 1e-12 relative). Moving 4.5024 % past 5 % needs the 10 g averages to shift by ≈ 0.5 % relative, which noise cannot do. It means the fixture or the pairing moved. - First compare the printed cells, phantom cells (537), (R) and the diagonal with …184215Z…:1881–1897. - Then run the gate once, as a diagnostic: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-106-wf16s4-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_WF16_DEGREE=1 timeout -k 30 400 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/package/test_wf16_study_sar.py -s -v --tb=short'" (item 321's W1 without the sweep module; ≈ 110 s). - If the gate is red too, the fixture moved under a recorded ✅ step (image or mesher). Write a known-issues entry ("WF-16 step 4 10 g C4 pair above the band on main"). The review rules on it, for example re-recording under (1*), or a degree-2 mri:14. - If the gate is green, this is an example/test divergence (centre ↔ drive pairing, sheet ids, ρ). Print the by_k and the centres beside the gate's, and write a known-issues entry. - Either way: never switch to degree 2 in-slot, never add phantom_resolution, and never re-mesh. - (B1) or (B3) red with (R) green: treat it as (ii), with item 322's W1 command as the diagnostic gate run (…185141Z_WF-16-s5-W1-deg1.log:12, labelled EX-106-wf16s5-regate). - (R) red: the Study's solve moved. Stop and report; it is a WF-16 finding. - (One) red: the Study re-solved. Report the two objects and the times. It is an API finding against WF-16 steps 4–5's cache, and the example does not work around it. - (i) red: a plumbing defect in ρ or the tags inside the example's mean_sar call. Fix it once in-slot (that is the example's own line) and re-run window 3; otherwise park. - (c1) or (cB) at or below the band: the comparator is blind. Stop. - Over 300 s, Status 124, or the slot at minute 50 before window 4: park with the last line printed; the review re-tiers. - A printed digit off its gate line (outside a .9e / .12e last digit): report it as above. It has no status effect unless an assertion is red.

(7) Status it can move. - The EX-106 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded), with census examples +1 and broken=0. - §10's Phase 9 (9a) ramp gains "10 g SAR and B₁⁺ through the Study: example present". - WF-16's row does not move (steps 4–5 are records beyond its Done-when, no glyph), and neither does MAT-4 or WF-6. - A red under (6) can add a known-issues entry against WF-16 step 4 or 5 instead.

Executor prompt (verbatim, for the example-runner spawn):

Execute EX-106 (§9 item 340) exactly as briefed in docs/planning/chunks/EX-106.md#§9-item-340; you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped; do not end the turn while a window runs. Degree 1 at -n 2 only; the mri: group sources the complex build. Add only examples/mri/14_study_sar_and_b1.py, its same-stem guide and its PNG; edit nothing under src/ or tests/ (import only), and call no private Study method. Import every band, restate none, and never loosen one: a 10 g C4 pair above 5 % is a finding — follow brief (6), never switch degree or mesh. Make no edit to the script after window 3 or to the guide after window 5. Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its cited gate-log line, the census before / after (dead list included), the elapsed times and the PNG size.

Review rulings (2026-10-08 18:00 review) on item 340 — these outrank the brief above. (1) Degree 1 at -n 2 as drafted; the guide states the 0.90× margin; no degree-2 rows. (2) Use an example-local REC dict with log:line comments, asserted at print precision (½ ulp of the printed digit), as EX-89 item 238 ruling Q1 did. (3) (iii) and (B2) stay in the gates — confirmed. (4) Keep the ball mask, labelled in the guide and XDMF as a picture, not the operator's quadrature ball. (5) EX-106 / mri:14 is correct; mri:15 is EX-107, mri:16 is EX-108. (6) The stale DRAFT comment at WF-16.md:519 was removed by this review.
