docs.title: §9 item 341 — 2026-10-08 (example; §5.4 ramp from WF-8)
docs.text:
Outcome (2026-10-09, 00:00 CDT slot, take-next): ✅ complete. Lift (_source_s(path=S4P), _source_slice(h5=H5, field=FIELD), _source_csv(column, path=CSV), bodies otherwise unchanged) re-gated 17 passed / 4 skipped, [wf8] and source sha256 lines identical to W0 (20261009T051030Z_EX-107-wf8-regate-W0.log, 78 s). Run of record 20261009T051318Z_EX-107.log (112 s) and control …051545Z_EX-107-control.log (110 s) green with equal integer readings: (S) 16 / 16, (X) 19 496 cells / 2 772 selected (display slab 2 772), (P) 41, (c1) [1] / [0] / [5], (c2) 3 / 2 772 / 40, (CLI) [0, 0, 0]. Regenerated .s4p / .h5 sha256s differ between the two windows (printed only). Census figures 102 → 103, docrefs dead=0 before and after. Disclosed: the first post-docrefs (…051749Z) read dead=3 on placeholder filenames in the guide's femem figure block; the guide was fixed and both post-censuses re-run on the final guide (…051759Z_EX-107-post-docrefs-2.log dead 0, …051828Z_EX-107-post-figures-2.log 103 / 103 / 0 / 0). Off rank 0 write_xdmf_with_tags returns (None, None), so the script names the XDMF / H5 paths itself.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §5.4 example ramp on a closed chunk (WF-8 ✅). No band, tolerance, record, Done-when or validation target is set or moved.

EX-107 (mri:15) adds examples/mri/15_figures_from_records.py and a same-stem guide examples/mri/15_figures_from_records.md. The guide carries the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step) plus ## Setup figure and ## Related. The setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB (scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py).

What the script shows, for the Phase 9 user who wants a picture of a Study output and needs to trust it: write the records, draw them, and prove the drawing is the record. One script writes the three kinds of record a Study user has, draws each through post.figures, reads every plotted array back from the figure object, and asserts it bitwise equal to the record parsed independently from disk. A planted 1e-6 change is caught at exactly one index.

Sources: the script writes its own (decided). The WF-8 gate reads four gitignored artifacts written by other examples (mri_11_…s4p, mri_10_…_combined.xdmf/.h5, materials_13_…_series.csv; paths and sha256 at 20261008T202057Z_WF-8-W0.log:85–88). An example must not do that. No example in examples/ reads another example's output: each script names only its own <group>_<NN>_<stem>_* files (checked at drafting with a grep over examples/**/*.py for <group>_NN_*.{s4p,csv,xdmf,h5}; every hit is the script's own stem). So mri:15 regenerates all three sources in-process, through the same gated fixtures those examples call, and writes them under its own stem: - (a) S, a three-frequency .s4p. study, _ = _port_study(1) (tests/package/test_wf16_study_sweep.py:112), sw = study.solve_sweep(tuple(FREQUENCIES.values()), comm) (FREQUENCIES from tests.validation.test_ans4_exact_strip_records), sw.write_touchstone(OUTPUT_DIR / "mri_15_figures_from_records.s4p"). This is mri:11's call sequence (examples/mri/11_study_frequency_sweep.py:106–109, 193–195). Use the sweep, never mri:8's single frequency: one point makes a degenerate plot against frequency (WF-8.md Sources (a)). - (b) SAR, a combined XDMF. study = _study(degree=1) (tests/package/test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere.py:111), res = study.solve(comm), th = study.temperature(RobinCooling(K, H, T_INF, source_scale=G)) (constants from tests.validation.test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere). Then the theta / SAR / q DG0 / P1 outputs exactly as mri:10 builds them (examples/mri/10_study_temperature.py:200–218), written by write_xdmf_with_tags(OUTPUT_DIR / "mri_15_figures_from_records_sar_combined", th.submesh, None, {...}, comm=comm). In the complex build DolfinX writes them as real_SAR / imag_SAR etc.; the slice reads real_SAR and the (c2) control reads real_q, as WF-8 did. - (c) A probe series CSV. run = _build_run() (tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py:178, the lifted fixture mat:13 calls). Rank 0 writes OUTPUT_DIR / "mri_15_figures_from_records_probe_series.csv" with header n,t_s,probe_c0_K,probe_c1_K,probe_c2_K and rows [n, f"{n * DT:.6f}", *(f"{np.real(run['s_cf'].values[n, j]):.9e}" for j in range(3))] for n in 0 … N_MAIN. That is mat:13's format for these columns (examples/materials/13_virtual_probe_in_gel_ball.py:353–370). Do not call _check_probe_series: it writes the gate's -n 2 npz (:88, :299). - After writing, rank 0 prints each file's path, byte size and sha256 (the WF-8 rule (i) audit trail). The sha256s are printed only; they are not compared with WF-8's, since the file names and columns differ. - Free each source's solver objects before the next build (del + gc.collect()). This is hygiene, not a gate.

Code. - Rule (a) lift, additive, disclosed (default; see Q2). In tests/post/test_wf8_figures.py, give the three independent source parsers a path keyword whose default is the module constant: _source_s(path=S4P) (:71), _source_slice(h5=H5, field=FIELD) (:78), _source_csv(column, path=CSV) (:88). The bodies are unchanged apart from reading the argument. Every test call stays as written, so the defaults reproduce today's behaviour. No assertion is added, removed or re-banded. The module is re-gated green (window 2) before the example is written. No src/ edit. - Imports (never restated). - From fem_em_solver.post.figures: plot_sparameters, plot_xdmf_slice, plot_probe_series, draw_sparameters, draw_slice, draw_series, select_slab, mismatch_indices. - From fem_em_solver.cli: main (for the femem figure leg). - From tests.post.test_wf8_figures: _source_s, _source_slice, _source_csv (lifted), _exact, _line_xy, _coll_values, _coll_xy, FIELD, COLUMN, WRONG_COLUMN. Importing the module is safe: its fixtures are pytest-decorated and do not run on import. It imports tests.unit.test_doc_reference_exit_codes (stdlib only). - The source fixtures and constants named in (a)–(c), plus N_MAIN, DT from the MAT-19 module. - From src: RobinCooling, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership, write_setup_figure. - Cited inputs (not records or bands; the EX-101 ruling (3) precedent): the plant indices [1, 0, 0] for S (test_wf8_figures.py:143) and 5 for the probe (:223); the slice plant rule "first non-zero selected value" (:182); the factor 1.0 + 1e-6; the wrong-field name "real_q" (:193). Each carries a comment citing its line. - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (10_study_temperature.py:54–56), so tests.* imports work with the runner's PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src. Never import another example's module. - Style: default only. No colour map, font, dpi or layout argument is added, and figures.py is not edited. Style stays the operator's choice (dashboard item 12).

Order of calls. Complex-build guard (raise in a real build, mat:13's check at :160–165) → (a) → (b) → setup figure → (c) → prints of the source audit → the three plot_* calls into OUTPUT_DIR → (S) / (X) / (P) read-backs → (c1) / (c2) controls → the femem figure leg → (F) → final asserts. Every assert runs on every rank on a boolean that rank 0 computed and broadcast (comm.bcast, the test's _all pattern).

(1) Anchor (asserted; all exact, no tolerance exists). The WF-8 Done-when's identity, on the example's own records: - (S) For each of the 16 (i, j): the |S| and arg S lines' get_xdata(orig=True) / get_ydata(orig=True) are _exact (float64 on both sides and np.array_equal) to _source_s(path).f / .s_mag[:, i, j] / .s_deg[:, i, j]. Assert 4 ports, 3 frequencies, and the count 16 / 16. Record on WF-8's source: 16 / 16 at [1e7, 6.4e7, 1.28e8] Hz (20261008T202057Z_WF-8-W0.log:90–91). - (X) plot_xdmf_slice(xdmf, FIELD, out, axis="z"): _coll_values(res.collection) is _exact to val[idx], and _coll_xy(res.collection) to cent[idx][:, :2], where (cent, val) = _source_slice(h5, FIELD) (h5py + vertex mean, independent of the plotter's reader) and idx = res.indices. Also assert len(idx) > 0. Predicted, printed: 19 496 cells and 2 772 selected, WF-8's counts (WF-8.md outcome). This is the same _study(degree=1) sphere submesh mri:10 writes, meshed serially, so the counts should repeat as integers. - (P) plot_probe_series(csv, COLUMN, out): the line's x / y are _exact to _source_csv(COLUMN, path), a csv + float parse. Printed: 41 rows (N_MAIN + 1). - (F) On rank 0, the three PNGs exist with size > 0; every other rank's plot_* returned None. The boolean is broadcast. - (CLI) main(["figure", kind, src, out, *extra]) for sparams / slice --name real_SAR / probe --column probe_c0_K returns [0, 0, 0] on every rank, and rank 0's three …_cli_<kind>.png files are non-empty. This is the test's (CLI) leg (test_wf8_figures.py:252–269) on this example's sources.

(2) Negative controls (asserted; rule (e)). - (c1) A planted 1e-6 change is caught at exactly one index, per figure. draw_* is fed a copy with one value multiplied by (1 + 1e-6). mismatch_indices(plotted, true_source) must equal exactly [1] (S, mag[1, 0, 0]), [k] (slice, k the first non-zero selected value) and [5] (probe). Backing, WF-8's same comparison: [1] / [0] / [5] (WF-8.md outcome). Ceiling: a single plant can produce at most one mismatching index, so [k] is both floor and ceiling. A blind comparator (array_equal(x, x) on the figure's own data) returns []. - (c2) A wrong column is caught. S12 is drawn under the S11 label, real_q stands in for real_SAR, and WRONG_COLUMN (probe_c1_K) for probe_c0_K. Each must give mismatch_indices(...).size > 0. Predicted 3 / 2 772 / 40 (WF-8.md outcome; the probe's row 0 is 0 in both columns, hence 40 of 41). No factor is asserted, since no ceiling applies beyond "all".

Printed, not asserted: each source's path, bytes and sha256; frequencies; cells and slab count with the first five slab indices; rows; the (c1) / (c2) indices and counts; the three PNG sizes; wall time per source build.

(3) Tier, ranks, cost. - Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents. - Build: complex. The mri: group sources /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode automatically (scripts/run_examples.sh:273–275). All three source fixtures need it (mri:10, mri:11 and mat:13 all ran complex). The plotting itself is build-independent: WF-8's W0 ran real, on files the complex build wrote. - Tier: heavy, by ceiling. -n 2 for the run of record and the control. That is the width of mri:11's records (ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH) and of the MAT-19 fixture. Runner -t 300; container timeout -k 30 300. - Price basis. The example window is predicted ≈ 125 s, range [95, 210]. The upper end is over the standard 180 s ceiling, so the tier is heavy: - mri:11's solve_sweep 53.66 s (mesh 27.73 s; 20261007T095449Z_EX-95-control.log:1937; wall 65 s, :1957); - mri:10's EM solve + mesh 14.7 s plus temperature() 0.48 s (20261007T094905Z_EX-94-control.log:108; wall 19 s, :123); - mat:13's fixture 34.3 s (20261005T201654Z_EX-90-control.log:202; wall 79 s, :208); - plus ≈ 8 s startup, ≈ 5 s of writes, ≈ 8 s for six plot_* / CLI figures and six control draws, and ≈ 5 s for the setup figure (flagged only). - Re-gate W0: reproduces WF-8 W0, 72 s (20261008T202057Z_WF-8-W0.log), predicted [50, 150] s, standard. - Cost: ≈ 13 measured (example class median) / ≈ 50 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 25 script and guide + ≈ 10 windows (the W0 re-gate ≈ 1.5 min, two example windows ≈ 2 min each, plus a dry run, four censuses, orphan check and sweep ≈ 2 min). - Depends on: nothing open. WF-8 is ✅ on main; mri:10, mri:11 and mat:13 are ✅ examples, but only their gate fixtures are imported, never their outputs or modules. Never beside another heavy window. - Numbering. examples/mri/ holds 01_ … 13_ on main. This item writes 15_ as assigned; 14_ is left to the sibling item that claims it. run_examples.sh discovers mri: scripts by number, so no registry edit is needed. If 15_ is taken when the slot starts, use the next free number and note it. - Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-107, §9 item 341 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-107.md, heading §9 item 341). You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained; the harness call is the whole Bash command, nothing piped or redirected. The only code edit outside examples/ is the rule (a) path-keyword lift in tests/post/test_wf8_figures.py; do not edit src/ (in particular not post/figures.py's style). Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window. Return the window logs, every asserted and printed value beside its WF-8 record or prediction, the census before / after, and the disclosed lift diff."

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. 0. Orphan check from a bare shell: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Then the rubric's cache sweep (docs/automation/daily-review.md:426) as one bare call labelled EX-107-cache-sweep. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written (the commands of 20261008T172115Z_EX-89-item332-pre-figures.log:12 and 20261008T172117Z_EX-89-item332-pre-docrefs.log:12): - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-107-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-107-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - At drafting: examples=98 ok=98 missing=0 broken=0 (…pre-figures.log:134) and dead=2 guide=0 stale=56 exit=1 (…pre-docrefs.log:98). The two dead references come from an unrelated, pre-existing entry. Use whatever the pre-census reads, and record the dead entries' names. 2. Lift, then re-gate W0 (predicted 17 passed / 4 skipped, [50, 150] s): WF-8 W0's command (20261008T202057Z_WF-8-W0.log:12) under a new label: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-107-wf8-regate-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/post/test_wf8_figures.py -v -s --tb=short'" Every [wf8] line must equal W0's, times excepted. The four source sha256 lines must equal W0's too. If they differ, someone regenerated a source: report it, but it is not a red while every test passes. 3. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-107-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:15 -n 2 -t 300 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 4. Run of record (flagged), -n 2, predicted ≈ 125 s, range [95, 210]: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-107 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/15_figures_from_records.py"' This is the dry run's emitted line with -T and the flag added (the EX-94 / EX-95 run-of-record form). Note any other difference. 5. Control, unflagged: git add the setup PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-107-control. Every assertion must be green. The integer readings (16 / 16, cells, slab count, rows, (c1) indices, (c2) counts) must equal window 4's. Whether the regenerated sources' sha256s repeat between the two windows is a printed reading, with no status effect. 6. Post-censuses, after the guide is final: EX-107-post-figures / EX-107-post-docrefs (window 1's commands with these labels). Write the prediction first: figures examples N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0. Docrefs: runnable +1, guide=0, and no new dead reference — dead and the dead entries' names are unchanged from window 1. exit stays whatever the unrelated entry makes it (1 at drafting). 7. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only examples/mri/15_figures_from_records.py, .md and examples/mri/figures/mri_15_figures_from_records_setup.png. tests/post/test_wf8_figures.py is the only other modified code path. Generated sources and PNGs under examples/mri/paraview_output/ are gitignored and never committed.

Output. - Sources (gitignored, examples/mri/paraview_output/): mri_15_figures_from_records.s4p, mri_15_figures_from_records_sar_combined.xdmf + .h5, mri_15_figures_from_records_probe_series.csv. - Figures (gitignored, same directory): mri_15_figures_from_records_sparams.png, …_slice.png, …_probe.png, and the CLI's …_cli_sparams.png, …_cli_slice.png, …_cli_probe.png. adopt_host_ownership(OUTPUT_DIR, comm=comm) runs after the writes. - Setup figure (tracked): examples/mri/figures/mri_15_figures_from_records_setup.png, through write_setup_figure, on th.submesh, with a display-only meshtags that is never asserted on (the EX-102 ruling (2) precedent): - tag 2 marks the cells whose centroid lies in the slab the slice figure draws; tag 1 marks the rest; - the slab centre and half-width come from the global centroid z min / max (MPI.MIN / MPI.MAX allreduce), passed explicitly to select_slab on the local centroids. These are select_slab's own defaults (mid-plane, 5 % of the range) made global; - region_names={1: "gel sphere (SAR source)", 2: "slab drawn by the slice figure"}, translucent_tags=(1,), slice_normal=(0, 1, 0) through the origin; - title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. mri:15 -- the slice figure is a selection: sphere cells on the z mid-plane slab (WF-8). If over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Print the display slab's owned-cell count (allreduced) beside (X)'s len(idx), predicted equal; printed only. - Guide. - The recipe in three calls: write with Study (write_touchstone, write_xdmf_with_tags, a CSV), then plot_sparameters(path, out) / plot_xdmf_slice(xdmf, "real_SAR", out, axis="z") / plot_probe_series(csv, "probe_c0_K", out), or the same through femem figure sparams|slice|probe <source> <out> [--name …|--column …]. - Three reading rules: - the S figure is linear |S| and degrees exactly as scikit-rf gives them: no dB, no unwrap; - the slice is a selection, not an interpolation: each dot is one cell at its centroid, coloured by that cell's stored value. A smoother picture would no longer be the record; - a complex-build XDMF stores real_<name> / imag_<name>, so ask for real_SAR. - How a reader checks a figure themselves: the three read-back calls (get_xdata(orig=True), get_array().data, get_offsets()) and mismatch_indices, with the (c1) result as the worked example. - A ParaView recipe: open mri_15_figures_from_records_sar_combined.xdmf, colour by real_SAR, Clip to a z slab about the mid-plane, compare it with …_slice.png. Whether ParaView opens it stays the operator's check, as in WF-8. - The scope sentences below. - ## Related, every artifact by full filename (rule (b)): examples/mri/10_study_temperature.md, examples/mri/11_study_frequency_sweep.md, examples/materials/13_virtual_probe_in_gel_ball.md, tests/post/test_wf8_figures.py, src/fem_em_solver/post/figures.py, src/fem_em_solver/cli.py.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Never interpolate onto a plane in the slice: bitwise breaks by construction (WF-8.md Sources (b)). Never add 20*log10, an unwrap or a cast to S. - Read-back calls: get_ydata() without orig=True may return a converted copy; get_array() is a masked array, so assert no mask and compare .data (the imported _coll_values does). Pass float64 ndarrays, not lists (WF-8.md traps). - Rank safety: only rank 0 reads files and draws; plot_* returns None elsewhere and every rank passes the Barrier inside. Compute verdicts on rank 0, bcast them, assert on every rank. Every allreduce (the slab extent, the display count) stays outside any rank == 0 branch (item 227's deadlock). The CSV is written on rank 0 only, then a comm.Barrier() before any rank reads or plots it. - _check_probe_series is never called: it writes /workspace/logs/mat19/step1-n2.npz (test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py:88, 299). _build_run() alone writes nothing. - Plants on non-zero values only. The probe's row 0 is exactly 0 (MAT-19 (A0)), so a plant there is a no-op; the cited index 5 and the slice's first-non-zero rule avoid it. - Root-owned outputs: container writes are root-owned on the host; adopt_host_ownership after the writes (WF-8 item 274 trap). Never commit a generated figure or source. - Complex-build UFL: the script adds no UFL comparison. sar_out / q_out take np.real of the arrays, as mri:10 does (OPS-22). - Bare harness calls only: no cd … &&, no ; date / | tail, no redirect (bash_guard.py). The orphan check needs -f docker/docker-compose.yml. A docker-socket denial means stop and report. Status 124 is a finding, never a retry, and never a longer timeout. - Docrefs: name no scratch path in guide prose (EX-97.md:149). The pre-existing dead=2 must not be "fixed" in this item. - Rule (i): the test module is frozen once window 2 starts, the script once window 4 starts, and the guide before window 6. Write ≈, never a tilde.

(5) Scope. - Covered: the three post.figures kinds and femem figure on records the script writes itself (a degree-1 three-frequency F-small .s4p, the degree-1 SAR-heated sphere XDMF, the MAT-19 probe series), with the bitwise read-back identity and the (c1) / (c2) controls, in the complex build at -n 2. - Not claimed: - that the sources are correct. They are records of other gates (WF-16 / PORT-11 through mri:11, WF-15 / MAT-10 through mri:10, MAT-19 through mat:13), none re-asserted here; - any S, SAR or temperature accuracy statement; resonance or tuning; degree 2; - a |B₁⁺| slice or an interpolated slice; style, colour maps or publication quality (the operator's, dashboard item 12); interactive viewing; a gallery; - ParaView opening the XDMF (the operator's check); - anything WF-8 does not claim.

(6) Negative result. Report the measurement and stop; never relax a bitwise check to allclose. Journal in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-107-<UTC>, and mark item 341 BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)). EX-107 stays ⬜. What each miss means: - Re-gate W0 red, or its [wf8] lines off W0's: the lift disturbed the gate. Revert it, mark BLOCKED, and write a known-issues entry. - (S) / (X) / (P) bitwise miss in the example with W0 green: the plotter transforms this source and not WF-8's, an example/test divergence finding. Print the first mismatching index, both values and both dtypes, write a known-issues entry and a §7 annotation on WF-8 for the review, and stop. Never patch figures.py from this item. - (c1) ≠ exactly one index, or (c2) size 0: the comparator is blind on this source. Stop and report. - A source build fails (sweep, sphere or MAT-19 fixture): that is a regression under a ✅ example's fixture, not this item's red. Record it verbatim, check orphans, and stop. - Over 300 s, or Status 124: check orphans (pgrep -c python3 reads 0), sweep only then, park, and let the review re-tier. Never lengthen the timeout or drop a source. - A printed prediction missed (2 772, 40, the display count): report it, with no status effect.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-107 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). Census examples +1 (98 → 99 at drafting) with broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, guide=0, no new dead reference. The review adds the §7 row in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). WF-8 stays ✅; its §7 state gains nothing beyond an optional "example: mri:15 (EX-107)" pointer. Phase 9 (9d)'s "tutorials drawn from examples/" gains its first figures tutorial, and the first example that uses post.figures.

Review rulings (2026-10-08 18:00 review) on item 341 — these outrank the brief above. (1) mri:15 stands (mri:14 is EX-106). (2) The path-keyword lift on _source_s / _source_slice / _source_csv (defaulting to today's constants), with the ≈ 72 s WF-8 W0 re-gate in the same slot — standing rule (a); no copied comparators. (3) In-script regeneration is confirmed: no example reads another's outputs. (4) The setup figure with display-only slab tags is accepted (EX-102 ruling (2)). (5) "No new dead reference" means the dead count and the dead entries' names equal the pre-census. (6) The plant indices and "real_q" as cited literals are accepted (EX-101 ruling (3)).

docs.title: EX-108 — mri:16, the Study on a copper birdcage
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened 2026-10-08 by the 18:00 daily review (step 5, §5.4 ramp). The base is WF-16 step 7 (§9 item 324, DONE 2026-10-08, df25001f; docs/planning/chunks/WF-16.md:559–591). It added LeontovichWall and FourPortBirdcageGeometry(as_hole=True, strip_fraction=…) to the Study API, gated by tests/package/test_wf16_study_copper.py.

No example runs a copper coil through the Study API. Checked at drafting: - ports:18 (examples/ports/18_birdcage_copper_leontovich.py, EX-59) is copper, but it drives the solver directly (_sheets_build, _build_ports, run_n_port_sparameter_sweep) on the ragged port sheet at 10 MHz. - mri:8 (examples/mri/08_study_four_port_birdcage.py, EX-92) is the Study on the σ = 800 S/m solid conductor. - mri:6 is the F-human copper loss partition, also off the API.

The angle: the same F-small birdcage on exact rectangles, κ off, through the Study API twice — once on copper, once on PEC — in a few lines of user code. The example then reads the loss partition (sheets / phantom / copper) of the copper Study and shows where on the coil the copper loss sits.

Outcome (2026-10-09, 00:00 CDT slot, take-next): ✅ complete. Run of record 20261009T052039Z_EX-108.log (76 s) and control …052203Z_EX-108-control.log (75 s) green. No dry-run harness log was written (the dry run is host-side; the run-of-record line is the brief's form). Rule (i): script 05:20:35Z < run 05:20:39Z; guide 05:23:52Z < post-censuses 05:23:56Z.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §5.4 example ramp on a closed step (WF-16 step 7, §9 item 324). No band, tolerance, record, Done-when or validation target is set or moved. Every band, record and helper is imported by name.

EX-108 (mri:16) adds examples/mri/16_study_copper_birdcage.py and the same-stem guide 16_study_copper_birdcage.md. The guide carries the three required headings (## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step) plus ## Setup figure and ## Related. The setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB (scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py:124).

Numbering. examples/mri/ holds 01_ … 13_ at drafting. This item writes 16_ only, as the review assigned (14_ / 15_ are left to the review's other items). run_examples.sh auto-discovers by number, so no registry edit is needed. If mri:16 is taken when the slot starts, use the next free number and note it. The script imports nothing from examples/.

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor is the executor: it does not spawn agents.
  • Build: complex. The mri: group sources it automatically (scripts/run_examples.sh:273). The gate window ran complex (20261008T190119Z_WF-16-s7-W1.log:12).
  • Tier: standard, -n 2, degree 1, 64 MHz. -n 2 is the record's width (ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, tests/validation/test_ans6_exact_strip.py:144). Runner -t 300; container timeout -k 30 300.
  • Cost: ≈ 13 measured (example class median) / ≈ 40 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 15 script and guide + ≈ 10 windows (two ≈ 1.5 min example windows, a dry run, four census windows).
  • Depends on: nothing open. WF-16 step 7 is on main (item 324, df25001f).
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-108, §9 item 342 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-108.md, heading §9 item 342). You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window."

What the user code looks like. The guide's section 1 shows these lines, and the script uses them as written:

phantom = GelledSalinePhantomMaterial(SALINE_SIGMA, SALINE_EPSILON_R, FREQUENCY_64_HZ)
geometry = FourPortBirdcageGeometry(as_hole=True, strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION)
cu = Study(geometry, phantom, LumpedPortDrive(), frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_64_HZ,
           degree=1, conductor=LeontovichWall(COPPER_SIGMA)).solve(comm)
pec = Study(geometry, phantom, LumpedPortDrive(), frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_64_HZ,
            degree=1, conductor=None).solve(comm)

Build a fresh geometry per Study, as the gate's _geometry() does (test_wf16_study_copper.py:80–81).

Imports (never restated). - From fem_em_solver: FourPortBirdcageGeometry, LeontovichWall, LumpedPortDrive, Study. From fem_em_solver.study: GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION, COPPER_SIGMA, and _conductor_setup (for (c2) only). From fem_em_solver.materials: GelledSalinePhantomMaterial. From fem_em_solver.ports.lumped: run_lumped_sheet_port_case. From fem_em_solver.io.mesh: BIRDCAGE_CONDUCTOR_SURFACE_TAG. From fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils: write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership. From fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure: write_setup_figure. - From the gate module tests.package.test_wf16_study_copper (unedited): - KEY (:65), NEGATIVE_CONTROL_FLOOR (:68); - helpers _rel_means (:76) and _identity (:84–110). - _identity re-runs the P1 field solve with the Study's own conductor_terms and returns the power dict. The example calls it unchanged, so the partition it prints is the gate's computation. - Through the gate module's own imports, re-imported from their defining modules: - tests.validation.test_ans6_exact_strip: ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, CLASSES, _class_means; - tests.validation.test_birdcage_power_identity: DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL; - tests.validation.test_lossy_sphere_fullwave: FREQUENCY_64_HZ, SALINE_EPSILON_R, SALINE_SIGMA; - tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_four_port: LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND, PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE; - tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_lumped_column: ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG; - tests.validation.test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep: RECIPROCITY_BAND; - tests.validation.test_th14_birdcage_copper as th14: th14.DRIVEN, th14.FREQUENCIES_HZ, th14._sweep_record. - Assert by import, as the gate does (:152–157): fem_em_solver.study.GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION == tests.validation.test_port_lumped_narrowed_sheet.GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION and COPPER_SIGMA == th14.COPPER_SIGMA. - No new number. The script states no band, record, σ, frequency, power or cell count as a literal. Default: no gate-module edit. If an import fails, stop and report; never lift or edit a gate module in this item.

Order of calls in the script. All on every rank; prints under rank == 0 with no collective inside (item 227's deadlock). 1. (W), then the two import-equality asserts, then (c2) (no mesh). 2. The copper Study: solve(comm). 3. The setup figure, from cu.mesh / cu.cell_tags (a no-op unless FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1). 4. The PEC Study: solve(comm). 5. power = _identity(cu, study_cu.omega, comm). 6. One more P1 field solve for the XDMF: run_lumped_sheet_port_case(cu.problem, cu.port_definitions, cu.specs, facet_tags=cu.facet_tags, driven_port_id=th14.DRIVEN, verbose=False, return_fields=True, extra_bilinear_terms=cu.conductor_terms, degree=cu.degree). This is _identity's own call (:85–88) repeated, because _identity returns no field. 7. Fields and the XDMF, then prints, then asserts.

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script, -n 2). Every record is from 20261008T190119Z_WF-16-s7-W1.log (Status 0, 13 passed, 69 s, :1841–1848). - (W) width: comm.size == ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH before any comparison. - (M) mesh: cu.cells == pec.cells == ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD (80 798; :943, :1821). Equality, as the gate asserts (:169–171). - (R) records: _rel_means(_class_means(cu.s_matrix), ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1[KEY]["cu"]) ≤ LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND per class, and the same for pec against ["pec"]. - Records: Cu 4.093e-11 / 8.673e-11 / 1.376e-10 (:1824); PEC 5.052e-11 / 3.878e-11 / 5.875e-11 (:1825). - Print the 10-digit class means as the gate does (:944, :1822). - (b) the copper power identity: on power, p_surf > 0 and residual ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. Record: p_surf 1.5168731494522984e-06 W, residual 8.507e-13 (:1823). - (g) TH-14's gates, both columns: th14._sweep_record(res.sweep); reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND, max(sigma) ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, every spread ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (the gate's :198–203). The gate log does not print these values, so print them as new readings, with no record to compare. - (L) the copper loss on the coil adds up: the DG0 field coil_surface_loss_per_cell_W (see Output) summed over owned dofs and allreduced equals power["p_surf"] within DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL relative. - This is a consistency check by construction (DG0 partition of unity, the ports:18 precedent, examples/ports/18_birdcage_copper_leontovich.py:157–183), on a second solve of the same system. - Predicted ≤ 1e-12. It is not a physics claim.

The loss partition (printed, not asserted; no gate band exists). From power: - p_src, p_sheets, p_phantom, p_non_phantom, p_surf; - P_in = p_src − p_sheets, P_coil/P_in = p_surf / P_in, and P_phantom/P_in.

Predicted from :1823: - P_in 3.386923e-06 W; - P_coil/P_in 0.4478617, equal to ANS-6 step 4's 64 MHz exact-route reading 20261003T095650Z_ANS-6-item193-W2-solve.log:3094 (P_coil/P_in 0.4478617, same definition p_surf / (p_src − p_sheets), test_ans6_exact_strip.py:532–533); - P_phantom/P_in 0.5521383; - p_non_phantom 0.0 (the hole route has no conductor cells, and the air is lossless).

The guide reads the result as: on this fixture, at 64 MHz, copper takes ≈ 45 % of the power delivered past the port sheets, and the gel takes ≈ 55 %. It says that ANS-6 checked this partition externally (public verdict AGREE, no number) and that it is a model reading on one fixture at degree 1, not an accuracy figure.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) asserted — the PEC Study cannot stand in for copper. _rel_means(_class_means(pec.s_matrix), ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1[KEY]["cu"]) > NEGATIVE_CONTROL_FLOOR per class (the gate's :183–186). - Backing: the gate log prints the related gap |cu − pec|/|pec|: 6.420e-04 / 2.811e-04 / 4.861e-04 (20261008T190119Z_WF-16-s7-W1.log:1826). The registered columns behind it are 20261003T095650Z_ANS-6-item193-W2-solve.log:3095–3096. Lines :3090–3092 are the 10 MHz rows, not the 64 MHz ones. - The asserted expression is relative to the Cu record, not to the PEC means. The two differ by a factor 1 + O(6e-4), so the example prints both: - the gate's form, to compare with :1826 digit for digit; - the asserted form, predicted equal to it at 3 significant figures. - Ceiling / separation: the floor is 1e-5. The measured gap is ≥ 2.8e-4 (28× the floor), and ≥ 2.8e5× LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. The ceiling is the physical Cu − PEC difference itself, so no factor is asserted beyond the gate's floor. - (c2) asserted — the API refuses copper on a solid conductor. _conductor_setup(Study(FourPortBirdcageGeometry(), phantom, LumpedPortDrive(), frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_64_HZ, conductor=LeontovichWall()), {}, comm) raises ValueError matching as_hole, on every rank, before any mesh. This is the gate's test_leontovich_needs_hole_route (:160–165). A deterministic raise, no factor. The guide states it as the user rule: copper needs the hole geometry.

Flag versus control. The mri:8 pattern (EX-92): - the run of record is flagged (FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, it writes the PNG); - the control is the same line unflagged, after git add of the PNG.

The executor compares the two logs at the band, never bitwise: - (M) as integers; - (R), (b), (g), (L) and (c1) each on the right side of its imported band or floor at both runs; - the loss partition ratios equal to 7 significant digits (printed, predicted).

The flagged run's printed rows must also equal the gate log's (:943–944, :1821–1826) at the printed digits, except times. A mismatch with every assertion green is reported, not a stop.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. Nothing is chained or piped. Never beside another heavy window. 0. Orphan check: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written (the headers of 20261008T172115Z_EX-89-item332-pre-figures.log:12 and 20261008T172117Z_EX-89-item332-pre-docrefs.log:12): - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-108-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-108-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - At drafting: figures examples=98 ok=98 missing=0 broken=0. Docrefs dead=2 guide=0 stale=56 exit=1, where both dead entries are examples/ansys_benchmarks/ans9_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz/SPEC.md:36, :38 (ans9_aed_results.json, ans9_corrected_rows.json; …pre-docrefs.log:36–38), unrelated to this item. Use whatever the pre-census reads. 2. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-108-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:16 -n 2 -t 300 --dry-run". It must print (complex build) (run_examples.sh:281). Pass the emitted docker line to the harness as its own call (run_examples.sh is host-side). 3. Run of record (flagged), -n 2. - Predicted ≈ 85 s, range [65, 160]. - Basis: the gate's W1 took 69 s: Cu Study 31.8 s (mesh 22.3 s), PEC Study 28.9 s, identity solve 4.6 s (:943, :1821, :1823). The example adds one field solve (≈ 5 s), the XDMF (≈ 3 s) and the figure (≈ 6 s: mri:8 flagged 51 s against unflagged 45 s, 20261007T094132Z_EX-92.log:1900, 20261007T094301Z_EX-92-control.log:1893). - Command (the EX-92 run-of-record form, 20261007T094132Z_EX-92.log:12; take the dry-run's line and add the flag): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-108 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/16_study_copper_birdcage.py"' - The script reaches tests.* by inserting the repo root into sys.path, as mri:8 does (08_study_four_port_birdcage.py:56–58), so PYTHONPATH stays the dry run's /workspace/src. The only difference from the dry-run line is the -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 flag; note any other. 4. Control, unflagged: git add the PNG first. Then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-108-control. Predicted ≈ 78 s, range [60, 150]. 5. Guide, written from the run-of-record log before the post-censuses. Rule (i): no script edit after window 3, and no guide edit after window 6. 6. Post-censuses: EX-108-post-figures / EX-108-post-docrefs, the window 1 commands with those labels. Write the prediction first: - figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, missing=0, broken=0; - docrefs: runnable +1, guide=0, no new dead reference (the dead list is the pre-census list, name for name). exit=1 is expected while the two ans9 entries stand.

Output. - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_16_study_copper_birdcage_combined.xdmf, written with write_xdmf_with_tags(…, cu.mesh, cu.cell_tags, {...}, facet_tags=cu.conductor_facet_tags, comm=comm). cu.conductor_facet_tags is the mesh facet tag set that carries tag 401 (study.py:526). Then call adopt_host_ownership. Fields, real-valued, set on owned dofs and scattered: - E_abs: |E| of the copper Study's P1 drive, interpolated to P1 Lagrange (the mri:8 pattern, 08_study_four_port_birdcage.py:213–219); - coil_surface_loss_per_cell_W: DG0, ½Re(1/Z_s)|n×E|² over tag BIRDCAGE_CONDUCTOR_SURFACE_TAG with a DG0 test function inserted (the ports:18 helper, 18_birdcage_copper_leontovich.py:157–183, rewritten in the script with a comment citing it; examples never import each other). - Z_s = LeontovichWall(COPPER_SIGMA).surface_impedance_ohm(study_cu.omega). - It is the facet-integrated loss per adjacent cell, in watts, not a density; the field name, the print and the guide all say so. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_16_study_copper_birdcage_setup.png from the copper Study's mesh. - Region names: PHANTOM_CELL_TAG "gel phantom" (translucent), with the air tags hidden and labelled "air (outer box PEC)". - Build the air tags as mri:8 does: every reduced cell tag that is not the phantom (08_…py:127–136). The hole route has no conductor cells, so the coil is the empty cavity. - slice_normal=(0, 0, 1) through the origin. - Title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. mri:16 -- Study on the copper F-small birdcage: Leontovich wall on the coil hole (WF-16 step 7, degree 1). - The guide says the coil is drawn as a void, because the renderer takes cell tags only and the copper is a facet condition on tag 401. The port sheets are facet tags and are not drawn either. - Guide. - The Study lines above. - The rule: a LeontovichWall needs as_hole=True, and (c2) shows the refusal. - A table of copper against PEC class means (10 digits) with the record gaps. - The loss partition table, quoted from the run's own log with log:line. - Reading rules: - the Cu − PEC S shift is ≈ 3e-4 to 6e-4 relative at 64 MHz on this fixture, so S alone barely shows copper. The loss partition shows it: ≈ 45 % of the delivered power; - (L) proves the per-cell field is the same p_surf, not a different estimator. - ParaView: open the combined XDMF; select the facet block, Threshold tag 401, and colour coil_surface_loss_per_cell_W on a log scale to see where on the legs and rings the copper loss concentrates; slice E_abs through z = 0. - Scope sentences (below). - ## Related, every artifact by full repo-relative filename (rule (b)): - examples/mri/08_study_four_port_birdcage.md (the same fixture on the σ = 800 S/m solid conductor); - examples/ports/18_birdcage_copper_leontovich.md (copper off the API, ragged sheet, 10 MHz); - examples/mri/06_f_human_copper_loss_partition.md; - tests/package/test_wf16_study_copper.py, tests/validation/test_ans6_exact_strip.py, tests/validation/test_th14_birdcage_copper.py; - src/fem_em_solver/study.py.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Complex build only; the runner sources it for mri:. Never set any FEM_EM_ANS6_* / FEM_EM_EXACT_ANS6* variable (item 324 trap: ans:7's main() refuses them), and do not run ans:6 / ans:7. - Rank-local quantities: cell_tags.values, assemble_scalar and local DG0 sums. _identity reduces its own powers. (L)'s owned sum uses index_map.size_local and allreduce. Gather the setup-figure tag set with allgather as mri:8 does. - Collectives on every rank: both solves, _identity, run_lumped_sheet_port_case, fem.assemble_vector, write_xdmf_with_tags, write_setup_figure. (c2)'s raise is caught on every rank, never under rank == 0. - The DG0 loss form in complex mode needs ufl.conj(v) on the test function (18_…py:173). No ufl.max_value or comparison on complex operands; take np.real after assembly. - -k 30 on every container timeout. Status 124 is a finding: check orphans, then stop; never lengthen the timeout. - Cache sweep only at pgrep -c python3 = 0, as one bare call (daily-review.md rubric (4)), labelled EX-108-cache-sweep. Never clear the cache wholesale. - Bare harness calls: cd … &&, ; date, | tail and redirects are denied by bash_guard.py. The orphan check from a bare shell needs -f docker/docker-compose.yml. A docker-socket denial means stop and report (the EX-89 item 332 post-figures precedent). - Docrefs: name no scratch path in guide prose (EX-93's first post-docrefs exited 1 on a bare filename). Write every artifact by full repo-relative filename. - No AED value anywhere (the ANS-6 partition verdict is quoted as AGREE only). Write ≈, never a tilde.

(5) Scope. - Covered: the F-small four-port birdcage on exact rectangles, κ off, hole route, 80 798 cells, degree 1, 64 MHz, -n 2, through the Study API on copper (Leontovich, σ = COPPER_SIGMA) and PEC. - (R) both columns against ANS-6 step 4's registered means; - the copper power identity and TH-14's gates; - the per-cell copper loss field summing to p_surf; - the PEC control and the solid-conductor refusal. - Not claimed: - an absolute S₁₁ / Z_in, a resonance, tuning or Q figure (ANS-6 / ANS-7 stay 🟡); - degree 2 (the _P2 record at -n 8), 10 / 128 MHz, F-human (U27), κ; - an accuracy statement on the copper loss: the partition is a model reading on one fixture at degree 1, and its external check is ANS-6's verdict, not this example's; - a surface loss density; - anything WF-16 step 7 does not claim.

(6) Negative result. If (W), (M), (R), (b), (g), (L), (c1) or (c2) misses, or a window hangs: - report the measurement and stop; - journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-108-<UTC>, and mark item 342 BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)); - leave EX-108 ⬜. Never widen a band, edit src/ or a gate module, or re-record a constant.

What each miss means: - (M), (R), (b), (g) or (c1) red through the example path: contradicts WF-16 step 7's green W1 at the same width. That is an example/test divergence finding: a known-issues entry and a §7 annotation on WF-16 for the review, not an example fix. - (R) missing by ≈ 1e-13 with (b) and (g) green: not possible through _identity's path (the γ literal was ruled in 324-3). Report it. - (L) red with (b) green: the example's DG0 form differs from th14._surface_loss_w (test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:174–182). That is an example defect: fix the form only if the cause is shown, before any window of record. Otherwise park. - (c2) does not raise: a study.py _conductor_setup regression; stop and report. - Cells ≠ 80 798 with an image change: a mesher-version event (rule (1*)) for record-reconciler. Stop.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. A new §7 row EX-108 (the review adds it in the same commit as this item, rule (j)) moves ⬜ → ✅: Done-when met, elapsed recorded. - Census examples +1 (98 → 99 at drafting), broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, guide=0, no new dead reference. - It is the first example of a copper coil through the Study API. - Phase 9 (9d), "tutorials drawn from examples/", gains the copper-Study tutorial; §10 chain U's U26 gains its example. - WF-16, ANS-6 and TH-14 do not move.

Review rulings (2026-10-08 18:00 review) on item 342 — these outrank the brief above. (1) mri:16 stands (mri:14 / mri:15 are EX-106 / EX-107). (2) Drop (c2): the example stays on the public API; (c1) is the control. (3) Keep (L) asserted with the extra ≈ 5 s P1 solve; no rule (a) lift. (4) The (g) values are new printed readings with no log record to match — print them, compare nothing. (5) The partition wording is acceptable as "on this fixture, at degree 1 — a record; ANS-6 stays 🟡". The backing-line correction (…item193-W2-solve.log:3095–3096, 64 MHz) and the asserted-vs-logged control form are accepted as drafted.

docs.title: EX-109 — history
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row in PROJECT_PLAN.md §7 is the status of record.

Opened by the 2026-10-10 18:00 daily review (daily-review.md step 5, the §5.4 example ramp) from H9′'s landed gates: WF-10 step 2 part 1 (§9 item 358, |B₁⁺|, mirror and power identities) and part 2 (§9 item 359, the 10 g hotspot), both DONE green on 2026-10-10. WF-10 itself holds 🟡 under rule (j) (step 1d BLOCKED; step 2's C16 wording awaits the weekly), so this chunk is named for the weekly to ratify; it moves no WF-10 status.

Gap. No example shows a tuned coil at human scale: - mri:4 (examples/mri/04_f_human_sar10g_hotspot.py, EX-62) is WF-7's untuned σ = 800 S/m solid coil, 32 × 50 Ω, refined phantom, 32-port quadrature; - mri:6 (examples/mri/06_f_human_copper_loss_partition.py, EX-80) is the copper hole mesh at 50 Ω, one drive at a time, loss partition only, no |B₁⁺|, no 10 g; - grep -rln 'build_tuned_quadrature\|C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF\|test_wf10_f_human_tuned' examples --include=*.py returns nothing.

Scope boundary with EX-75. This chunk is the two-port 90° drive only (P17 / P21, ring −1, slots 0 / 4, the clinical fixture). The four-port quadrature side branch (PROJECT_PLAN.md §7 EX-75, line ≈ 3045) stays EX-75's; this item does not touch, re-pose or pre-empt it.

docs.title: §9 item 362 — 2026-10-10 (§5.4 example from H9′; example-runner)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-10 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. No band, tolerance, record, Done-when of another chunk or validation target is set or moved; every band is imported.

EX-109 (mri:17): the tuned copper F-human birdcage under the clinical two-port 90° drive — |B₁⁺| and the 10 g SAR hotspot at C_in,F-human = 118.2437 pF, r = 0.2 Ω ESR on all 32 gaps. One build of H9′'s fixture (369 387-cell copper hole mesh, Leontovich wall, κ off, degree 1, 64 MHz, phantom at 0.015 m), one node pair at C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF, two sense superpositions (ccw = (1, −1j) co-rotating, cw = (1, +1j)), then both readings from the same fields: the |B₁⁺| sample and the 18-point 10 g lattice. The reader sees a tuned coil's B₁⁺ purity, where its 10 g hotspot sits, and why the feed-bisector mirror (not C16) is the identity a two-feed drive keeps.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: heavy, -n 8 (H9′'s record width), complex.
  • Depends on: nothing open. Items 358 and 359 are DONE on main (63bccf11, 7ef44c35). Needs the gitignored inputs logs/wf12/h12c-cu-s32-a2.npz (the builder asserts it, test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:208–209) and logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437.json ((S_rep) below). Absent ⇒ stop, mark BLOCKED; never re-solve the 32×32 or re-run 358 (10:30 rulings (3), (5)). Never beside another heavy window.
  • Cost: ≈ 8 measured (example class median, 10:30 restock table — it will run long of the median: the two heavy windows alone are ≈ 13 min) / ≈ 60 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 22 script + ≈ 8 guide + ≈ 7.5 flagged run + ≈ 7 control + ≈ 1.5 dry run and censuses. If the flagged run has not started by minute 35, park (rule (d)). Price basis, one build serving both readings:
  • build 112.6–112.8 s, node pair 34.4–49.9 s, superposition + partitions 6.5–7.6 s (20261010T170356Z_WF-10-step2-W1.log:6342, 20261010T171705Z_WF-10-step2s-W1.log:6384); no Z50 pair (with_z50=False, 359's call; (Z50) stays 358's record);
  • |B₁⁺|: two CG1 projections 1.55 s, 41 points × 19 images 1.82 s (…step2-W1.log:6332);
  • 10 g: 39 balls, 3.44 s mean / 4.69 s max, SAR phase 138.6 s with coverage (…step2s-W1.log:6384);
  • example-only: DG0 maps (four assemble_vector / interpolations) ≈ 5 s, ball markers ≈ 1 s, combined XDMF of ≈ 12 DG0 fields on 369 387 cells ≈ 10 s, start-up ≈ 10 s, setup figure ≈ 8 s flagged (mri:6 on this mesh: flagged 278 s vs control 270 s, EX-80 row);
  • predicted ≈ 345 s flagged, ≈ 337 s control; range [300, 480] s (1.32× box reading, item 349); runner -t 590, container timeout -k 30 590. Under 10 min, so the plain runner line (no durable capture) is the form, as mri:6. Summed RSS predicted ≤ 12 GiB (358: 10.38 GiB, :6342).

Code: no rule (a) lift, no gate-module edit, no src/ edit. build_tuned_quadrature already returns every field the example needs (e per sense, e17, e21, sigma, ctx, parts, anchors, say, omega, t_window; test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:482–489). The |B₁⁺| reads and the 10 g ball sequence live in the two test_* bodies (test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:540–613; test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py:173–289), which are never imported: the script re-states that sequence with a provenance comment citing those spans at 7ef44c35, through the same imported helpers and bands, and the printed rows must equal the W1 logs (the anchor's second part catches any divergence). If the review prefers the lift, see the open questions; it adds two heavy re-gate windows (the 358 and 359 W1 commands, below in Traps) and ≈ 9 min.

Imports (never restated). - tests.validation.test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar: build_tuned_quadrature (:147), C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF (:58), C_IN_SECANT_PF, NODE_JSON (:82), _signed_k_shares (:85), PREDICTED_SENSE_RATIO, PREDICTED_MIRROR (as B1_PREDICTED_MIRROR), PREDICTED_C16, PREDICTED_MISPAIRED. - tests.validation.test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g: _lattice (:58), _plane_distance (:80), _containment (:85), PREDICTED_MIRROR (as SAR_PREDICTED_MIRROR), PREDICTED_AZ_SPREAD, PREDICTED_CONTROL_MISS. - tests.validation.test_birdcage_b1_plus_map: C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3, _relative_l2, _rotate_z, _sample_points. tests.validation.test_birdcage_b1_quadrature: _mirror_xy, _read_senses. - Bands: DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (test_birdcage_power_identity), EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (test_birdcage_sar_mass_averaged), REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix), UNIT_WEIGHT_CONTROL_RTOL (test_port_drive_superposition), Y0_CODING_BAND (test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root), BLIND_FACTOR (test_wf12_f_human_copper_matrix); _residual (test_port_circuit_layer_field). - 10 g: CONDUCTOR_CLEARANCE_M, COVERAGE_BALL_PAD_M, FIRST_BALL_STOP_S, _phantom_geometry (test_wf7_f_human_sar10g_hotspot); QUADRATURE_DEGREE, TEN_GRAM_KG (test_mass_averaged_sar_standard_masses); F_HUMAN_RING_RADIUS (test_birdcage_f_human_rung); global_cell_tag_set (tests.mesh.helpers); _k1_shares (test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit); _rss_gib (test_wf12_f_human_hole). - Tags: PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column); PORT_LOWER, PORT_UPPER (tests.mesh.test_birdcage_port_sheets). - src: magnetic_flux_density_from_e, project_to_cg1, b1_plus, b1_minus (post/faraday.py); mean_sar, mass_averaged_sar, averaging_ball_radius, build_density_field (post/sar.py); write_setup_figure, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership. - The record digits are restated only as EX-89 item 238's REC was: an example-local REC dict, each entry commented with its log:line, compared at the printed precision (that ruling, EX-89.md item 332 (Q1)).

(1) Anchor. Two parts. - The gates, re-asserted at their imported bands, each printed beside its W1 line. - From the builder (asserted inside it): (A0) 369 387 cells = HOLE_CELL_RECORD within CELL_COUNT_BAND, census none (…step2-W1.log:6308); feeds 90° apart (:6309); (P_RC) ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (7.830e-13, :6317); node NEG ≥ BLIND_FACTOR× (7012.5×, :6318). - (S_rep): _residual(out["s_node"], s_json) ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL, the JSON read on rank 0 and broadcast before the builder (it rewrites the file); 359 read 6.027e-13 (…step2s-W1.log:6312). - Per sense: (P_w) ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (5.065e-13 / 5.893e-13, …step2-W1.log:6320, :6322); (Lin) currents ≤ UNIT_WEIGHT_CONTROL_RTOL, Y_in ≤ Y0_CODING_BAND (:6321, :6323). - (Σ_P): mean_sar dissipated on E_ccw = P_phantom ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (0.000e+00, :6340). - (Sense): mean|B₁⁺|_ccw / mean|B₁⁻|_ccw > 1, 358's bar (21.5155, :6333); n_mask > 0 (41 of 41, :6332). - (M_B): _relative_l2(|B₁⁻|_cw(Mx), |B₁⁺|_ccw(x), mask) ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, M the feed-bisector reflection at az₁₇ + 45° = 56.25° (1.9647e-03, :6335). - (i) coverage: the whole-phantom ball's power and mass equal mean_sar's ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, the ball inside F_HUMAN_RING_RADIUS − CONDUCTOR_CLEARANCE_M (2.442e-15 / 6.994e-15, …step2s-W1.log:6377). - (iii-a) mirror at c* ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (0.6413 %, :6373); (iii-b) lattice relative L2 over the 18 points (or the STOP-reduced 12) ≤ the band (1.2789 %, :6374); (iv) every ball 1 mm clear of the measured bbox (worst −4.8813 mm over 39 balls, :6382). - The map-sum identity (new, example side; asserted). (X1) The per-cell DG0 phantom loss vector of 0.5·σ·inner(E_ccw, E_ccw)·conj(v)·dx(PHANTOM_CELL_TAG) (v a DG0 test function; mri:6's _dg0_vec, 06_f_human_copper_loss_partition.py:87–91, :144, re-written in the script with a comment), summed over owned cells and allreduced, equals parts["ccw"]["p_phantom"] ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. The written local SAR map is that vector / (ρ·Vell) on antom cells, so Σ SAR·ρ·V = P_phantom by construction; the guide says the map is the cell-averaged local SAR, not a 10 g value. Predicted ≤ 1e-14. - Records. Every printed row above, plus the Y_in four readings and M-paired spreads (:6325–6329), signed k shares (:6330–6331), C16 (:6338), mean |B₁⁺| and CV (:6339), SAR per watt (:6341; …step2s-W1.log:6383), the 18-row ccw / cw(M) table (…step2s-W1.log:6354–6371) and c* (:6372), must equal the W1 logs at the printed digits. Round-off readings ((P_RC), (P_w), (Lin), (S_rep), (Σ_P), (i), (X1)) are asserted at their band only. A digit mismatch on a record row with every assertion green is reported, not a stop.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - Asserted, backed on this fixture: - (N1) the mis-paired sense: _relative_l2(|B₁⁺|_cw(Mx), |B₁⁺|_ccw(x), mask) > C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. Backed by …step2-W1.log:6336, 9.5476e-01 (19.1× the band). It shows the mirror pairs B₁⁺ with B₁⁻; pairing the wrong rotating component fails. The factor is printed, not asserted. - (N2) the single feed without the partner swap: |SAR10g_P17(Mc*) − SAR10g_P17(c*)| / SAR10g_P17(c*) > C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. Backed by …step2s-W1.log:6376, 3674.7755 % (735× the band). No ceiling caps it; no factor is asserted. - The node P_surf-blind miss ≥ BLIND_FACTOR × DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, asserted inside the builder (…step2-W1.log:6318). - Printed only (readings, never asserted): the (Sense) factor beside 358's PREDICTED_SENSE_RATIO 10 (record 21.5155); the single-feed M-partner P21(Mc*) vs P17(c*), record 7.3845 % (OUT of 359's predicted 5 %; never assert it); the z_c-row azimuthal spread 16.7 / 21.0 / 18.6 % (OUT of the predicted 10 %); C16 worst 0.80 % at m = 8; the wrong-plane (az₁₇) mirror 5.2887e-03; the per-sense (P_w) P_surf-blind reading ≈ 7.04e-3.

Output. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_17_f_human_tuned_quadrature_b1_sar_setup.png, through write_setup_figure, called right after the builder returns: mri:6's call on the same hole mesh (06_f_human_copper_loss_partition.py:170–187; its PNG is 443 KiB) with region_names labelling P17 / P21's port boxes "feed P17 (0°)" / "feed P21 (90°)" and the other thirty "C_in + 0.2 Ω gap"; hide_tags=(2,), translucent_tags=(PHANTOM_CELL_TAG,), slice_normal=(0, 0, 1) through z_c, window_size=(1400, 630), title ≤ 130 characters (e.g. mri:17 -- tuned copper F-human birdcage, two-port 90 deg feed at C_in 118.2437 pF, r = 0.2 Ohm (WF-10 H9')). Over 600 KiB ⇒ re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. The hole route has no conductor cells: the guide says the coil is drawn as a void. - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_17_f_human_tuned_quadrature_b1_sar_combined.xdmf, write_xdmf_with_tags(…, msh, cell_tags, fields, comm=comm) + adopt_host_ownership. Every field DG0, real-valued, named once: B1_plus_ccw, B1_minus_ccw, B1_minus_cw (from b1_plus / b1_minus of magnetic_flux_density_from_e, .real, as mri:4's _field_export); B1_purity_ccw (= B1_plus_ccw / B1_minus_ccw where B1_minus_ccw > 0, numpy); E_magnitude_ccw; phantom_loss_per_cell_W_ccw (X1's vector) and SAR_local_ccw (W/kg, phantom only); LatticeBall (k + 1 inside lattice ball k, 1–18) and CStar (1 at c*), from numpy cell midpoints over owned + ghost cells (marker only, not the quadrature ball); MirrorSide (+1 / −1 by the sign of the distance to the feed-bisector plane, for reading the mirror in ParaView). - CSV examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_17_f_human_tuned_quadrature_b1_sar_lattice.csv: label, r, dz, d_az, x, y, z, SAR10g_ccw, SAR10g_cw(M), rel, mass, wall_s, is_c_star. - The XDMF / H5 / CSV are gitignored; only the PNG is tracked. - Guide examples/mri/17_f_human_tuned_quadrature_b1_sar.md: ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step, ## Setup figure, ## Related. It explains: the node (C_in,F-human, H17's record at 0.10 pF resolution; r = 0.2 Ω on all 32 gaps, feeds driven across r + C); why ccw = (1, −1j) at slots 0 / 4 is the co-rotating sense (the convention code, not a choice made after reading |B₁⁺|); why a two-feed drive keeps only the feed-bisector mirror ({1, M}) and C16 is a reading; (N1) as the reason the mirror pairs B₁⁺ with B₁⁻; the 10 g regime (≈ 1.8 phantom cells per ball, so c* is a lattice argmax asserted pointwise and the lattice as a relative L2); that the two OUT readings (az spread, P21 partner) are records, not failures; a ParaView recipe (slice z = z_c on B1_plus_ccw; Threshold LatticeBall ≥ 1 coloured by SAR_local_ccw; compare B1_plus_ccw with B1_minus_cw across MirrorSide). ## Related by full filename (rule (b)): examples/mri/04_f_human_sar10g_hotspot.md, examples/mri/06_f_human_copper_loss_partition.md, tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py, tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py, tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root.py. It names EX-75 as the four-port side branch, not shown here.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and is one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call; nothing chained or piped. 0. Orphan check: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-109-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-109-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - Last reading: figures examples=104 ok=104 missing=0 broken=0 (20261009T052356Z_EX-108-post-figures.log:140). Use whatever the pre-census reads. 2. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-109-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:17 -n 8 -t 590 --dry-run". It must print (complex build) (run_examples.sh:281). run_examples.sh is host-side; pass the emitted docker line to the harness as its own call. 3. Run of record (flagged), -n 8, predicted ≈ 345 s, [300, 480]: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-109 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 examples/mri/17_f_human_tuned_quadrature_b1_sar.py"' The script inserts _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (04_f_human_sar10g_hotspot.py:94–96), so PYTHONPATH stays /workspace/src. The only difference from the dry-run line is -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1; note any other. 4. Control, unflagged: git add the PNG first, then the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-109-control. Predicted ≈ 337 s. Compared with window 3 at the band, never bitwise: assertions on the same side, record rows equal at the printed digits. 5. Guide, written from the run-of-record log before the post-censuses. 6. Post-censuses EX-109-post-figures / EX-109-post-docrefs (window 1's commands with those labels). Write the prediction first: figures examples N → N + 1, ok +1, missing=0, broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, guide=0, no new dead reference (exit != 1 if the pre-census read dead=0). 7. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new paths (script, guide, PNG). No other code path is modified.

(4) Traps already paid for. - The builder rewrites logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437.json (:475–480) with the reproduced values: read it before the builder, on rank 0, then bcast (359's pattern, test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py:173–182). Never delete it. - Sense: ccw = (1, −1j) lags with azimuth; (1, +1j) is cw. Never re-choose the sense after reading |B₁⁺| (10:30 ruling (1)). - Mirror plane: out["az_mirror"] (az₁₇ + 45°), never WF-7's az_ref plane; the wrong-plane reading is printed only. - B goes through project_to_cg1 (an L² projection) for the point reads, and points through evaluate_vector_field_parallel inside _read_senses, never f.eval; the DG0 XDMF maps are separate and are not read at points. - Never assert C16, the az spread or the P21 partner — the drive breaks C16, and the latter two are OUT records of 359. - Collectives on every rank: the builder, every mass_averaged_sar / mean_sar call (item 227's deadlock), fem.assemble_vector, write_xdmf_with_tags, write_setup_figure, every allreduce, _rss_gib. Ball wall times MAX-reduced so the FIRST_BALL_STOP_S decision is common; the STOP reduction is pre-registered, not a red. - Complex build: no ufl ordering or sqrt comparison on any operand (OPS-22, WF-6 4c); markers and purity are numpy on midpoints and reduced values; the DG0 loss form needs ufl.conj(v); take np.real after assembly. Ball centres go in as plain floats. - Rank-local: cell_tags.values, assemble_scalar, DG0 sums over index_map.size_local only; tag lookups include ghosts. - Name every Function (EX-79's HDF5 collision). Never import another example's module or any test_* function. - Harness shape: bare, whole, repo-relative; the orphan check from a bare shell needs -f docker/docker-compose.yml. A docker-socket denial means stop and report. Status 124 is a finding: pgrep -c python3 first; only at 0, the rubric's orphan-stem sweep as one bare call labelled EX-109-cache-sweep; never raise the timeout or -n. - Rule (i): the script is frozen once window 3 starts; the guide before window 6. PNG ≤ 600 KiB. Write ≈, never a tilde. No AED value or comparison anywhere (ANS-8's verdict may be named only qualitatively, and is not needed). - If the review chooses the lift (open question): the re-gate windows are the item 358 / 359 W1 commands verbatim (WF-10.md items 358, 359 "Windows"), relabelled EX-109-wf10s2-regate-W1 / EX-109-wf10s2s-regate-W1, serial, -n 8, before any example window.

(5) Scope. Degree 1, 64 MHz, κ off, one copper hole fixture (369 387 cells), one phantom at 0.015 m (≈ 1.8 cells per 10 g ball), r = 0.2 Ω on all 32 gaps, the two-port 90° feed at C_in,F-human, -n 8. Not claimed: the four-port quadrature drive (EX-75); f₀, Q, a match, S₁₁ / Z_in or any tuning-accuracy figure (C_in is a record at 0.10 pF resolution); homogeneity (CV is a reading); an absolute |B₁⁺| or SAR against anything external; C16 invariance; a global SAR maximum (c* is a lattice argmax); C95.3 / IEC / ASTM F2182 compliance or any absolute or normalised SAR limit; degree 2 (the 5.50 % human-scale order caveat, WF-7 step 0b); any AED comparison; a tissue model; anything WF-10 step 2 does not claim. WF-10 stays 🟡.

(6) Negative result. Report the measurement and stop; journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-109-<UTC>, and mark item 362 BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)). EX-109 stays ⬜. Never widen a band, edit a gate module or src/, or re-record a constant. - A gate anchor red, or a record row off its W1 digits beyond print rounding with the anchor red: an example/test divergence finding (the re-stated sequence differs from the test body) or a fixture move under H9′'s records — a known-issues entry and a note on the WF-10 row for the review. - (S_rep) red: 358's node record does not reproduce; report both; stop. - (X1) red with (Σ_P) green: an example defect in the DG0 form; fix once in-slot before the window of record if the cause is shown, otherwise park. - (N1) or (N2) inside the band: the sense or the partner swap did not reach the reading; stop and report. - An input file absent: BLOCKED; never re-solve. - Over 590 s, Status 124, or minute 50 before window 4: park with the last line printed; the review re-tiers (e.g. B₁⁺ and 10 g as two invocations). - A printed reading off its prediction has no status effect.

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

(7) Status it can move. The new §7 row EX-109 (added by the review in the same commit as this item, rule (j)) moves ⬜ → ✅ when its Done-when is met and elapsed is recorded. Census examples +1, broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, no new dead reference. It is the first example of a tuned coil at human scale and gives Phase 9 (9d) its tuned-coil tutorial. WF-10 (🟡, rule (j)), EX-75, EX-62 and EX-80 do not move; the weekly ratifies the row.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-109, §9 item 362 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-109.md, heading §9 item 362). Read the brief and any review rulings beneath it first; the rulings hold. You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Before window 3, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 and require 0. Edit no gate module and no src/ file; if logs/wf12/h12c-cu-s32-a2.npz or logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437.json is absent, stop. No edit to the script after window 3 or to the guide after window 6. If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command string. Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its W1 record, the census before / after, and elapsed."

Review rulings (2026-10-10 18:00 daily review, item 362). (362-1) (Sense) stays asserted at > 1, which is 358's own bar. The 21.52× is printed beside it and is never raised in-slot. (362-2) No lift: the example repeats the test bodies through imported module-level helpers and bands. Its printed rows must equal the two W1 logs at the printed digits, and no gate module or src/ file is edited, so there are no re-gate windows. (362-3) The minute-35 park rule stands. The class median (8 min) counts toward the floor by the protocol, but this item's honest window cost is ≈ 13 minutes of heavy compute plus the guide. (362-4) The inputs logs/wf12/h12c-cu-s32-a2.npz and logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437.json were checked present on the host at 18:00. (362-5) The row is opened from H9′'s asserted gates while WF-10 holds 🟡 (rule (j)). It is not the step-3 ✅ ramp. The weekly ratifies it or folds it into EX-75's re-pose.

Outcome (2026-10-10 19:30 slot): DONE. example-runner executed; every asserted gate and both controls ((N1) 9.5476e-1, (N2) 3674.7755 %) green in the flagged run (20261011T004348Z_EX-109.log, 241 s) and the unflagged control (20261011T004801Z_EX-109-control.log, 234 s). Record rows equal both W1 logs at the printed digits, except Im Y17 under cw, which differs in its tenth significant digit (round-off on a near-zero part; nothing asserts it). (X1) 4.441e-16. PNG 435 KiB. Figures census 104 → 105, missing=0 broken=0 (…T005315Z_EX-109-post-figures-r2.log). The first post-docrefs (…T005230Z_EX-109-post-docrefs.log) read dead=1: the guide named the gitignored node JSON by path.
