docs.title: EX-110 — mat:18, the six-minute window on an FEM heating history
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-110 (mat:18) is opened 2026-10-11 by the 18:00 daily review under daily-review.md step 5 (§5.4 ramp). Its base is MAT-20 ✅ (§9 item 370, 2026-10-11 12:00 slot): step 2's FEM clause, tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py, run of record docs/testing/logs/20261011T172810Z_MAT-20-step2-fem-W1.log (heavy, -n 2, 270 s, 13 passed). On MAT-17 step 3's fixture (MAT-15 step 1's _run_heated, the F-small coil-driven gel phantom at 10 MHz, drive k = 0, G = 1 W / P₁, P = t*/5 = 250.8 s, D = 0.5) it holds: - (H0) Duhamel on the per-step volume-mean series, 5.689e-14 ≤ L_BAND (:1968); - (FEM) running_average (W = 360 s, 11.48 samples, 29 windows) of the duty series equals Σ(−1)^m of it on the ten Heaviside series H_m, 3.434e-14 ≤ D_BAND (:1969); (FEM-2d) 3.444e-14 through the 2-D call, duty column equal to the 1-D call (:1971); - (Wc-FEM) the P/2-shifted control misses by 1.326e-1 (:1972); (Dc) m = 9 dropped, 0.043296, printed (:1973).

Proposed §7 row (to paste right after the EX-109 row; ≤ 2 KB):

| EX-110 | The six-minute window on an FEM heating history: windowing a duty-cycled coil drive equals windowing its ten switch-on runs (history and §9 briefs: docs/planning/chunks/EX-110.md) (mat:18; example-runner; opened 2026-10-11 by the 18:00 daily review, §5.4 ramp from MAT-20 ✅, §9 item 370; mat:17 windows closed forms only and mat:15 shows this history unwindowed) Done-when: examples/materials/18_six_minute_window_coil_heating.py + same-stem guide (three required headings + ## Setup figure + ## Related, PNG ≤ 600 KiB); complex, -n 2; rule (a) lift in tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py (_fem_history(*, keep_duty_fields=False), _identities(t, duty, hs); additive, prints unchanged), module re-gated green in-slot; every band imported, none restated, no src/ edit. Asserted in-script through the imported helper: (H0) ≤ L_BAND, (FEM) and (FEM-2d) ≤ D_BAND, control (Wc-FEM) > D_BAND; example-side (Cm) the volume mean of the per-vertex six-minute field equals the windowed series ≤ D_BAND, its one-sample-short control (Cm-c) misses; records printed beside 20261011T172810Z_MAT-20-step2-fem-W1.log:1957–1974. Outputs: θ and its six-minute mean as a 29-frame series XDMF, a t* combined XDMF and a history CSV. Census +1, broken=0, no new dead docref; elapsed recorded ⇒ ✅. Not claimed: a limit or compliance, tissue, perfusion, absolute temperature, a periodic state, a CEM43 gate. | ⬜ Queued §9 item 389. | heavy (-n 2, ≈ 225 s per window, -t 590) |

Gap. No example applies the six-minute operator to an FEM history, or to a field. - grep -rlE 'running_average|cem43' examples --include=*.py returns only examples/materials/17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle.py, and mat:17 (EX-104) is closed-form only by its Done-when ("never an FEM history"). - mat:15 (EX-99) runs this exact history and writes θ(t), but its guide's Not-claimed list includes "SAR averaging"; it never windows.

docs.title: §9 item 389 — 2026-10-11 (example, §5.4 ramp; example-runner)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-11 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, record, Done-when of another chunk or validation target. Every band is imported from MAT-20's FEM-clause module and MAT-17 step 3's module.

EX-110 (mat:18; examples/materials/ holds 01–17, and the runner selects mat:<n> by the %02d_ prefix, scripts/run_examples.sh:201–219, so 18_ is mat:18) adds three tracked files and edits one gate module: - examples/materials/18_six_minute_window_coil_heating.py; - the same-stem guide examples/materials/18_six_minute_window_coil_heating.md, with ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step, ## Setup figure and ## Related; - examples/materials/figures/materials_18_six_minute_window_coil_heating_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB; - the rule (a) lift in tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py (below).

The angle: the regulatory window on a real FEM history, and on a field. mat:17 showed the six-minute window on closed forms. mat:15 showed this coil-driven duty history without a window. This example joins them and adds three things no example has: 1. Windowing commutes with Duhamel on FEM data. The duty run's six-minute mean equals the signed sum of the ten switch-on runs' six-minute means ((FEM), gated). So a user can window the per-switch building blocks once and compose any on/off schedule on the same switch grid without re-windowing. The guide states this as the reason; the example asserts only the gated schedule. 2. The window of a field. The 2-D call windows θ at every P1 vertex of the phantom. The example writes θ and its six-minute mean as one ParaView time series (29 frames, n = 12 … 40). It also writes, at t*, the per-vertex six-minute maximum and the time at which each vertex's six-minute mean peaks. The volume mean peaks at t* (record :1974). But a window ending at the last on-phase end (n = 36, t = 1128.6 s) holds 234.6 s of on-time, against 125.4 s for the window ending at t* (n = 40). So vertices whose θ falls during the off phase may peak earlier. The map shows where. 3. Power against temperature. The source's six-minute on-fraction peaks at (P/2 + W − P)/W = 234.6/360 = 0.6517, which is 1.303 × D: plain arithmetic on HALF and W, printed. The volume-mean θ's six-minute peak is 0.5270 K against H_0's 1.0044 K, a ratio of 0.5247 ≈ D (:1974). The thermal mass flattens what the power window reports.

Part B (printed only; the §10 note "an example after MAT-20 ✅ (P20's dose figures, mat:18)"): if logs/mat15_s5/ holds step 3's series JSON (gitignored; present at drafting, written 13:36), recompute through cem43 and running_average and print, beside 20261011T183717Z_MAT-20-step3-W2.log, the tuned F-human's 10 g ball-mean CEM43 per accepted W and its six-minute peak. Nothing in Part B is asserted. If the file is absent, Part B prints one skip line and the run continues. The run of record must show Part B present.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: heavy, -n 2 (the gate's record width), complex build (the mat: group sources it).
  • Cost: ≈ 8 measured (example class median) / ≈ 55 predicted min (10 fixed + ≈ 8 lift + ≈ 15 script + ≈ 6 guide + ≈ 16 windows). If the re-gate (window 2) has not started by minute 25, or the flagged run (window 4) by minute 38, park (rule (d)). Price basis:
  • The gate's run of record took 270 s harness, 268.66 s pytest (20261011T172810Z_MAT-20-step2-fem-W1.log:2039, :2108). Inside it, _run_heated took 166.8 s (EM 143.3 s, :1954), and the 11 transients plus 451 reductions took 28.2 s (:1956).
  • The nearest example analogue is mat:15 on the same _run_heated, with 12 thermal runs and a 41-frame θ series: 230 s flagged / 220 s control (20261007T183803Z_EX-99.log:2006; …184229Z_EX-99-control.log).
  • This example adds the 2-D window over ≈ 1e4 local dofs × 41 samples (< 1 s), 29 frames × 2 P1 fields of series XDMF (≈ 5–15 s) and Part B (≈ 1 s; W2 was 3 s).
  • Flagged run predicted ≈ 225 s, range [190, 330] s; control ≈ 215 s. Re-gate ≈ 270 s, range [250, 330] s. Runner -t 590, container timeout -k 30 590. Each window is under 10 min, so the plain runner line is the form (no durable capture).
  • Dry run plus four census windows: ≈ 1.5 min together. Total compute ≈ 15 min.
  • Fewer Heaviside runs were considered and rejected. The ten runs cost ≈ 25 s of the ≈ 225 s; the EM fixture dominates. Dropping any H_m changes the identity: (Dc) shows that dropping m = 9 alone misses by 0.043. Truncating the history changes the window count (29). Reading the gate's gitignored logs/mat20/ JSON instead of re-solving would save ≈ 28 s. But the θ field series needs the duty run's fields, and so the EM solve. So all ten runs are kept and re-solved.
  • Depends on: nothing open. Item 370 is DONE on main. 18_ is free in examples/materials/, and no row or chunk names EX-110 (the mat:18 mentions in MAT-20.md:159, :347 and §10 are this example).
  • Shared files. One gate-module edit (the lift), the three new paths, and nothing under src/. dose.py stays unexported; import fem_em_solver.thermal.dose directly. Never beside another heavy window.

Code: the rule (a) lift (standing rule (a): additive, gate re-run green in-slot, disclosed; the EX-99 _run_duty precedent). In tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py: 1. _fem_history(*, keep_duty_fields=False) is hist()'s body (:72–91) moved verbatim, without the JSON dump. - Split the duty line (:83–84) into r_duty = _transient_s(sub, ft, q0, _chi_duty, snapshot_steps=STEPS) followed by duty = _series(r_duty, work, f_mean, comm, v_sub). This is behaviour-identical. - Under the flag only, take duty_fields = [np.real(r_duty.snapshots[n].x.array).copy() - T_INF for n in STEPS] before _series clears the snapshots (:66). - Return {"t", "duty", "H"} as now. Under the flag, also return base, sub, ft, V1, work, f_mean, v_sub, q0, duty_fields. - The MAT20fem fixture: print (:89–91) is unchanged. 2. hist() becomes out = _fem_history(), then the rank-0 JSON dump (:93–99, same keys and values) and comm.Barrier(), then return out. 3. _identities(t, duty, hs) holds the test body's computations (:107, :116–117, :122–128, :134–137, :142–144, :149–150, :154), moved verbatim. It returns a dict: - signs, h0, a, a_mx, a_tmx, ra, b, ok, scale, res, fem; - fem2d, fem2d_eq (the np.array_equal), idx, wc, dc, h0_mx, h0_tmx.

test_mat20_fem_history calls it, prints every line it prints today, from the dict and at the same format specs, and keeps its four asserts unchanged. - No band, assertion, print format or JSON key moves. git diff on the module shows a move plus a call, nothing else.

Imports (never restated). Use module aliases: two modules define W-like names, and _series / _say are generic. - import tests.validation.test_mat20_fem_history as m20f: _fem_history, _identities, _series, W, STEPS. - import tests.validation.test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven as m17s3: D_BAND, L_BAND, DT, HALF, N_SWITCH, STEPS_PER_HALF, _chi_duty. - import tests.validation.test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom as m15: N_MAIN, T_INF, T_STAR, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, _run_heated. - import tests.validation.test_mat20_running_average as s2: W_B2, for the structural check only. - import tests.validation.test_mat20_tuned_heating_dose as m20d (Part B): SERIES_JSON, _quad_dose, R_BELOW. - Setup-figure tags, as mat:15 imports them (15_duty_cycled_coil_heating_phantom.py:57–58, :81): PORT_LOWER, PORT_UPPER (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets.py), LEG_COUNT (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_tags.py), CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py). - From src: cem43, running_average (fem_em_solver.thermal.dose), write_setup_figure, write_xdmf_with_tags, write_xdmf_time_series, adopt_host_ownership. - Structural asserts at start-up (the mat:15 precedent, :100–108): - m20f.D_BAND is m17s3.D_BAND; - m20f.L_BAND is m17s3.L_BAND; - m20f._run_heated is m15._run_heated; - m20f.T_STAR is m15.T_STAR; - m20f.W == s2.W_B2 == 360.0. - Record digits go only into an example-local REC dict, each entry commented with its log:line (EX-89 item 332 (Q1)). Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (15_duty_cycled_coil_heating_phantom.py:53–55).

(1) Anchor. Part A runs r = m20f._fem_history(keep_duty_fields=True), then ids = m20f._identities(r["t"], r["duty"], r["H"]). It prints once, on rank 0. - Re-asserted at the imported bands, each printed beside its W1 line at the gate's format spec: - (H0) ids["h0"] <= m17s3.L_BAND, record 5.689e-14 (:1968); - (FEM) ids["fem"] <= m17s3.D_BAND, record 3.434e-14 over 29 windows (:1969); - (FEM-2d) ids["fem2d"] <= m17s3.D_BAND and ids["fem2d_eq"] is True, record 3.444e-14 / True (:1971). - Residuals are round-off readings: assert them at the band only, and print them beside the record. - Records, printed, predicted equal at the printed digits (same code, same width; item 370 matched MAT-17 step 3 to the last digit except one unit on H_8): - ⟨θ_Hm⟩(t*) for m = 0 … 9 (:1957–1966; H_0 1.153313650151e+00 K … H_9 1.302990494639e-01 K); - the duty ⟨θ⟩ at n = 32 / 36 / 40: 0.466250330 / 0.584438780 / 0.568835514 K (:1967); - the duty six-minute max 5.270483664e-01 K at t_max = 1254.0000 s; H_0's 1.004390808e+00 K at 1254.0000 s (:1974).

A last-digit difference is reported, not red: EX-99's flag and control differed at ≈ 1e-14 relative. A difference beyond the last two printed digits stops the item (Negative result). - (Cm) example-side, asserted: the window of the field commutes with the volume mean. This is exact on its premise, because both maps are linear: the volume mean is a fixed linear functional of the P1 dof vector, and the window is linear in time. - Build F = np.stack(r["duty_fields"]), shape (41, n_local), owned + ghost dofs, real. - means_F, mx_F, tmx_F = running_average(r["t"], F, window=m20f.W). - For the 29 valid n (ids["ok"]), put T_INF + means_F[n] into one named P1 Function per n (scatter_forward). Read their volume means through the gate's own m20f._series, on a types.SimpleNamespace(snapshots={n: f_n}) with T_INF + 0 at the 12 NaN rows. Pass r["work"], r["f_mean"], comm and r["v_sub"]. This uses the gate's own reduction, not a restated one. - Assert max_{n∈ok} |mean_F[n] − ids["a"][n]| / ids["scale"] ≤ m17s3.D_BAND. Predicted ≤ 1e-14. - Part B (printed only, no assertion). Load m20d.SERIES_JSON. On the 10 g ball-mean series at t_inf_c + theta_ball10g_k, print: - cem43(t, T) and m20d._quad_dose(t, T, math.log(m20d.R_BELOW)) at .15e, beside W2 :52 (1.846214193739186e-11 / 1.846214193739185e-11 s); - running_average(t, θ, window=m20f.W)'s max and t_max beside :57 (4.277005459539476e-02 K at 1254.000000 s); - the dose in minutes beside :62 (3.077024e-13 min).

Predicted bitwise equal: same JSON, same operators. Label every dose with its unit and "per accepted W (ruling 361-1); not a safety statement".

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (Wc-FEM), asserted: ids["wc"] > m17s3.D_BAND, record 1.326e-01 over 25 windows (:1972). The miss is a shifted comparison and has no ceiling issue; only "> band" is asserted, the row's form. - (Dc), printed only: ids["dc"], record 0.043296 (:1973). - (Cm-c), asserted: repeat (Cm) with window = m20f.W − m17s3.DT (one sample short) on the field, against ids["a"] at W. It must miss by > m17s3.D_BAND. - Predicted miss [5e-3, 6e-2]: shortening the window by DT/W = 8.7 % moves each mean by ≈ (DT/W)·(a − θ̄(t − W)) ≈ 0.01 K, against max a ≈ 0.527 K. There is no ceiling: it is a miss, not a factor. - Part B's (Rc′) stays the gate's. Not repeated.

Printed (no band; predicted beside measured). - The source's six-minute on-fraction: max (HALF + W − 2·HALF)/W = 0.651667 (1.3033 × D), attained at n = 36 (window [768.6, 1128.6] s). At n = 40 the fraction is 125.4/360 = 0.348333. This is arithmetic on imported HALF and W, printed as such. - The volume-mean ratio a_max / H_0 max = 0.5247 (from :1974), predicted [0.52, 0.53], and the χ ratio 1.3033 beside it. - Per-vertex six-minute field, over owned dofs, allreduced: - the max of mx_F beside the max θ(t*) of the duty run; - the count and fraction of owned vertices whose tmx_F < t*, binned by tmx_F (n = 36, other, t*). Predicted fraction [0, 0.5], concentrated at the hot spot near leg 1 and at the Robin surface. A zero count is a reading, not a red. - The window count: 29 (n = 12 … 40, W / DT = 11.4833).

Output. - Setup figure examples/materials/figures/materials_18_six_minute_window_coil_heating_setup.png: mat:15's write_setup_figure call (15_duty_cycled_coil_heating_phantom.py:126–142) on r["base"]["msh"], r["base"]["cell_tags"], with the same region_names / hide_tags / translucent_tags / slice. Title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. "mat:18 -- the six-minute window on the duty-cycled coil-heated gel phantom (MAT-20 FEM clause)". If over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Series XDMF examples/materials/paraview_output/materials_18_six_minute_window_coil_heating_series_combined.xdmf through write_xdmf_time_series(…, r["sub"], None, steps, comm=comm). - 29 frames at t_n = n·DT for n = 12 … 40. - Two P1 fields per frame: theta_K (the duty θ) and theta_six_min_mean_K. Each key equals its Function's name. - Combined XDMF …_combined.xdmf through write_xdmf_with_tags(…, r["sub"], None, fields, comm=comm): - P1 theta_duty_tstar_K, theta_six_min_mean_tstar_K, theta_six_min_max_K and theta_six_min_t_max_s; - DG0 q_h_k0 (r["q0"], renamed as mat:15 does). - CSV …_window_history.csv, rank 0, one row per n = 0 … 40. Columns: - n, t_s; - chi_step: m17s3._chi_duty(t_n − DT/2) for n ≥ 1, blank at n = 0; - chi_six_min_on_fraction (arithmetic, blank before n = 12); - mean_theta_duty_K, mean_theta_H0_K; - six_min_duty_K (a), six_min_sum_Hm_K (b), rel_residual; - six_min_H0_K. - Then adopt_host_ownership. The XDMF / H5 / CSV are under the gitignored paraview_output/; only the PNG is tracked. - Guide. The three required headings, ## Setup figure and ## Related. Related lists, by full filename (rule (b)): - examples/materials/17_thermal_dose_duty_cycle.md first, then examples/materials/15_duty_cycled_coil_heating_phantom.md; - tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py, tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py and tests/validation/test_mat20_tuned_heating_dose.py.

Name Part B's input by directory only (logs/mat15_s5/): EX-109's first post-docrefs read dead=1 on a full path to a gitignored JSON. The guide explains: - why the window commutes with Duhamel (linearity), and what that buys (window the building blocks once); - why the power's six-minute fraction (0.65) overstates the temperature's (≈ D); - why some vertices peak before t*; - that all temperatures are per 1 W at 20 °C, so Part B's CEM43 ≈ 1.8e-11 s is a negligible dose, not a safety figure; - a ParaView recipe: open the series, Play, colour by theta_six_min_mean_K; on the combined file, Threshold theta_six_min_t_max_s < 1254 to see the early-peaking region; open the CSV in a Line Chart View and plot six_min_duty_K against six_min_sum_Hm_K. - Write ≈, never a tilde.

(3) Windows. Each one is foreground with timeout: 660000, and each is one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call, nothing chained or piped. 0. Orphan check: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-110-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - the same with check_example_doc_references.py, label EX-110-pre-docrefs.

The last reading was figures 106, missing=0 broken=0 (20261011T172451Z_EX-75-post-figures.log), and docrefs dead=0 guide=0, exit 2, stale only (…T172453Z_EX-75-post-docrefs.log). Use what the pre-census reads. 2. The lift, then the re-gate (the W1 command verbatim, relabelled), predicted [250, 330] s: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-110-mat20-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && mkdir -p /workspace/logs/mat20 && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py -v -s --tb=short'" - Pass: 13 passed, Status 0. Every MAT20fem record line is equal to W1 :1957–1967, :1974 at the printed digits. (H0) / (FEM) / (FEM-2d) / (Wc-FEM) are green, with residuals at round-off of W1's. - It rewrites the gitignored logs/mat20/ JSON with the same content. 3. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-110-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:18 -n 2 -t 590 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). Copy its emitted string verbatim for windows 4–5. 4. Run of record (flagged), predicted [190, 330] s. The expected form, which must match the dry run apart from -T and the flag: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-110 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/materials/18_six_minute_window_coil_heating.py"' - Pass: Status 0; every assertion in (1) and (2) green; records as in (1); Part B present. 5. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-110-control. Compare at the bands, never bitwise. 6. The guide, written from window 4's log. Then the post-censuses EX-110-post-figures / EX-110-post-docrefs (window 1's commands with those labels). - Write the prediction first: figures N → N + 1, missing=0 broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, no new dead reference. - Any dead reference naming a materials_18_* file or 18_six_minute_window_coil_heating.md fails the item. 7. git status --porcelain examples/ tests/ lists exactly the three new examples/ paths and the modified tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Harness shape. Every harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, no cd … &&, no ; date / | tail, no redirect (bash_guard rule 3). ./scripts/run_examples.sh is host-side: emit it with --dry-run and pass the string to the harness. Never wrap it in docker compose exec (the Status-127 trap). A docker-socket denial means stop and report the exact command string. - Timeouts. Bash timeout: 660000 on every window, and container timeout -k 30 590. Status 124 is a finding, never a retry; never raise the timeout or -n. After a kill, run pgrep -c python3 first; only at 0, run the any-orphan cache sweep (daily-review.md rubric item 4) as one bare call labelled EX-110-cache-sweep. - Re-gate before the example (rule (a)), and rule (i): no edit to the module after window 2, to the script after window 4 starts, or to the guide after window 6 starts. Check file mtimes against window starts before committing. EX-99's deviation (a record the lift did not return, so it was not printable after the freeze) came from returning too little: return every key listed above. - _series clears snapshots (:66). Copy the duty fields before calling it, under the flag. The fields are absolute T (transient.py:126); subtract T_INF. - Snapshot index 1 is after two BE half-steps. Times are n·DT; never insert a Δt/2 sample. - Rule (h): never form b from a, or the Duhamel sum from the duty run. The ten H_m runs are the comparand, inside _identities. - The complex build. P1 .x.array is complex. Feed running_average / cem43 only real numpy arrays (np.real(...) copies); they raise on a non-zero imaginary part by design. Assign real values into Functions and scatter_forward. - NaN head. running_average returns NaN for t − W < t₀ (n < 12). Mask with ids["ok"], and never write a NaN into an XDMF field: the series starts at n = 12. - Rank safety. _run_heated, the transients, _series, write_setup_figure, both XDMF writes and adopt_host_ownership are collective. Call them on every rank, never inside rank == 0. Vertex counts use owned dofs (index_map.size_local) and allreduce. Only the CSV write and prints are rank-0. - Name every Function, each XDMF key equal to its Function's name: EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window. - Import collisions. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## Setup figure, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step and ## Related; - examples/implants/figures/implants_08_pec_oblate_disc_edge_in_gel_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB; - the rule (a) lift in tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py (below).

The angle: the edge of a flat body, and how it compares with a tip. imp:02 showed the prolate tip (1/L_z, a point-like hot spot that appears only for the field along the long axis). This example adds three things no example has: 1. A flat body's hot spot is its edge, and only under an in-plane field. Under E₀x̂ the rim field is E₀/L_x (1/L_x = 8.015515 at aspect 5); driven face-on (E₀ẑ) the same disc gives only E₀/L_z = 1.332474 at its flat faces and almost nothing at the rim (W2: Φ_rim 0.49). The asserted control is that axial drive. 2. The edge is two hot arcs, not a ring. Under E₀x̂ the rim's normal field goes as cos φ: maximal at (±a, 0, 0) and zero at (0, ±a, 0) (step 0 records |E(0, ±a, 0)| ≤ 2.2e-16, 20261012T183435Z_IMP-6-step0-W1.log:83). Printed on four azimuths, visible in ParaView. 3. Edge against tip at the same size and curvature (closed form, printed, not gated). At aspect 5 with the same 6 mm long semi-axis, imp:02's prolate tip and this disc rim have the same hot-spot curvature radius (ρ_r = c²/a = ρ_t = a_pro²/c_pro = 0.24 mm) and the same averaging-ball radius (2c²/a = 2a_pro²/c_pro = 0.48 mm). The depolarisation factors are scale-free, so the comparison is a function of aspect alone. Predicted: 1/L_z^pro / 1/L_x^obl = 17.914415 / 8.015515 = 2.2350, pointwise squares 320.9 / 64.25 = 4.995; the gate records' ball means 49.805748 / 23.024938 = 2.1631; ball-mean / pointwise retained fraction 0.155 (tip) against 0.358 (rim). The guide explains it as the edge being curved sharply in one direction only (the rim is line-like, so the field falls off more slowly away from it), and states this as explanation, not a claim.

docs.title: EX-112 — mat:19, the F2182-sized gel box: a slab at its centre, cooled through its two large faces
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-112 (mat:19) is opened 2026-10-13 by the 10:30 daily review under daily-review.md step 5 (§5.4 ramp from MAT-21 ✅, landed 0ee0cc49). The 03:00 review's journal named it (docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-13-daily.md §5, "mat:19 after MAT-21 ✅"), and so does the 10-12 weekly's examples-health paragraph ("mat:19, the F2182-sized box"). Its base is MAT-21 step 1 (§9 item 423): tests/validation/test_mat21_box_fem.py. The runs of record are docs/testing/logs/20261013T142646Z_MAT-21-step1r-W1-steady.log (heavy, -n 2, 129 s, 19 passed) and …142900Z_MAT-21-step1r-W2-transient.log (136 s, 17 passed). The closed form is step 0's (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_closed_form.py, records docs/testing/logs/20261013T004329Z_MAT-21-step0-W1.log). On the m = 6 rung (create_box, (78, 48, 12) hexahedra split into 6 tetrahedra each; 650 × 420 × 90 mm; gel k 0.6, ρc 4.18e6, h 10, q 2000; Robin on every face; P1) it holds: - 269 568 cells, 50 323 P1 dofs, 380 725 P2 points; whole L2 1.547121e-03; (S2) Gauss 1.682e-12 (W1 :106); - (S1) finest interior 1.417055e-03 ≤ INTERIOR_BAND 1e-2; θ_h(0) 12.005487 K against the series' 12.003947 K (W1 :108); - (c1) the comparand at 2h misses: 5.9734e-01 (W1 :110); - (T) CN N = 40 at t* = 0.2 t_C = 2 821.5 s: interior 9.071528e-04, whole 1.417652e-03, balance 2.809e-12 (W2 :92); - (c2) Dirichlet z-roots at t* miss: 3.6135e-01 (W2 :93); - closed-form records (step 0 W1): θ_ss(0) 12.003947 K, slab 12.3750 K (:92); corner 2.5524 K, face centres x / y / z 6.1504 / 6.2367 / 8.7340 K (:93); τ₁ 20 193 s, t_C 14 107.5 s (:94); θ(0, t*) 1.335697 K against qt*/ρc 1.3500 K (:80); surface area 0.7386 m², face-mean θ 6.6531 K = qV/(hA_s) (:68); truncation deficit 1 − ΠS_d(40) 4.6708e-06 (:67).

Proposed §7 row (to paste right after the EX-111 row; ≤ 2 KB):

| EX-112 | The F2182-sized gel box: a 90 mm slab to 3 % at its centre, cooled ≈ 80 % through its two large faces, and hours from steady (history and §9 briefs: docs/planning/chunks/EX-112.md) (mat:19; example-runner; opened 2026-10-13 by the 10:30 daily review, §5.4 ramp from MAT-21 ✅, §9 item 438; mat:10 is the Robin cylinder, no example builds the box) Done-when: examples/materials/19_f2182_gel_box_slab_and_faces.py + same-stem guide (three required headings + ## Setup figure + ## Related, PNG ≤ 600 KiB); complex, -n 2, the gate's m = 6 rung through its module-level helpers; no gate-module edit, no src/ edit; every band imported, none restated. Asserted at the imported bands, each beside 20261013T142646Z_MAT-21-step1r-W1-steady.log:106–110 / …142900Z_…-W2-transient.log:92–93: (S1) interior ≤ INTERIOR_BAND, (S2) Gauss ≤ S2_GAUSS_BAND, (T) ≤ INTERIOR_BAND, CN balance ≤ E_BAND; controls (c1), (c2) miss. Gap. No example builds the box or reads the triple series. - examples/materials/ holds 01–18: balls (02, 04, 06–08, 11–13, 17), the Robin cylinder against its double series (10, EX-81), and the coil-heated cylinder phantom (09, 14–16, 18). None imports test_mat21_box_fem.py / test_mat21_box_closed_form.py or calls robin_box_steady_temperature / robin_box_transient_temperature (grep -rn 'MAT-21\|mat21\|box_fem' examples/ is empty at drafting). - mat:10 shows a phantom-sized cylinder whose three dimensions are comparable. docs.title: §9 item 438 — 2026-10-13 (example, §5.4 ramp after MAT-21 ✅)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-13 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, record, Done-when of another chunk or validation target. Every band is imported from MAT-21 step 1's module, which imports them from MAT-12 / MAT-13 / MAT-15.

EX-112 (mat:19; examples/materials/ holds 01–18 and the runner selects mat:<n> by the %02d_ prefix, scripts/run_examples.sh:201–219, :243, so 19_ is mat:19; the mat: group sources the complex build; no runner edit) adds three tracked files and edits nothing else: - examples/materials/19_f2182_gel_box_slab_and_faces.py; - the same-stem guide examples/materials/19_f2182_gel_box_slab_and_faces.md, with ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## Setup figure, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step and ## Related; - examples/materials/figures/materials_19_f2182_gel_box_slab_and_faces_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

The angle: what the F2182 box's shape does to its heat. MAT-21 gates the FEM against the triple series. This example adds three readings no example has. All three are closed-form or FEM prints, and none is asserted. 1. A slab at the centre, not at the sides. The 1-D Robin slab θ_slab(z) = q(C² − z²)/(2k) + qC/h (step 0's (R5) slab limit, test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:273) gives 12.375 K at the centre against the box's 12.003947 K. Stdlib arithmetic at 40 terms per axis while drafting (predicted, not recorded) puts slab/series − 1 as follows: - ≈ 3.05–3.09 % all the way up the centre column (z/C = 0, 0.5, 0.9, 1: 3.09 / 3.07 / 3.05 / 3.05 %). The slab's z-profile is right there; only its level is high. - Along x (y = z = 0): 3.5 % at 0.25A, 5.7 % at 0.5A, 12.7 % at 0.7A, 42 % at 0.9A, 101 % at the face. Along y: 9.5 % at 0.5B, 20.7 % at 0.7B, 53 % at 0.9B, 98 % at the face. - So the slab picture holds to 10 % only for |x| ≲ 0.64A on the x-axis and |y| ≲ 0.51B on the y-axis. 2. Where the heat leaves. Per-face-pair convective power ∫h θ dA as a fraction of qV, against the series' face integrals. Predicted by the same arithmetic: ±z (the two 650 × 420 faces) 0.795501, ±y 0.126245, ±x 0.078249 (sum 0.9999953 = ΠS_d(40), step 0's deficit 4.6708e-06 at W1 :67). Their area shares are 0.7392 / 0.1584 / 0.1024, so the large faces carry more than their area share because they are hotter: face-mean θ 7.1595 / 5.3023 / 5.0862 K (z / y / x pairs) against the all-face mean 6.6531 K. 3. Hours from steady. τ₁ = 20 193 s ≈ 5.6 h (step 0 W1 :94). At t* = 47 min the centre is at 1.335697 K, 98.9 % of the adiabatic qt*/ρc = 1.35 K and only 11.1 % of its steady 12.003947 K. The FEM centre history (nine snapshots) is printed beside the series and qt/ρc.

The guide explains these as reasons, not claims: the box is thin in z (Bi_z 0.75), so its centre column sees the slab; its side walls are 3–5 face-heights away, so lateral cooling is a 3 % correction at the centre that grows toward the sides.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: heavy, -n 2 (the gate's record width), complex build (the mat: group sources it).
  • Cost: ≈ 10 measured (example class) / ≈ 40 predicted min: 10 fixed + ≈ 14 script + ≈ 6 windows + ≈ 6 guide + ≈ 4 censuses / journal / commit. No lift and no re-gate window: the example calls the gate's module-level helpers unchanged. Park if the flagged run (window 3) has not started by minute 28, or the control (window 4) by minute 38 (rule (d)). Price basis:
  • The gate's own m = 6 clocks (W1 :103–111, W2 :87–94): build 0.8 s, steady 2.6 s, steady P2 series interpolation 14.9 s, interior 0.8 s, (c1) 15.3 s, CN N = 40 9.0 s, t* interpolation 15.7 s, (c2) 16.3 s, ≈ 75 s in all.
  • This example adds the following:
    • the P2 → CG1 copies (< 2 s);
    • the series at 269 568 + ghost cell midpoints for the slab mask, ≈ 11 s (scaled from 380 725 points in 14.9 s);
    • the closed-form face quadrature, 6 × 128² points, ≈ 4 s;
    • three 101-point centre lines through evaluate_vector_field_parallel (< 3 s) and the nine-snapshot centre history (< 2 s);
    • the XDMF, ≈ 5–10 s;
    • the setup figure, ≈ 10–20 s, flagged run only;
    • interpreter start-up and JIT, ≈ 15–25 s. The gate's forms are cached; the six ds(tag) forms are new.
  • The nearest example analogue is mat:10 (EX-81): ≈ 270 s at -n 2 on a 58 866-cell cylinder with a P2 series comparand, -t 480. That example's series is a double series with Bessel roots; this one is a product of cosines.
  • Flagged run predicted ≈ 140 s, range [100, 280] s; control ≈ 125 s, range [90, 260] s. Runner -t 420, container timeout -k 30 420.
  • Dry run plus four census windows: ≈ 1 min. Total compute ≈ 6 min. Every window is under 10 min, so the plain runner form is used (no durable capture).
  • Depends on: nothing open. MAT-21 step 1 is on main (0ee0cc49). 19_ is free in examples/materials/, and no row or chunk names EX-112. Item 424 (MAT-21 step 2) may run before or after; it adds two new modules and edits neither of the modules this example imports (its brief, MAT-21.md:341).
  • Shared files. Three new paths, nothing under tests/ or src/. If anything under tests/ or src/ turns out to be needed, stop and report; do not edit it. Never beside another heavy window.

Imports (never restated). Use module aliases: both MAT-21 modules define _say, HALF, K, Q, H and RHO_C. - import tests.validation.test_mat21_box_fem as m1: RUNGS, T_STAR, V_BOX, _rung, _Clock, _exact, _interior_chi, _steady_ex, _trans_ex, and the names it imports: INTERIOR_BAND, E_BAND, S2_GAUSS_BAND, RHO_C, K_GEL, H_GEL, N_MAIN, T_INF, ROBIN_TAG, _allsum, _rel, _robin_tags, A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX, HALF, Q, T_C, SERIES_TERMS. - import tests.validation.test_mat21_box_closed_form as m0: ALPHA and _axis_data (to print γ₁ and τ₁ beside step 0's records). Its _steady carries T_INF, so use m1._steady_ex() (t_inf = 0) for every θ. - import tests.validation.test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere as m13, import tests.validation.test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere as m12 and import tests.validation.test_mat15_finite_cylinder_fem as m15b are used only for the identity checks below. - From src: solve_transient_conduction (fem_em_solver.thermal), write_setup_figure, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership, evaluate_vector_field_parallel. - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (examples/materials/10_finite_cylinder_robin_series.py:45–47). Raise if default_scalar_type is not complex. - Structural asserts at start-up (the mat:10 precedent, :108–113): - m1.INTERIOR_BAND is m13.INTERIOR_BAND, m1.E_BAND is m12.E_BAND, m1.S2_GAUSS_BAND is m15b.S2_GAUSS_BAND; - m1.HALF is m0.HALF, m1.RUNGS[-1] == 6, m1.T_STAR == 0.2 * m1.T_C, m1.K_GEL == m1.K and m1.H_GEL == m1.H (the gate's (P0)). - Record digits go only into an example-local REC dict, each entry commented with its log:line (EX-89 item 332 (Q1)). Never assert a record by equality; print it beside the reading.

(1) Anchor. One m = 6 rung through the gate's own helpers, mirroring its fixtures. Pytest fixtures cannot be called directly (see Traps). - Steady. msh, ft, ns, n, v_h, st = m1._rung(6, m1._Clock("EX-112")); th = st.temperature - T_INF; ex, npts = m1._exact(msh, m1._steady_ex()); chi = m1._interior_chi(msh). - (S1) m1._rel(msh, th, ex, chi) <= INTERIOR_BAND. Record 1.417055e-03 (W1 :108). - (S2) abs(∮h θ ds(ROBIN_TAG) − q·v_h)/(q·v_h) <= S2_GAUSS_BAND, the gate's expression (test_mat21_box_fem.py:175–178). Record 1.682e-12 (W1 :106). - Printed beside records: cells 269 568, whole L2 1.547121e-03 (:106), θ_h(0) through evaluate_vector_field_parallel 12.005487 K against the series' 12.003947 K (:108). - Transient. The gate's (T) call, copied verbatim from test_mat21_box_fem.py:247–250: solve_transient_conduction(msh, ft, k=K_GEL, rho_c=RHO_C, q=Q, h=H_GEL, t_inf=T_INF, t_init=T_INF, robin_tag=ROBIN_TAG, dt=T_STAR / N_MAIN, n_steps=N_MAIN, theta=0.5, startup_half_steps=2, degree=1, snapshot_steps=range(0, N_MAIN + 1, 5)). The only addition is snapshot_steps, which records copies and does not change the solve. - (T) interior _rel against m1._exact(msh, m1._trans_ex(T_STAR)) ≤ INTERIOR_BAND. Record 9.071528e-04 (W2 :92). - (E-cn) res.max_balance_residual <= E_BAND. Record 2.809e-12 (:92). - Printed: the whole-box L2, record 1.417652e-03. - The (T) record reproduced at the printed digits is the check that the copied call is the gate's. - Records predicted equal at the printed digits (same code, width and image), each printed beside its log:line: cells, whole L2, (S1) interior, θ_h(0), (c1), (T) interior and whole, (c2). Excluded (2026-10-13 10:30 ruling, MAT-21.md:442): the Gauss and balance prints (≤ 1e-10 relative, round-off floor). They are asserted at their bands only, and a last-digit move there is not a finding. A covered reading that moves past its last two printed digits stops the item (Negative result).

docs.title: §9 item 446 — 2026-10-14 (example, §5.4 ramp)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-14 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, record, Done-when of another chunk or validation target. Every band is imported from the gate module, which imports them from PORT-* / TH-17 / ANS-6 modules.

EX-113 (mri:19; the runner selects mri:<n> by the %02d_ prefix, scripts/run_examples.sh:201–219, :239–240, so 19_ is mri:19; the mri: group sources the complex build, :273; no runner edit) adds three tracked files and edits nothing else: - examples/mri/19_study_tune_mode_capacitance.py; - the same-stem guide examples/mri/19_study_tune_mode_capacitance.md, with ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## Setup figure, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step and ## Related; - examples/mri/figures/mri_19_study_tune_mode_capacitance_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

The angle: what tune reads, what it ignores, and which mode it tuned. The gate checks the number against TH-17. This example adds three readings no example has; the first two are exact circuit identities (asserted), the third is a field picture (printed). 1. C comes from Im z_k only. A uniform series resistance r on all four ports (Z′ = Z + r·I) shifts every z_k by exactly r (F is unitary, F·I·F^H = I), so C_1 is unchanged; a uniform series reactance jX shifts Im z_1 and moves C_1. The PEC and solid σ = 800 Studies show the same thing physically: Re z_1 is 0.025 Ω against 5.97 Ω (≈ 240×, the solid conductor's loss), while C_1 moves only −6.98 % (:945, :2761). 2. What C_mode tunes. Adding the series capacitor 1/(jωC_1) on every port (Z_t = Z + I/(jωC_1)) cancels Im z_1 (and Im z_3, the degenerate partner) exactly, and leaves mode 2 with Im z_2 − 1/(ωC_1) < 0 (predicted ≈ 25.19 − 37.53 = −12.3 Ω, from :945). This is a circuit-layer statement at 64 MHz on one degree-1 fixture — no resonance, f₀, Q or tuning-accuracy claim (§2; ANS-7 stays 🟡). 3. The mode fields. Study.b1_plus() returns one CG1 B per port drive. Superposing them with the DFT weights v_p = conj(F[k, p]) = e^{+2πi k p/4}/2 gives the incident-wave mode-k field (S is near-circulant, off-diagonal residual 3.8e-05, so a mode-k incident vector excites mode k). Printed: |B₁⁺| and |B₁⁻| at the coil centre for k = 1 and k = 3 (one co-rotating, one counter-rotating — which is which is the e^{jωt} convention, printed, not claimed), and |B_k=2(0)| / |B_k=1(0)| (predicted ≲ 1e-2: the k = 2 transverse field has a null on the axis in the C4-symmetric limit; first measurement).

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: heavy, -n 2 (ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, asserted), complex build.
  • Cost: ≈ 10 measured (example class) / ≈ 40 predicted min: 10 fixed + ≈ 14 script + ≈ 6 windows + ≈ 6 guide + ≈ 4 censuses / journal / commit. Park if the flagged run (window 3) has not started by minute 28, or the control (window 4) by minute 38 (rule (d)). Price basis:
  • The gate's own clocks (W1 :944, :2760): pec Study 29.1 s, solid Study 33.9 s; the whole gate window 66 s.
  • This example adds: the field-keeping sweep b1_plus() triggers (_solve_port_fields, a second build + sweep of the PEC Study, ≈ 30 s — it does not reuse self.result, study.py:1683), four project_to_cg1 projections (≈ 4–8 s), the circuit arithmetic (< 1 s), the centre-point evaluation (< 1 s), the XDMF on 80 798 cells (≈ 5 s), the setup figure (≈ 10 s, flagged only), start-up and JIT (≈ 15 s).
  • Nearest analogue: mri:16 (EX-108), two Studies on this hole fixture, 76 s flagged / 75 s control at -n 2 (20261009T052039Z_EX-108.log).
  • Flagged run predicted ≈ 125 s, range [90, 280] s; control ≈ 115 s, range [80, 260] s. Runner -t 420, container timeout -k 30 420. Every window is under 10 min, so the plain runner form is used.
  • Depends on: nothing open. WF-16 step 6(a) is on main (ac947c9c). 19_ is free in examples/mri/; no row or chunk names EX-113. Independent of item 447 (EX-114, mri:20); never run beside it (both heavy).
  • Shared files. Three new paths, nothing under tests/ or src/. If anything under tests/ or src/ turns out to be needed, stop and report; do not edit it.

Imports (never restated). import tests.package.test_wf16_study_tune as g and use its names: TH17_STEP3_C_MODE_RECORD_F, KEY, _solid_study, _py_copper, _class_means, _rel_means, _record, _rel, _modal_z, s_to_z, REDUCTION_BAND, EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, CLASSES, REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM, FREQUENCY_64_HZ, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG if needed from tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_lumped_column. From src: fem_em_solver.ports.circuit.z_to_s, write_setup_figure, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership, evaluate_vector_field_parallel. Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (the mri:16 precedent). Raise if default_scalar_type is not complex. Record digits go only into an example-local REC dict, each entry commented with its log:line; never assert a record by equality. - Structural asserts at start-up: comm.size == g.ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH; g._py_copper("pec").degree == 1 and .conductor is None; g.REDUCTION_BAND is the tests.validation.test_port_lumped_rlc_termination object (is). - Example-local inputs (cited, not records): r ∈ {0.2, 1.0} Ω (0.2 Ω is the F-human ESR the refusal test uses, test_wf16_study_tune.py:108) and X = 1.0 Ω. Name them as inputs in the guide.

(1) Anchor. The gate's two Studies through the API, mirroring its tuned fixture (test_wf16_study_tune.py:139–162; pytest fixtures cannot be called — see Traps). - pec = g._py_copper("pec"); res = pec.solve(comm); t1 = pec.tune(k=1, comm=comm); t2 = pec.tune(k=2, comm=comm). Same for solid = g._solid_study(). - (R0) res.cells == ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD; _rel_means(_class_means(S), ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1[KEY]["pec"])[c] <= LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND per class. Records 80 798, 5.052e-11 / 3.878e-11 / 5.875e-11 (:944, :2765). - (I) max |t1.z_k − _modal_z(s_to_z(S, REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM))[0]| / |·| <= EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL; residual likewise; Im z_1 > 0; |C_1·ω·Im z_1 − 1| <= EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (:2769). - (a) |t1.c_mode_farad / TH17_STEP3_C_MODE_RECORD_F − 1| <= REDUCTION_BAND. Record gap −2.976552e-04 (:2773). - Records predicted equal at the printed digits (same code, width, image): cells, C_1 6.626796421e-11 F, C_2 9.873468900e-11 F, solid C_1 6.166035422e-11 F, the gaps above. A covered reading that moves past its last two printed digits stops the item (Negative result).

Example-side anchors (asserted, imported bands only). All on the PEC Study's S, in numpy; tune is read on a fresh g._py_copper("pec") Study whose result = SimpleNamespace(s_matrix=S′) (the gate's own W0 pattern, test_wf16_study_tune.py:128 — no solve, no mesh). - (ESR) a uniform resistance leaves C. For each r: S′ = z_to_s(Z + r·I, z0); |C_1(S′)/C_1(S) − 1| <= EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, and max_k |z_k′ − z_k − r| / |z_k| <= EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. Predicted ≤ 1e-12 (z_to_s ↔ s_to_z round trip). - (Tuned) C_1 cancels mode 1. Z_t = Z + I/(jωC_1), ω = pec.omega; zt = _modal_z(Z_t)[0] (direct, no S round trip); |Im zt[1]| / Im z_1 <= EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL and the same for k = 3. Printed: Im zt[2] (predicted ≈ −12.3 Ω), Re zt[1] = Re z_1.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1), the gate's, asserted: k = 2 misses the record by > REDUCTION_BAND. Record +4.894874e-01 (:2777). - (c2), the gate's, asserted: the solid Study ties to its own record (_rel(S_solid, _record(1)) <= LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND, record 9.557e-11) and misses TH-17's by > REDUCTION_BAND. Record −6.980694e-02 (:2781). - (ESR-c), example-side, asserted only as a miss: Z + jX·I moves C_1, |C_1(S_X)/C_1 − 1| > EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. Predicted X/(Im z_1 + X) = 1/38.53 ≈ 0.02596, range [0.025, 0.027] (stdlib arithmetic from :945; first measurement). No saturation: ≈ 2.6e8× the band. - (Tuned-c), example-side, asserted only as a miss: tuning with C_2 instead, |Im z_1 − 1/(ωC_2)| / Im z_1 > EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. Predicted 1 − C_1/C_2 ≈ 0.3288, range [0.32, 0.34].

Printed only (no band; a value outside its prediction is reported, with no status effect). - The z_k table for both Studies (Re, Im), C_1 / C_2 / C_3, and the solid-over-PEC ratios of Re z_1 (predicted ≈ 239) and C_1 (≈ 0.9305). - |S(fields_result) − S(result)|_max / |S|_max between the plain sweep and the field-keeping sweep (predicted ≤ 1e-12; the two are separate solves of one problem). - Mode fields (angle 3): build B_k for k ∈ {1, 2, 3} as CG1 Functions (B_k.x.array[:] = Σ_p v_p · B_p.x.array, scatter_forward). The port order is [d.port_id for d in pec.fields_result.port_definitions], asserted equal to the S row order and to sorted(b1, key=lambda p: int(p[1:])). At the origin, through evaluate_vector_field_parallel: |B₁⁺| = |B_x + jB_y|/2, |B₁⁻| = |B_x − jB_y|/2 (the b1_plus_at form, study.py:1915–1920), for k = 1, 3; and |B_2(0)|/|B_1(0)|. Per unit incident-wave mode excitation — a record, not an absolute field.

Output. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_19_study_tune_mode_capacitance_setup.png, through write_setup_figure with mri:16's call on this mesh (16_study_copper_birdcage.py:170–191): air tags hidden, phantom translucent, slice_normal=(0, 0, 1); title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. "mri:19 -- Study.tune on the exact-rectangle PEC hole F-small birdcage, four gap ports, phantom (WF-16 step 6a)". Over 600 KiB ⇒ re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. The hole route has no conductor cells: the guide says the coil is drawn as a void. - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_19_study_tune_mode_capacitance_combined.xdmf, write_xdmf_with_tags(path, msh, cell_tags, fields, comm=comm): CG1 B_mode1_real, B_mode2_real (vector, .real copies), CG1 scalars B_mode1_abs, B_mode2_abs, B1_plus_mode1, B1_minus_mode1, B1_plus_mode3 (nodal |·| in numpy on the CG1 dofs, labelled nodal in the guide). Then adopt_host_ownership(OUTPUT_DIR, comm=comm) on every rank. Only the PNG is tracked. - CSV examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_19_study_tune_mode_capacitance_modes.csv, rank 0: one row per (study, k, variant ∈ {base, r=0.2, r=1.0, X=1.0, tuned_C1, tuned_C2}) with Re_zk_ohm, Im_zk_ohm, C_k_F (blank when Im ≤ 0). - Guide. Related lists, by full filename: examples/mri/16_study_copper_birdcage.md first, then examples/mri/08_study_four_port_birdcage.md; then tests/package/test_wf16_study_tune.py, tests/validation/test_th17_birdcage_eigenmodes.py. The guide explains z_k = diag(F Z F^H) and why k = 1 / 3 are degenerate; why a uniform r cannot move C and a uniform jX can; what "C_1 cancels Im z_1" means in circuit terms and why it is not a resonance or tuning claim; a ParaView recipe (colour by B_mode1_abs and B_mode2_abs on a z = 0 slice; Glyph B_mode1_real; compare B1_plus_mode1 with B1_plus_mode3). One sentence in ## 2: ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:19 -n 2 -t 420, heavy, the measured wall time. Write ≈, never a tilde.

(3) Windows. Each one is foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, and each is one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call, nothing chained or piped. 0. Orphan check: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-113-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" and scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-113-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'". Last reading examples=109 ok=109 missing=0 broken=0, docrefs dead=0 stale=90 exit=2 (…T033627Z_EX-112-post-figures.log, …033631Z_EX-112-post-docrefs.log). Use what the pre-census reads (item 447 may land first). Exit 2 is staleness info; exit 1 is a failure. 2. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-113-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:19 -n 2 -t 420 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). Copy its emitted string for windows 3–4, adding only -T (and the flag in window 3). 3. Run of record (flagged), predicted ≈ 125 s, range [90, 280] s, of the form scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-113 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/19_study_tune_mode_capacitance.py"' (must match the dry run apart from -T and the flag). Pass: Status 0; (R0), (I), (a), (ESR), (Tuned) and the four control asserts green; the covered records as in (1); the closing "All assertions hold" line. 4. Control: git add the PNG window 3 wrote, then the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, label EX-113-control. Compare at the bands, never bitwise. 5. The guide, written from window 3's log. Then EX-113-post-figures / EX-113-post-docrefs. Write the prediction first: figures N → N + 1, missing=0 broken=0; docrefs dead=0, exit ≠ 1. Any dead reference naming mri_19_* or 19_study_tune_mode_capacitance.md fails the item. 6. git status --porcelain examples/ tests/ src/ lists exactly the three new examples/ paths. 7. Before committing, run the pre-commit leak guard on the staged logs (it runs anyway on git commit). See the leak-guard trap.

(4) Traps already paid for. - The private-leak guard (EX-112, attempts.md 2026-10-14T03:38Z). scripts/testing/check_private_leak.py refuses any staged figure sharing an 8-significant-digit prefix (MIN_SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS = 8) with a raw AED export; figures already in a tracked file at HEAD are subtracted. EX-112's two run logs were blocked by a collision on our own gel-box θ and cost the item its ✅ (demoted 🧪 for custody by the 03:00 audit). The F-small fixture has private AED counterparts (ANS-4), so: print every new value (z_k tables, ratios, mode-field readings, CSV columns echoed to stdout) at ≤ 6 significant digits; only the asserted records' own reproduced prints may carry their gate-log digits (already tracked, so subtracted). The CSV and XDMF are gitignored and are not scanned. If the guard still fires: never bypass it and never edit a log — move the flagged logs unchanged into the gitignored logs/leak-held/, commit everything else, mark item 446 BLOCKED (not ✅; a ✅ needs its run logs committed), journal the flagged log:line (never the figure) in attempts.md, and stop. - Pytest fixtures are not callable. tuned is a @pytest.fixture; copy its two-Study loop (:145–152) and use only module-level helpers. - The field-keeping solve is separate. b1_plus() builds and sweeps again into fields_result; it never sets self.result, and tune() never reads fields_result. Call solve + tune first, then b1_plus. Do not assign result on the solved Study; the circuit-variant reads use a fresh _py_copper("pec") Study (no mesh is built while result is set). - tune raises on Im z_k ≤ 0. Never call it on Z_t (Im z_1 ≈ ±round-off) or for k = 0 / 3 after result is set; read those through _modal_z directly. - Port order. Superpose in port_definitions order (the S row order); a dict-order mismatch gives a mixed-mode field that still looks plausible. Assert the order. - Rank-local values. Point evaluation through evaluate_vector_field_parallel only, points identical on every rank; raise on any point not found; numpy maxima carry initial=; no collective inside a rank == 0 branch. A rank-local exception hangs the job: Status 124 is a finding, never a retry. - The complex build. .x.array is complex; nodal magnitudes are numpy on np.abs(...); scatter_forward after assigning; no UFL comparison; name every Function, each XDMF key equal to its Function's name (EX-79). - Harness shape. Every harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, no cd … &&, no ; date / | tail, no redirect (bash_guard rule 3). ./scripts/run_examples.sh is host-side: emit it with --dry-run and pass the string to the harness; never wrap it in docker compose exec (Status 127). A docker-socket denial means stop and report the exact command string. - Timeouts and foreground. Bash timeout: 660000 on every window; container timeout -k 30 420. Spawn executors foreground, and never background a harness window (the 2026-09-01 example-runner orphan). Never raise a timeout or -n. After a kill, pgrep -c python3 first; only at 0, the orphan-.c cache sweep (daily-review.md rubric item 4) as one bare call labelled EX-113-cache-sweep. - Rule (i): no edit to the script after window 3 starts, or to the guide after window 5 starts. Check mtimes before committing.

(5) Scope. One fixture (exact-rectangle PEC hole F-small, κ off) plus the gate's solid control, degree 1, 64 MHz, -n 2. The ESR / jX / C-closure statements are circuit identities on the field-derived Z; the mode fields are incident-wave superpositions, printed. Not claimed: a resonance, f₀, Q, S₁₁ / Z_in or tuning-accuracy figure (§2; ANS-7 🟡); copper (LeontovichWall) tuning; degree 2; 10 / 128 MHz; F-human (tune refuses it); an external check. WF-16 does not move.

(6) Negative result. Report and stop. Journal in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-113-<UTC>, and mark item 446 BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)). EX-113 stays ⬜. Never widen a band, never edit tests/ or src/, never re-record from the example side. - (R0) / (I) / (a) red, or a covered record off W1 beyond its last two printed digits: an example/gate divergence or main drifted; print the first differing value beside its log:line, file a known-issues entry, park. - (ESR) or (Tuned) red: the circuit algebra or the z0 convention is not what the brief says; print the residuals and stop. - A control inside its band: mislabelled variant; stop. - The leak guard fires: BLOCKED as in Traps, not ✅. - Status 124, over 420 s, or past the park minutes: park with the last printed line. - A printed value outside its prediction (Re z_1 ratio, Im zt[2], the mode-field ratios): report it; no status effect.

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

(7) Status it can move. EX-113 ⬜ → ✅ under the §7 Done-when the review pastes in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). Census examples +1 (109 → 110 if the pre-census reads 109), broken=0; docrefs dead=0. WF-16 unchanged. No §2 sentence moves. The angle: the YAML / CLI route of tune, and what it writes. The gate shows the number is right. This example shows a user what femem run does with a tune: section: one solve; what lands in summary["tune"], in memory and on disk; how its keys tie together; what an omitted k means; that the written Touchstone alone reproduces the capacitance; and the field of the mode the file named. It differs from mri:19 in its entry point (cli.main on a file, not Study.tune in Python), in its output quantity (the summary and the .s4p, not the circuit variants), and in its field (the mode is chosen by the file's k). 1. femem run in-process, captured. cli.main(["run", str(g.TUNE_FILE), "--output-dir", str(RUN_DIR)]) is the mri:9 pattern. cli.main imports run_study_file from fem_em_solver.study_yaml at call time (cli.py:151). This is the EX-114 counting-wrapper pattern: no pytest MonkeyPatch. The wrapper is called exactly once, and rc is (0, 0) through g._rc_all. 2. The summary is the same Study's tune(). The comparison is bitwise (decided: reuse, not re-run). The captured run.study is the solved Study. run.study.tune(k=1) reads the same self.result.s_matrix with the same arithmetic. So the comparison is float.hex equality, as item 442's (I=), and needs no second solve. A re-run would compare across builds. Re-running would cost ≈ 30 s and assert a weaker identity, so it is not done. 3. The keys tie together, from the summary alone: C·2π·frequency_hz·Im z_k[k] = 1. 4. An omitted k is Study.tune's default. tune: {} parses to {"tune": {}}, and _tune_summary(run.study, {}, comm) equals the k = 1 block by hex (Study.tune(k=1) default, study.py:1016). 5. The field of the mode the file tuned. run.study.b1_plus() is a second, field-keeping build and sweep, disclosed (mri:19 measured 30.9 s, 20261014T111653Z_EX-113.log:3626). Its per-port fields are superposed with the DFT weights of the summary's k, and of k = 2 for contrast, and written to XDMF.

For benchmark-lite, unsolved: est.cells == g.ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD and est.unknowns == REC["bl_unknowns"] (570 332, :2691), exact. - (W) A price is per width. _predict divides by ranks, so est_bl.predicted_seconds · est_bl.ranks (here -n 2) equals W3's 76.65 · 8 at the record check's 1e-2. Predicted ≈ 306.6 s at -n 2; the guide says the user should not run this preset at -n 2 on that price (W3 measured 73.53 s at -n 8). (2) Negative controls. - (c1), the gate's: debug's SAR against g.WF15_DEG2_RECORD misses L0_BAND (W1 3.4937 %, :285, 3.49e7× the band). - (c2), the gate's: dev's S against g._record(2) misses LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND (W2 0.0491, :5405). - (cL) A price does not transfer between presets. est_bl.predicted_seconds / summary_debug["elapsed_s"] lies outside [1/BRACKET, BRACKET] (the gate's (c5) shape; at -n 8 it read 5.35, :2692; at -n 2 the width law makes it ≈ 21, so no ceiling binds). This is the control for an estimator that returns one constant. - (cW) the -n 8 price applied at -n 2 unscaled (76.65 s against est_bl.predicted_seconds) misses the record check's 1e-2 by ≈ 75 %: the width term is not optional.

Printed only (no band). The price table, one row per preset, at ≤ 4 significant digits: degree, cells, unknowns, rows_used, predicted seconds and peak GiB, and for the two run presets the measured elapsed_s, ratio, and summed peak RSS (report_peak_rss); the cli.main wall times; the two output directories' file listings (names and byte sizes, never contents).

Output. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_22_presets_priced_then_run_setup.png on the captured debug run's mesh (run.result.mesh / run.result.cell_tags), mri:9's call (air hidden, sphere translucent, slice_normal=(0, 0, 1)). Each XDMF key equals its Function's name. dev's S is not written. - Run and estimate directories under the gitignored examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_22_*. Only the PNG is tracked. - Guide. Walk the three presets (what each reproduces, at which degree and width), femem check, femem run --estimate (what it prints, that it writes nothing, that its price is for the width it runs at), the price table, why benchmark-lite is priced but not run at -n 2, and the W3 measurement at -n 8 cited by log. Related by full filename: examples/mri/12_study_estimate.md, examples/mri/09_study_from_yaml.md, examples/mri/21_femem_run_tune_section.md, examples/presets/debug.yaml, examples/presets/dev.yaml, examples/presets/benchmark-lite.yaml, tests/package/test_wf4_presets.py. (3) Windows. Each one foreground, Bash timeout: 660000, one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. 0. (4) Traps already paid for. - Rank-0 stdout. femem check's family: line and --estimate's name: repr lines print on rank 0 only; parse on rank 0 and bcast before any every-rank assert (EX-115 attempt 1, 20261015T033235Z_EX-115.log:925, AssertionError: ((0, 0), '')). - Dict subscripts. summary is a dict; est is a frozen dataclass; g._parse returns {name: [raw, …]} (a list per key); rows_used is a tuple. (5) Scope. Three presets at -n 2, two solved (degree 1), one priced only (degree 2). Not claimed: a --preset flag or presets in the wheel; the price at any width other than the one run; a memory claim (peaks printed only — 471b's benchmark-lite peak was 18.27 predicted vs 12.86 measured); a predictive degree-1 estimator (P1 / P3 are the debug / dev fixtures themselves, disclosed in the gate's docstring); benchmark-lite's S at -n 2; a stable schema; any external check. (6) Negative result. Report and stop; journal in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-116-<UTC>, mark item 488 BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)). EX-116 stays ⬜. Never widen a band or BRACKET, never edit tests/, src/ or a preset. - *(Pd) / (R-) red, or a price off W1 / W2's 2-decimal print: example/gate divergence or main drifted (e.g. a PRICE_TABLE edit); print both, file a known-issues entry, park. - (P) outside ×2: a wall-clock reading under host load — report the ratio and the concurrent load (uptime), do not retry in-slot; the review decides. - (E) red: the estimate and the run built different meshes — a finding about Study.estimate; stop. - (W) red: the width law changed; print both and stop. - (cL) / (cW) inside their bands: a blind estimator or comparator; stop. - Leak guard: BLOCKED as in Traps.

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

(7) Status it can move. EX-116 ⬜ → ✅ under the §7 Done-when the review pastes in the same commit as this item (rule (j)); census examples +1, broken=0; docrefs dead=0. The angle: the clinical-scale fixture as a user sees it, and the box as a load. The gate proves the sheets and the box are right. This example puts the whole fixture in ParaView with its 64 sheets and the box interface as facet tags, and adds two box readings the gate does not make: the box's surface (its six planar faces recovered from the tag-3 / tag-2 interface) and its reach in the bore (the farthest box vertex from the axis is the CAD circumradius the generator exported), so a user can see the gel's clearance from the rungs. It differs from mesh:12 in scale, shield, conductor route (hole, not solid) and load shape, and from mat:19 in that the box sits in a coil.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: heavy, -n 4 (asserted), real build, mesh only.
  • Width choice. -n 4 is the measured-fastest window (339 s; gmsh is serial on rank 0, so width buys only the post-gmsh distribution) and the only width where owned and local-copy facet counts differ (excess 5, GEO-38.md:404), which is what the (cG) control shows. -n 2 measured 529 s under host load (GEO-38.md:401) and would leave < 60 s of headroom.

Park if window 3 has not started by minute 30 (rule (d)). Price basis: W3's build 335.4 s at -n 4; plus the setup figure on 1.15 M cells (unmeasured at this size — mesh:12 rendered ≈ 0.5 M cells inside a 196 s run, 20260906T033712Z_EX-51.log; predict 30–120 s), the combined XDMF with a DG0 field and two facet tag sets (≈ 20–40 s), the analysis (owned numpy sums, < 10 s), start-up (≈ 10 s). A host-loaded build like W2's (+160 s) plus a slow figure would overrun, so the window runs only on a quiet host (window 0). Because the range reaches ≈ 10 minutes, the window must use §5.1's durable-capture idiom (PROJECT_PLAN.md:1034–1037): container-side output to /workspace/logs/EX-117-raw.log, [capture] rc=$rc appended, cat, then ; exit $rc — copied verbatim, inside the container's quoted command, never as a host-side redirect.
  • No unflagged control re-run. The template asks for one only when retrofitting a figure (example-runner.md item 6); a second ≈ 7-minute build would not fit the slot. The setup figure renders after the build timer is captured, so the printed build time is not polluted.
  • Depends on: nothing. GEO-38 steps 1a and 2 are on main. Never run beside any heavy window or the 02:00 xl / xxl window (the W2 build lost 160 s to host load).
  • Shared files. Three new paths, nothing under tests/ or src/. If anything there turns out to be needed, stop and report.

docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-118 (mri:23) is opened 2026-10-15 by the 18:00 daily review under daily-review.md step 5. It is the §5.4 ramp from WF-16 step 12 (§10 U53, §9 item 472, landed 24088335; the (K0) re-band ratified by the same review, WF-16.md § "Review ruling 2026-10-15 18:00"). - Base. tests/package/test_wf16_study_tune_f_human_copper.py (the gate module) on the copper (Leontovich, σ = 5.8e7 S/m) F-human hole LumpedPortDrive Study, degree 1, 64 MHz, κ off. The code is _study_tune_ring (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:1065), reached from _study_tune (:1033), on ports/ring_modes.py. - Run of record. docs/testing/logs/20261015T213534Z_WF-16-s12-W1.log (heavy, -n 8, 9 passed in 203.4 s, :7383): cells 369 387, mesh 106.5 s, sweep 93.4 s (:7343), 9.765 GiB summed peak (:7344); (R0) S vs the stored H12c matrix 1.632e-12 (:7346); (I) 0.000e+00 against ring_mode_rows (:7359), z₀ / z₁ / z₂ and off-block 4.195925e-03 (:7361–7364); (a) C_mode 1.181185799070e-10 F, gap −3.544942e-13 (:7375); (c1) k = 2 C 7.881746394502e-11 F, gap −3.327259e-01 (:7380).

Gap (grep at drafting: tune(, ring_mode, F-human, f_human, C_mode over examples/). - mri:19 (EX-113) calls Study.tune from Python on the four-port F-small (4-point DFT read). mri:21 (EX-115) runs a four-port tune: YAML. Neither touches a 32-port ring. - mri:17 / mri:18 drive the copper F-human at a fixed C_in through test-module helpers; neither reads a C_mode from the 32×32 or calls Study.tune. - ports:20 reads birdcage eigenmodes on a ring fixture outside the Study. No example imports the gate module or reaches _study_tune_ring. - The angle: the first 32-port tune through the Study, at human scale. New geometry for tune (F-human, two 16-slot rings), new read (the k-block of W Z Wᴴ, ring-antisymmetric eigenvalue), and a new field (the 32-port k = 1 ring pattern superposed from kept drives, not mri:19's 4-point DFT).

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-15 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, record, Done-when of another chunk or validation target. Every band is imported from the gate module, which imports it from the PORT-* / MAT-* modules, or from a src constant already used the same way.

EX-118 (mri:23; the runner selects mri:<n> by the %02d_ prefix glob, scripts/run_examples.sh; mri: sources the complex build; no runner edit) adds three tracked files and edits nothing else: - examples/mri/23_f_human_study_tune_ring.py; - the same-stem guide examples/mri/23_f_human_study_tune_ring.md, with ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## Setup figure, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step and ## Related; - examples/mri/figures/mri_23_f_human_study_tune_ring_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

Collision check (the executor repeats it before writing): ls examples/mri/23_* is empty and no §7 row or chunk file names EX-118 or mri:23 other than this one (EX-116 holds mri:22; EX-117 is a meshing example). If 23_ is taken when the slot starts, stop and report; never renumber in-slot.

The field route (decided: one extra factorisation on the kept mesh, no re-mesh). The F-human LumpedPortDrive result keeps neither fields nor the factor (study.py:656–676: fields=None, solver=None), _solve_port_fields refuses any non-four-port geometry (:1735–1736), and LumpedPortDrive has no _b1_plus_port_study hook (:1922–1926), so study.b1_plus() raises on this Study. No field of this Study exists without a second factorisation; the cheapest is to re-sweep on the objects the result already holds — res.problem, res.port_definitions, res.specs, res.facet_tags, res.conductor_terms — with keep_fields=True, the argument list of _study_solve_ports (:646–653) copied verbatim plus keep_fields=True. That saves the ≈ 106 s rebuild mri:19 / mri:21 paid through b1_plus(). Rejected: (i) running the field-keeping sweep first and assigning its result to study.result — saves ≈ 95 s but the anchor would no longer be the gate's own study.solve → tune route; (ii) a TwoPortQuadratureDrive(C_mode, esr_ohm=0) Study for "the tuned field" — a lossless drive at the mode's own capacitance is ungated (U36 gated r = 0.2 Ω at C_in), and it re-meshes.

Executor: example-runner; it does not spawn agents. Class: example. Tier: heavy, -n 8 (g.RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, asserted), complex build; runner -t 590, container timeout -k 30 590; every window < 10 min, so the plain runner form.

Cost: ≈ 9 measured (example class median) / ≈ 50 predicted min: 10 fixed + ≈ 12 script + ≈ 15 windows (two ≈ 6.5 min runs) + ≈ 6 guide + ≈ 5 censuses / leak guard / commit. Park if window 3 has not started by minute 25, or window 4 by minute 35 (rule (d)). Price basis: - Start-up, import, JIT: ≈ 25 s (mri:18's flagged 241 s on the same mesh and width included it). - study.solve: mesh 106.5 s + sweep 93.4 s (20261015T213534Z_WF-16-s12-W1.log:7343). - Two tune reads and the npz read: < 2 s. - The field-keeping sweep on the kept problem: one factorisation (28.27 s solve + 6.58 s post) plus 31 held drives at ≈ 2 s (20261006T170222Z_WF-12-step3-a2-W1.log:6354, :6359): ≈ 95 s. Allow ≈ 20 s if keep_fields re-hashes a form. - Two superpose_drives and two CG1 B projections (project_to_cg1(magnetic_flux_density_from_e(…))) on 369 387 cells: ≈ 15–25 s. Combined XDMF: ≈ 10 s. Setup figure (flagged only): ≈ 20 s. - Flagged run predicted ≈ 390 s, range [300, 520] s; control ≈ 370 s, range [280, 500] s. Memory: ≈ 10–14 GiB summed (W1 9.77 GiB, :7344, plus 32 kept N1curl phasors ≈ 0.3 GiB); ≤ 20 GiB if the first factor is still live, which the trap below prevents. - Depends on: nothing open. WF-16 step 12 is on main (24088335). It reads g.NPZ_PATH (the stored H12c 32×32 under the gitignored logs/wf12/): absent ⇒ stop, BLOCKED, never a re-solve. Never beside another heavy window (EX-116 / EX-117 included). - Shared files. Three new paths; nothing under tests/ or src/. If anything under tests/ or src/ turns out to be needed, stop and report; do not edit it.

Imports (never restated). - import tests.package.test_wf16_study_tune_f_human_copper as g and use: _study, _rows, _residual, RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, NPZ_PATH, HOLE_CELL_RECORD, COPPER_SIGMA, DEGREE, FREQUENCY_HZ, WF12_STEP3_C_MODE_CU_F, WF12_STEP3_C2_CU_F, WF12_STEP3_OFF_BLOCK, WF12_STEP3_LAMBDA_ANTI, REDUCTION_BAND, REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL, EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND, C_MODE_CU_PF, C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF, study_mod, LumpedPortDrive. - Assert g.REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL is tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (1e-6) — two constants carry that name (EX-114's 18:00 ruling); the PORT-19 one (1e-12) is never imported. Assert g.REDUCTION_BAND is tests.validation.test_port_lumped_rlc_termination.REDUCTION_BAND. - From src: run_n_port_sparameter_sweep (fem_em_solver.ports.sparameters), superpose_drives (fem_em_solver.ports.superposition, POST-6 ✅), _dft_matrix, _canonical_permutation, ring_port_map_from_names, k_blocks, antisymmetric_eigenpair (fem_em_solver.ports.ring_modes), s_to_z, magnetic_flux_density_from_e, project_to_cg1 (post.faraday, the WF-6 step 1d estimator Study.b1_plus uses), evaluate_vector_field_parallel, write_setup_figure, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership, report_peak_rss. PHANTOM_CELL_TAG / CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG as mri:18 imports them. - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path. Raise if default_scalar_type is not complex. Record digits go only into an example-local REC dict, each entry commented with its log:line.

Structural asserts at start-up. comm.size == g.RECORD_RANK_WIDTH; study = g._study(); study.degree == 1; isinstance(study.conductor, g.study_mod.LeontovichWall) and study.conductor.sigma_s_per_m == g.COPPER_SIGMA; study.geometry.as_hole is True; study.result is None.

Record checks (the 2026-10-14 10:30 ruling's form, adopted in its own words). cells exact. Each string record compared at a relative 10^-(d−2), d its printed significant digits: C_mode 1.181185799070e-10 F and the k = 2 C 7.881746394502e-11 F (d = 13 ⇒ 1e-11); the (c1) gap −3.327259e-01 (d = 7 ⇒ 1e-5); z₀ / z₁ / z₂ and the off-block at their printed digits (:7361–7364). Excluded: the (R0) rel and the (a) gap (round-off readings at or below LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND) — asserted at their bands only and printed beside :7346 / :7375. A record off by more than its tolerance stops the item.

(1) Anchor (U53's gate, imported). res = study.solve(comm); then t1 = study.tune(k=1, comm=comm), t2 = study.tune(k=2, comm=comm); assert study.result is res (no re-solve). Then: - (R0) res.cells == g.HOLE_CELL_RECORD == npz cells; npz read on rank 0, bcast (the gate fixture's pattern, gate module :215–219); g._residual(S_study[p][:, p], s32_npz) <= g.REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL with p mapping the Study's port order to the npz order. Prior 1.632e-12 (:7346). - (I) t1.c_mode_farad against g._rows(S, names, t1.c_mode_farad)["c_mode_f"], t2 against ["c_k2_f"], t1.off_diagonal_residual against ["off_block"], each ≤ g.EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL; |t1.c_mode_farad · 2π · t1.frequency_hz · Im t1.z_k[1] − 1| <= g.EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. Prior 0.000e+00 (:7359). - (a) |t1.c_mode_farad / g.WF12_STEP3_C_MODE_CU_F − 1| <= g.REDUCTION_BAND. Prior −3.544942e-13 (:7375). Printed beside: against C_MODE_CU_PF (4-decimal, −1.701e-07 prior) and the npz's own c_mode.

Example-side anchors (asserted, imported bands only). - (W) The drive is the k-th ring-antisymmetric pattern. For k ∈ {1, 2}: in canonical order (_canonical_permutation(ring_port_map_from_names(names))), weights a_(j, bottom) = e^{+2πi jk/16}/(4√2), a_(j, top) = −a_(j, bottom), mapped back to the sweep's port_ids order. Assert _dft_matrix() @ a_canonical equals +1/√2 at index k, −1/√2 at 16 + k and 0 elsewhere, ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (abs). This is the example's own name → slot map checked against src's. - (S=) The field is the field of the S the tune read. fres = run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(res.problem, res.port_definitions, lumped_sheet_ports=res.specs, lumped_sheet_facet_tags=res.facet_tags, degree=study.degree, keep_fields=True, **({"extra_bilinear_terms": res.conductor_terms} if res.conductor_terms else {})). Assert fres.port_ids == [d.port_id for d in res.port_definitions] and g._residual(fres.s_matrix, res.s_matrix) <= g.REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL; predicted ≤ 1e-14 (same problem, code, partition; mri:19 read 1.681e-15 across a rebuild, 20261014T111653Z_EX-113.log:3626). Then study.tune(k=1) once more equals t1 by float.hex (study.result is res still). - (P) Passivity of the superposed drive. d1 = superpose_drives(fres, a1): d1.accepted_power_w >= 0 and <= d1.available_power_w · (1 + EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL) — σ_max(S) ≤ 1 (the gate printed 0.999993339 at :7346) read through POST-6's gated ½aᴴ(I − SᴴS)a. Same for d2.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1), the gate's, asserted only as a miss: |t2.c_mode_farad / g.WF12_STEP3_C_MODE_CU_F − 1| > g.REDUCTION_BAND; backing :7380 (−33.27 %, 332.7× the band). Printed: t2 against g.WF12_STEP3_C2_CU_F. - (cW), the pattern's own: the k = 2 weights fail (W)'s k = 1 target (their transform has 0 at index 1), asserted as > 0.5 in the max-abs gap; this shows (W) reads k. - (K) refusals, no mesh, before the solve: study.tune(k=0) and tune(k=3) raise ValueError, tune(k=True) raises TypeError, and study.result is None afterwards (study.py:1077–1081; the gate's (K0) without its monkeypatch, which is test-only — these raise before any build).

Printed only (no band; a value outside its prediction is reported, with no status effect). - z_k for k = 0…8 (Re / Im at ≤ 6 significant digits), C_k = 1/(ω Im z_k) where Im > 0, and the ring-antisymmetric fraction of each block's chosen eigenvector (antisymmetric_eigenpair(...)[1], predicted ≥ 0.99 for k = 1, 2), beside :7361–7364 for k ≤ 2. - t1.c_mode_farad against C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF (≈ −0.106 %, :7375), labelled "a different quantity (the r = 0.2 Ω in-model root), not a tuning error". - Centre (origin) |B|, |B₁⁺|, |B₁⁻| per volt-wave for the k = 1 and k = 2 drives and |B_2(0)| / |B_1(0)|, at 6 digits (predicted |B_2(0)| / |B_1(0)| ≪ 1: k = 2 has a centre null). The accepted power of each drive. - Mesh / sweep / field-sweep / projection / XDMF wall times at 1 decimal; report_peak_rss summed.

Output. - Setup figure on res.mesh / res.cell_tags, mri:18's call (air hidden, phantom translucent, slice_normal=(0, 0, 1)); title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. "mri:23 -- Study.tune on the 32-port copper F-human hole birdcage (Leontovich, degree 1), phantom (WF-16 step 12)". The hole route draws the coil as a void; the guide says so. Over 600 KiB ⇒ re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_23_f_human_study_tune_ring_combined.xdmf, write_xdmf_with_tags(path, res.mesh, res.cell_tags, fields, comm=comm). Fields: CG1 B_mode1_real (vector, .real); CG1 scalars B_mode1_abs, B1_plus_mode1, B1_minus_mode1, B_mode2_abs (nodal |·| in numpy, labelled nodal in the guide). Each XDMF key equals its Function's name. Then adopt_host_ownership(OUTPUT_DIR, comm=comm). - Guide. Related, by full filename: examples/mri/19_study_tune_mode_capacitance.md first, then examples/mri/18_f_human_four_port_quadrature.md, examples/mri/17_f_human_tuned_quadrature_b1_sar.md, examples/mri/21_femem_run_tune_section.md; then tests/package/test_wf16_study_tune_f_human_copper.py. It explains: the 32 ring-gap ports P17…P48 and their (slot, ring) map; why the read is a 2×2 per k (two rings) rather than mri:19's scalar; the ring-antisymmetric eigenvalue and C = 1/(ω Im z_k); why k = 2 is not the birdcage mode; why the field costs one extra factorisation here and none of a re-mesh; that the field is the incident-wave k-pattern with every port at z₀ = 50 Ω, not the field of a coil tuned with C_mode on every gap. ParaView recipe: B_mode1_abs vs B_mode2_abs on a z = 0 slice, Glyph B_mode1_real, B1_plus_mode1 against B1_minus_mode1. States plainly: a lossless mode read at 64 MHz, degree 1, one fixture — not a tuning, resonance, f₀, Q or compliance claim.
