Angle. mat:19's box is heated by P32's end-weighted source q = Q[1 − cos(πx/A)]. The source is zero at the centre and 2Q at the ±x ends, like end-ring SAR. It is handed to the solvers three ways on step 3's m = 4 rung at P2: UFL, DG0 cell average and P2 nodal interpolant. P2, the form that carries forward, runs steady and also by CN to t*. Three things are new to the examples: - the fields in ParaView; - the hot-end profile along the x centre line; - the face-heat split under this source against the uniform source on the same mesh.

Imports (never restated). _REPO_ROOT goes on sys.path.

Module Names Lines tests/validation/test_mat21_box_p2_source_fem.py STEP7_S1 :68 test_mat21_box_dg0_source_fem.py STEP6_S1 :70 test_mat21_box_separable_fem.py M4, PROFILES, SEP_TERMS, STEP3_M4, _sep_ex, _sep_trans_ex, _sep_floor, _point_vals :55–58, :74, :82, :90, :100 test_mat21_box_fem_p2.py DEGREE, CMP_DEGREE, QDEG_P, _dofs_pred, _exact_p, _rel_p, _rung_p :77–79, :86, :91, :108, :131 test_mat21_box_fem.py T_STAR, V_BOX, _steady_ex, _interior_chi :72, :74, :78, :111 test_mat21_box_closed_form.py A_BOX, Q, H, K — test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py _cell_average_dg0_tag, H_GEL, K_GEL, N_MAIN, T_INF :124

Records. Record digits go only in an example-local REC dict, each with its log:line in 20261016T033407Z_MAT-21-step8-W2-p2-source.log. They are printed beside the readings and never asserted by equality:

(4) Traps already paid for. - XDMF: dolfinx's write_function needs the mesh's degree, so interpolate every P2 field into P1 first (examples/mri/14_study_sar_and_b1.py:367). - Complex build: no UFL comparison, max_value or sqrt (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). The source spans a full period, and neither the source nor the cell average carries metadata (MAT-21.md:1355). - After status 124 or a kill: run pgrep -c python3 first, then the orphan-.c sweep (daily-review.md rubric 4) labelled EX-119-cache-sweep. - Runner: run_examples.sh runs host-side. Never background a window. - Rule (i): no script edit after window 3 starts, and no guide edit after window 5 starts. - Host speed: on 10-15/16 the host ran ≈ 1.4–2× slow. If the run of record approaches 590 s, that is a kill, not a result: report it.

(5) Scope boundary. One analytic source on the m = 4 rung at P2, -n 2. Not claimed: - a coil or EM SAR, or whether a coil SAR can be P2-interpolated (P33 / C6); - the exact series of the delivered DG0 source; - any h-rate or other rung; - F2182 compliance, perfusion, a container wall, or an external check.

MAT-21 does not move.

(6) What a negative result means. Report and stop: journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-119-<UTC>, and mark item 493 BLOCKED in the same commit. Never widen a band or edit tests/ or src/. - A gate anchor red: main has drifted from the gate. Print the first differing value beside its log:line and file a known-issues entry. - (F0) or (F1) red: a finding about the face tagging. docs.title: EX-120 — mri:24, tune then load: Study.tune(k=1)'s C_mode on three gap sheets through CapacitorSheets, the reduced network equals the circuit reduction, and the field of the loaded coil
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-120 (mri:24) is opened 2026-10-16 by the 10:30 daily review under daily-review.md step 5. It is the §5.4 ramp from WF-16 step 6(b) (§10 U52 = U25(b), §9 item 463, DONE 2026-10-15; accepted with the drafter's reading by WF-16.md § "Review ruling 2026-10-15 03:00 (items 463, 472)"), with WF-16 step 10 (§10 U37, §9 item 373, DONE 2026-10-11) as the gate of the CapacitorSheets API and of the field-side power identity on a capacitor-loaded Study. - Base. tests/package/test_wf16_study_tune_capacitors.py (the item-463 gate module) on the exact-rectangle PEC hole F-small Study (FourPortBirdcageGeometry(as_hole=True, strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION), conductor=None, degree 1, 64 MHz, κ off, -n 2). The code is CapacitorSheets (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:690–731), dispatched through the hook in _study_solve_ports (:614–618) to _study_solve_capacitor_sheets (:747–847), and _study_tune (:1019–1062). - Run of record. docs/testing/logs/20261015T201110Z_WF-16-s6b-W1.log (heavy by ceiling, -n 2, 9 passed in 67.6 s, :976; Elapsed 69 s, :983): S0 cells 80 798, 29.8 s, z_k (:939); C₁ 6.626796421e-11 F, C₂ 9.873468900e-11 F (:940); S_A 6.6 s on the cached mesh (:941); (R0) 5.052e-11 / 3.878e-11 / 5.875e-11 (:949); (a′) −2.976552e-04 (:950); (I-A) 1.391811e-05, S_A S₁₁ −2.787323415e-01 + 9.590409206e-01j (:954); (c1) 3.2883e-01 (:970); (c2) 3.5268e-01 (:971); field-side Z_in(P1) + zc at C_mode 4.988020e-02 + 1.071628e-02j Ω (:973, printed in the gate). - The field-side gate. docs/testing/logs/20261011T202050Z_WF-16-s10-W1.log (item 373, copper twin, C = C_F, r = 0.2 Ω): the (P) power identity on the Route-A Study's own problem through run_lumped_sheet_port_case(…, return_fields=True), residual 1.328e-12 ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (:992); (Z) the Study's reduced S against a fresh-factor direct solve on the same problem ≤ 9.122e-16 against LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND (:986–989).

Gap (grep at drafting: CapacitorSheets, all_port_definitions, capacitor_impedance_ohm, .tune( over examples/**/*.py). - No example constructs CapacitorSheets or reads a CapacitorStudyResult. .tune( appears only in mri:19, mri:21 and mri:23. - mri:19 (EX-113) "tunes" circuit-side only: Z + I/(jωC₁) in numpy on the untuned 4×4; its fields are the matched-port DFT mode patterns from Study.b1_plus(), with every port at 50 Ω. mri:21 runs the same read from YAML. mri:23 reads the 32-port ring; its own brief says the field it writes is not the field of a coil with C_mode on its gaps. - mri:05 (EX-78) does solve a capacitor-loaded F-small coil in-model and write its field, but outside the Study, on ANS-7's κ-corrected ragged-sheet copper hole mesh, with C = C_F as an input. mri:16 (EX-108) runs the copper power identity on the 50 Ω Study's problem, with no capacitors. - The angle: the first example that places capacitors in the solved model through the public Study API. It feeds the C_mode that Study.tune computed in the same run back into CapacitorSheets, on exact rectangles with κ off. It shows that the in-model reduced network equals the circuit reduction (PORT-22's circuit = field identity), and it writes the field of the loaded coil. A loaded Study refuses b1_plus() and keeps no fields (study.py:826–827), so the example also shows the one extra solve that gets that field, and the field-side checks that tie it to the S the identity read.

docs.title: §9 item 495 — 2026-10-16 (example, §5.4 ramp from WF-16 steps 6(b) / 10)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-16 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, record, Done-when of another chunk or validation target. Every band is imported from the gate modules, which import it from the PORT-* validation modules.

EX-120 (mri:24; the runner selects mri:<n> by the %02d_ prefix glob in scripts/run_examples.sh; mri: sources the complex build; no runner edit) adds three tracked files and edits nothing else: - examples/mri/24_study_tune_then_capacitor_sheets.py; - the same-stem guide examples/mri/24_study_tune_then_capacitor_sheets.md, with ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## Setup figure, ## 2. How to run it, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step and ## Related (mri:19's order); - examples/mri/figures/mri_24_study_tune_then_capacitor_sheets_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

Collision check (the executor repeats it before writing). ls examples/mri/24_* is empty, and no §7 row or chunk file other than this one names EX-120 or mri:24 (checked at drafting; EX-119 holds mat:20). If 24_ is taken when the slot starts, stop and report. Never renumber in-slot.

ESR (decided: no ESR run; lossless only, labelled lossless). The capacitor-ESR binding ruling (operator 2026-10-06, PROJECT_PLAN.md:3829–3848) scopes r = 0.2 Ω to "new steps and fixtures"; "lossless-C results stay valid as records, labelled lossless" (:3843). This example re-runs item 463's lossless record on its own fixture and adds no fixture. An ESR run was rejected for three reasons, none of them price (a copper pair would add only ≈ 60 s): - (i) No anchor on this fixture. Item 373's r = 0.2 Ω anchors are on the copper Leontovich Study at C_F, ANS-7's input C, not tune's C_mode. Its per-sheet (I) is at :979–982 and its (P) at :992. Its Route-A reading at r = 0.2 was printed only (:984). A PEC + C_mode + r = 0.2 run would therefore pair a gated read with an ungated load. - (ii) No single (conductor, degree) pair carries both gates. The copper Study.tune is gated only at degree 2 (items 445 / 452). Item 373's ESR gate is at degree 1 only. "Tune then load with ESR" on copper would pair an ungated read with a gated one. - (iii) The ruling's own exclusion. "r never re-reads or rescues" a lossless record (:3844).

The guide says the run is lossless and names the ruling. A copper CapacitorSheets(C_F, 0.2, …) example built on item 373's anchors alone is a separate candidate (reply, open question 2).

The field route (decided: one extra solve on the loaded Study's kept problem, no re-mesh). CapacitorStudyResult keeps fields=None, solver=None (study.py:826–827), and Study.b1_plus() on a CapacitorSheets Study raises TypeError before any mesh (_solve_port_fields, :1744–1745; item 373's (K), tests/package/test_wf16_study_capacitor_sheets.py:131–132). The field is therefore solved once more on the objects the result holds, with item 373's (P) call copied verbatim (test_wf16_study_capacitor_sheets.py:248–251): run_lumped_sheet_port_case(resA.problem, resA.all_port_definitions, resA.specs, facet_tags=resA.facet_tags, driven_port_id="P1", verbose=False, return_fields=True, extra_bilinear_terms=resA.conductor_terms, degree=resA.degree). On the PEC hole resA.conductor_terms is None (_conductor_setup, study.py:2022–2026; asserted).

Rejected alternatives: - (a) Re-assembling the loaded network by hand with dataclasses.replace on a 50 Ω Study's specs. That is item 463's trap ("do not build a reduced Study by hand"). - (b) A field-keeping LumpedPortDrive sweep with the drives superposed into the loaded state. That is a field-level identity no gate asserts. - (c) The gate's FourPortBirdcageGeometry.build monkeypatch cache. It is test-side machinery and has no place in a user-facing API example. The example pays two real builds (≈ 22 s each), and its combined XDMF holds only fields on S_A's mesh.

Executor: example-runner; it does not spawn agents. Class: example. Tier: heavy by ceiling, -n 2 (g.ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, asserted), complex build. The runner takes -t 420 (mri:19's) and the container timeout -k 30 420. Every window is under 10 min, so the plain runner form is used and no durable capture is needed (§5.1).

Cost: ≈ 8 measured (example class median, EX-119.md ruling 2026-10-16 03:00) / ≈ 40 predicted min: 10 fixed + ≈ 12 script + ≈ 5 windows (two ≈ 2 min runs, dry run, censuses) + ≈ 6 guide + ≈ 4 leak guard / commit + ≈ 3 spare. Park if window 3 has not started by minute 28, or window 4 by minute 36 (rule (d)). Price basis: - Start-up, import, JIT, prints: ≈ 12 s. mri:19's 98 s run less its two Study solves and its field sweep, 20261014T111653Z_EX-113.log:3608, :3626, :3637. - S0 = g._study(LumpedPortDrive()) solve: mesh 22.0 s + sweep 6.6 s (20261014T004318Z_WF-16-s6-W1.log:944); the gate read 29.8 s (20261015T201110Z_WF-16-s6b-W1.log:939). The two tune reads: < 0.1 s. - SA = g._study(CapacitorSheets(C_mode, 0.0, on=("P2", "P3", "P4"))) solve: a real rebuild ≈ 22 s plus the one-drive reduced solve 6.6 s (:941) ≈ 29 s. - Two fresh-factor single-drive solves on resA.problem (tuned and open-gap): ≈ 6 s each, like the Route-A Study's own single drive (:941). The (P) assemblies take ≈ 2 s. - Two DG0 → CG1 B projections on 80 798 cells take ≈ 1–2 s each; mri:19 ran four inside its 30.9 s field sweep (20261014T111653Z_EX-113.log:3626). The combined XDMF takes ≈ 3 s. The setup figure (flagged run only) takes ≈ 15 s. - Flagged run predicted ≈ 105 s, range [70, 220] s; control ≈ 90 s, range [60, 200] s. Memory: ≈ 2–4 GiB summed at this mesh and width (report_peak_rss printed; > 8 GiB is reported). - Depends on: nothing open. Items 373 and 463 are on main. Never run beside another heavy window. - Shared files. Three new paths; nothing under tests/ or src/. If anything under tests/ or src/ turns out to be needed, stop and report; do not edit it.

Imports (never restated). - import tests.package.test_wf16_study_tune_capacitors as g and use: _study, _phantom, PORTS, _relf, CapacitorSheets, LumpedPortDrive, REDUCTION_BAND, LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND, EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM, TH17_STEP3_C_MODE_RECORD_F, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD, ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH, CLASSES, _class_means, FREQUENCY_64_HZ, reduce_terminated_ports, s_to_z, _modal_z. Never import or call the s6b fixture or any test_* name. - from tests.validation.test_birdcage_power_identity import DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, _sheet_field_dissipation_w, _source_power_w, item 373's own import (tests/package/test_wf16_study_capacitor_sheets.py:58–62). - Assert g.REDUCTION_BAND is tests.validation.test_port_lumped_rlc_termination.REDUCTION_BAND and g.LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND is tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_four_port.LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. - From src: run_lumped_sheet_port_case (fem_em_solver.ports.lumped); _power_waves (fem_em_solver.ports.sparameters:72, the Study's own S definition, study.py:812–818); magnetic_flux_density_from_e, project_to_cg1 (fem_em_solver.post.faraday, the WF-6 step 1d estimator that Study.b1_plus uses); evaluate_vector_field_parallel; write_setup_figure; write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership; report_peak_rss (fem_em_solver.utils.instrumentation). PHANTOM_CELL_TAG as mri:19 imports it (tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_lumped_column). - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path. Raise if default_scalar_type is not complex. Record digits go only into an example-local REC dict, each entry commented with its log:line.

Structural asserts at start-up. comm.size == g.ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH. Then s0 = g._study(g.LumpedPortDrive()) with s0.degree == 1, s0.conductor is None, s0.geometry.as_hole is True and s0.result is None. Finally float(s0.excitation.z0_ohm) == g.REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM.

Record checks (the 2026-10-14 10:30 ruling's form, adopted in its own words). cells exact (80 798, :939). Each string record is compared at a relative 10^-(d−2), where d is its number of printed significant digits: - C₁ 6.626796421e-11 F and C₂ 9.873468900e-11 F (:940), d = 10 ⇒ 1e-8; - z₁ = 2.500348022e-02 + 3.752636761e+01j Ω (:939), per component, d = 10 ⇒ 1e-8; - (a′) −2.976552e-04 (:950) and (I-A) 1.391811e-05 (:954), d = 7 ⇒ 1e-5; - S_A S₁₁ −2.787323415e-01 + 9.590409206e-01j (:954), |ΔS|/|S| at d = 10 ⇒ 1e-8; - (c1) 3.2883e-01 (:970) and (c2) 3.5268e-01 (:971), d = 5 ⇒ 1e-3.

Excluded: the (R0) class-mean rels (round-off readings well under LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND). They are asserted at their band only and printed beside :949. The Z_in(P1) + zc reading (:973) is a cancellation of two ≈ 37.5 Ω reactances, so it is printed beside, never compared. The S0 and S_A meshes are two real builds here, whereas the gate shared one cached mesh. A rebuild reproduced the 4×4 to 1.681e-15 (20261014T111653Z_EX-113.log:3626), which moves the 1.4e-5 (I-A) residual by ≈ 1e-10 relative, far inside its 1e-5 record tolerance. A record off by more than its tolerance stops the item.

(1) Anchor (item 463's gate, imported). res0 = s0.solve(comm); t1 = s0.tune(k=1, comm=comm); t2 = s0.tune(k=2, comm=comm); assert s0.result is res0. Then: - (R0) res0.cells == g.ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD; g._class_means(res0.s_matrix) against g.ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1["64"]["pec"], per class ≤ g.LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND (gate module :149–162). Prior 5.052e-11 / 3.878e-11 / 5.875e-11 (:949). - (a′) |t1.c_mode_farad / g.TH17_STEP3_C_MODE_RECORD_F − 1| ≤ g.REDUCTION_BAND. Prior −2.976552e-04 (:950). - Load. exc = g.CapacitorSheets(t1.c_mode_farad, 0.0, on=("P2", "P3", "P4")), with C_mode from t1 in-run and never transcribed. Then sA = g._study(exc), resA = sA.solve(comm), and zc = exc.impedance_ohm(g.FREQUENCY_64_HZ). Assert all of the following: - [p.port_id for p in resA.port_definitions] == ["P1"]; - resA.capacitor_port_ids == ("P2", "P3", "P4"); - resA.capacitor_impedance_ohm == zc (the same call); - resA.s_matrix.shape == (1, 1); - resA.cells == res0.cells; - sA.degree == 1 and sA.conductor is None. - (I-A) Route A, PORT-22's construction. pA = g.reduce_terminated_ports(res0.s_matrix, z0, {1: zc, 2: zc, 3: zc}), with 0-based indices and z0 = float(g.REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM). Assert |resA.s_matrix[0, 0] − pA[0, 0]| / |pA[0, 0]| ≤ g.REDUCTION_BAND (gate module :176–182). Prior 1.391811e-05 (:954).

Example-side anchors (asserted, imported bands only). - (S=) The field is the field of the S the identity read. Run gc.collect() then comm.Barrier(). Then rT, fT = run_lumped_sheet_port_case(resA.problem, resA.all_port_definitions, resA.specs, facet_tags=resA.facet_tags, driven_port_id="P1", verbose=False, return_fields=True, extra_bilinear_terms=resA.conductor_terms, degree=resA.degree), after asserting not resA.conductor_terms. Read aT, bT = _power_waves(rT.responses["P1"].voltage_v, rT.responses["P1"].current_a, z0) and assert |bT/aT − resA.s_matrix[0, 0]| / |resA.s_matrix[0, 0]| ≤ g.LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. Predicted ≤ 1e-14. The arithmetic is the same: the Route-A Study's single drive is itself a first factorisation on this problem with these specs (study.py:798–818). Item 373's (Z) read 9.122e-16 for Study vs fresh-factor direct (20261011T202050Z_WF-16-s10-W1.log:986). Never compare bitwise (2026-10-15 18:00 standing note). - (P) The exact power identity on the loaded field, with the sheets' dissipation counted. Item 373's lines 252–264 are copied with a provenance comment, without the P_surf term (the PEC hole has no conductor facets): - p_vol = comm.allreduce of fem.assemble_scalar of 0.5 σ |E|² dx, from fT.sigma_field, fT.e_complex and resA.cell_tags; - sheets = {s.port_id: s.sheet(driven=(s.port_id == "P1")) for s in resA.specs}; - p_sheet[pid] = _sheet_field_dissipation_w(acct, sh, e, omega) and p_src = _source_power_w(acct, sheets["P1"], e, omega), with acct = {"mesh": resA.mesh, "facet_tags": resA.facet_tags} and omega = s0.omega.

Assert |p_src − Σ p_sheet − p_vol| / |p_src| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL and p_vol > 0. Predicted ≈ 1e-12. The copper twin at C_F, r = 0.2 read 1.328e-12 (…s10-W1.log:992); this fixture's conductor and r differ, so the value is a prediction, not a backed record.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1), the gate's, asserted (backed): zc2 = g.CapacitorSheets(t2.c_mode_farad, 0.0, on=("P2",)).impedance_ohm(g.FREQUENCY_64_HZ) (the excitation's own impedance, never a hand-written 1/(jωC)). Then zt2 = g._modal_z(g.s_to_z(res0.s_matrix, z0) + zc2·I₄)[0], and assert |Im zt2[1]| / |t1.z_k[1]| > g.REDUCTION_BAND. Same comparison, same fixture, same width: 3.2883e-01 = 328.8× the band (:970). The factor is printed beside the record. - (c2), the gate's, asserted (backed). It shows that (I-A)'s comparator reads C. pA2 = g.reduce_terminated_ports(res0.s_matrix, z0, {1: zc2, 2: zc2, 3: zc2}); assert |resA.s_matrix[0, 0] − pA2[0, 0]| / |pA2[0, 0]| > g.REDUCTION_BAND. Backing: 3.5268e-01 = 352.7× (:971). - (cO), the field route's own: the capacitors dropped. Predicted factor; only the exceedance is asserted, following item 463's practice for predicted controls (its "Every factor here is predicted … Only the exceedance of the band is asserted"): - The solve: rO, fO = run_lumped_sheet_port_case(resA.problem, resA.port_definitions, resA.specs, …), the same call as (S=) except for resA.port_definitions (kept ports only). - What it tests: run_lumped_sheet_port_case places sheets only for the ids in its ports argument (ports/lumped.py:518–532). P2–P4 are therefore open gaps. This is exactly the trap that item 373 named and that (S=)'s call must avoid. - The assertion: S11_open = bO/aO; assert |S11_open − resA.s_matrix[0, 0]| / |resA.s_matrix[0, 0]| > g.REDUCTION_BAND. - Predicted range [0.3, 2.0] (drafter's unlogged estimate: an open-gap loop presents P1 a large capacitive reactance, so S11_open lies near +1, ≈ 1.6 from the record's −0.2787 + 0.9590j). Ceiling 2/|S_A| = 2/0.99872 ≈ 2.003, since both reflections are passive; no bar above it is named. The factor is printed beside the range. - (K) Refusals, asserted, before any solve and with no mesh. On s0 (unsolved): s0.tune(k=0) raises ValueError and s0.tune(k=True) raises TypeError (study.py:1040–1047). Then build sk = g._study(g.CapacitorSheets(g.TH17_STEP3_C_MODE_RECORD_F, 0.0, on=("P2", "P3", "P4"))); the C is an imported constant, since the refusals do not depend on it: - sk.tune() raises TypeError (:1038–1039); - sk.b1_plus(comm=comm) raises TypeError (:1744–1745), which is why the field takes the route above; - g._study(g.CapacitorSheets(g.TH17_STEP3_C_MODE_RECORD_F, 0.0, on=g.PORTS)).solve(comm) raises ValueError, because the sheets leave no port to drive (:765–766, before geom.build at :768).

Afterwards assert s0.result is None and sk.result is None. Every refusal raises identically on every rank before any collective.

Printed only (no band; a value outside its prediction is reported, with no status effect). - z₀ … z₃ (Re / Im at ≤ 6 significant digits); C₁, C₂ beside :940; t1.off_diagonal_residual. - S_A S₁₁, |S_A S₁₁|, and Z_in(P1) + zc = z0(1 + S)/(1 − S) + zc beside :973. The guide labels the last "near-zero reactance seen from the feed, not a match". - (P)'s parts: P_src, P_sheet(P1), Σ P_sheet(P2–P4) / P_src (predicted ≤ 1e-9: lossless sheets, Re zc = 0 exactly, :969, so the term is round-off on a reactive quantity ≈ Q times the real power), and P_vol / P_src (predicted of order 1e-3, the copper twin's 6.276e-06 / 3.620e-03 at …s10-W1.log:992). - Centre (origin) |B|, |B₁⁺|, |B₁⁻| per unit incident wave for the tuned and open-gap fields. |B₁⁺| / |B₁⁻| of the tuned field is predicted ≈ 1 within a few % (one linear feed on the P1 mirror plane excites k = ±1 equally; the mesh is not mirror-exact). |B_T(0)| / |B_O(0)| is predicted ≫ 1 (order 10–10³, the drafter's unlogged estimate from an assumed ≈ 1 pF gap fringe capacitance). - Wall times (S0, SA, the two field solves, projections, XDMF) at 1 decimal; report_peak_rss summed.

Output. - Fields per unit incident wave. For X ∈ {T, O}: BX = project_to_cg1(magnetic_flux_density_from_e(fX.e_complex, omega), name=…). Its x.array is divided by aX (complex) in numpy, then scatter_forward. Never normalise by drive_voltage_v. - Setup figure on resA.mesh / resA.cell_tags, with mri:19's call (examples/mri/19_study_tune_mode_capacitance.py:143–159): air hidden, phantom translucent, slice_normal=(0, 0, 1). Title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. "mri:24 -- tune then load: CapacitorSheets(C_mode) on P2-P4 of the PEC hole F-small birdcage, P1 fed (WF-16 step 6b)". The hole route draws the coil as a void, and the guide says so. Write the coordinates; do not import test_mat19. - B3: near the wall, (0, 0, 9.5e-3). The faceting sagitta at h = R/10 is ≈ 1.3e-5 m, so B3 lies inside the polyhedral sphere. - B4: a mesh vertex. Take the submesh geometry node nearest (0, 0, 5e-3): each rank's local minimum, then allgather of (distance, xyz) and a lexicographic minimum on every rank. Print its xyz. A vertex has ≥ 4 incident tets, so DG0 values there depend on which cell owns the point. - B5: outside the sphere, inside the air box: (0, 0, 1.5e-2), with BOX_HALF_WIDTH 0.02 (test_lossy_sphere_sar.py:69).

(1) Anchors (asserted).

Part A — POST-10's own cube, on the gate's fixture and band. _fixture(comm) and _oracle(...), with the gate's planted DG0 and N1curl fields. Asserted as the gate does: - (S0) size_global == SUB_CELLS_GLOBAL, len(parent_cells) equal to the local + ghost count, and the kept originals unique with 288 in all. - (K) the owner integer equals the oracle's minimum at P0–P4, −1 at P5, with exactly one claim. The DG0 value equals float(min) with imaginary part 0. - (I) owner integers equal, and values / validity bitwise equal (np.array_equal, band 0), against point_owner_cells(msh, …, candidate_cells=keep) and the parent DG0 under candidate_cells=keep. - (N) N1curl A_VEC + B_VEC × x at P0–P4 ≤ CLOSED_FORM_TOL. - (W) owner / DG0 / N1 values bitwise equal on every rank.

Print the owner integers beside the record [217, 223, 126, 229, 132, -1]. Cost: < 2 s (a 384-cell cube).

Part B — MAT-10's gel ball. One EM solve, then: - (B) ≤ B_BAND, (P) ≤ P_BAND, (C) ≤ C_BAND and (A) ≤ A_BAND: the gate's four anchors at its bands, on the gate's code path. - Then the point-evaluation anchors at B0–B5, all through owner=RULE, parent=(msh, parent_ids): - (I-q) The DG0 q_h on the submesh against the parent DG0 q_par under owner=RULE, candidate_cells=keep. Owner integers are equal; values and validity are bitwise equal. To build q_par, put fem.Function(Wp) around _cell_average_dg0's array, which is already scattered (:108–113). This is POST-10's (I) at its band 0, on a physical field. The value is a copied dof (_to_sub, :122–130), so no round-off band applies. - (I-o) The same identity on the gate's planted original-index DG0 (_dg0(msh, _original(msh)) and _dg0(sub, _original(msh)[parent_ids])). Also assert value == float(owner_original) at B0–B4 (POST-10 (K)'s second clause, with the rule's own owner in place of the oracle). - (O) At B5: owner −1, invalid, and zero claims (allreduced), on both the submesh call and the parent candidate_cells=keep call. - (N-ball) N1curl A_VEC + B_VEC × x interpolated on the ball submesh, at B0–B4, ≤ CLOSED_FORM_TOL: the gate's (N) at its band, on a gmsh submesh. B5 is invalid. - (W-ball) Owner integers, q_h and θ values, and the N1 values are bitwise equal on every rank (_bitwise_equal_across_ranks).

Printed only, never asserted (the probe physics): - At B0–B4: θ_h[q_cf] and θ_h[q_h], read by point evaluation, beside θ(r) = robin_sphere_steady_temperature(r, radius=R, k=K, q=q_cf, h=H, t_inf=T_INF) − T_INF. - Predicted: |θ_h[q_cf]/θ − 1| of order (P)'s 3.2e-3, ≲ 1e-2. - Predicted: θ_h[q_h]/θ − 1 ≈ +3 % to +4 %, MAT-10's mean-SAR leg (:163, 3.5499e-02). - At B0–B2: the 2 mm ball probe ball_average(θ_h[q_cf], ProbeBall(c, 2e-3)) beside the point value. - Predicted at B0: ball/point − 1 ≈ −q_cf·a²/(10k)/θ(0) = −1.09 %, the steady quadratic profile's exact ball-mean offset. This is the volume effect mat:13 describes, now with the FEM point sample on the other side. - θ_h through owner=None against owner=RULE, parent=… at B0–B4: max |difference|. Predicted ≤ 1e-15 relative, because θ is continuous P1. - At B4: the spread (max − min) of q_h over the vertex's incident sub cells. Use owned-cell compute_colliding_cells and allgather. Print it beside the rule's chosen value. Predicted: ≥ 4 incident cells and a spread > 0. This is what a wrong owner would read. It is printed, not asserted (see (2)). - At B0–B5: the owner integers. They are compared across windows (see (3)).

(2) Negative controls (§9 rule (e); ceiling first). - (C1) Asserted, arithmetic, gate fixture. At P1 / P2 / P4 the oracle keep-set has ≥ 2 members with max − min ≥ 1. The ceiling is the set's own spread (9 / 131 / 121 in the POST-10 outcome), an integer ≥ 1 against band 0. Same comparison, same fixture, backed by W1–W3. - (C2) Asserted. No parent raises RuntimeError on every rank, with flags allgathered and a message containing parent= and create_submesh. - Run it on the cube (backed by the gate on that fixture). - Run it on the ball submesh. It is backed by the same raise on a different gmsh create_submesh (20261004T142026Z_ANS-9-step1a-W1.log:1949–1977). It is the same code path (evaluation.py:55–60, :101–105): any create_submesh mesh lacks the index. A ball (C2) that does not raise is a finding (see (6)), not a mislabel. - (C3) / (C4) Asserted, cube. parent without the rule raises ValueError. parent_cells[:-1] raises ValueError on every rank. - (a) / (b) Asserted "misses (A)'s 11 %", MAT-10's controls on MAT-10's fixture. The factors are printed beside 0.7932 / 1.0649 (:166–167), never asserted. - (cV) Predicted, printed. The B4 incident-set q_h spread over the rule's value, as a relative factor. No prior measurement exists, so per rule (e) it is printed only. Its ceiling is the q_h range over the whole ball, (2582.4 − 1701.1)/2002.1 ≈ 0.44 (:159). - (cB) Predicted, printed. The B0 ball-vs-point offset −1.09 % (above). Its magnitude exceeds P_BAND, which shows that a point probe and a 2 mm probe are not interchangeable at the 1 % level. It is not asserted.

Outputs. - Setup figure: write_setup_figure(msh, cell_tags, …) on the parent with region_names={1: "gel sphere (create_submesh, 19 496 cells)", 2: "air (parent only)"}, translucent_tags=(2,), a y = 0 slice (as 13_…py:187–204) and a title of ≤ 130 characters naming the six probes. - Combined XDMF: examples/materials/paraview_output/materials_21_point_probes_on_gel_ball_submesh_combined.xdmf on the submesh. It holds the P1 theta_q_cf, theta_q_h, theta_exact (the closed form interpolated) and theta_error, plus the DG0 q_h and owner_original_dg0. Each field takes an explicit real part, and each key equals its Function's name. Call adopt_host_ownership last. - CSV: …_probes.csv, written on rank 0 with no collective inside. Columns: label, xyz, owner_original, valid, q_h, theta_q_cf, theta_q_h, theta_exact, ball_2mm (B0–B2) and incident_spread_q_h (B4).

Guide. - Explain the owner rule on a submesh: why the parent map is needed (a create_submesh mesh has no original cell index), and why it gives the same cell at every width (POST-10.md:21). - When it matters: a discontinuous field (DG0 q_h) at a vertex or facet. When it does not: continuous P1 θ at a generic point. - One sentence: a point probe and a 2 mm ball probe differ by ≈ 1 % at the centre, printed and not gated. - A ParaView recipe: Probe Location at B4 on q_h and owner_original_dg0. - In ## 2: ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:21 -n 2 -t 300, with the measured wall time and the -n 4 reading. - Related, by full filename: examples/materials/13_virtual_probe_in_gel_ball.md, examples/materials/16_probe_readouts_in_coil_phantom.md, examples/materials/04_sar_heats_gel_ball.md, tests/post/test_submesh_owner_rule.py, tests/validation/test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py, src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py. - Write ≈, never a tilde.

(3) Tier, ranks and windows. Heavy by runner ceiling (-t 300, mat:13's), standard-sized. Complex build. Run of record at -n 2; control at -n 4 to show the owner integers are rank-independent.

Price, from logs. - The MAT-10 fixture costs 23.6 s at -n 2 (EM 15.5 s, :168), inside a 70 s harness window with tests/environment (…MAT-10-step1-W1.log.gz, Elapsed :302). - mat:13 on the same mesh family took 81 s end to end, with a 35.1 s fixture plus outputs and figure (20261005T201522Z_EX-90.log:211, :217). - Part A is < 2 s. The two extra steady solves for (a) / (b), the N1 interpolation and the point calls on 19 496 cells take ≈ 5–10 s. The figure, XDMF and imports take ≈ 20–30 s. - Predicted: ≈ 70 s per run at -n 2, range [45, 180] s. The -n 4 run is unmeasured for MAT-10; predicted similar, range [45, 200] s. - On the slow host of 10-15/16 (≈ 1.4–2× slow) the run of record stays under 300. A run approaching 300 s is a kill, not a result: report it.

Every window runs in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, as one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call.

  1. docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0.
  2. Pre-censuses, before any file is written:
  3. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-121-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'"
  4. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-121-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'"

The last reading on main was figures 116 broken=0 and docrefs dead=0, exit 2. Items 495–497 may land first; use whatever the pre-census reads. 2. Dry runs: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-121-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:21 -n 2 -t 300 --dry-run" must print (complex build). - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-121-dryrun-n4 "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:21 -n 4 -t 300 --dry-run" likewise. 3. Run of record, labelled EX-121: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-121 "<the -n 2 emitted string, with -T and -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 added as in EX-119>". It needs Status 0, every anchor and control green, and "All assertions hold". 4. git add the PNG. Then the unflagged -n 4 control, labelled EX-121-control-n4, with the -n 4 emitted string. - It needs Status 0 and every assert green. - (W across widths): the printed owner-integer lines for P0–P5 and B0–B5 must be character-identical to window 3's, and B4's printed xyz must be identical. The executor checks and records this. A difference is a negative result (6). - θ values are compared at the printed 6 digits only; differences are reported, not gated. 5. Post-censuses EX-121-post-figures and EX-121-post-docrefs. Predicted: figures N → N + 1, broken=0, dead=0, exit ≠ 1. 6. git status --porcelain examples/ tests/ src/ lists only the three new paths. 7. The leak guard runs on the staged logs (no AED counterpart exists; it runs anyway).

After status 124 or a kill: run pgrep -c python3 first, then the rubric-4 orphan-.c sweep labelled EX-121-cache-sweep.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Collectives. Every rank calls every point_owner_cells / evaluate_vector_field_parallel, including the must-raise calls. Allgather the raise flags after the call (K5 idiom, test_submesh_owner_rule.py:282–292). No comm. call goes inside if comm.rank == 0: (deadlock, item 227). Compare owner_original, never owner_local_cell, which is −1 off the owning rank. - The parent map. parent_cells must cover the sub's owned and ghost cells (len == size_local + num_ghosts), or (C4)'s ValueError fires. Use the parent_ids that _sphere_submesh returns, unchanged. - candidate_cells is parent-local over owned + ghost, as the idiom computes it. Never combine candidate_cells with parent=: that is allowed by the code but not gated (POST-10 scope). - Never key on local_to_global. The index-map number is partition-dependent (POST-8.md:28). - Complex build. DG0 and θ values are complex128. Assert imaginary part 0 before taking .real for (I-o)'s integer comparison. np.array_equal on complex is exact. No UFL comparison or sqrt (OPS-22, WF-6 4c): the closed form is evaluated in numpy at the points, and _theta_cf stays UFL for (P) / (A) only. Take np.real before every float. - Rank safety. Use _allsum for every assembled scalar. The B4 vertex search and the incident-set spread use allgather, then a deterministic minimum on every rank. - XDMF. Every field lives on the submesh at P1 / DG0. Do not write a parent field into the submesh file. - gz log. Read the MAT-10 record with zcat. Never rewrite or re-compress the log. - Runner. run_examples.sh runs host-side. Take its line from --dry-run and never wrap it in docker compose exec. Use -k 30. Never background a window. - Rule (i). No script edit after window 3 starts; no guide edit after window 5 starts.

(5) Scope boundary. One steady imposed-field fixture (MAT-10), degree-1 θ, at -n 2 and -n 4. Not claimed: - any pointwise θ accuracy. No gate asserts a pointwise θ band. (P) and (A) are interior-L2 bands, so the θ-vs-closed-form point readings are printed; - a real probe's tip volume, self-heating or response time (thermal/probe.py:24); - transient or coil-driven fields (mat:13, mat:16 keep their integral routes); - a submesh of a submesh, or candidate_cells with parent=; - an h-rate, compliance, or an external check.

POST-10 and MAT-10 do not move. The ans9 comment at 09_…py:356 is stale, but this item leaves it untouched: it is a run-of-record script, per POST-10.md:124. The review may file the comment fix separately.

(6) What a negative result means. Report and stop: journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-121-<UTC>, and mark item 498 BLOCKED in the same commit. Never widen a band or edit tests/ or src/. - Part A red (S0 / K / I / N / W / C1–C4): main has drifted from the POST-10 gate. Re-run nothing in-slot. Print the first differing value beside its log:line and file a known-issues entry. - MAT-10 anchor red (B / P / C / A / (a) / (b)): MAT-10 has drifted. Same disposition. - (I-q) / (I-o) / (O) red on the ball, with Part A green: a finding about the parent-keyed rule on a gmsh / ghosted submesh that the cube did not exercise. It goes to known-issues against POST-10, with the B-point, the two owners and the two values. - (N-ball) red: an evaluation defect on the submesh. Same. - (C2-ball) not raising: the image now gives this submesh an original index. Record what it returns, and stop: the review rules (POST-10.md:141). - (W across widths) differs: the rule is not partition-free on this mesh. That is a POST-10 finding; known-issues entry.

There is no PREDICTED RED: line, so any red stops the slot.

(7) Status it can move. EX-121 ⬜ → ✅ on the §7 Done-when, which is pasted in the same review commit (rule (j)). The census rises by one with broken=0 and docrefs dead=0. POST-10, MAT-10 and §2 are unchanged. A ball-side negative would instead open a known-issues entry against POST-10's scope.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-121, §9 item 498 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-121.md, heading §9 item 498). Read the brief and any review ruling beneath it first; the rulings hold. You are the executor — do not spawn agents. Never background a window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, run every window in the foreground, and never delete a log. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Before window 1, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 and require 0. Run both pre-censuses before writing any file. Edit nothing under tests/ or src/; import the gate modules' helpers and bands unchanged and never call a pytest fixture or a test_* function. Every rank calls every point-evaluation function, including the must-raise calls; allgather raise flags after the call; no collective inside a rank == 0 branch; compare owner_original, never local cells. Assert no new band: every assert uses a band imported from tests/post/test_submesh_owner_rule.py or tests/validation/test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py, or is an exact identity (band 0) the brief names; print every θ-versus-closed-form and ball-versus-point reading, never assert it. Emit the runner line with --dry-run and pass it to the harness; never wrap run_examples.sh in docker compose exec. Window 4 is the -n 4 control: check its printed owner-integer lines and B4 coordinates character-for-character against window 3 and report the result. No edit to the script after window 3 starts, or to the guide after window 5 starts. The leak guard still runs on staged logs. If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command string. Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record (log:line) or prediction, the cross-width owner comparison, the census before / after with the docrefs dead= list, and elapsed."

  • Shared files. Three new paths, nothing under tests/ or src/. If anything there turns out to be needed, stop and report.

Imports (never restated). Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path, then import tests.validation.test_imp3_disc_birdcage as g9. - Helpers, called unchanged: - g9._case_disc (:478–506), the gate's own both-arm body. It builds without the disc, then with it, in GEO-23 order, with the guard before the disc solve. - g9._report (:509–602), which prints every gate line in W1's format, so the digits line up with the log line for line. - g9._control_c1_disc (:628–674). - Bands, reached through g9's namespace: CELL_COUNT_BAND, REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL, RECIPROCITY_BAND, PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND, PEC_WALL_MAX_E, POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR. - Records and constants: SOLID_CELL_RECORD, SPHEROID_HOLE_CELL_RECORD, IMP3_FLAG_OFF_Z_64MHZ, RIM_POINTS, SPHEROID_CENTRE, SPHEROID_SEMI_MAJOR, SPHEROID_SEMI_MINOR, PORT_IDS, DRIVES, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3, QUADRATURE_DEGREE, OUTER_BOX_TAG, PHANTOM_HEIGHT, L_X_RECORD. - Helpers: _solve_driven, _exact_shares, _outer_box_tags, _wall_max_e, _in. - From src: mass_averaged_sar (fem_em_solver.post.sar), evaluate_vector_field_parallel, pec_oblate_spheroid_field, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership, write_setup_figure (imp:3's import lines :77–82). - Rules: - Never import a test_* name. Never call test_imp3_disc_default_phantom. - The natural-wall problem is built with the gate's three lines :634, :644–645 (_outer_box_tags(msh, disc["built"][2], comm); replace(sweep["problem"], facet_tags=outer, pec_facet_tags=(OUTER_BOX_TAG,)); dict(sweep, problem=problem)), copied, not edited. - _cellwise and _ball_mask are copied from examples/implants/03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.py:134–141, :179–189 (example to example). - Records: digits go only in an example-local REC dict, each with its log:line in 20261013T213344Z_IMP-3-step9-W1.log unless marked W2. They are printed beside the readings and never asserted by equality:

Record Value Line cells without / with 116 085 / 150 140 :3764 (R0) max entrywise 2.983e-10 :3765 (P) disc arm P1 2.988e-15 :3710 P_phantom disc arm P1 1.562944066e-06 W :3710 (E) tag-402 dofs / max |E| 6 669 / 0.000e+00 :3719 (M) disc-arm max 0.0425 % :3720 (S) without-arm separation 671.1× :3684 Q P1 top / bottom 1.637623 / 1.646293 :3751–3752 Q min over P1 / P3 / ccw / cw 1.531498 (cw bottom) :3762 C1 (P) / wall max |E| 3.154e-15 / 2.627e-04 :3768 C1 PEC / natural top / bottom 1.536348 / 1.551662 :3769–3770 W2 Q P1 top / bottom (ratio of record) 1.592094 / 1.593359 W2 :3862–3863 W2 Q / estimate P1 top / bottom 0.961546 / 0.964433 W2 :3862–3863

Structural asserts at start-up: the build is complex, comm.size == 2, len(RIM_POINTS) == 2, and SPHEROID_SEMI_MAJOR / SPHEROID_SEMI_MINOR == 5 within 1e-12.

(1) Anchor. These are the gate's anchors, asserted at the imported bands. The assert lines are copied from :682–696 and :605–625, one printed line per anchor, beside its REC entry.

Anchor Assertion (A0) \|cells / SOLID_CELL_RECORD − 1\| and \|cells / SPHEROID_HOLE_CELL_RECORD − 1\| ≤ CELL_COUNT_BAND (R0) without-arm Z against IMP3_FLAG_OFF_Z_64MHZ entrywise ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (i) reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND, both arms (ii) σ_max ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE and every column power ≤ 1, both arms (P) P_src = P_vol + P_sheet ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, every drive of both arms (W1 ≤ 7.0e-15) (M) the five σ_y pairs on the disc arm ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (E) tag-402 dofs > 0, and max |E| ≤ PEC_WALL_MAX_E on every drive (S) without-arm separation ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR containment the 1 g ball fits: x₀ + a_1g < R and a + a_1g < H/2

Example-side anchors (asserted; imported band only). Each is a discrete identity that the same comparison has already measured. - (F-pec) The fresh PEC solve. solved = _solve_driven(disc["case"], "P1"), on a fresh solver. - Assert (P) on _exact_shares(disc["case"], solved) ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. This is the gate's (P), measured with a fresh solver at :3768. - Assert (E): _wall_max_e(solved["fields"].e_complex, disc["owned_wall"], comm) ≤ PEC_WALL_MAX_E. - Printed only, never asserted: the reproduction of the sweep, |P_phantom,fresh / disc["shares"]["P1"]["phantom"] − 1| and |SAR_1g,fresh / disc["sar"][(rim, "P1")] − 1| at each rim point. Predicted ≤ 1e-8, since this is a different factorisation of the same problem. - (L) Loss-map sums. For each of the two P1 fields (PEC and natural), the owned sum of the DG0 phantom-loss vector _cellwise(0.5·Re σ·⟨E, E⟩·v̄·dx(PHANTOM_CELL_TAG)), reduced, equals that solve's _exact_shares(...)["phantom"] within DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. This is imp:3's check on the rod mesh, where it read 6.228e-15 / 1.519e-14 (20261003T051229Z_EX-83.log.gz:3814–3815). - (N) The natural solve. The natural-wall problem is built as above and solved with _solve_driven(nat_case, "P1"). - Assert its (P) ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (C1's (P), :3768). - Assert that its census reads exterior = outer + 402, with tag 499 absent (C1's census, :3767). - Every profile point's ok mask is True (structural).

(2) Negative controls. All three are rule (e). Each asserted one is backed by a logged measurement of the same comparison on the same fixture and mesh, W1. - (C1) The gate's, called unchanged. c1 = g9._control_c1_disc(case). Assert c1["resid"] ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL and c1["wall_max"] > PEC_WALL_MAX_E: the knob is wired, as read at :3768, 2.627e-4 against 1e-12. Its printed natural / without and PEC / natural lines come out in the gate's format. - (C1-r) The PEC wall raises the rim 1 g SAR over the natural wall. SAR_1g(PEC, P1) / SAR_1g(natural, P1) > 1 at both rim points, computed from the example's own natural solve with mass_averaged_sar(…, rho=disc["rho_field"], radius=case["off"]["a_1g"], quadrature_degree=QUADRATURE_DEGREE). Asserted: W1 measured 1.536 / 1.552 on this comparison (:3769–3770). The factor is printed beside the gate's [1.1, 3.0] prediction. No ceiling is claimed, because a ratio of positive SARs has none (the gate's note, IMP-3.md:1488). This reading must reproduce C1's printed digits. If it does not, it is a fresh-solve divergence: print both. - (Cq) The disc-blind arm under-reads the rim. Q = SAR_1g,rim(disc) / SAR_1g,rim(without) > 1 for drives P1, P3, ccw and cw at both rim points (8 pairs). Asserted: W1 minimum 1.531498 (cw bottom, :3762). - P2 / P4 are printed only, never asserted. On W1's default phantom their bottom-rim Q read 0.849 / 0.715 (:3754, :3758). The weak-drive rim SARs (≈ 30× below P1) are mesh-noisy at that resolution (IMP-3.md:1540), and an assertion there would be a coin toss. - Print W2's P1 Q (1.592 / 1.593) and Q / estimate (0.962 / 0.964) beside W1's as the ratio of record.

Printed only (predictions written in the script before window 3): - Rim-near map ratio. Over gel cells whose midpoint lies within 1.0 mm of each rim point: count, and the max and the volume-weighted mean of local SAR (PEC) / local SAR (natural). Predicted max > the 1 g ratio 1.54. No ceiling is claimed. - Rim profile. |E| along (0.015, 0, z) for z from a + 0.25 mm to a + 6.0 mm, 12 points, in the gel above the top rim, for the PEC and natural P1 fields. Print them normalised by their value at the far point, beside pec_oblate_spheroid_field(p_l, drive="inplane", semi_major=a, semi_minor=c, e0=1, interior="continue") normalised the same way (local frame p_l = (d_z, d_y, d_x), the gate's :244–245 map). This is a shape comparator only. Predicted: PEC/far at the first point is above natural/far, and within [0.5, 2]× of the closed-form shape there. The comparison is never asserted. The degree-1 coarse mesh, the non-uniform coil background and the finite-k field all enter it. - Elapsed for the gate case, C1, each fresh solve, maps, figure and XDMF, and summed peak RSS (g9._peak_rss_gib is reached via g9).

Outputs. - Setup figure via write_setup_figure(msh, cell_tags, …) on the disc mesh, imp:3's call (:227–241): region names {1 conductor, 2 air, 3 phantom (saline)} plus the port boxes, air hidden, phantom translucent, slice_normal=(0, 1, 0) through the axis. The y = 0 slice cuts the disc as its 2.4 mm × 12 mm section beside leg 1. Use a title ≤ 130 characters, e.g. "imp:9 -- PEC oblate disc (a = 6 mm, aspect 5) in the driven birdcage phantom (IMP-3 step 9, W1 mesh)". Render it after the timers. - Combined XDMF examples/implants/paraview_output/implants_09_pec_disc_in_birdcage_rim_sar_combined.xdmf via write_xdmf_with_tags(…, facet_tags=disc["built"][2]), so that tag 402 and the sheets are visible. - DG0 fields: E_magnitude_pec_P1, local_sar_pec_P1, E_magnitude_natural_P1, local_sar_natural_P1, local_sar_pec_over_natural_P1, one_gram_ball_top and one_gram_ball_bottom. - The ratio is set only on gel cells whose natural loss is > 0, and is 0 elsewhere; it is computed in numpy. - Each key equals its Function's name. Call adopt_host_ownership last. - CSV paraview_output/implants_09_pec_disc_in_birdcage_rim_sar_rim_profile.csv: z, |E| PEC, |E| natural, the closed-form shape. Written on rank 0 after the collective evaluations.

Guide. - Explain what the PEC wall does at the rim. Compare the in-plane rim enhancement (1/L_x)² = 64.25 pointwise, imp:8, with a 1 g ball that dilutes it to Q ≈ 1.6. - Explain why the with / without comparison is a 1 g ratio while the map ratio is PEC versus natural: one mesh, not two. - Explain why P2 / P4 rim SARs are noisy on the default mesh. - Say plainly that W1 is the coarse record mesh and W2 is the ratio of record. - A ParaView recipe: threshold cell tag 3, then local_sar_pec_over_natural_P1 on an x = 0.015 slice. Add the facet-tag-402 block, then Plot Over Line along z through the rim. - One sentence in ## 2: ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:9 -n 2 -t 590, heavy, with the measured wall time. - Related, by full filename: examples/implants/03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.md, examples/implants/08_pec_oblate_disc_edge_in_gel.md, tests/validation/test_imp3_disc_birdcage.py, tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid.py, tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py. - Never name the raw capture log, or any output by a bare basename outside figures/ or paraview_output/ (the docrefs checker, EX-115 item 461). - Write ≈, never a tilde.

(3) Tier and windows. Heavy by ceiling, -n 2, complex build.

Price. The gate case is 164.4 s (:3764) and C1 is 15.7 s (:3768). On top of those: - two fresh P1 solves, which predict ≈ 10–15 s each (the 4-drive disc sweep took 13.3 s and the arm 49.5 s, :3718); - _exact_shares ×2; - two 1 g natural SARs (≈ 6 s; 12 balls took 33 s at :3718); - the DG0 map JIT (≈ 15 s), the figure (≈ 10–30 s), the XDMF (≈ 10 s) and start-up (≈ 10 s).

The run of record is predicted at ≈ 270 s, range [200, 480] s, runner -t 590. On 10-15 / 10-16 the host ran ≈ 1.4–2× slow, and 2× reaches ≈ 540 s. So window 3 uses §5.1's durable-capture idiom (PROJECT_PLAN.md:1034–1037), verbatim inside the container command, with the trailing ; exit $rc. Summed RSS is predicted ≈ 2.5 GiB (W1 2.40).

Windows. Each runs in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, as one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call: 0. docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. No other heavy, xl or xxl window may be live. 1. Pre-censuses, run before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-122-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-122-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'"

The last reading on main was figures 116 with broken=0 (20261016T113243Z_EX-119-post-figures.log), and docrefs dead=0, exit 2. Use what the pre-census reads, because other 10-16 items may land first. 2. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-122-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:9 -n 2 -t 590 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 3. Run of record, labelled EX-122, flagged. This is the emitted inner command, with -T, the flag and the durable capture: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-122 "docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && mkdir -p /workspace/logs && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/implants/09_pec_disc_in_birdcage_rim_sar.py > /workspace/logs/EX-122-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo [capture] rc=\$rc >> /workspace/logs/EX-122-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/EX-122-raw.log; exit \$rc'"

Pass means all of the following: - Status 0 and [capture] rc=0; - every anchor and asserted control green; - the closing "All assertions hold" line.

If the dry run's inner string differs from the above in anything but the flag and the capture, use the dry run's and say so. 4. git add the PNG and check that it is ≤ 600 KiB. No unflagged control re-run. The template asks for one only when a figure is retrofitted (example-runner.md item 6, as EX-117), and a second ≈ 5-minute window does not buy an identity. 5. Write the guide from window 3's log. Then EX-122-post-figures and EX-122-post-docrefs (the window 1 commands, relabelled). Predicted: figures N → N + 1, broken=0; docrefs dead=0, exit ≠ 1. 6. git status --porcelain examples/ tests/ src/ lists exactly the three new examples/ paths. 7. The pre-commit leak guard runs on the staged logs. This fixture has no AED counterpart, but the guard still runs.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Gate fidelity. _case_disc(None) builds the record meshes (116 085 / 150 140). Never pass a phantom_resolution, and never build the disc any other way. The 2026-10-13 known-issues entry (IMP-6 step 2, the default spheroid_in_box_domain builder truncates the rim below ρ_r/3) concerns the imposed-field builder. The birdcage disc is item 427's exact revolve, and its rim fidelity reads 0 midpoints inside on W1 (:3717). Refining the rim is out of scope. - The sweep's fields are freed. _arm_disc deletes result and the superposed fields (:387–388), so the XDMF fields come only from the two fresh _solve_driven P1 solves. A held factorisation silently solves a different problem (PORT-19, WF-12), so use fresh solvers only. - Tag 402 lives in the build tuple (disc["built"][2]), not in the sweep's facet tags (IMP-3.md:1508). - Point evaluation inside the hole raises (post/sar.py:357–361). Profile points start 0.25 mm outside the rim in the gel. A failed ok mask is a red, never a skip. - The closed form near the focal ring (item 408): use interior="continue", evaluated only at the gel profile points. - Complex build: no UFL comparison, max_value or sqrt. Masks and ratios are built in numpy. Take np.real before every float. - Rank safety: reduce every assembled scalar and count, and use owned cells only. Point values go through evaluate_vector_field_parallel. No collective goes inside a rank == 0 branch. A rank-local exception hangs the job, and Status 124 is a finding. - XDMF: DG0 fields only. Each key equals its Function's name. adopt_host_ownership comes last. - Runner: run_examples.sh runs host-side. Take its line from --dry-run, and never wrap the script itself in docker compose exec. Use -k 30 and the durable capture. Never background a window. - After Status 124 or a kill: run pgrep -c python3 first. Only if it reads 0, run the orphan-.c sweep (daily-review.md rubric 4) labelled EX-122-cache-sweep. - Rule (i): no script edit after window 3 starts, and no guide edit after window 5 starts.

(5) Scope boundary. One aspect-5 PEC disc, normal x̂, at (0.015, 0, 0), in the untuned solid-coil F-small 4×4 with 50 Ω sheets, 64 MHz, degree 1, W1's default phantom, -n 2, P1 maps.

Not claimed: - the accuracy of the rim ratio (ANS-10 / (7c)); - absolute or pointwise SAR; - convergence, or the 1 g rung (W2 is cited, not run); - tissue, heating, ISO 10974 or F2182 compliance; - a tuned or copper coil; - a square-edged plate; - an external check.

IMP-6's Not-claimed "a plate in a coil" is not lifted. IMP-3 does not move.

(6) What a negative result means. Report and stop: journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-122-<UTC>, and mark item 499 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). EX-122 stays ⬜. Never widen a band, never edit tests/ or src/, and never re-record from the example side. - A gate anchor red, or (A0) / (R0) missed: main has drifted from the gate. Print the first differing value beside its log:line and file a known-issues entry. - (F-pec), (L) or (N) red: an example-side finding about the fresh solve or the DG0 assembly. Print both sides. - (C1), (C1-r) or (Cq) not separating: a mislabelled comparand, or the fixture moved. Print all 12 Q values and both C1 ratios. - Status 124, over 590 s, or past minute 30 before window 3: park with the last line of the raw capture log. - A defect after every assertion is green (figure, XDMF or CSV; the EX-114 shape): BLOCKED with the log:line and returned to the review. No in-slot fix after window 3.

There is no PREDICTED RED: line, so any red stops the slot.

(7) Status it can move. EX-122 ⬜ → ✅ under the §7 Done-when that the review pastes in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). The census rises by one with broken=0, and docrefs read dead=0. IMP-3, IMP-6 and §2 are unchanged.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-122, §9 item 499 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-122.md, heading §9 item 499). - Read the brief and any review ruling beneath it first; the rulings hold. - You are the executor — do not spawn agents. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Never background a window. Run every window in the foreground, pass timeout: 660000 on every harness Bash call, and never delete a log. - Window 3 uses §5.1's durable-capture idiom verbatim inside the container command, with container timeout -k 30 590. An overrun parks the item — never raise a timeout. - Before window 1, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 and require 0. Confirm no heavy, xl or xxl window is live. Run both pre-censuses before writing any file. Check that examples/implants/09_* is free. - Edit nothing under tests/ or src/. Call _case_disc(None), _report and _control_c1_disc from tests/validation/test_imp3_disc_birdcage.py unchanged. Never import a test_* name. Take every band through that module's namespace, and assert nothing at a band the gate did not use. - The XDMF fields come only from fresh _solve_driven P1 solves. Every count and sum is owned-only and reduced. No UFL comparison or sqrt. - Emit the runner line with --dry-run and pass it to the harness. Never wrap run_examples.sh in docker compose exec. - No edit to the script after window 3 starts, or to the guide after window 5 starts. - If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command string. On a red, park on attempt/EX-122-*, mark item 499 BLOCKED in the same commit, and report. - Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record (log:line) or prediction, the census before / after with the docrefs dead= list, and elapsed."

Never name the raw capture log. Before the census windows, grep -nE "\.(csv|json|msh|bp|s1p|s4p)\b" examples/mri/25_study_transient_duty_and_wall.md must read nothing. - Write ≈, never a tilde.

(3) Tier and windows. Heavy by runner ceiling, -n 2, complex build.

Price, from the gate logs (real) scaled to complex. - W1a's leg is 54.8 s: case A API solve + mesh 10.8 s, case B 8.0 s (:91, :96), plus two direct runs, two comparands and (c1). W1b's leg is 63.0 s: build 8.7 s, comparand 17.1 s, API 14.3 s, direct 5.8 s, plus (c2) (:85–94). - Complex solves cost ≈ 2× real here: EX-86's complex (T1) N 40 solve took 11.9 s (:71) against W1b's ≈ 5.6 s real API solve. The comparands are numpy-bound and do not scale (EX-86 :41 18.4 s against W1b's 17.1 s). - Estimate: Part A ≈ 90 s; Part B ≈ 80 s; (X) ≈ 35 s (mesh ≈ 9 s plus 95 half-steps ≈ 2.3× N 40's 11.9 s); start-up, imports and complex JIT ≈ 20 s; XDMF ≈ 10 s; the figure ≈ 15–25 s (flagged run only). - Run of record predicted ≈ 250 s, range [150, 450] s; runner -t 590. The host has run ≈ 1.4–2× slow on 10-15 / 10-16, and 2× reaches ≈ 500 s, so window 3 uses §5.1's durable-capture idiom (PROJECT_PLAN.md:1034–1037) verbatim inside the container command, with the trailing ; exit $rc (EX-122's form). - Summed RSS predicted ≈ 2.5–3 GiB (W1a 1.72, W1b 2.04; the walled mesh is held twice in the same process).

Windows. Each runs in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, as one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. 0. docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. No other heavy, xl or xxl window may be live. 1. Pre-censuses, run before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-123-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-123-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'"

The last reading on main was examples=119 ok=119 missing=0 broken=0 (20261016T184441Z_EX-122-post-figures.log:155) and dead=0 guide=0 stale=129 exit 2 (20261016T184443Z_EX-122-post-docrefs.log:169). Use what the pre-census reads, because other 10-16 items may land first. Exit 2 is staleness information; exit 1 is a failure. 2. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-123-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:25 -n 2 -t 590 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 3. Run of record, labelled EX-123, flagged. (4) Traps already paid for. - MAT-9's _interior_error / _rel_diff in the complex build (float() of a complex _allsum): use m13._interior_error, as mat:11 does. Never call g._interior_error. g._errors is safe. - ArityMismatch: Failure to conjugate test function in complex Form (EX-86 first window, Status 124 after a one-rank raise): the example assembles no linear form of its own. If one is ever needed, conjugate the test function with ufl.conj. - float() on a shape-(1,) array (EX-86 retry, :92): take np.ravel(v)[0] and then np.real. - The comparand is evaluated at tabulate_dof_coordinates() in chunks of 20 000 distinct radii (g._exact_duty). Never use f.interpolate(callable) per point: each MAT-17 / MAT-18 leg paid a 180 s kill for that (WF-15.md:439). - UFL cannot mix meshes: the API θ goes onto the direct mesh only through g._on after _same_mesh reads geometry equal (item 330's disclosed deviation (3)). The (X) comparison with the bare ball is a point-value print only. - Each g._duty_study / g._wall_study call builds its own gmsh mesh. Hold no Function across a mesh you did not keep. g._fine() is cached inside its module: call it once. - Switch times come from the integer step index (MAT-17.md:143); the Study does this inside solve_transient_conduction. Never pass a hand-written χ to the Study: duty must be a DutyCycle, and a tuple raises TypeError ((K)). - One ρc object feeds all three forms (MAT-18.md:310). The Study builds it; never rebuild ρc by hand for (X). - No solve output is compared bitwise, and there is no cross-run == (OPS-43). (UT) is bitwise upstream of the solve only, in-process. - Rank safety: every count and max is owned-only and reduced (_theta_owned_rel, _dg0_owned_diff, (Im) via allreduce MAX). Point values go through evaluate_vector_field_parallel with identical points on every rank. No collective goes inside a rank == 0 branch, and (c3) plants on rank 0 then broadcasts (:314–317). A rank-local exception hangs the job, and Status 124 is a finding, never a retry. - XDMF: P1 / DG0 fields only, per mesh. Each key equals its Function's name. adopt_host_ownership comes last. - Runner: run_examples.sh runs host-side. Take its line from --dry-run, and never wrap the script itself in docker compose exec. Use -k 30 and the durable capture. Never background a window. - After Status 124 or a kill: run pgrep -c python3 first. WF-15, MAT-17 and MAT-18 do not move.

(6) What a negative result means. Report and stop: journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-123-<UTC>, and mark item 501 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). EX-123 stays ⬜. Never widen a band, never edit tests/ or src/, and never re-record from the example side. - (K) or (χ) red: the API's validation or schedule has drifted from item 330. Print the first differing case and file a known-issues entry against WF-15 step 3. - (UT) red: the Study builds a different problem in the complex build. This is a finding against WF-15 step 3's build coverage. Most likely cause: _dg0_two_region on a complex array (study.py:1427). Print the first differing entry and file a known-issues entry. The review decides whether the transient module needs a complex leg. - (IT) red with (UT) green: two complex MUMPS solves of one P1 system differ above L0_BAND in one process. This is a solve-floor finding for the known-issues table; the band does not move. - (G), (R) or (Im) red with (UT) and (IT) green: the gate's comparison does not reproduce in the complex build through the Study, while EX-85 / EX-86 reproduced it through the direct path. Print both beside those logs' lines; known-issues entry. - (X) identity red, or _census raising on (X): the two knobs do not compose (the schedule is not applied on the walled mesh, or the balance breaks with DG0 ρc and a schedule). Print the multipliers and the balance. This is a WF-15 finding. - (c1), (c2) or (c3) not separating: the knob does not reach the solver, or the comparator is blind. The shrink is the review's (drop (X) first); never raise -t. - A defect after every assertion is green (figure or XDMF; the EX-114 shape): BLOCKED with the log:line and returned to the review. No in-slot fix after window 3.

There is no PREDICTED RED: line, so any red stops the slot.

(7) Status it can move. EX-123 ⬜ → ✅ under the §7 Done-when that the review pastes in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-124 (mri:26) is opened 2026-10-16 by the 18:00 daily review under daily-review.md step 5. It is the §5.4 ramp from WF-1 step 13 (§10 U57, §9 item 496, DONE 2026-10-16 12:00 slot, commit 57251b34; provisional until the 10-17 weekly ratifies, WF-1.md § "Review ruling 2026-10-16 10:30 (item 496)"). - Base. tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_capacitors.py (the item-496 gate module) on the tracked tests/package/wf1/f_small_hole_pec_capacitors.yaml: the exact-rectangle PEC hole F-small, degree: 1, 64 MHz, no conductor, κ off, lossless sheets on P2–P4 at the transcribed k = 1 C_mode 6.626796421e-11 F, -n 2. The code is run_study_file's CapacitorSheets branch (src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py:1168–1178, no Touchstone, a capacitors block, kept_ports) reached from cli.main(["run", …]), which imports run_study_file at call time (src/fem_em_solver/cli.py:152, :170). - Run of record. docs/testing/logs/20261016T170623Z_WF-1-s13-W1.log (heavy by ceiling, -n 2, 10 passed in 41.1 s, :992; Elapsed 43 s, :999): one real build, two cache hits (:965); tune file cells 80 798, mesh 21.8 s, sweep 6.3 s, run_study_file 28.5 s (:966); capacitor file sweep 6.5 s (:967); Python Study 4.5 s (:968); C k = 1 6.626796421e-11 F, k = 2 9.873468900e-11 F (:969); (R0) 5.052e-11 / 3.878e-11 / 5.875e-11 (:971); (a) −2.976552e-04 (:972); (a′) +6.139e-11 (:973); (I=) S₁₁ −2.787323414e-01 + 9.590409206e-01j, impedance_ohm [0.0, −37.52636761151026] (:977); (I-Py) 2.223e-16 on one mesh, not hex-equal (:981); (I-A) 1.391811e-05 (:985); (c1) 3.5268e-01 (:989); refusals (:64–86). The re-gates RG1–RG4 are green (RG4, item 484's -n 8 W1: 9 passed in 202.4 s, 20261016T170723Z_WF-1-s13-RG4.log:7407); they are cited, not re-run. - The neighbours that back the field route. docs/testing/logs/20261016T172544Z_EX-120.log (mri:24, API route, same fixture and width): (S=) 1.842e-13 (:1781); (P) 2.687e-16 with Σ P_sheet(P2–P4) / P_src exactly 0.000e+00 on lossless sheets (:1782); centre |B| 1.03902e-06, |B₁⁺| 4.86453e-07 T per unit incident wave (:1784); two real builds at 28.7 / 35.0 s (:1787); 83 s Elapsed (:1794). docs/testing/logs/20261011T202050Z_WF-16-s10-W1.log (item 373, copper at C_F, r = 0.2 Ω): (Z) Study vs fresh-factor direct ≤ 9.122e-16 (:986–989); (P) with the ESR sheets' dissipation counted 1.328e-12 (:992); Route-A S₁₁ at r = 0.2 Ω printed only, −2.760499211e-01 + 9.536216298e-01j, rel 1.406e-05 (:984).

Gap (grep at drafting: capacitor_sheets, f_small_hole_pec_capacitors, esr_ohm over examples/**/*.py|md|yaml). - Outside examples/ansys_benchmarks/ (ANS-7's own driven-sweep script) and mri:24, no example names any of the three. No example runs a capacitor_sheets YAML file, and no example sets esr_ohm on a CapacitorSheets excitation. - mri:24 (EX-120, examples/mri/24_study_tune_then_capacitor_sheets.py) places the capacitors through the Python API. It uses the in-run C_mode, writes the lossless loaded field and shows the open-gap control. mri:21 (EX-115, examples/mri/21_femem_run_tune_section.py) runs the tune file through femem run and writes the matched-port mode field. mri:09 / mri:13 / mri:20 run other YAML families. ports:21 (EX-105) has ESR on the copper coil at C_F through PORT-24's fixture body, outside the Study and outside YAML.

The angle (judged honestly against §5.4's four axes: geometry, materials, drive, output quantity). - The bare WF-1 step-13 reproduction is too thin on its own. It uses mri:24's geometry, material and drive (lossless C_mode on P2–P4, P1 fed) and reads the same output (reduced S₁₁). Only the entry point differs (file versus Python). mri:21 over mri:19 set the precedent that a YAML entry point is worth an example, but EX-115 also carried its own output angle (the .s4p alone, the tuned field). - The drafted angle adds two things, neither restating mri:24. - (i) Tune → place across two femem run files. Item 496 ruled the one-file form out of scope ("one file cannot hold two Studies"). Here the example reads C_mode from the tune run's JSON summary on disk and writes its own YAML variant of the tracked capacitor file with that c_f. It then runs that file through femem run, the workflow a user actually follows. Custody is asserted by float.hex (structural). - (ii) A different drive: the ruling's lossy capacitors. The written file carries esr_ohm: 0.2 (the binding 2026-10-06 ruling, PROJECT_PLAN.md:3832–3851: "every lumped capacitor carries a 0.2 Ω series resistance"; scope "new steps and fixtures"; a file the example writes is a new fixture in that sense). Its field is the loaded field with ESR. It is the first example field in which the capacitors dissipate. The output quantities are new: the ESR's share of the power, the circuit-side shift Re λ_k(r) − Re λ_k(0) = r with C_mode unmoved (the ruling's clause (i)), and what 0.2 Ω does to S₁₁. Every ESR-physical number is printed, never asserted (rule (e); item 496's scope does not license a solved ESR route through YAML, and the 2026-10-16 10:30 EX-120 ruling declined to pair a gated read with this ungated load). The only assertions on the ESR arm are structural custody and two solver identities whose code path item 373 asserted at r = 0.2 Ω (question 1 for the review). - Rejected stronger-looking angles. - (a) Export a reduced Touchstone. CapacitorStudyResult.write_touchstone raises NotImplementedError (study.py:743–744). A hand-written .s1p would be an ungated output, and a src change is outside an example. - (b) A lossless field from the file route. It duplicates mri:24's field to ≈ 1e-10 (the C differs by 6.1e-11) and teaches nothing new. - (c) ESR on copper. Item 373's ground at C_F. The copper YAML route is gated at parse only ((K-cu), W1 :66), and the copper Study.tune is gated only at degree 2. That repeats the EX-120 ruling's pairing objection.

docs.title: EX-125 — mat:22, the Pennes sink on the coil-driven gel phantom: w(T − T∞) at four w under MAT-15's birdcage drives, and where the watt goes
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-125 (mat:22) is opened 2026-10-16 by the 18:00 daily review under daily-review.md step 5. It is the §5.4 ramp from MAT-15 step 4 (§10 P15, §9 item 315, GREEN 42/42 on 2026-10-08, docs/planning/chunks/MAT-15.md:252–313). MAT-15 is ✅, and step 4 is a record on it. - Base. tests/validation/test_mat15_pennes_coil_driven.py (item 315's gate module). Its fixture is MAT-15 step 1's _run_heated(return_fields=True) (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:180–351): ANS-2's F-small at 10 MHz, σ = 800 S/m, the 0.0025 m phantom rung (199 920 / 58 866 cells), four single-leg drives, G = 1 W / P₁, P1 thermal on the tag-3 submesh with the gel constants (k 0.6, ρc 4.18e6, h 10, T∞ = T(0) = 20). The gate's whole body is the module-level _run_perfused() (:114–257). It runs CN to t* = 1254 s at w_ε = 1e-8 and at w ∈ W_VALUES = (24, 240, 2400) W/m³/K per drive, plus control (d). The sink is solve_transient_conduction(..., perfusion_w_per_m3_k=w) (src/fem_em_solver/thermal/transient.py:111; perfused_power at :90, :306–308). - Run of record. docs/testing/logs/20261008T140322Z_MAT-15-step4-W1.log: -n 2, complex, 54 passed with tests/environment in 301.39 s (:2154), Status 0, Elapsed 303 s (:2222–2223). The P1 fixture took 168.8 s (EM 143.7 s, :1954) and the sink block 62.9 s (:2007); each CN took 2.7–3.1 s.

Gap (grep at drafting: perfusion_w_per_m3_k, perfus, Pennes, test_mat15_pennes, _run_perfused over examples/**/*.py). - mat:6 (examples/materials/06_perfusion_sink_robin_ball.py, EX-69) puts the sink on MAT-11 / MAT-13's 10 cm Robin ball under a uniform imposed source (q = 2000 W/m³, w = 240), against the closed-form series. - mat:7 (examples/materials/07_sar_heats_perfused_ball.py, EX-73) heats MAT-14's 1 cm lossy ball with SAR from an imposed uniform field at 64 MHz, with w = 24 000 (m R = 2). - mat:9 (09_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py, EX-79) is coil-driven on this fixture, with "no perfusion" (:20). So are mat:15 (EX-99, duty cycle, "no perfusion", :24–25) and mat:18 (EX-110, "no perfusion", :25). mat:14 / mat:16 (wall, probes) never pass a w. mri:10 / mri:13 exclude perfusion by name. - _run_perfused and test_mat15_pennes_coil_driven are imported by no file. - The angle: the first example that puts the Pennes sink under a coil-driven source: the non-uniform, C4-rotated four-drive SAR of the F-small birdcage phantom, not a uniform source or an imposed field on a ball. It runs through the gate's own body, with the gate's identities at its imported bands. It also adds three things: - the heat budget at t* (storage / Robin wall / perfusion) per w as a table, so the reader sees the sink take ≈ 0.6 %, 6 % and 45 % of the watt; - the solver's own perfused_power set against the gate's ∫wθ^(n+½); - four θ maps at w = 0 / 24 / 240 / 2400 on one mesh for ParaView, plus the sink density and the heat it removed.

Gel has no perfusion: every w here is a numerical sink term, not a gel or tissue property.

The rule (a) lift (decided: an additive keyword on _run_perfused, re-gated). _run_perfused() returns only scalars. Its base (the step 1 fields) and its CN results are locals, so an example that calls it unchanged has no field to write. The lift adds a return_fields=False keyword, and only this: - the signature def _run_perfused(*, return_fields=False):, with one docstring sentence: "return_fields=True additionally returns base (step 1's _run_heated(return_fields=True) dict) and results keyed (k, w) for w ∈ (W_EPS,) + W_VALUES (EX-125, rule (a), additive); prints and the other keys are unchanged."; - results = {} before the drive loop; - if return_fields: results[(k, W_EPS)] = res_e after the w_ε solve, and if return_fields: results[(k, w)] = res after each w solve; - if return_fields: out.update(base=base, results=results) before return out.

perfused() (:109–111) still calls _run_perfused(). No print, band, key or test changes. The extra memory is 16 TransientResults on 58 866 cells (P1, two snapshots each), a few MB.

Rejected alternatives: - (a) Copying the ≈ 100-line loop into the example and calling _run_heated(return_fields=True) with the imported _cn_w / _e_prime_w. It saves the re-gate window (≈ 6 min), but the anchors would then be an example-side copy of the gate's body, and a copy can drift silently. Rule (a) exists for this case. mat:9 (EX-79) and mat:15 (EX-99) both took the lift. - (b) Calling _run_perfused() unchanged and then _run_heated a second time for the fields.
