docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-133 (mesh:16) is the example the 2026-10-17 weekly named for chain C: "mesh:16 (the 3 T twin) after C8" (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10, the examples paragraph of the 10-17 weekly, "The examples the chains name next"). Its gated base is GEO-38 C8 (§9 item 518, 976fb77c): the F-clinical-3T table through the 1.5 T bodies, C2's box gates green at -n 4 (docs/testing/logs/20261018T171406Z_GEO-38-C8-W3-box-n4.log). docs.title: §9 item 542 — 2026-10-18 (example; example-runner)
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only drafter for the 2026-10-18 18:00 daily review; the review checks every command against its source before queueing. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, record, Done-when of another chunk or validation target. Every band is imported from the GEO-38 modules or the modules they import from.

Gap. mesh:15 (EX-117) is the 1.5 T twin: Ø 0.745 m × 0.954285714 m can, 0.45 m rungs, the box 152 mm from each cap. No example shows the 3 T geometry (rung Ø 0.704 m, can Ø 0.743 × 0.70 m, leg span 0.58 m per ruling (b)), and nothing anywhere reads the can length off a mesh — the very quantity mesh:15's guide got wrong (item 543) — or the 25 mm cap-to-box clearance that ruling (c) names for the weekly. grep -rnE "3T|3 T|F_CLINICAL_3T|test_geo38_f_clinical_3t" examples --include=*.py --include=*.md should be empty at execution (ansys_benchmarks excluded); check it in window 0.

EX-133 (mesh:16; 16_ is free in examples/meshing/ — the highest on main is 15_f_clinical_coil_astm_box; meshing examples are auto-discovered by number and run in the real build, scripts/run_examples.sh:50–53; check --list before assuming any dispatch edit) adds three tracked files and edits nothing else: - examples/meshing/16_f_clinical_3t_coil_astm_box.py; - the same-stem guide examples/meshing/16_f_clinical_3t_coil_astm_box.md, with ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## Setup figure, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step and ## Related; - examples/meshing/figures/meshing_16_f_clinical_3t_coil_astm_box_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

The angle: the 3 T twin as a user sees it, and the can that bounds it. mesh:15 reads the box. This example reproduces mesh:15's structure on the 3 T twin, keeps its two box readings, and adds the can's own reading: its diameter and length taken from the mesh's vertices, and the gel box's clearance to the can's end caps — 25 mm at 3 T against 152 mm at 1.5 T, the modelling choice ruling (c) left for the weekly.

  • Executor: example-runner. It does not spawn agents.
  • Class: example. Tier: heavy, -n 4 (asserted), real build, mesh only.
  • Slots: 12:00, 13:30 or 15:00 local only, one per slot (daytime; a clinical r1-size build under the 10-17 epitaph, as items 518 / 522 / 530 / 538). Any other slot skips it at no attempt cost. It never shares a slot with item 538 (C8b), item 530 (I33) or any other clinical-scale build; two heavy windows never run at once.
  • Width choice. -n 4 is C8 W3's width, so the gate record the example reproduces is exactly that log's; it is also the width where owned and local-copy facet counts differ (3 T sheet excess 4, …C8-W3-box-n4.log:11911), which the (cG) control shows.
  • Depends on: nothing open. Item 518 (C8) is DONE on main. Independent of item 538 (C8b) by choice: the example runs at -n 4 and imports only C8 W3's -n 4 record; the -n 1 / 2 widths add nothing it reads. If item 538 lands first and reports a width-variant cell count, the example still runs; its cells stay printed only.
  • Cost: ≈ 9 measured (example class median) / ≈ 45 predicted min: 10 fixed + ≈ 12 script (a near-copy of mesh:15's) + ≈ 7 window + ≈ 8 guide + ≈ 5 censuses / leak guard / commit. Park if window 3 has not started by minute 30 (rule (d)). Price basis: C8 W3 build 312.6 s at -n 4, gmsh 289.4 s, summed RSS 2.516 GiB (…C8-W3-box-n4.log:11897, :11900); mesh:15's run of record 324 s harness / 321.8 s script with a 6.4 s figure on 1.15 M cells (20261016T110247Z_EX-117.log; EX-117.md item 489 outcome). Window 3 predicted ≈ 335 s, range [300, 560] s. Runner -t 600 (the EX-117 18:00 ruling: with -k 30, 630 s would reach the Bash tool's 660 s). Because the range reaches ≈ 10 minutes, window 3 uses §5.1's durable-capture idiom verbatim inside the container command.
  • Shared files. Three new paths, nothing under tests/ or src/. If anything there turns out to be needed, stop and report.

Imports (never restated). - The 3 T box kwargs by C8 W3's own route: import tests.validation.test_geo38_f_clinical_box as s2, import tests.validation.test_geo38_f_clinical_3t as c8, then with unittest.mock.patch.object(s2, "_f_clinical_kwargs", c8._f_clinical_3t_kwargs): kw = s2._box_kwargs() — the swap test_geo38_f_clinical_3t.py:288 makes before the body's _box_kwargs() call (box module :54–65). Never type a 3 T value; never import a test_* name (module objects only). - From c8: F_CLINICAL_3T_BOX_CELL_RECORD (:110), SHIELD_DIAMETER_3T_M, SHIELD_LENGTH_3T_M, RUNG_DIAMETER_3T_M, RUNG_LENGTH_3T_M (:45–48), LEG_BOX_CORNER_3T_M, LEG_BOX_CORNER_ABS_TOL (:90–91), and _assert_3t_table (:228–260) — called after the build with c8._RECORD["diag"] = diag and c8._RECORD["kw"] = kw set first, so the gate's own 3 T-table assertions run verbatim (it prints on rank 0 only and holds no collective). - Everything mesh:15 imports (examples/meshing/15_f_clinical_coil_astm_box.py:48–77), unchanged: MeshGenerator, _interface_facet_tags, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership, write_setup_figure; CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND, CELL_COUNT_BAND, PORT_LOWER, PORT_UPPER, SHEET_IFACE, STRIP_BAND, _census_checks, _owned_census; from test_geo38_f_clinical_build: DESIGN_CORNER_CLEARANCE_M, LEG_COUNT, _area, _facet_coords, _owned, _ring_ports, IDENTITY_BAND. - For one printed comparison only: can_length_m from tests.package.test_geo38_clinical_fixture_page (:46–50) applied to test_geo38_f_clinical_build.F_CLINICAL_15T_KWARGS (the 1.5 T can, 0.954285714 m). - Record digits only in an example-local REC, each commented with its correct log:line (the mesh:15 mis-cite of :11898 for the cell count is not repeated): tag-2 cells 973 728 and tag-3 cells 33 540 (…C8-W3-box-n4.log:11901), N_gmsh total 2 886 (:11902). The total cell count is not in REC: it is printed beside the imported F_CLINICAL_3T_BOX_CELL_RECORD (1 061 517, :11897 / :11900).

Structural asserts at start-up. comm.size == 4; default_scalar_type is real; len(_ring_ports()) == 2 * LEG_COUNT; kw["phantom_box"]["table_offset_m"] == 0.0; "phantom_radius" not in kw; kw["coil_length"] == c8.RUNG_LENGTH_3T_M and kw["shield_radius"] == c8.F_CLINICAL_3T_KWARGS["shield_radius"] (the swap took).

Angle. No example covers this delivery mechanism, and no example has run a second solver.

The Palace service mounts ..:/workspace (docker/docker-compose.yml, fem-em-palace service), so this directory is visible to it at /workspace/examples/mri/paraview_output/…. (E2-u16) 3 the same against D2_CASE/"postpro"/"port-S.csv", same band; predicted 0.000e+00 (P) 3 _p_rec(res.s_matrix) (Tie2) 3 per class |mean − mean_P2| / |mean_P2| ≤ TIE2_BAND, from _class_means on res.s_matrix and on ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["64"], printed beside TIE2_RECORDED. This is the tie to our degree-2 record: a cross-solver identity at matched order on a shared mesh, not an accuracy level.

Printed only: res.palace_total_s beside 261.6 s; res.sha256; the Palace window's own wall time, from its log footer, in the guide.

(2) Negative controls. - (c-stage), asserted by construction, stage 1. With no Palace output on disk, the call returns no S: it raises PalaceRunRequired, and CASE_DIR/"postpro" does not exist after the raise. A read path that returned a stale or default matrix would fail this. - (c-order), backed, asserted in stage 3. Each class mean of res.s_matrix differs from Palace order 1 (OPS61/"postpro_f05x"/"port-S.csv") by > C_ORDER_FLOOR relative. Backed: 6.6674 / 2.5442 / 4.5224 % (20261018T172228Z_ARCH-1-U16c-W1.log). The weakest class clears the floor by ≈ 2.5e4×. Ceiling: the order move itself. - (c-freq), printed. Frobenius-relative distance to OPS61/"postpro_f05x_o2_f10"/"port-S.csv". Predicted ≈ 8.515e-01 (measured twice). Never asserted.

Outputs (stage 3). - The DolfinX side for ParaView: geometry and tags only, which is cheap. After the read, the script calls study.geometry.build(comm) once more. That is ≈ 27 s, and it is deterministic: U16a's (W-msh) found the same bytes on every build. It writes paraview_output/mri_30_study_palace_backend_f_small_combined.xdmf with: - CellTags (automatic); - sigma_palace, a DG0 field of the conductivity each cell carries in the case's Materials block: conductor geometry.conductor_sigma_s_per_m, phantom SALINE_SIGMA, air 0; - facet_tags=built["facet_tags"], the four narrowed port sheets that Palace reads as attributes 21–24.

Call adopt_host_ownership(OUTPUT_DIR, comm=comm) last. - No field XDMF, and why. - The Palace backend returns S only (PalaceStudyResult). The case config carries no Save key, and adding one changes the input. (W-case) would then fail, along with the "same input" claim. - A DolfinX degree-2 field on F-small is a second heavy solve: ≈ 370 s at -n 8, the only width with a degree-2 record (docs/planning/chunks/WF-16.md:37, :143). That width cannot share a run with the serial writer. - mri:8 already writes the DolfinX |E| on this fixture at degree 1. - Setup figure: rendered from the stage-3 extra build, as 08_study_four_port_birdcage.py:126–148: air hidden, phantom translucent, z = 0 slice. Title mri:30 -- F-small four-port birdcage through backend='palace' (degree 2). - CSV: paraview_output/mri_30_study_palace_backend_f_small_s_classes.csv with one row per class: |mean| and arg of the Palace read, the same for our degree-2 record, the (Tie2) gap, and the recorded gap. Values at ≤ 6 significant digits.

Guide. - ## 1 says plainly that the Study cannot launch Palace: Palace runs in its own image, and the solver container has no docker socket (the 2026-10-18 03:00 ruling R2, docs/planning/chunks/ARCH-1.md). It also says the Palace figures are a cross-solver identity on our discretisation, not an accuracy level. - ## 2 gives the three commands with their measured times: 1. ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:30 -n 1 -t 180; 2. the docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace … line that stage 1 prints; 3. the first command again. - Docref trap (measured in the checker, scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py:120–122, :474–482): the reference pass matches any *.json / *.msh / *.csv token by basename. It looks the name up in examples/mri/paraview_output/, not in a subdirectory. So the guide must never write case.json, mesh.msh, port-S.csv, palace.json, f05x_o2.json or ops61_ans4_x1_strip.msh as tokens: each would read dead. Name the case directory (it has no extension), describe its contents in words, and write Palace's argument as "the case config". Guide artifacts are named by full filename, never a stem or a glob (§9 standing rule (b)). - Related: - 08_study_four_port_birdcage.md (the DolfinX twin); - docs/planning/chunks/ARCH-1.md; - tests/package/test_arch1_palace_backend.py; - docs/guide/backends.md only if item 529 has landed it on main when the guide is written. Otherwise omit it; never create it. This item does not wait for 529.

(3) Tier, ranks, price, windows. Heavy by the Palace window. The example runs at -n 1, complex, -t 180; Palace runs at -np 8 (≤ 12).

Price inputs (measured): - write stage 27.1 s (U16c W1 :1833); - Palace order 2 on these bytes: window 264 s, Total 261.6 s, 6.0 G (20261018T140040Z_ARCH-1-U16b-W1-palace-d2.log); - the U16c module, two full read stages among its nodes, 224 s; - setup figure ≈ 3 s (20261017T110217Z_EX-129.log:50).

Predictions: - stage 1 ≈ 40 s, range [25, 120] s; - Palace ≈ 265 s, range [240, 400] s; - run of record ≈ 70 s, range [45, 160] s: two builds, the byte check, the read, XDMF, figure.

Item minutes: ≈ 9 measured (example class median) / ≈ 50 predicted: fixed ≈ 9, code ≈ 15, windows ≈ 8, guide ≈ 9, commit and journal ≈ 6, pre-checks ≈ 3.

Slot-time rule. - Take this item only as a slot's first item (never take-next). - Park by minute (rule (d)): - stage 1 not green by minute 25: park; - the Palace window not started by minute 32: do not start it, park. It may not cross the timebox (517b's rule); - the run of record not started by minute 42: park.

Windows. Each runs in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, as one bare, whole, repo-relative call. Nothing is chained, piped or redirected. 0. Pre-checks (bare docker calls, not harness windows): - docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps shows fem-em-solver Up and no fem-em-palace container; - docker image ls fem-em-palace lists 0.18.1 (a missing image is a stop, 2026-10-13 ruling (4)); - docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0; - with Glob, confirm examples/mri/30_* does not exist and the comparands do: logs/ops61/{f05x_o2.json, ops61_ans4_x1_strip.msh, postpro_f05x_o2/, postpro_f05x/, postpro_f05x_o2_f10/} and logs/u16/f_small_d2_64/{case.sha256, postpro/}. A missing comparand is BLOCKED ("comparand absent"); never re-run Palace or OPS-61 to make one; - if examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_30_study_palace_backend_f_small_case/ already holds a postpro/, stop and report: never run Palace over a Palace output. A case directory without postpro/ may stay, because stage 1 re-checks its bytes. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-134-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-134-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" Exit 2 means stale; exit 1 is a failure. Write down the predicted delta (+1 example, +1 figure) before reading the post-census. 2. Write the script. 3. Import check: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-134-import "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 10 60 python3 -c \"import tests.package.test_arch1_palace_backend as a, tests.validation.test_ans4_exact_strip_records as b, fem_em_solver.backends.palace as p; print(a.TIE2_BAND, a.C_ORDER_FLOOR, sorted(b.ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1), p.CASE_FILES)\"'" 4. Dry run: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-134-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:30 -n 1 -t 180 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 5. Stage 1 (write): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-134-stage1-write "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 1 python3 examples/mri/30_study_palace_backend_f_small.py'" Pass means Status 0, (K) / (Arg) / (W-case) / (c-stage) green, and the stage-1 closing line. 6. Before the Palace window: pgrep -c python3 reads 0, and docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps shows no fem-em-palace container. Two heavy windows never run at once. 7. Palace (the item-517b W1 form verbatim, relabelled, new cwd): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-134-palace-d2 "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_30_study_palace_backend_f_small_case && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 case.json'" Log check (executor, journalled): 117 206 elements, Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on attributes 21–24, ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz, ND (p = 2): 753062, and four GMRES solver converged lines. After any kill: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps for a lingering fem-em-palace container before anything else. 8. Run of record, EX-134 (stage 3, read): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-134 "docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 1 python3 examples/mri/30_study_palace_backend_f_small.py'" Pass means all of: - Status 0; - every anchor and (c-order) green; - the closing All assertions hold line. 9. git add the PNG and check it is ≤ 600 KiB. Write the guide from windows 5, 7 and 8's logs. Then run EX-134-post-figures / EX-134-post-docrefs (window 1's commands, relabelled): N → N + 1 with broken=0, and dead=0. 10. git status --porcelain examples/ tests/ src/ scripts/ docker/ lists only the three new paths. Run scripts/testing/check_private_leak.py on the staged logs.

After a Status 124 in a solver window: pgrep first, then the rubric-4 sweep as EX-134-cache-sweep.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Bare whole commands. Every docker or harness call is the whole Bash command: no cd … && prefix, no ; date suffix, no pipe, no redirect. Otherwise the call is denied the docker socket (fcffa701, 2026-09-30). An executor that loses the docker socket mid-item stops and reports the exact command string. - The solver container cannot run Palace, and a slot never tries a workaround: no socket mount, no Palace in the solver image (§9 compose constraint; 2026-10-18 03:00 R2). The Palace window is its own host-side harness call. - Never write into logs/u16/* or logs/ops61/*, and never touch a postpro/ there (the 10:30 ruling). D2_CASE and OPS61 are read-only comparands here. The example writes only under examples/mri/paraview_output/ and examples/mri/figures/. - "Same input" includes -np 8, Order, Tol, MaxIts and Direction. Never change any of them in-slot. palace_ranks stays at its default of 8. - Palace writes postpro/ relative to its cwd. The window must cd into the case directory, as above. - A GMRES … did not converge line, or an abort on the port set, is a finding, not a retry. That run's S is "not measured". - The writer is serial. Run the example at -n 1 only. At -n 2 the backend raises before meshing (U16 T0), and an overridden -n is a deviation. - Rank 0. At -n 1 every rank is rank 0, but write the tail as if it were not. Rank-0-only values are used only under if comm.rank == 0:, with no collective inside (the EX-127 failure). Read every tail f-string before window 8. - Leak guard. Print example-side S values and class means at ≤ 6 significant digits. _p_rec's own 12-digit σ_max line passed the guard in U16c. If check_private_leak.py flags a log, move it unchanged to logs/leak-held/, mark the item BLOCKED and stop. Never read Palace's z_matrix_ohm. No AED figure appears, and no Palace figure is set beside an AED one, in any tracked file (§5.4 (iv)). - Docrefs: full filenames only, and none of the case files' basenames (above). - run_examples.sh is host-side. Never wrap it in docker compose exec. Its dry-run is the only form used here. - No raised -t or -n, no background window, no script edit after window 8 starts (rule (i)). An edit means windows 5 and 8 again. Window 7 is not re-run if (W-case) is still green. - ≈, never a tilde, in the guide.

(5) Scope. - Covered: the Python Study on the F-small ×1 exact strip, κ off, 64 MHz, degree 2 / Palace order 2. Written, run and read in a fresh directory. S only. - Not claimed: - femem run --backend palace (U16's T5 holds it); - order 1, other frequencies or rungs, sweeps or a Touchstone; - copper, hole or F-human fixtures; - fields from Palace: SAR, B₁⁺, the loss partition, thermal (ARCH-1 (1)–(2)); - a Study that launches Palace; - accuracy, tuning, Q, any AED comparison; - an XDMF that opens a field (geometry and tags only, for the reasons above).

(6) Negative result. Report and stop. Park on attempt/EX-134-<UTC>, mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit, and journal it. - (W-case) red: today's writer or fixture differs from item 517's bytes. That is a writer or environment drift: open a known-issues entry and BLOCK. It is a record-reconciler question, never a re-export of OPS-61's mesh. - (E2) or (E2-u16) red with the log check and (P) green: Palace did not reproduce its own read on the same bytes. Open a known-issues entry ("Palace re-run not reproducible at 1e-9 on a fresh case") and BLOCK. ARCH-1 does not move; the review rules. - The log check red (element count, Rs, ND or frequency): the case is not the U16 input despite (W-case). BLOCKED. - (Tie2) above TIE2_BAND with (E2) green: impossible unless the record moved. Print it and report. - (c-order) red: the read is blind to the case. BLOCKED. - Palace Status 124: a price finding. Record it; never lengthen the timeout. - A printed prediction missed (a stage time, (c-freq)): report it in the guide and the journal. It has no status effect.

There is no PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. - EX-134 ⬜ → ✅, with the census rising by one, broken=0 and docrefs dead=0. - ARCH-1 stays 🟡: an example is not its gate of record. WF-16, OPS-61 and §2 do not move. - If a review demotes item 533, EX-134 is withdrawn.

Spawn prompt (verbatim). "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-134, §9 item 544 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-134.md, heading §9 item 544). - Read the brief and any review ruling beneath it first; the rulings hold. - You are the executor: do not spawn agents. - The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Run every window in the foreground with timeout: 660000, never in the background. - Run pgrep -c python3 (require 0) before windows 1, 5, 7 and 8, and docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps (no fem-em-palace container) before window 7. - Edit nothing under tests/, src/, scripts/ or docker/. Import every record and band; never import a test_* name. - Never write into logs/u16/ or logs/ops61/, and never touch a postpro/ there. Never change -np, Order, Tol, MaxIts or Direction. - Do not start the Palace window after minute 32; park instead. - If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command string. - Print S at ≤ 6 significant digits. Use rank-0 values only under if comm.rank == 0:. Never name the case files' basenames in the guide. - Never raise -t or -n. If check_private_leak.py blocks a log, move it unchanged to logs/leak-held/, mark the item BLOCKED and stop. - On a red, park on attempt/EX-134-*, mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit, and report. - Return the log names, each asserted and printed value beside its record or prediction, the Palace log check, the census before and after, and elapsed per window."

Questions for the review. - Q1, the guide's Palace command. The docref checker reads case.json in the command line as a dead artifact. The brief has the guide write "the case config" in its place, and stage 1 prints the literal command. An ALLOWLIST entry in the checker would let the guide show the command verbatim, but that is a tooling edit outside an example item. Accept the workaround, or open the allowlist line as a separate lane-1 item. - Q2, the 529 link. The brief leaves item 544 independent of item 529 and links docs/guide/backends.md only if it exists. Alternatively, make 544 depend on 529.

docs.title: §9 item 546 — 2026-10-19 (example, §5.4 ramp from WF-1 steps 16–17)
docs.text:
Drafted read-only for the 2026-10-19 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. It sets and moves no band, record or Done-when.

Licence. §5.4 example ramp from WF-1 step 16 (§9 item 528, U64, DONE 2026-10-18 19:30, 181c1b2d) and step 17 (§9 item 539, U65, DONE 2026-10-18 22:30, 7dd35a6f). Only those two items' gated readings, and the bands their modules import, are asserted. No new YAML file is written: every file the example runs is tracked under tests/package/wf1/ and was gated by 528 or 539.

Gap evidence (drafter, grep 2026-10-19). - No examples/** file names transverse_quadratic, TransverseQuadraticHeatSource, test_wf1_yaml_thermal_box_quadratic or test_wf1_yaml_thermal_box_probes. - No example reads a probes block back from a run's JSON summary. ans:9 takes its probe points from a Python spec dict; mat:24 / mat:25 read Study.probe results in memory. - examples/mri/30_* is EX-134 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-134.md, §9 item 544, open); examples/mri/31_* does not exist. The runner resolves mri:31 by its own 31_ prefix (scripts/run_examples.sh:206–210), so it does not wait for mri:30.

Angle. Two firsts, on two separate sets of tracked files: - The first example whose prescribed heat source is non-uniform and set in the file. excitation.source: {kind: transverse_quadratic} gives q(x) = 3 q (y² + z²)/(B² + C²) (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:1491). mri:20's heat comes from a solved EM field, not a prescribed source. - The first example that reads a probe table back from the JSON summary. That is probes.{centres, radii, values_k, volumes_m3} (src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py:1605–1610), tied to U60's five ball-mean readings and the whole-box identity.

How it differs from its neighbours: - Unlike mri:29 (EX-132): that example runs uniform-source files with no outputs block. Here the source is non-uniform (P2), and the summary carries a probe table. - Unlike mat:24 / mat:25 (EX-130 / EX-131): those build Python objects (ThermalBoxGeometry → Study.temperature / Study.probe). Here the input is the text file and the output is the bundle.

No file combines the two capabilities. The quadratic source with outputs.probes is ungated: 528 scoped probes out (docs/planning/chunks/WF-1.md:2150), and 539 scoped out "probes … with U64's transverse source" (WF-1.md:2320). The example runs the two file sets separately, never writes a file that carries both, and asserts (F-none) below.

Executor and files. example-runner, which spawns no agents. It adds exactly three tracked files and edits nothing under tests/ or src/: - examples/mri/31_femem_run_gel_box_source_and_probe_files.py; - the same-stem guide, with ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## Setup figure, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step and ## Related; - examples/mri/figures/mri_31_femem_run_gel_box_source_and_probe_files_setup.png, ≤ 600 KiB.

Build: one run, complex, with reasons. Nothing is dropped; the probe leg asserts bands only. The two gates ran in different builds: - 528's solve legs assert IS_COMPLEX (tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_thermal_box_quadratic.py:234). P36's records are complex-build records, and both the steady and the CN leg are complex (20261019T003608Z_WF-1-s16-W1a-steady.log:12, …003738Z_WF-1-s16-W1b-cn.log:12). - 539's solve legs assert not IS_COMPLEX (test_wf1_yaml_thermal_box_probes.py:234). U60's box-probe records are real-build records (20261019T033412Z_WF-1-s17-W1-probes.log:12, with no complex-mode source).

The runner sources the complex build for every mri: example (scripts/run_examples.sh:273–274), so there is no real-build mri: run. A split would need a second group or a non-runner window, and neither has precedent for an EM-free solve.

The probe leg therefore follows EX-130's ruled and audited precedent (EX-130.md:35; audit PASS, EX-130.md:182): - the real-build gate's bands are asserted; - its digits are printed only, beside the complex readings EX-130 already measured on the same Study.probe route. Those match U60's .4e digits on all five centres, plus (A-box) and (c-wall) (20261018T214035Z_EX-130.log:64–70, :82).

539's own hypothesis is that the file calls the same Study.probe as the API (docs/testing/attempts.md:1712). Its scope line "Not claimed: the complex build for the probe legs" (WF-1.md:2322) is Q1 below. If the review answers Q1 "no", the probe leg is dropped as Q1 specifies, and the item stays openable on the quadratic leg alone.

CLI capture. cli.main imports run_study_file inside the call (src/fem_em_solver/cli.py:159) and calls it at :201. Copy mri:29's helpers verbatim from examples/mri/29_femem_run_f2182_gel_box_files.py:93–153: - fmt, hexeq, flat_diff; - cli_run, the call-through wrapper on fem_em_solver.study_yaml.run_study_file, restored in finally, with is original asserted; - cli_check, with stdout captured by contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()) and the lines read on rank 0; - read_summary, which does a Barrier and then json.load on every rank; - ones_tags.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Build. Never call b._require: it asserts the real build and raises here. Never compare a digit or hex across builds. Use d._on_p / d._owned_rel for the P2 box and b._on / b._theta_owned_rel for the P1 balls (docs/testing/attempts.md:1678). - (I-Py) on the ball compares temperatures, not θ, normalised by max|T − T∞| (the shared helper). Keep the copied bodies' arguments. - The ball file solves twice. _run_thermal_ball runs, then Study.probe re-solves (study_yaml.py:1634–1640). run.thermal and run.probes.thermal are different objects, and the body's two check compares them; keep it. - source_multipliers on an unscheduled run is empty (EX-135's in-slot red, EX-135.md:335). Assert a length only where a duty is set: 41 on the quadratic duty JSON, 95 on the duty ball. On m19, compare JSON == memory and print the length. - The ball summary is not the box summary. It has no temperature.source; dt_s / n_steps sit at the top of the temperature block, and there is a wall key (study_yaml.py:1497–1519). Name every artifact by its full filename, never a stem or a glob (§9 standing rule (b)). - Leak guard. - Print θ and probe values at ≤ 6 significant digits: fmt for θ, .6g for values_k (substitution 4; B19:82–83, :95–96 print full repr). - Print errors at .3e / .4e. The gate's .6e record string stays as the gate prints it; it passed the guard in D18. - Never print a summary dict or a JSON whole. - d._check_summary prints the unrounded θ_max and power (D18:70), so redirect its stdout (substitution 5). - The guard matches at 8 digits (check_private_leak.py:76). - Rank 0. Everything that exists only on rank 0 is used only under if rank0:. That includes check stdout lines, CSV rows and the return of write_xdmf_with_tags (the EX-127 failure). No collective inside if rank0:. Both _check_summarys, _same_mesh, _domain_mean, _rel_p, _exact_p, b._all and Study.probe are collective, so call them on every rank. Read every tail f-string before window 4. - Mesh mixing. There are three result meshes (box th.mesh, the m19 probe mesh, the duty-ball mesh), and each Python Study builds its own. Fields move only through _on / _on_p after a same-mesh check. That is why there is one XDMF per mesh. - Comparands. Use the body's _exact_p (chunked), never interpolate(callable) on a series. Reuse ex_d and ex_s for the XDMF; the two series cost most of the quadratic leg's ≈ 117 s. - .eval bytes depend on batch composition (item 537; PROJECT_PLAN §9 rulings, POST-8.md:870). Every byte comparison is made call by call on that call's own array. The JSON values and run.probes.values are one list from one ball_average pass (study_yaml.py:1645), not an .eval re-sample. Never re-sample θ or a probe by .eval and compare bytes against the run, and never concatenate or split a batch. - XDMF needs P1, and np.real before every float. - Wrapper. Restore study_yaml.run_study_file in finally and assert is original (31_…py:141–146). A leaked wrapper corrupts every later call. - Runner. ./scripts/run_examples.sh is host-side, so never wrap it in docker compose exec. Emit, then harness. Use -k 30. - Windows. No background window, no raised -t / -n, no script edit after window 4 starts, and no guide edit after window 5 starts (rule (i)). - No new YAML. Never write a file that sets a source with probes, duty-quadratic with probes, or a walled ball with probes (545 refuses the last, ruling Q3).

(5) Scope. - Covered: - femem check / femem run in-process (cli.main) on four tracked files: the duty-cycled transverse-quadratic thermal_box file, two ball-probe thermal_ball files and one malformed ball file; - one in-memory refusal (duty without transient); - P38's duty-cycled quadratic source CN to t* at m = 4, P2; - MAT-19's ball with five probes at P1, and the duty ball's pass-through; - complex, -n 2; - the summaries and the ball probe table read back from disk and tied to P38, SCHEDULE, Q·V, the CN balance and U60. - Not claimed: - a source with probes in one file, which is ungated; - a walled ball with probes (refused); - any comparand on the duty-ball probes; - probes at P2; - scalar point values (P37); - a complex-build gate of the ball-probe file route. The example's complex readings are example records, not a gate (Q1); - the real build; - another duty, period or weight; - the installed console script, --ranks or --estimate; - EM, a coil or SAR (the quadratic is the closed-form shape, not a solved field); - perfusion; - bundle reproducibility (mri:27); - F2182 compliance; - any external check.

That is a finding against _run_thermal_ball_probes (study_yaml.py:1628–1655). Handle it the same way. - (S-json), (Sch-json), (P-json) or (E-json) red: the summary misreports a gated quantity. Handle it the same way. - (F-diff) or (F-none) red: a tracked input changed since drafting. BLOCKED, re-pose. - The wrapper captures nothing: the CLI route differs from cli.py:159/:201. BLOCKED, with no fallback to calling run_study_file directly. - A printed value missed (the θ_max ratio, the duty-ball balance, a time, the m19 cell count): report it in the guide and the journal. It has no status effect. - A kill at 590 s: not a result; a price finding.

docs.title: Review ruling 2026-10-19 10:30 (item 550)
docs.text:
• Q1: yes — one complex run, ball leg kept. The item 546 pattern binds: the real-build gate's bands asserted, its .4e digits printed, never asserted as strings. The m19 leg is a first complex run of the ball-probe route; its readings are example records, not a complex gate of WF-1 step 19. A ball red with every quadratic anchor green is a reported finding (known-issues entry, item BLOCKED), not a re-pose inside the slot and never a band.
  • Q2: keep the duty-ball file, identities only, as 545 gated it. If the run of record exceeds 450 s, that is a price finding for the journal, not a reason to drop it in-slot.
  • Q3: run before the weekly. If the weekly reverts U66 or U67, EX-136 is withdrawn or narrowed exactly as (7) states, by the next review.
  • Measured minutes: the example class median is 10.0 (this review's table), not 8.4.
  • Ordering: 550 is independent; it may be taken as take-next under its minute lines.

Gap evidence (drafter, grep 2026-10-20). - grep -rl probes examples/mri/ hits only 01_coil_phantom_fields.md (a "Frequency probes" table column, :167), 29_*, 31_*, 32_* and their XDMFs: every probe example is a thermal ball-average probe (thermal_box / thermal_ball files). Angle. The first example whose output quantity is a point SAR / |E| table written by femem run from an EM study file: the user lists five [x, y, z] points under outputs.probes.points in a four-port F-small file, the CLI solves the four single-port drives once, and the JSON summary carries probes.{points, owner, sigma_s_per_m, rho_kg_m3, values.P<k>.{sar_w_per_kg, e_abs_v_per_m}} (study_yaml.py, _em_probe_summary, item 564 (P4)). The example reads that table from disk, ties it to an independent Python Study at L0_BAND, shows a 1 mm displaced probe reading differently, and puts the four per-port |E| maps with the probe sites in ParaView. Unlike mri:14 the input is the text file and the output is the bundle; unlike mri:27 the bundle carries probes; unlike mri:29–32 the probes are EM point values under the owner rule, not thermal ball averages.

Never sample these display fields at the probes and compare them to the table (P1 / DG0 interpolation, not the owner-rule point value). - One CSV, rank 0, paraview_output/mri_33_femem_run_em_file_point_probes_probe_table.csv: port, point index, x, y, z, SAR from disk (.6g), |E| from disk (.6g), Python-twin SAR (.6g), relative difference (.3e), REC digits equal; plus one row per port for the displaced point and its miss. - Run bundle paraview_output/mri_33_run_em_probes/ (t._fresh_dir first).

Guide. ## 1: the YAML's outputs.probes.points block line by line; the summary's probes keys; that values are per 1 V port drive for each single-port drive (not a quadrature drive and not a superposition: the table has no phases, so a combined-drive SAR cannot be rebuilt from it); that points outside the phantom are refused (σ and ρ are the phantom's); that the owner rule makes a point on a cell facet read the same at any width (cite POST-8). ParaView recipe: open the XDMF, colour by E_abs_P1, threshold probe_sites > 0, then local_sar_P1. ## 2: ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:33 -n 2 -t 300, with the measured wall time; femem run tests/package/wf1/f_small_em_probes.yaml is the same call from a shell. ## 3 walks the probe table CSV first. Related: examples/mri/14_study_sar_and_b1.md, examples/mri/27_femem_run_bundle_reproducible.md, examples/mri/32_femem_run_ball_probes_and_duty_quadratic_files.md, tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_em_probes.py, tests/package/wf1/f_small_em_probes.yaml, docs/planning/chunks/WF-1.md. Write ≈. Write "the JSON summary", never summary.json as a token.

(3) Tier, ranks, price, windows. Standard by prediction, heavy by ceiling (the EX-106 form): complex, -n 2, runner -t 300.

Price inputs (measured): W1 106 s at -n 2 (W1:5522): file run 68.2 s (W1:3686) + Python twin 34.3 s (W1:5509) + four small point_sar batches; check and the refusal rows, no mesh, < 5 s (W0 4 s); setup figure ≈ 5 s and XDMF of 9 fields on 117 206 cells ≈ 5–10 s (mri:14 wrote 8 fields on the same mesh in a 74 s run, EX-106 row; fr.mesh / fr.cell_tags / fr.fields[pid], 14_…py:205, :228, :319); start-up ≈ 10 s. Prediction: run of record ≈ 130 s, range [110, 260]. A kill at 300 s is a price finding, not a result.

Item minutes: ≈ 10.0 measured (example class median, 2026-10-19 10:30 review) / ≈ 40 predicted (fixed ≈ 9, script ≈ 14 — one copied body plus (J-disk) and the outputs, windows ≈ 6, guide and censuses ≈ 11).

Park by the minute (rule (d)). If windows 1–3 are not green and the script is not written by minute 28, park. If the run of record has not started by minute 35, park. Never start window 4 after minute 40. As take-next, count from the slot's start.

Windows. Each runs in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, as one bare, whole, repo-relative call — nothing chained, piped or redirected. 0. docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0, and no other heavy / xl / xxl window may be live. (4) Traps already paid for. - Harness calls are bare and whole (bash_guard.py, 2026-09-30): no cd … &&, no ; date, no | tail, no redirect. ./scripts/run_examples.sh is host-side: never wrap it in docker compose exec; emit with --dry-run, then run each printed line through run_and_log.sh as its own bare call. Container timeout -k 30 always. - Durable capture is not needed at ≈ 130 s; if used anyway, copy §5.1's idiom verbatim including the trailing ; exit $rc (a dropped ; exit $rc footers Status: 0 over a red, WF-6 step 4h). - Build. The mri: runner sources /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode (run_examples.sh:74, :279); the emitted line does not set FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 (it governs pytest skip markers only, tests/complex_mode.py:11–27), so the script asserts t.IS_COMPLEX on entry, and the import window sets it. A real build would fail loudly at (B), never skip. - point_sar takes f.e_real, f.e_imag — never the complex field twice (it takes np.real of each and silently halves SAR, tests/validation/test_birdcage_sar_map.py:295–302). - Point evaluation only through point_sar (collective; points identical on every rank); never f.eval(points, …). A bitwise claim names its batch (item 537; rubric 4): (U′) and (J-disk) compare the same five-point batch call by call; the displaced point is its own one-point batch and is compared by a relative band, never bytes. - One field solve per Study. _solve_port_fields caches on study.fields_result; never clear it; the only second Study is the declared Python twin. Free the twin (del, gc.collect(), Barrier) before the XDMF if RSS is printed high. - Never write the gate's npz (logs/wf1/s20/em-probes-n2.npz): item 564's width legs read it (substitution 4). - Leak guard. Print new values at ≤ 6 significant digits (.6g) and errors at .3e / .4e; the copied per-port .6e rows passed the guard in W1 and stay; never print .15e (_legacy not copied), a summary dict or a JSON whole. The guard matches at 8 digits (check_private_leak.py:76). No AED number appears anywhere. - Rank 0. check stdout lines, CSV rows and write_xdmf_with_tags's return exist on rank 0 only: use them only under if rank0:, with no collective inside (EX-127's failure). point_sar, _bitwise_equal_across_ranks, _solve_port_fields, write_setup_figure and the JSON read's Barrier are collective. - XDMF needs P1 / DG0 real arrays; np.real before every write and every float. - Wrapper. Restore study_yaml.run_study_file in finally and assert is original; a leaked wrapper corrupts every later call. - summary.json is not a guide token (check_example_doc_references.py:116–122); name every artifact by its full filename (§9 standing rule (b)). - Windows. No background window, no raised -t / -n, no script edit after window 4 starts, no guide edit after window 5 starts (rule (i)).

(5) Scope. Covered: femem check / femem run in-process (cli.main) on the tracked f_small_em_probes.yaml (item 192's F-small four-port fixture, PEC, degree 1, 64 MHz, κ off, exact-rectangle ports, complex, -n 2); five point SAR / |E| probes per single-port 1 V drive under the owner-rule default; the table read from disk and tied to an independent Python Study at L0_BAND; a 1 mm displaced probe missing; two out-of-phantom refusals. Not claimed: absolute, quadrature-drive or compliance SAR (per-1 V single-port values only); a combined-drive SAR rebuilt from the table (no phases); C4 symmetry of the table; probes on F-human, copper or capacitor files (copper F-small reachable, unmeasured; capacitor sheets refused); degree 2; the -n 1 / -n 4 widths (gated by item 564, not re-run here); a peak search or 10 g averaging (mri:14); the display fields' values at the probes; the installed console script, --ranks or --estimate; any external check.

(6) Negative result. Report and stop; journal in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-138-<UTC>, mark item 569 BLOCKED in the same commit. Never widen a band, never move a probe, never edit tests/ or src/. - (K) / (X-out) red: the parser moved since b688beed; BLOCKED, re-pose. - (R) or (I-Py) red: an example/test divergence on the build and width of record; print the first differing value beside W1, file a known-issues entry against WF-1 step 20. - (U′) or (J-disk) red with (I-Py) green: the JSON or the summary misreports point_sar; finding against _em_probe_summary, known-issues entry. - (c-disp) not missing: blind instrument; stop. - The wrapper captures nothing: the CLI route moved; BLOCKED, no fallback to calling run_study_file directly. - A printed value missed (REC digits, the near-point index, a time): reported in the guide and the journal, no status effect. - A kill at 300 s: not a result; a price finding.

No PREDICTED RED: line: any red stops the slot.

Licence. Daily-review.md step 5, the example ramp. It demonstrates a gated capability (IMP-7 ✅) from an angle no example covers: the output quantity is an implant-driven temperature rise, and the material is a high-k metal core. No band, tolerance, record, Done-when or target is set or moved. Every band is imported by name.

What the example does. It runs IMP-7 step 1's metal-core case (§9 item 594, tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py) on one rung, the middle one (LADDER[1] = 1.0e-3 m, 152 914 cells), and narrates it. - Fixture: two_layer_ball_domain(inner_radius=A, outer_radius=B, resolution=LADDER[1]) with A = 5 mm and B = 4A. - Conductivity: DG0 k = K_CORE in the core (tag 1) and K_GEL in the shell (tag 2). - Source: the β = 1 quasi-static dipole SAR of the PEC sphere, on shell cells only. It is interpolated into DG2 from the public pec_sphere_implant_source(points, radius=A, q_far=Q_FAR, beta=1.0), restricted with cells0= to tag-2 cells. - Boundary: Robin H, T_INF on r = B. - Solve: solve_steady_conduction(…, degree=1). - Comparand: pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature(points, radius=A, outer_radius=B, k_core=K_CORE, k_gel=K_GEL, q_far=Q_FAR, h=H, t_inf=T_INF), interpolated into P2.

Everything is imported, not re-implemented (the ANS-1 rule): - A, B, LADDER, FIX, S2_BAND, S3_BAND, R0_READ from tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py:52–66; - H, K_CORE, K_GEL, Q_FAR, T_INF from tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_closed_form.py; - QDEG, _allsum, _dg0, _indicator from tests/validation/test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_fem.py; - the private helpers _q_shell, _theta_metal, _errors, _source_dg2, _p2 from the IMP-7 step-1 module, by name. Standing rule (a) lets an example import a gate fixture's helpers; never a test_* name. If the executor prefers the public pec_sphere_implant_source over _q_shell for the source, it prints the source integral beside the gate module's src=6.802147e-02W at this rung (20261022T202402Z_IMP-7-step1-W1.log:67), and the two must agree to B1_BAND — then say which one it used.

Gates (asserted; bands imported). - (S2) interior rel L2 ≤ S2_BAND (1e-2) on the 1.0 mm rung. Record, printed beside it and never asserted: 1.2080e-03 (20261022T202402Z_IMP-7-step1-W1.log:67, real build). - (S3) balance ≤ S3_BAND (1e-9). Record: 9.099e-14 (:67). - (Src′) the assembled source power equals the closed-form shell integral to B1_BAND, as the gate module asserts it (test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py:316–317). - (Im) max |Im T_h| = 0 in the complex build (mat:12's gate, 12_gel_ball_in_container_wall.py:411). - (c-iso), asserted, backed. Backing: the same comparison on the same fixture at CONTROL_RES = 1.0e-3 m read 2.7326e-02 (20261022T202402Z_IMP-7-step1-W1.log:78), 2.7× the band.

Printed only, never gated. - The pole and equator temperature rise at R0_READ = 1.1a against the closed form. Record: pole 0.359626 vs 0.361610 K, equator 0.344320 vs 0.343661 K (:71, finest rung). - The l = 2 readout R₂,h: printed with the sentence that it is a difference of two near-equal numbers (pole − equator is ≈ 5 % of the mean). Both arms take the ccw superposition at 64 MHz and one normalisation G, then MAT-15's thermal route to t*. Leave out I41's vacuum control (unmapped 403, :3779). Check every name at execution, and never import a test_* name. - From tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_heating_matched.py (as i41): _merge_rod_into_phantom, _census, _arm_with_403, plus _run only if its body can skip the control by argument. If it cannot, write _run's body out without the control arm, and call nothing that runs it. - From tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_heating_phantom.py: SOURCE, _parent_wall_count, _heat_arm. - From tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py: _build_rod, _build_kept_rod, KEPT_ROD_CELL_RECORD. - From tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py: _arm, TIPS. - The bands as i41 imports them: B_BAND, E_BAND, S2_BAND, C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. - _arm_with_403 replaces build_four_port_sweep temporarily (i41 :104). Use it as the module does, restore in finally, and never leave the patch live across arms.

Gates (asserted; bands imported). - (A0m) cells = KEPT_ROD_CELL_RECORD, tag-403 = 15 000, arm M's tag 3 equal to arm R's 51 693, asserted before any solve, as i41 :147–149 does. - (W0), the discriminating check, asserted and backed: arm M excludes 0 rod-wall facets and arm R excludes exactly its parent tag-402 count (4 958). A build that left the rod in arm M reads 4 958, not 0 (:3679 against :3724). - (B) / (E) / (E′) / (S2) on both arms at B_BAND / E_BAND / S2_BAND. The records are under 6e-15, 5.1e-14 CN, 2.4e-14 and 5.13e-6 respectively. - (C4) on arm M at C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, worst 0.93 % (:3686–3689).

docs.title: EX-175 — refresh the stale example artifacts, in batches, on main
docs.text:
History file for the §7 EX-175 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-02 10:30 daily review; for the weekly to ratify, since EX-22 and EX-30 were weekly commissions. Lane 1's kind of work: a closing window on the current tree for rows whose last window is old.

Why. The docrefs checker reports stale=208 (20261102T124159Z_EX-174-docrefs.log:248): artifacts of 109 examples older than its 336 h limit, the oldest ≈ 1 010 h, each line saying "rerun the example that writes it". Reviews have recorded the exit 2 and moved on. What the count hides is that those examples have not run against main for up to six weeks, while the package has moved under them. A re-run is the only test that they still pass their own imported gates. It needs no new target: the anchor is each example's own assertions.

Done-when. Each batch's windows exit 0 with no script, guide, gate or band edited; each batch's named artifacts leave the stale list; a red or a kill is filed in known-issues and nothing is fixed in passing. EX-175 closes when the four batches below have landed. The remaining stale set goes to the weekly with its count.

The common brief (items 762, 763, 764, 766).

Windows. One harness call per example, bare, in the example's own documented form, labelled EX-175-<group><n>: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-175-imp1 "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:1 -n 2 -t 180". Then one docrefs window for the batch: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-175-b<k>-docrefs "timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py".

Anchor. Each window's Status 0 and the example's own closing assertion line, read in the log. The imported gates are the example's and nothing is restated.

Negative control. The artifact moved. Each batch's stems are in 20261102T124159Z_EX-174-docrefs.log and must be absent from the batch's docrefs window. Compare by name, not by count: artifacts age into the list by wall clock while a window runs, which is the whole of the 203 → 208 rise (EX-174's audit). A Status 0 with the stem still stale means the window did not write what the guide cites, and that is a finding.

After each window. git status --porcelain shows only logs and test-results.md. A tracked file that a run rewrites is a finding: name it, and restore nothing silently.

Tier, ranks. Each example's own -n and -t, listed below, unchanged. FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES stays unset. Pre-check pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Skip the slot if uptime loadavg (1 min) reads ≥ 16.

Executor. The implementer directly: there is no script to write.

Class. Example. The class median understates these: a batch is several windows, and each should run ≈ 10–25 min. The floor counts the median as the protocol says.

Timebox. A slot starts no new window after minute 45. Windows not run stay listed in the item's outcome, and the item lands partial.

Traps already paid for. Never edit an example to get green. No window above ≈ 600 s container-side; every -t below is at or under it. Foreground only, Bash timeout 660000 ms. A kill keeps its log, and a size kill is a finding, never raised. A leak-guard hit: the log moves unchanged to logs/leak-held/; these are not the ans: group, so one would be a surprise worth naming. Count verdicts per rank by token. mat:, imp: and th: run complex under run_examples.sh (EX-173's audit). A digit in a guide may differ from a new log at round-off: that is not a red, and the guide is not edited.

Scope. A re-run. Not claimed: a re-closure of any EX-* chunk, any guide digit, or any new capability.

Negative result. A red or a kill: stop the batch, keep the log, file a known-issues entry naming the example, the window and the first failing assertion, and mark the item BLOCKED with what ran. That is the item's most useful outcome. No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. EX-175 progress, then ✅; a new known-issues entry per red.

Otherwise mark the temperature claim "a reading, not measured". - :77 (Step 4): "Because the dose is nonlinear in temperature, the same drift reads as a larger fraction …". docs.title: §9 item 768 — 2026-11-02 (example; §5.4 ramp from IMP-8)
docs.text:
Licence. Daily-review.md step 5. No band or target is set or moved. It is not a chain step and takes no count on chain I.

What the example does. A create_box viewing grid, not a model: half-width 60 mm on each axis, 41 cells per axis, an odd count on a symmetric box, so no vertex lies on the line. The nearest vertex is at x = y = ±h / 2 with h = 120 / 41 ≈ 2.93 mm, so r ≈ 2.07 mm, outside the 1 mm ROD_RADIUS. Assert that minimum r > ROD_RADIUS on the mesh, reduced with comm.allreduce, because this is the geometry the whole file rests on. At t = T_PRINT (900 s), per watt of total power, on P1: - theta_line: Φ / (4πkL), the midpoint sum on N_FIELD = 64 points, written locally with the imported _point so it broadcasts over the vertices. _phi_midpoint itself is scalar (np.sum over all axes). - theta_tips: Φ₂ / (4πkL), from the imported _phi_tips, which broadcasts as written. - ratio: theta_tips / theta_line.

Set these through V.tabulate_dof_coordinates() or f.interpolate, real values into the complex build's x.array.

Gates (asserted; bands imported; collected first, then asserted). From tests.validation.test_imp8_rod_line_source_closed_form: - (Rate) the slope on RATE_LADDER at RATE_POINT (millimetres: multiply by MM), t = T_PRINT, inside [RATE_LO, RATE_HI]. Reference by _phi, as test_rate_midpoint_sum_against_line does. The band is item 760's, provisional. - (Far2) _far2_miss() against its bound, as test_far2_tip_pair_against_line does, Φ∞ the larger. - (Node) at the vertex nearest (20, 0, 0) mm, the theta_line value equals _phi_midpoint(r, z, T_PRINT, N_FIELD) / (4πkL) to B1_BAND, and the theta_tips value equals _phi_tips(r, z, T_PRINT) / (4πkL) to B1_BAND. On whichever rank owns it, reduced, so every rank agrees. This pins the broadcast form to the gated scalar one. - (c-one), asserted: _far2_miss(signs=(1.0,)) misses by > FAR2_A⁴, as test_control_one_source_dropped does. - (c-field), asserted: dropping one tip from theta_tips moves the value at the vertex nearest (0, 0, 15) mm by more than B1_BAND. Ceiling not computed: it is large by construction, since that vertex sits by one tip.

Read the two helpers' bodies in the module before writing these: the keyword form of _far2_miss's return, and how test_control_one_source_dropped calls it, are the module's, and this brief does not restate them.

Printed only (no band). - Φ₂ / Φ at (2, 15) and (2, 0) mm by _phi and _phi_tips, beside item 760's records 3.179482 and 0.1714577, named as that window's. Print 7 digits or fewer. - The min and max of ratio on the box. - The energy in the box, ρc ∫ θ dV per watt, against 900 J per watt, for both shapes, with np.real and an MPI sum. A reading, with no band: it runs low from leakage past the box and from P1 on the near-line field, and nobody has computed by how much, so the guide says the two are not separated.

Guide. Use imp:20's headings. State plainly that this is a closed form on a viewing grid: no FEM, no solve, no wall, no rod heat capacity, and neither shape is claimed to be a real rod's. Say where the two shapes differ most and where they agree. Related: imp:17, imp:20. Round-off digits (03:00 ruling): quote a round-off term as a bound, or name the window its digits came from. Write ≈, never a tilde. Check every derived number in the prose by hand. State no cause you did not measure (EX-176's audit: "because the dose there is smaller" has no log behind it).

Executor: example-runner, foreground. Tier: standard, -n 2. - Prediction: seconds of closed form plus the mesh and one XDMF. -t 180, with -k 30 on every container timeout. - Class: example. Cost: ≈ 7.8 measured / 25 predicted min. Depends on: nothing. Family: EX-178, attempt 1 of 4. - Skip this slot if pgrep -c python3 in the container reads above 0, or uptime loadavg (1 min) reads ≥ 16.

Windows. As EX-173.md, with the label EX-178, the group imp:21, -n 2 and -t 180. Closing window: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-178 "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:21 -n 2 -t 180", the last window. The setup figure comes from one earlier flagged window, labelled EX-178-figure, which closes nothing. Nothing is edited after the closing window, the guide included.

The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped.

Traps already paid for. The group runs complex, so np.real on each integral, and assert max|Im θ| as mat:35 does. assemble_scalar and local max / min are rank-local: reduce. write_xdmf_with_tags needs a cell_tags, built as mat:34 builds it (:160–164). Take _point and the constants by name, restate none. Not one .eval: (Node) compares dof values. _phi uses quad, so keep it to the few probes above and never call it per vertex. A kill parks the item; never raise the timeout.

Scope. One example. Not claimed: any F2182 figure, a rod's SAR shape, a wall effect, entry 55's tip θ, or the FEM half of IMP-8, which is the weekly's to pose.

Negative result. A gate red: stop, keep the log, BLOCKED. No PREDICTED RED: line.

docs.text:
History file for the §7 EX-179 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-03 03:00 daily review under the 11-02 weekly's refresh-lane rule (PROJECT_PLAN §10, "Rulings, 2026-11-02", the EX-175 / EX-177 bullet): while the census reads stale > 0 the daily keeps one refresh batch in the queue (≈ 6 examples, the oldest first, ≤ 480 s each, mri: / ports: / mesh: / ans: before the rest), under EX-177's Done-when. The mag: family and the -n 4 / -n 8 examples stay outside until priced. Lane 1's kind of work; not a chain step.

Why. docrefs' stale rule is a 336 h mtime limit on every referenced artifact (OPS-42), so every example goes stale a fortnight after its last run whether or not anything moved. EX-175 and EX-177 re-ran 56 examples green with nothing edited and left stale=108 (20261103T050726Z_EX-177-b10-docrefs.log:148). The re-runs are a regression result over examples the slots otherwise never re-run. Cost, measured by the weekly: ≈ 7.8 minutes per batch, ≈ 16 measured minutes a day.

Done-when (per batch, as EX-177's). Each batch's windows exit 0 with no script, guide, gate or band edited; each batch's named artifacts leave the stale list by name against the previous batch's docrefs log; a red or a kill is filed in known-issues and nothing is fixed in passing. The chunk stays 🟡 while the lane runs; the weekly closes it or names a successor.

The common brief (every batch below). EX-175.md's "common brief" binds, verbatim, with EX-177.md's amendments (full log basenames in this file; the leak guard on a hit — move the log unchanged to logs/leak-held/, report, go on; ./scripts/run_examples.sh is the form to run; -n as the guide's own; no new window after minute 45, unrun windows stay listed and the item lands partial), with the label EX-179-<group><n> and the docrefs label EX-179-b<k>-docrefs. Each window is one bare harness call, foreground, Bash timeout 660000 ms:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-179-<group><n> "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e <group>:<n> -n <n> -t <s>"

(the form EX-175 … EX-177 ran, EX-175.md:12), and the batch closes with one docrefs window: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-179-b<k>-docrefs "timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py". Pre-check once per slot: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0.

Anchor: each example's own asserted gates (its closing "hold" / "PASS" line and Status 0). Control: the artifact moved — the batch's stems present in the baseline docrefs log and absent from the batch's own. Traps, scope, negative result: as EX-175 / EX-177. A red is the item's most useful outcome: stop, file it, fix nothing. No PREDICTED RED: line. Status it can move: EX-179 progress (the stale count by name); a new known-issues entry per red. Class: example. Executor: the implementer directly. Depends on: nothing.

The -t ceiling (this review's reading of "≤ 480 s each"). Some guides' run lines carry no -n / -t, so run_examples.sh falls back to -n 2 -t 1200 (scripts/run_examples.sh:25–26). A 1200 s window breaks §9's ≈ 600 s window rule. Those examples run at -n 2 -t 480, the lane's ceiling, and the outcome says so. A kill at 480 s is a finding about the ceiling: file it and leave the example unedited. It is never a reason to raise the ceiling. Examples whose own guide -t is above 480 s are listed below for the weekly to price; they are not in these batches.

docs.text:
Executes §10 I77, the 11-07 weekly's enumerated step. Its words are: "I66, I69, I73's arms on a box of ≤ 120 000 cells, the table of θ(2, 0) and θ(2, 15) mm and the tip-point ratio per arm, (E) and (S0) asserted, (I) on the gel arm printed with the band beside it". The box is sized as I61's W0 did (EX-182). Family EX-188, attempt 1 of 4. Executor: example-runner, spawned in the foreground, with the bare-call sentence verbatim in the spawn prompt.

What the example does. Everything is written out in main(), because pytest fixtures (box) cannot be imported. - Mesh: one coarse box, a disclosed local copy of imp:23's _coarse_box(comm, scale). That function is itself a disclosed copy of _graded_box with H_IN, H_MID and H_OUT × SIZE_SCALE; examples do not import examples. Every other constant is imported, as imp:23 does, StopAtDistMax included. - Stepping: degree 2, CN with startup_half_steps=2, N_MAIN steps to T_PRINT, H_GEL Robin, P = 1 W. - Five CN runs: 1. tips / gel: I56's source, _tips_source (test_imp8_rod_tips_fem); 2. tips / Ti: I66; 3. tips / hole: I69, ε = EPS_HOLE; 4. rod / gel: I55's source, _rod_source (test_imp8_rod_line_source_fem); this is I73's gel arm; 5. rod / Ti: I73. OPS-82 made _rod_source and _tips_source build in both builds, so import them; do not copy them. - Material cells. - Runs 2–3 use I66's rod cells: the cylinder minus the two balls, with the overlap keeping gel and the source (the 2026-11-05 18:00 ruling, this repo's IMP-8.md). Make them by a local midpoint selection identical to _rod_cells's, without its volume form: _rod_cells assembles one * w * ufl.dx, which the complex build rejects (item 851's disclosure). - Run 5 uses I73's body, the cells of q's positive DG0 dofs. - Coefficients come from I66's _coefficients(msh, idx, arm) (test_imp8_rod_conducting_body_fem), imported. It builds no form and only writes real values into the arrays. Check that in the figure window. - Reads: _theta_pts at GATE_PTS + RATIO_PTS, one batch per run. - Outputs: θ on P1 per run, by imp:23's _p1_theta route, into one combined XDMF. The setup figure comes from imp:23's write_setup_figure call, with the rod and ball selections.

Gates (asserted; bands imported; all collected first, then asserted). - Cells: the count equals W0_CELLS (this item's W0 figure) and is ≤ 120 000 (CELL_LIMIT, the weekly's bound, as imp:23). - (E) ≤ E_BAND on all five runs. - (S0), as imp:23 computes it: - the line: |∫q − P|/P ≤ B_BAND; - each tip ball: |∫q/(P/2) − 1| ≤ B_BAND; - the selected, rod, overlap and body cell counts are all > 0 (allreduced). - max|Im θ| ≤ 1e-12 via _max_imag (test_mat15_finite_cylinder_fem), as imp:23 does. - Control (asserted, FEM over FEM on this mesh): each non-gel arm's θ(2, 0) mm moves off its same-source gel run's by more than CONTROL_FLOOR (test_imp8_rod_conducting_body_fem, 1e-9). That is |θ_arm/θ_gel − 1| for tips / Ti and tips / hole against run 1, and for rod / Ti against run 4. A DG0 path that ignored its coefficients returns the gel θ. - On the gates' mesh the moves are +55.5 % (…item846-W1.log:122), the hole's (item 851's Outcome, not reprinted) and −2.07 % (…item856-W1.log:120). - Here they are printed beside, with their signs predicted to repeat on the coarse box.

Printed only (≤ 7 digits). - The table: θ(2, 0), θ(2, 15) mm and the tip-point ratio θ(2, 15)/θ(2, 0) for each of the five runs. Beside each row goes the 485 291-cell record above, with its log basename; the hole row says "item 851, log leak-held". - (I) on both gel runs at GATE_PTS, with INTERIOR_BAND beside, not asserted (the weekly's "printed"): - run 1 against QP·_phi_tips; - run 4 against QP·_phi. - The ordering Ti / gel / hole at z = 0 and z = 15 mm. On the gates' mesh it was Ti > gel > hole at z = 0 and hole > gel > Ti at z = 15 mm (item 851's Outcome). - t_build, and t_call / n_factorizations for each run.

Guide. Use imp:23's headings, and Related imp:23, imp:24, imp:25, imp:15. Say plainly: - the box is coarser than the gates' box by design, so its digits are not the records; - the Ti pair is nominal (from memory; no source in the repo); - "hole" means rod cells at ε = 1e-6 × gel k and ρc, not a mesh hole; - the tip source and the body source are two idealised shapes, and neither is a Joule SAR shape; - nothing here is an F2182 reading. The probe is I75's (item 881).

Traps already paid for. - The complex build rejects one * w * ufl.dx (ArityMismatch, 20261105T193522Z_EX-182-figure.log:104), and a raising rank then hangs its peer to the ceiling. _rod_cells still has that form, so do not call it. Any linear form the page builds conjugates its test function. Wrap main() so that a raise calls MPI.COMM_WORLD.Abort(1), as imp:23 does. - fem.Constant(msh, 1.0) is float64 and the complex form constructor rejects it (EX-184's first figure window). Put real values into x.array, and make no ordering comparison on a complex operand. - box is a pytest fixture: do not import it. If the hook refuses this page's closing log, the log moves unchanged to logs/leak-held/ and the slot reports it. Never --no-verify. - A kill parks the item; never raise -t. It is printed. imp:23 at scale 1.8 read (I) inside the band at all four GATE_PTS on both sources (20261105T194909Z_EX-182.log:68, I_line / I_tips True), and scale 2.0 is coarser. - No PREDICTED RED: line.

docs.title: §9 item 886 — 2026-11-08 (example; §10 P77, chain P; §5.4 ramp from MAT-21 P73 / P74; serial on item 885)
docs.text:
Licence. §10 P77, enumerated by the 11-07 weekly ("a mat: example — the dose vs the wall's heat capacity: P73's closed form and P74's FEM on one page"). Queued under rule (4). No band or target is set or moved. Family EX-189, attempt 1 of 4.

What the example does. Two halves on one page. - The closed form (P73). Import item 875's module helpers by name (test_mat21_wall_capacity_dose_sweep_closed_form.py: W41, _cap_hist_w, _d_comp), and through P64's module Z, _dose, _hists. For P5, ADJ_PT and P0, at the four waits, compute: - the composite-drift dose; - the massless-wall (_drift_1d) dose; - their ratio. This half is numpy. If item 875 printed its thickness side table, the page reprints it, labelled "the heading's reading, printed only". - The FEM (P74). Item 885's knob run. Fixtures cannot be imported, so write P68's runs body out in main() for the reference run and tw1 (the wait call, then the D = 0.25 call from its end state), with the module's plain helpers imported by name (_hist_series, HIST_PTS, REPRO, and the names P68 imports: _ZField, _drift_z, _read, _series_z, DT, …). Read every signature first. Copy item 885's tw1 construction (TW1, N_W, DT_W, the zero schedule, the t_init_expr hand-off) exactly. Then read the FEM dose at P5.

Gates (asserted; bands imported; all collected first, then asserted). - P73's anchors, called through its helpers: - (Lim) at t_w = 0 against P70's _cap_hists()["0"] construction, ≤ B1_BAND; - (Mono) at P5 and ADJ_PT (one sign, |ΔD|/D > DOSE_BAR), and at P0 constancy ≤ DOSE_BAR; - (Q-d) ≤ DOSE_BAR with the R-swap control, and (Win-d) ≤ AVG_BAR, per point and wait. - The control (asserted, factor 1): at P5, at every wait, the massless-wall dose misses the composite dose by more than DOSE_BAR. - P74's FEM: - (I) tw1 against the composite drift at t* + TW1 ≤ INTERIOR_BAND; - (E) ≤ E_BAND on the reference run and on both of tw1's calls; - the hand-off precondition (≤ 1e-12 K); - (S0) on tw1's D = 0.25 call; - (Q-wf) ≤ DOSE_BAR; - (c-D): tw1's FEM dose at P5 misses P68's tw0 record 7.253626e-11 s by more than DOSE_BAR. - max|Im θ| = 0, since the mat: group runs complex. As mat:39 does, take np.real on each integral and on max_balance_residual.

Printed only. - The dose-by-wait table at P5, ADJ_PT and P0: for each wait, D(t_w), D(t_w)/D_ref − 1, the massless D and composite / massless − 1. P70's +3.7292e-02 at t_w = 0 sits beside it. - The FEM D(tw1) at P5 beside P73's _d_comp(0, TW1), FEM/series − 1, and P68's tw0 +4.756e-03 (…P68-W1.log:91). - No band, no rate, no recommended wait or thickness.

Guide. - Use mat:39's headings. Related: mat:39, mat:38, mat:36, mat:37. - Say plainly: - how much the wall's capacity adds to the D = 0.25 dose at each wait, quoting the closing log's ratios; - that the excess shrinks as the drift decays, with the sign of (Mono) as measured; - that the FEM at t_w = 1/λ₁ sits at the (I) the closing log reads; - that the case is 1D-reduced, one rung, one Δt; - that the PMMA k_w and ρ_wc_w are nominal (citation owed, W3). - Check every derived number by hand. Quote only closing-log digits, or arithmetic on them (implementer-run.md step 3 clause 3). Quote a round-off term as a bound. Write ≈, never a tilde.

Executor: example-runner, foreground. Its spawn prompt carries, verbatim: "The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Spawned executors run every window foreground with Bash timeout: 660000."

Tier. Heavy label, complex, -n 2, -t 480. Class: example. Cost: ≈ 5.8 measured / 30 predicted min. - Prediction: P73's closed form, ≈ 10–40 s (item 875's brief). P68's W1 took 51 s at -n 2, real, for three runs (…P68-W1.log:111), and P74's W2 is predicted at 70–110 s. Two FEM runs in the complex build, at ≈ 2–4 × per factorisation, take ≈ 60–150 s, and the XDMF plus figure ≈ 30–60 s. Total ≈ 150–300 s, under -t 480. - Skip this slot if pgrep -c python3 in the container reads above 0.

Windows. - Pre-check: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. - Follow EX-186.md's windows, with label EX-189, group mat:40, -n 2, -t 480. - Census pre, then one earlier flagged window EX-189-figure (FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1), which closes nothing. - Closing window: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-189 "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:40 -n 2 -t 480", run last. It is a bare foreground call with Bash timeout 660000 ms. The form is observed to run with no -T (OPS-74). - Census post and docrefs after it. - Nothing is edited after the closing window, the guide included. If the guide must change, re-run the closing window.

Traps already paid for. - EX-183 / EX-186's lists: - in the complex group use np.real, ufl.inner(d, d) and real-part comparisons on ρc arrays; - read on one fixed batch; - print ≤ 7 digits; - a kill parks the item. - mat:37's XDMF comparand route (EX-180's first figure window died at the fem.Expression comparand write). - Item 789's: copy P59′'s _dose, never re-derive it; use side="left" at a switch. - At t_w = 0, T_GRID row 0 is the unconverged IC series, so (Bq) is never asserted at t_w = 0. - Use _drift_cap_z vectorised through the cached call; never call it per point or per dof. - Item 885's tw1 is two solver calls. Its D = 0.25 call is P68's tw0 call with a new start state, so the schedule string is SCHEDULE_25. The wait call's multipliers are all 0, and its (E) is normalised by the full-on source_power. - A Function passed as t_init_expr must be an exact copy (the hand-off precondition).

Scope. One example. Not claimed: the six-wall box, a dose band, a recommended wait or thickness, a cited PMMA ρc, or a tissue dose.

Negative result. A gate red: stop, keep the log, BLOCKED. (I) red in the complex build alone, with item 885's real-build records green, would be a finding about the build: report it and change nothing. No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. EX-189 ✅; census +1; §10 P77 DONE.

Depends on: item 885 landing (and through it item 875). If 885 is not DONE, skip at no cost.

Outcome (2026-11-08, 21:00 CST slot, attempt 1 of 4) — DONE, green. Executor: example-runner, foreground; pre-check pgrep -c python3 0. Windows: census-pre 20261109T030126Z_EX-189-census-pre.log (183 runnable), docrefs-pre 20261109T030128Z_EX-189-docrefs-pre.log (exit 2, staleness only); flagged figure windows 20261109T030259Z_EX-189-figure.log (exit 1: the setup-figure title was 159 characters against the 130-character limit, a crash in the example's own non-gate code before any gate value; title shortened, log kept) and 20261109T030314Z_EX-189-figure.log (exit 0, 34 s, PNG 106 KiB); the closing window 20261109T030424Z_EX-189.log (Status 0, 31 s harness / 28.5 s in-script, [gates] 85 collected, 0 red); census-post 20261109T030506Z_EX-189-census-post.log (184), figures 20261109T030508Z_EX-189-figures.log (missing=0 broken=0), docrefs 20261109T030509Z_EX-189-docrefs.log (dead=0 guide=0 stale=121, exit 2, staleness only). Readings (closing log): (Lim) rel miss 0 at all three points ≤ B1_BAND; (Mono) one sign, decreasing at P5 (|ΔD|/D 1.5031e-01, 8.0575e-02, 7.7715e-02) and ADJ_PT, P0 constant; (Q-d) ≤ 3.581e-16, R-swap least miss 6.1904e+06; (Win-d) ≤ 1.470e-15; the massless-wall control at P5 misses by 3.5951e-02 … 9.9685e-03 across the four waits; (I) tw1 4.712673e-03 (item 885's real-build digits reproduced in the complex build); (E) 1.927e-13 / 2.575e-14 / 1.939e-13; hand-off 0 K; (Q-wf) ≤ 5.643e-16 (closing log :85–88; the 5.128e-16 first written here was the flagged figure window's, 20261109T030314Z_EX-189-figure.log:89 — corrected by the 2026-11-09 03:00 review); (c-D) miss 2.2209e-01; max|Im θ| 0. Also asserted, each an already-landed gate: (c-tw) 2.5314e-01, the reference run's (I) 1.849598706e-03 against P68's record, P70's printed digits. Composite / massless − 1 at P5: +3.7292e-02, +2.6602e-02, +1.9908e-02, +1.0069e-02 at t_w = 0, 0.5, 1, 2 / λ₁. No src/ or gate-module edit; nothing edited after the closing window. The combined XDMF is on disk, gitignored.

Audit (2026-11-09 03:00 daily review, auditor): PASS. Re-cited in the closing log 20261109T030424Z_EX-189.log: - :3 Commit a70b6773, which is the closing commit's parent. The script's mtime precedes the window. - :12 the Done-when command. - :42 every band imported by name. - :83 (I) tw1 4.712673e-03 ≤ 1e-02, asserted. The reviewer traced this line. - :85–88 (Q-wf), worst 5.643e-16 at :88, traced by the reviewer. - :94 [gates] 85 collected, 0 red, traced by the reviewer. - :102–104 Status 0, 31 s.

The asserts are at examples/materials/40_gel_box_wall_capacity_dose_vs_wait.py:415–448. The census moved 183 → 184 (20261109T030509Z_EX-189-docrefs.log:159–161, dead=0). The first figure window's exit 1 (title length, 20261109T030259Z_EX-189-figure.log:80) was in non-gate setup-figure code in a flagged window that closes nothing; that log was kept and disclosed.
