docs.title: EX-190 — the F2182-shaped probe on the rod bracket (imp:27)
docs.text:
History file for the §7 EX-190 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-08 18:00 daily review as §10 I82, chain I (daily, provisional under §9 rule (6)). It is a §5.4 ramp from IMP-8 steps 16 and 17, I78 and I75 (§9 items 874 and 881).

  • The records it draws on:
  • I75, item 881, on the 485 291-cell box, real build, -n 8. Probe mean θ(900 s) per watt in the rod at (0, ±16) mm:
    • Ti 1.057039e+01, D = 0.5 2.104578e+00 (20261108T194323Z_IMP-8-item881-W1.log:122);
    • gel 9.161894e+00 / 1.975098e+00 (20261108T195853Z_IMP-8-item881-W2b.log:122);
    • hole 8.783168e+00 / 1.891937e+00 (20261108T200636Z_IMP-8-item881-W3.log:122);
    • θ(900)/θ(675) between 1.059614 and 1.068419 on every arm (:120–121 of each).
  • I78, item 874, closed form, infinite gel, 1 W per rod. Line θ(900 s) is 9.648662 K at 16 mm and 6.810428 K at 17 mm; twin 63.14 / 29.97039. At D = 0.5 the line reads 1.978384 / 1.822237 (20261108T133157Z_IMP-8-item874-W1.log:58–62).
  • imp:26 (EX-188), the coarse box this page reuses: 64 140 cells at SIZE_SCALE 2.0 (20261108T210314Z_EX-188-W0.log). On it the rod / gel row is θ(2, 0) 17.7246 and θ(2, 15) 9.77473, rod / Ti 17.1764 / 10.6763, with 833 body cells (20261108T211230Z_EX-188.log:55, :70, :72).
  • Why an example. imp:26 puts the bracket on one page but reads it at (2, 0) and (2, 15) mm only; its guide says "Nothing here is an F2182 reading. The probe is IMP-8 I75's." No page shows the F2182-shaped probe, its D = 0.5 read by superposition, or how much the reading moves when the probe moves by the 1 mm separating I75's flat-ended rod from the clinical capsule's apex.
  • Gap check, run at this review: grep -l "test_imp8_rod_probe_f2182_fem\|test_imp8_probe_f2182_closed_form\|_superpose\|Z_P" examples/implants/*.py is empty (exit 1).
  • Its angle. The rod-source bracket (gel / Ti / hole) is read where the standard's probe would sit, 1 mm beyond the tip, on the axis, at 900 s (placement and time quoted from memory; W3). It is read at 16 mm (1 mm beyond this flat-ended rod) and at 17 mm (where 1 mm beyond a capsule apex lands), continuous and at D = 0.5. I78's closed form is set beside it.

Done-when. - examples/implants/27_rod_f2182_probe_bracket.py and its same-stem guide .md exist. imp:27 is the next free number (imp:26 was the last, EX-188's census 182 → 183). - The closing window ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:27 -n 2 -t 480 exits 0 with every gate in item 896 asserted. Bands and helpers are imported by name. There is no gate-module edit and no src/ edit. - A combined XDMF under examples/implants/paraview_output/ holds the three θ fields at 900 s and the DG0 k of the Ti and hole arms. There is a setup figure through write_setup_figure. - Census +1, docrefs dead=0 and guide=0.

docs.title: §9 item 896 — 2026-11-08 (§10 I82, chain I — daily, 2026-11-08, provisional, rule (6); example)
docs.text:
Licence. §9 rule (6), toward chain I's stated readout ("an F2182-shaped clinical implant-heating readout, read beside lumped/closed-form and bracket records"). An example step is in the chain's own family (I77 was one). No band or target is set or moved. Family EX-190, attempt 1 of 4. Executor: example-runner, spawned in the foreground, with the bare-call sentence verbatim in the spawn prompt.

What the example does. Everything is written out in main(). - Mesh. imp:26's coarse box at SIZE_SCALE 2.0, as a disclosed local copy of imp:26's _coarse_box(comm, scale), itself a copy of imp:23's; examples do not import examples. Every other constant is imported as imp:26 imports it (26_rod_bracket_gel_ti_hole.py:59–116), StopAtDistMax included. - Stepping: degree 2, CN with startup_half_steps=2, N_MAIN steps to T_PRINT = 900 s, H_GEL Robin, P = 1 W, θ₀ = T_INF. - Three CN runs, each with snapshot_steps=SNAP_STEPS (10, 20, 30): 1. rod / gel: I55's _rod_source (test_imp8_rod_line_source_fem); this is imp:26's run 4; 2. rod / Ti: I73's arm; imp:26's run 5; 3. rod / hole: I75's W3 arm at ε = EPS_HOLE, new on this box. - Body cells: q's positive DG0 dofs, by a local copy of imp:26's _body_cells. Coefficients come from I66's _coefficients(msh, idx, arm) (test_imp8_rod_conducting_body_fem), imported. - Reads, one batch per call (the batch rule): - (a) imp:26's batch GATE_PTS + RATIO_PTS on the final field, unchanged, for the reproduction; - (b) the probe batch ((0, 16), (0, −16), (0, 17), (0, −17)) mm on the final field and each snapshot. The z values are built from I75's Z_P and I78's Z_C, never typed. - D = 0.5 comes from I75's _superpose (θ(900) − θ(675) + θ(450) − θ(225)). It is a superposition, not a switched solve, and the page says so. - The closed form beside: I78's _reads(kern, steady, z) for both SHAPES at Z_P and Z_C (test_imp8_probe_f2182_closed_form.py:131–134). - Outputs: θ on P1 per run, by imp:26's _p1_theta route, into one combined XDMF. The setup figure comes from imp:26's write_setup_figure call, with the body cells. The four probe points are named in the caption.

Gates (asserted; bands imported; all collected first, then asserted). - Cells: the count equals 64 140 (imp:26's W0 figure at scale 2.0) and is ≤ 120 000. The body count is > 0 and equals imp:26's 833 (…EX-188.log:55), allreduced. - (E) ≤ E_BAND on all three runs. (S0) |∫q − P|/P ≤ B_BAND. max|Im θ| ≤ 1e-12 via _max_imag. No non-finite coefficient dof. - The reproduction (anchor). Rod / gel and rod / Ti θ(2, 0) and θ(2, 15) equal imp:26's closing-log prints within one unit of their 6th significant digit (I75's _sixth): 17.7246 / 9.77473 and 17.1764 / 10.6763 (…EX-188.log:70, :72). It is the same box, source, solve and batch. snapshot_steps adds only copies. - Coefficient control: the Ti and hole arms' θ(2, 0) are off the gel run's by more than CONTROL_FLOOR, as in imp:26. Rod / Ti read −3.0925e-02 there (:76). - I75's re-posed control (factor 1, strict): θ_probe(900 s) > θ_probe(675 s) at (0, ±16) mm on every arm. - I78's placement control on the FEM (factor 1 on INTERIOR_BAND, ceiling 1 since θ > 0): 1 − θ(0, ±17)/θ(0, ±16) > INTERIOR_BAND on every arm at 900 s, continuous. The infinite-medium line reads 0.2941583 (…item874-W1.log:54). A source with a 1 mm radius on a mesh of h ≈ 2.2 mm near the tip (…EX-188.log:51) is predicted to read lower, as a sign only.

Printed only (≤ 7 digits). - The table, per arm: θ(900 s) at ±16 and ±17 mm with their means; the D = 0.5 superposed means; θ(900)/θ(675); θ(17)/θ(16). - Beside each row: I75's 485 291-cell mean (log basename) and I78's line / twin at 16 and 17 mm (log basename). - The ordering Ti / gel / hole at 16 mm. On the gates' mesh it is Ti > gel > hole (item 881). - t_build, and t_call / n_factorizations for each run.

Guide. Use imp:26's headings, and Related imp:26, imp:23, imp:22, imp:21. Say plainly: - the box is coarser than the gates' box by design, so its digits are not I75's records; - the probe placement and the 900 s are quoted from memory (W3 confirms or corrects); - 16 mm is 1 mm beyond this flat-ended rod, and 17 mm is where "1 mm beyond the apex" lands on the clinical capsule rod, 2 mm beyond the same line; - the Ti pair is nominal; "hole" means rod cells at ε = 1e-6 × gel k and ρc, not a mesh hole; - the source is idealised, not a Joule SAR shape; - the D = 0.5 read is a superposition; - nothing here is a clinical or published F2182 figure.

Quote only closing-log digits, or arithmetic on them. Write ≈, never a tilde.

Price. - On this box, imp:26's rod runs took 50.8 s and 47.6 s of t_call at -n 2 complex. Its five-run closing window was 242.5 s in-script and 245 s harness (20261108T211230Z_EX-188.log:60–61, :99, :107). - Predicted for three runs plus probe reads, I78's closed forms (a few seconds; I78's module ran in 2.73 s), XDMF and figure (unlogged review arithmetic): ≈ 160–200 s in-script. - The hole arm with the source in the hole is new on this box. On the gates' box its t_call sat between the Ti and gel arms' (436.9 against 449.6 / 419.7 s, item 881's logs :112). - No re-size rule: the box is fixed at imp:26's scale. If the flagged figure window's in-script total exceeds 400 s, park the item.

Windows. Pre-check: pgrep -c python3 in the container reads 0. Skip the slot if it does not. Every harness call is the whole command, foreground, Bash timeout 660000 ms; no container-side timeout above 480 s. 1. Census-pre and docrefs-pre, as EX-188's (./scripts/run_examples.sh --list; python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py). Expected 183 at EX-188's close, or 184 if EX-189 (mat:40, item 886) lands first, and dead=0 guide=0. Read both; never assume them. Run them before the script is written (EX-188's disclosure). 2. W1 EX-190-figure: the flagged full run, in the form of 20261108T210330Z_EX-188-figure.log:12 with this file: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-190-figure "docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc \"cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 480 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/implants/27_rod_f2182_probe_bracket.py\"" It closes nothing. 3. Closing window: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-190 "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:27 -n 2 -t 480". Nothing is edited after it, the guide included. If the guide must change, re-run the closing window. 4. Census-post, figures and docrefs, as EX-188's (check_example_setup_figures.py).

Tier. Heavy label, complex (the imp: group sources the complex build), -n 2, -t 480. Class: example. Cost: ≈ 3.4 measured / 30 predicted min.

Traps already paid for. - The complex build rejects one * w * ufl.dx (ArityMismatch, 20261105T193522Z_EX-182-figure.log:104), and a raising rank then hangs its peer to the ceiling. Wrap main() so that a raise calls MPI.COMM_WORLD.Abort(1), as imp:26 does. - fem.Constant(msh, 1.0) is float64 and the complex form constructor rejects it. Put real values into x.array. - No ordering comparison on a complex operand: _theta_pts returns the complex build's scalars. Assert max|Im θ| first, then compare np.real(...). That covers both controls and the ordering print. - I75's module must import in the complex build. If it does not (its I60 / I73 imports are real-build records), make PROBE_PTS / SNAP_STEPS / _superpose / _sixth disclosed local copies (three constants and two one-line functions) and say so. Never edit I75's module. - box is a pytest fixture: do not import it. Set StopAtDistMax on the inner threshold. - The hole arm: the rod core reaches ≈ 4e6 K/W at ε = EPS_HOLE (item 881's trap). Print no rod-interior or max θ. The XDMF holds it, and the guide says so. Every probe is outside the source cells (I75's 16 mm hole read was 8.8 K/W). - .eval bytes depend on the batch: (a) is imp:26's batch unchanged; the probe batch is separate. Print ≤ 7 digits. - The leak guard: if the hook refuses the closing log, the log moves unchanged to logs/leak-held/ and the slot reports it. Never --no-verify. - A kill parks the item; never raise -t. A refresh-shaped red is a finding: stop, file it, fix nothing.

Scope. One example on one coarse box. The gated records are I75 and I78 (items 881, 874), plus imp:26's rows reproduced. Not claimed: - the gates' mesh, a rate or a Ti property; - the clinical fixture (entry 63 / I76) and the ladder (I80 / I81, items 894 / 895); - a switched-source duty solve, an implant SAR shape, or a gate on the rod's effect at the probe; - any F2182 or published value (W3).

Negative result. - (E), (S0), a cell or body-count mismatch, the reproduction, or a control red: stop, keep the log, BLOCKED. - The reproduction red alone means this page's box or route is not imp:26's. Print both and stop. Never loosen the sixth-digit unit. - No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. EX-190 ⬜ → ✅; census +1; §10 I82 DONE.

Depends on: nothing (items 874, 881 and 882 / imp:26 are on main).

Outcome (2026-11-09, 04:30 slot, fourth item): DONE. examples/implants/27_rod_f2182_probe_bracket.py + same-stem guide + setup figure figures/implants_27_rod_f2182_probe_bracket_setup.png (313 KiB). Closing window 20261109T105242Z_EX-190.log (exit 0, 152 s harness, 149.7 s in-script, -n 2); flagged figure window 20261109T104907Z_EX-190-figure.log (exit 0, 156 s; closes nothing). Cells 64 140, body 833, (E) ≤ 1.510e-14, (S0) 4.441e-16, max|Im θ| 0, no non-finite coefficient dof. Reproduction: rod / gel 17.72459 / 9.774734, rod / Ti 17.17645 / 10.67626 against imp:26's 17.7246 / 9.77473 / 17.1764 / 10.6763, all inside one sixth-digit unit. Controls: Ti −3.0925e-02, hole −1.7516e-03 off gel at (2, 0); θ(900)/θ(675) ≥ 1.057953 at ±16 on every arm; 1 − θ(17)/θ(16) between 0.2545369 and 0.2982887. Probe means at 16 mm Ti 10.56687 / gel 9.252419 / hole 8.814547, ordering Ti > gel > hole as item 881. Census 20261109T104717Z_EX-190-census-pre.log → 20261109T105520Z_EX-190-census-post.log, 184 → 185; docrefs 20261109T104738Z_EX-190-docrefs-pre.log / 20261109T105522Z_EX-190-docrefs-post.log dead=0 guide=0 (exit 2, staleness info); figures 20261109T105523Z_EX-190-figures-post.log broken=0. The guide's digits are the closing log's (the flagged window's differ only in (E) round-off and timings).

Review note (2026-11-09 10:30 daily review): audit PASS (auditor; 20261109T105242Z_EX-190.log:12, :78, :85, :89–92 re-traced by the review). Caveat, not demoting: the guide's 0.2941583 cites I78's gate log (20261108T133157Z_IMP-8-item874-W1.log:54) rather than the closing log; the value is 1 − 6.810428 / 9.648662, and both inputs print in the closing log (:70–71). The guide stays unedited after its closing window.

docs.title: EX-191 — the rod's finite radius at the probe: gel and Ti beside the uniform-cylinder closed form (imp:28)
docs.text:
History file for the §7 EX-191 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-09 10:30 daily review as §10 I84, chain I (daily, provisional under §9 rule (6)). It is a §5.4 ramp from IMP-8 step 20, I83 (§9 item 911), on imp:27's box (EX-190, §9 item 896).

  • The records it draws on:

docs.text:

What the example does. Everything is written out in main(); this is a closed-form page with no solve. - Imports, through module objects: - p75 (test_mat21_wall_uniform_source_probe_points_closed_form): _u3, P_DEP, PROBE_PTS, PROBE_LABELS, T_STAR, T_GRID; - p80 (test_mat21_eddy_source_probe_points_closed_form): _data, _eddy_at, _ball_mean, _ball_cub, _parse_c52, _cstar_idx, C52_STAR, THETA_TSTAR; - p81 (test_mat21_end_source_probe_points_closed_form): the names item 921 lands. Read that module first; its history and ball helpers are expected under the brief's names, _ball_mean_end / _ball_cub_end. - Bands come by name from where P80 / P81 import them (B1_BAND, INTERIOR_BAND). Never import a test_* name or a fixture. - Mesh: step 3's m = 2 box, dolfinx.mesh.create_box on [−A, A] × [−B, B] × [−C, C] with (26, 16, 4) cells (test_mat21_box_fem.py:71, BASE × 2), tetrahedra. One cell tag, region "gel". - All 24 readout points are mesh vertices: x ∈ {0, ±0.05, ±0.15, ±0.25, ±A} on the 0.025 m grid, y ∈ {0, ±0.105, ±B} on the 0.02625 m grid, z ∈ {0, C} on the 0.0225 m grid. - Fields: U3/P, eddy/P and end/P at t* on P1. Interpolate each with the page's own chunked callable, a disclosed local copy of test_mat21_box_fem.py:94–108's _exact pattern on P1 instead of P2. Use the gates' term counts: SERIES_TERMS for U3, QUAD_TERMS for eddy, SEP_TERMS for end. - Reads, one batch per call (the batch rule): the six probe points as one batch, and the 18 lattice points as one batch, through evaluate_vector_field_parallel(..., owner="lowest_original_cell") (mat:25's route).

Gates (asserted at imported bands). - P80's, re-asserted on the page: - (P-eq) |ratio − 1| ≤ 4ε; - (Q2-p) np.array_equal on P75's batch; - (Rep-s) the six θ_s(t*) :.6f strings equal p80.THETA_TSTAR; - (Lim) ≤ B1_BAND; - (Ball) ≤ B1_BAND at 18 points; - (K-lat) 18 matches with the c* token custody; - (c-u) > INTERIOR_BAND at six probes; - (c-ball) > B1_BAND at 18 points. - P81's, re-asserted the same way: (P-eq), (Q2-s), (Rep-s) on step 6's own scalar calls, (Lim), (Lin), (Ball), (c-u), (c-e), (c-ball), each at the band item 921 uses. - Example-side: - (V-pt): at the 24 vertices, each P1 field read through the owner route equals its series at the point within B1_BAND relative. Every point is a vertex, so the interpolant's nodal value is the series. The comparison is relative, not bitwise, because the node batch differs from the point batch (item 537). - (cV), the control: at six z-edge midpoints, the P1 field misses the series by more than B1_BAND, for all three fields. The points are P0…P4 at z = 0.01125 m, and P5 at z = C − 0.01125 m (half the 0.0225 m z spacing). The ceiling is none: P1 is not exact on a curved θ. Predicted ≥ 1e-6 relative, printed; only the separation is asserted. - Shift along z, never along x or y. The eddy source has no x-dependence, and U3 and the eddy θ are flat in x and y to round-off near P0: the ±x / ±y faces are ≥ 105 mm away, against √(αt*) = 20.1 mm. An x-shifted midpoint would miss by ≈ 0 and the control would be red by construction. - max|Im θ| = 0, since the mat: group runs complex. Take np.real before every comparison.

Printed only. - The six-probe table: U3/P, eddy/P and end/P at t* (K/W), then eddy/U3 and end/U3. - The lattice table: for each of the 18 labels, the three θ/P at t*, the three 10 g-ball shapes / c*, and entry 52's SAR10g / SAR10g(c*). Also the x+0mm column profile (dz±50 / dz±250 and dz±150 / dz±250) for the end-weighted ball mean and for entry 52. - Tie sets within 1e-4 relative, never an exact argmax (P80's disclosure (1)). - The normaliser line: per deposited gel watt; entry 59 is per accepted watt.

Guide. - Use mat:23's headings. docs.title: EX-193 — the field-strength lever on one page: F-clinical at 1.5 T and 3 T per accepted watt (mri:41)
docs.text:
History file for the §7 EX-193 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-09 10:30 daily review as §10 C47, chain C (daily, provisional under §9 rule (6)). It is a §5.4 ramp from GEO-38 C33 (§9 item 917) on xl entries 52 and 58.

  • The records it draws on (all tracked; every digit below is a log print or unlogged review arithmetic on log prints, ≤ 7 significant digits):
  • Entry 52 (1.5 T, 64 MHz, node 193.5996 pF, degree 1): 20261103T080009Z_GEO-38-C6.log. The lattice is at :12289–12306. The normalisers are at :12310: SAR10g(c*) per box watt 4.303111e-02, per P_acc 2.274234e-03, per P_src 1.668025e-03 W/kg/W, and mean |B1+|_ccw per √W box 3.692558e-07, per P_acc 8.488944e-08 T.
  • Entry 58 (3 T, 128 MHz, node 44.0525 pF, degree 1): 20261109T080008Z_GEO-38-C6-3T.log. The lattice is at :12238–12255. The normalisers are at :12259: per box watt 4.778381e-02, per P_acc 9.327634e-03, per P_src 3.269910e-03 W/kg/W, and per √W box 2.582372e-07, per P_acc 1.140944e-07 T.
  • C33 (item 917), the 3 T / 1.5 T ratio table: 20261109T103601Z_GEO-38-C33-W1-n1-r2.log:126–135. Lattice mean |B1+| per √P_acc 1.410682, centroid mean 1.344035, SAR10g(c*) per P_acc 4.101440, P_box / P_acc 3.693500. c* x−105 mm dz−50 mm → x+105 mm dz+50 mm.
  • Why an example. No page reads entry 58, and no page sets the two field strengths side by side.
  • Gap check, run at this review: grep -rln "C6-3T\|c33_field_strength\|GEO-38-C6-3T" examples/ is empty (exit 1).
  • The ans:11 page reads entry 52 alone. mesh:15 / mesh:16 are build-only.
  • C33's table lives in a test log, which a user does not read.
  • Its angle (new; no existing page or log prints these). The 4.10× SAR lever per accepted watt factors into how much more of the accepted power the gel box takes (P_box / P_acc, 3.6935×) and how much more SAR each box watt makes at c* (≈ 1.110×, review arithmetic: 4.778381e-02 / 4.303111e-02). The |B1+| lever factors the same way: ≈ 0.6993× per √(box watt), times √3.6935.
  • The hotspot "move" is measured as a margin.
    • At 1.5 T, c* (x−105 mm dz−50 mm, 1.378897e-04 W/kg) leads the mirror ball x+105 mm dz−50 mm (1.378033e-04, :12303) by ≈ 6.27e-04 relative.
    • At 3 T the lead is ≈ 8.24e-03 over x+105 mm dz−50 mm (:12252).
    • At a fixed ball (1.5 T's c*) the SAR ratio reads ≈ 4.021, against 4.101 at each side's own c*.

docs.title: §9 item 924 — 2026-11-09 (daily, 2026-11-09 — provisional; chain C step C47)
docs.text:
Licence. §9 rule (6), toward chain C's subgoal: two viable clinical body-coil models; ladder step (6), the box loaded, |B₁⁺|, 10 g SAR and the located hotspot; F-clinical as the fixture for "the Phase 9 examples that claim clinical relevance" (PROJECT_PLAN §10, "Clinical-scale coil fixtures"). It also serves entry 58's own first branch ("printed beside entry 52's 1.5 T figures (the 1.5 T / 3 T ratio of the mean and of the hotspot, a record)", xl-pending.md entry 58). No band, tolerance or target is set or moved. Family EX-193, attempt 1 of 4. Chain C's rule-(6) count since the 11-07 weekly: 4 of 6 with this item. Executor: example-runner, spawned in the foreground, with the bare-call sentence verbatim in the spawn prompt.

Serial on the 11-09 weekly (21:00 tonight). The decision rule's branch on entry 58 is the weekly's (item 917). This page is a user-facing record of that branch, so it does not run before the weekly reads it. - Take the item only if the weekly has read entry 58 as its first branch (every assertion green ⇒ a record) and has not reverted C47. The xl-pending.md entry 58 Status reads "READ … first branch", or §10 chain C says so. - Otherwise skip at no cost, and say which condition failed.

What the example does. Everything is written out in main(). It is a no-solve record page, like ans:11. - Reader. Import from tests/validation/test_geo38_c33_field_strength_reader.py by name: _load_page, find_log, side, check_side, ratios, ENTRY52_NODE_PF, ENTRY58_NODE_PF and ENTRY58_GLOB. - The page module is loaded through _load_page(), so it is the same sys.modules["ans11_record_page"] object C33 uses. Use its parse_c6_log, _read_log and SOURCE_LOG. - Never call _c33_body, print_table, custody_json or any test_* function. Never re-implement a log regex. - Rank safety. Parse on rank 0, then bcast (C33's _on_root shape). Only rank 0 prints. - Reads: - entry 52 is SOURCE_LOG; - entry 58 is find_log(ENTRY58_GLOB), which must read "tracked"; - C33's closing log is docs/testing/logs/20261109T103601Z_GEO-38-C33-W1-n1-r2.log, gzip-tolerant via _read_log. A local regex reads its four "C33 table" ratio rows (the third | field) and its c* row. The four row titles are disclosed local copies of C33's print_table titles. - Derived (floats from parsed strings; never a literal): - C33's four ratios, through ratios(side(p52), side(p58)); - the per-box-watt ratios sar_per_box_w and b1_per_sqrt_box_w (the page's normalisers fields); - the 18-row per-point table: |B1+|_ccw / √P_acc and SAR10g / P_acc at each lattice label on each side, with their ratio; - each side's runner-up ball (the second-largest lattice SAR10g) and the c* margin (c* − runner-up) / runner-up; - the SAR ratio at each side's c* label, read at the same label on both sides; - SAR10g(c*) per P_acc ratio / (|B1+| ratio)² for the lattice mean and for the centroid mean; - P_acc / P_src on each side.

Gates (asserted; all collected first, then asserted). - (X) Both logs parse. The node strings equal ENTRY52_NODE_PF / ENTRY58_NODE_PF. There are 18 lattice lines per side, and the labels are equal in order across the two sides. - (D) check_side is green on both sides at C33's own half-unit bounds: (D-Pacc), (D-box), (D-sar), (D-cen), argmax = c*, the c* string equals its lattice string, S₁₂ = S₂₁, and (Node). C33 recorded these as green (…C33-W1-n1-r2.log:108–125). - (R33) The reproduction (anchor). Each of the four ratios formatted .6e equals the C33 closing log's printed string, and both c* labels equal its c* row (:127–131). String equality, no tolerance. - (Dec-S) The SAR lever factored (identity). R(sar_per_p_acc) equals R(sar_per_box_w) × R(p_box_over_p_acc). The bound is Σ half-units of the six tokens, C33's _half_ulp_rel, imported. This review's arithmetic, unlogged: 1.110448 × 3.693500 = 4.101440 against 4.101440, rel ≈ 7.7e-08, against a bound of ≈ 8.5e-07. - (Dec-B) The |B1+| lever factored (identity). R(b1_per_sqrt_p_acc) equals R(b1_per_sqrt_box_w) × √R(p_box_over_p_acc) at the same kind of bound. Review arithmetic: 0.6993450 × 1.921848 = 1.344035. - (Lat) The lattice mean from its parts. The mean of the 18 parsed |B1+| tokens / √P_acc on each side equals side()'s lattice_mean_per_sqrt_p_acc, rel ≤ 1e-12. It is the same arithmetic, so this checks that the per-point table and the record share their inputs. - (Arg) The runner-up ball is not c* on either side, and the margin is > 0 (strict; argmax by construction).

Controls (asserted). - (N-norm), the wrong normaliser. Substitute R(sar_per_p_src) for R(sar_per_box_w) in (Dec-S). It goes red. - Review arithmetic: 1.960348 × 3.693500 / 4.101440 − 1 = 0.7654 rel, against a bound of ≈ 8.5e-07. - The miss is fixed by the records, so its ceiling is ≈ 9e5× the bound. Assert only "red": the residual exceeds the bound. - (N-plant), one digit. Plant one digit in the 4th significant place of the 3 T sar_per_box_w string, in memory. (Dec-S) goes red (≈ 2.1e-04 rel against ≈ 8.5e-07), and (R33) stays green, which shows the two gates are independent. - (N-swap), the sides swapped. ratios(side(p58), side(p52)) misses (R33)'s strings on all four rows. The (Node) check of check_side(p58, ENTRY52_NODE_PF, …) is red.

Printed only (≤ 7 significant digits; never a raw 10-digit log token). - C33's table, with each row's two factors beside it (per box watt, and the P_box / P_acc share). - The 18-row per-point table. - The c* labels, the runner-ups and the margins. - The SAR ratio at a fixed ball. - SAR per |B1+|², for the lattice and the centroid. - P_acc / P_src at each side. - Im Y_in under both senses at both feeds, side by side, never as a ratio (cw P33 first, C33's order). - The ω²σ quasi-static scaling (4 at equal σ) is named in the guide only, as context. It is never printed as a comparand and never asserted. The guide says why it need not hold: 128 MHz in gel is far from quasi-static on a 650 mm box.

Guide. Use ans:11's headings. Related: ans:11, mesh:15, mesh:16, mri:17. Say plainly: - these are degree-1 internal records, each at its own unloaded in-model root (Im Y_in with the box loaded is printed, not zero); - the lattice is 18 balls, and c* is the lattice argmax, not a box-wide maximum; - the 1.5 T c* leads its mirror ball by ≈ 6e-04, so "the hotspot moves" means a near-tie resolved differently, not a moved hot region; - the per-box-watt factor is the physics-facing split: the box takes ≈ 3.7× more of the accepted power, and each box watt makes ≈ 1.11× the c* SAR; - no tuning, absolute, compliance, homogeneity or external claim; no ANS case (a 3 T case is the weekly's to pose); not degree 2 (xxl entry 62 / C37).

Quote only closing-log digits, or arithmetic on them. Write ≈, never a tilde.

Windows. Pre-check: pgrep -c python3 in the container reads 0, otherwise skip the slot. Every harness call is the whole command, foreground, Bash timeout 660000 ms. 1. Census-pre and docrefs-pre, as EX-190's. Read both; never assume them. Expected: 185 at EX-190's close, plus any example that has landed since (EX-191 / imp:28 may land first). 2. W1 EX-193-W1 (closes nothing): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-193-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc \"cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/41_f_clinical_field_strength_lever.py\"" 3. Setup figure: a byte-identical copy of examples/meshing/figures/meshing_16_f_clinical_3t_coil_astm_box_setup.png (62 827 B) to examples/mri/figures/mri_41_f_clinical_field_strength_lever_setup.png. The guide's caption says it is mesh:16's render of the 3 T twin; the 1.5 T twin is mesh:15. Entry 58's mesh is C20's, with the rod mapped to gel. 4. Closing window: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-193 "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:41 -n 2 -t 120". Nothing is edited after it, the guide included. 5. Census-post, figures and docrefs, as EX-190's.

Tier. Standard, complex (the mri: group sources the complex build; the page imports C6a, which imports dolfinx), -n 2, -t 120, no solve, no mesh. Class: example. Cost: ≈ 8.3 measured (the example class median at the 10:30 review) / 30 predicted min. The windows are priced from: - the ans:11 page's closing window, 2 s (20261108T152642Z_ANS-11-C43-page.log, Elapsed (s): 2); - C33's window, 4 s (…C33-W1-n1-r2.log, Elapsed (s): 4).

The hour goes on the page and the guide. If the closing window is not green by minute 45, park.

Traps already paid for. - The leak hook (MIN_SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS = 8): print ≤ 7 significant digits and never echo a parsed 10-digit token. If the hook refuses the closing log, move it unchanged to logs/leak-held/, report it, and never use --no-verify. - Pytest-interleaved log lines: use re.search, as the page does. Retention gzips logs: read either suffix, and cite the base name. - Never write under /workspace/logs/geo38. It holds C33's JSON and entry 62's outputs. Never call C33's gated body. - Wrap main() so that a raise calls MPI.COMM_WORLD.Abort(1); a raising rank otherwise hangs its peer to the ceiling (imp:26). - Do not import a test_* name. Importing the C33 module imports pytest, which is present in the image. - A kill parks the item. Never raise -t. - Never delete a log, a red one included (item 907's breach).

Traps already paid for. - Glued log lines. In I86's log, :117, :124, :136 and :140 carry a pytest node prefix. Use re.search per line, never ^-anchored, and never line adjacency. - Nested parentheses in the rung labels (:129: "(z 16 mm, the bracket's probe (I75: …))"). Key on rung (\d) \(z (\d+) mm; never match to a closing paren. - The radius-factor and tip-weighting lines carry no rung key. Take them in order, and assert the count of 4 in (X). - Small-a cancellations (I86's own): at a = A_LIM, call only _twin_a (the quadrature route). Never call _twin_a_steady or _twin_a_dot there: the g-difference and the erf difference lose every digit. - _phi_cyl asserts |z| > L/2 strictly; every rung is beyond the face. _twin_a / _twin_a_dot assert r == 0.0, so pass 0.0. - _phi_steady and I58's _line(·, ·, ∞) divide by r. Never call them on the axis. Point-twin steady is _tips_steady(0.0, z), as in I86. - I86's strings came from the real build; this page runs in the complex build. The closure is numpy / scipy in one venv, so the strings are expected identical. If (K) / (K-rec) is red, one diagnostic window may be run, EX-195-W1r: W1's command without the source …complex-mode && clause, closing nothing. It separates the environment from the route. Never loosen string equality. - The import closure reaches entry 63's held module. I58's test_imp8_entry48_lumped imports test_geo36_rod_f_clinical_heating. Importing is allowed; editing is not (ruling (c)). The page edits nothing. - The leak hook: print ≤ 7 significant digits. A refused log goes unchanged to logs/leak-held/; never --no-verify. - Abort(1) on a raise (imp:26's hung peer). Never delete a log, a red one included (item 907's breach). A kill parks the item; never raise -t.

docs.text: An asymmetric drive through ports.superpose_drives in ParaView — the 4-leg birdcage under a two-port "linear" drive (P1 and P2 at equal amplitude, 0° relative phase) beside the quadrature drive, with the linearity identity between the two halves and the sum (POST-6 step 1's newly gated capability, 2026-09-04: the package-level multi-port drive, gated on the quadrature records and on linearity — the drive angle: ports:7 and ports:9 show the fixed four-port quadrature through the test module's sum, no example shows an arbitrary weight vector or the package entry point). Executor example-runner, spawned foreground, both census windows through the harness. examples/ports/13_birdcage_asymmetric_drive.py / .md (ports:13): the sweep from the imported build_four_port_sweep(keep_fields=True) route the gate module uses (tests/validation/test_port_drive_superposition.py:150, superposition_case), 10 MHz, degree 1, 116 085 cells; three superpositions through ports.superpose_drives — w_lin = (1, 1, 0, 0)/√2, w_a = (1, 0, 0, 0)/√2, w_b = (0, 1, 0, 0)/√2, and the ccw quadrature weights from the imported quadrature_phase_weights; writes |B₁⁺|_lin and |B₁⁺|_quad (DG0, phantom cells) as two named arrays in one combined XDMF through write_xdmf_with_tags(…, facet_tags=…). Anchors (asserted in-script, imported, never restated): cells = STEP2_CELL_COUNT at STEP2_CELL_COUNT_BAND; the four single-drive power residuals ≤ POWER_BALANCE_BAND and P1's reproducing STEP1_GATE_I_P1_RESIDUAL at CG1_RECORD_RTOL; linearity through the package — E(w_lin) equals E(w_a) + E(w_b) on the N1curl dof array at 1e-12 relative, and the combined port currents are the weighted sums at 1e-12; the quadrature drive's C4 reading reproduces STEP2_IDENTITY_RECORDS[0] (0.9818%) at CG1_RECORD_RTOL. One ungated reading, printed only: P_acc = ½aᴴ(I − SᴴS)a for the three drives beside ½∫σ|E_w|² — the guide says why the ratio reads ≈0.88 (known-issues POST-6 step 1, the open denominator question) and that no band exists. EX-75 (mri:18, the next free number; examples/mri/ ends at 17_…, and no other row or chunk names mri:18): examples/mri/18_f_human_four_port_quadrature.py + .md. One build of H9′'s fixture (369 387-cell copper hole mesh, Leontovich wall, κ off, degree 1, 64 MHz, phantom at 0.015 m). Then two loadings at the same C: - two-port: build_tuned_quadrature(comm, with_z50=False), unchanged: P17 / P21 at Z_th, 30 gaps at Z_RC, the ccw / cw superpositions; - four-port: feeds at slots 0 / 4 / 8 / 12 on the feed ring at Z_th, the other 28 gaps at Z_RC, one factorisation plus three held solves, superposed with quadrature_phase_weights([0, 1, 2, 3], "ccw") normalised to its first entry.

Per drive, the reader sees the feed-ring k-spectrum (k = 0 leak, k = +1 and k = −1 shares), |B₁⁺| and |B₁⁻| on one colour scale, and why the four-port drive excites no k = 0: its weights sum to zero, and its loading is C4-symmetric.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 03:00 daily review; the review reviewed it.

EX-84 (imp:4) shows that one adjoint solve gives an implant lead's transfer function. It prints the TF(z) profile along the σ = 800 S/m lead and folds it against the lead-free field of three drives: the gate's D1 and D2, plus a new drive D3 that the adjoint never saw. Each fold is checked against the direct with-lead tip response. - Executor: example-runner. - Tier: heavy, complex. The example and the W1 re-gate run at -n 2; the W2 re-gate runs at -n 4. - Cost: ≈ 18 measured (class median) / ≈ 50 predicted min. Price basis: - WF-9 W1 took 129 s at -n 2, of which the gate body was 73.7 s (20261003T003327Z_WF-9-step0-W1.log:150–151). W2 took 104 s at -n 4. - A factorisation on this fixture costs ≈ 6.5–8.2 s at -n 2 (:150). D3 and the Born control add two more. - EX-83's overhead (dry run, censuses, figure, unflagged control) was ≈ 9 min of windows. - So the windows total ≈ 13 min, and ≈ 50 min is the honest expectation including writing. - Depends on: nothing. WF-9 step 0 is green at both widths (§9 item 183). The row is 🟡, but every identity this example uses is asserted there. - Gap: no example computes a transfer function or runs an adjoint solve. grep -rniE 'transfer.function|adjoint' examples --include=*.py outside */aed/ returns nothing. imp:3's guide lists WF-9 as not claimed (03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.md:68). imp:1 / imp:2 / imp:3 read the field near a PEC body and never fold a lead response.

Code: rule (a), disclosed (EX-83's _run_one_gram_rung is the precedent). - Lift test_wf9_identities's body (test_wf9_transfer_function_identity.py:220–410) verbatim into a module-level _run_identities(), asserts included. - After the last assert, add one statement: return {...}, with keys fx, q, ell, w, drives, results, tf_step, tf_adj, tf_herm, ndofs, sym_ratio (= sym_norm / a_norm), t2_dev, h_dev, c1_dev, v_ball, times, rss and elapsed. - test_wf9_identities keeps @complex_only and becomes a single call to _run_identities(). - test_wf9_census is untouched. Every print stays byte-identical except the timings. - No new keyword, no src/ edit and no other edit.

Imports (never restated): - From the gate module: _run_identities, _problem, _free, _scalar, SYMMETRY_RTOL, DELTA_SIGMA, LOAD, J_BLOCK, N_LAYERS, LEAD_HALF_Z, BLOCK_CELL_COUNT, HOST_TAG and LEAD_TAG. - DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL from tests.validation.test_birdcage_power_identity, the same place the gate imports it from (:50). - Nothing else carries a number.

Anchor (asserted on the returned case). Each is printed beside 20261003T003327Z_WF-9-step0-W1.log:96–124: - (A1) sym_ratio ≤ SYMMETRY_RTOL; - (T2) t2_dev and (H) h_dev ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL; - (T1) and (T3) on D1 and D2 from results, both at DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL × |dq|. (T3) is the row's identity: −jωμ₀Δσ∫χ_lead w·E_inc = q_with − q_without (Jin §6.4 eqs (6.78)–(6.85)).

Example-side checks (asserted; true by construction, EX-80 / EX-83 precedent): - (X0) D3 census. D3 is a ẑ block: cells, owned + ghost, with midpoint −6 < x < −4 mm, |y| < 1 mm and −10 < z < −2 mm. That is D2's block mirrored through x = 0 and z = 0, built from numpy midpoints in the _build idiom. - The owned count equals BLOCK_CELL_COUNT: 32 hexes × 6 tets, the same as D2. - D3 is disjoint from the lead, the tip ball and D2's block. Reduce with MPI.LAND. - (X1) TF-density map. The per-cell complex vector of LOAD·DELTA_SIGMA·χ_lead·w[2]·conj(v)·dx (v a DG0 test function), summed over the owned cells of layer j and allreduced, equals tf_adj[j] for all 24 layers. Max relative miss ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. - (X2) Fold-integrand maps. For D1 and D2, the owned sum of LOAD·DELTA_SIGMA·χ_lead·ufl.dot(w, E_inc)·conj(v)·dx equals results[d]["t3_fold"] within DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. - (X3) The new drive. Two solves: - Lead out: TimeHarmonicSolver(_problem(fx, with_lead=False, dirichlet=False), degree=1). A full solve on case["ell"] gives w₀, which the Born control uses. A held back-substitution with LOAD·inner(J_BLOCK·χ_D3·ẑ, v)·dx gives E_inc,D3. Then _free. - Lead in: a fresh solve(current_density=lambda xx: J_BLOCK*chi_d3*zhat, project_source=False) gives E_with,D3. Then _free. - The check: |LOAD·Δσ∫χ_lead w·E_inc,D3 − (q(E_with,D3) − q(E_inc,D3))| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|dq_D3|. - w is the gate's with-lead adjoint field, re-used as is. This is the example's angle: the TF is computed once and predicts the tip response to an exposure it never saw.

Printed (no band): - The TF(z) table: j, z_mid (−11.5 + j mm), |TF_adj|, |TF_adj|/max and arg TF_adj in degrees. - Predicted: the peak is at j = 19 (W1:145), and j = 22 / 23 have phase within 20° of ±180° (W1:148–149). Print beside those lines. - D3: |q_with/q_without|, predicted [0.05, 50]. Also the ISO path fold for D3 at N = 24 (Σ_k TF_k·Ē_k over tf_step, segment means from _scalar over the layer masks), predicted relative error [1e-4, 1e-1], with the transverse term beside it. - W1/W2 TF agreement: the gate body prints it against the -n 4 exchange file from re-gate W2. Predicted ≤ 1e-10.

Negative controls (rule (e)): - C1 (asserted on the case): the Hermitian read-back is wired, c1_dev > DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. - Predicted: [190 %, 200 %], against a record of 199.87 % (W1:100). - Its ceiling is 200 %, since |a − ā| ≤ 2|a|, so no factor is claimed. - C2 (asserted): the total-field fold misses on D1, D2 and D3: |fold(w, E_with) − dq| > DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|dq|. - Predicted: [80 %, 105 %] on all three. The records are 94.6 / 97.3 % (W1:106, :118). - C3, the Born control (asserted wired; new to this example): the lead-free adjoint fold Q_B,d = LOAD·Δσ∫χ_lead w₀·E_inc,d, for d ∈ {D1, D2, D3}, misses dq by > DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|dq|. This is why the TF must come from an adjoint solve with the lead present. - Predicted: |Q_B|/|dq| in [3, 300] on D1. The reasoning: the field inside the lead is ≈ 4 % of the lead-free field (C2's premise), which suggests ≈ 25×. - Predicted: [1, 1000] on D2 and D3, with low confidence. - The ratio has no ceiling, so no factor is asserted.

docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 18:00 daily review; the review reviewed it.

EX-85 (mat:11) shows duty-cycled RF heating of the gel ball. It compares the on/off temperature history with the closed form, and the periodic peak with the steady state of the time-averaged power. It also shows what a continuous source at the same average power hides. - Executor: example-runner. - Tier: heavy (the predicted range crosses the 180 s standard ceiling), -n 2, complex build (the mat: group sources it). - Cost: ≈ 18 measured (class median) / ≈ 45 predicted min. The price basis: - Solves. MAT-17 W1b measured the 0.005 m mesh build at 5.3 s (…W1b.log:94–95), a case-A CN N 94 solve at 5.5 s (:98), a case-B N 20 solve at 2.9 s (:101), and a closed-form P2 interpolation on this mesh at 9.3–9.8 s each (:97, :100). - The example's work: four solves, five interpolations, ≈ 70 centre point evaluations, two XDMF writes and one figure. Add the first complex-build JIT of the scheduled forms. - Flagged run: predicted [80, 240] s. - Overhead: the censuses and the dry run are ≈ 1–2 s each (20261003T184030Z_EX-84-post-figures.log, …184032Z…-post-docrefs.log), and the unflagged control repeats the run. That gives ≈ 8 min of windows, and ≈ 45 min is the honest total with writing. - Depends on: nothing. MAT-17 is ✅.

Code: no lift is needed, and no gate or src/ edit is made. Every helper the example needs is already module-level in the gate: - _run, _census, _chi, _n, _exact_duty, _theta_centre, _closed; - the constants CASES, P_A, D_A, P_B, D_B, T_END_A, T_END_B, DT_B, ON_TIME_A, ON_TIME_B, INTERIOR_BAND, BALANCE_BAND.

If the executor still finds a helper it must extend, rule (a) applies: an additive keyword or return key only, then re-gate the module green in the same slot (W-R below) and disclose it.

Imports (never restated): - From tests.validation.test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem (m17): the helpers and constants above. Also take _ball, R, K, Q, H, RHO_C, T_INF, T_R, ROBIN_TAG and _allsum through it; it re-exports them from MAT-9. - From tests.validation.test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form (m17cf): CASES, _modal, TH_SS0, LAM1 and TAU1. - From tests.validation.test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere (m13): the complex-safe _interior_error, _rel_diff and _interior_indicator, plus INTERIOR_BAND and BALANCE_BAND for the structural checks. - Add the repo root to sys.path, as mat:8 does (08_gel_ball_settling_time.py:53–55). - Nothing else carries a number.

Structural checks (asserted, printed): - m17.CASES is m17cf.CASES; - m17.INTERIOR_BAND == m13.INTERIOR_BAND and m17.BALANCE_BAND == m13.BALANCE_BAND; - (m17.R, m17.K, m17.Q, m17.H, m17.RHO_C, m17.T_INF, m17.ROBIN_TAG) equals m13's tuple, and m17cf's R, K, RHO_C, Q, H, T_INF.

Runs. Use msh, cell_tags, ft = m17._ball(0.005). Every run is CN + Rannacher (theta=0.5, startup=2) through m17._run. - A-duty: Δt 150, N = _n(T_END_A, 150) = 94, schedule _chi(P_A, D_A), snapshot_steps=range(0, 95). - A-full: the same Δt and N, no schedule, all snapshots. This is the gate's (c1) run. - B-duty: Δt DT_B, N 20, schedule _chi(P_B, D_B), all snapshots. - B-full: the same, no schedule. - The average-power stand-in is θ_avg = D·(T_full − T∞), built in numpy on the full run's arrays. It is exact for the linear θ-scheme from T(0) = T∞; MAT-17 (L) gates that linearity. Never run a fractional χ ≡ D: fractional χ is ungated (MAT-17 step-2 scope). - Time mapping. Snapshot n is at t = n·Δt: the Rannacher pair counts as full step 1 (thermal/transient.py:125–126). In case A, cycle j's steps are 8j (cycle start, trough), 8j + 2 (mid-on), 8j + 4 (end of on, peak) and 8j + 6 (mid-off). In case B, DP is step 8 and t_end is step 20.

Anchors (asserted at imported bands, each printed beside its record): - (S0) _census on A-duty and B-duty, with on-times ON_TIME_A / ON_TIME_B (it asserts internally). - (iii) Every run's max_balance_residual ≤ BALANCE_BAND. The record is the worst on the 0.005 m runs, 2.823e-14 (W1b :107). - (i) This is the gate's comparison, re-run in the complex build: - m13._interior_error(msh, A-duty T, _exact_duty(msh, T_END_A, P_A, D_A)) ≤ INTERIOR_BAND, beside W1b :98 (4.3870e-04, 151 548 cells); - the same for case B at T_END_B, beside W1b :101 (1.0683e-03). - Predicted equal to the printed digits. A last-digit difference between the builds is reported, with no status effect. - (H) Two new instants, mid-phase as the closed-form trap requires. - Case A at cycle 11 mid-on, t = 13 500 s (step 90). Predicted [1e-4, 3e-3]. - Case B at cycle 0 mid-on, t = DP/2 (step 4). Predicted [2e-4, 5e-3]. - Both are asserted ≤ INTERIOR_BAND. - (AVG) A-full against _exact_duty(msh, T_END_A, P_A, 1.0) (duty 1 = step response, step 1 (P4)) ≤ INTERIOR_BAND. Predicted ≈ 4e-4; MAT-9's CN read 4.6327e-4 on this mesh at t* = 13 933 s (20260929T170037Z_MAT-9-step2b.log:114). D cancels in the relative error.

Printed (no band) — the example's angle: - Time constants: P/τ₁ for both cases, with TAU1 and LAM1 beside 20261003T010113Z_MAT-17-step1-W1.log:141. Predicted 0.0626 / 0.727. - Periodic steady state (closed form, gated in numpy by step 1). For each case, compute the centre peak m17cf._modal(0.0, D*P*(1 - 1e-12), P, D, periodic=True), the trough at P*(1 - 1e-12), and the mean D·TH_SS0. These are the step-1 idiom of test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py:235–236. Print peak/(D·θ_ss) − 1 beside …step1-W1.log:144 (A: +1.174 %) and :239 (B: +20.440 %). Also print j* = ⌈30τ₁/P⌉ beside :142 / :237 (479 / 42) and case A's 111 cycles to 1e-3 (:234). Predicted digit-identical: pure numpy. - Centre history CSV materials_11_duty_cycled_gel_ball_centre_history.csv, one row per even step of case A and every step of case B, with columns: - t; - θ_h(0) from m17._theta_centre; - the closed form m17._closed(0.0, t·(1 − 1e-12), P, D); - D·θ_full(0); - duty minus average. - The hidden peak. At A step 92 (t = 13 800 s, the last peak) and at B step 8 (t = DP), print θ_h(0), the closed form (left limit) and D·θ_full(0), with peak/avg − 1. - Predicted for A, from rest: [3 %, 7 %]. The excess of D(1 − D)P·q/ρc = 0.1435 K over a still-rising mean decays toward the periodic +1.17 %. - Predicted for B: exactly 1/D − 1 = 300 % to round-off, because the first on-phase is a full-power exposure. Also print ‖θ_duty − θ_full‖/‖θ_full‖ at step 8 through m13._rel_diff, predicted ≤ 1e-14. - The average-power stand-in at A's t_end (mid-off, cycle 11) against the duty comparand: m13._interior_error. Predicted [0.5 %, 4 %]: an on-time excess of ≈ 150 s·q/ρc ≈ 0.07 K over ≈ 3 K. It straddles the band, so it is printed only. - θ_h(0) against the closed form at both t_end values, beside W1b :98 / :101 (3.053003 vs 3.050426 K; 1.537399 vs 1.535862 K).

Negative controls (rule (e)): - (c1), asserted, backed. A-full against case A's duty comparand at t_end misses: > INTERIOR_BAND. This is the gate's own control on the same run and fixture: record 9.7087e-01 (W1b :104). Print beside it, predicted to the printed digits. Its ceiling is ≈ 1, so no factor is claimed. - (c-avg B), asserted wired, predicted. θ_avg against B's duty comparand at T_END_B misses: > INTERIOR_BAND. Never measured, so the factor is printed only. - Predicted interior miss [0.15, 0.6]. At the centre, ≈ 1.04 K average against ≈ 1.54 K duty (W1b :101), ≈ 32 %. - The ratio has no tight ceiling, so no factor is asserted.

Output. - Setup figure. Use write_setup_figure with msh and cell_tags, as mat:8 does (08_gel_ball_settling_time.py:189–199): - region_names={1: "gel ball (Robin h = 10, Bi = 5/3; duty-cycled uniform source)"}; - translucent_tags=(1,), slice normal (0, 0, 1) through the origin, and a title ≤ 130 characters. - The path is examples/materials/figures/materials_11_duty_cycled_gel_ball_setup.png. If it is over 600 KiB (this mesh is 8× mat:8's, and mat:8's PNG is 363 KiB), re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Time-series XDMF examples/materials/paraview_output/materials_11_duty_cycled_gel_ball_history_combined.xdmf. Write it with write_xdmf_time_series(…, msh, None, frames). - Frames: case A, steps 0, 2, …, 94 (48 frames, t = n·150 s). - P1 fields, each a fresh named Function whose key equals its name: theta_duty, theta_avg_power and theta_hidden (= duty − average). - Static XDMF …/materials_11_duty_cycled_gel_ball_tend_combined.xdmf, written with write_xdmf_with_tags(…, msh, None, fields). - P1 for each case at t_end: theta_h_A, theta_series_A (the P2 comparand interpolated into P1), theta_err_A, theta_avg_A, and theta_h_B, theta_series_B, theta_err_B, theta_avg_B. - DG0 interior_mask: a named copy of m13._interior_indicator. - Then call adopt_host_ownership(OUTPUT_DIR). - The 1e-6 tracked-artifact rule does not apply: paraview_output/ is gitignored (.gitignore:63), and only the PNG is tracked. - Guide: the three required headings, ## Setup figure and ## Related (mat:4, mat:6, mat:8, mat:10). It explains: - The governing ratio. Why P/τ₁ decides whether averaging the power is safe: case A's periodic peak is +1.17 % and case B's +20.4 %. - What the cycle mean hides. The cycle mean equals D·θ_ss exactly (step 1 (P1)), yet the peak above it is invisible to a continuous source. - The first on-phase. It is a full-power exposure (case B, 4× at the centre). - A ParaView recipe: open the history file and Play; use Probe Location at the origin + Plot Data Over Time, theta_duty against theta_avg_power; threshold interior_mask on the t_end file and colour by theta_err_A. - Not claimed: the scope list below, verbatim in meaning.

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000, and makes one bare harness call. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-85-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-85-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" 2. Then run the dry run after the script exists (EX-84's first dry run exited 2 because it came too early): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-85-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:11 -n 2 -t 420 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 3. Flagged run, predicted [80, 240] s. Copy the emitted string; if it differs from this line, use the emitted one and note it: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-85 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/materials/11_duty_cycled_gel_ball.py"' 4. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-85-control. The readings must be unchanged up to round-off. 5. Post-censuses EX-85-post-figures / EX-85-post-docrefs (step 1's lines, relabelled). Write the prediction first: N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0, docrefs exit != 1. Take N fresh from step 1; it was 79 at 20261003T184030Z_EX-84-post-figures.log. 6. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new tracked paths (script, guide, PNG). No test module and no src/ file is modified. - W-R, conditional (only if a rule (a) lift was made). Run before step 3, real build, ≈ 124 s (W1b's elapsed): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-85-mat17-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem.py -v -s --tb=short'" The W1b digits at :98, :101 and :104 must be reproduced. - Cache sweep, conditional (only after a killed window). First check that pgrep -c python3 reads 0 in the container, then run the rubric's any-orphan sweep verbatim as EX-85-cache-sweep. The scheduled forms compile for the first time in the complex build here.

Traps already paid for: - MAT-9's _interior_error / _rel_diff call float() on a complex value and fail in the complex build (08_gel_ball_settling_time.py:13–16). m17 re-exports them, so never call m17._interior_error; use m13's twins. - The scheduled path has only ever run in the real build (MAT-17 W1b; W3 re-gated only the None path in complex). The (S0), (iii) and (i) results here are its first complex-build reading. A red there is a finding, never an example bug to work around. - Never evaluate the closed form near a switch on the right-hand side. Switch instants use the left limit t·(1 − 1e-12), which is step 1's idiom: there the series decays as e^{−sₙτ} with τ = a full phase. Comparands for interior errors are taken mid-phase only. - Fractional χ is ungated: build the average-power stand-in by scaling, never by schedule=lambda t: D. - _exact_duty costs ≈ 9.5 s per call on this mesh (W1b :97). Call it exactly five times: A t_end, A step 90, A duty 1 at t_end, B t_end, B step 4. Never interpolate per frame. - _theta_centre is collective; call it on every rank. Time the first call. If it exceeds 1 s, restrict the CSV to the switch and mid-phase instants of cycles 0, 1, 10 and 11, and say so. - Name every Function, and give each time-series key its function's name. Otherwise the fields silently collide (write_xdmf_time_series docstring; EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window). - Masks: midpoints over owned + ghost cells, collectives outside rank == 0, np.real in every reduction. Do not use cell_tags.values counts unreduced. - PNG ≤ 600 KiB (ans:8's first was 631 KiB). - No edit after the script's last window (rule (i)). - Status 124 is a finding, never a retry: pgrep -c python3 before any sweep. - A docker-socket denial means stop and report. - You are the executor: do not spawn agents, and never background a harness window.

Scope. MAT-9's ball, 0.005 m, P1, CN + Rannacher, a uniform source switched 0/1 on step boundaries, from rest to MAT-17's two t_end values (Fo ≤ 0.2), in the complex build.

Not claimed: - the FEM periodic steady state (≈ 111 cycles away; printed only from the gated closed form); - an SAR- or coil-driven duty cycle; - perfusion under a schedule; - a fractional χ or switches off step boundaries; - the BE rate (the gate's (ii)); - any pulse-sequence, 6-min-averaging, IEC 60601-2-33 or other regulatory statement.

There is no src/ edit and no PREDICTED RED line.

Status it can move: EX-85 ⬜ → ✅ on the §7 row's Done-when, which this item matches term for term (rule (j)), and the census N → N + 1. MAT-17 stays ✅.

Negative result: - (S0), (iii) or (i) red in the complex build with the gate green in the real build: this is a complex-build defect in the scheduled path. Write a known-issues entry and print the χ list and the balance per step. Park on attempt/EX-85-<UTC> and mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). The unblock condition is a MAT-17 complex-build re-gate, which the review rules on. No band moves. - (H) or (AVG) red with (i) green: print the interior error at every even step and the closed form at r = 0, R/2 and R. Write a known-issues entry; park, BLOCKED. - (c1) or (c-avg B) failing to miss: the brief's premise is wrong. Stop, report and park. - A structural check red: the gate modules drifted apart. Stop and report; never edit a gate module to make it pass. - Over 420 s: park with the last line printed; the review re-tiers. - A printed value outside its prediction (the hidden-peak ratios, the case-A stand-in, P/τ₁): report it. It has no status effect.

Executor prompt (verbatim): - "you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window" - "pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log" - "call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained" - "The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped" - "Execute EX-85 per docs/planning/chunks/EX-85.md#§9-item-207: write examples/materials/11_duty_cycled_gel_ball.py and its same-stem guide, importing every band and helper from tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem.py, its step-1 module and MAT-13's complex-safe twins; make no gate or src/ edit; run windows 1–6 in order; journal the outcome under this item."

Outcome (2026-10-04 00:38–00:50 UTC, 19:30 CDT slot, take-next; example-runner): ✅, row ⬜ → ✅. Logs: 20261004T003825Z_EX-85-pre-figures.log (79/79/0/0), …003829Z_EX-85-pre-docrefs.log (exit 2, stale=36), …004003Z_EX-85-dryrun.log ((complex build)), flagged …004009Z_EX-85.log (Status 0, 317 s), control …004534Z_EX-85-control.log (Status 0, 259 s, readings unchanged to round-off), …005023Z_EX-85-post-figures.log (80/80/0/0, as predicted), …005025Z_EX-85-post-docrefs.log (exit 2, stale=36, 80 guides). Printed: P/τ₁ 0.0626 / 0.7274; periodic peak over mean +1.174 % / +20.440 %, j* 479 / 42, 111 cycles — all equal to step 1; hidden peak A +4.088 % (predicted [3, 7] %), B +300.000 % with duty − full 2.5e-15 at step 8; case-A stand-in 1.4574e-02. docs.title: EX-86 — history
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened by the 2026-10-03 18:00 daily review under the §5.4 example ramp (daily-review.md step 5), from MAT-18 ✅ (c371c5a4, §9 item 205, step 2(b)), audited PASS. MAT-18 is the first thermal material interface the project gates: a gel core inside a low-k container wall, Robin outside, with θ and k∂ᵣθ continuous at r = a. No example demonstrates it. - Gap checked. grep -rlE 'two_layer|mat18|two_layer_ball' examples --include=*.py --include=*.md returns nothing (exit 1). Every thermal example solves one homogeneous medium: mat:4 (SAR heats the gel ball), mat:6 (perfusion sink), mat:7 (perfused ball), mat:8 (the bare ball's settling time), mat:10 (the finite cylinder against its double series); mat:11 (item 207, EX-85) is the duty cycle. - New angle: what the container wall does to the gel. It is the steady profile across the interface (the temperature kink with a continuous flux) against the closed form, the series-resistance budget (core, wall, film) against the bare MAT-9 ball, and the slower settling (the composite's slowest mode against the bare ball's), with the gated transient at t* against the composite series.

Done-when: examples/materials/12_gel_ball_in_container_wall.py + same-stem guide (three required headings + ## Setup figure, PNG ≤ 600 KiB), run through ./run_examples.sh -e mat:12. It imports MAT-18's fixture, helpers and comparands, and the bands from MAT-13 (the mat:8 precedent), and restates none of them. At -n 2, degree 1, complex build, on the 0.005 rung: steady interior ≤ INTERIOR_BAND and balance ≤ BALANCE_BAND; CN + Rannacher N 40 at t* interior ≤ INTERIOR_BAND; every transient run's balance ≤ BALANCE_BAND; each printed beside its MAT-18 log record. docs.title: §9 item 208 — 2026-10-03 (§5.4 example)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 18:00 daily review; the review reviewed it.

EX-86 (mat:12) shows what the container wall does to the gel ball: the steady temperature kinks at r = a while the heat flux stays continuous, the wall's series resistance raises the core above the bare MAT-9 ball, and the composite's slowest mode slows the settling. The gated transient at t* is checked against the composite series. - Executor: example-runner. - Tier: heavy, -n 2, complex build (the runner sources it for the mat: group). -t 420. - Cost: ≈ 18 measured (class median) / ≈ 45 predicted min. Price basis: - MAT-18 2(b) W1b (20261003T184850Z_MAT-18-step2b-W1b.log): the 0.005 build took 9.4 s (:85), the two-layer comparand at t* 18.0 s (:87), and CN N 40 7.6 s (:88). 2(a) W1's steady solve took 1.8 s at 0.005 (20261003T172548Z_MAT-18-step2a-W1.log:90). - The example adds the uniform-k and uniform-ρc controls (≈ 2 s and ≈ 7 s), a CN N 120 settle run (≈ 20 s), the core-mean assemblies and one point evaluation per printed time (≈ 10 s), the XDMF (≈ 5 s), the figure (≈ 10–20 s), and a first compile of the DG0-coefficient forms in the complex build (≈ 10–40 s, flagged run only). - Flagged run predicted ≈ 150 s, range [90, 300]; the control run is ≈ 30 s shorter (warm cache, no figure). There is no re-gate window (no gate edit). Windows total ≈ 7 min; ≈ 45 min is the honest expectation including writing. - Depends on: nothing. MAT-18 is ✅ (item 205), and examples/ gets new files only. - Shared with item 207 (EX-85, mat:11): nothing in code. run_examples.sh selects by file-name prefix (select_by_number, scripts/run_examples.sh:201–219), so there is no registry to edit and mat:12 resolves whether or not 11_*.py exists. The only common state is the census count and the append-only records (test-results.md, attempts.md, the §7 row and §9 entry). If 207 lands first, rebase; never path-checkout a record file. git diff --stat must show insertions only on test-results.md. Take N fresh from this item's own pre-census, never from 207's.

Code. No src/ edit and no gate edit. Every helper the example needs is already module-level in the gate modules, so no rule (a) lift is expected. If one turns out to be needed, it is additive, disclosed, and its module is re-run green in the same slot with the record digits (windows 2a / 2b below).

Imports (never restated): - From step 1 (test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form): A_, B_, K1, K2, Q1, Q2, RC1, RC2, H, T_INF, T_R. - From 2(a) (test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_fem, alias m18a): _ball, _dg0, _indicator, _comparand, _two_layer (steady), _errors, _vcore, _allsum, ROBIN_TAG. - From 2(b) (test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_transient_fem, alias m18b): _fine (0.005 rung, cell guard, DG0 k / ρc / q, the cached t* comparand), _run, _exact_theta, _two_layer (transient), _errors, _rel_diff, T_STAR, N_CN. - m18b imports _ball from m18a, so both share one mesh cache: one build. - Import by module alias. The two _two_layer names collide. - From MAT-9 (test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere, alias mat9): R, K, Q, RHO_C, H, T_INF, T_R, T_END, for the structural check only. - From MAT-13: INTERIOR_BAND, BALANCE_BAND. These are the same 1e-2 / 1e-9 that MAT-18's modules assert as literals (their docstrings cite MAT-9's bands). MAT-18 exposes no band constant; mat:8 imports the same two names. - From utils/analytical.py: two_layer_sphere_steady_temperature, two_layer_sphere_transient_temperature, two_layer_sphere_eigenvalues, robin_sphere_steady_temperature, robin_sphere_transient_temperature, robin_sphere_eigenvalues. Also evaluate_vector_field_parallel, write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership, write_setup_figure, solve_steady_conduction. - Records (log digits) are not importable. They go in one RECORD dict with a log:line comment per entry, printed beside the run and never asserted (mat:8's RECORD precedent): - 20261003T172548Z_MAT-18-step2a-W1.log:89–90: cells 215 542, steady interior 1.1206e-03, balance 1.019e-14; - the same log, :110: (c1) uniform k 0.1986; - 20261003T184850Z_MAT-18-step2b-W1b.log:88–89: (T1) 8.2066e-04, (T2) 1.040e-14; - W1b :90–92: θ_h at t* 5.9481 / 3.7877 / 2.3703 K; - W1b :94: (c1) uniform ρc 5.3140e-02; - 20261003T140149Z_MAT-18-step1-W2.log:89, :106: θ(0) 14.2550 K; no wall 12.2222 K; composite 1/s₁ = 2.4549e+04 s; - 20261002T051536Z_EX-74.log:39, :70: bare-ball τ₁ 19 155.0 s; volume-mean t₉₉ 88 118 s (series).

Anchors (asserted, each printed beside its record). - (S) Steady, 0.005 rung. solve_steady_conduction with _dg0(K1, K2) and _dg0(Q1, Q2), compared against m18a._comparand(msh, m18a._two_layer). - Interior (m18a._errors) ≤ INTERIOR_BAND; record 1.1206e-03. The gate asserts (S2) at 0.003536; at 0.005 the gate's reading is a record and this example asserts the band on it. - Balance |P_conv − Q1·V_core,h| / (Q1·V_core,h) ≤ BALANCE_BAND, with m18a._vcore; record 1.019e-14. - (T1) Transient at t*. m18b._fine() + m18b._run(…, k=k_f, rho_c=rc_f, q=q_f, n=N_CN, theta=0.5, startup=2), interior (m18b._errors) against the cached comparand ≤ INTERIOR_BAND; record 8.2066e-04. - (T2) Every transient run's max_balance_residual ≤ BALANCE_BAND: (T1), (c-ρc) and the settle run. - Structural (asserted; it licenses the bare-ball comparison): A_ == mat9.R, K1 == mat9.K, Q1 == mat9.Q, RC1 == mat9.RHO_C, H == mat9.H, T_INF == mat9.T_INF, T_R == mat9.T_R, m18b.T_STAR == mat9.T_END. The gel core is MAT-9's ball, so "the wall" is the only difference. - Complex build: max |Im T_h| over every solve, allreduced, equals 0 (the EX-81 precedent).

Negative controls (asserted, rule (e) backed: the same comparison on the same fixture is recorded). - (c-k) Ignore the wall's conductivity: scalar k = K1 with the piecewise q (the gate's test_c1_uniform_k_control call). The steady interior misses INTERIOR_BAND; record 0.1986 (…step2a-W1.log:110), ≈ 20× the band. - (c-ρc) Ignore the wall's heat capacity: scalar rho_c = RC1 with DG0 k (the gate's (c1) call). The (T1) interior misses INTERIOR_BAND; record 5.3140e-02 (W1b :94), ≈ 5× the band. - Each is asserted only as "misses the band", with the measured value printed beside the record. In the guide, these are the example's point: a model that treats the wall as more gel is 20 % wrong at steady state and 5 % wrong at t*.

Printed (no band; predicted where stated). - The steady profile across the interface. Use one evaluate_vector_field_parallel call on the +x axis at r ∈ {0, 0.25a, 0.5a, 0.75a, 0.9a, 0.97a, a, a + 0.25(b − a), a + 0.5(b − a), a + 0.75(b − a), 0.999b}. Print θ_h, the two-layer closed form, their relative difference, and, for r ≤ a only, the bare-ball closed form robin_sphere_steady_temperature(r, radius=A_, k=K1, q=Q1, h=H, t_inf=T_INF). - Predicted: θ_h(0) within 1e-3 of 14.2550 K (the 0.003536 rung read 14.2498, …step2a-W1.log:94). - The resistance budget. Core drop θ(0) − θ(a), wall drop θ(a) − θ(b) and film drop θ(b), from the closed form and from θ_h (at 0.999b), beside the bare ball's core drop and film drop θ_bare(a). - Predicted from step 1's records: 5.556 / 3.190 / 5.510 K against 5.556 / 0 / 6.667 K. The wall adds 3.190 K, while its larger outer area takes 1.157 K off the film. The net is +2.033 K at the centre (14.26 %, …step1-W2.log:89). - Also print the critical radius of insulation 2·K2/H (= 0.038 m < a), from the imported constants: any thickness of this wall raises the core. The guide explains it. - Flux continuity against the kink. Interpolate ufl.grad(T_h) into a DG0 vector space with fem.Expression(expr, W.element.interpolation_points) (the mri:3 idiom). Then, in numpy, take ∂ᵣθ per cell on the unit vector of the cell midpoint and q_r = −k ∂ᵣθ with the DG0 k. - Two bands of cells: tag-1 cells with midpoint r ∈ [a − 2.5e-3, a), and tag-2 cells with r ∈ (a, a + 2.5e-3]. Take volume-weighted means over owned cells, allreduced, with cell volumes from assemble_vector(TestFunction(DG0)·dx). - Print |∂ᵣθ| shell/core, predicted [2.7, 3.6] (k₁/k₂ = 3.158); q_r shell/core, predicted [0.9, 1.1]; and both band fluxes beside Gauss's Q1·V_core,h/(4πa²). - Settling. - A CN + Rannacher run on the 0.005 rung to 3·T_R: m18b._run(…, n=120, dt=3*T_R/120, theta=0.5, startup=2, snapshot_steps=range(0, 121)). Δt = 1741.7 s; the shell's h²/α₂ ≈ 224 s, so the Rannacher start is required. - The core-volume mean θ̄_core,h(t) at every step is ∫χ_core(T − T∞)dx / V_core,h, with χ_core = _dg0(1, 0). - The series core mean is 3/a³∫₀ᵃθ r² dr by 64-point Gauss–Legendre on [0, a] (the core is one smooth layer, so no split is needed). It is evaluated at all frames and on an Fo grid of step 0.01 over [1, 3], in calls of ≤ 50 times. - The bare-ball whole-ball mean comes from robin_sphere_transient_temperature(radius=A_, …), the same way. - Print a table at Fo ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 3}: FEM core mean, series core mean, their difference, the bare-ball mean, and θ_h(0, t) beside the series at r = 0 (one point call per printed time only). - τ₁ = 1/s₁ from two_layer_sphere_eigenvalues(n=1), beside the record 2.4549e+04 s, against the bare ball's τ₁ = T_R/λ₁² from robin_sphere_eigenvalues(H*A_/K1, 1), beside 19 155.0 s. Predicted ratio 1.282. - t₉₉ of the core mean (deficit 1 %), by log-linear interpolation between bracketing points. Do it for the series and for the bare ball (beside EX-74's 88 118 s; predicted within 1 %). For the FEM, use every step, normalised by the discrete steady core mean from (S)'s solve on the same mesh; this is mat:8's lesson, because the late-time deficit is a small difference of two nearly equal means. - Predicted two-layer series t₉₉ in [100 000, 130 000] s, and the ratio to the bare ball in [1.15, 1.45]. - Steady core mean, two-layer against bare: predicted 10.92 K against 8.889 K (+22.9 %). - The settle end at Fo 3 against the (S) steady solve, as a whole-ball relative difference (m18b._rel_diff). Predicted ≈ 1e-4 (e^{−3T_R/τ₁} ≈ 2e-4 times the slow mode's weight). - Mesh: cells and V_core,h / V_shell,h deficits, beside …step2a-W1.log:89 and W1b :85.

Output. - Setup figure on the 0.005 mesh with the gate's cell_tags: - region_names 1 "gel core" and 2 "container wall", each with k and ρc formatted from the imported constants, never typed; - translucent_tags=(2,), so the core shows through the wall; - slice normal (0, 1, 0) through y = 0, which shows the 1 cm ring; - window_size=(1400, 630), title ≤ 130 characters; - over 600 KiB ⇒ re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False.

Path: examples/materials/figures/materials_12_gel_ball_in_container_wall_setup.png. - Combined XDMF examples/materials/paraview_output/materials_12_gel_ball_in_container_wall_combined.xdmf, written with write_xdmf_with_tags(…, msh, ct, fields) + adopt_host_ownership. Every Function is named. - P1: theta_h_steady, theta_cf_steady (P2 comparand interpolated into P1), theta_err_steady, theta_h_uniform_k_steady (the (c-k) field), theta_h_tstar, theta_series_tstar, theta_err_tstar. - DG0: k, rho_c, radial_gradient_steady, radial_flux_steady, interface_band (1 core band, 2 shell band, 0 elsewhere), interior_mask. - CSV: …/paraview_output/materials_12_gel_ball_in_container_wall_settle_curve.csv with Fo, t, the FEM core mean, the series core mean and the bare-ball mean at every frame. - Guide: ## 1. What this demonstrates, ## 2. How to run it, ## Setup figure, ## 3. How to analyze it, step by step, ## Related (mat:8, mat:4, mat:10; mat:11 only if it exists at write time). - The steps cover: the profile and the kink; the resistance budget and the critical radius; ParaView "Plot Over Line" along x on theta_h_steady, radial_gradient_steady and radial_flux_steady (the gradient jumps by k₁/k₂ at r = a, the flux does not); the two controls; and the settle table and t₉₉. - Artifact references carry full filenames (rule (b)). The XDMF / H5 / CSV are gitignored; only the PNG is tracked.

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000, and makes one bare harness call. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-86-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-86-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" 2. Orphan check, then the sweep. docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0 (it exits 1 on 0 matches; the reading is what counts). Then: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-86-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - 2a / 2b, only if a rule (a) lift was made (not expected). Take N fresh from window 1; it was 79 after EX-84 (20261003T184030Z_EX-84-post-figures.log), and 80 if item 207 has landed. 7. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new tracked paths (script, guide, PNG), and nothing under src/ or tests/ is modified.

Traps already paid for: - The transient comparand at the dof coordinates only. MAT-18 2(b)'s first W1 hit the 180 s ceiling in the comparand: f.interpolate(callable) asks for ≈ 1.1M points per rank at 0.005, and each 20 000-point call costs 2.2–2.6 s because it recomputes 400 roots (20261003T184348Z_MAT-18-step2b-W1.log, status 124; probe …184829Z…-probe-comparand.log). - Use m18b._exact_theta / m18b._fine, which evaluate at tabulate_dof_coordinates() in 20 000-point chunks. Never call the transient series through interpolate, and never evaluate it pointwise in a Python loop. - Evaluate the series core mean with r of shape (64, 1) against a vector of t (one root computation per call). - Never evaluate any series at t = 0 (the tail goes as 1/N²). Frame 0 is θ = 0 by the initial condition. - This is the first complex-build run of the DG0-coefficient path. MAT-18's windows ran in the real build, while the mat: group runs complex. 2(b)'s brief lists "the new module in the complex build" as not covered. - The helpers are complex-safe: _allsum takes np.real, and the positivity checks take the real minimum (steady.py:186, transient.py:74). - Do not use MAT-9's own _interior_error / _rel_diff; they call float() on a complex value (mat:8's note). - The new forms compile on the flagged run. A killed compile leaves an orphan .c, so run pgrep and then the sweep before any re-run. - Masks and radii in numpy, from midpoints over owned + ghost cells, with counts and sums over owned cells and collectives outside rank == 0. No UFL comparison and no sqrt comparison (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). cell_tags.find and assemble_scalar are rank-local, so reduce everything. - Points on the faceted surface can fall outside the mesh. Evaluate at 0.999b, as the gates do. Print a NaN as the gates do (valid=False), and never raise on it. - The comparand picks its layer by exact r. Points between the faceted interface and r = a get the other layer's formula; that is consistent (θ and the flux are continuous), so do not special-case it. The interface bands are cut by cell tag and midpoint radius, never by radius alone. - Round-off readings ((S) balance, (T2), |Im|) vary from run to run. Assert them at their band only. The O(1e-3) records are expected to match to the printed digits, because the mesh is deterministic at -n 2. - Name every Function: EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window. Keep the PNG ≤ 600 KiB (ans:8's first was 631 KiB). - No edit after the script's last window (rule (i)). Status 124 is a finding, never a retry. A docker-socket denial means stop and report. - Item 207 overlap: rebase, never path-checkout; append record rows by hand (the 2026-09-10 8d4cf58 lesson).

Scope. The MAT-18 fixture (a 0.1 m gel core and a 1 cm wall with representative acrylic k and ρc), P1, perfect contact, a uniform core source, the 0.005 rung, steady, t* and a settle run to 3·T_R.

Not claimed: - the LSQ rate (2(a)'s four-rung ladder); - contact resistance or a real container's properties; - degree 2; - SAR or EM drive, the cylinder, perfusion; - any physiological or compliance reading; - the settle quantities (τ₁, t₉₉, the budget), which are printed only.

There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Status it can move: EX-86 ⬜ → ✅, and the census N → N + 1. MAT-18 stays ✅.

Negative result: - (S), (T1), (T2), a control or the structural check red: an example/gate divergence. Write a known-issues entry, park on attempt/EX-86-<UTC>, and mark item 208 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). Never loosen a band. - |Im T_h| ≠ 0, or an asserted O(1e-3) reading off its real-build record in the third significant figure or worse: the complex build does not reproduce the gate on the DG0 path. Do the same (known-issues, park, BLOCKED). The review decides whether to queue a complex-build re-gate of both MAT-18 FEM modules. - A difference only in the last printed digit: report it, with no status effect. - A printed value outside its prediction (the ratios, t₉₉, the budget): report it, with no status effect. - Over 420 s: park with the last line printed; the review re-tiers. - PNG over 600 KiB after the one re-render: stop and report.

Executor prompt (verbatim): - "Execute EX-86 (§9 item 208, brief docs/planning/chunks/EX-86.md#§9-item-208): you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window." - "The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped." - "Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained." - "Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log."

Outcome (2026-10-04 00:51–01:08 UTC, 19:30 CDT slot, second take-next; example-runner): ✅, row ⬜ → ✅ — with two disclosed script-bug reds.
