docs.title: §9 item 209 — 2026-10-03 (§5.4 example)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-87 (imp:5): a lead shaft in the gel. The wire shorts the field that runs along it and doubles the field that crosses it. One mesh and one 1 mm PEC shaft in IMP-1's host (σ 0.57 S/m, εᵣ 78, 64 MHz) are driven two ways: - E along the shaft (TM_z, E_z). The surrounding gel goes cold: the annulus a < ρ < 1.5a carries Φ ≈ 3.7e-3, so SAR there is ≈ 0.4 % of the open-gel SAR at E₀. The drive's energy turns into the axial current I ≈ 2.9 mA per V/m. On a finite lead, that current is what imp:2 – imp:4 find at the tip. - E across the shaft (TE_z, E_⊥). The field doubles at the two points facing it, so the surface SAR there is ≈ 4× open gel, and falls to zero on the two flanks. The annulus mean is Φ ≈ 1.44. - The finite-k angle. The TE near field is quasi-static to ≈ 2e-4. The TM field has no quasi-static limit: as |k|a → 0 it falls only as 1/ln(1/|k|a). A 10× thinner wire still carries ≈ 65 % of the current. - The fixture angle. A 3D slab stands in for the infinite wire only if each polarisation gets its own end condition. With the end conditions swapped, the field never reaches the shaft.

  • Executor: example-runner.
  • Tier: heavy. Every window runs at -n 2 in the complex build.
  • Cost: ≈ 18 measured (example class median) / ≈ 55 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 25 code and guide + ≈ 15 windows). Price basis, all from IMP-4 step 1 at -n 2:
  • TM gate solve 37.1 s including the mesh, TE 29.3 s, 4.28 GiB summed (20261003T200454Z_IMP-4-step1-W1.log:133,139). The natural-cavity solves took 32.8 / 27.7 s (20261003T200703Z_IMP-4-step1-W2.log:133,139).
  • The W0 / W1 / W2 windows took 96 / 123 / 117 s.
  • The example makes four solves (≈ 130 s), plus maps, XDMF, figure and startup ≈ 40–90 s. Predicted [150, 300] s per example window.
  • The re-gate is W0 + W1 + W2's bodies in one complex window, predicted [190, 330] s.
  • Depends on: nothing. IMP-4 is ✅ (§9 item 206).
  • Shared files.
  • IMP-5 (the coated cylinder) is being opened in parallel and may edit io/mesh.py and utils/analytical.py additively. This item edits neither; it imports only.
  • If IMP-5 has landed an edit to tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py (for example to _solve_cylinder), rebase, keep both sets of keywords, and re-gate the module as it stands at HEAD.
  • Never land anything by path checkout.
  • Gap. No existing example covers this:
  • grep -rnlE 'pec_cylinder|hankel|TE_z|TM_z' examples --include=*.py returns nothing.
  • cylindrical_domain appears only in meshing/02_cylindrical_phantom.py (the fragment phantom) and time_harmonic/08_poynting_power_balance.py (a rod smoke mesh), never with as_hole=True.
  • imp:1 is the sphere and imp:2 is the spheroid tip, both quasi-static. imp:2 shows that the axial field makes a tip hot.
  • imp:3 is a finite rod under a coil. imp:4 is the adjoint TF.
  • None shows a 2D-invariant shaft, a field that is intrinsically finite-k, or the two polarisations of one conductor with polarisation-specific end conditions.
  • None shows that the axial field which heats a tip leaves the gel cold along the shaft.

Code: rule (a), disclosed. EX-77's return_fields on _solve_spheroid is the precedent. - In tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py, give _solve_cylinder(drive, pec_tags) (:241) two keyword-only parameters: *, return_fields=False, trace=None. - trace=None keeps dirichlet_e_field=_dirichlet(drive). Otherwise the passed callable is used. - return_fields=True adds fields to the returned dict and changes nothing else. - The three test bodies are untouched and every print stays byte-identical. - No src/ edit, and no other edit. - The module is re-gated green before any example window.

Imports (never restated): - From tests.validation.test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem: - functions: _solve_cylinder, _mesh (one _MESH_CACHE entry serves the four solves, the figure and the XDMF), _cf, _dirichlet, _eval_complex, _circle, _annulus_mask, _continuous_annulus_mean, _static_te_numpy; - constants: PEC_TAGS, A, C, LENGTH, END_TAG, K, OMEGA, MASK_FACTOR. - Re-exported there: - from IMP-1: TH15_BETA_BAND (4.886 %), MAT4_BAND (10 %), E0, DEGREE, OUTER_BOUNDARY_TAG, CAVITY_TAG; - from IMP-2: QDEG, _owned_masked_cells, _rss_gib. - From src: pec_cylinder_tm0_field, pec_cylinder_te1_field and pec_cylinder_tm0_current (utils/analytical.py). Cite them by name: line numbers may move under IMP-5. - Nothing else carries a number.

Anchor (asserted, imported bands). Run _solve_cylinder(d, PEC_TAGS[d], return_fields=True) for d ∈ {"tm", "te"}. These are the asserts of test_both_drives:394–399: - (i) |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND. β is the complex LSQ amplitude of the closed-form scattered field (pec_cylinder_tm0_field / pec_cylinder_te1_field; Jin 3e §11.2.1 eq (11.56) and Exercise 11.4, after Harrington §5-8) on 24-point circles at ρ = 1.2a, 1.5a and 2a. - (ii) |Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1| ≤ MAT4_BAND on the annulus mask (a < ρ < 1.5a). - (iii) n_cavity > 0 and cavity_max < 1e-12.

Print each value beside the W1 record (20261003T200454Z_IMP-4-step1-W1.log): - :133: cells 25 568, degree-2 dofs 174 112, annulus cells 9 735, h_wall/a 0.396. - TM: β 0.999655 − 0.000093j (:134); Φ_h 3.742390e-03 vs Φ_cf,h 3.704934e-03 (:135); cavity 10 704 dofs, max 3.726e-20 (:136). - TE: β 0.992258 − 0.000001j (:140); Φ_h 1.440373 vs Φ_cf,h 1.443759 (:141); max 2.095e-34 (:142). - The TM fitted current β·pec_cylinder_tm0_current(k=K, radius=A, omega=OMEGA, e0=E0) beside :137 (|I| 2.91733e-3 A per V/m).

Any difference at the printed digits is reported. The gate module exports no record constants, so this is a printed comparison, as in EX-77.

Example-side checks (asserted; true by construction, the EX-77 / EX-84 precedent): - (X1) The FEM SAR-ratio map. The per-cell vector of ufl.inner(e, e) * ufl.conj(v) * dx (v a DG0 test function; dx with metadata={"quadrature_degree": QDEG}) is divided by the per-cell ufl.conj(v) * dx volume and E0². The result is the DG0 sar_ratio_<drive> = |E_h|²/E₀² (= SAR/SAR₀ in the uniform-σ host). - Its volume-weighted mean over the owned annulus cells (_owned_masked_cells(msh, _annulus_mask(msh))), allreduced, equals the returned phi_h within 1e-12 relative, for both drives. - (X2) The closed-form map. This is an example-local per-cell version of _numpy_quadrature_mean's basix degree-QDEG rule (test_imp2_spheroid_fem.py:181–201), applied to _cf(drive, "continue") on every owned cell. Its masked mean equals the returned phi_cf_h within 1e-12 relative, for both drives. - (X3) All four solves report the same ncells, which confirms the one cached mesh.

Printed (no band; predicted beside measured): - The polarisation contrast. - Φ_TE,h/Φ_TM,h, predicted 384.9 (W1 :141 / :135). - The same ratio for Φ_cf,h (389.7) and for the continuous values (396.9). - Pointwise |E|²/E₀² at z = 0, FEM (_eval_complex) beside the closed form, at ρ ∈ {1.2a, 2a} and φ ∈ {0, π/2}. E_inc is E₀ŷ, so φ = π/2 faces the field and φ = 0 is the flank. - Closed-form predictions (static values, good to ≈ 2e-4): - TE at 1.2a: 2.871 (facing) / 0.0934 (flank); - TE at 2a: 1.5625 / 0.5625; - TM (axisymmetric): 1.83e-3 at 1.2a and 2.65e-2 at 2a. - FEM/closed-form − 1 is predicted within ±5 %, or ±10 % at the TE flank, where the value is a small difference. - Also printed: the closed-form TE surface value at ρ = a, φ = π/2, predicted 4.0009 (step 0's 2.00022², IMP-4.md:99), and TM 0 there. - Finite k against quasi-static, TE. - _continuous_annulus_mean(_cf("te", "continue")) beside _continuous_annulus_mean(_static_te_numpy), which is predicted 1.444444 (= 1 + 4/9). - The relative difference is predicted +1.9e-4, range [+1.5e-4, +2.3e-4] (the finite-k value 1.444718 is at W1 :141). - Finite k against quasi-static, TM: a closed-form radius sweep (numpy only, no FEM). It covers a ∈ {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2} mm plus a = 1 nm. a = 1 nm is equivalent to k → 1e-6·k at 1 mm, step 0's (Q) scaling, because the fields depend only on ka and kρ. - |E_z(1.5a)|/E₀ from pec_cylinder_tm0_field, predicted 0.0622 / 0.0722 / 0.0821 / 0.0952 / 0.1129 / 0.0226. This is ln(1.5)/|D| with D = −ln(ka/2) − γ − jπ/2; ±3 %, ±5 % at 1 nm. - |I| from pec_cylinder_tm0_current, predicted 1.907e-3 / 2.214e-3 / 2.519e-3 / 2.918e-3 / 3.462e-3 / 6.92e-4 A per V/m, with the same tolerances. - The TE value |E(1.5a, π/2)|/E₀ from pec_cylinder_te1_field, predicted 1.4444 at every radius (static, scale-free), within 1e-3. - The guide reads the table as follows: the TE shaft near field is quasi-static and independent of radius. The TM field has no static limit; it vanishes only logarithmically as |k|a → 0, so a quasi-static solver has no answer for the axial drive at any frequency. - z-invariance. - For the gate drives: z_inv beside W1 :136 / :142 (7.335e-3 / 1.333e-2; IMP-4 predicted ≲ 1e-3, cause untested). - For the two controls: predicted [0.1, 1.0]. That is the cos(πz/L) profile of the lowest evanescent slab mode, 1 − cos(π/4) ≈ 0.29 at z = L/4. - The guide states only the scale this gives: a wrong end condition reads one to two decades above the gate drives. It does not explain the gate's 1e-2.

Negative controls (rule (e): unmeasured on this fixture, so each factor is predicted, printed beside the measurement, and asserted only as missing the band).

The swapped end condition. Item 206's traps name the opposite pairing as "the trap, not the fixture" (IMP-4.md:140), and this example measures it. - C1. TM with natural ends: _solve_cylinder("tm", (OUTER_BOUNDARY_TAG, CAVITY_TAG), return_fields=True). - The weak form with natural ends imposes n̂·E = E_z = 0 there. The exact field has E_z ≠ 0, so the trace on the outer wall reaches the shaft only through slab modes that decay as e^{−πd/L}. From ρ = c to ρ ≤ 2a that is ≈ e^{−6.3}. - Asserted: |Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1| > MAT4_BAND. - Predicted: Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1 in [−100 %, −90 %] (≈ −99.9 %). The ceiling is 100 %, which is 10× the band, so no factor is claimed. - β is printed, not asserted. It is predicted |β − 1| ≈ 0.11, range [0.05, 0.2]. Next to a PEC wire the TM scattered field nearly cancels the incident one, so a field-free slab fits β ≈ 1/(1 − ε) ≈ 1.10 + 0.03j. β therefore separates it by only ≈ 2× the band, and Φ is the TM discriminator. - C2. TE with PEC ends: _solve_cylinder("te", PEC_TAGS["tm"], trace=t0, return_fields=True). - Here t0 = lambda x: _dirichlet("te")(x) * (np.abs(x[2]) < LENGTH / 2 - END_TOL), with END_TOL = 1e-6 * LENGTH. It returns shape (3, N) and is safe for N = 0. - The zeroing is what makes this a control (see the traps). Tangential E is forced to 0 on the plates, and the transverse trace decays inward the same way as in C1. - Asserted: |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND and |Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1| > MAT4_BAND. - Predicted: β ≈ 0, because the uniform incident field is orthogonal to the n = 1 dipole on full 24-point circles. That gives |β − 1| in [0.9, 1.1], with a ceiling ≈ 1, or ≈ 20× the band. The Φ miss is predicted in [−100 %, −90 %]. - For the guide. The gate's own TE natural-cavity control can miss only on β: a line dipole of either sign has the same annulus-mean |E|² (IMP-4.md:198, the ruling that it is printed, not asserted). C2 removes the field outright, so here Φ does discriminate.

Output. - Setup figure examples/implants/figures/implants_05_lead_shaft_polarisation_in_gel_setup.png, through write_setup_figure: - on _mesh()'s mesh with a figure-only meshtags that is never passed to a solve: tag 2 for the host and tag 3 for the cells whose numpy midpoint has x² + y² < (MASK_FACTOR·A)², over owned + ghost cells; - region_names={2: "gel host sigma 0.57 S/m (1 mm PEC lead shaft cut out as a hole)", 3: "annulus a < rho < 1.5a (Phi readout)"}; - translucent_tags=(2,), clip_normal=(0, -1, 0), slice_normal=(0, 0, 1) through z = 0, which shows the graded ring around the hole; - window_size=(1400, 630), title ≤ 130 characters; - if the PNG is over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Combined XDMF examples/implants/paraview_output/implants_05_lead_shaft_polarisation_in_gel_combined.xdmf: - written by write_xdmf_with_tags(…, facet_tags=facet_tags) + adopt_host_ownership, on the gate mesh with its cell and facet tags (1 outer wall, 2 cavity, 3 end annuli); - every Function named; - DG0 fields: sar_ratio_tm, sar_ratio_tm_closed_form, sar_ratio_te, sar_ratio_te_closed_form, sar_ratio_tm_natural_ends (C1), sar_ratio_te_pec_ends (C2) and annulus_mask; - E_real_tm / E_real_te from each fields.e_real, renamed (the imp:2 pattern, 02_pec_spheroid_tip_in_gel.py:198–199). - Build each drive's outputs, then release fields before the next solve. - Guide. The three required headings, ## Setup figure and ## Related (imp:1 – imp:4; IMP-4's gate files by full filename, rule (b)). It explains: - why E along a PEC wire is shorted, and becomes current, while E across it doubles at the facing points; - the finite-k reading of the radius sweep; - why each polarisation needs its own end plane (Jin §1.4.2 eqs (1.44)/(1.45), §11.2.1 eq (11.53)), and what C1 / C2 show; - a ParaView recipe: Slice z = 0; colour by sar_ratio_te on a log scale, then by sar_ratio_tm; a Calculator sar_ratio_te/sar_ratio_te_closed_form; Plot Over Line along the x and y axes; a Slice x = 0 on sar_ratio_te_pec_ends to see the field die toward the plates. - The XDMF / H5 are gitignored; only the new PNG is tracked.

Complex build. The script checks default_scalar_type and raises in a real build (the imp:4 guard, 04_lead_transfer_function_adjoint.py:124–128). The imp: group sources source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode automatically. The pytest re-gate window carries both source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, so the complex_only tests cannot skip silently.

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000, and makes one bare harness call. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-87-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-87-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" 2. Make the rule (a) edit, then re-gate the whole module (complex; predicted [190, 330] s). The expectation: - 15 passed: 12 environment + census + both drives + controls; - cells 25 568; - the β / Φ / cavity lines equal 20261003T200454Z_IMP-4-step1-W1.log:133–142 and 20261003T200703Z_IMP-4-step1-W2.log:133–143 at the printed digits.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-87-imp4-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 600 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py -v -s --tb=short'" 3. Dry run, after the script exists (EX-84's first dry run ran too early): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-87-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:5 -n 2 -t 420 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 4. Flagged run, predicted [150, 300] s. Copy the emitted string; if it differs from this line, use the emitted one and note it: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-87 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/implants/05_lead_shaft_polarisation_in_gel.py"' 5. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-87-control. The readings must be unchanged up to round-off. 6. Post-censuses EX-87-post-figures / EX-87-post-docrefs. - Write the prediction first: N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0, docrefs exit != 1. - Take N fresh from step 1. It was 79 at 20261003T184030Z_EX-84-post-figures.log, but other example items may land first. 7. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new paths. tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py is the only other modified code path.

Traps already paid for: - A PEC tag constrains to the trace callable, not to zero. pec_facet_tags selects the facets that dirichlet_e_field is applied to (core/time_harmonic.py:346–389). TE with tags (1, 2, 3) and the unmodified _dirichlet("te") is therefore exact again and not a control. C2 needs the end-zeroing trace=. TM's exact trace is already zero on the ends, which is why the gate's TM PEC ends are exact. - End conditions are polarisation-specific (IMP-4.md:132–140). Never swap them for the anchor drives. - Masks and fields. Use the "zero" interior for traces (inside _dirichlet) and "continue" for every closed-form map and Φ (the chord sliver, IMP-1 item 146). Never sample ρ = 0: the TE conversion divides by ρ. - ufl.inner conjugates its second argument. inner(e, e) is |E|²; the DG0 test function enters as conj(v). Take np.real only after the sums. - Complex build. No UFL comparison and no ufl.max_value. Real operands do not save a comparison that contains a sqrt (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). Every mask is numpy. - Quadrature. Pin metadata={"quadrature_degree": …} on every SpatialCoordinate-bearing or map form (POST-5). - Rank safety. - Owned cells only (size_local) in sums. - Midpoints over owned + ghost cells for the figure tags. - _rss_gib, _eval_complex and every allreduce stay outside any rank-0 branch (IMP-2 W0, 20261001T200855Z). Print on rank 0. - Name every Function: EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window. - seconds includes the mesh only on the first call. - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (01_pec_sphere_in_gel.py:58–60). Never import another example's module. - ./run_examples.sh runs host-side: emit, then pass the string to the harness. - Round-off readings ((X1), (X2), the cavity max) vary from run to run. Assert them at their band only. - PNG ≤ 600 KiB: ans:8's first was 631 KiB. - Rule (i): the test module is frozen after window 2, the script after window 4. - Status 124 is a finding, never a retry. Run pgrep -c python3 in the container before any orphan-stem cache sweep (the rubric's bare call, <ID> = EX-87). - A docker-socket denial means stop and report.

Scope. One mesh (25 568 cells), degree 2, a = 1 mm, c = 10 mm, L = 4 mm; an exact imposed trace; single-mode drives; IMP-1's host at 64 MHz; -n 2.

Not claimed: - a finite lead, a tip, or an insulated or coated lead (IMP-5); - the plane-wave multi-mode series, modes n ≥ 2, or Jin's (11.63) global boundary condition; - FEM at any other radius (the sweep is closed form only); - h-convergence, or the cause of the gate's z-invariance reading; - a coil, heating, 1 g SAR, ISO 10974 or ASTM F2182.

There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Status it can move: EX-87 ⬜ → ✅, and the census N → N + 1. IMP-4 is unchanged: ✅, with its opening still the weekly's to ratify.

Negative result: - A re-gate red, or its cells / β / Φ digits off W1 / W2: revert the keywords, write a known-issues entry (the fixture moved under a ✅ gate), and mark BLOCKED. - (i)–(iii) red with the re-gate green: an example/test divergence finding. Write a known-issues entry, park on attempt/EX-87-<ts>, and mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). Never loosen a band. - (X1) / (X2) red: an example bug. Fix it once in-slot and re-run the flagged window; otherwise park. - A control inside its band: the swapped condition is not reaching the probes. For C2 that means the zeroing wrapper is not applied. Print z_inv, β and Φ, stop and report. - Over 420 s: park with the last line printed; the review re-tiers. - A printed value outside its prediction (including C1's β and the sweep): report it. It has no status effect.

Executor prompt (verbatim, for the example-runner spawn):

Execute EX-87 (§9 item 209) exactly as briefed in docs/planning/chunks/EX-87.md#§9-item-209; you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. The re-gate runs with source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1; the example run is complex through the imp: group. Do not edit src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py or src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py (IMP-5 may be editing them; import only, rebase if needed, never path-checkout). Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record or prediction, the census before / after, and the disclosed rule (a) diff.

Outcome (2026-10-04 22:30 CDT slot, example-runner): ✅ complete. - Rule (a), disclosed: _solve_cylinder(drive, pec_tags, *, return_fields=False, trace=None) in tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py; dirichlet_e_field=_dirichlet(drive) if trace is None else trace; fields added to the dict only under return_fields. Re-gate 20261004T033046Z_EX-87-imp4-regate.log: 15 passed, 233 s (predicted [190, 330]); cells 25 568 and the β / Φ / cavity lines equal W1 :133–142 / W2 :133–143. - Windows: pre-censuses 20261004T033032Z_EX-87-pre-figures.log / 20261004T033034Z_EX-87-pre-docrefs.log; dry run 20261004T033619Z_EX-87-dryrun.log; first flagged 20261004T033622Z_EX-87.log Status 1 — the XDMF writer rejected fields.e_real (DG at degree 2); fixed once by interpolating to CG1 (the imp:2 pattern); flagged run of record 20261004T033913Z_EX-87.log Status 0, 146 s (predicted [150, 300]); control 20261004T034145Z_EX-87-control.log Status 0, 134 s, same readings; post-censuses 20261004T034436Z_EX-87-post-figures.log / 20261004T034440Z_EX-87-post-docrefs.log. - Anchors (digit-identical to W1): TM β 0.999655 − 0.000093j (|β − 1| 0.0357 %), Φ_h 3.742390e-03 vs Φ_cf,h 3.704934e-03 (+1.011 %), cavity 10 704 dofs max 3.726e-20, |β·I| 2.91733e-3 A per V/m; TE β 0.992258 − 0.000001j (0.774 %), Φ_h 1.440373 vs 1.443759 (−0.234 %), cavity max 2.095e-34. (X1) ≤ 9.1e-15, (X2) 2.2e-16, (X3) 25 568 cells on all four solves. - Controls: C1 (TM, natural ends) Φ miss −99.84 %, β 1.1023 + 0.0287j (|β − 1| 0.106, predicted ≈ 0.11); C2 (TE, zeroed PEC ends) |β − 1| 0.9994, Φ miss −99.9998 %. Both inside their predicted ranges. - Printed vs predicted: Φ_TE/Φ_TM 384.9 / 389.7 / 396.8 (396.9 predicted for the continuous ratio); TE surface 4.0009; TE finite-k vs static +1.897e-4; all eight pointwise points and the radius sweep within tolerance. One miss, no status effect: C1 z-invariance 1.597 against predicted [0.1, 1.0] (C2 0.295, in range). - Census: setup figures 81 → 82, broken=0 (predicted +1); docrefs exit 2, dead 0, guide 0, stale 36 unchanged. docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened by the 2026-10-04 03:00 daily review (daily-review.md step 5, the §5.4 example ramp) for IMP-5 ✅ at d2bc2ca9 (§9 item 211), which the same review audited PASS. The gated capability is the insulated lead shaft: a lossless εᵣ 3 sleeve a < ρ < b around IMP-4's 1 mm PEC cylinder in IMP-1's lossy gel host at 64 MHz, meshed as a conforming cell tag 4 on the TH-15 hole route (cylindrical_domain(as_hole=True, coat_radius=b)), assigned through material_map, and checked at degree 2 against step 0's exact coated Bessel/Hankel series for both drives (TM_z n = 0, TE_z n = 1), on β and on the sleeve and host-annulus ⟨|E|²⟩. It is the project's first conforming dielectric interface under a closed form at finite k. No example puts a dielectric layer on a conductor.

Done-when. examples/implants/06_insulated_lead_shaft_in_gel.py + same-stem guide (three required headings, ## Setup figure, ## Related, PNG ≤ 600 KiB), run through ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:6; imports IMP-5's fixture, helpers and bands, restates none; rule (a) return_fields / trace on _solve_coated, module re-gated in-slot; IMP-5's gates re-asserted per drive; asserted controls miss; combined XDMF opens; census +1, broken=0.

docs.title: §9 item 223 — 2026-10-04 (§5.4 example)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-04 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-88 (imp:6): an insulated lead shaft in the gel. The sleeve takes the field that crosses the wire and moves its hot spot 90°; the field that runs along the wire does not notice it. One mesh (25 878 cells: host 16 255, sleeve 9 623) and one 1 mm PEC shaft with a 0.5 mm εᵣ 3 lossless sleeve, in IMP-1's host (σ 0.57 S/m, εᵣ 78, 64 MHz): - E across the shaft (TE_z). Normal D is continuous at ρ = b, so the normal E jumps by |ε_c,host/ε_c,coat| ≈ 59 (59.36 at finite k, 20261004T003556Z_IMP-5-step0-W1b.log:115). The field crowds into the insulation: |E| at the conductor surface inside the sleeve is ≈ 7.06·E₀ (…W1b.log:122, |E_ρ| max 7.056), against 2.00·E₀ on a bare wire, and the sleeve mean ⟨|E|²⟩/E₀² is 17.99 against the bare wire's 1.445 over the same annulus. The gel just outside sees its normal field suppressed (|E_ρ(b⁺)| ≈ 0.086·E₀) and its tangential field nearly doubled (|E_φ(b)| ≈ 1.96·E₀): the near-lead hot spot moves from the two facing points (bare wire) to the two flanks, and the host-annulus SAR b < ρ < 1.5b rises ≈ 30 % (1.411 against 1.088, …W1b.log:116). The induced dipole reverses (t/t₀ ≈ −2.16, :114). - E along the shaft (TM_z). A non-magnetic sleeve is invisible at leading order. The scattering coefficient moves by |s/s₀ − 1| = 3.1e-6 and the wire current by 4.3e-5 (:113). The FEM's own TM |β − 1| is 3.1e-4 (20261004T035027Z_IMP-5-step1-W1a.log:146), 7× the current shift and 100× the s shift, so the FEM cannot see the coating in TM, and the TM gate is not a coating test. The guide says so plainly, and also says this is a k_z = 0 statement: on a real insulated lead, k_z ≠ 0 propagation is where insulation sets lead heating, and that is not this fixture. - The same-mesh angle. A bare wire solved on the same mesh (sleeve cells set to gel, IMP-4's exact bare trace) gives the per-cell SAR gain of insulation directly in ParaView.

  • Executor: example-runner.
  • Tier: heavy. Every window runs at -n 2 in the complex build.
  • Cost: ≈ 16 measured (example class median) / ≈ 60 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 25 code and guide + ≈ 20 windows). Price basis, all from IMP-5 step 1 at -n 2:
  • one solve per window: TM gate 56.0 s (solve 53.1 s), TE gate 60.5 s (57.1 s), TE coating omitted 53.7 s, TM natural cavity 51.8 s, ≈ 4.2 GiB summed RSS each (20261004T035027Z_IMP-5-step1-W1a.log:145, …035247Z_…-W1b.log:145, …035543Z_…-W2a.log:145, …035832Z_…-W2b.log:145);
  • windows W1a / W1b / W2a / W2b took 133 / 168 / 162 / 152 s, so the environment tests cost ≈ 75 s per window; W0 (real, census + re-gates) took 104 s;
  • EX-87's four-solve example window took 146 s for solves of ≈ 30 s, i.e. ≈ 30 s of example overhead (20261004T033913Z_EX-87.log).
  • The example makes four solves (≈ 225 s) plus mesh, maps, XDMF, figure and startup ≈ 30–90 s. Predicted [250, 400] s per example window; -t 600.
  • The re-gate is the whole module in one complex window: environment + census + four solves ≈ 75 + 25 + 225 s. Predicted [290, 420] s; container timeout -k 30 600.
  • The slot is close to its hour. If it reaches minute 50 before the control run, park what exists (see Negative result).
  • Depends on: nothing. IMP-5 is ✅ (§9 item 211), audited PASS.
  • Shared files. This item edits only tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_fem.py (rule (a), below) and adds the three example paths. It does not edit src/ (io/mesh.py, utils/analytical.py) or tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py; it imports from them. If another item has edited the IMP-5 module first, rebase, keep both sets of keywords, and re-gate the module as it stands at HEAD. Never land anything by path checkout.
  • Gap. No existing example covers this:
  • grep -rnlE 'coated_pec_cylinder|coat_radius|test_imp5' examples --include=*.py returns nothing.
  • imp:5 is the bare shaft (the reference this one is read against); imp:1 – imp:4 are the sphere, the spheroid tip, a rod under a coil and the adjoint TF, all uncoated.
  • th:3 (a dielectric sphere in a uniform field) is the only example with an εᵣ interface in the field. No example puts a dielectric layer on a conductor, shows a normal-E jump of ≈ 59× across a conforming interface at finite k, or compares a coated and a bare conductor on one mesh.
  • material_map examples (mat:1, mat:3, mri:2, ports:*, ans:3) assign materials to phantoms or ports, never to a sleeve on a PEC.

Code: rule (a), disclosed. EX-87's return_fields / trace on IMP-4's _solve_cylinder is the precedent. - In tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_fem.py, change _solve_coated(drive, pec_tags, coated=True) (:207) to _solve_coated(drive, pec_tags, coated=True, *, return_fields=False, trace=None). - trace=None keeps dirichlet_e_field=_dirichlet(drive). Otherwise the passed callable is used. - return_fields=True adds fields to the returned dict and changes nothing else. - The five test bodies are untouched and every print stays byte-identical. - No src/ edit, and no other edit. - The module is re-gated green before any example window.

Imports (never restated): - From tests.validation.test_imp5_coated_cylinder_fem: - functions: _solve_coated, _mesh (one _MESH_CACHE["coat"] entry serves the four solves, the figure and the XDMF; never call _mesh(False)), _cf, _dirichlet, _masks, _continuous_mean, _probe_points; - constants: A, B, C, LENGTH, END_TAG, COAT_TAG, HOST_TAG, EPS_R_COAT, K, K_COAT, OMEGA, HOST_MASK_FACTOR, MASK_RANGE, PROBE_FACTORS; - re-exported there: from IMP-1 TH15_BETA_BAND (4.886 %), MAT4_BAND (10 %), E0, DEGREE, OUTER_BOUNDARY_TAG, CAVITY_TAG, SIGMA_HIGH; from IMP-2 QDEG, _owned_masked_cells, _numpy_quadrature_mean, _rss_gib; from IMP-4 PEC_TAGS, _eval_complex, _incident, _circle. - From tests.validation.test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem: _cf as _cf_bare and _dirichlet as _dirichlet_bare (the bare-wire closed form and its exact trace, for B0 only). - From src (utils/analytical.py, cited by name): coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_current, pec_cylinder_tm0_current. - Nothing else carries a number.

Anchor (asserted, imported bands). Run _solve_coated(d, PEC_TAGS[d], return_fields=True) for d ∈ {"tm", "te"} (TM pec tags (1, 2, 3), TE (1, 2)). These are the asserts of _assert_gates (:291–297): - (i) |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND. β is the complex LSQ amplitude of the coated closed-form scattered field (coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_field / coated_pec_cylinder_te1_field with region="host", minus _incident) on 24-point circles at ρ = 1.2b, 1.5b and 2b. - (ii) |Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1| ≤ MAT4_BAND on the sleeve mask (cell tag 4). - (iii) the same on the host-annulus mask (cell tag 2, midpoint ρ < 1.5b). - (iv) n_cavity > 0 and cavity_max < 1e-12.

Print each value beside its record: - TM (20261004T035027Z_IMP-5-step1-W1a.log:145–150): cells 25 878 (per tag {2: 16 255, 4: 9 623}), degree-2 dofs 176 216, h_wall/a 0.383, sleeve max edge/(b − a) 0.858; β 0.999703 − 0.000089j (0.0310 %); sleeve Φ_h 3.634296e-03 vs Φ_cf,h 3.596754e-03 (+1.0438 %); host Φ_h 2.315906e-02 vs 2.307528e-02 (+0.3631 %); cavity 10 704 dofs, max 0.000e+00; z-invariance 4.868e-03; β·I 6.92592e-4 − 2.83402e-3j A per V/m. - TE (20261004T035247Z_IMP-5-step1-W1b.log:145–149): β 0.994548 − 0.000062j (0.5452 %); sleeve Φ_h 1.799486e+01 vs 1.802471e+01 (−0.1656 %); host 1.410011 vs 1.412624 (−0.1850 %); cavity max 7.272e-34; z-invariance 2.364e-02.

Any difference at the printed digits is reported. The gate module exports no record constants, so this is a printed comparison, as in EX-87.

Example-side checks (asserted; true by construction, the EX-77 / EX-87 precedent): - (X1) The FEM |E|² map. The per-cell vector of ufl.inner(e, e) * ufl.conj(v) * dx (v a DG0 test function; dx with metadata={"quadrature_degree": QDEG}), divided by the per-cell ufl.conj(v) * dx volume and E0², is the DG0 e2_ratio_<drive> = |E_h|²/E₀². Its volume-weighted mean over each mask's owned cells (_owned_masked_cells(msh, chi) for each chi of _masks(msh, cell_tags)), allreduced, equals the returned phi[mask]["h"] within 1e-12 relative, for both gate drives and both masks. - (X2) The closed-form map. An example-local per-cell version of _numpy_quadrature_mean's basix degree-QDEG rule (EX-87's cf_cell_map, written afresh here, not imported), applied to _cf(drive, region="coat") on cell-tag-4 cells and _cf(drive, region="host") on cell-tag-2 cells. The region is forced by cell tag, never by radius (traps). Its masked means equal the returned phi[mask]["cf"] within 1e-12 relative, for both drives and both masks. - (X3) All four solves report the same ncells (25 878), which confirms the one cached mesh.

Printed (no band; predicted beside measured). Predictions are quasi-static (step 0's (Q) form, IMP-5.md item 210) unless cited; the script evaluates the exact closed form beside the FEM. - The interface jump, TE, φ = π/2 (the point facing E_inc = E₀ŷ, where E = E_ρ ŷ): - closed form at exactly ρ = b, region="coat" against "host": |E_y(b⁻)|/|E_y(b⁺)| predicted 59.36 (…step0-W1b.log:115); - FEM against closed form at ρ = 0.97b (sleeve) and 1.03b (host): the ratio |E_y(0.97b)|/|E_y(1.03b)|, closed form predicted 43.5 [42, 45]; FEM/closed-form ratio − 1 predicted within ±15 % (the host value is a small difference, ≈ 0.12·E₀); - the bare wire (B0) at the same two points: ratio predicted 1.038 (no jump). - Pointwise |E|²/E₀² at z = 0, FEM beside closed form, coated TE and bare B0, at ρ ∈ {1.1a, 0.97b, 1.03b, 2b} and φ ∈ {π/2 (facing), 0 (flank)}: - coated: 1.1a 41.56 / 0.375; 0.97b 27.01 / 3.468; 1.03b 0.0143 / 3.632; 2b 0.578 / 1.538; - bare: 1.1a 3.336 / 0.0301; 0.97b 2.168 / 0.278; 1.03b 2.013 / 0.338; 2b 1.235 / 0.790; - closed form within ±1 % of these (±5 % at the coated 1.03b facing point, a cancellation); FEM/closed-form − 1 within ±5 %, or ±15 % at the three small values (coated 1.03b facing, coated 1.1a flank, bare 1.1a flank). - The guide reads two things off the table. Inside the sleeve the field is the bare wire's static pattern scaled by |C|/E₀ ≈ 3.53, i.e. |E|² × 12.46 (1.1a: 41.56 against 3.336). Just outside it the pattern is rotated: the gel is cold where the bare wire is hot (facing 0.014 against 2.013) and hot where the bare wire is cold (flank 3.63 against 0.338). - Coated against bare on one mesh (TE): - host-annulus FEM Φ ratio Φ_h,coated/Φ_h,bare predicted 1.297 [1.26, 1.34] (…step0-W1b.log:116); - sleeve-region ratio predicted 12.45 [12.0, 12.9] (17.99/1.445). The guide states this is |E|² in a σ = 0 dielectric, i.e. dielectric stress, not SAR. - B0 against its own closed form (_cf_bare("te", "continue"), example-local, printed): β_bare, the complex LSQ amplitude of the bare scattered field (_cf_bare minus _incident("te")) on _probe_points(), predicted |β_bare − 1| ≲ 2 % (IMP-4 TE measured 0.774 %); sleeve-region and host-annulus Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1 within ±2 % (IMP-4 −0.23 %); Φ_cont from _continuous_mean(_cf_bare("te", "continue"), *MASK_RANGE[m]), predicted 1.4447 (sleeve region, = IMP-4's annulus) and 1.0878 (host). - TM, said honestly: - closed form |coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_current / pec_cylinder_tm0_current − 1| predicted 4.27e-5 (…step0-W1b.log:113), and the s shift 3.084e-6 cited from the same line (not recomputed: the coefficient helper is private); - the FEM gate's |β − 1| (W1a 0.0310 %) printed beside them with the ratios ≈ 7× and ≈ 100×; - the TM sleeve Φ_cont from _continuous_mean, predicted 3.640e-3: the value IMP-4 measured on the bare wire's identical annulus.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - C1. TE, coating omitted — IMP-5's own control, re-run: _solve_coated("te", PEC_TAGS["te"], coated=False, return_fields=True) (host material in tag 4, the coated trace on the wall). - Asserted (as test_control_te_coating_omitted, :427–429): |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND and both |Φ misses| > MAT4_BAND. - Printed beside the record (measured on this fixture, 20261004T035543Z_IMP-5-step1-W2a.log:146–148): β −0.473107 − 0.035938j (|β − 1| 1.4735, 30× the band); sleeve −91.4590 %; host −18.0148 % (1.8× the band). - B0. TE, the bare wire on the same mesh — _solve_coated("te", PEC_TAGS["te"], coated=False, trace=_dirichlet_bare("te"), return_fields=True). This is a physical bare wire, not a broken solve: it is the reference the coating is read against, and it must fail the coated gate. - Unmeasured on this fixture, so each factor is predicted, printed beside the measurement, and asserted only as missing the band. - Asserted: against the coated closed form (the returned β and Φ), |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND, and the sleeve and host Φ misses each > MAT4_BAND. - Predicted: β = t₀/t ≈ −0.4606 − 0.0354j (from step 0's t/t₀ = −2.1584 + 0.16582j, :114), |β − 1| in [1.3, 1.65], ceiling ≈ 30× the band; sleeve miss in [−95, −88] % (≈ −92 %, 1.44 against 18.02); host miss in [−27, −19] % (≈ −23 %, 1.09 against 1.41; 2.3× the band). Each Φ miss is capped at −100 %, 10× the band, so no larger factor is claimed. - Not run: IMP-5's TM natural-cavity control (c2). TM is not the story of this example, and C1 already shows a material map that does not reach the sleeve. Its record (…W2b.log:146–148) is cited in the guide's Related section.

Output. - Setup figure examples/implants/figures/implants_06_insulated_lead_shaft_in_gel_setup.png, through write_setup_figure: - on _mesh()'s mesh with a figure-only meshtags that is never passed to a solve: tag 4 for the cells in cell_tags.find(COAT_TAG), tag 3 for the cells in cell_tags.find(HOST_TAG) whose numpy midpoint has x² + y² < (HOST_MASK_FACTOR·B)², tag 2 for the remaining cells; - region_names={2: "gel host sigma 0.57 S/m (1 mm PEC lead cut out as a hole)", 3: "host annulus b < rho < 1.5b (Phi readout)", 4: "insulation sleeve eps_r 3, sigma 0, a < rho < b = 1.5 mm"}; - translucent_tags=(2,), clip_normal=(0, -1, 0), slice_normal=(0, 0, 1) through z = 0; - window_size=(1400, 630), title ≤ 130 characters; - if the PNG is over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Combined XDMF examples/implants/paraview_output/implants_06_insulated_lead_shaft_in_gel_combined.xdmf: - written by write_xdmf_with_tags(…, facet_tags=facet_tags) + adopt_host_ownership, on the gate mesh with its real cell tags (2 host, 4 sleeve) and facet tags (1 outer wall, 2 cavity, 3 end annuli); - every Function named; - DG0: e2_ratio_tm, e2_ratio_te, e2_ratio_te_closed_form (region by tag), e2_ratio_te_bare (B0), e2_ratio_te_bare_closed_form, e2_ratio_te_coating_omitted (C1), sar_ratio_te (= e2_ratio_te on host cells, 0 in the σ = 0 sleeve), sar_ratio_te_bare (= e2_ratio_te_bare: every cell is gel in B0), host_annulus_mask; - CG1 vector: E_real_tm, E_real_te, E_real_te_bare, each interpolated to ("Lagrange", 1, (3,)) before writing (EX-87 lines 244–250; the traps). Build each solve's outputs, then release fields before the next solve. - Guide. The three required headings, ## Setup figure and ## Related (imp:5 first, then imp:1 – imp:4, th:3; IMP-5's gate files by full filename, rule (b)). It explains: - why normal D continuity makes the normal E jump by the ε ratio while tangential E is continuous, and why Nédélec elements carry that without an interface condition (Jin §1.5.1 eqs (1.46)–(1.49)); - the rotated hot spot and the +30 % host-annulus SAR, read off the pointwise table; - why TM cannot see a non-magnetic sleeve at k_z = 0 (μ equal; ε enters only through k²ρ² terms), and that the FEM's TM error is larger than the effect; and that k_z ≠ 0 propagation along a real insulated lead, which is what insulation controls, is out of scope; - why B0 needs the bare trace (C1 keeps the coated trace and is not a bare wire); - a ParaView recipe: Slice z = 0; colour by e2_ratio_te on a log scale to see the jump at ρ = b; then sar_ratio_te and sar_ratio_te_bare on one linear scale; a Calculator sar_ratio_te/sar_ratio_te_bare on the host for the per-cell SAR gain; Plot Over Line along the y axis (facing) and the x axis (flank) on the DG0 maps. E_real_* are CG1 and smear the jump: read it from the DG0 maps or the printed probes. - The XDMF / H5 are gitignored; only the new PNG is tracked.

Complex build. The script checks default_scalar_type and raises in a real build (the imp:4 guard, as in 05_lead_shaft_polarisation_in_gel.py:126–131). The imp: group sources source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode automatically, and registers imp:6 from the 06_ filename prefix (run_examples.sh:133). The pytest re-gate window carries both source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, so the complex_only tests cannot skip silently.

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000, and makes one bare harness call. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-88-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-88-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" 2. Make the rule (a) edit, then re-gate the whole module (complex; predicted [290, 420] s). The expectation: - 17 passed: 12 environment + census + two drives + two controls; - the census lines equal 20261004T034835Z_IMP-5-step1-W0.log (25 878 cells, (R) 25 568, tag areas and volumes) and the β / Φ / cavity lines equal …W1a.log:145–150, …W1b.log:145–149, …W2a.log:145–150 and …W2b.log:145–150 at the printed digits.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-88-imp5-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 600 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_fem.py -v -s --tb=short'" 3. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-88-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:6 -n 2 -t 600 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 4. Flagged run, predicted [250, 400] s. The dry run emits the line without -T; EX-87's run of record used it with -T (20261004T033913Z_EX-87.log:12). Use this line and note any other difference: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-88 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 600 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/implants/06_insulated_lead_shaft_in_gel.py"' 5. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-88-control. The readings must be unchanged up to round-off. 6. Post-censuses EX-88-post-figures / EX-88-post-docrefs. - Write the prediction first: N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0, docrefs exit != 1. - Take N fresh from step 1. It was 82 at 20261004T034436Z_EX-87-post-figures.log:118, but other example items may land first. 7. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new paths. tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_fem.py is the only other modified code path.

Traps already paid for: - The XDMF writer rejects the degree-2 field. EX-87's first flagged window went red (20261004T033622Z_EX-87.log, Status 1) on writing fields.e_real directly. Interpolate to CG1 first. Here CG1 also smears the 59× normal jump into a continuous field, so never read the jump from E_real_*. - Region by cell tag, never by radius, at either circle (IMP-5.md item 211 traps). The TE normal E jumps 59× at ρ = b, and the chord slivers put host-cell quadrature points at ρ < b and sleeve-cell points at ρ < a. Region-by-radius hands a host point the sleeve formula. Every closed-form map and mean uses region="coat" on tag 4 and "host" on tag 2; the trace keeps _dirichlet's region=None, interior="zero". - Probe points clear of the faceted circles. The chord sag at ρ = b is ≈ 1 % of b at the sleeve's max edge (0.858·(b − a)), so 0.97b and 1.03b are each on the intended side; 1.1a is in the sleeve. Never sample ρ = 0: the TE conversion divides by ρ. - A PEC tag constrains to the trace callable, not to zero (EX-87 traps, core/time_harmonic.py:346–389). coated=False without trace= is C1 (the coated trace on an uncoated interior), not a bare wire. B0 needs trace=_dirichlet_bare("te"). - The returned β and Φ are always against the coated closed form. B0's comparison with its own closed form is example-local and printed only. - SAR is not |E|² in the sleeve. σ = 0 there, so SAR is zero; sar_ratio_te is masked to host cells. Never call the 17.99 a heating figure. - TM β against EX-87's. The two gate meshes differ (25 878 against 25 568 cells), so any TM β difference between them is mesh, not coating. Do not print it as a coating effect. - End conditions are polarisation-specific (IMP-4): TM PEC ends, TE natural. Never swap them for the anchor drives. - ufl.inner conjugates its second argument. inner(e, e) is |E|²; the DG0 test function enters as conj(v). Take np.real only after the sums. - Complex build. No UFL comparison and no ufl.max_value. Real operands do not save a comparison that contains a sqrt (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). Every mask is numpy, from cell tags. - Quadrature. Pin metadata={"quadrature_degree": …} on every SpatialCoordinate-bearing or map form (POST-5). - Rank safety. - Owned cells only (size_local) in sums. - Figure tags over owned + ghost cells. - _rss_gib, _eval_complex and every allreduce stay outside any rank-0 branch (IMP-2 W0, 20261001T200855Z). Print on rank 0. - Name every Function: EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window. - seconds includes the mesh only on the first call. - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (05_lead_shaft_polarisation_in_gel.py:60–62). Never import another example's module. - ./run_examples.sh runs host-side: emit, then pass the string to the harness. - Round-off readings ((X1), (X2), the cavity max) vary from run to run. Assert them at their band only. - PNG ≤ 600 KiB: ans:8's first was 631 KiB. - Rule (i): the test module is frozen after window 2, the script after window 4. - Status 124 is a finding, never a retry. Run pgrep -c python3 in the container before any orphan-stem cache sweep (the rubric's bare call, <ID> = EX-88). - A docker-socket denial means stop and report.

Scope. One mesh (25 878 cells), degree 2, a = 1 mm, b = 1.5 mm, c = 10 mm, L = 4 mm; one lossless εᵣ 3 sleeve; an exact imposed trace; single-mode drives at k_z = 0; IMP-1's host at 64 MHz; -n 2.

Not claimed: - k_z ≠ 0 guided waves along an insulated lead (the regime where insulation sets lead heating); - a lossy, thin or real-thickness insulation, or a measured insulation material; - a finite lead, a tip, a coil, heating, 1 g SAR, ISO 10974 or ASTM F2182; - the plane-wave multi-mode series or modes n ≥ 2; - h-convergence, or a gate on B0 (its comparison with the bare closed form is printed only); - the cause of the gate's z-invariance reading.

There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Status it can move: EX-88 ⬜ → ✅, and the census N → N + 1. IMP-5 is unchanged (✅).

Negative result: - A re-gate red, or its census / β / Φ digits off W0 – W2b: revert the keywords, write a known-issues entry (the fixture moved under a ✅ gate), and mark BLOCKED. - (i)–(iv) red with the re-gate green: an example/test divergence finding. Write a known-issues entry, park on attempt/EX-88-<ts>, and mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). Never loosen a band. - (X1) / (X2) red: an example bug (check the region-by-tag first). Fix it once in-slot and re-run the flagged window; otherwise park. - C1 inside its band: the material_map default is not reaching tag 4, against its W2a record. Stop and report. - B0 inside its band: the bare trace is not applied (trace= ignored). Print β, both Φ and z-invariance, stop and report. - Over 600 s, or the slot at minute 50 before window 5: park on attempt/EX-88-<ts> with the last line printed and journal it; the review re-tiers or re-slots. - A printed value outside its prediction (the jump ratio, the pointwise table, B0 against its closed form, the ratios): report it. It has no status effect.

Executor prompt (verbatim, for the example-runner spawn):

Execute EX-88 (§9 item 223) exactly as briefed in docs/planning/chunks/EX-88.md#§9-item-223; you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. The re-gate runs with source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1; the example run is complex through the imp: group. The only code edit outside examples/ is the rule (a) keyword pair on _solve_coated; do not edit src/ or tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py (import only, rebase if needed, never path-checkout). Interpolate E_real_* to CG1 before the XDMF write. Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record or prediction, the census before / after, and the disclosed rule (a) diff.

Flagged run 20261005T033928Z_EX-88.log Status 0, 154 s (predicted [250, 400]; the run came in under it); unflagged 20261005T034212Z_EX-88-control.log Status 0, 155 s, readings unchanged. Anchors equal records at printed digits; (X1) ≤ 4e-14, (X2) ≤ 4.4e-16; C1 equals the W2a record; B0 β = −0.4582 − 0.0352j, |β − 1| = 1.4586, sleeve −91.99 %, host −23.08 % (all inside predictions, asserted outside the bands). Jump 59.36 at ρ = b, 43.55 closed form / 40.91 FEM at 0.97b/1.03b; coated/bare host 1.298, sleeve 12.46; TM FEM |β − 1| 7.3× the current shift, 100× the s shift. Printed values outside prediction: FEM/closed-form − 1 at 0.97b flank, +6.12 % coated and +6.19 % bare (predicted ±5 %); no status effect. Census 20261005T033348Z_EX-88-pre-figures.log 83/82/1/0 → 20261005T034538Z_EX-88-post-figures.log 84/83/1/0; docrefs 83 → 84, dead=0 guide=0 stale=38 exit=2.

Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened by the 2026-10-04 18:00 daily review (daily-review.md step 5, the §5.4 example ramp) for WF-9 ✅ as a fixture (step 1, §9 item 224, a0d675c5, audit PASS). The gated capability is the implant transfer function in a coil-driven field: a σ = 800 S/m capped rod kept as cell tag 403 in the F-small untuned 4-leg birdcage's gel phantom at 64 MHz (GEO-36 step 3 keep_cells mesh, 182 371 cells), switched by material only. On all four port drives the adjoint fold equals the direct with-lead tip response to ≤ 3.7e-12, the N = 32 path fold is within ≤ 1.47e-3 (band 5 %), and the Born fold misses by 1 344–1 435 %. No example folds a lead's transfer function with a coil-driven field: imp:3 is a direct with/without-rod tip SAR on two meshes, imp:4 is the adjoint TF in IMP-1's host with current-block drives and no coil, and imp:5 / imp:6 are lead-shaft polarisation in gel.

docs.text:
Outcome (2026-10-05 09:00 CDT slot): ✅. W1 20261005T141440Z_EX-89-wf9-regate-W1.log 14 passed 184 s; W2 20261005T141755Z_EX-89-wf9-regate-W2.log 14 passed 167 s (TF agreement 4.4e-13); flagged run 20261005T142237Z_EX-89.log 142 s (3.07 GiB summed RSS), control 20261005T142536Z_EX-89-control.log 133 s, readings unchanged. Per-port q / (PF) / (BF) equal the step 1 records at the printed digits; (X1) 1.4e-15, (X2) ≤ 1.2e-14, (X3) 1.9e-13 (fold = Δq_ccw = −2.5035522599e-01−2.9872376444e-01j), ccw |Δq| 0.3898, |q_with/q_without| 2.3407, ccw path fold 3.54e-4, ccw Born miss 1 394.44 % (|B|/|Δq| 14.84), C4 24.53 %, cw/ccw 2.29e-3, in-lead ratio 0.0678, TF peak k = 27 (7.477e-02), arg [−6.45°, −1.85°]. Census 84 → 85 (ok 83 → 84, missing 1, broken=0), docrefs exit 2 (staleness only), guide pass 85. Every printed prediction IN. Rule (a) lift in tests/validation/test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py only.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-04 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-89 (imp:7): why a lead's tip response cannot be read off the lead-free field. One mesh (182 371 cells; 15 000 lead cells, 7 605 tip-ball cells) and one σ = 800 S/m capped rod (r = 1 mm, tip to tip 32 mm, centre (15, 0, 0) mm) in the coil-driven gel phantom at 64 MHz: - One adjoint solve gives the TF. A unit tip load (the mean E_z in a 3 mm ball at the top tip) solved with the lead present gives w, and TF(z) = −jωμ₀Δσ·w_z along the lead. Folded with each port drive's lead-free field it predicts the with-lead tip response exactly (T3), and as a 1-D path integral ∫TF(z)·E_z(z) dz within the 5 % band (PF). - The new angle: a drive the adjoint never saw. The clinical quadrature drive (all four ports at once, phases from the fixture's own azimuths) is solved fresh with the lead. Folding the same w with the superposed lead-free field predicts its tip response at DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. The TF is a property of the lead in this coil and phantom, not of the drive. - Why the lead-free field is not enough. The Born fold (the adjoint solved without the lead) overstates the response ≈ 14×, because the lead excludes the axial field from its own interior (quasi-static depolarisation ≈ 0.07 at aspect 16, WF-9.md item 224). The fold of w with the with-lead field (C2) captures only ≈ 6.5 %.

  • Executor: example-runner.
  • Tier: heavy, complex. The example and the W1 re-gate run at -n 2; the W2 re-gate runs at -n 4 (WF-9 step 1's widths).
  • Cost: ≈ 16 measured (example class median) / ≈ 55 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 25 code and guide + ≈ 14 windows). Price basis:
  • WF-9 step 1 W1 took 190 s at -n 2: mesh + guard 49.9 s (20261004T201655Z_WF-9-step1-W1.log:1888), the identities body 78.09 s (:1985; three factorisations ≈ 12 s each, 6.9 s of held solves, (A1) 4.5 s, the rest read-backs), so ≈ 60 s of environment tests, imports and census. W2 took 165 s at -n 4 (20261004T202017Z_WF-9-step1-W2.log:2312). Summed RSS 2.91 GiB at -n 2 (W1:1985).
  • EX-84's example window on the step 0 fixture took 87 s for a 73.7 s gate body (20261003T183658Z_EX-84.log:171), so ≈ 15 s of example overhead with the figure; its unflagged control took 79 s.
  • The example: mesh ≈ 50 s + lifted body ≈ 78 s + one fresh quadrature factorisation ≈ 13 s + DG0 maps, (X1)–(X3) ≈ 15 s + XDMF and figure ≈ 20 s + startup ≈ 10 s. Predicted [150, 320] s; -t 420.
  • The re-gates reproduce W1 / W2: predicted [150, 260] s at -n 2, [130, 240] s at -n 4; container timeout -k 30 420, as WF-9 step 1.
  • If the slot reaches minute 50 before the control window, park what exists (see Negative result).
  • Depends on: nothing. WF-9 is ✅ as a fixture (§9 item 224), audited PASS.
  • Shared files. This item edits only tests/validation/test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py (rule (a), below) and adds the three example paths. It does not edit src/, tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py, tests/validation/test_wf9_transfer_function_identity.py or any other gate module; it imports from them. If another item has edited the step 1 module first, rebase, keep both changes, and re-gate the module as it stands at HEAD. Never land anything by path checkout. imp:6 (EX-88, item 223) may or may not have landed; the 07_ prefix is independent of it.
  • Gap. No existing example covers this:
  • grep -rnlE 'test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom|_build_kept_rod|keep_cells' examples --include=*.py returns nothing.
  • grep -rnliE 'transfer.function|adjoint' examples --include=*.py outside */aed/ returns only 04_lead_transfer_function_adjoint.py, whose fixture is IMP-1's host block with current-block drives and no coil (EX-84.md item 204, "Not claimed: … a coil or F-small drive").
  • imp:3 computes the rod's tip SAR directly, with and without the rod on two meshes; it has no TF, no adjoint and no fold. Its ccw drive is a superposition, never a fresh phased solve.

Code: rule (a), disclosed (EX-84's _run_identities lift is the precedent, EX-84.md item 204). - In tests/validation/test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py, lift test_wf9_step1_identities's body (:355–525, less its first line fx = _case) verbatim into a module-level _run_step1_identities(fx), asserts and prints included. - After the last assert, add one statement: return {...} with keys q (the closure), v_ball, e_without (the dict e_o, P1–P4), e_with (e_w), w, w0, res, tf_k, v_k, y_with (y_w), y_without (y_o), recip, sym_ratio (= sym_norm / a_norm), ndofs, h_dev, times, rss, elapsed, tf_agreement. - test_wf9_step1_identities keeps @complex_only and becomes a single call _run_step1_identities(_case). test_wf9_step1_census, _build_case, _arm, _symmetry and every constant are untouched. Every print stays byte-identical except the timings. - No new keyword, no src/ edit, no other edit. The module is re-gated green at both widths before any example window.

Anchor (asserted on the returned case, imported bands). fx = _build_case() then case = _run_step1_identities(fx); the lifted asserts fire inside it, and the example re-asserts on the returned values and prints each beside its record in 20261004T201655Z_WF-9-step1-W1.log: - (A0) cells = KEPT_ROD_CELL_RECORD within CELL_COUNT_BAND (record 182 371, W1:1888); lead / ball counts 15 000 / 7 605 (:1889), as owned-count allreduces. - (A1) sym_ratio ≤ SYMMETRY_RTOL (record 9.757e-17, :1896). - (i′) recip["with"], recip["without"] ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND (1.505e-15 / 1.796e-15, :1897). - (H) h_dev ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (0.000e+00, :1898). - (T3), the row's identity, per port drive d: |−jωμ₀Δσ∫χ_lead w·E_without,d − (q_with,d − q_without,d)| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|Δq_d| (Jin §6.4 eqs (6.78)–(6.85)). Records 2.886e-13 / 3.689e-12 / 6.736e-13 / 1.005e-12 (:1902, :1915, :1928, :1941); q_without / q_with at the printed 10 digits (:1900, :1913, :1926, :1939) must match. - (PF) per d: |Q₃₂ − Δq_d| ≤ PATH_FOLD_BAND·|Δq_d| (1.441865e-04 / 1.473321e-03 / 1.509399e-04 / 1.022076e-03, :1903, :1916, :1929, :1942). - (BF) per d, asserted as a miss: |B_d − Δq_d| > PATH_FOLD_BAND·|Δq_d| (1 399.15 / 1 434.96 / 1 388.53 / 1 344.16 %, :1904, :1917, :1930, :1943).

Any digit difference from W1 in q, (PF) or (BF) is reported; round-off readings ((A1), (i′), (H), (T3)) vary and are asserted at their band only.

Example-side checks (asserted): - (X0) The phase pattern. Port azimuths from fx["sweep"]["sheets"] ("azimuth_deg", port id f"P{s['tag'] - SHEET_IFACE}"), ks = [_port_index(az[p], az["P1"], QUADRATURE_STEP_DEG) for p in PORT_IDS] (it asserts the 90° grid), a = quadrature_phase_weights(ks, "ccw"). Print azimuths, ks and a. Assert ks is a permutation of {0, 1, 2, 3}. - (X1) TF-density map. The per-cell complex vector of LOAD·Δσ·chi_lead·w[2]·conj(v)·dx (v a DG0 test function, Δσ = fx["delta_sigma"]), summed over the owned lead cells of slab k (fx["flags"]["slabs"][k][:n_owned]) and allreduced, equals case["tf_k"][k] for all 32 slabs, max relative miss ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. Keep the vector complex. - (X2) Fold-integrand maps. For d in P1–P4, the owned sum of the per-cell LOAD·Δσ·chi_lead·ufl.dot(w, E_without,d)·conj(v)·dx equals case["res"][d]["t3"] within DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|t3|. - (X3) The quadrature drive, fresh, with the lead. One new factorisation, mirroring _arm's first solve: TimeHarmonicSolver(fx["p_with"], degree=1).solve(current_density=None, project_source=False, extra_bilinear_terms=<every sheet of _sheets(specs), undriven>, extra_linear_terms=<for each spec: lumped_port_linear_term(msh, tags_f, dataclasses.replace(spec.sheet(driven=True), source_voltage_v=complex(a_d)), v, omega_rad_per_s=OMEGA)>), then _free. Define, by superposition of the returned fields, E_without,ccw = Σ a_d E_without,d (no solve; same operator), q_without,ccw = Σ a_d q_without,d, and the prediction fold_ccw = LOAD·Δσ∫χ_lead w·E_without,ccw. - Asserted: |fold_ccw − (q(E_with,ccw) − q_without,ccw)| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|Δq_ccw|. Predicted ≤ 1e-11. - Also asserted (true by linearity, a wiring check on the superposition): |fold_ccw − Σ a_d t3_d| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|fold_ccw|.

Printed (no band; predicted beside measured). The ccw predictions are arithmetic on W1's per-port q and Q₃₂ records with ks = (0, 1, 2, 3) for P1–P4; a different ks only permutes the weights. - ccw: |Δq_ccw| predicted ≈ 0.390 (V/m per V); |q_with/q_without| predicted 2.34 [2.0, 2.7] (per port 2.29–2.39, :1901, :1914, :1927, :1940); the path fold Q₃₂,ccw = Σ a_d Q₃₂,d against Δq_ccw, predicted 3.5e-4 [5e-5, 1e-2]; the Born fold B_ccw = Σ a_d B_d, predicted miss ≈ 1 400 % [100 %, 3000 %]. - The two senses at this lead: |Δq_cw/Δq_ccw − 1| with the cw weights (superposition only, no solve), predicted 2.3e-3 [1e-4, 1e-2]. The rod lies on leg 1's azimuth in the y = 0 mirror plane, so Δq_P2 ≈ Δq_P4 (:1913 against :1939) and the lead cannot tell the two rotation senses apart. The guide says so. - In-lead field: |∫χ_lead E_with,ccw,z| / |∫χ_lead E_without,ccw,z|, predicted [0.03, 0.2] (quasi-static 0.07; C2's complement ≈ 6.5 %). This is the reason Born fails. - The TF(z) table: k, z_mid, |TF_k|, |TF_k|/max, arg TF_k in degrees, beside W1:1952–1983. Predicted peak at k = 27 (z = 11.5 mm, 7.477e-02), arg within [−7°, −1.5°] on every slab. - Path fold against N: |Q_N − Δq|/|Δq| for N ∈ FOLD_NS per port and for ccw, beside the W1 N lines (non-monotone on P2 / P4 is the record, WF-9.md item 224).

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (BF), the Born fold — asserted per port drive inside the lift, and on ccw by the example: |B_ccw − Δq_ccw| > PATH_FOLD_BAND·|Δq_ccw|. No ceiling exists, so no factor is asserted; predicted [100 %, 3000 %]. - C1, the Hermitian read-back (conj(w)) and C2, the total-field fold (E_with) — asserted wired inside the lift (> DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL); records ≈ 199.5 % (ceiling 200 %, since |a − ā| ≤ 2|a|) and ≈ 93.5 % (:1905–1906 etc.). Printed beside the records. - C4, the unphased drive (new; wiring control on (X3)). The fold of w with Σ_d E_without,d (all weights 1) against the fresh ccw Δq. Asserted: misses by > DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|Δq_ccw|. Predicted: ≈ 24.5 % [10 %, 40 %] (Σ Δq_d against Δq_ccw from the W1 records). It shows that (X3) reads the phased solve, not any four-port sum. No factor is asserted.

Output. - Setup figure examples/implants/figures/implants_07_lead_tf_in_the_coil_setup.png, through write_setup_figure, called right after _build_case(): - on the fixture mesh with a figure-only meshtags that is never passed to a solve: the values from _cell_values_with_ghosts(msh, fx["built"][1]) over owned + ghost cells, with the tip-ball cells (fx["flags"]["ball"]) set to 404; - region_names={1: "conductor (birdcage)", 2: "air", 3: "gel phantom (sigma 0.5 S/m)", 403: "lead (kept rod cells, sigma 800 S/m)", 404: "tip ball r = 3 mm (q readout)", **port_names}, port_names built as imp:3 does (03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.py:227–228, from PORT_LOWER / PORT_UPPER); - hide_tags=(2,), translucent_tags=(3,), slice_normal=(0, 1, 0) through the origin (cuts the lead and the ball lengthwise); - window_size=(1400, 630), title ≤ 130 characters; - if the PNG is over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Combined XDMF examples/implants/paraview_output/implants_07_lead_tf_in_the_coil_combined.xdmf: - write_xdmf_with_tags(…, msh, fx["built"][1], fields, comm=comm, facet_tags=fx["built"][2]) + adopt_host_ownership (imp:3's call); - every field DG0 and named: tf_density_magnitude, tf_density_phase_deg (per unit volume, lead cells, 0 elsewhere); adjoint_w_magnitude, adjoint_w0_magnitude (|w| with and without the lead: the lead shields its interior); fold_integrand_magnitude_P1 … _P4, _ccw; born_integrand_magnitude_ccw; E_without_magnitude_ccw, E_with_magnitude_ccw; lead_slab_index (k + 1 on the lead, 0 elsewhere); tip_ball_mask. - Guide. The three required headings, ## Setup figure and ## Related (imp:4 first, then imp:3, imp:5, imp:6 if it exists; WF-9's gate files by full filename, rule (b)). It explains: - why A = Aᵀ (not Aᴴ) makes the adjoint fold exact, and why the adjoint must be solved with the lead (C1, Born); - that the TF is the lead's property in this coil and phantom, shown by the quadrature drive the adjoint never saw; - the depolarisation argument for the ≈ 14× Born overstatement, and the in-lead field ratio; - why cw and ccw agree at this lead (mirror plane), so the result is not a statement about B₁⁺ polarisation; - that the 5 % path-fold band is the weekly's (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10 WF-9 ruling); - a ParaView recipe: Threshold CellTags = 403, colour by tf_density_magnitude; Plot Over Line along x = 15 mm, y = 0; compare adjoint_w_magnitude with adjoint_w0_magnitude on the lead; Slice y = 0 on E_without_magnitude_ccw. - The XDMF / H5 are gitignored; only the new PNG is tracked.

Complex build. The script checks default_scalar_type and raises in a real build (the imp:3 guard, 03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.py:197). The imp: group sources source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode automatically and registers imp:7 from the 07_ prefix. The re-gate windows carry both source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, with tests/environment first.

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000, and makes one bare harness call. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-89-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-89-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" 2. Make the lift edit, then re-gate W1 (predicted [150, 260] s; 14 passed). The census lines and the per-drive q / (PF) / (BF) lines must equal 20261004T201655Z_WF-9-step1-W1.log:1888–1891, :1899–1950 at the printed digits: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-89-wf9-regate-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py::test_wf9_step1_census tests/validation/test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py::test_wf9_step1_identities -v -s --tb=short'" 3. Re-gate W2 (predicted [130, 240] s): the same line with label EX-89-wf9-regate-W2 and -n 4. The digits must equal 20261004T202017Z_WF-9-step1-W2.log, and the W1/W2 TF agreement must be ≤ 1e-10 (record 2.860e-12, W2:2032). 4. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-89-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e imp:7 -n 2 -t 420 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 5. Flagged run, predicted [150, 320] s. Use this line (EX-84's / EX-87's run of record used -T); if the emitted string differs otherwise, use the emitted one and note it: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-89 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/implants/07_lead_tf_in_the_coil.py"' 6. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-89-control. The readings must be unchanged up to round-off. 7. Post-censuses EX-89-post-figures / EX-89-post-docrefs (the step 1 commands with those labels). - Write the prediction first: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, missing unchanged, broken=0; docrefs exit != 1. - Take N fresh from step 1. It was 83 (ok=82 missing=1 broken=0) at 20261004T143016Z_ANS-9-post-figures.log:119, but EX-88 may land first. 8. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new paths. tests/validation/test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py is the only other modified code path.

Traps already paid for: - The lifted body writes /workspace/logs/wf9_step1_tf_n{size}.npy. The example's -n 2 run overwrites the re-gate's n2 file with the same computation (benign, the EX-84 precedent). Never delete either file between windows 2 and 5; the W2 agreement line reads it. - Unmapped kept cells silently become vacuum (WF-9 item 224 traps): never build a problem by hand. Use only fx["p_with"] / fx["p_without"]; (M0) inside the census is the guard. - Every sheet's bilinear term goes into the quadrature factor, undriven (_sheets(specs)); only the linear terms carry the phases. A missing termination solves a different problem silently (PORT-19, WF-12). C4 and (X3) catch a wrong phase, not a wrong termination, so copy _arm's bil construction exactly. - Phases go on source_voltage_v through dataclasses.replace, never by multiplying a returned form; the linear term reads sheet.source_voltage_v (ports/lumped.py:328). - project_source=False on the fresh solve, as _arm does. - ufl.inner conjugates its second argument. Read q, TF, folds and maps through components or ufl.dot; only inner(w, w) for |w|² and the DG0 test function's conj(v) conjugate. Keep (X1) / (X2) vectors complex; take magnitudes in numpy after the sums. Do not copy imp:3's np.real per-cell helper. - Masks are DG0 from numpy midpoints over owned + ghost cells, counts over owned cells only; no UFL conditional, no comparison on complex operands and no sqrt comparison (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). Use the fixture's fx["flags"], never rebuild them. - Tag lookups include ghost cells (_cell_values_with_ghosts); cell_tags.values is rank-local. - Rank safety: every _scalar, allreduce and _rss_gib stays outside any rank == 0 branch (WF-7 step 0e, item 227: a rank-0-only collective deadlocked a window). Print on rank 0. - Memory: the lift keeps eight drive fields plus w, w0; the quadrature solver is freed with _free before the maps. Summed RSS predicted ≤ 3.5 GiB at -n 2 (record 2.91). - Name every Function: EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window. - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (03_rod_in_birdcage_tip_sar.py:73–75). Never import another example's module. - ./run_examples.sh runs host-side: emit, then pass the string to the harness. - Round-off readings ((A1), (i′), (H), (T3), (X1)–(X3)) vary from run to run. Assert them at their band only. - PNG ≤ 600 KiB: ans:8's first was 631 KiB. - Rule (i): the test module is frozen after window 3, the script after window 5. - Status 124 is a finding, never a retry. Run pgrep -c python3 in the container before any orphan-stem cache sweep (the rubric's bare call, <ID> = EX-89). - A docker-socket denial means stop and report.

Scope. Degree 1, 64 MHz, the untuned solid-coil F-small 4-leg birdcage with 50 Ω sheets as WF-9 step 1 built them (the gate's narrowed sheets, a record per the 2026-10-02 ruling), one σ = 800 S/m capped rod on leg 1's azimuth, a linear tip functional (mean E_z in a 3 mm ball at the top tip), four port drives and one quadrature drive, -n 2.

Not claimed: - a measured or ISO 10974-calibrated TF; - heating, SAR or tip temperature (q is a mean axial field, not |E|²); - a PEC, insulated or real lead, F-human, or a tuned coil; - a B₁⁺ polarisation statement (cw ≈ ccw at this lead); - any S, Z or port-accuracy figure from the sheets; - the path-fold band (the weekly's), or h-convergence.

There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Status it can move: EX-89 ⬜ → ✅, and the census N → N + 1. WF-9 is unchanged (✅ as a fixture).

Negative result: - A re-gate red, or its census / q / (PF) / (BF) digits off W1 / W2: revert the lift, write a known-issues entry (the fixture moved under a ✅ gate), and mark BLOCKED. - An anchor red in the example with the re-gates green: an example/test divergence finding. Write a known-issues entry, park on attempt/EX-89-<ts>, and mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). Never loosen a band. - (X3) red with (T3) green on all four ports: the fresh phased solve is not the superposed operator. Print Δq_ccw, fold_ccw, Σ a_d t3_d and the (X0) weights, check the termination list first, then park and report. - (X0) red (ks not a 90° permutation): the sheet records moved. Stop and report. - C4 inside DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL: the phases did not reach the solve. Stop and report. - (X1) / (X2) red: an example bug (complex vectors, owned cells). Fix it once in-slot and re-run the flagged window; otherwise park. - Over 420 s, or the slot at minute 50 before window 6: park on attempt/EX-89-<ts> with the last line printed and journal it; the review re-tiers. - A printed value outside its prediction (ccw ratios, cw/ccw, in-lead ratio, TF peak): report it. It has no status effect.

Executor prompt (verbatim, for the example-runner spawn):

Execute EX-89 (§9 item 238) exactly as briefed in docs/planning/chunks/EX-89.md#§9-item-238; you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. The re-gates run with source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1; the example run is complex through the imp: group. The only code edit outside examples/ is the rule (a) lift of test_wf9_step1_identities's body into _run_step1_identities(fx) with an additive return; do not edit src/ or any other test module (import only, rebase if needed, never path-checkout). Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record or prediction, the census before / after, and the disclosed rule (a) diff.

docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain I, I19 ("imp:7 gains the coated-lead rows (I18b); example-runner. Serial on I18b."). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Make no edit to the script, guide or module after its last window."

Code (rule (a), additive, disclosed). 1. tests/validation/test_wf9_insulated_lead.py: lift test_wf9_step3_identities's body (:284–487, less its first line fx = _case) verbatim into a module-level _run_step3_identities(fx), asserts and prints included. Two additive changes only: - in the shaft/tip loop (:460–463), set shaft_tip = {} before the loop and shaft_tip[arm] = shaft / tips inside it; the print is unchanged; - after the last assert, one statement: return {...} with keys res (per arm, per drive: q_with, q_without, dq, t3, born, c1, c2, rod_only, coat_part, folds), tf_prof (arm → (tf_k, v_k)), r1, sym, recip, h_dev, ndofs, v_ball, shaft_tip, times, rss, elapsed, tf_agreement. Return no field (no w, e_o or arms), so the body's locals are freed on return. - test_wf9_step3_identities keeps @complex_only and becomes the single call _run_step3_identities(_case). _build_case, _case, test_wf9_step3_census, _contrast, _eps_c_cells, _minmax_on and every constant are untouched. Every print stays byte-identical except times and RSS. - No new keyword, no src/ edit, no edit to test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py or any other module. The module is re-gated green at both widths before the example is edited. 2. examples/implants/07_lead_tf_in_the_coil.py: append a coated-lead section after the XDMF write and before the final "All anchors and controls hold" line. - Free the step 1 objects first: either wrap the existing body in a function whose locals die on return, or del them and call gc.collect(). This is hygiene, not a gate.
