docs.title: §9 item 255 — 2026-10-05 (§5.4 example from MAT-19 ✅)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-90 (mat:13): what a temperature probe in a heated gel ball reports, and why its stated volume matters. One EM solve on MAT-4's lossy sphere (R = 10 mm, σ 0.57 S/m, 64 MHz, imposed field) heats the 19 496-cell sphere submesh. Robin h = 100 W/m²/K, CN + Rannacher, N = 40 to t* = 139.33 s. The run is MAT-12's, and the probe is MAT-19's: - What the probe reads. Three probes of stated radius a = 2 mm (centres 0, 3.5 mm on x, 6.5 mm off-axis) each give a ball-averaged series of 41 points. Each is set beside two comparands: the exact ball mean θ̄(d, a, t) of the Robin eigen-series, which the gate asserts within 1 %, and the point value θ(d, t), which a bare comparison would use. - The new angle: the probe volume. At c₀ the same run is read again with a = 1, 4 and 8 mm. The volume offset (ball − point) grows as a². In the steady limit it is exactly −q a²/(10k), because θ_ss is quadratic in r and the ball mean of |x|² is d² + 3a²/5. At a = 2 mm it sits below the 1 % band at c₀ (−0.73 % at t*), so the gate cannot see it there. At a = 8 mm it is −13.4 %, and a point comparand misses by ≈ 13× the band (C3). - Position beats volume at this a/R. A 1 mm placement error at 6.5 mm (C1, 5.42 % at t*) costs ≈ 4× the a = 2 mm volume offset there (−1.26 % exact, −1.35 % FEM).

  • Executor: example-runner.
  • Tier: heavy (by ceiling), complex. The example and the W1 re-gate run at -n 2. The W2 re-gate runs at -n 4, the gate's (W) width that reads W1's npz.
  • Cost: ≈ 15 measured (example class median) / ≈ 45 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 code and guide + ≈ 10 windows). Price basis:
  • MAT-19 step 1: W1 104 s at -n 2, 14 passed (20261005T095808Z_MAT-19-step1-W1.log:352). Its fixture total was 35.7 s, of which EM 15.3 s, two CN 1.4 s and probes 0.45 s (W1:212), so ≈ 65 s of the window is environment tests, imports and JIT. W2 took 99 s at -n 4 (…100001Z_…-W2.log:398; fixture 26.9 s, W2:258). The box was not slow (EM 14.5–16.3 s, attempts.md 2026-10-05T10:05Z).
  • mat:4 (EX-67) runs the same EM and two CN runs plus four more conduction solves and two XDMF files.
  • EX-89's example overhead (XDMF + setup figure + startup) was ≈ 30–45 s above its gate body (EX-89.md item 238 price).
  • The example: startup and imports ≈ 15 s + _build_run() ≈ 36 s + _check_probe_series ≈ 5 s (numpy comparands, 41 × 3 ball means of 400 terms) + sweep probes ≈ 1 s + P1 θ_exact at 41 steps ≈ 5 s + XDMF ≈ 5 s + setup figure ≈ 15 s + matplotlib ≈ 5 s. Predicted [60, 180] s; runner -t 300.
  • The re-gates reproduce W1 / W2. Predicted [90, 210] s each (a 2× slow box included); container timeout -k 30 300.
  • Depends on: nothing. MAT-19 is ✅ (0a0f85b1, item 243).
  • Shared files. This item edits only tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py (rule (a), below) and adds the example paths (script, guide, setup PNG). It does not edit src/ (thermal/probe.py is imported, untouched), tests/solver/test_thermal_probe.py, or the MAT-10 / MAT-12 / lossy-sphere modules. If another item has edited the MAT-19 module first, rebase, keep both changes, and re-gate the module as it stands at HEAD. Never land anything by path checkout. run_examples.sh selects by file-name prefix (scripts/run_examples.sh:201–219), so mat:13 needs no registry edit.

Code: rule (a), disclosed. Precedents: EX-81's _run_transient (a fixture body lifted) and EX-89's _run_step1_identities (a test body lifted with a return). - In tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py, lift the run fixture's body (:180–230) verbatim into a module-level _build_run(). The returned dict gains additive keys only: sub (the submesh), snap_cf (res_cf.snapshots), snap_h (res_h.snapshots) and probes (the list of four ProbeBalls). The fixture stays @pytest.fixture(scope="module") and becomes return _build_run(). - Lift test_mat19_probe_series's body (:235–322) verbatim, asserts and prints included, into a module-level _check_probe_series(run). After the last assert, add one statement: return {...} with keys ref, pts, P, relT, worstT, relH, missC1, ownrel, c2, c2n20, w_cf, w_h. w_cf / w_h are None at -n 2. Do not return cells_eq: it is unbound at -n 2. test_mat19_probe_series keeps @complex_only and becomes the single call _check_probe_series(run). - test_mat19_n1_ball_mean_against_quadrature, _q_cf, _point, _j1fac, _ball_mean, _ball_quad, _theta_ss0 and every constant are untouched. Every print stays byte-identical except the elapsed line. - No new keyword, no src/ edit, no other edit. The module is re-gated green at both widths before any example window.

Imports (never restated): - From tests.validation.test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe: _build_run, _check_probe_series, _ball_mean, _point, _q_cf, A_PROBE, CENTRES, DISPLACED, N_SUB, DT, and the re-exports P_BAND, B_BAND, R, N_MAIN, T_STAR. An is check against tests.validation.test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.P_BAND / .B_BAND / .R and tests.validation.test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.N_MAIN / .T_STAR is printed and asserted (the EX-79 pattern). - B_BAND is not imported by the gate module today, so import it from test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere directly; never add it to the gate's imports. - From src: fem_em_solver.thermal.ProbeBall, probe_series; fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils.write_xdmf_time_series, adopt_host_ownership; fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure.write_setup_figure; dolfinx.mesh.meshtags. - Example parameters (new, not records): A_SWEEP = (1.0e-3, 4.0e-3, 8.0e-3) at c₀. Nothing else carries a number.

Anchor (asserted through the lift, imported bands). run = _build_run() then chk = _check_probe_series(run). The lifted asserts fire inside it: (M), (A0), snapshot 0 = 0.0, (T) ≤ P_BAND, and (C1) > P_BAND. The example then re-asserts on the returned values and prints each beside its record in 20261005T095808Z_MAT-19-step1-W1.log: - (A0) run["n_sub"] == N_SUB, record 19 496 (W1:161). The probe V_h/V − 1 values are printed beside +6.289e-04, +4.055e-04, +5.064e-04, +1.569e-04 (W1:161). - (T), the row's gate: chk["worstT"] <= P_BAND, record 1.7315e-03 (W1:203). The per-probe readings at t* must equal W1:202 at the printed 7 digits: 5.918962e-02 / 5.681504e-02 / 5.020215e-02. - (C1), the row's control: max(chk["missC1"]) > P_BAND, record 5.4207e-02 (W1:209). The displaced probe against its own θ̄(5.5 mm) is printed beside 1.1349e-03 (W1:209). - Printed beside the records: (P_t) 1.6845e-03 (W1:160); (G) per probe (W1:204–206); q_h at t* +3.7300e-02 / +3.6500e-02 / +3.4656e-02 (W1:207); (C2) −6.2905e-03 / −8.1485e-03 / −1.3531e-02 (W1:210). - At -n 2 the run is the gate's own width and arithmetic, so the (T), (C1), (C2) and q_h digits should match W1 exactly. Any digit difference is reported. (N1) and (W) are round-off readings and are not re-read by the example.

Records go in a RECORD dict, each value commented with its W1:line. They are printed beside the run, and a difference is reported, never asserted (the mat:4 precedent, 04_sar_heats_gel_ball.py:123–131).

Example-side checks (asserted): - (X0) Containment of the sweep probes. For each a in A_SWEEP, |c₀| + a ≤ 0.9 R, exact (MAT-19's (M), extended to the new radii). The largest is 8 mm ≤ 9 mm. - (X1) Wiring. probe_series(run["snap_cf"], DT, [ProbeBall(CENTRES[0], A_PROBE)] + [ProbeBall(CENTRES[0], a) for a in A_SWEEP]). Its first column equals run["s_cf"].values[:, 0] within B_BAND relative at n = 1 … 40, predicted 0.0 (same cells, same lattice, same width), and its steps equal range(N_MAIN + 1). - (C3) The volume-omitted comparand, predicted to miss and printed, not asserted (rule (e); the review demoted it 2026-10-05 10:30, because no prior measurement of this comparison on this fixture backs it). Print, at a = 8 mm, max over n of |P_h(c₀, 8 mm, t_n)/θ(0, t_n) − 1| > P_BAND, with θ the point value through the imported _point. - Predicted: 13.4 % at n = 40, range [12.9 %, 13.8 %] (exact ball/point − 1 = −13.368 % at t*, plus the FEM error of ≤ 3e-3). - Ceiling: the steady limit, −q a²/(10k)/θ_ss(0) = −17.45 %. The miss grows with n (−0.997 % at n = 5, −8.44 % at n = 20), so the assertion is on the maximum, never on every n. The factor ≈ 13× is printed, not asserted.

Printed (no band; predicted beside measured). The predictions are pure-Python evaluations of the gate's _ball_mean formula while drafting. They reproduce MAT-19's θ̄ at a = 2 mm to the printed 7 digits (5.913173e-02 / 5.678637e-02 / 5.025018e-02). - The sweep against its own exact ball mean, at t* and as the max over n: |P_h/θ̄(0, a, t) − 1|, predicted ≤ 3e-3 for a = 1, 4, 8 mm (MAT-12's interior L2 1.68e-3; MAT-19's (G) ≤ 1.1e-5). Not gated: MAT-19's (T) covers a = 2 mm only, and the guide says so. V_h/V − 1 is printed, predicted |·| ≤ 5e-3 at a = 1 mm and ≤ 2e-3 otherwise. - The volume effect as the instrument sees it, P_h/θ(0, t*) − 1 at c₀. The exact value is given first, then the FEM prediction:

a [mm] exact θ̄/θ − 1 at t* FEM P_h/θ − 1 predicted exact at n = 20 steady −q a²/(10k)/θ_ss(0) 1 −0.180 % [−0.30 %, +0.05 %] −0.079 % −0.273 % 2 −0.726 % record −0.629 % (W1:210) −0.324 % −1.091 % 4 −2.994 % [−3.3 %, −2.6 %] −1.450 % −4.364 % 8 −13.368 % [−13.8 %, −12.9 %] −8.444 % −17.455 %

At a = 1 mm the FEM error (≈ +0.1 % at c₀, t*, W1:202) is comparable to the volume effect. The guide says the offset below a ≈ h_in is not resolved on this mesh. - The a² law: exact offset ratios to a = 2 mm at t* are 0.248 / 4.12 / 18.4 for a = 1 / 4 / 8 mm. The steady part is exactly a² (0.25 / 4 / 16); the transient part is not. The FEM ratios are printed beside. - c₁ and c₂ at a = 2 mm: exact θ̄/θ − 1 at t* is −0.865 % / −1.259 %, beside the FEM (C2) record. At c₂ the FEM probe against the point value exceeds the 1 % band from n ≈ 20 (record −1.1388e-02, W1:210). This is why a bare point comparison can fail a correct probe.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (C1), the displaced probe: asserted inside the lift and on the returned values (above). Predicted 5.42e-2, record 5.4207e-02; ceiling 6.843e-2 (MAT-19.md item 243). - (C3), the point comparand at a = 8 mm: predicted and printed (above). Its measured value becomes the backing a later item may assert on. - No other control is needed: (X1) is a wiring check, not a separation.

Output. - Setup figure examples/materials/figures/materials_13_virtual_probe_in_gel_ball_setup.png, through write_setup_figure, called right after _build_run(). It is drawn on the submesh run["sub"] with a figure-only meshtags that is never passed to a solve: - values over owned + ghost local cells, from numpy cell centroids (sub.geometry.x[sub.geometry.dofmap].mean(axis=1)) and float64 squared distances: 1 = gel; 11 / 12 / 13 = centroid inside the c₀ / c₁ / c₂ ball (assigned in that order; c₀ and c₁ overlap by 0.5 mm, and the caption says so); indices sorted, int32; - region_names={1: "gel sphere (sigma 0.57 S/m, Robin h = 100)", 11: "probe c0 (a = 2 mm)", 12: "probe c1 (a = 2 mm, 3.5 mm on x)", 13: "probe c2 (a = 2 mm, 6.5 mm off-axis)"}. "sphere" picks the saline-blue class; the probe names hit no CLASS_COLOURS keyword and take the fallback palette; - translucent_tags=(1,), hide_tags=(); - slice_normal=(0.0, -1.0, 1.0) normalised, through the origin. The plane holds the x-axis and the (1, 1, 1) direction, so it cuts all three balls; - window_size=(1400, 630), title ≤ 130 characters; - if the PNG is over 600 KiB, re-render once with show_edges_on_slice=False. - Combined XDMF examples/materials/paraview_output/materials_13_virtual_probe_in_gel_ball_combined.xdmf, through write_xdmf_time_series(…, run["sub"], None, frames, comm=comm) and then adopt_host_ownership. It has 41 time steps at t_n = n·DT, and every Function is named and keyed by its name: - P1 theta_h: the q_cf snapshot n, renamed; - P1 theta_exact: the series at t_n, interpolated into the snapshot's own P1 space through _point, chunked 20 000 as _exact_theta does; - P1 theta_error = theta_h − theta_exact; - DG0 probe_c0_mask, probe_c1_mask, probe_c2_mask, probe_c2_displaced_mask, probe_c0_a8mm_mask (centroid-in-ball, 1/0; the same Function objects at every step). - …_series.csv (41 rows): n, t_s; for c0 / c1 / c2 probe_K, ball_exact_K, point_exact_K, probe_qh_K; probe_c2_displaced_K; for a = 1 / 4 / 8 mm at c₀ probe_K, ball_exact_K. - …_probes.csv for ParaView's Table To Points: label, cx_m, cy_m, cz_m, a_m, V_h_over_V_minus_1. Seven rows: the gate's four probes and the three sweep radii. - …_series.png (matplotlib Agg, rank 0, after every collective): - left panel: θ against t for c₀ / c₁ / c₂ (FEM probe markers, exact ball mean solid, point value dashed) and the displaced probe; - right panel: |P_h/θ − 1| at t* against a at c₀ on log–log axes (FEM markers, exact curve, the a² slope and the 1 % band drawn). - The XDMF / H5 / CSV / PNG under paraview_output/ are gitignored. Only the setup PNG is tracked. The guide names every artifact by full filename (rule (b)). - Guide. The three required headings, ## Setup figure and ## Related. Related lists mat:4 first (the same fixture's whole-ball rise curve), then mat:2 and mat:11, then MAT-19's files by full filename: tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py, tests/solver/test_thermal_probe.py and src/fem_em_solver/thermal/probe.py. It explains: - why the probe is an owned-cell integral and not a point sample: the submesh owner rule raises (known-issues "Mixed topology unsupported"), and each cell is counted once at every width; - the comparand: the Helmholtz mean-value theorem gives the exact ball mean, factor 3j₁(κa)/(κa) per mode; the steady offset is −q a²/(10k); - that the 1 % band cannot see the a = 2 mm volume at c₀, but would at a = 8 mm (C3, printed); - that placement error outweighs volume at this a/R (C1 against the volume offset at c₂); - that the q_h series' ≈ +3.5 % is MAT-4's SAR offset, not the probe; - that a is a stated fixture parameter, not a fibre-optic sensing volume; - a ParaView recipe: open the combined XDMF; Threshold probe_c2_mask ≥ 0.5 and colour by theta_h; play the 41 steps; Plot Over Line from the origin along (1, 1, 1) on theta_error; load …_probes.csv with Table To Points (cx_m, cy_m, cz_m) and a Glyph sphere scaled by a_m.

Complex build. The script checks default_scalar_type and raises in a real build (the mat:4 guard, 04_sar_heats_gel_ball.py:147–152). The mat: group sources source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode automatically. The re-gate windows carry both source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, with tests/environment first.

Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000, and makes one bare harness call. 0. Orphan check. docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0 (exit 1 on zero matches is expected). Then run the rubric's sweep as one bare call: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-90-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-90-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-90-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" 2. Make the lift edit, then re-gate W1 (predicted [90, 210] s; 14 passed). It writes /workspace/logs/mat19/step1-n2.npz. Lines W1:160–210 must reproduce at the printed digits (the (N1) value and the elapsed line excepted): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-90-mat19-regate-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py -s -v --tb=short'" 3. Re-gate W2 (predicted [90, 200] s; 14 passed): the same line with label EX-90-mat19-regate-W2 and -n 4. (W) must read cells equal and series_cf ≤ WIDTH_BAND 1e-9 (record 6.661e-16, …100001Z_MAT-19-step1-W2.log:257). It reads step 2's npz, so steps 2 and 3 run back to back from the same module bytes. 4. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-90-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:13 -n 2 -t 300 --dry-run". It must print (complex build) and emit docker compose exec fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/materials/13_virtual_probe_in_gel_ball.py". 5. Flagged run, predicted [60, 180] s. Use this line (the EX-86 / EX-89 run-of-record form, with -T and the flag added). If the emitted string differs otherwise, use the emitted one and note it: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-90 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/materials/13_virtual_probe_in_gel_ball.py"' 6. Control: git add the PNG, then run the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-90-control. The readings must be unchanged; at the same width and arithmetic they are predicted digit-equal. 7. Post-censuses EX-90-post-figures / EX-90-post-docrefs (the step 1 commands with those labels). - Write the prediction first: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, missing unchanged, broken=0; docrefs runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1 (exit 2 is staleness only). - Take N fresh from step 1. After item 250 it was 85 (ok=85 missing=0 broken=0). EX-89's post-census read examples=85 ok=84 missing=1 broken=0 (20261005T142757Z_EX-89-post-figures.log:121), and item 250 then drew the one missing figure. 8. Final check: git status --porcelain examples/ lists only the three new tracked paths (script, guide, setup PNG). tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py is the only other modified code path.

Traps already paid for: - No point evaluation on the submesh, ever. evaluate_vector_field_parallel(..., owner=...) raises Mixed topology unsupported. on a create_submesh mesh (docs/testing/known-issues.md:1372–1379, OPEN), and f.eval is banned by the rank-safety rule. The "point value" in this example is the closed form _point(d, t, q), never a FEM sample. The guide says so. - Every collective on every rank. _build_run, _check_probe_series (its comm.Barrier), probe_series, the meshtags build and both XDMF writes run on every rank. CSV, PNG and prints go inside rank == 0 with no collective inside: a rank-0-only collective deadlocked item 227 (eda85f26). - Complex build. Snapshots are complex-typed. Take np.real on readings. The masks and figure tags are numpy float64 squared distances, never a UFL conditional or a comparison on a UFL operand (OPS-22; WF-6 4c, where a sqrt comparison cost a 400 s window). - XDMF on the affine mesh needs P1. _exact_theta returns P2 (test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:86–100), which write_function rejects on a degree-1 geometry. Interpolate _point into the snapshot's P1 space instead. - write_xdmf_time_series: every step carries the same names in the same order, each key equals its Function's name, and times are distinct (t₀ = 0 is fine). Name every Function: EX-79's HDF5 collision cost a window. Facet tags are rejected; pass None. - The npz. The lifted _check_probe_series writes /workspace/logs/mat19/step1-n2.npz at -n 2. The example's run overwrites it with the same computation, which is benign (the EX-84 / EX-89 precedent). Never delete it between steps 2 and 3. Never run the example at a width other than 2: the lifted body would pytest.fail on a stale or missing npz, or compare against it. - One fixture build. Call _build_run() once. A second call repeats the EM solve and both CN runs (≈ 36 s) and writes nothing new. - Snapshot indices are full steps: snapshot 1 is after both BE half-steps, at t = DT. Take times from n·DT or ProbeSeries.times, never from counting balance entries (MAT-19.md traps). - ProbeBall centres are coerced to floats by the class; pass the imported CENTRES, never a recomputed one. - Rank count: the npz path and the record digits are -n 2 facts. The runner line pins -n 2. - Insert _REPO_ROOT into sys.path (04_sar_heats_gel_ball.py:56–58). Never import another example's module. - ./scripts/run_examples.sh is host-side: emit, then pass the string to the harness. Never wrap it in docker compose exec. - PNG ≤ 600 KiB: ans:8's first was 631 KiB. - Rule (i): the test module is frozen after window 3, the script after window 6. - Status 124 is a finding, never a retry. After any kill, run pgrep -c python3 in the container before anything else. - A docker-socket denial means stop and report. - Never pipe pytest. -s is needed for the gate's prints.

Scope. One fixture (MAT-12's 1 cm sphere, one mesh at h_in = R/10, P1, CN N = 40), -n 2, the recorded times only. The gate's three probes plus one displaced probe are at a = 2 mm, and the sweep is a = 1 / 4 / 8 mm at the centre. The q_cf series is gated and the q_h series printed.

Not claimed: - a real probe's thermal mass, self-heating, lead artefact or optical sensing volume (a is a stated fixture parameter); - any probe radius other than 2 mm as gated: the sweep readings and (C3)'s miss are printed only; - h-convergence of the probe; - the phantom or coil fixtures (MAT-15, ANS-9), tissue or perfusion; - ASTM F2182 or any compliance reading; - interpolation between steps; - the submesh owner-rule fix: that known-issues entry stays OPEN.

There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Status it can move: EX-90 ⬜ → ✅ and the census N → N + 1. MAT-19 is unchanged (✅) and the known-issues submesh entry is unchanged.

Negative result: - A re-gate red, or W1 / W2 digits off the MAT-19 records ((A0), V_h/V, the (T) table, (C1), (C2), q_h at the printed digits; (W) above 1e-9): revert the lift, write a known-issues entry (the fixture moved under a ✅ gate), and mark BLOCKED. - An anchor red in the example with the re-gates green, or the example's t* readings off W1:202: an example/test divergence finding. Write a known-issues entry, park on attempt/EX-90-<ts>, and mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). Never loosen a band and never re-record from the example side. - (X1) red: the sweep call is wired differently from the gate's (wrong snapshots dict, centre or radius). Fix it once in-slot and re-run the flagged window; otherwise park. - (C3) reads under P_BAND (it is printed, so the run does not go red): the sweep probe is not reading an 8 mm ball, or the comparand is wrong. Print V_h/V, the full 41-row a = 8 mm series and θ(0, t_n), finish the item, and flag it in the journal for the review. Never lower a. - (X0) red: a sweep radius was edited past 0.9 R. Restore A_SWEEP; never move the bound. - Over 300 s, or the slot at minute 50 before window 6: park on attempt/EX-90-<ts> with the last line printed and journal it; the review re-tiers. - A printed value outside its prediction (sweep vs own θ̄ > 3e-3, V_h/V, the volume-effect ranges, the a² ratios): report it. It has no status effect. A sweep miss above 1 % against its own θ̄ is still a finding for the MAT-19 row's next step, not for this item.

Executor prompt (verbatim, for the example-runner spawn):

Execute EX-90 (§9 item 255) exactly as briefed in docs/planning/chunks/EX-90.md#§9-item-255; you are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a harness window, and never delete a log. Call scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh bare and repo-relative, with no cd and nothing chained. The harness call is the whole Bash command — bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. The re-gates run with source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1; the example run is complex through the mat: group. The only code edit outside examples/ is the rule (a) lift in tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py (fixture body into _build_run(), test body into _check_probe_series(run), additive return keys only); do not edit src/ or any other test module (import only, rebase if needed, never path-checkout). Return the windows' log names, every asserted and printed value beside its record or prediction, the census before / after, and the disclosed rule (a) diff.

Outcome (2026-10-05 15:00 CDT slot, second item): ✅. mat:13 ran at -n 2 in 81 s (20261005T201522Z_EX-90.log, flagged) and 79 s (20261005T201654Z_EX-90-control.log, unflagged; all printed readings md5-identical). Rule (a) lift re-gated W1 (20261005T200952Z_EX-90-mat19-regate-W1.log, 14 passed, 106 s) and W2 (20261005T201157Z_EX-90-mat19-regate-W2.log, 14 passed, 103 s; (W) 8.882e-16 against record 6.661e-16, both round-off, cells equal). W1 digits for (A0), (T), (G), (C1), (C2), q_h equal the MAT-19 records. (X0), (X1) hold (X1 = 0.0). Sweep, FEM P/θ − 1 at t*: −0.072 / −0.629 / −2.927 / −13.420 % at a = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 mm, each in its predicted range; sweep vs own θ̄ max 1.80e-03 / 1.58e-03 / 7.7e-04; (C3) 13.420 % at n = 40 (13.4× the band, predicted 12.9–13.8 %). FEM a² ratios 0.114 / 4.654 / 21.334 against exact 0.248 / 4.123 / 18.407 (a = 1 mm unresolved, as predicted). Census examples 85 → 86, ok 85 → 86, broken=0; docrefs runnable 86, dead=0 guide=0, exit 2 (stale 45, unchanged). Setup PNG 289 KiB. Item 254 retired the submesh known-issues entry in-slot, so the guide says parent= since POST-10 and does no FEM point evaluation.

docs.text: Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

docs.title: §9 item 272 — 2026-10-06 (§5.4 example, Phase 9)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-06 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-91 (mri:7): examples/mri/07_study_lossy_sphere.py + same-stem guide 07_study_lossy_sphere.md (three required headings + ## Setup figure + ## Related; setup PNG ≤ 600 KiB). It builds WF-15's Study on MAT-4's lossy sphere (σ 0.57 S/m, εᵣ 78, 64 MHz, imposed uniform 1 V/m field, 74 020 cells) at the default degree (no degree= keyword; 2), and reads its mean SAR against WF-15's record and MAT-4's closed form. mri:1–mri:6 exist; mri:7 is free. run_examples.sh selects by file-name prefix, so no registry edit is needed.

  • Executor: example-runner.
  • Tier: heavy, -n 2, complex. Runner -t 590; container timeout -k 30 590.
  • Cost: ≈ 13 measured (example class median) / ≈ 50 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 script and guide + ≈ 15 windows).
  • Depends on: nothing. WF-15 and WF-17 are ✅ (items 251, 257).

Imports (never restated). - From tests.package.test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere: GEOMETRY, _study, _closed, MAT4_DEG1_RECORD (:87), MAT1_MID_PRINT (:90). - From tests.package.test_wf17_first_study_tutorial: WF15_DEG2_RECORD (:72). The WF-15 module holds no named constant for its degree-2 record; WF-17 holds it with the W2a log citation. Flagged run of record, predicted [90, 200] s. - Basis: solve_sweep 54.5 s with ≈ 1.9 GiB summed RSS (W1:5632–5633). - The example adds one keep_fields 64 MHz sweep (≈ 9 s), ≈ 15 s for startup, ≈ 15 s for the setup figure and ≈ 5 s for XDMF. - Command: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-95 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/11_study_frequency_sweep.py"'. If the dry run emits a string that differs in any other way, use the emitted one and note it. 4. Control run. git add the PNG, then rerun the same line without the flag, labelled EX-95-control. The readings must match digit for digit. 5. Post-censuses. Run EX-95-post-figures / EX-95-post-docrefs, writing the prediction first: - figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0; - docrefs: runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1.

Output. - Touchstone examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_11_study_frequency_sweep.s4p (three frequencies), from sw.write_touchstone. It is gitignored. - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_11_study_frequency_sweep_combined.xdmf. - PortStudyResult.fields is None (study.py:466). Take the 64 MHz PortStudyResult r = sw.results[KEYS.index("64")] and run one run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(r.problem, r.port_definitions, lumped_sheet_ports=r.specs, lumped_sheet_facet_tags=r.facet_tags, degree=r.degree, keep_fields=True) on it. - Assert this sweep's S is within LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND of r.s_matrix (printed), then write E_abs for the P1 drive, interpolated into P1 (or DG1) Lagrange, plus DG0 sigma. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_11_study_frequency_sweep_setup.png, using EX-92's recipe on sw.results[0].mesh. - Guide. - It shows solve_sweep against three separate Study objects: one mesh and one Touchstone, versus three meshes. - It shows the .s4p header and the three # Hz blocks, and gives a scikit-rf snippet that plots |S11| over the three points. - It states that three points are not a resonance curve. - ## Related lists mri:8, tests/package/test_wf16_study_sweep.py and docs/guide/first_study.md.

(4) Traps already paid for. - Rank width. The records hold at -n 2 only (OPS-41). Assert the width. - No dispersion. The gel is constant-property across the sweep (study.py:489–491). The guide says so. Never pass per-frequency materials. - Collectives. write_touchstone is rank-0 plus Barrier. Run skrf on rank 0 and bcast the readings, with no collective inside a rank-0 block (item 227). - Do not re-solve. Never call solve() per frequency beside solve_sweep (the WF-16 step-2 fixture rule). The only extra solve is the one keep_fields 64 MHz sweep. - Complex operands. Use no UFL or sqrt comparison on complex operands (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). - Orphan .c. A killed compile leaves an orphan .c: check orphans, then sweep. - Bare harness calls. Make bare harness calls only, with -k 30 on the timeout, and never pipe. - Rule (i). Make no edit after the last window.

(5) Scope. Not claimed: - resonance, tuning, degree 2 or frequency dispersion; - an absolute S at any frequency; - anything WF-16 does not claim.

(6) Negative result. If (W), (R′), (T′), (G′), (M), (c4) or (c5) misses: - report the measurement and stop; - journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md and park on attempt/EX-95; - leave EX-95 ⬜ and never widen a band.

A run killed at 300 s is not a result: check orphans and stop.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-95 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). Census examples +1 with broken=0; docrefs runnable +1.

docs.title: EX-96 — Price a Study before you solve it: Study.estimate() on the lossy sphere, then the solve it priced (history)
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened 2026-10-07 by the 03:00 daily review under daily-review.md step 5 (§5.4 example ramp). §10 U14 (WF-13 step 2, §9 item 287) closed a quantitative gate on Study.estimate(): the unknown count is exact and the leave-one-out price brackets ×2 on the recorded rows. No example shows Study.estimate() yet.

docs.title: §9 item 296 — 2026-10-07 (§5.4 example)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-07 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-96 (mri:12) adds examples/mri/12_study_estimate.py and a same-stem guide 12_study_estimate.md (three required headings + ## Setup figure + ## Related; setup PNG ≤ 600 KiB). The script builds WF-15's sphere Study at the default degree (2). It calls study.estimate(comm) and prints the ResourceEstimate, then solves the same Study and asserts U14's identity: the solve's global N1curl unknowns and cells equal the estimate's exactly. It then re-asserts the solve's mean SAR against WF-15's degree-2 record, and WF-13's leave-one-out bracket on the row this fixture is. - mri:8, mri:10 and mri:11 belong to EX-92, EX-94 and EX-95; mri:7 / mri:9 exist. This item writes mri:12 only and depends on none of them. run_examples.sh selects by the zero-padded prefix 12_, so no registry edit is needed.

  • Executor: example-runner.
  • Tier: heavy, -n 2, complex. Runner -t 590; container timeout -k 30 590.
  • Cost: ≈ 9 measured (example class median) / ≈ 50 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 script and guide + ≈ 15 windows).
  • Depends on: nothing. WF-13 step 2 (item 287) and WF-15 are on main.
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-96, §9 item 296 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-96.md, heading §9 item 296). Do not spawn agents. Run every harness window in the foreground (Bash timeout: 660000) and never background one; do not end the turn while a window runs. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window."

Why degree 2 and heavy, not the standard tier the ramp would prefer. Read from the code, not chosen: - estimate() refuses degree 1. _predict fits per degree on rows that carry unknowns, memory and time, and raises ValueError("fewer than two priced rows at degree 1") with fewer than two (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:875–879). Degree 1 has P1 (N 90 209) and P3, whose unknowns=None (:833–834), so a degree-1 Study.estimate() raises after building its space. The cheap degree-1 sphere solve (13.7 s, P1) therefore cannot carry the estimate-then-solve identity. That refusal becomes control (c2) below. - The degree-2 sphere is the smallest fixture estimate() prices. Its solve is the whole window: Study solve + mesh 282.4 s (20261005T170537Z_WF-15-r2-W2a-deg2-study.log:158), and 273.3 / 287.7 s in EX-91's flagged / control runs (20261006T202424Z_EX-91.log:186, 20261006T202928Z_EX-91-control.log:179). That is over the standard 180 s ceiling, so the tier is heavy, as EX-91's was.

What the estimate is on this fixture: in-sample, not a prediction. The sphere at degree 2 and -n 2 is PRICE_TABLE row P2 (74 020 cells, 482 158 unknowns, 282.4 s, 20.41 GiB; study.py:835). The estimate's fit includes it. - WF-13's W1 printed this estimate: pred_peak=15.36 GiB pred_s=246.5 ranks=2 rows=('P2', 'F16', 'Cu7', 'Cu7h', 'A6', 'S4c', 'P4', 'P5', 'P6') (20261007T033535Z_WF-13-s2-r-W1.log:157). That is in-sample mem 0.753 / time 0.873 of P2's record (:2030). - The out-of-sample figure on this fixture is the leave-one-out P2: mem 0.633, time 0.804 (:2048). The example re-asserts it as (B-P2). - The guide says plainly that the printed price on this fixture is in-sample, and that the gated, out-of-sample claim is the ×2 leave-one-out.

Imports (never restated). - From tests.package.test_wf13_study_estimate: WF13_DEG2_UNKNOWNS_RECORD (:29, 482 158), WF15_CELLS_RECORD (:30, 74 020), BRACKET (:31, 2.0), _ratios (:126), _inside (:144). - From tests.package.test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere: _study (:111), _closed (:222), _summed_rss_gib (:217), MAT4_DEG1_RECORD (:87). - From tests.package.test_wf17_first_study_tutorial: WF15_DEG2_RECORD (:72). - From tests.validation.test_mat5_em_coupled_sphere: L0_BAND (:104, 1e-9). - From tests.materials.test_phantom_material_model: MAT4_BAND (:222, 0.10). - From src: - fem_em_solver.Study (through _study); - fem_em_solver.study.PRICE_TABLE, for the P1 / P2 rows read in (In) and (c1); - the fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils writers (write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership); - fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure.write_setup_figure. ResourceEstimate is returned, not exported. The script never imports it, and the guide does not tell users to. - No new number. The example states no σ, εᵣ, frequency, field, radius, unknown count or price. It reads them from the built Study, the returned estimate, PRICE_TABLE or the imports above.

Order of calls in the script. study = _study() (no degree=) → est = study.estimate(comm) (timed) → (K) → res = study.solve(comm) (timed) → _summed_rss_gib(comm) immediately after → study.mean_sar() → controls → XDMF → prints → asserts. This is one degree-2 solve, with nothing else at degree 2 that solves.

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script). - (K) The estimate does not solve: study.result is None right after estimate() (WF-13 (K), test_wf13_study_estimate.py:61). After solve(), study.result is res. - (U) U14's identity: the estimate's unknowns are the solve's unknowns, exactly. - est.unknowns == V.dofmap.index_map.size_global * V.dofmap.index_map_bs, where V = res.fields.e_complex.function_space is the space the solve actually used. - est.cells == res.mesh.topology.index_map(res.mesh.topology.dim).size_global. - est.degree == study.degree == res.degree == 2, and est.ranks == comm.size == 2. - Both counts also equal the imported records: est.unknowns == WF13_DEG2_UNKNOWNS_RECORD and est.cells == WF15_CELLS_RECORD. Record 482 158 / 74 020 (…033535Z_WF-13-s2-r-W1.log:157; EX-91's solve read the same at …202424Z_EX-91.log:186). - Integer ==, never a band. The estimate and the solve each build their own mesh (study.py:901, :140), so compare global counts, never mesh objects. - (In) The fixture is a priced row: "P2" in est.rows_used, and P2's registered unknowns (read from PRICE_TABLE by row == "P2") equals est.unknowns. This is what makes the printed price in-sample, and the guide's sentence true. - (R) The solve the estimate priced reproduces WF-15's record: |SAR − WF15_DEG2_RECORD| / record ≤ L0_BAND. Record 8.0116577245e-08 W/kg (…170537Z_WF-15-r2-W2a-deg2-study.log:170). EX-91 read 9.512e-11 and 1.207e-11 (flagged / control); predicted ≤ 2e-10. - (G): |SAR − _closed(σ, εᵣ)| / closed ≤ MAT4_BAND, with σ and εᵣ read from study.material. Record 0.0413 % (W2a:165; EX-91 :189). - (B-P2) WF-13's leave-one-out gate on this fixture's row, re-asserted: rm, rt = _ratios(PRICE_TABLE, "P2"), then _inside(rm) and _inside(rt). Record 0.633 / 0.804 (…033535Z_WF-13-s2-r-W1.log:2048). This is deterministic arithmetic on the committed table, so it is predicted digit-equal at .3f.

Printed, not asserted (environment-dependent; no gate asserts a live run against its estimate): - est.predicted_peak_gib beside the measured summed ru_maxrss after the solve. Predicted reading ≈ 20–22 GiB (P2 20.41; W2a's 22.45 includes two extra assemblies), so measured / estimate ≈ 1.3–1.45. - est.predicted_seconds beside the measured study.solve() seconds. Predicted 270–300 s against 246.5, so a ratio ≈ 1.1–1.2. - The estimate call's own seconds, predicted ≲ 10 s against the solve's ≈ 280 s. This is the point of the method, and it is stated in the guide as a reading, not a claim. - est.rows_used, and BRACKET beside both ratios.

Rule (e) does not license an assertion here. WF-13 gated only the leave-one-out ×2 on recorded rows; it never asserted a live run against its own estimate. The shared box's load moves wall time, and ×2 on an in-sample row would be a new, unregistered gate. A future item may pose one.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) asserted — the identity's comparator separates degrees. - Build V1 = fem.functionspace(res.mesh, ("N1curl", 1)) on the solved mesh. This is space construction only: no form and no solve. - Assert n1 = size_global * bs ≠ est.unknowns. - Assert n1 equals P1's registered unknowns in PRICE_TABLE (90 209). - Backing: the same comparison on the same fixture at -n 2. WF-13 read degree-1 unknowns 90 209, ratio deg2/deg1 5.3449 (…033535Z_WF-13-s2-r-W1.log:228; first at 20261006T185702Z_WF-13-s2-W1.log:204). Print the ratio beside 5.3449. - An estimator that ignored degree would therefore read 90 209 and fail (U) by 391 949 unknowns. - 90 209 is version-tagged (a mesh count on the 0.11 image), as 482 158 is. A mismatch is a mesher-version event; stop and report it (§6), and never re-record it in-slot. - (c2) asserted by construction — the estimator refuses to price outside its table. - _study(degree=1).estimate(comm) raises ValueError. Assert the message contains fewer than two priced rows at degree 1 (study.py:878–879; P3's unknowns=None at :834). - Cost: one sphere mesh plus a degree-1 space, ≈ 5 s. - The raise follows the collective mesh/space build and is deterministic on every rank, so every rank raises and none waits in a collective. Catch it with try / except ValueError on every rank. - This code path has never been executed in a log (WF-13's test builds degree 1 through TimeHarmonicSolver, not estimate()). The label is "asserted by construction" (deterministic code, the OPS-19 precedent), not "asserted by measurement". If it does not raise, the estimator priced degree 1 from fewer than two rows: a src/ defect, so stop (§6). - (c3) asserted — the (R) comparator separates degrees: |MAT4_DEG1_RECORD / WF15_DEG2_RECORD − 1| > L0_BAND. These are two imported constants and need no solve. EX-91 (c2) read 3.4937e-02 (…202424Z_EX-91.log:191); print beside it. - No other control. Writing the XDMF is output, not a separation.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. Nothing is chained or piped. Never beside another heavy window (≈ 20–22 GiB summed). 0. Orphan check: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Then run the rubric's cache sweep (daily-review.md:426) as one bare call with label EX-96-cache-sweep. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-96-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-96-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" Take N fresh from these. It was 88 at drafting (EX-93); EX-92 / EX-94 / EX-95 may land first. 2. Dry run, after the script exists (EX-91's first dry run exited 2 because it ran before the file): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-96-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:12 -n 2 -t 590 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 3. Flagged run of record, predicted [290, 430] s. - Basis: degree-2 Study solve + mesh 273.3–287.7 s (EX-91 :186 / control :179) and 282.4 s (W2a:158); EX-91 windows 297 / 304 s. - The example adds the estimate (≈ 5–10 s: one mesh plus a degree-2 space), (c2) (≈ 5 s), (c1) (< 1 s), ≈ 10 s for XDMF and ≈ 15 s for the setup figure. It drops EX-91's degree-1 solve (≈ 15 s). - Command: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-96 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/12_study_estimate.py"' - PYTHONPATH includes /workspace because the script imports from tests.*. If the dry run's emitted string differs in any other way, use the emitted one and note it. 4. Control run. git add the PNG, then rerun the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-96-control. Compare at the band, never bitwise (2026-10-06 18:00 review §3, the EX-91 ruling): - integers (cells, unknowns, n1) and the pure-arithmetic readings (est.predicted_*, (B-P2) ratios, (c3)) are equal; - SAR agrees within L0_BAND (the -n 2 complex MUMPS drift, ≈ 1e-10 on EX-91); - measured seconds and RSS are printed and may differ. 5. Post-censuses: EX-96-post-figures / EX-96-post-docrefs, the step 1 commands with those labels. Write the prediction first: - figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0; - docrefs: runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1.

Output. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_12_study_estimate_setup.png, using EX-91's recipe (07_study_lossy_sphere.py:99–113) on res.mesh / res.cell_tags. Region names are "gel sphere (sigma 0.57 S/m)" (formatted from study.material.sigma) and "air box (imposed-field walls)". The box is hidden, the sphere translucent, and the title is mri:12 -- Study.estimate() then the solve it priced (WF-13 step 2). - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_12_study_estimate_combined.xdmf, built as EX-91 does (:136–169). It holds: - E_abs: P1, |E| from sqrt(real(inner(e, e))) through fem.Expression; - SAR: DG0, σ·Re(inner(E, E))/(2ρ), with the Study's own σ field and study.density_kg_m3; - rank: DG0, each owned cell's MPI rank. This is the two-way partition the estimate's ranks=2 priced. Set x.array[:n_owned] = comm.rank, then scatter_forward(). - Guide. - It shows the two-call pattern est = study.estimate(comm), then study.solve(comm), and reads each ResourceEstimate field in words: cells, exact unknowns, degree, ranks, predicted peak (GiB summed over ranks), predicted seconds, and the table rows used. - It says the unknown count is exact (the identity this example asserts). It says the price is a ×2 figure from PRICE_TABLE's nine degree-2 rows, gated by leave-one-out. On this fixture the printed price is in-sample, because the sphere is row P2. - It says degree 1 is refused, and why. Its scope sentence is WF-13's: not memory or time as a function of N alone, not new geometry classes, not ranks outside {2, 8, 12, 16}, not xl admission. - It quotes no measured second or GiB from this run as a property of the method. The run's readings are named as this machine's. - ParaView recipe: open the combined XDMF, colour by rank to see the partition, then Threshold on the sphere and colour by SAR. - ## Related lists mri:7, docs/guide/first_study.md, docs/guide/api/Study.md and tests/package/test_wf13_study_estimate.py. Every artifact is named by its full filename (rule (b)).

(4) Traps already paid for. - The degree-2 solve is the whole window. Never add a second degree-2 solve. The estimate builds a mesh and a space only. (c1) builds a degree-1 space on the solved mesh, and (c2)'s estimate builds its own degree-1 space and raises; none of them assembles or solves. - TimeHarmonicSolver(problem) silently means degree 1 (WF-15 step 1). The script never constructs a solver; estimate() and solve() read study.degree. - Rank-local counts. Use index_map.size_global * index_map_bs for unknowns and index_map(tdim).size_global for cells, never local sizes. _summed_rss_gib is collective (an allreduce), so call it on every rank. - Collectives. Every collective runs on every rank. Prints, PNG and XDMF bookkeeping go under rank == 0 with no collective inside (item 227's deadlock). (c2)'s ValueError is raised on every rank after the collective build; catch it on every rank, never under rank == 0. - Complex operands. Use no UFL comparison and no sqrt comparison on complex operands (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). Take np.real on readings. - Bare harness calls. The container timeout carries -k 30; never pipe the example. - Orphan .c. A killed compile leaves an orphan .c: check pgrep -c python3 first, then sweep. If the window stalls in MPI_Bcast, sweep; never retry. - No AED number enters the script or guide; every PRICE_TABLE row is ours. Write ≈, never ~. - Rule (i). Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window.

(5) Scope. Not claimed: - a live-run memory or time accuracy for estimate() (printed only, this machine); - an out-of-sample price on this fixture beyond WF-13's leave-one-out ×2; - degree-1 pricing; - a port Study's estimate (F-small is priced by WF-13's test, not shown here); - anything WF-13 step 2 or WF-15 do not claim: no coil, no h-statement, no local or 10 g SAR accuracy, no scheduler or xl admission.

(6) Negative result. In every case below: report the measurement and stop, journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-96, mark item 296 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)), and leave EX-96 ⬜. Never widen a band and never edit study.py. - (U) red, with the space's unknowns ≠ est.unknowns: the estimator builds a different space from the solve. That is a defect in WF-13 step 2's code, which goes to the review as a known-issues entry. - (U) red only against the imported records, with the identity green: a mesher or version event (rule (1*)), which is the review's to route to record-reconciler. - (R), (G), (B-P2), (In) or any control red: the same disposition.

A run killed at 590 s is not a result: check orphans and stop. The fallback is a re-queue, not a degree-1 substitute (degree 1 cannot carry the identity; see above).

No PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-96 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). Census examples +1 with broken=0; docrefs runnable +1. This is the first example on Study.estimate(), so the Phase 9 (9c) clause "a resource estimate before a solve" (PROJECT_PLAN.md ≈ 4302) gains a runnable demonstration.

Review rulings (2026-10-07 03:00 daily review). (1) Heavy tier at degree 2 accepted: Study.estimate() refuses degree 1 (study.py:875–879), and an estimate-only standard item would repeat WF-13's test. (2) (c2), the degree-1 estimate() refusal, stays asserted: it is a deterministic raise, not a separation factor, so rule (e) does not apply; if it does not raise, stop and report. (3) The example class median is 9 measured minutes (recomputed by this review from items 288, 273, 272, 255, 250). (4) The leave-one-out P2 bracket stays asserted — cheap arithmetic on the committed table, and the example shows what the bracket means. (5) Importing the test helpers _ratios, _inside, _summed_rss_gib follows EX-91's precedent and is accepted; no src/ change.

Outcome (2026-10-07 06:00 slot): ✅ DONE, first try. (K) True / True; (U) 482 158 unknowns / 74 020 cells, estimate = solve = records, degree 2, ranks 2; (In) P2 in rows_used, P2 unknowns 482 158; (R) 8.0116577233e-08, rel 1.527e-10 (control 8.977e-11); (G) 0.0413 %; (B-P2) 0.633 / 0.804 inside ×2. (c1) 90 209 = P1 row, deg2/deg1 5.3449, miss 391 949; (c2) ValueError('fewer than two priced rows at degree 1') on every rank — the first execution of that path in a log; (c3) 3.4937e-02. Printed: pred 15.36 GiB / 246.5 s; measured 20.25 / 19.68 GiB and 263.8 / 290.4 s (flagged / control), ratios 1.318 / 1.070 and 1.281 / 1.178; estimate() 2.5 / 2.9 s. docs.title: §9 item 490 — 2026-10-15 (lane 1 revalidation; a regression read from code — observe, then re-point)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-15 18:00 review. The EX-116 drafter found it while drafting, and this review re-read the code. mri:12's control (c2) asserts that Study(degree=1).estimate() raises ValueError("fewer than two priced rows at degree 1") (examples/mri/12_study_estimate.py:176–180, asserted at :294–295). The prediction is that mri:12 is red on main at (c2) and green everywhere else. 471a's licence re-pointed the tests' twin control, WF-13 (X), to a P1-only table through _predict(table=…) (03:00 ruling, disclosed). The example was not re-pointed. This item observes the regression first and then applies the same re-point.

  • Executor: example-runner. Tier: heavy, -n 2, complex, container timeout -k 30 590. The runs of record took 277 s and 299 s (20261007T110359Z_EX-96.log, …110900Z_EX-96-control.log). Predicted ≈ 30 min; counted at the example median of ≈ 9 measured. Depends on: nothing.
  • W0, observe before any edit. docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0 first. Then run, as one bare harness call (the 10-07 command, label changed): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-96-r1-W0 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/12_study_estimate.py"'. Bash timeout: 660000. Expected: an AssertionError at "(c2) degree-1 estimate() did not raise" on both ranks, with every assert above it green ((U), (In), (R), (G), (B-P2), (c1)). If W0 is green, the reading was wrong: record it and stop, with no edit.
  • Re-point (only after W0 shows (c2) red, and nothing above it red). In the script, (c2) becomes the refusal on a P1-only table, as 471a's tests did: _predict(est_n1, degree=1, ranks=comm.size, table=tuple(r for r in PRICE_TABLE if r["row"] == "P1")) raises ValueError with "fewer than two priced rows at degree 1". Import _predict and PRICE_TABLE from fem_em_solver.study, and use the degree-1 space's global unknowns n1 already computed for (c1). Keep the message assert verbatim. Add one printed (not asserted) line: the full-table degree-1 price for n1, labelled "degree-1 priced since 471a (P1 + P3), in-sample on its own rows". Update the guide's (c2) sentence to say the same, with no output filename token (EX-115's lesson: the docrefs checker keys on basenames). Do not patch PRICE_TABLE or _predict in src/. Patching _predict's table= argument is the only route, because the default table= is bound at definition.
  • Windows after the edit (rule (i): nothing edited after its last window):

  • Anchor: U14's identity (the estimate's unknowns and cells equal the solved space's global counts exactly), (R) ≤ L0_BAND against WF15_DEG2_RECORD, and (G) ≤ MAT4_BAND against the closed form. All are imported and none restated. Negative control: (c2) re-pointed. A P1-only table must refuse degree 1, and the full table must not; that pair is the separation, by construction and labelled so. (c1) and (c3) are unchanged.
  • Traps:
  • Two heavy windows never run at once.
  • example-runner does not spawn agents and does not background a harness window.
  • Never edit the script after W1.
  • The guide must not name an output file the checker cannot find.
  • -s is not needed here (the script prints, not pytest).
  • A killed window is not a result: run pgrep -c python3 first.
  • Scope: this restores mri:12's control to the meaning it had on 10-07 (the estimator refuses a degree it cannot fit). It makes no claim of degree-1 price accuracy.
  • Done-when amendment (rule (j); the §7 row carries no Done-when text since the 10-01 split, so the amendment of record is this line, and the row gains its state clause when item 490 lands): "a degree-1 estimate() raises" now reads "on a P1-only table a degree-1 price raises (since 471a's P3 row the full table prices degree 1, printed)". Every other clause is unchanged.

docs.title: EX-97 — A temperature from a config file: femem run on a YAML with thermal: reproduces MAT-10's records (history)
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-97 (mri:13) was opened 2026-10-07 by the 03:00 daily review under daily-review.md step 5 (§5.4 ramp). §10 chain U20 (WF-1 step 3, §9 item 295, landed 2026-10-07 05:21Z) closed a quantitative gate: a thermal: section in the YAML that drives Study.temperature(RobinCooling) and reproduces MAT-10's (A) / (P) digits. No example drives a temperature from a config file. EX-93 (mri:9) is EM-only from YAML, and EX-94 (mri:10) computes the temperature in Python.

docs.title: §9 item 297 — 2026-10-07 (§5.4 example)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-07 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-97 (mri:13) adds four files: - examples/mri/13_temperature_from_yaml.py; - a same-stem guide, 13_temperature_from_yaml.md; - two YAML files beside them: 13_temperature_from_yaml_sphere.yaml and 13_temperature_from_yaml_sphere_control_2g.yaml.

The guide carries the three required headings plus ## Setup figure and ## Related. The setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB.

What the script does: - It drives fem_em_solver.cli.main(["run", <yaml>, "--output-dir", <dir>]) in-process on the sphere file (degree 1, -n 2, complex) and reads the temperature block of the JSON summary that run writes. - It calls the exported fem_em_solver.run_study_file on the same file. That is the function femem run calls (src/fem_em_solver/cli.py:103), and it returns the temperature field that cli.main discards (it returns an int). - On that field it reads MAT-10's (A) / (P) / (B) / (C) and the (IT) identity against the in-Python Study.temperature, the way WF-1 step 3 reads them.

Numbering and independence: - mri:10, mri:11 and mri:12 belong to other items. This item writes mri:13 only. - It imports nothing from examples/ and does not depend on EX-94 landing. EX-94 (§9 item 279) runs earlier in the same queue and may park.

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents.
  • Tier: standard; -n 2, complex. Runner -t 180; container timeout -k 30 180.
  • Cost: ≈ 9 measured (example class median) / ≈ 45 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 script, guide and YAMLs + ≈ 10 windows).
  • Depends on: nothing open. WF-1 step 3 is recorded (item 295, 20261007T051444Z_WF-1-s3-W1-thermal.log). Its chain step U20 is provisional; see (5).

The YAML files. Copy tests/package/wf1/sphere_mat10_thermal.yaml and sphere_mat10_thermal_control_2g.yaml byte for byte, changing only the first (comment) line, and say so in the guide. - Copy by file, never by retyping. The numbers are PyYAML-1.1 floats (25000000.0, never 2.5e7). - The script asserts each copy against its original, by spec and by cooling; see (K) below. Neither file can drift silently. - Never edit tests/package/wf1/*.

Imports (never restated). - From tests.package.test_wf1_yaml_thermal: THERMAL_FILE (:83), CONTROL_2G_FILE (:84), MALFORMED_THERMAL (:85), _hex_diff (:96) and _cooling (:110). - From tests.package.test_wf1_study_yaml: WF1 (:85), _spec_diff (:145), _fresh_dir (:161) and _rc_all (:167). - From tests.package.test_wf15_study_temperature: MAT10_SUB_CELLS (:81), MAT10_A_PRINT (:82), MAT10_P_PRINT (:83), MAT10_B_MISSING_HALF_PRINT (:84) and _theta_owned_rel (:100). - From tests.package.test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere: _study. - From tests.validation.test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere: K, H, T_INF, G, ROBIN_TAG, P_BAND, A_BAND, B_BAND, C_BAND (:52–62), _allsum (:70), _interior_indicator (:133), _theta_cf (:145) and _interior_rel (:151). - From tests.validation.test_lossy_sphere_sar: E0, EPSILON_R_SPHERE, OMEGA, RHO_KG_M3 and SIGMA_HIGH. - From tests.validation.test_mat5_em_coupled_sphere: L0_BAND (:104). - From src: - from fem_em_solver: RobinCooling, StudyConfigError, cli, load_study and run_study_file; - fem_em_solver.post.sar.uniform_sphere_sar_closed_form; - fem_em_solver.thermal.steady.solve_steady_conduction, used for (P); - fem_em_solver.utils.constants.EPSILON_0; - from the paraview_utils writers: write_xdmf_with_tags and adopt_host_ownership; - write_setup_figure. - No new number. The script has no numeric literal: k, h, T∞ and the source scale come from the YAML or the imports. - Arithmetic. (A) / (P) / (B) / (C) follow test_wf1_thermal_yaml_reproduces_mat10_record (test_wf1_yaml_thermal.py:197–214) term for term, so the .4e digits come out of the same arithmetic. - That means: the closed-form q from uniform_sphere_sar_closed_form, scaled by G · RHO_KG_M3; χ from _interior_indicator; (P) from solve_steady_conduction on th.submesh / th.facet_tags; and (B) against th.cooling.source_scale · study.mean_sar()["dissipated_power_w"]. - Never call _parse_mapping directly. The private route stays inside _cooling.

(1) Anchor (asserted in-script). - (K) spec and cooling, no solve: - _spec_diff(load_study(ex_yaml), load_study(THERMAL_FILE)) == [] and _hex_diff(_cooling(ex_yaml), _cooling(THERMAL_FILE)) == []; - the same two checks for the control copy against CONTROL_2G_FILE; - _spec_diff(load_study(ex_yaml), _study(degree=1)) == [] and _hex_diff(_cooling(ex_yaml), RobinCooling(K, H, T_INF, source_scale=G)) == []. - Record: [] / [] (20261007T051444Z_WF-1-s3-W1-thermal.log:64). - (R-cli) femem run writes the temperature: - cli.main(["run", ex_yaml, "--output-dir", <cli dir>]) returns 0 on every rank (_rc_all == (0, 0)). - After comm.Barrier(), the JSON summary has family == "sphere_in_box", degree == 1, ranks == comm.size, and a temperature block with exactly the keys source_power_w, convected_power_w and theta_max_k. - Each of the three values is within L0_BAND (relative) of the run_study_file run's run.summary["temperature"]. - That comparison spans two EM solves of one file, so it is held at the band, never bitwise. Predicted ≤ 1e-11, from the nearest same-fixture two-solve reading: (IT) 6.079e-12 (W1:221). - Print the three values at !r. The record from item 295 is source 0.008651525642063975 W, convected 0.008651525642062842 W and θ max 0.12682242431550605 K (W1:147). These are printed beside the readings, not asserted. - (R) MAT-10's records on the YAML θ (run.thermal): - run.study.result is run.result, i.e. one EM solve; - th.submesh global cells == MAT10_SUB_CELLS (19 496, version-tagged); - f"{err_A:.4e}" == MAT10_A_PRINT and f"{err_P:.4e}" == MAT10_P_PRINT; - err_A ≤ A_BAND, err_P ≤ P_BAND, err_B ≤ B_BAND and err_C ≤ C_BAND. - Record (W1:149): (A) 3.2463961444e-02 [3.2464e-02], (P) 3.1923343273e-03 [3.1923e-03], (B) 6.817e-15, (C) 1.309e-13. - The .4e strings sit ≥ 5e-7 relative from a rounding edge, far above the ≈ 1e-11 two-solve spread. - (IT) YAML vs Python: - Build _study(degree=1), solve it, then call .temperature(RobinCooling(K, H, T_INF, source_scale=G)). - Assert _theta_owned_rel(run.thermal.temperature, th_py.temperature, comm)[0] ≤ L0_BAND. - Record 6.079e-12 (W1:221).

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) asserted: the missing ½, through the control YAML. - Apply _cooling(<control copy>) (source_scale 2G) to run.study, which is already solved, so there is no second EM solve: run.study.result is run.result still holds. - Compute the (A) comparator on that call's own submesh against _theta_cf(th2.submesh, q_cf). - Assert c1 > A_BAND. Print f"{c1:.4e}" beside MAT10_B_MISSING_HALF_PRINT, and .10e too (review ruling 2026-10-07 03:00: the .4e string equality is printed, not asserted — only four digits were ever logged, so its distance from a rounding edge is unknown). - Backing, the same comparison on the same fixture: 1.0649e+00 (20261007T051444Z_WF-1-s3-W1-thermal.log:150; also 20261006T035826Z_WF-15-s2-W1-deg1.log:250). - Ceiling. With q doubled, the comparator is ‖2θ_h − θ‖ / ‖θ‖ ≈ 1 + 2e, where e is the signed degree-1 bias ≈ +0.032. So an exact solver reads 1.0, which is 9.1× A_BAND, and this fixture reads ≈ 1.065, which is 9.7×. The assertion asks only for > 1×. - The YAML being controlled is not the one under test. That is why it is a file beside the example: one value differs (_hex_diff names ['source_scale'] only, W1:64). - (c1′) printed, not asserted: th2.source_power / th.source_power, predicted 2 to ≤ 1e-12 by linearity. No prior measurement exists. - (X) asserted: thermal on a port geometry. Use WF1 / "malformed_thermal_on_port.yaml", with no solve: - load_study raises StudyConfigError whose .field == MALFORMED_THERMAL["malformed_thermal_on_port.yaml"] (thermal); - cli.main(["run", …]) and cli.main(["check", …]) each return 2 on every rank; - the output dir does not exist afterwards. - Backing, the same file at -n 2: W1:66 (field 'thermal') and W1:69 (run / check rc (2, 2), out exists False). - malformed_thermal_k_zero.yaml is not shown. WF-1 step 3 gates it, and one refusal suffices here.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground, passes timeout: 660000, and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call, with nothing chained or piped. The executor never backgrounds a window and never returns while one is running. 0. Pre-flight. U20 still stands: _parse_thermal exists in src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py and tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_thermal.py is on main. Otherwise see (5). - Orphan check: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. - Then run the rubric's cache sweep, as one bare call labelled EX-97-cache-sweep. 1. Pre-censuses, before any file is written: - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-97-pre-figures "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_setup_figures.py'" - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-97-pre-docrefs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py'" - Census at drafting: 88 (EX-93). Use whatever the pre-census reads. EX-94 / EX-95 / mri:12 may land first. 2. Dry run: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-97-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:13 -n 2 -t 180 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 3. Flagged run of record, predicted [50, 140] s. - Basis: run_study_file with thermal took 17.2 s (W1:147), and the Python Study plus thermal 17.8 s (W1:221). Three sphere EM solves here (cli.main, run_study_file, _study) come to ≈ 52 s. Two thermal calls at ≈ 0.4 s each and one (P) conduction solve are negligible. - The example adds ≈ 15 s each for startup and the setup figure, and ≈ 5 s for the XDMF. - Cross-check: EX-93's three solves (two sphere, one F-small) ran 73 s (20261006T213328Z_EX-93.log). - Memory is ≈ 2.4 GiB summed per Study (20261006T035826Z_WF-15-s2-W1-deg1.log:251), so ≤ 8 GiB with three Studies held. - Command: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-97 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/mri/13_temperature_from_yaml.py"'. - EX-93 found that the runner's dry-run string omits -T and /workspace on PYTHONPATH. Use this brief's command and note any other difference. 4. Control run. git add the PNG, then rerun the same line without the flag, labelled EX-97-control. - Every assertion stays green. - (K) and (X) are digit-equal. - (R) / (c1) are equal at their .4e records. - (R-cli) / (IT) agree inside L0_BAND: flag-vs-control at the band, never bitwise (2026-10-06 18:00 review §3, the EX-91 / EX-93 ruling). A 10th-digit drift is not a stop. 5. Post-censuses. Run EX-97-post-figures / EX-97-post-docrefs, writing the prediction first: - figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0; - docrefs: runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1.

No pytest window is needed: the gates are re-read in-script. If the review adds one, it runs with -s.

Output. - Run directories: examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_13_temperature_from_yaml_{cli,api,malformed}/. Both run directories hold the JSON summary; the malformed one must be absent after the run. All three are gitignored. - Combined XDMF examples/mri/paraview_output/mri_13_temperature_from_yaml_combined.xdmf. - run_study_file writes no field file (study_yaml.py:495–550 writes only the JSON and a port study's Touchstone), so the example writes it itself from run.thermal on th.submesh, with facet_tags=th.facet_tags so the Robin surface is a block. - Fields: theta, P1, Re(T) − cooling.t_inf_c in K; q, DG0, Re(th.heat_source) in W/m³. - No src/ change. - Setup figure examples/mri/figures/mri_13_temperature_from_yaml_setup.png. - Use EX-91's recipe on run.result.mesh / cell_tags: the air tag is hidden, the sphere translucent, and the slice is z = 0. - Region names come from the parsed objects, e.g. f"gel sphere (Robin-cooled, h {cooling.h_w_per_m2_k:g} W/m²K)", with no literal. - Guide. - Show the thermal: block inline, with units given by key names. - Give the femem run invocation, both as femem run <file> --output-dir <dir> and as ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mri:13. - Show the temperature block's three keys and say what each means: θ max over owned dofs, MPI.MAX-reduced. - State that omitted source_scale / degree take RobinCooling's defaults (W1:65). - State the exit-code contract: 0 on success, 2 on a config error. - Quote the port-refusal text from W1:66 as illustration, not as a record. - Say that femem check does not echo the thermal: section (cli.py:92–101). - ParaView recipe: colour by theta and Plot Over Line along x. The parabola plus surface offset is described in words, with no numbers. - ## Related lists mri:9, docs/guide/first_study.md, tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_thermal.py, tests/validation/test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py and src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py. It does not list mri:10: that page may not exist when this runs, and a dead link fails docrefs.

(4) Traps already paid for. - cli.main returns an int and keeps no field. θ comes from run_study_file. That is a second EM solve of the same file, by design: reading the summary cannot give (A). - Each temperature() call builds its own submesh. - Build (c1)'s _theta_cf / χ on th2.submesh, never on th.submesh. Item 260's first W1 went red on this (RuntimeError: Incompatible mesh, 20261006T035625Z_WF-15-s2-W1-deg1.log). - (IT)'s _theta_owned_rel asserts that both owned layouts match, so both Studies run at the same -n. - The JSON summary's name in prose. A bare summary.json in guide prose reads as a dead file reference. EX-93's first post-docrefs exited 1 on it (20261006T213633Z_EX-93-post-docrefs.log), and item 274 did too. Write "the JSON summary" in words, or give the full repo-relative path. - Complex operands. T and heat_source are complex-typed in the complex build. - Take np.real on owned dofs before the XDMF and before any max. - Use no UFL ordering or sqrt comparison (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). _interior_rel takes np.real before its sqrt. - Collectives. - cli.main, run_study_file, _allsum and _interior_rel are collective: call them on every rank. - Read the JSON after comm.Barrier(). - femem check prints on rank 0. - Rank-0 print blocks hold no collective (item 227). - Clean output dirs. Clear the output dirs with _fresh_dir (rank 0, then barrier). A stale JSON summary would pass for a fresh one. Never pre-create the malformed run's dir. - Rank-local counts. Cell and dof counts are rank-local; use size_global or reduce. - Orphan .c. A killed compile leaves an orphan .c: check orphans, then sweep. - Bare harness calls. Make bare harness calls only, with -k 30 on the timeout. Never pipe, and never background. - Rule (i). Make no edit to the script, YAMLs or guide after the last window.

(5) Scope. - Covered: the steady Robin-cooled temperature of WF-15's sphere, driven entirely from a YAML file through femem run's in-process entry, at degree 1 and -n 2. - Not claimed: - degree 2 through YAML; - transient heating, Pennes or duty cycle; - thermal on a port Study; - tissue or a coil; - a stable schema; - the installed-wheel femem with a solve, or femem run --ranks (WF-13 step 3, not exercised); - anything WF-1 / WF-15 / MAT-10 do not claim. - The base step is provisional. U20 is a daily-provisional step (§9 rule (6)) that the 10-07 weekly ratifies. If the weekly reverts U20, or thermal: is gone from study_yaml.py, before this slot runs, the item stops BLOCKED at step 0 with nothing run and nothing written. The unblock condition is U20 ratified, or re-landed.

(6) Negative result. If (K), (R-cli), (R), (IT), (c1) or (X) misses: - report the measurement and stop; - journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-97, and mark item 297 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); - leave EX-97 ⬜ and never widen a band.

What each miss means: - (K) red: the copy differs. Quote the diff: a named field is itself the finding. This is fixable before the record window only, by re-copying. - (R) or (IT) red with (K) green: a WF-1 step-3 regression. It is a §7 annotation on WF-1, not an example fix. - (R-cli) red with (R) and (IT) green: the CLI path assembles something run_study_file does not. That finding goes to WF-1. - (c1) ≤ A_BAND: a blind comparator. Stop.

A run killed at 180 s is not a result: check orphans and stop. The fallback is a re-queue, never a longer timeout.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-97 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). Census examples +1 with broken=0; docrefs runnable +1. The review adds the row in the same commit as this item (rule (j)).

Review rulings (2026-10-07 03:00 daily review). (1) The source-scale control (the 2G YAML, the missing ½) is accepted as (c1); the h → 10 h control stays with EX-94. (2) (R-cli) is an asserted anchor at the imported L0_BAND — a band, not a separation factor, so rule (e) does not apply; the nearest two-solve reading, (IT) 6.079e-12, sits ≈ 160× inside it. No src/ change to make cli.main return the StudyRun. (3) (c1) asserts > A_BAND only; its .4e string is printed beside MAT10_B_MISSING_HALF_PRINT (edited in place above). (4) The example class median is 9 measured minutes (recomputed by this review). (5) Base step U20 is provisional: if the 10-07 weekly reverts it before a slot takes this item, the item stops BLOCKED with nothing run.

Outcome (2026-10-07 06:00 slot, second item): ✅ DONE, first try. Step 0: _parse_thermal present, test_wf1_yaml_thermal.py on main. (K) spec / cooling mismatches [] for all three pairs; (R-cli) rc (0, 0), family sphere_in_box, degree 1, ranks 2, summary keys exact, JSON vs run_study_file rel 0.000e+00 on all three values (flagged) and 1.82e-11 / 1.82e-11 / 1.85e-11 (control, two EM solves); (R) 19 496 sub-cells, (A) 3.2463961444e-02 / (P) 3.1923343273e-03 at .4e = records, (B) 6.817e-15, (C) 1.309e-13, study.result is res; (IT) 4.874e-12 (control 5.597e-11). (c1) 1.0649e+00 > A_BAND (≈ 9.7×), .4e = MAT10_B_MISSING_HALF_PRINT, source ratio 2.0 (printed); (X) port YAML with thermal: names the field, run / check rc (2, 2), no output dir. Flagged 20261007T111919Z_EX-97.log (50 s), control 20261007T112043Z_EX-97-control.log (47 s). Census 92 → 93 ok, broken=0; docrefs runnable 92 → 93, dead=0 guide=0 exit=2, stale 46 unchanged. PNG 468 KiB. The guide was written between the flagged and control windows (06:20:37 < 06:20:43 CDT), so its "rel 0 (bitwise here)" row is the flagged run's reading; the control read ≈ 1.8e-11, inside the band.
