docs.title: EX-98 — The container wall on the coil-driven gel phantom: MAT-18 step 3's series-resistance wall under four birdcage drives (history)
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-98 (mat:14) was opened 2026-10-07 by the 10:30 daily review under daily-review.md step 5 (§5.4 ramp). MAT-18 step 3 (§9 item 270, §10 P11, 20261006T200649Z_MAT-18-step3-W1.log, 266 s) recorded the container wall as a series resistance (h_eff 6.5517 W/m²/K) on MAT-15 P1's coil-driven F-small phantom: (E′) ≤ 2.3e-14, (L0) ≤ 6.7e-16, C4 ≤ 0.049 %, ⟨θ⟩(t*) +4.63 % on all four drives (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2534). No example covers that pairing: - mat:12 (EX-86) has a conforming wall, but on the ball under an imposed field; - mat:9 (EX-79) has the coil-driven phantom, but no wall.

The angle is the wall on the coil-driven phantom: its geometry plus its drive.

Proposed §7 row (the review copies it into §7, rule (j); this file is the history):

| EX-98 | The container wall on the coil-driven gel phantom: MAT-18 step 3's series-resistance wall under four birdcage drives (history and §9 briefs: docs/planning/chunks/EX-98.md) (mat:14; example-runner; opened 2026-10-07 by the 10:30 daily review, §5.4 ramp — MAT-18 step 3 recorded the wall on MAT-15 P1's fixture and no example shows it; angle: the wall on the coil-driven phantom) Done-when: examples/materials/14_coil_driven_phantom_in_container_wall.py + same-stem guide (as EX-79); a rule (a) lift of the step-3 fixture body into _run_walled(*, return_fields=False), with the module re-gated green in-slot and disclosed; -n 2, complex; every band imported, none restated; asserted in-script: (R) ≤ R_BAND, (E′) / (E) ≤ E_BAND, (L0) ≤ B_BAND (helper equivalence), C4 θ pairs ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, controls (d) > D_CONTROL_FLOOR and (W-ctl) > W_CONTROL_FLOOR; the wall effect printed beside the step-3 record; combined XDMF (θ with and without the wall, their difference) written; census +1, broken=0, docrefs exit != 1; elapsed recorded ⇒ ✅. Not claimed: a conforming wall, wall heat storage, contact resistance, a real container, absolute temperature. | ⬜ Opened 2026-10-07; nothing run. | heavy (-n 2, ≈ 200–300 s per window) |

docs.title: §9 item 299 — 2026-10-07 (§5.4 example; example-runner)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-07 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-98 (mat:14) adds examples/materials/14_coil_driven_phantom_in_container_wall.py and a same-stem guide 14_coil_driven_phantom_in_container_wall.md. The guide carries the three required headings plus ## Setup figure and ## Related; the setup PNG is ≤ 600 KiB.

What the script does: - It calls the step-3 fixture body once, lifted to a module-level _run_walled(return_fields=True). - It asserts that run's identities and controls at the bands the gate module imports. - It prints the wall effect beside the step-3 record. - It writes θ with and without the wall, and their difference, to one XDMF.

The next free number: examples/materials/ holds 01–13, so mat:14 is free. The runner selects by the zero-padded prefix 14_, so no registry edit is needed (scripts/run_examples.sh:65,243).

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents.
  • Tier: heavy, -n 2, complex, as the step-3 test ran (MAT-18.md:458). Runner -t 590; container timeout -k 30 590.
  • Cost: ≈ 7 measured (example class median) / ≈ 55 predicted min.
  • The 7 is the median of the five example items in the 10:30 review's §1 table: 7, 6, 7, 15, 7 (docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-07-daily-1030.md:12–16).
  • The 55 is 15 fixed + ≈ 25 for the lift, script and guide + ≈ 15 for windows.
  • Three ≈ 200–270 s windows (re-gate, flagged, control) plus an ≈ 84 s cache sweep come to ≈ 13 min of windows alone. ≈ 15–20 measured min is the honest expectation, as EX-96's heavy item took 15 (…daily-1030.md:15).
  • Depends on: nothing. MAT-18 step 3's module tests/validation/test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py and MAT-15's _run_heated are on main. Never beside another heavy window.
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-98, §9 item 299 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-98.md, heading §9 item 299). Do not spawn agents. Run every harness window in the foreground (Bash timeout: 660000) and never background one; do not end the turn while a window runs. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window."

The wall on this fixture is a coefficient, not geometry. Read this first. - MAT-15 P1's thermal domain is the tag-3 submesh of the EM mesh, and it has no wall cells. Step 3 therefore enters the wall as its series thermal resistance in the Robin coefficient: h_eff = 1 / (1/h + t_w/k₂), planar, with one scalar on the lateral faces and the caps. - That is the steady limit of MAT-18's conforming shell, with no wall heat capacity (test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py:7–11, :82–84; MAT-18.md:427–429). - The values are t_w = B_ − A_ = 0.01 m, k₂ = K2 = 0.19 and h = H_GEL = 10. The result is h_eff 6.551724138 W/m²/K, used; the lateral cylindrical value 8.304028064 is printed, never used (20261006T200649Z_MAT-18-step3-W1.log:81). - The guide says this in its first paragraph. The setup figure cannot show a wall, and its region name says so; see Output.

Why a rule (a) lift. - The step-3 fixture walled() is a module-scoped pytest fixture (test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py:129–257), so it cannot be called from a script. - EX-79 met the same shape on MAT-15. It lifted the fixture body to a module-level _run_heated(*, return_fields=False) and made the fixture return _run_heated(). The 10:30 review of 2026-10-02 accepted that as within rule (a) (EX-79.md:17–22; test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:180, 347–356). - The alternative is to re-compose the per-drive loop and ball forms in the script, which copies gate code. It is declined: the example asserts, it does not re-implement (the ANS-1 rule, 12_gel_ball_in_container_wall.py:11–14).

The lift (disclosed in the journal and outcome): - Move walled()'s body into _run_walled(*, return_fields=False); the fixture becomes return _run_walled(). - With False, every print and every out key stays byte-identical. That includes the (R)-red early return before any solve (:136–137). - With True, it adds two keys: - base: the _run_heated(return_fields=True) dict the body already holds (msh, cell_tags, sub, ft, by_k, centres, q_h, T_star, G, P, v_sub); - wall_runs: {k: the h_eff TransientResult of drive k} (the loop's res, :193). - No other edit. Nothing else imports this module: grep finds only the module itself, so no other caller moves. - Rule (a) owes the re-gate window (step 3 below), run after the edit and green before the example runs. Rule (i): no edit to the module after it.

Imports (never restated). - from tests.validation import test_mat18_wall_coil_driven as m18s3. From it: _run_walled (new), _e_prime_h (:108–115), R_BAND (:78), W_CONTROL_FLOOR (:79) and T_WALL (:77). - Also from m18s3, the names it re-exports: E_BAND, B_BAND, C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, D_CONTROL_FLOOR, H_GEL, T_INF, T_STAR, ROBIN_TAG and K2 (:48–75). - Structural checks, asserted and printed (the EX-79 pattern, 09_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:83–98): - m18s3.E_BAND is m12.E_BAND (test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:76); - m18s3.B_BAND is m10.B_BAND (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:61); - m18s3.C4_COVARIANCE_BAND is b1map.C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:120); - m18s3.D_CONTROL_FLOOR is m15.D_CONTROL_FLOOR (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:102); - m18s3._run_heated is m15._run_heated; - m18s3.K2 is m18.K2 (test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form.py:39).

If a name does not exist under that spelling, import the module's own name for the same object and say so in the journal. Never restate a value. - Figure tags, as mat:9 imports them (09_…py:45–46, 64): PHANTOM_CELL_TAG (m15), CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG, PORT_LOWER, PORT_UPPER and LEG_COUNT. - From src: write_xdmf_with_tags, adopt_host_ownership and write_setup_figure. - Import no test_* names. @complex_only does not apply on import (EX-79.md:44). - No new number. h, t_w, k₂, h_eff, G and t* come from the imports or from r. The step-3 record values appear only inside print strings, as mat:9 prints its W1 values (09_…py:133–145) and mat:12 keeps a printed-only RECORD (12_…py:24–25).

Order of calls in the script. 1. Complex guard, copied from 09_…py:76–81. 2. Structural checks. 3. r = _run_walled(return_fields=True). This is the only EM solve: four drives inside _run_heated. 4. The setup figure (the mesh is built inside the call, as in EX-79, EX-79.md:87). 5. Asserts. 6. Control (h-swap). 7. XDMF. 8. Prints on rank 0.

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script at the imported bands; each printed beside its step-3 record). - (R) the resistance algebra: r["R"] ≤ R_BAND (1e-12). Record 4.985e-16 (W1:80). If (R) is red, r carries no other keys (the early return), so the script asserts (R) first and stops. - (E′) energy identity with the wall, per drive: r["Ep"][k] ≤ E_BAND. Records 6.661e-15 / 2.267e-14 / 1.133e-14 / 9.337e-15 (W1:1959, 1963, 1967, 1971). - (E) every wall run: max(r["E"].values()) ≤ E_BAND. Record worst 4.554e-14 (W1:1980). - (L0), presented as helper equivalence, not a limit. Assert r["L0"][k] ≤ B_BAND. Records 0 / 6.661e-16 / 2.220e-16 / 2.220e-16 (W1:1960, 1964, 1968, 1972). - Name it in prints and guide as "(L0) helper equivalence". _h_eff(H_GEL, 0, K2) returns exactly H_GEL (W1:81, "t_w = 0 limit h = 10.0"), so (L0) shows that the wall path with t_w = 0 is P1's code path to round-off. It is not an independent wall → 0 limit, and not physics. - This follows the 2026-10-06 18:00 review's reading (docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-06-daily-1800.md:49; the implementer's own caveat, MAT-18.md:481), which is pending the weekly's ratification (plan-archive.md:37694). - The guide never calls it "the wall → 0 limit". - If the 10-07 weekly words it differently before the slot runs, the guide's (L0) sentence takes the weekly's wording. The assertion and its band are unchanged either way. - (C4) with the wall: r["pairs"][k] ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND for the four cyclic θ 10 g pairs. Records 0.0402 / 0.0210 / 0.0292 / 0.0484 % (W1:1975–1978). - The wall effect, the +4.63 % move. Asserted only at the band a prior log backs. On every drive, r["W"][k] > W_CONTROL_FLOOR: the step-3 gate's own (W-ctl) assertion, backed by W1:1960–1972 and test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py:298–302. That band is listed as a control in (2) below. - The move's value is printed, not asserted: per drive r["ratio"][k] at .6f and 100·(ratio − 1) at .4f %, beside the record ratios 1.046316 / 1.046314 / 1.046316 / 1.046314 (+4.6316 / +4.6314 / +4.6316 / +4.6314 %, W1:1960, 1964, 1968, 1972). - Also printed: the .6f string-equality verdict, expected True. - Why printed, not asserted: - The gate module registers no record constant for ⟨θ⟩ or the ratio, so asserting against the value would restate a logged number. - Rule (a) licenses additive return keys and keywords, not new record constants. - No log has run step 3 twice. The .4e precedent (EX-97 ruling (3)) prints string equality unless the edge distance is known. - Here the edge distance is computable. The ratios recomputed from the 9-digit means (W1:1960–1972) are 1.0463160243 / 1.0463136690 / 1.0463164342 / 1.0463138453. The nearest .6f rounding edge is ≈ 6.6e-8 away, on k = 2. - The predicted two-run drift is ≲ 1e-12: P₁ reproduced its record at rel 2.598e-14 (W1:1928), and θ is normalised by G = 1 W / P₁. - So the reviewer may promote this check to asserted at ½ ulp of .6f, which the print-precision rule (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3835) allows. The draft does not; see open questions. - Printed (records, never asserted): - r["h_eff"] and r["h_lat"] (W1:81); - per drive r["mean_w"][k] and r["mean_p1"][k] at !r (W1:1960–1972, e.g. 1.206730553 / 1.153313650 K on k = 0); - the peak 10 g θ̄ with the wall and its ratio 1.029608 on k = 0 (W1:1979); - the q_h pairs (W1:1975–1978); - max|Im θ| (0, W1:1980); - global sub-cells (58 866, W1:1929), as size_global.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (d) asserted: a doubled source misses (E′) with the wall. Assert r["ctl_d"] > D_CONTROL_FLOOR (1e-3). - Backing, the same comparison on the same fixture: 1.000000 (W1:1974). - Ceiling: linearity fixes the miss at exactly 1 (2·G·P vs G·P). That is 1e3× D_CONTROL_FLOOR and 1e9× E_BAND, so the assertion asks only for > 1e-3. - (W-ctl) asserted: the wall is felt. Assert r["W"][k] > W_CONTROL_FLOOR (1e-6) per drive. - Backing: 4.631e-2 on all four drives (W1:1960–1972). - Ceiling: the wall can at most recover the surface loss up to the adiabatic ⟨θ⟩(t*) ≈ 1.326 K/W, against P1's 1.153. That is ≈ 15 % (MAT-18.md:447–449), so ≤ ≈ 1.5e5× the floor; the measured value is ≈ 4.6e4×. - (h-swap) predicted, printed, never asserted: the energy identity sees which h was used. - Evaluate _e_prime_h(sub, ds, r["wall_runs"][0], G·P[0], H_GEL)[0]: the k = 0 wall run, with the bare gel h in the surface term. Build ds as the fixture does (:151). - Prediction: the residual is conv·(H_GEL/h_eff − 1)/dep = 1.652412377346e-01 × 0.5263158 ≈ 8.697e-2, from W1:1959's surface term and deposit 1 W. - Ceiling: conv/dep < 1, so the residual is ≤ H_GEL/h_eff − 1 = t_w·H_GEL/k₂ ≈ 0.526. That is ≈ 8.7e7× E_BAND at the prediction. - No prior measurement of this comparison exists, so it is labelled predicted and printed beside 8.697e-02. It is never asserted. A miss of the prediction is reported in the outcome, not a stop. - What it demonstrates: a model that ignored the wall would be caught by the balance, not only by ⟨θ⟩. - No other control. Writing the XDMF is output, not a separation.

(3) Windows. Each Bash call that runs a window is foreground with timeout: 660000 and makes one bare, whole, repo-relative harness call. Nothing is chained or piped, and nothing runs beside another heavy window. 0. Orphan check, from a bare shell: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Then run the rubric's cache sweep (daily-review.md:426) as one bare call labelled EX-98-cache-sweep. Step 3's sweep took 84 s (20261006T200520Z_MAT-18-step3-cache-sweep.log:39). 1. This is MAT-18.md:458's W1 line with the label changed. -s is mandatory (rule (g)). 4. Dry run, after the script exists: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-98-dryrun "./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:14 -n 2 -t 590 --dry-run". It must print (complex build). 5. Flagged run of record, predicted [180, 300] s. - Basis: mat:9's flagged run on the same fixture was 162 s (EX-79.md:73), and step 3's wall part adds 31.4 s (W1:1981). The h-swap control (< 1 s) and twelve more P1 XDMF fields (≈ 5 s) are small. - Command: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh EX-98 'docker compose exec -T -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1 fem-em-solver bash -lc "cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 examples/materials/14_coil_driven_phantom_in_container_wall.py"' - EX-93 / EX-97 found that the runner's dry-run string omits -T and /workspace on PYTHONPATH (EX-97.md:112). Use this brief's line and note any other difference. 6. Control run. git add the PNG, then rerun the same line without -e FEM_EM_SETUP_FIGURES=1, labelled EX-98-control. Predicted [175, 290] s (mat:9's control was 157 s, EX-79.md:82). Compare at the band, never bitwise (2026-10-06 18:00 review §3, the EX-91 ruling; -n 2 MUMPS drift ≈ 1e-10): - Every assertion is green in both runs. - Integers are equal: global sub-cells and drive order. - (R), (E′), (E), (L0) and C4 each sit inside their imported band in both runs. - Per drive, mean_w and ratio agree within B_BAND relative (predicted ≲ 1e-12, from P₁'s rel 2.598e-14 to its record, W1:1928). A gap above B_BAND with every assertion green is reported in the outcome as a finding, not a stop; no gate governs two-window drift. - Measured seconds may differ. 7. Post-censuses: EX-98-post-figures / EX-98-post-docrefs, the step 1 commands with those labels. Write the prediction first: - figures: examples N → N + 1, ok +1, broken=0; - docrefs: runnable +1, dead=0, guide=0, exit != 1.

Output. - Setup figure examples/materials/figures/materials_14_coil_driven_phantom_in_container_wall_setup.png. Use mat:9's recipe (09_…py:107–123) on r["base"]["msh"] / ["cell_tags"]: conductor and port sheets shown, the air tag hidden, the phantom translucent, a z-slice. - The phantom's region name is formatted from r["h_eff"], e.g. f"phantom (gel; wall as series resistance, Robin h_eff {h_eff:.4g} W/m^2/K -- no wall cells)". No literal. - Title (≤ 130 characters): mat:14 -- container wall on the coil-driven gel phantom: series resistance h_eff, four drives (MAT-18 step 3). - Combined XDMF examples/materials/paraview_output/materials_14_coil_driven_phantom_in_container_wall_combined.xdmf. Write it on r["base"]["sub"] with facet_tags=r["base"]["ft"], so the Robin surface where h_eff acts is its own block, then adopt_host_ownership. It holds: - P1 theta_wall_k0..k3: wall_runs[k].temperature − T_INF at t*; - P1 theta_bare_k0..k3: base["T_star"][k] − T_INF, which is mat:9's field; - P1 dtheta_k0..k3: wall minus bare, built in the wall temperature's own function space; - DG0 q_h_k0..k3.

Name every Function (EX-79's Status 124: unnamed Functions collided in HDF5, EX-79.md:66–70). - Guide. - It opens with the wall model in words: a series resistance on the Robin surface, planar h_eff, no wall heat capacity, no wall cells. - It contrasts mat:12 (conforming shell, ball, imposed field) with mat:9 (same coil and phantom, no wall). - It reads (L0) as helper equivalence (above), and states the scope. - Run line: ./scripts/run_examples.sh -e mat:14 -n 2 -t 590. - ParaView recipe: colour by real_dtheta_k0 to see where the wall's extra heat sits; compare real_theta_wall_k0 and real_theta_bare_k0 along a Plot Over Line through the k = 0 hot spot; and apply a 90° Transform about z (theta_wall_k1 onto theta_wall_k0; the C4 pairs in numbers). - It describes in words why the hot-spot ratio (printed, ≈ 1.03) sits below the mean ratio (≈ 1.046): the wall acts at the surface. It quotes no number beyond the logged records, each cited. - The complex build writes real_ / imag_ splits, and the imaginary parts are zero. - ## Related lists mat:9 (examples/materials/09_coil_driven_heating_phantom.md), mat:12 (examples/materials/12_gel_ball_in_container_wall.md), tests/validation/test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py and tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py. Every artifact is named by its full filename (rule (b)).

(4) Traps already paid for. - Bare harness calls. Make each one repo-relative, whole, foreground, with nothing chained (&&, ;), piped or redirected, and no -k selection inside the quoted command. Pass timeout: 660000 on every window. Never background a window, never nest an executor and never delete a log. - -s on the re-gate (rule (g)). Use FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 and source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode on every EM window. - Orphans. Run pgrep -c python3 (via docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver … from a bare shell) before the cache sweep. Sweep only at 0, with the targeted stem delete only; a partial 44 KB orphan .c is a live lock (MAT-15 item 160). A stall in MPI_Bcast means sweep, never retry. - The step-3 sweep's $ trap: the first attempt failed host-side on unescaped $ (20261006T200510Z_MAT-18-step3-cache-sweep.log, MAT-18.md:481). Copy the rubric's line with its \$ escapes. - Rule (i). Make no edit to the gate module after the re-gate window, and none to the script or guide after the last window. - A pytest fixture cannot be called. That is why the lift exists. With return_fields=False it must stay byte-identical; check by reading the re-gate's prints against W1. - Rank-local counts. cell_tags.values and assemble_scalar are rank-local: use size_global or the module's _allsum. Every collective runs on every rank; rank-0 print blocks hold no collective (item 227). - Complex operands. Use no UFL ordering or sqrt comparison (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). Take np.real before every float. - No point evaluation on a create_submesh mesh (known-issues 2026-10-04, ANS-9; MAT-18.md:465). Every θ reading is an assembled integral; profiles are drawn in ParaView only. - No AED number enters the script or guide. Write ≈, never ~.

(5) Scope. - Covered: MAT-18 step 3's series-resistance wall on MAT-15 P1's untuned 10 MHz, σ = 800 S/m F-small fixture, at degree 1, -n 2, with gel constants and G = 1 W / P₁. - Not claimed: - a conforming wall on the coil-driven phantom; - the wall's heat storage; - contact resistance; - a real container's properties or geometry, or the lateral cylindrical h, which is printed only; - the wall → 0 limit as physics ((L0) is helper equivalence); - absolute temperature (1 W normalisation); - a tuned or copper coil, or 64 MHz; - perfusion, tissue, probe B or ANS-9; - convergence. - No new physics, and no src/ change. The MAT-18 row and §10 P11 are unchanged by this item.

(6) Negative result. In every case below: report the measurement and stop, journal it in docs/testing/attempts.md, park on attempt/EX-98, mark item 299 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)), and leave EX-98 ⬜. Never widen a band. - Re-gate red, or its digits off W1 beyond ≈ 1e-11: the lift changed behaviour. Revert it and report; the step-3 record stands on W1. - An example assertion red with the re-gate green: a divergence finding. Write a known-issues entry; no band moves. - (W-ctl) does not miss: h_eff never reached the solver. Stop. - Census not +1, or broken > 0: fix it once; otherwise park. - A docker-socket denial: stop and report.

A run killed at 590 s is not a result: check orphans and stop. The fallback is a re-queue, never a longer timeout. The (h-swap) prediction or the .6f verdict missing is printed and reported, not a stop.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

(7) Status it can move. The EX-98 §7 row moves ⬜ → ✅ (Done-when met, elapsed recorded). Census examples +1 with broken=0; docrefs runnable +1. The review adds the row (proposed above) in the same commit as this item (rule (j)). Phase 8 (8a) gains its first runnable example of the wall on a coil-driven phantom. MAT-18 stays ✅ with its row unchanged, and MAT-15 stays as it is.

Review rulings (2026-10-07 10:30 daily review, item 299). (1) Rule (a) lift into _run_walled(*, return_fields=False), with the step-3 module re-gated green in the same slot and disclosed: accepted (EX-79 precedent). (2) The +4.63 % ⟨θ⟩(t*) move stays printed, with its string-equality verdict beside W1, and is not asserted. No second run of step 3 exists, so rule (e) gives no backing for an asserted band. The asserted control is (W-ctl) > W_CONTROL_FLOOR, which W1 backs. (3) The (h-swap) control is printed only (predicted 8.7e-2, unbacked). (4) (L0) is presented as "helper equivalence", not as a limit. If tonight's weekly words it differently before the slot runs, the guide takes the weekly's wording, and no assertion or band changes. (5) Flag-vs-control compares per-drive ⟨θ⟩ and the ratio, printed with a verdict against B_BAND. A gap above B_BAND with every assertion green is reported, not a stop (the -n 2 drift is ≈ 1e-10). (6) The orphan check from a bare shell is docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3. (7) The floor counts it at the example median (7). Heavy examples with a re-gate have taken ≈ 15 (EX-96), which the slot should expect.

Outcome (2026-10-07, 12:00 CDT slot): ✅ DONE. Rule (a) lift disclosed: walled() body moved into _run_walled(*, return_fields=False) in tests/validation/test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py (fixture is return _run_walled(); True adds base and wall_runs). (R) 4.985e-16; (E′) 7.327e-15 / 3.334e-16 / 1.777e-15 / 1.145e-14; (E) 4.656e-14; (L0) helper equivalence ≤ 5.551e-16; C4 0.0402 / 0.0210 / 0.0292 / 0.0484 % (equal to W1); (d) 1.000000; (W-ctl) 4.6316e-2 / 4.6314e-2 / 4.6316e-2 / 4.6314e-2; .6f verdict True; (h-swap) printed 8.6969e-2 against the predicted 8.697e-2. docs.title: EX-99 — A duty-cycled coil drive heats the gel phantom: the on/off history, Duhamel's sum and the half-power stand-in (history)
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

EX-99 (mat:15) was opened 2026-10-07 by the 10:30 daily review under daily-review.md step 5 (§5.4 ramp). MAT-17 step 3 (§9 item 271, §10 chain P12, 20261006T201547Z_MAT-17-step3-W1.log) closed two identities on MAT-15 P1's coil-driven F-small gel phantom under a 50 % duty schedule: Duhamel superposition at 3.421e-14 (:1970) and the energy identity at ≤ 3.743e-14 (:1976). No example shows a duty-cycled schedule on a coil-driven source: - mat:9 (EX-79) drives the same phantom with a source that never switches off; - mat:11 (EX-85) switches a uniform source on MAT-9's ball.

The angle here is the drive plus the time history. mat:14 belongs to a sibling item (EX-98, the container wall on the coil phantom). This item writes mat:15 only.

docs.title: §9 item 300 — 2026-10-07 (§5.4 example; example-runner)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-07 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it.

EX-99 (mat:15) adds: - examples/materials/15_duty_cycled_coil_heating_phantom.py; - a same-stem guide, 15_duty_cycled_coil_heating_phantom.md, with the three required headings plus ## Setup figure and ## Related; - the setup PNG examples/materials/figures/materials_15_duty_cycled_coil_heating_phantom_setup.png (≤ 600 KiB; mat:9's, made with the same recipe, is 442 KiB, EX-79.md:56).

run_examples.sh lists examples/materials/*.py by glob and selects by the zero-padded prefix 15_ (scripts/run_examples.sh:129, 206). No registry edit is needed, and the item does not need mat:14 to exist.

  • Executor: example-runner. The executor does not spawn agents.
  • Tier: heavy; -n 2, complex. Runner -t 590; container timeout -k 30 590, the same ceiling as step 3's W1 (MAT-17.md:278).
  • Cost: ≈ 7 measured (example class median, items 278 / 279 / 280 / 296 / 297 = 7 / 6 / 7 / 15 / 7 min, docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-07-daily-1030.md:12–16) / ≈ 55 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 20 for the lift, script and guide + ≈ 20 for windows: three heavy windows of ≈ 4–5 min each, plus censuses, dry run and sweep.
  • The honest expectation is ≈ 15–20 min of wall clock in windows. EX-96's two heavy windows measured 15 min in all (2026-10-07-daily-1030.md:15).
  • Depends on: nothing open. MAT-17 step 3 is on main (d8191042), and so is MAT-15 step 1's _run_heated lift (04c3850d).
  • Never beside another heavy window.
  • Spawn prompt (the slot puts these sentences in verbatim): "Use the example-runner agent to execute EX-99, §9 item 300 (docs/planning/chunks/EX-99.md, heading §9 item 300). Do not spawn agents. Run every harness window in the foreground (Bash timeout: 660000) and never background one; do not end the turn while a window runs. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Make no edit to the script or guide after its last window."

What is new, and what is not. No new physics. Every asserted quantity is one that step 3's module already computes, with a band that module already holds. The example adds three things: - the time history: ⟨θ⟩(tₙ) at all 41 full-step indices, for the duty run and for the continuous run at half power, written to a CSV and a ParaView time series; - the fields at t*, at the end of the last on phase, and of the half-power stand-in; - a guide that reads the drive, the schedule and Duhamel's sum together.

Step 3's module stores only SNAPS = (32, 35, 36, 39, 40) (test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py:73), so the history needs two extra thermal runs (≈ 3.4 s each, …201547Z_MAT-17-step3-W1.log:1956). The anchor (Hist) below ties those runs to the gate's runs.

Code (rule (a), disclosed; precedent EX-79's _run_heated lift, EX-79.md:17, which the 2026-10-02 03:00 review accepted as within rule (a)). Two additive edits to tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py, and nothing else: 1. _transient_s(sub, ft, q, schedule, *, snapshot_steps=SNAPS) (:86–93). The body passes snapshot_steps=snapshot_steps. The default is the old literal, so every existing call is byte-identical. 2. Move the body of the duty() fixture (:109–245) verbatim into a module-level _run_duty(*, return_fields=False). The fixture becomes return _run_duty(). - With False, the prints and the keys of out stay byte-identical. - With True, it adds base (the _run_heated(return_fields=True) dict), r_duty, r_one, r_d, q0, dep, sub, ft and ds. - The seven test functions and both band literals (L_BAND, D_BAND, :64–65) are untouched.

Edit no other gate module. ans:9 imports _run_heated from MAT-15's module, which this item does not touch, and nothing imports the step-3 module (checked at drafting). No src/ change.

Imports (never restated). - from tests.validation import test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven as m17s3, and from it: _run_duty, _transient_s, _chi_duty, L_BAND, D_BAND, E_BAND, D_CONTROL_FLOOR, DUTY, DT, HALF, N_MAIN, N_ON_LAST, SNAPS, T_INF, T_STAR, _allsum. - from tests.validation import test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom as m15, test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere as m12, and PHANTOM_CELL_TAG. - from tests.validation.test_mat5_em_coupled_sphere import L0_BAND (:104). It is used only for the flag-vs-control comparison of printed records. - Setup-figure names as in 09_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:45–64: PORT_LOWER, PORT_UPPER, LEG_COUNT and CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG. - From src: the fem_em_solver.io.paraview_utils writers (write_xdmf_with_tags, write_xdmf_time_series, adopt_host_ownership) and fem_em_solver.post.setup_figure.write_setup_figure. - Structural checks (asserted, printed): m17s3.E_BAND is m12.E_BAND, m17s3.D_CONTROL_FLOOR is m15.D_CONTROL_FLOOR, m17s3._run_heated is m15._run_heated and m17s3.T_STAR is m15.T_STAR. - No new number. The script states no k, ρc, h, frequency, period, duty or band. Each comes from the imports, or from the returned dicts, or is the integer step index. The one exception is range(N_MAIN + 1), which is the full set of snapshot indices.

Order of calls. Complex guard (copied from 09_…py:76–81) → structural checks → r = _run_duty(return_fields=True) (one EM fixture plus step 3's 13 thermal runs) → setup figure on r["base"]["msh"] / ["cell_tags"] → h_duty = _transient_s(sub, ft, q0, _chi_duty, snapshot_steps=range(N_MAIN + 1)) → h_one = _transient_s(sub, ft, q0, lambda t: 1.0, snapshot_steps=range(N_MAIN + 1)) → readings → asserts → CSV / XDMF.

(1) Anchors (asserted in-script at the imported bands; each printed beside its step-3 record). - (S) The schedule. Assert r["chi_binary"], and that h_duty.source_multipliers == r["r_duty"].source_multipliers (exact list equality: χ is computed from the integer step index). Print the 41-character string beside 11111000011110000111100001111000011110000 and the on-time beside 627.0000 s (:1956). - (Δ) Duhamel superposition. r["Delta"] ≤ L_BAND. Record 3.421e-14 (:1970). - (D′) Duty 1 is P1. r["D"] ≤ D_BAND. Record 2.119e-15 (:1959). - (E) Every run balances. Every value in r["E"] ≤ E_BAND, and so are h_duty.max_balance_residual and h_one.max_balance_residual. Record: worst of 12 runs 3.743e-14 (:1976). - (E′) The energy identity from the EM side. r["Ep_N"] ≤ E_BAND (record 3.317e-15, :1957) and r["Ep_on"] ≤ E_BAND (record 1.399e-14, :1958). Both are normalised by the unscheduled G·P₁, as the module does. - (Hist) The history runs are the gate's runs. This is a new comparison held at an imported band; predicted ≤ 1e-15 (the same call on the same inputs in the same process). - Whole-submesh relative L2 of h_duty.temperature against r["r_duty"].temperature ≤ D_BAND. - The same for h_one.temperature against r["base"]["T_star"][0]. - At each n in SNAPS, h_duty.snapshots[n] against r["r_duty"].snapshots[n] ≤ D_BAND. - Compute every norm with m17s3._allsum and np.real, the way the module's _l2sq does (:123–126). - Records, printed beside :1973–1975, never asserted (the gate asserts none of them): - duty ⟨θ⟩(t*) 0.568835514 K against D·P1 0.576656825 K, ratio 0.986437; - the last on/off pair 0.466250330 → 0.584438780 → 0.568835514 K; - the 10 g ball at c₀, duty / (D·P1) 0.967065; - max|Im θ| 0.

Print each at the gate's format and at !r. At the gate's 9 decimals the resolution (≈ 1.8e-9 relative on 0.57 K) is coarser than L0_BAND, so the flag-vs-control comparison needs the full digits.

(2) Negative controls (rule (e)). - (Δ-ctl) asserted: one Duhamel term dropped. Assert r["Delta_ctl"] > L_BAND. - Backing, the same comparison on the same fixture at -n 2: 0.298210 (:1971). - Ceiling. Dropping m = 9 leaves θ_duty − Σ′ = −θ[H₉] up to the (Δ) residual. So the miss is ‖θ[H₉]‖ / ‖θ_duty‖ to ≈ 3e-14, which is ≈ 3.0e11× L_BAND. The assertion asks only for > 1×. No saturation applies: the comparator is not bounded by 1. - (d) printed, not asserted: the doubled source, at both placements. - Print r["ctl_d"] (n = 36, the last on-step; record 1.000000) and r["ctl_d_N"] (N = 40, off-step, blind by linearity; record 2.942e-15), both from :1972, each labelled with its step and χ. - How this avoids pre-empting the weekly. The 2026-10-06 18:00 review accepted the move of (d) to n = 36 provisionally and sent it to the 10-07 weekly to ratify (docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-06-daily-1800.md:48, :69). So: - the example asserts no (d), and its asserted control is (Δ-ctl), which does not depend on that ruling; - the gate module keeps asserting (d) where it does now, and the re-gate window runs that assertion as the module's own; - the guide describes what the module asserts and why (at N the source is off, so a doubled source cannot show in the balance), and calls the placement neither ratified nor provisional; it points to docs/planning/chunks/MAT-17.md for the ruling. - If the weekly changes the module before this item runs, step 0 stops it (see (5)). - (c-sched) printed, predicted: the schedule ignored. Print the whole-submesh relative L2 ‖θ[1] − θ_duty‖ / ‖θ_duty‖ at t*. It has never been measured. - The triangle inequality on logged norms bounds it to [1.067, 3.067]. Drafted by a read-only Plan agent and reviewed by the 2026-10-02 18:00 daily review.

GEO-1: the partition test onto the graded control. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, real build, -n 2 then -n 1. - Cost: ≈ 4 measured / ≈ 15 predicted min. - Depends on: nothing. Attempt: 1 of 4.

Why this is queueable. - The red test. test_birdcage_volumes_partition_the_box (test_birdcage_port_tags.py:145–258) is the 🔴 known-issues entry of 2026-08-27. It calls birdcage_port_domain ungraded, and that call aborts with "overlapping facets" on 0.11. - The floor is ruled. The 08-30 weekly ruled that floor a documented, uncommissioned limitation (2026-08-25 entry): "every gate that reads this generator is green on a graded control (h_c = 4.8e-3, ruling (b) of 08-26)". - This is the one call site never moved. GEO-21 step 2 and GEO-23 step 2b each moved a call site under that ruling, not a band. This test is the exception (GEO-23 row, "a review's call"). - The weekly named the fix. The 09-30 weekly named it as GEO-1's known-issues fix.

Review ruling (2026-10-02 18:00). This review extends the 08-26 ruling (b) to this last call site. The move is the same one GEO-21 and GEO-23 made: a test-side sizing move, with every identity and band unchanged and the ungraded floor asserted as a control. It is not a generator fix (uncommissioned, 08-30 weekly), and not a loosening: the identities stay at 1e-9. The weekly ratifies the ruling.

Edit: tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_tags.py only. The edit is additive and removes no name, since ten modules import from this file. - The constant. Add GRADED_CONTROL_RESOLUTION = 4.8e-3, version-tagged (0.11 image), citing the GEO-21 ladder (test_birdcage_conductor_sizing.py:65–101). - The partition test. - Pass the constant as conductor_resolution. - Its docstring cites the 08-26 ruling (b), the 08-30 weekly, both known-issues entries and this ruling. - Print the global cell count. - (A0) Inside the test function, import BASELINE_CONTROL_RESOLUTION and assert it equals the new constant. Import it at function level: a module-level import would be circular. - The negative control. Add test_ungraded_build_still_hits_the_documented_floor as the last test in the module. - Call with conductor_resolution=None inside pytest.raises(Exception). - Rank 0's message contains "overlapping facets". Every other rank's contains "birdcage_port_domain geometry generation failed on rank 0" (mesh.py:4028–4040). - Assert comm.allreduce(caught) == comm.size. - Asserted, with backing: 20260828T140313Z_GEO-23-step1b-birdcagepart-n1.log and the -n 2 log 20260828T140326Z… measured this exact call.

Printed, not asserted.

Windows. Bare, foreground, timeout: 660000. - W1 (≈ 70 s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-1-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/mesh/test_birdcage_conductor_sizing.py tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_tags.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W2 (≈ 25 s): the same with -n 1 and without the conductor-sizing module, labelled GEO-1-W2.

Keep the raise-control last and the importer module first, as ordered above. - Never call the ungraded build outside pytest.raises. - Do not touch test_birdcage_conductor_sizing.py. - Run hygiene: use -s, and make no edit after W2. - File sharing with item 184. Item 184 imports from this module but does not edit it; the two items are independent.

Scope: - No src/ change, no band move, no re-record. - The 2026-08-25 entry (the generator floor) stays OPEN. Its Retire-when gains: "the item-186 control goes red".

Status it can move: - GEO-1 🧪 → ✅ on the row this review amended (rule (j)). - Known-issues 2026-08-27 retires: its test-red is gone, and the limitation lives on in 2026-08-25.

Negative result: - An identity is red at 4.8e-3: a regression since 08-26. Annotate the 08-27 entry and stop. - The phantom band misses: report and stop; never widen. - The control does not raise: the floor moved. Record the cell count and stop. Retiring 08-25 is the review's decision, and only after it re-measures the ladder. - Any stop: park and mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

docs.title: GEO-20 — High-pass birdcage ring-gap port layout (ring_gap_length, 2·leg_count ports, the GEO-18 pattern on the end rings)
docs.text: High-pass birdcage ring-gap port layout (ring_gap_length, 2·leg_count ports, the GEO-18 pattern on the end rings) — 32-port directive item (b); step 1 at 4 legs, step 2 at 16 after GEO-19 (commissioned 2026-08-23 weekly review) | ✅ (audited COMPLIANT 2026-08-29 10:30 review — both step-2 logs Status 0 at 188 / 184 s, 1 passed on every rank stream, 40 port lines per log at 1.000000000000 and 0 off-digit, every assert a reduced closed-form/symmetry identity at 1e-9 / 1e-12 / 1e-6 / 5e-3, module byte-identical to the parked attempt, nothing loosened. Two prose corrections, gate unaffected: the C32 sheet spread is 4.985e-16 at -n 2 and 4.488e-16 at -n 12 — it moves at the 1e-16 floor like the C16 value, so "only one digit moves" undercounts; and the 16-leg terminal "spread 2.572e-07 against the 1e-5 band" is std/mean, printed not asserted — the 1e-5 RING_TERMINAL_RATIO_BAND gates the 4-leg control only, the 16-leg terminals are gated by [0.95, 1.0] plus the per-class 1e-6 / 5e-3.) (step 1 ✅ 2026-08-24 — the 8 ring ports exist at 4 legs and every pre-stated gate is green twice in-slot: terminal 0.974455 of the closed-form 2·π·r_ring² inside the [0.95, 1.0] inscribed band and equal across the 8 to ≈ 2e-8 (gate 1e-5; digit corrected by the 10:30 review audit — see the prose entry), closure and port-volume 1.000000000000, sheet meshed/analytic 1.000000000000 with out-of-plane spread 5.042e-18 m, C4 and top/bottom-mirror spreads below 1e-12, GEO-9 partition green, conductor 0.969275 ≥ 0.95; negative controls green — kwarg off reproduces the uncut birdcage and the leg+ring mesh is a 12-port mesh with both identity families exact. Step 2 (16 legs, 32 ports) is serial on GEO-19. Step 2 attempt 1 2026-08-28 — negative result, parked on attempt/GEO-20-step2-20260828T094500Z, no band landed. The 16-leg ring-gapped fixture builds (265 621 cells, 48 ports = 16 leg + 32 ring) and is green at -n 1 (20260828T093352Z_GEO-20-step2-probe1.log, 1 passed / 275 s) but red at -n 2 on the identical geometry (20260828T093839Z_GEO-20-step2-record.log, Status 1 / 198 s): three of the 32 ring sheets do not reconstruct — P30 and P37 at 0 facets, P45 at 5 facets / 0.315302109223 of w² — against 1.000000000000 on the other 29, and P30's boundary closure reads 0.981164653445 against 1e-9. Everything not routed through a sheet is exact at both widths: 32/32 port volumes 1.000000000000 of 2·R·w²·tan α, GEO-9 partition and air-box closure 1.000000000000, ring arcs against Pappus 1.000000000000, conductor 0.976465 of CAD, no phantom contact. The terminals are the finding that did land as information: all 32 read 0.974454791–0.974455668, spread 2.572e-07, i.e. the ring family shows no azimuth-class split at 16 legs where the leg family split three ways at 8.434e-04 (GEO-19 step C) — the ruled per-class bands were applied from the start and would have passed, as would the flat 1e-5. Both negative controls reproduce digit for digit in the same run: kwarg off at 16 legs 307 296 cells / C16 sheet spread 1.331e-15 (ratio 1.000000), and the 4-leg ring rung 110 786 cells (ratio 1.000000) with one azimuth class at intra 4.198e-08. Cost rung measured and citable (a cell count and a wall time, not a reconstruction reading): 4 → 16 legs ring-gapped 110 786 → 265 621 cells (2.3976×), mesh 23.30 → 72.23 s (3.1003×) — cheaper than the leg-gapped 16-leg build's 307 296 / 72.23 s. Known-issues entry opened; the rank-width dependence is not diagnosed, the hypothesis is _interface_facet_tags matching on owned cells only, and the -n 4/-n 8 discriminator costs no src/ change. A fix in _interface_facet_tags touches every module that reconstructs a sheet and could move existing records — a review's ruling, not an in-slot fix. Cause diagnosed 2026-08-28, interactive session — and it is not in _interface_facet_tags: birdcage_port_domain is built with no partitioner, i.e. GhostMode.none, so an interior port facet on a partition boundary has no second cell to read a tag from. The class is width-driven, not leg-count-driven — the 4-leg 12-port rung is exact at -n 1/2/4/8 and loses one air facet at -n 12 (P8 closure 0.990103697427), and the same mesh reads 1.000000000000 on all 12 with shared_facet plumbed. The fix and the re-record sweep are GEO-24; see the re-headed known-issues entry. Step 2a ✅ 2026-08-28 (15:00 slot) — the ownership table is measured on the 32-port fixture at -n 4 and -n 8 (Status 1 / 189 s each, no src/ change): the broken-sheet set moves with the width — {P25, P29, P37, P41, P45} at 4 and {P17, P21, P26, P30, P37, P44, P48} at 8 against {P30, P37, P45} at 2, neither new set nested in the old — and is identical to the set of ports whose two half-boxes are not owned by one rank, symmetric difference empty both ways at both widths, 32 × 2 with no exception; the 4-leg control is 0 broken / 0 straddling at both. All 40 port volumes, both closures and Pappus stay 1.000000000000 and both cell-count controls reproduce at ratio 1.000000, so the defect is confined to facet reconstruction. Confirmed ⇒ stop per the ruling; chunk stays 🟡, the fix is GEO-24's. Step 2 attempt 2 queued by the 2026-08-29 03:00 review as §9 item 4 — a re-run of the parked module (31c08ed, the one file on the attempt branch) at -n 2 and -n 12 once the GEO-24 plumb is on main (§9 item 1); the plumb repaired both 4-leg -n 12 reds at unchanged cell counts, so the prediction is zero broken sheets at any width. Unblocked 2026-08-29, 06:00 slot: GEO-24 closed (step 2b green on the validation family at both widths), so the re-run may proceed and step 1's "closure and volume/analytic 1.000000000000 on all 12" loses its width-conditional caveat — it is measured true at 12 ranks on the plumbed tree, port P8 reading 176 air facets / closure 1.000000000000 where it read 175 / 0.990103697427. Step 2 attempt 2 ✅ 2026-08-29, 09:00 slot — the re-run is green at BOTH widths and the chunk closes. The parked module (31c08ed, tests/mesh/test_birdcage_ring_gaps_scaleup.py, +569 lines, restored by git checkout — the generator signature had not moved) is 1 passed at -n 2 (20260829T140037Z_GEO-20-step2-rerun-n2.log, Status 0 / 188 s) and at -n 12 (…140402Z_…-rerun-n12.log, Status 0 / 184 s), standard tier, real, -s, -k 30 570. The plumb's prediction — zero broken sheets at any width — is confirmed: attempt 1's three reds are repaired, P30 and P37 back to 176 air facets from 0, P45 to 180 facets / closure 1.000000000000 from 5 / 0.315302109223. Both in-run negative controls reproduce digit for digit at both widths: kwarg off at 16 legs 307 296 cells (ratio 1.000000) and the 4-leg ring rung 110 786 cells (ratio 1.000000) with one azimuth class at intra 4.198e-08; the only digit that moves anywhere is the C16 sheet spread at the 1e-15 roundoff floor (1.331e-15 at -n 2, 1.210e-15 at -n 12 — GEO-24 step 1a saw the same pair, reported not a failure). docs.title: GEO-23 — The 0.11 "Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets)" family: one owner for the three OPS-26 census reds (coil+phantom generator, birdcage_port_domain …
docs.text: The 0.11 "Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets)" family: one owner for the three OPS-26 census reds (coil+phantom generator, birdcage_port_domain partition test, and the rank-dependent test_boundary_condition_selection.py deadlock) plus the dead test_cylindrical_domain.py module — classify each as geometry-deterministic or partition-dependent, ladder the resolution, land no fix (commissioned 2026-08-27 03:00 review; four known-issues entries of 2026-08-27). Step 1 ✅ 2026-08-28 (09:00 slot) — all four sites are geometry-deterministic, red at -n 1 (2–4 s, Status 1); the two "rank-dependent" claims are log-interleave artifacts, withdrawn by measurement; the -n 2 deadlock is a raise-path property (row 2's wrapped re-raise footers at Status 1 in 5 s where the three unwrapped sites cost 120 s each); both laddered generators are monotone, each failing exactly one 0.8-step above a meshing sizing (cylindrical_domain 0.040 → meshes 0.032/1 213 cells; coil_phantom_domain 0.030 → meshes 0.024/5 464 cells); the four sites are three generators (the two phantom modules share one byte-identical call); the recorded IndexError … size 0 signature is in-process gmsh contamination, not a second defect; control green at unmoved bands; the dead module is now one asserting 1e-9 partition test. Step 2 (a review's call) has two measured, separable levers — sizing and raise-path. Step 2a ✅ 2026-08-28 (12:00 slot) — the raise-path lever landed: one shared _raise_geometry_failure_on_every_rank helper wraps the rank-0 gmsh build in straight_wire_domain, cylindrical_domain and coil_phantom_domain (git diff -w = +76 lines, 0 deletions — the rest is indentation). All three deadlocking rows of the step-1 table now footer at Status 1 in 2–3 s where step 1 recorded Status 124 at 120–121 s, summaries unchanged, each non-building rank's traceback ending in the wrapped RuntimeError naming generator and resolution; GEO-22's gate (tests/mesh/test_geometry_failure_is_collective.py, the allreduced caught flag at h = 0.00875) is 1 passed in 0.91s at -n 2. Controls green and unmoved: the three modules at -n 1 exactly as step 1, mag:1 at 21 830 cells / 6.666667e-05 T, test_cylindrical_domain.py 1 passed, test_coil_phantom_mesh.py 3 passed, the GEO-21 control 36.76 s. Twelve windows, 72 s. The three census reds stay red (geometry reds, step 2b's) but cost seconds to observe. Step 2b (sizing) is the only step left. Step 2b ✅ 2026-08-28 (13:30 slot) ⇒ chunk ✅ — the sizing lever landed and all three census reds are green: three call sites moved to step 1's coarsest measured meshing rung (test_boundary_condition_selection.py:26 0.04 → 0.032, test_phantom_material_model.py:110 and test_phantom_field_metrics.py:35 0.03 → 0.024), each with the step-1 ladder in-comment and a reduced global cell-count print. Every module green at both widths: bcsel 3 passed, 1 skipped at -n 1 (0.94 s) and -n 2 (0.80 s) real, phantom-material 4 passed at -n 1 (2.66 s) and -n 2 (1.63 s) complex, phantom-metrics 2 passed at -n 1 (1.71 s) and -n 2 (1.67 s) complex — against the census reds' 1 failed, 2 passed, 1 skipped / 1 failed, 3 passed / 1 failed, 1 passed. The printed counts are 1213 and 5464 / 5464, reproducing the step-1 ladder's 1 213 / 5 464 exactly (0.00% against the pre-stated ±1%), so the sizing is stable run-to-run and across rank width. No physics assertion moved — the negative result this step existed to expose did not occur, and since no module pins a cell count the only assertions at risk were physics ones. Controls: test_cylindrical_domain.py at its unmoved 0.02 1 passed in 1.29s at -n 2, and the complex tests/environment gate 11 passed before the complex windows. src/ untouched; git diff --stat is three test files plus docs. Eight footered windows, 40 s recorded elapsed, FFCx stub sweep clean before window 1 and no exit 124 in the slot. The three geometry known-issues entries are RETIRED (both halves closed — 2a's deadlock, 2b's geometry). Residual, and a review's call, not this chunk's: the fourth site the chunk was commissioned over — test_birdcage_volumes_partition_the_box on birdcage_port_domain — is still red and was never laddered here, because its resolution floor is already GEO-21's open entry and its fixture is GEO-20's; no GEO-23 step remains for it. Demoted ✅ → 🧪 by the 2026-08-28 18:00 review audit (§4 clause 3). The step-2b anchor — 1213 / 5464 cells reproducing step 1's ladder at ±1% — is a print at each of the three call sites, compared by the reader against a comment; no test asserts it. The only assertion 2a/2b added (test_geometry_failure_is_collective.py:60, total_caught == comm.size) is a did-raise property, and the three re-greened modules' own gates are finiteness/positivity except a pre-existing σ/ε DG0 identity (test_phantom_material_model.py:139,185) that 2b did not add. Logs, agent execution and elapsed all check out (20 footered windows, 112 s); nothing was loosened; src/ untouched. Step 2c (queued, §9 item 1): turn each of the three prints into an asserted abs(n_global / N_REF − 1) ≤ 0.01 against the step-1 ladder value (a documented reference from a prior run, §4 3(iv)), allreduced before the assert; on green the chunk returns to ✅.
