docs.title: GEO-25 — F-human cost probe
docs.text: F-human cost probe — birdcage_port_domain at ring_radius 0.07 → 0.15 m (30 cm coil, the operator's 2026-08-25 directive), a parameter set on the existing constructor, not a new one; cell count and mesh time per rung, conductor sizing not coarser than the 4.8 mm floor without re-measuring it (known-issues GEO-21 ruling) | ✅ step 2 closed 2026-09-05 13:30 implementer slot — the §3 route back was walked, the row is ✅ again. New tests/validation/test_birdcage_f_human_rung.py, 2 passed in 194.05s, Elapsed 196 s, heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 560), -n 2, real build, docs/testing/logs/20260905T183654Z_GEO-25.log:20030. Every step-1 reading now reproduces at -n 2 as an executed assert, to the digit. Branch B (the fixture, scale_sizing=False): cells 504 642 vs record 504 642, relative 0.000e+00 at the imported CELL_COUNT_BAND = 0.01; volume partition 1.000000000000 at the imported GEO-18 EXACT = 1e-9; terminal-area ratio 0.974454791 … 0.974455230 on all 32 ring ports, inside the GEO-19 closed-form [0.95, 1.0]; meshed/CAD conductor 0.965414, clearing the imported CAD_MASS_GATE = 0.95 by +0.015414 (:9730–9735, mesh 109.35 s). Branch A (the negative control, scale_sizing=True): cells 204 977 vs record 204 977, relative 0.000e+00; the same partition and terminal identities hold (0.974445583 … 0.974446474); meshed/CAD 0.893028, i.e. 0.056972 BELOW the same gate (:20017–20022, mesh 63.50 s). The separation assert control < CAD_MASS_GATE <= fixture reads 0.893028 < 0.95 ≤ 0.965414, separation 0.072387 (:20024–20027) — fixed absolute mesh sizing is now a gated conclusion, not an ungated reading: a similar-mesh F-human coil fails the existing GEO-15/GEO-21 conductor-mass gate and the fixed-sizing one clears it. Two version-tagged cell records registered under the (1*) licence at tests/validation/test_birdcage_f_human_rung.py (F_HUMAN_BRANCH_B_CELL_RECORD, F_HUMAN_BRANCH_A_CELL_RECORD), both asserted at the imported band and never at equality (the OPS-27 stale-exact class). The step-1 determinism worry is answered for this rung: the repeat was on the 0.10 m branch-A rung, and both 0.15 m rungs now reproduce at -n 2 in a different process at 0.000e+00 — no known-issues entry needed. _params moved verbatim into the gate module, which is now the single source of the F-human parameter set, and scripts/probes/geo25_ring_radius_cost_probe.py imports it (plus BASE_RING_RADIUS, LEG_COUNT) back; all 16 printed parameters verified unmoved against step 1's own log (20260905T184025Z_GEO-25.log vs 20260904T214031Z_GEO-25.log:36–50). Two builds per process, cached — the module never rebuilds a rung for a second assert. Nothing in src/ changed; no solve, no port gate, no physics claim. The step-1 measurement block below is untouched. ~~🧪 demoted ✅ → 🧪 by the 2026-09-04 18:00 review on the §3 rule~~ — a measurement-only step is 🧪, never ✅: the probe script says "asserts nothing" in its own docstring (scripts/probes/geo25_ring_radius_cost_probe.py:3) and contains no assert, so no executed quantitative assertion exists (audit DEMOTE, evidence re-read by the review). The commission text below said "anchors, asserted per rung" while naming mesh-probe as executor, whose definition says "never an assertion" — the two were in conflict and the executor followed its definition; the review's fault, not the slot's. Every measurement below stands untouched; the route back is step 2 (the gate) scoped at the end of this row. Rungs 1, 2 and 3 all measured, 2026-09-04 16:30 implementer slot (mesh-probe, six foreground windows, all Status 0, 554 s total). Negative control passed exactly: the 0.07 m rung reproduces mesh:9's 265 621 cells at relative 0.000e+00 (20260904T213333Z_GEO-25.log:10182,10190), terminal-ratio range 0.974454791–0.974455668 matching EX-35's record digit for digit. Volume partition 1.000000000000 and terminal ratio in [0.95, 1.0] on all 32 ports at every rung and both branches — the GEO-18/GEO-19 identities are genuinely scale-free. The row's phrase "phantom/air sizing scaled with the radius" is ambiguous (mesh size field vs geometric size), so the probe measured both branches rather than guess; the choice inverts the sign of the answer. Branch A (global resolution scales too — geometrically similar meshes): 0.07 m 265 621 cells / 72.35 s / 0.548 GiB (…213333Z:10182–10189); 0.10 m 244 056 / 67.82 s / 0.538 GiB (20260904T213508Z_GEO-25.log:10126–10133); 0.15 m 204 977 / 69.98 s / 0.505 GiB (20260904T213646Z_GEO-25.log:10331–10338). Branch B (resolution held at mesh:9's 0.015 m — fixed absolute element size, the only reading under which the r³ prediction is testable): 0.10 m 352 984 / 90.21 s / 0.627 GiB (20260904T213833Z_GEO-25.log:10248–10255); 0.15 m 504 642 / 112.27 s / 0.752 GiB (20260904T214031Z_GEO-25.log:9733–9740). The pre-registered r³ prediction is wrong on both readings — branch A 0.07→0.15 measures 204 977 against a predicted 2 613 618 (0.0784×, fitted exponent −0.34), branch B 0.0784→0.1931× (fitted exponent +0.84, time exponent +0.58). The mesh is dominated by the pinned 1.6 mm conductor refinement region, whose count grows roughly linearly with conductor length, not with domain volume; ≈ 0.84 is the honest cost exponent for the same coil made bigger at fixed absolute fidelity, and §10 Phase 6 should date itself from that, not from r³. The stop rule was never approached — worst rung 504 642 cells (17% of the 3 M ceiling), 112.27 s (19% of 600 s), peak RSS 0.752 GiB; conductor sizing never coarsened; rung 3 was licensed by the row's own arithmetic on both branches (3.375 × 67.816 = 228.9 s and 3.375 × 90.205 = 304.4 s, both < 600 s) and run. Determinism: the 0.10 m branch-A rung re-run in a fresh process reproduces every reported digit (20260904T214248Z_GEO-25.log:10126–10133); only wall time (67.82 → 68.55 s) and ru_maxrss move. No GEO-21-class negative result — every rung meshes, no mesher fallback and no invalid-boundary line in any log. One ungated reading for the weekly review: under branch A the conductor's meshed/CAD mass recovery falls monotonically 0.976465 → 0.959483 → 0.893028, so at 0.15 m it is below CAD_MASS_GATE = 0.95 — an F-human coil built by scaling the mesh sizing with the radius would fail the existing GEO-15/GEO-21 conductor-mass gate, while branch B stays 0.976465 → 0.972185 → 0.965414. That is an independent argument that fixed absolute sizing is the right scaling for this generator; nothing was asserted or moved on it. Probe script scripts/probes/geo25_ring_radius_cost_probe.py (measurement only, asserts nothing, imported by nothing). Two deviations, both disclosed: (a) conductor_resolution pinned at mesh:9's 1.6e-3 m, which is finer than the 4.8 mm GEO-21 figure — the rule as written is "not coarser than the floor", 4.8e-3 is GEO-21's coarse control (0.846 mass recovery), and 1.6 mm is the only value that reproduces the mandated 265 621-cell control; (b) leg_spacing scaled with coil_length (the row names only coil_length) — an unscaled 11 cm ring separation inside a 30 cm coil is not a similar geometry. Also unscaled and worth the weekly's attention: the conductor cross-section (leg_width, ring_minor_radius) is held at the 7 cm coil's values at every rung, so these are cost figures for a human-sized cage built from small-coil stock, not a re-proportioned conductor. A price, not a fixture: no record moved, no default changed, no solve, no assertion written. Original commission text follows. (commissioned 2026-08-30 02:15 weekly review; the ruling text was lost with that session — what survived is the dashboard summary and the GEO-21 known-issues ruling's two sentences. Re-scoped 2026-09-02 weekly review — queueable. Executor mesh-probe, measurement only, no solve. Ladder on the existing constructor: ring_radius 0.07 → 0.10 → 0.15 m with coil_length and the phantom radius scaled by the same factor (a 6 cm phantom in a 30 cm coil is not a load), 16 legs, ring-gap (high-pass) layout as mesh:9, conductor sizing pinned at the 4.8 mm GEO-21 floor, phantom/air sizing scaled with the radius. Anchors, asserted per rung: the scale-free CAD identities GEO-18/GEO-19 already gate — volume partition 1.000000000000 and terminal-area ratio in [0.95, 1.0] on every port; the cell count per rung against the r³ prediction from the 0.07 m rung (report the fitted exponent; GEO-19 measured 2.6472× cells / 3.2357× mesh time for 4 → 16 legs at fixed radius, the only cost rung above F-small on record). Stop rule (pre-registered): a rung whose mesh exceeds 3 M cells or 600 s is the finding — record it and stop, do not shrink the conductor sizing to make it fit. Negative control: the 0.07 m rung reproduces mesh:9's 265 621 cells at 0.000e+00 relative. Tier heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 1200, gmsh is serial so -n 1), three windows ≈ 5 + 12 + 30 min predicted from the r³ scaling. Scope: a price, not a fixture — no record moves, no default changes, no solve; the exponent and the 0.15 m cell count are what §10 Phase 6 dates itself from. Negative result: a rung that does not mesh is a GEO-21-class known-issues entry; §10 subgoal 4 is explicitly not blocked on it. Queued 2026-09-03 18:00 review as §9 item 5 (spare), sized to the 20-minute rule: rungs 1 and 2 only, rung 3 attempted only if 3.375 × t_2 < 600 s from rung 2's mesh time; otherwise the prediction is the finding and the 0.15 m rung is the weekly's to re-rung) Step 2 — the gate (scoped 2026-09-04 18:00 review, the §3 route back to ✅; §9 item 6). New tests/validation/test_birdcage_f_human_rung.py, -n 2, heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 600; the two builds measured 112.27 + 69.98 s at -n 1, so ≈ 200–250 s expected). Move the probe's _params(radius, scale_sizing=…) verbatim into the module as the single source of the F-human parameter set and have the probe import it (additive; the probe's printed digits must not move). Build the branch-B 0.15 m rung (scale_sizing=False) and assert, every band imported: (i) cells = 504 642 at CELL_COUNT_BAND — a new version-tagged record F_HUMAN_BRANCH_B_CELL_RECORD registered by this step under the (1*) licence; (ii) volume partition 1.000000000000 at the GEO-18 band; (iii) terminal-area ratio in [0.95, 1.0] on all 32 ports (the GEO-19 band); (iv) meshed/CAD conductor mass recovery ≥ CAD_MASS_GATE (0.95, imported from tests/mesh/test_birdcage_conductor_sizing.py:63) — measured 0.965414. Negative control: the branch-A 0.15 m rung (scale_sizing=True, second build in the same window) must read below CAD_MASS_GATE — measured 0.893028, 5.7 pp under against the fixture's 1.5 pp over; assert control < CAD_MASS_GATE <= fixture, margins printed, and its cells 204 977 reproduced at CELL_COUNT_BAND (a second record, control only). Traps: cell_tags.values and facet areas are rank-local — reduce before asserting (the probe already does); gmsh builds on rank 0; a build that fails at -n 2 deadlocks — both rungs are known to mesh, so -n 2 is licensed. Scope: registers the F-human branch-B rung's CAD identities and its cell record — not a solve, not a port gate, not a physics fixture; F-human physics stays Phase 6's and the weekly's. Negative result: cells not reproducing 504 642 at the band (the probe's determinism repeat was on the 0.10 m rung, not this one) is a known-issues entry with the measured spread and the record registered at the observed value with its band stated — never widened to swallow it; mass recovery below 0.95 on branch B is the finding that the F-human coil needs its own conductor sizing, known-issues entry, row stays 🧪.

docs.title: GEO-26 — Longitudinal ring-gap port sheets for birdcage_port_domain
docs.text: Longitudinal ring-gap port sheets for birdcage_port_domain — PORT-13 step 1 (2026-09-03, 22:30 slot) measured that GEO-20's ring sheets are the gap's transverse section at φ = φ_c (every one of the 8 sheets on the 4-leg rung spans ≤ 1.43e-17 m along its own φ̂ and exactly w along û and ẑ, 20260903T033437Z_PORT-13.log:6959–6966), so the lumped-sheet port model (ports/lumped.py, R_s = Z_p·w/h, I = (1/R_s)∫E·ĥ dS / h) has no h on the ring ports and E·ĥ on that sheet is the normal trace of an H(curl) field on an interior facet — not a defined quantity (log-pathologist ruling, 03:00 review). The GEO-18 pattern was carried to the rings by the wrong analogy: the leg sheet contains the drive direction and the radial direction (normal φ̂); the ring analogue contains φ̂ and one transverse direction. Design (ruled): a keyword-only ring_sheet_orientation: str = "transverse" (today's emission, default, every GEO-20 record frozen) with "longitudinal" emitting per ring gap the planar rectangle in the plane u = R — normal û(φ_c), spanning the gap chord 2R·tan α along φ̂ (α = ring_gap_length/2R; the chord, not the arc, is what the box's planar radial caps deliver — +0.10% at 0.008 m / 0.07 m, both diagnostics emitted) and w = ring_port_box_width_m along ẑ, corners in global coordinates (GEO-19 (4*)), splitting the box into inner/outer halves with closed-form volumes w·tan α·(R·w ∓ w²/4). The horizontal trapezoid at z = z_ring was rejected: planar and box-spanning too, but its h(u) = 2u·tan α varies ±7% across the sheet and the port model needs one h. Step 1 (4-leg rung, RING_GAP_LENGTH = 0.008, -n 2 and -n 12): the five identities in the §9 item — sheet area / (chord·w), φ̂-extent / chord and ẑ-extent / w at 1e-9, out-of-plane ≤ 1e-12 m, both half-volumes at 1e-9, C4 / top-bottom spreads ≤ 1e-12, every GEO-20 step-1 identity still exact — plus a version-tagged cell record; negative control: the default reproduces 110 786 at ratio 1.000000 with its transverse sheets at φ̂-extent ≤ 1e-12 m (the parked tests/mesh/test_birdcage_ring_sheet_orientation.py, attempt/PORT-13-20260903T033437Z 30756cf, cherry-picked as this chunk's control). Step 2 (16 legs, EX-35's parameters): the same family on 32 sheets, C16, new cell record — the control PORT-13 step 1 re-opens on. Mesh only; no solve, no port-model change, no GEO-20 record moves, EX-35 unchanged. Negative result: a sheet that does not split its box or reconstructs off 1e-9 at either width is a known-issues entry with both widths' readings; the kwarg lands only if the default's control holds. Opened 2026-09-03 03:00 review, §9 item 1. Step 1 ✅ 2026-09-03 (04:30 implementer slot) — ring_sheet_orientation landed on birdcage_port_domain (keyword-only, validated, refused without ring_gap_length), plus the two new diagnostics ring_port_gap_chord_m and ring_port_sheet_longitudinal_area_m2; tests/mesh/test_birdcage_ring_sheet_orientation.py gates both modes. Measured on the 4-leg rung, identical at -n 2 (20260903T093852Z_GEO-26.log, Status 0, 51 s) and -n 12 (…093949Z_GEO-26.log, Status 0, 50 s), standard tier: chord 8.008718871e-03 m against the arc 8.000000000e-03 m (+0.1090%, as designed); all 8 sheets read φ̂-extent/chord = 1.000000000000, ẑ-extent/w = 1.000000000000, area/(chord·w) = 1.000000000000, out-of-plane along û ≤ 1.53e-16 m, flatness ≤ 1.43e-16 m; both halves V_in = 3.861346599e-07 / V_out = 4.147372273e-07 m³ meshed/analytic = 1.000000000000 on all 8 with sum/ring_port_volume_m3 = 1.000000000000; C8 sheet spread 4.273e-16 (-n 12: 4.477e-16); GEO-9 partition, air-box closure, Pappus arcs all 1.000000000000; terminals 0.974219–0.974235 of the closed form, inside [0.95, 1.0] (…093852Z:13904–13915). RING_LONGITUDINAL_CELL_RECORD = 111 898 (0.11 image, -n 2; the transverse rung is 110 786). Negative control green: the default reproduces RING_GAP_CELL_RECORD 110 786 at ratio 1.000000 with φ̂-extent ≤ 1e-12 m (…093852Z:6956). One measured difference, recorded not absorbed — the longitudinal sheet's two φ edges lie in the terminal planes φ_c ± α and run w = 1e-2 m through each disk's centre, i.e. they are diameters of the two 2r = 8e-3 m terminal disks (the transverse sheet sits mid-gap and touches neither), so the inscribed triangulation of a terminal is constrained and its C4 covariance drops from 4.198e-08 to 1.605e-05; every terminal stays inside the [0.95, 1.0] band and every exact (polyhedral) form is unmoved. TERMINAL_INTRA_CLASS_BAND (1e-6) is not widened — _assert_ring_identity_family grew a terminal_intra_band kwarg defaulting to it, and only this one call site passes the measured LONGITUDINAL_TERMINAL_INTRA_BAND = 2.0e-5, with the reading and the mechanism in the constant's comment (MAG-10/MAG-15 precedent). A review should adjudicate whether that constrained-diameter triangulation is acceptable for the port model — it is a terminal-area reading, not a sheet reading, and PORT-13 integrates over the sheet. Helper edits proved inert by re-running GEO-20 step 1 + step 2 at their defaults: 3 passed, 260 s (20260903T094101Z_GEO-26.log, Status 0). Discovery window (record unmeasured, 1 failed 1 passed) is …093604Z_GEO-26.log. Step 2 (16 legs) not started — the slot ran out; it is the next queue item and PORT-13 stays 🚫 until its record exists. Audited PASS 2026-09-03 10:30 review (eight checks; TERMINAL_INTRA_CLASS_BAND untouched in the diff, the new band confined to test_birdcage_ring_sheet_orientation.py:141,412; the discovery red 1.605441790373545e-05 < 1e-06 is a genuine pre-kwarg failure at 5202f75; the 262 s regression window inherits GEO-20's heavy label, not this step's). Ruled, same review — the constrained-diameter terminal triangulation is acceptable for the port model: every terminal stays inside its [0.95, 1.0] band, every polyhedral identity is exact, and the 1.605e-05 per-class terminal-area covariance sits four decades under the coarsest port-level band it could feed (PORT-9 reciprocity 1e-3, C4 class spread 5%); it is a record at 2.0e-5, not a defect, and no known-issues entry is opened. Step 2 re-measures it on the 16-leg rung's four azimuth classes with the band unmoved — a class above 2.0e-5 there is a stop, not a widening (§9 item 1, queued 10:30). PORT-13 step 1 is pre-queued as §9 item 5, serial on step 2's record. Step 2 executed 2026-09-03 (12:00 implementer slot) and hit its pre-registered STOP. The 16-leg rung landed as a second parametrised leg count in the same module (SCALED_LEG_COUNT, EX-35's parameters; no constant or helper renamed, so EX-44's imports are unaffected), and every anchor but one is green at both widths (-n 2 20260903T170351Z_GEO-26.log, Status 1, 160 s; -n 12 …170701Z_GEO-26.log, Status 1, 158 s; heavy tier declared, 158–160 s measured): all 32 sheets at φ̂-extent/chord = ẑ-extent/w = area/(chord·w) = 1.000000000000 with out-of-plane ≤ 1e-12 m, both halves at their closed forms summing to ring_port_volume_m3, C32 sheet spread 6.035e-16 / 5.998e-16 and top/bottom mirror spread 5.551e-16 against 1e-12, the GEO-9 partition / air-box closure / Pappus arcs / terminal ratio band all exact, inter-class spread inside 5e-3, and the negative control green — the default orientation at 16 legs reproduces EX-35's 265 621 cells at ratio 1.000000 with all 32 transverse sheets at φ̂-extent ≤ 1.741094e-17 m (…170351Z:26462–26494). RING_LONGITUDINAL_SCALED_CELL_RECORD = 270 728 (0.11 image, identical at -n 2 :53400 and -n 12 :53490). The stop: the four azimuth classes' intra-class terminal-area covariance reads 9.989957e-05 / 3.792060e-11 / 3.792129e-11 / 9.990206e-05 at -n 2 and 9.989957e-05 / 3.792088e-11 / 3.792129e-11 / 9.990206e-05 at -n 12 (…170351Z:53436–53439, …170701Z:53526–53529) — two classes five times over the unmoved 2.0e-5 band. LONGITUDINAL_TERMINAL_INTRA_BAND is not widened (10:30 pre-registration), the [16] case is a deliberate red on main with a known-issues entry carrying all four readings at both widths, and PORT-13 stays 🚫. Mechanism measured, not inferred: the 32 terminals take exactly two areas (9.791961125e-05 / 9.792939386e-05 m², 9.99e-05 apart) with the low one taken by 5 of the 16 gap azimuths (11.25 / 78.75 / 101.25 / 191.25 / 281.25 deg) — 5 is no subgroup of C16, so this is not GEO-19 step C's azimuth-class effect but the bistable constrained-diameter triangulation step 1 recorded, resolving one of two ways against the surrounding air mesh; at four legs all four gaps happened to land the same way. A review owns the next move — either rule the bistability acceptable and re-register the band on this measurement (it is a terminal-area reading; every terminal is inside [0.95, 1.0] and PORT-13 integrates over the sheet, exact to 1e-16 here) or classify by the two-valued partition rather than _azimuth_class. The parametrisation is inert on step 1, re-run at its own rung after the refactor: 2 passed, Status 0, 51 s, 110 786 and 111 898 both at ratio 1.000000, C8 spread 4.273e-16 and terminal 1.605442e-05 — step 1's digits to the digit (20260903T171154Z_GEO-26.log:6956,13904,13915–13916,13919) Ruled 2026-09-03 18:00 review — the bistable triangulation is acceptable; the 16-leg rung gets its own record band; the _azimuth_class fold is kept. The reading is a terminal-area covariance — a mesh-reproducibility record, not a physics band or a closed-form comparison; all 32 terminals sit inside [0.95, 1.0]; the sheet PORT-13 integrates over is exact to 1e-16 on all 32; the 9.99e-05 two-state amplitude is a decade under PORT-9's 1e-3 reciprocity band and three under the 5% class band; and the mechanism is measured (two discrete areas, 5 of 16 azimuths), not inferred. Classifying by the two-valued partition was rejected — it fits the assertion to the artifact and would hide a third state. Step 3 (§9 item 3): LONGITUDINAL_TERMINAL_INTRA_BAND_16 = 2.0e-4, version-tagged with all four class readings and both areas, passed for the [16] case only; the [4] band 2.0e-5 and TERMINAL_INTRA_CLASS_BAND 1e-6 do not move; the low-state terminal count (expected 10 of 32) printed; negative control = the [16] case pointed back at 2.0e-5 reading step 2's 1 failed (5.0× separation is this measurement's ceiling); on green the known-issues entry retires and the chunk closes. PORT-13 step 1 is unblocked by the ruling alone (§9 item 4) — it reads the 270 728 record and the sheet, not this test's colour. Step 3 ✅ 2026-09-03 (22:30 implementer slot) — the 16-leg rung's band is registered and [16] is green at both widths; GEO-26 closes. LONGITUDINAL_TERMINAL_INTRA_BAND_16 = 2.0e-4 landed version-tagged (0.11 image) with all four class readings, both terminal areas and the five low-state azimuths in its comment, passed as terminal_intra_band for the [16] case only through a LONGITUDINAL_TERMINAL_BAND rung→band table; LONGITUDINAL_TERMINAL_INTRA_BAND stays 2.0e-5, TERMINAL_INTRA_CLASS_BAND stays 1e-6, no helper or step-1 name changed (EX-44's imports untouched) and no src/ change. Negative control, run first and footered: the [16] case pointed back at the unmoved 2.0e-5 reads exactly step 2's failure — assert np.float64(9.989956525036291e-05) < 2e-05, 1 failed, 3 passed, Status 1, 226 s (20260904T033238Z_GEO-26.log:26282,26286,26303–26304); the one-line edit was reverted before the recorded windows, so the 5.0× separation is executed, not asserted. Recorded windows, 4 passed / Status 0 at both widths, heavy by measurement (221–224 s, over standard's 180 s — the whole module, four cases, two 16-leg meshes): -n 2 20260904T034052Z_GEO-26.log (222 s) and -n 12 20260904T034441Z_GEO-26.log (224 s). Class readings identical to step 2 and to each other across widths: 9.989957e-05 / 3.792060e-11 (-n 12: 3.792088e-11) / 3.792129e-11 / 9.990206e-05 against 2.0e-4 (…034052Z:26267–26270, …034441Z:26377–26380). State census, now printed: exactly 2 discrete terminal areas at 16 legs — 9.791961125e-05 m² ×10 and 9.792939386e-05 m² ×22, i.e. 10 of 32 on the low area, at both widths (…034052Z:26271–26272, …034441Z:26381–26382) — the pre-registered expectation to the count, no third state. Every step-2 anchor unmoved: all 32 sheets at φ̂-extent/chord = ẑ-extent/w = area/(chord·w) = 1.000000000000 with out-of-plane ≤ 1.94e-16 m, both halves V_in/V_out at their closed forms summing to ring_port_volume_m3 = 1.000000000000, C32 spread 6.035e-16 / 5.998e-16 and mirror 5.551e-16 against 1e-12, RING_LONGITUDINAL_SCALED_CELL_RECORD 270 728 at ratio 1.000000 (that assert reachable for the first time), the default controls 265 621 and 110 786 both at ratio 1.000000, and the [4] case green with step 1's digits — 111 898 at ratio 1.000000, C8 4.273e-16 (-n 12: 4.477e-16), terminal 1.605442e-05. One measurement corrected in passing, not absorbed: the state census shows the 4-leg rung is two-state as well (6 terminals at 9.793917647e-05 m², 2 at 9.794074883e-05 m², …034052Z:15663), so step 2's "at four legs all four gaps happened to land the same way" is wrong — the states there are merely 1.605e-05 apart rather than 9.99e-05, which is why that rung reads inside 2.0e-5. The 4-leg band did not move; only the comment now says what was measured. Known-issues entry for test_the_longitudinal_ring_sheets_span_the_gap_chord_and_split_the_box[16] retired in the same commit. | ✅

docs.title: GEO-27 — Phantom-resolution cost probe for the 1 g SAR rung
docs.text: Phantom-resolution cost probe for the 1 g SAR rung — opened 2026-09-07 10:30 review from MAT-4 step 4's printed 1 g column (worst C4 pair 6.8383% on the 7.5 mm rung, 20260907T003548Z_MAT-4-step4.log:1934–1947: a 6.2 mm ball spanning ≈1.7 cells is a mesh statement, not an operator one, and the route to a 1 g gate is h). Executor mesh-probe, measurement-only, asserts nothing — 🧪 by the §3 rule until a gate consumes it. A ladder on MeshGenerator.birdcage_port_domain(phantom_resolution=…) exactly as tests/mesh/test_birdcage_phantom_resolution.py calls it (F-small defaults, real build, no solve): rungs 0.0075 (the record rung — the control that must reproduce 120 499 cells / 2 746 phantom cells, 20260907T140658Z_EX-53.log:1875), 0.005, 0.00375, 0.0025; per rung print total cells, phantom cells (tag 3), mesh wall time, the phantom share of the cells, and the cells across the two C95.3 balls, 2a_1g/h and 2a_10g/h (a_1g = 6.2 mm, a_10g = 13.4 mm at ρ = 1000 kg/m³, the gate's own averaging_ball_radius); the table lands in this row and the script as scripts/probes/geo27_phantom_resolution_probe.py. Stop rule: a rung above 300 k cells or 120 s to mesh is recorded and the ladder stops there — no finer rung is attempted. Tier / cost: the 120 499-cell mesh builds in ≈23–29 s (20260906T213913Z_TH-15.log:2628, …093741Z_TH-15.log solid 28.70 s); four rungs ≈ 200 s class ⇒ -n 2, timeout -k 30 600, heavy by ceiling, standard by expectation. Traps: the meshing happens on rank 0 and the counts are size_global after distribution — print the global count, never cell_tags.values lengths; the PHANTOM_GROWTH_BAND in the resolution module is a gate on the 0.0075 rung only and is not re-asserted here. Question the probe answers: the first rung with ≥ 4 cells across the 1 g ball and its cell count — the input to a MAT-4 step 5 (the 1 g column gated at that rung, or ruled ungateable on this box) that a review scopes from the table, never the slot that runs it. Negative result: the 0.0075 control not reproducing 120 499 is a mesher-drift finding (OPS-18 class) — record, stop. Executed 2026-09-08 (22:30 slot, mesh-probe, one window -n 2, timeout -k 30 600, elapsed 132 s, 20260908T033218Z_GEO-27.log). All four rungs meshed; the ladder ran to completion. The control REPRODUCED to the integer — 120 499 cells / 2 746 tag-3 cells against the record (:1803–1810), so no OPS-18-class drift and the ladder proceeded. The stop rule was never approached — the worst rung is 199 920 cells (67% of the 300 k ceiling) and 36.27 s to mesh (30% of the 120 s ceiling); no rung failed to mesh, and the log carries no "overlapping facets" and no MeshAdapt fallback, so there is no GEO-23-class record either. The table (:7152–7155): | h_p (m) | cells (size_global) | phantom cells (tag 3) | phantom share | mesh s | 2a_1g/h | 2a_10g/h | — | 0.0075 | 120 499 | 2 746 | 0.0228 | 25.26 | 1.65 | 3.57 | — | 0.005 | 129 505 | 8 497 | 0.0656 | 25.94 | 2.48 | 5.36 | — | 0.00375 | 144 212 | 18 570 | 0.1288 | 28.81 | 3.31 | 7.15 | — | 0.0025 | 199 920 | 58 866 | 0.2944 | 36.27 | 4.96 | 10.72 |. Answer: the first rung with ≥ 4 cells across the 1 g ball is h_p = 0.0025 m at 4.96 across (10.72 across the 10 g ball), costing 199 920 cells (1.66× the record rung), 58 866 phantom cells (21.4× it), a 29.4% phantom share, and 36.27 s to mesh (1.44× it) — the three coarser rungs reach only 1.65 / 2.48 / 3.31, the 0.0075 figure confirming MAT-4 step 4's "≈1.7 cells" reading. Two ungated observations for the review that scopes MAT-4 step 5: (i) the cost is cheap in total cells because the refinement stays confined to the phantom — total cells grow 1.66× and mesh time 1.44× while phantom cells grow 21.4× — so a 1 g-resolved F-small mesh is a ≈200 k-cell / ≈36 s build, not the runaway the phantom's 1/h³ alone suggests; (ii) the phantom count tracks (h_ref/h)³ from slightly below throughout (3.09× vs 3.38, 6.76× vs 8, 21.4× vs 27) and cell growth is monotone in 1/h on every rung (no GEO-22-class non-monotonicity here). Caveat the consuming step must carry: the three finer rungs are single readings — only the 0.0075 rung has a cross-process repeat (today against 2026-09-02) — so none of them may be pinned as a record without its own repeat. Nothing was asserted, no band moved, no src/ change, PHANTOM_GROWTH_BAND not re-asserted; the row stays 🧪 until a gate consumes the table. | 🧪 (opened 2026-09-07; table delivered 2026-09-08; measurement-only, no band, no src/)

docs.title: §9 item 377 — 2026-10-11 (GEO-27 step 2 — the 1 g rung's price at degree 2 on exact rectangles; lane-1 revalidation)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-11 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

Weekly re-pose being executed. The 2026-10-10 weekly (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4810–4814, listed under "Lane 2 (revalidation / Tier B)") reads: "GEO-27 🧪 re-posed as step 2 — the 1 g rung's price on the exact-rectangle degree-2 F-small fixture (h_p = 0.005 / 0.0025 m, -n 8): cells, unknowns, time, memory in a table, MAT-4 step 5's 1 g C4 identity asserted at the imported band on the rung that fits ⇒ ✅ (a measurement with one imported gate)". - It is 🧪 → ✅ work, so it falls in the revalidation class (§9 rule (5)'s lane 1 by kind). - Target: the weekly's text. No band, tolerance or validation target is set or moved. C4_COVARIANCE_BAND is MAT-4's, imported. - The row's Done-when must be amended to match (rule (j); exact text below).

Executor and cost. - Executor: implementer. It is not mesh-probe: the item solves and asserts. - Tier: heavy, -n 8, complex build. Class: lane-1 revalidation (median 17). - Cost: ≈ M measured / ≈ 50 predicted min: 15 fixed + 15 code + W0 ≈ 1 + W1 ≈ 4 + W2 ≈ 7 + spare. - Depends on: nothing. - Memory guard: coarse first, with the stop rule below.

The fixture is already priced at 0.0025 m (read this first). The exact-rectangle degree-2 F-small at h_p = 0.0025 m is IMP-3 I14's off arm. - Construction: _build(True, phantom_resolution=PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG, leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION) → build_four_port_sweep(built=…, build_only=True, degree=2) → run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(…, keep_fields=True, degree=2) (tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py:121–178). - Measured at -n 8 on 2026-10-06 (20261006T111406Z_IMP-3-item263-W2-d2off.log:2029, :2080–2084): 201 072 cells, 1 284 856 degree-2 dofs = 2E + 2F; build 43.59 s; one-factorisation 4-port sweep 246.15 s; 12 ball SARs 26.26 s; window 397 s; summed peak RSS 44.17 GiB. - The integers are registered as I14_OFF_CELLS, I14_OFF_DOFS (tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py:94). - So 0.0025 m is predicted to fit the heavy tier at -n 8. 44 GiB is well under the container's 128 GiB limit (docker/docker-compose.yml:34), and the window is under the 590 s container ceiling even on the 1.32× box (≈ 525 s). - That run was at 64 MHz. This item runs at MAT-4's 10 MHz (build_four_port_sweep's default FREQUENCY_HZ = 10.0e6, tests/validation/test_port_reaction_impedance.py:108). It is the same matrix pattern, so the price carries over. - The 0.005 m rung has no degree-2 measurement on this fixture; it is predicted below.

Why not _build_mass_averaged. MAT-4 steps 4–5 call _build_mass_averaged(phantom_resolution=…) (tests/validation/test_birdcage_sar_mass_averaged.py:209–331). That routine: - builds the ragged default fixture (no built=, no strip fraction); - runs at degree 1 (build_four_port_sweep's default); - solves with four fresh factorisations (_solve_driven per port, :249). At degree 2 on 1.28 M dofs that is ≈ 4 × 200 s, which does not fit.

Editing it (an additive built= / degree= / held-factor path) would owe re-runs of MAT-4 steps 4 and 5b under rule (a). Instead this item copies its centres-and-pairing block (:239–331) with a provenance comment (base commit, line span) and feeds it I14's one-factorisation sweep fields. run_n_port_sparameter_sweep holds one factorisation; with matched 50 Ω terminations its held drives equal fresh single-drive solves (the PORT-19 premise). The pairing, centres, radii, density map, operator and QUADRATURE_DEGREE stay MAT-4's.

New module tests/validation/test_geo27_one_gram_rung_degree2.py. - @complex_only. Knob FEM_EM_GEO27_STEP2 ∈ {h005, h0025}: unset ⇒ skip; any other value ⇒ ValueError. One test dispatches on it (never -k). - Imports (names only, never test_*): - _build, SHEET_IFACE (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets.py); - GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION (tests/validation/test_port_lumped_narrowed_sheet.py:132); - build_four_port_sweep (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:219) and run_n_port_sparameter_sweep; - PHANTOM_CELL_TAG (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py); - _sheet_areas (test_imp3_palace_twin.py:69); NOMINAL_STRIP_AREA (test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py:105); STRIP_BAND (test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58); - I14_OFF_CELLS, I14_OFF_DOFS (test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py:94); PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG (test_birdcage_sar_1g_rung.py:114); - C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:120); - CENTRE_RADIUS_M, WHOLE_PHANTOM_BALL_RADIUS_M, EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3, _global_tag_cell_count (test_birdcage_sar_mass_averaged.py:149, :158, :163); - ONE_GRAM_KG, TEN_GRAM_KG, QUADRATURE_DEGREE (test_mass_averaged_sar_standard_masses.py:121–124); - _port_index, QUADRATURE_STEP_DEG (test_birdcage_b1_quadrature.py); - DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, _exact_shares (test_birdcage_power_identity.py:227); - RECIPROCITY_BAND (test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py); - _matrix_quantities, _peak_rss_gib (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:275, :498); - CELL_COUNT_BAND (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheet_prerequisite.py:57). - Constants defined here: - PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_005 = 0.005, step 1's rung (20260908T033218Z_GEO-27.log:7152–7155); - MAT4_STEP5B_ONE_GRAM_PAIRS = {0: 0.000957, 1: 0.001199, 2: 0.001305, 3: 0.001065} and MAT4_STEP5B_ONE_GRAM_CONTROL_K0 = 0.870143 (the k = 0 mis-paired control), both from 20260908T200629Z_MAT-4-step5b.log.gz:1990–1993. They are printed comparands (degree 1, ragged sheets, same h_p), never bands. - Body (both modes): 1. Build at the mode's h_p. Then build_four_port_sweep(built=…, build_only=True, degree=2) with the default frequency. 2. Before the sweep: cells and (D) are checked, and the mode h0025 checks the cells-and-dofs record. 3. run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(…, keep_fields=True, degree=2), timed. 4. The copied MAT-4 block: - azimuths → _port_index → by_k; centres at CENTRE_RADIUS_M on each drive's azimuth, z = 0; - ρ = build_density_field (0 off tag 3); σ = result.fields[pid].sigma_field; - balls: 1 g diagonal (k, k) ×4; 1 g mis-paired (k, k+2) ×4; 10 g diagonal ×4; the whole-phantom ball and mean_sar on tag 3 for P1. 5. Per-drive exact power shares (_exact_shares, I14's :181–184). 6. Print the price line: h_p, cells, tag-3 cells, E, F, d2 dofs, build s, sweep s, balls s, test-body s, _peak_rss_gib() and ranks. 7. The h005 window prints a stop-rule line (below).

Anchors (asserted; every band imported). - Both windows: - (D) d2 dofs = 2E + 2F exactly. - (G2) the four N_i strip areas equal NOMINAL_STRIP_AREA within STRIP_BAND. This is the exact-rectangle fixture tie; I14 read 5.600000000000e-05 ×4 (…d2off.log:2029). - (i) ‖S − Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND. - (P) P_src = P_vol + P_sheet per drive ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. docs.title: GEO-28 — C4 census of the unloaded F-small birdcage mesh
docs.text: C4 census of the unloaded F-small birdcage mesh — is quadrant 2 different? — opened 2026-09-08 03:00 review from two readings on the same 116 085-cell fixture that name one quadrant: WF-6 step 4b's FEM \|B₁⁺\| at r = 0.5R differs by 3.4% between +x̂ and +ŷ (20260908T004020Z_WF-6.log:1894, 1899) and step 4c's junction 2 is the worst on both rings (2.19 / 2.16%) while leg 2 is the only leg whose current rises with z (20260908T051300Z_WF-6.log:1927–1949, on the branch). The CAD is C4-symmetric to the digit (GEO-18: terminal areas spread 8.470e-16), so any per-quadrant difference is the mesher's. Executor mesh-probe, measurement-only, asserts nothing, 🧪 by the §3 rule; real build, no solve, -n 2. The mesh: birdcage_port_domain exactly as tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets._build(True) calls it (the WF-6 step-4 fixture; control — must reproduce 116 085 size_global, …004020Z:1881). Per quadrant Q_n = {φ ∈ [φ_n − 45°, φ_n + 45°]} about each leg azimuth (legs at 0 / 90 / 180 / 270°, sector membership by the squared-projection test of step 4c — no atan2, no sqrt in a comparison — evaluated on cell midpoints, rank-local counts reduced MPI.SUM): (1) cell count and meshed volume of the coil tag, of the phantom tag and of the air tag; (2) the coil tag's volume against the CAD's quarter (legs + ring quarters + gap boxes, from the generator's parameters — an identity to CAD precision the mesher meets or not); (3) the cell-size statistic in the shell 0.4R ≤ r ≤ 0.6R, \|z\| ≤ 0.01 m, per quadrant — count, mean and max circumradius (dolfinx.cpp.mesh.h) — the near field 4b evaluates at; (4) per leg, the conductor cells and volume of the leg's own cylinder (\|z\| ≤ 0.05, radius test on the leg's axis); (5) the per-quadrant spread (max − min)/mean of each of (1)–(4), printed as a table. The question it answers: whether quadrant 2 (leg 2 / the +ŷ…−x̂ neighbourhood) carries a cell-count, volume or h spread of the order of 3% that the other three do not — the shared mesh-side candidate for 4b's r = 0.5R miss and 4c's junction 2. Tier / ranks / cost: the mesh builds in 23–29 s (20260906T213913Z_TH-15.log:2628); the census is a midpoint pass, seconds ⇒ one window -n 2, timeout -k 30 300, standard by expectation. Traps: cell_tags.values and size_local are rank-local — reduce; ghost cells are counted once via index_map(dim).size_local (OPS-39's _census fix); dolfinx.cpp.mesh.h takes local cell indices; print size_global after distribution. Deliverable: the table in this row and scripts/probes/geo28_birdcage_c4_census.py. Negative result: the control not reproducing 116 085 is an OPS-18-class drift — record, stop; every spread ≲ 1% is itself the finding (the mesh is not the mechanism and the near-field miss is the CG1 estimator's) — record, stop. — MEASURED 2026-09-08 13:30 slot (mesh-probe), the negative-result branch: quadrant 2 is not the different one. Two windows, -n 2, real build, no solve, 29 / 30 s, both Status: 0, every count / volume / ratio / spread character-identical between them (20260908T183317Z_GEO-28.log, 20260908T183401Z_GEO-28.log, lines 1787–1830). Control holds: size_global=116085, ratio 1.000000, mesh 23.15 s (…183317Z:1786); owned cells assigned to no quadrant 0 (:1791); core tags sum 110 780 vs 116 085, the balance being the port-box tags 100+i / 200+i (:1830). CAD line (:1793–1795): R=0.07, r_leg=0.006, r_ring=0.004, g=0.008, stub 0.066 m; ring CAD 4.421582772e-05 m³ against the analytic 2·2π²Rr² to ratio 1.000000000; conductor CAD total 9.939058968e-05 ⇒ C4-exact quarter 2.484764742e-05 m³. The table (Q1…Q4, spread (max−min)/mean, :1798–1816): coil cells 9116 / 9006 / 9083 / 8712, 4.4993e-02; coil volume 2.410808 / 2.411316 / 2.410442 / 2.409004e-05 m³, 9.5943e-04; phantom cells 155 / 124 / 121 / 137, 2.5326e-01; phantom volume 5.637544 / 5.495989 / 5.344115 / 5.475299e-05 m³, 5.3465e-02; air cells 18 779 / 18 497 / 18 477 / 18 573, 1.6253e-02; air volume 2.793005 / 2.801239 / 2.792245 / 2.811294e-03 m³, 6.8048e-03; meshed/CAD quarter 0.970235759 / 0.970440489 / 0.970088615 / 0.969509780, spread 9.5943e-04; shell cells 30 / 22 / 19 / 25, 4.5833e-01; shell mean h 2.125110 / 2.302944 / 2.627863 / 2.310792e-02 m, 2.1470e-01; shell max h 2.532223 / 2.745158 / 3.195599 / 2.753950e-02 m, 2.3635e-01; leg cells 3158 / 3108 / 3207 / 2983, 7.1933e-02; leg volume 1.023516 / 1.023494 / 1.023644 / 1.020585e-05 m³, 2.9902e-03; leg volume / 2-stub CAD 0.983681379 / 0.983660190 / 0.983803942 / 0.980864617. The verdict: Q2 is never the outlier — it carries the largest coil volume, a leg volume equal to Q1 / Q3 to 2e-5 relative, and mid-range shell statistics. Where an outlier exists it is Q4 in every conductor count (coil −4.1% off the max, leg −7.0%, and the only leg whose volume/CAD drops, 0.98086 vs 0.98366–0.98380) and Q3 in the shell h. Every mass spread is ≲ 0.1% (coil, leg) or ≤ 0.7% (air) — an order below the 3.4% field effect — so the mesh is not the mechanism for 4b's +ŷ r = 0.5R miss or 4c's junction 2, and the near-field miss stays with the degree-1 solve / CG1 curl E estimator (the h question is GEO-29 → WF-6 step 4f). Two caveats for the review: the shell rows rest on 19–30 cells per quadrant and the phantom rows on 121–155 — the large count spreads there (4.6e-01, 2.5e-01) are small-sample, and their volume spreads (5.3e-02 for the phantom) are an order smaller; and the shell's mean h of 2.1–2.6e-02 m across a 1.4e-02 m-thick shell is direct evidence for GEO-29's premise that the global 0.015 m resolution puts on the order of one cell across the near-field shell WF-6 step 4b evaluates in. Probe: scripts/probes/geo28_birdcage_c4_census.py (asserts nothing beyond printing the 116 085 control). | 🧪 measured 2026-09-08 (measurement-only — 🧪 by the §3 rule, never ✅; the row's question is answered and the deliverable landed)

docs.title: GEO-29 — Global-resolution cost ladder of the unloaded F-small birdcage port fixture
docs.text: Global-resolution cost ladder of the unloaded F-small birdcage port fixture — the price of the h-ladder WF-6 step 4f and ANS-4 both need — opened 2026-09-08 10:30 review from the WF-6 step-4d ruling: the converged image-lattice comparand sits below S_3 (S_∞ − S_3 ≈ −0.00977 on 1.16929, 20260908T093332Z_WF-6.log:41–46), so the eleven-point B₁⁺ miss (≈ 3% at the centre, ≈ 5–8% at r ≥ 0.4R along +ŷ, predicted from …004020Z:1889–1899) is the FEM's to explain, and the 116 085-cell fixture has never been refined in its global resolution (0.015 m — 1.5 cm air cells inside a 7 cm coil; PORT-14 step 1b's ×0.75 / ×0.6 rungs refined the conductor and GEO-27's ladder the phantom). Executor mesh-probe, measurement-only, asserts nothing, 🧪 by the §3 rule; real build, no solve, -n 1 (gmsh is serial). The mesh: birdcage_port_domain with exactly the parameter set tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets._build(True) passes (import its constants; conductor_resolution pinned at the fixture's CONDUCTOR_RESOLUTION, phantom_resolution at its default), the global resolution stepped 0.015 (control — must reproduce 116 085 size_global, 20260908T004020Z_WF-6.log:1881), 0.012, 0.0095, 0.0075. Per rung print size_global; the air / coil / phantom / gap tag cell counts (reduced); mesh wall time; peak RSS; and the mean circumradius (dolfinx.cpp.mesh.h, reduced) of the air cells inside r ≤ 0.5R, \|z\| ≤ 0.01 m — the cell size the B₁⁺ gate actually samples at. Stop rule (pre-registered): a rung above 900 k cells or 300 s to mesh is recorded and the ladder stops; the next rung is attempted only if the previous rung's count × (h_prev/h_next)³ stays under the ceiling (GEO-25's licence arithmetic). Tier / ranks / cost: the ×1 mesh builds in 23–29 s (20260906T213913Z_TH-15.log:2628); if the air dominates the count, 0.0075 is ≈ 8× the air cells ⇒ predicted ≤ 600 k cells / ≤ 200 s; one window -n 1, timeout -k 30 900, heavy by ceiling. Traps: rank-0 meshing, size_global after distribution, never cell_tags.values lengths; ghosts once via index_map(dim).size_local (OPS-39); a count non-monotone in 1/h (GEO-22 class) is a finding to print, not a failure; no solve, no assertion. Deliverable: the table in this row and scripts/probes/geo29_birdcage_resolution_ladder.py. The question it answers: which rungs WF-6 step 4f can afford at -n 4 / -n 8 inside a 560 s window (four single-drive solves per rung; the ×1 rung solves eight in 71 s, …004020Z:1998), and whether the interior cell size actually falls with resolution or is pinned by the conductor refinement's gradient — and, for the weekly, whether the same ladder can carry ANS-4's 64 / 128 MHz convergence question on the ordinary service. Negative result: the control not reproducing 116 085 is an OPS-18-class drift — record, stop; a rung that does not mesh is a GEO-21/GEO-23-class known-issues entry — record, stop. — MEASURED 2026-09-08 19:30 slot (mesh-probe): the ladder is cheap, it runs to completion, and the interior cell size does fall with resolution. One window, -n 1, real build, no solve, timeout -k 30 560, harness elapsed 145 s, Status: 0 (20260909T003221Z_GEO-29.log, probe wall time 141.30 s at :7052). Control REPRODUCED to the integer: size_global=116085, ratio 1.000000 against 20260908T004020Z_WF-6.log:1881 (:1792) — no OPS-18-class drift. The ladder (:7038–7042, per-rung prints at :1792–1795, :3520–3523, :5289–5292, :7032–7035): h=0.015 → 116 085 cells (air 74 326 / coil 35 917 / phantom 537 / gap 5 305), mesh 21.60 s, peak RSS 0.353 GiB, interior air cells 41, interior mean h 2.189033e-02 m; h=0.012 → 149 049 (100 997 / 41 720 / 867 / 5 465), 26.44 s, 0.408 GiB, 70 cells, 1.708717e-02 m; h=0.0095 → 197 393 (143 330 / 46 728 / 1 497 / 5 838), 32.91 s, 0.492 GiB, 148 cells, 1.366960e-02 m; h=0.0075 → 281 728 (217 687 / 54 590 / 2 746 / 6 705), 45.56 s, 0.529 GiB, 324 cells, 1.069368e-02 m. The tag counts sum to size_global exactly on every rung — no cell unaccounted. Stop rule never fired (:7051): the worst rung is 31% of the 900 k ceiling and 15% of the 300 s ceiling, and the pre-registered GEO-25 licence arithmetic printed before each rung (226 729 / 42.2 s, 300 401 / 53.3 s, 401 161 / 66.9 s, :1796, 3524, 5293) over-estimated every time — the measured 0.0075 rung came in 30% under its own licence figure. The question is answered YES: the interior mean circumradius inside r ≤ 0.5R, \|z\| ≤ 0.01 m falls 2.189e-02 → 1.709e-02 → 1.367e-02 → 1.069e-02 m, h/h₀ = 1.0000 / 0.7806 / 0.6245 / 0.4885 against nominal ratios 1.0 / 0.80 / 0.633 / 0.50 (slightly slower than nominal at the two middle rungs, slightly faster at the finest), and the interior cell count grows 41 → 70 → 148 → 324 (7.9×) — the interior is not pinned by the conductor refinement's gradient. The absolute scale is the finding for WF-6: at the ×1 rung the interior mean circumradius is 2.19e-02 m — 1.46× the nominal 0.015 m and larger than the 1.4e-02 m-thick shell GEO-28 measured in (GEO-28 read 2.1–2.6e-02 m there, the same number by an independent route); only at h = 0.0075 does it drop to 1.07e-02 m, i.e. below the shell thickness. Cost (:7044–7048): total cells grow only 2.43× over a nominal 8× volumetric refinement (air 2.93× against the ideal 8.00×, coil 1.52×, gap 1.26×, phantom 5.11×) and mesh time only 2.11× — the fixture's budget is already dominated by the conductor-graded region, so the air is 64% of cells at 0.015 and 77% at 0.0075. The count is monotone in 1/h on every rung (:7050) — no GEO-22-class non-monotonicity — and no rung failed to mesh: zero Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets), zero Frontal-Delaunay → MeshAdapt fallbacks, so no GEO-21/GEO-23 known-issues entry opens. The phantom's 2 746 cells at 0.0075 is GEO-27's 0.0075-phantom figure, as expected with phantom_resolution=None letting the global value drive it. What step 4f may assume and what it may not: the mesh side of all four rungs is affordable (the finest is 2.4× the ×1 fixture's cells at 46 s to mesh, single-rank); the solve side is unmeasured — this probe ran no solve, so the -n 4 / -n 8 window arithmetic against the ×1 rung's eight-drive 71 s (…004020Z:1998) is the 18:00 review's to make, not this row's. Caveat (three of the four rungs are single readings): gmsh initialises and finalises per birdcage_port_domain call and all four rungs ran in one process; only the 0.015 rung has a cross-process repeat (today, against …004020Z:1881). None of 0.012 / 0.0095 / 0.0075 may be pinned as a version-tagged record without its own repeat — they are a cost table, not MAT-4-style records. Probe: scripts/probes/geo29_birdcage_resolution_ladder.py (asserts nothing; the 116 085 control is printed, not asserted). | 🧪 measured 2026-09-08 (measurement-only — 🧪 by the §3 rule, never ✅; the row's question is answered and the deliverable landed)

docs.title: GEO-30 — Does the four-port birdcage fixture stay C4-symmetric under refinement? One geometric census across both refinement axes
docs.text: Does the four-port birdcage fixture stay C4-symmetric under refinement? One geometric census across both refinement axes — opened 2026-09-09 10:30 review, ruling (1), because two items refined the same fixture along two different axes on the same day and both broke the same symmetry. ANS-4 step 2a refined conductor_resolution ×1 → ×0.75 and the Z class spreads went 0.1012 / 0.0916 / 0.0654% → 0.5390 / 0.4591 / 1.6886% past the imported, unmoved 0.5% (20260909T093534Z_ANS-4-step2a.log; known-issues 2026-09-09). WF-6 step 4f refined the global resolution 0.015 → 0.0095 and the power residual — port-symmetric to five figures on the two coarse rungs (P1 9.795836e-03 / P2 9.796294e-03, then 8.113516e-03 / 8.111819e-03) — split between the ports and doubled at ×0.0095: P1 1.853642e-02, P2 1.419812e-02 (20260909T123716Z_WF-6.log:2089–2090, 3910–3911, 5777–5778), on the rung that also printed ungated Z class spreads 1.3475 / 0.4544 / 0.9165%. The measurement (no solve, mesh-probe): at conductor_resolution ×1 / ×0.75 and global resolution 0.015 / 0.012 / 0.0095, per rung — the four C4-image quadrant volumes and owned-cell counts, the four leg/conductor tag volumes and counts, the four port gap-sheet facet areas, and size_global; all comm-reduced, reusing GEO-28's quadrant partition as the template. Anchors (asserted): (i) at ×1 the four quadrant mass spreads reproduce GEO-28's ≲ 0.1% (20260908T183317Z_GEO-28.log:1800–1830) and size_global reproduces 116 085 at the imported unmoved 1% CELL_COUNT_BAND (ratio 1.000000 at …183317Z:1786 and 20260909T003221Z_GEO-29.log:1792); (ii) the four gap-sheet areas agree across the C4 images to ≤ 1e-3, the tolerance TH-15 step 2h met at 2.53e-15 / 8.70e-15 on the two-torus gap tags. Negative control (asserted): the mis-paired quadrant assignment must exceed the ×1 spread by ≥ 10× — ANS-2 step 1 measured that construction at 87.01–87.06% against a 5% band, ≈ 17× (20260909T140558Z_ANS-2-step1.log:1918–1923). Printed, asserted nowhere: all four quantities at all four rungs with each rung's spread and its ratio to ×1 — the table both blocked items' rulings are written from. Scope: closes nothing and unblocks nothing by itself; no band is widened or re-registered, no src/ changes, ANS-4 keeps its INCONCLUSIVE Larmor verdict and WF-6 stays 🟡. Negative result — the more informative one: four images equal to ≤ 0.1% at every rung means the mesh is not the mechanism and both symptoms move onto the degree-1 N1curl solve or the port/sheet reconstruction; record the table, do not guess a mechanism in-slot. EXECUTED 2026-09-09 (scripts/probes/geo30_birdcage_c4_refinement_census.py, 20260909T171106Z_GEO-30.log, -n 2, real build, no solve, 133 s; attempt 1 20260909T170657Z_GEO-30.log is the same sweep with a wrong negative control, see below). All three anchors green: (i) ×1 size_global 116 085 vs record 116 085, ratio 1.000000, imported 1% CELL_COUNT_BAND unmoved, and ×1 quadrant coil-mass spread 9.594261e-04, reproducing GEO-28's 9.5943e-04 to seven figures; (ii) ×1 gap-sheet area spread 6.050235e-16 against 1e-3; (iii) mis-paired control (C4 pairing rotated by one quadrant — leg n's cylinder read against quadrant n+1) 1.000815 = 1043× the ×1 spread, bar 10×. (A half-quadrant sector rotation was tried first and read only 4.13×; it is mass-preserving by construction — the 45°-offset sector spans 0…90°, losing leg n and gaining leg n+1 — so it is printed and never asserted. No band moved; the 10× bar is the item's own.) The table — spread (max−min)/mean over the four C4 images, by rung (…171106Z:7002–7076): rungs ×1/h=0.015 (116 085 cells, mesh 23.5 s) / conductor_resolution ×0.75 (161 695, 31.4 s) / resolution 0.012 (149 049, 28.3 s) / resolution 0.0095 (197 393, 34.4 s). quadrant volume 7.07e-3 / 7.57e-3 / 4.22e-3 / 3.15e-3 (1.00× / 1.07× / 0.60× / 0.45×); coil volume 9.59e-4 / 1.35e-3 / 1.01e-3 / 1.73e-3 (1.00× / 1.40× / 1.05× / 1.80×); leg volume 2.99e-3 / 3.28e-3 / 1.57e-3 / 1.06e-3 (1.00× / 1.10× / 0.53× / 0.35×); air volume 6.80e-3 / 7.13e-3 / 2.78e-3 / 2.96e-3; phantom volume 5.35e-2 / 3.92e-2 / 7.95e-2 / 2.69e-2 (155/124/121/137-cell counts — small-N, symptomatic of nothing); gap-sheet area 6.05e-16 / 3.63e-16 / 8.47e-16 / 6.05e-16. THE NEGATIVE RESULT, and it is the informative one: no conductor mass quantity leaves 0.35% at any rung — coil volume ≤ 0.173% and leg volume ≤ 0.328% across all four. (Corrected in-slot against the log: the summary sentence as first written said "no mass quantity", which the table does not support — the quadrant totals run 0.315–0.757% and the phantom 2.7–8.0%. Neither weakens the finding: the quadrant total is dominated by the air and phantom it contains, the phantom sits on 121–390 owned cells at every rung including ×1, and the anchor GEO-28 set and this probe reproduced to seven figures is the coil-mass spread, not the quadrant total.) The finest global rung's coil-volume spread is 0.17% and the ×0.75 rung's is 0.13% — a factor 1.4–1.8 on a number that starts at 0.096%, an order of magnitude below the 0.5% ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND and two below the 1.6886% Z spread ANS-4 step 2a measured on the very same ×0.75 mesh. The refined mesh is still C4-symmetric in mass and in gap-sheet area; the mesh is therefore not the mechanism, and both symptoms move onto the degree-1 N1curl solve or the port/sheet reconstruction. One ungated observation, recorded not interpreted: the gap-sheet facet counts — as opposed to their areas — are C4-equal on the two rungs that behaved (×1: 58/58/58/58, resolution 0.012: 62/62/62/62, spread 0) and drop to C2, not C4, on exactly the two rungs that broke (×0.75: 80/74/80/74, spread 7.79e-2; 0.0095: 70/76/70/76, spread 8.22e-2) — opposite ports equal, adjacent ports differing, the same symmetry class as WF-6's residual splitting P1-vs-P2 and ANS-4's adjacent/opposite class spread. The sheets have identical area to 1e-15 and different triangulations. Whether that is the mechanism is the next review's ruling, not this probe's. Repeat: the two windows are bit-identical in every count, volume, area and spread (mesh wall times differ, 23.15 vs 23.48 s on ×1). Scope honoured: no src/ change, no existing test edited, no band widened or re-registered, nothing closed; ANS-4 keeps its ✅/INCONCLUSIVE and WF-6 stays 🟡. | 🧪 measured 2026-09-09 — table delivered, anchors green, mesh excluded as the mechanism; the ruling on ANS-4 step 2a and WF-6 step 4f is the next review's

docs.title: GEO-31 — The port gap-sheets' triangulation under the C4 rotation
docs.text: The port gap-sheets' triangulation under the C4 rotation — same area, different cut, or different surface? — opened 2026-09-09 18:00 review, ruling (1), on the one ungated lead GEO-30 handed back. GEO-30 excluded the mesh as the mechanism in mass and in gap-sheet area (conductor spreads ≤ 0.33% at every rung, sheet areas agreeing to 1e-15) but printed one quantity that tracks the two failures exactly: the four gap-sheets' facet counts are C4-equal on the two rungs that behaved (×1: 58/58/58/58, resolution 0.012: 62/62/62/62, spread 0) and go C2, not C4, on precisely the two that broke (conductor_resolution ×0.75: 80/74/80/74, spread 7.79e-2; resolution 0.0095: 70/76/70/76, spread 8.22e-2) — opposite ports equal, adjacent ports differing, the same class split as ANS-4 step 2a's Z/S adjacent-vs-opposite spreads and WF-6 step 4f's P1-vs-P2 power residual (20260909T171106Z_GEO-30.log:7016, 7030, 7044, 7058, 7073). Four surfaces with identical area to 1e-15 and different triangulations is exactly the object the lumped-sheet port model integrates over (ports/lumped.py, I = (1/R_s)∫E·ĥ dS / h), so this is the cheapest remaining candidate and it needs no solve. Executor mesh-probe, measurement-only, asserts only a reproduction and a probe self-test, 🧪 by the §3 rule; real build, -n 2. The measurement, on the same four rungs and the same generator call GEO-30 used — import scripts/probes/geo30_birdcage_c4_refinement_census.py's rung construction and its SHEET_IFACE + i facet-tag selection; do not rebuild the geometry or re-derive the tags by hand. Per rung, per sheet i = 0…3: (1) the facet count and total area (reproducing GEO-30's table, so the two probes are comparable); (2) the sorted per-facet-area vector and its min / mean / max; (3) each facet's centroid, and the C4-congruence metric d_i = the symmetric Hausdorff distance between sheet i's centroid set and sheet 0's centroid set rotated by i·90° about ẑ; (4) the same metric on the sheets' boundary-vertex sets alone; (5) whether the four sheets' supports coincide under the rotation at all — the bounding box of each rotated-image difference. Anchor (asserted — a reproduction of numbers already measured on this fixture, and the only asserted physical content): at the ×1 rung the four facet counts are 58/58/58/58 exactly and at resolution 0.012 62/62/62/62 exactly (GEO-30 measured spread 0.0000e+00 at both), and at both rungs the four sheet areas agree to ≤ 1e-3 relative (measured 6.050235e-16 and 8.4703e-16). Without this the finer rungs compare nothing. Negative control (asserted — by construction, so its separation is arithmetic rather than predicted): the congruence metric of (3) applied to sheet 0 against sheet 0 rigidly displaced by one mean facet edge length ℓ = sqrt(4A/(n√3)) (computed in-probe; ≈ 2.1e-3 m at the ×1 rung from A = 1.12e-4 m², n = 58) must read ≥ ℓ/2, while the same metric on sheet 0 against itself reads exactly 0.0. A metric that returns 0 regardless — the one failure mode that would make the whole table meaningless — fails this and nothing else would catch it. This is a probe self-test, not a symmetry claim; the symmetry readings are the deliverable and are printed, never asserted. Printed, asserted nowhere (rule (e)): all of (1)–(5) at all four rungs side by side, plus the explicit discriminator sentence the review needs — same support and same boundary but a different interior cut (a triangulation/quadrature question, and the follow-on is whether the lumped-sheet reconstruction is cut-sensitive at fixed area) versus different support or different boundary (a generator defect in birdcage_port_domain's sheet emission). Tier / ranks / cost: four meshes, a facet pass, no solve and no linear algebra — GEO-30 built exactly these four in 133 s total at -n 2 (23.5 / 31.4 / 28.3 / 34.4 s of meshing) and the centroid work is seconds ⇒ one window -n 2, timeout -k 30 500, -s, real build, standard by expectation and heavy by ceiling. Traps already paid for: facet tags, cell_tags.values, assemble_scalar, size_local and compute_midpoints are rank-local — reduce every one before printing, and count ghost entities once via index_map(dim).size_local (OPS-39); a facet integral bearing a SpatialCoordinate on a gmsh mesh must pin metadata={"quadrature_degree": …} or FFCx can take a nine-minute compile and poison that form's cache entry (POST-5 step 1) — this probe integrates over facets, so pin it; no UFL ordering comparison and no sqrt inside one (OPS-22; WF-6 step 4c — UFL types Sqrt as complex whatever its argument, so compare squares), and the Hausdorff distance is plain numpy on gathered arrays, not UFL; gather the four centroid sets to rank 0 with comm.gather before comparing them — a rank-local Hausdorff is meaningless and evaluate_vector_field_parallel's collective rule (OPS-40) is the same lesson; real build, no complex, no FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX; timeout -k 30; no run_in_background; -k a or b splits into stray argv inside an already-quoted container command; sweep find /root/.cache/fenics -name '*.c' -size 0 and delete stubs only. Scope: closes nothing, unblocks nothing by itself, and rehabilitates no rung. ANS-4 keeps its ✅ for the runnable half and its INCONCLUSIVE Larmor verdict, WF-6 stays 🟡, the ×0.0095 rung stays out of WF-6's ladder (18:00 ruling (2)), and ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (0.5%), POWER_BALANCE_BAND (1e-2), CELL_COUNT_BAND (1%) and every port band are not widened or re-registered here. No src/ change. Deliverable is the table, this row, and scripts/probes/geo31_birdcage_port_sheet_congruence.py. Negative result — and both branches are informative: if the four sheets are C4-congruent to mesh round-off at every rung (so the facet-count split of GEO-30 is a counting artefact rather than a geometric one), the sheet is excluded too and the two symptoms move onto the degree-1 N1curl solve — record the table and stop. If they are not congruent, record which of support / boundary / interior cut differs and stop: do not fix the generator in-slot and do not touch the port model, because a sheet-emission change moves every PORT-9/PORT-11/ANS-4 record at once and the review that reads this table owns that decision. MEASURED 2026-09-09 19:30 slot (mesh-probe, one measurement window -n 2, Status 0, 144 s, 20260910T003835Z_GEO-31.log; a first, character-identical window 20260910T003421Z_GEO-31.log Status 0 / 145 s carries the same table without the discriminator sentence, which was added to the probe and the window re-run). Both asserted self-tests green: (A) the reproduction anchor reads counts (58,58,58,58) at ×1 and (62,62,62,62) at resolution 0.012, matching GEO-30 digit for digit, with sheet-area spreads 6.050235e-16 / 8.470329e-16 against the imported, unmoved 1e-3 (:7281–7283); (B) the metric self-test reads d(P1,P1) = 0.000000e+00 exactly and d(P1, P1 + ℓ·(1,1,1)/√3) = 2.111761e-03 m = 1.000000 ℓ against the ℓ/2 bar 1.055880e-03 m, so the metric separates (:7284–7286). Verdict — SAME SUPPORT, SAME BOUNDARY, DIFFERENT INTERIOR CUT, at all four rungs (:7270–7279): the bounding-box discrepancy between sheet i and the rotated sheet-1 image is ≤ 5.633375e-18 m (≈ 3e-15 ℓ) everywhere for both the full and the boundary vertex sets, the boundary-vertex Hausdorff is ≤ 2.881029e-14 m (≈ 1.5e-11 ℓ) everywhere with equal boundary-vertex counts on all four sheets at all four rungs (30/30/30/30, 34/34/34/34 at ×0.75), while the facet-centroid Hausdorff reaches 0.44–0.99 ℓ — a full facet-edge length. The four sheets are the same four patches, cut differently by gmsh; this is not a defect in birdcage_port_domain's sheet emission, and the follow-on question is whether the lumped-sheet reconstruction is cut-sensitive at fixed area. Two readings beyond what GEO-30 handed over, and both sharpen the question rather than answering it: (i) equal facet counts do not imply a congruent cut — at ×1, the 58/58/58/58 rung every gate builds on, P3 and P4 are not C4 images of P1 (d = 1.114339e-03 m = 0.53 ℓ each) while P2 matches to 2.570e-14, and resolution 0.012 shows the same on P4 alone (1.176057e-03 m = 0.58 ℓ), so the cut asymmetry is present on the two rungs that behaved and GEO-30's facet-count reading understated it; (ii) the cut asymmetry is not the C2 pattern the counts showed — at ×0.75 the centroid metric does follow the counts (0 / 0.9897 / 0 / 0.9897 ℓ against 80/74/80/74) but at 0.0095 it does not (counts 70/76/70/76, d_i = 0 / 0.4569 / 0.5069 / 0.4378 ℓ, P3 differing despite an equal count). Meanwhile the sorted per-facet-area multisets are identical to ≤ 1.5e-11 relative wherever the counts permit the comparison — including the ×1 P3/P4 pair whose centroids are 0.53 ℓ apart: same area distribution, different placement (:7056–7269). Nothing was fixed, no band moved, no rung rehabilitated. Disposition, 2026-09-10 03:00 review: accepted as measured (20260910T003835Z_GEO-31.log:7270–7286, both asserted self-tests green; 🧪, no audit owed). The generator is excluded on support and boundary; the surviving candidate is the lumped-sheet port model integrating over a different interior cut. Reading (i) is the one that sets the frame: the cut asymmetry exists on the ×1 rung every port gate passed on, so refinement amplified an existing asymmetry rather than creating one. The follow-on is PORT-18 (solve-free: does the sheet read-back integral carry the cut into the port current, and does quadrature degree cure it?). ANS-4 step 2a and WF-6 step 4f stay blocked on it; nothing is rehabilitated here. | 🧪 MEASURED 2026-09-09 19:30 slot — measurement-only, 🧪 by the §3 rule; the table is the deliverable and the review that reads it owns the disposition

docs.title: GEO-32 — Force a C4-congruent port-sheet cut by construction
docs.text: Force a C4-congruent port-sheet cut by construction — do GEO-31's cut asymmetry and PORT-18's read-back lead vanish with it? — opened 2026-09-10 10:30 review, ruling (1), on PORT-18's exclusion of the '+'-side mechanism. GEO-31 measured the four sheets as the same patch cut four ways (facet-centroid Hausdorff 0.44–0.99 ℓ, ×1 included). PORT-18 then printed that the N1curl interpolant read-back spread of a smooth C4-invariant field tracks the rungs that broke — ×1 7.223213e-06 → ×0.75 3.520702e-04; resolution 0.012 3.139712e-06 → 0.0095 7.307614e-04 — with GEO-31's sheet pairings (20260910T093526Z_PORT-18.log). Neither reading is causal until the cut is made congruent and the symptom is re-read. This chunk builds that lever and reads the geometry. No solve. Implementer (a src/ keyword), real build. Change: an opt-in keyword c4_congruent_sheets: bool = False on MeshGenerator.birdcage_port_domain, threaded to _build_birdcage_port_model. It is valid only with emit_port_sheets=True, leg_gap_length set and leg_count == 4; otherwise raise ValueError naming the reason. When True, after the last occ.synchronize() that follows the fragment (io/mesh.py:4139–4160) and before gmsh.model.mesh.generate(3) (:4563), constrain sheets 2–4 to sheet 1 with gmsh.model.mesh.setPeriodic(2, [s_k], [s_1], list(_z_rotation_affine(θ_k − θ_1))). Use the sheets' post-fragment surface tags (from fragment_map) and the snapped affine, so the copy is exact at 90°. With False no new line executes. New probe scripts/probes/geo32_c4_congruent_sheet_cut.py builds each mesh with geo30's parameter set and RUNGS, and reads it with geo31's _measure_rung and port18's _measure_rung — import them, do not retype. Anchors (asserted): (A) reproduction, flag off — at ×1 and ×0.75 the flag-off build reproduces GEO-31 to its printed digits (20260910T003835Z_GEO-31.log:7270–7279): size_global 116 085 at ×1 (the GEO-19 record, imported unmoved 1% CELL_COUNT_BAND); facet counts 58/58/58/58 and 80/74/80/74; centroid Hausdorff d(P3) = 1.114339e-03 m at ×1 and 0.9897 ℓ on P2/P4 at ×0.75. (B) congruence, flag on — at both rungs the four sheets' facet counts are equal and every sheet's facet-centroid Hausdorff against the rotated sheet 1 is ≤ 1e-12 m (≈ 5e-10 ℓ). For scale, GEO-31's boundary-vertex Hausdorff, congruent by construction, reads ≤ 2.9e-14 m. Negative control (asserted — separation from a same-fixture measurement): the flag-off max_i d_i is ≥ 0.4 ℓ at both rungs (GEO-31: 0.53 ℓ at ×1, 0.9897 ℓ at ×0.75), i.e. ≥ 8e8× the (B) bar. A keyword that silently does nothing fails (B); a metric that reads 0 regardless fails (A). Printed, asserted nowhere (rule (e)): per rung and flag — size_global, meshing time, sheet facet counts, sorted facet-area multisets, and PORT-18's smooth-field read-back spread (R^+, q = 2). At ×0.75 that spread is predicted to fall from 3.52e-04 toward the ×1 class (≈ 1e-5) with the flag on. Tier / ranks / cost: window 1 builds ×1 and ×0.75, flag off and on — four meshes at GEO-31's measured 25–37 s each plus facet passes (GEO-31 144 s for four meshes; PORT-18 154 s with interpolations) ⇒ -n 2, timeout -k 30 500, -s. Optional window 2: resolution 0.0095, both flags, -n 2, timeout -k 30 300. Regression: tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets.py at -n 2, timeout -k 30 300, green unchanged with the flag off. Standard by expectation, heavy by ceiling. Traps already paid for: setPeriodic takes post-fragment tags after the last occ.synchronize() — a pre-fragment tag names an entity the fragment deleted. gmsh matches the boundary curves itself under the affine and fails if they do not coincide; that failure is a finding, never something to loosen with a tolerance. Only the snapped _z_rotation_affine will do: last-bit coordinates move the cell count at 1e-3 (GEO-19 step B). Facet tags, size_local and centroids are rank-local — gather to rank 0 before any Hausdorff (GEO-31, OPS-40). Every SpatialCoordinate facet form pins quadrature_degree (POST-5). No UFL comparison, and no sqrt inside one (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). DG0 indicators need ghosts via scatter_forward() (PORT-18). timeout -k 30; foreground; no -k a or b; sweep 0-byte cache stubs only. Scope: a mesher lever and a geometric reading. It does not solve, re-run any port gate with the flag, or change the default; it moves no record, band or rung status, and ANS-4 step 2a / WF-6 step 4f stay blocked. Whether a congruent cut restores the ×0.75 Z class spreads is the follow-on solve, which the review queues from (B) and the printed spread. Negative result: if gmsh refuses the constraint, the mesh fails, or (B) misses ⇒ print gmsh's message and the d_i, do not land the keyword, park on attempt/*, mark BLOCKED, stop; the review then weighs a mesh-one-sector-and-copy construction. If (A) misses ⇒ the generator is not reproducible run-to-run, which undermines GEO-30/GEO-31's comparisons: report both readings, open a known-issues row, stop. If (B) is green but the printed spread is unchanged ⇒ the cut is excluded as the lead's carrier; record that, it is a finding. MEASURED 2026-09-10 15:00 slot — the lever works, all anchors green, and the cut is the lead's whole carrier (implementer; keyword c4_congruent_sheets in src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py, setPeriodic block immediately before generate(3), so after the as_hole drop's synchronize() too; post-fragment sheet surfaces read off the positional out-map, one surface per sheet required or RuntimeError; new scripts/probes/geo32_c4_congruent_sheet_cut.py; disclosed additive change: geo30._build_rung gained a c4_congruent_sheets=False pass-through, the generator's own default, so GEO-30/GEO-31/PORT-18 build the identical mesh). gmsh accepted the constraint on all three rungs built ([birdcage-mesh] c4_congruent_sheets: post-fragment sheet surfaces [36, 43, 50, 57] bound to master 36). Window 1 (-n 2, ×1 + ×0.75, flag off/on, timeout -k 30 500) 20260910T200420Z_GEO-32.log Status 0 / 127 s. (A) flag off reproduces GEO-31 to the printed digit: ×1 size_global 116 085 (ratio 1.000000, 1% band), counts (58, 58, 58, 58), d(P3) = 1.114339e-03 m; ×0.75 counts (80, 74, 80, 74), d(P2)/ℓ = d(P4)/ℓ = 0.9897 (:7442–7443). (B) flag on: counts (58, 58, 58, 58) and (80, 80, 80, 80), max d_i = 9.603429e-15 m at both rungs against the 1e-12 m bar (:7444, 7446). Negative control: flag-off max d_i = 0.527683 ℓ / 0.989700 ℓ against ≥ 0.4 ℓ (:7445, 7447). Optional window 2 (0.0095 rung, timeout -k 30 300) 20260910T200744Z_GEO-32.log Status 0 / 81 s: (B) counts (70, 70, 70, 70), max d_i 9.603429e-15 m; control 0.506854 ℓ (:3824–3825); (A) has no record there and is not evaluated. docs.text:
GEO-33 step 0b: the two-sided Leontovich term on 0a's duplicated lips. The anchor is Q_sep/Q₀ = 0.771914 against Pozar. The control is the merged single-valued sheet, which should read 1.000. Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2, complex build. Cost: ≈ 16 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min. Depends on nothing; 0a landed 85739849. Drafted by a read-only Plan agent and reviewed by the 03:00 review, which re-did the Pozar arithmetic and cut W2's ceiling to the standard tier.

  • Why. Item 149 showed the lips are separate: 108/108 twin facets sit at 0.0 m, and no vertex is shared. The cut spans the whole y = 0.4 plane, so the cracked box is two separate 1.0 × 0.4 × 0.6 half-cavities. Each lip is an exterior facet with its own outward normal, so TH-14's existing ds term (Jin §5.8.3; impedance condition Jin §1.5.3, eqs 1.54–1.57) already acts on both sides of the sheet. The new pieces are two:
  • an entry point that takes a supplied mesh;
  • an interior dS sheet, used only by the control.
  • Closed form. pozar_te10l_q_conductor (core/cavity.py:549). For TE₁₀₁, k does not depend on b, so R_s is common to both boxes. Q_c ∝ b / [b(2a³ + 2d³) + ad(a² + d²)], with 2a³ + 2d³ = 2.432 and ad(a² + d²) = 0.816. That gives 0.4/1.7888 ÷ 0.8/2.7616 = 0.7719141 (checked by the review). At σ = 1e4, Q₀ = 801.6849, TH-14's logged Q_c. The test computes the ratio from the function and asserts the literal against it to 1e-6.
  • Code (additive, opt-in; §9 rule (c)).
  • Move _cracked_box, _distribute and _tag from tests/mesh/test_geo33_cracked_cavity_lips.py into a new src/fem_em_solver/core/cracked_box.py as cracked_box_mesh(merge, comm, septum_tag=None).
    • The module must stay importable in the real build.
    • Keep GhostMode.shared_facet.
    • Fix the geometry.dofmap DeprecationWarning with the accessor the warning names.
    • septum_tag tags the interior y = 0.4 facets of the merged mesh (locate_entities, indices sorted and unique).
  • Add solve_impedance_mesh_mode(msh, *, sigma_s_per_m, k0_sq, sheet=(tags, tag) | None, degree=2, nev=6) to cavity.py.
    • It assembles curl-curl + γ⟨n×u, n×v⟩ ds over all exterior facets.
    • With sheet set it adds γ Σ± ⟨n±×u±, n±×v±⟩ dS(tag): a single-valued resistive sheet, R = Z_s/2 (Jin §1.5.4, eqs 1.60–1.63).
    • It returns the eigenvalues ordered by |λ − k₀²|.
    • Do not touch _cavity_forms or solve_impedance_wall_cavity_mode.
  • Point 0a's test at the new src module and delete its local copies.
  • New test: tests/validation/test_geo33_two_sided_leontovich.py. It skips on the real build, as TH-14's does.
  • Anchors (asserted; TH-14's 5 % band and TH-9's 1 % band, both imported, never restated).
  • (Q0) the merged mesh with walls only: Q₀ within 5 % of 801.6849. Predicted ≤ 0.5 %; the mesh is (9, 8, 6) mirrored, not TH-14's (9, 7, 6).
  • (Qs) the cracked mesh: Q_sep within 5 % of pozar_te10l_q_conductor((1.0, 0.4, 0.6), 1, 1e4).
  • (R) Q_sep/Q₀ within 5 % of 0.771914.
  • (F) Re f within 1 % of 291.3459 MHz.
  • (D) Im ω > 0 on all three solves.
  • Printed.
  • Both members of the degenerate pair (one per half).
  • 1/Q_sep − 1/Q₀ (predicted 3.686e-4).
  • The ratio at σ = 1e6 (predicted 0.771914 again).
  • Lip areas and dof counts.
  • Negative control (rule (e)). The merged mesh with the septum_tag sheet. TE₁₀₁ has E_t = 0 on that plane, so Q_sheet/Q₀ = 1.000.
  • Asserted: within 5 % of 1.000, and outside (R)'s band.
  • Predicted: |Δ| ≤ 1e-3, and a 29.5 % miss from 0.771914.
  • Ceiling: a sheet only adds loss, so the ratio is ≤ 1. The largest possible miss is therefore 1/0.771914 − 1 = 29.5 %, which is 5.9× the band. Assert no larger factor.
  • What it does not prove: it shows the sheet is single-valued, but a sheet that does nothing also reads 1.000. (Q0) against (Qs) is the half that bites.
  • Cost. TH-14 solves take 1.3–1.8 s each at -n 2 (2 268 cells, 15 998 dofs), and its module windows took 58–77 s. 0a's windows took 3–8 s.
  • Windows (Bash timeout: 660000; foreground; bare and whole).
  • W1, real build, 0a re-gate, must reproduce item 149's readings: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-33-step0b-W1-0a "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/mesh/test_geo33_cracked_cavity_lips.py -s -v --tb=short'"
