The preflight therefore tags the wall dolfinx-side as the exterior facets, and prints that it did. The test counts the wall independently (3310 = 3310); the wall area of 0.3072 m² is printed against the model bbox, rel −1.77e-6. Not ratified: the review's † readings. The fallback is removed; the import's wall group written (§9 item 119: exterior skin of all volumes, no tolerance; 6 surfaces, 3310 = 3310 owned exterior facets on both configs, ∫ds(1) = 0.3072 m² rel −3.3e-16; 20261001T003201Z_GEO-34-wall-W1.log, W2 20261001T003338Z_GEO-34-wall-W2.log:5718–5722), so the wall re-enters step 2's identity. (Ruled 2026-09-30 18:00 review: step 2 ✅ stands on the solve path's own groups — the 11 cell tags and sheets 211–214 — with (ii), (n1) and (n2). The wall leg is a record, not part of the identity (rule (h)): the solve path's wall group is empty, so "3310 = 3310" compares the preflight's exterior-facet fallback with the test's own exterior-facet count — a writer round trip, not C_file = C_solve. The fallback is kept as a disclosed workaround until the import_step wall predicate is fixed (§9 item 119, which restores the wall to the identity and removes the fallback); the † readings go to the weekly as before.) Step 2 Done-when (written 2026-09-30 10:30 review, rule (j); §9 item 118; the readings marked † are the review's and are named in the dashboard for ratification): scripts/run_step_case.py STEP CONFIG --preflight --out DIR († "the runner" is this new entry point, preflight-only — no STEP runner exists today and a solve mode is not step 2's), in the real build and with no solve, writes the combined .xdmf / .h5 (cell tags; the outer wall and the four gap sheets as facet tags, † declared by one new config key port_sheets) and the setup PNG for the F-small STEP under the congruent config; the census read back from that file — owned cells and volume per cell tag, facets per facet tag, area per sheet — equals that of an independent import_step on the same STEP and config with the solve path's sheet rebuild (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:349–352), counts exactly and volumes and areas to 1e-9 relative; each sheet's area in the file is SHEET_AREA_M2 within SHEET_AREA_TOL; and the preflight run from 1a's config fails that equality (asserted control). † The file carries the full gap sheet (66 facets), not the f = 0.5 narrowed drive sheet, which is test-level. Why: every fixture so far is built from Gmsh primitives inside io/mesh.py; the research coil, implants and anything an HFSS user would bring exist as CAD. The space of open solvers without a CAD path is full; the differentiator is a path that keeps the gates. Step 1 — import + tag map (standard): io/step_import.py (additive): import_step(path, config) runs gmsh.model.occ.importShapes, synchronises, and maps the config's named groups — CAD entity names where the STEP carries them, else geometric selectors (bounding box / centroid / axis, the same predicates the generator already uses) — to the project's physical-group tags (volumes: conductor / phantom / air / implant; surfaces: PEC, impedance, port sheets with drive direction and reference impedance); sizing fields per group; returns the same (mesh, cell_tags, facet_tags, diagnostics) tuple the primitive generators return. Config is one YAML/JSON file next to the STEP — the same shape as a Palace config and what an HFSS user thinks in. Gate (asserted): the F-small four-leg birdcage rebuilt from a STEP that a new CadQuery/build123d emitter writes from the same parameters (geo/step_emit.py, additive) reproduces, through import_step, the GEO-18 CAD identities (meshed/CAD conductor mass ≥ 0.95, terminal-area ratios in the imported band) and PORT-9's four-port gates at 10 MHz (reciprocity / passivity / C4 spread, imported bands) — the same identities, not the same cell count: a STEP round-trip changes the CAD kernel's tessellation, so cell-count records are printed beside the primitive rung's and not asserted (the (1*) licence question is named in the row: mesher-dependent records become routine under STEP, and a re-record needs the reconciler, never this step). Negative control (asserted): the config with the port-sheet group deliberately unmapped fails the import with a message naming the missing group — a silent untagged port is the failure a config invites. Step 2 — preflight export (standard): --preflight on the runner: mesh, tag, and write the combined XDMF plus the setup figure with materials, boundaries and ports as coloured regions and no solve; gate: the preflight's tag census equals the solve path's on the same STEP. This is the "see what I am doing before I solve" the operator asked for; an interactive viewer (pyvista/trame) is a later EX item, not a product surface. Step 3 — an external STEP (heavy by prediction, cost probe first): a STEP not written by our emitter — a 16-leg high-pass birdcage drawn in FreeCAD or CadQuery by the operator with named groups — imported, meshed, port-gated at 10 MHz; the first design that did not come from io/mesh.py. Not in scope: editing, a GUI, IGES/STL (STL has no CAD entities to name; a later step if needed). Sequencing: independent of the physics chains; step 1 is a slot item once the review costs it (the emitter and importer are pure Gmsh/OCC — measured in seconds on F-small); GEO-33's strip coil is the first consumer. Costed and split by the 2026-09-23 03:00 review (§9 item 37): step 1a = the STEP round trip, the config's group map and the mesh-level gates only (tag census, GEO-18's analytic sheet area, the CAD-mass gate; the unmapped-group control) — no solve; step 1b = PORT-9's four-port gates at 10 MHz on the imported mesh; step 1c = the independent-kernel emitter. Emitter substitution in 1a: CadQuery / build123d are not in the image (docker/Dockerfile), and adding them is an operator rebuild; 1a emits the STEP with Gmsh's own OCC writer (gmsh.write("….step") on the generator's model before meshing), which exercises the STEP reader, entity renumbering and the group map but not an independent CAD kernel — that independence is 1c's, when the image carries one (the weekly / operator decides).

docs.title: §9 item 289 — 2026-10-06 (chain U12)
docs.text:
Outcome 2026-10-07 03:30 slot — 🚫 BLOCKED at W0, branches (b) and (c) together (20261007T034333Z_GEO-34-step1d-W0-names.log, Status 0, 1 s, one rank, gmsh 4.15.2, probe tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step_names.py). The writer reported 396 STEP entities, 18 597 bytes; the strings PortSheet and AirBox occur 0 times in the file text, although both were set by setEntityName and as named physical groups. On re-import the one volume is named with the translator's label (Shapes/Open CASCADE STEP translator 7.6 1/…), every dim-2 name is empty, and there are no physical groups (:47–60). The embedded 0.48 m² rectangle is gone too: after import there are only 6 faces, each of area 1.0 (the box skin), getEmbedded is empty, and nothing changes after removeAllDuplicates (:61–74). So Gmsh's own writer cannot author this fixture on this image, whether by name or by geometry. No src/ edit and no test were written. There is no geometric-selector substitute (brief rule). Unblock: a STEP from a kernel that writes named, embedded faces, for example cq-python (dashboard item 10, step 1c). After that the weekly re-poses U12. Known-issues entry 2026-10-07.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-06 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 U12 (grep "U12. GEO-34 step 1d"), quoted, not changed: "A STEP from Gmsh's own OCC kernel (the operator's independent-kernel STEP is step 1c, dashboard item 10, and stays open): one box, one named interior rectangle; the config maps the name to port; the importer tags it natively (U11) and the meshed area equals the CAD rectangle at STRIP_BAND at -n 1 / 2 / 4. Target: CAD identity. Serial on U11." U11 landed green as item 267 (f0144df2): the native interior tag works on a shared_facet-ghosted mesh, and the unghosted -n 4 leg hangs. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved.

GEO-34 step 1d: a named interior STEP face becomes a port tag through import_step. - Executor: implementer. It makes an additive src/ change (io/step_import.py) and adds tests. Spawn prompt: "Use the implementer agent to execute GEO-34 step 1d (§9 item 289) per docs/planning/chunks/GEO-34.md § '§9 item 289'; W0 first, before any code." - Tier: standard by ceiling (180 s), smoke-sized by prediction. The fixture is item 222's: 10 150 tets, import 0.14 s, item 267's W2 56 s for seven launches. -n 1 / 2 / 4, real build (every integrand is real). - Class: chain step (solve). Time: ≈ 9 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 code + W0 ≈ 1 + W1 ≈ 1.5 + W2 ≈ 2 + ≈ 5 spare). - Depends on: U11 (item 267), landed. Nothing open.

The importer today (src/fem_em_solver/io/step_import.py, read 2026-10-06). - import_step claims volumes only, by geometric selectors (claim_volumes, :108). - The only surface groups it writes are the optional outer_boundary_tag (:196–240) and the congruent_sheets binding (:328). It reads no STEP entity names. - It already distributes through _model_to_mesh with GhostMode.shared_facet (:411–417), so U11's ghost requirement holds by construction. The step must not add a path that meshes unghosted. - The preflight's port_sheets key (io/step_preflight.py:12) rebuilds sheets dolfinx-side from volume pairs (between). It is not a native tag and is not touched here.

W0 — name survival (decides the item; run before any code). It is unknown whether Gmsh 4.15.2's OCC STEP writer carries a face's name, and whether importShapes surfaces it through gmsh.model.getEntityName. Nothing in the repo has measured this; scripts/maintenance/install_cadquery_image.sh:111 prints names only for a CadQuery file. - Probe tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step_names.py (not collected; committed as the record). On one rank: 1. Item 222's box plus rectangle: import RECT / RECT_AREA / H from tests/mesh/probe_geo37_interior_facet.py; occ.fragment([(3, box)], [(2, rect)]). 2. Name the rectangle PortSheet both ways: gmsh.model.setEntityName(2, s, "PortSheet") and a dim-2 physical group setPhysicalName(2, 201, "PortSheet"). Name the volume AirBox the same two ways. 3. gmsh.write(<tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="geo34_1d_")>/box_port.step), then finalize. 4. Re-open with a fresh session and occ.importShapes. Print getEntityName for every dim-2 / dim-3 entity, the face count, and each face's bbox and getMass area, both before and after occ.removeAllDuplicates(). Also print whether the 0.48 m² face is in the volume's getBoundary (embedded) or free. - Command:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-34-step1d-W0-names "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 10 30 python3 tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step_names.py'" - Branches: - (a) A face named …PortSheet (exact, or as the last /-separated component, since OCC labels can carry an assembly path) exists after import, with area 0.48 to 1e-12. Proceed. Record which naming route survived and whether the name also survives removeAllDuplicates. - (b) No name survives. Stop: commit the probe and log as a record, journal the attempt, mark BLOCKED. The finding is that Gmsh's writer cannot author a named STEP on this image. A geometric selector is not "a named face", so the review re-poses U12 (for example onto cq-python once dashboard item 10 lands). Do not substitute a bbox selector. - (c) The name survives but the face is not re-embedded after removeAllDuplicates (free face, or two faces). Stop as in (b), with that finding.

Code (on W0 branch (a) only). 1. io/step_import.py, additive config key surface_groups: [{"name": "port_1", "step_name": "PortSheet", "role": "port", "tag": 201}, …]. If the key is absent, the import is byte-identical (rule (c), W2). - Resolve names before healing. Right after importShapes + synchronize and before removeAllDuplicates, map each step_name to its dim-2 entities by getEntityName (exact, or last path component), and record each face's bbox and occ.getMass(2, ·) area. Entity tags renumber under removeAllDuplicates, so a pre-heal tag is never used afterwards. - After the heal, re-find each face among the post-heal dim-2 entities: bbox equal per coordinate to 1e-6 (the OCC padding trap, item 222 W1) and area equal to 1e-12 relative. Require exactly one match. - Errors are ValueError, raised on the building rank and re-raised on every rank by the existing broadcast. They cover: - a step_name absent from the file (the message names it and lists the names present); - zero or several post-heal matches; - a role other than "port" (the only role this step licenses); - a tag colliding with a volume tag or outer_boundary_tag. - Then addPhysicalGroup(2, [s], tag) and setPhysicalName(2, tag, name). - Diagnostics gain surface_groups: {name: {"tag", "role", "step_name", "surface", "cad_area", "n_triangles"}}. n_triangles is read after generate(3) from gmsh.model.mesh.getElements(2, s). - The module docstring's config block gains the key. 2. Config tests/mesh/data/geo34_step1d_port_sheet.json: - resolution = item 222's H (0.08; the test asserts equality, as test_config_sizes_are_the_gates does); - one volume group air (tag 1, bbox_contains the unit box's interior point box); - outer_boundary_tag 101; - surface_groups [{"name": "port_1", "step_name": "PortSheet", "role": "port", "tag": 201}]. 3. Test tests/mesh/test_step_import_port_sheet.py, real build, any width. - A module fixture writes the STEP on rank 0 into a tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="geo34_1d_") directory, broadcast as test_step_import.py:113–117 does. The writer is W0's naming route, factored into a function and imported from the probe. The STEP is never written into the tree. - Then import_step(step, CONFIG, comm).

Anchors (asserted at every width; STRIP_BAND = 1e-9 imported from tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58). - (P0) ghosts: comm.allreduce(index_map(3).num_ghosts) is > 0 at -n 2 / 4 and 0 at -n 1. The width's cells_ghost is printed. This is U11's precondition, checked on the imported mesh. - (P1) CAD identity: the owned tag-201 facet area (numpy triangle areas over facets with index < index_map(2).size_local, allreduced) satisfies |A/RECT_AREA − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND and |A/diagnostics cad_area − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND. - (P2) completeness: the reduced owned tag-201 facet count equals diagnostics n_triangles exactly. Every tag-201 facet has two incident cells on the ghosted mesh: the one-sided count, reduced, is 0. That proves the face is embedded, not a skin. - (P3) the port form (U11): assemble_scalar(form(1 * dS(201))), allreduced, with metadata={"quadrature_degree": 2}, satisfies |I/RECT_AREA − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND. - (P4) the role reaches the port layer: the globally reduced facet-tag set is {101, 201}, and validate_required_port_tags_exist (ports/definitions.py:82) passes on 201 with that set.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (n1) asserted, unknown name: the same STEP with step_name "PortSheetX" raises ValueError on every rank, and the message contains PortSheetX. This is the "silent untagged port" failure the config invites (1a's unmapped-group control, for faces). - (n2) asserted, the mapping makes the tag: the same STEP with surface_groups removed imports, and its reduced tag set lacks 201. So the tag comes from the config, not from any physical group or label the STEP carries (W0 records which ones survive). - (n3) asserted, the comparator is not blind: re-tag 201 without its first owned facet on the lowest owning rank (item 267's (c2)). |A′/RECT_AREA − 1| > STRIP_BAND. The ceiling is ≈ 1/n_triangles (item 267: −4.5e-3 / −5.1e-3), ≈ 10⁶ × the band.

Predictions (printed): (P1) / (P3) residuals ≤ 1e-14 (item 267: ≤ 1.6e-15); n_triangles near 192 (item 222's count on the primitive). The count is printed, not asserted against 192, because a STEP round trip may move the tessellation (1a's licence). There is no PREDICTED RED: line.

Windows (each bare, whole and foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; -s; pytest is the last command of each launch). - W0: above (≈ 5–15 s). - W1 (closing). Widths are chained with && so the footer carries the first failure. tests/environment is narrowed to test_complex_mode.py: item 267's W1 lost its whole 30 s pytest ceiling to test_dolfinx_api_migration.py's repository scan.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-34-step1d-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 10 60 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/mesh/test_step_import_port_sheet.py -v -s --tb=short && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 10 60 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/mesh/test_step_import_port_sheet.py -v -s --tb=short && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 10 60 mpiexec -n 4 python3 -m pytest tests/mesh/test_step_import_port_sheet.py -v -s --tb=short'"

Predicted 25–60 s. - W2, rule (c): the key-absent path is unchanged. It runs 1a's module at -n 2. The precedent is the 1b′ rule-(c) window, 85 s, 4 passed (20260926T094036Z_GEO-34-step1bprime-ruleC.log).

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-34-step1d-W2-ruleC "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/mesh/test_step_import.py -v -s --tb=short'" - No edit after W1 starts (rule (i)). If W2 must follow an edit, W1 is re-run.

Traps already paid for. - Unghosted dS hangs at -n 4 (item 267 (c3); 2026-08 PORT-1 3b-iv). Mesh only through import_step, which ghosts. Never call _model_to_mesh with the default partitioner in this test. - OCC bbox padding ≈ 1e-7: match at 1e-6 and guard with the exact area (item 222 W1). - Pre-heal tags die in removeAllDuplicates: resolve names before the heal, then re-find faces by geometry. - Rank-local reads: allreduce every count, area and assemble_scalar. Gather the tag set before the validator (OPS-14). Use the owned filter index_map(2).size_local. - A rank-0 gmsh throw must reach every rank before the collective: reuse import_step's broadcast, never a rank-0-only raise (GEO-23). - A SpatialCoordinate-free measure still needs a pinned quadrature degree on gmsh meshes (POST-5). - One gmsh session at a time in a process: finalize the writer's session before import_step initializes its own. - After a kill: run pgrep -c python3 first, then clear /dev/shm/mpich_shm_* (known-issues). Run the orphan-.c sweep only at pgrep 0. - No pipes. PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace. Write ≈, never ~.

Scope. Covered: one planar rectangle in one box from Gmsh's own OCC writer; a name-to-port mapping; the native tag on the ghosted import at -n 1 / 2 / 4; area, completeness and dS against the CAD rectangle. Not claimed: - an independent-kernel STEP (1c); - any port solve, S or F14 integration line; - roles other than port (PEC / copper / lumped sheets); - curved, multi-face or interface sheets; - the F-small STEP (U13); - the preflight's facet grid for surface_groups; - xl widths.

Status it can move. - Green: the GEO-34 §7 row gains a "step 1d" record clause (the name route that survived, P1–P3 residuals per width, elapsed). §10 U12 is marked DONE and U13 (the Study on a STEP-imported F-small) is unblocked. - No glyph: steps 1c and 3 stay open (row read 2026-10-06), so GEO-34 stays 🟡. - Rule (j): the row has no step-1d Done-when. The review adds this one at queueing: "a Gmsh-OCC STEP of one box with one named interior rectangle, mapped by surface_groups to port, imports with the rectangle as a native facet tag whose owned area equals the CAD rectangle at STRIP_BAND, count equal to gmsh's triangles, dS at STRIP_BAND, at -n 1 / 2 / 4 in one logged window; unknown-name control raises". - W0 (b) / (c): a known-issues entry ("Gmsh 4.15.2's STEP writer drops entity names", or "does not keep an embedded face"), and U12 goes back to the weekly for re-posing.

Negative result. Report and stop. Never substitute a geometric selector, and never widen a band. - (P1) / (P3) red with (P2) and (n3) green: the imported tag is wrong on 0.11. Open a known-issues entry and park on attempt/GEO-34-step1d-<UTC>, BLOCKED. - (P0) zero ghosts at -n 2 / 4, or a 60 s kill at -n 4: this contradicts U11 on an imported mesh. Record it and mark BLOCKED. - (n1) / (n2) / (n3) red: the instrument is wrong and the verdict void. Fix it once in the new test, re-run in-slot and disclose. If it is still red, park and mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). - W2 red: the key-absent path moved. Revert the src/ edit and mark BLOCKED.

docs.title: §9 item 333 — 2026-10-08 (chain U12a — GEO-34 step 1d probe; mesh-probe)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 U12a (grep "U12a. GEO-34 step 1d probe"), quoted, not changed: "mesh-probe: the box-and-rectangle model exported as a compound (solid + the face as its own shell) and as a shell-only STEP; after importShapes, the number of dim-2 bodies and their areas against 0.48 m², names present or not, at -n 1. Measurement only; green ⇒ U12′ gains a same-kernel rehearsal branch, red ⇒ 9b waits on item 10. Serial on nothing." No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved. Measurement only (§3): nothing is asserted, and GEO-34 stays 🟡.

GEO-34 step 1d probe: can Gmsh's own OCC kernel carry an interior face through a STEP file in any export form? - Executor: mesh-probe. It produces a table and one probe script. There is no src/ change, no test, and no assertion. Spawn prompt: "Use the mesh-probe agent. Generator: Gmsh 4.15.2's OCC STEP writer and occ.importShapes on GEO-37 item 222's box-and-rectangle fixture. Swept parameter: the export form (F-frag / F-solid / F-comp / F-shell / F-two) × the importShapes read (default / highestDimOnly=False). Question: does the 0.48 m² rectangle come back as exactly one face embedded in the one volume after removeAllDuplicates? Brief: docs/planning/chunks/GEO-34.md § '§9 item 333'. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Pass timeout: 660000 and run in the foreground." - Tier: smoke (30 s), by prior measurement. W0 wrote and re-read this exact fixture in one process in 1 s elapsed (20261007T034333Z_GEO-34-step1d-W0-names.log:79). This item runs five child processes, so predict ≈ 5–10 s per window. Width -n 1, plain python3 with no mpiexec: a gmsh throw on rank 0 at -n 2 deadlocks the command (mesh-probe rule). Real build; no DolfinX object is built. - Class: chain step (no solve). Time: ≈ 7 measured / ≈ 30 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 10 script + 2 windows ≈ 1 + ≈ 4 journal / table). - Depends on: nothing. - Family: the 03:00 review counted the GEO-34 1d family at 1 of 4 (item 289's W0 BLOCKED). The review rules whether a measurement-only probe counts. If it does, this item makes it 2 of 4 and leaves U12′ at 3.

What exists today. - The importer: src/fem_em_solver/io/step_import.py:154–166 (_build). It runs gmsh.model.occ.importShapes(str(path)) with the default arguments (:164), then occ.removeAllDuplicates() (:165), then synchronize. It sets no Geometry.OCC* option except the optional OCCTargetUnit (:159–161). - The fixture: RECT = (0.1, 0.2, 0.47, 0.8, 0.6), RECT_AREA = 0.48, in tests/mesh/probe_geo37_interior_facet.py:30–31. - W0's writer: write_named_box_port_step in tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step_names.py:28–64. It fragments the box with the rectangle, names both entities two ways, writes, and finalizes. - What W0 already paid for: neither name string occurs in the file (:45–46). On re-import there is 1 volume and 6 faces, each of area 1.0. No 0.48 face exists, nothing is embedded, and removeAllDuplicates changes nothing (:47–74). The OCC bbox carries ±1e-7 padding (:49–56).

Probe: tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step1d_export_forms.py (new; not collected; committed as the record). It imports RECT / RECT_AREA from probe_geo37_interior_facet and write_named_box_port_step, PORT_NAME and VOL_NAME from probe_geo34_step_names. It restates none of them. - Fresh process per form. The driver runs subprocess.run([sys.executable, __file__, "--form", F]) once per form. Each child writes its STEP in one gmsh session, finalizes it, and reads the file back in a second session that it also finalizes. - Exit code. The driver prints each child's stdout. A crashed child becomes a FAIL cell holding the last stderr lines. The driver exits with the largest child return code, so the footer is honest. - Scratch files. STEP files go to /workspace/logs/geo34_step1d_probe/<form>/, which is the gitignored /logs/. They are never written into the tracked tree. - The forms. Wherever a form has them, the face is named PortSheet and the volume AirBox, both by setEntityName and by a named physical group, exactly as in W0. - F-frag (control, W0 reproduction): write_named_box_port_step, unchanged. - F-solid (control): the unfragmented unit box only. - F-comp (the compound): the unfragmented box plus addRectangle(*RECT) as a free face, in one model with no fragment, and one gmsh.write. - F-shell (shell-only): the rectangle alone. - F-two (two-file merge): F-solid's file and F-shell's file are both passed to importShapes in one reader session. - The two reads. Each file is read (r1) with the default importShapes(path), which is how the importer reads at :164, and (r2) with importShapes(path, highestDimOnly=False). - What each child prints: - first, inspect.signature(gmsh.model.occ.importShapes); - the value of every Geometry.OCC* option the reader can read: OCCImportLabels, OCCSewFaces, OCCMakeSolids, OCCFixDegenerated, OCCFixSmallEdges, OCCFixSmallFaces. These are read, never set; - the file's size and the number of STEP entities the writer reports; - how often PortSheet and AirBox occur in the file text; - the rest before and after removeAllDuplicates(): the dim-3 and dim-2 entity counts, and for every face its getEntityName, occ.getMass, bbox and upward adjacencies; - the counts of faces with |A/0.48 − 1| ≤ 1e-12 and bbox equal to RECT's per coordinate to 1e-6, of free faces (no upward adjacency), and of embedded faces (upward adjacency equal to the one volume); - mesh.getEmbedded(3, v) and the physical groups. - The table. The last line block is one row per form × read × stage, in the mesh-probe format.

Windows (each bare, whole and foreground; Bash timeout: 660000). - W1: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-34-step1d-probe "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 30 python3 tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step1d_export_forms.py'" - W2 (repeat, the mesh-probe determinism rule): the same command under the ID GEO-34-step1d-probe-repeat. Only a bit-identical table licenses the word "deterministic".

The anchor: fixed comparands, read as brackets in the readout, never asserted. - A_rect = 0.8 × 0.6 = 0.48 m² (RECT_AREA), matched at |A/0.48 − 1| ≤ 1e-12, with the bbox matched at 1e-6 (the padding trap). Box faces are 1.0 m² and the volume is 1.0 m³. - Expected counts per form (dim-3 / dim-2 / 0.48-faces / free / embedded, after the heal). Rule (e) labels:

Form Read Expected Label F-frag r1 1 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 0 backed: W0 :47–74, same writer, same fixture F-frag r2 1 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 0 predicted (the face is not in the file, by W0) F-solid r1, r2 1 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 0 predicted F-comp r1 1 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 0, the free face dropped by highestDimOnly=True predicted, from the Gmsh API's documented default; unverified on this image F-comp r2 before the heal 1 / 7 / 1 / 1 / 0; after it 1 / 7 / 1 / 0 / 1 predicted F-shell r1, r2 0 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 0 predicted F-two r2 after the heal 1 / 7 / 1 / 0 / 1 predicted all — PortSheet / AirBox occurrences 0 / 0 backed for F-frag (W0 :45–46), predicted for the rest

Decision rule (§10, unchanged). - Green means that F-comp (under either read) or F-two leaves exactly one 0.48 face, embedded in the one volume, after removeAllDuplicates. Then U12′ gains a same-kernel rehearsal branch. The readout names the form and the read. If the face survives only under r2, the readout says so: the rehearsal (and any CadQuery-assembly STEP) then needs an additive import_step read option, which is U12′'s change, not this item's. - Red means no form returns an embedded 0.48 face. Then 9b waits on dashboard item 10. - Amber means the face survives free but is not embedded after the heal (W0's branch-(c) shape). It is read as red for the decision; the review rules. - Names do not enter green. They are recorded. U12′'s name-to-port map still needs a kernel that writes labels, and a geometric-selector substitute stays forbidden.

Negative control. F-frag reproduces W0's 6-face, no-0.48 reading. F-solid shows zero free dim-2 bodies and zero 0.48 faces. If F-frag departs from W0 :47–74, the instrument or the image has moved: the window is void, and the executor stops and reports without taking a decision. If F-solid shows a 0.48 face or a free face, the face-matching code is wrong; the same applies.

Traps already paid for. - highestDimOnly (new, unmeasured). The importer's default read may silently drop a free face that sits beside a solid. That is why every file is read both ways and the signature is printed. Do not "fix" step_import.py:164. - One gmsh session per process. Finalize the writer before the reader initializes (item 289 trap). Use one child process per form. - Healing: removeAllDuplicates renumbers tags. Identify the face by area plus bbox, never by a pre-heal tag (item 289). Print the OCCSewFaces / OCCMakeSolids / fix options and never toggle them, because a sew could merge the free face into a shell. - Names: W0 found that the writer emits no label string at all (:45–46), so no reader option (OCCImportLabels) can recover a name. No writer-side label option is known to the repo. Toggling one is a follow-up for the review, not this item. - OCC bbox padding ≈ 1e-7: match at 1e-6 and use the exact area (item 222 W1; W0 :49–56). - Harness and shell: - The harness call is the whole Bash command (bash_guard rule 3). Container-side timeout -k 30, ceiling 30 s. - No pipe, no tee, no redirect. PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace. - STEP scratch goes under /workspace/logs/, never /tmp in the tree, and never as a committed artifact. Never delete a log. - After a kill: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 comes first. A kill at 30 s is not a result. Shrink to one --form per window, never a longer timeout. - Write ≈, never ~.

Scope. Covered: Gmsh 4.15.2's OCC writer and reader on one unit box and one planar rectangle; five export forms × two reads; counts, areas, adjacency and name strings at -n 1. Not claimed: - any gate, Done-when or glyph (GEO-34 stays 🟡; steps 1c, 3 and U12′ stay open); - a name route; - a mesh, a facet tag, dS, or any multi-rank reading; - a CadQuery STEP; - the F-small STEP (U13).

Status it can move. - §10 U12′: a green adds the same-kernel rehearsal branch, naming the form and read. A red adds "9b waits on dashboard item 10, measured: no Gmsh-OCC export form carries the face". - Dashboard item 10: its wording gains the measured clause ("Gmsh's own writer keeps no face names and no interior face in any export form", or "…keeps no names; a compound export carries the face, so a same-kernel rehearsal runs meanwhile"). - Known-issues 2026-10-07 (the "Gmsh 4.15.2's OCC STEP writer drops entity names…" entry): a Scope addendum on which forms keep the face. It does not retire, because names are still dropped. - highestDimOnly: if r1 drops a free face that r2 keeps, the readout flags it to the review as a finding against U12′'s importer read and against scripts/maintenance/install_cadquery_image.sh:111–120 (step 4b's len(faces) >= 7 read with the default). The review decides whether that is a known-issues entry. - The GEO-34 §7 row gains a one-clause U12a record (🧪 measurement, glyph unchanged). This chunk file gains the outcome paragraph.

Outcome (2026-10-08 16:30 slot): AMBER, read as red. A measurement record; GEO-34 stays 🟡; 1d family 2 of 4. Executor: mesh-probe. The probe is tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step1d_export_forms.py. W1 20261008T214725Z_GEO-34-step1d-probe.log and W2 20261008T214738Z_GEO-34-step1d-probe-repeat.log each ran Status 0 in 5 s at -n 1, with tables bit-identical (deterministic). Each cell below reads dim-3 / dim-2 / 0.48 / free / embedded. The heal changed nothing, so pre and post are equal everywhere. - Controls valid. F-frag reproduces W0 (1 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 0 under both reads), and F-solid is clean (1 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 0). - Compound (F-comp). r1 reads 1 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 0: the free face is dropped and importShapes returns [(3, 1)]. r2 reads 1 / 7 / 1 / 1 / 0. - Shell only and two-file merge. F-shell reads 0 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 0 under both reads. F-two, which goes beyond §10's two forms, reads 1 / 7 / 1 / 1 / 0 under both reads, because highestDimOnly applies per file. - Departure from the prediction. The brief predicted that removeAllDuplicates would embed the free face (1 / 7 / 1 / 0 / 1). It does not on this image: getEmbedded(3, v) is [], upward adjacency is [], and OCCSewFaces / OCCMakeSolids are 0, read and never set. - Names and options. PortSheet / AirBox occur 0 times in every file. OCCImportLabels is 1; the other OCC* options are 0. - Decision. The result is W0's branch-(c) shape in every form, so 9b waits on dashboard item 10. - highestDimOnly finding. r1 drops F-comp's free face. docs.title: §9 item 985 — 2026-11-14 (§10 U12′, chain U — rule (4), the weekly's enumerated step; GEO-34 step 1d re-posed; chain step (no solve))
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-11-14 10:30 daily review under §9 rule (4); drafted by a general-purpose agent and reviewed here. Corrections made at review: - the cost uses the current class median; - no Done-when is added to the §7 row (a daily never sets one); - the module hold is checked.

It does not count against rule (6). The target is the weekly's U12′ (docs/planning/plan-archive.md:39275–39281), quoted, not changed: "a CadQuery-authored STEP with a named interior face … the config maps the name to port, the importer tags it natively (U11, shared_facet ghosts) and the meshed area equals the CAD rectangle at STRIP_BAND at -n 1 / 2 / 4. Target: CAD identity." The serial prerequisite has landed: the operator's CadQuery install, 2026-11-14 (fa4a6e7f). Family GEO-34 1d: attempt 3 of 4. Item 289 was attempt 1 (BLOCKED at W0), and U12a / item 333 was attempt 2 (ruling Q2 above). A red here leaves one attempt.

Facts verified (by reading). - Install log (operator directive (b); gitignored logs/maintenance/cadquery_image_20261114T091828Z.log): - step 4a is green: cadquery 2.8.0, then wrote …cq_sample_…step (:381–382); - step 4b FAILED on -noenv (:434, :478), and the log stops there; - the corrected read (1 volume, 7 faces, both names) is in fa4a6e7f's message only. No log records it, so W0b re-measures it in a logged window. - The 4d log does not test interior facets. 20261114T093413Z_GEO-34-cadquery-image-4d.log reads 5 passed, 13 skipped, 104 s, Status 0. The passes are all test_step_import.py's. Every test_geo37_interior_facet.py node skipped because GEO37_RECORD_DIR is unset. Cite this log for the image, not for interior facets. - The sample's sheet is a free face, not an embedded one. It is its own product, PRODUCT('PortSheet') → OPEN_SHELL, beside the AirBox solid. U12a measured that removeAllDuplicates does not embed a free face. So the importer must embed it explicitly, as item 222 did with occ.fragment([(3, box)], [(2, rect)]) (probe_geo37_interior_facet.py:40). - Units. The STEP declares millimetres but holds the numbers as drawn. Leave occ_target_unit unset. - The importer (src/fem_em_solver/io/step_import.py): - _build calls importShapes(str(path)) with defaults (:164), then removeAllDuplicates (:165); - it claims volumes only, and the wall is the combined boundary of every volume; - it ghosts with shared_facet; - unknown config keys are ignored (step_preflight.py:14), so additive keys have a seam. - Fixture. RECT = (0.1, 0.2, 0.47, 0.8, 0.6), RECT_AREA = 0.48, H = 0.08 (probe_geo37_interior_facet.py:30–32). STRIP_BAND = 1.0e-9 (tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58). - U11. The native-tag dS passed at STRIP_BAND only on a ghosted mesh. Unghosted -n 4 was killed at 45 s (GEO-37.md:165–176). - Ignore rules. *.step is gitignored (.gitignore:57–58). - Hold (checked at review). No queued window (64, 65) imports io/step_import.py; io/mesh.py names it only in a docstring (:4385). The importer is free.

Code (scripts, tests, one committed STEP, two additive importer keys). 1. tests/mesh/cq_author_geo34_step1d.py (new; not collected). It runs under cq-python, which clears PYTHONPATH (Dockerfile:41), so it restates RECT as literals. - Build the box with cq.Workplane("XY").box(1, 1, 1, centered=False). - Build the sheet as an explicit polygon with corners (0.1, 0.2, 0.47) … (0.1, 0.8, 0.47). Do not use makePlane: its orientation is ambiguous. - Assemble the products AirBox and PortSheet, as the sample did. - Assert, CadQuery-side, face area 0.48 to 1e-12 and the bbox. - Export with asm.export(out); 2.8 warns that save is going. If export is absent, fall back to save and disclose it. - Print the sha256 and the byte count. 2. Commit the STEP as tests/mesh/data/geo34_step1d_port_sheet.step, with a narrow !tests/mesh/data/geo34_step1d_*.step negation after .gitignore:58. Never regenerate it per run: - pytest runs in the DolfinX interpreter, which never imports CadQuery; - only fem-em-solver carries the venv, so other services would skip, and a skip hides a failure; - the STEP header carries a timestamp; - an externally authored file is what 9b's user brings.

The test pins W0a's logged sha256 for custody. This departs from item 289's "never in the tree", which was written for an in-process Gmsh STEP. 3. io/step_import.py, two additive keys. With both absent, behaviour is byte-identical (rule (c)). - "highest_dim_only": false makes the call importShapes(str(path), highestDimOnly=False). When the key is absent, :164 stays verbatim. - "surface_groups": [{"name": "port_1", "step_name": "PortSheet", "role": "port", "tag": 201}]. - Resolve each step_name by getEntityName: an exact match, or the last / component. Exactly one dim-2 entity must match. Resolve before or after the heal, whichever W0b shows the names survive. - Then call out, out_map = occ.fragment(<all dim-3>, <named faces>) and trace each named face's children through out_map. This is identity by name plus topological lineage. A bbox or centroid selector stays forbidden. - Require exactly one child, with area equal to the pre-fragment getMass to 1e-12, and upward adjacency equal to the volume. If W0b shows the child in the wall set, remove the named faces from the wall group by tag. - Raise ValueError through the existing broadcast for: a name absent (list the names present), a non-unique match, a non-embedded child, role != "port", or a tag collision. - Add diagnostics surface_groups[name] = {tag, role, step_name, surface, cad_area, n_triangles, route}, and document both keys in the docstring. 4. Config tests/mesh/data/geo34_step1d_port_sheet.json: - resolution 0.08, asserted equal to H; - air tag 1 (bbox_contains); - outer_boundary_tag 101; - highest_dim_only false; - the surface_groups above. 5. Probe and test. tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step1d_cq_read.py (W0b; not collected) and tests/mesh/test_step_import_cq_port_sheet.py (a real build, at any width).

W0b prints (one rank, both reads): - per-entity names and dims, before and after removeAllDuplicates; - the fragment map, with each child's area, bbox and upward adjacency; - whether the child is in getBoundary(getEntities(3), combined=True, oriented=False, recursive=False); - the bbox and the sha256.

Decision: - Name found and the fragment child embedded ⇒ write the importer code. - No name, or no embedded child ⇒ stop, BLOCKED (family 3 of 4), with no in-slot workaround.

Anchors (asserted at every width; every count reduced). - (P0) allreduce(index_map(3).num_ghosts) is > 0 at -n 2 / 4 and 0 at -n 1. - (P1) CAD identity. allreduce the owned tag-201 triangle areas (filter by index_map(2).size_local). Assert |A / RECT_AREA − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND and |A / cad_area − 1| ≤ STRIP_BAND, with cad_area = 0.48 to 1e-12. - (P2) The reduced owned 201 count equals n_triangles exactly, and the reduced count of one-sided 201 facets is 0 (embedded, not a skin). - (P3) allreduce(assemble_scalar(form(1*dS(201)))), with quadrature_degree pinned at 2, is within STRIP_BAND of 0.48. - (W) The instrument check: the ds(101) area is within STRIP_BAND of 6.0. - (P4) The gathered tag set is {101, 201}, and validate_required_port_tags_exist (ports/definitions.py:82) passes on 201. - Custody. The file's sha256 equals W0a's logged value. - Printed, not asserted: the residuals (predicted ≤ 1e-14; item 267 read ≤ 1.6e-15) and n_triangles.

Negative controls. - (n-hDO) The same config without highest_dim_only raises ValueError naming PortSheet. This is predicted from U12a's r1 reading (20261008T214725Z_GEO-34-step1d-probe.log), and asserted once W0b prints it on this fixture, with that line cited in the docstring (rule (e)). - (n1) step_name "PortSheetX" raises on every rank, and the message contains the name. - (n2) Without surface_groups, the reduced tag set lacks 201. - (n3) Drop the first owned 201 facet on the lowest owning rank. Then |A′ / 0.48 − 1| > STRIP_BAND. The ceiling is ≈ 1 / n_triangles ≈ 5e-3 (item 267: −4.48e-3 / −5.07e-3), ≈ 5×10⁶ × the band. The factor is printed and labelled predicted.

Windows. Bare, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000. docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0 first. No complex build is needed, because every integrand is real. - W0a (author): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-34-U12p-W0a-author "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 cq-python tests/mesh/cq_author_geo34_step1d.py tests/mesh/data/geo34_step1d_port_sheet.step'" (≈ 6 s; the sample took 6 s). - W0b (read): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-34-U12p-W0b-read "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 30 python3 tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step1d_cq_read.py tests/mesh/data/geo34_step1d_port_sheet.step'" (≈ 1–5 s). - W1 (closing): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-34-U12p-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/mesh/test_step_import_cq_port_sheet.py -v -s --tb=short && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/mesh/test_step_import_cq_port_sheet.py -v -s --tb=short && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 mpiexec -n 4 python3 -m pytest tests/mesh/test_step_import_cq_port_sheet.py -v -s --tb=short'". Predicted 25–60 s (item 267: 56 s for seven launches). The && stops at the first red width. - W2a (rule (c)): the 4d command (that log's :12), labelled GEO-34-U12p-W2a-ruleC, plus -v -s and tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py on the path (104 s on record). - W2b (rule (c)): the same command, labelled GEO-34-U12p-W2b-preflight, with path tests/mesh/test_step_preflight.py (117 s on record).

Tier. Standard by ceiling (180 s), smoke-sized by prediction; -n 1 / 2 / 4. Class: chain step (no solve). Cost: ≈ 10.8 measured (the class median) / ≈ 50 predicted min. About 20 min goes on code; the windows take ≈ 6 min.

Traps already paid for. - Harness discipline: - timeout -k 30 on every window; - every harness call is the whole Bash command (bash_guard): no pipes, tee or redirects; - PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace, and pytest runs with -s. - Parallel correctness: - rank-local values (assemble_scalar, facet tag values) are allreduced, and the tag set is gathered before the validator; - pytest verdicts are counted per rank, by token; - never delete a log. - Unghosted dS hangs at -n 4: mesh only through import_step. - fa4a6e7f's two check bugs: gmsh 4.15.2 has no -noenv, and the default highestDimOnly=True drops a free sheet (known-issues 2026-10-08). Change :164 only through the key. - Gmsh tags: - removeAllDuplicates and fragment renumber tags: never carry a pre-heal tag past them, and trace through out_map; - OCC bbox padding is ≈ 1e-7: print bboxes, never select by them; - one gmsh session per process. - Forms and ranks: pin quadrature_degree (POST-5), and broadcast a rank-0 throw to every rank (GEO-23). - Ownership: files the container writes are owned by nobody on the host, so author only from inside the container. - Commit hygiene: - after a kill, pgrep -c python3 first; - no edit after W1 (rule (i)); - never --no-verify. If the hook refuses the STEP, stop and report.

Scope. One planar rectangle in one box, authored by CadQuery 2.8.0: a name-to-port map, a native tag, and area, completeness and dS at three widths. Not claimed: - U13 (the Study on a STEP-imported F-small); - step 1c's F-small emitter; - 9b closure; - any port solve, S-parameter or band; - roles other than port; - multi-face or interface sheets; - the preflight's facet grid.

Negative result. Report and stop. Park on attempt/GEO-34-U12p-<UTC> and mark the item BLOCKED with the unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)). Open a known-issues entry. - W0b finds no name or no embedded child ⇒ BLOCKED. The review may re-pose to a CadQuery-side fragment with a named sub-shape (the family's last attempt); this slot does not try it. - (P1) or (P3) red with (P2), (n3) and (W) green ⇒ an import-tag defect: BLOCKED. - Any (n·) or (W) red ⇒ the instrument is void. Fix it once and re-run in-slot; if it is still red, BLOCKED. - W2 red ⇒ revert src/, then BLOCKED. - No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. - §10 U12′ → DONE, and U13 opens for the weekly to queue. - The GEO-34 §7 row gains a step-1d record clause. The glyph stays 🟡 (1c's F-small emitter and step 3 stay open). No Done-when is added by this review. - Known-issues 2026-10-08 (highestDimOnly) retires through its "Resolves with" clause if that clause names this read option; otherwise the review decides. - Either outcome: dashboard item 10 retires, because the operator's install is done.

Depends on: nothing open. Independent of 983 / 984.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim, if delegated). "Execute §9 item 985 — GEO-34 step 1d / U12′ — per docs/planning/chunks/GEO-34.md § '§9 item 985'. Read logs/maintenance/cadquery_image_20261114T091828Z.log first and cite its 4a lines. Run W0a, then W0b, before any src/ edit; if W0b finds no named face or no embedded fragment child, stop, BLOCKED. Identify the face by STEP name and the fragment map only — never a geometric selector. Both new config keys are additive, and key-absent behaviour is byte-identical (W2a / W2b). Mesh only through import_step. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped; foreground, Bash timeout: 660000. Never delete a log. Never --no-verify. Do not spawn agents."

Outcome (2026-11-14 12:00 CST slot): DONE, green (family 1d attempt 3 of 4). Install log 4a: cadquery 2.8.0 and wrote …cq_sample_…step (cadquery_image_20261114T091828Z.log:381–382). W0a (20261114T181641Z_GEO-34-U12p-W0a-author.log:35–39): Assembly.export exists, polygon face area 0.4800000000000001, 21468 B, sha256 f729d87d88fee04de4f44524fe0edc204f273bf00123e99a6c37fce3c3fde392. W0b (20261114T181729Z_GEO-34-U12p-W0b-read.log): the default read drops PortSheet (:60–67); highestDimOnly=False names face 7 Shapes/geo34_step1d/PortSheet/PortSheet before and after removeAllDuplicates (:136, :174); fragment maps (2,7) → [(2,7)] with the area unchanged, outside the wall set (:182–183). Upward adjacency reads [], but getEmbedded(3,1)=[(2,7)] (:184) and all 115 sheet nodes lie in tets (:237); the importer checks embedding with getEmbedded. Disclosed src/ change: the first W1 (20261114T181903Z_GEO-34-U12p-W1.log:110–116) died with SEGV in optimize("Netgen") ("456 illegal tets") on the embedded face, so with surface_groups set the Netgen pass is skipped; the key-absent path is unchanged. W1 (20261114T181927Z_GEO-34-U12p-W1.log, 11 s): at -n 1 / 2 / 4, (P1) +2.2e-16, (P3) ≤ 8.9e-16, (W) ≤ 5.2e-15, (P2) 192 = 192 and 0 one-sided, (P0) ghosts 0 / 581 / 1152, (n3) −4.06e-3 / −5.74e-3 / −5.48e-3 (predicted ≈ 5e-3), (n-hDO) / (n1) / (n2) green. Rule (c): W2a 20261114T181947Z_GEO-34-U12p-W2a-ruleC.log (6 passed, 85 s) and W2b 20261114T182116Z_GEO-34-U12p-W2b-preflight.log (5 passed, 141 s). Known-issues 2026-10-08 retired. U13 opens for the weekly.

Not verified at review (W0a / W0b measure these): - the CadQuery 2.8.0 calls (Assembly.export, the polygon-to-face route); - which dimension carries the product name after the gmsh import; - whether names survive removeAllDuplicates; - whether occ.fragment embeds an imported free face, and whether its child leaks into the wall group; - the pre-commit hook's handling of a STEP file.

docs.title: §9 item 996 — 2026-11-15 (GEO-34 1e, lane 1 — the 11-14 weekly's target; mesh-probe)
docs.text:
Posed by the 11-14 weekly at PROJECT_PLAN.md:4995–4998 (the Netgen workaround "accepted as disclosed under rule (c), with its diagnosis posed as GEO-34 1e") and :5300–5305 (lane 1: "the Netgen SEGV on the 1d fixture across a mesh-size ladder and with / without the embedded face — the illegal-tet count and whether the crash reproduces, a table and a probe script, no fix; it resolves known-issues 2026-11-14 or names its scope"). Brief drafted 2026-11-15 as execution detail. Measurement only: no gate, no assertion, no band; a mesh-probe is 🧪 by §3 until a gate lands. Family GEO-34 1e, attempt 1 of 4. Executor: mesh-probe (spawned by the slot).

What the step is. U12′'s first W1 (20261114T181903Z_GEO-34-U12p-W1.log) died inside gmsh.model.mesh.optimize("Netgen") on the 1d fixture: "Remove Illegal Elements" / "456 illegal tets" (:111–112), "Caught signal number 11 SEGV" (:116), Status 15, 2 s. Nobody has measured whether the crash depends on h, on the embedded face, or on the CadQuery route. 1e runs the same mesh-then-optimise sequence on the 1d fixture over an h ladder, with and without the embedded face, and tabulates per rung: whether Netgen crashes, the illegal-tet count it reports, and the pre-optimise quality.

Facts verified against the tree (this review, by grep / reading; unlogged, not a record). - Fixture: tests/mesh/data/geo34_step1d_port_sheet.step (sha256 f729d87d…de392, tests/mesh/test_step_import_cq_port_sheet.py:38), unit box AirBox + free face PortSheet = rectangle x 0.1, y 0.2, z 0.47, 0.8 × 0.6, area 0.48 (tests/mesh/cq_author_geo34_step1d.py:19–20). So the "without" arm already ran Netgen once at h = 0.08 without a crash — with highest_dim_only: false the face is still read; whether it is still embedded on that path is a thing the probe prints, not assumes. - Known-issues 2026-11-14 (docs/testing/known-issues.md:895–902): cause "not diagnosed"; the slot's comment ("Netgen's optimiser does not respect an embedded face") is a hypothesis. Resolves with: "a measured quality reading on the un-optimised named-sheet mesh with the step's gates green [U13a, item 993], or an optimiser route that keeps the embedded face. Never by re-enabling the pass on the key-absent path." - A quality helper exists: _tet_quality(x) (tests/mesh/probe_wf6_sheet_facet_census.py:83–110) — radius ratio and min dihedral per tet. In a gmsh-only probe use gmsh.model.mesh.getElementQualities(tags, "minSICN") / "gamma" instead (no DolfinX object needed); print which. - The 1d probe precedent: tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step1d_cq_read.py (W0b), plain python3, -n 1, no mpiexec — "a gmsh throw on rank 0 at -n 2 deadlocks the command" (docs/planning/chunks/GEO-34.md:122).

The probe. tests/mesh/probe_geo34_step1e_netgen_ladder.py (not collected), gmsh only, no DolfinX. One invocation = one rung (h, arm) given on argv, so a SEGV kills exactly one rung's process and the harness records its status. It replicates import_step's gmsh sequence directly (importShapes(highestDimOnly=False), removeAllDuplicates, synchronise; arm E then occ.fragment of the volume with the named face and synchronise), sets Mesh.MeshSizeMin/Max = h, General.Terminal = 1 (so gmsh's own "illegal tets" line reaches stdout before a crash), runs generate(3), prints the pre-optimise census (tets, min / p1 of minSICN, count with minSICN ≤ 0, getEmbedded(3, vol)), then flush, then optimize("Netgen"), then the post census. It calls gmsh, never import_step, so no src/ file is touched and the workaround cannot mask the result. It prints gmsh.__version__ and the OCC version.

Arms × ladder (10 rungs + 2 repeats). - Arms: E — the face fragmented into the box (1d's embedded face, the crashing configuration); N — the same STEP read, face discarded before meshing (box only). Stop going finer in an arm once a rung's generate(3) exceeds 60 s. - Repeats: (E, 0.08) twice more — does the crash reproduce bit-for-bit (same illegal-tet count)?

One row per rung: arm, h, tets pre, min minSICN pre, # tets minSICN ≤ 0 pre, embedded (Y/N from getEmbedded), Netgen "illegal tets" count (from the log line, — if none printed), crashed (Y/N; harness Status, 139/15/–11 named as printed), tets post and min minSICN post (if survived), elapsed s, log:line. docs.title: GEO-35 — Drop the floating leg-port boxes from unbroken-leg birdcages (history)
§9 item 275 — 2026-10-06 (chain U17)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-06 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: the 2026-10-05 weekly's enumerated step U17 (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10, grep "U17. GEO-35 step 1"; target "CAD identities"; serial on nothing). No band, tolerance, record or Done-when is set or moved. Every band below is imported by name from the file:line cited.

GEO-35 step 1: the inert leg-port boxes dropped behind a knob. birdcage_port_domain gains one additive keyword-only argument, emit_leg_ports: bool = True. With False on an unbroken-leg layout (leg_gap_length=None) the 16 floating boxes at the mid-leg azimuths (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:4817–4846, the addBox at :4837) are not built; everything else is unchanged. On the F-human fixture (WF-7's build, tests/validation/test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py:451–456) the step asserts the CAD identities and the ring-port census, prints the cell count, and prints how far the degree-1 32×32 moves from WF-7's record. The identities are the gate. The move is expected to be at discretisation level and is printed only. - Executor: implementer. Changes: additive src/ in io/mesh.py, one new mesh test module, and one additive environment knob in the WF-7 step-1 module. No existing default path, record, band or other caller is edited, and no fixture is switched. Switching the fixtures and re-recording under (1*) is step 2 (record-reconciler). - Tier: W0 standard; W1 and W2 heavy. Ranks: -n 2 for W0 and W1 (the rank-safety width); -n 8 for W2 (WF-7's own width, under the 12 ceiling). - Class: chain step (solve). Cost: ≈ 19 measured (class median) / ≈ 48 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 15 code + W0 ≈ 2 + W1 ≈ 5.5 + W2 ≈ 6.5 + ≈ 4 spare. If W1 is not green by minute 35, park (rule (d)). - Depends on: nothing open. It shares no file with any queued item that this draft knows of. io/mesh.py is also touched by the GEO-36 / GEO-34 lines, so add by edit and rebase, never check out by path.

Settled from the code (read before designing). - Where the boxes come from. port_tags is filled once per leg in for idx, angle in enumerate(theta_leg) (mesh.py:4830). With leg_gap_length is None each box sits at the mid-azimuth between adjacent legs (:4831–4836) and is an axis-aligned addBox (:4837–4846). The ring-gap boxes are appended after it. The constructor already refuses to drive these boxes: emit_port_sheets without a gap raises an error (:4346–4353), and leg_azimuth_offsets_rad without a leg gap is refused because the boxes "float" (:4379–4390). - Ordinals are positional. port_ordinal = {tag: idx for idx, tag in enumerate(port_tags, start=1)} (:5218). Every ring-port caller keys on ordinals LEG_COUNT + 1 … 3·LEG_COUNT = 17–48 (_ring_ports, tests/validation/test_birdcage_f_human_rung.py:134–136), that is, cell tags PORT_LOWER + i / PORT_UPPER + i = 117–148 / 217–248. With the knob off the leg boxes, the ring ordinals must stay 17–48. Build the map explicitly and keep the leg ordinals 1–16 as reserved gaps. A plain enumerate over a shorter list would renumber every ring port. - The group census. expected_groups (:5527–5530) demands 100 + i for every port_ordinal value, and group_names[100 + idx] (:5479) names them. Both must skip the dropped ordinals, or the build raises a missing-group error. - The F-human fixture. It is built from _params(F_HUMAN_RING_RADIUS, scale_sizing=False) (test_birdcage_f_human_rung.py:101–131: LEG_COUNT 16 at :76, radius 0.15 at :79, leg_gap_length=None, ring gaps, emit_port_sheets=True), plus ring_sheet_orientation="longitudinal", which is what WF-7 adds (test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py:451–452). _build_f_human (test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py:64) drives only the ring ordinals. - The CAD identities and their bands. These are the four from GEO-25 step 2 (test_birdcage_f_human_rung.py:232–288): cells within CELL_COUNT_BAND (1 %, tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheet_prerequisite.py) of F_HUMAN_BRANCH_B_CELL_RECORD 504 642 (:87); the GEO-18 volume partition at EXACT (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_ring_gaps.py); GEO-19 terminal-area ratios on all 32 ring ports in TERMINAL_RATIO_BAND (0.95, 1.0) (:98); and meshed/CAD conductor mass ≥ CAD_MASS_GATE (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_conductor_sizing.py). _build_rung (:139–193) computes the readings. Its port_cell_tags includes the 16 leg tags PORT_LOWER + i (:163), so the new module must build its own tag list from the ring ports only. Do not reuse the leg entries: an absent tag has zero volume, so the partition would still pass and hide the drop. - WF-7's degree-1 record. It is the 0.11 image at -n 8 (20261005T003402Z_WF-7-H15a-r3-W2.log): cells 507 266 (:10583, relative 5.200e-03 to 504 642; build 129.65 s at :10521); reciprocity 1.041217e-14 (:10584); σ_max 0.999914648 (:10585); 18 class means with worst spread 3.6997e-02 against band 0.05 (:10587–10605); S_driven(P17) 0.407423+0.344417j (:10606); P17 P_src,exact 7.037117061e-03 W and pooled κ 4.590991e-03 (:10524). The window took 357.9 s with 11.149 GiB summed ru_maxrss (:10610) and finished "3 passed, 1 skipped" (:10613). The module constants are SIGMA_MAX_D1_RECORD, CLASS_MEAN_D1_RECORD, P17_P_SRC_EXACT_RECORD_W, P17_POOLED_KAPPA_RECORD and S_DRIVEN_STEP0_RECORD (test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py:154–194).

Code (the names are proposals; the executor may rename and disclose the mapping). - (1) MeshGenerator.birdcage_port_domain, additive. Add the keyword-only emit_leg_ports: bool = True after implant_rod. The request contradictions are checked before any gmsh state exists, in the existing pattern. False raises ValueError with leg_gap_length set, because the leg boxes are the drive in the gapped layout. For step 1 it also raises with as_hole or symmetry_quadrant; those are later steps (the WF-12 / TH-20 layouts). With False, the leg iteration skips addBox, the ordinal map is explicit (ring ordinals unchanged), and expected_groups / group_names skip ordinals 1…leg_count. The diagnostics gain "leg_ports_emitted": bool. git diff on mesh.py shows insertions plus if emit_leg_ports guards around the existing lines only. Disclose anything else. - (2) New tests/mesh/test_geo35_leg_port_boxes.py. It imports _params, _ring_ports, F_HUMAN_RING_RADIUS, LEG_COUNT and the bands above, plus _tag_volume / _total_volume / _port_boundary_partition exactly as _build_rung does. Nothing is restated. Nodes: - test_geo35_knob_contract (no mesh): the default is True (inspect.signature); the three refusals raise before gmsh. - test_geo35_f_human_drops_leg_ports_keeps_identities (W1): one default build and one emit_leg_ports=False build in one process, at -n 2, with the WF-7 kwargs. - (3) tests/validation/test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py, additive knob FEM_EM_GEO35_DROP_LEG_PORTS=1, read inside the test like the POST-7 knobs (:393–412). When it is set, kwargs["emit_leg_ports"] = False and four anchors become printed, not asserted, with a relative move against each record: (i) the cell record; the P17 reproduction; the save-file (L2) reproduction (refused if combined with FEM_EM_WF7_SAVE_NPZ); and the S_driven(P17) / σ_max / 18 class-mean figures. (ii) reciprocity, (iii) passivity, (iv) the C16 × mirror classes and (v) the exact identity stay asserted at their imported bands. When the knob is unset, no key is added to kwargs, so the landed run's path is unchanged. This is the phantom_resolution precedent (test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py:64–80, "adds no key … byte-identical").

Anchors (asserted). - (K) Contract, no mesh. The default is True; False with leg_gap_length, as_hole or symmetry_quadrant raises ValueError before gmsh. Exact. - (D) The knob-off build is digit-identical (W1, default build). Its global cell count == 507 266 exactly, the WF-7 record at …r3-W2.log:10583, same image and same kwargs. gmsh meshes serially, so the count does not depend on the rank count. The leg-port tags 101–116 are present and the cell count is also inside CELL_COUNT_BAND. How "digit-identical" is asserted: (a) this exact count; (b) the mesh.py diff touches the default path only through if emit_leg_ports guards; (c) the WF-7 knob adds no key when unset; (d) W0 re-runs tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_tags.py, which builds the floating-box layout with the default, green at its unchanged bands. A 32×32 re-run with the knob off is not bought, because (c) makes it the landed run. - (N) No leg-port tags on the knob-on build. The global cell census of tags PORT_LOWER + i and PORT_UPPER + i for i = 1…16 is exactly 0 (allreduced), and diag["leg_ports_emitted"] is False. - (R) Ring-port census unchanged. On the knob-on build, every ring ordinal 17–48 has both halves PORT_LOWER + i / PORT_UPPER + i with global cell count > 0. The 32 sheet interfaces built by _interface_facet_tags (as test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py:118–121 does) each have area > 0. Volume partition (conductor, phantom, air and ring halves only) within EXACT of 1. All 32 terminal ratios in TERMINAL_RATIO_BAND. Meshed/CAD conductor ≥ CAD_MASS_GATE. - (I) The identities gate the knob-on 32×32 (W2, degree 1). These are WF-7's (ii)–(v) at their imported bands: reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND; σ_max ≤ MATRIX_PASSIVITY_CEILING; exactly N_SYMMETRY_CLASSES (18) classes, worst spread ≤ OPPOSITE_SPREAD_BAND; the exact identity ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL on the driven columns. Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) The leg-tag detector, on the default build. Asserted: the same census that reads 0 in (N) must read > 0 on all 16 leg tags of the knob-off build in the same process. This shows that (N)'s zero is not an empty comparator. It is a separation of "16 present" against "0 present"; no factor is involved. - (c2) The partition comparator. Asserted: on the knob-off build, dropping the 16 leg tags from the tag list must break the partition by more than EXACT, by 16 box volumes / V_total. Predicted ≈ 16 × (0.0214 × 0.0171 × 0.0214) m³ over V_total. The boxes are PORT_BOX_SIZE scaled by 0.15 / 0.07. Print the measured reading. This shows that (C)'s partition sees missing volume. - (c3) WF-7's identity control (omit the smallest undriven sheet, 4.8e+02× the band at …r3-W2.log:10524) stays printed on the landed route, as landed. Predicted ≈ 480× on the knob-on build.

Printed (not asserted). - The knob-on cell count against 507 266 and against 504 642. Predicted to fall by a few thousand cells, roughly 0.3–3 %. A reading outside CELL_COUNT_BAND is not a red: it is the record that step 2 re-records. - Build seconds for both builds. - The degree-1 32×32 move against WF-7's record: relative |Δ| of S_driven(P17), σ_max, P17 P_src,exact, pooled κ, and each of the 18 class means beside CLASS_MEAN_D1_RECORD. Windows. Run every window in the foreground; the harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative. Bash timeout: 660000; -s; node IDs, never -k; tests/environment first; no pipe or redirect (every window is under 10 min). - W0, regression on the default path (rule (c): io/mesh.py is edited). Standard, -n 2. Unpriced in this draft; predicted ≤ 120 s. Mesh-only. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh GEO-35-s1-W0-porttags "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_tags.py tests/mesh/test_geo35_leg_port_boxes.py::test_geo35_knob_contract -v -s --tb=short'" - W1, mesh-only on the F-human fixture (the gate for (D), (N), (R), (C), (c1) and (c2)). Traps already paid for. - Positional ordinals (mesh.py:5218). If the ring ports are renumbered to 1–32, every downstream sheet, spec and record silently re-keys. (R) is the check, and it is meant to fail on exactly this. - An absent tag has zero volume. A partition computed over a tag list that still names the 16 leg tags passes vacuously. (C) uses the ring-only list, and (c2) shows that the comparator sees missing volume. - Rank-safety. cell_tags.values is rank-local. Every census is allreduced, using _tag_volume / _port_boundary_partition with comm (GEO-9 step 2b paid for this). At -n 2 rank 0 does not own every port. np.max / np.min on an owned slice raise on an empty rank, so use initial= and reduce. - A gmsh build that fails deadlocks at rank > 1 (GEO-23). The (K) refusals must raise before any gmsh state exists, on every rank. - The cell record is not a red here. The knob-on count is printed. The WF-7 knob must demote (i) and the degree-1 reproduction anchors to printed-only, or W2 fails on records that step 2 owns. Never widen CELL_COUNT_BAND or REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL. - FEM_EM_WF7_SAVE_NPZ + the knob would overwrite or compare against the degree-1 record file. The knob refuses the combination. - Do not edit any exact rectangles or sheets. The ring sheets are untouched, and κ stays a diagnostic (operator ruling 2026-10-02). - Orphan .c. W2 compiles the degree-1 forms, which should be warm from r3. If a window is killed: pgrep -c python3 first, then the rubric's sweep. Never use pgrep -f "python3 -m pytest". - Status 124 is a finding, not a retry. Never lengthen a timeout or change -n. - Rule (i): no edit to the new module, the knob or mesh.py after their last green window. - Write ≈, never ~, in tracked Markdown. No AED file is touched.

Scope. - Covered: the F-human fixture only (branch B, 0.15 m, 16 legs, ring gaps, longitudinal sheets) with the knob on; mesh identities at -n 2; one degree-1 32×32 at 64 MHz at -n 8. - Not claimed: switching any fixture's default; mesh:9–12, WF-10, EX-62, WF-12 (as_hole) or TH-20 (quadrant); any re-recorded constant; degree 2; B1+, SAR or tuning; any absolute S.

Status it can move. No glyph. Step 1 meets the row's first Done-when clause: a mesh test asserts no leg-port tags and an unchanged ring-port census on the switched fixture. It does not meet the second clause: records re-recorded under (1*) by record-reconciler, with C16 / mirror / exact identities re-run green on the switched fixtures. The Done-when does not match step 1. GEO-35 goes ⬜ → 🟡 at most, with a step-1 record sentence: (N) / (R) / (C) green, the knob-on cell count, and the 32×32 move. §10 U17 is marked DONE.

Negative result. In every case: report the measurement, park on attempt/GEO-35-step1-*, mark item 275 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)), and journal it in attempts.md. - (K) or W0 red: the default path changed. Revert (1); BLOCKED. - (D) count ≠ 507 266 with W0 green: an image or environment drift since 2026-10-05 (the 10-05 e0672b91 docker change is the first suspect). This is a finding for record-reconciler under (1*). Do not re-register it in-slot; stop before W2. - (N) or (R) red: a renumbering or census bug in the new code. Fix and re-run in-slot only if the fix stays inside the if not emit_leg_ports branches; otherwise stop. - (C) red on the knob-on build only: removing the boxes changed the conductor mesh. That is a real finding, so stop; no band moves. - (c1) or (c2) not separating: the comparator is broken. Stop. - (I) red in W2: an inert-box removal broke an identity. That is a real finding; the mesh legs stand as a record. - W1 over its gate, or W2 killed at 590 s: BLOCKED without a result; the review re-poses the step.

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

docs.text: Drop the floating leg-port boxes from unbroken-leg birdcages — with leg_gap_length=None birdcage_port_domain still emits one port box per leg, "floating in the air at the midpoint azimuth between adjacent legs, touching no metal" (its docstring; the PORT-9 step 3 placeholder ports), so the F-human (high-pass, ring-gap) fixture carries 16 inert vacuum boxes with their own PORT_LOWER/UPPER + i cell tags and interior sheets in the isocenter plane — no port or material is ever defined on them (_build_f_human drives only the ring ordinals 17–48), but the mesh conforms to their faces and they clutter every ParaView view (operator, 2026-09-30, interactive session: "they shouldn't be there"). Shape: an additive keyword on birdcage_port_domain (e.g. emit_leg_ports, default unchanged so every existing caller builds the identical mesh) that omits the leg-port boxes when the legs are unbroken; the high-pass fixtures (F-human, mesh:9–12, WF-7/WF-10, EX-62) switch to it. Done-when: a mesh test asserts no leg-port tags and an unchanged ring-port census on the switched fixture; every record the switch moves (F-human cell counts such as F_HUMAN_BRANCH_B_CELL_RECORD 504 642, printed WF-7 / EX-62 figures) is re-recorded under the (1*) licence by record-reconciler, with the gated anchors (C16, mirror, exact identities) re-run green at their unchanged bands — no band moves. | 🟡 ~~Deferred to Phase 9 clean-up (operator, 2026-09-30): not queueable before Phase 6 closes~~ — placed by the 2026-10-05 weekly as §10 chain U17 (step 1, §9 item 275); step 1 covers the mesh-test clause only and can move ⬜ → 🟡, the fixture switch and re-record are step 2. Step 1 (2026-10-06 19:30 slot): emit_leg_ports=False on F-human leaves zero leg-port cells, ring ordinals 17–48 intact and the GEO-25 CAD identities green (partition 1.000000000000, terminal ratios 0.9739–0.9743, mass 0.9653), 502 704 cells (−0.90 % vs 507 266); the knob-on degree-1 32×32 holds reciprocity / passivity (σ_max 0.999914557) / 18 classes / exact identity, every printed figure moving ≤ 9.1e-4 except pooled κ (4.67 %, inside the 5.50 % degree-1 caveat; 20261007T004311Z_GEO-35-s1-W1-mesh.log, 20261007T005016Z_GEO-35-s1-W2-wf7.log). Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-09 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: the 2026-10-07 weekly's enumerated step U21 (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10, grep "U21. GEO-35 step 2"; "serial on xl 10-09 (H15b's matrix is saved on the boxed mesh first)"). That prerequisite landed: 20261009T070009Z_WF-7-step0e-H15b.log (boxed build 507 266 cells at :10924, /workspace/logs/wf7/wf7-s32-degree2-n16.npz saved and round-tripped at :12318–12319). No band, tolerance or Done-when is set or moved. Every band below is imported by name. Every new record value is copied from a footered log on the current image and cited by log:line; none is computed.

This item is step 2a of two (U21 split; question Q4 below). U21 as written does not fit one slot. It touches four families with moved records: the WF-7 σ = 800 solid matrix and quadrature (steps 1 and 2); the 10 g SAR family (WF-7 step 3, EX-62 / mri:4); GEO-25 / mesh:12; and the κ-corrected WF-10 / ANS-8 lineage. Re-running all of them is ≈ 50 min of windows alone (prices under Remains). 2a lands the switch and re-records the WF-7 step 1 / step 2 family: the records U27 (WF-16 step 8, "serial on U21") reproduces. Every other _build_f_human caller is pinned to the boxed build in the same commit, and the copper hole / quadrant paths are exempt by construction. That makes 2a independently landable: no pinned or exempt caller's mesh changes, which the W0 contract asserts without meshing and W1 asserts on a real build.

GEO-35 step 2a: the solid F-human fixture switches to emit_leg_ports=False, and WF-7 step 1's degree-1 records are re-recorded under (1*). - Executor: an implementer slot, then record-reconciler. The implementer slot writes the code (1)–(4) below and runs W0 and W1. It then spawns record-reconciler in the foreground (the spawn prompt states the foreground rule: no backgrounded harness window, Bash timeout 660000) with the site table below. The reconciler edits the constants and runs the anchors W2 and W3. One commit at the end holds code, logs and plan text. If Q1 is not ruled, do not spawn. - Tier: W0 standard. W1 heavy by ceiling. W2 and W3 heavy. Ranks: -n 2 for W0 and W1 (rank-safety width; W1 is xl entry 32's own build width); -n 8 for W2 and W3 (WF-7's record width, under the 12 ceiling). - Cost: ≈ 13 measured (class median) / ≈ 53 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + W0 ≈ 1.5 + W1 ≈ 3.1 + W2 ≈ 7.7 + W3 ≈ 4.5 + reconciler spawn and edits ≈ 6 + ≈ 3 spare. If W2 is not green by minute 42, park (rule (d)). - Depends on: H15b (landed, above); GEO-35 step 1 (landed, item 275); the review's ruling Q1. It shares test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py with two parked branches (see Settled (c)). Pins are two one-line edits there; add them by edit, never by checking out a path.

Settled from the code (read before designing). - Who calls _build_f_human (tests/validation/test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py:64–208; kwargs at :114–119, built from _params(F_HUMAN_RING_RADIUS, scale_sizing=False) + ring_sheet_orientation="longitudinal"): - Solid route, switched in 2a: WF-7 step 2's fixture (b1_quadrature.py:226). - Solid route, pinned boxed in 2a; their records move in 2b: - test_wf7_f_human_sar10g_hotspot.py:154 (WF-7 step 3; examples/mri/04_f_human_sar10g_hotspot.py imports it, so EX-62 follows the pin); - test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py:159 and :454; - examples/ansys_benchmarks/ans8_f_human_quadrature_mode_content_64MHz/08_f_human_quadrature_mode_content.py:193. - as_hole=True, exempt (boxed): - test_wf12_f_human_hole.py:425; - test_wf12_f_human_copper_matrix.py:148; - test_wf12_f_human_copper_degree2.py:114 (xl entry 32, queued for 10-13); - test_wf12_f_human_copper_c_sweep.py:279; - test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root.py:310; - examples/mri/06_f_human_copper_loss_partition.py:115–167 (a pass-through wrapper, *args, **kwargs). - Its own build, switched in 2a: WF-7 step 1 builds its fixture itself, not through _build_f_human (test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py:602–606). - Why the hole and quadrant paths must stay boxed: birdcage_port_domain refuses emit_leg_ports=False with as_hole or symmetry_quadrant (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:4272–4285; step 1's (K)). A _build_f_human that forwarded the new default on the hole route would make every copper caller raise, including xl entry 32 on 10-13. (a) Settled: the WF-12 hole mesh, TH-20's quadrant and every copper path are out of scope for U21. Lifting the refusal is a mesh.py change with its own CAD gate (a later GEO-35 step, if the weekly wants one). WF-12's own solid control (test_wf12_f_human_hole.py:286) calls birdcage_port_domain directly and is untouched. - What the switch moves on the solid route. These are the step 1 knob-on readings on the exact kwargs 2a switches to (20261007T005016Z_GEO-35-s1-W2-wf7.log, Status 0 at :10305): - cells 507 266 → 502 704 (:9694), −0.384 % to F_HUMAN_BRANCH_B_CELL_RECORD 504 642. So the reproduction asserts at test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py:1021–1028 (P17) and :1045–1057 (through the file) go red on the switched default unless re-recorded. That is the set 2a re-records. - Mesher stable since step 1. H15b rebuilt the boxed fixture at exactly 507 266 on 10-09 (…H15b.log:10924), the same count step 1's (D) asserted on 10-07 (20261007T004311Z_GEO-35-s1-W1-mesh.log:19872). The 10-07 knob-on readings are therefore current-image measurements, as (1*) requires. - (b) Saved-npz consumers. Two files are on the boxed mesh, each carrying cells, order, slot_k, slot_sign, s32 and κ keys (…H15b.log:12318): - /workspace/logs/wf7/wf7-s32-degree1-n8.npz (κ-off degree 1, H15a); - /workspace/logs/wf7/wf7-s32-degree2-n16.npz (H15b).

All of them read stored arrays and rebuild nothing, so the switch cannot break them provided (i) neither file is ever overwritten, (ii) any fresh solve paired with them is built boxed, and (iii) a consumer that pairs a build with a file checks the file's cells against that build (507 266 boxed). 2a enforces (i) with a save-path guard. It provides (ii) with _build_f_human(..., emit_leg_ports=True) and a module knob FEM_EM_WF7_LEG_PORTS=boxed, and documents (iii). Observation for the review, outside 2a: H13b's quarter is the copper hole layout (TH-20.md:22), while H15b's file is the σ = 800 solid route. A 1e-9 reassembly of one against the other is not like for like, whatever GEO-35 does. TH-20.md:568 reads the H15b number as H13b's price comparand. - (c) Open attempt/* branches. attempt/WF-10-step1b-20260929T020339Z (+337 lines) and attempt/WF-10-step1d-20261001T140319Z (+712 lines) both append to test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py. 2a's two pins there (:159, :454) are a small textual conflict if either branch is ever revived. Their disposition stays with the review; nothing in 2a depends on them. attempt/WF-12-step3* add only test_wf12_f_human_copper_c_mode.py (an as_hole module, exempt) and a script. attempt/PORT-24-step1-* (ports/ring_modes.py), attempt/OPS-50-* (a probe) and attempt/TH-15-step2proper-* (two-torus) do not overlap.

Code (the names are proposals; the executor may rename and disclose the mapping). No src/ edit; mesh.py is not touched. - (1) _build_f_human gains keyword emit_leg_ports: bool | None = None. The kwargs construction is lifted into a pure helper _f_human_kwargs(phantom_resolution=None, as_hole=False, emit_leg_ports=None) -> dict (rule (a) lift, no mesh) and called from _build_f_human. Resolution: - None resolves to boxed under as_hole and to False (dropped) otherwise; - the key emit_leg_ports=False is added only when the resolved value is False. The boxed result adds no key, so the kwargs are byte-identical to the pre-switch dict (the phantom_resolution / as_hole precedent, :116–119); - as_hole=True with emit_leg_ports=False raises ValueError in the helper, before any gmsh state. - (2) Pins. Pass emit_leg_ports=True at test_wf7_f_human_sar10g_hotspot.py:154, test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py:159 and :454, and 08_f_human_quadrature_mode_content.py:193, each with the comment # GEO-35 step 2b: unpin with the re-record. The as_hole callers are not edited. - (3) test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py. - Retire step 1's FEM_EM_GEO35_DROP_LEG_PORTS knob (:231–252). The default build (:602–606) adds kwargs["emit_leg_ports"] = False. - Add the inverse knob FEM_EM_WF7_LEG_PORTS: unset ⇒ dropped; boxed ⇒ no key (the pre-switch build), with the moved reproductions printed against the *_BOXED constants (the mirror of step 1's knob semantics); any other value raises. - The default path asserts again the (i) cell band (:993–996), the P17 reproduction (:1021–1028) and, with a save path, (L2) (:1045–1057).
