docs.title: §9 item 242 — 2026-10-05 (chain I12, daily — provisional)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain I12 (daily, 2026-10-05 — provisional) under rule (6) (PROJECT_PLAN.md ≈ lines 3694–3704), the next step after I9 toward chain I's stated target (Palace). ANS-10 was re-homed to Palace by the 10-03 weekly (≈ line 4493). Item 235's journal named this step (docs/testing/attempts.md:2346): the tip question "needs Palace field output, not more S". No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target moves.

IMP-3 step 4 — the near-tip field, ours against Palace. This runs on item 235's two exact-rectangle meshes, at order 1 / degree 1, at 64 MHz, with drive P1 as the reading of record. It compares E at six fixed phantom points and the phantom's electric energy, with the rod (PEC wall), with the natural wall, and without the rod. Palace's identities are asserted. The rod's tip-field effect is printed beside the two codes' disagreement. Target: Palace — a reading, not a gate, as in I9. - Executor: implementer. One new probe and one new test module. No src/, and no edit to any existing file. - Tier: heavy. Configs -n 1; Palace -np 8; ours -n 2. Use the complex container for every non-Palace window. - Class: chain step (solve). Measured median ≈ 18–23 min (item 235's brief). - Cost: ≈ 18 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + ≈ 7 compute + ≈ 6 spare). Basis: item 235 took ≈ 10 min of compute in a ≈ 30 min slot (attempts.md:2341–2345; §9 line "≈ 16 measured"). This item rebuilds no mesh. - Depends on: item 235's gitignored artifacts in logs/imp3/, which are present on this box (pre-check below).

Feasibility, settled from the repo (read before designing). - Palace v0.18.1 writes both quantities as CSV, so no field-format reader is needed. The image's own driven example /opt/palace/examples/cpw/cpw_lumped_uniform.json carries Domains.Postprocessing.Energy: [{Index, Attributes}] and Domains.Postprocessing.Probe: [{Index, Center}] (docs/testing/logs/20260929T110106Z_OPS-61-step1a-W0.log:65,97–117). Palace then writes probe-E.csv (complex E at each Center, per excitation) and per-domain columns in domain-E.csv. - Item 235's runs already write domain-E.csv, with total energies only and one column set per excitation: E_elec[1] (J) … E_ind[4] (J) (logs/imp3/postpro_imp3x_rod/domain-E.csv:1). OutputFormats defaults to Paraview: true, but nothing is saved without Save. ParaView / GridFunction output is not used. - Ours evaluates on a full mesh, not a submesh. _build / _build_rod cut the rod as a gmsh hole; no create_submesh appears in io/mesh.py, test_birdcage_implant_rod.py, test_birdcage_port_sheets.py, test_port_birdcage_four_port.py or test_imp3_palace_twin.py. The owner rule evaluate_vector_field_parallel(f, pts, owner="lowest_original_cell") (src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py:131,279–286) is therefore usable. Known-issues entry 2026-10-04 (owner rule vs create_submesh) does not bite. - Normalisation. Palace drives each port at V_inc = 7.071 V on 50 Ω (logs/imp3/postpro_imp3x_rod/port-V.csv:2). Ours has its own incident scale, the same in every sweep of one code. So every comparison below is either a ratio inside one code (arm to arm, same incident) or one fitted complex constant g shared by all arms and points. Absolute V/m are never compared. - The time convention is shared. Item 235's _read_port_s builds S as |S|·e^{i·arg} with no conjugation (scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py:391–414) and matched ours to 2e-10, so the phase convention agrees. The conjugate form is printed as a trap check.

Probe points (metres, L0 = 1; all in phantom tag 3, outside the rod hole; generic offsets keep them off symmetry planes and mesh faces). The rod has r = 1 mm, centre (0.015, 0, 0), and tips at z = ±0.016 (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py:93–96). The phantom is R 0.03 × H 0.08 (test_birdcage_port_tags.py:28–29). - T1 (0.015023, 0.000017, 0.017531): 1.53 mm beyond the top tip. - T2 (0.015023, 0.000017, 0.019031): 3.03 mm beyond. - T3 (0.015023, 0.000017, 0.022031): 6.03 mm beyond. - S1 (0.017523, 0.000017, 0.000031): beside the shaft, 1.52 mm off the wall. - F1 (−0.014977, 0.000017, 0.000031): 30 mm from the rod axis. This is the reference point of g. - F2 (0.000023, −0.017983, 0.010031): ≈ 23 mm from the axis.

Code (new files only; additive; disclosed). - New probe scripts/probes/imp3_step4_palace_fields.py. It loads scripts/probes/imp3_step3_palace_rod.py by importlib for OUT_DIR, RUNS, csv_of, class_means, line and _ops61() (and through it _p_check, _read_port_s). Do not edit either earlier probe. Dispatch is configs | read, nothing else. - configs (serial; assert comm.size == 1): - (X0) Parse the $Elements blocks of logs/imp3/imp3x_off.msh and imp3x_rod.msh read-only. The type-4 (tet) counts must equal imp3x_meta.json's cells exactly (117 206 / 168 507), and the type-2 triangle attribute set must be {1, 21–24}, plus {402} on the rod arm. - Load imp3x_off.json, imp3x_rod.json and imp3x_rodnat.json read-only. Assert their PEC lists are [1] / [1, 402] / [1], as item 235 wrote them (imp3_step3_palace_rod.py:257–262). - Deep-copy each config, add Domains.Postprocessing = {"Energy": [{"Index": 1, "Attributes": [PHANTOM_CELL_TAG]}], "Probe": [{"Index": k, "Center": p_k}, k = 1…6]} and set Problem.Output = "postpro_imp3p_<arm>". Write imp3p_off.json, imp3p_rod.json and imp3p_rodnat.json. - Also write the energy-only fallbacks imp3e_<arm>.json (no Probe, Output postpro_imp3e_<arm>). They run only if Palace refuses Probe. - Open every target with mode "x": never overwrite. PHANTOM_CELL_TAG = 3 is imported (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py, as item 235 imports it). - read: - (H) Parse probe-E.csv and domain-E.csv in each postpro_imp3p_* by header, mapping each column to (probe, component, Re/Im, excitation) and (domain, excitation). The map must be a bijection onto 6 × 3 complex × 4 excitations and onto one Energy domain × 4 excitations. If it is ambiguous, print the header verbatim and stop. - Run _p_check on imp3p_off / imp3p_rod (fails asserted). On imp3p_rodnat, print only. - (RP) Each imp3p_* S must match item 235's postpro_imp3x_* S entrywise. - Print Palace's own η (below). Save the parsed probe and energy arrays to logs/imp3/palace_imp3p_fields.json (mode "x"). - Never read z_matrix_ohm, docs/private/ or aed_results/. - New module tests/validation/test_imp3_palace_fields.py (@complex_only, one test): - Use the same builds, the same order and the same three sweeps as test_imp3_palace_twin.py:110–159, through probe.build_arm(arm) → build_four_port_sweep(…, built=…, build_only=True) → run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(…, degree=1). keep_fields=True on all three sweeps. The natural-wall sweep is the same replace(problem, facet_tags=outer, pec_facet_tags=(OUTER_BOX_TAG,)) on _outer_box_tags(msh, built[2], comm). κ stays off. - Import helpers only, never a test_* name: _sweep, _ids and _sheet_areas from test_imp3_palace_twin, and _matrix_quantities, _wall_dofs, _wall_max_e and PEC_WALL_MAX_E from test_imp3_rod_birdcage. - Per arm, before del res, do three things for every drive: 1. E at the six points: evaluate_vector_field_parallel(res.fields[p].e_complex, PTS, owner="lowest_original_cell"), with PTS a module constant identical on every rank. 2. W_ph ∝ ∫_tag3 e·ē dx: assemble_scalar over ufl.Measure("dx", domain=msh, subdomain_data=built[1], metadata={"quadrature_degree": 2}), then allreduce(SUM) and take .real. 3. (B) For each point, the number of owned colliding cells (geometry.bb_tree / compute_collisions_points / compute_colliding_cells, as in evaluation.py:270–278, links < size_local), reduced with SUM. - Write logs/imp3/ours_imp3p_fields.json on rank 0 with mode "w", a new name. Never write ours_imp3x_p1.json. - Read palace_imp3p_fields.json and print the comparisons below.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - (X0), configs window: exact tet counts and attribute sets (above). This is item 235's (X1)/(X2) count, re-read from the file that Palace reads. - (P) Palace, W5, on imp3p_off / imp3p_rod, via _p_check (ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py:742–782): - RECIPROCITY_BAND (test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86); - PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, with column power ≤ 1 + 1e-9 (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:129); - ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:121); - POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:173). - Backed on these meshes by item 235's W5 (reciprocity 1.556e-10 / 1.390e-10, spreads ≤ 0.0937 %). - (RP) Palace reproduction: every imp3p_* S against item 235's imp3x_* S, entrywise, within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL 1e-6 (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py:171, = STEP2_COLUMN_POWER_RTOL :164). Postprocessing does not enter the solve. The same Palace on one mesh tied at 2.9e-14 (item 235 W5, imp3x_off vs f05x). - (H) The header bijection (above). It is a structure check, with no band. - Palace log check (executor, journalled), W2–W4: - elements total equals the (X0) count; - Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on 21–24; - ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz; - four GMRES solver converged lines. - Ours, W6: - (F) cells equal imp3x_meta.json exactly, and N_i equals 5.6e-5 within STRIP_BAND (test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58). - (R) S per arm reproduces item 235's logs/imp3/ours_imp3x_p1.json entrywise within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL. It is backed by IMP-3 (R0), 2.98e-10 against that band (20261002T170428Z_IMP-3-step1-W1.log). Repeated complex MUMPS solves differ at ≈ 2.7e-12 (item 237), far inside it. - (i)/(ii) on all three sweeps (_ids). - (E) rod PEC wall max |E| ≤ PEC_WALL_MAX_E (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:135), every drive. - (Kw) natural wall, P1: > PEC_WALL_MAX_E (item 235 W6: 1.297e-4). - (V) valid_mask is all True for the six points on all three arms. A False means a coordinate fell in the hole or outside the mesh, so the fixture is not the one designed.

Printed, never gated (ours against Palace, P1 the reading of record, P2–P4 printed beside): - (B) The owned-cell count per point, predicted 1 everywhere. A point reading ≠ 1 sits on a face, where the two codes may evaluate different cells. It is flagged face-ambiguous and left out of (T_E). This is a filter, not a stop. - (T_E) The field tie. g = E^ours_c(F1) / E^Pal_c(F1) on the without-rod arm, with c* = argmax_c |E^Pal_c(F1)|. - Per arm, the reading is max over (p, c) of |E^ours_c(p) − g·E^Pal_c(p)| / ‖g·E^Pal(p)‖ over the five non-reference points plus F1's other components. Predicted ≤ 1e-6 on all three arms. - Derivation: same mesh, same N1curl order 1 and the same discrete operator (S tied at ≤ 2.2e-10, item 235). Evaluation is in the same cell, so the residual is solver tolerance (Palace Tol 1e-10) times a local amplification. The 1e4 margin covers that amplification. - Print g itself (the ratio of incident scales; a constant, no prediction), and the same reading against conj(E^Pal): predicted O(1), which confirms the convention. - (T_W) The energy tie. q_a = W^ours_ph,a / W^Pal_ph,a for P1. The reading is max_a |q_a / q_off − 1|, predicted ≤ 1e-6. Print q_off / |g|² (the codes' energy-prefactor convention; a constant, no prediction). - The rod's tip-field effect, inside each code, then ours against Palace: - η_wall(p) = |E_rodPEC(p)| / |E_rodnat(p)|: one mesh, no remesh. Predicted for P1: - T1 [1.5, 20], T2 [1.2, 8], T3 [1.05, 4]; - S1 [0.2, 1.5] (n × E = 0 suppresses the axial field beside the shaft); - F1, F2 |η − 1| ∈ [3e-3, 1e-1]. This is a PEC-spheroid dipole estimate: a·b²/(3 L_z) = 5.5e-7 m³ over r³ = 2.7e-5 / 1.7e-5 m³ ≈ 2 % / 3 %, with L_z(16) = 0.009692 (item 174 W2). - η_rod(p) = |E_rod(p)| / |E_off(p)|: two meshes, the remesh included. The tip predictions are as for η_wall. At F1 and F2, |η − 1| ∈ [1e-3, 0.3]; the without-rod phantom has 537 cells, so a point value moves with the remesh. - Ours against Palace: d_η = |η^ours − η^Pal|, predicted ≤ 2e-6·η, i.e. two ratio errors at (T_E)'s level. - ΔW: W_ph(rod) / W_ph(rodnat) − 1 and W_ph(rod) / W_ph(off) − 1, per code and per drive, ours against Palace. Predicted |Δ| ∈ [1e-3, 0.1] and code gap ≤ 1e-6. IMP-3 C2 read +4.80 % (P1) on the ragged 1 g rung; that is a record on another mesh, not a comparand. - Closed form beside it: |E_cf(p)| / E₀ from pec_prolate_spheroid_field(p − ROD_CENTRE, semi_major=0.016, semi_minor=0.001, e0=1.0) (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:1576) at T1–T3 and S1, beside η_rod(p) / η_rod(F1). The ratio is predicted in [0.3, 3]. It carries no accuracy claim: the record mesh cannot resolve a 1 mm rod's apex. - Palace prices: Total time, peak memory and ND unknowns per run, as in item 235.

Negative controls (rule (e); there is no prior field-level comparison on this fixture, so every factor is predicted and printed, with its ceiling computed). - (C1) The tip effect against the two codes' disagreement (the without-rod arm sets the floor). Separation = |η^Pal_wall(T1) − 1| / d_η(T1). - Predicted ≥ 1e5. Least case η = 1.5: 0.5 / (2e-6 · 1.5) ≈ 1.7e5. - Ceiling ≈ 2.4e9: (20 − 1) / (2 · 2e-10 · 20), with the tie at item 235's S round-off. - Tie_off (T_E on the rod-free arm) is printed beside it as the floor the rod has to clear. - (C2) Tip against far: the effect is local. Separation = |η_wall(T1) − 1| / max_F |η_wall(F) − 1|, per code. - Predicted ≥ 5 (least: 0.5 / 0.1). - Ceiling ≈ 6e3 ((20 − 1) / 3e-3). - Below 5, the far points are not "far" on this mesh. That is a reading about placement, not a stop. - (C3) The arm swap: the probe reading sees which arm it is on. Take ours without the rod at T1 against Palace with the rod at T1, with g applied: |E^ours_off(T1) − g·E^Pal_rod(T1)| / ‖g·E^Pal_rod(T1)‖. - Predicted ≥ 0.3, i.e. ≥ 3e5× over (T_E). - Ceiling ≈ 1 for a relative difference against the rod field when η > 1. In ×, it is bounded by (T_E)'s round-off (≈ 1e9). - (Kw) is the asserted knob on the wall (above). (RP) and (R) prove that both codes solved item 235's problems, not new ones.

Windows (bare, whole, foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; -np ≤ 12; Palace v0.18.1, image fem-em-palace:0.18.1, compose profile palace). - Pre-check (not a harness call): ls logs/imp3/ logs/imp3/postpro_imp3x_off logs/imp3/postpro_imp3x_rod logs/imp3/postpro_imp3x_rodnat. - Required: imp3x_off.msh, imp3x_rod.msh, the three imp3x_*.json, imp3x_meta.json, ours_imp3x_p1.json, and three port-S.csv. - Absent: every imp3p_*, imp3e_*, postpro_imp3p_* and *_imp3p_fields.json. - Any miss ⇒ stop and report. Never re-run item 235's export. - W1, configs (≈ 15 s; two ASCII .msh scans):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-item242-W1-configs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/imp3_step4_palace_fields.py configs'" - W2, Palace without the rod (≈ 25 s; item 235 W2 Total 24.364 s, 1.8 G, 20261005T035015Z_IMP-3-item235-W2-palace-off.log:326,342). This is the box-speed gate.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-item242-W2-palace-off "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/imp3 && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 imp3p_off.json'" - Box-speed gate (binding, after W2): r = W2 Total / 24.364 s. - r ≤ 2.5 ⇒ run everything. - r > 2.5 ⇒ run W3–W5, skip W6, BLOCKED (slow box). W6 projects to ≥ 430 s against its 420 s ceiling. - W3 / W4, Palace with the rod and with the natural wall. These are W2's command with imp3p_rod.json / imp3p_rodnat.json, labelled IMP-3-item242-W3-palace-rod / IMP-3-item242-W4-palace-rodnat. Predicted ≈ 35 s each; item 235 measured 34.19 / 35.46 s and 2.5 G. Probe and Energy postprocessing add < 1 s (Postprocessing 0.28 s, …035048Z_IMP-3-item235-W3-palace-rod.log:324). After any kill, check docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps for a lingering fem-em-palace container. - W5, read (≈ 3 s). This is the probe's last window: no probe edit after it starts.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-item242-W5-read "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/imp3_step4_palace_fields.py read'" - W6, ours (≈ 190 s, range 150–300). Basis: item 235 W6 took 172 s at -n 2 for the same three sweeps (20261005T035322Z_IMP-3-item235-W6-ours-p1.log). Keeping the without-rod fields, 72 point evaluations and 12 energy integrals add ≈ 10–20 s. This is the closing window: no module edit after it starts.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-item242-W6-ours-fields "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp3_palace_fields.py -v -s --tb=short'" - Fallback W2e–W4e, only if W2 aborts on Probe: the same commands with imp3e_<arm>.json, labelled IMP-3-item242-W2e-… and so on. W5 and W6 then run with the probe readings marked "not measured".

Traps already paid for. - Pointwise N1curl depends on the MPI width without the owner rule (known-issues 2026-09-27, ans:2 Row 1: −19 % … +112 % between -n 2 and -n 4). - Always pass owner="lowest_original_cell" and evaluate e_complex once. - Do not copy IMP-3 step 1's pattern (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:385–386: e_real / e_imag, default owner). - Never f.eval(points, np.arange(n)). The point array must be bitwise identical on every rank (OPS-40/55 digest). - The owner rule raises on create_submesh meshes (known-issues 2026-10-04). It does not apply here (full mesh, above). If it raises anyway, that is a finding: stop and report; never fall back to the default owner. - Never overwrite item 235's artifacts. Write with mode "x", use new imp3p_ / imp3e_ names, and leave ours_imp3x_p1.json alone (item 235's module writes it with "w"; this module must not call that code path). logs/ops61/ is read-only. - Tag 402 lives in the build tuple's facet tags. The cell tags for the energy integral are the build tuple's built[1], too. - Build order. Build without the rod first, then with it (GEO-23). Free the without-rod arm's fields after its readings and before the rod build. Evaluate before del res. - A held factorisation silently solves a different problem (PORT-19, WF-12). The natural-wall arm is its own sweep, and (Kw) proves the knob. - Rank-local quantities. assemble_scalar, collision counts and wall dofs are rank-local: reduce them, and count owned cells only. Keep collectives outside any rank == 0 branch. - Pin quadrature_degree on the energy form (POST-5). Do no UFL or sqrt comparisons; take ratios in numpy. - Palace CSV headers are parsed, never assumed. The excitation index sits in brackets: V_inc[1][1] (port-V.csv:1), E_elec[1] (domain-E.csv:1). An unparseable header is a stop, not a guess. - A GMRES … did not converge line is a finding. Never change Order, Tol or MaxIts in-slot. - Harness discipline: - -s, tests/environment first, FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, foreground, no pipes, no -k; - Status 124: run pgrep -c python3 first and never lengthen the timeout; - rule (i): no edit after a file's last window. - Palace numbers go in at full detail (version, config, mesh). No AED number, and no Palace figure set against one, in any tracked file. Never open docs/private/, aed_results/ or COMPARISON_private.md.

Scope. Covered: Palace order 1 and ours at degree 1, 64 MHz, on item 235's exact-rectangle record meshes (117 206 / 168 507 cells, σ = 800 S/m untuned coil, 50 Ω, κ off). The comparison is E at six fixed points and phantom electric energy, on three arms, with drive P1 of record. Agreement is a matched-order check of the near-tip field between two independent codes. It is not a discretisation statement. Not covered: - the 1 g tip SAR, the ratio Q and its accuracy (ANS-10's question). Palace has no mass-averaged SAR, and this mesh cannot hold a 1 g ball (finding 1, item 174). That needs the rod + strip build on PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG (never built) and an order-2 or h-rung Palace run: a later I-step for the weekly to price; - any h- or p-statement, or absolute |E| / SAR; - tissue, heating, compliance, ISO 10974 (WF-9), ASTM F2182 (7c); - the tuned or copper coil, F-human, other rod placements, the kept-cells rod; - AED, src/, any band.

Status it can move. - §7 IMP-3 stays ✅ (no glyph). Its Done-when names step 1 only (rule (j) read: the row's Done-when is "identities green … on the 1 g rung with the tip ratio printed there ⇒ ✅ as a fixture"). The review appends a step-4 record sentence beside item 235's. Candidate text, which holds only if W5 and W6 are green, (T_E) ≤ 1e-6 on all three arms and (C1) ≥ 1e5×: "Palace order 1 matches ours at degree 1 on E at six fixed phantom points and on phantom electric energy to ≤ ⟨x⟩ per arm (P1); the rod's near-tip field effect (PEC against natural wall, one mesh) exceeds the two codes' disagreement by ≥ ⟨y⟩×. Record mesh, no 1 g or accuracy claim." - §10 I12 is done, as a provisional step for the weekly to ratify or revert. - ANS-10 has no §7 row. The weekly reads this as its first field-level Palace reading (agree / disagree / inconclusive on the near-tip effect at matched order). The Q-accuracy clause at §2 ≈ line 437 stays. - §2 ≈ line 437 may gain one clause ("the near-tip field agrees with Palace at matched order").

Negative result. - Pre-check miss, or (X0) red: item 235's artifacts are not the fixture. BLOCKED, and the review decides whether to re-export. - Palace refuses Probe (no GSLIB in the image is the likely cause; the Dockerfile does not set PALACE_WITH_GSLIB, docker/palace.Dockerfile:40–50): record it verbatim, open a known-issues entry, and run the imp3e_* fallback. The item lands with the energy readings only, and the row sentence drops its point clause. If Energy is refused too: BLOCKED (rule (d)). - (H) unparseable: print the header, BLOCKED pending a header ruling. - (P) or (RP) red: report every number, park, BLOCKED. Never widen. - Ours (F), (R), (i), (ii), (E), (Kw) or (V) red: park on attempt/IMP-3-step4-<ts>, open a known-issues entry, BLOCKED. - (T_E) or (T_W) without the rod > 1e-6, with (RP) and (R) green: this is not a stop. It is the first field-level disagreement at matched order, on the arm without the rod. Print it per point and component beside (B) and the conj reading, and report. The candidates are cell choice at the point, Palace's probe interpolation, or the convention. No record sentence; the review reads it. - (T_E) green without the rod but > 1e-6 on a rod arm: a reading located at the PEC hole. Report it. - Box-speed gate trips: a partial record (Palace only), BLOCKED (slow box). The review re-queues W6. - A printed reading outside its prediction: report it; no status effect. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Outcome, 2026-10-05 06:00 CDT slot — ✅ DONE, all six windows green. New files are scripts/probes/imp3_step4_palace_fields.py and tests/validation/test_imp3_palace_fields.py. Neither earlier probe was edited. Item 235's artifacts were read only, and nothing was overwritten. The fallback configs imp3e_* were written but not run, because Palace accepted Probe (it also writes probe-B.csv). - W1 20261005T110133Z_IMP-3-item242-W1-configs.log (4 s, -n 1): (X0) 117 206 / 168 507 tets equal the meta counts exactly; triangle attributes {1, 21–24} and {1, 21–24, 402}; the PEC lists are [1] / [1, 402] / [1]. - Palace v0.18.1, -np 8, all log checks met (elements equal the (X0) count, Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on 21–24, 6.400e-02 GHz, four GMRES solver converged lines at 31–32 its): - W2 off 20261005T110142Z: Total 25.782 s, peak 2.2 G, ND 140 460. Box-speed r = 1.058. - W3 rod 20261005T110223Z: 38.333 s, 3.0 G, ND 204 156. - W4 rodnat 20261005T110306Z: 37.319 s, 3.0 G. - The probe header form is Re{E_x[<probe>][<excitation>]} (V/m). The energy form is E_elec[<domain>][<excitation>] (J). The read regex was fitted to the W2 header before W5. - W5 20261005T110353Z_IMP-3-item242-W5-read.log (2 s): (H) bijections PASS; (P) PASS on imp3p_off / imp3p_rod (rodnat printed, PASS). (RP) against item 235's S read 8.2e-14 / 1.3e-13 / 1.7e-13. - W6 20261005T110512Z_IMP-3-item242-W6-ours-fields.log (179 s, -n 2, 13 passed): - (F) cells equal the meta counts exactly, N_i = 5.6e-5; - (R) 1.5e-13 / 3.5e-15 / 2.5e-15; - (V) all True; - (E) 0.0 on every drive; - (Kw) P1 1.297e-4; - (B) 1 owned hit at every point on both meshes, so no point is face-ambiguous. - (T_E) (P1; off / rod / rodnat): 1.32e-8 / 1.46e-8 / 8.3e-9, ≤ 9.2e-8 over P1–P4. The conj form reads 0.49 / 0.25 / 0.23, so the convention is confirmed. g = −7.071067853e-2 + 6e-11 j, i.e. 1/(10 √2) and real. - (T_W): 1.2e-9. q_off/|g|² = 2.896e9. - η_wall P1 (identical in both codes, d_η/η ≤ 5e-9): T1 4.053, T2 2.370, T3 1.573, S1 0.439, F1 1.255, F2 0.838. η_rod P1: T1 3.782, T2 2.359, T3 1.461, S1 0.454, F1 1.051, F2 1.461. - ΔW P1: rod/rodnat +4.799 %, rod/off +3.809 %. The code gap is ≤ 1.1e-9 on every drive. - Closed form |E_cf|/E₀ against η_rod(p)/η_rod(F1): ratios 0.71 / 0.74 / 0.90 / 0.85 at T1 / T2 / T3 / S1, inside [0.3, 3]. - Negative controls: - (C1) tip effect / code gap at T1 = 3.053 / 5.85e-9 = 5.2e8× (≥ 1e5; ceiling ≈ 2.4e9). - (C2) 11.99× in both codes (≥ 5). - (C3) arm swap 0.750, i.e. 5.7e7× over the off tie (≥ 0.3). - Outside prediction (reported, no status effect): - η_wall P1 at F1 / F2: |η − 1| = 0.255 / 0.162, against [3e-3, 0.1]. - η_rod at F2: 0.461, against ≤ 0.3. - So the "far" points are not dipole-far on this record mesh: a 1 mm rod in 537 phantom cells perturbs the field well beyond the PEC-spheroid estimate. That is a reading about placement and resolution, not a stop. - Reading: the near-tip field and the phantom electric energy agree between Palace order 1 and ours at degree 1 on all three arms, to ≤ 1.5e-8 (field, P1) and ≤ 1.2e-9 (energy). The rod's tip effect exceeds the codes' disagreement by 5.2e8×. This is not a 1 g SAR, h- or p-statement.

docs.title: §9 item 252 — 2026-10-05 (chain I13, daily provisional)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain I13 (daily, 2026-10-05 — provisional) under rule (6) (PROJECT_PLAN.md ≈ lines 3705–3720). This is the second provisional step on chain I since the 10-03 weekly (I12 was the first), so it is inside the three-per-chain cap. It is the next step toward chain I's stated target, Palace. Item 242's journal named it (docs/testing/attempts.md:2402): "ANS-10's tip-ratio accuracy is now purely a discretisation question … Palace order 2 on these meshes". Degree 2 is the production order (operator order rule, 2026-10-01). No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target moves.

IMP-3 step 5: I12 at matched order 2. Palace order 2 against ours at degree 2, on item 235's exact-rectangle meshes, at 64 MHz, with P1 as the drive of record. The comparison is E at item 242's six points plus the phantom electric energy. Each code's S on the arm without the rod must reproduce that code's own order-2 record on the same mesh (f05x). Palace's identities are asserted. Each code's order 1 → 2 shift of the near-tip field is printed beside the gap between the two codes. Target: Palace — a reading, not a gate, as in I9 and I12.

Two arms, not three (slot price, below). The item runs the arm without the rod (off) and the rod PEC arm (rod). It drops the natural-wall arm (rodnat). The three-arm plan prices at ≈ 60 min predicted, which is over the slot. The off arm stays because: - it is the only arm with order-2 records in both codes; - it is the cheapest Palace run; - it is the reference arm for g.

So the order-2 tip effect is read as η_rod (two meshes, remesh included), not η_wall. Adding rodnat at order 2 costs ≈ 8 min of Palace plus ≈ 2 min of ours. That is a later step for the weekly to price.

  • Executor: implementer. One new probe and one new test module. No src/, and no edit to any existing file.
  • Tier: heavy. Configs -n 1; Palace -np 8; ours -n 8. Use the complex container for every non-Palace window.
  • Why -n 8 and not -n 2: a single degree-2 solve of 482 158 dofs took 291.7 s at -n 2 (WF-15 cost probe, attempts.md:2419). This fixture has 753 062 / 1 090 614 dofs (below), so -n 2 cannot fit 590 s.
  • The rank-local reductions are item 242's code, already exercised at -n 2 (…110512Z_IMP-3-item242-W6-ours-fields.log).
  • The (R2) record was measured at -n 8 (ours_f05x_p2.json "ranks": 8).
  • Class: chain step (solve).
  • Cost: ≈ 9 measured / ≈ 50 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + ≈ 19 compute + ≈ 4 spare). Price arithmetic below.
  • Depends on: nothing. Item 235's and item 242's gitignored artifacts in logs/imp3/, and items 166 / 194's in logs/ops61/, are present on this box (pre-check below).

Price, from measurement (each per-run figure is divided by the solves actually in its interval; item 237's lesson). - Palace off, order 2 (W2): ≈ 285 s, range 265–300 s. - Basis: f05x order 2 at 64 MHz is the same 117 206-cell mesh. One run (one frequency, four excitations) at -np 8 took Total 265.630 s, peak 6.1 G, ND (p = 2) 753 062, with 37 GMRES iterations per excitation (20261003T110249Z_OPS-61-item194-W4-palace-o2.log:110,164,351,368). - Box factor: item 242's order-1 off run with Probe read 25.782 s, against f05x order 1's 23.35 s (×1.104), and against item 235's 24.364 s (×1.058). - Palace rod, order 2 (W3): ≈ 460 s, range 400–520 s, peak ≈ 9–11 G. - Split f05x order 2 into Preconditioner 149.377 s and the rest 116.25 s (…item194-W4-palace-o2.log:343,351). - Rod against off at order 1, on these meshes (item 242): Preconditioner 7.097 / 4.179 = ×1.698 and Total 38.333 / 25.782 = ×1.487 (20261005T110223Z_IMP-3-item242-W3-palace-rod.log:320,327; 20261005T110142Z_IMP-3-item242-W2-palace-off.log:319,326). - The order-2 preconditioner grew faster on the hole mesh: Preconditioner 88.158 s at ND 570 332 (20261005T021936Z_OPS-61-item234-W4-palace-hole-pec-o2.log:110,316), against 149.377 s at 753 062, i.e. exponent ≈ 1.9 in ND. - Low: 149.377 × 1.698 + 116.25 × 1.487 ≈ 427 s. High: 149.377 × 1.444^1.9 (= 2.01) + 173 ≈ 473 s. - Multiply by the box factor ≈ 1.06. - Item 241's copper hole run at order 2 (175.95 s, 4.5 G, 20261005T093309Z_OPS-61-item241-W5-palace-hole-cu-o2.log:327,344) is the same 80 798-cell hole mesh as item 234. It confirms the order-2 price is stable run to run (+9.6 % with the conductivity term). - Ours, degree 2, both arms in one window (W5): ≈ 290 s, range 240–450 s. - Off sweep: one four-drive sweep on the 117 206-cell mesh at -n 8 printed "four driven solves in 64.14 s wall" at 64 MHz (20261003T094036Z_ANS-4-item192-W3-p2.log:2080). That window holds four such sweeps (10 / 64 / 128 / 128 κ, :2031,2080,2129,2178; 429 s elapsed), so 429 / 4 is not the per-sweep price. 64–73 s is. - Item 166's sweep read 72.33 s (20261002T095914Z_OPS-61-F10b-ii-W1-ours-p2.log:2031). - Rod sweep: 1 090 614 / 753 062 = ×1.448 dofs. The scaling exponent from item 192 (70.70 s at 117 206 cells, 10 MHz) to item 212 W1 (186.93 s at 259 524 cells, 10 MHz, 36.12 GiB summed; attempts.md:2145) is ln 2.644 / ln 2.214 = 1.23. That gives 64.14 × 1.438^1.23 ≈ 100 s (range 95–135 s), and ≈ 20 GiB summed. - Builds: off mesh 23.90 s (…item192-W3-p2.log:2031); rod mesh ≈ 47 s (IMP-3 W1 :3646, item 235 brief). - Total: environment tests ≈ 10 + 24 + 64–72 + 47 + 100–135 + readings ≈ 15 ⇒ ≈ 260–305 s. - Configs (W1) ≈ 5 s; read (W4) ≈ 3 s (item 242: 4 s / 2 s). - Compute ≈ 5 + 285 + 460 + 3 + 290 ≈ 1 043 s, plus ≈ 1 min of container overhead, ≈ 18.5 min. The tops of every range give 1 278 s ≈ 21.3 min. The slot is then ≈ 15 + 12 + 21 ≈ 48 min, with spare left. - The third arm does not fit. rodnat would add one more Palace rod run (≈ 460 s) and one more rod sweep (≈ 110 s), ≈ +9.7 min, for ≈ 60 min predicted.

Feasibility, settled from the repo. - The order knob is Solver.Order. ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py:734–741 writes f05x_o2 by asserting Order == 1 on the source and setting it to 2. Nothing else changes except Output. That run solved at ND (p = 2) 753 062 (…item194-W4-palace-o2.log:110). - Palace's Probe / Energy output and its header form are known (item 242 outcome; imp3_step4_palace_fields.py:156–206 parses them). The parsers are imported, never re-written. - The two meshes are f05x's and item 235's. Palace imp3x_off against f05x tied at 2.9e-14 at order 1 (item 235 W5). Ours without the rod against ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P1_RECORDS["64"] tied at ≤ 1.2e-10 (item 235 W6). So the order-2 records on f05x are this fixture's off-arm records: - Palace: logs/ops61/postpro_f05x_o2/port-S.csv; - ours: logs/ops61/ours_f05x_p2.json, "degree": 2, "ranks": 8, "cells": 117206, key s_kappa_off. This is the file ANS-4's (X) reproduces at 8.9e-13 (attempts.md:1951). - The ND (p = 2) count is predictable exactly. It is 2E + 2F, with F = 2·cells + F_bdry/2. - Off: E = 140 460, F = 2 · 117 206 + 3 318/2 = 236 071, giving 753 062. This equals item 194's count, so the formula checks. - Rod: E = 204 156, F = 2 · 168 507 + (3 316 + 4 958)/2 = 341 151, giving 1 090 614. - DOLFINx N1curl degree 2 spans the same space, so our global dof count is predicted equal.

Code (new files only; additive; disclosed). - New probe scripts/probes/imp3_step5_palace_o2.py. It loads imp3_step4_palace_fields.py by importlib for _step3, _msh_census, parse_probe, parse_energy, PROBE_NAMES and PROBE_POINTS. Through _step3()._ops61() it gets _p_check, _read_port_s and _fmt. Edit no earlier probe. Dispatch is configs | read, nothing else. - configs (serial; assert comm.size == 1): - (X0) Re-run item 242's census: tets 117 206 / 168 507 equal imp3x_meta.json exactly, and the triangle attributes are {1, 21–24} / {1, 21–24, 402}. - Load imp3p_off.json / imp3p_rod.json read-only. Assert Solver.Order == 1, PEC [1] / [1, 402], Domains.Postprocessing keys {Energy, Probe}, and Output postpro_imp3p_<arm>. - Deep-copy each, set Solver.Order = 2 and Problem.Output = "postpro_imp3q_<arm>", and write imp3q_off.json / imp3q_rod.json with mode "x". - (X0q, printed) List every key path where imp3q_off.json differs from logs/ops61/f05x_o2.json, excluding Model.Mesh, Problem.Output and Domains.Postprocessing. Predicted: empty. A non-empty list is printed verbatim and is not a stop, because (RP2) below is the asserted test of the same fact. - read: - (H) Run parse_probe / parse_energy on each postpro_imp3q_* (bijection or stop). - Run _p_check on imp3q_off / imp3q_rod (fails asserted). - (RP2) Below. - Print Palace's own order 1 → 2 shifts against logs/imp3/palace_imp3p_fields.json (read-only). - Save the parsed arrays to logs/imp3/palace_imp3q_fields.json (mode "x"). - Never read z_matrix_ohm, docs/private/ or aed_results/. - New module tests/validation/test_imp3_palace_fields_o2.py (@complex_only; one test, test_imp3_palace_fields_degree2): - Builds: probe.build_arm("off"), then build_arm("rod") (GEO-23 order), each through build_four_port_sweep(frequency_hz=STEP2D_FREQUENCY_HZ, built=…, build_only=True). - Sweeps: its own wrapper _sweep2(case) = run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(case["problem"], case["port_defs"], lumped_sheet_ports=case["specs"], lumped_sheet_facet_tags=case["facet_tags"], keep_fields=True, degree=2). test_imp3_palace_twin._sweep hard-codes degree=1 (:81–89) and must not be used. κ stays off. - Import helpers only, never a test_* name: - _ids and _sheet_areas from test_imp3_palace_twin; - _owned_hits, _pal_fields, PTS, PNAMES and FP from test_imp3_palace_fields; - _matrix_quantities, _wall_dofs, _wall_max_e, PEC_WALL_MAX_E and PORT_IDS from test_imp3_rod_birdcage. - A local _readings2: item 242's _readings with quadrature_degree 4. |e|² of a degree-2 field is degree 4, so quadrature 4 is exact on affine cells. Item 242's pinned 2 was exact only at degree 1. - Per arm, before del res, for every drive: - E at PTS via evaluate_vector_field_parallel(e_complex, PTS, owner="lowest_original_cell"); - W_ph, allreduced; - (B); - the global dof count V.dofmap.index_map.size_global * V.dofmap.index_map_bs. - Write logs/imp3/ours_imp3q_fields.json on rank 0 (mode "w", a new name). - Read palace_imp3q_fields.json (order 2), and item 242's palace_imp3p_fields.json and ours_imp3p_fields.json (order 1), all read-only, and print the readings below. - Never write ours_imp3p_fields.json, ours_imp3x_p1.json or anything under logs/ops61/.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - (X0), W1: exact tet counts and attribute sets, as item 242 (X0) measured them. - (K2) The order reached Palace's solve, read by the executor from the W2 / W3 logs and journalled: - W2's ND (p = 2) equals 753 062 exactly. This is backed by the same mesh at the same order (…item194-W4-palace-o2.log:110). - W3's ND (p = 2) is printed, predicted 1 090 614. - Palace log check, W2 / W3: - elements equals the (X0) count; - Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on 21–24; - 6.400e-02 GHz; - four GMRES solver converged lines. - (P) Palace, W4, on imp3q_off / imp3q_rod via _p_check (ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py:742–782): - RECIPROCITY_BAND (test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86); - PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, with column power ≤ 1 + 1e-9 (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:129); - ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:121); - POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:173). - Backed at order 2 on the off mesh by item 194 (P) green (20261003T110728Z_OPS-61-item194-W5-read.log). On the rod arm it is backed only at order 1 (item 235 W5). - (RP2) Palace reproduces its own order-2 record: imp3q_off S against logs/ops61/postpro_f05x_o2/port-S.csv, entrywise max|ΔS| / max|S|, within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL 1e-6 (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py:171). This is backed by the same comparison at order 1, 2.9e-14 (item 235 W5). Postprocessing does not enter the solve. There is no rod-arm record at order 2, so the rod arm has no (RP2). - Ours, W5: - (F): cells equal imp3x_meta.json exactly, and N_i equals 5.6e-5 within STRIP_BAND (test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58). - (R2) Ours without the rod at degree 2 reproduces logs/ops61/ours_f05x_p2.json s_kappa_off, entrywise, within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL. - Assert the file's "ranks" equals comm.size (8) and "degree" equals 2. A mismatch is a stop, not a skip, because (R2) is this item's anchor. - Backing: the same builder coincidence at degree 1 (≤ 1.2e-10, item 235 W6), and ANS-4 (X) at degree 2 against this file (8.9e-13, item 192 W3). - (i)/(ii) on both sweeps (_ids). - (E): rod PEC wall max |E| ≤ PEC_WALL_MAX_E (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:135) on every drive, on the degree-2 space's wall dofs (_wall_dofs(msh, built[2], V)). - (V): valid_mask all True for the six points on both arms.

Printed, never gated. P1 is the reading of record; P2–P4 are printed beside it. I12's (T_E) / (T_W) ≤ 1e-6 were predictions, printed and never asserted (item 242 brief, "Printed, never gated"). They are not code-agreement bands, so here they stay predictions. - (D) Our global dof count per arm, against Palace's ND (p = 2). Predicted equal: 753 062 / 1 090 614. - (B) Owned-cell hits per point. Predicted 1 everywhere, as item 242 measured on these meshes. - (T_E2) The field tie at order 2. g₂ = E^ours_c(F1) / E^Pal_c(F1) on the off arm, with c* = argmax over c of |E^Pal_c(F1)|. Per arm, the reading is the max over (p, c) of |E^ours − g₂·E^Pal| / ‖g₂·E^Pal(p)‖, with item 242's exclusions. - Predicted ≤ 1e-6. The derivation is I12's: same mesh, same order, same operator, Palace Tol 1e-10. Order 1 measured ≤ 1.5e-8. - Print g₂ against item 242's g = −7.071067853e-2. It is the ratio of incident scales, which does not depend on order: predicted |g₂/g − 1| ≤ 1e-6. - Print the conj form, predicted O(1). - (T_W2) The energy tie. q_rod / q_off − 1, predicted ≤ 1e-6. Also q_off / |g₂|² against item 242's 2.896e9 (a convention constant), predicted equal to ≤ 1e-6 relative. - (T_S2) The S tie per class, per arm (_circulant_classes). Predicted ≤ 1e-6. On the off arm it is implied by (RP2) + (R2) + item 194's 0.0000 %. - The order 1 → 2 shift, per code (the item's reading for ANS-10). Same code and same incident scale at both orders, so the ratios are meaningful: - δ_p = |E^o2(p)| / |E^o1(p)| − 1, per arm, at each point. Predicted |δ| ∈ [1e-3, 1] at T1–T3 and S1, and [1e-3, 0.3] at F1 / F2. For scale, the S class shift on the off arm is 6.667 / 2.544 / 4.522 % (item 194). - η_rod^o2(p) / η_rod^o1(p) − 1 at every point. Predicted [1e-3, 0.5] at T1. - ΔW(rod/off) at order 2, beside order 1's +3.809 %. Predicted in [1e-3, 0.1]. - Per class, the S shift for both arms. - Ours against Palace on each shift: |δ^ours − δ^Pal|, predicted ≤ 2e-6 (two ties). - Closed form beside it: pec_prolate_spheroid_field (utils/analytical.py:1576) against η_rod^o2(p) / η_rod^o2(F1) at T1–T3 and S1. Predicted [0.3, 3], with no accuracy claim, as in I12. - Palace prices: Total, Preconditioner, peak memory and ND per run.

Negative controls (rule (e)). No order-2 field comparison exists on this fixture, so every factor below is predicted and printed, with its ceiling computed. (K2), (RP2) and (R2) are the asserted knobs. - (C1′) The order shift of the tip effect against the matched-order code gap. Separation = |η^o2_rod(T1) / η^o1_rod(T1) − 1| / max(d_η^o1(T1), d_η^o2(T1)) / η. - Predicted ≥ 1e3. Least case: 1e-3 / 1e-6. - Ceiling ≈ 1e8: a shift ≤ 1 against I12's measured d_η/η ≤ 5e-9, doubled. - Below 1e3, the two codes do not agree on the order shift at the tip: report it. - (C2′) The arm swap at order 2. |E^ours,o2_off(T1) − g₂·E^Pal,o2_rod(T1)| / ‖g₂·E^Pal,o2_rod(T1)‖. - Predicted ≥ 0.3. Order 1 measured 0.750 (item 242), but that is a different order, so the factor is predicted, not asserted. - Ceiling ≈ 1 relative, i.e. ≈ 1e8× over (T_E2) at the round-off floor. - (C3′) The order swap: the probe reading sees the order. On the rod arm at T1: |E^ours,o2 − g·E^Pal,o1| / ‖g·E^Pal,o1‖, using item 242's Palace array. - Predicted ≥ 1e-3, so ≥ 1e3× over (T_E2). - Ceiling ≈ |δ_p(T1)| / 1e-8 ≤ 1e8×. - It catches a Palace run that ignored Order in the solve but not the ND count, and an ours that silently ran degree 1.

Traps already paid for. - Degree is hard-coded in item 235's _sweep (degree=1). Importing it would silently run order 1 against Palace order 2, and (T_E2) would read the order shift, not a tie. Use _sweep2. (D) and (C3′) are the tell. - Quadrature pinned for the degree. Use quadrature_degree=4 on the degree-2 energy form (POST-5's rule; item 242's 2 under-integrates here and would put a quadrature error into (T_W2)). Do no UFL or sqrt comparisons; take ratios in numpy. - Pointwise N1curl depends on the MPI width without the owner rule (known-issues 2026-09-27). Always pass owner="lowest_original_cell" and evaluate e_complex once. Keep PTS bitwise identical on every rank (it is imported). Never call f.eval(points, np.arange(n)). - The owner rule raises on create_submesh meshes (known-issues 2026-10-04). It does not apply here (full mesh, item 242). If it raises anyway, stop: never fall back. - Never overwrite earlier artifacts. - Write with mode "x" for the configs and Palace arrays. - Use new imp3q_ names. - logs/ops61/ and every imp3x_* / imp3p_* file are read-only. - Do not call any code path that writes ours_imp3x_p1.json or ours_imp3p_fields.json. - Tag 402 and the cell tags live in the build tuple (built[2] / built[1]), not in the sweep's. - Build order and memory. Build without the rod first (GEO-23). Evaluate before del res, and free the off arm's fields, case and mesh before the rod build. - Rank-local quantities. assemble_scalar, collision counts and wall dofs are rank-local: reduce them. Keep collectives outside any rank == 0 branch. At -n 8, a rank-0-only collective deadlocks the window (item 227's W1). - Palace CSV headers are parsed, never assumed. Reuse item 242's parsers. An unparseable header is a stop. - A GMRES … did not converge line is a finding. That run's fields are not measured. Never change Order, Tol, MaxIts or -np in-slot. - Divide window prices by the solves in them (item 237). The 64.14 s is per sweep. Item 192 W3's 429 s holds four sweeps. - Harness discipline: - -s, tests/environment first, FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, foreground, no pipes, no -k; - Status 124: run pgrep -c python3 in the container first and never lengthen the timeout. A killed compile leaves an orphan .c: run the rubric's cache sweep only when nothing is running; - rule (i): no edit after a file's last window. - Palace numbers go in at full detail (version, config, mesh). No AED number, and no Palace figure set against one, in any tracked file. Never open docs/private/, aed_results/ or COMPARISON_private.md.

Scope. Covered: Palace order 2 and ours at degree 2, 64 MHz, on item 235's exact-rectangle record meshes (117 206 / 168 507 cells, σ = 800 S/m untuned coil, 50 Ω, κ off), on two arms (without the rod, and rod PEC). The comparison is E at six fixed points and phantom electric energy, P1 of record. The order 1 → 2 shift of the near-tip field is printed per code. Agreement is a matched-order check at the production order between two independent codes. The order shift is a one-mesh p-reading, not an h-statement and not a convergence rate (two orders, one mesh). Not covered: - the 1 g tip SAR, the ratio Q and its accuracy. These need the rod + strip build on PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG (never built) or an h-ladder: a later I-step for the weekly to price; - the natural-wall arm at order 2 (η_wall), dropped for price; - absolute |E| / SAR; - tissue, heating, compliance, ISO 10974 (WF-9), ASTM F2182 (7c); - the tuned or copper coil, F-human, other rod placements, the kept-cells rod; - AED, src/, any band.

Status it can move. - §7 IMP-3 stays ✅ (no glyph; rule (j) read: the row's Done-when, "identities green … on the 1 g rung with the tip ratio printed there ⇒ ✅ as a fixture", is met by step 1 and says nothing about order). The review appends a step-5 record sentence beside steps 3 and 4. Candidate text, valid only if W4 and W5 are green, (T_E2) ≤ 1e-6 on both arms and (C1′) ≥ 1e3×: "Palace order 2 matches ours at degree 2 on E at six fixed phantom points and on phantom electric energy to ≤ ⟨x⟩ per arm (P1; off, rod PEC), each code reproducing its own order-2 f05x record; the order 1 → 2 shift of the rod's near-tip effect, η_rod(T1), is ⟨y⟩ % in both codes, agreeing to ⟨z⟩. Record mesh, one-mesh p-reading, no 1 g or accuracy claim." - §10 I13 is done, as a provisional step for the weekly to ratify or revert. - ANS-10 (no §7 row; §10 ≈ line 4460): the weekly reads this as the first order-2 field-level Palace reading, and as the first measured size of the tip ratio's order sensitivity on the record mesh. If |η_rod^o2(T1) / η_rod^o1(T1) − 1| is small (say < 1 %), the order-1 tip ratio is p-stable on this mesh. If it is large, ANS-10's accuracy question needs the 1 g rung or an h-ladder before anything else. The weekly decides; this item sets no threshold. - §2 ≈ line 437 keeps "the ratio's accuracy is ANS-10's". It may gain one clause: "the near-tip field agrees with Palace at matched order 1 and 2; its order shift is ⟨y⟩ %".

Negative result. - Pre-check miss, or (X0) red: not the fixture. BLOCKED; the review decides. - (K2) red (W2's ND ≠ 753 062): Palace did not solve at order 2 on f05x's mesh. Stop before W3, BLOCKED. - A Palace abort or a non-converged GMRES: record it verbatim, open a known-issues entry, BLOCKED (rule (d)). Never re-run with changed solver settings. - (P) or (RP2) red: report every number, park, BLOCKED. Never widen. - Ours (F), (R2), (i), (ii), (E) or (V) red: park on attempt/IMP-3-step5-<ts>, open a known-issues entry, BLOCKED. (R2) red at matched width means ours at degree 2 did not reproduce item 166, which is a finding about degree-2 reproducibility, not about the rod. - (T_E2) or (T_W2) on the off arm > 1e-6, with (RP2) and (R2) green: not a stop. It is the first field-level disagreement at order 2. Print it per point and component beside (B), (D) and the conj form, and report. The candidates are Palace's point evaluation of a p = 2 field, our degree-2 evaluation, or the energy quadrature. No record sentence; the review reads it. - (T_E2) green on the off arm but > 1e-6 on the rod arm: a reading located at the PEC hole. Report it. - (D) unequal: the two codes discretise different spaces. Report the counts; with (RP2) / (R2) green it is a counting-convention reading, not a stop. - Box-speed gate trips: a partial record (W2 only), BLOCKED (slow box). The review re-queues. - A printed reading outside its prediction: report it; no status effect. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

The 1 g ratio of record is on PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG, because the record mesh's 537 phantom cells cannot hold a 1 g ball.) docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-06 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain I14 (PROJECT_PLAN.md ≈ line 4655), a weekly-enumerated step (§9 rule (4)), posed by the 10-05 weekly beside its ruling bullet "I13 — the tip ratio is not p-stable at 1 %" (≈ line 4490). No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target moves.

IMP-3 step 6 — the tip ratio on the 1 g rung at degree 2. This runs item 235's exact-rectangle rod fixture at phantom_resolution=PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG (0.0025 m, tests/validation/test_birdcage_sar_1g_rung.py:114), at 64 MHz with κ off. The fixture is _build(True, …) / _build_rod(…) with leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION (tests/validation/test_port_lumped_narrowed_sheet.py), built as scripts/probes/imp3_step3_palace_rod.py:54–58 builds it. Two arms (off and rod PEC) are solved at degree 1 and at degree 2. The identities are asserted at the imported bands. Printed: η_rod(T1) at both orders, its p-move against I13's −4.961 % on the record mesh, and the 1 g tip SAR ratio Q at both orders. Target: the identities. The p-stability question is a reading.

  • Executor: implementer. One new test module (tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py). No src/, and no edit to any existing file.
  • Tier: heavy. W1 -n 1; W2 / W3 -n 8; W4 -n 4. Every window runs in the complex container.
  • Class: chain step (solve).
  • Cost: ≈ 17 measured / ≈ 55 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 15 code + ≈ 18 compute + ≈ 7 spare).
  • Depends on: nothing. Every module named below is on main. The rod + strip + 1 g rung combination has never been built: it is new geometry, so W1 builds it serially first.

Settled from the code. - The modules items 235 / 252 used: - tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py (step 1): _arm :295, _case :503, _assert_identities :617, _control_c1 :639, _wall_dofs :188, _wall_max_e :199, _outer_box_tags :205, _matrix_quantities :275, _ball_mean_closed_form :229, _peak_rss_gib :498 and TIPS :140. The 1 g ball goes through mass_averaged_sar at QUADRATURE_DEGREE 16 (test_mass_averaged_sar_standard_masses.py:121). - tests/validation/test_imp3_palace_twin.py (item 235): _ids and _sheet_areas. - tests/validation/test_imp3_palace_fields.py (item 242): PTS, PNAMES, FP and _owned_hits. - tests/validation/test_imp3_palace_fields_o2.py (item 252): _readings2 :68 (quadrature 4), and the η_rod / p-move print at :207–225. - _arm cannot run degree 2. It calls build_four_port_sweep(…, build_only=True) without degree, then sweeps at case["degree"], whose default is 1 (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:219,230). - The new module therefore carries a local _arm_d(built, label, rod, degree, field_hook): _arm copied, with degree=degree passed to build_four_port_sweep. - It also carries a local _case_d(degree, arms), which builds with both phantom_resolution=PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG and leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION. Step 1's _case passes neither the strip nor a degree. - Import helpers and constants only, never a test_* name. - η_rod is item 252's definition: η_rod(p) = ‖E_rod(p)‖ / ‖E_off(p)‖ per drive, where ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm over components. - E comes from evaluate_vector_field_parallel(e_complex, PTS, owner="lowest_original_cell"), evaluated inside field_hook before the fields are freed. - The record-mesh values are η_rod^o2(T1) P1 = 3.594534 and η^o2/η^o1 − 1 = −4.961114e-02 (20261005T173453Z_IMP-3-item252-W5-ours-p2.log:3910–3911). - Q = SAR_1g,tip(rod) / SAR_1g,tip(off) per tip and drive, which is step 1's reading. Step 1 read P1 top 4.496087 on the ragged 1 g rung at degree 1 (20261002T170843Z_IMP-3-step1-W2.log:3864). - Sizes, from the ragged sibling: - 199 920 / 250 866 cells (…170843Z_IMP-3-step1-W2.log:1918,3758). - On the record mesh the exact strip added 1 121 cells (116 085 → 117 206, item 235 W1), so the prediction is ≈ 201 000 / ≈ 252 000 cells. - Degree-2 dofs are predicted at ≈ 1.3 M / ≈ 1.6 M (2E + 2F, item 252's counting identity).

One knob, four windows. The env knob FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP6 takes one of {build, d2off, d2rod, d1}, and one test function dispatches on it (never -k). - Each degree-2 arm gets its own window. One arm at degree 2 is priced at ≈ 240–320 s, so the pair would cross 590 s. - Each window saves its arrays to logs/imp3/ours_imp3g_<knob>.json on rank 0 (mode "x"). - The closing window (W4) reads the two degree-2 files read-only.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - W1, census (build, -n 1): - (G0) Both builds complete serially. Off-arm cells are printed against ONE_GRAM_RUNG_CELL_RECORD 199 920 (test_birdcage_sar_1g_rung.py:125), beside CELL_COUNT_BAND (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheet_prerequisite.py). This is printed, not asserted: it is the first record of the exact-rectangle 1 g rung, and no record exists yet. - (G1) Rod cells < ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 320 000 (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:115), asserted before any solve. - (G2) Every N_i area = 5.6e-5 within STRIP_BAND 1e-9 (test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58), on both arms. - (G3) Rod arm: tag-402 facets > 0, all of them exterior. Off arm: 402 count 0. - (G4) The 1 g ball fits: the two geometric asserts at the end of _assert_identities (:636–637). - W2 / W3 / W4, per arm and degree. This is _assert_identities's set, applied to each arm the window solves: - (i) ‖S − Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND (test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86). - (ii) σ_max ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:129), and every column power ≤ 1. - (PP) The PORT-16 exact power partition, |p_src − p_vol − sheet| / |p_src| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL 1e-6 (test_birdcage_power_identity.py:227), per drive, via _exact_shares. It is backed at degree 2 by test_birdcage_power_identity_degree2.py:168. - (M) Rod arm: σ_y mirror pairs ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:121). - (S) Off arm: separation ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:173). - (E) Rod arm: max |E| on the reduced tag-402 dofs ≤ PEC_WALL_MAX_E 1e-12 (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:135), on every drive, on the space of the degree being solved. - (V) valid_mask all True at the six PTS. - (D) The global dof count equals 2E + 2F at degree 2, and E at degree 1, where E and F are that mesh's global edge and face counts. This is an exact counting identity and it is the order knob: item 252 measured it exactly (753 062 / 1 090 614).

Negative controls. - (Kw) asserted. The rod wall is left natural, P1, at degree 1, in W4 only. It runs on a fresh solver on replace(problem, facet_tags=outer, pec_facet_tags=(OUTER_BOX_TAG,)), using _outer_box_tags and _control_c1's construction (:639). - Assertion: max |E| on the 402 dofs > PEC_WALL_MAX_E. - Backing: the same exact-rectangle fixture at the record resolution, item 235 W6, read 1.297e-4 against 1e-12 (20261005T035322Z_IMP-3-item235-W6-ours-p1.log:3797). - Ceiling ≈ 1e8×. - (D) asserted is the order control. A run that silently solved degree 1 fails it by a factor of ≈ 5.4. - (C-p) predicted (rule (e)), printed: |η_rod^o2(T1)/η_rod^o1(T1) − 1| on the 1 g rung ≥ 1e-3. - Ceiling ≈ 1, since a shift cannot exceed the field itself. Then a = _arm_d(built, "degree 2 rod r/(4√2)", True, 2). - The writer is local: rank 0 writes logs/imp3/ours_imp3h_r4s2.json (mode "x") with _ser(a) plus rss_gib, ranks, tip_size_m, the near-T1 and T1-cell edges, and a barrier outside the rank branch. - Env knob: FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP7 ∈ {r4s2}. One test function dispatches on it and skips otherwise. Never -k. - Record constants the module registers, each citing its log line: - I14_ETA_O2_T1_P1 = "3.482328" (20261006T173320Z_IMP-3-item284-W4-d1-readout.log:3894); - I14_Q_O2_P1_TOP = 4.463326 (…:3905); - GEO36_R4S2_CELLS = 276_088, GEO36_R4S2_D2_DOFS = 1_775_954, GEO36_R4S2_N402 = 6_256, GEO36_R4S2_NEAR_T1 = (19, 6.422237e-04) and GEO36_UNSET_NEAR_T1_EDGE = 6.983224e-04 (20261007T170700Z_GEO-36-step4-W2-rungs.log:5612–5613, 7516). These are printed comparands, not bands. - η_rod is item 252's definition, as I14 used it (IMP-3.md:784): η_rod^h(p) = ‖E_rod^h(p)‖ / ‖E_off(p)‖ per drive, with the Euclidean norm over components. - E_off(p) comes from ours_imp3g_d2off.json (I14 W2) via _cplx, read-only. - η_rod^{r/4} comes from ours_imp3g_d2rod.json (I14 W3), read-only. - E_rod^{r/(4√2)} is this window's a["E"]. - Geometry already known (GEO-36.md:175, 209 (4), 227). T1 sits 2.531 mm from the cap centre, outside the 2 mm cap ball, so the knob refines T1's neighbourhood only by grading spill-over. GEO-36 W2 measured the near-T1 (0.5 mm) mean edge at 6.983224e-04 → 6.422237e-04 m (−8.0 %) at r/(4√2), and −27 % at r/8 (log :7516). The local step at T1 is therefore ≈ 1.087, not the requested √2. This item prints the edge; it names no step ratio.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported by name, never restated). On the rod arm at r/(4√2), degree 2, through the imported helpers: - (G1) cells < ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:115), inside _arm_d before the solve. The predicted 276 088 passes. r/8's 342 072 would trip it, but r/8 is not run here. - (G2) every N_i area = 5.6e-5 within STRIP_BAND (test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58), inside _identities. - (G3) tag-402 facets > 0 and all exterior, via _outer_box_tags(msh, built[2], comm), as I14's _census does it (test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py:317, 342–343). - (i) ‖S − Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND (test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86). - (ii) σ_max ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:129), and every column power ≤ 1. - (PP) the PORT-16 exact power partition ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (test_birdcage_power_identity.py:227) per drive, via _exact_shares. It is backed at degree 2 by test_birdcage_power_identity_degree2.py:168. - (M) σ_y mirror pairs ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:121). - (E) max |E| on the reduced tag-402 dofs ≤ PEC_WALL_MAX_E (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:135), on every drive. - (V) valid_mask is all True at the six PTS. - (D) global dofs = 2E + 2F exactly (the counting identity I14 W3 and GEO-36 (D) measured). - (S) is off-arm only and is not re-run. Its record is I14 W2's 1 270.3× (IMP-3.md:914).

Negative controls (rule (e) labels). - (Kc) asserted — the knob reached gmsh. Two checks: - built[3]["implant_rod_cad"]["tip_size_m"] == TIP_R4S2 bitwise; - rod cells > ROD_1G_RUNG_CELL_RECORD. - Backing, same comparison on the same build: GEO-36 W2 read tip_size_m equal to the request bitwise (log :7503) and 276 088 / 252 118 = 1.0951 (:7516). - A build that silently took I14's _built("rod"), or a key that never reached gmsh, reads exactly 252 118 and fails by an integer. There is no ceiling: the separation is the integer itself. - (D) asserted is the order control. A run that silently solved degree 1 fails it by a factor of ≈ 5.4 (331 014 against 1 775 954, GEO-36 W2 :5612). - (Rb) asserted — the off-arm reuse is wired. η_rod^{r/4}(T1), P1, is recomputed in this window from the two I14 JSONs. It must be string-equal at 6 d.p. to I14_ETA_O2_T1_P1 "3.482328", the same comparison on the same files (W4 log :3894). The JSONs' cells / ndofs must equal 201 072 / 1 284 856 and 252 118 / 1 620 748 as integers. A red means the reading path is wrong, and no η at r/(4√2) may be printed as a reading. - (C-h) predicted, printed: |η_rod^{r/(4√2)}(T1)/η_rod^{r/4}(T1) − 1| (P1) ≥ 1e-3. - Ceiling ≈ 1, since the move cannot exceed the field. - Basis: the near-T1 edge moved −8 %, and I14's remesh move record → 1 g rung was −3.122 % at degree 2 (IMP-3.md:950). - Below 1e-3 is reported, not a stop. With (Kc) and (D) green, that would be the first rung's answer, not a defect. - (C2) predicted, printed: |η_rod(T1) − 1| / max over F1, F2 of |η_rod(F) − 1| at r/(4√2) ≥ 3 (r/4 read 16.321, IMP-3.md:950). - Mesh identity predicted, printed: - cells, tag-402 facets and degree-2 dofs equal GEO36_R4S2_* as integers; - near-T1 count and mean edge equal GEO36_R4S2_NEAR_T1 to the printed digits. - Basis: gmsh builds serially on rank 0 (io/mesh.py:3998,4480), and 252 118 read the same at -n 1 and -n 8 (GEO-36.md:145). - A mismatch is reported, not a stop. (Kc) is the asserted knob check.

Printed, never gated. P1 is the reading of record; P2–P4 and ccw / cw are printed beside it. - η_rod^{r/(4√2)}(p) at all six points, beside η_rod^{r/4}(p) (recomputed under (Rb)). Per point, the relative move η^{r/(4√2)}/η^{r/4} − 1. - The first ladder step at T1, P1: η_rod(T1) at r/4 (3.482328) → r/(4√2), and its relative move. It is printed beside I14's p-move −5.995 % and the remesh move −3.122 % for scale. The step ratio is not computed: it needs r/8 (xl). - The F1 / F2 moves, printed as this remesh's floor beside T1's move. - T1's local mesh: - the near-T1 (T1_RADIUS) cell count and mean edge via _ball_and_t1(msh, built[1], cad["tip_ball_radius_m"], comm), beside GEO-36's r/4 6.983224e-04 and r/(4√2) 6.422237e-04 m, with the local edge ratio h(r/4)/h(r/(4√2)) beside the requested √2; - the T1 cell's own mean edge: point_owner_cells(msh, T1[None, :], comm), then _mean_edge(_cell_geometry(msh)[[cell]]) on the owning rank, made global by an allreduce (MAX, 0 elsewhere) outside any rank branch, printed with its original cell index. This is a first record at this rung: no r/4 value exists. - N_ball and the mean ball edge from the same call, beside GEO-36 W2's 32 826 / 2.433e-4 m. - Q = SAR_1g,tip(rod) / SAR_1g,tip(off) per tip and drive, with SAR_off from ours_imp3g_d2off.json. It is printed beside the r/4 value recomputed from ours_imp3g_d2rod.json (P1 top 4.463326, log :3905), together with the rod-arm 1 g ball masses (r/4: 0.982 g). - pec_prolate_spheroid_field (utils/analytical.py:1576) beside η_rod(p)/η_rod(F1) at T1–T3 and S1, as I14 prints it. No accuracy claim. - Cells, E, F, global dofs, build seconds, sweep seconds, SAR seconds and summed peak RSS (_peak_rss_gib, called on every rank) against GEO-36's price row (GEO-36.md:233: sweep 318.8–322.9 s, window 491.3–495.4 s, 57.04–57.77 GiB).

Windows (bare, whole, foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; container-side timeout -k 30 ≤ 590 s; -s; tests/environment first; FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1; no -k; no pipes). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. - Gate (not a harness call): the three conditions at the top of this item. If any fails, the item is BLOCKED and nothing below runs. - Pre-check (not a harness call): - ls logs/imp3/: ours_imp3g_d2off.json and ours_imp3g_d2rod.json must be present, and ours_imp3h_r4s2.json absent (mode "x"). - git diff 0f6bbbc7 -- tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py and git diff a49f997c -- tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py must both be empty: the imported helpers are the ones that ran. - Any mismatch: stop and report. Never delete or move a file. - First: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Then run the rubric's cache sweep, label IMP-3-item305-cache-sweep (≈ 85 s; item 284's took 85 s). - W0, import smoke (-n 1, knob unset, so the test skips; ≈ 40 s, range 20–90). It catches an import or collection error before an eight-minute window.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-item305-W0-import "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W1, the rod arm at r/(4√2), degree 2, plus the readout (≈ 495 s, range [450, 570]; ≈ 57–58 GiB summed at -n 8). - Basis: GEO-36's price row, 491.3 / 495.4 s at e = 1.23 / 1.37 (GEO-36.md:233), scaled from I14 W3's 450 s window (sweep 284.88 s at 1 620 748 dofs, 50.97 GiB). The readout adds ≈ 5 s of JSON reads and norms. This is a prediction, not a measurement on the refined mesh. - This is the closing window (rule (i)): no module edit after it starts. - Durable capture is §5.1's idiom verbatim, trailing ; exit $rc included:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-item305-W1-d2rod-r4s2 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && mkdir -p /workspace/logs && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP7=r4s2 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py -v -s --tb=short > /workspace/logs/imp3-item305-w1-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/imp3-item305-w1-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/imp3-item305-w1-raw.log; exit \$rc'" - Compute ≈ 85 + 40 + 495 ≈ 620 s ≈ 10.3 min, plus ≈ 1 min of container overhead. The tops of the ranges give 745 s ≈ 12.4 min. - Fallback. If W1 returns Status 124: - run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 first, then the cache sweep (the daily-review.md rubric's trap list), and only when it reads 0; - if the wrapper itself died, recover with scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh --capture-orphan IMP-3-item305-W1-d2rod-r4s2 logs/imp3-item305-w1-raw.log once the container command has finished; - the killed window is I15's price record: "r/(4√2) rod arm at degree 2 on the 1 g rung > 590 s at -n 8". Journal the last printed phase (build / sweep / SAR / readout) with its seconds; - park on attempt/IMP-3-step7-<ts> and mark BLOCKED (over the ceiling; the weekly commissions xl for both rungs); - never lengthen the timeout, never raise -n, never split in-slot.

Traps already paid for. - Item 263's list carries in full (IMP-3.md:866–887): - degree defaults to 1 in two places; - never build without leg_sheet_strip_fraction (binding ruling 2026-10-02); - quadrature 4 at degree 2; - no UFL ordering or sqrt comparison on complex operands; - owner="lowest_original_cell" with PTS imported bitwise; - rank-local quantities reduced, with no collective inside a rank == 0 branch (item 227's -n 8 deadlock); - tag 402 and the cell tags live in built[2] / built[1]; - evaluate before freeing fields; - divide window prices by the solves in them; - Status 124 means pgrep first; - an orphan .c means the cache sweep, only with nothing running. - New here: - _built and _save are not reusable (above). Calling _built("rod") gives the r/4 mesh and a run that looks green; (Kc) is the tell. - _ball_and_t1 takes the cell tags built[1] and reduces internally. Call it on every rank. - The T1 owner lookup is collective (point_owner_cells allreduces). Call it on every rank, outside any rank branch. - Importing test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip runs its module-level probe load (:83), which is harmless. Never import its builds fixture: pytest would collect it into the new module. - A requested VIn is not the step at T1: print the measured local edge and never write "step ratio √2" for T1. - The module writes with mode "x", so a second W1 in the same slot fails on its own file. There is no second attempt. - If the permission layer denies the $rc capture form (it did once, PORT-21 step 5 W0b, docs/planning/chunks/PORT-21.md:38), stop and report. Do not improvise a different capture. - Never write ours_imp3g_*, ours_imp3p_fields.json, ours_imp3q_fields.json or anything under logs/ops61/. Never open docs/private/, aed_results/ or COMPARISON_private.md.

Scope. Covered: ours at degree 2, 64 MHz, on the exact-rectangle hole-rod fixture at the 1 g rung (σ = 800 S/m untuned coil, 50 Ω, κ off), with the cap-ball VIn = r/(4√2), rod arm only. The off arm is I14's record, reused. It measures the identities on the refined mesh and prints the first step of the near-tip ladder. Not covered: - any convergence claim. One step gives no rate, and the step ratio and observed order need r/8 (xl, the weekly's). Because T1 sits outside the cap ball, even the step's size in local h is a measured ≈ 1.087, not √2; - any accuracy claim on η_rod or Q (ANS-10's); - the r/8 rung; the degree-1 arm at r/(4√2); the natural-wall control at this rung (I14's (Kw) at r/4 stands, IMP-3.md:949, and is not re-run); - a ball-radius knob (GEO-36.md:209 (4), the weekly's question); - absolute |E| / SAR, tissue, heating, compliance, ISO 10974 (WF-9), ASTM F2182 (7c); F-human, the tuned or copper coil; AED, src/, any band.

Status it can move. - §7 IMP-3 stays ✅ (no glyph); rule (j) read as in item 263 (IMP-3.md:897). The review appends a step-7 record sentence. Candidate text, valid only if W1 is green: "Step 7 part 2 (§9 item 305): with the cap-ball tip size at r/(4√2) on the exact-rectangle 1 g rung (⟨n⟩ cells, ⟨d⟩ degree-2 dofs) the rod-arm identities hold at degree 2; η_rod(T1) (P1) reads ⟨η⟩ against 3.482328 at r/4 (⟨Δ⟩ %), with the near-T1 edge ⟨e⟩ % shorter. One ladder step, no rate, no accuracy claim." - §10 I15 part 2 is done; I15 stays open until r/8 lands. The review annotates I15's bullet. The slot makes no §10 edit. W1's measured window, sweep and RSS re-price r/8 for the weekly's xl commissioning, replacing the scaled prediction. - ANS-10: no reading moves. The convergence statement waits for r/8.

Negative result. - Gate fails: BLOCKED ("waits on the weekly's I15 ruling"), nothing run. This is not a negative result about the fixture. - Pre-check mismatch, or pgrep non-zero: stop and report. Mark BLOCKED with the unblock condition (rule (d)). Never delete. - W0 red (import or collection): this is a module defect. Fix it in-slot only if W1 has not started, then re-run W0. Otherwise park. - gmsh FAIL at W1: record it verbatim with its surface pairs, open a known-issues entry, and mark BLOCKED on the mesher. Never retry. GEO-36 W2 built this rung cleanly, so a FAIL here would be a rank-count finding. - (Kc) red: the knob did not reach the build. No η reading. Park, mark BLOCKED, and open a GEO-36 known-issues entry. - (Rb) red: the reading path is wrong. Report the identities as measured but print no η / Q reading. Park and mark BLOCKED. - (G1)–(G3), (i), (ii), (PP), (M), (E), (V) or (D) red: report every number, park on attempt/IMP-3-step7-<ts>, open a known-issues entry, and mark BLOCKED. Never widen. (PP) red only here would be a finding about _exact_shares on the refined hole mesh. - Status 124: the fallback above. The killed window is the price record. - A printed reading outside its prediction ((C-h) < 1e-3, (C2) < 3, a mesh-identity mismatch, W1 outside [450, 570] s): report it. No status effect. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Review rulings (2026-10-07 18:00 daily review, item 305). (1) "Weekly not yet committed" is a dependency that has not landed, not a block: a slot that finds no docs(plan): weekly review 2026-10-07 commit on main skips item 305 and leaves it ⬜ (implementer-run.md step 2: never an item whose stated dependency has not landed). Only a weekly commit that rules xl, changes the rung set or the question, or reads ambiguously makes the slot mark it BLOCKED. This replaces the brief's "if the commit is absent … BLOCKED" for the absent case only. (2) The unequal local step at T1 (edge ratio ≈ 1.087 then ≈ 1.264, because T1 sits outside the 2 mm cap ball) goes to the weekly with I15's ball-radius question; the item claims no step ratio and no observed order, as drafted. (3) Capture: if the durable-capture form is denied, stop and report, as drafted; do not improvise a bare window. (4) W1's predicted range [450, 570] s is a scaled prediction with 20 s of margin; a kill at 590 s is the price record, never a reason to lengthen, raise -n or split. (5) The new module tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py imports I14's and part 1's helpers and edits neither, so no re-gate window is owed; the brief's reasons for not reusing _built (no tip_size) and _save (fixed prefix) are accepted.

Outcome (2026-10-07 22:30 CDT slot, implementer): GREEN — every anchor and both asserted controls green on W1; no reading outside its prediction. Gate checked by the slot (weekly 732f960b). Pre-check matched (both I14 JSONs present, ours_imp3h_r4s2.json absent, both helper diffs empty); pgrep -c python3 0; cache sweep 20261008T033202Z_IMP-3-item305-cache-sweep.log (93 s, no orphan); W0 20261008T033340Z_IMP-3-item305-W0-import.log (71 s, 12 passed, 1 skipped). - W1 20261008T033458Z_IMP-3-item305-W1-d2rod-r4s2.log (459 s, -n 8, 13 passed, [capture] rc=0, in [450, 570]): rod arm at r/(4√2), degree 2, 276 088 cells — (G1) < 320 000; (G2) all four N_i 5.600000000000e-05; (G3) 6 256 tag-402 facets, all exterior; (i) 2.829e-15; (ii) σ_max 0.999828051, column powers ≤ 0.834917; (PP) ≤ 3.4e-15 per drive; (M) ≤ 0.0221 % (band 0.50 %); (E) 31 280 tag-402 dofs, max |E| 0 on all four drives; (V) True; (D) 1 775 954 = 2E + 2F exact (E 331 014, F 556 963). - Controls: (Kc) tip_size_m 0.00017677669529663688 == TIP_R4S2 bitwise, cells 276 088 > 252 118 (1.0951); (Rb) η_rod^{r/4}(T1) P1 recomputed from the I14 JSONs reads "3.482328", string-equal; sizes 201 072 / 1 284 856 and 252 118 / 1 620 748 equal. Mesh identity against GEO-36 W2: cells, 402 facets, d2 dofs and near-T1 (19, 6.422237e-04 m) all equal. N_ball 32 826, mean ball edge 2.433349e-04 m. - Readings (printed, never gated; P1 of record): η_rod(T1) r/4 3.482328 → r/(4√2) 3.556262, move +2.123 % (beside I14's p-move −5.995 % and remesh move −3.122 %; no step ratio — it needs r/8). F1 / F2 moves +0.027 % / −0.116 % (this remesh's floor). (C-h) 2.123e-2 ≥ 1e-3: IN. (C2) r/4 16.321, r/(4√2) 16.773 (≥ 3: IN). Near-T1 edge −8.033 %, local ratio h(r/4)/h(r/(4√2)) 1.0874 (the requested VIn ratio 1.4142 is not the step at T1). T1 cell (original index 187 478) mean edge 7.732801e-04 m, a first record. Q P1 top 4.463326 → 4.468599 (+0.118 %), bottom +0.112 %; every drive moves ≤ +0.12 %. Rod-arm 1 g masses 0.9817 / 0.9820 g. Closed form / η ratio at T1–T3, S1: 0.825 / 0.911 / 1.020 / 1.080 — no accuracy claim. - Price (re-prices r/8 for the weekly): build 74.92 s, sweep 267.03 s, 12 SAR balls 35.52 s, arm 308.0 s, body 383.2 s, summed peak RSS 53.85 GiB at -n 8 — under GEO-36's scaled row (sweep 318.8–322.9 s, 57.04–57.77 GiB). One ladder step, no rate, no accuracy claim.

docs.title: §9 item 327 — 2026-10-08 (chain I15 part 3a — the r/8 knob, xl entry 33's prerequisite)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

What it is. Add r8 to FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP7 in tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py, so xl entry 33 (docs/testing/xl-pending.md, entry 33) has a module to run. No solve. Item 305's knob set is KNOBS = ("r4s2",) (:68) and the dispatch at :240–244 calls _r4s2() only.

How (G1) is applied: a module global, not a parameter. - _arm_d(built, label, rod, degree) (test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py:150) does assert ncells < ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 at :165, when rod is true, after build_four_port_sweep(build_only=True) and before the solve. - The name resolves at call time in test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g's namespace. It is imported at :74 from test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:115 (320_000, "W2 rod-arm guard", §9 item 174 (A0)). It is a resource pre-check, not a physics band. - rod=False is not a way round it: it also drops wall_dofs, wall_max, case and built (:227–234), which _identities(a, True) needs for (M) and (E). - Proposal: the r8 path only does monkeypatch.setattr(tests.validation.test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g, "ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2", ROD_CELL_GUARD_XL). This changes neither file nor the constant's definition, and pytest restores it at teardown. The weekly ruled exactly this (xl-pending.md entry 33 Price: "the window's module raises the guard for the knobbed rung only, disclosed, never for the default path"). So this item is not "write the anchor". - The constant: ROD_CELL_GUARD_XL = 400_000, defined in the new module with a comment calling it an xl resource guard, not a band. It is derived from item 305 W1's measured 53.85 GiB summed at -n 8 for 276 088 cells (20261008T033458Z_…W1-d2rod-r4s2.log). - At the guard, ×1.449 cells gives 78–89.5 GiB at e = 1.0 / 1.37. - r/8 (342 072, ×1.239) gives 66.7–72.2 GiB. That is far inside 512 GiB, and r/8 sits at 0.855 of the guard. - r/16 (≈ 1 M cells, GEO-36.md:236) still trips it, so the guard keeps its purpose of catching a wrong rung or a runaway mesh before the solve. - The r8 path prints one disclosure line: patched value, original 320 000, measured cells.

Code (additive). - KNOBS = ("r4s2", "r8", "r8build"). Add TIP_R8 to the test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip import. The test takes monkeypatch. - A new _r8(build_only) beside _r4s2(). _r4s2()'s body is not touched. Duplicate rather than refactor. git diff on the module may delete only the KNOBS line, the docstring's knob sentence, the test signature and the dispatch lines. - _r8 reads ours_imp3g_d2off.json, ours_imp3g_d2rod.json and ours_imp3h_r4s2.json, and writes logs/imp3/ours_imp3h_r8.json with mode "x". - GEO-36 W2 r/8 comparands become constants with log-line cites from 20261007T170700Z_GEO-36-step4-W2-rungs.log: cells 342 072, d2 dofs 2 200 500, 402 facets 8 790, near-T1 (26, 5.08e-4 m, exact digits from the log), N_ball 93 132 / 1.722e-4 m. Add item 305's ITEM305_ETA_T1_P1 = "3.556262", sizes 276 088 / 1 775 954, and the price row (sweep 267.03 s, body 383.2 s, 53.85 GiB at -n 8). All of these are printed comparands except where asserted below. - Readout: η_rod(T1) P1 at r/4 → r/(4√2) → r/8. Print Δ₁ (+0.073934), Δ₂, their signs and |Δ₂| / |Δ₁| beside entry 33's 0.7 threshold (0.7 |Δ₁| = 0.051754). Printed, never asserted; the 10-14 weekly reads the rule. Also print the near-T1 edge ratio h(r/(4√2)) / h(r/8) beside 1.264, and Q at three rungs. - r8build builds the r/8 fixture and runs (Kc8), (G3), the census, _ball_and_t1 and the T1 owner on every rank. It does not call _arm_d and writes no JSON.
