docs.title: §9 item 381 — 2026-10-11 (chain I21b — the rod under the tuned copper F-human's two-port drive; chain step (solve))
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-11 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 I21b (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4753–4761, the 2026-10-10 weekly), lane 3 / Phase 7 (7b), serial on I21a; §9 rule (4). - Target: identities. The tip ratio is a record with no published comparand until (7c). - No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved; every band is imported. It is a record on a ✅ row. - The 2026-10-02 sheets-and-κ ruling, the capacitor-ESR ruling and the 10-10 10:30 rulings on items 358 / 359 bind (WF-10.md, "Review rulings (2026-10-10 10:30 review)"). So do the 2026-10-10 18:00 rulings on item 361 (MAT-15.md, 361-1 … 361-5), which govern how 358's builder is reused.

IMP-3 step 8: WF-9's lead-in-phantom construction on H9′'s tuned copper F-human. The fixture is: - I21a's kept-rod hole mesh, at degree 1, 64 MHz, κ off; - r = 0.2 Ω on all 32 gaps, with the two Thevenin feeds P17 / P21 at C_in,F-human = 118.2437 pF; - the rod switched by material: σ = 800 S/m (SIGMA_WIRE_S_PER_M) against the gel.

Executor and cost. - Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy, -n 8, complex build. - Windows: cache sweep, W0 (smoke, -n 1), W1a (rod-free reproduction) and W1b (rod arms), all foreground. - Class and cost: chain step (solve); ≈ M measured / ≈ 55 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 25 code + ≈ 10 compute (W1a ≈ 3 min, W1b ≈ 5–7 min) + spare. If W1b has not started by minute 45, park (rule (d)). - Depends on item 372 (I21a) landing. This means tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_f_human.py exists with ROD_FH and F_HUMAN_KEPT_ROD_CELL_RECORD, and GEO-36-step6-W2 is green in test-results.md. If it did not land, skip this item; it stays ⬜. - Gitignored inputs, both on disk when this brief was drafted: - logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437.json (5 468 bytes, rewritten 2026-10-10 19:50 CDT by item 361's builder call); - logs/wf12/h12c-cu-s32-a2.npz (20 812 bytes; build_tuned_quadrature asserts it, test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:208–209).

If either is absent, stop and mark the item BLOCKED; never re-run 358 or re-solve the 32×32 in-slot. - Family: IMP-3 step 8, attempt 1 of 4.

The reproduction question, answered: the rod-free mesh is not item 358's mesh. The weekly's "the rod-free drive reproduces item 358's node record at REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL" is posed as follows. - On I21a's mesh, "rod-free" means the rod's cells switched to gel. That is WF-9's without arm, which the fold needs. It is a different triangulation from item 358's 369 387-cell hole mesh: ≈ +66 k cells, the r/3 grading out to 10 mm and the cap balls. Its node S therefore differs from 358's record by a discretisation move. On this family that move is O(1e-4 – 1e-2), so it cannot be held to 1e-6. It is printed as the remesh move (_residual(s_without, s_rec)), predicted in [1e-5, 1e-2]. - The reproduction is posed on 358's own mesh, a separate build (W1a). build_tuned_quadrature(comm, with_z50=False) builds _build_f_human(comm, as_hole=True) at 369 387 cells, exactly as items 359 and 361 did. (S_rep) is _residual(s_node, s_rec) ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL, with s_rec read from the JSON before the builder rewrites it. The same comparison on the same fixture read 6.027e-13 (20261010T171705Z_WF-10-step2s-W1.log:6312) and 2.705e-13 (item 361). - It is a separate window from the rod arms. The rod arms do not need anything W1a computes; they re-read the JSON themselves. Splitting keeps each window well inside the 590 s container ceiling (a single window would be ≈ 480–650 s).

Helper edit (rule (a) / (c) style, additive, disclosed). _f_human_kwargs and _build_f_human (tests/validation/test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py:67, :101) gain a keyword implant_rod=None. - None adds no key and leaves the material map unchanged, so the call is byte-identical to today. - A rod requires as_hole=True; anything else raises ValueError before gmsh, because the solid route is not gated. With a rod: - kwargs["implant_rod"] = implant_rod; - the material map gains BIRDCAGE_IMPLANT_CELL_TAG: <the gel's HomogeneousMaterial>. This is the without arm. The tag is never left unmapped: unmapped cells are vacuum, WF-9's trap (WF-9.md:262); - the returned dict gains an additive key problem. - Re-gate. - W0 asserts _f_human_kwargs(as_hole=True) == _f_human_kwargs(as_hole=True, implant_rod=None), the same for as_hole=False, and that "implant_rod" is in neither. - W1a runs the default path through the edited _build_f_human on the H9′ consumer and asserts (A0) 369 387 and (S_rep) at 1e-6. - _build_f_human's own gate module, WF-7 step 2 (test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py, heavy -n 8), is not re-run. That is disclosed for the review to rule on: W1a exercises the edited default path at the same comparand grain. - 358's, 359's and H17's modules are not edited, and neither is any MAT-15 or WF-9 module.

New module tests/validation/test_imp3_f_human_tuned_rod.py. It is @complex_only. - Knob FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP8 ∈ {repro, rod}. Unset ⇒ the gated test skips; any other value ⇒ ValueError. - Ungated test test_imp3_s8_coding (numpy only): - the knob parser; - W0's kwargs identity; - ROD_FH == dict(ROD, keep_cells=True); - TIPS["top"] = ROD_CENTRE + (0, 0, ℓ/2 + r) bit for bit; - LOAD = −jωμ₀ computed from FREQUENCY_HZ (not WF-9's OMEGA constant), equal to test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.LOAD to 1e-15 relative.

Imports. Names only, never a test_* symbol. - 358's module (test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py): build_tuned_quadrature (:147), C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF (:58), NODE_JSON (:82), _sense_weights (:108). - H17's module (test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root.py): ESR_OHM, _z_rc, _thevenin_feed_impedance, _source_voltage, _current_route_s, _active_y_in, Y0_CODING_BAND. - test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py: QUADRATURE_SLOT_OFFSET (:52), _respec (:64). - test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py: AZ17_RECORD_DEG (:45), _lattice (:58). - test_wf7_f_human_sar10g_hotspot.py: _phantom_geometry (:95), COVERAGE_BALL_PAD_M, CONDUCTOR_CLEARANCE_M (:65–66). - test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py: FREQUENCY_HZ, DEGREE, _build_f_human. - test_wf12_f_human_copper_matrix.py: COPPER_SIGMA, BLIND_FACTOR. - test_wf12_f_human_hole.py: _census_checks, _owned_census, _rss_gib. - test_th14_birdcage_copper.py: _leontovich_term (:160), _surface_loss_w (:174). - test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py: TIPS (:140), SPHEROID_SEMI_MAJOR, SPHEROID_SEMI_MINOR, QDEG_CF, CF_CHUNK, AXIS_SAMPLES, PRED_Q_OVER_ESTIMATE (:138–159). - test_wf9_transfer_function_identity.py: BALL_RADIUS (:72, 3 mm), _free (:165). - tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py: ROD, ROD_CENTRE, _cell_values_with_ghosts (:171). - I21a's module: ROD_FH, F_HUMAN_KEPT_ROD_CELL_RECORD, F_HUMAN_KEPT_ROD_CELL_GUARD. - Bands and helpers: - DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, _sheet_field_dissipation_w, _source_power_w (test_birdcage_power_identity.py:227); - EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (test_birdcage_sar_mass_averaged.py:163); - REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py:171) and _residual (test_port_circuit_layer_field.py:142); - UNIT_WEIGHT_CONTROL_RTOL (test_port_drive_superposition.py:303) and _ring_quadrature_slots (:1208); - CELL_COUNT_BAND (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheet_prerequisite.py:57); - PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3 (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:139); - ONE_GRAM_KG, TEN_GRAM_KG, QUADRATURE_DEGREE (test_mass_averaged_sar_standard_masses.py:121–124); - PHANTOM_CELL_TAG (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py); - SIGMA_WIRE_S_PER_M (test_port_gap_voltage_impedance.py:235); - AZIMUTH_MATCH_DEG (test_port_birdcage_ring_column.py); - REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM, TERMINATED_PORT_IMPEDANCE_OHM; - averaging_ball_radius, build_density_field, mass_averaged_sar, mean_sar (src/fem_em_solver/post/sar.py); - evaluate_vector_field_parallel, pec_prolate_spheroid_field, BIRDCAGE_IMPLANT_CELL_TAG, MU_0.

Lifted, never imported (provenance comment: base commit and line span). - (L1) 358's _drive, _pair and _partition closures (test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:245–349) and its order block (:305–326), verbatim except one change: _drive takes the solver as an argument instead of ctx["solver"]. They are closures inside build_tuned_quadrature, so they cannot be imported. 358's module stays unedited (rule (a) cascade into 359 / 361 / EX-75). - (L2) _ball_mean_closed_form (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:229–272), with one added filter: only owned cells whose _cell_values_with_ghosts value is PHANTOM_CELL_TAG contribute. On F-small the hole excluded the rod by construction; here the rod's 403 cells exist and must be excluded the same way.

W1a — repro (rod-free reproduction on 358's own mesh). 1. Read 358's JSON (rank 0, bcast). Assert c_in_pf == C_IN_F_HUMAN_PF exactly and keep s_rec. 2. out = build_tuned_quadrature(comm, with_z50=False). 3. (S_rep) ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL. 4. Re-assert from out["anchors"]: (A0) 369 387 within CELL_COUNT_BAND with the census clean; (P_RC) ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL; node NEG ≥ BLIND_FACTOR × DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL; (P_w) both senses ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. The builder already asserts them; this re-states them in this module's log. 5. Printed: SAR10g(c*) under ccw on this mesh (σ = the builder's field, as 359 did) beside 359's 4.852895959e-03 W/kg (…step2s-W1.log:6372), with c* the 18-point lattice point "r=45 dz=+0 az17+0" of _lattice(az₁₇, z_c). Predicted equal to ≤ 1e-9 relative (same mesh, same drive). It is a reading, not an anchor.

W1b — rod (the two arms on I21a's mesh). 1. Read the JSON first (as W1a). 2. Build. built = _build_f_human(comm, as_hole=True, implant_rod=ROD_FH). - Check the guard (F_HUMAN_KEPT_ROD_CELL_GUARD) first. - (A0r) cells vs F_HUMAN_KEPT_ROD_CELL_RECORD within CELL_COUNT_BAND; _census_checks clean; tag 403 > 0 owned cells. 3. Problems. gel = built["problem"].material_map[PHANTOM_CELL_TAG]. - p_without = built["problem"]. - p_with = dataclasses.replace(p_without, material_map={**map, BIRDCAGE_IMPLANT_CELL_TAG: HomogeneousMaterial(sigma=SIGMA_WIRE_S_PER_M, epsilon_r=gel.epsilon_r, mu_r=gel.mu_r)}). - Δσ = SIGMA_WIRE_S_PER_M − gel.sigma, computed and never typed. - (M0) DG0 σ and εᵣ on owned 403 cells, rank-reduced min = max: 800 / gel εᵣ (with) and gel σ / εᵣ (without). Use WF-9's _material_minmax pattern (test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py:229–248). 4. Masks (DG0 from numpy midpoints over owned + ghost cells, WF-9's _build_case pattern :174–195): - χ_lead = tag-403 cells; - χ_b = tag-3 cells whose midpoint lies within BALL_RADIUS of TIPS["top"]; - V_b = ∫χ_b dx; - χ₃ = tag-3 cells. - σ₃ = a DG0 field equal to gel.sigma on tag 3 and 0 elsewhere, used for every SAR ball and the coverage (see Traps). - Asserted: χ_b and χ_lead are disjoint, and both counts are > 0. 5. The without arm first. - TimeHarmonicSolver(p_without, degree=DEGREE). - The node pair at C_in via (L1): P17 factorises, P21 is held, fields kept. - The P17 drive's partition gives (P_RC) and its NEG. - The ccw / cw superpositions via 358's :414–461 body give (P_w) on both senses; (Lin) is printed. - Then _free(solver). 6. The with arm. - The same solver and node pair on p_with, then one more held solve on ℓ = ufl.inner((χ_b / V_b)·ẑ, v)·dx (WF-9 :414), giving w on the same factorisation. - (P_RC), NEG, (P_w) and (Lin) as above. - Then _free(solver). - Only one factorisation is alive at a time. 7. (T3), per node drive d ∈ {P17, P21}. - q(e) = (1/V_b)∫χ_b e_z dx and Δq_d = q(E_with,d) − q(E_without,d). - fold_d = LOAD·Δσ·∫χ_lead w·E_without,d dx (ufl.dot, never inner), as WF-9 :456–459. - Asserted: |fold_d − Δq_d| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL·|Δq_d|. The ccw value follows by linearity and is printed. 8. (Σ_P), both arms, ccw: mean_sar(e_ccw, sigma=<solver σ field>, rho=PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3, cell_tags=…, subdomain_ids=PHANTOM_CELL_TAG)["dissipated_power_w"] against the partition's p_phantom, ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. 9. Coverage, both arms, ccw — 359's anchor (i) (test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py:258–269), with σ₃ in place of the solver σ. - The whole-phantom ball (radius hypot(R, H/2) + COVERAGE_BALL_PAD_M < F_HUMAN_RING_RADIUS − CONDUCTOR_CLEARANCE_M) has dissipated power = mean_sar(…, sigma=σ₃, subdomain 3) and mass = ρ·V(tag 3), both ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. - ρ = build_density_field(…, density_map={t: 0 for t ≠ 3}) (359's construction; it zeroes 403 too). 10. Readings (printed, never asserted): - Tip 1 g ratio. Q_tip,d = SAR1g(tip; with) / SAR1g(tip; without) for tip ∈ {top, bottom} and d ∈ {ccw, P17, P21}, with σ₃ and ρ in both arms and a₁g = averaging_ball_radius(ONE_GRAM_KG, …). Ball masses are printed and are identical in both arms. - The local background field's IMP-2 estimate, IMP-3 step 1's construction (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:379–394, :604): - η_z,d = Σ|E_z|² / Σ|E|² over AXIS_SAMPLES points on the rod axis (x = 0.015 m, z ∈ [−0.016, 0.016]) of the without arm's field, read through evaluate_vector_field_parallel with the rank-0 bcast of test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py:138–147; - M_cf(tip) from (L2) at a₁g; - est = η_z·M_cf + (1 − η_z); - Q / est is printed beside PRED_Q_OVER_ESTIMATE (0.6, 2.5). - The rod's effect on SAR10g(c*). SAR10g(c*; with) / SAR10g(c*; without) − 1 under ccw, with σ₃, with c* as in W1a. The without-arm value is printed beside 359's 4.852895959e-03 as the remesh move. - |q_with / q_without| per drive. - _residual(s_without, s_rec) (remesh move) and _residual(s_with, s_without) (the rod's effect on the coil's 2×2). - P_rod = ½∫σ|E|² over 403 in the with arm, and P_rod / P_phantom. - Cells, E, degree-1 dofs, phase times and _rss_gib.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported by name, none restated). - W1a: (S_rep); (A0); (P_RC); node NEG; (P_w) ccw / cw. - W1b: - (A0r); (M0); mask disjointness; - (P_RC) and node NEG per arm; - (P_w) ccw / cw per arm; - (T3) on P17 and P21; - (Σ_P) per arm; - coverage power and mass per arm.

Bands, read against rule (f). None was registered by measurement on this fixture. - DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (1e-6), EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (1e-10) and REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (1e-6) are round-off bands that 358 / 359 / 361 and WF-9 assert. - CELL_COUNT_BAND is the record band. - Nothing here is compared with an analytic comparand that the fixture's mesher cannot meet.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - Asserted (backed, same fixture class): - The node NEG, the P_surf-blind miss of (P_RC), at ≥ BLIND_FACTOR × the band. It read 7.0125e-3 on 358's mesh (…step2s-W1.log:6304). The rod-mesh arms are predicted ≈ 7.0e-3, since the rod barely moves the copper loss. The ceiling is P_surf/P_src ≈ 7e-3. - W1b's own NEG on the rod mesh has no prior measurement. It is asserted at the same ≥ BLIND_FACTOR × band bar, which sits ≈ 700× under the prediction. That is the bar 358 / 361 assert on a rod-free mesh. The review may relabel it printed. - (C1) Hermitian read-back: the fold with conj(w). (C2) Total-field fold: the fold with E_with in place of E_without. Both are asserted only as wired (> DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL), as WF-9 step 1 did (WF-9.md:248–251). That is the trap the σ₃ construction avoids.

Predictions (written first in the module, printed): - (S_rep) ≤ 1e-12. - (P_w), (P_RC) ≤ 1e-12. (T3) ≤ 5e-12 (WF-9 step 1: ≤ 3.7e-12). (Σ_P) ≤ 1e-14. Coverage ≤ 1e-13. - Cells = I21a's record. Tag-403 cells ≈ 15 000. Degree-1 dofs ≈ E of I21a's printout. - Q_top,ccw in [1.5, 8]: IMP-3's PEC Q on F-small's 1 g rung read 4.46–4.50 (P1 top), and WF-9's σ = 800 S/m 3 mm-ball field ratio read 2.46–2.61. - η_z,ccw in [0.2, 1.0]. - Q / est in (0.6, 2.5). - |SAR10g(c*) with / without − 1| in [1e-4, 3e-2]: c* sits ≈ 30.4 mm from the rod axis, and its 10 g ball's edge ≈ 17 mm. - The remesh move _residual(s_without, s_rec) in [1e-5, 1e-2]; _residual(s_with, s_without) ≤ 1e-3. - 1 g ball masses ≈ 0.98 g at both tips (IMP-3 I14's rod arm: 0.982 g).

Windows. Foreground. The harness call is the whole Bash command, bare. Bash timeout: 660000; -s; tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py first. - Price, measured on this route. - Item 361's W1: the builder with with_z50=False took 152.7 s (build 112.6 s, node pair 34.4 s, superposition 6.5 s); harness 162 s; summed RSS 9.59 GiB at -n 8 (20261011T003520Z_MAT-15-step5-W1.log). - Item 359's 10 g balls: mean 3.44 s, max 4.69 s (…step2s-W1.log:6384). - W1a, predicted 150–220 s. - W1b, predicted 270–450 s, ≤ 560 s on the 1.32× box. Summed RSS ≈ 10–13 GiB, with one solver alive at a time. - First: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Then run the any-orphan sweep as one bare call:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-step8-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - W0 (smoke, -n 1, numpy only): test_imp3_s8_coding green and the gated test skipped.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-step8-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp3_f_human_tuned_rod.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W1a (heavy, -n 8). §5.1's durable capture idiom is copied verbatim, trailing ; exit $rc included, as in 358 / 359 / 361:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-step8-W1a-repro "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && mkdir -p /workspace/logs/wf10 && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP8=repro PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp3_f_human_tuned_rod.py -s -v --tb=short > /workspace/logs/imp3-step8-w1a-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/imp3-step8-w1a-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/imp3-step8-w1a-raw.log; exit \$rc'" - Before W1b: pgrep -c python3 reads 0. - W1b (heavy, -n 8): the same command with label IMP-3-step8-W1b-rod, FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP8=rod and raw file /workspace/logs/imp3-step8-w1b-raw.log (all three occurrences). - No edit after W0 starts (rule (i)). Any edit re-runs W0, W1a and W1b. W1a and W1b plus one re-run of either fit the hour. No src/ file is edited. The helper edit's re-gate is W0 plus W1a, as stated above.

Traps already paid for. - Orphan .c of any size (item 160, 44 KB). Sweep only when pgrep -c python3 reads 0, and delete orphan stems only. After a kill or status 124: run pgrep -c python3 first, then the sweep, then park. Never raise the timeout or -n. - Complex build. - No ufl ordering on complex operands and no sqrt in a comparison (OPS-22; WF-6 4c). - Masks are DG0 from numpy midpoints, never UFL conditionals. - Ball centres go in as plain floats. - Call np.real before every float. - ufl.inner conjugates its second argument. q, fold, C2 and TF read with ufl.dot or components. Only ℓ's linear form uses inner against the test function, as WF-9 :414 does. - Unmapped kept cells silently become vacuum (WF-9.md:262). (M0) is the guard, and the helper maps 403 to gel. - Every sheet's bilinear term and the Leontovich wall go into both factorisations. A held solve under a different termination solves a different problem silently (PORT-19, WF-12). ℓ is held on the with-arm factorisation, which the P17 node solve made. - The kept σ = 800 S/m rod is inside every whole-phantom ball and inside the tip balls' reach. Every SAR ball and the coverage use σ₃, never the solver's σ field. The F-small IMP-3 ratio had a hole there and needed nothing. - _ball_mean_closed_form integrates every owned cell in the ball. (L2) restricts it to tag 3. The ROD_CENTRE it pins is the rod's centre only because I21a placed the rod at ROD. If the review moves the rod, (L2) must take the centre as an argument. - Rank-local values. cell_tags.values and assemble_scalar are rank-local; reduce everything. Every rank enters every collective (item 227's deadlock). Point evaluation goes through evaluate_vector_field_parallel with bcast. - Sense and plane. ccw = (1, −1j) comes from the convention code (_sense_weights, 10:30 ruling (1)). Never re-choose it, and never recombine fields with hand-typed weights. - The builder rewrites logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437.json. Read it before W1a's builder call. W1b reads it before anything. Write nothing else outside the harness logs and the raw capture files. - Memory. Free each solver (_free) before the next factorisation. Two heavy windows never run at once. - Harness hygiene. Calls are bare and whole; no -k inside the quoted command; no pipe; -s always; foreground with timeout: 660000. Never delete a log; never path-checkout a record file.

Scope. Covered: - I21a's kept-rod copper F-human hole mesh at degree 1, κ off, r = 0.2 Ω on all 32 gaps, the two-port 90° drive at C_in,F-human = 118.2437 pF, 64 MHz; - one σ = 800 S/m capped rod (r = 1 mm, ℓ = 30 mm, axis ẑ, centre (0.015, 0, 0)) in the 0.015 m cylindrical gel phantom; - WF-9's exact fold identity and H9′'s power identities on this fixture.

File a known-issues entry; never re-band. - (A0r), (M0) or a mask check red: the fixture is wrong (I21a's mesh, or the helper's material map). Stop. - (P_RC), (P_w) or a NEG red on a rod arm, green on W1a: the rod's partition accounting (P_rod in P_rest), or a termination mismatch between arms. Print the (A1) Frobenius asymmetry diagnostic of WF-9 :360–389 in a follow-up, never in-slot. File a known-issues entry. - (Σ_P) or coverage red: σ₃ / ρ construction. File a known-issues entry. - (C1) or (C2) not wired: w or the fields are swapped. Stop. - Status 124 or > 590 s: BLOCKED without a result; the killed window is the price record. - Every Q, η_z, M_cf, estimate, ΔSAR10g(c*), remesh move, P_rod and mass is a reading, never a red.

Its Done-when is "identities green with the rod in on GEO-36's 167 371-cell record mesh ⇒ 🟡; the same identities green on the 1 g rung with the tip ratio printed there ⇒ ✅ as a fixture" (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2569). Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Execute §9 item 381 — IMP-3 step 8 (§10 I21b) — per docs/planning/chunks/IMP-3.md §9 item 381. docs.text:
IMP-3 step 9: the PEC oblate disc in the coil-driven F-small phantom — the 64 MHz four-port fixture, with / without, exactly as step 1 (item 174) did for the rod (implementer; heavy, complex: W1 at -n 2, W2 at -n 4; ≈ 12 measured / 60 predicted min: ≈ 10 min of windows + 15 fixed + ≈ 35 code; depends on item 427 — skip if it did not land). Licence: §10 I25 (the 10-12 weekly, PROJECT_PLAN.md:4763–4767), §9 rule (4). A record on a ✅ row; no band, record or Done-when moves.

Skip check (before anything else). tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid.py on main with SPHEROID_HOLE_CELL_RECORD registered and _build_spheroid defined (item 427's outcome). Absent: skip item 428, leave it ⬜, take the next item (implementer-run.md step 2: never an item whose stated dependency has not landed). Item 427 BLOCKED: the same.

Fixture. Step 1's, with GEO-36 step 7's disc in place of the rod: the four-port F-small birdcage, solid σ = 800 S/m coil (SIGMA_WIRE_S_PER_M), 50 Ω lumped sheets, untuned, STEP2D_FREQUENCY_HZ = 64e6 (tests/validation/test_birdcage_power_identity.py:182), degree 1, phantom σ / εᵣ as step 1. The disc: a = 6 mm, c = 1.2 mm (aspect 5, IMP-6's gated aspect), centre (0.015, 0, 0), symmetry axis x̂, cut as a hole (PEC by its exterior wall, tag 402) — _build_spheroid(**kw) from item 427's module, the twin of step 1's _build_rod. Without the disc: tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets._build(True, **kw). Both enter build_four_port_sweep(frequency_hz=STEP2D_FREQUENCY_HZ, built=<tuple>, build_only=True) (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:219). The rim points of interest are RIM_POINTS = (0.015, 0, ±0.006): the disc lies in the yz-plane, the P1 field there is ≈ 99 % E_z (η_z = 0.990426 on the rod axis, 20261002T170843Z_IMP-3-step1-W2.log.gz:3864), i.e. in the disc's plane and normal to the rim at those points — IMP-6's in-plane rim case (1/L_x = 8.0155).

Mirror symmetry the disc keeps (as the rod): σ_y (y → −y) kept — it swaps P2 ↔ P4 and fixes P1, P3; σ_z kept — it maps the top rim point onto the bottom one; C4 and σ_x broken. The revolve seam (item 427) breaks σ_y only in where the mesher puts nodes, as any mesh does.

Code: tests only, no src/ and no imported module edited. New module tests/validation/test_imp3_disc_birdcage.py with test_imp3_disc_default_phantom (W1) and test_imp3_disc_one_gram_rung (W2). It imports by name and never a test_* symbol: - from tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py (private, rod-agnostic names only): IMP3_FLAG_OFF_Z_64MHZ (:120), PEC_WALL_MAX_E (:135), PORT_IDS, DRIVES, MIRROR_PAIRS, SIGMA_X_PAIRS, QDEG_CF, CF_CHUNK, AXIS_SAMPLES, ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 (320 000), _say, _in, _wall_dofs (:188), _wall_max_e (:199), _outer_box_tags (:205), _matrix_quantities (:275), _pair_spread (:467), _peak_rss_gib (:498). Not _arm, _case, _report, _assert_identities, _control_c1 or _ball_mean_closed_form: each hard-codes TIPS, ROD_CENTRE or the rod's 0.016 m. - from item 427's module: SPHEROID_SEMI_MAJOR, SPHEROID_SEMI_MINOR, SPHEROID_CENTRE, RIM_POINTS, SPHEROID_HOLE_CELL_RECORD, _build_spheroid, _inside_true_spheroid; - every band, record and helper step 1 imports, from the same files (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:53–109): CELL_COUNT_BAND, SOLID_CELL_RECORD, ONE_GRAM_RUNG_CELL_RECORD / PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG (tests/validation/test_birdcage_sar_1g_rung.py), REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL, RECIPROCITY_BAND, PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND, POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR, C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, _solve_driven, _exact_shares, OUTER_BOX_TAG, PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3, ONE_GRAM_KG, QUADRATURE_DEGREE, the quadrature-weight helpers, PHANTOM_RADIUS / PHANTOM_HEIGHT. - _arm_disc(built, label, disc): step 1's _arm (:295–411) copied with TIPS → RIM_POINTS, and the without-arm background sampled on the disc's in-plane diameter — AXIS_SAMPLES = 9 points at (0.015, 0, z), z ∈ [−a, a] (gel in that arm) — returning per drive η_∥ = Σ|E_z|²/Σ|E|² (world z, toward the rim points), η_t (world y, in-plane tangential there) and η_n (world x, the disc normal). On the disc arm: the wall dofs from the build tuple's facet tags, tag 402, max |E| per drive. - _disc_ball_means(msh, centre, radius): step 1's _ball_mean_closed_form (:229–272) with the local map d = p − SPHEROID_CENTRE, p_l = (d_z, d_y, d_x) (local x = world z toward the rim, local z = the normal) and three closed forms from pec_oblate_spheroid_field (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:1831, semi_major=a, semi_minor=c, e0=1, interior="continue"): M_∥ (drive "inplane" at p_l), M_t (drive "inplane" at (y_l, −x_l, z_l), the 90°-rotated in-plane drive) and M_n (drive "axial" at p_l), each ⟨|E_cf|²⟩/E₀² over the ball's quadrature points on existing (gel) cells. Also return the number of those quadrature points inside the true spheroid (printed). - The estimate, derived in the docstring: for a uniform local background E_bg, Q_cf = η_∥M_∥ + η_t M_t + η_n M_n exactly in the quasi-static limit, because every cross term ⟨e_i·e_j⟩ vanishes by the ball's two mirrors about a rim point (y → −y and the disc's mid-plane). This is step 1's η_z·M_cf + (1 − η_z) with the disc's three-way split. - Step 1's order otherwise: the without-disc arm first, freed (del, gc.collect()), then the disc arm; print everything before the first assert; the C1 control in W1.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported — step 1's set, test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:617–636, :702–707, :725–727): - (A0) Census within CELL_COUNT_BAND: W1 without = SOLID_CELL_RECORD 116 085; W1 with = SPHEROID_HOLE_CELL_RECORD (item 427); W2 without = ONE_GRAM_RUNG_CELL_RECORD 199 920. W2's disc-arm count is a first record, predicted [235 k, 300 k] (199 920 + item 427's hole increment of [35 k, 85 k]; step 1's rod arm read 250 866). Guard ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 320 000, checked before any solve. - (R0) W1 without-arm Z reproduces IMP3_FLAG_OFF_Z_64MHZ entrywise within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (step 1 measured 2.98e-10, docs/planning/chunks/IMP-3.md § item 174 outcome). - (i) ‖S − Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND, both arms. (ii) σ_max(S) ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE and every column Σ|S|² ≤ 1, both arms. (P) P_src,exact = P_vol + P_sheet,exact within DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL on every drive of both arms. - (M) σ_y mirror on the disc arm: each of the five MIRROR_PAIRS spreads ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (rod arm read ≤ 0.0819 %; predicted here [0.005 %, 0.15 %]). - (E) n × E = 0 on the disc wall: tag-402 dof count (reduced) > 0, max |E| ≤ PEC_WALL_MAX_E on every drive. - (S) Separation, without-disc arm: pooled off-diagonal spread ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR × the worst class spread — asserted because the same comparison on the same fixture measured 671× (20261001T171613Z_PORT-21-step5-W2.log:3682) and step 1's W1 / W2 read 671.1× / 402.7×. Printed on the disc arm. - Containment: 0.015 + a_1g < R and a + a_1g < H/2 (12.2 mm < 40 mm).

Negative controls (rule (e)): - (C1) The disc wall left natural (W1, P1 only, step 1's _control_c1 pattern, :639–685, re-written for RIM_POINTS): exterior facets minus 402 tagged OUTER_BOX_TAG 499 via _outer_box_tags; first assert 499 absent and exterior = outer + 402; a fresh _solve_driven. Asserted: (P) still closes at DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (a theorem) and the knob is wired — max |E| on the 402 dofs > PEC_WALL_MAX_E (step 1 read 1.29e-4 on the rod wall). Printed beside predictions written first — never asserted (the ratio's accuracy is ANS-10's / (7c)'s): - The rim 1 g ratio Q = SAR_1g,rim(disc) / SAR_1g,rim(without) at both rim points, for P1–P4, ccw, cw (W2 of record; W1's coarse value beside). - The closed form from the local background field (computed here by a stdlib Monte Carlo of IMP-6's closed form over the continuous 6.204 mm ball centred on a rim point, 200 000 gel points; the discrete mask will differ by a few %): M_∥ ≈ 1.650, M_t ≈ 0.880, M_n ≈ 1.068; gel fraction 0.923. Predicted η_∥ ≈ 0.99 for P1 (the rod-axis η_z at the same x), [0.3, 0.6] for P2 / P4; estimate ≈ 1.64 for P1 and ≈ 1.2–1.3 for P2 / P4. Predicted Q: P1 in [1.3, 2.6], P2 / P4 in [0.9, 2.0]; Q / estimate in [0.7, 1.6] (step 1's rod read 0.855–1.552, …170843Z_IMP-3-step1-W2.log.gz:3864–3875; the disc's quasi-static scale (|k|a)² = 1.04 % against the rod's 7.37 %). The 1 g ratio is a weak observable of the rim: the pointwise rim value (1/L_x)² = 64.25 is spread over a ball ≈ a in radius. - Ball masses: 1.000 g without; predicted 0.923 g with (the gel fraction). - Rim fidelity on each disc mesh: gel cells within 2ρ_r = 0.48 mm of each rim point and the number whose midpoints lie inside the true spheroid (item 427's (S8) asserts 0 on the default-resolution build; the 1 g rung is new — printed), and the count of closed-form quadrature points inside the body. A non-zero count on W2 means the estimate there is read against a truncated rim; the outcome says so and the estimate is not interpreted. - Also: P_phantom per drive, sheet facet counts, ΔS, cells, times, summed peak RSS, L_x = 0.124758 (oblate_spheroid_depolarisation, analytical.py:1756).

Windows. Bash timeout: 660000, foreground, each harness call bare and whole. Basis: step 1's W1 241 s at -n 2 and W2 260 s at -n 4 (20261002T170428Z_IMP-3-step1-W1.log.gz, …170843Z_IMP-3-step1-W2.log.gz:4162); the rod build 42 s mesh; item 427 prices the disc build (its W2a). - W0 (smoke, collect, ≈ 10 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-step9-W0-collect "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp3_disc_birdcage.py --collect-only -q'" - W1 (the default phantom, predicted [180, 360] s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-step9-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp3_disc_birdcage.py::test_imp3_disc_default_phantom -v -s --tb=short'" - W2 (the 1 g rung, the ratio of record, predicted [220, 500] s), with §5.1 durable capture and the trailing ; exit $rc: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-step9-W2 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && mkdir -p /workspace/logs && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 4 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp3_disc_birdcage.py::test_imp3_disc_one_gram_rung -v -s --tb=short > /workspace/logs/imp3-step9-w2-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo [capture] rc=\$rc >> /workspace/logs/imp3-step9-w2-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/imp3-step9-w2-raw.log; exit \$rc'" - Order: skip check → code → W0 → W1 → W2 → commit (module, logs, the record) → journal. docs.title: §9 item 464 — 2026-10-15 (§10 chain I17; chain step, no solve)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-15 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

What it is. A cap-ball radius knob on implant_rod: the key tip_ball_radius [m], absent / None = today's 2·radius (2 mm for ROD). The I17 builds then show that with the knob at 4 mm the cells the pointwise tip sample is read from sit inside the ball, and print the I30 price. No solve. - Licence: §10 I17 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4800–4804, the 2026-10-14 weekly), a weekly-enumerated step under §9 rule (4). The weekly's ruling on entry 33 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4595–4602) opens it: "I17 opens (the ball-radius knob on implant_rod, no solve); no finer cap-ball rung is bought". Known-issues 2026-10-14 "Next" (docs/testing/known-issues.md:955–961) agrees. No band, tolerance, Done-when or target is set or moved. - Executor: implementer. - Class: chain step, no solve. - Tier: heavy, not standard as the weekly wrote. The measured basis does not fit 180 s: one 1 g-rung off build takes 41 s, the 2 mm rod build 62 s and the r/8 build 87 s at -n 2 (20261007T170700Z_GEO-36-step4-W2-rungs.log:1917, 3752, 7500). Four builds with their dof counts took 330 s (…:7674). Each I17 window builds off + 2 mm + 4 mm, so ≈ 200 s of builds plus ≈ 60 s of collection and dof spaces. The review may re-tier it. - Ranks: -n 1 and -n 2, as the weekly names. - Cost: ≈ 20 measured / ≈ 50 predicted min (15 fixed + 15 code + ≈ 20 of windows). That is above the chain no-solve median (10 min) because rule (c) owes three re-gate windows (≈ 11 min). See "Problems for the review". - Depends on: nothing. Serial on nothing. Never run concurrently with another heavy window.

Settled from the code. - The hard-coded 2 mm. MeshGenerator._build_birdcage_port_model (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:5086) sets each cap Ball field's Radius to 2.0 * rod_r (:6598). Its print says "radius 2r" (:6602–6608). - implant_rod_cad["tip_ball_radius_m"] = 2.0 * float(implant_rod["radius"]) (:6120) reports it. - The ball is centred on each cap centre rod_c ± ½·rod_l·rod_a (:6593), z = ±0.015 m for ROD. It is not centred on the tip apex at z = ±0.016 m. - The normaliser _normalise_implant_rod (:4952–5083) validates every key and returns a fixed dict (:5075–5083). A new key that is not added to that return dict never reaches the sizing code. tip_size (:5011–5029, GEO-36 step 4) is the precedent to copy. - Code (src/, additive, rule (c)): - In _normalise_implant_rod: read tip_ball_radius = implant_rod.get("tip_ball_radius", None). - If it is not None, refuse it before gmsh with a ValueError matching "implant_rod" when it is a bool, not a number, not finite, ≤ radius, or > 4·radius. A ball no bigger than the cap is pointless; the upper bound is a runaway guard. Also refuse it unless both cap centres satisfy hypot(x, y) + tip_ball_radius < phantom_radius and |z| + tip_ball_radius < ½·phantom_height, following the coat check at :5064–5074. - Add "tip_ball_radius": tip_ball_radius to the return dict. - At :6598: ball_r = 2.0 * rod_r if implant_rod.get("tip_ball_radius") is None else float(implant_rod["tip_ball_radius"]), then setNumber(ball, "Radius", ball_r). - At :6120, report the same ball_r. - The print at :6602–6608 may append ball radius={ball_r:.6e} m. It is a print, not a gate; disclose it. - Nothing else in src/ changes. - Default bitwise: 2.0 * 1e-3 == 0.002 in IEEE double (scaling by 2 is exact), so the unset path and an explicit 0.002 feed gmsh the same double. - New test module tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_ball.py, real build, no solve. - Env knob FEM_EM_IMP3_I17 ∈ {run}. A module fixture builds off → 2 mm → 4 mm, coarse to fine (GEO-23). The refusals run ungated. - Imported by name, never a test_* name and never the builds fixture: - from tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py: FIXTURE_KW (:131), ROD_1G_RUNG_CELL_RECORD (:90), RUNAWAY_CELL_GUARD (:98), T1 (:84), T1_RADIUS (:100), _ball_and_t1 (:158–183), _cell_geometry (:142), _mean_edge (:150), _dofs (:186), _summarise (:199), AIR_CELL_TAG, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG; - the A1–A6 helpers and bands, exactly as that module imports them (:49–71); - ROD, ROD_RADIUS, ROD_LENGTH, ROD_CENTRE, _build_rod (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py:93–97, :125); - PHANTOM_RADIUS / PHANTOM_HEIGHT (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_tags.py:28–29); - point_owner_cells (fem_em_solver.post.evaluation). - _summarise already passes cad["tip_ball_radius_m"] to _ball_and_t1 (:221–223). N_ball is therefore counted inside each build's own ball radius. - The build calls are _build_rod(implant_rod=dict(ROD, tip_ball_radius=TIP_BALL_2MM), **FIXTURE_KW) and the same with TIP_BALL_4MM. Here TIP_BALL_2MM = 2.0 * ROD_RADIUS and TIP_BALL_4MM = 4.0 * ROD_RADIUS. tip_size stays unset, so VIn = r/4, "the r/4 grain" I30 needs. - "Near-T1 edge", defined exactly as the r/8 window printed it. The definition is _ball_and_t1 (test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:158–183): every owned cell, of any tag, whose centroid lies within T1_RADIUS = 0.5 mm of T1 = (0.015023, 0.000017, 0.017531) m (scripts/probes/imp3_step4_palace_fields.py:43), reduced over ranks. - The near-T1 edge h is the mean over those cells of each cell's mean of its six edge lengths. 20261014T070008Z_IMP-3-step7-I15-r8.log:2639 prints "near-T1 (5.0e-04 m) 26 cells, mean edge 5.081837e-04 m". - The near-T1 edge ratio is h(build A) / h(build B). …:2640 prints "local edge ratio h(r/(4√2))/h(r/8) 1.2638" = 6.422237e-04 / 5.081837e-04, from tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py:384–388. - The T1 cell is point_owner_cells(msh, T1[None, :], comm), with its mean edge allreduced (MAX, 0 elsewhere) (…:2641, code :365–369). - Why the 2 mm ball misses T1: geometry, not a measurement. |T1 − top cap centre| = √(0.023² + 0.017² + 2.531²) mm = 2.5312 mm. So every near-T1 centroid lies ≥ 2.031 mm from the cap centre, outside a 2 mm ball. With the ball at 4 mm, the farthest near-T1 centroid is ≤ 3.031 mm out, and a vertex sits within about one local edge of its centroid. The phantom_resolution = 2.5 mm (tests/validation/test_birdcage_sar_1g_rung.py:114) does not reach T1's cells.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported by name, never restated). - (R-b) refusals before gmsh: tip_ball_radius ∈ {0.0, −1e-3, nan, inf, ROD_RADIUS (the boundary), 4.0001e-3, "big", True} each raises ValueError matching "implant_rod", and gmsh.isInitialized() is False afterwards. This is the (R) pattern at test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:263–273. - (B0) default unchanged. On the 2 mm build: - tip_ball_radius_m == 2.0 * ROD_RADIUS bitwise; - cells == ROD_1G_RUNG_CELL_RECORD 252 118 as integers. The basis is the same build measured at -n 1 and -n 8 (test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:87–89) and at -n 2 (20261007T170700Z_GEO-36-step4-W2-rungs.log:3752); gmsh builds serially on rank 0. - Printed with True / False beside, not asserted: the tag census, tag-402 facets, N_ball and near-T1 against GEO-36 W2's unset line …:3752–3753 (census {1: 36258, 2: 99975, 3: 109724, …}, 402 facets 4 958, N_ball 11 938, near-T1 (11, 6.983224e-04 m)). - (A0) CAD masses, OCC wall area and wall centroid are bitwise equal between the 2 mm and 4 mm builds (the knob is sizing-only), as :295–311. - (A1–A6) per rod build, against the window's own off build, exactly as :315–364, at CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND / EXACT / TERMINAL_AREA_BAND. - (D) N1curl d2 = 2E + 2F and d1 = E, exactly, on every build (:368–378). - Guard: every build has fewer than RUNAWAY_CELL_GUARD 1 000 000 cells, checked before (D). - (Kb) the knob reached gmsh, on the 4 mm build: - tip_ball_radius_m == TIP_BALL_4MM bitwise; - cells > 252 118; - N_ball(4 mm) > N_ball(2 mm). - (T1in) the near-T1 cells sit inside the 4 mm ball, on the 4 mm build: - n_t1 > 0; - the largest distance from the top cap centre (0.015, 0, 0.015) m of any vertex of any near-T1 cell is ≤ tip_ball_radius_m; - the same holds for the T1 owner cell's four vertices. - Every rank computes this (MAX allreduce) outside any rank branch. This is the weekly's "the near-T1 edge sits inside the 4 mm ball", made strict: whole cells, not centroids.

Negative controls (rule (e) labels). - (T1out), asserted — the same predicate on the 2 mm build is false for every near-T1 cell. The count of near-T1 cells with all four vertices inside the 2 mm ball is 0, with n_t1 > 0. - The backing is a convexity identity, not a measured factor: a cell inside a ball has its centroid inside it, and every near-T1 centroid is ≥ 2.031 mm from the cap centre. - n_t1 > 0 at this build is backed by GEO-36 W2's 11 near-T1 cells at the same build (…:3753). - The review may relabel it predicted if it reads rule (e) as measurement-only. - (Kb) is the knob control. A key that never reached gmsh (dropped by the normaliser's fixed return dict) reads exactly 252 118 and fails by an integer. - Predicted, printed beside the measured values, never asserted (no prior 4 mm measurement exists): - 4 mm cells ≈ 350 k, range [320 k, 390 k]. docs.text: A rod in the coil-driven phantom: with / without on the loaded F-small birdcage at 64 MHz (Phase 7 subgoal (7b)) (opened 2026-09-30 by the weekly; §10 chain … | ✅ Audit PASS 2026-10-02 18:00 review: the rod's identities are green on the record mesh and the 1 g rung, tip Q printed (4.50 at P1), a fixture with no accuracy claim. Steps 3 and 4 (items 235 / 242) are Palace records: ours = Palace to ≤ 2.2e-10 per class on all three arms and to ≤ 1.5e-8 on near-tip E at matched order; the tip ratio's accuracy is ANS-10's, re-homed to Palace. Step 5 (item 252, 2026-10-05): at matched order 2 the codes still agree on near-tip E, and η_rod(T1) moves −4.961 % from order 1 to 2 in both — not p-stable at 1 %; steps 6 / 7 (§10 I14 / I15, 2026-10-05 weekly) carry the question on item 235's exact-rectangle fixture, now the fixture of record. Step 7 / I15 record (parts 1–3; xl entry 33, 2026-10-14): η_rod(T1) at degree 2 on the cap-ball rungs r/4 / r/(4√2) / r/8 reads 3.482328 / 3.556262 / 3.530461 (Δ₁ +0.0739, Δ₂ −0.0258, opposite signs) with I14's identities and the 1 g ball ratio green on every rung (20261014T070008Z_IMP-3-step7-I15-r8.log); entry 33's pre-registered rule read its "otherwise" branch (2026-10-14 weekly): the pointwise tip ratio is not resolved by the cap ball alone — the near-T1 edge sits outside the 2 mm ball (known-issues 2026-10-14); no bracket, no finer cap-ball rung; §10 I17 (the ball-radius knob) and I30 (the ratio with the edge inside the ball) follow. I17 (item 464, 2026-10-15): tip_ball_radius knob, default bitwise (252 118); at 4 mm the near-T1 cells lie inside the ball (130 cells, every vertex ≤ 3.151970e-03 m from the cap centre; none wholly inside 2 mm), 351 478 cells, I30 over the guard → xl (20261015T123700Z_IMP-3-I17-W2-n2.log). Done-when: the identities green with the rod in on GEO-36's 167 371-cell record mesh ⇒ 🟡; the same identities green on the 1 g rung with the tip ratio printed there ⇒ ✅ as a fixture. The ratio's accuracy is ANS-10's (commissioned by the weekly that reads this). No heating or compliance claim. History: docs/planning/chunks/IMP-3.md.

docs.title: §9 item 532 — 2026-10-18 (§10 I30a, IMP-3 step 10a — the b4 knob for xl entry 43; chain no-solve)
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-18 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

What it is. Add the selectors b4 and b4build to FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP7 in tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py, so that xl entry 43 (docs/testing/xl-pending.md, "### 43.") has a module path to run. Today KNOBS = ("r4s2", "r8", "r8build") (:84) and the test skips on anything else (:458–459), so entry 43's FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP7=b4 would read Status 0 with one skip. b4 is the full path: build, solve, readout. It is written here and run only by entry 43. b4build builds the 4 mm mesh and stops. It is this item's window of record. No solve.

  • Licence: §9 rule (6) (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3868–3877). This re-poses a blocked step of live chain I toward the weekly's pre-registered target: §10 I30 = xl entry 43 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4676–4678, :4834). Entry 43's own text licenses the guard patch: "the guard is patched to the xl value on this path only, as entry 33 did, and disclosed in the log" (xl-pending.md, entry 43 Status). Item 327's review ruling (1) (IMP-3.md:1180) is the precedent; it covered the build-only twin (r8build) in-slot. No band, tolerance, Done-when or target is set or moved. ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 (320 000) and ROD_CELL_GUARD_XL (400 000) keep their values and their definitions.
  • Supersedes item 465's code plan (IMP-3.md:1723–1730) on exactly one point. Item 465 called _arm_d unpatched, because it was written for an -n 8 slot. On the xl path the 351 478-cell mesh is over 320 000, so the unpatched (G1) would trip before the solve. Everything else in item 465's anchors and readout carries over, but item 465 itself stays unqueued.
  • Executor: implementer.
  • Class: chain no-solve, lane 1.
  • Family: I30, attempt 1 of 4.
  • Depends on: nothing in §9. Inputs on disk, all present 2026-10-18: logs/imp3/ours_imp3g_d2off.json, ours_imp3g_d2rod.json, ours_imp3h_r4s2.json, ours_imp3h_r8.json (342 072 / 2 200 500). ours_imp3h_b4.json is absent.
  • Tier per window (all measured on the same family):
  • W0 import, -n 1, knob unset, timeout -k 30 120. Measured 5 s on a warm cache (20261008T123440Z_IMP-3-item327-W0-import.log, footer) and 71 s cold (item 305, IMP-3.md:1110).
  • W1 b4build, -n 2, heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 300). The basis is the same 4 mm build at -n 2: 77.98 s (mesh 72.79 s), 20261015T123700Z_IMP-3-I17-W2-n2.log:5648. The build-only twin r8build ran 88 s harness with an 83.57 s build, body 84.3 s and 0.87 GiB summed (20261008T123452Z_IMP-3-item327-W1b-r8build.log:1961, footer :1985). Predicted ≈ 90 s, range [70, 200].
  • W2 r8build re-gate, -n 2, heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 300). It is item 327's W1b verbatim except for the label; 88 s measured (same log). Predicted ≈ 90 s, range [70, 200].
  • Compute is ≈ 3–5 min. Every window is under 10 min, so durable capture is not owed.
  • Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 20 predicted slot-minutes.
  • The measured figure is the twin, item 327: slot start 07:30 CDT to commit 6c65dee5 at 07:37 CDT, with the same shape (one build-only window plus W0).
  • The prediction adds the re-gate window, a larger body (three JSON reads and a dry-run readout) and the entry-43 edit. Class medians: chain no-solve 18.6, lane 1 ≈ 3.5.
  • If W2 has not started by minute 40, park (rule (d)).

What the module is today (git diff 6c65dee5 -- tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py is empty, checked 2026-10-18). - Dispatch, :452–464: - (N2) asserts _ratio.ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 == ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 == 320_000 before anything else (:456–457); - an unknown knob skips (:458–459); - r4s2 returns before the patch (:460–462); - monkeypatch.setattr(_ratio, "ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2", ROD_CELL_GUARD_XL) (:463) then covers every later path; - _r8(build_only=KNOB == "r8build") (:464). - The guard. _arm_d asserts ncells < ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 when rod is true, after build_four_port_sweep(build_only=True) and before the solve (test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py:165). It resolves the name at call time in _ratio's namespace; the value is imported from test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:115. - ROD_CELL_GUARD_XL = 400_000 (:117, comment :109–116). At 351 478 cells the 4 mm build sits at 0.879 of it. - _r8(build_only) (:282–449) is the shape to duplicate: - mode-"x" pre-check only when not build_only (:287–289); - JSON reads and (Rb8) before the build (:290–309); - (Kc8), (G1x) and (N1) with the DISCLOSURE print (:318–340); - mesh anchors stop the solve path (:341–346); - build_only never calls _arm_d (:348–352); - collective mesh measurements on every rank (:361–369); - _ratio._edge_face_counts for 2E + 2F at build-only (:370–374). - Item 464's helpers (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_ball.py; git diff fee90cf8 -- on it and on test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py / test_birdcage_implant_rod.py is empty, checked): - TIP_BALL_4MM = 4.0 * ROD_RADIUS (:73); - TOP_CAP (:75–77); - _t1_geometry(msh, comm) (:108–145). This is the (T1in) predicate as item 464 asserted it (:332–335): n_t1 > 0, t1_vmax <= r, owner >= 0, owner_vmax <= r. It is collective. - tip_size_m default is float(implant_rod["radius"]) / 4.0 (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:6292–6296). This equals TIP_R4 = ROD_RADIUS / 4.0 (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py:112) bitwise.

Code. Edit only tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py, and only additively. Do not edit src/, test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py, test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py, test_birdcage_implant_rod_ball.py, test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py or test_birdcage_implant_rod.py. - What git diff may delete: only the docstring knob sentence (:7–8) and the KNOBS line (:84). Everything else is insertions. _r4s2() and _r8() are untouched: duplicate, never refactor (item 327's rule, IMP-3.md:1135). - KNOBS = ("r4s2", "r8", "r8build", "b4", "b4build"). The docstring gains one paragraph naming item 532, the two paths and the patch. - Imports, insertions only: - TIP_R4 joins the test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip import block; - a new line from tests.mesh.test_birdcage_implant_rod_ball import TIP_BALL_4MM, TOP_CAP, _t1_geometry. - Never import builds or any test_* name from it. Pytest would collect it (IMP-3.md:1078). - A module-level assert TIP_BALL_4MM == 4.0 * ROD_RADIUS is allowed as an import-time identity. - Dispatch. Insert two lines between :463 and :464, so b4 / b4build run inside the existing patch and r8 / r8build are byte-for-byte unchanged: if KNOB in ("b4", "b4build"): / _b4(build_only=KNOB == "b4build"); return (two lines, return on its own line). - New record constants, each with its log-line citation in a comment; printed comparands except where asserted: - I17_B4_CELLS = 351_478 (asserted). From 20261015T123700Z_IMP-3-I17-W2-n2.log:5648, and identical at -n 1 (…I17-W1-n1.log, item 464 Outcome, IMP-3.md:1703). - I17_B4_D2_DOFS = 2_251_660, E 418 532, F 707 298 (:5648, :5661). - I17_B4_N402 = 5_366 (:5649). - I17_B4_N_BALL, I17_B4_BALL_EDGE = 111_415, 3.489008e-04 (:5649). - I17_B4_NEAR_T1 = (130, 3.383011e-04) (:5649). - I17_B4_T1_VMAX = 3.151970e-03 and the T1 cell (227_010, 3.282035e-04, 2.768817e-03) (original index, mean edge, largest vertex distance; :5650). - I17_B4_BUILD_S = 77.98 (:5648). - I17_2MM_T1_VMAX = 3.068100e-03 (:3755), for the control below. - R8_ETA_T1_P1 = "3.530461" (20261014T070008Z_IMP-3-step7-I15-r8.log:2643). The r/8 JSON sizes are asserted against the existing GEO36_R8_CELLS / GEO36_R8_D2_DOFS (:121–122), the same integers. - ENTRY33_PRICE = "build 93.47 s, sweep 278.25 s, SARs 24.57 s, body 402.2 s, 82.47 GiB summed at -n 16 (…r8.log:2663); window 511 s, memory.peak 86 486 282 240 B = 80.55 GiB (:3773, :3778)". - ENTRY43_PRICE_PRED = "500–700 s, 75–100 GiB". - ENTRY43_READOUT_INTERVAL = (3.48, 3.56). This is entry 43's pre-registered decision interval, printed IN / OUT, never asserted, never called a band. - New _b4(build_only) beside _r8, in this order: 1. If not build_only, assert ours_imp3h_b4.json does not exist (mode "x": fail before the build). 2. Read the four JSONs (off, r/4 rod, r/(4√2), r/8). Assert (Rb) "3.482328" with I14's sizes, (Rb8) "3.556262" with item 305's sizes, and (Rb-r8) "3.530461" with sizes 342 072 / 2 200 500, each string-equal at 6 d.p. and with integer sizes. These run on both paths, so W1 proves the reading wiring before the xl window. Item 465 called the r/8 check "(Rb16)"; that was a misnomer, so it is renamed here. 3. built = _build_rod(implant_rod=dict(ROD, tip_ball_radius=TIP_BALL_4MM), **FIXTURE_KW). tip_size stays unset, which gives the r/4 grain. Then cad = built[3]["implant_rod_cad"] and cells = int(msh.topology.index_map(3).size_global). 4. Mesh anchors (below), the DISCLOSURE line and the (G1x) / (N1) prints copied from _r8:329–336 with the labels changed. On the b4 path, any mesh red asserts before _arm_d, as _r8:341–346 does. 5. If not build_only: a = _arm_d(built, "degree 2 rod b4", True, 2), fails += _identities(a, True), msh = a["case"]["mesh"]. 6. Every rank, outside any rank branch: - (G3) via _outer_box_tags(msh, built[2], comm); - _ball_and_t1(msh, built[1], cad["tip_ball_radius_m"], comm); - _t1_geometry(msh, comm); - at build-only, _ratio._edge_face_counts(msh), with d2 = 2E + 2F printed beside 2 251 660; - _peak_rss_gib(). 7. Print the mesh identity against item 464's W2 constants, each with True / False. 8. On b4 only: write logs/imp3/ours_imp3h_b4.json (mode "x", rank 0, then Barrier) before the readout prints. This is a change of order from _r8, so that a readout typo after a ≈ 500 s xl solve cannot cost the data. Payload: _ser(a) plus rss_gib, ranks, tip_size_m, tip_ball_radius_m, near_t1, t1_cell, n_ball, t1_vmax, guard_patched. 9. Readout, through a new helper _b4_readout(eta_new, sar_new, mass_new, label), printed and never asserted: - η_rod at six points × four drives as r/4 / r/(4√2) / r/8 / b4; - η_rod(T1), P1, beside 3.482328 / 3.556262 / 3.530461, with the move against r/4 and ENTRY43_READOUT_INTERVAL IN / OUT; - the F1 / F2 remesh floors against r/4; - Q per tip and drive at the four meshes; - the 1 g masses; - the near-T1 edge ratio h(r/4 unset, 6.983224e-04 = GEO36_UNSET_NEAR_T1_EDGE, :102) / h(b4).

 **On `b4build`, call it once with the r/8 JSON as a stand-in**, every line prefixed `DRY-RUN (r/8 JSON stand-in — not a reading)`. That executes every readout line in-slot, so the `xl` window cannot be the first run of that code. On `b4`, call it with `a`.
  1. Price. On b4: cells, E, F, dofs, build, sweep, SARs, arm, body, summed RSS and -n, beside ENTRY33_PRICE and ENTRY43_PRICE_PRED. On b4build: build, body, RSS and -n, beside I17_B4_BUILD_S.
  2. _say(anchors failed (all) …), del, gc.collect(), assert not fails.

Anchors (asserted on both paths; on b4 they run before the solve). - (Kb4) the knob and the grain reached gmsh: - cad["tip_ball_radius_m"] == TIP_BALL_4MM bitwise; - cad["tip_size_m"] == TIP_R4 bitwise (= ROD_RADIUS / 4, the r/4 grain); - cells == I17_B4_CELLS (351 478) as integers. - The cell-count backing: item 464's -n 1 and -n 2 builds of the same call (…I17-W2-n2.log:5648; W1 identical). gmsh builds serially on rank 0. Mode independence (item 464 ran real, this runs complex) is measured twice in this family: 276 088 real (GEO-36 W2) = complex (item 305 W1, IMP-3.md:1112), and 342 072 real = complex (item 327 W1b, IMP-3.md:1183–1184). - (T1in) item 464's predicate on this mesh via _t1_geometry: n_t1 > 0, t1_vmax <= tip_ball_radius_m, owner >= 0, owner_vmax <= tip_ball_radius_m. Printed beside 130 / 3.151970e-03 / 227 010 / 2.768817e-03 (:5650, :5665). - (G1x) _ratio.ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 == ROD_CELL_GUARD_XL and cells < it (0.879 predicted). - (G3) tag-402 facets > 0, all exterior. Printed beside 5 366. - (Rb), (Rb8), (Rb-r8) as in step 2 above. - On b4 only (entry 43's window, not run here): (G1) inside _arm_d at the patched value; (G2), (i), (ii), (PP), (M), (E), (V), (D) via _identities(a, True) at the bands I14's helpers import. None of these is restated.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (N1), asserted: cells > the unpatched ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 320 000, so the unpatched (G1) would trip. Ratio 1.098. Backed by item 464's measurement of the same build: "cells 351478 vs ROD_CELL_GUARD_W2 320000 (over)" (…I17-W2-n2.log:5650). - (Kb4-blind), asserted through (Kb4): a selector that dropped the key (dict(ROD)) builds the 2 mm mesh at 252 118 cells with tip_ball_radius_m 0.002 (…I17-W2-n2.log:3753–3754). It fails the integer equality by 99 360 cells and the bitwise radius. Measured on the same fixture. - (T1in-blind), asserted through (T1in): on that 2 mm mesh the largest near-T1 vertex distance is 3.068100e-03 m > 2 mm (:3755), so the predicate fails against its own radius. Same fixture, same predicate. - (N2), asserted (existing, :456–457): the unpatched guard reads 320 000 before every dispatch, so r4s2 and the unset path never run inside the patch. - (N3), predicted: unset knob ⇒ skip (W0). - Predicted, printed only: - W1 summed RSS ≤ 1.5 GiB at -n 2 (r8build 0.87 GiB); - W1 near-T1 / N_ball / T1-cell / 402 values equal to item 464 W2's (True on every line); - the dry-run's η(T1) reads 3.530461, the stand-in's own value.

Windows (bare, whole, foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; container timeout -k 30; -s; complex build; FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1; only tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py first, as item 327; no -k; no pipes). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. - Pre-check (read-only): - docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0; - ls logs/imp3/ shows the four input JSONs and no ours_imp3h_b4.json; - git diff 0f6bbbc7 -- tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ratio_1g.py tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py is empty; - git diff fee90cf8 -- tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_ball.py tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod_tip.py tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py is empty; - git diff 6c65dee5 -- tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py is empty before the edit. - On any mismatch, stop and report. - No cache sweep is owed: no window compiles a form (W0 imports, W1 / W2 never call _arm_d), as item 464 ruled. - W0 (import, -n 1, knob unset; (N2) runs, then the test skips): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-I30a-W0-import "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W1 (b4build, -n 2, the window of record; predicted ≈ 90 s, range [70, 200]): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-I30a-W1-b4build "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP7=b4build timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py -v -s --tb=short'" - Before W2: pgrep -c python3 reads 0. - W2 (r8build re-gate, -n 2; item 327 W1b's command with only the label changed; must reproduce (Kc8) 342 072, (G1x) 0.855, (N1) 1.069, (G3) 8 790, (Rb8) "3.556262" and the GEO-36 mesh identity, as at …item327-W1b-r8build.log:1952–1960; predicted ≈ 90 s, range [70, 200]): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-3-I30a-W2-r8build-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_IMP3_STEP7=r8build timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp3_tip_ladder_1g.py -v -s --tb=short'" - Not re-gated, and why: - r4s2 and r8 solve and write mode-"x" JSONs that already exist, so both would fail on their own files by design. - Their bodies are diff-unchanged, and the dispatch lines they reach (:460–464) are byte-unchanged. W0 proves the module imports and the unset path skips. - Order: pre-check → code → W0 → W1 → pgrep → W2 → commit. No module edit after W0 starts (rule (i)); any edit means W0–W2 again. - Never run b4 in-slot. Item 464's scaled -n 8 window is 552.6–564.7 s (…I17-W2-n2.log:5671–5672), over the 545 s cap, and the window is entry 43's.

Traps already paid for. - Item 305's list carries in full (IMP-3.md:1061–1082): degree defaults to 1 in two places; leg_sheet_strip_fraction always; quadrature 4 at degree 2; no complex ordering or sqrt comparison; owner="lowest_original_cell"; rank-local values reduced and no collective inside a rank == 0 branch; tags in built[1] / built[2]; evaluate before freeing; Status 124 means pgrep first; mode "x" means no second window; a denied $rc capture means stop and report. - Item 327's list (IMP-3.md:1162–1168): monkeypatch must target the module object _arm_d lives in (_ratio). Patching the new module's imported name, or test_imp3_rod_birdcage's, has no effect on :165. The existing :463 line already does it right, so do not add a second setattr. - The patch covers only the b4 / b4build / r8 / r8build paths. Never move the dispatch above :463, never patch on r4s2 or on the unset path, and keep (N2) first. Item 465's "unpatched, do not monkeypatch" instruction is superseded on this path by entry 43's licence. It is not a trap to obey. Copying it would make entry 43 red at (G1) before the solve. - _t1_geometry, _ball_and_t1, point_owner_cells and _outer_box_tags are collective. Call them on every rank. - b4build never calls _arm_d. A build-only path that solves is an unpriced heavy window. - The 4 mm build has not been built since src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py moved. git diff fee90cf8 -- src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py is +183/−10 from GEO-38 items 478 / 470 (090178c2, c1b8debc, 2026-10-15; phantom_box-gated by design). A (Kb4) cell mismatch is therefore a finding about the shared builder, not a constant to re-record in-slot (see Negative result). - tip_size is never set. The r/4 grain is the default, and (Kb4) asserts it. - b4build never appears in entry 43's command. The implementer does not edit that command. - Never -k; -s on every window; never lengthen a timeout or raise -n; never delete a log; never write ours_imp3g_*, ours_imp3h_r4s2.json or ours_imp3h_r8.json; no slot opens docs/private/ or aed_results/.

Scope. Covered: the selectors, the disclosed patch path, the 4 mm / r/4-grain build identity in the complex build at -n 2, the near-T1-inside-the-ball predicate on that mesh, the three stored-reading paths (Rb / Rb8 / Rb-r8), a dry run of every readout line, and the r8build path re-gated. Not covered: - any solve, η / Q reading or identity at b4 (all of that is entry 43's); - convergence or an observed order; accuracy (ANS-10); - entry 43's command, tier, date or price; - other radii; F-human; - src/; any band; the two guard values.

Negative result. Report and stop. Park on attempt/IMP-3-I30a-<ts>, mark item 532 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)), and leave entry 43 PENDING PREREQUISITE. - W0 red: a module defect. Fix it before W1 and re-run W0. - (Kb4) cells ≠ 351 478, with the radius and grain bitwise: the 4 mm build moved since fee90cf8. Report both counts and the census. - Open a GEO-36 / GEO-38 known-issues entry naming 090178c2 / c1b8debc, and stop. - Re-recording is the review's (via record-reconciler), never in-slot. Entry 43 cannot run against an unverified mesh. - W2 still runs: it tells whether r/8 moved too. - (Kb4) radius or grain red: the key or the default did not reach gmsh. Fix in-slot only if it is the new module's call; otherwise park. - (T1in) red with (Kb4) green: a finding (the 4 mm ball no longer contains the near-T1 cells). Report the vertex distances; the weekly re-poses I30. - (G1x) / (N1) / (G3) red: report every number and park. - *(Rb) red: the reading path or a stored JSON is wrong. Print no dry-run reading and park. - W2 red: the edit is not additive on the r8build path. Revert nothing on main; the review rules. - Status 124: not a result. docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-25 03:00 daily review from the 10-24 weekly's enumerated step I39 (§9 rules (4) / (5)). Two execution readings below go to the 10-26 weekly; neither changes the target.

Question. What does the rod's own SAR do to the F-small gel phantom's temperature, compared with the same coil drive without the rod? This is the first implant-driven heating on a coil-driven phantom.

Execution readings (this review's): 1. "The two-port drive" on this mesh. IMP-3's F-small module drives four single ports P1–P4 and their ccw / cw superpositions (tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:145–146). No two-port drive exists on F-small; that drive belongs to the F-human tuned rod (step 8). The source here is the ccw superposition, the coil's circular drive and the one whose 1 g tip ratio IMP-3 records. 2. Ranks. The weekly wrote -n 8. The measured with-rod case is 171 s at -n 2: build 47.4 s, arm 53.2 s, 2.61 GiB summed peak RSS (20261002T170428Z_IMP-3-step1-W1.log.gz:3646, :3719, :3764). The thermal CN on a ≈ 60 k-cell submesh is 2.4–2.8 s per solve at -n 2 (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log.gz:1929–1944). The smallest width that fits is -n 2, which is also the width that exposes a missing reduction.

Route. One new module, tests/validation/test_imp3_rod_heating_phantom.py, gated by FEM_EM_IMP3_I39=1. It runs IMP-3's with-rod and without-rod arms on the 167 371-cell record mesh (ROD_CELL_RECORD_W1, test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:113) at 64 MHz through _case / _arm, with run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(…, keep_fields=True). Fields are not saved to disk, so the SAR is taken through the module's field_hook(label, rod, msh, cell_tags, e_of, sigma_field, rho_field) (:405–406) before the fields are freed. - The ccw source is q = SAR · ρ on the phantom (tag 3) as a DG0 / DG1 Function interpolated onto the P1 thermal submesh. - Then MAT-15 step 1's scheme (tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py): _cn θ = ½, N = 40, two BE half-steps (:154–157); _be_one at DT_1 (:89, :160); t_R, t* as :86–87. - Import these by name, never copy them: _cn, _be_one, the energy helper, E_BAND, S2_BAND, C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, B_BAND. If a helper is bound to MAT-15's own 10 MHz sweep (_run_heated is), call the pieces below it and say which.

Anchors (imported bands, both arms). - (E′) Stored + surface = G · P_k at E_BAND (1e-9; MAT-15 module :164–171, :378–379). - (S2) The calorimetric first-step slope against q at S2_BAND (1e-4; :384–385). - Both on the with-rod and on the without-rod source.

Control (printed, predicted to miss). (C4) The C4 covariance at C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (5e-2; test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:120). The rod breaks the coil's C4 symmetry, so the with-rod θ field should miss. It is printed with its miss, never asserted. The without-rod arm's (C4) is asserted (MAT-15 asserted it on the uniform phantom, :390–392), so the comparison is backed.

Printed (the record, no band): the tip-region 1 g ball-mean θ(t*) over the without-rod value at the same ball, beside IMP-3's 1 g SAR ratio Q on the same mesh; the whole-phantom ΔT_max ratio; P_phantom per arm.

Windows. 1. W0: knob unset, coding tests and the knob refusal. 2. W1 IMP-3-I39-W1: both arms, -n 2, complex build, heavy, timeout -k 30 1200.

Predicted ≈ 2 × 171 s + ≈ 2 × 120 s of thermal (40 CN + the BE step + the energy forms) ≈ 550–700 s, ≤ 6 GiB summed. Run the pgrep -c python3 pre-check (must read 0) first.

Tier: heavy, -n 2. Class: lane-3 closed form (the class median applies). Cost: ≈ 7.5 measured / 50 predicted slot-minutes. Executor: implementer. Depends on: nothing. Family: IMP-3 step 11, attempt 1 of 4. Daytime: no.

Traps already paid for. - The rod wall must be adiabatic. _robin_tags puts Robin on every exterior facet of the submesh (test_mat10_…:92–98), so the rod's hole wall (facet tag 402) would become a Robin sink. Apply Robin only on the phantom's outer surface (IMP-7's trap 2, IMP-7.md:382–395), and say which tags. - MAT-9's float(np.sqrt…) is not complex-safe (MAT-15.md:19). Take np.real before any float. - ufl.max_value and complex comparisons do not compile. - cell_tags.values and assemble_scalar are rank-local. - A killed compile leaves an orphan .c. Sweep only with pgrep -c python3 reading 0 (MAT-15.md:44, :73). - Never background the window.

A negative result means: - (E′) or (S2) red on the without-rod arm: the port from MAT-15's 10 MHz route is wrong. Report it and park; nothing is read. - Red on the with-rod arm only: the rod wall's boundary is the suspect. Record it in IMP-3.md and on an attempt/* branch. - A without-rod (C4) red: the source transfer is wrong.

Two findings for the review: - The with-rod (C4) control did not miss. Its pairs read 2.96 / 3.66 / 2.61 / 3.79 %, all inside the 5 % band (:3669–3672), against a prediction of a miss. It was printed, never asserted, and it carried a "predicted" label. It is reported here as a wrong prediction, not a red. The consequence: at this band and at 10 g, (C4) does not separate the rod from mesh asymmetry (the worst without-rod pair is 2.07 %). docs.title: §9 item 639 — 2026-10-25 (§10 chain I, I41 — daily, 2026-10-25, provisional; chain step (solve))
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-25 10:30 daily review under §9 rule (6), toward chain I's subgoal (7b) — the rod in the coil-driven phantom — and I39's validation target, unchanged: MAT-15's identities at their imported bands on both arms, the tip 1 g θ ratio printed. Question. I39's 1 g tip θ ratio (1.111 / 1.088) compares a 537-cell phantom (the solid record mesh, phantom_resolution=None) with a 51 693-cell one (the rod mesh, refined around the rod). What is the ratio when both arms share one mesh?

The matched mesh exists. The rod mesh of I39 is a hole build (no rod cells; tag 402 an exterior PEC facet group, src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:268–272), so there is nothing to map to gel on it. Its kept-cells twin _build_kept_rod() (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py:154–168, KEPT_ROD_CELL_RECORD 182 371 at :102–108) is "the hole build's 167 371 + 15 000 implant cells, the rest of the census identical cell for cell"; on it tag 402 is an interior interface (mesh.py:274–280) and the rod's cells carry tag 403 (BIRDCAGE_IMPLANT_CELL_TAG). With tag 403 mapped to the gel, the rod is gone and the mesh is the with-rod arm's, cell for cell outside the rod. WF-9 step 1 already solved exactly this rod-as-gel problem on F-small (tests/validation/test_wf9_lead_in_coil_phantom.py:151–172: p_without = replace(problem, material_map={**mmap, BIRDCAGE_IMPLANT_CELL_TAG: gel})); item 381 did the same on F-human (tests/validation/test_imp3_f_human_tuned_rod.py:110–146).

Window. W0: --collect-only plus the knob test, -n 2, smoke. W1 IMP-3-I41-W1: -n 2, complex, heavy, container timeout -k 30 590 (the 660 s foreground cap), bare harness call, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000, after pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Predicted ≈ 45 s kept-rod build + 60 s arm-M EM + 44 s rod build + 61 s arm-R EM + 2 × ≈ 8 s thermal ≈ 230–300 s.

Tier: heavy, -n 2, complex. Class: chain step (solve). Cost: ≈ 7.0 measured / 45 predicted slot-minutes. Executor: implementer. Depends on: nothing. Family: I41, attempt 1 of 4. Daytime: no. Never beside another heavy window.

Traps already paid for.
