docs.title: IMP-4 — history
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record. Opened by the 2026-10-03 03:00 daily review under §9 rule (5), lane 3, inside Phase 7 subgoal (7a) (canonical conductors in a lossy host against closed forms); the weekly ratifies or reverts the opening.

Citation, corrected. The 2026-10-02 18:00 review named this candidate "the IMP-1-style finite cylinder (Jin §11.3)" and the eqs (11.56)–(11.63). In the repo's copy those equations sit in §11.2.1, Two-Dimensional Scattering (docs/references/jin-fem-3e/11_fem-eigenfunction-expansion-methods.md:355–419); §11.3 (:575) is the unimoment method. - What §11.2.1 contributes: eq (11.56), the outgoing expansion in H⁽²⁾ₙ(kρ)e^{jnφ} (stated in prose at :383), and Exercise 11.4 (:461): plane-wave scattering by a circular conducting cylinder, for both polarisations, compared with Harrington. - The Bessel identities are Jin App. E: Bessel's equation (E.1) and the Wronskian (E.19) (appE_special-functions.md:15, 69–71). - The equation bodies in the repo's markdown are image placeholders ([eq (11.56)]), so only their numbers can be cited. The series itself is Harrington's (Time-Harmonic Electromagnetic Fields, §5-8), which the repo does not hold. That is the same footing as Carslaw & Jaeger for MAT-9…MAT-18: the docstring derives every form. - "Finite-k" means a finite wavenumber, not the quasi-static limit. The cylinder is infinite and the problem is 2D-invariant. There is no closed form for a finite-length rod; that is IMP-2's spheroid and IMP-3's rod.

docs.title: §9 item 202 — 2026-10-03 (lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 03:00 daily review; the review reviewed it.

IMP-4 step 0: the PEC circular cylinder in IMP-1's lossy host at finite k, in closed form. It is numpy only, verified by residuals and by the current identity before any FEM. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2, real build. Class: lane-3 closed form (measured median 8 min). - Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 code + one ≈ 1-min window + spare). - Depends on: nothing. Shared file: item 199 also appends to utils/analytical.py. This item is append-only after item 199's MAT-18 block; rebase if 199 lands first.

Not already covered. IMP-1 (the sphere, quasi-static, then the exact l = 1 field) and IMP-2 (the spheroid, quasi-static) have no 2D canonical conductor and no lead-current quantity. A 2D PEC wire under an axial field has no quasi-static limit: the n = 0 coefficient carries ln(ka). Finite k is intrinsic here, not a correction.

Fixture. - Host: IMP-1's — σ 0.57 S/m (SIGMA_HIGH), εᵣ 78, 64 MHz, k = K_FIXTURE (test_imp1_step3_exact_comparand.py:51–53). Principal root ≈ 15.18 − 9.49j 1/m, |k| = 17.90 1/m (IMP-2's W0 print, docs/planning/chunks/IMP-2.md). - Cylinder: radius a = 1 mm (GEO-36's rod radius). Outer radius for step 1, c = 10 mm, so |k|c = 0.179, MAT-4's gated reach and IMP-1's box half-width. - Convention e^{+jωt}, with H⁽²⁾ as outgoing (Im k < 0, so it decays outward).

Closed forms (single-mode drives; the docstring derives each): - TM_z, n = 0 (axial E): E_z = E₀[J₀(kρ) − J₀(ka)H₀⁽²⁾(kρ)/H₀⁽²⁾(ka)], with H_φ = ∂_ρE_z/(jωμ₀) from Faraday. - TE_z, n = 1 (transverse E): H_z = H₀[J₁(kρ) − J₁′(ka)H₁⁽²⁾(kρ)/H₁⁽²⁾′(ka)] cos φ, with H₀ = −2jωε_cE₀/k so that the incident field on the axis is E₀ŷ. E = ∇ × (H_zẑ)/(jωε_c). The PEC condition is E_φ(a) = 0 ⇔ ∂_ρH_z(a) = 0.

Code (additive in utils/analytical.py; scipy imported inside the functions): - pec_cylinder_tm0_field(points, *, k, radius, e0=1.0, interior="zero") and pec_cylinder_te1_field(points, *, k, radius, omega, e0=1.0, interior="zero"). - Both take points of shape (N, 3) and return complex (N, 3) Cartesian E. - interior="zero" returns 0 for ρ < a, as IMP-1's trace does for the chord points. "continue" evaluates the formula there, as pec_prolate_spheroid_field does (analytical.py:1576). - pec_cylinder_tm0_current(*, k, radius, omega, e0=1.0), which returns 4E₀/(ωμ₀H₀⁽²⁾(ka)). - The test, tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py. - scipy.special.jv, hankel2, jvp and h2vp all accept complex arguments; check that in the test rather than assume it.

Anchors (asserted). - (B1) Bessel's equation (Jin (E.1)) for both radial functions, with f′ and f″ from scipy's recurrence derivatives (jvp/h2vp, n = 1, 2), at 64 radii in [a, c]. The residual is bounded by ≤ 1e-12 of the sum of the term magnitudes |f″| + |f′/ρ| + |(k² − n²/ρ²)f|, the scale before cancellation (item 190's lesson). - (B2) Wronskian (Jin (E.19), written for H⁽²⁾): J_nH_n⁽²⁾′ − J_n′H_n⁽²⁾ = −2j/(πz) at z ∈ {ka, kc} for n ∈ {0, 1, 2}, ≤ 1e-13 relative. - (P) PEC traces on the Cartesian output at 64 points on ρ = a: the tangential components φ̂·E and ẑ·E are ≤ 1e-14·E₀ for both drives. This catches a bad Cartesian conversion, not just the radial algebra. - (I) Wire current: 2πa·H_φ(a), from the field's analytic ρ-derivative, equals pec_cylinder_tm0_current = 4E₀/(ωμ₀H₀⁽²⁾(ka)) to ≤ 1e-12 relative. This is the Wronskian applied to the axial-drive current. Predicted |I| ≈ 2.9e-3 A per V/m, from the small-argument H₀⁽²⁾(ka) ≈ 0.64 + 2.64j. - (Q) TE static limit: at k → s·k with s = 1e-6 (arg k kept), on 200 points with a ≤ ρ ≤ c, the field equals the 2D PEC-cylinder static field E_ρ = E₀(1 + a²/ρ²) sin φ, E_φ = E₀(1 − a²/ρ²) cos φ (potential −E₀(ρ − a²/ρ) sin φ) to ≤ 1e-9·E₀. Predicted ≲ 1e-11: the correction goes as (s|k|c)² ln. - (L) Layout: a dolfinx-style adapter on x of shape (3, N) returns the (N, 3) function's output transposed, bitwise. Step 1 passes it as dirichlet_e_field; this is IMP-1 step 3(b)'s (L) lesson.

Printed (predicted, never asserted). - k, |k|a, |k|c. - The TM n = 0 scattering coefficient J₀(ka)/H₀⁽²⁾(ka) (predicted |·| ≈ 0.37). - |E_z|/E₀ at ρ = 1.2a, 1.5a, 2a: the axial field the wire suppresses. - The TE surface field |E_ρ(a, π/2)|/E₀, predicted ≈ 2.00, the static doubling; so the side-of-wire SAR is ≈ 4× the far-field SAR. - |I| and arg I.

Negative controls. Rule (e): all are predicted, since nothing has been measured on this fixture. Each is asserted only as missing its anchor's band, with the measured value printed beside the prediction. - (c1) H⁽¹⁾ in place of H⁽²⁾ in the TM field, the wrong outgoing convention for e^{+jωt}, against (I). The current becomes −4E₀/(ωμ₀H₀⁽¹⁾(ka)), so the miss is predicted ≈ 0.7 from the small-argument forms. Asserted > 1e-3. (B1) and (P) still pass, which is why (I) is the discriminating anchor. - (c2) The Dirichlet condition in TE (H_z(a) = 0 instead of ∂_ρH_z(a) = 0), against (P). The tangential E_φ(a) is predicted O(E₀). Asserted > 1e-3·E₀. - (c3) σ dropped (real k = k₀√εᵣ) in the current, against (I) evaluated at K_FIXTURE. Predicted miss ≈ 0.15. Asserted > 1e-3.

Window. Foreground, Bash timeout: 660000. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Predicted 45–60 s: IMP-1 step 3(a) took 45 s (20261001T142052Z_IMP-1-step3a-W1.log:263) and IMP-2 step 0 W1b 45 s (20261001T142617Z_IMP-2-step0-W1b.log:308), both numpy windows in the real build.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-4-step0-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/unit/test_analytical_lightweight.py tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py -s -v --tb=short'"

The lightweight test is the rule (c) re-gate of the additive analytical.py change.

Traps. - Convention: e^{+jωt} throughout, H⁽²⁾ outgoing. K_FIXTURE is the principal root (Re > 0, Im < 0, :53); never np.sqrt of a negated ε_c. - Derivatives: use analytic or recurrence derivatives. An FD check on these functions would need δ ≳ 1e-2·a and the Richardson or ratio form (IMP-2's (F) ruling); none is pre-registered here. - The ρ = 0 axis is outside [a, c]. The TE Cartesian conversion still divides by ρ, so guard ρ = 0 and never sample it. - Normalise (B1) by the parts before cancellation, never by |f|: J₁ and H₁ are small or large at small kρ. - Run hygiene: print on rank 0; the real build skips the four complex-only environment tests, as expected; -s; rule (i) — no edit after the last window. - Rule (f) applies to a parameter (s, the radii), never to a bound. - Shared file: append at the end of analytical.py, and rebase if item 199 lands first.

Scope. Numpy only, two single-mode drives on an infinite cylinder. Not included: - the FEM (step 1); - the plane-wave multi-mode series; - a finite rod or its tip (IMP-2, IMP-3); - a coil, heating, or any published-data comparison.

Status it can move. The proposed §7 IMP-4 row moves ⬜ → 🟡 on its step-0 Done-when, which this item matches (rule (j)). The review adds the row in the commit that queues this item, and names it in the dashboard for the weekly to ratify (rule (5) lane 3). Step 1 then becomes draftable.

Negative result. - (B1), (B2), (P) or (L) red: a code bug. Fix it in-slot, run W1b, and disclose. - (I) red with (B2) green: a sign or convention error in H_φ. Print both sides and their ratio, then stop. - (Q) red: print the miss at s ∈ {1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6}. If it scales as s² ln s, s is a parameter: re-register it under rule (f), disclosed; otherwise stop. - On a stop: park on attempt/IMP-4-step0-<UTC> and mark BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); the row stays ⬜. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Outcome — DONE 2026-10-03 (12:00 CDT slot, second item, implementer). W1 20261003T172120Z_IMP-4-step0-W1.log passed first time: -n 2, real build, 55 s, 25 passed, 4 skipped (complex-only environment tests). No W1b.

Anchors: - (B1) residual over term sum 1.8e-16 – 2.6e-16 (J₀, H₀, J₁, H₁, both radial functions). - (B2) 4.467e-16. (P) TM φ̂ 0 / ẑ 2.235e-16; TE φ̂ 1.142e-16 / ẑ 0 (·E₀). - (I) 2.601e-16; I = 6.92952e-4 − 2.83487e-3j A per V/m. - (Q) 9.302e-15·E₀ at s = 1e-6 (predicted ≲ 1e-11). (L) bitwise, both drives.

Controls: (c1) 0.6749 (predicted ≈ 0.7; the H⁽¹⁾ field still passes B1 2.3e-16 and P 2.3e-16); (c2) 1.999·E₀ (predicted O(1)); (c3) 0.1443 (predicted ≈ 0.15).

Printed: k = 15.178 − 9.48858j 1/m, |k|a 0.0179, |k|c 0.179; J₀(ka)/H₀⁽²⁾(ka) magnitude 0.3687 (H₀⁽²⁾(ka) = 0.644055 + 2.63483j); |E_z|/E₀ 0.0428 / 0.0952 / 0.1627 at 1.2a / 1.5a / 2a; TE surface |E_ρ(a, π/2)|/E₀ 2.00022; |I| 2.91833e-3, arg −1.33106 rad.

Disclosed: - Private control keywords (_hankel_kind, _condition on the public functions; hankel_kind / condition on the radial helpers); defaults are the brief's forms. - (P) evaluates with interior="continue", because hypot can return ρ a hair below a, and "zero" would then pass vacuously. A guard asserts that the normal TE component on that ring is > E₀. - The TE field is independent of omega (μ = μ₀ host; −H₀/(jωε_c) = 2E₀/k); the ρ = 0 axis is guarded. - An extra test_scipy_accepts_complex_arguments checks jv against the power series for J₀ and J₁ to 1e-14. That bound is the executor's choice and was not pre-registered. - Fixture constants are imported from test_imp1_step3_exact_comparand.py.

Row ⬜ → 🟡; step 1 (item 206) is unblocked.

What step 1 would be (not briefed; for the row). - Mesh: TH-15's hole route, degree 2. An additive as_hole=True on MeshGenerator.cylindrical_domain (io/mesh.py:833, today a fragment): the inner cylinder is cut, the cavity wall gets facet tag 2 from the meshed boundary (TH-15's lesson, :2335–2340), the outer lateral wall tag 1, the end annuli a new tag 3, with graded cavity sizing as in IMP-2. False stays bit-identical, re-gated by tests/mesh/test_cylindrical_domain.py and tests/solver/test_cylinder.py. - Boundary conditions: TimeHarmonicProblem(boundary_condition="pec_zero_tangential_a", dirichlet_e_field=…, pec_facet_tags=…), IMP-1's _solve pattern (test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py:198–257). - TM constrains tags {1, 2, 3}: the exact z-invariant field has zero tangential E on the end planes, so PEC there is exact. - TE constrains {1, 2} and leaves the ends natural, which is PMC (core/time_harmonic.py:345–354). That is exact because n × curl E = 0 there. - Gates at each drive: - the complex LSQ amplitude of the closed-form scattered field on probe circles at ρ = 1.2a, 1.5a, 2a in the mid-plane: |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND; - the annulus-mean |E|² (a < ρ < 1.5a) against the closed form on the same discrete mask: ≤ MAT4_BAND; - the cavity dofs are zero; - control: the natural cavity misses. - Price: IMP-1 at degree 2 ran 54 524 cells in 101.8 s (20261001T033100Z_IMP-1-land-W1.log:446), so ≈ 20–40k cells per solve here and a heavy window.

docs.title: §9 item 206 — 2026-10-03 (lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 daily review; the review reviews it.

IMP-4 step 1: the FEM half. The PEC cylinder is cut from a coaxial host annulus, the outer wall carries step 0's exact finite-k trace, and the end planes carry the condition that makes the 3D solve z-invariant for each drive. - Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy, -n 2; complex build for W1–W2, real build for W0. Class: lane-3 closed form (measured median 8 min). - Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 65 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 25 code + W0 ≈ 4 + W1 ≈ 6 + W2 ≈ 5 + ≈ 10 spare). - Depends on item 202 (step 0's closed form); if it did not land, skip. The check is grep -n 'def pec_cylinder_tm0_field' src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py non-empty, plus 202's W1 green in test-results.md. This item does not edit utils/analytical.py: it imports 202's three functions, and the incident-mode split is test-local. Should an edit become necessary, the file is append-only after items 199 / 201 / 202's blocks; rebase if any lands first.

Why this fixture is exact, not approximate. The z-invariant reduction is Jin §1.4.2 (eqs (1.44), (1.45), 01_basic-electromagnetic-theory.md:265–277) and §11.2.1 eq (11.53) (11_fem-eigenfunction-expansion-methods.md:361): ϕ = E_z for E_z-polarisation, ϕ = H_z for H_z-polarisation. A finite slab of the infinite problem reproduces the infinite solution exactly when every boundary condition is one that the exact z-invariant field already satisfies. With the solve well posed (lossy host), the FEM's continuous solution is then the closed form, and only discretisation and faceting remain. - TM_z, n = 0 (E = E_zẑ, H = H_φφ̂). On a plane z = const, n̂ = ±ẑ: - n̂ × E = 0 identically, so the PEC end condition (Jin §1.5.2 eq (1.52), 01:315–321; the Dirichlet "electric wall" n̂ × E = 0, 08_vector-finite-elements.md:1533) is exact. - n̂ × H = ∓H_φ ẑ × φ̂ ≠ 0, so the natural end (the Neumann "magnetic wall" n̂ × (∇ × E) = 0, 08:1533; core/time_harmonic.py:345–348 "NATURAL … is PMC") is wrong: it forces H_φ = 0 on the ends and breaks z-invariance. - The ends are therefore tag 3 constrained: pec tags (1, 2, 3). - TE_z, n = 1 (H = H_zẑ, E transverse). On the end planes: - n̂ × E = (E_x, E_y) rotated ≠ 0, so a PEC end is wrong. - n̂ × H = H_z ẑ × ẑ = 0, so the natural (PMC) end is exact. - The ends are tag 3 left out: pec tags (1, 2). - This is the step-0 brief's assignment (:92–93), and the §7 row's ("end planes PEC (TM) or natural/PMC (TE)"). The opposite pairing (PMC ends for E_z, PEC for TE) is the trap, not the fixture. - Truncation. The outer wall ρ = c carries the exact total field's tangential trace from step 0, so it is exact at finite k. Jin's own §11.2.1 route, the global third-kind condition (11.61)/(11.63) from the outgoing expansion (11.56), is not implemented or tested here. Imposing the exact trace is the IMP-1 step 3(b) idiom, and it removes truncation from the error budget. - The sizing rule does not bind. The rule "(|k|c)² under a third of the band" (IMP-2.md:9) bounded a quasi-static comparand. Here comparand and trace are exact at finite k. c = 10 mm keeps |k|c = 0.179, IMP-1's and MAT-4's reach, for continuity only.

Fixture. - Host: step 0's, which is IMP-1's. Import FREQUENCY_HZ, SIGMA_HIGH, EPSILON_R_HOST, E0, DEGREE = 2, OUTER_BOUNDARY_TAG = 1, CAVITY_TAG = 2, TH15_BETA_BAND, MAT4_BAND, _assemble_real and _cavity_dofs from test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py. Import K_FIXTURE from test_imp1_step3_exact_comparand.py:53. Import _owned_masked_cells and _numpy_quadrature_mean from test_imp2_spheroid_fem.py:172–201. Never re-derive these. - Geometry: a = 1 mm, c = 10 mm, length L = 4 mm, centred on z = 0. - Permittivity: ε_c = K_FIXTURE²/(ω²μ₀) wherever the TE normalisation needs it. That keeps the incident split consistent with the k step 0 used; never rebuild ε_c from σ and εᵣ separately.

Code. - Mesher (additive; rule (c), disclosed). Add keyword-only *, as_hole=False, resolution_wall=None, resolution_far=None to MeshGenerator.cylindrical_domain (io/mesh.py:833). as_hole=False takes the existing branch untouched; passing either resolution without as_hole raises, so nothing is silently ignored. Under as_hole=True, modelled on sphere_in_box_domain's branch (:2403–2436): - occ.cut the inner cylinder from the outer; exactly one volume remains (raise otherwise). Volume tag 2. - Facet groups come from getBoundary of the meshed air volume (TH-15's rule, :2338–2341), classified z first. Faces with z-extent < tol at |z| = L/2 are tag 3. Then bbox r_max within tol of c is tag 1. The rest is the cavity, tag 2. Raise if any group is empty, and print the face count per group. - Use tol = _WALL_TOL_FRACTION·(c − a) = 9e-5 m, ≥ 10× OCC's 1e-7 bbox padding (IMP-2's W0 failure 20261001T200341Z). - Sizing: Distance from the cavity faces → Threshold (SizeMin resolution_wall = a/6 at DistMin 0, SizeMax resolution_far = c/6 at DistMax c − a), set as the background mesh. This is h(ρ) = ρ/6 exactly, the radial grading the ln and 1/ρ² fields want. Turn off MeshSizeExtendFromBoundary, MeshSizeFromPoints and MeshSizeFromCurvature as sphere_in_box_domain does. generate(3) only, with no Netgen optimise on this branch. Print the minimum SICN. - Module tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py: - Trace: lambda x: np.ascontiguousarray(f(x.T).T).astype(PETSc.ScalarType) around pec_cylinder_tm0_field / pec_cylinder_te1_field with interior="zero". This is IMP-2's _dirichlet_axial pattern and step 0's (L). - Incident split (test-local, numpy): - TM: E_inc = E₀J₀(kρ)ẑ. - TE: H_inc = H₀J₁(kρ) cos φ with H₀ = −2jωε_cE₀/k, and E_inc = ∇ × (H_incẑ)/(jωε_c) in Cartesian form via jv / jvp. - The scattered basis is E_s = E_cf − E_inc. - Probes: 24 points on each of ρ = 1.2a, 1.5a and 2a at z = 0, angles (i + ½)·2π/24, evaluated with evaluate_vector_field_parallel on e_real and e_imag; raise unless every point is valid. β is the complex LSQ over all components, β = Σ conj(E_s)·(E_h − E_inc) / Σ |E_s|². Do not use IMP-1's Re-only fit: arg k = −32°, and the 18:00 pathologist found the Re-only fit absorbs h² error (IMP-1.md:33). - Annulus mask: a DG0 indicator of cell midpoints with x² + y² < (1.5a)², numpy only. Φ_h = ⟨|E_h|²⟩/E₀² by UFL at quadrature_degree 8. Φ_cf,h comes from _numpy_quadrature_mean over the same owned cells, using the closed form with interior="continue": quadrature points in the chord sliver have ρ < a, and the "zero" mask would read them as zero (IMP-1's trap, item 146). - Solve: a module-local _solve_cylinder(drive, pec_tags) following test_imp2_spheroid_fem.py:213–295, using boundary_condition="pec_zero_tangential_a", dirichlet_e_field, pec_facet_tags=pec_tags. It returns β, Φ_h, Φ_cf,h, the cavity dof count and max |E|, cells, seconds and summed RSS. - Tests: test_census_and_numpy (W0, not complex_only: mesh, numpy and real UFL only), test_both_drives (W1, complex_only), test_natural_cavity_controls (W2, complex_only).

Anchors (asserted). - W0 (census, before any solve): - (Guard) global cells ≤ 60 000. Predicted 20–45 k: h = ρ/6 gives 6·216·2πL(1/a − 1/c) ≈ 29 k, calibrated on IMP-1 a/6's ≈ 6.1 tets per h³ (13 467 cells, 20261001T033100Z_IMP-1-land-W1.log:370). - (Tag) reduced ds(t) areas (pinned quadrature_degree 2): tag 1 against 2πcL, tag 2 against 2πaL, tag 3 against 2π(c² − a²), each within 2 %. The faceting deficit is predicted ≤ 0.5 % ((Δφ)²/6 at Δφ = 1/6). A mis-tag is O(1): annuli tagged 1 would read +250 %. - (M′) on the annulus mask, the numpy quadrature of the 2D static PEC-cylinder TE field E = (2E₀a²xy/ρ⁴, E₀ + E₀a²(y² − x²)/ρ⁴, 0) equals the same field's UFL cell integral at degree 8 to ≤ 1e-12 relative. The field is a polynomial ratio, so it needs no sqrt and no comparison. The continuous value 1 + ⟨a⁴/ρ⁴⟩ = 1.4444 is printed beside it. - (S) the incident split: TM (E_cf,z − E₀J₀(kρ))/H₀⁽²⁾(kρ) is constant and equals −E₀J₀(ka)/H₀⁽²⁾(ka); TE E_cf − E_inc equals E_inc's formula with J₁ → H₁⁽²⁾ (and J₁′ → H₁⁽²⁾′) times −J₁′(ka)/H₁⁽²⁾′(ka). Each holds to ≤ 1e-12 relative on 64 points in [1.2a, 2a]. - W1, per drive (TM pec tags (1, 2, 3); TE pec tags (1, 2)). These are the §7 row's step-1 Done-when, verbatim in substance: - (i) |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND (4.886 %); - (ii) |Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1| ≤ MAT4_BAND (10 %); - (iii) cavity dofs located > 0 (reduced), with max |E| < 1e-12 (reduced with MPI.MAX).

Printed (predicted, never asserted; rule (e)). - TM, faceting-led. Faceting puts the effective wall at a(1 − (Δφ)²/12) ≈ a(1 − 0.23 %). - Φ_cf,h is ≈ 3.6e-3: |E_z|/E₀ ≈ 0.235 ln(ρ/a) by the small-argument forms, and ⟨ln²⟩ = 0.0661 over the annulus. Note that this is small, so it is the fragile gate. - The miss is predicted positive, +1 to +3 %: 2·0.23 %·⟨ln⟩/⟨ln²⟩ ≈ 1.7 %, plus discretisation. - |β − 1| is predicted ≤ 1.5 %; faceting alone gives ≈ 0.235·0.23 % ≈ 0.05 %. - TE. - β is predicted ≈ 0.995, since the 2D dipole goes as a_eff². |β − 1| ≤ 1.5 %. - Φ_cf,h ≈ 1.444, with a miss of ≲ 1 %. - For each drive: Φ_cf,h beside the continuous annulus value (a numpy radial / angular quadrature of step 0's field), which isolates faceting; cells, degree-2 dofs, seconds and summed RSS; h_wall/a; min SICN. - z-invariance: max|E_h(z = ±L/4) − E_h(0)| / max|E_h(0)| on the 1.5a circle, predicted ≲ 1e-3. A large value means an end condition is wrong. - TM current: β·pec_cylinder_tm0_current (|I| ≈ 2.9e-3 A per V/m from step 0), the induced current the fitted amplitude implies.

Negative controls (rule (e): nothing has been measured on this fixture, so each is predicted and asserted only as missing the band). - (c1) TM, natural cavity (pec tags (1, 3)), which makes the wire PMC: H_φ(a) = 0. - Prediction. The scattered coefficient J₁(ka)/H₁⁽²⁾(ka) is O((ka)²) ≈ 1e-3. The annulus therefore carries the regular mode pinned to the trace, E_z ≈ C₁J₀(kρ) with C₁ = E_cf(c)/J₀(kc) ≈ 0.525 + 0.128j (|C₁| 0.54). The LSQ β is then ≈ 0.53 − 0.13j, so |β − 1| ≈ 0.49 (range [0.3, 0.7]), and Φ_h ≈ |C₁|² ≈ 0.29 against Φ_cf,h ≈ 3.6e-3 gives a miss ≈ +7 900 % (range [+3 000, +15 000] %). - Ceilings. On β, 0.49/0.04886 ≈ 10× the band. On Φ there is no saturation, because the comparand is small. - Asserted: |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND and |Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1| > MAT4_BAND. - (c2) TE, natural cavity (pec tags (1,)), which makes H_z(a) = 0, the void cylinder. - Prediction. In the static annulus, ψ = A(ρ + a²/ρ) sin φ with ∂_ρψ(a) = 0 and ψ(c) on the PEC trace gives A = −E₀(1 − (a/c)²)/(1 + (a/c)²). Hence β ≈ −0.980, and |β − 1| ≈ 1.98, with a ceiling of 1.98/0.04886 ≈ 40×. The uniform residual (A + E₀) is orthogonal to the dipole on full circles, so it does not leak into β. - Calibration of the method. The same annulus argument for IMP-1's 3D control, A = −(1 − (a/b)³)/(1 + (a/b)³/2), gives −0.41 against the measured −0.433 / −0.439 (IMP-1.md:94; 20261001T033747Z_IMP-1-land-W2.log:152), on a box rather than a sphere. - Asserted: |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND only. - Φ cannot discriminate in TE. A 2D line dipole of either sign carries the same annulus-mean |E|², A²(1 + ⟨q²⟩) against 1 + ⟨q²⟩. The predicted miss is 1 − A² ≈ 3.9 %, inside the band. It is printed beside its prediction, and not asserted either way. For the review: the row's "natural-cavity control misses" is met on β for TE, and on β and Φ for TM.

Windows (foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; each harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative; -s; no -k; no pipes). PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace because the module imports tests.validation.*, as IMP-1 / IMP-2's windows do. - W0 (real build). Predicted 2–5 min; the two re-gate modules are unmeasured as a pair, the rest is IMP-2 W0's 109 s (20261001T201413Z_IMP-2-step1-W0.log). This window is the rule (c) re-gate of as_hole=False (bit-identical branch), step 0's module re-run as the dependency check, and the census: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-4-step1-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 400 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/mesh/test_cylindrical_domain.py tests/solver/test_cylinder.py tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py::test_census_and_numpy -v -s --tb=short'" - W1 (complex). Predicted 250–400 s: two solves at 20–45 k cells, against IMP-2's 105.8 s / 83.3 s per solve at 37 359 / 44 304 cells and 6.46 GiB summed (20261001T201608Z_IMP-2-step1-W1.log:381,449), where that W1 took 307 s. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-4-step1-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py::test_both_drives -v -s --tb=short'" - W2 (complex). Predicted 250–350 s: two solves, against IMP-2 W2's 179 s for one at 76.8 s (20261001T202123Z_IMP-2-step1-W2.log:151). scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-4-step1-W2 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py::test_natural_cavity_controls -v -s --tb=short'"

Traps (all paid for). - End conditions are polarisation-specific (above). Swapping them is an O(1) wrong field that the probes would read as a β miss, not a small error. - Mesh classification. cylindrical_domain's existing bbox-r_max classification would put the end annuli (r_max = c) into tag 1, so classify z first. The cavity group comes from the meshed boundary, never the cut tool (TH-15). - Masks and fields. Use the "zero" interior for the trace and "continue" for Φ_cf,h. Guard N = 0 on a rank inside every callable. Never sample ρ = 0 (the TE conversion divides by ρ). - Complex build: no UFL comparison and no ufl.max_value. Real operands do not save a comparison containing sqrt (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). Every mask is numpy. - Quadrature: every SpatialCoordinate-bearing form carries metadata={"quadrature_degree": …} (POST-5 step 1); the ds area forms are pinned too. - Rank safety. - assemble_scalar, cell_tags.values and local max/min are rank-local; reduce before asserting. - Do the RSS allreduce outside any rank-0 branch: IMP-2's W0 failure 20261001T200855Z. - Owned cells only (size_local). Read the geometry.dofmap shape at runtime. - JIT cache. If an earlier window today was killed, sweep orphan .c stems first, and only when pgrep -c python3 in the container reads 0, with the rubric's one bare harness call (<ID> = IMP-4-step1). Never clear the cache wholesale. - Run hygiene. Foreground; container timeout -k 30; never pipe or filter inside the harness command. Print on rank 0. Rule (i): no edit to a file after its last window. - Rule (f) reaches a parameter (a resolution, L), never a bound.

Scope. One mesh, degree 2, two single-mode drives on an infinite PEC cylinder with an exact trace. These are accuracy-level bands, not a convergence claim. Not included: - Jin's (11.63) global boundary condition; - the plane-wave multi-mode series of Exercise 11.4 proper; - modes n ≥ 2; - a finite rod or tip (IMP-2, IMP-3); - a coil, heating, 1 g SAR, or published data.

Status it can move. The IMP-4 §7 row, whose Done-when reads: "Step 1 (FEM, degree 2, TH-15 hole route): additive as_hole=True on cylindrical_domain; exact trace on the outer wall; end planes PEC (TM) or natural/PMC (TE); per drive |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND, annulus ⟨|E|²⟩ on the same mask ≤ MAT4_BAND, cavity dofs zero, natural-cavity control misses ⇒ ✅". - With step 0 green (🟡), this item green moves 🟡 → ✅, auditable. The opening itself is the weekly's to ratify (rule (5) lane 3), as IMP-1's was. - The review may then add IMP-4 to §2's closed-form-lane sentence: imposed trace, no coil. - Flag for the review (rule (j)): the control clause is read as β for TE, because Φ cannot miss there (see (c2)).

Negative result. - Over the cell guard in W0: stop before any solve, report the counts, BLOCKED. - (Tag), (S) or (M′) red: a mesher or helper bug. Fix it in-slot, run W0b, and disclose. - A re-gate red on as_hole=False: the branch is not bit-identical. Fix it; if it was red at HEAD already, cite known-issues and continue. - (i) or (ii) red with (iii), (M′) and (Tag) green: print h_wall/a, Φ_cf,h against the continuous value and the z-invariance number. Park on attempt/IMP-4-step1-<UTC> and mark BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); no band moves. If TM (ii) is the red, positive, and near the faceting prediction, the review may re-pose the wall resolution (a/10) under rule (f). - A control inside its band: the cavity condition is not reaching the probes, which points at a tag or solver bug. Stop and report. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Outcome (2026-10-03 15:00 slot): DONE, row 🟡 → ✅. Executor implementer, foreground; W0 / W1 / W2 green on first run, rule (i) holds (both files predate W0). - Windows: 20261003T200309Z_IMP-4-step1-W0.log (real, 22 passed / 4 skipped, 96 s; re-gates test_cylindrical_domain.py, test_cylinder.py and step 0 green); 20261003T200454Z_IMP-4-step1-W1.log (complex, 13 passed, 123 s); 20261003T200703Z_IMP-4-step1-W2.log (complex, 13 passed, 117 s). - W0: 25 568 cells (guard 60 000), faces 1 / 1 / 2, min SICN 0.2988, h_wall/a 0.396. (Tag) −0.088 % / −0.088 % / −0.455 % (band 2 %). (M′) 2.0e-15 (numpy 1.443486, continuous 1.4444). (S) TM 3.0e-16, TE 6.0e-16. - W1: TM β 0.999655 − 0.000093j (|β − 1| 0.036 %), Φ_h 3.742e-3 vs Φ_cf,h 3.705e-3 (+1.01 %; Φ_cf,h vs continuous +1.77 %, the predicted faceting offset); TE β 0.992258 (0.774 %), Φ −0.23 %. Cavity 10 704 dofs, max|E| 3.7e-20 / 2.1e-34. 174 112 dofs, ≈ 37 / 29 s per solve, 4.28 GiB summed. TM current β·I |I| 2.917e-3 vs 2.918e-3 A per V/m. - W2 controls: c1 β 0.527 − 0.126j (|β − 1| 0.489, predicted 0.49), Φ +7 790 % (predicted ≈ +7 900 %); c2 β −0.972 (|β − 1| 1.97, predicted 1.98), Φ −4.0 % (printed, predicted ≈ 3.9 %). - Off prediction (printed only): z-invariance 7.3e-3 (TM) / 1.3e-2 (TE) against ≲ 1e-3. Every gate is tight, so this is not read as a wrong end condition; the executor attributes it to unstructured discretisation differing between z-planes — untested. - Disclosed src/ change (rule (c)): cylindrical_domain gains keyword-only as_hole / resolution_wall / resolution_far; the as_hole=False body moved verbatim into _cylindrical_fragment_domain; the new branch is the module-level _cylindrical_hole_domain.

docs.title: IMP-5 — history
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

Opened by the 2026-10-03 18:00 daily review under §9 rule (5), lane 3, on a closed-form licence: the anchor is the exact Bessel/Hankel series of a dielectric-coated PEC circular cylinder. This is Phase 7 subgoal (7a), canonical conductors in a lossy host against closed forms, and the natural successor of IMP-4 (✅ 2026-10-03, the bare PEC cylinder on the hole route). The weekly ratifies or reverts the opening.

What it adds over IMP-4. The insulated lead shaft. A lossless dielectric sleeve a < ρ < b around the PEC conductor puts the project's first conforming dielectric interface (n̂ × E, n̂ × H and n̂·D continuous) under a closed form at finite k, in the lossy host. In the TE drive the contrast across that interface is |ε_c,host/ε_c,coat| ≈ 59.

Done-when. - Step 0 (numpy closed form, §9 item 210) green ⇒ ⬜ → 🟡. - Step 1 (FEM on the TH-15 hole route with a coating subdomain, §9 item 211) green ⇒ 🟡 → ✅.

Citation. - Jin 3e does not print the coated-cylinder series. It uses it without stating it. §10.2.3, Fig. 10.11 (10_fem-boundary-integral-methods.md:625–631) compares an FE–BI solution for a coated circular conducting cylinder with "the exact eigenfunction expansion solution". §11.1, Fig. 11.4 (11_fem-eigenfunction-expansion-methods.md:127–133) is a dielectric-coated conducting post in a waveguide. - What Jin does supply, cited for each piece the docstring derives: - §1.4.2 eqs (1.44)/(1.45) (01_basic-electromagnetic-theory.md:269–277): the z-invariant scalar reductions with piecewise εᵣ, μᵣ. They give the scalar interface conditions: TM, E_z and μᵣ⁻¹∂_ρE_z continuous; TE, H_z and ε_c⁻¹∂_ρH_z continuous. - §1.5.1 eqs (1.46)–(1.49) (01:285–299): the four field-continuity conditions, of which only two are independent. - §1.5.2 eq (1.52) (01:319–321): PEC, n̂ × E = 0. - §11.2.1 eq (11.53) with (u_r, v_r) per polarisation, and eq (11.56), the outgoing H⁽²⁾ₙ expansion (11:355–383). - App. E: Bessel's equation (E.1) and the Wronskian (E.19) (appE_special-functions.md:15, 69–71). - The series itself is the standard layered-cylinder eigenfunction solution. Cite Harrington, Time-Harmonic Electromagnetic Fields (1961), ch. 5 (§5-8, scattering by cylinders; the coated case is an extension of that section's method), and Balanis, Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics, ch. 11 (scattering by circular cylinders). Neither book is held in the repo, and neither section was re-verified against its text. That is the same footing as IMP-4 (Harrington §5-8) and MAT-9…MAT-18 (Carslaw & Jaeger): the docstring derives every coefficient from the Jin equations above. - The quasi-static anchor (Q) is derived independently, by 2D potential theory for a coated PEC cylinder in a uniform field. It shares no Bessel algebra with the series.

Fixture. - Host: IMP-4's, which is IMP-1's: σ 0.57 S/m, εᵣ 78, 64 MHz, k_host = K_FIXTURE = 15.178 − 9.4886j 1/m. - Conductor and coating: a = 1 mm, b = 1.5 mm, c = 10 mm. - A real lead conductor (≈ 0.3–0.6 mm radius, ≈ 0.1–0.3 mm insulation) is too fine for IMP-4's mesh. So a keeps IMP-4's radius, and b/a = 1.5 puts ≈ 2–3 degree-2 cells across the sleeve under IMP-4's h(ρ) = ρ/6 sizing (measured h_wall/a 0.396). - The thin-insulation limit is carried only by the analytic b → a anchor. - Coating: εᵣ 3, σ 0 (lossless), μ = μ₀. This is order-of-magnitude silicone or polyurethane, not a measured material. - k_coat = K0·√3 ≈ 2.3217 1/m (real), with K0 the same free-space wavenumber K_FIXTURE is built from. - The ratio ε_c,coat/ε_c,host = k_coat²/k_host² ≈ 7.39e-3 + 1.515e-2j (|·| ≈ 0.0169).

docs.title: §9 item 210 — 2026-10-03 (lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

IMP-5 step 0: the dielectric-coated PEC circular cylinder in IMP-4's lossy host at finite k, in closed form. It is numpy only, verified by residuals, interface identities, two exact limits onto IMP-4 and an independent quasi-static form, before any FEM. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2, real build. Class: lane-3 closed form (measured median ≈ 12 min). - Cost: ≈ 12 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 25 code + one ≈ 1-min window + spare). - Depends on: nothing. Shared file: utils/analytical.py is append-only after IMP-4's block (analytical.py:2230–2376). Rebase if another item appends first.

Closed forms (single-mode drives, e^{+jωt}, H⁽²⁾ outgoing; the docstring derives each). Regions: coating a ≤ ρ < b (k₁ = k_coat), host ρ ≥ b (k₂ = k_host). - TM_z, n = 0 (axial E). - Coating: E_z = E₀·c·g(ρ), with g = J₀(k₁ρ)Y₀(k₁a) − Y₀(k₁ρ)J₀(k₁a), so g(a) = 0. - Host: E_z = E₀[J₀(k₂ρ) + s H₀⁽²⁾(k₂ρ)]. - At ρ = b, E_z and ∂_ρE_z are continuous (μ equal, so H_φ = ∂_ρE_z/(jωμ₀) is continuous). That is a 2 × 2 solve for (c, s). - Wire current I = 2πaH_φ(a) = −4E₀c/(jωμ₀), because g′(a) = −2/(πa) by the J/Y Wronskian (E.19). - TE_z, n = 1 (transverse E). - Coating: H_z = H₀·c·h(ρ) cos φ, with h = J₁(k₁ρ)Y₁′(k₁a) − Y₁(k₁ρ)J₁′(k₁a), so h′(a) = 0 ⇔ E_φ(a) = 0. - Host: H_z = H₀[J₁(k₂ρ) + t H₁⁽²⁾(k₂ρ)] cos φ, with IMP-4's H₀ = −2jωε_c,host E₀/k₂ (incident E₀ŷ on the axis). - At ρ = b, H_z a ε_c⁻¹∂_ρH_z are continuous, with ε_c,coat/ε_c,ht = k₁²/k₂². That is a 2 × 2 solve for (c, t). - E = ∇ × (H_zẑ)/(jωε_c) uses the region's own ε_c, so in the coating E carries the factor k₂²/k₁². ω cancels out of E, as in IMP-4. - Quasi-static TE (k → 0, ratio r = k₁²/k₂² kept), derived independently. Let q = a²/b² and Δ = (1 − q) + r(1 + q). - Host: E_ρ = (E₀ + B/ρ²) sin φ and E_φ = (E₀ − B/ρ²) cos φ, with B = E₀b²[r(1 + q) − (1 − q)]/Δ. - Coating: E_ρ = −C(1 + a²/ρ²) sin φ and E_φ = −C(1 − a²/ρ²) cos φ, with C = −2E₀/Δ. - At r = 1 this is IMP-4's static field (B = E₀a²).

Code (additive in utils/analytical.py, appended after pec_cylinder_tm0_current; scipy imported inside the functions): - coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_field(points, *, k_host, k_coat, radius, coat_radius, e0=1.0, interior="zero", region=None) and coated_pec_cylinder_te1_field(…, omega, …). - Points have shape (N, 3); the output is complex (N, 3) Cartesian E. - region=None selects by ρ: below a it applies interior ("zero" / "continue"), as IMP-4 does; a ≤ ρ < b is the coating, ρ ≥ b the host. - region="coat" / "host" forces that region's formula at every point. Step 1 needs this for per-cell-tag quadrature, and (IF) needs it to evaluate both sides at exactly ρ = b. - Validate 0 < radius ≤ coat_radius. coat_radius == radius is legal: the solve stays non-singular because g′(a) and h(a) are non-zero by the Wronskian. - coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_current(*, k_host, k_coat, radius, coat_radius, omega, e0=1.0) returns −4E₀c/(jωμ₀). - Private helpers _coated_cylinder_coefficients(drive, …, condition="exact") (the 2 × 2 solve) and _coated_cylinder_radial(rho, drive, region, …) (f, f′, f″ from jv/yv/jvp/yvp/hankel2/h2vp). - A private _condition="swapped" on both public functions applies the other polarisation's flux condition; it exists for the controls only. This is IMP-4's private-keyword pattern (_hankel_kind, _condition). - The test: tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_closed_form.py. - Fixture constants are imported from test_imp1_step3_exact_comparand.py (K_FIXTURE, K0) and test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py (FREQUENCY_HZ, E0, TH15_BETA_BAND). - IMP-4's three public functions are imported as the limit comparands.

Anchors (asserted). - (Z) scipy takes complex arguments for Y. yv, yvp at n = 0 and 1 agree with the ascending series (docstring-derived) at z = k_host·a to ≤ 1e-13 relative. The (Lε) limit evaluates Y at a complex argument, so this is checked rather than assumed (IMP-4's test_scipy_accepts_complex_arguments, extended to Y). - (B1) Bessel's equation (Jin (E.1)) in each region with that region's k, for both radial functions of both drives, at 64 radii in [a, b] (k₁) and 64 in [b, c] (k₂). The bound is ≤ 1e-12 of the term sum |f″| + |f′/ρ| + |(k² − n²/ρ²)f|. IMP-4 measured 1.8e-16 – 2.6e-16. - (B2) Wronskian (Jin (E.19)). - J_nY_n′ − J_n′Y_n = 2/(πz) at z ∈ {k₁a, k₁b}. - J_nH_n⁽²⁾′ − J_n′H_n⁽²⁾ = −2j/(πz) at z ∈ {k₂b, k₂c}. - Both for n ∈ {0, 1, 2}, ≤ 1e-13 relative. - (P) PEC trace at ρ = a (region="coat", 64 points). On the Cartesian output, φ̂·E and ẑ·E are ≤ 1e-14·E₀ for both drives. region="coat" replaces IMP-4's interior="continue" fix for hypot landing a hair below a. - (IF) Interface at ρ = b, 64 points, region="coat" against region="host". Each residual is ≤ 1e-12 of the sum of the two sides' magnitudes (the scale before cancellation): - tangential E (TM ẑ·E; TE φ̂·E, ẑ·E) — Jin (1.46); - tangential H (TM H_φ from the radial f′; TE H_z from f) — Jin (1.47); - TE normal D, k₁²·E_ρ,coat = k₂²·E_ρ,host — Jin (1.48), dependent but checked on the Cartesian output, where it catches a wrong ε factor in the conversion. - (I) Wire current. 2πa·H_φ(a), from the analytic coating-region derivative, equals coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_current to ≤ 1e-12 relative. - (Lε) Coating → host. With k_coat = k_host (complex), on 200 points with a ≤ ρ ≤ c and region=None, both coated fields equal pec_cylinder_tm0_field / pec_cylinder_te1_field, and the current equals pec_cylinder_tm0_current, to ≤ 1e-12 relative to max|E| (or |I|). Predicted ≈ 3e-16: the coefficient misses were computed at 3.4e-16 (TM) and 2.9e-16 (TE) by an independent pure-Python series. - (Lb) Thickness → 0. With coat_radius = radius exactly, the same three equalities hold to ≤ 1e-12. - (Q) TE quasi-static limit. With k_host → s·k_host and k_coat → s·k_coat at s = 1e-6 (r kept), on 200 points with a ≤ ρ ≤ c spanning both regions, the field equals the quasi-static form above to ≤ 1e-9·E₀ (IMP-4's (Q) band). Predicted ≲ 1e-11. - (L) Layout. A dolfinx-style adapter on x of shape (3, N) returns the (N, 3) output transposed, bitwise, for both drives (IMP-4 (L)).

Printed (predicted, never asserted; rule (e)). All predictions come from an independent pure-Python series computed while drafting. That series reproduces IMP-4's measured H₀⁽²⁾(ka) = 0.644055 + 2.63483j. - k_host, k_coat, |k_coat|b ≈ 3.48e-3, r = k₁²/k₂² ≈ 7.39e-3 + 1.515e-2j. - TM: the coating is invisible at leading order. |s/s₀ − 1| ≈ 3.1e-6 and |I/I_IMP-4 − 1| ≈ 4.3e-5, with I ≈ 6.9305e-4 − 2.8348e-3j A per V/m. - Why: in the quasi-static sleeve E_z = C ln(ρ/a), and the matching reproduces IMP-4's H₀⁽²⁾(ka) denominator exactly. With μ equal, ε enters only through k²ρ² terms. - TE: the coating reverses the dipole. t/t₀ ≈ −2.158 + 0.166j, against the quasi-static B/(E₀a²) = −2.159 + 0.170j. - In the sleeve C/E₀ ≈ −3.53 + 0.14j. - At ρ = b: |E_ρ(b⁻)|/|E_ρ(b⁺)| ≈ 59.4, |E_ρ(b⁺)| ≈ 0.086·E₀ and |E_φ(b)| ≈ 1.960·E₀. The tissue next to the insulation sees the normal field suppressed and the tangential field doubled, a void-like response. That is the reverse of the bare wire's normal doubling (IMP-4: 2.00). - Continuous annulus means ⟨|E|²⟩/E₀² (step 1's comparands): - TE: coating (a, b) 17.99; host (b, 1.5b) 1.411, against the bare wire's 1.088 on the same host annulus, i.e. near-lead SAR +30 % in TE. - TM: coating 3.640e-3 (= IMP-4's TM annulus); host 2.296e-2.

Negative controls (rule (e): predicted, not measured on this fixture; each is asserted only as missing its anchor's band, with the measured value printed beside the prediction). - (c1) TE: the uncoated IMP-4 comparand against the coated β. - Measurement. The complex LSQ amplitude, on step 1's probe circles (ρ = 1.2b, 1.5b, 2b; 24 points each; z = 0), of the coated scattered field fitted to pec_cylinder_te1_field − E_inc. The mode shapes are identical in the host, so β = t₀/t. - Prediction: β ≈ −0.461 − 0.035j, so |β − 1| ≈ 1.461. The ceiling is 1.461/0.04886 ≈ 30× the band. - Asserted: |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND. - TM has no "uncoated misses" control. The same fit gives |β − 1| ≈ 3.1e-6, far inside the band. It is printed as a record, and it is the reason (c2) exists. - (c2) TM, swapped flux condition (_condition="swapped": ε-weighted ∂_ρE_z continuity, TE's condition, applied to E_z). - Tested against (IF)'s H_φ residual. The derivative ratio becomes r, so the predicted residual is |r − 1|/(|r| + 1) ≈ 0.98. Asserted > 1e-3. - Its β separation from the correct coated TM is printed: predicted |s/s − 1| ≈ 0.104. -c3) , swapped flux condition* unweighted ∂_ρH_z continuity: the ε jump is dropped). - Tested against (IF)'s φ̂·E residual. The predicted residual is ≈ 0.98. Asserted > 1e-3. - Its β separation is printed: predicted ≈ 1.461, the same as (c1) to 1e-4, because at |k|b ≪ 1 dropping the ε weight is omitting the coating. - (B1) and (P) still pass under (c2) and (c3). That is why (IF) is the discriminating anchor.

Window. Foreground, Bash timeout: 660000. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. - Predicted 55–75 s: IMP-4 step 0 W1 took 55 s with the same environment and lightweight modules (20261003T172120Z_IMP-4-step0-W1.log); this module adds ≈ 10–20 s of numpy. - IMP-4's closed-form module and test_analytical_lightweight.py are the rule (c) re-gate of the additive analytical.py change. - PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace because the module imports tests.validation.*.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-5-step0-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/unit/test_analytical_lightweight.py tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_closed_form.py -s -v --tb=short'"

Traps (paid for). - Convention. e^{+jωt}, H⁽²⁾ outgoing in the host. K_FIXTURE is the principal root (Re > 0, Im < 0); never np.sqrt of a negated ε_c. - The sleeve uses J/Y with real k₁ (Y is regular there: the sleeve excludes ρ = 0). (Lε) puts a complex k into Y, hence (Z). - The ε ratio is k₁²/k₂² (μ = μ₀ in both). Never rebuild ε_c from σ and εᵣ with a separately typed ε₀: k_coat = K0·√3, with K0 imported. - Derivatives are analytic or recurrence derivatives only. No finite-difference check is pre-registered (IMP-2's (F) ruling). - Normalise residuals by the parts before cancellation, never by |f| (item 190's lesson). Y₁ ≈ −270 and J₁ ≈ 1e-3 in the sleeve. - The ρ = 0 axis is outside every sample set. Guard the TE conversion's 1/ρ. - Run hygiene. Print on rank 0. The real build skips the four complex-only environment tests, as expected. Use -s. Rule (i): no edit after the last window. Rule (f) reaches a parameter (s, b), never a bound. - Shared file: append only; rebase if another item appends first.

Scope. Numpy only: two single-mode drives on an infinite coated PEC cylinder, with one lossless coating at one thickness. Not included: - the FEM (step 1); - the plane-wave multi-mode series; - k_z ≠ 0 propagation along an insulated lead (the insulated-antenna / transmission-line regime). That is where insulation actually controls lead heating, so TM's coating-invisibility is a k_z = 0 statement and must not be read as "insulation does not matter"; - a lossy or thin real-lead coating; - a finite lead or tip (IMP-2, IMP-3); - a coil, heating, or published data.

Status it can move. The proposed §7 IMP-5 row moves ⬜ → 🟡 on its step-0 Done-when, which this item matches (rule (j)). The review adds the row in the commit that queues this item and names it in the dashboard for the weekly to ratify (rule (5) lane 3).

Negative result. - (Z), (B1), (B2), (P) or (L) red: a code bug. Fix it in-slot, run W1b, and disclose. - (IF) red with (B1) green: a wrong ε factor or region selection. Print both sides and their ratio, then stop. - (Lε) or (Lb) red: the coated algebra disagrees with IMP-4. Print the coefficient pairs, then stop. - (Q) red: print the miss at s ∈ {1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6}. If it scales as s² ln s, s is a parameter: re-register it under rule (f), disclosed; otherwise stop. - A control inside its band: the anchor does not discriminate. Stop and report. - On a stop: park on attempt/IMP-5-step0-<UTC> and mark BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); the row stays ⬜. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Outcome (2026-10-04 00:30 UTC, 19:30 CDT slot; implementer): ✅ step 0, row ⬜ → 🟡. Windows 20261004T003434Z_IMP-5-step0-W1.log (39 passed, 4 complex-only skips, 63 s) and 20261004T003556Z_IMP-5-step0-W1b.log (same, Status 0, 59 s; the closing window). Disclosed: W1 was all green, but its (Q) area-uniform draw put 1 of 200 points in the sleeve; the test now draws 100 coat + 100 host points and asserts ≥ 90 per region (no band moved), and W1b re-ran the same command under rule (i). Anchors: (Z) 2.3e-16; (B1) ≤ 3.2e-16; (B2) ≤ 6.7e-16; (P) ≤ 8.9e-16; (IF) ≤ 9.0e-15 (TE normal D); (I) 4.5e-16; (Lε) ≤ 6.8e-16 (predicted ≈ 3e-16); (Lb) ≤ 5.6e-16; (Q) 4.3e-14 at s = 1e-6 (W1 1.75e-14 on the one-coat-point draw); (L) bitwise. Readings vs prediction: TM |s/s₀ − 1| 3.084e-6 (3.1e-6), |I/I_IMP-4 − 1| 4.27e-5 (4.3e-5), I = 6.9305e-4 − 2.8348e-3j; TE t/t₀ −2.1584 + 0.16582j vs quasi-static B/(E₀a²) −2.1587 + 0.17033j; C/E₀ −3.527 + 0.136j; |E_ρ(b⁻)|/|E_ρ(b⁺)| 59.36, |E_ρ(b⁺)| 0.0859·E₀, |E_φ(b)| 1.960·E₀. Annulus ⟨|E|²⟩/E₀²: TE coat 17.987, TE host 1.411 (bare 1.0878, ×1.297), TM coat 3.6404e-3, TM host 2.2963e-2. Controls: (c1) |β − 1| 1.461 (> 0.04886); (c2) H_φ residual 0.9763, |s_w/s − 1| 0.104; (c3) E_φ residual 0.9763, |β − 1| 1.461. Brief wording miss (not a gate): under (c3) the printed, unasserted (P) TE φ reads 1.005e-14, a hair over the 1e-14 band the brief says "still passes" — the swapped coefficient enlarges the sleeve field ≈ 11×, so rounding scales with it; (IF) still discriminates. Code: additive block after pec_cylinder_tm0_current in utils/analytical.py (three public functions, four private helpers, private _condition); test tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_closed_form.py. IMP-4's closed-form module and test_analytical_lightweight.py re-gated green in the same window (rule (c)).

docs.title: §9 item 211 — 2026-10-03 (lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

IMP-5 step 1: the FEM half. It is IMP-4 step 1's fixture with a conforming εᵣ 3 sleeve a < ρ < b meshed as its own cell tag and assigned through material_map. The outer wall carries step 0's exact coated trace, and the end planes carry IMP-4's polarisation-specific conditions. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2; real build for W0, complex for W1a–W2b. Class: lane-3 closed form (measured median ≈ 12 min). - Cost: ≈ 12 measured / ≈ 70 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 30 code + five windows of ≈ 1.5–2.5 min + ≈ 10 spare). - Depends on item 210; if it did not land, skip. The check is grep -n 'def coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_field' src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py non-empty, plus 210's W1 green in test-results.md. - This item does not edit utils/analytical.py. Should an edit become necessary, the file is append-only; rebase if another item lands first.

Why the fixture is still exact. IMP-4 step 1's argument (IMP-4.md, item 206) carries region by region. - TM: E = E_zẑ in both regions, so n̂ × E = 0 on z = const and the PEC ends are exact: pec tags (1, 2, 3). - TE: H = H_zẑ in both regions, so n̂ × H = 0 there and the natural (PMC) ends are exact: pec tags (1, 2). - The interface needs no condition. The curl-curl weak form imposes tangential E and tangential μ⁻¹ curl E continuity naturally. Nédélec elements carry tangential continuity and leave the normal component free to jump by 59×. - Truncation: the outer wall carries the exact trace. Only discretisation and faceting remain.

Fixture. - Imports from test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py: FREQUENCY_HZ, SIGMA_HIGH, EPSILON_R_HOST, E0, DEGREE = 2, OUTER_BOUNDARY_TAG = 1, CAVITY_TAG = 2, TH15_BETA_BAND, MAT4_BAND, _assemble_real, _cavity_dofs. - Imports from test_imp1_step3_exact_comparand.py: K_FIXTURE, K0. - Imports from test_imp2_spheroid_fem.py: QDEG, _numpy_quadrature_mean, _owned_masked_cells, _rss_gib. - Imports from test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py: A, C, LENGTH, END_TAG, RESOLUTION_WALL, RESOLUTION_FAR, CELL_GUARD, TAG_BAND, M_BAND, S_BAND, N_PROBE, PEC_TAGS, _say, _ncells, _circle, _eval_complex, _te_mode, _incident, _static_te_numpy, _h_wall_over_a. - Never re-derive these. New constants: B = 1.5 * A, COAT_TAG = 4, EPS_R_COAT = 3.0, K_COAT = K0 * sqrt(3).

Code. - Mesher (one additive keyword; rule (c), disclosed). Add keyword-only coat_radius: Optional[float] = None to MeshGenerator.cylindrical_domain (io/mesh.py:941), passed through to _cylindrical_hole_domain (io/mesh.py:70) with default None. - Passing it without as_hole=True raises, as resolution_wall does. It must satisfy a < coat_radius < c, or raise. - None takes the existing hole branch untouched. - When it is set: - Build the sleeve as cut(cyl_b, cyl_a) and the host as cut(cyl_c, cyl_b), then occ.fragment them so the ρ = b face is shared (conforming). Raise unless exactly two volumes remain. - Identify the volumes by bbox r_max (b against c). The host is volume tag 2 (unchanged); the sleeve is the new cell tag 4 "coating". - Facet groups come from getBoundary of both volumes combined, so the shared face drops out. They are classified z first exactly as now: tag 3 ends (now four annular faces), tag 1 outer wall, tag 2 cavity. - No interior-interface facet group is emitted, because the material jump is carried by cell tags. - The sizing field is unchanged: a Distance from the cavity faces gives h(ρ) = ρ/6. - Print the face count per group, the cells per volume tag and the min SICN. - Module tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_fem.py: - Material: HomogeneousMaterial(sigma=SIGMA_HIGH, epsilon_r=EPSILON_R_HOST) as the default, plus material_map={COAT_TAG: HomogeneousMaterial(sigma=0.0, epsilon_r=EPS_R_COAT)}, and cell_tags. - Trace: step 0's fields with region=None, interior="zero", through IMP-4's (3, N) adapter. - Incident split: IMP-4's _incident(drive), which is host k and host ε_c. The scattered basis is E_s = E_cf(region="host") − E_inc. - Probes: 24 points on each of ρ = 1.2b, 1.5b and 2b at z = 0, all in the host. β is IMP-4's complex LSQ over all components; raise unless every point evaluates. - Two masks, both built from cell tags (numpy DG0, never a radius test at the interface): - coat = cell tag 4; - host annulus = cell tag 2 with midpoint x² + y² < (1.5b)². - Φ_h,m = ⟨|E_h|²⟩/E₀² by UFL at quadrature_degree QDEG. - Φ_cf,h,m is _numpy_quadrature_mean over the same owned cells, using the closed form with region forced to the mask's region ("coat" on tag 4, "host" on tag 2). Quadrature points in the chord slivers lie on the wrong side of the true circles, at ρ < a or ρ < b, and region-by-radius would hand a host point the coating formula: a 59× E_ρ error. - Φ_cont,m is a numpy radial / angular quadrature of step 0's field over the true annulus, printed beside Φ_cf,h,m to isolate faceting. - Solve: a module-local _solve_coated(drive, pec_tags, coated=True) following IMP-4's _solve_cylinder. coated=False drops the material_map, which is control (c1). It returns β, both Φ triples, the cavity dof count and max|E|, z-invariance, cells, seconds and summed RSS. - Tests: - test_census_and_numpy (W0, not complex_only); - test_tm_drive (W1a), test_te_drive (W1b); - test_control_te_coating_omitted (W2a), test_control_tm_natural_cavity (W2b). - All four solve tests are complex_only, with one solve per window to hold the standard tier.

Anchors (asserted). - W0 (census, before any solve): - (Guard) global cells ≤ CELL_GUARD (60 000). Predicted 26–33 k: IMP-4's 25 568, plus the conforming ρ = b surface, which the ρ/6 field already resolves. - (R) cylindrical_domain(as_hole=True, coat_radius=None) reproduces IMP-4 W0's 25 568 cells exactly (20261003T200309Z_IMP-4-step1-W0.log:465). This is the None branch's bit-identity, alongside the re-gates below. - (Tag) reduced ds(t) areas (pinned quadrature_degree 2): tag 1 against 2πcL, tag 2 against 2πaL, tag 3 against 2π(c² − a²), each within TAG_BAND (2 %). IMP-4 measured −0.088 / −0.088 / −0.455 %. - (Vol) reduced dx(4) and dx(2) volumes against π(b² − a²)L and π(c² − b²)L within TAG_BAND. Predicted ≈ −0.5 % (polygon deficit). Swapped tags read O(1). This is the check that material_map targets the sleeve. - (M′) On each of the two masks, the numpy quadrature of IMP-4's polynomial static TE field equals its UFL cell integral to ≤ M_BAND (1e-12). - (S) The incident split, on 64 points in [1.2b, 2b]: TM (E_cf,z − E₀J₀(k₂ρ))/H₀⁽²⁾(k₂ρ) is constant = s; TE E_cf − E_inc = t·(the H-mode of _te_mode). Each holds to ≤ S_BAND (1e-12). - W1a / W1b, per drive (TM pec tags (1, 2, 3); TE pec tags (1, 2)): - (i) |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND (4.886 %); - (ii) |Φ_h/Φ_cf,h − 1| ≤ MAT4_BAND (10 %) on the coat mask; - (iii) the same on the host-annulus mask; - (iv) cavity dofs located > 0 (reduced), with max|E| < 1e-12 (reduced with MPI.MAX).

Printed (predicted, never asserted; rule (e)). - TM. - |β − 1| ≲ 0.2 % (IMP-4 measured 0.036 %; the coating moves s by 3e-6). - Coat Φ miss +1 to +3 %. This is IMP-4's TM annulus a < ρ < 1.5a, measured +1.01 % there, wall-faceting-led; Φ_cont 3.640e-3. - Host Φ miss +0.3 to +2 %, with Φ_cont 2.296e-2. - TM current β·I against step 0's I. - TE. - |β − 1| ≲ 2 %: the dipole goes as b_eff², the faceting deficit is ≈ −0.46 %, and IMP-4 TE measured 0.774 %. - Coat Φ |miss| ≲ 2 %: the sleeve thins by ≈ 0.23 % under faceting, giving ≈ +0.46 % in |E|². Φ_cont 17.99. - Host Φ |miss| ≲ 1.5 %, with Φ_cont 1.411. - Both drives: cells per tag, degree-2 dofs, seconds, summed RSS, h_wall/a, the sleeve's max edge/(b − a) (predicted 0.5–0.8), min SICN, and z-invariance (IMP-4 measured 7.3e-3 / 1.3e-2).

Negative controls (rule (e): predicted by the drafting series with the exact coated trace at c, not measured; each is asserted only as missing its band). - (c1) TE, coating omitted (W2a; coated=False: host material in tag 4, same mesh, pec tags (1, 2)). The material map must reach the sleeve, or TE cannot tell. - Prediction. β ≈ −0.476 − 0.036j, |β − 1| ≈ 1.476 (range [1.3, 1.65]), with a ceiling of 1.476/0.04886 ≈ 30×. Coat Φ miss ≈ −91.4 % (range [−95, −85] %). Host Φ miss ≈ −17.8 % (range [−22, −14] %, 1.8× the band). - Asserted: |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND, and both |Φ misses| > MAT4_BAND. - (c2) TM, natural cavity (W2b; PMC wire, pec tags (1, 3), coated). - Prediction. β ≈ 0.590 − 0.123j, |β − 1| ≈ 0.428 (range [0.25, 0.6]), with a ceiling of ≈ 8.8×. Coat Φ miss ≈ +7 940 % (range [+3 000, +15 000] %). Host Φ miss ≈ +1 175 % (range [+500, +2 500] %). - Asserted: |β − 1| > TH15_BETA_BAND, and both |Φ misses| > MAT4_BAND. - The calibration of the method: the same trace-pinned annulus argument predicted IMP-4's c1 at 0.49, measured 0.489. - Not run: TM with the coating omitted. It is predicted at |β − 1| ≈ 2.4e-6, the step-0 invisibility. A solve would only restate it, so no window is spent there.

Windows (foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; each harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative; -s; node IDs, never -k; no pipes). - W0 (real build). Predicted 100–140 s: IMP-4 W0 took 96 s with the same two re-gates plus a closed-form module (20261003T200309Z_IMP-4-step1-W0.log:620), and this window adds one census (mesh 2.1 s there). - It is the rule (c) re-gate of coat_radius=None: test_cylindrical_domain.py, test_cylinder.py, and IMP-4's census, whose tag areas must match its record. - Step 0's module is re-run as the dependency check.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-5-step1-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/mesh/test_cylindrical_domain.py tests/solver/test_cylinder.py tests/validation/test_imp4_pec_cylinder_fem.py::test_census_and_numpy tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_closed_form.py tests/validation/test_imp5_coated_cylinder_fem.py::test_census_and_numpy -v -s --tb=short'" - W1a / W1b / W2a / W2b (complex, one solve each). Traps (all paid for). - End conditions are polarisation-specific (IMP-4): TM ends PEC, TE ends natural. Swapping them is an O(1) β miss, not a small error. - Region by cell tag, never by radius, at either circle. The TE normal E jumps 59× at ρ = b, and the chord slivers put quadrature points of host cells at ρ < b and of sleeve cells at ρ < a. This generalises IMP-1 / IMP-4's chord-sliver trap (item 146). Use the "zero" interior for the trace only. - Mesh classification. Classify z first (IMP-4). Facet groups come from the meshed boundary of the combined volumes (TH-15). The fragment must leave the ρ = b face shared, or the sleeve is a disconnected solid and the weak form never couples the regions. - ε_c consistency. The solver builds ε_c from (σ, εᵣ) with its own ε₀ (core/time_harmonic.py:782–783). The comparand uses k₂ = K_FIXTURE and k₁ = K0·√3, which are the same constants. Never mix in a separately typed ε₀. - Complex build. No UFL comparison, no ufl.max_value, and no comparison containing sqrt, even on real operands (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). Every mask is numpy, from cell tags. - Quadrature. Every SpatialCoordinate-bearing form, and the ds / dx area and volume forms, carries metadata={"quadrature_degree": …} (POST-5 step 1). - Rank safety. - cell_tags.values, assemble_scalar and local max/min are rank-local; reduce before asserting. - material_map tag validation is rank-reduced (core/time_harmonic.py:150–180); do not pre-check tags rank-locally. - Do the RSS allreduce outside any rank-0 branch (IMP-2 W0 20261001T200855Z). Owned cells only. - JIT cache. Never clear the cache wholesale. - Run hygiene. - Foreground; container timeout -k 30; never pipe or filter inside the harness command. - PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace. Print on rank 0. Rule (i): no edit to a file after its last window. - Rule (f) reaches a parameter (b, a resolution), never a bound. Rule (h) applies: no in-slot comparand substitution. - Reading TM. A green TM gate is not a coating test, because TM cannot see the sleeve (step 0). The coating is tested by TE's gates and by (c1).

Scope. One mesh, degree 2, two single-mode drives on an infinite coated PEC cylinder with an exact trace and one lossless coating. These are accuracy-level bands, not a convergence claim. Not included: - k_z ≠ 0 guided waves along an insulated lead (the regime where insulation sets lead heating); - a lossy or real-thickness insulation; - Jin's (11.63) global boundary condition; - modes n ≥ 2; - a finite lead or tip (IMP-2, IMP-3); - a coil, heating, 1 g SAR, or published data.

The opening is the weekly's to ratify. - The review may then add IMP-5 to §2's closed-form-lane sentence: imposed trace, no coil, k_z = 0.

If the image changed since IMP-4 W0, stop instead: that is a record re-registration for record-reconciler, not a code bug. - (Tag), (Vol), (M′) or (S) red: a mesher or helper bug. Stop and report. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

docs.title: IMP-6 — history
docs.text: Opened 2026-10-12 by the 10:30 daily review under §9 rule (5) lane 3 (Phases 7/8), for the weekly to ratify. §10 "Phase 7 — implants" names "wires, rods, plates": wires and rods have canonicals (IMP-4 / IMP-5 the lead shaft, IMP-2 the rod tip), plates have none. IMP-6 is IMP-2's companion: the PEC oblate spheroid, whose rim enhancement 1/L_x under an in-plane field is to a plate or disc edge what 1/L_z is to a rod tip. Same host, same hole route, same bands, same grain. Sources: Landau & Lifshitz ECM §4; Stratton Electromagnetic Theory §3.27 (the commissioning text also names §3.28); Osborn, Phys. Rev. 67, 351 (1945). These are the citations IMP-2 uses, and they are not verified in-repo. docs/references/jin-fem-3e/ has no spheroid (ch. 11 mentions spheroidal surfaces only as a truncation boundary). The docstring therefore derives every identity the test asserts, and the in-repo cross-check is the ellipsoid integral (Int) below.

docs.title: §9 item 403 — 2026-10-12 (lane 3, closed form)
docs.text:
IMP-6 step 0: the PEC oblate spheroid in a uniform field, axial and in-plane, numpy only (implementer; smoke, no MPI, real build; src/ additive + test; ≈ 11 measured / 40 predicted min: ≈ 1 min of windows + 15 fixed + ≈ 25 code; depends on nothing).

  • Geometry and notation. Semi-axes a along x and y, c along z, with a > c. Aspect m = a/c. e = √(1 − c²/a²), focal-ring radius f = a·e, ξ₀ = c/f = √(1 − e²)/e. Oblate spheroidal coordinates: ρ = f√((ξ² + 1)(1 − η²)), z = fξη, with ξ ≥ 0 and the body surface at ξ = ξ₀. Name swap versus IMP-2: here semi_major = a is the equatorial radius (x, y) and semi_minor = c lies along z. Keep semi_major > semi_minor as the check.
  • Anchor (derive in the docstring). Write both drives in one Cartesian form:
  • φ = −E₀ x_i [1 − D_i(ξ)/D_i(ξ₀)], with x_i = z for the axial drive and x for the in-plane drive.
  • Axial: D_z = h(ξ) = arccot ξ − 1/ξ, so h = q₁(ξ)/ξ with q₁ = ξ arccot ξ − 1, the decaying n = 1 oblate function.
  • In-plane: D_x = g(ξ) = arccot ξ − ξ/(1 + ξ²), which is K(ξ)/√(1 + ξ²) for the decaying m = 1 solution K = √(1 + ξ²)[arccot ξ − ξ/(1 + ξ²)]. Reduction of order from the regular solution √(1 + ξ²) gives K, with Wronskian −2/(1 + ξ²).
  • Derivatives: h′ = 1/(ξ²(1 + ξ²)), g′ = −2/(1 + ξ²)².
  • Field: E = E₀x̂_i − ∇φ_s, where φ_s = E₀ x_i D(ξ)/D(ξ₀) and ∇φ_s = (E₀/D₀)[D(ξ) x̂_i + x_i D′(ξ) ∇ξ]. Get ∇ξ by implicit differentiation of F = ρ²/(ξ² + 1) + z²/ξ² − f² = 0: ∇ξ = −∇F/F_ξ, ∇F = (2x/(ξ² + 1), 2y/(ξ² + 1), 2z/ξ²), F_ξ = −2ξρ²/(ξ² + 1)² − 2z²/ξ³.
  • Depolarisation factors, each from its own drive's Wronskian:
    • L_z = (1 + ξ₀²)(1 − ξ₀ arccot ξ₀) = (1/e²)[1 − √(1 − e²) arcsin(e)/e].
    • L_x = L_y = (ξ₀/2)[(1 + ξ₀²) arccot ξ₀ − ξ₀]. Computed independently of L_z, so the sum rule is a real test.
  • Surface identities: rim E_x(±a, 0, 0) = E₀/L_x (in-plane drive); pole E_z(0, 0, ±c) = E₀/L_z (axial drive).
  • Far-field dipoles: p_i = E₀a²c/(3L_i), which is a³ for the sphere.
  • Disc limit: L_x → πξ₀/4 − ξ₀² + O(ξ₀³), so p_x/a³ → 4/(3π).
  • Code (append to src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py directly after pec_prolate_spheroid_field, ≈ line 1654, under a new IMP-6 step 0 banner, before the MAT-15 block; additive, nothing reordered).
  • oblate_spheroid_depolarisation(e, *, branch=None) -> (l_x, l_z).
  • oblate_spheroid_d_functions(xi, *, branch=None) -> (h, h′, g, g′).
  • oblate_spheroidal_xi(points, focal).
  • pec_oblate_spheroid_potential(points, *, semi_major, semi_minor, drive="axial"|"inplane", e0=1.0, scattered_only=False).
  • pec_oblate_spheroid_field(points, *, semi_major, semi_minor, drive=…, e0=1.0, interior="zero"|"continue") (step 1's trace; same contract as pec_prolate_spheroid_field).
  • Interior mask: (x² + y²)/a² + z²/c² < 1 − 1e-12.
  • Test file: tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_closed_form.py.
  • Anchors (asserted). Aspects {1.01, 2, 5, 20, 100} unless stated.
  • (L) The two L_z forms agree ≤ 1e-13.
  • (Sum) |2L_x + L_z − 1| ≤ 1e-13.
  • (Int) Each L_i equals the ellipsoid integral (a²c/2)∫₀^∞ ds/((a_i² + s)(a² + s)√(c² + s)), by scipy.integrate.quad at epsrel=1e-13, to ≤ 1e-10 relative at aspects 2, 5, 20.
  • (Br) The closed and series branches of h and g agree ≤ 1e-13 relative on ξ ∈ [5, 20].
  • (Bd) |φ|/(E₀a) ≤ 1e-12 at 200 Fibonacci surface points, both drives, aspects 2 and 5.
  • (Tg) Tangential E on the same points ≤ 1e-12·E₀.
  • (Rim) |E_x(±a, 0, 0)·L_x − 1| ≤ 1e-12, plus |E(0, ±a, 0)| ≤ 1e-12·E₀ (zero normal field where n·x̂ = 0).
  • (Pole) |E_z(0, 0, ±c)·L_z − 1| ≤ 1e-12.
  • (F) Field against the central-difference gradient of the potential at δ = 2e-3·a and 4e-3·a, both drives, 40 points with ξ ∈ [1.2ξ₀ + 0.05, 3] and |η| ≤ 0.95. Asserted in Richardson / ratio form (the lesson ratified on IMP-2): ratio ∈ [3.8, 4.2] and |E − (4D(δ) − D(2δ))/3| ≤ 1e-7·E₀.
  • (Lap) FD Laplacian of both potentials at the same δ pair: ratio ∈ [3.8, 4.2], and the Richardson residual ·a/E₀ ≤ 1e-7.
  • (Far) The P₁ projection R²(3/2)∫φ_s μ dμ = p_z (axial). The sinθcosφ projection R²(3/4π)∫φ_s sinθ cosφ dΩ = p_x (in-plane; 64-node Gauss–Legendre × 64-point trapezoid). Both at R = 2a and 4a, ≤ 1e-12 relative.
  • (Sph) At e = 1e-2: |(L_z − 1/3)/e² − 2/15| ≤ 1e-3 and |(L_x − 1/3)/e² + 1/15| ≤ 1e-3. Both potentials match the sphere's −E₀x_i(1 − a³/r³) to ≤ 1e-3·E₀a for r ∈ [1.2a, 3a].
  • (Disc) At c/a = 1e-3: |(L_x − πξ₀/4)/ξ₀² + 1| ≤ 2e-3 (the next term is (π/4)ξ₀ ≈ 7.9e-4).
  • Printed (predicted here by stdlib arithmetic).
  • Aspect 2 / 5: L_z = 0.527200 / 0.750484, L_x = 0.236400 / 0.124758.
  • Aspect 2 / 5: 1/L_x = 4.2301 / 8.0155, 1/L_z = 1.8968 / 1.3325, pointwise rim (1/L_x)² = 17.89 / 64.25.
  • Aspect 100: L_x 0.007755 against πc/(4a) = 0.007854; p_x/a³ 0.429822 against 4/(3π) = 0.424413.
  • Osborn's oblate table values beside these, only if the executor can quote them. They are not in-repo; (Int) is the in-repo check.
  • Negative controls (rule (e): every factor below is predicted, computed here, printed beside the measured value; only the separation is asserted).
  • (c1) The prolate formula used for the oblate shape: prolate_spheroid_depolarisation(e) at the same e gives L_x^pro = (1 − L_z^pro)/2. In the rim identity this reads E_x(rim)·L_x^pro = L_x^pro/L_x^obl = 1.748 / 3.784 at aspect 2 / 5. The prolate rim enhancement under-reads by 43 % / 74 %. Assert only |· − 1| > 0.1. The axial counterpart L_z^pro/L_z^obl = 0.329 / 0.0744 is printed.
  • (c2) The regular (growing) solution in place of the decaying one: D_i ≡ 1, i.e. φ_s = E₀x_i. This is IMP-2's Q₁ → P₁ swap, since the regular axial solution ξ gives φ_s = E₀fηξ = E₀z. (Far)'s 4a/2a projection ratio reads 8 (derived, R³). Assert |ratio − 1| > 1e-3, on both drives.
  • Window (smoke; real build, the IMP-2 step-0 pattern without mpiexec; split so each part fits 30 s):
  • W1 (≈ 15 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step0-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_closed_form.py -s -v --tb=short'"
  • W1r (≈ 15 s, the rule (c) re-gate of the additive analytical.py change): label IMP-6-step0-W1r, same command with paths tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/unit/test_analytical_lightweight.py tests/validation/test_imp2_spheroid_closed_form.py.
  • Traps.
  • 1 − ξ₀ arccot ξ₀, arccot ξ − 1/ξ and arccot ξ − ξ/(1 + ξ²) cancel catastrophically at large ξ. Use series branches for ξ > 10 (IMP-2's threshold, 40 terms): h = Σ_{k≥1} (−1)^k ξ^{−(2k+1)}/(2k + 1) and g = Σ_{k≥1} (−1)^{k+1} (2k/(2k + 1)) ξ^{−(2k+1)}. (Sph) at e = 1e-2 (ξ₀ ≈ 100) runs on the series.
  • ξ from the quadratic f²ξ⁴ + (f² − r²)ξ² − z² = 0, taking the stable root:
    • ξ² = [(r² − f²) + √((r² − f²)² + 4f²z²)]/(2f²) for r² ≥ f²;
    • ξ² = 2z²/[√((r² − f²)² + 4f²z²) − (r² − f²)] otherwise.
  • Never evaluate inside the focal disc (ξ → 0, interior). Use arccot ξ = arctan(1/ξ) only for ξ > 0.
  • The real build skips the four complex-only environment tests; that is expected, and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX stays unset.
  • The smoke path carries only tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py (10:30 ruling, item 364).
  • A window killed at 30 s is not a result. Shrink the path list; never raise the ceiling.
  • Foreground, timeout: 660000; -s; append to analytical.py, never reorder.
  • Scope. Quasi-static, PEC, no host, no k. Not: step 1's FEM, SAR, a square-edged plate (a real plate edge carries a wedge singularity the smooth spheroid does not), a thin-plate FEM.
  • Status it can move. IMP-6 ⬜ → 🟡 ("step 0 green ⇒ 🟡" in the row above; the review inserts the row in the same commit that queues this item, rule (j)).
  • Negative result.
  • (Rim) / (Pole) red with (Far) and (Int) green: an L formula is wrong (prolate / oblate swapped, or L_x taken as (1 − L_z)/2 instead of the independent form).
  • (Sum) red with (Int) green for one factor: the other factor's closed form is wrong.
  • (Bd) red: the ξ map.
  • (F) ratio ≈ 1: a gradient bug.
  • Fix in-slot. Still red ⇒ park on attempt/*, BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); item 404 stays unqueued.
