docs.title: §9 item 404 — 2026-10-12 (lane 3, closed form; depends on item 403)
docs.text:
IMP-6 step 1: FEM at aspect 2 and 5, in-plane drive, on IMP-2's hole route (implementer; heavy, -n 2, complex; ≈ 20 measured / 70 predicted min: ≈ 14 min of windows + 15 fixed + ≈ 40 code; depends on 403; skip if it did not land).

  • Sizing, stated first.
  • |k| = 17.90 1/m (IMP-1's host: σ 0.57 S/m, εᵣ 78, 64 MHz).
  • a = 6 mm (the long semi-axis, as IMP-2's c), so (|k|a)² = 1.1535 % ≤ 4.886/3 = 1.629 %.
  • c = 3 mm at aspect 2 and 1.2 mm at aspect 5. Rim curvature radius ρ_r = c²/a = 1.5 / 0.24 mm, numerically IMP-2's ρ_t.
  • Box half-extents (1.75a, 1.75a, a) = (10.5, 10.5, 6) mm. The 1.5× probe spheroid (9 mm in x) clears the wall.
  • Corner 16.02 mm, (|k|R)² = 8.22 %, between IMP-2's 6.92 % and IMP-1's 9.6 %. Printed beside I2a's 1.56e-2 face departure.
  • Code.
  • Mesher (rule (c), disclosed). spheroid_in_box_domain does not build an oblate spheroid today: it raises unless semi_major > semi_minor with semi_major along z, dilates (a, a, c) = (minor, minor, major), and puts its tip Balls at (0, 0, ±c). Add a keyword-only oblate: bool = False, with the default path byte-identical. With oblate=True:
    • Rotate the unit sphere 45° about z before dilate, so the OCC seam stays off the drive's rim points (±a, 0, 0).
    • dilate(…, semi_major, semi_major, semi_minor).
    • Enclosure check bx, by > semi_major and bz > semi_minor.
    • The two Balls at (±semi_major, 0, 0): radius 3ρ_r, VIn = resolution_tip, where ρ_r = semi_minor²/semi_major is the same expression as today's ρ_t.
    • plus a rim tube: a MathEval field with the distance to the rim circle, f"Sqrt((Sqrt(x*x+y*y)-{a!r})^2+z*z)", feeding a Threshold with SizeMin ρ_r, SizeMax resolution_far, DistMin ρ_r, DistMax 4ρ_r, added to the Min.
    • Cavity Distance→Threshold, mass reference 4πa²c/3 and the absolute wall tol = 1e-6 all unchanged.
  • Fixture: resolution_tip = ρ_r/3, resolution_surface = a/12 = 0.5 mm (IMP-2's aspect-2 surface grain), resolution_far = a/4 = 1.5 mm.
  • Test module tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py. Import from test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py as IMP-2 does: TH15_BETA_BAND, MAT4_BAND, the tags, DEGREE, E0, the host constants, _assemble_real, _cavity_dofs, _phi_closed_form_on_mask. Copy IMP-2's _numpy_quadrature_mean / _owned_masked_cells / _rss_gib patterns.
  • β: the least-squares amplitude of item 403's in-plane scattered field (pec_oblate_spheroid_field(drive="inplane") − E₀x̂) fitted on Re E − E₀x̂, on 24 Fibonacci points on each of the 1.2× and 1.5× scaled oblate spheroids.
  • Rim mask: DG0 indicator of cell midpoints within r_r = 2c²/a (3 mm / 0.48 mm) of (±a, 0, 0). Squares in numpy, no UFL comparison.
  • Φ_rim,cf,h: the degree-8 numpy quadrature over the same cells with interior="continue".
  • Anchors (asserted per aspect at imported bands, as IMP-2 asserted them; the bands come from TH-15 / MAT-4, not from a measurement on this fixture):
  • (i) |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND (4.886 %).
  • (ii) |Φ_rim,h/Φ_rim,cf,h − 1| ≤ MAT4_BAND (10 %).
  • (iii) cavity dofs > 0 and max |E| < 1e-12.
  • (M′) In W0, on each mesh, the numpy quadrature of IMP-1's dipole equals _phi_closed_form_on_mask to ≤ 1e-12.
  • Predicted, printed and not asserted (rule (e)).
  • |β − 1| ≲ 1.5 % and Φ miss ≲ 3 %. IMP-2 measured 0.46 / 0.90 % and 1.11 / 0.20 % at h_tip/ρ_t 0.80 / 0.67, but on a different fixture, so this is evidence that the bands are reachable, not a backing.
  • h_rim/ρ_r.
  • The meshed body-volume deficit (8b_xb_yb_z − Σ air-cell volumes)/(4πa²c/3) − 1. The faceted rim is the likeliest bias at aspect 5.
  • Pointwise rim (1/L_x)² = 17.89 / 64.25.
  • |Im E|/|Re E|; cells, seconds, RSS (reduced outside the rank-0 branch).
  • Negative control (W2, aspect-5 mesh, predicted, rule (e)). Drive axially: the wall trace is item 403's closed-form axial field, zero on the cavity.
  • β fitted against the in-plane basis on Re E − E₀ẑ: predicted ≈ 0 by parity. The ceiling is 1/0.04886 = 20.5×. Assert only |β − 1| > band.
  • Rim-ball Φ_h against the in-plane Φ_rim,cf,h: the axial normal field vanishes at the rim (x_z/a_z² = 0 at z = 0), so the miss is predicted at 90–100 %. It saturates at 100 %, so it can show at most 10× the band. Assert only > 10 %.
  • Also printed: β_axial fitted on the axial basis. This is a record, not asserted, because no prior measurement of that comparison exists on this fixture.
  • Price (measured on the parent fixtures).
  • IMP-2 W1: 37 359 / 44 304 cells, solves 105.8 / 83.3 s, 6.46 GiB summed (20261001T201608Z_IMP-2-step1-W1.log).
  • IMP-2 W0: 109 s (…201413Z…-W0.log:456).
  • IMP-1: 54 524 cells 101.8 s / 10.1 GiB; 90 713 cells 221.9 s / 19.4 GiB.
  • Complex tests/environment costs ≈ 70–80 s per window (IMP-5 step 1 note: 49–57 s solves in 133–168 s windows).
  • Predicted ≈ 40–80 k cells at either aspect: oblate cavity area ≈ 1.6× / 3.4× IMP-2's at aspect 2 / 5, balls of IMP-2's size, a box 1.5× larger, and the rim tube ≈ 7 k cells at aspect 5. That gives ≈ 60–180 s per solve.
  • Cell guard 95 000, checked in W0 before any solve.
  • Windows (complex, -n 2; one solve per window, so each footer returns inside the 660 s Bash ceiling).
  • W0 (≈ 150 s; census, numpy and the mesher re-gate): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step1-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 400 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/unit/test_analytical_lightweight.py tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_closed_form.py tests/validation/test_imp2_spheroid_fem.py::test_census_and_numpy tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py::test_census_and_numpy -s -v --tb=short'". IMP-2's census is the rule (c) re-gate of the oblate=False path. Its printed cells sit beside 37 359 / 44 304; a mismatch is reported (it may be an image move), and it is a defect only if the default branch's diff is non-empty.
  • W1a (≈ 170–260 s): label IMP-6-step1-W1a, timeout -k 30 600, paths tests/environment tests/validation/test_pec_sphere_hole.py tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py::test_in_plane_aspect2. test_pec_sphere_hole.py is the mesher-module re-gate IMP-2 ran.
  • W1b (≈ 140–260 s): label IMP-6-step1-W1b, timeout -k 30 600, tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py::test_in_plane_aspect5.
  • W2 (≈ 140–260 s): label IMP-6-step1-W2, timeout -k 30 600, tests/environment tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py::test_axial_control.
  • Traps.
  • The basis is the in-plane field minus E₀x̂. IMP-2's uniform[:, 0 if drive == "transverse" else 2] is inverted here; copying it is the trap.
  • MathEval takes a literal expression: bake a in with repr, print the string, and use gmsh's Sqrt.
  • A Threshold returns SizeMax beyond DistMax. Never give one a fine SizeMax, or it caps the whole box.
  • OCC poles land on the flat faces (0, 0, ±c). If W0 prints minimum SICN under 0.1, report it and do not proceed to solves.
  • IMP-2's two pre-W0 failures:
    • The wall tolerance stays absolute 1e-6 (OCC pads the bounding box by 1e-7).
    • The collective RSS reduction stays outside the rank-0 branch.
  • Cavity group from the meshed boundary, never the tool. Owned cells only (size_local). Read geometry.dofmap's shape at runtime. No UFL < and no sqrt comparisons: masks in numpy.
  • Probe points never sit on a wall.
  • A killed compile leaves an orphan .c in /root/.cache/fenics. Use the rubric's sweep, only when pgrep -c python3 reads 0.
  • Foreground, timeout: 660000; -s; no edit after the last window (rule (i)).
  • Scope. Quasi-static trace, PEC, one a, imposed closed-form trace, accuracy-level bands at one mesh per aspect (not a convergence claim). Not: a square-edged plate (edge singularity), a plate in the coil-driven phantom, SAR or 1 g SAR, finite-k spheroid, thin-plate aspects (≥ 20).
  • Status it can move. IMP-6 🟡 → ✅ ("step 1 at both aspects ⇒ ✅" in the row). Rule (j): the executor closes on the row.
  • Negative result.
  • W0 over the cell guard: one pre-stated fallback is allowed, resolution_surface = a/9 and rim-tube SizeMin 1.5ρ_r, disclosed and printed. Still over ⇒ stop before any solve, report the counts, BLOCKED.
  • IMP-2 census red: the keyword broke the default path. Fix in-slot, and never go on to solves.
  • (M′) red: a quadrature bug. Fix in-slot.
  • (i) or (ii) red with (iii) and (M′) green: print h_rim/ρ_r and the body-volume deficit, park on attempt/*, BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). No band moves (rule (f) applies only to a mesher-unmeetable analytic comparand, ruled by the review).
  • A control that passes the gate: the basis or drive is mislabelled. Report it and stop.

Outcome 2026-10-12 (13:30 CDT slot, second item, implementer): DONE, IMP-6 🟡 → ✅. MeshGenerator.spheroid_in_box_domain gains the keyword oblate=False (rule (c), additive; the oblate path is a separate private builder, so the default branch's diff is the dispatch only); test tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py. Heavy, -n 2, complex. - SICN trap, disclosed. The first W0 (20261012T183906Z_IMP-6-step1-W0.log, 55 passed) printed min SICN 0.0247 at aspect 2 (0.1517 at aspect 5). Per the trap, no solve was run on that mesh. A gmsh.model.mesh.optimize("Netgen") pass was added on the oblate path only, and W0 was re-run (20261012T184107Z_IMP-6-step1-W0.log, 97 s, 55 passed): min SICN 0.267 / 0.371; cells 39 142 / 32 676 (guard 95 000); IMP-2 census re-gate 37 359 / 44 304, unchanged; (M′) 2.6e-14 / 5.5e-14; body-volume deficit −4.40e-3 / −5.78e-3; air OCC mass rel 4.1e-5 / 1.5e-5. - Anchors. W1a (20261012T184250Z_IMP-6-step1-W1a.log, 162 s, test_pec_sphere_hole.py re-gate green): aspect 2 β = 0.999220 (0.078 %), Φ_rim,h / Φ_rim,cf,h = 4.755198 / 4.762429 (miss 0.152 %), h_rim/ρ_r 0.648, 70.5 s solve, 6.99 GiB summed, cavity 15 026 dofs at max |E| 0. W1b (20261012T184537Z_IMP-6-step1-W1b.log, 126 s): aspect 5 β = 1.006343 (0.634 %), Φ 23.024938 / 22.702995 (miss 1.418 %), h_rim/ρ_r 0.665, 41.9 s, 4.06 GiB, cavity 19 952 dofs at 0. Both inside the predicted ≲ 1.5 % / ≲ 3 %. |Im E|/|Re E| 8.3e-3 / 8.5e-3. - Control (rule (e)). W2 (20261012T184748Z_IMP-6-step1-W2.log, 121 s): axial drive on the aspect-5 mesh, β on the in-plane basis −0.001796 (predicted ≈ 0), Φ miss 97.84 % (predicted 90–100 %); both separated. β_axial on the axial basis 1.005469 (record, not asserted).

Every-item rules that bind both items (PROJECT_PLAN §9 "Every item"): - The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. - An executor that loses the docker socket mid-item stops and reports. - No edit to a script, test or page after its last window (rule (i)). - Every window passes timeout: 660000 and runs pytest with -s. Never delete a log. - An item that parks marks itself BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). - A window killed at its tier ceiling is not a result. After a kill, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 first. - Two heavy windows never run at once. - A smoke window puts only tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py on the path. - Every frequency-domain command sources complex mode, sets FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, and puts tests/environment first. - No slot opens docs/private/ or aed_results/. - Standing rules (c) (disclosed src/ change, gate re-run green) and (e) (asserted / predicted labels) apply as marked above.

docs.title: Review ruling 2026-10-12 10:30 (daily) on the item 403 / 404 drafts
docs.text:
(Q1) The opening. IMP-6 is opened under §9 rule (5) lane 3. Its target is a closed form, the oblate depolarisation factors and the PEC spheroid's exterior field, cited to Landau & Lifshitz ECM §4, Stratton §3.27 and Osborn (1945), the same sources IMP-2 cites. None of the three is held in the repo. So the in-repo check is (Int), the ellipsoid integral by quadrature, which the docstring derives; the citations are pointers, not comparands. The row goes into §7 in this commit, and the opening is named in the dashboard for tonight's weekly to ratify or revert.

(Q2) Item 403's control (c2) is re-stated (the draft's wording was garbled). Replace each drive's decaying ratio D_i(ξ)/D_i(ξ₀) by the regular solution's ratio: ξ/ξ₀ for the axial drive, √(1 + ξ²)/√(1 + ξ₀²) for the in-plane drive. Then compute (Far)'s projections at R = 2a and 4a. The projected "dipole" grows with R instead of staying constant (predicted ratio ≈ 8, printed). Assert only |p(4a)/p(2a) − 1| > 1e-3. The predicted factor is printed beside the measured one (rule (e)).

(Q3) Item 404's bands are imported (TH15_BETA_BAND, MAT4_BAND), exactly as IMP-2 step 1 imported them. IMP-2's measured misses (0.46–1.11 %) are evidence that the bands are reachable; they are not a backing for the predicted values, which stay printed only. A red on (i) or (ii) parks the item as written. No band moves, and the weekly or the next review rules any re-pose.

(Q4) 404 depends on 403 landing in the same or an earlier slot. If 403 parks, 404 is skipped and stays queued. The cell guard (95 000 in W0, one pre-stated fallback) is binding.

(Q5) Measured minutes. The lane-3 class has no recent landings, so both items are costed at predicted × 0.29, this interval's ratio: ≈ 12 for 403 and ≈ 20 for 404. The draft's "≈ 11" for 403 used 0.28.

docs.title: §9 item 408 — 2026-10-12 (lane 3, closed form)
docs.text:
IMP-6 step 2: the rim resolution ladder at aspect 5, in-plane drive, degree 2 (implementer; heavy, -n 2, complex; ≈ 20 measured / 55 predicted min: ≈ 12.5 min of windows + 15 fixed + ≈ 25 code. Predicted × 0.29 gives ≈ 16, which is under the window floor. Item 404 took 15 measured minutes on ≈ 8.4 min of windows, so this item adds ≈ 4 min of windows to that; depends on nothing).

  • The knob, named from the code. _oblate_spheroid_in_box_domain (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py ≈ line 2903) exposes no rim-tube parameter. The tube's Threshold SizeMin is hard-wired to ρ_r = c²/a (≈ line 3005). The rim-local knob is resolution_tip, the VIn of the two Ball fields of radius 3ρ_r at (±a, 0, 0). Step 1 passes ρ_r/3. The rim mask (_rim_mask, cell midpoints within r_r = 2c²/a = 2ρ_r of (±a, 0, 0)) lies wholly inside those Balls. There Min picks resolution_tip (ρ_r/3 < ρ_r), so the tube never governs inside the mask, and the ladder needs no src/ edit. Hold resolution_surface = a/12 and resolution_far = a/4 fixed.
  • Rungs (aspect 5: a = 6 mm, c = 1.2 mm, ρ_r = 0.24 mm, step 1's box and host): resolution_tip = ρ_r/3 (rung 0, step 1's mesh), ρ_r/4 (rung 1) and ρ_r/5 (rung 2).
  • Predicted cells ≈ 33 k / ≈ 55 k / ≈ 92 k. The basis: step 1's 4 905 rim-mask cells in the 2ρ_r balls scale to ≈ 16.5 k in the 3ρ_r Balls, ≈ 16 k lie outside, and the Ball count scales as divisor³. Gradation outside the Balls makes rung 2 the uncertain one.
  • Predicted h_rim/ρ_r ≈ 0.665 / 0.50 / 0.40 (step 1 read 0.665 at rung 0).
  • Code. New module tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_rim_ladder.py. Do not edit test_imp6_oblate_fem.py; it is step 1's closing module (rule (i)).
  • Import step 1's private helpers and constants only: SEMI_MAJOR, BOX_HALF_EXTENTS, CELL_GUARD, QDEG, _semi_minor, _rho_r, _ncells, _rss_gib, _field, _dirichlet, _probe_points, _rim_mask, _owned_masked_cells, _numpy_quadrature_mean, _body_volume_deficit, _beta. Import the rest from test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py as step 1 does: TH15_BETA_BAND, MAT4_BAND, tags, DEGREE, E0, EPSILON_R_HOST, _assemble_real, _cavity_dofs. Import FREQUENCY_HZ and SIGMA_HIGH from test_lossy_sphere_sar.py.
  • Never import a test_* name. pytest collects imported test functions and would re-run step 1's solves inside this window.
  • _mesh_rung(divisor): step 1's _mesh with resolution_tip = _rho_r(5.0)/divisor, cached per divisor, timing the mesh.
  • _solve_on(mesh_tuple): step 1's _solve_oblate (lines 225–304) with the mesh passed in and drive "inplane". β uses the in-plane basis with the uniform part on axis 0.
  • Anchors (asserted per rung at imported bands; bands never restated in the module):
  • (i) |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND.
  • (ii) |Φ_rim,h/Φ_rim,cf,h − 1| ≤ MAT4_BAND.
  • (iii) cavity dofs > 0 and max |E| < 1e-12.
  • W0 asserts, before any solve, cells ≤ CELL_GUARD (95 000) and mask cells > 0 for every rung.
  • Record (printed, not asserted). Per rung:
  • cells, nominal divisor, measured h_rim/ρ_r, min SICN (the mesher prints it), rim-mask cells, body-volume deficit, Φ_h, Φ_cf,h, the signed ratio − 1, β, |Im E|/|Re E|, seconds and summed RSS.
  • The observed order per adjacent pair, p = ln(m_k/m_{k+1}) / ln(H_k/H_{k+1}), using the measured h_rim/ρ_r for H, with the nominal-divisor version beside it. Each window prints its own rung. The executor computes the pairwise orders in the outcome from the cited log lines (pure arithmetic). If the signed miss changes sign, the order is reported as undefined, not forced.
  • Why the rate is not asserted. No imported bar backs this comparison. MAT-9's RATE_BAR = 1.7 (re-used in test_mat15_finite_cylinder_fem.py:68) is a P1 thermal L2 rate on a ratio-2 whole-ball ladder, a different comparison on a different fixture, so rule (e) does not license it. IMP-2 has no ladder.
  • Predicted (rule (e), printed beside the measured value).
  • Rim miss ≈ 1.418 % × (H₁/H₀)² ≈ 0.8 % at rung 1 and ≈ 0.5 % at rung 2 if the rim-local error dominates (affine faceting of a 0.24 mm curvature radius, O(h²)).
  • The surface grain and the far-field grain are held fixed. Step 1's |β − 1| = 0.634 % on rung 0 measures a global error of that size, which can floor the local miss. Predicted rung-2 miss in [0.3 %, 1.4 %]; predicted pairwise order in [0, 2.5]. A floor (order → 0) is a finding, not a failure.
  • β per rung within ≈ ±0.2 % of 0.634 %, because the knob is rim-local.
  • Rung 0 should reproduce step 1's 32 676 cells, ratio 1.014181 and β 1.006343 (20261012T184537Z_IMP-6-step1-W1b.log:189–191). gmsh was deterministic across step 1's W1b and W2 (same cells, same min-SICN centroid). Printed beside; a mismatch is reported (it may be an image move), not asserted.
  • Negative control. None new. The comparand and the gate are step 1's, and step 1's axial-drive control (20261012T184748Z_IMP-6-step1-W2.log:190–191) already separates this fixture's gates from a wrong drive. A ladder adds no control the record needs.

  • rung 2 at ≈ 92 k cells: ≈ 225 s solve, ≈ 15 GiB summed, ≈ 330 s window.
  • Every window is inside timeout -k 30 600 and the 660 s Bash ceiling. The heavy tier holds at -n 2; no -n 4 is needed.
  • Windows (complex, -n 2, one solve per window, foreground, timeout: 660000; the shape of step 1's Command: lines):

docs.title: §9 item 466 — 2026-10-15 (§10 chain I29, IMP-6 step 2e — the body grain, the last step-2 sub-step; lane 3, no solve)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-15 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

What it is. For each of I28's three rim rungs: measure the meshed body (its volume and its equatorial and polar semi-axes), re-evaluate the depolarisation factors and the rim-ball comparand on that measured body, and print the corrected k → 0 miss beside I28's +0.390 / +0.651 / +0.776 %. - Licence: §10 I29 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4812–4817), weekly-enumerated, §9 rule (4). The 10-14 weekly ruled it "the fourth and last step-2 sub-step" (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4603–4616). - Executor: implementer. - Class: lane 3. - Tier: no solve, standard (-n 2, complex, 180 s). - Cost: ≈ 3 measured / ≈ 30 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + ≈ 2 of windows). - Depends on: nothing. Serial on nothing. - No band, tolerance, Done-when or target moves.

THE FREEZE (binding; the 10-14 weekly, PROJECT_PLAN.md:4613–4616). Whatever I29 reads, the IMP-6 step-2 family freezes after it: - the row carries the residual as a stated level: "≈ +0.9 % at k → 0 on this comparand, not rim grain"; - no band moves; - there is no fifth sub-step: no further rung, knob, comparand, body or grain variant is posed by any daily, whatever the reading. - Any later rim or body work is a new numbered step that only a weekly opens. - An executor that finds the reading "invites" a follow-up writes it in the outcome as a note for the weekly. It poses nothing.

Why no solve. The body, the rim mask and the comparand depend on the mesh alone. Φ_h at s = 0.1 on these exact meshes is I28's record: - ρ_r/3: 22.781980 (20261014T183329Z_IMP-6-step2d-W1a.log:173); - ρ_r/4: 22.852453 (20261014T183202Z_IMP-6-step2d-W1b.log:181); - ρ_r/5: 22.888993 (20261014T183415Z_IMP-6-step2d-W1c.log:194).

The window proves it is on those meshes ((Ce), (V0) below). The finite-k share left at s = 0.1 is s²·δ_D = 0.0084 pp (IMP-6.md:831), below every reading here. Existing logs print only the body-volume deficit, not the semi-axes. The deficit is −5.147e-03 / −5.148e-03 / −5.088e-03 (20261014T183126Z_IMP-6-step2d-W0r.log:173, :292, :424). So one -n 2 build per rung is needed (the weekly's "else" branch).

What "the meshed body's equatorial radius and polar half-height" can mean here (settled from the code). - The body is a hole. _body_volume_deficit computes the box volume minus the summed air-cell volumes (tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py:196–205). The hole's wall is the CAVITY_TAG facets (tests/validation/test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py, imported by test_imp6_oblate_rim_ladder.py:84–95). - On oblate_rim="edge" the equator is a model edge and the poles are model vertices (known-issues 2026-10-13, known-issues.md:930). gmsh places every wall node on the CAD surface. - So the vertex extents, max ρ and max |z| over the wall nodes, read a and c by construction, and cannot carry the facet error. The weekly's "extents differ" (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4609) is true of the faceted surface between the nodes, not of the extremal nodes. - This item therefore defines the measured body by its second moments. The semi-axes of the spheroid with the same per-volume moments are a_I = √(5·(I_xx + I_yy)/(2V_h)) and c_I = √(5·I_zz/V_h). On an exact spheroid they return a and c exactly, since ∫x² dV = V a²/5. - The vertex extents a_v, c_v are printed as the control that shows why. The review ratifies this definition or substitutes another before the slot runs.

Code (new test module only; no src/; no edit to test_imp6_oblate_rim_ladder.py or step 1's module, so no re-gate is owed). New tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_body_grain.py, @complex_only, one test test_body_grain. - Imports, private names only, never a test_* name: - from tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_rim_ladder.py: ASPECT, DIVISORS, ITEM426_RUNGS (:179–189), ITEM440_R1 (:155), ITEM450_REPRO_BAR (:191), _mesh_rung (:219), _mesh_seconds; - from tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_fem.py: SEMI_MAJOR, BOX_HALF_EXTENTS, _semi_minor, _rho_r, _rim_mask (:149), _owned_masked_cells (:164), _numpy_quadrature_mean (:173, degree-8 QDEG), _body_volume_deficit, _ncells; - from test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host: CAVITY_TAG, MAT4_BAND, E0; - pec_oblate_spheroid_field (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:1831) and oblate_spheroid_depolarisation (:1756). - Importing the rim-ladder module runs its knob checks (:117–206); no knob is set. - Records, cited: - I28_PHI_H (the three values above); - I28_MISS_STR = "+0.3900%" / "+0.6506%" / "+0.7762%" (same lines); - I28_DEFICIT_STR = "-5.147e-03" / "-5.148e-03" / "-5.088e-03" and I28_CELLS = 33 334 / 53 959 / 89 530 (…W0r.log:173, :292, :424). - Per rung d ∈ DIVISORS (3, 4, 5; FEM_EM_IMP6_RIM=edge, defaults otherwise), on msh, cell_tags, facet_tags = _mesh_rung(d): - (a) Volume path: V_h, the first moments and I_xx, I_yy, I_zz of the hole, computed as the box's closed-form moments minus Σ over owned air cells of the exact P1-tet moments. The tet moment is ∫_T x_i x_j dV = (|T|/20)·(Σ_k x_i^k x_j^k + (Σ_k x_i^k)(Σ_k x_j^k)); the box term is 8 b_x b_y b_z · b_i²/3. Then reduce. - (b) Surface path (independent): over owned CAVITY_TAG facets, each normal oriented into its one adjacent air cell (outward from the hole): V = Σ∫n dS and I_ii,s = Σ∫(x_i³/3) n_i dS, ing basix's degree-3 triangle rule (exact for cubics). Then reduce. - (c) Vertex extents a_v = max ρ and c_v = max |z| over the wall facets' vertices, reduced with MAX. - (d) a_I, c_I and the hole centroid. - (e) L_x, L_z at (a, c) and at (a_I, c_I) via oblate_spheroid_depolarisation(e) with e = √(1 − (c/a)²). Print 1/L_x at each and (L_x/L_x^I)² − 1, the leading-order rim |E|² scale. - (f) One function _phi_cf(msh, cells, a_, c_) = _numpy_quadrature_mean(msh, cells, lambda p: pec_oblate_spheroid_field(p, semi_major=a_, semi_minor=c_, drive="inplane", e0=E0, interior="continue")), on the rung's own _rim_mask cells. The mask stays nominal: it is the measurement volume. Call it twice: nominal (a, c) and measured (a_I, c_I). A closure counts non-finite |E|² values; the count is reduced and printed. - (g) r_d = I28_PHI_H/Φ_cf(a, c) − 1 and r_d^I = I28_PHI_H/Φ_cf(a_I, c_I) − 1. - All reductions are called on every rank before any if comm.rank == 0: print. The asserts sit outside the branch.

Anchors (asserted). - (Ce) cells == I28_CELLS[d] as integers. This is the mesh of record. - (V0) the nominal call reproduces I28's comparand: |Φ_cf(a, c)/ITEM426_RUNGS[d]["phi_cf_h"] − 1| ≤ ITEM450_REPRO_BAR (5e-8). On rung 4 the bar is also ≤ 1e-12 against ITEM440_R1["phi_cf_h8"]. These are reproduction tolerances, not bands (the 10-14 10:30 ruling, IMP-6.md:935). - (Vr) f"{r_d:+.4%}" == I28_MISS_STR[d]. This is the reading path, as item 305's (Rb). - (V1) f"{_body_volume_deficit(msh, ASPECT):.3e}" == I28_DEFICIT_STR[d], and |V_h/V − 1 − deficit| ≤ 1e-12. - (Mv) the divergence theorem, two paths: |V/V_h − 1| 1e-9 and |I_ii,s/I_ii,h − 1| ≤ 1e-8 for i = x, y, z. These are instrument tolerances, set ≫ round-off. The box cancellation is ≈ 1 200× on I_zz; predicted ≲ 1e-10. - (B) the imported band: |r_d^I| ≤ MAT4_BAND on every rung. - Non-finite count == 0 on both calls (item 428 read 0 on the same continued field, IMP-3.md:1545). - β, |β − 1| ≤ TH15_BETA_BAND and the cavity check are I28's solved records (IMP-6.md:922–926). They are not re-read here because there is no field.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (N-nom), asserted: the corrected path with the nominal axes is (V0). It is the same function on the same cells, backed by I28's (Wk′) / (Wk) on these meshes: 1.325e-8 / 1.199e-14 / 6.947e-10 (…W1a.log:179, …W1b.log:188, …W1c.log:199). A body correction that silently fell back to (a, c) reads r_d^I == r_d to every digit; that is printed as "no correction applied". - Predicted, printed beside, never asserted: - (N-ext) a_v/a − 1 and c_v/c − 1 ≤ 1e-9: the extents carry nothing; - |a_I/a − 1| and |c_I/c − 1| in [1e-4, 5e-3], with c_I/c − 1 more negative than a_I/a − 1 (the sag of the flat faces at grain a/12 weighs more on the thin axis); - a_I and c_I equal across rungs to ≤ 1e-4 relative (the deficit is flat: −5.147 / −5.148 / −5.088e-3; the surface grain a/12 is fixed); - |Φ_cf(a_I, c_I)/Φ_cf(a, c) − 1| in [0.05 %, 3 %], sign not predicted. Two effects compete. A smaller body moves the rim away from the fixed mask (comparand down). A thinner aspect raises 1/L_x and sharpens ρ_r = c²/a (comparand up). - Because the correction is predicted rung-flat, I28's rung trend survives: Δ^I₃₄ within ±0.05 pp of +0.261 pp and Δ^I₄₅ within ±0.05 pp of +0.126 pp.

Reading rule (pre-registered; printed, never asserted; it decides nothing but the row's wording). - (E3-level): |r_d^I| ≤ |r_d| on all three rungs and |r₅^I| ≤ 0.25·|r₅| = 0.194 %. The faceted body accounts for the k → 0 level. - (E3-partial): |r_d^I| < |r_d| on all three rungs, but not (E3-level). - (E3-not): otherwise. - Every threshold is predicted. 0.25 is item 450's (Fix) quarter. - Also printed: r∞^I = r₅^I + Δ^I₄₅·q^I/(1 − q^I) when 0 < q^I < 1, beside I28's ≈ +0.893 %. - Predicted verdict: not (E3-level), because a rung-flat correction cannot remove a rung-rising residual. Whether it is partial or not depends on the unpredicted sign. - Whatever the verdict, the freeze above holds.

Windows (complex, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; I28's Command: shape, 20261014T183126Z_IMP-6-step2d-W0r.log:12). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. - Measured basis: - I28's W0r built all three rungs with the census in 31 s (…W0r.log:491); - item 440's W1q built rung ρ_r/4 and evaluated three comparands in 15 s (20261014T022856Z_IMP-6-step2b-W1q.log:224). - Six degree-8 comparands over 4 861 / 11 468 / 21 548 mask cells, plus the moments, add ≈ 10–30 s. - W0 collect (smoke, ≈ 5 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step2e-W0-collect "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_body_grain.py --collect-only -q'" - W1 (-n 2, the closing window, predicted ≈ 60 s, range [35, 150]): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step2e-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_IMP6_RIM=edge timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_body_grain.py -s -v --tb=short'" - Order: code → W0 → W1 → commit. No module edit after W1 starts (rule (i)). No heavy pre-check: a standard tier, no solve.

Traps already paid for. - A collective inside a rank-0 branch deadlocks (item 440's W1q, IMP-6.md:879). No _ncells, _rss_gib, _body_volume_deficit, _numpy_quadrature_mean, allreduce or facet census inside if comm.rank == 0:. - Never set an FEM_EM_IMP6_* knob other than RIM=edge. The rim-ladder module's one-knob and RUNG2 guards raise at import (:148–152, :202–206). Never set FEM_EM_IMP6_RUNG2. - The default oblate path truncates the rim (known-issues 2026-10-13). RIM=edge is mandatory; (Ce) catches a wrong variant. - Facet orientation: a cavity facet's adjacent cell is its single air cell. Build create_connectivity(2, 3) first and use owned facets only (index_map(2).size_local), or exterior facets are double-counted across ranks. A sign error reads (Mv) at ≈ 2 or ≈ −1, not a small miss. - interior="continue" near the focal ring (a − 0.121 mm): the corrected body's ring sits ≈ a_I − 0.12 mm. Item 428 read no non-finite values on the same construction. A non-zero count is a finding, never masked. - The basis is the in-plane field, drive="inplane", with no −E₀x̂ subtraction: that belongs to β, not to Φ (item 404's trap). - Masks stay in numpy, with no UFL < / sqrt comparison. -s on every window. Node IDs only, never -k. Status 124 means pgrep -c python3 first.

Scope. Aspect 5, the in-plane rim ball, I28's three meshes, one body definition (second moments), and I28's Φ_h. Not covered: - a re-solve; - β against the measured body; - a curvature-matched or locally fitted rim (the moment spheroid is a global summary); - aspect 2; the axial drive; - any band; any fifth sub-step (the freeze).

Status it can move (rule (j)). IMP-6's Done-when covers steps 0 / 1 / 3 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2610), and step 2 is a record. No glyph moves; the row stays ✅. - The step-2 sentence is rewritten to the frozen statement: "≈ +0.9 % at k → 0 on this comparand, not rim grain". It gains the I29 clause: "item 466 (I29): moment-equivalent body a_I/a − 1 ⟨…⟩, c_I/c − 1 ⟨…⟩, L_x ⟨…⟩ → ⟨…⟩; body-corrected miss r^I ⟨…⟩ / ⟨…⟩ / ⟨…⟩ % (⟨verdict⟩); the step-2 family is frozen (10-14 weekly)." - Known-issues 2026-10-13 is untouched: it documents the default builder.

Negative result. - (Ce), (V0), (Vr) or (V1) red: not I28's meshes, or the reading path is wrong. No r^I is printed as a reading. Fix a transcription in-slot and re-run W1; otherwise park on attempt/IMP-6-item466-<ts>, BLOCKED (rule (d)). - (Mv) red: the moment code is wrong (orientation or ownership). Fix it in-slot and re-run W1. It is never a finding about the body. - (B) red (|r_d^I| > MAT4_BAND): a real reading. The measured body moves the comparand by more than the band. Report it, record it on the row as measured, and the freeze still holds: no band moves and no follow-up is posed. Park only if the reading came with any identity red. - Non-finite > 0: report the count and where it is; no r^I is read on that rung. - No PREDICTED RED line.

Every-item rules (PROJECT_PLAN §9 "Every item"): - bare whole harness calls; - a lost docker socket stops the slot; - no edit after the last window; - timeout: 660000 and -s; - never delete a log; - BLOCKED in the parking commit; - a killed window is not a result; - complex mode and FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1; - no slot opens docs/private/ or aed_results/.

Spawn line: "Use the implementer agent to execute IMP-6 §9 item 466 per docs/planning/chunks/IMP-6.md (read the latest Review ruling paragraph first). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Run every window in the foreground with timeout: 660000, pytest with -s, container timeout -k 30. New module tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_body_grain.py only; no src/ edit; never import a test_* name; set no FEM_EM_IMP6_* knob but RIM=edge. Every collective is called before any rank-0 branch. No solve. Compute the pre-registered reading in the outcome; assert none of it. The step-2 family freezes after this item whatever it reads — pose no follow-up."

docs.title: Review ruling 2026-10-15 03:00 (item 466)
docs.text:
Accepted, with the drafter's definition ratified provisionally (for the 10-17 weekly): the meshed body is measured by its second-moment semi-axes (on oblate_rim="edge" every wall node lies on the CAD surface, so node extents read a and c by construction and cannot see the facet error); the node extents are printed as the control. The corrected miss is printed, its sign not predicted. The step-2 family freezes after this item whatever it reads (10-14 weekly): no fifth sub-step; the row carries the residual as a stated level. Known-issues 2026-10-13 (the oblate builder) leaves only when that freeze is written on the row.

Outcome (2026-10-15 07:30 CDT slot, take-next, DONE; reading E3-not). Code: new test module only (tests/validation/test_imp6_oblate_body_grain.py), no src/ edit, no knob but RIM=edge. Two windows, -n 2, complex: 20261015T125644Z_IMP-6-step2e-W0-collect.log (5 collected, 2 s), 20261015T125651Z_IMP-6-step2e-W1.log (5 passed, 29 s; predicted ≈ 60 s, range [35, 150] — under the range). - Anchors, all green (log :169–:451): (Ce) 33 334 / 53 959 / 89 530; (V0) 1.325e-8 / 1.118e-9 / 6.947e-10 (rung 4 vs item 440: 1.199e-14); (N-nom) the nominal path reproduces I28's (Wk′)/(Wk) to the printed digit; (Vr) +0.3900 / +0.6506 / +0.7762 %; (V1) −5.147e-3 / −5.148e-3 / −5.088e-3, identity 0 / 4.7e-15 / 4.8e-15; (Mv) |V_s/V_h − 1| ≤ 3.6e-15, |I_s/I_h − 1| ≤ 9.0e-12 (rung 4, I_zz); cavity facets 4 178 / 4 918 / 6 032, each with exactly one adjacent cell; non-finite 0 on all six calls; (B) |r^I| ≤ MAT4_BAND. - Measured body: (N-ext) a_v/a − 1 = 2.2e-16, c_v/c − 1 = 0 (as predicted). a_I/a − 1 = −2.170e-3 / −2.169e-3 / −2.129e-3; c_I/c − 1 = −8.09e-4 / −8.13e-4 / −8.32e-4; c_I/a_I 0.20027 (nominal 0.20000). Centroid ≤ 2.2e-7 m. 1/L_x 8.015515 → 8.006876 / 8.006914 / 8.007285; (L_x/L_x^I)² − 1 = −0.216 / −0.215 / −0.205 %. - Comparand: Φ_cf(a_I, c_I)/Φ_cf(a, c) − 1 = −3.535 / −3.533 / −3.472 %. Body-corrected miss r^I = +4.068 / +4.337 / +4.401 % beside I28's +0.390 / +0.651 / +0.776 %. Δ^I₃₄ = +0.269 pp, Δ^I₄₅ = +0.064 pp, q^I = 0.238, r∞^I = +4.42 % (I28 ≈ +0.893 %). - Reading rule: E3-not (predicted: not E3-level — met). Predictions missed, reported (rule (e), none asserted): the comparand moved −3.5 %, outside [0.05 %, 3 %]; a_I shrinks more than c_I (−2.17e-3 vs −8.2e-4), the reverse of "c more negative"; Δ^I₄₅ = +0.064 pp is outside ±0.05 pp of +0.126. a_I / c_I are rung-flat to ≈ 2e-5 relative on c, ≈ 4e-5 on a (within the 1e-4 prediction). - Reading: the moment spheroid is ≈ 0.22 % smaller in a, and the in-plane rim field near ρ = a falls steeply with distance from the rim, so a rim moved inward by ≈ 13 µm against a fixed nominal mask drops the comparand by ≈ 3.5 %. The meshed rim itself is not displaced (its nodes are on the CAD surface), so a global moment summary is the wrong body for a rim-local comparand: the faceting deficit lives on the flat faces, not at the rim. This sharpens the frozen statement rather than moving it — the ≈ +0.9 % k → 0 residual is not the global body-volume deficit. - Freeze: the step-2 family is frozen (10-14 weekly); nothing is posed. Note for the weekly (not a proposal): a curvature-matched or rim-local body measure is the only body variant this reading leaves open, and the brief's Scope excludes it. Known-issues 2026-10-13 is left untouched per the brief ("it documents the default builder"); the 03:00 ruling's removal condition is now met on the row — the review decides.

docs.title: §9 item 482 — 2026-10-15 (§10 chain I31; lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted for the 2026-10-15 18:00 daily review; the review rules on it. IMP-6 step 4: the disc in the F-clinical phantom. implant_spheroid (kept, the GEO-36 step 7 body) composed with C2's tagged ASTM box (phantom_box, GEO-38 step 2, item 470, landed c1b8debc). CAD identities only. Licence: §10 I31 (the 10-14 weekly: "all new human-scale implant work moves to F-clinical (chain C, I31)"), Phase 7 (7b), §9 rule (4). No band, tolerance, target or Done-when moves; every band is imported.

Executor and cost. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: heavy (1200 s ceiling), build-only, real image (C2's box module ran real). Container timeout -k 30 590 on every build window. - Ranks: -n 4 for the window of record. C2's three widths built the same mesh (1 149 150 cells at -n 1 / 2 / 4), and -n 4 measured fastest: 339 s, against 382 s at -n 1 and 529 s at -n 2. The -n 2 window lost ≈ 160 s to host load, 61 s from the ceiling. A missing reduction shows at any width > 1. The chain line says -n 2; that deviation is for the review (below). - Cost: ≈ 23 measured (chain no-solve class median) / ≈ 55 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 20 code (≈ 30 lines of src/, a ≈ 220-line module lifted from two existing modules) + ≈ 17 of windows: W0 ≈ 10 s, W1 ≈ 430 s, R1 ≈ 340 s, R2 ≈ 175 s. - Depends on nothing. C2 is on main. - No take-next. At ≈ 55 min there is no slack for a second item.

Why src/ must change (three defects in today's code, each read off src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py): 1. The refusal. birdcage_port_domain refuses phantom_box with implant_spheroid (:4552–4555), so the composition cannot be built today. 2. The containment test. With phantom_box set, phantom_radius becomes the box's xy circumradius hypot(0.21, 0.045) = 0.214767 m (:4573). _normalise_implant_spheroid then applies its cylinder test, |centre_xy| + a < R (:5036–5039). For a 90 mm-deep box that test is not conservative: a disc centred at y = 0.040 m passes it with a 166 mm margin while poking 1 mm out of the top of the gel. 3. The conductor mass. conductor_cad_mass is the can's mass read before the implant cut (shield_air_cad_mass, :5660) minus the cut air (:5914). The implant cut (:5857–5862) has already taken the body out of that air. With a body present the diagnostic therefore reads conductor + V, and C2's (V1) partition would miss by V / can = 4.350023e-7, 435× STRIP_BAND.

src/ change (rule (c): keyword-only, additive, disclosed; ≈ 30 lines). Every phantom_box=None path must execute the lines it executes today. - (a) Composition. The phantom_box refusal keeps implant_rod (scope: one body, the disc) and drops implant_spheroid. New message: "phantom_box cannot be combined with implant_rod". No test matches the old string (grep of tests/, 2026-10-15). - (b) Box containment. _normalise_implant_spheroid gains keyword-only phantom_box: Optional[Dict] = None. - When it is set, the containment test is the box test: |c_x| + a < Lx/2, |c_y − off| + a < Ly/2 and |c_z| + a < Lz/2, all strict. The bounding sphere of radius a is conservative for any axis. - Refusal message: "implant_spheroid is not strictly inside the phantom_box". - When phantom_box is None, the existing cylinder test runs unchanged. - Both call sites pass the normalised phantom_box: the public one (:4587) and the builder's (:5269). - (c) Conductor mass. In the phantom_box + shield_radius branch (:5910–5916), when an implant body was cut from the air, also subtract its OCC mass (rod_occ_mass, set at :5823). Write it as a separate if on the implant, so that the no-implant line is not rewritten. - The diagnostic then means what its name says. - Disclose this as a definition repair of item 470's diagnostic. It is not a band. - Docstrings. One sentence each on phantom_box and implant_spheroid. - Not changed: - implant_rod with phantom_box stays refused; - the spheroid's sizing fields, construction and tags (402 / 403); - the box's own CAD; - GEO-38 step 1a's shield and corner refusals.

Fixture. - Kwargs: _box_kwargs() (tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_box.py:54, item 470's r1 kwargs with the box) plus implant_spheroid = dict(SPHEROID, keep_cells=True), with SPHEROID from tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid.py:76. - Body and placement: a = 6 mm, c = 1.2 mm, centre (0.015, 0, 0), axis x̂. This is GEO-36 step 7's body and placement, so RIM_POINTS, _rim_census, _spheroid_volume, _spheroid_area and _inside_true_spheroid import unchanged. - Inside the box: |c_x| + a = 0.021 < 0.21, |c_y| + a = 0.006 < 0.045, |c_z| + a = 0.006 < 0.325. - The placement is a modelling choice, and the item claims nothing for it. ASTM F2182's high-E site near a lateral wall belongs to the solve step that follows, with the operator's source.

New module tests/validation/test_imp6_disc_f_clinical.py. - Selection: the build test is selected by FEM_EM_IMP6_STEP4=1 only, never by -k, and skips when the variable is unset. The refusal tests are pure and always run. - Imports, by name only, never a test_* symbol: - _box_kwargs (box module); - _ring_ports, _owned, _facet_coords, _area, LEG_COUNT (tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_build.py); - SPHEROID, SPHEROID_CENTRE, SPHEROID_SEMI_MAJOR, _rim_census, _spheroid_volume, _spheroid_area (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid.py); - _interior_facet_check (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_rod.py:184); - _census_checks, _owned_census (tests/validation/test_wf12_f_human_hole.py, as C2 imports them); - _interface_facet_tags (fem_em_solver.io.mesh); SHEET_IFACE, PORT_LOWER, PORT_UPPER (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets.py); - the bands: STRIP_BAND (1e-9, tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58), CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND (1e-7) and EXACT (1e-9) (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_conductor_hole.py:117, :123), TERMINAL_AREA_BAND ((0.95, 1.0), tests/mesh/test_birdcage_leg_gaps.py:73). - Do not import tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid_f_human.py. It only ever ran in the complex image, and it imports the WF-12 copper-matrix module. This module runs real. - New constants: - F_CLINICAL_DISC_CELL_GUARD = 1_400_000: a guard, checked before any facet reading; the predicted count plus ≈ 17 % headroom, as F-human's 600 000 sat over 417 653. - C2_CONDUCTOR_CAD_MASS_M3 = 1.994040484843362e-03: printed comparand only, cited to 20261015T185056Z_GEO-38-s2-W3-n4.log:11903. - One build per process. No cell record is written into code: rule (i) forbids an edit after the last window. The cells go in this file and on the row.

Anchors (asserted at -n 4; owned cells / facets, every count reduced, collectives before any rank-0 branch). - (D0) Guard. Cells < F_CLINICAL_DISC_CELL_GUARD before any facet reading. - (D1) Body CAD. - body_mass_m3 = V = 4πa²c/3 = 1.809557368e-7 m³ at CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND. - The OCC wall_area_m2 = A = 2.473638076e-4 m² at CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND. - Step 7 read 2.2e-16 and 2.451e-11. - (D2) Box / body CAD partition. With L³ = Lx·Ly·Lz from _box_kwargs(), never retyped: - CAD(403) = kept_mass_m3 = body_mass_m3 at STRIP_BAND; - CAD(3) = L³ − body_mass_m3 at STRIP_BAND; - CAD(3) + CAD(403) = L³ at STRIP_BAND. - These are step 7's (H1)–(H3) with the box for the cylinder. Predicted ≈ 1e-16: C2's phantom group read 0.024569999999999995. - (D3) Meshed partition. - The owned tag-3 and tag-403 tet volumes, summed and reduced, = L³ at STRIP_BAND. The box is planar-faced and the 3 / 403 interface facets are shared, so the union is exact. Predicted ≈ 1e-16; C2's (B1) read 1.110e-16 at -n 4. - The tag-3 vertex extents equal C2's (B2) box extents at STRIP_BAND. - (D4) Can partition with the body. Σ cad_mass_by_group + conductor_cad_mass_m3 = air_domain_cad_mass_m3 at STRIP_BAND. This is C2's (V1), which needs src/ change (c). Predicted ≈ 4.8e-11 (C2: 4.780e-11). - (D5) Interface. _interior_facet_check on 402: - owned count > 0, exterior 0; - every owned facet is interior, between one tag-3 and one tag-403 cell; - meshed dS(402) / A inside TERMINAL_AREA_BAND. - Call msh.topology.create_entity_permutations() unconditionally on every rank first (the standing 3b-iv caution). - (D6) Centroid. The OCC wall centroid lies at SPHEROID_CENTRE to EXACT·a. - (D7) Rim fidelity. _rim_census gives n_mask > 0, n_inside 0, n403 > 0 and n403_outside 0. That is item 408's defect, made a gate, on the box path. - (D8) Census. - _census_checks(census, n_cells, _ring_ports()) is empty; - tags 3 and 403 are present, with no tag 1; - implant_rod_cad is None. - If the coil cavity swallowed the body, the 402 facets would read exterior, and (D5) catches that. - (D9) Ports undisturbed. Per ring sheet: owned facets of 210+i (reduced) = ring_sheet_gmsh_triangles[i] on 64 / 64 sheets, and area = chord·w at STRIP_BAND. These are C2's (T1) and (T2) area clause, using owned-facet numpy sums, never UFL dS. - (D10) Refusals (pure; _refuse_before_gmsh's tripwire pattern, tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_build.py:384): - the planted poke-out (N3) is refused before gmsh; - implant_rod with phantom_box is still refused; - a hole spheroid (keep_cells=False) under as_hole is still refused; - the kept request with the box is accepted by _normalise_implant_spheroid (it returns keep_cells True).

Negative controls (rule (e): each factor labelled). - (N1) The C2 comparand misses (D2). Asserted binary, factor predicted. - CAD(3) against L³ misses by body_mass_m3 / (L³ − body_mass_m3). Predicted 7.364960e-6, 7.36e3× STRIP_BAND. - That factor is also the ceiling: it is a fixed geometric quantity, not a saturating one. - Assert the miss > STRIP_BAND and print it with the factor. - Meaning: a build that silently dropped the body passes C2's (B1) and fails (D2). - (N2) The pre-repair conductor reading misses (D4). Asserted by construction, factor predicted. - (Σ groups + conductor_cad_mass_m3 + body_mass_m3) / can − 1 is the diagnostic as item 470 defined it. Predicted 4.350023e-7, 435× STRIP_BAND. - Assert the miss > STRIP_BAND. - Meaning: (D4) can see a body-sized accounting error. - (N3) A planted poke-out, the control for src/ change (b). Both outcomes asserted (W0). - The request: centre (0.015, 0.040, 0), a = 6 mm. - With phantom_box=None and R = 0.214767 m, H = 0.65 m, _normalise_implant_spheroid accepts it: a margin of 0.214767 − 0.048720 = 0.166 m. - With the box it refuses it before gmsh: |c_y| + a = 0.046 > 0.045, a 1 mm breach. - Separation: accept vs refuse, binary by construction. - (N4) The body's mesh is coil-independent. Predicted, printed only. - The tag-403 cell count = 14 047 and meshed 403 / V = 0.995984, as on F-human (20261013T203250Z_GEO-36-step7-W2b.log:6269, :6295). The sizing fields that reach the body are its own: the coil is ≥ 0.33 m away. - A different count is a reading, never a red. - The conductor mass against C2_CONDUCTOR_CAD_MASS_M3 is also printed only, predicted ≤ 1e-9. OCC's partition noise on this can is ≈ 2e-11 m³, which is ≈ 1e-8 relative to a 2e-3 m³ mass, so an assertion at STRIP_BAND would be the rule-(f) trap.

Printed predictions, written first. - Cells: 1 149 150 + [35 k, 100 k], point ≈ 1 197 416. Step 7 added 48 266 to F-human at the same resolution and body sizing. - Build at -n 4: ≈ 400 s [380, 510]. - The gmsh wall over C2's 310 s is predicted at +[50, 170] s. On F-human the body took the gmsh wall from 97.65 s (20261013T204028Z_GEO-36-step7-W3b-regate.log) to 158.68 s (…203250Z_…-W2b.log:6264), +61 s. - The upper end assumes the field-evaluation share scales with the ≈ 3.1× cell count. - The window is predicted at ≈ build + 25 s. - Unknowns: E, F, U₁ = E and U₂ = 2E + 2F, printed. They are the price input for the solve step the weekly will pose. - Memory: summed RSS ≈ 2.7 GiB (C2: 2.61 GiB at -n 4).

Windows. - General: foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; each harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative; -s on every window; node IDs only; durable capture verbatim, trailing ; exit $rc included. - Pre-checks before every build window: - docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0; - also run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver cat /proc/loadavg and journal the reading. - Order: code → W0 → W1 → R1 → R2 → commit → journal. Every window runs on the final files. - If the 1-min load is above 24 before W1, run R2 (the cheapest) first, then re-read the load and run W1. - Two heavy windows never run at once. - W0 (pure refusals plus the existing refusal tests; The disc module, additive only. - Import the helper by name. - The build test takes monkeypatch, and before the builder call (:191) runs if gmsh_stop_armed(): arm_gmsh_stop_rule(monkeypatch, comm, "IMP-6 s4"). - One print states whether the rule is armed. - Nothing else in the module or in src/ changes. With FEM_EM_GMSH_STOP_RULE unset, the module is the parked one.

Anchors. (D0)–(D10) exactly as in item 482, asserted at -n 4, owned and reduced, collectives before any rank-0 branch.

Imported bands (by name, never retyped). - STRIP_BAND 1e-9 (tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58); - CAD_ANALYTIC_BAND 1e-7 and EXACT 1e-9 (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_conductor_hole.py:123, :117); - TERMINAL_AREA_BAND (0.95, 1.0) (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_leg_gaps.py:73).

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (N1)–(N4) as in item 482. (N3) is now asserted on a measurement: cylinder margin 0.166047 m, box breach 1.000000e-03 m (20261016T020256Z_IMP-6-step4-W0-refusals.log:44–45). (N1)'s 7.36e3× and (N2)'s 435× stay predicted factors, because no W1 anchor was ever read. The builder's CAD print, body = kept = 1.809557368468e-07 m³ (20261016T020315Z_…:92), is a printed reading only. - (N5) The stop rule itself. Asserted by construction, in W0, in subprocesses ([sys.executable, "-c", …], importing only the helper): - (N5a) Armed at 1 s around ctypes.CDLL(None).sleep(3), a C call through ctypes as gmsh's API is. The subprocess returns GMSH_STOP_RC with the marker on stdout, in < 2.9 s. - (N5b) Armed at 2 s around usleep(100000) and then cancelled. It returns 0 and prints no marker. - (N5c) gmsh.lib is a ctypes.CDLL and not a ctypes.PyDLL, so the GIL is released during meshing. - Separation: fires vs silent, binary. - Printed, never asserted: the host factors h₂ = R2 gmsh / 158.68 s and h₁ = R1 gmsh / 310.01 s, and before W1 the prediction T̂ = R1 gmsh × [1.29, 1.47, 1.55].

Windows. Foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; each harness call is the whole Bash command; -s; durable capture verbatim, ending ; exit \$rc. Before each of R2, R1 and W1, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3, which must read 0, then docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver cat /proc/loadavg, and journal the reading. Order: code → W0 → R2 → R1 → W1 → commit → journal. The re-gates run first so that the code can land on any W1 outcome. Every window runs on the final files (rule (i)). - W0 (pure; ≈ 15 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step4-a2-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/validation/test_gmsh_stop_rule.py tests/validation/test_imp6_disc_f_clinical.py tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid.py::test_s9_refusals_raise_without_meshing tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid.py::test_s9_kept_accepted_with_as_hole tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_build.py::test_geo38_shield_refuses_attempt1_table tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_build.py::test_geo38_shield_refuses_leg_gap_length -v -s --tb=short'" - R2 (rule-(c) re-gate of the F-human phantom_box=None path, and the cheap calibrant; complex; 172–344 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step4-a2-R2-ruleC-GEO-36-step7-W2b "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 420 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/mesh/test_birdcage_implant_spheroid_f_human.py -s -v --tb=short'" It must read item 482's R2 list bitwise (20261013T203250Z_GEO-36-step7-W2b.log:6266–6295). Print h₂. - R1 (rule-(c) re-gate of C2, and the direct calibrant; ≈ 340 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step4-a2-R1-ruleC-GEO-38-s2-n4 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_GEO38_STEP2=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 4 python3 -m pytest tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_box.py -s -v --tb=short > /workspace/logs/imp6-s4a2-r1-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/imp6-s4a2-r1-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/imp6-s4a2-r1-raw.log; exit \$rc'" It must read item 482's R1 list bitwise (20261015T185056Z_GEO-38-s2-W3-n4.log:11897–11908). Print h₁ and T̂. - W1 (the window of record, -n 4, rule armed; ≤ ≈ 495 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-6-step4-a2-W1-n4 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_IMP6_STEP4=1 FEM_EM_GMSH_STOP_RULE=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 4 python3 -m pytest tests/validation/test_imp6_disc_f_clinical.py -s -v --tb=short > /workspace/logs/imp6-s4a2-w1-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/imp6-s4a2-w1-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/imp6-s4a2-w1-raw.log; exit \$rc'" - How the rule is recorded. Under the rule, the log prints the under the rule: <t> s line, then [birdcage-mesh] mesh wall time T s, which is the price, then the anchors. - A stop prints the gmsh phase lines completed so far, then GMSH_STOP_MARKER, then the [capture] rc= footer, which reads non-zero. The marker line is the record, not the rc. - The fallback. A Timeout (0:08:00)! traceback with no marker means the Timer did not fire and the faulthandler fallback stopped the build. That is a helper defect, and the item reports it.

Traps already paid for. Item 482's list holds. Added: - The lift. A path checkout of a record file from an attempt/* branch deletes main's rows (8d4cf58, rubric 4). Only the two code paths come over. - The subprocess and MPI. The (N5) children must not import mpi4py, and the controls never run under -n > 1. That is why the helper is stdlib-only and its tests sit in their own module. - The stop is not a kill. After a stop, pgrep -c python3 must still read 0 before the commit. Run the rubric-4 orphan-stem sweep only on a ceiling kill (Status 124 without the marker). No FFCx compile runs before gmsh finishes. - No rule outside W1. Never set FEM_EM_GMSH_STOP_RULE in R1 or R2: they are bitwise re-gates, not priced builds. Never set it in an xl command either. Unset is the default path. - Never retry. Neither a stop nor a kill is retried, at a higher width or in a later slot (epitaph). No third heavy attempt.

Scope. Item 482's scope, plus the price. Not claimed: a solve, a placement claim, the rod in the box (I33, item 530), or a cost model beyond the printed T̂. IMP-6 stays ✅ and GEO-38 stays 🟡.

What each outcome means, and what happens to the branch. - GREEN. T ≤ 450 s, (D0)–(D10) green, and R1 / R2 bitwise. - Commit the lifted src/ and module, the helper and its tests, the four logs, and the IMP-6 row clause from item 482 (:1270), giving T and the cell count. - Item 522 is DONE, and item 530 becomes runnable (its gate). - Branch: the next daily review deletes attempt/IMP-6-20261016T020000Z. Before deleting, it checks that git diff main attempt/IMP-6-20261016T020000Z -- src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py is empty and that the module's diff is only the helper lines. - STOPPED AT THE RULE. The marker is in the log, and R1 / R2 are bitwise. This is the item's priced outcome, not a red. - The code still lands on main, with the rule off by default. This is item 494's precedent (GEO-38.md:569), so that the xl window can run the same module from main. - Item 522 is DONE as "priced: gmsh > 450 s at -n 4, phases <…>, h₁ / h₂ <…>". The §10 I31 line gets the price. - The xl 10-25 build is the weekly's to pre-register. Its command is W1's with FEM_EM_GMSH_STOP_RULE unset. The implementer writes no xl-pending.md text. - In the same commit, mark item 530 BLOCKED, to xl. - Branch: deleted by the next review, as for GREEN. - R1 or R2 not bitwise. Revert src/, so nothing lands. - Park the lifted files and the helper on attempt/IMP-6-step4-a2-<UTC>, and mark items 522 and 530 BLOCKED (rule (d)). - Branch: keep the old branch until the review confirms the new one is a superset of it. - (D) red under the rule. Report and stop. Park everything on attempt/IMP-6-step4-a2-<UTC>, mark items 522 and 530 BLOCKED, and send nothing to xl until the review rules. - The reds are item 482's: a gmsh FAIL (recorded verbatim, with a known-issues entry), (D2) / (D3), (D4) at ≈ 4.35e-7, and (D5) / (D7). - Branch: as above. - Killed at the container ceiling without the marker. Not a result; the helper failed. Run pgrep and the sweep, then park as above and mark BLOCKED. The build goes to xl regardless. - Skipped by the slot-time gate, or deferred at minute 42: nothing changes, and the branch stays. - A printed reading outside its prediction (cells, T, h, (N4)) is a reading, never a red.

No PREDICTED RED line: the stop is not an assertion. Any other red stops the slot.

Status it can move. - On GREEN: the IMP-6 row's step-4 clause (✅ stays; rule (j) does not bind) and §10 I31's DONE line. The printed E / F / U₂ become the price input of the F-clinical disc solve. - On a stop: §10 I31 gains its price, and the xl 10-25 entry becomes poseable by the weekly. I33 moves to BLOCKED → xl.

For the review to rule on. 1. The rule sits on the predicted point (454 s [401, 482] at h = 1). Decide whether attempt 2 is worth its slot, or whether I31 goes straight to xl 10-25. 2. An optional calibrant gate. Skip W1, and defer to the next eligible slot, when T̂(low) = 1.29 × R1 gmsh > 450 s (that is, R1 gmsh > 348 s). Default: printed only, per the weekly's letter. 3. Landing the code on a stop, under item 494's precedent. 4. The FEM_EM_GMSH_STOP_RULE helper as the shared mechanism for I33.

Every-item rules (PROJECT_PLAN §9 "Every item"): - bare whole harness calls; - a lost docker socket stops the slot; - no edit after the last window; - timeout: 660000 and -s; - never delete a log; - BLOCKED in the parking commit; - a killed window is not a result; - two heavy windows never at once; - no slot opens docs/private/ or aed_results/.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Execute §9 item 522 — IMP-6 step 4 attempt 2 (§10 I31) — per docs/planning/chunks/IMP-6.md §9 item 522. Read the brief and any review ruling beneath it first; the rulings hold. Run it only if this session's start line reads 12:00, 13:30 or 15:00 (≤ 5 min late) and it is the slot's first item; otherwise skip it silently. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a window; run pytest with -s; container timeout -k 30. Lift only src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py and tests/validation/test_imp6_disc_f_clinical.py from attempt/IMP-6-20261016T020000Z (path checkout after the e06c8a4a guard, else cherry-pick --no-commit 8d6ffdd1); never path-checkout any other file. Add tests/validation/gmsh_stop_rule.py and tests/validation/test_gmsh_stop_rule.py, and the armed-rule lines in the disc module; nothing else. Run W0, R2, R1, W1 in order, foreground, on the final files; W1 only by minute 42; set FEM_EM_GMSH_STOP_RULE=1 in W1 only. R1 and R2 must read their logs' numbers bitwise or you revert src/ and stop. A stop at the rule is the priced outcome: land the code, mark item 530 BLOCKED to xl, write no xl-pending.md text. Never retry a stop, a kill or a gmsh failure. You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command string. On a red, park on attempt/IMP-6-step4-a2-*, mark items 522 and 530 BLOCKED in the same commit, and report."

docs.title: Review ruling 2026-10-18 03:00 (item 522, I31 attempt 2)
docs.text: Accepted as the weekly posed it: a daytime heavy window with a 450 s gmsh stop rule, in the 12:00 / 13:30 / 15:00 slots only. A slot at any other time skips it, and the skip costs no attempt. 1. Worth a slot: yes. The weekly's design makes a stop at the rule a result: the build's price is recorded and the build goes to xl 10-25. The drafter's prediction, 454 s [401, 482] on a quiet host, is printed beside the measured value. 2. No skip rule. W1 runs whatever the C2 re-gate reads, and the re-gate's gmsh time is printed as a slow-host indicator. A third heavy attempt is never queued (10-17 epitaph). 3. The code lands on main after a green build, or after a stop at the rule when both re-gate builds reproduce their logged numbers exactly (item 494's precedent). The xl window can then run from main. docs.title: IMP-7 — history
docs.text:
Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record once the review adds it. Proposed 2026-10-20 for the 18:00 daily review under §9 rule (5) lane 3 (Phases 7 / 8), for the weekly to ratify or re-home.

Why this chunk. Every Phase 7 row says "no heating": IMP-1 … IMP-6 gate the near-implant field, and Phase 8 (MAT-9 … MAT-21) heats spheres, cylinders and boxes with no implant. No closed form in the repo joins the two. IMP-7 is that join on the simplest implant: IMP-1's PEC sphere (a = 5 mm), whose quasi-static dipole field gives a near-implant SAR that heats a Robin-cooled gel shell around a thermally conducting core. The steady temperature is an exact two-term Legendre series (l = 0 and l = 2). It reduces to MAT-18's two-layer sphere when the dipole is switched off, and it gives the implant's own heating factor and pole / equator hot spot in closed form.

Sources. - Field: the PEC sphere in a uniform quasi-static field, β = 1, as TH-15 and IMP-1 gate it (tests/validation/test_pec_sphere_hole.py:3–14, test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py:4–16). The general dipole β = (ε − 1)/(ε + 2) is dielectric_sphere_quasistatic_field (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:595–626). - Legendre: Jin 3e App. E §E.3, eqs (E.34)–(E.36) (docs/references/jin-fem-3e/appE_special-functions.md:119–135). The equation bodies are image placeholders, so only the numbers are cited. - Conduction: Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids 2e, ch. IX (the sphere), the same pointer and footing as MAT-9 … MAT-18 (analytical.py:2530–2532). Equation numbers are not pinned (the repo holds no copy); the docstring derives every form. - No published implant-heating datum is claimed. (7c) still waits on the operator's reference (dashboard W3).

docs.title: Proposed §7 row
docs.text: | IMP-7 | (history and §9 briefs: docs/planning/chunks/IMP-7.md) SAR heating around a PEC-sphere implant in a Robin-cooled gel ball: the implant-heating canonical in closed form (Phase 7 × Phase 8) (proposed by the 2026-10-20 18:00 daily under rule (5) lane 3; for the weekly to ratify or re-home). IMP-1's sphere (a = 5 mm) as a thermally conducting core (k₁) inside a gel shell (k₂ 0.6) to b = 4a, Robin h 100 on r = b. The source is q = q_far·|E|²/E₀² of the quasi-static dipole field (β = 1 PEC) in the shell and zero in the core. θ = T − T∞ = Σ_{l=0,2} R_l(r)P_l(cos ϑ), exact. Done-when: step 0 (numpy, §9 item 579): the source, radial-PDE, interface, Robin, balance and FD-Laplacian identities and the β = 0 → MAT-18 and Φ → IMP-1 reductions at the bands in the chunk file; three controls miss ⇒ 🟡. Step 1 (FEM, real build, P1 ladder + P2 on two_layer_ball_domain(inner_radius=a, outer_radius=b)): MAT-18 step 2(a)'s gates — interior rel L2 ≤ 1 %, P1 L2 rate ≥ 1.7, balance ≤ 1e-9 — on the metal core (DG0 k) and on the adiabatic hole (shell submesh, where the l = 2 part is ≈ 13 % of θ at the pole), with the isotropic-source and β = 0 controls missing ⇒ ✅. Bands for any l = 2 moment are the review's when it briefs step 1. Not claimed: a FEM SAR source (a later step, composed band as MAT-10), finite k, a rod or tip, a coil, transient, perfusion, published data. | ⬜ Open. | step 0 standard, no MPI, real; step 1 standard / heavy, -n 2, real |

docs.title: §9 item 579 — 2026-10-20 (lane 3; IMP-7 step 0, closed form)
docs.text:
Drafted read-only for the 2026-10-20 18:00 daily review; the review rules on it.

Licence. §9 rule (5) lane 3 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3937–3948): a Phase 7/8 chunk whose validation target is a closed form, named in the dashboard for the weekly to ratify. Precedents: IMP-4 / IMP-5 / IMP-6 / MAT-21, each opened by a daily at step 0 and then ratified. Independent of every §10 chain (H/C/I/T/P/U and their xl entries) and of the queued items 556, 574, 542, 553 and 560. Nothing waits on the operator. This brief moves no existing band. Every bound below is imported by name, except (Rk)'s ratio window, which is flagged for the review.

IMP-7 step 0: the steady temperature around IMP-1's PEC sphere heated by its own dipole SAR, numpy only. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, no mpiexec (-n 1), real build. - Class: lane-3 closed form. Cost: ≈ 9.7 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 code + one ≈ 0.5-min window + spare). - Depends on: nothing. Family: step 0, attempt 1 of 4. - Comparable windows: IMP-4-step0-W1 55 s (-n 2, test-results.md:2980); IMP-6-step0-W1 3–4 s (no MPI, :3986–3988); IMP-1-step3a-W1 45 s (real build, importing the IMP-1 module, :2699).

Fixture (rule (f) parameters, not bands): - a = SPHERE_RADIUS = 0.005 (test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py:61) and b = 4a = 0.02. b is chosen so step 1's uniform 1 mm mesh stays below MAT-18 step 2(a)'s finest rung. - k₂ = MAT-9's K = 0.6 and q_far = Q = 2000 W/m³ (test_mat9_steady_conduction_sphere.py:37–39). - h = MAT-10's H = 100 (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:53), so Bi = hb/k₂ = 3.33. T∞ = 20. - k₁ (the core): K_CORE = 20.0, metal-like and representative, not a material claim (MAT-18's wording). Two exact branches as well: k_core=0.0 (adiabatic: the core is excluded, as on IMP-1's hole mesh) and k_core=np.inf (isothermal core). - β = 1 (PEC). β = −½ (void) and β = ½ are used for cross-checks only.

The closed form. The docstring derives every line. Let μ = z/r, u = (a/r)³ and E = E₀ẑ + βE₀a³(3(ẑ·r̂)r̂ − ẑ)/r³ for r > a. - Source. |E|²/E₀² = (1 + 2βu)²μ² + (1 − βu)²(1 − μ²) = 1 + 2β²u² + (4βu + 2β²u²)P₂(μ). In the shell, q = q_far × that; in the core, q = 0. At β = 1 this is 9 at the poles of r = a and 0 at its equator. - l = 0, shell: R₀ = A₀ + B₀/r − q_far r²/(6k₂) − β²q_far a⁶/(6k₂r⁴). The core is constant, R₀ = A₀ (zero net flux at r = a for every k₁). This gives: - B₀ = (2β² − 1)q_far a³/(3k₂); - θ₀(b) = q_far(b³ − a³ + 2β²a³ − 2β²a⁶/b³)/(3hb²); - A₀ = θ₀(b) − B₀/b + q_far b²/(6k₂) + β²q_far a⁶/(6k₂b⁴). - l = 2, shell: R₂ = D r² + E r⁻³ + C₁/r + C₂/r⁴, with C₁ = 2βq_far a³/(3k₂) and C₂ = −β²q_far a⁶/(3k₂). The particular solutions come from Δ_l rⁿ = [n(n + 1) − 6]rⁿ⁻². The core is F r². - Conditions: R₂(a⁻) = R₂(a⁺); k₁R₂′(a⁻) = k₂R₂′(a⁺); k₂R₂′(b) + hR₂(b) = 0. - Eliminate F = R₂(a)/a² and solve the 2 × 2 system for (D, E) by Cramer's rule. - Adiabatic branch: R₂′(a⁺) = 0. Isothermal branch: R₂(a⁺) = 0. - Total power: P = (4πq_far/3)(b³ − a³ + 2β²a³ − 2β²a⁶/b³) = 4πb²hθ₀(b). Only l = 0 crosses r = b.

Code (append at the end of src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py, after coated_pec_cylinder_tm0_current, :3116, under an IMP-7 step 0 banner; additive, numpy only): - pec_sphere_implant_source(points, *, radius, q_far, beta=1.0): (N, 3) → q, zero for r < a. - pec_sphere_implant_coefficients(*, radius, outer_radius, k_core, k_gel, q_far, h, beta=1.0) → a dict of A₀, B₀, C₁, C₂, D, E, F. k_core takes 0.0 and np.inf as explicit branches. - pec_sphere_implant_radial(r, coeffs, l, *, derivative=0) → R_l and its first and second derivatives in the shell (analytic power laws). - pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature(points, *, radius, outer_radius, k_core, k_gel, q_far, h, t_inf, beta=1.0) → T. Core points return T∞ + A₀ + F r²P₂, or NaN on the adiabatic branch. - Test: tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_closed_form.py, prefix IMP7-0.

Anchors (asserted). The only §10 mentions of the file are :4818 and :4930, both IMP-7. - P45 (:4904–4914) re-uses MAT-21 / MAT-20 operators. - U74–U76 are package code. - C10 / C12 and I36a are GEO-38 / GEO-36 modules. - H30–H32 are the ans:8 record route. - TH-5 step 3 (the PML) is the one step with plausible closed-form content. For the review. 1. Three of the eight bands are literals restated by value, not named imports (correction 2). This is the MAT4_BAND / MAT-18 2(a) practice. Accept it, or name the anchors as unimportable. 2. (FD)'s 1e-4 level is transplanted. In IMP-1 (H) it bounds a curl-curl residual normalised by |k²E|. Here it bounds a 7-point Laplacian residual normalised by 9q_far. The [3.8, 4.2] ratio is the same second-order signature (central-difference truncation), but the level is applied to a new quantity. Predicted 1.1e-5, which is ≈ 9× inside. The review may keep both, or demote the level to printed and keep the ratio. 3. Correction 5 (the extra dict keys; pec_sphere_implant_radial unmasked) is relied on by item 594. 4. Shared file: confirm that TH-5 step 3's brief does not touch analytical.py.

Execution order. Read this file's rulings → code → W1 (W1b on an in-slot fix) → commit (the analytical.py append, the new test, the log, the test-results.md rows, §9 item 579 DONE, §7 row ⬜ → 🟡, an Outcome paragraph here) → attempts.md journal.

Outcome (2026-10-22, 18:30 UTC slot, third item) — DONE, green; row ⬜ → 🟡 (audit owed). Four pec_sphere_implant_* functions (plus a private _pec_sphere_implant_terms helper) appended at the end of src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py, numpy only, nothing reordered; module tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_closed_form.py (prefix IMP7-0). One window, 20261022T185726Z_IMP-7-step0-W1.log: 14 passed / 3 skipped (complex-only environment tests), 1.35 s pytest, 3 s harness, no MPI, real build — inside the predicted [3, 60] s. Measured (bands in brackets): (Src) β = 1 vs _pec_exterior_numpy 4.95e-16, β = −½ / ½ vs dielectric_sphere_quasistatic_field 3.02e-16 / 2.67e-16 [B1_BAND 1e-12 × max q]; (PDE) worst 2.38e-16; (I) worst 5.92e-16; (Rb) worst 7.71e-17; (Bal) pairwise ≤ 1.22e-15 (P = 6.803512e-2 W, pred 6.803512e-2); (Φ) 9.33e-15 [1e-10 restated]; (R0) 0.000 on all three branches [1e-13 restated]; (FD) level 1.422e-5 at δ = 1e-2·a (pred ≈ 1.1e-5; IMP-1 (H)'s 1e-4 printed only, per the 03:00 ruling), 2δ 5.688e-5, ratio 4.000 [3.8, 4.2 asserted]. Controls (predicted, asserted only > CONTROL_MISS): (c1) 0.6496 (pred 0.6667, the ceiling at r = a; samples start at 1.001a), (c2) 0.030303 (pred 0.030303), (c3) 0.9320 (pred 1.0 — the scale is the term sum, which includes the shell flux's pre-cancellation terms, so it reads below the ceiling). (Rk) printed: e(ε)/e(ε/2) toward adiabatic 1.9934 / 1.9993 / 1.9999 and toward isothermal 1.9852 / 1.9985 / 1.9999 at ε = 1e-2 / 1e-3 / 1e-4 (pred 2; e is |ΔR₂(a)| in K, so the levels differ from the draft's unnamed metric). Every printed record matches its prediction to the printed digit: θ₀(a) 0.350684, θ₀(b) 0.135352, R₂(a) 0.045660 / 0.001966 / 0, pole / equator 0.396344 / 0.327854 (adiabatic) and 0.352650 / 0.349700 (k₁ = 20), heating factor 1.1002, void pole / equator 0.310844 / 0.334678. Disclosed clarification of the letter: the draft's "the core is constant, R₀ = A₀" holds only at β = ±1 (there B₀/a cancels the two particular terms at r = a); the code carries the core constant as theta0_core = R₀(a⁺) = A₀ + B₀/a − (1 + β²)q_far a²/(6k₂) for every β, which is what (R0) at β = 0 checks against MAT-18 (0.318750 = θ(a), not A₀ = 0.360417). Dict keys as ruled: radius, outer_radius, q_far, k_gel, k_core, h, beta, A0, B0, C1, C2, D, E, F, theta0_core, theta0_b, power; pec_sphere_implant_radial unmasked. Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Execute §9 item 579 — IMP-7 step 0 (§10 I37, lane 3) — per docs/planning/chunks/IMP-7.md § '§9 item 579 — 2026-10-22' and the 10-20 draft above it. Write tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_closed_form.py (prefix IMP7-0). Import B1_BAND and CONTROL_MISS from test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py. Restate the 1e-13, [3.8, 4.2] / 1e-4 and 1e-10 literals by value, each with a file:line comment. From test_imp1_pec_sphere_lossy_host.py, import only _pec_exterior_numpy, SPHERE_RADIUS, SHELL_OUTER_FACTOR and PHI_CLOSED_FORM_PEC; from test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form.py, import only _gl. Never import a fixture or a test_* name. Field callables take (3, N). (Rk) is printed only, never asserted. Controls are asserted only as missing by > CONTROL_MISS. Print every prediction beside its measurement. Run W1 in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, pytest -s, container timeout -k 30 120, no mpiexec, and no complex-mode source. Edit nothing after the last window (rule (i)). You are the executor: do not spawn agents and never background a harness window. If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command.
