docs.title: §9 item 594 — 2026-10-22 (I38, lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted read-only for the 2026-10-22 03:00 daily review; the review rules on it.

Licence. §10 chain I, "I38 (lane 3; standard / heavy, -n 2, real build; serial on I37). IMP-7 step 1 — the FEM on two_layer_ball_domain(inner_radius=a, outer_radius=b): MAT-18 step 2(a)'s gates (interior rel L2 ≤ 1 %, the P1 L2 rate ≥ 1.7 on two rungs, balance ≤ 1e-9) on the metal core (DG0 k) and on the adiabatic hole, the isotropic-source and β = 0 controls missing; the l = 2 moment at the pole printed, no band (a band is briefed only if a consumer appears) ⇒ IMP-7 ✅" (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4934–4940). The §7 row's step-1 Done-when is at :2638. The weekly ruling above names it I38. If item 579 did not land (row not 🟡, or pec_sphere_implant_coefficients absent from analytical.py), skip this item at no attempt cost. No band, tolerance, Done-when or target is set or moved.

IMP-7 step 1: P1 FEM of the implant-heated gel ball, on the metal core and on the adiabatic hole, against step 0's closed form at MAT-18 step 2(a)'s gates. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: standard, two windows (each ≤ 180 s container), -n 2, real build. - Class: lane-3 closed form. Cost: ≈ 7.9 measured (lane-3 median; the weekly priced I38 at the chain-solve median, 16.7, PROJECT_PLAN.md:5013) / ≈ 55 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 30 code + W1 ≈ 2.5 + W2 ≈ 2 + commit and journal ≈ 5). - Depends on: item 579 (serial; take-next only if 579 committed before minute 30). Daytime: no. Slot-first: no. Family: step 1, attempt 1 of 4.

What exists (read 2026-10-22). - Mesher: MeshGenerator.two_layer_ball_domain(inner_radius, outer_radius, resolution, comm, rank) (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:3199–3283). - Cell tag 1 is the core and cell tag 2 the shell. Facet tag 1 is r = b only. - There is no interface facet group (known-issues 9, :3213–3215). - Sizing is uniform (:3269–3273). - It has only been run at a/b = 0.91. This fixture's a/b = 0.25 is new to it. - MAT-18 step 2(a)'s module: tests/validation/test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_fem.py. - Geometry-free helpers: _allsum (:71–74), _dg0 (:77–85), _indicator (:88–97). - Helpers bound to MAT-18's geometry: _errors (:115–130, interior mask midpoint |x|² < 0.81b² at :120) and _census (:133–172). Both close over A_ = 0.1 / B_ = 0.11 / AREA_B / T_INF (:50–51, :120, :198), so do not import them. - CELL_GUARD = 800 000 (:48) and QDEG = {"quadrature_degree": 4} (:49). - The ladder pattern with an LSQ rate on h_eff = (V_h/N)^{1/3} is at :213–215 and :243–254. - MAT-18 step 2(a)'s bands are literals in two places, both restated by value: - (S3) balance ≤ 1e-9 (:226), (S1) LSQ rate ≥ 1.7 (:253), (S2) interior ≤ 1e-2 (:254); - the same three in MAT-9 (test_mat9_steady_conduction_sphere.py:139, :154, :156), which is where MAT-18 took them "by value" (MAT-18.md:181). - MAT-18's measured window: 20261003T172548Z_MAT-18-step2a-W1.log, 121 s, -n 2, real build, four rungs plus controls (:261). - The 215 542-cell rung: build 8.7 s, solve 1.8 s (:90). - The 584 228-cell rung: build 27.4 s, solve 9.2 s (:93). - Balance ≤ 1.02e-14, LSQ rate 1.822, finest interior 6.79e-4 (:86–101). - Solver: solve_steady_conduction(mesh, facet_tags, *, k, q, h, t_inf, robin_tag, degree=1) (src/fem_em_solver/thermal/steady.py:151–198). - k is a scalar or a DG0 fem.Function (allreduced positivity check, :183–189). - q is a scalar or a UFL expression / fem.Function, used as-is in L and in source_power (:165–169). - It returns temperature, source_power and convected_power, all allreduced. - Submesh pattern: MAT-10's _sphere_submesh (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:74–89; create_submesh on a cell-tag value). - Its _robin_tags (:92–98) tags every exterior facet. On the shell submesh that would put Robin on r = a too (trap 2). - Restricted interpolation: Function.interpolate(f, cells0=…) (tests/validation/test_lossy_sphere_fullwave.py:391). - Point sampling: evaluate_vector_field_parallel on a scalar temperature (MAT-18 fem :229–230). - Step 0 (item 579): pec_sphere_implant_source, pec_sphere_implant_coefficients, pec_sphere_implant_radial (unmasked, 579 correction 5) and pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature.

Code. No src/ edit and no analytical.py edit, so rule (c) does not bind. Do not edit any test_mat18_*, test_mat10_* or test_imp7_*_closed_form module.

New module tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py, prefix IMP7-1. - Constants. a = SPHERE_RADIUS; b = 4a; K_CORE, k₂, q_far, h and T∞ from step 0's module (test_imp7_implant_heating_closed_form.py, constants only); B1_BAND, CELL_GUARD and QDEG imported by name. The (S1) / (S2) / (S3) literals are restated with file:line comments. Robin tag 1. - Ladder (rule (f) parameter): resolution ∈ {1.414e-3, 1.0e-3, 0.7071e-3} m, ratio √2. - h/b is 0.071 / 0.050 / 0.035, which spans MAT-18's three finer rungs (0.064 / 0.045 / 0.032). - Predicted cells ≈ 59k / 160k / 440k (±25 %). These are scaled from MAT-18's ≈ 19–22 cells per (b/res)³ (MAT-18 W1 :85–93); they are not measured at a/b = 0.25. - The 2 mm rung is left out: the core would be ≈ 2.5 cells in radius, which is pre-asymptotic. - Module helpers. All new and private: - _q_shell(x): q_far·[1 + 2β²u² + (4βu + 2β²u²)P₂(μ)] with no r-mask, taking x of shape (3, N); - _theta_shell(x, coeffs): R₀ + R₂P₂ from pec_sphere_implant_radial (unmasked); - _errors(msh, chi_in, T_h, theta) and _census(msh, ct, ft, a, b): MAT-18's forms, parametrised by a and b; - _robin_outer(sub, a, b): exterior facets with midpoint |x| > (a + b)/2 only; - a module-level mesh cache, as MAT-18's _MESHES. - Source and coefficients. - The source is a DG2 fem.Function: zero, then interpolate(_q_shell, cells0=<shell cells>), then scatter_forward(). - k is a DG0 function (_dg0: K_CORE on the core, k₂ on the shell). - The source is never a SpatialCoordinate expression (trap 4). - test_imp7_1_source_guard (numpy, ungated): - (Src′) _q_shell equals pec_sphere_implant_source at 512 points with r ∈ [1.001a, b], ≤ B1_BAND × max q; - (Th′) _theta_shell (adiabatic coefficients) equals pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature(k_core=0.0) − T∞ at the same points, ≤ B1_BAND × max|θ|.

These tie the unmasked continuations to step 0's gated functions. - test_imp7_1_metal_core_ladder, on the full two-layer mesh. The comparand is pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature(k_core=K_CORE) − T∞ (layer chosen by exact r, MAT-18's trap; θ and flux are continuous), interpolated into P2. Per rung: - (G) as MAT-18; - the cell guard before the finest solve; - (S3), printed and asserted; - the whole / interior / shell errors, printed.

After the ladder: (S1) LSQ rate and (S2) finest interior asserted; pairwise rates, ∫q_h against the closed-form P, and V_core,h printed; the l = 2 readout at the finest rung. - test_imp7_1_metal_core_controls, on the 1.0 mm rung, against the β = 1 comparand: - (c-iso) q = q_far(1 + 2u²) on the shell; - (c-β0) q = q_far on the shell.

Each interior miss is asserted > 1e-2, i.e. it misses (S2)'s band. - test_imp7_1_hole_ladder. Use create_submesh of cell tag 2 (the MAT-10 pattern), Robin tags from _robin_outer, the natural (zero-flux) condition on r = a, scalar k = k₂, and _q_shell on every cell. The comparand is _theta_shell with k_core=0.0 coefficients, never pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature (trap 1). Assert that the interpolated comparand holds no NaN (allreduced). Apply the same per-rung and ladder gates. Also: - (G-hole): the Robin facet area is within 1 % of 4πb² (MAT-18 (G)'s 1e-2, :198); - the r = a facet area is printed beside 4πa². - test_imp7_1_hole_controls: (c-iso) and (c-β0) on the 1.0 mm hole. - l = 2 readout (printed, no band). On the finest rung of each fixture, at r₀ = 1.1a: - R₂,h(r₀) = (5/2) Σⱼ wⱼ P₂(μⱼ) · mean_φ θ_h(r₀, μⱼ, φ), with order-16 GL in μ and 8 φ, as one evaluate_vector_field_parallel batch; - θ_h at the pole (0, 0, r₀) and at the equator (r₀, 0, 0).

r₀ = 1.1a lies well outside the faceting: the chord depth h²/(8a) ≈ 1.2e-5 m against 0.1a = 5e-4 m.

Anchors (asserted; bands restated by value or imported by name, each with file:line). These apply on both fixtures (metal core, adiabatic hole): - (G) census and conformity as MAT-18 (:193–198): owned tag-1 + tag-2 cells equal the global count; core vertices satisfy |x| ≤ a(1 + 1e-9); shell vertices lie in [a(1 − 1e-9), b(1 + 1e-9)]; tag-1 facets are exterior; their area is within 1e-2 of 4πb². On the hole: the cell count equals the parent's tag-2 count (allreduced), plus (G-hole). - Cell guard: finest-rung cells ≤ CELL_GUARD (800 000, test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_fem.py:48), checked before its solve. - (S3) balance, every rung: |convected_power − source_power| / source_power ≤ 1e-9 (:226; MAT-9 :139). source_power = ∫q_h dV is MAT-18's q₁V_core,h in this fixture's form. A DG2 q on affine tets is integrated exactly by both the L-form and the source-form rules, so this is a round-off identity. Predicted ≤ 2e-14 (MAT-18 read ≤ 1.02e-14). - (S1) rate: the LSQ slope of the whole-domain relative L2 error on θ against h_eff = (V_h/N)^{1/3}, over the three rungs, ≥ 1.7 (:253; MAT-9 :154). Predicted 1.8–2.1. Pairwise rates are printed. - (S2) interior: the relative L2 error on θ over cells with midpoint |x|² < 0.81b², at the 0.7071 mm rung, ≤ 1e-2 (:254; MAT-9 :156). Predicted 5e-4 to 5e-3 (MAT-18 read 6.79e-4 at h/b 0.032; the near-field source steepens θ″ ≈ 9× within ≈ a/4 of r = a, in a small volume). - (Src′) / (Th′) ≤ B1_BAND (test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py:46).

Negative controls (rule (e)). No measurement of these comparisons exists on this fixture, so all four are predicted. Each is asserted only as missing (S2)'s 1e-2, as MAT-18's (c1) / (c2) were (:313, :329). Predicted interior misses are comparand-level, from the drafter's unlogged pure-Python quadrature of the closed form over r < 0.9b:

Control Metal core Adiabatic hole (c-iso) l = 2 source dropped 2.730e-2 3.603e-2 (c-β0) uniform shell source 5.671e-2 6.195e-2
  • Ceiling and separation. The isotropic control's miss is exactly the l = 2 share of θ, and the β = 0 control's miss is the l = 2 share plus the near-field l = 0 term. These are the most each control can show on this fixture.
  • Since |θ_h,ctl − θ| ≥ |θ_ctl − θ| − |θ_h,ctl − θ_ctl| and the FEM error at 1.0 mm is predicted ≤ 3e-3, the measured misses should be ≥ 2.4e-2 / 3.3e-2 / 5.4e-2 / 5.9e-2. That is 2.4× to 5.9× the 1e-2 band. The metal-core isotropic control is the thinnest (item 3 for the review).

Predictions (printed, never asserted). Pure-Python, unlogged, 2026-10-22: - P(β = 1) = 6.803512e-2 W. ∫q_h is predicted below it by ≈ the faceted-sphere volume deficit (≈ −1e-3 to −4e-3; MAT-18's area deficits were −4.2e-4 to −1.7e-3). - At r₀ = 1.1a: - metal core: R₂(r₀) 1.1966e-2, pole / equator 0.361610 / 0.343661 K; - adiabatic hole: R₂(r₀) 4.4793e-2, pole / equator 0.394437 / 0.327248 K. - At r = a: R₂(a) metal 1.966e-3 / hole 4.566e-2. Metal core θ ≈ A₀ = 0.350684 K.

Windows. Foreground, Bash timeout: 660000, pytest -s. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Node IDs select the tests (never -k). Two standard windows, because one would predict ≈ 160–250 s against the 180 s ceiling. - W1 (metal core; predicted 90–150 s, range [45, 175]; the first window pays the new FFCx compiles):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-7-step1-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py::test_imp7_1_source_guard tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py::test_imp7_1_metal_core_ladder tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py::test_imp7_1_metal_core_controls -s -v --tb=short'" - W2 (adiabatic hole; predicted 70–130 s, range [40, 175]):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-7-step1-W2 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py::test_imp7_1_hole_ladder tests/validation/test_imp7_implant_heating_fem.py::test_imp7_1_hole_controls -s -v --tb=short'" - Price basis. MAT-18 W1 (121 s for ≈ 0.90M cells over four rungs plus three 0.2M-cell control solves, :261). The ladder here totals ≈ 0.66M cells per fixture. - Kills. A window killed at 180 s is not a result. Run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 first, then the orphan-.c sweep (rubric item 4). Then stop and mark the item BLOCKED. Never raise the timeout and never drop a rung in-slot: re-tiering or shrinking the ladder is the review's call. - No durable capture is needed (both windows are well under ≈ 10 min). No module edit after W1 starts (rule (i)). W1b / W2b after an in-slot fix use the same commands, relabelled.

Traps already paid for. 1. Chord slivers at r = a. Shell cells carry interpolation points just inside r = a (chord depth ≈ h²/(8a)). - There, pec_sphere_implant_source returns 0 and the adiabatic pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature returns NaN (by design, item 579). - On shell cells, use _q_shell / _theta_shell (unmasked, guarded by (Src′) / (Th′)). - Assert no NaN in the hole comparand. - On the metal-core comparand, layer by exact r is consistent (MAT-18 2(a) trap: "do not special-case it"). 2. Robin on the hole submesh only at r = b. MAT-10's _robin_tags tags every exterior facet, which would add a Robin sink on r = a and silently cool the hole. Select by facet midpoint radius. 3. Do not import MAT-18's _errors / _census (they close over MAT-18's a = 0.1, b = 0.11). Parametrise copies. 4. q as a DG2 Function, never a SpatialCoordinate expression. A rational UFL expression lets FFCx estimate a large quadrature degree, and source_power's ufl.dx carries no metadata, so the L-form and the source-form rules could differ and (S3) would stop being a round-off identity. Pin QDEG on every error form (the gmsh SpatialCoordinate compile trap, rubric item 4). 5. Ghosts. Set DG0 / DG2 values from ct.find(·), then scatter_forward() (MAT-18 2(a) trap). Reduce every count, integral, min and max (rank-safety). 6. (3, N) vs (N, 3). Dolfinx interpolate passes (3, N), while step 0's functions take (N, 3). Transpose inside the wrappers. 7. cells0= is the keyword on this image (test_lossy_sphere_fullwave.py:391). The interpolated cells are local, so scatter_forward() afterwards. 8. Point samples are printed only. No bitwise or cross-batch comparison (.eval batch trap, item 537). 9. Run hygiene. Print on rank 0; use -s; never -k; never pipe; after a kill, pgrep -c python3, then the sweep; never delete a log.

Scope. P1, steady, one fixture (a = 5 mm, b = 4a), closed-form dipole source. Not claimed: - a FEM SAR source (the source is step 0's closed-form field; a composed band is a later step, as in MAT-10); - finite-k EM or the isothermal-core FEM (no Dirichlet on r = a); - degree 2; - a band on any l = 2 moment; - a rod, tip or disc, a coil, transient heating, perfusion, CEM43, or any published implant-heating datum ((7c)).

Negative result. There is no PREDICTED RED: line, so a red anywhere stops the slot. On every stop, park on attempt/IMP-7-step1-<UTC> and mark item 594 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); the row stays 🟡.

Red Meaning and action (Src′) / (Th′) The unmasked continuation disagrees with step 0. Fix in-slot, run W1b. (G) The mesher at a/b = 0.25 is non-conforming or mis-tagged. Allow one in-slot fix (test side only; never edit mesh.py), then stop. (S3) A code bug (q's form, Robin tags). Fix in-slot and disclose. (S1) < 1.7 with (S2) green Print the pairwise rates and stop. Never drop a rung (rules (f), (h)). The review rules. (S2) > 1e-2 Report it beside the volume, area and ∫q_h deficits, and stop. A control inside the band A mislabelled comparand or source. Report it. Over the cell guard Stop before the solve and report the counts. A kill See Windows.

Status it can move. The §7 IMP-7 row (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2638) moves 🟡 → ✅ on its step-1 Done-when: "MAT-18 step 2(a)'s gates — interior rel L2 ≤ 1 %, P1 L2 rate ≥ 1.7, balance ≤ 1e-9 — on the metal core and on the adiabatic hole, the isotropic-source and β = 0 controls missing". This item asserts exactly those, plus (G) and (Src′) / (Th′), and prints the l = 2 moment (rule (j)). The row does not say "on two rungs"; the §10 text does (item 1 for the review). The executor closes on the row. The audit is owed. After ✅, the Phase 7 §6 digest's "no heating" clause becomes the weekly's to re-word (not this item's).

Adiabatic hole only (Neumann at r = a). It returns θ(r, ϑ, t) = θ_ss − Σ_{l∈{0,2}} P_l(cos ϑ) Σ_n c_{l,n} R_{l,n}(r) exp(−κ λ_{l,n}² t), with κ = k / ρc and: - θ_ss from pec_sphere_implant_steady_temperature(…, k_core=0.0, …) (:3275) and its radial parts pec_sphere_implant_radial (:3258) on the adiabatic branch (:3231); - R_{l,n}(r) = j_l(λr) y_l′(λa) − y_l(λr) j_l′(λa) (Neumann at a), with λ the roots of k R′(b) + h R(b) = 0 (Carslaw & Jaeger ch. IX, the hollow sphere; Jin App. E for the spherical Bessel identities); - c_{l,n} = ⟨θ_ss,l − θ_init, R_{l,n}⟩{r²} / ⟨R{l,n}, R_{l,n}⟩_{r²} on (a, b), with θ_init = t_inf; - a helper pec_sphere_implant_eigenvalues(l, n, *, radius, outer_radius, k, h): bracket sign changes of the determinant on a grid finer than π / (b − a) / 8, then brentq. Assert the count: the n-th root lies within one spacing of (n + l/2) π / (b − a) asymptotically, and no bracket holds two roots.

Identities — new module tests/validation/test_imp7_transient_closed_form.py (fixture constants imported from the step 0 module test_imp7_implant_heating_closed_form.py; B1_BAND = 1e-12 and CONTROL_MISS = 1e-3 imported from test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py:46, :51, as step 0 does): - Per-mode, at B1_BAND: (PDE) each R_{l,n} satisfies the spherical Bessel ODE with analytic derivatives; (N) R′(a) = 0; (Rb) k R′(b) + h R(b) = 0, all relative to the mode's scale; (Orth) ⟨R_{l,n}, R_{l,m}⟩{r²} / norms ≤ B1_BAND for n ≠ m on the first 20 modes (high-order quadrature). - Series-level, exact at any truncation, at B1_BAND: (Lim) θ(t → ∞) = θ_ss (the decaying sum underflows); (Duh) a 50 % duty cycle by Duhamel superposition of the step response equals the direct modal duty-cycle sum (the _duty_cycle_modal pattern, :2370) on the same modes. - Series-level, truncation-limited: (IC) θ(t = 0) reconstructs θ_init, and (Slope) ρc ∂θ/∂t at t → 0⁺ equals the SAR. docs.title: IMP-8 — the heated rod in gel: the finite line source in closed form
docs.text:
History file for the §7 IMP-8 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-02 10:30 daily review under §9 rule (5) lane 3 (a Phase 7 chunk whose validation target is a cited closed form); for the weekly to ratify. Not a chain step, so it takes no count on chain I.

Why this chunk. IMP-7 is the implant-heating canonical on a sphere, and I36 and entry 55 read a rod in the clinical box. Nothing in the repo gives a closed form for the temperature around a rod, which is the F2182 geometry: erfc and exp1 appear in no validation module and not in src/. In gelled saline there is no perfusion, so the infinite-medium solution is exact until the walls are felt.

The closed form. Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids, 2nd ed., ch. X, the continuous point source and the continuous line source. The text is not in the repo, so the chapter citation is from memory; the derivation below is what the module rests on. A point source of power P switched on at t = 0 in an infinite medium gives θ(R, t) = P / (4πkR) · erfc(R / (2√(κt))), the time integral of the instantaneous source. So a uniform line of power q′ per length on |z′| ≤ L/2 gives

θ(r, z, t) = q′ / (4πk) · Φ, with Φ(r, z, t) = ∫ erfc(R / (2√(κt))) / R dz′ over |z′| ≤ L/2, and R² = r² + (z − z′)².

Its limits. As t → ∞, Φ∞ = asinh((z + L/2) / r) − asinh((z − L/2) / r). As L → ∞ at z = 0, Φ → E₁(r² / (4κt)).

Done-when. Steps 0 and 1 green at their gates, each module asserting its limits and controls. The FEM half is the weekly's to pose.

docs.title: Review ruling 2026-11-05 03:00 — chain I's I64 / I65 as execution detail
docs.text:
Writing the briefs for the 11-04 weekly's I64 and I65, this review fixed the values the step text leaves open and corrected two premises. Each target is kept. All of this is named in the dashboard for the 11-07 weekly to ratify.

The fixture values. - a = ROD_RADIUS = 1 mm. - b = 5a = 5 mm. This is sized so that I65's cylinder, of length 10 b = 50 mm, fits a -n 2 window. - t_c = a²/κ_gel = 6.966667 s. This is the weekly's control time. - t* = 5 t_c = 34.83333 s. Chain I's 900 s is 5.2 b²/κ_gel here, and steady to ≈ 1e-13, so a read there would repeat the steady check. - ROD_K = 6.7 W/(m·K) and ROD_RHO_C = 2.33018e6 J/(m³·K) are Ti-6Al-4V room-temperature values, quoted from memory. No source is in the repo, so they are registered as # nominal. - Carslaw & Jaeger ch. XIII is cited from memory, and marked so.

I64's (Lim). MAT-9 is the Robin sphere, not a cylinder. The repo's only homogeneous cylinder is MAT-15's Robin-cooled robin_finite_cylinder_*, which takes a whole-volume source. (Lim)'s comparand is therefore the Dirichlet J0 series with the source confined to the shell, written in the module. Its roots are jn_zeros(0, N)/b, independent of the composite bisection, so (Lim) is not true by construction. It plays the role of MAT-18's (R4).

I65's control, as written, cannot fire. - The weekly's control is "k_r = K_GEL misses (I) by the closed form's own difference, asserted at factor 1 on the band". At the weekly's points that difference is below INTERIOR_BAND: - 0 at the steady limit (the core is uniform at θ(a) whatever k_r is); - ≈ 4e-4 at (a, t*); - ≤ 7.4e-3 at (a, t_c). - The control is therefore read on the axis at (0, t_c), where the predicted difference is ≈ 0.133 (unlogged review arithmetic, printed as predicted). - (I0), θ_FEM(0, t_c) against the composite at INTERIOR_BAND, is added as a fifth asserted (I) read, so that the control has a matched gate. No band is set or moved; the weekly ratifies or reverts the added read.

I65's Dirichlet wall and geometry. - solve_transient_conduction takes Robin only, so θ = 0 at r = b is a Robin wall at H_DIR = 1e7 W/(m²·K). The predicted offset is 2.8e-5 of θ_ss(a), printed. - Affine cells at r = b would move θ_ss(a) by ≈ −1.7 %, over the band. So the mesh is curved P2 (setOrder(2), the IMP-7 step 3 route).

Results are in K per W/m. - Steady state: θ_ss = q(b² − r²)/(4k_g) − q a² ln(b/r)/(2k_g) on a ≤ r ≤ b, and θ_ss(a) for r < a. It does not depend on (k_r, ρc_r). Review arithmetic: θ_ss(a) = 0.1148409 and θ_ss(3 mm) = 0.0827736 K per W/m. - Modes, with μᵢ = √(s/κᵢ): - core: J0(μ₁r); - shell: Z = A J0(μ₂r) + B Y0(μ₂r), with θ and k∂ᵣθ continuous at a; - A and B come from the Wronskian (Jin 3e App. E, (E.18)–(E.19)); - the eigencondition is F(√s) = Z(b) = 0. - Roots: - scan √s at a step of π/(32Λ), with Λ = a/√κ_r + (b − a)/√κ_g; - refine each sign change by bisection to 4ε relative; - start the scan at x > 0. - Series: - Nₙ by Lommel's integral; - cₙ = q ∫ₐᵇ Z r dr / (sₙNₙ); - θ = θ_ss − Σ cₙψₙe^{−sₙt}, with N_MODES 400.

It converges as 1/N², so it is never a gate.

Window. W1, bare and foreground, Bash timeout 660000 ms. Window form: 20261104T103134Z_IMP-8-item811-W1.log:12. scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh IMP-8-item824-W1 "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 60 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_imp8_composite_cylinder_closed_form.py -v -s --tb=short'"

docs.title: Review ruling 2026-11-05 10:30 — item 824 (I64) re-posed as item 843 under rule (6)
docs.text:
The red is on a precondition the 03:00 brief worded and did not define: "|F| at every root ≤ 1e-12 of F's pre-cancellation scale". The executor's reading, |A J0(μ₂b)| + |B Y0(μ₂b)|, is |F| itself wherever B = 0, so on the gel core (Lim's homogeneous case) the ratio is identically 1.0 and the precondition cannot pass for any root finder. Defined here (the band 1e-12 unchanged): the scale is the outer cylinder function's local amplitude at b,

env(√s) = √( Z₀(μ₂b)² + Z₁(μ₂b)² ), Z_ν = A J_ν + B Y_ν with the same A, B as F,

which does not vanish at a root of Z₀ (Z₀ and Z₁ have no common zero), so |F| / env measures how close the refined root is to the zero, which is what the precondition is for. Attempt 1's diagnostic read max |F| ≤ 2.25e-13 against exactly this envelope on all four cores (20261105T134627Z_IMP-8-item824-diag.log), so a green is expected; that diagnostic is the precondition's measurement, not a gate. No gate, band or target moves, and this is not a new §10 step.

docs.title: §9 item 874 — 2026-11-08 (§10 I78, chain I — IMP-8 step 16, the lumped F2182-shaped prediction; lane 3 → chain step (closed form), smoke, numpy)
docs.text:
Outcome (07:30, 2026-11-08 slot, implementer): DONE. Attempt 1 of 4. IMP-8 step 16 is a 🟡 record; §10 I78 is DONE. New tests/validation/test_imp8_probe_f2182_closed_form.py (imports as the brief, no src/ or landed-module edit, not edited after W1). W1 20261108T133157Z_IMP-8-item874-W1.log (-n 1, real, 5 passed, 5 s harness, [capture] rc=0; pgrep -c python3 read 0 before). (Lim) 1.110e-16, (Bq) 4.030e-14 (t = 900 s) / 2.520e-14 (t = ∞), (Dut) 2.486e-16 line / 5.839e-17 twin, all ≤ band. Control 1 − θ(Z_C)/θ(Z_P) at 900 s: line 0.2941583, twin 0.5253344 (steady-form prediction 0.1926 / 0.4854, printed). Record, the F2182-shaped probe (placement and time quoted from memory; W3 confirms or corrects), K per watt per rod at (0, ±16 mm): line θ(900 s) 9.648662 continuous, 1.978384 at D = 0.5, θ_ss 15.18156; twin 63.14 / 2.498341 / 68.45374; twin/line 6.543912 continuous, 1.262819 at D = 0.5; ±Z_P symmetry 0 exactly.

Executes §10 I78, the 11-07 weekly's enumerated step (PROJECT_PLAN §10 chain I). The target, anchor and control are the weekly's; what follows is execution detail. Family I78, attempt 1 of 4. Executor: the implementer.

Code. New tests/validation/test_imp8_probe_f2182_closed_form.py, numpy / scipy, the image's default (real) build. No src/ edit and no landed module edited. - Imports, unchanged (read every signature first): - step 0 (test_imp8_rod_line_source_closed_form): _phi, _phi_tips, _point, KAPPA, L, MM, T_PRINT, QUAD; - I58 (test_imp8_entry48_lumped, item 786): _tips_steady, _gl01, BQ_BAND; - I59 (test_imp8_rod_line_source_duty_closed_form, item 787): _phi_dot, PERIOD, SCALE, T_STAR; - I62 (test_imp8_rod_tips_duty_closed_form, item 811): _duhamel, _convolution, _phi_tips_dot. These are item 787's MAT-17 Duhamel rule made kernel-generic: _duhamel(kernel, r, z, t, duty) is the step sum Σⱼ ±θ_step(t − tⱼ) over _edges(duty), and _convolution(kernel_dot, r, z, t, duty) is the from-rest convolution; - B1_BAND (test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form, 1e-12) and INTERIOR_BAND (test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere, 1e-2), by name. - The probe: on the axis, 1 mm beyond each tip, (r, z) = (0, ±Z_P) with Z_P = L/2 + 1 mm = 16 mm. The control point is Z_C = L/2 + 2 mm. Both are module constants. - The duty form is D = 0.5 at PERIOD = 450 s (on [0, 225) s, off [225, 450) s, and so on). That is the period I59–I63 share. I56 itself has no period. The weekly's "period as I56's" is read as the two-tip duty runs' period (I62 / I63 import the same PERIOD), and the brief says so here. Read at t = 900 s, the end of an off phase: the edge at 900 s is excluded by both routes (t > te, j·PERIOD < t). - Per watt: 1 W per rod, through SCALE = 1/(4πK_GELL). Both shapes carry the same total power.

Gates (asserted, bands imported). - (Lim) t → ∞ equals the steady line-source form. _phi(0.0, Z_P, np.inf) (erfc → 1, a quad of 1/|z − z′|) against the on-axis steady form ln((Z_P + L/2)/(Z_P − L/2)), relative ≤ B1_BAND. This axis form is the r → 0 limit of _phi_steady and is written in the module, because _phi_steady and I58's _line(r, z, np.inf) divide by r (see Traps). Printed beside, not asserted: _phi_tips(0.0, Z_P, np.inf) against _tips_steady(0.0, Z_P), which is exact by construction; and _phi_steady(1e-9, Z_P) against the axis form, whose expected O(r²/(Z_P − L/2)²) ≈ 1e-12 sits at the band, so it is printed only. - (Bq) N vs 2N on the line kernel. A Gauss–Legendre rule in z′ on [−L/2, L/2] (I58's _gl01(n), mapped) applied to _point(|Z_P − z′|, t) at n = 64 and 2n = 128, at t = T_PRINT and t = ∞: |GL_n/GL_2n − 1| ≤ BQ_BAND (I58's (Bq) band, imported). |GL_2n/_phi − 1| is printed beside. Predicted round-off, unlogged review arithmetic: the integrand's nearest singularity is 1 mm past the endpoint, Bernstein ρ ≈ 1.44, so ρ^(−2n) ≈ 1e-20 at n = 64. - (Dut) the duty-cycled read at t = 900 s equals Duhamel's form. The step sum _duhamel(_phi, 0.0, Z_P, T_STAR, 0.5) against _convolution(_phi_dot, 0.0, Z_P, T_STAR, 0.5), and the same pair for the twin (_phi_tips / _phi_tips_dot). Each |difference| is normalised by θ_ss at the probe, as I59's (Duh) normalises (test_imp8_rod_line_source_duty_closed_form.py:162), and must be ≤ B1_BAND. Precedents at the looser DUH_BAND (1e-10): 2.952e-16 (20261103T211919Z_IMP-8-item787-W1.log:60) and 2.951e-16 (20261104T103134Z_IMP-8-item811-W1.log:61).

Control (the weekly's, asserted at factor 1 on INTERIOR_BAND). The probe moved to 2 mm reads lower: 1 − θ(0, Z_C)/θ(0, Z_P) > INTERIOR_BAND at t = 900 s under the continuous source, for both shapes, with θ(Z_C) < θ(Z_P). The ceiling is 1, since θ > 0. Predicted from the steady forms (unlogged review arithmetic, printed beside the measurement): line 1 − ln 16/ln 31 ≈ 0.19, twin ≈ 0.49. A flat readout would mean the probe cannot see its own placement.

Printed (🟡 record, no band, ≤ 7 digits, K per watt per rod). At (0, ±Z_P), for the line and the twin: - θ(900 s) continuous, θ(900 s) at D = 0.5 and θ_ss; - duty/continuous and twin/line; - the same reads at Z_C; - |θ(+Z_P) − θ(−Z_P)|, which is round-off by symmetry. Label the block "the F2182-shaped probe (placement and time quoted from memory; W3 confirms or corrects)". These are the numbers I75 and I76 are read beside.

Window. W1, smoke, -n 1, real, container timeout -k 30 60, label IMP-8-item874-W1. Make one bare foreground harness call with Bash timeout 660000 ms, using the durable capture of 20261106T103149Z_IMP-8-item856-W1.log:12 verbatim including the trailing ; exit $rc, with this module, -n 1, no knob env and raw log /workspace/logs/imp8-item874-w1-raw.log. Pre-check docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Predicted < 15 s: I58 took 9 s (20261103T211525Z_IMP-8-item786-W1.log:91), I59 3 s (20261103T211919Z_IMP-8-item787-W1.log:89) and I62 6 s (20261104T103134Z_IMP-8-item811-W1.log:90).

Tier. Smoke, numpy, -n 1. Class: lane 3 → chain step (closed form). Cost: ≈ 3.6 measured / 15 predicted min.

Traps already paid for. - _phi_steady and I58's _line(·, ·, np.inf) divide by r. At r = 0 that is a ZeroDivisionError on Python floats, or inf − inf = nan on numpy. Never call them on the axis; use the axis form above. - At Z_P > L/2, _phi takes one piece (no split at z′ = z). The integrand peaks at the endpoint z′ = L/2, 1 mm from the probe. Use the QUAD settings unchanged. I58 disclosed a quad IntegrationWarning near the axis, and (Bq) is what shows whether it reaches the reading. - _step guards t ≤ 0. Never evaluate a kernel at age 0. - Use -s, or the prints are lost. Print ≤ 7 digits. - The leak guard: if a printed θ line is refused by the hook, the log moves unchanged to logs/leak-held/ and the slot reports it, as for item 851's W3. Never --no-verify.

Scope. An infinite gel medium, two idealised source shapes (a zero-radius line and two point tips), 1 W per rod, one probe placement. Not claimed: the box walls, the rod's own conduction (I73 / I75), a ball-averaged read, any F2182 figure or published value. The weekly's caveat stands: the standard's probe placement (1 mm beyond the tip, on the axis) and time (900 s) are quoted from memory and marked so (§10 I32b), and W3 confirms or corrects them. The twin's point source sits 1 mm from the probe, so it reads a point's 1/R there. The FEM's 1 mm balls (I56) put their surface at the probe, so the twin is not the FEM's source shape at that distance. That is printed, never compared.

Negative result. - (Lim), (Bq) or (Dut) red is a derivation or quadrature error: stop, BLOCKED, band unmoved, every value printed. - A control under the band contradicts the steady arithmetic above: report the measurement and stop. - No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. IMP-8 gains step 16, a 🟡 record line: the lumped prediction at the F2182-shaped probe. §10 I78 is DONE, and I75 / I76 have their closed form beside them.

Depends on: nothing (items 786, 787 and 811 are on main).

docs.title: §9 item 881 — 2026-11-08 (§10 I75, chain I — IMP-8 step 17, the F2182-shaped readout on the bracket fixture; chain step (solve), heavy, real, -n 8)
docs.text:
Executes §10 I75, the 11-07 weekly's enumerated step. The target, anchor and control are the weekly's, and what follows is execution detail. Family I75, attempt 1 of 4. Executor: the implementer.

The control as the weekly wrote it is degenerate, so it is re-posed here for the review to ratify. The step says "the probe read at t = 900 s exceeds the read at t* on every arm (monotone heating under a continuous source; asserted at factor 1)". On I73's fixture t* is 900 s: T_PRINT = 900.0 (test_imp8_rod_line_source_closed_form.py:48), I73's CN run is N_MAIN steps of T_PRINT / N_MAIN (test_imp8_rod_self_heated_fem.py:131–136), and its log prints t*=900 s (20261106T103149Z_IMP-8-item856-W1.log:113). The weekly's own words are "monotone heating under a continuous source", so this brief asserts that monotonicity against the step-30 snapshot, t₂ = 675 s (I60's T2 / STEP_T2, test_imp8_rod_line_source_duty_fem.py:56–57):

θ_probe(900 s) / θ_probe(675 s) > 1 (factor 1) at both probes on every arm, under the continuous source.

The size of the rise is predicted, not asserted: per-cent level (unlogged review arithmetic, 1 mm from a heated end). Flagged in the slot report for the review.

The duty read is a superposition, not a second solve, and that choice is flagged for the review. "Under I56's duty form" is read as D = 0.5 at PERIOD = 450 s, the two-tip duty runs' period (I56 has none of its own; I62 / I63 import I59's PERIOD). It is taken from the continuous run by linearity: the problem is linear and time-invariant from rest, with θ₀ = T_INF = 0. The read is θ_D(900) = θ(900) − θ(675) + θ(450) − θ(225), from snapshot_steps=(10, 20, 30).

This costs no extra solve. It is not bit-identical to a switched solve: each shifted step response restarts with the two backward-Euler half-steps, while I60's direct run goes through the switches in CN with no restart (I60's disclosure, item 799). The gel arm prints the difference. If the review reads the step as a direct switched solve, that is three more windows of ≈ 7.3 min each (I60's D = 0.5 window: 418 s, 20261104T044429Z_IMP-8-I60-W1-item799.log:181). Together with W1–W3 that does not fit one slot, so it is a second item, not this one.

Code. New tests/validation/test_imp8_rod_probe_f2182_fem.py, real build, degree 2. No src/ edit and no landed module edited. - Imports, unchanged (read every signature first): - I73 (test_imp8_rod_self_heated_fem): BODY_CELLS, I55_THETA, READ_PTS, CONTROL_FLOOR; - I55 (test_imp8_rod_line_source_fem): the box fixture, GATE_PTS, QP, T_INF, W0C_CELLS, DEGREE, _need, _theta_pts, _source_and_s0; - I66 / I69 (test_imp8_rod_conducting_body_fem): _coefficients(msh, rod_idx, arm), which handles ti / gel / hole with EPS_HOLE, and EPS_HOLE itself, printed; - ROD_K, ROD_RHO_C (both # nominal) and ROD_RADIUS as I73 imports them; - step 0's L, MM, T_PRINT, _phi and I59's _duhamel (test_imp8_rod_line_source_duty_closed_form; the line's, _duhamel(r, z, t, duty)), for the printed closed forms; - I60's T2, STEP_T2; - K_GEL, H_GEL, N_MAIN, RHO_C, E_BAND, B_BAND, ROBIN_TAG, _say, INTERIOR_BAND from the modules I73 takes them from. - Knob FEM_EM_IMP8_I75_ARM = ti (default) / gel / hole. Anything else is refused. The phase knob FEM_EM_IMP8_I55_PHASE=transient goes on the command, as I73's did. - Body cells are I73's, the positive DG0 dofs of q from _source_and_s0(msh), converted to cell indices through the DG0 dofmap (owned + ghost). Then call I66's _coefficients(msh, body_idx, arm). Print the allreduced owned count, which must equal BODY_CELLS (6 495). Do not call I73's _coefficients with hole: it overwrites only on ti, so any other arm silently returns gel (test_imp8_rod_self_heated_fem.py:109–111). - Solve: I73's call exactly (test_imp8_rod_self_heated_fem.py:133–136) plus snapshot_steps=(10, 20, 30). Assert that snapshot step j is at t = j·T_PRINT/N_MAIN (225, 450, 675 s). - Reads, one batch per call (the batch rule): 1. _theta_pts(res.temperature, READ_PTS), I73's batch unchanged, so the reproductions compare call for call; 2. _theta_pts(·, PROBE_PTS) with PROBE_PTS = ((0.0, 16.0), (0.0, −16.0)) mm on the final field and on each snapshot; 3. on arm gel only, _theta_pts(·, GATE_PTS) on each snapshot, for the printed duty comparison.

Gates (asserted, bands imported). - Every arm: - (E) max_balance_residual ≤ E_BAND; - (S0) |∫q − P|/P ≤ B_BAND; - cells = W0C_CELLS (485 291), body cells = BODY_CELLS, no non-finite coefficient dofs. - Arm gel — I73's anchor and its (I). - Each of I55_THETA's five θ is reproduced within one unit of its sixth significant digit. - The new gel point is reproduced the same way: θ(2, 15) = 9.482226e+00 (20261106T103928Z_IMP-8-item856-W2.log:118). - I55's (I) holds: |θ/(QP·_phi) − 1| ≤ INTERIOR_BAND at the four GATE_PTS. - Arm ti — the route control. I73's six Ti θ are reproduced within one sixth-digit unit through I66's _coefficients route: 4.583697e+00, 1.098572e+00, 2.774057e+00, 7.112581e-01, 1.735615e+01, 1.041661e+01 at READ_PTS (20261106T103149Z_IMP-8-item856-W1.log:113–118). A route that missed the body cells would return I55's θ. - Arm hole — the coefficient control. |θ_hole(2, 0)/1.772315e+01 − 1| > CONTROL_FLOOR, as item 851's on I66's box. A path that ignored ε would return the gel arm's θ. - Every arm — the re-posed weekly control: θ_probe(900 s) > θ_probe(675 s) at both probes (factor 1, strict).

Printed (🟡 record, no band, ≤ 7 digits, K/W, 1 W in the rod). - Per arm: - θ_probe(900 s) at +16 and −16 mm, their mean and |difference| (mesh asymmetry); - the superposed D = 0.5 θ_probe(900 s); - θ_probe at 225 / 450 / 675 s and the ratio θ(900)/θ(675); - t_call, n_factorizations and t_build. - Beside them, labelled "infinite medium, line source, no rod": QP·_phi(0.0, ±Z_P, T_PRINT) and the line's _duhamel(0.0, Z_P, T_PRINT, 0.5). These are the numbers I78 gates (item 874). They are computed inline here, so this item does not depend on 874 landing. - Arm gel: the superposed duty θ at GATE_PTS beside I59's _duhamel and beside I60's direct FEM reads 2.240893e+00, 6.683594e-01, 1.366131e+00, 4.289727e-01 (20261104T044429Z_IMP-8-I60-W1-item799.log:112–115). It also prints the restart-vs-no-restart difference. Rule (e): printed, never asserted. - Across the three windows (slot report): the probe ordering of Ti / gel / hole. Item 856 measured a −2.07 % move at (2, 0) mm and the axial ratio 0.535 → 0.600 toward the tips (…item856-W1.log:119–120, …item856-W2.log:119), so the Ti probe is predicted to read above the gel's. That is a sign only, printed; if it comes out the other way, that is the finding.

Windows. Pre-check docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0 before each. - Every window is a bare foreground harness call, Bash timeout 660000 ms, using the durable capture of 20261106T103149Z_IMP-8-item856-W1.log:12 verbatim including the trailing ; exit $rc. - Use this module, raw log /workspace/logs/imp8-item881-w<N>-raw.log, env FEM_EM_IMP8_I55_PHASE=transient FEM_EM_IMP8_I75_ARM=<arm>, and container timeout -k 30 600. - Each arm is its own window, since one CN run on this box is ≈ 408 s of t_call (…item856-W1.log:112, …item856-W2.log:112).

The windows: - W0 IMP-8-item881-W0 (-n 2, timeout -k 30 120): -k k0 only. This is the knob test that ti / gel / hole parse and junk is refused (no mesh). - W1 IMP-8-item881-W1, arm ti, -n 8. Predicted ≈ 430–445 s; I73's W1 took 430 s (…item856-W1.log:190). The three snapshot copies add only copies. - W2 IMP-8-item881-W2, arm gel, -n 8. Predicted ≈ 430–445 s; I73's W2 took 429 s (20261106T103928Z_IMP-8-item856-W2.log:190). - W3 IMP-8-item881-W3, arm hole, -n 8. Predicted ≈ 430–450 s; item 851's hole window took 438 s per its Outcome above (that log is leak-held, so none of its digits is quoted here).

A kill parks the item. Never raise the ceiling, and never run two heavy windows at once.

Tier. Heavy, real, -n 8. Class: chain step (solve). Cost: ≈ 6.8 measured / 35 predicted min (W0 plus three ≈ 7.3-minute windows).

Traps already paid for. - Items 846 / 856's list: - real build only, since I55's and I73's records are real and every reproduction here compares real-build digits; - reduce every rank-local count and integral before asserting, and count verdicts per rank by token; - one batch per read, with I73's READ_PTS batch unchanged; - -s on pytest. - The hole arm with the source in the hole is new (I69's source sat in gel). With k = ε·K_GEL, the rod core reaches ≈ q′/(4π·ε·K_GEL) ≈ 4e6 K/W within a few seconds (κ is unchanged by ε; unlogged review arithmetic). Print no rod-interior or max θ. The gel reads are what is recorded. If (E) comes back above E_BAND, that is the finding (item 851's rule): report the residual and stop. A review may re-pose ε, never the band. - _phi_steady divides by r. The printed closed forms on the axis use _phi at finite t only. - Leak guard: a hook refusal on a printed θ line moves the log unchanged to logs/leak-held/ and the slot reports it (item 851's W3). The gate values are quoted in this file. Never --no-verify.

Scope. One mesh, one Δt, nominal Ti, perfect thermal contact, and I55's uniform source in the rod cells. The probe placement and time are the weekly's, quoted from memory of the standard and marked so (§10 I32b); W3 confirms or corrects them. Not claimed: - a published F2182 value or an F2182 measurement (W3); - a direct switched-source duty solve (see above); - the clinical probe (entry 63 / I76); - a Joule SAR shape in a metal rod; - a gate on the rod's effect at the probe (no closed form has the finite conducting rod).

Negative result. - (E), (S0) or a precondition red: stop, BLOCKED. - The gel arm's anchor or (I) red, or the Ti arm's reproduction red: the body route is not I73's. Print every θ, stop, BLOCKED; no arm's record is banked without both. - The hole control red (θ unmoved): ε never reached the form. BLOCKED. - The re-posed control red, meaning θ falls under a continuous source from rest: that contradicts the physics of a heating from rest. Print every snapshot read, stop, BLOCKED, and loosen nothing. - No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. IMP-8 gains step 17, a 🟡 record line: the F2182-shaped probe on the gel / Ti / hole bracket, continuous and D = 0.5, per watt. §10 I75 is DONE, and I76 gets its bracket arms.

Why. Item 895's Outcome flags a sign: ti's first FEM drop (16 → 17 mm) is steeper than the infinite line's 0.2941583, where the brief predicted flatter. The logged first drops are ti 0.295119 / 0.294595 (20261109T060343Z_IMP-8-item895-W1.log:149–150), gel 0.273386 / 0.272288 (20261109T061107Z_IMP-8-item895-W2.log:134–135) and hole 0.262420 / 0.263417 (20261109T061832Z_IMP-8-item895-W3.log:134–135), all +z / −z.

Two readings are open: - (a) discretisation. The ti-vs-line excess is +0.000961 / +0.000437. That is the same size as each arm's +z/−z spread of the first drop (gel 0.001098, ti 0.000524, hole 0.000997). - (b) physics. The brief's "flatter" was a prediction about the source's 1 mm radius, and the conducting rod is a second effect that I81 could not separate from it.

I75 / I81 printed every arm beside the zero-radius line. I55's source, however, is the DG0 cylinder r ≤ ROD_RADIUS, |z| ≤ L/2 (test_imp8_rod_line_source_fem.py:152–177; effective radius 1.0022 mm, 20261103T182153Z_IMP-8-I55-W1s.log:56), and 1 mm from its end face the line is the wrong comparand.

The uniform finite cylinder has a closed form on its axis. The disc integral of the point kernel is exact:

2π∫₀ᵃ erfc(√(r′² + d²)/s)/√(r′² + d²) r′ dr′ = 2πs[ierfc(d/s) − ierfc(√(a² + d²)/s)], with s = 2√(κt).

Reading the gel arm against that form separates the two readings: - if the gel arm sits on it, the gel arm's flattening is the radius, not the mesh; - ti − gel is then the rod's effect, on a gated baseline, on the same mesh and source cells.

Unlogged drafter arithmetic (numpy Gauss–Legendre, host; printed beside by the module, never asserted as values). SCALE·Φ_a(900 s) at 16 / 17 / 18 / 20 mm is 9.197899 / 6.682151 / 5.184508 / 3.407212 K/W. The same code reproduces I80's line 9.648662 / 6.810428 / 5.242317 / 3.427288 (20261109T043829Z_IMP-8-item894-W1.log:98, :101). Steady values are 14.72925 / 12.12776 / 10.54176 / 8.581375. The cylinder's first drop is 0.273513, against the line's 0.2941583.

Against I81's ± means, (G) is predicted at: - continuous: −3.914e-03 / −2.992e-03 / −2.420e-03 / −1.921e-03; - D = 0.5: +6.4e-04 / +3.6e-04 / +1.9e-04 / +3.7e-05.

The decomposition the record will carry, on the ± means, is:

Term First-drop change radius (cylinder − line) −0.020645 mesh (gel − cylinder) −0.000673 rod (ti − gel) +0.022019

So reading (b) is predicted: the radius flattens, the rod steepens by slightly more, and ti's net +0.0007 over the line is the near-cancellation of two effects ≈ 30× larger.

docs.text:
Enumerated by the 11-09 weekly (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4964–4974). Written by the 2026-11-10 03:00 daily review as execution detail. The bands are imported, and none is set or moved. One execution detail is flagged for the weekly: the step's "short cylinders" get a length here (below). Family I86, attempt 1 of 4. Executor: the implementer. Depends on nothing; no queued window's module is touched (numpy only, new module).

Why. I83 measured how much the uniform source's radius moves the 16 mm read: 1 − Φ_a/Φ = 0.0467 (20261109T110006Z_IMP-8-item911-W1.log:119). The point twin reads 6.543912 × the line there (20261109T043829Z_IMP-8-item894-W1.log:100). The twin's point sources sit 1 mm from the probe, where a 1/R kernel is most sensitive to the source's size. So it is open whether the radius or the tip weighting dominates the twin's probe read.

The fixture (execution detail, flagged). Each tip is a uniform cylinder of radius a = ROD_RADIUS and length h = 2a, centred on z = ±L/2 and carrying P/2 (I58's split, test_imp8_rod_line_source_closed_form.py:89–91). - It circumscribes I56's tip ball, radius ROD_RADIUS about ±L/2 (this file, item 846's _rod_cells). - As a → 0 it collapses to I58's points, which is what (Lim-a) needs. - At rung 1 (16 mm) the probe sits on the near cylinder's end face, as I56's balls put their surface there (test_imp8_probe_f2182_closed_form.py:31–32). On the axis d ≥ 0 and 2/(D + d) ≤ 2/a, so the kernel is finite. - A second length is printed beside as a sensitivity: the cylinder [L/2 − a, L/2] (h = a, inside the rod's end).

The kernel, per unit SCALE (θ = SCALE·Φ₂,a):

Φ₂,a(0, z, t) = (L/2)·[M(|z − L/2|, t) + M(|z + L/2|, t)], with: - M(ζ, t) = ½∫₋₁¹ B(|ζ − a u|, t) du, the segment mean in the unit variable u. Assert ζ ≥ a: the probe is on or beyond the face. - B(d, t) = (2s/a²)[ierfc(d/s) − ierfc(D/s)], with D = hypot(a, d) and s = 2√(κt). At t = ∞, B = 2/(D + d). This is I83's disc integral (test_imp8_probe_cylinder_source_closed_form.py:5–13). - Steady: M(ζ, ∞) = [g(ζ + a) − g(ζ − a)]/(2a), with I83's _g (:122–123). - Rate: per tip, (L/(2h))·_phi_cyl_dot(0, ζ, u, a=a, length=h), I83's closed form (:112–119). Use it at a = ROD_RADIUS only.

Code. New tests/validation/test_imp8_probe_twin_cylinder_closed_form.py, numpy / scipy, the image's default (real) build. No src/ edit and no landed module edited. - Imports, unchanged (read every signature first): - I83 (test_imp8_probe_cylinder_source_closed_form): _g, _phi_cyl, _phi_cyl_dot, _GL_B; - I80 (test_imp8_probe_ladder_closed_form): RUNGS, LADDER_MM, _lab; - I78 (test_imp8_probe_f2182_closed_form): DUTY, N_GL, _axis_steady, _p; - I58 (test_imp8_entry48_lumped): _gl01, _tips_steady, BQ_BAND; - step 0 (test_imp8_rod_line_source_closed_form): L, MM, KAPPA, QUAD, T_PRINT, _phi, _phi_tips; - I59 (test_imp8_rod_line_source_duty_closed_form): SCALE, T_STAR, PERIOD; - I62 (test_imp8_rod_tips_duty_closed_form): _duhamel, _convolution, _phi_tips_dot; - ROD_RADIUS (tests.mesh.test_birdcage_implant_rod); - B1_BAND (test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form) and INTERIOR_BAND (test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere), by name. - _bracket_cf(d, t, a). I83's _bracket with y − x written as a²/((D + d)s), never D/s − d/s. The GL16 nodes go on [x, x + (y − x)]. I83's _bracket takes the difference (:100–103), and at a = 1e-10 m that loses every digit. - _seg_mean(zeta, t, a, n=None). quad over u ∈ [−1, 1] with QUAD when n is None; otherwise _gl01(n) mapped onto [−1, 1]. - The twin functions. - _twin_a(r, z, t, a=ROD_RADIUS) (assert r == 0.0) builds the sum above. - _twin_a_dot(r, z, u, a=ROD_RADIUS) and _twin_a_steady(z, a) are the matching closed forms.

Done-when (rule (j)). On MAT-9's ball (R 0.1 m, k 0.6, h 10, q 2000 W/m³) at w = 240 W/m³/K (mR = 2, so conduction and perfusion each carry about half the power — a numerical choice, not a tissue claim), against θ(r) = (q/w)[1 − A·sinh(mr)/(mr)], m² = w/k, A = Bi·mR/[mR cosh mR + (Bi − 1) sinh mR] (utils/analytical.py: robin_sphere_perfusion_temperature; Pennes 1948; Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids, ch. docs.title: MAT-13 — The transient Pennes equation on the Robin ball: the perfusion sink in the θ-scheme
docs.text: The transient Pennes equation on the Robin ball: the perfusion sink in the θ-scheme — Phase 8, perfused regime (§9 rule (5) lane 3; opened by the 2026-09-30 10:30 daily review under lane 3's closed-form licence — the weekly ratifies or re-homes it, dashboard). thermal/transient.py gains steady.py's additive perfusion_w_per_m3_k (arterial = ambient temperature): ρc ∂ₜθ = k∇²θ − wθ + q in Ω, −k ∂ₙθ = hθ on ∂Ω — MAT-11 has the sink only at steady state, MAT-12 the transient only without it. Done-when (rule (j)). On MAT-9's ball (R 0.1 m, k 0.6, h 10, q 2000 W/m³, ρc 4.18e6 J/m³/K, T∞ = T(0) = 20) at MAT-11's w = 240 W/m³/K (mR = 2), real build, -n 2, P1, the 0.01 m rung, against θ(r, t) = θ_ss^w(r) − Σ Bₙ^w e^{−(λₙ² + (mR)²)Fo} sin(λₙr/R)/(λₙr/R), Bₙ^w = (qR²/k)·Cₙ/(λₙ² + (mR)²), Fo = kt/(ρcR²) (λₙ, Cₙ MAT-9's, θ_ss^w MAT-11's; utils/analytical.py: robin_sphere_perfusion_transient_temperature; derived in the docstring, no textbook equation pinned; numpy anchors N1–N4: Bₙ^w is the quadrature projection of θ_ss^w, the t = 0 / truncation / t → ∞ limits, w → 0 = MAT-9's series, and the time-convolution of MAT-9's series reproduces it at w = 240): (P_w) CN with Rannacher start, N = 40 to t* = 0.2 R²ρc/k = 13 933 s — storage, convection and perfusion carry ≈ 21 / 39 / 40 % of the power there: interior relative L2 on θ ≤ 1 % (MAT-9 (i), imported); (T) CN self-difference LSQ rate over N = 10…160 ≥ 1.8 (MAT-9 (ii), imported); (E) per-step balance ρc∫Δθ/Δt dV + ∮hθ dS + ∫wθ dV = ∫q dV (θ at the scheme's t_{n+θ}) ≤ 1e-9 on every run, and recomputed from snapshots on the last step; (∞) backward Euler 20 × 5 R²ρc/k equals solve_steady_conduction(perfusion_w_per_m3_k=w) on the same mesh to ≤ 1e-8; (S) one backward-Euler step of 1e-5 R²ρc/k from θ = 0: interior ρcθ/Δt equals q to ≤ 1e-3 (MAT-12 (S1), imported) — the sink does not change the initial slope; (w → 0) the w = 0 run reads MAT-9's recorded 1.7085e-03 against the unperfused series; the perfusion-dropped and sign-flipped controls each miss (P_w)'s band and the perfused-term-dropped balance misses 1e-3; MAT-9's modules (real build) and MAT-12's (complex build) re-run green on their recorded digits (rule (c)) ⇒ ✅. Out of scope: a SAR source with perfusion, arterial ≠ ambient temperature, T-dependent w, σ(T) (MAT-5), implants, coil-driven and mass-averaged SAR, adaptive Δt, thermal dose (CEM43), tissue property claims, any ASTM F2182 compliance claim. (Queued §9 item 108.) State (2026-09-30 12:00 take-next slot, §9 item 108) ⇒ ✅. The perfusion sink is added to the θ-scheme (thermal/transient.py: _solve_transient body, public perfusion_w_per_m3_k ≥ 0, perfused_power), with the closed form robin_sphere_perfusion_transient_{coefficients,temperature} in utils/analytical.py. The perfusion docstring there is now a raw string, so its SyntaxWarning is gone. Numpy anchors: (N1) 1.5e-13; (N2) 2.8e-11 / 0 / 2.7e-15; (N3) 5.6e-5 K; (N4) the convolution identity to 1.8e-15 K. Logs: 20260930T172102Z_MAT-13-W1.log:77–111 (75 s, 16 passed, 4 complex-only env skips), 20260930T172227Z_MAT-13-W2-ruleC.log (118 s), 20260930T172429Z_MAT-13-W3-ruleC.log (94 s). What discriminates: N4 (independent of the new closed-form code), (P_w) with controls (a) / (b) at 39× / 103× the band, (∞) against MAT-11's steady sink, N1's wrong-coefficient check. What does not: (S) at 5.5e-5 against 1e-3 would pass a sink ≈ 20× too large — a consistency check; (E) is structural; N2's 400-vs-800-term 0.0 is float underflow, inherited from MAT-9 — N2's substance is the t = 0 leg. (3) Keep the parked chunk sizes (STEADY_CHUNK 20 000, TRANSIENT_CHUNK 1 000, :67–68): the (points × 200 × 200) complex einsum at 20 000 points would be ≈ 12.8 GB per rank. Outcome 2026-10-01 (22:30 CDT slot) — 🚫 BLOCKED, parked attempt/MAT-15-step2b-20261002T034707Z (7120eeed). Slot deviation, disclosed: W2 ran at container timeout -k 30 590, not 900 (the foreground Bash window is 660 s; see the slot note below). Trap step: one 0-byte .c stub deleted, no orphans. W1 steady green — 20261002T033219Z_MAT-15-step2b-W2-steady.log (-n 2, complex, 244 s, 19 passed): cells 2 746 / 8 497 / 18 570 / 58 866; LSQ slope 2.1511 (bar 1.7), pairwise 2.2106 / 2.1415 / 2.1015; finest interior 7.374e-4; Gauss ≤ 1.3e-14; centroid |c|/a 2.101e-6 (bar 1e-5), z and r exact; θ_h(0) 2.980951 vs 2.983150 K; V_sub −8.6995e-4; (c1) 0.7394 (predicted 0.739); max |Im θ| 0; phase clocks: builds 26.2 / 27.8 / 29.9 / 40.0 s, steady solves ≤ 0.6 s, steady series interpolation 0.9 / 3.4 / 5.8 / 27.8 s, (c1) 29.1 s. W2 transient, first run 20261002T033630Z_MAT-15-step2b-W3-transient.log (286 s, 4 errors): FFCx JIT lock on libffcx_forms_9f4f0568….c. That was a 44 345-byte .c with no .o / .so, written at 20:36:19 UTC, the instant item 145's W1 was killed. The brief's 0-byte sweep cannot see a killed compile that already wrote its source. Only that file was deleted and W2 re-run once (no code change). W2 re-run 20261002T034149Z_MAT-15-step2b-W3-transient.log (273 s, 15 passed / 1 failed): (T) CN N = 40 interior 3.4945e-4 (predicted 3.49e-4), whole 4.16e-4; (c2) 0.7795 (predicted 0.779); (E) worst 7.234e-14 (CN), BE 1.3e-14; max |Im θ| 0; (∞) 0.9999999999999808 > INF_BAND 1e-8 — red outside the predictions, so the slot stopped. Phase clocks: build 39.4 s, steady 0.6, CN 2.3, transient series interpolation 95.1, (c2) 86.1, BE (∞) 1.2 s, fixture 225.9 s (item 145's overrun was the two 1 000-point-chunk interpolations, not (∞)). Diagnosis (code reading, the arithmetic fits): a test bug, inherited verbatim from item 145's module. _rel(sub, a, b) returns ‖a − b‖/‖b‖, but the (∞) call passes a = T_be − T_st and b = T_st − T∞. So it reads ‖(T_be − T_st) − θ‖/‖θ‖ = 1 − ⟨T_be − T_st, θ⟩/‖θ‖², which is 1 − 1.9e-14 when T_be = T_st. The 1.9e-14 deficit is the BE-vs-steady agreement. Unblock: one line, out["inf"] = _rel(sub, res_inf.temperature - T_INF, st.temperature - T_INF) (MAT-12's :238 form, with T∞ ≠ 0), then re-run W1 and W2 per rule (i). Both fit (244 + 273 s). Attempt 3 of 4. Pre-register the trap as "any FFCx .c without a sibling .so", not "0-byte".

Slot note (2026-10-01 21:00 CDT slot, not started — no attempt spent). W2's timeout -k 30 900 exceeds the 660 000 ms foreground Bash window. implementer-run.md caps container time at ≈ 590 s, so the call would be killed host-side mid-window. A review should re-price W2 at ≤ 590 s, or split (∞) into a third window, before a slot takes this item.

Read 2026-10-02 03:00 review. The diagnosis holds on the parked module (7120eeed): _rel(sub, th_h, th_ex) is ‖th_h − th_ex‖/‖th_ex‖ (:125), and :290 passes th_h = T_be − T_st and th_ex = T_st − T∞. So (∞) reads ‖(T_be − T_st) − θ_st‖/‖θ_st‖ = 1 − O(‖T_be − T_st‖/‖θ_st‖), and the printed 1 − 1.9e-14 says T_be = T_st to ≈ 1.9e-14. Correcting the comparand's arguments is a bug fix, not a band move: INF_BAND 1e-8 and the quantity (BE(∞) against the steady solve, MAT-12's :238 form) are unchanged. Every other anchor and both controls were green on their predictions. Re-queued as item 168 (attempt 3 of 4).

docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-04 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain P5 (weekly 2026-10-03), quoted, not changed: "MAT-15 step 3 — heating per accepted watt at 64 MHz on copper. ANS-7's tuned fixture as the source, degree 2, exact rectangles: the energy identity, the calorimetric slope and the σ_y mirror image of the one-port drive at MAT-15's imported bands. Target: identities. The first thermal figure on a tuned coil. Serial on nothing." The 2026-10-02 sheets-and-κ ruling binds: exact rectangles, κ off. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target moves.

MAT-15 step 3: step 1's thermal identities, run once on the SAR of ANS-7's tuned copper F-small birdcage, driven across C₁ at 64.0 MHz, normalised per accepted watt. - Executor: implementer. One new test module; no src/ change and no edit to any existing module. - Tier: heavy, -n 8, complex build. - Class: chain step (solve). Time: ≈ 23 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min. - Depends on nothing on main. It needs two gitignored files that T21 wrote, logs/ans7_exact/tune_p2.json and logs/ans7_exact/tune_inmodel_p2.json (item 217 W1 / W2, 2026-10-04 09:07 / 09:11 CDT). Both were on disk when this brief was drafted. If either is absent, stop and take the next item. Do not re-create them: T21's W2 is red by pre-registration.

What changes against steps 1–2. Step 2 used no EM, so nothing from it is imported here.

Step 1 (§9 item 130) This step Fixture ANS-2's solid-conductor F-small, build_four_port_sweep(phantom_resolution=0.0025), 199 920 cells, 58 866 tag-3 cells The ×1 exact-strip hole mesh (_exact_geo(th14, comm, GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION), h = 0.015), 80 798 cells (ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD), default phantom sizing. The tag-3 count has never been printed on this mesh Conductor Volumetric, σ = 800 S/m Copper by Leontovich on tag 401, σ = 5.8e7 (_route_a_solve(…, "cu") builds the term) Sheets Ragged f = 0.5 cut, κ none Exact CAD rectangles, κ off (_build_ports(width_correction_kappa=None)) EM order Degree 1 Degree 2 (thermal stays P1) Circuit Untuned: every port at 50 Ω, four single-leg drives at 10 MHz Tuned: Z_C(C_mode,Cu) on P2–P4, C₁ across the P1 port (circuit layer, lossless), one drive (P1) at 64.0 MHz Normalisation G = 1 W / P₁, one deposited watt G = 1 W / P_acc, one accepted watt at the coil terminals Map identity C4 across the four drives σ_y mirror of the one drive

Which C, and what "tuned" means here. The capacitor is C_mode,Cu = 6.358914053477356e-11 F (63.589141 pF): the k = 1-block construction at 64 MHz on the degree-2 exact 4×4. It is read from tune_p2.json["c_mode"]["cu"] and never recomputed (20261004T140347Z_ANS-7-item217-W1-cmode.log:2088). Known-issues 2026-10-04 (T21) is open: with this C, the in-model zero of Im Y_in sits at 64 000 308.55 Hz, 4.82e-6 above 64 MHz against the 1e-6 BANDS band (20261004T140738Z_ANS-7-item217-W2-inmodel.log:2049–2050). Whether "tuned" means C_mode or C_in is the weekly's question. This item does not claim the coil is tuned to 64.000 MHz. It drives at 64.0 MHz at C_mode,Cu. That frequency is 308.55 Hz from the in-model zero, i.e. 9.4e-3 of the half-linewidth f₀/(2Q_A) = 32.9 kHz (Q_A 972.90). Normalising per accepted watt removes the mismatch, and the detuning moves the field shape at O((9.4e-3)²) ≈ 1e-4 (printed estimate). Every asserted anchor below is an identity that holds for any C.

Code. New tests/validation/test_mat15_tuned_copper_heating.py, @complex_only, with one module-scoped fixture so the EM solve runs once. - Opt-in knob FEM_EM_MAT15_STEP3=1. Unset ⇒ every test in the module skips; any other value raises ValueError. That keeps default suites from collecting a -n 8 heavy job that needs gitignored inputs. No existing module, helper default or record moves, so the change is unset-identical by construction. - Imports only, never test_* names. - From step 1's module: _tag_submesh, _cell_average_dg0_tag, _cn, _be_one, _e_prime, _max_imag, K_GEL, H_GEL, T_INF, A, T_R, T_STAR, N_MAIN, DT_1, D_CONTROL_FLOOR, F_CONTROL_FLOOR, CAD_AREA_M2. - From MAT-10: _robin_tags, _to_sub, _allsum, _say, B_BAND, ROBIN_TAG. - From MAT-12: E_BAND, S2_BAND, RHO_C. - Ball means: C4_COVARIANCE_BAND and PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3 (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map), CENTRE_RADIUS_M, QUADRATURE_DEGREE, TEN_GRAM_KG, averaging_ball_radius, mean_sar. - From TH-14: the module as th14 (for _exact_geo / _route_a_solve), plus _surface_loss_w, DRIVEN, COPPER_SIGMA and PHANTOM_CELL_TAG. - From test_birdcage_power_identity: _source_power_w, _sheet_field_dissipation_w, DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. - From test_ans7_exact_strip: _exact_geo, _fixture_tie, _assert_tie, _route_a_solve, OUT_DIR, GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION. - From test_ans7_sparse_route_b: _ANS7 (z_cap, TUNING_TERMINATED_INDICES), NODE_S_RTOL, _p_inc_w. - _sheet_azimuth_deg from tests.mesh.test_birdcage_leg_offset, and SHEET_IFACE. - Do not edit step 1's module, test_ans7_exact_strip.py, test_ans7_sparse_route_b.py or the ans:7 script. ans:9 imports step 1's _run_heated, and item 230 has just re-issued ans:7. An edit to any of them owes those gates' windows under rule (a). - Fixture body, in this order. 1. Read the two T21 JSONs and fail if either is absent. Check: degree == 2; |f_hz − 64e6| < 1; cells == 80798; tune_inmodel_p2.json["tune_mhz"] == [63.9, 64.0, 64.1]; and its c_mode equal to tune_p2.json["c_mode"]["cu"] bit for bit. Take S11_ref = s11_a[1], the 64.0 MHz point. 2. tie = _fixture_tie(), then geo, specs, cells = _exact_geo(th14, comm, GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION). 3. φ₁ = _sheet_azimuth_deg(msh, tags_f, SHEET_IFACE + 1, comm), the bbox centre of an exact rectangle. This precondition runs before the solve. 4. s11, fields = _route_a_solve(th14, geo, specs, 64.0e6, "cu", c_f=c_mode, return_fields=True, degree=2). 5. Power. - Rebuild the solve's specs exactly as _route_a_solve does: dataclasses.replace(s, port_impedance_ohm=_ANS7.z_cap(ω, c_mode)) for i ∈ TUNING_TERMINATED_INDICES. - Build the sheets as sp.sheet(driven=(sp.port_id == DRIVEN)) and set acct = {"mesh": msh, "facet_tags": tags_f}. - Compute P_src, ΣP_sheet, P_total = ½∫σ|E|², P_phantom (both _vol(dx(PHANTOM_CELL_TAG)) and mean_sar(...)["dissipated_power_w"]), and P_surf = _surface_loss_w(msh, facet_tags, z_s, e, comm), with z_s = (1 + j)·surface_resistance_ohm(ω, COPPER_SIGMA). This is TH-14's (b) block, test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:375–407, verbatim. - P_acc = P_src − ΣP_sheet. C₁ is lossless, so P_acc is the power accepted at the coil terminals. Then G = 1 W / P_acc. 6. Thermal. Step 1's per-drive loop body (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:217–301) for this one drive, with dep = G·P_phantom (= η W): - submesh and Robin tags, q_h through _cell_average_dg0_tag → _to_sub; - (B), κ_s, _cn, (E′) through _e_prime, then _be_one and (S2); - control (d) on a doubled q_h; - max|Im θ|. 7. Ball means at t*. Eight centres at radius CENTRE_RADIUS_M, azimuths φ₁ + m·45° (m = 0 … 7), with step 1's compiled ball forms (:231–261). Print each ball volume beside (4/3)π·a₁₀³.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported, none restated): - (F) _assert_tie(cells, tie): 80 798 cells within CELL_COUNT_BAND, and all four N_i rectangles within STRIP_BAND. This is the ruling's CAD identity. - (Φ) precondition: |sin φ₁| ≤ 1e-9, so the mirror through the driven leg is σ_y (y → −y). Step 1 printed P1 at 360.0° on its fixture. The bbox of an exact rectangle is a set of CAD corners. - (W) source wiring: |S11 − S11_ref|/|S11_ref| ≤ NODE_S_RTOL. This is a deterministic re-solve of T21's own 64.0 MHz C_mode drive on the same mesh, at the same width and degree. It is backed by the same comparison on the same fixture, T21 (W) at 2.77e-14 (…140738Z…-W2-inmodel.log:2045), with S11_A printed at :2047. - (P) accepted-power identity: |P_src − ΣP_sheet − P_phantom − P_(Ω∖phantom) − P_surf|/|P_src| ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. This is TH-14's (b) on the tuned configuration, and it ties the accepted watt to the phantom's deposited share. Item 196 measured it at degree 2 on this mesh, in the 50 Ω-terminated configuration: 1.355e-12 (20261003T124111Z_ANS-7-item196-W2-p2.log:2038). - (B) |∫_sub q_h dV − G·P_phantom|/(G·P_phantom) ≤ B_BAND. - (E) Every thermal run's max_balance_residual ≤ E_BAND. - (E′) the energy identity: ρc∫Δθ/Δt + ∮hθ^(n+½) = G·Phantom, **from t EM side, ≤ E_BAND. - **(S2)he calorimetric slope: |ρc·θ̄¹Δt₁·G·P_phantom/V_sub) − 1| ≤ S2_BAND, one BE step Δt₁ from θ = 0. - (M) σ_y mirror image: 10 g ball means of θ at t*. (M1) θ̄(φ₁ + 90°) against θ̄(φ₁ − 90°), and (M2) θ̄(φ₁ + 45°) against θ̄(φ₁ − 45°), each relative to the first ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND.

Imported vs printed — the bands, read against rule (f). - Imported: B_BAND 1e-10 (MAT-10) and E_BAND 1e-9 (MAT-12) are pre-stated round-off bands. Neither depends on EM order. - Imported: S2_BAND 1e-4 is MAT-12's pre-stated time-truncation bound, on the P1 thermal side. EM order enters only through κ_s. The deficit is ≈ 3.44e-6·κ_s, so the bound holds to κ_s ≈ 29. - Imported: C4_COVARIANCE_BAND 5 % was pre-registered before any reading. Its provenance was measured at degree 1 (CG1 |B₁⁺| 2.19 % worst, WF-6 step 1b, test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:108–120), but the value was never registered by measurement under rule (f). It can therefore be imported at degree 2. The asymmetry it bounds here comes from the phantom's P1 mesh, which does not depend on EM order. - Imported: DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL 1e-6 and NODE_S_RTOL 1e-9. - No band in MAT-15 was registered by measurement at degree 1. The rule (f) moves in its history (2(a)'s (R0) / (R2) parameters, 2(b)'s centroid bar 1e-5·a) belong to step 2 and are not used here. - Printed only: step 1's records are ANS-2-rung numbers: V_SUB_RECORD_M3, P1_RECORD_W, κ_s 1.65, and mean θ(t*) 1.153 K per deposited watt. On this mesh they appear only as references beside the new values, never as comparands, and this item registers no new record.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (d) doubled source: (E′) against G·P_phantom reads 1.000, by linearity on any fixture. Step 1 measured 1.000000 (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1948). Like step 1's test_control_d_…, it is asserted only as a miss, > D_CONTROL_FLOOR. - (f′) off-mirror pair: θ̄(φ₁ + 90°) against θ̄(φ₁), relative to θ̄(φ₁). - Prediction: 40–80 %. Leg currents go as cos(φ − φ₁), so the gap voltages at φ₁ ± 90° are ≈ 0, and the eddy E_z ∝ x vanishes on x = 0. - Never measured, so the factor is printed beside the reading. Only the miss is asserted (> F_CONTROL_FLOOR), as step 1's (f) was. - Ceiling: ≤ 1 when θ̄(φ₁ + 90°) ≤ θ̄(φ₁), so the 5 % floor sits 20× under it. - (P-ctl): the identity with ΣP_sheet dropped misses by ≈ P_sheet/P_src ≈ 0.998, because R_bare ≈ 0.08 Ω sits against the 50 Ω source sheet. Predicted, printed, never asserted.

Predictions (written first, printed): - Tag-3 cells in [300, 3 000]. V_sub against πa²·2L = 2.26195e-4 m³: deficit in [−3e-2, 0]. - (W) ≤ 1e-12. (P) ≤ 1e-10. - P_phantom, mean_sar against _vol: ≤ 1e-12. - η = P_phantom/P_acc in [0.52, 0.62]. The estimate is Q_Cu/Q_PEC at C_mode,Cu, 969.21/1664.90 = 0.582 (T21 (T1), …140347Z…-W1-cmode.log:2090–2091). P_surf/P_acc = 1 − η to (P). - L_S = 1 − |S11|² ≈ 4.05e-3 (from :2047's S11_A) against L_F = P_acc/_p_inc_w(): |L_S − L_F| ≤ 1e-4 absolute. Printed only: in the 50 Ω configuration this is item 196's (L), and it is unmeasured here. - (B) ≤ 1e-13. (E), (E′) ≤ 1e-12. κ_s in [1.5, 6]: a uniform E_z ∝ x alone gives 1.73, and the gap-voltage E adds surface weight. - (S2) ≈ 3.44e-6·κ_s, in [5e-6, 2.1e-5]. - The first thermal figure on a tuned coil: mean θ(t*) per accepted watt in [0.55, 0.75] K, which is η × step 1's 1.153 K per deposited watt (:1929). The peak 10 g θ̄ per accepted watt is printed with its azimuth. - (M1), (M2) ≤ 1 %. The q_h 10 g mirror pairs are printed, predicted ≤ 3 %. The C2 pair θ̄(φ₁) against θ̄(φ₁ + 180°) is not a symmetry of a one-port drive; it is printed, predicted ≤ 2 %. - max|Im θ| = 0.

Windows (-n 8; bare, whole, foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; -s; tests/environment first). - Price, measured at -n 8 on this mesh: - pytest start-up + tests/environment + _fixture_tie ≈ 90 s (T21 W2: 261 s window less its 171.4 s fixture, :2052); - _exact_geo mesh 24.4 s; - one degree-2 C_mode drive 41.8–50.3 s (:2052); - degree-2 post-processing forms ≈ 10–40 s (first compile of the mean_sar and DG0-average forms at degree 2); - the thermal side ≈ 5 s on ≈ 10³ phantom cells. Step 1 ran four drives plus the control on 58 866 cells in 29 s at -n 2. - Total ≈ 200–260 s, or ≤ 365 s on item 214's ×1.4 slow box. That is inside the container's 590 s. - First: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Then run the any-orphan sweep (item 160's 44 KB partial .c trap) as one bare call:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-15-step3-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - W1 (≈ 200–260 s), the closing window:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-15-step3-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_ANS_SKIP_PRIVATE=1 FEM_EM_MAT15_STEP3=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat15_tuned_copper_heating.py -v -s --tb=short'" - No edit after W1 (rule (i)). Any edit re-runs W1. One window and one re-run fit the hour.

Traps already paid for. - Orphan .c: a stem with no .so, not only 0-byte (item 160, 44 345 bytes). docs.title: Proposed §7 row (draft)
docs.text:
CEM43 thermal dose as a post-processor on a temperature history — Phase 8. fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py: cem43(times_s, temperatures_c, *, rule="trapezoid", r_above=0.5, r_below=0.25) returns minutes:

CEM43 = (1/60)∫ R(T)^(43 − T) dt, with R = 0.5 for T ≥ 43 °C and 0.25 below (Sapareto & Dewey 1984, Int. J. Radiat. Oncol. Biol. Phys. 10:787).

rule="interval_mean" is the paper's discrete sum Σ Δtᵢ R^(43 − T̄ᵢ). The function is numpy only. The closed forms go into utils/analytical.py (additive).

Done-when, step 1 (numpy, real build, -n 1). Write κ = −ln R and G(T) = expm1(κ(T)(T − 43))/κ(T). G is continuous at 43 °C, and G′ = R^(43 − T). - (C1) Constant T. Five exact binary cases, and an unevenly sampled constant history, to ≤ 1e-13. - (C2) Ramp. The ramp equals [G(T_end) − G(T₀)]/(60a), against the explicit two-piece split ≤ 1e-13 and against Gauss–Legendre ≤ 1e-12 (37 → 47 °C at 0.01 K/s: 37.26933 min). The cooling ramp equals the heating ramp. - (C3) Exponential approach. Via Ei, against Gauss–Legendre ≤ 1e-11 on five cases. The late-time slope is asserted ≤ 1e-9. - (C4) Convergence. The trapezoid rule on the 43 °C-crossing ramp has an LSQ rate in [1.9, 2.1], and so does interval_mean. - (K) The 43 °C kink. The ramp from 43 − ε to 43 + ε reads 1 − (ln 2/4)ε within 1e-6 at ε = 1e-3.

Controls, each asserted: - R swapped: misses by ×4 on the constant cases and ×8.2894 on the ramp. - Kelvin input: misses by a log₂ factor of 273.15 / 275.15 / 273.194. - The antiderivative without its 43 °C anchor: misses the ramp by exactly 1.2023 min.

Out of scope: tissue-damage thresholds and any biological or regulatory claim; Arrhenius damage; spatial dose maps; ASTM F2182.

Step 2 (not drafted for queueing): CEM43 of MAT-12's FEM centre history beside the closed-form series. Dose amplifies θ errors exponentially: MAT-12's ≈ 3.5 % SAR offset on an 8 K rise becomes ≈ 21 % in CEM43 above 43 °C. Setting that band is the weekly's.

docs.text:
• Measured class. Lane-3 closed form, median 8 min (n = 5). Predicted ≈ 35 min: a ≈ 1 min window, 15 fixed, ≈ 20 for code.
  • Traps the drafter found.
  • Compute G with np.expm1. The naive exp − 1 loses ≈ 1e-7 relative at ε = 1e-9, and (K) catches that.
  • Use one 43-anchored G on every piece. A per-piece f/κ is exactly the unanchored control.
  • e^{−t/τ} underflows past t/τ ≈ 745, so refuse a duration > 200τ.
  • Do not export from thermal/__init__.py. It imports dolfinx, and an export would force rule (c) windows on MAT-9 … MAT-14.
  • Inputs are absolute °C, not θ.
  • Pre-derived numbers. Trapezoid errors on N = 12·2^j are ≈ +2.88e-2 / 6.98e-3 / 1.80e-3 / 4.36e-4 / 1.12e-4. The kink-cell term makes the pairwise rates alternate (2.04 / 1.96), so only the LSQ slope is asserted. The exponential case (37 → T∞ 45, τ 300 s, 1800 s) is ≈ 72.45 min by hand.

Closing note (2026-10-25). The (K) kink and expm1 hazards drafted here were read against MAT-20's cem43 (§9 item 638, docs/planning/chunks/MAT-20.md#§9-item-638): both held at DOSE_BAR; this draft is not queued.
