docs.title: §9 item 189 — 2026-10-02 (lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only Plan agent and reviewed by the 2026-10-02 18:00 daily review.

MAT-17 step 1: the duty-cycled Robin gel ball in closed form. It is verified by residuals and by two independent routes before any FEM. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2, real build. - Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min (≈ 1 min window + 15 fixed + ≈ 25 code). - Depends on: nothing.

Not already covered. MAT-9…MAT-14 and MAT-5 use one homogeneous ball with a constant or once-switched source. solve_transient_conduction cannot switch a source off ("step source", thermal/transient.py:20). No row mentions duty cycles.

Fixture. - MAT-9's ball: R 0.1, k 0.6, ρc 4.18e6, q 2000, h 10 (Bi 5/3), T∞ = T(0) = 20, t_R = R²ρc/k = 69 667 s. - The source is on while 0 ≤ (t mod P) < DP, from t = 0. - Case A: P = 1200 s, D = 0.5. Case B: P = 0.2 t_R, D = 0.25.

Anchor (closed form). - Modal form: θ = Σ Bₙ Xₙ(r) gₙ(t). λₙ come from robin_sphere_eigenvalues; Bₙ and Xₙ from robin_sphere_transient_coefficients (θ_ss = Σ Bₙ Xₙ); sₙ = λₙ²/t_R. - Cycle j, t = jP + τ: - start value g_{j,0} = Gₙ(1 − e^{−j sₙ P}), with Gₙ = e^{−sₙ(1−D)P}(1 − e^{−sₙDP})/(1 − e^{−sₙP}); - on phase: θ = θ_ss(r) − Σ Bₙ Xₙ (1 − g_{j,0}) e^{−sₙτ}, with θ_ss in closed form; - off phase: θ = Σ Bₙ Xₙ g_end e^{−sₙ(τ − DP)}. - Fourier route (uses neither λₙ nor Bₙ): - θ_p = D·θ_ss + 2 Re Σ_{m≥1} ûₘ Θ(r; ωₘ) e^{iωₘt}, with ωₘ = 2πm/P and ûₘ = (1 − e^{−iωₘDP})/(iωₘP); - Θ = (q/w)[1 − Bi·R·S(r)/Dₙ] at w = iωρc, γ = √(w/k). This is MAT-11's perfused steady state continued to complex w. - Duhamel: θ(t) = Σⱼ (−1)ʲ θ_step(t − tⱼ), summed over the switch instants tⱼ. - Sources: Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids 2e, ch. I (Duhamel's theorem) and ch. IX (the sphere with heat production and a radiation boundary); Incropera §5.6 for the λₙ equation, as robin_sphere_eigenvalues already cites. Equation numbers are unpinned because the repo holds no copy, the same footing as MAT-9…MAT-15. The docstring derives every form.

Code (additive in utils/analytical.py; scipy imported inside the functions; nothing exported from thermal/__init__, which imports dolfinx): - robin_sphere_duty_cycle_temperature(r, t, *, radius, k, rho_c, q, h, t_inf, period, duty, n_terms=400, periodic=False); - _robin_sphere_complex_w(r, w, *, radius, k, q, h), the complex Θ, with robin_sphere_periodic_harmonic(r, omega, *, radius, k, rho_c, q, h) on top of it; - the test, tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py.

Evaluation set. r ∈ {0, R/2, R}; eight times per phase, at fractions 0.05 … 0.95 of the phase. Never within 0.05 of a switch.

Anchors (asserted). - (H0) _robin_sphere_complex_w at a real w > 0 equals robin_sphere_perfusion_temperature (t_inf 0) to ≤ 1e-13 relative. - (H1) Robin residuals. - −kΘ′(R) − hΘ(R) at m ∈ {1, 10, 1000}: ≤ 1e-12 relative to h|Θ(R)|. - The periodic modal form's residual, from analytic derivatives: ≤ 1e-10·qR/h. - (P1) The periodic cycle mean (each phase's time integral taken analytically per mode) equals D·θ_ss(r) to ≤ 1e-12·θ_ss(0), in both cases. - (P2) The periodic modal form matches the Fourier route at M = 2¹⁶ to ≤ 1e-9·θ_ss(0), in both cases (predicted ≲ 5e-11). - (P3) The from-rest form matches the Duhamel superposition of robin_sphere_transient_temperature (t_init = t_inf) over cycles 0–5 to ≤ 1e-10·θ_ss(0). - (P4) duty = 1 equals robin_sphere_transient_temperature to ≤ 1e-13. duty ∉ (0, 1] raises ValueError. - (P5) From rest, at cycle j* = ⌈30τ₁/P⌉, the form equals the periodic one to ≤ 1e-12·θ_ss(0).

Printed (predicted, never asserted). - θ_ss(0) = 12.2222 K. - λ₁ ≈ 1.91, so τ₁ = t_R/λ₁² ≈ 1.91e4 s. - Case A: - centre mean 6.1111 K (exact by (P1)); - centre ripple peak to peak ≈ q(1−D)DP/ρc = 0.1435 K, so peak/(D·θ_ss) − 1 ≈ +1.2 %; - ≈ 110 cycles to come within 1e-3 of the periodic state. - Case B: peak, trough and mean (no hand prediction). - The Fourier ladder M = 2¹⁰…2¹⁶ on the evaluation set and at the switch instants, where the convergence is O(1/M).

Negative controls. Rule (e): all are predicted, since nothing has been measured on this fixture. Each is asserted only as exceeding its anchor's band, with the measured factor printed beside the prediction. - (c1) Dirichlet roots λₙ = nπ (Bₙ re-projected) in the periodic modal form, against (P2). Predicted ≈ 0.27·θ_ss(0) at the centre in case A. Asserted > 1e-3. - (c2) The geometric sum dropped (g_{j,0} = 0 every cycle), against (P5). Predicted ≈ 0.49. Asserted > 1e-3. - (c3) The e^{−iωt} convention (Θ at −ωₘ, same ûₘ), against (P2). Predicted ≈ 1e-2 in case A and ≈ 1e-1 in case B. Asserted > 1e-6.

Window. Foreground, Bash timeout: 660000. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Predicted 50–70 s; the three lane-3 numpy windows on 10-01 measured 45–52 s (closest: 20261001T143248Z_MAT-15-step2a-W1b.log).

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-17-step1-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py tests/unit/test_analytical_lightweight.py -v -s --tb=short'"

The lightweight test is the rule (c) re-gate of the additive analytical.py change.

Traps. - Series convergence. Σ Bₙ Xₙ alone converges only as 1/N²: at r = 0 the tail is ≈ 2e-5 K at N = 400. Use the closed-form θ_ss in the on phase and keep the decaying factor in the off phase. s_N ≈ 22.7 /s, so never assert near a switch. - Cancellation. Compute 1 − e^{−sP} with -np.expm1. - Overflow. Θ overflows once |γR| reaches a few hundred. Use the scaled form, as _robin_sphere_perfusion_scaled does: - S(r) = e^{−γ(R−r)}(1 − e^{−2γr})/(2r); - S(0) = γe^{−γR}; - Dₙ = [γR(1 + e^{−2γR}) + (Bi − 1)(1 − e^{−2γR})]/2.

Check that np.expm1 accepts complex input, or write the expression out. - m = 0 is handled separately as D·θ_ss: q/(iω) is singular there. - Sign convention. Use e^{+jωt} throughout (the repo convention), with ûₘ taken against e^{−iωₘt}. - Memory. Sum the harmonics in blocks of ≤ 8192 to bound memory on two ranks. - Output. Print on rank 0. The real build skips the four complex-only environment tests; that is expected. - Rule (i): no edit after the last window. - Rule (f): a W1 red on a pre-registered parameter (δ, a time fraction), never on a bound, may be re-registered by measurement. Disclose it, run W1b, and the review ratifies (the 10-01 lesson, items 136–137). - Shared file. Item 190 also appends to analytical.py: append at the end, and rebase if 190 lands first.

Scope. Numpy only: a uniform source on MAT-9's ball. Not included: - the FEM (step 2) and the solver's source schedule; - an SAR- or coil-driven duty cycle; - perfusion; - any pulse-sequence or 6-min-averaging claim.

Status it can move. §7 MAT-17 ⬜ → 🟡 on the row's step-1 Done-when, which this item matches (rule (j)). Step 2 then becomes draftable.

Negative result. - (H0), (H1), (P1), (P4) or (P5) red: a code bug. Fix it in-slot, run W1b and disclose. - (P2) red with (P3) green, or the reverse: one route is wrong. Print both routes and the M ladder at the failing points, then stop. Park on attempt/MAT-17-step1-<UTC>, mark BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); the row stays ⬜. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Outcome — DONE 2026-10-03 (19:30 CDT slot, implementer). W1 20261003T010113Z_MAT-17-step1-W1.log passed first time: -n 2, 66 s, 26 passed, 4 skipped. No W1b was needed.

Anchors, case A / case B: - (H0) ≤ 1.6e-16. - (H1) The complex Robin residual is ≤ 3.3e-16, and the periodic modal residual is 1.1e-15 / 1.3e-15 of qR/h. - (P1) 1.5e-16 / 0. - (P2) 2.1e-12 / 8.1e-11. Case B is above the predicted ≲ 5e-11 but inside the 1e-9 band. - (P3) 1.2e-15 / 1.0e-15. - (P4) 5.8e-16, and a duty outside (0, 1] raises. - (P5) 4.9e-14 at j* = 479 / 1.1e-14 at j* = 42.

Controls, case A / case B: - (c1) 0.278 / 0.442 (predicted ≈ 0.27 in case A). - (c2) 0.494 / 0.195 (predicted ≈ 0.49, which was case A's figure). - (c3) 1.06e-2 / 9.7e-2 (predicted ≈ 1e-2 / 1e-1).

Records: - θ_ss(0) = 12.2222 K, λ₁ = 1.90709, τ₁ = 1.9155e4 s. - Case A, centre: mean 6.1111 K, ripple 0.14354 K, peak +1.17 % above D·θ_ss. It takes 111 cycles to come within 1e-3 of D·θ_ss(0), the reading the executor chose because the brief left the reference unstated. - Case B, centre: peak 3.6801 K, trough 2.4042 K, mean 3.0556 K. - Fourier ladder: O(1/M) at the switch instants.

Disclosed: - The complex 1 − e^{−z} uses a 13-term series below |z| = 0.1 rather than np.expm1. - The case B c1 print line reuses case A's prediction text. It is a print only.

Row ⬜ → 🟡; step 2 is draftable.

docs.title: §9 item 200 — 2026-10-03 (lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 03:00 daily review; the review reviewed it.

MAT-17 step 2: a per-step source schedule in solve_transient_conduction, gated against step 1's closed form on MAT-9's ball. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2; W1 and W2 real build, W3 complex. Class: lane-3 closed form (measured median 8 min). - Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 25 code + three ≈ 2-min windows). - Depends on: nothing. utils/analytical.py is not edited by this item; if the executor finds it must add a helper there, append-only after item 199's MAT-18 block, and rebase.

Target — the §7 row's step-2 Done-when, verbatim: "an additive per-step source schedule in solve_transient_conduction reproduces step 1 on MAT-9's ball at MAT-9 step 2's imported bands (interior ≤ 1 %, BE rate ∈ [0.9, 1.2], per-step balance ≤ 1e-9), with MAT-9…MAT-14's transient gates re-run green ⇒ ✅". "Default digit-identical" is the item's letter (below).

Code (additive; rule (c), disclosed). - thermal/transient.py: keyword source_schedule=None on solve_transient_conduction and _solve_transient (transient.py:73–91, :122–140). It is a callable χ(t_mid) -> float, evaluated at the midpoint of every (half-)step, that multiplies the ufl.inner(q_c, v) * ufl.dx term of L (:184) through a new fem.Constant s_c set before each solve. - Step times come from the integer index, never accumulated: half-step i spans [i·Δt/2, (i + 1)·Δt/2]; full step i after the start spans [(m/2 + i)·Δt, (m/2 + i + 1)·Δt]. - Build the scaled L only when a schedule is given — the perfused pattern (:171–189). With None every form is byte-identical, so it hits the same JIT cache entry and gives the same digits. - Balance under a schedule: |stor + conv + perf − s_n·src| / |src|, normalised by the full-on source_power (:199–201, :247), never by s_n·src (zero on an off step). The None path is unchanged. - Additive result field source_multipliers: one entry per (half-)step, filled only under a schedule. - New test tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem.py. - Imported read-only from test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere.py: R, K, Q, H, T_INF, RHO_C, T_R, ROBIN_TAG, QDEG, _ball, _interior_error, _rel_diff, _say. From step 1's module: CASES (test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py:44). - Comparand: robin_sphere_duty_cycle_temperature(…, periodic=False) (analytical.py:1909), evaluated in numpy at the P2 dof coordinates in chunks of 20 000 points (MAT-9's _exact_theta, :93–106).

Fixture. MAT-9's ball (R 0.1, k 0.6, ρc 4.18e6, q 2000, h 10, T∞ = T(0) = 20), P1. - Case A (P 1200 s, D 0.5): t_end = 11P + 900 s = 14 100 s (Fo 0.2024), the middle of cycle 11's off phase. Every Δt used divides both DP = 600 s and (1 − D)P/2 = 300 s. So every switch is a step boundary, every step midpoint is ≥ Δt/2 from a switch, and χ is exactly 0 or 1. - Case B (P = 0.2 t_R, D 0.25): t_end = 2.5·DP = 8 708.3 s (Fo 0.125), the middle of cycle 0's off phase; Δt = DP/8, so 20 steps.

Anchors (asserted). The bands are MAT-9 step 2's, imported by value: they are literals at test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere.py:274–275, 301–302, with no module constant to import. - (S0) Schedule census, every run: Σ s_n·Δt_n equals the on-time in [0, t_end] to ≤ 1e-12 relative. That is 12 × 600 = 7 200 s for case A, and DP for case B. - (D) Default path: source_schedule=lambda t: 1.0 against the default call, on the 0.01 m mesh, BE, Δt 300, 47 steps. Whole-ball ‖ΔT‖/‖θ‖ ≤ 1e-13 (predicted ≤ 1e-15). - (L) Linearity: θ[χ] + θ[1 − χ] = θ[1], BE, Δt 150, 0.01 m. Whole-ball relative ≤ 1e-12 (predicted ≈ 1e-15). It is exact because the θ-scheme is linear in the source when T(0) = T∞. - (i) Interior: CN with the Rannacher start (startup_half_steps=2) on the 0.005 m mesh — case A at Δt 150 (N 94), case B at Δt DP/8 (N 20). Interior relative L2 on θ (MAT-9's mask |x|² < 0.81R²) ≤ 1 % in each case. Predicted 5e-4 – 2e-3; MAT-9's CN N 40 read 4.6327e-4 on this mesh (20260929T170037Z_MAT-9-step2b.log:114). - (ii) BE rate: 0.01 m mesh, case A, Δt ∈ {300, 150, 75, 37.5, 18.75} (N 47 … 752). The whole-ball self-difference LSQ rate is in [0.9, 1.2] (predicted ≈ 1.0; MAT-9's BE read 0.984, …step2b.log:124). - (iii) Balance: every run's max_balance_residual ≤ 1e-9 (predicted ≤ 5e-14). - (R) Re-gate: W2 and W3 run the MAT-9, MAT-12, MAT-13 and MAT-14 transient modules green. The slot also checks that W2's MAT-9 lines reproduce …step2b.log:114, 124, 130 digit for digit (interior 4.6327e-04, BE LSQ 0.984, CN 2.001) and journals the comparison. A changed digit on the None path is a stop.

Printed (predicted, never asserted). - The CN ladder rate on case A (predicted ≈ 2.0), and the interior error of CN without the Rannacher start. - The BE N 752 interior error against the series. Predicted ≈ 2.8e-3, the 0.01 m spatial floor: MAT-9's BE N 160 read 2.8063e-3 (20260929T112146Z_MAT-9-step2.log:122). - θ_h(0) beside the closed form at t_end. - On/off step counts (case A at N 94: 48 on, 46 off). - The wall clock of every run.

Negative controls. Rule (e): all are predicted, since this comparison has never been measured. Each is asserted only as missing its anchor's band, with the measured value printed beside the prediction. - (c1) Schedule ignored — the default call, source always on — against case A's duty comparand at t_end, on (i)'s mesh and Δt. Predicted ≈ 1.0 (range 0.8–1.2): the step response is about twice the D = 0.5 history. Asserted > 1e-2. - (c2) Schedule dropped from the balance. On case A's CN run, take snapshots 93 and 94. Step 93→94 is an off step (midpoint 14 025 s, τ = 825 s). Compute |ρc∫(T₉₄ − T₉₃)/Δt + ∮h(½T₉₄ + ½T₉₃ − T∞) − ∫Q|/∫Q, the form of MAT-9's control (b) (:285–292). Predicted 1.000; asserted > 1e-3. - (c3) Half-phase shift, printed only: χ(t − 300 s) against the true comparand. Interior miss predicted 2–4 % (the half ripple, 0.072 K, over θ ≈ 2.5 K). It is not asserted because its ceiling is too close to the band.

docs.title: §9 item 190 — 2026-10-02 (lane 3)
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only Plan agent and reviewed by the 2026-10-02 18:00 daily review.

MAT-18 step 1: the two-layer sphere in closed form — a gel core, a container-wall shell and a Robin outer surface, verified by residuals before any FEM. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2, real build. - Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min (≈ 1 min window + 15 fixed + ≈ 30 code). - Depends on: nothing.

Every thermal gate so far uses one homogeneous medium. This is the first material interface: θ and k∂ᵣθ continuous across it.

Fixture. - Core, r < a = 0.1, gel: k₁ 0.6, ρc₁ 4.18e6, q₁ 2000. - Shell, a < r < b = 0.11: k₂ 0.19, ρc₂ 1.7e6, q₂ 0. These are representative acrylic-wall parameters, not a material claim. - Outside: h 10 on r = b; T∞ = T(0) = 20; t_R = a²ρc₁/k₁ = 69 667 s.

Anchor (closed form). - Steady, general q₂: - θ(b) = [q₁a³ + q₂(b³ − a³)]/(3hb²); - shell: θ = θ(b) + (q₁ − q₂)a³(1/r − 1/b)/(3k₂) + q₂(b² − r²)/(6k₂); - core: θ = θ(a) + q₁(a² − r²)/(6k₁).

This is the spherical-wall resistance (1/r₁ − 1/r₂)/(4πk) of Incropera ch. 3 (radial systems), in series with the convective film. - Transient, with u = rψ and μᵢ = √(s/αᵢ): - core: u = sin μ₁r; - shell: u₂ = u₂(a)cos μ₂(r − a) + u₂′(a) sin μ₂(r − a)/μ₂, with u₂(a) = sin μ₁a and u₂′(a) = [k₁μ₁cos μ₁a − (k₁ − k₂) sin μ₁a/a]/k₂ (flux continuity); - eigencondition: F(s) = k₂u₂′(b) − (k₂/b − h)u₂(b) = 0. F is entire in s, with no poles; - solution: θ = θ_ss − Σ cₙψₙe^{−sₙt}, with cₙ = ∫qψₙr²dr/(sₙNₙ) and Nₙ = ∫ρc uₙ²dr. - Source: Carslaw & Jaeger 2e, ch. IX (the sphere; the composite-sphere case). Equation numbers are unpinned (no copy in the repo); the docstring derives every form.

Code (additive in utils/analytical.py, scipy imported inside the functions): - two_layer_sphere_steady_temperature(r, *, a, b, k1, k2, q1, q2=0.0, h, t_inf); - two_layer_sphere_eigenvalues(*, a, b, k1, k2, rho_c1, rho_c2, h, n); - two_layer_sphere_transient_temperature(r, t, *, …, t_init, n_terms=400); - the test, tests/validation/test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form.py.

Anchors (asserted). - (S1) Steady. - θ and k∂ᵣθ continuous at a, ≤ 1e-13 relative. - Robin residual at b, ≤ 1e-13. - 4πb²hθ(b) = q₁·4πa³/3 to ≤ 1e-13. - With k₂ = k₁ and q₂ = q₁, it equals robin_sphere_steady_temperature(radius=b) to ≤ 1e-13. - With b = a(1 + 1e-9), it equals …(radius=a) to ≤ 1e-7 (predicted ≈ 4e-9). - (R0) Roots. - |F(sₙ)| ≤ 1e-12 of scale. - For n ≤ 60, ψₙ has exactly n − 1 sign changes in (0, b): Sturm–Liouville oscillation, so no root is missed or doubled. - Nₙ analytic against Gauss–Legendre split at r = a: ≤ 1e-12 in |ΔN|/max N. - Weighted Gram: |⟨ψₘ, ψₙ⟩_{ρc r²}|/√(NₘNₙ) ≤ 1e-10 for m ≠ n ≤ 60. - (R1) cₙ in the Green form against the direct ∫ρcθsψₙrr/Nₙ by Gauss–Legendre: ≤ 1e-10 in |Δc|/max|c|. - (R2) Transient interface residuals (θ and k∂ᵣθ) and the Robin residual, from analytic derivatives at Fo 0.05, 0.2 and 1: ≤ 1e-10·q₁a²/k₁. - (R3)** The bance d/dt∫ρcθ dV + 4πb²hθ(b) = q₁V_core, analytic per mode at Fo 0.05, 0.2 and 1: ≤ 1e-10 relative. - (R4) Limits. - Fo 50 gives θ_ss to ≤ 1e-12. - At equal properties with q₂ = q₁, it matches robin_sphere_transient_temperature(radius=b) to ≤ 1e-10·θ_ss(0) at Fo 0.05, 0.2 and 1. - The root difference against robin_sphere_eigenvalues(hb/k) is printed.

Why split. The row's step 2 bundles a new mesher, piecewise k and ρc in both solvers, a steady ladder, a CN run and a six-module re-gate. That is ≈ 70 predicted minutes, more than one slot. So: - 2(a), this item: the mesher, piecewise k in solve_steady_conduction, the steady anchors and the uniform-k control, plus the re-gate of steady.py's users; - 2(b), not briefed here: see the end of this brief.

The review amends the row's step-2 Done-when into 2(a) / 2(b) in the commit that queues this item (rule (j)).

Code (additive; rule (c), disclosed). - io/mesh.py: MeshGenerator.two_layer_ball_domain(inner_radius=0.1, outer_radius=0.11, resolution=0.01, comm=MPI.COMM_WORLD, rank=0), modelled on ball_domain (io/mesh.py:2649–2701). - OCC spheres of radius a and b, then occ.fragment, following the sphere_in_box_domain precedent (:2320). Identify the two volumes by occ.getMass(3, ·) (the core is 4πa³/3), never by tag order. - Cell tag 1 is the core and cell tag 2 the shell. Facet tag 1 is the r = b surface only. - Uniform Mesh.MeshSizeMin = Mesh.MeshSizeMax = resolution, with point, boundary and curvature sizing off, exactly as ball_domain does. - No dim-2 physical group on the r = a interface. Interior facet groups hang model_to_mesh at -n 2 (known-issues 9, io/mesh.py:124–130). If a later step needs the interface, use _interface_facet_tags(msh, cell_tags, {2: (1, 2)}, existing=facet_tags) (:108). - thermal/steady.py: k in solve_steady_conduction and _solve may be a UFL expression or a fem.Function (DG0). - A scalar still goes through fem.Constant exactly as now (steady.py:96), so the scalar path's forms are byte-identical. - The positivity check (:174) applies to scalars. A Function is checked by an allreduced minimum of its array > 0. - solve_steady_conduction_picard is untouched. - New test tests/validation/test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_fem.py. - Constants come from step 1's module (A_, B_, K1, Q1, K2, Q2, H, T_INF; test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form.py:37–41 on the parked branch, landed by item 199). - DG0 k and q are set from cell_tags.find(1) / find(2), then x.scatter_forward(): ghost cells are not carried by cell_tags (io/mesh.py:132–136). - Comparand: two_layer_sphere_steady_temperature, interpolated into P2. It is cheap: there is no series.

Fixture. - a = 0.1 and b = 0.11. - Gel core: k₁ 0.6, q₁ 2000. Shell: k₂ 0.19, q₂ 0. - h 10 on r = b, T∞ 20. P1. - Rungs: resolution ∈ {0.01, 0.007071, 0.005, 0.003536}, ratio √2. - Predicted cells ≈ 26k / 73k / 0.20M / 0.57M: MAT-9's R = 0.1 ball read 19 463 / 151 548 cells at 0.01 / 0.005 (20260929T034247Z_MAT-9-step1.log:87–88), scaled by (b/R)³ = 1.331. - Cell guard: 800 000 at the finest rung, checked before its solve. Over it, stop.

The bands are MAT-9 step 1's, imported by value: they are literals at test_mat9_steady_conduction_sphere.py:139, 154, 156. - (G) Conformity and census, on every rung, rank-reduced, owned cells only (size_local): - owned tag-1 cells plus owned tag-2 cells equal the global cell count; - every vertex of a core cell has |x| ≤ a(1 + 1e-9); - every vertex of a shell cell has a(1 − 1e-9) ≤ |x| ≤ b(1 + 1e-9), so no tet straddles r = a; - tag-1 facets are exterior, and their area is within 1 % of 4πb² (predicted −1e-3 to −4e-3). - (S1) Rate: the whole-ball relative L2 error on θ, fitted as the LSQ slope of log e against log h_eff with h_eff = (V_h/N)^{1/3} (MAT-15's form), is ≥ 1.7. Predicted ≈ 2.0. - (S2) Interior: the interior relative L2 error ≤ 1 % at 0.003536. Interior means cells with midpoint |x|² < 0.81 b², MAT-9's mask scaled to the outer radius. Predicted 4e-4 to 1.5e-3. - (S3) Balance, every rung: |∮hθ dS − q₁V_core,h| / (q₁V_core,h) ≤ 1e-9, with V_core,h the allreduced tag-1 volume. Predicted ≤ 2e-14. - (D) Coefficient path: DG0 k ≡ K1 everywhere against scalar k = K1, on the 0.01 rung with the same piecewise q. Whole-ball relative difference ≤ 1e-13; predicted ≤ 1e-15. - (E) Equal properties: DG0 k ≡ K1 and q ≡ Q1 in both regions, against robin_sphere_steady_temperature(radius=b, k=K1, q=Q1, h=H) at 0.005. Interior ≤ 1 %; predicted ≈ 8e-4 (…MAT-9-step1.log:88).

docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for a 2026-10-03 daily review; the review reviewed it.

MAT-18 step 2(b): piecewise k and ρc in the transient solver, gated against step 1's composite series at Fo 0.2 on 2(a)'s two-region ball. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard, -n 2; W1, W2a, W2b and W2c real build, W3a and W3b complex. No width check: the MAT-9…MAT-17 thermal idiom has none, and -n 2 is the width where a missing reduction shows. Class: lane-3 closed form (measured median 8 min). - Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 50 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 20 code + six ≈ 2-min windows). - Depends on: item 201 (2(a): MeshGenerator.two_layer_ball_domain and DG0 k in solve_steady_conduction) and item 200 (MAT-17 step 2: source_schedule in thermal/transient.py, the same file). If either did not land, skip this item. At drafting (2026-10-03, after 657d4721) neither had: transient.py has no source_schedule, and tests/validation/test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_fem.py does not exist. - utils/analytical.py and io/mesh.py are only imported here, not edited.

Target — the §7 row's 2(b) Done-when, verbatim: "2(b) is the transient: CN at Fo 0.2 ≤ 1 % with piecewise ρc, and MAT-9…MAT-14 re-run green. 2(a) + 2(b) ⇒ ✅." The row names no rung and no Fo convention. This item pins them from item 201's "What 2(b) would be" notes: the 0.005 rung, with Fo = t/t_R and t_R = a²ρc₁/k₁, item 190's core time.

Code (additive; rule (c), disclosed). - thermal/transient.py: k and rho_c in solve_transient_conduction and _solve_transient may be a UFL expression or a fem.Function (DG0). Rebase on item 200's source_schedule edit; the two compose and do not interact. - A scalar still goes through fem.Constant exactly as now (transient.py:158–159 before item 200), so the scalar path's forms are byte-identical and hit the same JIT cache entries. Reuse 2(a)'s scalar-or-Function helper from steady.py if it exposes one (as _as_source is reused at :55, :160); otherwise mirror it. - The positivity check (:143) applies to scalars. A Function is checked by an allreduced minimum of np.real(f.x.array) > 0. - rc_c enters three forms: a_form (:180), the L storage term (:182) and storage_form (:190). All three take the same object. A uniform ρc in storage_form alone would leave the solve right and the balance wrong by control (c2)'s ≈ 0.07. - The balance stays |stor + conv + perf − src| / src with src = ∫q dx. Under 2(a)'s piecewise q (q₂ = 0) that is already q₁V_core,h, as the row's normalisation requires. - New test tests/validation/test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_transient_fem.py. It is new so that 2(a)'s module stays as committed (rule (i)). - Constants come from step 1's module (A_, B_, K1, RC1, Q1, K2, RC2, Q2, H, T_INF, T_R; test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form.py:37–41). Helpers from 2(a)'s module (mesh cache, DG0 builders from cell_tags, interior indicator) are imported read-only where it exposes them; anything else is re-built here. _say, _allsum and _rel_diff's form come from test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere.py, read-only. - DG0 k, ρc and q are set from cell_tags.find(1) / find(2), then x.scatter_forward() (2(a)'s ghost-cell rule). - Comparand: two_layer_sphere_transient_temperature(r, t, a=A_, b=B_, k1=K1, k2=K2, rho_c1=RC1, rho_c2=RC2, q1=Q1, q2=Q2, h=H, t_inf=T_INF, t_init=T_INF) (analytical.py:2189, default n_terms=400). It is evaluated in numpy at the P2 dof coordinates in chunks of 20 000 points, as MAT-9's _exact_theta does (test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere.py:93–106).

Fixture. 2(a)'s ball and coefficients (a 0.1, b 0.11; core k₁ 0.6, q₁ 2000; shell k₂ 0.19, q₂ 0; h 10, T∞ 20), plus ρc₁ 4.18e6 and ρc₂ 1.7e6. T(0) = T∞, with the source on for t > 0. P1. - t* = 0.2·T_R = 0.2·a²ρc₁/k₁ = 13 933 s. That is numerically MAT-9's T_END, because a = R and the core constants are MAT-9's. So N 40 gives Δt 348.33 s, MAT-9's (i) step. - Rungs: 0.005 for (T1), (E) and (c1); 0.01 for (D), (T3) and the printed CN ladder. - Cell guard: 400 000 at 0.005, checked before the first solve on it. 2(a)'s W1 log has the measured count; item 201 predicted ≈ 0.20M. Over it, stop.

Anchors (asserted). The bands are MAT-9 step 2's, imported by value: they are literals at test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere.py:274–275, 301, 321–322, with no module constant to import. (D)'s band is 2(a)'s (D) literal. - (T1) Interior, the row's criterion: CN with the Rannacher start (theta=0.5, startup_half_steps=2), N 40 to t, on the 0.005 rung with DG0 k and DG0 ρc. Interior relative L2 on θ against the comparand ≤ 1 % (:275). Interior means 2(a)'s mask, cell midpoints with |x|² < 0.81 b²; that is r < 0.099, inside the core. Predicted 5e-4 to 2e-3: MAT-9's CN N 40 read 4.6327e-4 on its 0.005 ball (20260929T170037Z_MAT-9-step2b.log:114), and 2(a)'s steady interior is predicted 4e-4 to 1.5e-3. - (T2) Balance: every run's max_balance_residual ≤ 1e-9 (:274, :301), normalised by q₁V_core,h. Predicted ≤ 5e-14 (MAT-9 read ≤ 3.086e-14, …step2b.log:138). - (T3) Long BE = steady: BE, 20 steps of 5·T_R, piecewise k, ρc and q, on the 0.01 rung, against solve_steady_conduction with 2(a)'s DG0 k and the same q on the same mesh. Whole-ball relative difference ≤ 1e-8 (:322). Predicted ≈ 1e-14 (MAT-9's (iv) read 4.301e-15, …step2b.log:141; the slowest decay is item 190's τ₁ ≈ 2.3e4 s, so the BE factor (1 + 5T_R/τ₁)⁻²⁰ ≈ 16⁻²⁰). - (D) Coefficient path: DG0 k ≡ K1 and DG0 ρc ≡ RC1 against scalar k = K1, rho_c = RC1, with the same piecewise q, on the 0.01 rung, BE N 10 to t. Whole-ball relative difference ≤ 1e-13 (2(a)'s (D) band); predicted ≤ 1e-15. - (E) Equal properties: DG0 k ≡ K1, ρc ≡ RC1 and q ≡ Q1 in both regions against robin_sphere_transient_temperature(r, t*, radius=B_, k=K1, rho_c=RC1, q=Q1, h=H, t_inf=T_INF, t_init=T_INF), CN N 40 + Rannacher at 0.005. Interior ≤ 1 % (:275); predicted ≈ 5e-4 to 2e-3. This separates a mesh or comparand fault from a ρc fault if (T1) goes red. - (R) Re-gate, the row's second criterion: W2a–W3b green. W2a's MAT-9 transient lines reproduce …step2b.log:114, 124, 130 digit for digit (interior 4.6327e-04, BE LSQ 0.984, CN 2.001). W2b's MAT-13 (P_w) reads 1.6426e-03 (20260930T172102Z_MAT-13-W1.log:97). W3a's MAT-12 (P_t) reads 1.6845e-3 (20260930T110230Z_MAT-12-W1.log:161). W3b's MAT-14 (P_w′) reads 1.6089e-03 (20261001T004928Z_MAT-14-W1.log:162). W2c's MAT-17 (i) digits equal item 200's own W1 log. Journal the comparison. A changed digit on the scalar path is a stop.

Printed (predicted, never asserted). - Per run: cells; V_core,h/(4πa³/3) − 1 and V_shell,h/(4π(b³ − a³)/3) − 1; build, solve and comparand seconds. - (T1)'s shell-only error. θ_h beside the comparand at r = 0, a and b at t*. A two-node lumped estimate puts the core mean at ≈ 4.8 K and the shell at ≈ 3.0 K. It is crude, so it is printed only. - The CN + Rannacher self-difference on the 0.01 rung, N 20 / 40 / 80, and its pairwise rate. Predicted ≈ 2.0 (MAT-9 read 2.001, …step2b.log:130). - CN without the Rannacher start at N 40 on 0.005.

Negative controls. Rule (e): both are predicted, since this comparison has never been measured on this fixture. Each is asserted only as missing its anchor's band, with the measured value printed beside the prediction. - (c1) Uniform ρc: DG0 k piecewise, scalar rho_c = RC1 everywhere (the shell gets 4.18e6 instead of 1.7e6, so its capacity is 5 796 instead of 2 357 J/K), against the two-layer comparand. Same run as (T1) otherwise. - Predicted interior miss ≈ 0.05 (range 0.02–0.10). This comes from a two-node lumped model (core C₁ 17 509 J/K; shell node at the middle of the wall resistance; R_core 0.265, R_wall 0.381, R_film 0.658 K/W; its slow time constant 2.42e4 s reproduces item 190's τ₁ ≈ 2.3e4 s). The model takes the core mean at t* from 4.80 K to 4.56 K. - Ceiling: an infinitely capacitive wall in the same model holds the core mean to 3.15 K, a 0.34 miss. A bar is reachable below ≈ 0.3; the asserted 1e-2 sits ≈ 5× under the central prediction. - Asserted > 1e-2. - (c2) Uniform ρc in the balance: on the (T1) run, take snapshots 39 and 40. Compute |ρc₁∫(T₄₀ − T₃₉)/Δt + ∮h(½T₄₀ + ½T₃₉ − T∞) − ∫q| / ∫q, i.e. the storage term weighted by ρc₁ everywhere instead of the DG0 ρc. This is the form of MAT-9's control (b) (test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere.py:285–292). - Predicted ≈ 0.07 (range 0.03–0.15): the shell's mis-weighted storage rate, (ρc₁ − ρc₂)·V_shell·dθ_shell/dt ≈ 3 439 J/K × 1.70e-4 K/s ≈ 0.58 W, over P = q₁V_core = 8.38 W. - Asserted > 1e-3.

Windows. Foreground, Bash timeout: 660000. Each harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Run W1 first; the re-gate windows follow on the final code. - W1 (real build; predicted 80–130 s). The environment tests take ≈ 30 s. At 0.005 there are four CN N 40 runs ((T1), (c1), (E), no-startup) at ≈ 5 s each: MAT-9 took 3.7 s at 152k cells (…step2b.log:114), scaled to ≈ 0.2M. Two comparand evaluations take ≈ 5–10 s; each chunk's call recomputes the 400 roots (≈ 0.5 s predicted, printed). Add 2(a)'s ≈ 10–15 s build at 0.005 and the 0.01-rung runs at ≈ 10 s.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-18-step2b-W3b-regate "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat14_sar_pennes_transient_sphere.py -s -v --tb=short'" - Not re-run, disclosed: MAT-15's two FEM modules (test_mat15_finite_cylinder_fem.py, test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py; heavy, 252–273 s), 2(a)'s module, and examples/materials/04_sar_heats_gel_ball.py, 07_sar_heats_perfused_ball.py and 08_gel_ball_settling_time.py also call solve_transient_conduction or the steady solver with scalar coefficients. The evidence for them is the byte-identical scalar path, shown by W2a–W3b's digits.

Traps. - The positivity check on a Function: k <= 0.0 at transient.py:143 is a truthiness error on a fem.Function, and an ordering on complex values in the complex build. Branch scalar or Function; use the real part and allreduce. - One ρc object in all three forms (above). A mismatch reads as a (T2) red of ≈ 0.07, not as a (T1) red. - Ghost cells: set DG0 values from the tags, then scatter_forward. cell_tags.find and assemble_scalar are rank-local, so reduce every count and integral (MAT-9's _allsum). - Time truncation is not the lever. MAT-9's CN self-difference at N 40→80 was 4.3898e-5 whole-ball (…step2b.log:130), ≈ 200× under the band. A (T1) red is spatial or a coefficient fault: never raise N in-slot. - The shell's stiff modes: at the 0.005 rung, h²/α₂ = 0.005²/(0.19/1.7e6) ≈ 224 s < Δt 348 s, and the source jumps at r = a. CN leaves those modes undamped without the Rannacher start, so (T1) and (E) use startup_half_steps=2 (even). The no-startup run is printed only. - The comparand: never evaluate it at t = 0 (the series tail goes as 1/N²); t* is Fo 0.2. Its points × 400 arrays are chunked at 20 000 points. It chooses its layer by exact r; points between the faceted interface and r = a get the other layer's formula, which is consistent because θ and the flux are continuous there. Do not special-case it. - Masks are built in numpy (a DG0 indicator from cell midpoints), never with UFL comparisons. - The new DG0-coefficient forms compile on first use. A killed window leaves an orphan .c (a 0-byte or partial file). Before any re-run, pgrep -c python3 in the container must read 0; then run the rubric's sweep as one bare call:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-18-step2b-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - Shared files: analytical.py is not edited. If a helper must be added, append it after the last block (item 199's MAT-18 block; item 202's IMP-4 block if it has landed) and rebase. io/mesh.py is not edited either: a defect in 2(a)'s generator is a stop, never an in-slot edit or a path checkout from a branch. - Records: append test-results.md rows by hand; git diff --stat must show insertions only on it. - Builds: real-build windows skip the four complex-only environment tests; that is expected. - Run hygiene: print on rank 0; run with -s; never -k inside the quoted command; no pipes. Rule (i): no edit to transient.py or the new test after its last window. A W1b fix that touches transient.py re-runs W2a–W3b after it.

Scope. The transient with piecewise k and ρc, P1, perfect contact, a uniform core source, from rest, to Fo 0.2. Not included: - contact resistance; - a real container's properties (k₂ and ρc₂ are representative acrylic, not a material claim); - the cylinder (MAT-15); - perfusion; - a SAR or coil-driven source in the two-layer ball; - degree 2; - the new module in the complex build (the forms use ufl.inner(·, v) and should compile there, but W3a/W3b gate only the scalar path); - interface-flux extraction.

Status it can move. §7 MAT-18 🟡 → ✅ on the row's Done-when: "2(a) … 2(b) is the transient: CN at Fo 0.2 ≤ 1 % with piecewise ρc, and MAT-9…MAT-14 re-run green. 2(a) + 2(b) ⇒ ✅." This item matches 2(b) term for term (rule (j)): (T1) is the CN criterion, and W2a, W2b, W3a and W3b cover MAT-9…MAT-14. ✅ needs 2(a) recorded green by item 201. If 2(a) is on the row only as BLOCKED or parked, the row is held 🟡 whatever this item reads. The chunk's opening and step 1's R0 re-pose are the weekly's to ratify, so the ✅ stands subject to that ratification.

Negative result. - (D), (T2) or (T3) red: a code bug. Fix it in-slot, run W1b, re-run W2a–W3b if transient.py moved, and disclose. - (E) red: the two-region mesh or the transient comparand path is at fault, not ρc. Print (E) beside 2(a)'s steady (E) reading and the volume deficits, then stop. - (T1) red with (D), (T2), (T3) and (E) green: the piecewise-ρc transient disagrees with the composite series. Print θ_h against the comparand at r = 0, a and b, the shell-only error, and one extra CN N 80 run at 0.005 (≈ 5 s) to separate time from space. Then stop. Step 1's R2 / R3 are green, so suspect the FEM first, but rule nothing in-slot. No band moves (rule (f) never applies to a bound). - (c1) ≤ 1e-2 or (c2) ≤ 1e-3: the shell's ρc does not reach the reading, and the anchor does not discriminate. Report the values and stop. - Any W2a / W2b / W2c / W3a / W3b red, or a changed digit: the scalar path is not byte-identical, so stop. - Over the cell guard: stop before the solve, report the counts. - On every stop, park on attempt/MAT-18-step2b-<UTC> and mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). The row stays 🟡. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Outcome (2026-10-03 13:30 slot, implementer): DONE, row 🟡 → ✅ (subject to the weekly's ratification of the opening and the R0 re-pose). - W1 20261003T184348Z_MAT-18-step2b-W1.log: status 124 at the 180 s ceiling, in the comparand (f.interpolate(callable) at ≈ 1.1M points per rank). pgrep 0; sweep 20261003T184659Z_MAT-18-step2b-cache-sweep.log found no orphans; probe 20261003T184829Z_MAT-18-step2b-probe-comparand.log (2.23 s per 20 000-point call). Fix in the new test only: evaluate at tabulate_dof_coordinates() as the brief specifies (same P2 interpolant). docs.text:
Drafted for the 2026-10-06 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 P11 (quoted, not changed): "MAT-18 step 2 — the container wall on the coil-driven phantom. MAT-18's wall model (thickness, k_wall, outer Robin) on MAT-15 P1's fixture. Asserted: the scheme's energy identity with the wall at MAT-15's E_BAND, the wall → 0 limit reproducing P1's ⟨θ⟩(t*) at B_BAND, the C4 identity; printed, the wall's effect on ⟨θ⟩(t*) and on probe B. Target: identities and a limit. Serial on nothing." Numbering: MAT-18 step 2 (2(a) / 2(b)) is already green, so this is filed as step 3. A record on a ✅ row: no glyph moves.

MAT-18 step 3 puts MAT-18's container wall (thickness b − a, k₂, outer Robin h) on MAT-15 step 1's coil-driven phantom. That fixture is ANS-2's F-small: four single-leg drives at 10 MHz, the 0.0025 m phantom rung, 58 866 tag-3 cells, G = 1 W / P₁ (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:180–301, _run_heated). - Executor: implementer. One new module tests/validation/test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py, @complex_only, one module-scoped fixture. No src/ change. Do not edit test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py: ans:9 imports _run_heated, and an edit owes its windows under rule (a). - Tier: heavy (step 1's own window is 218 s at -n 2), -n 2, complex. Time: ≈ 17 measured / ≈ 30 predicted min. - Depends on nothing.

The wall model on this fixture — read first. The P1 thermal domain is a submesh of the EM mesh. It has no wall cells, and building a conforming wall layer would be a new mesh (out of scope). So the wall enters as its series thermal resistance in the Robin coefficient. That is the steady limit of MAT-18's conforming shell, with no wall heat capacity. - h_eff = 1 / (1/h + t_w/k₂), planar. Import MAT-18's constants (A_, B_, K1, K2, Q1, H) from test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form.py (or from wherever that module imports them): t_w = B_ − A_ = 0.01 m and k₂ = 0.19, with step 1's H_GEL = 10. Predicted h_eff ≈ 6.552 W/m²/K. - solve_transient_conduction takes a scalar h (transient.py:101), so one h_eff serves the lateral faces and the caps. The lateral cylindrical value, 1 / (a·ln(1 + t_w/a)/k₂ + a/((a + t_w)·h)) at a = A = 0.03 m, is printed beside it and never used. - (R) precondition, asserted — the tie to MAT-18. On the sphere the series reduction is exact in steady state. two_layer_sphere_steady_temperature(r, a=A_, b=B_, k1=K1, k2=K2, q1=Q1, q2=0, h=H, t_inf=T_INF) at 20 points r ∈ [0, A_] must equal robin_sphere_steady_temperature(r, radius=A_, k=K1, q=Q1, h=h_sph) with h_sph = 1 / (A_²(1/A_ − 1/B_)/K2 + A_²/(B_²·H)), relative ≤ 1e-12. This is numpy round-off; MAT-18 step 1's steady residual band is 1e-13. It shows the resistance algebra is right before the algebra touches the coil fixture.

Code. - The fixture calls _run_heated(return_fields=True) once. That gives the four EM drives, P1's CN runs, the ball centres, and q_h and T_star keyed by k. - For each k, run CN with h_eff through a local _transient_h(sub, ft, q, h, …): _transient's body (:145–151) with h as an argument. - Use a local _e_prime_h: :164–171 with H_GEL replaced by h. Step 1's _e_prime hard-codes H_GEL, so using it with the wall would fail (E′) on a correct field. - Ball means at t* reuse step 1's compiled ball forms: copy :231–261 into the new module. Do not import test_* names.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported by name): - (R) above, ≤ 1e-12. - (E′) energy identity with the wall: ρc∫(θᴺ − θᴺ⁻¹)/Δt + ∮h_eff θ^(n+½) = G·P_k, from the EM side, ≤ E_BAND (1e-9, test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:76) for all four drives. (E): every wall run's max_balance_residual ≤ E_BAND. - (L0) wall → 0 limit: t_w = 0 (h_eff = H_GEL) reproduces P1's volume-mean ⟨θ⟩(t*) per drive, relative ≤ B_BAND (1e-10, test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:61). The comparand is the mean of _run_heated's T_star[k], the same run that printed 1.153 K per deposited watt (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1929). - (C4) with the wall: the four drives' 10 g ball means of θ at t*, in the cyclic pairs step 1 forms, each ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (5 %, test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:120). Step 1 measured 0.020–0.049 % (…MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1924–1954). The prediction is the same order with the wall, because a uniform h does not break C4.

Negative controls. - (d) doubled source, asserted (prior same-fixture measurement): (E′) with 2·q_h against G·P_k reads 1.000000 on this fixture (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1948). Assert a miss > D_CONTROL_FLOOR, as step 1 does. - (W-ctl) the wall is felt, predicted (rule (e)). The wall-on ⟨θ⟩(t*) misses P1's by more than B_BAND. - Estimate: the adiabatic ⟨θ⟩(t*) = t*/(ρc·V_sub) ≈ 1 254/(4.18e6 × 2.262e-4) ≈ 1.326 K per watt, against P1's 1.153 K. So ≈ 13 % is lost through the surface by t*. - h → 0.655 h cuts that loss by ≈ 20–35 %, so the predicted wall effect is +2 % … +6 % on ⟨θ⟩(t*). - Asserted only as a miss > 1e-6. Ceiling: the effect cannot exceed the 15 % adiabatic gap, so 1e-6 sits ≥ 10⁴× under any non-null reading.

Printed (records): h_eff (planar) and the lateral cylindrical value; per-drive ⟨θ⟩(t*) with the wall and its ratio to P1's; the peak 10 g θ̄ with the wall and its ratio; the C4 pairs; max|Im θ|.
