docs.title: §9 item 243 — 2026-10-05 (chain P7)
docs.text:
Outcome (2026-10-05 09:30 UTC slot): ✅ GREEN, MAT-19 ✅ (the row was amended under rule (j) by the 03:00 review). W0 (20261005T095530Z_MAT-19-step1-W0.log, 87 s, 14 passed): (U1) 0.0, (U3) 2.0e-14 / volume 0.0, (U3c) ghost miss 8.3e-2 volume, (U4) bitwise; MAT-12 re-gated at its record ((P_t) 1.6845e-03). W1 -n 2 (…095808Z_…W1.log, 104 s): (N1) 1.168e-14·θ_ss(0), a → 0 1.1e-16; (A0) 19 496 cells, V_h/V − 1 ≤ 6.3e-4; (T) max 1.7315e-03 (n = 22, c₀); (G) ≤ 1.12e-5, so (T) is FEM error; q_h series +3.47 … +3.73 % at t* (printed); imag ratio 0; (C1) miss max 5.4207e-02 (predicted 5.466e-2). W2 -n 4 (…100001Z_…W2.log, 99 s) and W3 -n 1 (…100145Z_…W3.log, 117 s): (W) series_cf 6.661e-16, cells equal; series_h 3.1e-11 / 7.9e-11 (printed). (C2) as printed is FEM-ball / point − 1 (−0.629 %, −0.815 %, −1.353 % at t*), the sign-inverted form of the brief's point / exact-ball offsets (+0.732 / +0.872 / +1.275 %), shifted by the FEM error; it is a record only.

MAT-19 step 1: the ball-averaged probe on MAT-12's sphere (implementer; standard by prediction, heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 590), -n 2 / -n 4 / -n 1, complex; ≈ 16 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min; depends on nothing). This is the family's first step: attempt 1 of 4.

The owner-rule trap, and how this item routes around it (read first). - MAT-12's thermal solve is on a submesh: _sphere_submesh (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:74–89, dmesh.create_submesh), called at test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:159. - evaluate_vector_field_parallel(owner="lowest_original_cell") raises RuntimeError: Mixed topology unsupported. on any create_submesh mesh (docs/testing/known-issues.md:1372–1379, OPEN). That entry's Watch clause says MAT-12's sphere is "full-mesh" and unaffected. That clause is wrong: the thermal field lives on the tag-1 submesh. - Route. A ball average is an integral, not a point sample, so it needs no point owner. Each rank sums its owned cells only (index_map(3).size_local, never ghosts). It then comm.allreduce(SUM)s the pair (∫θ, ∫1) over the probe ball and divides. Every cell is counted exactly once at every width, by construction of the cell index map. That is the ownership discipline the POST-8 rule exists to enforce, applied to cells instead of points. - Never call evaluate_vector_field_parallel(..., owner=...) or f.eval on the submesh, and never read original_cell_index there. - Wording flag for the review (rule (j)). The row's parenthetical reads "owner rule as POST-8". This item does not call POST-8's point-owner rule. It meets the rule's intent, width invariance to 1e-9 at -n 1 / 2 / 4, with the row's own gate (W). Before writing "→ ✅", the review should amend the parenthetical in its own commit to: "(ball-averaged temperature against time: an integral over owned cells, no point owner — width-invariant as POST-8)". §10 P7's "through evaluate_vector_field_parallel's owner rule" is the weekly's text and the weekly re-reads it. If the row is not amended, the executor closes on the row as written: it holds 🟡 and flags the clause.

The fixture (imported, never restated). - The EM side is MAT-10's and MAT-12's: _solve_lossy_sphere(SIGMA_HIGH, R / 10.0, R / 5.0, return_fields=True) (test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:141). Here R = 0.01 m, h_in = R/10 = 1 mm, ρ 1000, σ 0.57 S/m, 64 MHz. - The thermal side is the tag-1 submesh with every exterior facet Robin (_robin_tags, test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:92–98). Its parameters are K 0.6, H 100 (Bi 5/3), RHO_C 4.18e6, T∞ = T(0) = 0 and G (:52–55; MAT-12 :67–72). - q_cf = G·RHO_KG_M3·SAR_cf = 2002.088514 W/m³, as at MAT-12 :146–150 (log 20260930T110230Z_MAT-12-W1.log:157). - The submesh is 19 496 cells with volume 4.173655e-06 m³ (…MAT-12-W1.log:159–160; reproduced in 20261003T171523Z_MAT-17-step2-W3-regate.log:159). Mean cell volume is 2.14e-10 m³, an ≈ 1.2 mm equilateral edge, consistent with h_in = 1 mm. - Recorded times. The run is MAT-12's own _cn(sub, ft, q, snapshot_steps=range(N_MAIN + 1)) (test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:115–125; the snapshot_steps pass-through is additive, EX-67). It is CN with a Rannacher start, N = 40 to t* = 0.2 t_R = 139.3333 s, so Δt = 3.4833 s. - The recorded times are t_n = n·Δt, n = 1 … 40 (snapshot n is full step n; the two BE half-steps produce snapshot 1, thermal/transient.py:323–330). - n = 0 is θ ≡ 0. It is asserted to read exactly 0 and is excluded from relative checks. - The run reproduces MAT-12's (P_t) interior relative L2 1.6845e-03 at t* (…MAT-12-W1.log:161; …MAT-17-step2-W3-regate.log:161). Print it beside.

The probes (pinned). - Probe radius a = 2 mm = 2 h_in = 0.2 R, ≈ 156 mean cell volumes per ball. The volume is a fixture parameter, not a real probe size. - The three centres: - c₀ = (0, 0, 0); - c₁ = 3.5 mm · (1, 0, 0); - c₂ = 6.5 mm · (1, 1, 1)/√3 (off-axis, generic). - (M), asserted exactly: |cⱼ| + a ≤ 0.9 R for every probe. The ball must lie inside _interior_indicator's r < 0.9 R (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:140), which is where MAT-12's (P_t) 1.68e-3 was measured, and away from the faceted surface (mesh volume −0.36 % from 4πR³/3).

Code. - (1) New src/fem_em_solver/thermal/probe.py (additive), plus exports in thermal/__init__.py. - ProbeBall(centre: tuple[float, float, float], radius: float). The centre is plain floats. - ball_average(temperature, probe, *, levels=3) -> (value, volume). - probe_series(snapshots: Mapping[int, fem.Function], dt: float, probes, *, levels=3) -> ProbeSeries, with fields times, values (n_t × n_probes), volumes, nominal_volumes = 4πa³/3 and max_imag_ratio. - Restrictions, which raise: scalar Lagrange degree 1 on an affine tetrahedral mesh (geometry.cmap.degree == 1). The ball must be given in mesh coordinates. - Algorithm (pure numpy, no UFL form, no JIT, no comparison on a UFL operand). - Per owned cell K (0 … size_local − 1): the dof coordinates come from V.tabulate_dof_coordinates()[V.dofmap.list[K]]. For P1 these are the vertices, ordered like the dofs by construction, so never mix them with geometry.dofmap. Take the centroid and the bounding radius ρ_K = max vertex distance. Skip the cell if |centroid − c| − ρ_K > a. - Each remaining cell is sampled on a fixed barycentric lattice: the centroids of the 8^L equal-volume sub-tetrahedra of L-fold red (Bey) refinement of the reference tetrahedron. L = 3 gives 512 points of weight |K|/512, precomputed once. - At each lattice point, θ = λ·θ_K (exact for P1). The indicator is the squared distance compared with a² in numpy float64. - Geometry is precomputed once per probe. Each snapshot is then one weighted sum. Return the real part and record max |Im θ|/max |Re θ| over the dofs used (the complex build). - Reduction: one comm.allreduce(np.array([num, vol]), op=MPI.SUM) on every rank, including ranks with zero candidate cells. A collective entered by a subset of ranks deadlocks (item 227, eda85f26). - An internal _ball_average_on_cells(..., cells) takes the cell list. The public path passes owned cells only. The test uses the internal path for the planted ghost control. - The docstring cites this item and states the restriction and the known-issues route. - (2) New tests/solver/test_thermal_probe.py, smoke tier: dolfinx.mesh.create_box on [−1, 1]³, 8³ × 6 tets, P1 real-valued fields. In the complex build they are complex-typed with Im 0. - (U1) θ ≡ 3.7 inside a ball of radius 0.5 at (0.1, 0.2, 0.05) reads 3.7 to ≤ B_BAND 1e-10 relative (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:61, imported). V_h/(4πa³/3) − 1 is printed, predicted |·| ≤ 5e-3. - (U2) The affine θ = 2 + x − 0.5y + 0.25z reads θ(c). This is printed, not asserted: the predicted relative deviation is ≤ 1e-3, from the lattice centroid shift ≈ 3h_s²/(2√π a) with h_s = h/8. - (U3) A ball of radius 10 ⊇ the box, on θ = interpolant of 2 + x² + y. The probe equals _allsum(θ dx)/_allsum(1 dx) (MAT-10's _allsum, :70–71) to ≤ B_BAND, and the volume equals 8 to ≤ B_BAND. This is the rank-safety identity. It is visible only at -n 2, the width where a missing reduction or a double-counted ghost shows. - (U3c) Planted ghost control, at comm.size > 1 only: _ball_average_on_cells over owned + ghost cells must miss (U3)'s identity by more than B_BAND. That miss is asserted. The predicted separation is O(1e-2), printed. Rule (e): no prior measurement, so the factor is predicted. - (U4) At -n 2, the c₀ reading is bitwise identical on every rank (allgather, ==). - (3) New tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py (complex_only), with one module-scoped fixture. It imports and never restates: - E0, EPSILON_R_SPHERE, OMEGA, RHO_KG_M3, SIGMA_HIGH, _solve_lossy_sphere (test_lossy_sphere_sar.py); - R, K, H, G, ROBIN_TAG, P_BAND, A_BAND, B_BAND, _allsum, _say, _sphere_submesh, _robin_tags, _cell_average_dg0, _to_sub (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py); - RHO_C, T_R, T_STAR, N_MAIN, _cn (test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:67–72,115); - robin_sphere_eigenvalues, robin_sphere_transient_coefficients, robin_sphere_transient_temperature (utils/analytical.py:1192,1220,1232).

Two runs on the same submesh, q_cf (uniform) and q_h (MAT-12's DG0 FEM SAR, :164–166), each with snapshot_steps=range(41). The probe series is taken on both. - Width artefact. At -n 2, rank 0 writes /workspace/logs/mat19/step1-n2.npz (/logs/ is gitignored, .gitignore:82; os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)) with series_cf, series_h, volumes and cells, then Barrier. At -n 4 and -n 1 the module loads it. If it is missing, pytest.fail; never recompute (POST-8 step 3a's guard, docs/planning/chunks/POST-8.md:171–173).

The comparand: the closed form averaged over the same ball (pinned). - θ(r, t) is robin_sphere_transient_temperature with θᵢ = 0, T∞ = 0: θ = θ_ss(r) − Σₙ Bₙ e^{−λₙ² αt/R²} Xₙ(r), with Xₙ = sin(κₙr)/(κₙr), κₙ = λₙ/R, and Bₙ from robin_sphere_transient_coefficients (analytical.py:1220–1229, 400 terms as the default). - Its exact mean over the ball B(c, a), d = |c|, is:

θ̄(d, a, t) = qR/(3h) + q(R² − d² − 3a²/5)/(6k) − Σₙ Bₙ e^{−λₙ²αt/R²} Xₙ(d) · 3[sin(κₙa) − κₙa cos(κₙa)]/(κₙa)³.

  • The steady part: θ_ss is quadratic, and the ball mean of |x|² is d² + 3a²/5.
  • The modes: Xₙ solves ∇²u + κₙ²u = 0 in all of ℝ³, so the Helmholtz mean-value theorem holds. Its spherical mean at radius s is u(c)·sin(κs)/(κs). Integrating with weight 3s²/a³ gives the factor 3j₁(κa)/(κa).
  • A small-argument guard: use 1 − x²/10 for x < 1e-4.
  • (N1), asserted numpy anchor. θ̄ above against a direct radial Gauss–Legendre quadrature of robin_sphere_transient_temperature. The quadrature uses the shell-cap weight: the area of the sphere of radius r inside B(c, a) is πr(a² − (r − d)²)/d on |d − a| ≤ r ≤ d + a, plus 4πr² on r < a − d, normalised by 4πa³/3. Use ≥ 200 nodes per sub-interval. The check runs at all 3 probes × 40 times, together with the a → 0 limit against the point value. The band is ≤ 1e-10·θ_ss(0), the series-route agreement band of MAT-17 step 1 (P3), imported from test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py:206–207, where θ_ss(0) = 0.1223499 K. Predicted ≤ 1e-13.
  • Predicted comparands (pure-Python evaluation of the formula above while drafting; it reproduces the logged θ(0, t*) 0.059564 and θ(R, t*) 0.035599 of …MAT-12-W1.log:158):
probe θ̄(t₁) [K] θ̄(t₁₀) [K] θ̄(t*) [K] point θ(cⱼ, t*) [K] c₀, d = 0 1.668407e-03 1.666485e-02 5.913173e-02 5.956431e-02 c₁, d = 3.5 mm 1.668407e-03 1.658213e-02 5.678637e-02 5.728180e-02 c₂, d = 6.5 mm 1.668186e-03 1.595905e-02 5.025018e-02 5.089074e-02

The probe reads these to the printed digits (n = 1 is q_cf t₁/ρc = 1.6684e-3 at the interior probes).

Anchors (asserted). - (A0) The submesh has 19 496 cells at every width, compared exactly (…MAT-12-W1.log:159). Probe volume ratios V_h/(4πa³/3) − 1 are printed, predicted |·| ≤ 2e-3. Snapshot 0 reads exactly 0.0 at every probe. - (T), the row's gate. For every probe j and every n = 1 … 40, on the q_cf series: |P_h,j(t_n) − θ̄_cf(dⱼ, a, t_n)|/θ̄_cf(dⱼ, a, t_n) ≤ 1 %. This is the row's band, carried by the imported constant P_BAND = 1.0e-2 (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:59, "MAT-9 (i)"). - Predicted: max over (j, n) ≤ 3e-3, ≥ 3× headroom. MAT-12's (P) interior L2 on the me run is 1.6845e-3 at t* (:161), and for n ≤ 3 the interior probes sit in the uniform-growth core, which P1 + BE/CN reproduce to round-off. - Why q_cand not q.** On klzzw:0230's sphere only the uniform closed-form-SAR leg, (P), carries a 1 % band. The FEM-SAR leg (A_t) carries A_BAND 11 % and measured 3.48e-2, almost all of it MAT-4's +3.54 % SAR offset (:162–163). So the q series again the closed form is printed*beside A_BAND (predicted ≈ +3.4–3.6 % at t*) and not asserted. - (G), pried.** The probe's geometric error alone: the same lattice, with θ_cf evaluated in numpy at the lattice points (no FEM), against θ̄ at t*, per probe. The predicted |·| is ≤ 1e-3; the dominant term is centroid shift ≈ 0.01 mm × the outer probe's sensitivity of 5.5 %/mm. The split of (T) into geometry (G) and FEM (T − G) is printed per probe at t*. - (W), the row's gate, at -n 4 and -n 1 against the -n 2 npz. - cells must be equal. - Every entry of series_cf, n = 1 … 40 × 3 probes, must be within 1e-9 relative of its -n 2 value. This is the row's band, as WIDTH_BAND = 1.0e-9 # MAT-19 row, PROJECT_PLAN.md:2512, a band this item does not set. - Predicted ≤ 1e-12: the thermal solve is real-valued, and the probe is a sum whose order alone moves with the width. - Printed: the same comparison on series_h. It carries the complex EM solve's width round-off. Predicted ≤ 3e-10: the worst cross-width figure this project has measured is POST-8's 2.98e-10 (docs/planning/chunks/POST-8.md:13), and MAT-15's P₁ spread across six runs is ≤ 5.3e-12. - Printed: max_imag_ratio, predicted 0 for q_cf.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (C1) The displaced probe: the row's control, its miss asserted, its factor predicted. The FEM probe is moved 1 mm radially inward, c₂′ = (5.5/6.5)·c₂ with the same a, and its q_cf series is compared with the nominal θ̄_cf(6.5 mm, a, t_n). Asserted: max over n of the relative miss > P_BAND (it misses (T)). - Predicted, printed beside (closed form only; no prior measurement on this fixture):

| n | 1 | 5 | 6 | 10 | 20 | 40 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| miss | 1.28e-4 | 8.15e-3 | 1.089e-2 | 2.116e-2 | 3.887e-2 | **5.466e-2** |

The miss grows monotonically with n. It first exceeds 1 % at n = 6, so the assertion is on the maximum over n, which is n = 40, never on "every n". An early-time series is uniform in r, so no displacement can show there.
  • Ceiling: the steady limit, t → ∞, is 6.843e-2. That is the most a 1 mm radial displacement at 6.5 mm can show on this fixture, 6.8× the band. At t* the predicted miss is 5.5× the band, less the FEM error of ≤ 3e-3.
  • Printed: the displaced probe against its own closed form θ̄(5.5 mm), predicted within (T)'s 1 %. It is a fourth radius for free and is not asserted.
  • (C2) The volume-omitted comparand: predicted, printed only. The q_cf ball series is compared with the point closed form θ(dⱼ, t_n). At t* the predicted offsets are +0.732 % (c₀), +0.872 % (c₁) and +1.275 % (c₂). At c₂ the point comparand exceeds 1 % from n ≈ 20 (1.14 %). This is what stating the probe volume buys at this a/R. It is printed as a record because the separation from the band (1.27×) is too thin to assert.
  • (U3c) is in W0 (see above): the ghost-included sum misses B_BAND. The miss is asserted; the factor is predicted.

Windows (complex; foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; each command bare, whole and repo-relative; -s; no -k inside the quoted command; no pipes or redirects). - First, two checks. pgrep -c python3 in the container reads 0. Then run the rubric's orphan sweep as one bare call:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step1-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - Pricing basis. MAT-12's own window took 77 s at -n 2, test body 30.5 s, EM 15.4 s (20260930T110230Z_MAT-12-W1.log:171, footer). Its 2026-10-03 re-gate read EM 14.4 s / body 21.1 s inside a 105 s window together with MAT-14 (20261003T171523Z_MAT-17-step2-W3-regate.log:171,396). - Today's box is slow: MAT-5 step 3 measured its EM at ≈ 2× its own basis (20261005T050759Z_MAT-5-step3-W1-alpha0.log; journal in docs/planning/chunks/MAT-5.md:96). Hence the 590 ceiling on a standard prediction. A window killed at 590 is not a result: stop BLOCKED as a slow box, never lengthen. - W0, the probe and the rule (c) re-gate (-n 2; predicted ≈ 100 s, up to 200 s on a slow box). - The thermal/__init__.py edit is imported by MAT-12's module, so that module re-runs green in the same window. Its (P_t) / (A_t) / (S1) / (S2) / (E) / (∞) / controls must reproduce …MAT-12-W1.log:161–170 at their bands. - A red W0 stops the item before W1: revert the src/ edit and park.

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step1-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/solver/test_thermal_probe.py tests/validation/test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W1, -n 2, which writes the npz (predicted ≈ 85 s: environment ≈ 45 s, EM ≈ 15 s, two CN runs ≈ 1–4 s each, numpy comparands and (G) ≈ 5 s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step1-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W2, -n 4 (predicted ≈ 80 s): the same command with -n 4, label MAT-19-step1-W2. - W3, -n 1 (unmeasured; predicted ≈ 110 s, with the EM ≤ 2× its -n 2 time): the same command with -n 1, label MAT-19-step1-W3. - Order: W0 → W1 → W2 → W3. W2 and W3 need W1's npz from the same module bytes.

Traps. - The owner rule on a submesh raises (known-issues :1372). Use no point evaluation at all, with or without an owner. The probe is an owned-cell integral. - cell_tags.values and assemble_scalar are rank-local. The probe's partial sums are rank-local until the one allreduce. Every rank enters that allreduce (item 227 deadlocked on a rank-0-only collective). (U3) / (U3c) at -n 2 are the check. - Ghosts. V.dofmap.list has rows for owned + ghost cells. Iterate range(size_local) only. The ghost dof values, however, are needed, and the snapshots copy T_new.x.array after scatter_forward (transient.py:265–269,302). - Complex build. θ arrays are complex-typed. Take np.real after the weighted sum and print the imaginary ratio. Put no ordering comparison on any UFL operand: the indicator is numpy-side on float64 squared distances, never ufl.conditional / lt / sqrt (OPS-22; WF-6 step 4c). _allsum returns complex: take np.real. - Dof coordinates, not the geometry dofmap, for the P1 vertices of a cell. The ordering matches by construction only that way. - The ball centre is plain floats, not a numpy scalar of a complex dtype (POST-8 3a's trap, sar.py:257). - Snapshot indices are full steps. With startup_half_steps=2, snapshot 1 is after both BE half-steps, at t = Δt. Times come from n·Δt, never from counting balance entries (41 balance residuals for 40 steps, …MAT-12-W1.log:161). - No cross-run comparison is bitwise (OPS-43). (W) is relative 1e-9; only (U4) is bitwise, and it is in-run. - Orphan .c sweep before W0. After any kill, run pgrep -c python3 first. - Rule (i): no edit to probe.py or either test module after its last window. An edit after W1 re-runs W1, W2 and W3, because the npz must come from the committed bytes. Check file times against the log starts before committing. - The durable-capture idiom is not needed: every window is ≪ 10 min. Never pipe pytest; the footer must be pytest's status.

Scope. This step covers one fixture (MAT-12's 1 cm sphere, one mesh at R/10, P1, CN N = 40), three probes of one stated volume (a = 2 mm), the q_cf series gated and the q_h series printed, and recorded times only (no interpolation between steps). Not covered: - a real probe's thermal mass, self-heating or lead artefact (the row); - a fibre-optic probe's actual sensing volume; - an h-convergence statement on the probe; - the phantom or coil fixtures (MAT-15, ANS-9); - tissue or perfusion; - any compliance or ASTM F2182 reading; - the submesh owner-rule fix itself. The known-issues entry stays OPEN; it resolves only with a post/evaluation.py fix.

Status it can move. - MAT-19 ⬜ → ✅ per the row: (T) green at three radii and 40 times, (W) green at -n 1 / 2 / 4, (C1) misses, elapsed recorded in the row. This is conditional on the review's rule (j) amendment of the "owner rule as POST-8" parenthetical (see the flag above). Without it the executor holds 🟡 and flags the clause. - §10 P7 can then be read closed by the weekly. - In the closing commit, the executor corrects the known-issues Watch clause at :1378: MAT-12's thermal is on a submesh too, and MAT-19 routes around the rule by integration. The entry stays OPEN.

Negative result. In every case: report the measurement, park on attempt/MAT-19-step1-*, mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)) and journal it in attempts.md. Never widen 1 % or 1e-9, and never change a, L or the radii after reading. - (N1) red: the mean-value comparand or the shell-cap quadrature is wrong. This is a numpy bug: stop before any FEM reading is interpreted. - (U1) / (U3) / (U4) red: a probe or reduction bug. Stop at W0. - (A0) red: the mesh has drifted from MAT-12's record. Stop; a record-reconciler ruling is needed, never a new count. - (T) red with (G) ≤ 3e-3: the FEM probe misses the closed form at a radius or time where MAT-12's interior L2 says it should not. Print the full 3 × 40 table and the (G) / (T − G) split. The review rules. - (T) red with (G) > 3e-3: the lattice does not resolve the ball. Report it. The review re-poses L or a; the executor does not raise L in-slot. - (W) red on series_cf: the probe or the thermal solve depends on the width. Print the entries and the cell counts, and stop. - (C1) does not miss: the FEM series is insensitive to position, which contradicts (T). Stop. - A slow-box kill at 590: BLOCKED. W0 and W1 records stand, and the unblock is a re-run on a box whose MAT-12 EM reads ≤ 20 s.

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

docs.title: §9 item 253 — 2026-10-05 (chain P8, daily provisional)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §9 rule (6), a provisional next step on chain P after P7 (MAT-19 ✅, item 243). The weekly ratifies or reverts it. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is invented: every asserted anchor is an identity at an imported band.

MAT-19 step 2: step 1's probe, unchanged, read on MAT-15 P1's coil-driven gel phantom at ANS-9's SPEC probe centres (implementer; heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 590), -n 2 / -n 4 / -n 1, complex; ≈ 12 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min; depends on nothing). Family MAT-19 step 2: attempt 1 of 4.

Why this step (read first). - ANS-9's SPEC (examples/ansys_benchmarks/ans9_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz/SPEC.md, row 4) asks for the point rise at t = 1254 s at five probes, metres: A (0, 0, 0), B (0.020, 0, 0), C (0, 0.020, 0), D (−0.020, 0, 0), E (0, 0, 0.030). Its readout puts A–D at 10 % and E as a record. ans:9 produces row 4 by point evaluation through the legacy owner=None path. θ is continuous P1, so that is sound (09_coil_driven_gel_heating_10MHz.py:286–291). Our side reads, at 20261004T142653Z_ANS-9-step1a-W1.log:1943: A 0.905798, B 3.564854, C 0.685305, D 0.697444, E 0.958639 K. - A real gel-phantom measurement is a fibre-optic probe with a sensing volume, placed to a tolerance. The 09-30 weekly's sampling ruling says "public comparison rows quote cell or mass averages" (POST-8.md:24). Row 4 is the one SPEC row that quotes neither. - This step therefore measures two things on our own side, before the operator's AED run: the probe-volume sensitivity of row 4 (a stated ball against the point) and its placement sensitivity (a 0.1 mm displacement at B). It also asserts the identities that make a ball-averaged row 4 trustworthy on this fixture: whole-phantom = volume mean, width invariance with the EM in the loop, and the σ_y mirror image of the one-port drive. - Which probes: the SPEC's centres, as named, plus C′ = (0, −0.020, 0), the σ_y image of C. MAT-19 step 1's three-radii analogue is not used, because the SPEC names its points. - What is new against step 1. Step 1's (W) was already on a create_submesh mesh (MAT-12's tag-1 sphere; known-issues :1378 as corrected). It asserted (W) on the closed-form-source series and only printed the EM-sourced series_h (3.1e-11 / 7.9e-11). Here the asserted series carries a complex MUMPS solve on 199 920 cells at every width. (A) is step 1's (U3) identity, until now asserted only on a create_box mesh, on a coil-driven submesh partition.

The fixture (imported, never restated). - The fixture is MAT-15 step 1's: _run_heated(return_fields=True) (tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:180–351). That is ANS-2's 10 MHz loaded F-small birdcage at phantom_resolution 0.0025, 199 920 / 58 866 cells, N1curl degree 1, ragged f = 0.5 sheets with κ none, the four single-leg drives, G = 1 W / P₁, P1 thermal on the tag-3 submesh with Robin on every face, and gel k 0.6, ρc 4.18e6, h 10, T∞ = T(0) = 20. - This is an existing fixture. The 2026-10-02 exact-rectangle ruling binds new fixtures, and ragged-sheet records stay valid as records. This step builds nothing new and its readings are records on the fixture ANS-9's SPEC names. - Drive k = 0 only (out["by_k"][0] == "P1", asserted). Take sub, ft, q_h = out["q_h"][0], v_sub and T_star[0]. - The series. Re-run CN with every full step kept: _transient(sub, ft, q_h, dt=T_STAR / N_MAIN, n_steps=N_MAIN, theta=0.5, startup_half_steps=2, snapshot_steps=range(N_MAIN + 1)). This is ans:9's snap_run (09_…py:222–224), with _transient imported from the MAT-15 module. Δt = 31.35 s, and t_n = n·Δt for n = 1 … 40. The SPEC times 313.5 / 627 / 940.5 / 1254 s are n = 10 / 20 / 30 / 40. - Also run one _be_one(sub, ft, q_h) (Δt₁ = 2.5e-6 t_R) for (S). - Imports. - From the MAT-15 module: _run_heated, _transient, _be_one, A, N_MAIN, T_STAR, T_INF, DT_1, RHO_C, E_BAND, B_BAND, V_BAND, V_SUB_RECORD_M3, F_CONTROL_FLOOR, C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. - PHANTOM_HEIGHT from tests.mesh.test_birdcage_port_tags. - WIDTH_BAND from test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe.py:85. - ProbeBall, probe_series and ball_average from fem_em_solver.thermal, plus the internal _ball_average_on_cells, _lattice and _owned_cells from thermal.probe. - The SPEC centres come from ans:9's SPEC_THERMAL["probes"] (09_…py:91–97), loaded by importlib as ans:9 loads ans:2 (_load_example, :102–107; the stem starts with a digit). Never restate them. - No edit to src/, to the MAT-15 module, to the ans:9 script, or to its metrics.json / COMPARISON.md. Each owes a gate's window under rule (a). Do not add a drive selector to _run_heated: the three unused drives cost ≈ 60 s per window, which is cheaper than two re-gates.

The probes (pinned). - Radius a = 5 mm = 2 h_p, as step 1's 2 h_in. The mean cell volume is V_sub/58 866 = 3.84e-9 m³, a ≈ 3.2 mm regular-tet edge, so the ball holds ≈ 136 mean cell volumes against step 1's 156. a is a fixture parameter, not a fibre-optic sensing volume. - Centres: A, B, C, D and E from the SPEC, plus C′ = (0, −0.020, 0). - (M), asserted exactly: √(x² + y²) + a ≤ A and |z| + a ≤ PHANTOM_HEIGHT/2 for every centre. The closest are B / C / C′ / D, at 25 mm against a 30 mm radius, and E, at 35 mm against a 40 mm half-height. Lateral faceting sags inward by ≤ h²/(8a) ≈ 2.6e-5 m. V_h/(4πa³/3) − 1 is printed, predicted |·| ≤ 5e-3. - Ω, the whole-phantom ball: centre (0, 0, 0), radius 0.1 m. Its distance to the farthest phantom vertex is √(0.03² + 0.04²) = 0.05 m. - B⁺, the displaced control: (0.0201, 0, 0), B moved 0.1 mm radially toward the driven leg.

Code. One new module, tests/validation/test_mat19_probe_coil_phantom.py (complex_only), with one module-scoped fixture and no src/ change. - θ Functions: θ_n.x.array = snapshot_n.x.array − T_INF, then scatter_forward. Probe θ, never T. A ball mean of T = 20 + θ dilutes every relative comparison by θ/20; (W) would then be 20/θ ≈ 60× too lenient at n = 1. - probe_series over {A, B, C, C′, D, E, Ω, B⁺} on θ_0 … θ_40, at the default levels=3. - (S) helper, test-only numpy. For each probe and each owned cell K, the lattice-inside volume v_K(B) is computed with the same _lattice(3) mask as probe._geometry. The q_h ball mean is then Σ_K q_K·v_K(B)/Σ_K v_K(B), one allreduce on every rank, so numerator and denominator share one quadrature. q_K = q_h.x.array[Wq.dofmap.list[K, 0]]. - Width artefact. At -n 2, rank 0 writes /workspace/logs/mat19/step2-n2.npz: the series for the eight probes, the volumes, the cell count, and the sha256 of this module's bytes and of thermal/probe.py. Then Barrier. - At -n 4 / -n 1 the module loads it. It runs pytest.fail if the file is missing or either hash differs. Never recompute. - The hash is new against step 1: it makes rule (i)'s "npz from the committed bytes" mechanical. - Wrap the phases in time.perf_counter() and print each with flush=True: _run_heated, the snapshot re-run, probe geometry, the series sums and the (S) helper.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported). - (A0) Fixture identity. - by_k[0] == "P1". - Submesh cells == 58 866 at every width (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1926). - |V_sub/V_SUB_RECORD_M3 − 1| ≤ V_BAND. - (M) as above. - θ_0 reads exactly 0.0 at every probe. - (R0) The re-run is the gated run. ‖θ⁴⁰_rerun − θ*_gated‖/‖θ*_gated‖ ≤ E_BAND, in ans:9's (R0) form (09_…py:246–252). Predicted ≤ 1e-14. - (A) The whole-phantom probe is the volume mean. This is step 1's (U3) on the coil-driven submesh. - For n = 0 … 40 and for the BE θ¹: |P(θ) − ∫θ dx/V_sub| ≤ kzwxh:0528·|∫θ dx/Vubkzwxh:0555 (n ≥ 1), and |V,h/V_sub − 1| ≤ B_BAND. - Why it is exact, n banded by luck: the 8^L equal-volume red children's centroids average to the pare centroid at every L, so each vertex weight is |K|/4. Σ |Kkzwxh:0561·mean(θ) is ∫θ for P1, and FFCx degree-1 rule for θ·dx is exact for P1 too. Predicted ≤ 1e-14. - Printed beside: the four SPEC-time values against row 2's 0.318096 / 0.614315 / 0.892104 / 1.153314 K (…142653Z_ANS-9-step1a-W1.log:1936), predicted equal to the printed digits. - (U4) At -n 2, every probe reading at n = 40 is bitwise identical on every rank (allgather, ==). This is in-run. - (W) Width invariance, with the EM in the loop (-n 4 and -n 1 against the -n 2 npz). - Cells are equal. - Every entry of the series, 8 probes × n = 1 … 40, is within WIDTH_BAND 1e-9 relative of its -n 2 value. - Predicted ≤ 1e-10. Backing, measured on this EM fixture (same 199 920-cell mesh, same _solve_driven): the P1 phantom power moves 4.9e-12 / 8.9e-13 / 1.1e-11 across -n 2 / 4 / 1, and raw point SARs move ≤ 2.98e-10 pairwise, on the smallest-magnitude entries (docs/planning/chunks/POST-8.md:12–13). G = 1/P₁ cancels the global scale, and θ at a probe is a smoothed integral of q, so it should sit at the integral class (≈ 1e-11), not the pointwise one. - max_imag_ratio is printed, predicted 0. - (Σ) The σ_y mirror image of the one-port drive at t*. - |θ̄_C(t₄₀) − θ̄_C′(t₄₀)|/θ̄_C(t₄₀) ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (5 %), the band MAT-15 step 1 imported for 10 g θ ball means and step 3 applied to σ_y pairs. - Precondition: P1 sits at 360.0° (…123309Z…W1.log:1924, printed by _run_heated), and its ragged sheet is σ_y-symmetric to O(h) only. - Predicted ≤ 0.5 %. Step 1's C4 θ 10 g pairs read 0.020–0.049 % (:1924–1954). Step 3's σ θ pair at φ₁ ± 90° read.36 % on only 537 phantom cells; this fixture has 58 866. - Asserted at n = 40 only. Early-time θ is local q, and the q_h pair at ±90° can be large: step 3 read 22.7 % at the q minimum. The full C / C′ series and the q_h C / C′ pair are printed.

Printed, not asserted (with the reason). - (P4) Probe volume against point, row 4. θ̄_j(t₄₀) / θ_point,j − 1 for A–E, against the logged row-4 values above. (R0) makes the logged θ⁴⁰ the same field to 1e-14. - Predicted: B in [−8 %, 0] (B sits on the steep flank of the leg hot spot; the secant from B to the row-5 maximum, 4.457206 K at r = 27.5 mm, is 0.119 K/mm). A, C, D and E within ±3 %. - This is the number the weekly needs to judge whether row 4's 10 % is robust to a probe volume. - (P5) Placement sensitivity at B. |θ̄_B⁺ − θ̄_B|/θ̄_B at n = 40 is predicted ≈ 3.3e-3 (0.1 mm × 0.119 K/mm / 3.565 K), range [1e-3, 1e-2]. Equivalently ≈ 3 %/mm against the 10 % readout. - (S) Local calorimetric slope per probe. ρc·θ̄_j(θ¹)/(Δt₁·q̄_j) − 1, where q̄_j is the lattice q_h ball mean. - Why print only. MAT-15's S2_BAND 1e-4 is a bound on the volume-mean slope. There, testing with v = 1 removes the consistent-mass projection exactly, and the only deficit is the Robin leak (measured 5.754e-6 on P1: row 3, 1.058563285e-3 against 1.058569376e-3 K/s, …142653Z…W1.log:1938). - The physical premise holds locally: the Fourier number αΔt₁/a² = 1.435e-7 × 0.015675 / 2.5e-5 = 9.0e-5, so conduction is negligible at the probe. - The discrete premise fails locally. θ¹/Δt₁ → P_h q/ρc, the L2 projection of the DG0 source onto P1, and its ball mean differs from q_h's by a projection layer at the ball surface on a ball ≈ 3 cells across. That deficit does not vanish as Δt₁ → 0, and no imported band covers it. - Magnitude unpredicted; order estimate 1e-3–3e-2. The Ω row reads MAT-15's (S2) 5.754e-6 by (A). - The C / C′ q_h pair, the series table at n = 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 for every probe, the ball volumes, the phase clocks and the pairwise width spread at -n 1 vs -n 4.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (U3c) Ghost-included sum, asserted, factor predicted. At comm.size > 1 only: _ball_average_on_cells on Ω over owned + ghost cells (range(size_local + num_ghosts)) must miss (A)'s volume identity by more than B_BAND. - Ceiling first: at -n 2 a cell is ghost on at most one other rank, so the ghost-included volume is ≤ 2 V_sub and the miss is ≤ 1. The floor is > 0 whenever the partition has ghosts. - Predicted ≈ 3e-2, range [1e-2, 1e-1], at -n 2. That is step 1's 8.3e-2 on a 3 072-cell box, scaled by the interface fraction (3 072/58 866)^{1/3} = 0.374. Predicted [2e-2, 2e-1] at -n 4. - (C1″) Displaced probe against (W)'s band, asserted, factor predicted. |θ̄_B⁺(t₄₀) − θ̄_B(t₄₀)|/θ̄_B(t₄₀) > WIDTH_BAND, at every width. - Predicted ≈ 3.3e-3, so (W)'s 1e-9 resolves a 0.1 mm probe-geometry change by ≈ 3e6×. This is the control that (W) would see a rank-dependent probe geometry. - No prior measurement exists on this fixture. - (f″) Off-mirror pair, asserted, factor predicted. |θ̄_C(t₄₀) − θ̄_B(t₄₀)|/θ̄_B(t₄₀) > F_CONTROL_FLOOR (= C4_COVARIANCE_BAND), in MAT-15 step 3's (f′) form (θ̄(φ₁ + 90°) against θ̄(φ₁)). - Predicted ≈ 0.81 (1 − 0.685305/3.564854 from row 4's points), range [0.6, 0.9]. - Ceiling: < 1 while θ̄_C ≤ θ̄_B, so the 5 % floor sits ≈ 16× under the prediction. - C against D is not a control: their points differ by only 1.8 % (0.685305 / 0.697444).

Windows (complex; foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; each command bare, whole and repo-relative; -s; no -k inside the quoted command; no pipes or redirects; every window ≪ 10 min, so the durable-capture idiom is not needed). - First: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Then the any-orphan sweep as one bare call:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step2-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - Pricing basis (measured). Per the 03:00 pathologist lesson, divide by the number of solves in the cited interval. - MAT-15 step 1 W1 took 218 s at -n 2 (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:2132). Its fixture total was 171.4 s, split as mesh + rung 61.3 s, EM 81.3 s for four _solve_driven (≈ 20 s each), and thermal 28.8 s for nine runs (:1924,1954). Re-gates read 208 s and 220 s (20261002T112729Z_EX-79-mat15-regate.log:2132, 20261004T141433Z_ANS-9-step1a-mat15-regate.log:2132). - The snapshot re-run and the BE step cost ≈ 3 s: ans:9's three thermal re-runs took 4.2 s (…142653Z…W1.log:1956). - The probe geometry is dominated by Ω, which materialises (m × 512 × 3) float64 over all owned cells: ≈ 0.36 GB per rank at -n 2 and ≈ 0.72 GB at -n 1, a few seconds. - There is no MAT-15 window at -n 4 or -n 1. POST-8 step 2 ran the same 199 920-cell EM (four drives) at 195 / 191 / 228 s for -n 2 / 4 / 1 (20261002T200331Z_POST-8-step2-W1.log:2137, …200654Z…W2.log:2341, …201013Z…W3.log:2034). The width ratios are 0.98 and 1.17. - Measured-basis total: 218 + 218 × 0.98 + 218 × 1.17 ≈ 687 s ≈ 11.5 min. - W1, -n 2, writes the npz (predicted 225–245 s; ≤ 345 s on item 214's ×1.4 slow box):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step2-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat19_probe_coil_phantom.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W2, -n 4 (predicted 220–245 s): the same command with -n 4, label MAT-19-step2-W2. - W3, -n 1 (predicted 270–320 s; ≤ 450 s slow): the same command with -n 1, label MAT-19-step2-W3. The thermal side is ≈ 2× its -n 2 28.8 s. - Order: W1 → W2 → W3. A red W1 stops the item. Total predicted window time ≈ 13 min; the slot fits in ≈ 40 min including the module.

Traps. - No point evaluation on the submesh with an owner (known-issues :1372, OPEN). The probe is an owned-cell integral. Row 4's point values are read from the ans:9 log, never re-evaluated here. - θ, not T (see Code). (W) on T is 60× too lenient. - Every rank enters every allreduce, including the (S) helper on ranks with no candidate cells (item 227 deadlocked on a rank-0-only collective). (U3c) at -n 2 is the check on the probe path. - Ghosts. Iterate range(size_local) for owned cells. Ghost dof values are needed: snapshots copy x.array after scatter_forward. - Complex build. np.real before every float. Make no ordering comparison on a UFL operand: the probe's indicator is numpy-side, and this module compiles no new indicator form. _run_heated's own ball forms are unchanged. - Snapshot indices are full steps. Snapshot 1 is after both Rannacher half-steps, at t = Δt; times are n·Δt. - No cross-run comparison is bitwise (OPS-43; complex MUMPS is not bit-reproducible across processes). (W) is relative 1e-9; only (U4) is bitwise, and it is in-run. - Stale npz. logs/ persists between sessions. The hash check in the npz is the guard. Never delete-and-recompute at -n 4 / -n 1. - Orphan .c: any stem without its .so, not only 0-byte (item 160's 44 KB partial). Sweep only when pgrep -c python3 reads 0. - Rule (i): no edit to the module after W1. An edit re-runs W1–W3, and the hash enforces it. - The SPEC and ans:9 are not this item's to edit. Changing row 4 to a ball average is the weekly's decision and the operator's export.

Scope. Covered: MAT-15 P1's fixture (ragged sheets, degree-1 EM, P1 thermal, one mesh), drive P1 only, the SPEC's five centres plus C′, one stated volume (a = 5 mm), recorded times only. Not covered: - ANS-9's row 4 as specified (a point), or any adjudication, AED reading or AED number; - a real probe's sensing volume, thermal mass or lead artefact; - exact rectangles or degree 2: this is a record on the SPEC's fixture, not a new one; - an h-statement on the probe readings; - the copper / tuned fixture (MAT-15 step 3); - tissue, perfusion, ASTM F2182; - the submesh owner-rule fix (known-issues stays OPEN); - any edit to ans:9's metrics or COMPARISON.

Status it can move. - MAT-19 is ✅ on step 1 and stays ✅ whatever this step reads, unless (A) is red (see below). - On green: the §7 row gains a step 2 record sentence: the probe on the coil-driven phantom at the SPEC centres; (A), (W) with the EM in the loop and (Σ) asserted; and the (P4) / (P5) sensitivities printed. Rule (j): the reviewing daily adds the Done-when clause "step 2 (§10 P8): identities green ⇒ a record, no glyph", in the pattern of MAT-15 step 3. - §10 P8 is marked DONE. - (8c): the weekly gets the measured probe-volume and placement sensitivity of row 4 at the 10 % AGREE level. It can then decide, before the operator's AED run, whether ANS-9's SPEC should also ask for a ball-averaged row 4 under the POST-8 ruling ("public comparison rows quote cell or mass averages"). That decision and any SPEC edit are the weekly's. If the AED run has already been made, the weekly judges from the private side whether a re-export is worth asking for. This brief does not read that side.

Negative result. In every case: report the measurement, park on attempt/MAT-19-step2-*, mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)) and journal it in attempts.md. Never widen a band, and never change a, L or the centres after reading. - (A0) or (R0) red: the fixture moved under MAT-15's record. Stop; a record-reconciler ruling is needed. - (A) or (U4) red: the probe's ownership contract fails on a coil-driven submesh partition. Open a known-issues entry. The review re-reads MAT-19's ✅, because the row's Done-when is width invariance as POST-8. - (W) red with (A0) / (R0) / (A) green: the complex solve's width round-off reaches 1e-9 in a probe reading, contradicting POST-8's ≤ 2.98e-10 on this EM. Print the 8 × 40 spread, P₁ and G per width, and stop. The review rules whether a probe readout on an EM-driven series carries a width caveat. The band is not moved. - (Σ) red: print the q_h C / C′ pair and the series. If the q_h C / C′ ball pair is also beyond 5 %, the ragged P1 sheet breaks σ_y. Record it in known-issues as a ragged-sheet consequence. Stop. - A control does not miss ((U3c), (C1″) or (f″)): stop. That contradicts (A), (W) or (Σ) respectively. - A slow-box kill at 590: BLOCKED. W1's record stands, and the unblock is a re-run on a box whose MAT-15 EM reads ≤ 30 s per solve (the 03:00 re-price).

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

docs.title: §9 item 258 — 2026-10-05 (chain P8, daily provisional; re-pose of item 253, attempt 2 of 4)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §9 rule (6), the re-pose of a blocked step inside the four-attempt family cap. The weekly ratifies or reverts it. Unchanged: the step's target (a whole-phantom probe = ⟨θ⟩ at B_BAND; width invariance at WIDTH_BAND 1e-9 with the EM in the loop; the σ_y mirror pair within C4_COVARIANCE_BAND at t*), every band, the centres, a, L and the family count. Changed: only where the planted control (U3c) and the "partition" reading of (A) / (U4) are asserted, with the rule pre-registered below, plus one optional speed-up of a printed helper.

MAT-19 step 2, re-pose of item 253: step 1's probe, unchanged, on MAT-15 P1's coil-driven gel phantom at ANS-9's SPEC centres (implementer; heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 590), -n 2 / -n 4 / -n 1, plus -n 8 only by the decision table below, complex; ≈ 9 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min; depends on nothing). Family MAT-19 step 2: attempt 2 of 4.

What attempt 1 measured (read first). Journal: docs/testing/attempts.md 2026-10-05T18:34Z. Code and logs are parked on attempt/MAT-19-step2-20261005T1834Z (e4ffe9a4). - W1 -n 2 (20261005T183423Z_MAT-19-step2-W1.log, 326 s, Status 1) was red only on (U3c). The ghost-included Ω volume missed by 9.770e-15 and the value by 1.577e-14, against "> B_BAND 1e-10" (:1977). - Every other W1 reading was green (:1956–1980): - (A0) 58 866 cells, V_sub rel 3.447e-13; - (R0) 2.525e-15; - (A) 2.386e-14, BE 7.351e-15, volume 9.770e-15, and row 2 reproduced to the printed digits; - (U4) bitwise; - (Σ) 5.919e-4; - (C1″) 4.398e-3; - (f″) 0.8018. - Phase clocks (:1980): _run_heated 168.2 s (EM 144.9 s for four solves, :1955), snapshot re-run + BE 3.1 s, probe geometry + sums 17.0 s, (S) helper 59.2 s, fixture total 258.7 s. - The cause was measured by the diagnostic mat19_step2_ghost_probe.py at -n 2 (20261005T184012Z_MAT-19-step2-ghost-diag.log:1871–1873, 82 s): - parent owned 101 934 / 97 986 cells, ghosts 869 / 883; - tag-3 submesh owned 58 866 / 0, ghosts 0 / 0. - So at -n 2 the phantom is not partitioned: - (U3c) iterates range(size_local + num_ghosts) on the submesh index map, so it has nothing to double-count; - (A) and (U4) are true there, but they do not exercise a submesh partition.

The correct "something to double-count" condition (checked against the parked module, lines 193–198). (U3c) calls _ball_average_on_cells(θ⁴⁰, Ω, arange(size_local + num_ghosts)) on the tag-3 submesh sub.topology.index_map(3). It then allreduces. Every ghost cell on a rank is owned by another rank, and Ω contains every phantom cell. The planted volume miss is therefore exactly Σ_ranks (volume of that rank's submesh ghost cells) / V_sub, up to round-off: for Ω every lattice point of every cell is inside, so each cell weighs its exact |K|. It follows that: - (U3c) applies iff G_w := Σ_ranks num_ghosts(submesh) > 0. Ownership by ≥ 2 ranks is neither necessary nor sufficient for this. A rank can hold ghosts of phantom cells while owning none. Whether the parent's ghost phantom cells reach the submesh at all depends on whether cell_tags.indices covers parent ghost cells; _tag_submesh keeps tagged cells over size_local + num_ghosts, test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:106–121. - The partition reading of (A) / (U4) applies iff O_w := #{ranks with submesh size_local > 0} ≥ 2.

These two conditions are what this item pre-registers. The review may tighten them to the conjunction "O_w ≥ 2 and G_w > 0" for (U3c) if it prefers; see the open question in the return.

Pre-registered applicability rule (the slot does not decide). - D4 comes first. Run the parked diagnostic at -n 4 (window D4 below). It prints the per-rank submesh owned / ghost counts, from which O_4 and G_4 are read. - D8 runs only if G_4 = 0 or O_4 < 2. It is the same diagnostic at -n 8. - Decision table. It is fixed now and is applied to the D logs as printed:

D4 reads D8 (U3c) asserted at partition reading of (A) / (U4) at W4 (-n 8) window G_4 > 0 and O_4 ≥ 2 not run -n 4 (W2) -n 4 (W2) not run G_4 > 0, O_4 < 2 run -n 4 (W2) -n 8 if O_8 ≥ 2, else not exercised run iff O_8 ≥ 2 G_4 = 0, O_4 ≥ 2 run -n 8 if G_8 > 0, else inapplicable -n 4 (W2) run iff G_8 > 0 G_4 = 0, O_4 < 2 run -n 8 if G_8 > 0, else inapplicable -n 8 if O_8 ≥ 2, else not exercised run iff G_8 > 0 or O_8 ≥ 2
  • "Inapplicable" / "not exercised" is a record, not a red. In that case the item closes on the remaining anchors. The chunk-file outcome and the journal state, in these words: "(U3c) inapplicable on this fixture: the tag-3 submesh carries no ghost cells at -n 2 / 4 / 8 (G_w = 0, <D logs>)". For the partition: "(A) / (U4) asserted on a submesh owned by one rank at every measured width; the submesh partition is not exercised on this fixture". No band moves, and no other width is tried in-slot.
  • Predicted (no prior measurement at -n 4; rule (e), predicted, printed):
  • O_4 ≥ 2 by counting. At -n 2 the parent split was 101 934 / 97 986, a 2 % imbalance. At -n 4 each rank owns ≈ 49 980 × [0.97, 1.03] < 58 866 cells, so the phantom cannot fit on one rank unless the partitioner's imbalance exceeds ≈ 17 %.
  • G_4 is genuinely unmeasured. The -n 2 reading of 0 / 0 is consistent with either answer to the cell_tags-covers-ghosts question, because the rank-0/1 cut did not touch the phantom. The predicted G_4 is in [500, 6000] if ghosts propagate and 0 if they do not.
  • The expected row is therefore row 1 or row 3.

Carried verbatim from item 253's brief (above; read it there, it is not restated): - "Why this step"; - "The fixture (imported, never restated)", including the Imports list and the no-edit clause on src/, the MAT-15 module, ans:9, its metrics and its COMPARISON; - "The probes (pinned)", including (M), Ω and B⁺; - "Code", except the edits E1–E6 below; - the anchors (A0), (R0), (A) and (Σ) as stated; - (W) as stated, asserted at -n 4 and -n 1 against the -n 2 npz at WIDTH_BAND; - "Printed, not asserted", meaning (P4), (P5), (S) and the tables; - the negative controls (C1″) and (f″) as stated. Both misses are asserted. Their factors are now predicted equal to attempt 1's measured 4.398e-3 and 0.8018 (W1 :1972, :1975), printed beside; - every trap in item 253's list; - the scope list; - every negative-result disposition in item 253's list. The (U3c) line, "A control does not miss", is amended below.

Landing the parked code (by path; never a record file by path). 1. git checkout attempt/MAT-19-step2-20261005T1834Z -- tests/validation/test_mat19_probe_coil_phantom.py mat19_step2_ghost_probe.py docs/testing/logs/20261005T183255Z_MAT-19-step2-cache-sweep.log docs/testing/logs/20261005T183423Z_MAT-19-step2-W1.log docs/testing/logs/20261005T184012Z_MAT-19-step2-ghost-diag.log 2. git mv mat19_step2_ghost_probe.py scripts/probes/mat19_step2_ghost_probe.py. Keep its bytes identical: no edit, so its -n 2 log stays a record of the same bytes. The repo root holds no tracked .py, and scripts/probes/ is where the project's probes live. The -n 2 log's command names the old root path; the journal says it was moved unedited. 3. Append the attempt's three test-results rows by hand to docs/testing/test-results.md (copy them from git show e4ffe9a4 -- docs/testing/test-results.md). git diff --stat must show only insertions on that file. 4. The stale /workspace/logs/mat19/step2-n2.npz from attempt 1 carries the old module hash. W2 / W3 / W4 refuse it by construction. Never delete it by hand; W1 overwrites it.

Code: edits to the parked module, all made before W1 (rule (i)). Every constant, centre, band and import stays as parked. - E1, docstring. Cite item 258 and the applicability rule: (U3c) is asserted iff G_w > 0, and the partition reading is iff O_w ≥ 2. - E2, the partition table in the fixture. Every rank enters comm.allgather((imap.size_local, imap.num_ghosts)) on sub.topology.index_map(3), at every width including -n 1. Compute O_w and G_w from it. Print one line, MAT19-2 (part) -n w: sub owned [...] ghosts [...] O_w G_w; partition exercised: <O_w ≥ 2>. - E3, (U3c). At comm.size > 1 the ghost-included Ω reading is computed and printed always, as parked. Asserted (volume miss > B_BAND) iff G_w > 0. When G_w = 0 it prints MAT19-2 (U3c) inapplicable at -n w: G_w = 0 and asserts nothing. This makes the module's assertion mechanical at every width. The item-level table above says which width must carry it. - E4, (U4). Assert the in-run bitwise allgather at every comm.size > 1; it was only at == 2. It costs nothing. - Predicted True at -n 4 / -n 8: it was measured True at -n 2 on this fixture (:1978). Each reading is a quotient of identical allreduced sums, and float addition is commutative, so the power-of-two pairwise exchanges give the same bits on every rank. - E5, (W) widths. Assert (W) (cells equal; series ≤ WIDTH_BAND) at comm.size ∈ {4, 1} only, as the row's -n 1 / 2 / 4 reads. At -n 8, (W) against the -n 2 npz is printed with the hash guard intact, and no -n 8 npz is written. The -n 4 npz write and the -n 1 vs -n 4 print stay as parked. - E6, the optional speed-up of the (S) helper (printed-only quantity), applied before W1. In _lattice_q_mean, pre-filter owned by bounding radius exactly as thermal/probe.py's _geometry does (probe.py:115–119): take X = xdof[V.dofmap.list[owned]], cen = X.mean(1), rho = sqrt(max ‖X − cen‖²), and keep ‖cen − c‖ − rho ≤ a. Then run the parked chunk loop over the kept cells. - Why it cannot change a reading beyond round-off: every lattice point is a convex combination of the cell's vertices, so ‖P − c‖ ≥ ‖cen − c‖ − ρ_K > a for a dropped cell. Its v_K is exactly 0, and dropping it changes only the pairwise-summation grouping of np.sum. - For Ω (r = 0.1 m against a farthest vertex at 0.05 m), every cell is kept and the path is byte-identical. - Predicted: the (S) phase drops from 59.2 s to ≈ 8 s (Ω's ≈ 1/8 share), and every (S) value equals attempt 1's (:1976) to the printed 5 digits. - If the slot does not apply E6, nothing else changes; the pricing below then adds ≈ 50 s per window.

Anchors and controls, re-posed parts (everything else carries verbatim, see above). - (U3c), the planted ghost control, asserted where the table says, factor predicted. At the width the table names: the ghost-included Ω volume misses (A)'s identity by > B_BAND. The miss is asserted; the factor is predicted. - Floor: one ghost cell is ≈ 3.84e-9 / 2.26e-4 ≈ 1.7e-5 of V_sub, so any G_w ≥ 1 clears 1e-10 by ≥ 1e4× unless a ghost is a sliver below 1e-5 of the mean cell volume. - Ceiling: ≤ w − 1, since each cell is ghost on at most w − 1 other ranks. - Predicted factor: item 253's range [2e-2, 2e-1] at -n 4 is kept and printed. The sharp prediction, printed beside, is G_w / 58 866 within ×[0.5, 2], with G_w from the D log at that width. The phantom mesh is uniform at h_p = 2.5 mm, so ghost cells are ≈ mean-sized. - The value miss is printed. - The partition reading of (A) / (U4). (A) stays asserted at every width as in item 253. (U4) is asserted at every width > 1 (E4). The reading "(A) and (U4) hold on a coil-driven submesh partition" is licensed only from the window at the width the table names, whose own (part) line shows O_w ≥ 2. - Cross-check, D against the in-run partition (printed; a mismatch stops the item). At the width that carries (U3c) or the partition reading, the window's (part) line must match its D log's per-rank owned / ghost counts. The mesh and partitioner path is the same build_four_port_sweep(PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG).

Windows (complex; foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; each command bare, whole and repo-relative; -s; no -k inside the quoted command; no pipes or redirects; every window ≤ 590 s container-side, so the §5.1 durable-capture idiom is not needed). - First: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Then the any-orphan sweep as one bare call:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step2-a2-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - Pricing basis (measured: attempt 1's W1 at -n 2, 326 s). The fixture took 258.7 s, so environment tests, collection and teardown are ≈ 67 s. The width ratios are POST-8 step 2's 0.98 (-n 4) and 1.17 (-n 1) on the same EM (item 253's basis). This box's EM read 144.9 s for four solves (:1955), above item 253's ≤ 30 s / solve unblock bar, and W1 still finished at 326 s, so the 590 ceiling holds ≈ 1.8× headroom. There is no -n 8 window on this fixture. - D4, ownership at -n 4 (predicted 70–120 s; the -n 2 diagnostic took 82 s, mesh build dominated):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step2-a2-D4 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 4 python3 scripts/probes/mat19_step2_ghost_probe.py'" - D8, ownership at -n 8. Run only per the table (predicted 70–150 s): the same command with -n 8, label MAT-19-step2-a2-D8. - Then make the E1–E6 edits. No edit after W1. - W1, -n 2, writes the npz. This is the rule (i) re-run on the landed bytes (predicted 240–330 s; ≈ 275 s with E6, ≈ 326 s without):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-19-step2-a2-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat19_probe_coil_phantom.py -s -v --tb=short'"

  • Expected (part) line: O_2 = 1, G_2 = 0, so (U3c) prints inapplicable at -n 2 and is not asserted.
  • If the in-run line at -n 2 instead shows G_2 > 0, the module asserts (U3c) there too. That is harmless, and it is recorded.
  • W2, -n 4 (predicted 230–330 s): the same command with -n 4, label MAT-19-step2-a2-W2. It asserts (W), and (U3c) / (U4) per E3 / E4.
  • W3, -n 1 (predicted 260–360 s; the thermal side at -n 2 was already serial on rank 0, so only the EM ratio applies): the same command with -n 1, label MAT-19-step2-a2-W3. It asserts (W).
  • W4, -n 8. Run only per the table (unmeasured on this fixture; predicted 230–400 s): the same command with -n 8, label MAT-19-step2-a2-W4. (W) is printed there (E5); (U3c), (U4) and (A) are asserted per E3 / E4.
  • Order: pgrep → sweep → land → D4 → [D8] → E1–E6 → W1 → W2 → W3 → [W4].
  • A red W1 stops the item. W2 / W3 / W4 need W1's npz from the same bytes, and the hash enforces it.
  • Total window time: ≈ 16.5 min on table row 1 (81 + 82 + 275 + 260 + 290 s), ≈ 23 min with D8 + W4. The slot fits its hour with the edits.

Traps (added to item 253's list). - Rule (i) and the npz hash. E1–E6 all land before W1. Any edit afterwards re-runs W1 and everything after it. Check file mtimes against the W1 log start before committing. - Every rank enters E2's allgather and every allreduce of the (S) helper, including ranks that own no phantom cells. At -n 2 rank 1 owns none (item 227's rank-subset deadlock). - The diagnostic is not a gate. It is moved unedited, never edited, and runs through the harness like any window. Its GHOSTPROBE lines are the D reading. - Never pick the width after seeing W-window readings. The table is applied to the D logs only. - The bash guard denies any docker / run_and_log.sh call that is not bare and whole. The spawn prompt carries the every-item harness sentence verbatim. - Landing. Record files are never checked out by path (the 8d4cf58 trap). Only the module, the diagnostic and the three logs are.

Scope (added to item 253's list). Not covered: - a submesh partition at widths other than those the table runs; - any statement about DolfinX's ghost propagation through create_submesh beyond the counts printed; - (W) at -n 8 as a gate (printed only).

Status it can move (restated, because the record wording now depends on the table row). - MAT-19 is ✅ on step 1 and stays ✅ whatever this step reads, unless (A) or (U4) is red (item 253's disposition: a known-issues entry, and the review re-reads the ✅). - On green: the §7 row gains a step 2 record sentence. It reads: the probe on the coil-driven phantom at the SPEC centres; (A) and (U4) asserted, "on a submesh partition at -n w" only if the table's partition width ran with O_w ≥ 2, else "on a phantom owned by one rank (partition not exercised)"; (W) with the EM in the loop at -n 4 / -n 1; (Σ) asserted; (U3c) "missed by x at -n w" or "inapplicable on this fixture (G_w = 0 at -n 2 / 4 / 8)"; the (P4) / (P5) sensitivities printed. Elapsed times and logs are cited. - Rule (j): if the row still lacks it, the reviewing daily adds the Done-when clause "step 2 (§10 P8): identities green ⇒ a record, no glyph", as item 253's brief asked; it is not in the row as of this draft. - §10 P8 is marked DONE. (8c) is as item 253's brief states.

Negative result (amended; item 253's list otherwise carries). In every case: report the measurement, park on attempt/MAT-19-step2-*, mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)), and journal it in attempts.md as attempt 2 of 4. Never widen a band, and never change a, L, the centres or the table after reading. - (U3c) asserted (G_w > 0) and does not miss: ghost cells were present and not double-counted. That contradicts the probe's cell loop. Stop, print the (part) line and both volumes, and open a known-issues entry. The review re-reads step 1's (U3c). - (U3c) inapplicable per the table: a record, not a red. Continue on the remaining anchors. - D / in-run mismatch at the width that carries (U3c) or the partition reading: the partition is not reproducible across runs. Stop BLOCKED with both counts. The review rules; the slot does not reassign the width. - D4 or D8 fails to run (import error or kill): stop. W windows do not start without the D reading that sets the table. - (U4) red at -n 4 / -n 8: item 253's "(A) or (U4) red" disposition. - A slow-box kill at 590: BLOCKED. Every window that finished stands as a record. The unblock is a re-run, never a longer timeout.

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

Outcome (2026-10-06 01:11Z, 19:30 CDT slot, third item): ✅ GREEN, attempt 2 of 4. - Landed the parked module, the diagnostic (moved unedited to scripts/probes/) and attempt 1's three logs by path from e4ffe9a4. Attempt 1's three test-results rows were appended by hand. Sweep 20261006T005419Z_MAT-19-step2-a2-cache-sweep.log. - D4 (20261006T005546Z_MAT-19-step2-a2-D4.log:1871–1875, 68 s): sub owned 23 401 / 35 465 / 0 / 0, ghosts 701 / 677 / 0 / 0, so O_4 = 2 and G_4 = 1 378. That is table row 1: (U3c) and the partition reading go on -n 4, with no D8 and no W4. The row-1/row-3 prediction held, and ghosts do propagate through _tag_submesh at -n 4. - E1–E6 applied before W1. No edit came after W1, and the npz hash held across W2 / W3. - W1 -n 2 (20261006T005727Z_MAT-19-step2-a2-W1.log, 275 s, 13 passed): - (part) [58 866, 0] / [0, 0], O 1, G 0, so (U3c) printed "inapplicable at -n 2: G_w = 0"; - (A0) 58 866 cells, V_sub rel 3.447e-13; (R0) 2.531e-15; - (A) 2.190e-14, BE 2.654e-15, volume 9.770e-15, with row 2 reproduced to the printed digits; - (U4) True; - phase clocks: _run_heated 175.0 s; (S) helper 6.8 s with E6, against 59.2 s before. The (S) values equal attempt 1's (:1976) to all printed digits. - W2 -n 4 (20261006T010208Z_MAT-19-step2-a2-W2.log, 248 s, 13 passed): - (part) matches D4 exactly; - (A) 6.825e-15, volume 1.332e-15; (U4) True; - (U3c) volume miss 2.6047e-2 (asserted > 1e-10), value miss 3.080e-3. That is inside the predicted [2e-2, 2e-1]. The sharp prediction G_4/58 866 = 2.341e-2 is within ×1.11; - (W) 3.714e-11 (band 1e-9, predicted ≤ 1e-10), volumes 4.4e-16. - W3 -n 1 (20261006T010623Z_MAT-19-step2-a2-W3.log, 290 s, 13 passed): (A) 1.780e-14; (W) 5.735e-11; the pairwise -n 1 vs -n 4 print is 7.287e-11. - Width-independent readings (all three windows): - (Σ) 5.919e-4; - (C1″) 4.398e-3 and (f″) 0.8018, equal to attempt 1; - (P4) A +7.18e-3, B −1.238e-2, C +1.807e-2, D −4.35e-3, E +2.84e-3. B is inside its predicted [−8 %, 0], and A / C / D / E are inside ±3 %; - (P5) 4.398e-3, inside [1e-3, 1e-2]; - the q_h C / C′ ball pair, printed: 9.55e-3. - Record wording: (A) and (U4) hold on a submesh partition at -n 4; (U3c) misses by 2.6e-2 at -n 4. "Execute §9 item 258, MAT-19 step 2, re-pose of item 253 (attempt 2 of 4), per docs/planning/chunks/MAT-19.md ### §9 item 258 and the parts of ### §9 item 253 it carries verbatim. docs.text:
Outcome (2026-10-06 09:00 CDT slot, attempt 1 of 4): BLOCKED — (Σ) red at W1; parked on attempt/MAT-19-step3-20261006T1405Z (a5b3c631). W1 20261006T140518Z_MAT-19-step3-W1.log (168 s, -n 8, summed ru_maxrss 12.96 GiB; clocks mesh+tie 48.6 s, EM drive 41.5 s, transient 0.8 s, probe 0.1 s). Red: (Σ) |C − C′|/C at t* = 5.7365e-2 against C4_COVARIANCE_BAND 5e-2. Per the brief's named disposition, printed: q_h ball pair C 340.33 / C′ 264.85 W/m³ (22.18 %, cf. item 236's 22.7 % 10 g q_h pair), ball volumes C 5.0774e-7 / C′ 5.1643e-7 m³ (V_h/nominal − 1: C −3.03e-2, C′ −1.37e-2). Green before it: (A0) 80 798 cells, tag-3 537 (record :1926), (Φ) |sin φ₁| = 0, (M) true, snapshot 0 = 0.0; (Src) (W) 1.116e-12 (NODE_S_RTOL 1e-9), (P) 7.393e-13 (1e-6); (A) max 4.549e-16, BE 0, V_Ω/V_sub − 1 = 4.441e-16 (B_BAND 1e-10), on a submesh partition at -n 8 (owned 100/29/45/57/130/30/79/67, ghosts 40/19/25/25/51/19/28/22, O_w 8, G_w 229); (U4) bitwise; (U3c) asserted (G_w > 0) and missed by 0.5474 (predicted G_w/537 = 0.4264, within ×[0.5, 2]). Computed but not reached as asserts (the (Σ) assert stopped the test): (C1″) 1.9498e-3 (predicted [1e-4, 1e-2]), (f″) 0.5474 (predicted [0.1, 1.0]). Printed: ⟨θ⟩(t*) 0.687806 K per accepted watt vs item 236's 0.687806 (rel 1.6e-8, 6-digit record); (P4′) ball/point − 1 at A +2.35 %, B +0.02 %, C +0.10 %, D −1.20 %, E −2.04 % (A and E above the predicted ≤ 2 %); ratio (i) (mixed normalisation) A 0.6926, B 0.3195, C 0.7296, D 1.5990, E 0.6799, C′ 0.6874, Ω 0.5964; ratio (ii) (per deposited watt at both) A 1.1989, B 0.5530, C 1.2631, D 2.7680, E 1.1769, C′ 1.1899, Ω 1.0324. W2 / W3 not run, so (W) is not measured. Other logs: 20261006T140242Z_MAT-19-step3-cache-sweep.log (no orphans), 20261006T140407Z_MAT-19-step3-import.log (knob-unset collection smoke, killed at its own 60 s ceiling during tests/environment; the module collected, pgrep 0 afterwards). For the review: the brief's (Σ) disposition applies: on ≈ 15 mm cells the 5 mm probe pair inherits the unsymmetric phantom mesh (q_h pair 22 %). Re-pose on a phantom-refined exact hole mesh (a new fixture with its own C_mode), not in-slot. No band moved.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-06 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain P10 (grep "P10. MAT-19 step 3" in PROJECT_PLAN.md), quoted, not changed: "the probe series on the tuned copper fixture at 64 MHz (P5's source, degree 2, exact rectangles) at ANS-9's six centres, 40 steps. Asserted: P8's identities (whole-phantom probe = ⟨θ⟩ at B_BAND, width invariance at 1e-9 with the EM in the loop, the σ_y mirror pair at C4_COVARIANCE_BAND); printed, ball/point at A–E and the 64 MHz / 10 MHz ratio of the probe rises per accepted watt. The first probe-level thermal figure on a tuned coil; a record. Target: identities. Serial on nothing." The 2026-10-02 sheets-and-κ ruling binds (exact rectangles, κ off). §10 ruling P8 (item 258's ghost / width rule) binds. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved. Every band is imported by name.

MAT-19 step 3: step 2's probe series (item 258), unchanged, on MAT-15 step 3's tuned copper source (item 236). - Executor: implementer. One new test module, tests/validation/test_mat19_probe_tuned_copper.py. There is no src/ change. Do not edit thermal/probe.py, item 236's module (test_mat15_tuned_copper_heating.py), item 258's module (test_mat19_probe_coil_phantom.py), step 1's MAT-15 module, the ans:7 / ans:9 scripts, or any ans7_exact test. An edit to any of them owes those gates' windows under rule (a). - Tier: heavy, -n 8 / -n 4 / -n 2, complex build. - Cost: ≈ 17 measured / ≈ 50 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + sweep 0.5 + W1 ≈ 3.3 + W2 ≈ 5 + W3 ≈ 8 + ≈ 6 spare. - Depends on nothing on main. It needs T21's two gitignored JSONs, logs/ans7_exact/tune_p2.json and tune_inmodel_p2.json, which item 236's _read_t21 reads. If either is absent, stop and take the next item. Never re-create them.

The fixture (imported, never restated). - The source is item 236's, exactly. Use the _exact_geo ×1 hole mesh (80 798 cells), Leontovich copper, and C_mode,Cu read from tune_p2.json. Apply Z_C on P2–P4 and C₁ across P1. Drive one P1 at 64.0 MHz through _route_a_solve(..., degree=2), with G = 1 W / P_acc. - Reuse before you copy. Read test_mat15_tuned_copper_heating.py:142–310 (_run) first. - If _run() returns the submesh, Robin tags, q_h, G, P_acc and η, call it. - If it does not, rebuild the same steps in the same order from the imported helpers: _read_t21, _fixture_tie, _exact_geo, _route_a_solve, the TH-14 (b) power block with the Z_C-replaced specs, _tag_submesh, _robin_tags, _cell_average_dg0_tag and _to_sub. Disclose the mapping. - Never edit item 236's module to make it return more. - The series is item 258's: _transient(sub, ft, q_h, dt=T_STAR / N_MAIN, n_steps=N_MAIN, theta=0.5, startup_half_steps=2, snapshot_steps=range(N_MAIN + 1)), _be_one, then probe_series over θ = T − T_INF. - The probes are item 258's _probe_set(), imported: ANS-9's SPEC centres A–E plus C′ (σ_y image of C), so six centres, plus Ω (r = 0.1 m) and the control ball B⁺. Keep a = A_PROBE 5 mm. - Imports: B_BAND, C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, E_BAND, F_CONTROL_FLOOR, DT_1, N_MAIN, T_STAR, T_INF, RHO_C, _transient, _be_one, _allsum and _say, from test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom exactly as item 258's module imports them (test_mat19_probe_coil_phantom.py:56–74). Also import WIDTH_BAND from test_mat19_virtual_temperature_probe, and _probe_set, A_PROBE, OMEGA_RADIUS and _lattice_q_mean from item 258's module. Restate none of them. - (Φ) is reused. Item 236 measured φ₁ = 0.000000000000° on this mesh (20261005T040135Z_MAT-15-step3-W1.log), so C′ = (x, −y, z) is the drive's σ_y image here as on step 2's fixture. Re-assert item 236's (Φ) in-run. - Opt-in knob FEM_EM_MAT19_STEP3=1, in item 236's pattern. When it is unset, every test skips. Any other value raises ValueError. - npz: /workspace/logs/mat19/step3-n8.npz. Guard it with the SHA-256 of the new module, thermal/probe.py and item 236's module.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported). - (A0) _assert_tie (80 798 cells), (Φ) |sin φ₁| ≤ item 236's PHI_BAND, and the tag-3 cell count == 537. That count is item 236's printed record (…040135Z_MAT-15-step3-W1.log; cite the line). Snapshot 0 reads exactly 0.0, and every probe ball lies inside the phantom ((M), item 258's test). - (Src) item 236's (W), |S11 − S11_ref|/|S11_ref| ≤ NODE_S_RTOL, and (P) ≤ DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL, re-asserted on this run's field. This ties the source to item 236's gated run. - (A) whole-phantom probe P_Ω = ∫θ/V_sub at n = 1 … 40 and for the BE θ¹, plus V_Ω/V_sub − 1, all ≤ B_BAND. - (U4) the rank rows agree bitwise at n = 40, at every width > 1. - (W) width invariance with the EM in the loop. The -n 4 and -n 2 series against the -n 8 npz: cells equal, and max rel ≤ WIDTH_BAND. The hash guard stays as item 258's. - (Σ) |θ̄_C − θ̄_C′|/θ̄_C at t* ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND.

§10 ruling P8 (item 258's rule), applied mechanically. Every rank enters comm.allgather((size_local, num_ghosts)) on the tag-3 submesh's index_map(3), at every width. Print item 258's (part) line with O_w and G_w. - (U3c) is asserted iff G_w > 0 (as item 258's E3). - The reading "(A) / (U4) on a submesh partition" is licensed iff O_w ≥ 2. - The widths are fixed now, before any reading: 8 / 4 / 2. No width is added or chosen after a reading. "Inapplicable" and "not exercised" are records, not reds, in item 258's words. - Predicted, not measured: the phantom is 537 of 80 798 cells (0.66 %). It may sit on one rank at every width, giving O_w = 1 and G_w = 0. In that case, record the outcome in item 258's wording.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (U3c) ghost-included Ω misses (A)'s volume identity by > B_BAND. Asserted iff G_w > 0. The factor is predicted: ≈ G_w/537 within ×[0.5, 2]. A single ghost cell is ≈ 1/537 ≈ 1.9e-3 of V_sub, ≥ 1e7× the band. Backing on another fixture: item 258's W2 measured 2.605e-2 against a sharp prediction of 2.341e-2 (20261006T010208Z_MAT-19-step2-a2-W2.log). - (C1″) B⁺ vs B > WIDTH_BAND, predicted. This fixture has no prior measurement. Step 2 read 4.398e-3 on 2.5 mm cells. Here the cells are ≈ 15 mm (V_sub/537 ≈ 4.1e-7 m³), so the 0.1 mm shift moves the lattice set less. The prediction is [1e-4, 1e-2], with a ceiling far above the band. Assert only the miss. - (f″) C vs B > F_CONTROL_FLOOR, predicted. The 64 MHz tuned field is not the 10 MHz one. Item 236's off-mirror (f′) read 35.78 % on this fixture with 10 g balls. The prediction is [0.1, 1.0]. Assert only the miss. - The width controls are not re-bought. Item 258's (U3c) / (C1″) record stands.

Printed (not asserted). - (P4′) ball/point − 1 at t* at A–E. "Point" means the P1 θ at the centre. Compute it from the owned cell that contains the centre (barycentric λ ≥ −1e-12) with allreduce((Σ value, count)), and average over the containing cells. No eval and no evaluate_vector_field_parallel on the submesh: the owner rule raises there (known-issues 2026-10-04). On 15 mm cells a 5 mm ball is smaller than a cell, so the predicted magnitudes are ≤ 2 %. Also print each ball's V_h/(4πa³/3) − 1 (level-3 lattice, sub-tet edge ≈ 1.9 mm, predicted ≤ 3e-2). - The 64 / 10 MHz ratio of the probe rises at t* at A–E, C′ and Ω, printed twice: - (i) this run's rise per accepted watt ÷ step 2's rise at 10 MHz. Step 2 was normalised per deposited watt, G = 1 W / P₁, from the MAT19-2 n=40 row of 20261006T005727Z_MAT-19-step2-a2-W1.log (cite the line). Hard-code those values as printed records with their log line, never as comparands; - (ii) the same with the 64 MHz rise divided by η (per deposited watt at both frequencies, a shape-only ratio). - Label the mixed normalisation of (i) in the print. No 10 MHz per-accepted-watt figure exists. - Also printed: the series table at n = 1, 10, 20, 30, 40; ⟨θ⟩(t*) beside item 236's 0.687806 K per accepted watt (R0-style, ≤ E_BAND expected, printed); (S) via _lattice_q_mean; the q_h C / C′ pair; per-phase clocks; summed ru_maxrss.

Windows. Foreground. The harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative. Bash timeout: 660000; -s; tests/environment first; no pipe or redirect. Each window is ≤ 590 s, so the durable-capture idiom is not needed. - Price. Item 236's W1 measured 156 s at -n 8 (fixture 90.2 s, EM drive 41.8–50.3 s, mesh 24.4 s). The probe adds the 40-step transient on 537 cells plus the probe sums, ≈ 5–20 s (item 258's series on 58 866 cells took 17 s). The -n 4 / -n 2 degree-2 EM on this mesh is unmeasured. It is predicted at ×1.6–2 and ×3–4 of the -n 8 drive. Memory is predicted at ≈ 10–14 GiB (ANS-4 item 225: 36.3 GiB on 259 524 cells at degree 2, scaled by cells). - First: docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0.
