Operator. cem43(times, temps, *, r_above=0.5, r_below=0.25, t_ref=43.0) takes a 1-D series, or a (n_t, n_cells) array (the "one DG0 series": one value per cell per time). Between samples it treats T as piecewise linear in t and integrates R^(t_ref − T) exactly on each segment: - ∫ R^(43−T) dt = (R^(43−T₀) − R^(43−T₁)) / (b ln R), with b = (T₁ − T₀)/Δt. - A segment that crosses 43 °C is split at t₍₄₃₎ = t₀ + (43 − T₀)/b. R = 0.5 applies on the side T ≥ 43 and R = 0.25 on the side T < 43. The integrand is continuous at 43, where both sides equal 1. - The b → 0 limit uses the expm1 form, Δt·R^(43−T₀)·(−expm1(−ΔT ln R))/(ΔT ln R), never the raw difference quotient, which cancels catastrophically when ΔT ≈ 0. - The §7 row's Σ R^(43−T_i) Δt_i is the piecewise-constant special case. It is printed as a record, never asserted: a rectangle rule cannot reach 1e-10 on a ramp.

Anchors (asserted at 1e-10 relative — the §7 row's bar). - (A1) Three linear ramps straddling 43 °C against the analytic piecewise integral above, written out in the test as its own two-line function. The test does not call the operator for this; that independence is the point. The ramps, one per branch of the operator: - 41 → 45 °C over 600 s (rising); - 42.5 → 43.5 °C over 60 s (a shallow straddle); - 45 → 40 °C over 900 s (falling, b < 0).

For a straight line the operator is exact to rounding on any sampling, so each ramp is also run at 2, 7 and 1 000 samples. That catches a split-point bug that only one sampling would hide. - (A2) MAT-9's closed-form step response. The source is utils.analytical.robin_sphere_transient_temperature (analytical.py:1266) at r = 0, with MAT-9's constants (R = 0.1, k = 0.6, Q = 2000, h = 10; test_mat9_transient_conduction_sphere.py:41–44; ρc as test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py:41). - The temperatures are re-based to t_inf = t_init = 37 °C. Only the additive offset changes, so θ is unchanged. The centre's steady rise of ≈ 12.2 K means T crosses 43 °C. At MAT-9's 20 °C the response never reaches 43, so the dose would test only the R = 0.25 branch. - Reference: scipy.integrate.quad of R^(43−T(t)) with points=[t₄₃], where t₄₃ comes from brentq on the same closed form, at epsabs / epsrel ≤ 1e-13. Quad's own error estimate is printed. - Operator: run on N uniform samples of the same closed form. The executor sizes N from a printed N, 2N, 4N sequence, whose rate should be ≈ 2 for a piecewise-linear interpolant, and asserts at the first N whose predicted error is ≤ 1e-11. - Sizing estimate: N ≈ 10⁵ gives an error near 1e-11. That is 4 × 10⁷ series operations at 400 terms, under a second.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (Rc) asserted — the planted R swap misses. With r_above=0.25, r_below=0.5 the operator must miss (A1) by more than 1e-10 on every ramp. Predicted misses, computed analytically while drafting: - 41 → 45: 1.378; - 42.5 → 43.5: 0.194; - 45 → 40: 1.398.

The shallow ramp has the smallest separation (≈ 2 × 10⁹ × the bar) and is the binding case. - (Sc) predicted, printed — no split at 43. Using one R across a crossing segment misses (A1). The size is printed and not asserted.

Traps. - Real build only. Nothing here needs complex DolfinX, and a np.real belongs nowhere in the operator. If a DG0 series from a complex run is ever passed in, the operator raises on a non-zero imaginary part rather than dropping it. - Pytest captures prints unless -s is passed. Never pipe the harness command. - A brentq bracket at t = 0 needs T(0) < 43 < T(t_end). Assert the bracket; do not let it be assumed.

Public API (rule). If dose.py's names enter thermal/__init__.py's __all__ (thermal/__init__.py:13), the same slot re-runs scripts/docs/generate_api_reference.py and tests/package/test_wf17_api_reference.py. The same holds if the slot touches tests/package/validation_envelope.toml. That costs one more smoke window. Keeping the module unexported in step 1 avoids it. Step 2 adds to the same module, so either choice is fine.

Scope. This is a post-processor against a closed form. It makes no claim to a dose limit, a damage threshold, compliance, tissue or perfusion, and does not apply it to any FEM field.

Negative result. A red on (A1) is an operator defect: report it, park the slot on attempt/MAT-20-step1, and journal it in attempts.md. A red on (A2) with (A1) green is a sampling or quad-accuracy matter. Print the N-sequence, do not raise N past the smoke ceiling, and stop. Either way the bar stays as it is.

Status it can move. The §7 MAT-20 row goes ⬜ → 🟡 under step 1's Done-when (rule (j)). ✅ waits on step 2.

Outcome — ✅ DONE 2026-10-08 (12:00 slot). MAT-20-step1, smoke, -n 2, 12 s, 8 passed (docs/testing/logs/20261008T171434Z_MAT-20-step1.log). src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py (cem43, not exported from thermal/__init__.py) and tests/validation/test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py. - (A1) the three ramps at 2 / 7 / 1000 samples: relative residuals 0 … 6.3e-16 against the independent two-piece closed form; a (1000, 3) DG0-shaped call ≤ 2.4e-15. The 7-sample rise puts 43 °C exactly on a sample (the touching-end branch). The rectangle sum Σ R^(43−T_i)Δt_i, printed only, is 37.5 / 572.4 / 749.5 against 750.65 on the rise (2 / 7 / 1000 samples). - (A2) MAT-9's centre response re-based to 37 °C, t_end = 36 000 s (T rises to 47.24 °C; brentq t₄₃ = 14 087.0956 s); quad 1.708516120835631e5 with error estimate 1.1e-14 relative. N = 2¹⁰ … 2¹⁸: relative errors 5.885e-7, 1.471e-7, 3.678e-8, 9.196e-9, 2.299e-9, 5.747e-10, 1.437e-10, 3.592e-11, 8.980e-12, measured rate 2.000 throughout; the Richardson prediction equals the measured error to the printed digits. Asserted at the first N with predicted ≤ 1e-11: N = 262 144, 8.980e-12 ≤ 1e-10. The truncated 400-term series gives T(0) = 37.000000028 (the same function feeds quad and the operator, so it cancels). - (Rc) asserted: the R swap misses by 1.3784 / 0.1937 / 1.3982 on every sampling — the drafted predictions (1.378 / 0.194 / 1.398) to the printed digits. - (Sc) printed: one R (the start side) across the crossing segment misses by 1.2973 / 0.1292 / 0.1096.

docs.title: §9 item 319 — 2026-10-08 (chain P14 — the six-minute running average)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-08 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 P14 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4663–4668), a weekly-enumerated step. It is serial on item 318, the same module: if 318 did not land, skip. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, Done-when or target.

MAT-20 step 2 — running_average(times, values, *, window=360.0) in thermal/dose.py. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: smoke. Numpy plus the closed form, with no new solve. - Cost: ≈ 0 measured / ≈ 35 predicted min. - Ranks: -n 2. - New file: tests/validation/test_mat20_running_average.py. - Command: as item 318's, with ID MAT-20-step2 and that path.

Operator. It integrates the piecewise-linear interpolant over [t − W, t] exactly, including fractional end segments. It returns the series of window means, the maximum, and the position t_max. The window must not need to be an integer number of samples: on the FEM grid, 360 s / 31.35 s = 11.48 samples.

Anchors. - (B1) Integer number of periods. The input is MAT-17's periodic closed-form history: robin_sphere_duty_cycle_temperature(..., periodic=True) (analytical.py:1943), case A (P = 1200 s, D = 0.5; test_mat17_duty_cycle_closed_form.py:44), at r = 0, with switch times on the sampling grid. - The window is W = kP for k = 1 and 2. - The window mean must equal D·θ_ss(0) at 1e-12, the §7 row's bar. θ_ss(0) is robin_sphere_steady_temperature and appears as TH_SS0, :48. - MAT-17 P1 reached 1e-12 only by an analytic cycle integral (:146–163). A sampled operator relies on the trapezoid kink terms cancelling (the jumps in θ′ at on and off are equal and opposite), and that is not guaranteed below O(Δt²). See question 2. - (B2) The phase of the window maximum. For W = 360 s on case A, the maximum of the window mean lies where θ(t) = θ(t − W) on the falling side. That point is pre-computed by brentq on the closed form, independently of the operator. The operator's t_max must fall within one sample of it, and the root and the offset are printed. - (B3) The FEM history at D_BAND. D_BAND = 1.0e-13 is imported by name from tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py:65 (restated there from test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem.py:183). See question 3 before queueing. As written, this assertion is unreachable on the log's records.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (Wc) asserted — a window shifted by half a period misses (B1). For W = kP the window mean is phase-invariant, so a shift alone does not move it. The control is therefore W = kP + P/2. Its miss from D·θ_ss is O(ripple). The predicted size comes from the closed form's peak and trough, which the MAT-17 P5 records print at :241. The miss is asserted > the bar. - (Pc) predicted, printed — the maximum's position under a window one sample short.

Traps. These are item 318's, plus three: - MAT-17 case B's P = 0.2 t_R is not a multiple of any round Δt. Pin the grid to P/M. - The log values are text. Parse them with a regex anchored on the MAT17s3 H_m prefix (20261006T201547Z_MAT-17-step3-W1.log:1960–1969). Never hand-copy them into constants without citing the line. - The log prints every line twice (two ranks' worth of test IDs). Take the first match.

Scope. This is a time-average operator against closed forms. It makes no claim to the six-minute SAR/temperature limit itself, compliance or tissue, and says nothing about the coil-driven fixture beyond reproducing a record.

Negative result. If (B1) misses 1e-12 on a sampled history, report the M / 2M sequence and stop. Never loosen the bar. Park the slot on attempt/MAT-20-step2 and record a §7 annotation. A (B3) red is answered per question 3.

Status it can move. The §7 MAT-20 row goes 🟡 → ✅ under step 2's Done-when, provided step 1 is 🟡-landed (rule (j)).

Questions for the review. 1. Item 318: the §7 row writes CEM43 as Σ R^(43−T_i)Δt_i but asks for 1e-10 against the analytic ramp integral. The brief resolves this by making the operator exact on piecewise-linear segments, with the Σ form printed. Ratify, or rule otherwise. 2. Item 319 (B1): is 1e-12 meant for a sampled operator, or for the analytic cycle integral that MAT-17 P1 already holds? The brief asserts it on samples, with the cancellation argument unproven. A dense M (2¹⁶ per period, as MAT-17 P2 used) may or may not reach it. 3. Item 319 (B3) has a ceiling: - The W1 log records only end-time values: ⟨θ⟩(t*) per H_m to 13 significant figures, the duty ⟨θ⟩ at n = 32 / 36 / 40 to 9 decimals, and no per-step series. - Measured while drafting: Σ(−1)^m ⟨θ[H_m]⟩(t*) from :1960–1969 = 0.5688355135425 K, against the duty record 0.568835514 K (:1973). That is a relative difference of 8.0e-10. The print-precision ceiling is 5e-10 / 0.5688 ≈ 8.8e-10. - D_BAND = 1e-13 is therefore unreachable on the records by ≈ 4 orders of magnitude. Nor can a 360 s window be formed on three duty samples.

The options are: - (a) re-run _run_duty(return_fields=True) with every step snapshotted. That is standard, ≈ 276 s for W1's whole window, and the §7 row says "no new solve"; - (b) the weekly re-poses (B3); - (c) leave (B3) out, which holds the row at 🟡.

The daily may not choose a band. If (a) is chosen, the anchor becomes: on the per-step ⟨θ⟩ series, the operator's window mean of the duty series equals Σ(−1)^m of the operator applied to the H_m series, at D_BAND. That identity is linearity, and it is exact to rounding.

Review rulings (2026-10-08 03:00 daily review, items 318 / 319). (318-1) Ratified: the operator integrates each linear segment of θ(t) exactly — the exact CEM43 of the piecewise-linear interpolant — and the plain sum Σ R^(43−T_i)Δt_i is printed beside it; the Done-when's anchor (1e-10 against the analytic ramp integral) is unchanged. (319-2) No range can be pre-registered for the sampled 1e-12 clause: a red there stops the slot and is reported. (319-3) The FEM clause is not queued. The Done-when says "no new solve" and the W1 log holds end-time records only, so D_BAND cannot be met from it (the 9-decimal print limits agreement to ≈ 8.8e-10). Option (a) is a new solve the row forbids; the choice between (a) re-posing the clause on a re-run with the per-step series kept, and (b) another comparand, is the weekly's (dashboard). Item 319 executes the closed-form half only — the integer-period mean = D × θ_ss at 1e-12, the window-maximum phase, and the kP + P/2 control — and records it in the row; MAT-20 stays 🟡 until the weekly rules on the FEM clause.

Outcome — ✅ DONE 2026-10-08 (12:00 slot), closed-form half only. MAT-20-step2, smoke, -n 2, 19 s, 11 passed (8 step-1 tests re-run against the edited module + 3 new; docs/testing/logs/20261008T171843Z_MAT-20-step2.log). running_average(times, values, *, window=360.0) added to src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py (not exported from thermal/__init__.py); test tests/validation/test_mat20_running_average.py. Grid: M samples per period, switch times on the grid, MAT-17 case A periodic closed form at r = 0. - (B1) max |mean − D·θ_ss(0)| / (D·θ_ss(0)) over every window: k = 1: 5.96e-15 (M = 2¹²), 8.14e-15 (M = 2¹³); k = 2: 1.03e-14, 9.01e-15 — rounding level, no M-trend (the trapezoid kink terms cancel, as the brief argued). Bar 1e-12 unchanged. - (B2) W = 360 s (1228.8 / 2457.6 samples — fractional): brentq root of θ(t) = θ(t − W) on the falling side 779.999309 s; t_max 779.882812 s (offset −0.398 sample, M = 2¹²) and 780.029297 s (+0.205 sample, M = 2¹³). - (Wc) asserted: W = kP + P/2 misses by 1.957e-3 (k = 1) and 1.174e-3 (k = 2), inside the drafted O(ripple) ceiling (3.9e-3 / 2.3e-3). - (Pc) printed: a window one sample short moves t_max by 0 (M = 2¹²) and −1 sample (M = 2¹³) — within one sample, as the half-sample prediction implies. - A linear ramp (fractional W = 360, 120π, 100 s; 87 samples) is reproduced to ≤ 1.2e-15; the 2-D (DG0-shaped) call equals the column-wise calls exactly. - (B3) not executed (ruling 319-3): it awaits the weekly. MAT-20 stays 🟡.

Not claimed: a limit value, a compliance statement, tissue, perfusion. State 2026-10-08: step 1 landed — cem43 exact on the piecewise-linear interpolant matches the three ramps to ≤ 6.3e-16 and MAT-9's re-based step response to 8.98e-12 at N = 2¹⁸ (rate 2.000), the R swap misses by ≥ 0.194 (20261008T171434Z_MAT-20-step1.log, smoke, 12 s). Step 2 closed-form half landed 2026-10-08 (item 319): running_average (exact on the interpolant, fractional windows) gives the integer-period mean = D × θ_ss(0) to ≤ 1.03e-14 for W = P, 2P at M = 2¹² / 2¹³ per period, the W = 360 s maximum within 0.40 sample of the brentq root (779.9993 s), the kP + P/2 control misses by ≥ 1.17e-3 (20261008T171843Z_MAT-20-step2.log, smoke, 19 s, step 1 re-run green). docs.title: §9 item 370 — 2026-10-11 (chain P19 — MAT-20 step 2's FEM clause; chain step (solve))
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-11 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain P19 ("Chain P — Phase 8, gel first", the 2026-10-10 weekly), a weekly-enumerated step (§9 rule (4)). This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, Done-when or target. D_BAND, L_BAND and the step-2 controls are imported by name.

Weekly ruling being executed (2026-10-10 weekly, §10 P19), with the drafter's finding. The weekly wrote: "ruling 319-3, ratified tonight as written: running_average on MAT-17 step 3's FEM history reproduces its Duhamel sum at D_BAND, the shifted-window control misses ⇒ MAT-20 ✅. Smoke, no solve." The "smoke, no solve" half cannot be executed as written. The FEM history is not stored anywhere: - logs/ on the host has no MAT-17 or mat20 JSON / npz (checked 2026-10-11). - _run_duty (tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py:107) snapshots only SNAPS = steps 32, 35, 36, 39, 40 (:73). The ten Heaviside runs keep only their end state (:167–175). - The W1 log prints end-time ⟨θ⟩(t*) per H_m to 13 significant figures and the duty ⟨θ⟩ at n = 32 / 36 / 40 to 9 decimals (20261006T201547Z_MAT-17-step3-W1.log:1960–1974). That is three samples of the duty history, and no 360 s window fits in three samples. Ruling 319-3's measured print ceiling (≈ 8.8e-10) stands against D_BAND = 1e-13.

Ruling 319-3, as written, names exactly one route to the clause: option (a), a re-run of the step-3 fixture with the per-step series kept, under the anchor "the operator's window mean of the duty series equals Σ(−1)^m of the operator applied to the H_m series, at D_BAND; that identity is linearity" (MAT-20.md, item 319 question 3). This brief executes option (a) and re-tiers the item honestly: heavy, -n 2, one window ≈ 4–5 min. It needs the §7 row amendment given under "Status it can move" (rule (j)). If the review will not amend the row, the item is "write the anchor" for the 10-12 weekly and is not queued.

MAT-20 step 2, FEM clause — the six-minute operator on MAT-17 step 3's per-step history. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: heavy, -n 2 (the step-3 record's width), complex build. Class: chain step (solve). - Cost: M measured / ≈ 40 predicted min (15 fixed + 12 code + one window ≈ 4–5 min + one re-run ≈ 5 + spare). - Depends on: nothing open. - Gitignored inputs: none. The fixture is MAT-15 step 1's mesh, built in-run.

Code. One new module, tests/validation/test_mat20_fem_history.py: @complex_only, one module-scoped fixture, no knob (the MAT-17 step 3 module's precedent). There is no src/ change and no edit to any existing module. - Imports only. - From tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py: _transient_s (:86, it already takes snapshot_steps=), _chi_duty (:76), _heaviside (:81), N_SWITCH, HALF, DT, STEPS_PER_HALF, D_BAND, L_BAND (:64–71). - From tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py: _run_heated (:180), T_INF, N_MAIN, T_STAR. - From tests/validation/test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py: _allsum, _say. - From src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py: running_average, which is unexported, so the import is direct. - Fixture body. 1. base = _run_heated(return_fields=True). Take sub, ft, v_sub and q0 = base["q_h"][0]. 2. steps = tuple(range(N_MAIN + 1)). Run the duty schedule _transient_s(sub, ft, q0, _chi_duty, snapshot_steps=steps) and the ten _transient_s(sub, ft, q0, _heaviside(m), snapshot_steps=steps). 3. At every snapshot, reduce ⟨θ⟩ₙ = ∫(Tₙ − T_INF)/V_sub. Drop each run's snapshots once its series is taken (memory). 4. Times are tₙ = n·DT. Snapshot 1 lands after the two Rannacher half-steps, so the grid is uniform (transient.py:125–126). - Persist (rank 0): write logs/mat20/mat17s3-series-n2.json (gitignored, .gitignore:82). It holds times, the duty series, the ten H_m series, DT, HALF, N_SWITCH, and the rank count. P20 does not need it, but a later example (mat:18) can then avoid this solve.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported). - (H0) The series obeys Duhamel before any averaging: max over n of |⟨θ_duty⟩ₙ − Σ_m (−1)^m ⟨θ_Hm⟩ₙ| / maxₙ|⟨θ_duty⟩ₙ| ≤ L_BAND (1e-12), MAT-17 step 3's own (Δ) band. - Backed on the same fixture: (Δ) read 3.421e-14 in whole-submesh L2 at t* (…MAT-17-step3-W1.log:1970). - Predicted ≤ 5e-14. - (FEM) The six-minute operator reproduces the Duhamel sum (the row's clause): with W = 360.0, a = running_average(t, duty, window=W)[0] and b = Σ_m (−1)^m running_average(t, H_m, window=W)[0], max over valid entries of |a − b| / max|a| ≤ D_BAND (1e-13). - The operator is linear in values on a fixed grid, so this is (H0) carried through the operator, plus rounding. - W / DT = 11.48 samples, so the fractional-segment path is exercised. - Predicted ≤ 5e-14. The margin is ≈ 2–3×, which is thinner than the other anchors (see Negative result). - (FEM-2d) The same identity through the operator's 2-D call: an (n_t, 11) array of [duty, H_0 … H_9], with the signed column sum taken afterwards, also ≤ D_BAND. Step 2 showed the 2-D call equals the column-wise calls exactly (item 319 outcome).

Negative control (rule (e); the Done-when's "shifted-window control misses"). - (Wc-FEM) Compare a at tᵢ with the Duhamel sum b at tᵢ₋₄, a shift of P/2 = STEPS_PER_HALF samples (item 319's half-period (Wc) analogue). - The miss is asserted only > D_BAND, the row's form. - The factor is predicted, printed: ≈ 1e-2–1e-1 relative. The duty ⟨θ⟩ moves 0.466 → 0.584 K over one on-phase (…:1974), and a 360 s mean shifted by 125 s moves by a comparable fraction. - No same-fixture prior exists. - (Dc) Printed only: b with the m = 9 term dropped, the windowed analogue of MAT-17's (Δ-ctl), which read 0.298 at t* (:1971).

Printed records. - The reproduction of the step-3 log's end-time records, which shows this is "MAT-17 step 3's history": - ⟨θ_Hm⟩(t*) for m = 0 … 9 against :1960–1969; - the duty ⟨θ⟩ at n = 32 / 36 / 40 against :1974 (0.466250330 / 0.584438780 / 0.568835514 K).

Predicted equal at the printed digits (same code, same width). Printed, not asserted. A mismatch beyond the last printed digit stops the item, and it is reported. - t_max and the maximum six-minute mean of the duty series. - The maximum six-minute mean of H_0 (P1 alone, rising throughout; t_max predicted at t*).

Window. Foreground; the harness call is the whole Bash command, bare, repo-relative; Bash timeout: 660000; -s; tests/environment first. - First: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. - W1 (heavy, -n 2, complex): - Predicted harness 230–300 s. The prior run was 20261006T201547Z_MAT-17-step3-W1.log, 276 s, with the whole step-3 module. Serial on nothing. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, Done-when or target. Template: item 380 above (step 3, P20) — this is the same operator pair on the same fixture's series at the degree-2 root.

Why MAT-20 and not MAT-15. The step applies MAT-20's operators through step 3's module pattern (its helpers are imported); the data is MAT-15 step 6's (entry 42). Item 380 filed the degree-1 twin here, so the degree-2 twin is step 4 of this chunk; the MAT-15 row gains a pointer (below).

The input and its provenance (checked on the host 2026-10-20 03:00). - logs/mat15_s5/theta-series-ccw-d2.json (gitignored; 4 500 bytes, mtime 2026-10-19 02:09) — written by xl entry 42 (docs/testing/xl-pending.md § 42; docs/testing/xl-ledger.md row 2026-10-19), docs/testing/logs/20261019T070008Z_MAT-15-step6-P22-d2root.log:6887–6929 (MAT15s5 SERIES block; :6929 "wrote logs/mat15_s5/theta-series-ccw-d2.json (rank 0)"). Code: one new module, tests/validation/test_mat20_tuned_heating_dose_d2.py (numpy only; prefix [MAT-20 s4]). Edit no landed module (not step 3's, not MAT-15 step 5's). - Imports: cem43, running_average (src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py:45, :108); BAR as DOSE_BAR (1e-10, tests/validation/test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py:35); BAR as AVG_BAR (1e-12, tests/validation/test_mat20_running_average.py:34) and W_B2 (360.0, :36); from step 3's module tests/validation/test_mat20_tuned_heating_dose.py: SERIES_JSON (the degree-1 path, :47), R_BELOW, T_REF (:48–49), _quad_dose (:78–89), _rect (:92–93). Step 3 asserted them on the 10 g ball-mean series; the weekly's −1.27 % is the volume-mean series (entry 42's "ball-mean θ(t*)" is the phantom volume mean — label trap below), so both are asserted here, at the same bars (an execution choice; the review may strike the volume-mean rows to printed). Predicted: t_mx = t* = 1 254 s on both (both series rise monotonically, entry-42 log :6888–6928); (iii) ≤ 1e-15 (step 3: 3.245e-16).

Traps already paid for. - Label trap — "ball-mean". Print the JSON key beside every figure. - Label trap — per P_src. docs.title: §9 item 638 — 2026-10-25 (§10 lane 1, R3: MAT-16's kink and expm1 readings against MAT-20's cem43)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-25 10:30 daily review from the 10-24 weekly's lane-1 entry R3 ("optional: MAT-16's (K) kink and expm1 reading against MAT-20's implementation, printed"). The weekly wrote "printed"; this brief adds no band — every assertion below is MAT-20's own DOSE_BAR, imported.

Question. MAT-16's draft (never opened; docs/planning/chunks/MAT-16.md) named two hazards of a CEM43 integrator: the 43 °C kink, and cancellation in (exp(x) − 1)/x at small slope. MAT-20 landed cem43 without a test at either: no test sits at a ramp of half-width ε ≪ 1 K across 43 °C, none at a near-zero slope, and none on a constant segment (the _phi x == 0 branch). Does cem43 hold DOSE_BAR there?

Facts (read 2026-10-25). - src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py: _phi(x) = expm1(x)/x, 1.0 at exactly x == 0.0 (:32–37); _piece(t_a, t_b, dur, ln_r, t_ref) = dur·exp(ln_r·(t_ref − t_a))·_phi(−ln_r·(t_b − t_a)) (:40–42); cem43(times, temps, *, r_above=0.5, r_below=0.25, t_ref=43.0) (:45), output in the units of times. Crossing is strict, (T0 − 43)(T1 − 43) < 0 (:89); a non-crossing segment's side is 0.5(T0 + T1) >= 43 (:96). - tests/validation/test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py: BAR = 1e-10 (:35, imported elsewhere as DOSE_BAR); _side / ramp_dose (:50–60) is the raw difference quotient (r^(43−ta) − r^(43−tb)) / (b·ln r) — itself the naive form MAT-16 warned of, accurate at ε = 1e-3 (cancellation ≈ 1e-13) but not at ε ≈ 1e-9.

Route. New module tests/validation/test_mat20_kink_expm1.py, numpy + math only, real build, prefix [MAT-20 R3]. Import cem43 (dose.py:45), BAR as DOSE_BAR and ramp_dose from the closed-form module (helpers, never a test_* name). No src/ edit, no edit to any landed module.

Anchors (asserted at DOSE_BAR, imported). - (K) the kink at ε = 1e-3. cem43([0, τ], [43 − ε, 43 + ε]) against ramp_dose(43 − ε, 43 + ε, τ) (the split two-piece closed form) ≤ DOSE_BAR, τ = 600 s; and the same on the descending ramp. Printed beside it: mean = dose/τ, its miss from MAT-16's 1 − (ln 2/4)ε, and the predicted remainder 5(ln 2)²ε²/12 ≈ 2.0e-7 (this review's expansion, not asserted — MAT-16's 1e-6 bar is not adopted). - (E) the small-slope limit. On one non-crossing segment T₀ = 41 → T₀ + δ over Δt = 600 s, δ ∈ {1e-6, 1e-9, 6e-10}: cem43 against the second-order Taylor form Δt·R^(43 − T₀)·(1 + x/2 + x²/6), x = −δ·ln R (truncation ≈ x³/24 < 1e-27) ≤ DOSE_BAR; the same at T₀ = 45 (R = 0.5). - (Z) the constant segment. cem43([0, Δt], [T, T]) = Δt·R^(43 − T) at T = 41 and 45, ≤ DOSE_BAR (the x == 0 branch). - MAT-20 step 1's module re-run unedited in the same window (its A1 / A2 / R-swap assertions stay green).

Controls (rule (e)). - (Kc) R swapped, predicted, printed: cem43(…, r_above=0.25, r_below=0.5) on the ε-ramp moves the mean by ≈ +(ln 2/2)ε ≈ 3.5e-4 relative. Printed beside the measured miss; not asserted (no prior measurement on this fixture). - (Ec) the naive quotient, predicted, printed: ramp_dose(T₀, T₀ + δ, Δt) against the Taylor form at δ = 6e-10 — predicted ≈ 2e-7 relative (stdlib arithmetic, ≈ 2.3e-7 at Δt = 600 s), i.e. ≈ 2 000× DOSE_BAR. Printed with the ratio; if it does not miss, say so — that would mean the trap is not live on this platform, a finding. - The asserted, backed control is step 1's test_rc_r_swap_misses (re-run, unedited).

Window (bare harness call, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000). One smoke window, -n 1, real build, no mpiexec: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-20-R3-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py tests/validation/test_mat20_kink_expm1.py -v -s --tb=short'" (the smoke rule: only test_complex_mode.py from tests/environment). No FFCx form compiles, so no cache sweep is owed.

Tier: smoke, -n 1. Class: lane-1 revalidation. Cost: ≈ 7.4 measured / 20 predicted slot-minutes. Executor: implementer. Depends on: nothing. Family: R3, attempt 1 of 4.

Traps. Inputs are absolute °C, not θ. Do not import from thermal/__init__.py's exports for anything but cem43's module path. _piece / _phi are private: call cem43 only (the test is of the public function). Write ≈, never a tilde, in the journal. Never pipe the pytest call.

Scope boundary. A numerical-hazard read of one post-processor. Not claimed: Arrhenius damage, any threshold, any biological or regulatory statement, MAT-16's other draft items (C3 exponential, C4 trapezoid convergence — cem43 is exact per linear piece, so they do not apply).

A negative result means: a red (K), (E) or (Z) is a defect in cem43 at that input: stop, report the measured miss, park the module on attempt/*, add a known-issues entry naming the input; never loosen DOSE_BAR.

Status it can move. §10 R3 → DONE. The MAT-20 row's state line gains "R3: the 43 °C kink at ε = 1e-3, the small-slope limit and the constant segment at DOSE_BAR (§9 item 638)". MAT-16.md gains a one-line closing note that its (K) and expm1 hazards were read against MAT-20. MAT-20 stays ✅.

Outcome (2026-10-25, 15:00 CDT slot, DONE). tests/validation/test_mat20_kink_expm1.py; window 20261025T200112Z_MAT-20-R3-W1.log (smoke, -n 1, real, 14 s harness-wall, 12.69 s pytest; 21 passed, 3 skipped — the complex-mode environment tests on the real build; step 1's module re-run unedited, test_rc_r_swap_misses green). (K) rise / fall rel 2.255e-14 / 2.274e-14 against ramp_dose (bar 1e-10); mean 0.999826913345066, its miss from 1 − (ln 2/4)ε = 2.0014e-7 against the predicted remainder 5(ln 2)²ε²/12 = 2.0019e-7. (E) at δ = 1e-6 / 1e-9 / 6e-10, T₀ = 41 and 45: rel 0, 0 / 1.895e-16, 0 / 1.895e-16, 0 against the Taylor form (truncation ≤ 1.1e-19). (Z) rel 0.000e+00 at T = 41 and 45. (Kc) predicted, printed: the R swap moves the mean by +3.466337e-4 against the predicted +3.465736e-4 (ratio 1.000173), both directions. (Ec) predicted, printed: the naive quotient misses the Taylor form at δ = 6e-10 by 2.218e-9 at T₀ = 41 (22× DOSE_BAR; predicted ≈ 2e-7 — the miss is ≈ 100× smaller than predicted, a rounding-luck matter of where 41 + 6e-10 lands) and 2.645e-7 at T₀ = 45 (2 645× the bar); cem43 itself misses by ≤ 1.9e-16 at both. Finding: the trap is live on this platform at both T₀, but the T₀ = 41 magnitude was over-predicted by ≈ 100×. No defect in cem43.

docs.title: MAT-21 — history
docs.text:
Opened 2026-10-12 by the 18:00 daily review under §9 rule (5) lane 3 (Phases 7/8), for tonight's weekly to ratify. Phase 8 (8a) is the closed-form lane (MAT-9 … MAT-20), and MAT-15 step 2 checked the finite Robin cylinder against its eigen-series. §10 (8e) names an ASTM-style gel phantom, and PROJECT_PLAN.md line 4814 gives the F2182 phantom as 650 × 420 × 90 mm. That phantom is a rectangular box, and the lane has no box. MAT-21 is the box version of MAT-15 step 2: the same gel, Robin walls and a uniform source, solved as a triple eigen-series and then by P1 FEM on a structured create_box mesh.

Source. Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids: the rectangular parallelepiped by product solutions of three slab problems. The book is not held in-repo. docs/references/ holds Jin's FEM in Electromagnetics (jin-fem-3e/, which has no heat conduction), the birdcage-tuning literature, human body models and the dolfinx-0.11 migration notes. As with MAT-15 (analytical.py:1950, "Carslaw & Jaeger ch. III / VIII style; derived here, not pinned to a textbook equation"), the citation is a pointer and no chapter or equation number is claimed. The docstring derives every identity the test asserts. The in-repo cross-checks are the real test: - Robin residuals on all six faces; - the Gauss balance ∮hθ dA = qV, in its truncated-identity form; - a second route that is exact in z; - Duhamel; - the large-lateral limit, which must reach the 1-D slab closed form q(C² − z²)/(2k) + qC/h; - cube permutation symmetry; - transient → steady at long t; - the initial slope dθ/dt|₀ = q/ρc in the interior.

Its pieces are already in-repo. robin_slab_eigenvalues and _robin_slab_coefficients (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:1874–1940) were checked by MAT-15 step 2(a) at Bi_z 0.667 (20261001T143248Z_MAT-15-step2a-W1b.log:85–86).

Fixture numbers (stdlib-only Python arithmetic for this brief, not a harness run; every value below is predicted). - Half-widths A = 0.325, B = 0.21, C = 0.045 m (650 × 420 × 90 mm halved). V = 8ABC = 0.02457 m³; surface area A_s = 0.7386 m². - Gel constants as in MAT-15: k 0.6, ρc 4.18e6, h 10, q 2000, T∞ = T(0) = 20. - Biot numbers hL/k: Bi_x = 5.4167, Bi_y = 3.5000, Bi_z = 0.7500. First roots γ₁ = 1.330018 / 1.232272 / 0.771359. - Time scales: α = k/ρc = 1.4354e-7 m²/s; t_C = C²ρc/k = 14 107.5 s. Slowest mode: Λ₁₁₁ = 345.005 m⁻², τ₁ = 1/(αΛ₁₁₁) = 20 193 s. - Steady centre θ_ss(0): - 12.003947 K at n = (40, 40, 40); - 12.003956 K at (60, 60, 60); - 12.003958 K by the z-reduced route at (160, 160); - the slab limit is 12.375 K, so lateral cooling takes off ≈ 3.0 %. - Steady values elsewhere: corner (A, B, C) 2.5526 K; face centres x / y / z 6.1505 / 6.2367 / 8.7340 K; mean surface θ = qV/(hA_s) = 6.6531 K. - Transient centre: θ(0, 0.2 t_C) = 1.335705 K, against qt/ρc = 1.35 K; θ(0, t_C) = 5.511718 K.

docs.title: §9 item 406 — 2026-10-12 (lane 3, closed form)
docs.text:
MAT-21 step 0: the rectangular gel box with Robin walls under a uniform source, as a triple eigen-series in numpy only. - Executor and tier: implementer; smoke, no MPI, real build. - Change: src/ additive, plus one new test. - Time: ≈ 12 measured / 40 predicted min (≈ 2 min of windows + 15 fixed + ≈ 23 code). - Depends on nothing.

  • Anchor (derive in the docstring). θ = T − T∞ on the box |x| ≤ A, |y| ≤ B, |z| ≤ C, with −k∂ₙθ = hθ on all six faces and a uniform q.
  • 1-D pieces. For each axis d with half-width L_d and Bi_d = hL_d/k: γ_{d,n} are the roots of γ sin γ = Bi_d cos γ, and X_{d,n}(s) = cos(γ_{d,n} s/L_d). Each X_{d,n} satisfies the Robin condition at s = ±L_d. C_{d,n} = 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) is the projection of 1 (_robin_slab_coefficients).
  • Expansion of 1. The product basis X_l(x)Y_m(y)Z_n(z) is orthogonal on the box, so 1 = Σ C_l C_m C_n X_l Y_m Z_n.
  • Steady state. ∇²(XYZ) = −Λ·XYZ with Λ_lmn = (γ_l/A)² + (γ_m/B)² + (γ_n/C)². Hence θ_ss = (q/k) Σ C_l C_m C_n X_l Y_m Z_n / Λ_lmn.
  • Transient with a uniform start θ₀ = t_init − T∞: θ(t) = Σ C_l C_m C_n X Y Z [(q/(kΛ))·(−expm1(−αΛt)) + θ₀ e^{−αΛt}], α = k/ρc. From θ₀ = 0 this is the task's form θ_ss × (1 − e^{−αΛt}) term by term.
  • Truncated identities. The truncated sum satisfies two identities exactly.
    • Gauss: h∮θ_N dA = qV·Π_d S_d(N_d), where S_d = Σ_{n ≤ N_d} C_{d,n} sin γ_{d,n}/γ_{d,n}. This is Parseval: h∮θ_N = −k∫∇²θ_N = q∫P_N 1.
    • Duhamel: θ(t) = (q/ρc)∫₀ᵗ U_x U_y U_z ds, where U_d(s, ·) = Σ C_{d,n} X_{d,n} e^{−α(γ_{d,n}/L_d)² s}, at the same truncation.
  • Code. Append to src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py directly after robin_finite_cylinder_transient_temperature (ends ≈ line 2034), under a new MAT-21 step 0 banner and before the MAT-17 step 1 banner (≈ line 2037). The change is additive and reorders nothing.
  • robin_box_steady_temperature(x, y, z, *, half_widths, k, q, h, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), roots=None, return_gradient=False). It returns T, or (T, (∂ₓT, ∂ᵧT, ∂_zT)) when return_gradient is set.
  • robin_box_transient_temperature(x, y, z, t, *, half_widths, k, q, h, rho_c, t_inf=0.0, t_init=None, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), roots=None, return_gradient=False). The default t_init is T∞.
  • roots is a 3-tuple of None or an array per axis, for the negative control only. An overridden axis takes its length from the array, and C is the same projection formula at those roots (as radial_roots works for the cylinder).
  • Both functions share one private contraction, _robin_box_sum(W, x, y, z, …). It is separable and done in BLAS, never as a 3-index einsum over points. Form R = X(P × N_x) @ W.reshape(N_x, N_y·N_z), then multiply by Y and reduce over m, then dot with Z.
  • The function chunks internally so that the (P × N_y·N_z) intermediate stays ≤ 2²² doubles (32 MiB). Every caller (step 1's P2 interpolation included) is safe without chunking of its own.
  • Steady and transient use the same truncated term set, so t → ∞ returns θ_ss to round-off.
  • Constants: test module tests/validation/test_mat21_box_closed_form.py, which imports K, RHO_C, H, Q and T_INF from tests/validation/test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py. Do not restate them.
  • Module constants:
    • A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX = 0.325, 0.21, 0.045, with a comment citing PROJECT_PLAN.md:4814 (650 × 420 × 90 mm, halved);
    • HALF;
    • T_C = C_BOX**2 * RHO_C / K;
    • FOS = (0.05, 0.2, 1.0);
    • SERIES_TERMS = (40, 40, 40).
  • Anchors (asserted). Each bar is either a closed-form identity at round-off or MAT-15 step 2(a)'s pre-registered bar of the same form, as written in test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py: (R0) roots and coefficients at :95–97, (R1) Robin residual at :116, (R5) limits at :229–231.
  • (R0) Roots and coefficients.
    • For Bi ∈ {Bi_x, Bi_y, Bi_z}, 400 roots, each in ((n − 1)π, (n − ½)π). Residual |γ sin γ − Bi cos γ|/γ ≤ 1e-12.
    • C in the two closed forms, 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) and 2Bi cos γ(γ² + Bi²)/(γ²(γ² + Bi² + Bi)). They must agree to ≤ 1e-12 in the series norm max|ΔC|/max|C|. The per-root relative difference is printed only: see Traps.
  • (R1) Robin residuals on all six faces.
    • Sample points: a 7 × 7 grid over [−0.95, 0.95] of the two tangential half-widths on each face.
    • Analytic gradients; |−k∂ₙθ − hθ|/(qC) ≤ 1e-10.
    • Run for steady and for transient at t = Fo·t_C, Fo ∈ FOS.
  • (R2) A second route that is exact in z. Write a test-local function for the z-reduced double series:
    • θ = (q/k) Σ_{l,m} C_l C_m X_l Y_m g_lm(z)/μ², with μ² = (γ_l/A)² + (γ_m/B)²;
    • g = 1 − h cosh(μz)/(kμ sinh μC + h cosh μC), the 1-D Robin solve in z for each (l, m);
    • form the cosh ratio as e^{μ(|z| − C)}(1 + e^{−2μ|z|})/[(kμ/h)(1 − e^{−2μC}) + 1 + e^{−2μC}], which cannot overflow.
    • Compare it with the triple series at the same (N_x, N_y) = (40, 40) and N_z = 200, at five points: (0, 0, 0), (0.5A, 0.5B, 0.5C), (0.9A, 0.9B, 0.9C), (0.9A, 0, 0) and (0, 0, 0.95C). Bar: |Δ|/θ_ss(0) ≤ 1e-7. Predicted ≲ 1e-9: the z-tail beyond 200 terms is a stdlib estimate.
    • Printed only: the default (40, 40, 40) against the reduced route at (160, 160). Predicted 8.5e-7 at the centre and 2.4e-6·θ_ss(0) at (0.9A, 0.9B, 0.9C); this is the comparand truncation step 1 inherits.
  • (R3) Gauss, truncated identity.
    • Compute h∮θ_N dA at n = SERIES_TERMS with 128 × 128 Gauss–Legendre nodes per face, all six faces (γ_40 ≈ 125 needs more than 70 nodes).
    • Assert |h∮θ_N/(qV) − Π_d S_d(40)| ≤ 1e-10. Predicted ≤ 1e-13.
    • Printed: the truncation deficit 1 − ΠS_d, predicted 4.671e-6 at 40 and 1.368e-6 at 60 (S-deficits at 60: 9.52e-7 / 3.98e-7 / 1.83e-8).
  • (R4) Duhamel.
    • Series at SERIES_TERMS against (q/ρc)∫₀ᵗ U_x U_y U_z ds, with U_d at the same truncation. Use MAT-15's quadrature: 80 log-spaced intervals from 1e-10·t, 16 Gauss–Legendre nodes each, as in test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py:172–183.
    • Points (0, 0, 0), (0.5A, 0.5B, 0.5C), (0.9A, 0.8B, 0.8C); Fo ∈ FOS.
    • Bar: max|Δ|/θ_ss(0) ≤ 1e-10. Predicted ≤ 1e-13. MAT-15 measured 3.536e-14 on its analogue, …143248Z…W1b.log:112.
  • (R4s) Initial slope.
    • (q/ρc)·Π_d U_d(s) at the centre, s = 0.01·t_C, n = (200, 200, 60): |ΠU_d − 1| ≤ 1e-9. Predicted 4.4e-14.
    • At (0.5A, 0.5B, 0.5C) the same product reads 1 − 1.05e-5. Print it: it is the z-faces' physical cooling at 22.5 mm depth, not a defect.
    • Printed only: the centred time-FD slope of robin_box_transient_temperature itself at that t (δ = 1e-2·t, n = (200, 200, 60)), over q/ρc. Predicted within 1e-8 of 1.
  • (R5) Limits.
    • (a) t = 100·t_C equals the steady function at the same n to ≤ 1e-12 relative. Predicted 0, since e^{−69.9} underflows the slowest mode.
    • (b) Large-lateral limit: A = B = 20C, n = (400, 400, 60), at z ∈ {0, 0.5C, 0.9C} on x = y = 0. |θ/θ_slab − 1| ≤ 1e-6, where θ_slab = q(C² − z²)/(2k) + qC/h. That is MAT-15 step 2(a)'s limit bar, :230–231.
    • (b) is predicted at 4.0e-7 (stdlib arithmetic: 3.98e-7 / 3.94e-7 at z = 0 / 0.9C). At (200, 200, 60) it reads 4.4e-7, and at A = B = 40C with (200, 200, 60) 3.4e-7. The margin is 2.5×; see Negative result.
  • (R6) Cube permutation.
    • A = B = C = 0.045 m, so Bi = 0.75 on every axis. Take the six permutations of p = (0.2, 0.5, 0.8)·C.
    • Steady and at Fo 0.2: max spread/θ(0) ≤ 1e-12. Predicted ≤ 1e-14.
    • This catches an axis or half-width swap.
  • Printed (predicted above).
  • γ₁ per axis.
  • θ_ss(0) at n = 40 / 60 / 120 per axis: 12.003947 / 12.003956 / —, against the reduced route's 12.003958 and the slab 12.375 K.
  • The corner and the three face centres.
  • qV/(hA_s) = 6.6531 K beside the face-quadrature mean of θ.
  • θ(0, t*) = 1.335705 K and θ(0, t_C) = 5.511718 K.
  • τ₁ = 20 193 s.
  • The centre FD Laplacian residual |k∇²θ_N + q|/q, predicted 1e-4 to 1e-3: the truncated triple series does not solve the PDE pointwise (Traps). Printed, never asserted.
  • Negative control (rule (e): predicted, computed here by stdlib arithmetic, printed beside the measured value; only the separation is asserted). Dirichlet z-roots: roots=(None, None, (np.arange(1, 41) - 0.5) * np.pi).
  • (R1-ctl): the z = ±C face residual/(qC) is predicted 0.95–1.0. On those faces θ = 0, so the residual is the escaping flux, which is ≈ qC for the slab. Assert > 1e-3. The four lateral faces stay at round-off: printed.
  • (R4-ctl): the series with Dirichlet z against the Robin Duhamel route, max|Δ|/θ_ss(0) over the (R4) grid. Predicted 0.235, reached at Fo 1; it reads 0.203 / 0.235 / 0.227 at the three points. Assert > 1e-3.
  • Printed: the steady Dirichlet-z centre 3.3735 K against qC²/(2k) = 3.375 K.
  • Ceiling: neither control saturates (a residual and an L∞ miss), and both sit at least 200× above their 1e-3 floors.
  • Windows (smoke, real build, no mpiexec: IMP-6 step 0's pattern; MAT-15 2(a) ran its numpy module at -n 2, which this item does not need).

  • W1 (predicted 5–20 s; the largest arrays are 128² face points × 64 000 terms per face, and the (400, 400, 60) limit tensor of 77 MB):

    scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step0-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_mat21_box_closed_form.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W1r (standard; the rule (c) re-gate of the additive analytical.py change beside MAT-15's functions; measured 49 s for the same two files at -n 2 with full tests/environment, 20261001T143248Z_MAT-15-step2a-W1b.log):

    scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step0-W1r "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 120 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/unit/test_analytical_lightweight.py tests/validation/test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py -s -v --tb=short'" - If W1 is killed at 30 s, it is not a result. Split it into two windows by node ID: (R0)–(R3) + (R6), then (R4)–(R5) + control. Never raise the ceiling. - Traps already paid for. - Per-root relative C is unmeetable at 1e-12. At large n, sin γ ≈ Bi/γ is computed from γ ≈ nπ with absolute error ≈ eps·γ. MAT-15 2(a)'s first W1 read 2.65e-10 per root (20261001T143051Z_MAT-15-step2a-W1.log, the norm disclosure at test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py:84–89). Assert in the series norm from the start. - No FD-Laplacian anchor. MAT-15 2(a)'s (R2) is not transferable. There θ_ss was θ_slab + ΣD I₀ cos, which solves the PDE exactly term by term. Here k∇²θ_N + q = q(1 − Π_d P_N 1) pointwise, which converges like the alternating tail of C_n (≈ Bi/γ_N²). The PDE is carried by (R3) and (R4), which converge as N⁻³ or are exact identities. (R2)'s FD δ-ratio lesson (1e-3·a to 1e-2·a, round-off of a long sum) is moot for that reason. - Chunk inside the function, and contract by BLAS. MAT-15 2(b)'s (points × 200 × 200) einsum in 1 000-point chunks cost 95.1 s + 86.1 s of one window and overran item 145 (20261002T034149Z_MAT-15-step2b-W3-transient.log). Item 407 inherits whatever this function costs. - Never evaluate at t = 0 with θ₀ ≠ 0. Use −expm1 term by term, so that θ(t) from θ₀ = 0 has no cancellation at small t. - The cosh ratio in (R2) overflows if formed directly at μC ≈ 30 (the reduced route at (160, 160) reaches μC ≈ 100). Use the scaled form above. - Smoke hygiene. The real build skips the four complex-only environment tests, which is expected; FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX stays unset. The smoke path carries only tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py (10:30 ruling, item 364). - Foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; -s; append to analytical.py, never reorder; no edit after the last window (rule (i)). - Scope. Covered: the closed form only, for a uniform q with Robin walls on every face, one h and one gel. Not covered: step 1's FEM, a non-uniform (SAR) source, perfusion, a container wall (MAT-18 did one for the sphere), the phantom's fit inside any coil ((8e)'s fixture question, the operator's; dashboard W5), any external check. - Status it can move. §7 MAT-21 ⬜ → 🟡 ("step 0 ⇒ 🟡 (records)" in the row; the review inserts the row in the same commit that queues this item, rule (j)). The records registered are θ_ss(0) and θ(0, t*) at SERIES_TERMS. - Negative result. - (R1) red with (R4) and (R3) green: a gradient sign or a half-width mix-up. Fix it in-slot. - (R3) red: the face quadrature or the S_d formula. Check the GL node count before anything else. - (R4) red: the contraction (the axis order in the reshape). - (R6) red: an axis or half-width swap. - (R5b) red inside [1e-6, 1e-5] with everything else green: print the sequence at (200, 200, 60) / (400, 400, 60) / (800, 800, 60). A value that falls with N is x/y truncation, and one that holds steady is the lateral term. Do not change n or A/C in-slot (rules (f), (h)). Record it, park on attempt/* and mark BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)); the review rules. Item 407 stays unqueued. - Any other red that survives one in-slot fix: park, BLOCKED.

Spawn line: "Use the implementer agent to execute MAT-21 §9 item 406 (then 407 if 406 commits before minute 30), per docs/planning/chunks/MAT-21.md (read the latest Review ruling paragraph first, if one exists). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Run every window in the foreground with timeout: 660000, pytest with -s, container timeout -k 30. The src/ change is additive (rule (c)): W1r re-gates it in the same slot."

W1 20261013T004329Z_MAT-21-step0-W1.log Status 0, 5 s, 11 passed / 3 skipped (complex-only env); W1r 20261013T004342Z_MAT-21-step0-W1r.log Status 0, 7 s, 14 passed. Asserted: (R0) root residual ≤ 1.70e-13, C forms ≤ 3.7e-16; (R1) ≤ 7.1e-16 steady and ≤ 3.9e-16 at every Fo; (R2) 7.009e-12; (R3) 5.218e-15; (R4) 2.960e-16; (R4s) 4.363e-14; (R5a) 0; (R5b) 3.985e-7 / 3.965e-7 / 3.945e-7 (bar 1e-6); (R6) 6.5e-16 / 1.7e-15; controls R1-ctl 4.991e-1, R4-ctl 2.350e-1 (> 1e-3). Printed as predicted: γ₁, Λ₁₁₁, τ₁ 20193 s, 1 − ΠS_d 4.6708e-6 / 1.3683e-6, face mean 6.6531 K, θ_ss(0) 12.003947 / 12.003956 / 12.003957 K (40 / 60 / 120), corner 2.5524 K, FD Laplacian residual 6.18e-4. Off prediction (printed only, no status effect): θ(0, t*) 1.335697 K and θ(0, t_C) 5.511710 K against predicted 1.335705 / 5.511718 (≈ 8e-6 K low, the size of the 40-term truncation — the prediction was likely at more terms, unverified); R1-ctl 0.499 against predicted 0.95–1.0 — the control is sampled at Fo 0.2, where the Dirichlet-face flux has reached only about half of the developed qC (still ≈ 500× above its floor). docs.title: §9 item 407 — 2026-10-12 (lane 3, closed form; depends on item 406)
docs.text:
MAT-21 step 1: P1 FEM on a structured dolfinx.mesh.create_box mesh of the gel box, compared with item 406's series, steady and transient. - Executor and tier: implementer; heavy, -n 2, complex build. That is the build MAT-15 2(b) ran its thermal FEM on. The thermal solvers are real-valued (steady.py:27) and only need their forms to compile in complex mode (transient.py:36). - Change: test only, no src/ change. - Time: ≈ 17 measured / 60 predicted min (≈ 6 min of windows + 15 fixed + ≈ 39 code). - Depends on 406. Skip this item if 406 did not land.

  • Mesh ladder, stated first.
  • create_box(comm, [np.array([-A, -B, -C]), np.array([A, B, C])], [13m, 8m, 2m], cell_type=dmesh.CellType.tetrahedron), following the pattern at tests/validation/test_poynting_balance.py:71–75. Each hexahedron splits into 6 tetrahedra, so there are 6·N_x·N_y·N_z cells.
  • How N_z is chosen. The box is thin in z, so the three counts are set in the ratio 13 : 8 : 2. Cells are then 50/m × 52.5/m × 45/m mm, aspect ≤ 1.17, rather than a uniform N that would leave the z direction 7× under-resolved. N_z = 2m puts 2m cells across the 90 mm thickness.

docs.text: (Q1) The opening. MAT-21 is opened under §9 rule (5) lane 3 as Phase 8 (8a)'s closed-form lane on the F2182-sized box (PROJECT_PLAN §10 (8e) note, 650 × 420 × 90 mm), the same move MAT-15 step 2 made for the cylinder. Its comparand is the triple Robin eigen-series (Carslaw & Jaeger's product solution, not held in docs/references/: a pointer only), built from the in-repo slab pieces MAT-15 step 2(a) already verified; the in-repo checks are the test. It does not answer (8e)'s fixture question (dashboard W5), which stays the operator's. The §7 row goes in with this commit; the weekly ratifies or reverts. (Q3) Thin margins stay as written: the slab limit (bar 1e-6, predicted 4.0e-7) and the finest interior (band 1e-2, predicted 2.8e-3, worst case ≈ 8.4e-3) are pre-registered gates; a red parks with the reading, and no band moves (rule (f) is the review's to apply). (Q4) 407 depends on 406 landing in the same or an earlier slot; if 406 parks, 407 is skipped and stays queued. Say so in the journal. docs.title: §9 item 424 — 2026-10-13 (§10 chain P26; chain step, solve; depends on item 423)
docs.text:
MAT-21 step 2: the box under MAT-17 step 3's duty cycle, read through MAT-20's operators. The closed form is the triple series' Duhamel sum over the ten switch runs, and the FEM reproduces it on P25's finest rung (m = 6). - Licence. §10 P26 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4734–4738): "closed form (the triple series' Duhamel sum over the ten switch-on runs) and the FEM reproduction on P25's finest rung at D_BAND / L_BAND; the six-minute maximum's position and the dose per W printed". This brief sets no band. D_BAND, L_BAND, INTERIOR_BAND, E_BAND are imported by name, and the closed-form bars copy item 406's literals. - Executor and tier: implementer; W1 smoke (numpy, real build, no mpiexec, item 406's pattern); W2 and W3 heavy, -n 2, complex. - Change: two new test modules, tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_closed_form.py (W1) and tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py (W2, W3). No src/ change. Step 0's and step 1's modules are not edited (rule (i)). - Time: ≈ 12 measured / 70 predicted min (≈ 12.5 min of windows: sweep ≈ 2 if needed, W1 ≈ 0.5, W2 ≈ 4.6, W3 ≈ 5.3; + 15 fixed + ≈ 40 code for two modules). - Depends on item 423. Skip this item if item 423 did not land: W2 and W3 import step 1's helpers from the landed module, and the rung is P25's.

  • The schedule (MAT-17 step 3's shape, re-timed to the box).
  • t* = 0.2·t_C = 2 821.5 s (step 1's T_STAR); N = 40 CN steps, DT_BOX = t*/40 = 70.5375 s; two BE start-up half-steps (step 1's (T) call, branch :245–248).
  • Period P = t*/5 = 564.3 s, D = 0.5, half-period HALF_T = 4·DT_BOX = 282.15 s. χ = 1 on [jP, jP + P/2), 0 otherwise. The switches are t_m = m·HALF_T, m = 0 … 9 (even m on, odd m off), and every switch is a grid point, so every (half-)step midpoint χ is exactly 0 or 1.
  • Shape constants imported from tests/validation/test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py:68–71: STEPS_PER_HALF (4), N_SWITCH (10), DUTY (0.5); N_MAIN (40) from test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:88.
  • Write _chi_box(t) and _heav_box(m) test-locally on HALF_T in _chi_duty / _heaviside's form (:76–83). See Traps: the originals bind MAT-15's t* = 1 254 s.
  • The W1 module stays dolfinx-free. It pins N_STEPS, STEPS_PER_HALF, N_SWITCH, DUTY = 40, 4, 10, 0.5 locally, with a comment citing those lines. W2's first test asserts the pins equal the imported originals and T_STAR == 0.2 * T_C ((P0′), the analogue of step 1's (P0)).
  • Anchor 1 — the closed form (W1, numpy, smoke).
  • _duty_cf(x, y, z, t) = Σ_{m: t > t_m} (−1)^m θ_step(x, y, z, t − t_m), where θ_step is robin_box_transient_temperature from rest (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:2148) at SERIES_TERMS, t_inf=0. This is the ten-run Duhamel sum P26 names.
  • _box_mean_step(t) = (q/k)·Σ_lmn Π_d(C_d s_d)·(−expm1(−αΛ_lmn t))/Λ_lmn, with s_d = sin γ/γ (the mean of cos(γs/L) over [−L, L]) and γ, C from step 0's _axis_data (test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:61). _box_mean_duty(t) = Σ(−1)^m _box_mean_step(t − t_m). It is the exact volume mean of the truncated series.
  • (C1) Duhamel with χ, asserted ≤ 1e-10·θ_ss(0) (item 406's (R4) bar, test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:247).
    • _duty_cf against (q/ρc)·Σ_on-intervals ∫ ΠU_d(τ) dτ over the lag τ = t − s. Each on-interval [t_{2j}, t_{2j+1}] ∩ [0, t] maps to τ ∈ [max(0, t − t_{2j+1}), t − t_{2j}]. Use step 0's _uprod (:212) and its quadrature (:204–209): 16 Gauss–Legendre nodes on each of 80 intervals, log-spaced from 1e-10·τ_hi when τ_lo = 0 and geometric between τ_lo and τ_hi otherwise.
    • Points: step 0's R4_PTS (:221). Times: 8.5·HALF_T (mid last on-phase), 9·HALF_T = t₉ (end of the last on-phase), t*.
    • Predicted ≤ 1e-13 (step 0's (R4) measured 2.960e-16).
  • (C2) Mean route, asserted ≤ 1e-10·θ_ss(0) (same literal). _box_mean_step(t) against (q/ρc)∫₀ᵗ Π_d ū_d(τ) dτ with ū_d = Σ C s e^{−α(γ/L)²τ}, step 0's quadrature, at Fo ∈ FOS. Predicted ≤ 1e-13. This validates the helper W2 prints against, and the printed records below.
  • (C1-ctl), asserted only as a miss > 1e-10·θ_ss(0) (rule (e), predicted): _duty_cf with m = 9 dropped against the full Duhamel quadrature at t*. Predicted ≈ 1.12e-2·θ_ss(0) at the centre (θ_step(HALF_T) = 0.1350 K / 12.004 K, stdlib arithmetic at 30 terms per axis while drafting), smaller at (0.9A, 0.8B, 0.8C). Ceiling: does not saturate, ≈ 1e8× above the bar.
  • Printed records (W1; predicted by stdlib arithmetic at 30 terms per axis, ±2e-5 K).
    • Duty centre θ at n = 32 / 36 / 40: 0.53622 / 0.66914 / 0.66654 K; volume mean 0.49931 / 0.62470 / 0.61419 K; the step response at t* 1.33568 / 1.23889 K beside them.
    • The six-minute maximum and its position. running_average(t, v, window=360.0) (src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py:108) on the duty history sampled at 64 points per half-period (641 samples). Sample θ_step once on the grid and shift it by 64·m samples, since the switches are grid points. Predicted: the window mean is monotone on [W, t*] (no interior local maximum at 32 samples per half-period or on the 41-step grid), so t_max = t* = 2 821.5 s, with value 0.61684 K (mean) / 0.66420 K (centre). The box is far from periodic (τ₁ = 20 193 s ≫ t*), so this is a from-rest record and there is no MAT-20 (B2) brentq phase to assert.
    • Dose per W. "Per W" means per W of the on-phase deposited power qV = 49.14 W, i.e. the history θ/(qV) (MAT-20 step 3's per-watt convention); per W of the time-averaged D·qV is printed beside it (× 1/D). Predicted six-minute peak per W 1.2553e-2 (mean) / 1.3516e-2 (centre) K/W. cem43 (dose.py:45) of T∞ + θ/(qV) ≈ 4.05e-11 s per W (both); at the fixture's q, 6.7e-11 / 6.9e-11 s. Printed as a record, not a safety statement.
  • Anchor 2 — the FEM reproduction (W2, heavy), on P25's m = 6 rung (step 1's _rung(6, clk), branch :146; 269 568 cells, 50 323 P1 dofs).
  • Runs, each CN N = 40 with two start-up half-steps and snapshot_steps = range(41): the duty run (_chi_box); ten Heaviside runs H_m (_heav_box(m)); χ ≡ 1 (lambda t: 1.0); and the unscheduled default call. That is 13 runs. After each run, reduce every step to ⟨θ⟩ₙ = ∫(T − T∞)/V_h through _allsum, then res.snapshots.clear() (MAT-20's _series, test_mat20_fem_history.py:60–67). Keep only each run's final field.
  • (S0) schedule census: Σχₙ Δtₙ = D·t* = 1 410.75 s ≤ 1e-12 relative, via _census imported from test_mat17_duty_cycle_fem.py:105 (it asserts at that literal). Print the schedule string.
  • (Δ) Duhamel on fields: θ_duty − T∞ = Σ(−1)^m (θ_Hm − T∞) at t*, whole-box _rel ≤ L_BAND (1e-12, test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py:64). Build the signed sum as one numpy-summed P1 Function. Predicted ≤ 1e-13 (MAT-17 step 3 measured 3.421e-14 on its fixture, 20261006T201547Z_MAT-17-step3-W1.log:1970; a different fixture, so this is context, not backing).
  • (D′) duty one is the default: _rel(θ[χ≡1] − T∞, θ_default − T∞) ≤ D_BAND (1e-13, :65). Predicted ≤ 5e-15 (MAT-17 step 3: 2.119e-15, …:1959).
  • (H0) Duhamel on the per-step series: maxₙ|⟨θ_duty⟩ₙ − Σ(−1)^m⟨θ_Hm⟩ₙ| / maxₙ|⟨θ_duty⟩ₙ| ≤ L_BAND. Predicted ≤ 1e-13 (MAT-20: 5.689e-14).
  • (FEM) the six-minute operator: with W = 360 s (5.104 samples, 35 valid windows from n = 6), a = running_average(t, duty), b = Σ(−1)^m running_average(t, H_m). Assert max|a − b|/max|a| ≤ D_BAND, and the same through the 2-D call ((FEM-2d)). Port MAT-20's _identities (test_mat20_fem_history.py:124–150) locally; it is a plain function. Predicted ≤ 5e-14 (MAT-20 measured 3.434e-14 on the coil fixture).
  • (E) every run's max_balance_residual ≤ E_BAND. Predicted ≤ 1e-11 (step 1's worst was 8.485e-12).
  • Printed:
    • the FEM ⟨θ_duty⟩ₙ beside _box_mean_duty(t_n) at every step, with the max relative difference (predicted 1e-4 to 3e-3; not asserted);
    • the FEM six-minute maximum and t_max (predicted t* and ≈ 0.6168 K);
    • cem43 per W of qV on the FEM mean series beside W1's closed-form figure;
    • phase clocks per run (step 1's _Clock), max |Im θ| (predicted 0).
  • Anchor 3 — the FEM against the closed form (W3, heavy), the physics gate.
  • (T-duty) the duty run at t* on m = 6 against _duty_cf interpolated into P2 (step 1's _exact, branch :92, with a callable that sums the ten shifted series calls per chunk); interior _rel with step 1's _interior_chi ≤ INTERIOR_BAND (1e-2, test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere.py:64).
  • Predicted 5e-4 to 3e-3: step 1's (T) read 9.072e-4 on this rung; MAT-17 step 2's duty interior read 4.39e-4 / 1.07e-3 on the ball. That is a cross-fixture analogy, not backing.
  • Whole-box L2 and θ_h(0) (predicted ≈ 0.6665 K) printed.
  • Negative controls (rule (e): every factor predicted by stdlib arithmetic while drafting; only the separations are asserted).
  • (Δ-ctl), W2: m = 9 dropped from the field sum at t*. Predicted miss 0.20–0.22 (H₉(t*)/duty = 0.218 on the mean, 0.202 at the centre), range 0.18–0.26. Asserted only > L_BAND. Ceiling: an L2 miss that does not saturate, ≈ 2e11× the band.
  • (Wc-FEM), W2: a(tᵢ) against b(tᵢ₋₄), a P/2 shift over 31 windows. Predicted 0.141 (the closed-form mean sampled on the FEM grid), range 0.10–0.18. Asserted only > D_BAND. MAT-20's analogue read 1.326e-1 on another fixture (context).
  • (c3), W3: the comparand replaced by the unscheduled step response at t* (one robin_box_transient_temperature call). This is what a solver that ignored source_schedule would match. Predicted interior miss 0.50 (1 − duty/step = 0.504 mean, 0.501 centre), range 0.45–0.55. Asserted only > INTERIOR_BAND; ≈ 50× the floor, no saturation.
  • Windows. W1 is smoke; W2 and W3 are complex, -n 2, tests/environment first, node IDs only, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000, container timeout -k 30. Two heavy windows never run at once.
  • Price:
    • pytest start-up plus complex tests/environment ≈ 95 s (item 407's W2: 162.9 s total less the 67.4 s fixture, 20261013T005149Z_MAT-21-step1-W2-transient.log:99, :172);
    • m = 6 build and steady 5.3 s (:87–88);
    • CN N = 40 at m = 6 13.3 s (:90), so 13 runs ≈ 173 s;
    • one P2 series interpolation at t* 18.0 s (:91), so ten ≈ 180 s;
    • per-step reductions are negligible (MAT-20's 451 reductions and 11 transients took 28.2 s, 20261011T172810Z_MAT-20-step2-fem-W1.log:1956).
  • So W1 ≈ 5–15 s, W2 ≈ 275 s (220–330), W3 ≈ 315 s (250–380), each under the 590 s container ceiling with ≥ 1.5× margin. W2 and W3 are separate windows so that neither carries both the 13 solves and the ten interpolations (≈ 470 s together).

  • First (skip it if item 423 swept in this slot and no window has been killed since): docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0, then

    scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step2-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - W1, closed form (smoke, real build, no mpiexec; only test_complex_mode.py from tests/environment):

    scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step2-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_closed_form.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W2, FEM identities:

    scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step2-W2-identities "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_precondition_schedule_shape tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_s0_schedule_census tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_delta_duhamel_fields tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_d_prime_duty_one_is_default tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_h0_series_duhamel tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_fem_six_minute_operator tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_e_every_run_balances tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_control_delta_m9_dropped_misses tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_control_wc_shifted_window_misses -s -v --tb=short'" - W3, FEM against the closed form (after W2 returns):

    scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step2-W3-closed-form "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_t_duty_interior_against_closed_form tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py::test_control_c3_step_response_misses -s -v --tb=short'" - Use two module-scoped fixtures, runs (W2) and duty_cf (W3), so that no W3 node triggers W2's 13 solves. If the module names its nodes differently, use the actual IDs and say so in the journal. If W1 is killed at 30 s, it is not a result: split it by node ID, never raise the ceiling. - Traps already paid for. - The schedule import trap (new, found while drafting). test_mat17_duty_cycle_coil_driven.py's HALF, DT, _chi_duty, _heaviside and _transient_s are bound to MAT-15's t* = 0.2·6 270 = 1 254 s (DT 31.35 s, test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:86–87), not the box's 2 821.5 s. Importing them gives a silently wrong schedule, and HALF would also shadow step 0's half-width tuple HALF (test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:35). Import only STEPS_PER_HALF, N_SWITCH, DUTY, L_BAND, D_BAND. (S0) catches a mistimed schedule. - The W1 module must not import dolfinx (directly or through a test module): the smoke window is 30 s on the real build. Step 0's module and thermal/dose.py are numpy-only; test_mat17_* and step 1's module are not. - source_multipliers are per (half-)step: two half-steps of DT/2 and then 39 full steps. _census weights them; a plain sum of χ is wrong. - Snapshot memory: 13 runs × 41 snapshots × 50 323 complex dofs is ≈ 430 MB if all are kept. Reduce and clear() per run, keeping only final fields. - The (∞)-style argument form: _rel(msh, A − T_INF, B − T_INF), never _rel(msh, A − B, …) (item 160's trap, test_mat15_finite_cylinder_fem.py:297). - Complex build: np.real before every float; running_average / cem43 raise on a non-zero imaginary part, so pass np.real series; masks in numpy; no UFL < or sqrt comparison. - Rank-local values: assemble_scalar, local min/max and size_local go through _allsum / allreduce. The series and operators run on the reduced (rank-identical) arrays; printing goes through _say on rank 0. - Orphan .c (any stem without .so): sweep only when pgrep -c python3 reads 0. - Harness hygiene: bare whole-command harness calls, repo-relative; -s; foreground; -k 30; never pipe pytest. Status 124 is a finding: pgrep -c python3 first, never lengthen the timeout. - Scope. Covered: one 50 % duty, P = t*/5 schedule from rest on the uniform-source box, P1 on one rung (m = 6), CN N = 40, gel constants, Robin h 10, and MAT-20's two operators read on it. Not covered: - a periodic steady state (τ₁ ≫ t*), any pulse sequence, an SAR or coil-driven source; - a regulatory, compliance or safety statement (the dose and the six-minute peak are records); - perfusion, a container wall, degree 2, a rung ladder or time-step convergence; - ANS-9 or any external check, and the (8e) fixture question (the operator's). - Status it can move. Here a = running_average(t, duty) and b = Σ(−1)^m running_average(t, H_m), as at test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py:115–121 on the branch. - running_average is linear in its input series (src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py:108–174). Drafted for the 2026-10-15 18:00 review. Rule (6): chain P's second provisional step since the 10-14 weekly (cap three). P33 (MAT-15 step 7, the ASTM box heated by F-clinical's SAR) is serial on C6. P34 (item 481) found that the DG0 hand-off leaves a residual after the amplitude correction a_h: (S1-dg0a) 1.179001e-4, ≈ 3.4× P32's P2 error. Its journal hypothesis (attempts.md 2026-10-15T20:07Z) is that this residual is the DG0 staircase's higher-mode content, and that a P2-interpolated source would remove it. P35 tests that hypothesis directly. No new target is set and no band moves.

Choice, and why. - Chosen: candidate (i), reduced to a source-path decomposition on m = 4. The same mesh carries three sources: the UFL source (P32), the DG0 cell average (P34) and the P2 nodal interpolant (new). Each is read against P32's series at imported bands. The result decides which hand-off form P33 should give its coil SAR. P34's journal named the P2 source as the remedy, so the decision needs this measurement before P33 is written. - Rejected: (ii), the h-rate. At P2, m = 8 is beyond the slot (m = 6 alone is 380 725 dofs and 9.9 GiB, item 455). There is also no imported rate for a source-hand-off error to assert against, so a rate would be print-only. - Rejected: (iii), the 3D cosine source. It needs (80, 80, 80) comparand terms, ≈ 4× the P3 interpolation memory of SEP_TERMS, with no measured price. It also changes two variables at once. - Dropped from (i): the "exact discrete" comparand. This would be the series of the DG0 source the mesh actually delivers. It is not exact on create_box: the per-tet averages of cos(πx/A) differ within one hex (under a Kuhn split, the tet centroids sit at x offsets h/4, h/2 and 3h/4), so the delivered source is not a function of x alone. The 10:30 ruling also left the split unverified. A separable staircase series would therefore carry an O(h²) intra-hex term (drafting estimate ≈ 1e-5 to 4e-5) of the same size as P2's error. It is out of scope.

  1. What. Add one new module, tests/validation/test_mat21_box_p2_source_fem.py, prefix MAT21-8, with a local _Clock8 copied from _Clock7. Edit nothing in src/ or in any landed module, and leave analytical.py alone. The P2 interpolant's amplitude needs no new closed form: the series at profile (1, −a, 1) is already landed and was checked by P32's (Q1). The amplitude itself, a_p, is printed only.

    scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step8-W2-p2-source "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_mat21_box_p2_source_fem.py -s -v --tb=short'" - Price ≈ 150 s, range [125, 220] s. The basis is P34's measured clocks (log :67–89; window 125.9 s, fixture 123.1 s): - P34's fixture: 123.1 s; - minus the DG0 CN (31.4 s) and the two transient interpolations (23.9 s); - plus the P2 interpolation and a_p (≈ 1 s), the P2-source steady solve (≈ 11 s, as the DG0 one), its readings (≈ 2 s), the CN (≈ 31 s) and ex_t (≈ 12 s); - plus 10–30 s of JIT for the forms with a P2 coefficient. - The slot. ≈ 35 predicted min (≈ 20 code, ≈ 3 window, sweep and journal). The lane-3 measured median is 9, and P34 committed at minute ≈ 8. - If killed, the review re-prices at -n 4, never in-slot. 7. Traps already paid for. - Complex build: - np.real before every float; - no UFL comparison, max_value, conditional or sqrt (OPS-22, WF-6 4c); - the interpolation lambda is numpy, and the cast into a complex Function is implicit. - Rank safety: - _allsum for every assemble_scalar (including a_p); - owned cells only for a_h, as P34 did, because the DG0 array carries ghosts; - size_global for (Pdeg); - evaluate_vector_field_parallel (via _point_vals) for point values. - Readings: every reading goes through _rel_p (degree 6) against a P3 comparand at SEP_TERMS. The uniform comparands stay at SERIES_TERMS, because (U) reproduces step 3 through them. - Keep the profile a full period (MAT-21.md:1140–1141). Do not put metadata on the source or on the cell average, because (S7) must reproduce P34's path exactly. - No dg0_m4 / sep_m4 import. Pytest would otherwise run those fixtures inside this window and break the price. - Harness hygiene: - the harness call is the bare whole command; - never pipe pytest; - on status 124, run pgrep -c python3 first; - no edit after the window starts (rule (i)). 8. Scope. - Covered: one analytic source handed to the thermal solvers three ways (UFL, DG0 cell average, P2 nodal interpolant), on m = 4 at P2, steady, plus CN to t* for the P2 source. - Not covered: - coil or EM SAR (P33 / C6); - whether a coil SAR can be P2-interpolated on the thermal mesh (P33's design choice, informed by this record); - the exact series of the delivered DG0 source (see "Dropped" above); - a rate in h, other rungs, degree 1, DG1 / DG2 projections; - non-matching EM / thermal meshes, perfusion, a container wall, any external check. - No coil, no EM. 9. Negative result. There is no PREDICTED RED: line; every assertion is predicted green. Any red: report the measurement and stop. Park the work on attempt/* and mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit. - (U), (S6) or (S7) red: a determinism finding (item 423 precedent). The review rules. - (c-ord) red with (S1-p2s) green: the hypothesis is refuted. The residual is not the DG0 source's representability: it is either a P2-FEM effect shared by the non-UFL sources, or a gap in the a_h account. Record both readings in this file. The review re-poses; the staircase series is the candidate, with the intra-hex term named. - (S1-p2s) or (T-p2s) > INTERIOR_BAND: a finding on the Function-source path. Write a known-issues entry. No band moves. - (S2-p2s) or (E-p2s) red: read source_power / (Q·V_h) − 1 first. - At the same level, the periodic node-lattice argument failed (for example on the diagonal edges): this is the source's quadrature, not the scheme. - At round-off, it is a scheme finding. - A control inside its band: a mislabelled comparand. - Killed at 590 s: pgrep -c python3 first, then report the last MAT21-8 clock. 10. Status it can move. - The MAT-21 glyph stays ✅. Rule (j), licensed by the queuing review: the slot appends one record clause to the §7 state line ("P35: P2-interpolated source of P32's profile within INTERIOR_BAND, (S1-p2s) … < (S1-dg0a) …; the DG0 residual is the source's representability") and changes nothing else in the row. - A red (c-ord) leaves P33 without a remedy for the DG0 residual. docs.title: §9 item 497 — 2026-10-16 (§10 chain P36, daily — provisional; lane 3 closed form)
docs.text:
Drafted for the 2026-10-16 10:30 review. Rule (6): chain P's third and last provisional step since the 10-14 weekly (P34, P35, P36 — the cap). P33 (MAT-15 step 7, the ASTM box heated by F-clinical's SAR) is serial on C6, and chain C is parked (GEO-38 item 485 BLOCKED). P32 called itself "the first step toward C6's thermal half (a prescribed non-uniform source in the ASTM box)"; P34 / P35 settled the hand-off form. P36 is the source-shape half: the transverse profile a body coil's quasi-static field deposits in a long phantom, in closed form and at P2. No new target and no band moves: the anchors are step 1's INTERIOR_BAND, S2_GAUSS_BAND and E_BAND, imported from the gate modules, against a closed form, exactly as P32 / P34 / P35 used them.

MAT-21 step 9: the gel box under the transverse quadratic source

q(x, y, z) = 3Q·(y² + z²)/(B² + C²) = Q·[w_y (y/B)² + w_z (z/C)²], with w_y = 3B²/(B² + C²) = 2.868293 and w_z = 3C²/(B² + C²) = 0.131707.

The source is uniform along the 650 mm axis x and quadratic in the two transverse axes. It is the sum of two separable sources. It is checked in numpy (W1), then solved by P2 FEM on step 3's m = 4 rung, steady and CN to t* (W2). This is a record; the glyph stays ✅.

Why this source (physics, stated once; nothing here is asserted). - Orientation. In the F2182 placement the 650 mm axis lies along the bore: GEO-38 step 2 puts MAT-21's x on the coil axis, y (420 mm) horizontal and z (90 mm) vertical (GEO-38.md:354). So the transverse pair is MAT-21's (y, z), and B₁ rotates in the y–z plane. - The long-prism limit is exact. Take an infinitely long prism along x in a uniform B = (0, B_y, B_z)e^{jωt}, quasi-static (low induction number, displacement current neglected). Then E = E_x(y, z) x̂ with E_x = jω(B_z y − B_y z) solves Faraday's law exactly, for any cross-section: - ∇·E = 0 holds; - n·E = 0 holds on every side wall, because E is axial and the side-wall normals are transverse; - the axial constant vanishes, because the net axial current is zero on a symmetric section. - Under circular polarisation (B_z = ∓jB_y, |B_y| = B₁) the two terms are in quadrature, so |E_x|² = ω²B₁²(y² + z²). The SAR is ∝ y² + z² in absolute units. That fixes the weights at w_y : w_z = B² : C² once each term is written in (s/L)², so the 90 mm axis carries (C/B)² = 4.6 % of the y-term's power: 0.131707 / 3 = 4.39 % of the total. - Normalisation. The mean of (s/L)² is 1/3, and w_y + w_z = 3. So the mean source is exactly Q, ∫q dV = QV = 49.14 W as in steps 1–8, and the Gauss comparand Q·V_h is unchanged. - Not claimed. This is the transverse shape of the long-body limit, not the box's own EM SAR. A 650 × 420 mm box is not long. Near x = ±A the axial current must turn (n·J = 0 at the end faces), and at 64 / 128 MHz the wavelength in gel is comparable to the box. No EM is solved.

Choice, and why (one paragraph). Two candidates were weighed. - Chosen: (a), the sum of the two transverse quadratics. It is the long-prism CP eddy SAR derived above, with its physical z-weight. Against P32 it introduces exactly one new ingredient: the projection of (s/L)² onto the Robin eigenfunctions. That ingredient is exercised on two axes of very different Biot number (y 3.50, z 0.75). The x axis keeps the landed C. Two further points favour it: - The source is a degree-2 polynomial, so both of the solvers' source integrals are exact on affine tets. The balance anchors therefore hold without P32's full-period crutch (MAT-21.md:1140–1141). - It is the first MAT-21 step whose source varies along y and z. P32's scope excluded "a y/z-varying profile" (MAT-21.md:1229). - Rejected: (b), the product Q·[1 − cos(πx/A)]·(transverse quadratic). It is still separable, but it changes two things at once. It also has no physical derivation: the long-body axial E falls toward the end faces, while P32's cosine rises there. Its only extra content is P32's landed x-coefficient multiplied in, which (c-src) on (a) does not need. - Is it assertable beyond P32? Yes, modestly; no band is needed. - A new closed-form projection E_n, checked against quadrature and against two reduced routes. Each route is independent of E on its own axis. - The FEM anchors under a two-axis transverse source. - A new discriminating control (c-z): the FEM against the series with the z² term dropped misses by ≈ 4.8 % (≈ 4.8× INTERIOR_BAND). So the record shows the solver resolves a 4.4 %-power term on the 90 mm axis. - It does not move a glyph. It is lane-3 supply for a drained queue, priced at P32's measured windows.

Licence. §10 chain P36, provisional under rule (6) (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3850–3860). This brief sets no band and moves none. - Bands, imported by name as step 8 imports them (test_mat21_box_p2_source_fem.py:32–43): - INTERIOR_BAND (1e-2, test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere.py:64); - S2_GAUSS_BAND (1e-9, test_mat15_finite_cylinder_fem.py:69); - E_BAND (1e-9, test_mat12_transient_sar_heating_sphere.py:76). - The W1 numpy bars are step 0's literals (test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:10–17), applied to the same identities as P32's W1 applied them.

Executor and tier: implementer. - W1 is standard: numpy only, the real build, no mpiexec. It carries rule (c)'s same-window re-gate of the landed analytic modules. - W2 is heavy, -n 2, in the complex build (FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1); every fixture-using node is @complex_only.

Change. - src/ (additive, rule (c)): three new functions in src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py. Insert them after robin_box_separable_transient_temperature (:2224–2237) and before the MAT-17 banner (:2240). No landed function is edited. - robin_slab_quadratic_coefficients(gamma) returns E_n, the projection of (s/L)² onto cos(γ_n s/L) on |s| ≤ L:

E_n = 2[sin γ + 2 cos γ/γ − 2 sin γ/γ²]/(γ + sin γ cos γ).

- Derivation: ∫_{−L}^{L}(s/L)² cos(γs/L) ds = 2L[sin γ/γ + 2 cos γ/γ² − 2 sin γ/γ³], divided by ∫cos² = L(γ + sin γ cos γ)/γ.
- This form is valid at any γ and has no division by sin γ.
- At a Robin root (cot γ = γ/Bi) it equals **C_n(1 + 2/Bi − 2/γ_n²)**. That identity is checked in W1, not used in the code.

  • robin_box_quadratic_steady_temperature(x, y, z, *, half_widths, k, q, h, weights, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), return_gradient=False).

    • The source is q·[w₀ + w_x(x/A)² + w_y(y/B)² + w_z(z/C)²], with weights = (w0, wx, wy, wz).
    • Build axes = _robin_box_axes(half_widths, k, h, n_terms, None), then the coefficient tensor in this order:
