    where axes_Ed is axes with axis d's C replaced by E. - Then W = (q / k) * T / _robin_box_lambda(axes) (the association of :2144), evaluated by _robin_box_eval unchanged. - At weights = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0) this is bitwise robin_box_steady_temperature, because 1.0 * c3 == c3 and c3 + (±0.0) == c3. - robin_box_quadratic_transient_temperature(x, y, z, t, *, half_widths, k, q, h, rho_c, weights, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), return_gradient=False). - It starts from θ₀ = 0, and computes W = T * ((q / (k * lam)) * (-np.expm1(-at))) (P32's :2236 order). - At unit weights it is bitwise robin_box_transient_temperature at t_init = t_inf. - The docstrings carry the derivation, the truncated Gauss identity h∮θ_N dA = qV[w₀ΠS_d + Σ_d w_d S″d Π{e≠d} S_e], with S″_d = Σ E_n sin γ_n/γ_n → 1/3, and Duhamel. Carslaw & Jaeger is cited as a pointer, as at :2122. - W1 module: new tests/validation/test_mat21_box_quadratic_closed_form.py, numpy only, with no dolfinx import. - It imports step 0's non-test names (HALF, A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX, K, H, Q, RHO_C, T_C, FOS, SERIES_TERMS, R2_PTS, R4_PTS, _face_residuals; test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:34–38, :87, :135, :221), and T_INF from test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form (as P32's W1 does). - It defines the module constants that W2 imports: - WEIGHTS = (0.0, 0.0, 3*B²/(B²+C²), 3*C²/(B²+C²)); - WEIGHTS_NOZ = (0.0, 0.0, WEIGHTS[2], 0.0); - UNIT = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0); - QUAD_TERMS = (80, 80, 40). - W2 module: new tests/validation/test_mat21_box_quadratic_fem.py, prefix MAT21-9, with a local _Clock9 copied from _Clock8. Edit no landed module. Its import surface: - From step 8's module (test_mat21_box_p2_source_fem.py:29–65): the same imports, plus B_BOX, C_BOX, HALF and SERIES_TERMS from step 0. - From step 6: M4, STEP3_M4 and _point_vals (test_mat21_box_separable_fem.py:57–58, :100). - From step 1: T_STAR, V_BOX, _interior_chi, _steady_ex and _trans_ex (test_mat21_box_fem.py:72–121). - From step 3: CMP_DEGREE, DEGREE, QDEG_P, _dofs_pred, _exact_p, _rel_p and _rung_p. - From W1: WEIGHTS, WEIGHTS_NOZ and QUAD_TERMS. - Never import a fixture (sep_m4, dg0_m4, p2s_m4, steady, transient, steady_p, transient_p, runs_p, duty_cf_p, steady_m6), any _Clock*, any test_* name, or step 1's _rel. - Time: ≈ 7.4 measured / 50 predicted min. - Windows ≈ 6 min: W1 ≤ 0.5, sweep ≤ 2.5 (the step 8 sweep read 134 s on a slow host), W2 ≈ 2.7. - Plus 15 fixed and ≈ 30 for code: ≈ 50 lines in src/ and two modules of ≈ 200 lines each. - Depends on nothing. Steps 0, 1, 3, 6 and 8 are on main, and every imported name exists at the line cited (checked while drafting).

The closed form (Anchor 1, W1). Drafting values come from stdlib Python with bisection roots and 64 × 16-point Gauss–Legendre. They reproduce step 0's uniform records (12.003947 K at the centre), which validates the drafting code. - Coefficients, first three per axis.

axis Bi γ C E x 5.4167 1.330018 / 4.068213 / 6.945535 1.243794 / −0.351594 / 0.165527 0.296788 / −0.438925 / 0.219782 y 3.5000 1.232272 / 3.876052 / 6.760880 1.220619 / −0.306479 / 0.128253 0.310445 / −0.440810 / 0.195929 z 0.7500 0.771359 / 3.361135 / 6.399844 1.096808 / −0.121881 / 0.035729 0.334851 / −0.425321 / 0.129260
  • S″ at 40 terms: 0.3333288835 / 0.3333311989 / 0.3333331044, against 1/3.
  • E_n ≈ C_n(1 + 2/Bi) as n → ∞. So the quadratic series converges at the uniform series' rate, but with a larger constant on the axis that carries it.
  • Comparand truncation (measured while drafting). The reference is the y-reduced route at (200, 200). Misses of the triple series:
  • (40, 40, 40) misses by up to 8.2e-5 K at 0.9(A, B, C);
  • (40, 80, 40) misses by up to 5.6e-5 K (x-limited);
  • (80, 80, 40) misses by ≤ 3.8e-6 K (≤ 3e-7 relative to 13.34 K);

So QUAD_TERMS = (80, 80, 40) for every FEM comparand of the quadratic source. Its Gauss floor 1 − Π is 1.2484e-6, against 9.5217e-6 at (40, 40, 40) and step 0's 4.6708e-6. - The reduced routes (independent of E on their own axis). - For the y-route, take each (l, n) in x and z with μ² = (γ_l/A)² + (γ_n/C)². Solve g″ − μ²g = −(Q C_l/k)[w_y C_n (y/B)² + w_z E_n] by g_p = α y² + β, with α = a/(B²μ²), β = (2α + b)/μ², a = Q C_l w_y C_n/k and b = Q C_l w_z E_n/k. - Add the scaled homogeneous term −(k g_p′(B) + h g_p(B)) e^{μ(|y|−B)}(1 + e^{−2μ|y|})/[kμ(1 − e^{−2μB}) + h(1 + e^{−2μB})] (step 0's _z_reduced form, test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:119–132). Then θ = Σ_ln C_l X_l Z_n g_ln(y). - The z-route is the same with y ↔ z. - Each route uses E only on the other transverse axis, so the pair checks both E's and the assembly. - Drafting values. - Steady at (80, 80, 40): θ(0) = 4.276700 K; θ(0, 0.9B, 0) = 13.337014 K; θ(0.9A, 0, 0) = 2.682231 K; θ(0.9A, 0.9B, 0.9C) = 8.585064 K. - Uniform at the first three points: 12.003947 / 8.074905 / 8.706255 K. - Transient at t* = 0.2 t_C (2 821.5 s), (80, 80, 40): θ(0) = 0.063466 K; θ(0, 0.9B, 0) = 2.892661 K; θ(0.9A, 0, 0) = 0.061875 K. - W1 asserts (numpy; bars copied from step 0 and P32). - (P0) |w_y + w_z − 3| ≤ 1e-15, which makes the source mean exactly Q. - (Q1) the anchor's own check. robin_slab_quadratic_coefficients against composite Gauss–Legendre (64 panels × 16 points on [−L, L]) of ∫(s/L)² X_n ds/∫X_n² ds, for n ≤ 80 on all three axes. Asserted: max|ΔE|/max|E| ≤ 1e-12 (R0's bar). Drafting read 4.2e-15 (worst, y axis). - (Q1b) The Robin-root identity E = C(1 + 2/Bi − 2/γ²) against the direct form, on the same roots: ≤ 1e-12. Do not run it at 80 terms, because 128 points under-resolve cos(γ₈₀ s/L) (P32's note). Predicted ≤ 1e-14. Print the floors at (40, 40, 40), QUAD_TERMS and step 0's uniform. - (Q5) the two reduced routes: - |triple(40, 200, 40) − y-reduced(40, 40)|/θef ≤e-7**, th drafting reading 2.489; - lzzwxh:1181triple(40, 40, 200) − z-reduced(40, 40)|/θef ≤ **1e- with draftinreading 1.46e1; both at R2TS, with θ_ref = maxklzxh:1183y-reduced| over R2TS = **8.5072 K. - **(Q6)uhamel: θ(t) = /ρc)∫₀ᵗ[w_y U_x U″_y U_z + w_z U_x U_y U″_z] ds, with U″_d = Σ E_n X_n e^{−α(γ_n/L_d)²s}. Use P32's time quadrature (_duhamel_sep, :207–212) at R4_PTS and every Fo in FOS: ≤ 1e-10·θef (R. Also t = 100 t = steady, relative ≤ **-12 (R5a). (Q-ctl) negave control (label predicted**; only the separation > 1e-3 is asserted): WEIGHTS_NOZ at (40, 200, 40) against the full y-reduced route at R2_PTS. It misses by 0.0516·θ_ref (drafting). Ceiling: the z² term's own share of θ, so ≈ 52× the 1e-3 bar is the most it can show. - Printed: γ, C, E (first three per axis) beside the table above, S″ per axis, the three floors, and the drafting θ values beside their predictions.

Code state. - Comparand: robin_box_quadratic_steady_temperature (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:2268–2288) with weights=WEIGHTS, n_terms=QUAD_TERMS = (80, 80, 40) (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_quadratic_closed_form.py:46–49) and t_inf=0. The reduced routes _y_reduced / _z_reduced (:189–220) are exact in y and in z respectively. - FEM: P36's quadratic steady solve, exactly as at tests/validation/test_mat21_box_quadratic_fem.py:141–145, on _rung_p(M4, …) (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_fem_p2.py:131–145). - Point route: - Use evaluate_vector_field_parallel(T, pts, owner="lowest_original_cell") (src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py:224–423), whose owner rule is point_owner_cells (:133–221). - The family's _point_vals (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_separable_fem.py:100–103) takes the legacy owner=None path (evaluation.py:379–388: the first colliding cell on each rank, and the last gathered rank wins). It returns θ = Re(value) − T_INF, with NaN where the point is invalid, together with the validity mask. It is module-level and not a test. - Fixture probe_m4 (module scope; every phase clocked with flush=True): 1. (U), exactly as at step 9 :124–138. 2. The quadratic steady solve, step 9 :141–145. 3. _probe_vals on the uniform and on the quadratic solution at PROBE_PTS + ADJ_PTS, then the legacy _point_vals on the same points, then point_owner_cells(msh, pts) once for the owner integers. 4. The series at the eight points, one vectorised call each: the quadratic at QUAD_TERMS; the no-z series (WEIGHTS_NOZ, SERIES_TERMS); the uniform series robin_box_steady_temperature at SERIES_TERMS; and the references _y_reduced(*p, 200, 200) / _z_reduced(*p, 200, 200). 5. If it is absent, pytest.fail("run W2a first; never recompute"). Print the file's mtime. 6. Print max |Im θ| and the fixture's elapsed time.

Anchors (asserted; imported bands only). - Preconditions: - (P0) K == K_GEL, H == H_GEL, RHO_C_0 == RHO_C (step 9 :215–216). - (Pdeg) 116 025 dofs on both solves (_dofs_pred(M4)), at both widths. - (V) all six PROBE_PTS are valid on the owner route, with owner integers ≥ 0, at both widths. P1–P5 lie on ∂Ω, which no owner-rule gate covers ("Flagged", below). - (U) At -n 2, the whole-box and interior errors match step 3's printed digits (STEP3_M4, test_mat21_box_separable_fem.py:58). e_p = |θ_h(p) − θ_N(p)| / |θ_N(p)| ≤ INTERIOR_BAND

INTERIOR_BAND is 1e-2 (test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere.py:64), MAT-9 (i)'s interior relative-L2 band (test_mat9_steady_conduction_sphere.py:10–11, :156). - Series values (drafting, stdlib, at (80, 80, 40); they reproduce P36's 4.276700 K):

| point | θ_N (K) |
|---|---|
| P0 | 4.276700 |
| P1 / P2 | 10.890636 |

| P5 | 3.127848 |

This is POST-8 3a's (G) (test_post8_step3a_averaged_row1.py:410–425).

Printed, not asserted. - Comparand truncation at each point: |triple(80, 80, 40) − y-route(200, 200)|, with the z-route beside it. - Drafting reads ≤ 1.1e-6 K at P0, P3 and P5. - It reads 3.3e-5 K (3.0e-6 relative) at P1 / P2, because the y-series converges slowest at the y wall; there the y-route gives 10.8906687 K and the z-route 10.8906667 K. - So the comparand floor at the walls sits ≈ 3 000× under the band. - The uniform FEM at the points, beside the uniform series and step 0's records: 12.003947 / 6.236654 (y face) / 6.150392 (x face) / 8.733966 (z face) K (MAT-21.md:23–27). - Legacy route minus owner route at each point. The diagonal split of create_box is not mirror-symmetric; predicted ≤ 1e-4. The series pairs are printed as np.array_equal, which should be True because cos is even. - ADJ_PTS: e_p and θ_h beside P36's printed 13.337975 / 2.682175 K. - The wall is not the box's hottest point: at steady state θ is 10.89 K at (0, B, 0) but 13.34 K at (0, 0.9B, 0), because the Robin wall cools. This is a reading for P39's "hot side wall".

Negative controls (rule (e): every factor is predicted, and only the separation is asserted). - (c-u-pt) The quadratic FEM against the uniform series, at each point, must exceed INTERIOR_BAND. - Predicted e: 0.644 (P0), 0.746 (P1–P2), 0.704 (P3–P4), 0.642 (P5), ± 5 %. - Ceiling ≈ 64× the band at P5. That is the closed forms' own difference, so a larger factor is unreachable. - (c-z-pt) The quadratic FEM against the no-z series (WEIGHTS_NOZ, SERIES_TERMS), at each point, must exceed INTERIOR_BAND. - Predicted 0.1189 (P0), 0.0214 (P1–P2), 0.1403 (P3–P4), 0.1401 (P5), ± 10 %. - Ceiling 2.1× the band at the ±y walls, where the z² term is 2 % of θ. Windows. Run each in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, pytest -s and container timeout -k 30 590, with tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py first. The harness call is the whole Bash command. - Before W2a: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Then sweep:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step10-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - W2a (-n 2, writes the npz; predicted 45–70 s, range [40, 150] s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-step10-W2b-points-n1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_mat21_box_probe_points_fem.py -s -v --tb=short'" - Price basis (P36's log :67–86): - build 0.2 s, uniform solve 10.8 s, ex_u + χ 8.2 s, (U) 0.3 s, quadratic solve 11.8 s; - the eight-point series ≲ 1 s, because there is no field interpolation of ex_q; the reduced routes ≲ 1 s; the three point calls ≲ 2 s; - no new form, so nothing compiles beyond P36's cache. - At -n 1 the two LU solves and ex_u run serial, ≈ 1.5–2× slower (MAT-19 measured 1.13× on a lighter fixture). - No module edit after W2a starts (rule (i)). An edit re-runs both windows.

Traps already paid for. - Complex build: np.real before every float; no UFL comparison, max_value, conditional or sqrt (OPS-22, WF-6 4c). - Rank safety: - _allsum for every assemble_scalar; size_global for (Pdeg). - Point values only through evaluate_vector_field_parallel, with a bitwise-identical point array on every rank (OPS-40 / OPS-55, evaluation.py:303–358). Build the points from module constants, never rank-local. - The owner keyword must be identical on every rank. - Only rank 0 writes the npz; every rank reads it. - The npz lives under the gitignored /workspace/logs/, never in docs/. Scope. Covered: the steady point values of one prescribed source at six named positions (five of them on the Robin walls), on m = 4 at P2, at two MPI widths. Not covered: - transient or duty point values (P38 / P39 read histories); - a rate in h, other rungs or degrees; - probe-volume averaging (that is MAT-19's); - an implant, or the F2182 standard's own probe protocol; - the box's EM SAR, any coil, any external check. No coil, no EM.

Negative result. There is no PREDICTED RED: line. Any red: report the measurement and stop. Park on attempt/MAT-21-step10-* and mark item 520 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). - (V) red (a wall point invalid or NaN): the owner route misses a ∂Ω point. Write a known-issues entry against POST-8, whose gates cover only interior, facet and interior-vertex points (tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py:9–12, :39–45; POST-10's "boundary" points are submesh-interface points, tests/post/test_submesh_owner_rule.py:39–50). Never nudge a point inward in-slot: that re-targets the step (rule (4)). - (Pt) red at a wall point with P0 green: a finding on the P2 Robin boundary nodes. Record e_p per point; the weekly reads it together with the flag below. No band moves. - (W) red: print the legacy and owner values and the owner integers at each width; it is a partition finding. - (W-c) red: the comparator is wrong. Stop. - (U) red: a determinism finding (the item 423 precedent). - A control inside its band: a mislabelled comparand. Stop. - Killed at 590 s: not a result. Run pgrep first, then report the last MAT21-10 clock.

On green, the slot makes one edit to the MAT-21 §7 state cell (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2619), licensed by the queuing review under rule (j): - "steps 2–9 (…)" becomes "steps 2–10 (…, P37)"; - "the six F2182 probe-point values (five on the walls) within INTERIOR_BAND, width-invariant at -n 1 / 2" is added to that sentence's list.

The full readings go into this file's Outcome. A (V) red moves a known-issues entry onto POST-8.

Flagged for the review (not changed here). The step applies INTERIOR_BAND "at every point", but five of the six named points lie on ∂Ω: - The band is MAT-9 (i)'s interior relative-L2 band. It was defined on cells with midpoint |x|² < 0.81R², to exclude the sphere's faceting error. - MAT-19's (T) has already applied the same 1 % pointwise (as P_BAND, test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:59), but only at interior probes. - Here the band is imported outside both its norm and its region. On create_box the faceting reason is absent and the ≈ 100× headroom makes a red unlikely, so the defect is the licence, not the risk. - The step's words ("mid-wall points", "end-wall mid-points", "top-face centre") do not allow reading the points as wall-adjacent. The ADJ_PTS prints give the weekly the interior alternative. - The weekly owns either ratifying INTERIOR_BAND as a pointwise band at ∂Ω points or naming another.

Write one new module, tests/validation/test_mat21_box_probe_points_fem.py (prefix MAT21-10), importing step 9's helpers and imports. Never import a fixture, a _Clock* or a test_* name. Run the sweep, W2a (-n 2) and W2b (-n 1) in that order, in the foreground with timeout: 660000, pytest -s and container timeout -k 30 590; run pgrep -c python3 first and require 0. You are the executor: do not spawn agents, and never background a window. On a red, park on attempt/MAT-21-step10-*, mark item 520 BLOCKED in the same commit, and report."

Outcome 2026-10-18 (11:00 UTC slot, second item): DONE, every asserted anchor and both controls green, first try. (P0) green. (Pdeg) 116 025 on both solves at both widths. (V) all six points valid on the owner route at both widths; owner integers 34782 / 39774 / 30103 / 34938 / 34636 / 74718. (U) 2.489307e-05 / 1.669359e-05 at -n 2 (asserted) and -n 1 (printed) — step 3's digits. (Pt), identical digits at both widths: P0 θ_h − θ_N −9.643e-5 K (θ_N 4.276700 K), e_p 2.255e-5; P1 / P2 −2.002e-4 K (θ_N 10.890636 K), 1.839e-5; P3 / P4 +8.092e-5 K (θ_N 1.822844 K), 4.439e-5; P5 +5.054e-4 K (θ_N 3.127848 K), 1.616e-4 (worst; inside the predicted ≤ 3e-4) — all against INTERIOR_BAND 1e-2, ≥ 62× headroom. θ_N equals the drafting table to every printed digit. docs.title: §9 item 524 — 2026-10-18 (§10 P38, MAT-21 step 11; lane 3, closed form)
docs.text:
Drafted read-only for the 2026-10-18 03:00 daily review.

Licence. §10 chain P38 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4817–4821), weekly-enumerated, queued under §9 rule (4). No band is set or moved. Templates: item 497 (P36) and items 424 / 439 / 451 (P26 / P29).

MAT-21 step 11: P36's source under MAT-17's χ. The closed form is the ten-run Duhamel sum of P36's quadratic step response. It is checked in numpy (W1), then read against P2 CN to t* on m = 4 (W2). - Executor: implementer. - Tier: - W1 standard (numpy, real build, no mpiexec); - W2 heavy (-n 2, complex). - Measured bases: - P36 W1: 16 s harness (20261016T171632Z_MAT-21-step9-W1-closed-form.log). - P36 W2: 126 s; its CN runs 31.7 s, ex_t + ex_ut 30.5 s (20261016T171904Z_MAT-21-step9-W2-quadratic-fem.log:81–82). - Step 4 W3 (scheduled P2 duty CN on m = 4): 31.5 s (20261014T184606Z_MAT-21-step4-W3-p2-closed-form.log:89–90). - Class: lane 3, a chain step with solves. Cost: ≈ 7.4 measured / ≈ 40 predicted slot-minutes (two modules ≈ 25, windows ≈ 6, journal ≈ 8). - Depends on: nothing. Steps 0, 2, 3, 4 and 9 are on main. - Family: step 11, attempt 1 of 4.

The schedule and the closed form. - The schedule is step 2's, unchanged. Its pins are N = 40, DT_BOX = t*/40, HALF_T = 4 DT_BOX, D = 0.5 and T_SW = m·HALF_T for m = 0 … 9 (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_closed_form.py:53–57). χ is _chi_box (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py:86–88). - The closed form is θ_duty(t) = Σ_{t > t_m} (−1)^m θ_q(t − t_m), where θ_q is robin_box_quadratic_transient_temperature (analytical.py:2291–2304). - It costs one series call, not ten. The time factor is linear, so the sum collapses onto one coefficient tensor: - axes, T = _robin_box_quadratic_tensor(HALF, K, H, n_terms, WEIGHTS) (analytical.py:2256–2265); - lam = _robin_box_lambda(axes) (:2105–2108); - F = Σ_m (-1.0)**m * (-np.expm1(-(ALPHA * lam * float(t - t_m)))) over t > t_m, accumulated in m order and starting from the m = 0 term; - W = T * ((Q / (K * lam)) * F), which is P36's association at :2303; - then _robin_box_eval(W, x, y, z, axes, 0.0, False) (:2092–2102).

These are three private helpers, imported by a test. There is no src/ edit. If the review prefers a public src/ function, it becomes a rule (c) addition with W1's re-gate, and the review re-poses the item. - Drafting values (stdlib, (80, 80, 40)). The ratio is θ_duty(t*) / θ_continuous(t*):

where θ_continuous(t*) (K) θ_duty(t*) (K) ratio centre 0.063466 0.034567 0.54466 (0, B, 0) 2.647811 1.285771 0.48560 (0, 0.9B, 0) 2.892661 1.430931 0.49468 (A, 0, 0) 0.048327 0.026173 0.54159 (0, 0, C) 0.100217 0.048678 0.48572 volume mean 1.209979 0.598518 0.49465
  • The same arithmetic on the uniform source reproduces P26's mean, 0.614195 / 1.238893 = 0.49576.
  • "The duty drop predicted from P26's":
  • P26's uniform ratios are the prediction: the volume mean 0.49576 (0.61419 / 1.23889, test_mat21_box_duty_closed_form.py:210–215) and the centre 0.49902 (0.666540 / 1.335705, MAT-21.md:548, :28).
  • They predict the quadratic mean to 0.2 % (0.49576 against 0.49465). They do not predict the centre (0.499 against 0.545): the source vanishes on the axis, so the centre heats late, by diffusion, and keeps the early on-phases' heat.
  • That is a printed reading, not a target.

W1 module: tests/validation/test_mat21_box_quadratic_duty_closed_form.py (numpy only, no dolfinx). - Imports: - step 2 W1's pins and helpers (test_mat21_box_duty_closed_form.py:53–63, _quad_nodes :80–91, _on_lags :94–101, C1_TIMES :140, R_BAR :61); - step 9 W1's WEIGHTS, QUAD_TERMS, _uprod_quad and _y_reduced (test_mat21_box_quadratic_closed_form.py:46–49, :189–203, :243–253); - step 0's HALF, K, H, Q, RHO_C, R2_PTS, R4_PTS, SERIES_TERMS and T_C. - It defines _quad_duty(x, y, z, t, switch_times=T_SW, n_terms=QUAD_TERMS, drop=()) and _quad_duty_mean(t, …). The mean contracts W with sin γ/γ on each axis. - Asserted: - (D0) bitwise. At switch_times=(0.0,), _quad_duty is np.array_equal to robin_box_quadratic_transient_temperature at t*. Check this on P36's (Q2) point set (R2_PTS plus the 7 × 7 × 3 grid, test_mat21_box_quadratic_closed_form.py:124–129), at both SERIES_TERMS and QUAD_TERMS. This is the closed-form half of "the 100 % duty control reproducing P36 bitwise", read as the 10-15 03:00 ruling read P32's letter (MAT-21.md:1253). - (D1) The one-tensor ten-run sum against Σ (−1)^m of ten public calls, at R4_PTS × C1_TIMES: ≤ 1e-12·θ_ref. This is a new-code identity, at step 0's R0 bar (the 10-16 ruling's class, MAT-21.md:1659). Here θ_ref = 8.805072 K (P36's (Q6) reference, :265). Predicted ≤ 1e-15. - (D2) Duhamel with χ. _quad_duty at SERIES_TERMS against (Q/ρc) Σ over the on-lags of ∫ _uprod_quad ds, at R4_PTS × C1_TIMES: ≤ R_BAR·θ_ref. docs.text:
Drafted read-only for the 2026-10-20 18:00 daily review; the review rules on it.

Licence: §9 rule (6) (docs/automation/daily-review.md ≈ :196–214). This is the third and last provisional step chain P may carry between weeklies; P42 and P43 are the first two (PROJECT_PLAN.md ≈ :4888–4904). It works toward chain P's stated subgoal, Phase 8 (8e)'s closed-form half: the F2182 gel box's thermal dose against MAT-20's operators (MAT-21; Phase 8 subgoals ≈ :4428–4449; the 10-19 weekly's P39 ruling ≈ :4768–4778). It uses that chain's existing validation targets only: MAT-20's operator identities at their imported bands, P39′'s (Bd) bound, and reproduction of earlier records' strings. Serial on nothing: items 565 / 567 / 570 / 571 are DONE on main (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4103–4110), and no open §9 item touches a MAT-21 module. This brief sets and moves no band, tolerance, Done-when or target. Every band is imported, and the (Bd) bound is the 10-19 weekly's, applied to more histories. Templates: item 571 (P43), item 570 (P42), item 567 (P41).

MAT-21 step 16: the duty-cycled dose at P37's P3–P5. P41's D = 0.5 and P42's D = 0.25 schedules on P36's source are read at P43's NEW_PTS, so every F2182 probe point carries a dose under every schedule. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: W1 standard (numpy, real build, no mpiexec); W2 heavy (-n 2, complex). - Class: lane 3. Cost: ≈ 9.7 measured (class median) / ≈ 15 predicted min. - Basis: P42 and P43 together took ≈ 19 min of the 13:30 slot, ≈ 9.5 min each. That runs from EX-138's last log at 18:48:03 UTC to P43's journal at 19:06Z (docs/testing/attempts.md:1730, :1743), with 3.6 / 3.5 min of windows. - P44 has ≈ 5.2 min of windows (W1 ≈ 0.75, sweep ≈ 2.1, W2 ≈ 2.3) and two modules ≈ 1.3× the size of one of theirs, so ≈ 14 min. - The drafter convention of items 570 / 571 (itemised writing + windows + journal) would have said ≈ 40. - Depends on: nothing. Family: step 16, attempt 1 of 4.

Why this step (the rule (6) choice). After P39′ / P41–P43 the probe × schedule matrix has two empty columns: P3–P5 under D = 0.5 and under D = 0.25. The (Bd)(ii) leg is also asserted on only one duty cell (D = 0.25 at P0–P2). P41 printed it on D = 0.5 but did not assert it.

The cells are not equally informative, and the measured scaling says where the bound is tightest. On going from the continuous source to a duty schedule, the max pointwise miss M_p barely moves: ×1.13 / ×1.20 at the walls and ×0.95 at the centre, for D = 0.5 / 0.25. Meanwhile max θ_s falls to 0.51–0.55 (D = 0.5) and 0.26–0.28 (D = 0.25) of its continuous value. These come from P41's printed and P42's asserted readings against P39′'s. Headroom therefore shrinks by roughly the θ ratio. P5 starts at the smallest continuous headroom of the six points (5.04×, the 8-cell z direction), so P5 under D = 0.25 should land at ≈ 1.1–1.5×. That is the tightest cell anywhere in the matrix, and exactly where P43's journal hypothesis places "the first place two-step on-phases and coarse z resolution compound" (attempts.md:1750). A green there completes the matrix with the weekly's bound asserted on every cell. A red is the first measured failure of the (Bd)(ii) leg at Δt = t*/40 on m = 4, a resolution finding for the weekly. Either result changes what chain P can claim.

Alternatives considered and set aside: - A different period: the 10:30 ruling (1) did not pose the half-period half. - D = 0.125 with a Δt-halving rung (P42's journal, attempts.md:1741): the rung is a Δt-rate, which is not a chain P target. - The -n 1 width: FEM strings are batch- and width-specific, so it asserts nothing new. - Re-basing to 37 °C: excluded by every chain P scope.

Running D = 0.5 beside D = 0.25 costs one CN run (≈ 35 s) and fills the whole matrix in one step.

The matrix, the schedules and the two batches. No new source, no new form. - Points: item 565's HIST_PTS (P1 +y, P2 −y, P0 centre, plus (0, 0.9B, 0) printed only) and P43's NEW_PTS (P3 +x, P4 −x, P5 top face; test_mat21_box_probe_dose_closed_form.py:39–41). At ×4, P42 measured max T 22.77 °C at the walls, and P3–P5 are below 0.11 K continuous. So R = 0.25 throughout; it is still asserted on every history.

Then r.snapshots.clear(); del r before the next run. 5. Series: W1's six histories (continuous, D = 0.5 and D = 0.25 on each batch). - Asserted: - Preconditions: - (Pdeg) 116 025 on four solves, and NEW_PTS == PROBE_PTS[3:6]. - (S0) both censuses (≤ 1e-12 inside _census), with the strings == SCHEDULE and == SCHEDULE_25. - Every evaluation valid on both batches in all three runs. - (E) max_balance_residual ≤ E_BAND on all three runs. - T_INF == T_INF_0. - (R36) on the default HIST_PTS batch. - On the default run, the n = 40 snapshot is np.array_equal to the final field on each batch. - Max T < 43 on every history at both normalisations. - String reproductions: - (R39′) The default HIST_PTS doses print P39P_FEM_DOSE at :.10e. - (R43) The default NEW_PTS doses print P43_FEM_DOSE at :.10e. - (R41-h) The D = 0.5 FEM equal-mean ratio on HIST_PTS against the default run prints P41_FEM_EQ at :.6f, using P41's expression (test_mat21_box_duty_dose_fem.py:216–218, :226). - (R42-h) The same for D = 0.25 against P42_FEM_EQ, using P42's expression (test_mat21_box_duty25_dose_fem.py:229–231, :240). - (Q-hP), (Win-hP) at each NEW_PTS point on both duty FEM histories, at peak and at equal mean power, at DOSE_BAR / AVG_BAR. - (Bd50) and (Bd25), (i) and (ii), at all six points (DOSE_PTS from the HIST_PTS batch and NEW_PTS), at peak and at equal mean power, through _bd (test_mat21_box_dose_fem.py:187–193): - θ_s is the matching duty series history: m_p ≤ ln 4·M_p and M_p ≤ INTERIOR_BAND·max_n θ_s. - This is the weekly's first-order form. Traps already paid for. - Same-batch bytes (item 537). The four string reproductions hold only on the two fixed batches, HIST_PTS then NEW_PTS, one call each per snapshot, at -n 2. Merging them changes P0–P2's bytes. - Run order differs from P41's (default → χ ≡ 1 → duty there; default → d50 → d25 here). Traps already paid for. - Every inherited helper is grid-bound (T_GRID, N_MAIN, MID_T). Calling one on 81-row arrays either raises or silently integrates on the wrong times. docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-25 03:00 daily review from the 10-24 weekly's enumerated step P46 (§9 rules (4) / (5)). Three execution readings below go to the 10-26 weekly; none changes the target. (Placed above the 10-24 row-migration block so that block stays the file's tail.)

Question. At what Δt-order does the F2182 box's dose converge under Crank–Nicolson with the Rannacher start, against the triple Robin series? The answer is a record on the scheme's time order.

Execution readings (this review's): 1. Build. The weekly wrote "real build". Every MAT-21 FEM module is @complex_only (test_mat21_box_dose_fem.py:139, :161), and its windows ran complex. The step runs complex. 2. "The finest-Δt dose equal to P39′'s string at t*/40". The finest Δt here is t*/80. The clause is read as the t*/40 history's dose equals P39′'s FEM string (P39P_FEM_DOSE, test_mat21_box_duty_dose_fem.py:64). That history is P39′'s run, so the clause is a re-read identity. 3. Which six points. P39′ covers P0–P2. P3–P5 are P43's (step 15, NEW_PTS, test_mat21_box_probe_dose_closed_form.py:39). "P39′'s six probe-point doses" is read as P0–P5 on the source P39′ used. The re-read identity applies to P39P_FEM_DOSE (P0–P2), and to P43_FEM_DOSE (test_mat21_box_probe_duty_dose_fem.py:77) only if P43 ran the same source. Otherwise P3–P5's t*/40 strings are printed, not re-read, and the commit says so.

Anchors. - (Rt) The LSQ slope of log |D_h(Δt) − D_series| on log Δt over Δt = t*/20, /40, /80 is ≥ RATE_BAR (1.7, test_mat15_finite_cylinder_fem.py:68, read on Δt as the weekly states), per point. - (Re) The t*/40 dose equals the stored FEM strings (reading 2). - MAT-20's identities on each history at their imported bands: (Q) cem43 against _quad_dose at DOSE_BAR 1e-10 (test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py:35), and (Win) at AVG_BAR 1e-12 / W_B2 360 s (test_mat20_running_average.py:34–36).

The known risk to (Rt), stated, not pre-registered. The comparison against the series carries the P2 spatial error, which does not shrink with Δt (P45's (FEM-X) gives 1.8e-3 to 5.6e-3 of it). If it dominates the t*/80 error, the slope is floor-bound. Print the spatial floor first: P45's (FEM-X) at each point, beside |D_h(t*/80) − D_series|. Print the self-difference rate (mat:27's route, examples/materials/27_duty_cycle_time_step_rate.py:103) beside (Rt); it is not asserted. No range is pre-registered, so an (Rt) red stops the slot under the default rule, with the floor reading recorded as the diagnosis.

Control (printed). The backward-Euler history's rate on the same three Δt, ≈ 1, as mat:27's 0.996 record (:70–79).

Route. New module tests/validation/test_mat21_box_dt_rate_dose_fem.py, gated by FEM_EM_MAT21_P46=1. - Use P45's _cn_snap_n(…, n) (test_mat21_box_dt_duty125_dose_fem.py:115) and the grid-parameterised _series_hist_g, _q_check_g, _win_check_g (test_mat21_box_dt_duty125_dose_closed_form.py:110–165). - Add N = 20 with T_GRID20 beside P45's N80 / T_GRID80 (:70–74). Δt is a fem.Constant, so no new form compiles (MAT-21.md:2828). - The series is robin_box_quadratic_transient_temperature (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:2291) through _series_hist.

Windows. 1. W0: coding tests. 2. W1 MAT-21-step18-W1: three CN histories plus one BE, -n 2, complex, heavy, timeout -k 30 1200.

Predicted ≈ fixture 46 s + CN at N = 20 / 40 / 80 (≈ 16 / 31 / 42 s, from P39′ and P45) + BE ≈ 40 s + series ≈ 11 s ≈ 190–250 s.

Tier: heavy, -n 2 (earlier MAT-21 W2s were tiered heavy). Class: lane-3 closed form. Cost: ≈ 7.5 measured / 40 predicted slot-minutes. Executor: implementer. Depends on: nothing. Family: MAT-21 step 18, attempt 1 of 4.

Traps already paid for (MAT-21.md:2224–2233, :2988–2992): - cem43 raises on a nonzero imaginary part: pass T_INF + θ as real values. - _probe_vals is collective, and point-sample bytes depend on the batch (item 537): sample call by call on the same batch. - Call the grid-bound helpers only through the local copies. - Keep startup_half_steps=2. - Switch times are physical (k · DT_BOX). - (Bd)(i) is first order: never swap in the exponential form. - -k 30 on every timeout; never background a window; pgrep -c python3 after any kill.

Scope boundary. A record on the time scheme only. No new physics claim, no coil, no perfusion. MAT-21 stays ✅ on step 1.

A negative result means: (Re) red ⇒ the N = 40 path drifted. That is a defect: stop and report. (Rt) red ⇒ a measured negative on the scheme's order against the series, recorded with the floor reading in MAT-21.md and on an attempt/* branch. Never loosen RATE_BAR. Whether a floor-bound (Rt) is re-posed on the self-difference is the weekly's call.

Status it can move. §10 P46 → DONE. MAT-21's row records step 18, the CN Δt-rate of the dose. The mat: example the weekly names is opened only after this lands.

Outcome (2026-10-25, 11:00 UTC slot, fourth item) — BLOCKED, attempt 1 of 4: (Rt) red, a measured negative, floor-bound. Module tests/validation/test_mat21_box_dt_rate_dose_fem.py and its log are parked on attempt/MAT-21-step18-20261025T112325Z (not on main). W1 (20261025T112325Z_MAT-21-step18-W1-dt-rate-dose-fem.log, on the branch): 7 passed / 1 failed in 220.49 s, harness 222 s (:197, predicted 190–250 s), -n 2, complex, timeout -k 30 590 (the brief's 1200 exceeds the 660 s foreground cap); pgrep 0 before and after, no kill. Clocks: steady 10.3 s; CN N = 20 / 40 / 80 25.6 / 31.8 / 42.1 s; BE 15.9 / 20.7 / 32.6 s; series 3.4 s (:65–83). - Green: (Pdeg) 116 025 ×7, validity, (E) ≤ 2.288e-13 (:91); (Re) the t*/40 CN doses equal P39P_FEM_DOSE (P0–P2) and P43_FEM_DOSE (P3–P5) — P43 ran the same source, so both are true re-reads (reading 3) (:93–94); (Q) / (Win) on all nine histories (3 CN, 3 BE, 3 series) at all six points. - Red: (Rt) LSQ slope vs RATE_BAR 1.7 (:169, :176): ±y walls −0.403 (|D_h − D_s| rel 8.80e-4 → 1.41e-3 → 1.54e-3, :152); centre 0.938 (the error crosses zero near t*/40, :158); ±x 0.4999 (1.02e-4 → 6.17e-5 → 5.12e-5, :161); P5 −0.061 (1.94e-4 → 2.07e-4 → 2.12e-4, :167). - Spatial floor, printed first (P45-route (FEM-X) as a fraction of max θ₄₀ / |D_h(t*/80) − D_s| rel): walls 3.27e-4 / 1.54e-3; centre 2.63e-4 / 1.66e-5; ±x 3.14e-4 / 5.12e-5; P5 7.59e-4 / 2.12e-4 (:151, :157, :160, :166). Self-difference rate (printed, not asserted): walls 1.988, centre 1.978, ±x 1.971, P5 1.724 — CN is second order in Δt against itself. BE control (printed): walls 1.167, centre 1.018, ±x 0.902, P5 −0.293 (:153, :159, :162, :168). - Executor's diagnosis (a reading, not asserted): against the series the error is bound by the P2 spatial error, which does not shrink with Δt; at the walls the time error has the opposite sign to a ≈ 1.5e-3 spatial offset (Richardson on the CN doses puts the Δt→0 offset at ≈ 1.58e-3), so the total grows as Δt shrinks; P5 is flat at its floor. Readings made: D_series at each Δt is cem43 of the series sampled on that grid; three BE runs, one per Δt. For the 10-26 weekly: whether (Rt) is re-posed on the self-difference (the brief's own branch). RATE_BAR untouched; MAT-21 stays ✅ on step 1.

docs.title: Review ruling 2026-10-25 10:30 (item 629, P46 — BLOCKED, attempt 1 of 4)
docs.text: Diagnosis accepted, re-pose not made here. The W1 reading (on the branch, 20261025T112325Z_MAT-21-step18-W1-dt-rate-dose-fem.log:151–176) is the risk the brief named: against the series, the dose error is bound by the P2 spatial error, which does not shrink with Δt; the self-difference rates (1.988 / 1.978 / 1.971 / 1.724) say CN is second order against itself. Every other assertion was green, and (Re) re-read P39′ / P43 exactly, so the N = 40 path did not drift. Two re-poses keep the series as comparand and were examined: coarser Δt (t*/5, /10, /20) fails on the executor's own Richardson offset — at the walls the time error (≈ 0.7e-3 at t*/20, ×4 per halving) crosses the ≈ 1.58e-3 spatial offset between t*/10 and t*/20, so the series difference passes through zero there and the slope is meaningless; finer h is a new fixture (the weekly's). The remaining re-pose — the rate on the self-difference — changes the comparand from the series to the scheme itself, which the brief reserved for the weekly. Returned to the 10-26 weekly; the branch attempt/MAT-21-step18-20261025T112325Z stays (its module is not captured in the plan). Family count: P46 attempt 1 of 4. RATE_BAR untouched.

docs.title: §9 item 659 — 2026-10-27 (§10 P47a, chain P — MAT-21 step 19, the box from a non-uniform initial temperature; lane 3 closed form)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-27 03:00 daily review from the 10-26 weekly's P47a (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10 chain P). One fact the weekly's text did not have: every Robin-box helper uses even slab modes only (cos(γ s / L) with γ sin γ = Bi cos γ; robin_slab_eigenvalues, analytical.py:1874; _robin_box_basis, :2057), and robin_box_transient_temperature takes only a uniform t_init (:2148). θ₀ = g·z is odd in z, so its projection needs the odd family.

Anchor — new closed forms, appended after the MAT-21 step 0 section (analytical.py:2038 onward, before MAT-17 at :2308; insertions only). - robin_slab_odd_eigenvalues(biot, n): the roots of γ cos γ = −Bi sin γ (odd modes sin(γ s / L)), one per interval ((n − ½)π, nπ), by brentq, in the pattern of robin_slab_eigenvalues. - robin_box_initial_gradient_temperature(x, y, z, t, *, half_widths, k, h, rho_c, g, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=40): θ(t) − t_inf for θ₀ = t_inf + g·z with the source off. Separation: the x and y factors carry only the zeroth-order projection of a constant (θ₀ is uniform in x, y), i.e. the even-mode coefficients of 1 (robin_slab_cosine_coefficients, :2173); the z factor carries the odd-mode projection of z on (−C, C): b_n = ∫ z sin(γ_n z / C) dz / ∫ sin²(γ_n z / C) dz, in closed form. Cite Carslaw & Jaeger §3.10 (the slab with radiation at both faces) for the odd family. - Box and gel: A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX = 0.325, 0.21, 0.045 m (test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:34); K, RHO_C, H, T_INF from test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py:43–47. g = 10 K/m (a 0.9 K top-to-bottom gradient over 90 mm; printed as the fixture's choice, not a measured phantom value).

Identities — new tests appended to tests/validation/test_mat21_box_closed_form.py (or a new module test_mat21_initial_gradient_closed_form.py if the existing one's fixtures do not fit; never edit an existing test). Bars as step 0 uses them (literal bars R0–R6 in that module; B1_BAND is not a MAT-21 name): - (Odd) each odd root satisfies its characteristic equation to ≤ 1e-12, one root per interval. - (Rob) the six face Robin residuals ≤ 1e-10, _face_residuals' pattern (:87, asserted at :110 / :115). - (IC) the L2 reconstruction of g·z at t = 0 by the z-series: error at n_terms = 160 ≤ ½ × the error at 40 (a convergence statement; z does not satisfy the Robin condition, so pointwise 1e-12 is out of reach). Print all truncations. - (Dec) θ(t → ∞) → t_inf to ≤ 1e-12 (the decaying sum underflows), as test_r5_limits (:281). - (Bal) ∫ρc(θ(t) − t_inf) dV + the cumulative wall flux to t equals ∫ρc(θ₀ − t_inf) dV at three times, ≤ 1e-10 (the Gauss check's bar, :200). For g·z the initial integral is zero by symmetry, so assert it at the truncation's precision and print the wall-flux integral separately (it is zero too: odd in z on the top and bottom faces cancel). Because both sides vanish, (Bal) alone cannot catch a sign error: also assert (Half), the same balance over the upper half-box z > 0 with the flux through z = 0, which is non-zero.

Controls. - (U) A uniform θ₀ = ḡ through the new function's even path equals robin_box_transient_temperature(…, q=0, t_init=ḡ) to ≤ 1e-12 (asserted equal: the reduction). - (Dz) The Dirichlet-z version (sin(nπz/2C) modes) misses the Robin solution at t* by > 1e-3 (test_negative_control_dirichlet_z's bar, :342–343).

Window. W1 MAT-21-step19-W1 (smoke, numpy, -n 1, real image, timeout -k 30 120; step 0 took 5–7 s). W-env (-n 1, timeout -k 30 300).

Executor: implementer. Tier: smoke, -n 1. Class: lane-3 closed form. Cost: ≈ 7.2 measured / 30 predicted slot-minutes. Depends on: nothing. Family: P47a (MAT-21 step 19), attempt 1 of 4.

Traps already paid for. The odd characteristic equation has a root near (n − ½)π for small Bi and near nπ for large Bi: bracket each interval, never seed Newton. The truncation error of a non-Robin initial condition decays like 1/n, so a pointwise bar there is unreachable; that is why (IC) is a ratio.

Scope. The closed form of what a pre-equilibration gradient leaves. Not claimed: a measured phantom gradient, the FEM (P47b), a source.

Negative result. (Odd), (Rob), (U) or (Half) red ⇒ a defect: report, park, BLOCKED. (IC) not converging at the ratio ⇒ report the truncations and stop. No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. MAT-21 gains step 19 (🟡 record; the chunk stays ✅); §10 P47a → DONE; unblocks item 669 (P47b).

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim, if delegated). "Execute §9 item 659 — MAT-21 P47a — per docs/planning/chunks/MAT-21.md "§9 item 659". The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Append functions; never edit an existing one. Spawned executors run every window foreground with Bash timeout: 660000."

Outcome (2026-10-27, 06:00 CDT slot, ≈ 11:07 UTC) — DONE, step 19 🟡 record. Three functions appended after robin_box_quadratic_transient_temperature in analytical.py (no existing function edited): robin_slab_odd_eigenvalues (brentq on ((n − ½)π, nπ)), robin_slab_odd_linear_coefficients (b = 2(sin γ − γ cos γ)/(γ(γ − sin γ cos γ)), the projection of s/L) and robin_box_initial_gradient_temperature (keywords theta_uniform for the ḡ path, roots_z for the control; returns T with T∞ included, as every Robin-box helper does — the brief's "θ − t_inf" is the rise at t_inf = 0). Since e^{−αΛt} factorises over axes, the triple sum is evaluated exactly as U_x·U_y·[ḡU_z + gC·V_z]. New module tests/validation/test_mat21_initial_gradient_closed_form.py (step 0's module not edited). W1 20261027T110416Z_MAT-21-step19-W1.log: 8 passed in 74.01 s, harness 76 s, -n 1, real, timeout -k 30 120. - (Odd) one root per interval ×400 at Bi 5.4167 / 3.5 / 0.75, max residual/γ 1.70e-13 / 1.48e-13 / 1.14e-13 (:43–45); γ′₁(z) = 1.939740990931. - (Rob) max face residual/(k g) 3.11e-15 at Fo 0.05 / 0.2 / 1 (:47–50). - (IC) rel L2 ‖z − S_N z‖/‖z‖: 7.90e-3 / 2.80e-3 / 9.91e-4 / 3.50e-4 / 1.24e-4 / 4.38e-5 at N = 10 … 320; decay exponent 1.500 (coefficients ∝ 1/n², so the L2 tail is N^−1.5, not the brief's 1/n); ratio e(160)/e(40) = 0.125 ≤ ½ (:52–55). b₁…₄ closed form = Gauss quadrature to 12 digits (printed). - (Dec) |T(100 t_C) − T∞|/(g C) = 0 (:57). - (Bal) whole box: series E(0) = −7.2e-14 J, mode-space wall flux exactly 0, residual ≤ 2.5e-18 of ρc g C V. (Half) upper half box, volume integrals by Gauss quadrature of the function and cumulative fluxes in mode space (top, four half side faces, k∂_zθ through z = 0): residual ≤ 3.8e-15 of ρc g C²/2·4AB at Fo 0.05 / 0.2 / 1; the z = 0 flux is the largest term (1148 / 4025 / 7656 J) (:59–66). Series half-box E(0) is 6.65e-6 below the exact g·z integral (truncation, printed). - (U) ḡ = 1 K through the even path equals robin_box_transient_temperature(q=0, t_init=T∞+1) to 0.0 K at Fo 0 / 0.05 / 0.2 / 1 (:68–72). - Printed: θ at (0, 0, C) 0.2775 / 0.1468 / 0.0072 K at Fo 0.05 / 0.2 / 1 (g C = 0.45 K), centre 0 by symmetry; slowest odd mode τ = 3649 s (:74–77). - Control (Dz) Dirichlet odd roots γ = mπ miss the Robin solution at t* by 0.317 g C (bar > 1e-3) (:79). - W-env 20261027T110546Z_MAT-21-step19-Wenv.log: 8 passed, 4 skipped (the complex-only tests on the real image), 104 s. - Not asserted: a separate per-mode (PDE) check (the weekly's text lists it; this brief did not). Unblocks item 669 (P47b).

docs.title: §9 item 660 — 2026-10-27 (§10 P48a, chain P — MAT-21 step 20, the acrylic container wall on the box in closed form; lane 3 closed form)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-27 03:00 daily review from the 10-26 weekly's P48a. No two-layer slab series exists (MAT-18's are spherical: two_layer_sphere_steady_temperature :2508, …_eigenvalues :2591, …_transient_temperature :2706), and no PMMA constant exists in the repo. The wall precedent is _h_eff(h, t_w, k_w) at tests/validation/test_mat18_wall_coil_driven.py:82.

Anchor — new closed forms after the MAT-21 step 0 section (insertions only). - two_layer_slab_steady_temperature(z, *, half_thickness, wall, k, k_w, q, h, t_inf): the 1D symmetric slab −C < z < C of gel (k, uniform q) with a wall layer C < |z| < C + d (k_w, no source), Robin h outside. Exact: piecewise quadratic in the gel, linear in the wall, flux and temperature continuous at |z| = C. - (i) h_eff = (1/h + d/k_w)⁻¹, d = 6 mm, k_w = 0.19 W/m/K. Citation: search docs/references/ for a PMMA / acrylic conductivity first; if none is there, record k_w = 0.19 as a nominal handbook value, citation owed (dashboard item for the operator, as W3's references are), and say so in the module docstring. The identity in (i) is algebraic and does not depend on the value being right. - (ii) the transient wall share bound: ε_w = ρ_w c_w d / (ρc · C), with ρ_w c_w for PMMA (≈ 1190 kg/m³ × 1470 J/kg/K, the same citation rule) — printed.

Identities — a new module tests/validation/test_mat21_wall_closed_form.py (box and gel constants imported as step 0 does): - (W1) In steady state, the gel-side temperature of the two-layer slab equals the bare Robin slab at h_eff (_robin_slab_coefficients / the steady box z-factor at Bi = h_eff C / k) at every gel point, ≤ 1e-12. - (W2) Flux continuity at |z| = C and the Robin residual at |z| = C + d, ≤ 1e-12. - (W3) The steady box series at h_eff on all six faces (robin_box_steady_temperature, :2116, with h → h_eff) equals the bare series at h_eff: a consistency print, not a new claim. Assert (W1) only in 1D; the 3D box with a wall on every face is P48b's FEM question. - (Print) ε_w, and the steady centre rise with and without the wall.

Controls. (K∞) k_w → ∞ (1e9) returns the bare Robin series at h to ≤ 1e-9 (asserted equal: the reduction). (Wneg) the bare series at h (no wall) misses the two-layer gel temperature by > 1e-3 at the centre.

Window. W1 MAT-21-step20-W1 (smoke, numpy, -n 1, timeout -k 30 120). W-env.

Executor: implementer. Tier: smoke, -n 1. Class: lane-3 closed form. Cost: ≈ 7.2 measured / 25 predicted slot-minutes. Depends on: nothing. Family: P48a (MAT-21 step 20), attempt 1 of 4.

Traps already paid for. A literature value written without a source is a fabrication: write "citation owed" rather than a reference you have not read. MAT-18's wall is spherical (t_w = 0.01 m); do not reuse its geometry constants.

Scope. The wall as an effective Robin coefficient in steady state, exact in 1D. Not claimed: the wall's transient (only bounded), the 3D box with a meshed wall (P48b), a measured phantom container.

Negative result. (W1), (W2) or (K∞) red ⇒ algebra defect: park, BLOCKED. No PREDICTED RED: line.

Spawned executors run every window foreground with Bash timeout: 660000."

Two functions appended after robin_box_initial_gradient_temperature in analytical.py (no existing function edited): wall_effective_heat_transfer(h, wall, k_w) and two_layer_slab_steady_temperature(z, *, half_thickness, wall, k, k_w, q, h, t_inf, return_gradient) (gel branch for |z| ≤ C, wall branch outside; T∞ included, as every Robin helper does). That is the precedent this item follows in slab geometry. The item executes the weekly's own target and adds no new one. Depends on nothing (item 660's functions and module are on main).

Anchor — a new closed form appended after two_layer_slab_steady_temperature (analytical.py:2446), insertions only. - The function. two_layer_slab_transient_temperature(z, t, *, half_thickness, wall, k, k_w, rho_c, rho_c_w, q, h, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=…) covers the symmetric 1D slab: gel in |z| < C (k, ρc, uniform q switched on at t = 0), wall in C < |z| < C + d (k_w, ρ_w c_w, no source), Robin h at |z| = C + d, and θ(0) = 0. - The solution. θ = θ_ss(z) − Σ aₙ Xₙ(z) e^{−λₙ t}, where θ_ss is item 660's two_layer_slab_steady_temperature. - The even eigenfunctions. In the gel, Xₙ = cos(μ₁ z) with μ₁ = √(ρc λ / k). In the wall, Xₙ = cos(μ₁C) cos(μ₂(|z| − C)) − (k μ₁ / (k_w μ₂)) sin(μ₁C) sin(μ₂(|z| − C)) with μ₂ = √(ρ_w c_w λ / k_w), which builds in T and flux continuity at |z| = C. - The eigenvalues. λₙ are the roots of the Robin condition at |z| = C + d (one scalar equation in λ), bracketed and refined with scipy.optimize.brentq as two_layer_sphere_eigenvalues does. - The coefficients. aₙ = ∫ ρc(z) θ_ss Xₙ dz / ∫ ρc(z) Xₙ² dz, with the piecewise weight. Compute both integrals in closed form or by Gauss–Legendre per layer, and say which. - Derivation. It goes in the docstring. No composite-slab text is in docs/references/: write "citation owed" for a textbook form, never a chapter you have not opened.

Item 669 (P47b). 1. (Sym) was this review's own gate, not the weekly's target. The 03:00 brief added it as a "symmetry identity". The weekly's P47b target is the interior band, the balance and the printed drift, and those three were green: (I) 7.543e-3, (E) 4.110e-15, (Dz) miss 2.9493 (W1 :59–61 on the branch). 2. The red is a mesh fact, not a solver fault. P1 = −P2 and P3 = −P4 to every printed digit (W1 :64–67), and P0 reads 3.6e-15 K. create_box's tetrahedra map onto themselves under point reflection through the centre, but not under z → −z. Every MAT-21 create_box call passes only cell_type, and no z-mirror box helper exists in the repo (fact sheet A4). The exact identity on this mesh is therefore point reflection: θ₀ = g·z is odd under (x, y, z) → (−x, −y, −z), so θ_h(−p) = −θ_h(p). 3. Re-pose (Sym′): |θ(P1) + θ(P2)|, |θ(P3) + θ(P4)| and |θ(P0)| are each ≤ SYM_BAR · g C. The bar is the same 1e-10. The four mid-plane values print as the O(h²) record. This is item 676, P47b attempt 2 of 4. 4. The balance normalisation is ratified provisionally as executed: ∫ρc|θ₀ − T∞| dV / Δtₙ per step. The residual is a power, so the brief's bare energy normaliser was dimensionally wrong. The executed form is the consistent one, and it is the stricter of the two readings. The branch is taken only when ∫Q = 0.0 exactly, so the sourced path is byte-for-byte unchanged (Wreg proves it). 5. Wreg runs on the complex image. Step 1's transient tests are @complex_only (test_mat21_box_fem.py:41, :373–394), so the brief's "real" Wreg would have skipped them all. The new module carries no @complex_only and stays on the real build.

Item 673 (P48a′). 1. The (Root) red sits below float64 resolution. One ulp moves F/scale by ≥ 1.33e-12 on the five worst modes and by 2.9e-11 at n = 159. Each of the 200 roots is the |F|-minimiser among its neighbouring doubles (probe :44, :49). This is the MAT-18 R0 finding of item 199. 2. Re-pose (Root) as MAT-18's ratified R0a / R0b, copied, not re-invented (MAT-18.md:110; code test_mat18_two_layer_sphere_closed_form.py:133, :141–156, :172–178, :221–223): - (Root-a) ROOT_BAND 1e-12 on n ≤ 60; - (Root-b) for all 200 roots, F changes sign between the stored root's neighbouring doubles within ±2 ulp, and the stored root is the |F|-minimiser among the doubles within ±2 ulp; - the +8-ulp control is asserted > 0. This is item 677. On the slot's count it is P48a attempt 3 of 4. 3. t_s = 1/λ₁ is ratified provisionally. The weekly's text leaves t_s undefined. 1/λ₁ is the slowest mode's time constant, and at 50 t_s the series is exactly at its limit (Lim 0.0). The module docstring's "t_s ≈ 2.8 T_C" (:18) contradicts the logged 2.162790 T_C (probe :43), so it is corrected to the logged value. 4. Everything else lands unchanged: the nine green tests, the analytical.py additions, both logs and their test-results rows.

(D1) 1.751e-16, (Duh) 2.568e-15, both controls and the off-phase decay green.

Ruling. The brief's (Edge) asked a bar on the raw jump that the brief's own evaluation form cannot meet at any finite N: θ = sθ_ss − Σ(aₙs − Aₙ)Xₙ = s·(θ_ss − Σ aₙXₙ) + Σ AₙXₙ, so a switch of s by Δs moves θ by exactly Δs·r_N, where r_N = θ_ss − Σ aₙXₙ is the series' truncation residual (6.6e-10 at N = 400; the step helper carries the same residual at t = 0⁺). The physical statement (edge continuity) is that the state does not jump, and that whatever does jump is exactly the known truncation residual. That is what the re-post asserts, at the same bar and the same 32 instants: - (Edge′a) max |A_R − A_L| / max |aₙ| == 0 (already asserted on the branch; read 0). - (Edge′b) max over the instants and Z_GEL of |(θ_R − θ_L) − Δs·r_N| ≤ EDGE_BAND = 1e-13 of θ_ss(0) (read 7.588e-16 on the branch). - The raw jump max |θ_R − θ_L| is printed as a record, labelled "the N = 400 truncation residual", beside r_N — never asserted. - The off-phase strict decay stays asserted, unchanged.

This changes the assertion's form, not its bar: the same 1e-13 now bounds the quantity a truncated series can actually hold continuous (item 677's precedent: an assertion below the series' own floor re-posed to the form that expresses the identity, MAT-21.md "Review ruling 2026-10-27 18:00"). It is not a loosening — no red is absorbed: the re-posed assertion was already computed and printed at 7.6e-16 by the failing run, and the raw jump stays visible. Provisional; the 10-28 weekly ratifies or reverts. Family P49a attempt 2 of 4. Item 688's dependency now reads item 689 DONE.

Route. New module tests/validation/test_mat21_pre_equilibration_closed_form.py, numpy. Superposition: θ(t; t_w) = θ_drift(t + t_w) + θ_sourced(t), with θ_drift = robin_box_initial_gradient_temperature through test_mat21_initial_gradient_closed_form._theta (g = G_GRAD, T∞ = 0 offset) and θ_sourced = robin_box_transient_temperature (MAT-21 step 0's, KW, HALF, SERIES_TERMS). PROBE_PTS and PROBE_LABELS imported from test_mat21_box_probe_points_fem.py. The bias at a point: b(t_w) = θ_drift(t* + t_w) / θ_sourced(t*). The wait grid: t_w ∈ {0, 0.5, 1, 2} / λ₁, with λ₁ the slowest odd-in-z mode's decay rate: the drift is odd in z, so its slowest mode is not step 0's.

One execution detail, returned to the 11-02 weekly. Five of P37's six points lie in z = 0, where the odd drift is exactly zero (item 669's finding), so the ratio holds at P5 only, and five rows read 0 by symmetry. The slot asserts that as (Sym0): |θ_drift| ≤ 1e-13 g C at P0–P4, and prints the six-point table as the weekly asked. For the same reason the decay gate is read at P5 and at ADJ_PT = (0, 0, 0.9 C), so the gate has two points rather than one. That is a clarification, not a new target.

Anchors (asserted). - (Sup) the two limits: the combined helper with q = 0 equals θ_drift(t + t_w), and with g = 0 equals θ_sourced(t), each ≤ B1_BAND; plus the time shift: θ_drift evaluated at t + t_w equals the series at t with its amplitudes advanced by e^{−λ t_w} mode by mode, ≤ B1_BAND. The problem is linear, so the shift is the only part that is not true by construction. - (Dec∞) on the first odd mode alone (n_terms = 1): the bias ratio over t_w ∈ {1/λ₁, 2/λ₁} is e^{−λ₁ · 1/λ₁} to B1_BAND. This is the rate identity free of every other mode. - (Dec), the weekly's gate as written, on the full series: R = [b(2/λ₁) / b(1/λ₁)] · e − 1, |R| ≤ B1_BAND, at P5 and ADJ_PT.

(Dec) is expected red, and why. λ₁ = α(γ_z²/C² + γ_x²/A² + γ_y²/B²) with γ_z ≈ 1.94 at Bi = 0.75. The lateral modes barely separate from it: the second x mode adds ≈ 128 m⁻² to λ₁/α ≈ 1 907 m⁻², a factor e^{−0.067} over Δt_w = 1/λ₁, and the second y mode adds ≈ 300 m⁻², e^{−0.16}. With relative weights ≈ 0.2 at this age, R ≈ 0.2 × 0.065 + 0.2 × 0.15 ≈ 4e-2 (review arithmetic, not a measurement). A single exponential to 1e-12 at t_w = 2/λ₁ is therefore out of reach by ten decades. The gate stays as the weekly wrote it, unmoved; the 11-02 weekly decides whether (Dec∞) is what it meant.

docs.text:

P75's U3 is P51's sourced series. - (Id), a synthetic entry 59. - Build a parsed record whose six probe θ_acc are s·_u3(T_STAR)/P_dep. Take s = 2.858205069e-05, the stub's cw factor (…P61b-W0.log:129). - The table's ratio is 1 within B1_BAND at every point (predicted ≤ 1e-15). - Its cem43 pair agrees within DOSE_BAR.

One bare foreground harness call, Bash timeout 660000 ms, complex build, -n 1 (a numpy reader; the JSON has one writer): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-P79-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/validation/test_mat21_clinical_probe_reader.py tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py -v -s --tb=short'" - Price: P75's W1 took 3 s, with its histories and 41 × 6 series rows in 2.09 s of pytest (…P75-W1.log:102). docs.text:
Written by the 2026-11-09 03:00 daily review under rule (6), toward chain P's stated subgoal (8e): the ASTM gel box heated by the clinical coil, read against closed forms. Serial on nothing. Family P80, attempt 1 of 4. Proposed as MAT-21 step 44 (the review confirms the number). No band, tolerance, done-when or target is set or moved; P76's text is unchanged. Chain P's provisional count since the 11-07 weekly: 3 of 6.

Why this step. P76 will set entry 59's six probe θ beside one picture, the uniform source (P75). Chain P already owns a second, physically motivated picture: P36's long-prism CP eddy-SAR shape q = 3Q(y² + z²)/(B² + C²), ratified by the 10-17 weekly, with the bore along the box's long axis (GEO-38.md:354). Its series is already gated at these very points: step 10 (steady), P39′ and P43 (θ and dose on the 41-row grid). docs.text:
Written by the 2026-11-09 10:30 daily review under rule (6), toward chain P's stated subgoal (8e): the ASTM gel box heated by the clinical coil, read against closed forms. Serial on nothing. Family P81, attempt 1 of 4. Proposed as MAT-21 step 45 (the review confirms the number). No band, tolerance, done-when or target is set or moved; P76's text is unchanged. Chain P's provisional count since the 11-07 weekly: 4 of 6.

Why this step. P80 set the eddy picture beside P75's uniform one, and its own printed shape reading shows what neither picture carries. Entry 52's ccw SAR10g along the lattice's x+0mm column rises toward the box ends: 0.08345 / 0.5125 / 0.8023 of c*'s at dz−50 / −150 / −250 mm, and 0.07112 / 0.4718 / 0.7529 on the + side (20261109T120350Z_MAT-21-P80-W1.log:98–103). The eddy source has no a-dependence, so its ball-mean shape is 0.006439 at every x+0mm point (:113). Chain P already owns a ratified end-weighted source: MAT-21 step 6's q = Q[1 − cos(πx/A)] (PROFILES, test_mat21_box_separable_closed_form.py:45). It is zero at the box centre and 2Q at the ±x ends, with FEM in step 6 / step 8 and on mat:20. Its ball-mean ratios along the x+0mm column, worked from the closed form below, are 0.0664 (dz±50 / dz±250) and 0.5035 (dz±150 / dz±250). Entry 52's are 0.1040 / 0.6388 on the − side. docs.title: §9 item 935 — 2026-11-10 (§10 P83, chain P — rule (4), the 11-09 weekly's step; lane 3 → chain step (closed form))
docs.text:
Enumerated by the 11-09 weekly (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10 chain P, P83, "now"). Serial on nothing. Family P83, attempt 1 of 4. MAT-21 step 46. No band, tolerance, done-when or target is set or moved; the brief supplies execution detail only.

Timing (read first). The step is "a prediction written before its windows". Entry 59 ran at 02:00 11-10 (20261110T080008Z_GEO-38-P33.log), so P83 can now precede only entry 60 (xl Wednesday 11-11 02:00). It should land in a slot before then. The module never opens, imports or parses entry 59's or entry 60's log. Setting entries 59 / 60 beside P83 is C39's job.

Reading of the step text (execution detail, target kept). 1. "C33's JSON strings, (K) re-read equal". C33 writes /workspace/logs/geo38/c33-1p5t-3t.json (20261109T103557Z_GEO-38-C33-W1-r2.log:204). That file is under the gitignored /logs/ and is host-only. By the 11-09 ruling (b) and the §9 digest ("Every new step's reader of a pending window parses its tracked log"), the SAR10g columns are therefore sourced from the tracked C6a logs: entry 52 20261103T080009Z_GEO-38-C6.log (lattice :12289–12306, c* :12307, (i) :12308, normalisers :12310) and entry 58 20261109T080008Z_GEO-38-C6-3T.log (lattice :12238–12255, c* :12256, (i) :12257, normalisers :12259). They are parsed through C33's own route, the ans:11 page's parse_c6_log, loaded by c33._load_page() and never a new regex. - (K) is the string re-read. C33's table strings are rebuilt from those parses and must equal C33's tracked closing log 20261109T103601Z_GEO-38-C33-W1-n1-r2.log:126–131 by string. - The host JSON, where present, is a custody check only: its ratios strings must equal the rebuilt ones. If it is absent, print that it is absent; it is never a red. 2. "Through P80's 10 g-ball source model". Each picture's closed-form 10 g ball mean at each side's c* gives the picture's predicted SAR10g. Per box watt that is ⟨q⟩_ball/(Q·M_box), with M_box = ρ·8ABC. Per accepted watt it is that value × P_box/P_acc. It is printed beside the measured SAR10g(c*); the measured/picture quotient is the shape part. The ball means are P80's _ball_mean (eddy), P81's _ball_mean_end (end) and Q itself (uniform), at r = c6._a10(). 3. "Scaled by each side's P_box / P_acc". θ and the dose come from the picture's series per deposited watt (÷ p75.P_DEP), multiplied by side = P_box/P_acc. s_de is taken from the side's .9e normaliser token(p_box, klzzwxh:97), not from the 7-digit ratio. Both are printed. 4. "On the walled box".** A walled closed form exts only for the unifo picture: P75's 1D-reduced walled sourced rise W_src. c* lies at mid-depth (c = 0 so it is Wrc's z = 0 column, and the drift is 0 there (P79's trap). The 11-09 weekly declined the eddy table in the walled box (a src/ edit). So: The primary rows are on the unwalled six-face box.** That is entry 59 / 6s geometry, and the rows C39 compares against. - The wled uniform row** (W_src at z = 0) is printed beside them as the PMMA-wall variant. - (Sup) / (Bq) are P75's walled-form gates; (Lim) is the three pictures' late-time gate. - If the review reads "on the walled box" otherwise, this point returns to the weekly as "write the anchor" for eddy / end. The rest queues unchanged. 5. "The power-share part 3.6935 printed separately from the shape part". - For each picture, the predicted 3 T / 1.5 T ratio of θ(c*, t*) per accepted watt = (s₃/s₁.₅) × [θ_pic(c*₃)/θ_pic(c*₁.₅)] per deposited watt. - c* moves from x−105mm dz−50mm to its mirror x+105mm dz+50mm (…C33-W1-n1-r2.log:131). All three pictures are even in a and in b, so the shape factor is 1: the (Sym) identity below. The pictures therefore predict the lever as the power share alone. - The measured SAR lever's shape part, 4.101440 / 3.693500 = 1.110448 (:129, :130), is what a fixed-shape picture cannot carry. It is printed as the ball-model quotient's 3 T / 1.5 T ratio.

Code. New tests/validation/test_mat21_field_strength_heating_closed_form.py, complex build (it imports P79 → P61 / C6, and C33), print prefix MAT21-46. No src/ edit; no landed module edited. Read every signature before use. Never import a fixture or a test_* name. - Module objects: - p75 (test_mat21_wall_uniform_source_probe_points_closed_form): P_DEP, T_STAR, T_GRID, _hists (key Wsrc_raw; column 2 is z = 0, as p79._hot_row reads it), _src_q, N_SERIES. - p79 (test_mat21_clinical_probe_reader): _u3_hist_at, _u3_at. - p80 (test_mat21_eddy_source_probe_points_closed_form): _data() (L, lat, lat_pts, U3_lat), _eddy_at, _ball_mean, _cem_bracket. - p81 (test_mat21_end_source_probe_points_closed_form): _data() (SL), _end_at, _ball_mean_end. - c6: _a10, _lattice. - c33 (test_geo38_c33_field_strength_reader): _load_page, side, ratios, check_side, _half_ulp_rel, find_log, ENTRY58_GLOB, ENTRY52_NODE_PF, ENTRY58_NODE_PF, HOST_JSON_DIR, C33_JSON_NAME. - C33's row reader: read_c33_rows(text, log52, log58) from examples/mri/41_f_clinical_field_strength_lever.py:91. Load it by importlib.util.spec_from_file_location under one sys.modules name, as c33._load_page loads the ans:11 page. Its main() is guarded (:333). Never re-implement it. - By name: - robin_box_steady_temperature, robin_box_quadratic_steady_temperature, robin_box_separable_steady_temperature (analytical.py:2116, :2268, :2205); - step 0's HALF, A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX, SERIES_TERMS, T_C, T_INF, K, H, Q, RHO_C as RHO_C_0; - P36's WEIGHTS, QUAD_TERMS; step 6's PROFILES, SEP_TERMS; - PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3 (as c6._a10 imports it); - B1_BAND, INTERIOR_BAND, DOSE_BAR, AVG_BAR, W_B2, _q_check_g, _win_check_g (as P81 imports them); - cem43, running_average. - Sides: S = {"1.5T": parse(entry 52), "3T": parse(entry 58)}. - Entry 52 is page.SOURCE_LOG. Entry 58 is c33.find_log(c33.ENTRY58_GLOB), which must return kind == "tracked". - c33.check_side is run on each side with its node (193.5996 / 44.0525), and every check must pass. c*'s label comes from the parse. - The c* index on the lattice is looked up by label in p80._data()["lat"], never by position. - Per side and picture (u = uniform, e = eddy, n = end; per deposited watt): - histories on T_GRID: u = p79._u3_hist_at(box_pt); e = p80._data()["L"][:, idx]; n = p81._data()["SL"][:, idx]; walled = p75._hists()["Wsrc_raw"][:, 2] / p75.P_DEP. - Each is × s_side for per accepted watt. - θ(c*, t*) is row −1. cem43(T_GRID, T_INF + h). The 360 s running-mean maximum is running_average(T_GRID, h, window=W_B2). - The dose baseline: D0 = cem43(T_GRID, np.full(T_GRID.size, T_INF)), the unheated 20 °C dose. It is printed beside every cem43, with the excess D − D0. - A cem43 "per accepted watt" is the dose of the 1 W history, ≈ D0 plus an excess of order ln 4 · mean θ · D0. It is not a scalable per-watt dose. So its 3 T / 1.5 T ratio is printed only, with that caveat on the line. The excess ratio is printed beside it.

Gates (asserted, bands imported; all collected, then asserted — item 668). - Preconditions: - p75.T_STAR == T_GRID[-1] within 1e-9 s. - p80._data()["lat"] labels equal c6._lattice() labels, in order. - Both c* labels are on the lattice, and every lattice point maps inside at c = 0 (P80 asserted this, 20261109T120350Z_MAT-21-P80-W1.log:47). - (M) M_box = ρ·8ABC formatted .9e equals both logs' (i) mass token 2.457000000e+01 (…C6.log:12308, …C6-3T.log:12257) by string. - (K), C33 re-read by string: - f"{v:.6e}" of c33.ratios(side(p52), side(p58)) equals read_c33_rows(…)'s four ratio tokens: 1.410682e+00 / 1.344035e+00 / 4.101440e+00 / 3.693500e+00 (…C33-W1-n1-r2.log:127–130). - The eight per-side strings and the two c* labels (:131) are equal too. - The parsed 18 SAR10g tokens per side, re-formatted .9e, equal themselves (P80's (K-lat) form). - The full-token power share s₃/s₁.₅ is within sum(c33._half_ulp_rel(t)) over its four .9e tokens plus the two 7-digit tokens of C33's 3.693500e+00 (EX-193's rel_bound pattern). - (Sym), the mirror identity, per picture: |θ_pic(c*₃)/θ_pic(c*₁.₅) − 1| at t* ≤ B1_BAND, and the same on the 41-row history (rows 1–40). Predicted 0: P80 / P81 print the two rows identical (…P80-W1.log:94, :107 0.02078249 / 0.0271814; …P81-W1.log:95, :108 0.00356031). - (Sup): - Homogeneity θ(2Q) = 2θ(Q) for each picture at both c* points at t* (u: p79._u3_at with q; e: p80._eddy_at(…, q=2Q); n: p81._end_at(…, q=2Q)). - Per-watt invariance θ(2Q)/(2P) = θ(Q)/P. - The walled form p75._src_q(t, 2Q)[2] = 2·p75._src_q(t, Q)[2] at t* and 360 s. - All ≤ B1_BAND. - (Lim): each picture at 1000·T_C against its steady series at both c* points, ≤ B1_BAND: - u against robin_box_steady_temperature(n_terms=SERIES_TERMS); - e against the quadratic steady form (QUAD_TERMS); - n against the separable steady form (SEP_TERMS, PROFILES). - P80 / P81's (Lim) read 4.872e-16 / 6.772e-16 at the probes. - (Bq): the walled sourced form at N_SERIES against 2·N_SERIES, z = 0, t* and 360 s, ≤ B1_BAND. P75 read this comparison 0.000e+00 (printed there, 20261108T134258Z_MAT-21-P75-W1.log:92). - MAT-20's forms on the per-accepted-watt histories at c*, each side × the three unwalled pictures + walled (8 histories): (Q-d) ≤ DOSE_BAR with the R-swap miss > DOSE_BAR; (Win-d) ≤ AVG_BAR, window located. This is P80's pattern. - (Cem): p80._cem_bracket holds on the 8 histories. - (Ball): P80's _ball_cub / P81's _ball_cub_end against the closed forms at both c* points, ≤ B1_BAND (P80 3.150e-16, P81 3.944e-14).

Controls (asserted, factor 1 at the gate's own band; rule (e) — each backed by a printed prior measurement at the same point). - (c-u): |n/u − 1| and |e/u − 1| at c*, both sides, > INTERIOR_BAND. - From the logs: 0.8690 (end/U3 0.1309833, …P81-W1.log:95) and 0.2354 (eddy/U3 0.764585, …P80-W1.log:94). - (c-e): |n/e − 1| at c* > INTERIOR_BAND. From the logs: 0.8287 (0.1713129, …P81-W1.log:95). - Ceiling: each ratio is < 1, so |·−1| < 1, and the separation is at most 100× the band. 86.9× / 23.5× / 82.9× are predicted. No factor bar. - (c-sym): (Sym)'s quotient with c*₃ replaced by the non-mirror x+105mm dz+150mm, under the end picture, misses 1 by > B1_BAND. Predicted ≈ 5.73 (0.8817/0.1310 − 1, from …P81-W1.log:111–112), printed.

Printed (🟡 record, no band, ≤ 7 digits; predictions computed from the cited prints, a miss outside a range disclosed, never red). - s₁.₅, s₃ and the power share. Predicted 5.285093e-02 / 1.952049e-01 / ≈ 3.6935. - θ(c*, t*) per accepted watt (K/W).

picture 1.5 T 3 T u ≈ 1.43656e-03 ≈ 5.30594e-03 e ≈ 1.09837e-03 ≈ 4.05684e-03 n ≈ 1.88166e-04 ≈ 6.94990e-04 walled u (z = 0) ≈ 1.427548e-03 ≈ 5.272645e-03

Each is 0.0271814 / 0.02078249 / 0.00356031 / 0.02701082 K/W per deposited watt (…P80-W1.log:94, …P81-W1.log:95, …P75-W1.log:71) × s, range ± 1e-4 relative. The 3 T / 1.5 T ratio is the power share × (Sym) 1 for every picture. - The dose, per side and picture: D0 = t*·0.25²³ = 4.009592657894245e-11 s (20261020T190033Z_MAT-21-step15-W1-probe-dose-closed-form.log.gz:83), cem43 per accepted watt, the excess D − D0 and excess/D0, and the 360 s running-mean maximum with its time. - Predicted excess/D0 under u at 1.5 T is ≈ 9.9e-04, range [9.0e-04, 1.1e-03] (ln 4 · mean θ ≈ 0.69 · θ(t*)). - The excess ratio 3 T / 1.5 T is ≈ 3.698, range [3.694, 3.705] (convexity of 4^θ lifts it above 3.6935). - The cem43 ratio is ≈ 1.003, printed with the caveat. - Whether the running-mean maximum sits at t* (predicted: yes, the history still rises). - The ball model, per side: - Measured SAR10g(c*) per box watt: 4.303111e-02 / 4.778381e-02 (…C6.log:12310, …C6-3T.log:12259). - Per picture per box watt: u 1/M_box ≈ 4.070004e-02; e ≈ 2.93740e-02 (3(b² + 2r²/5)/(B² + C²)/M_box at b = 0.105); n ≈ 4.7221e-03 ((1 − cos(πa/A)·3j₁(u)/u)/M_box at a = 0.05). - Measured/picture: 1.5 T ≈ 1.0573 / 1.4649 / 9.113; 3 T ≈ 1.1741 / 1.6268 / 10.12. - Their 3 T / 1.5 T quotient is ≈ 1.110448 for every picture, the shape part. - The same per accepted watt. - The tie sets (ANS-11 SPEC v2.1's clause: lattice balls within 1 % of the side's maximum), with θ under each picture at each member. - Predicted 1.5 T: {x−105mm dz−50mm, x+105mm dz−50mm, x−105mm dz+50mm} (1.378896513e-04, 1.378032615e-04, 1.368277819e-04; …C6.log:12291, :12303, :12292). - Predicted 3 T: {x+105mm dz+50mm, x+105mm dz−50mm} (…C6-3T.log:12253, :12252). - Every member is a sign-mirror of c*, so θ is identical across each set under all three pictures. - (c-pow), printed: |4.101440/3.693500 − 1| ≈ 0.1104. The SAR lever is not the power share alone. - The normaliser line: per accepted watt = per deposited gel watt × P_box/P_acc, with P_dep = 49.14 W stated.

Window. Pre-check: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. One bare foreground harness call, Bash timeout 660000 ms, complex build, -n 1 (P80 / P81's shape): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-21-P83-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/validation/test_mat21_field_strength_heating_closed_form.py tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py -v -s --tb=short'" - Price: - P81's W1: harness 8 s, P80's 7 s (…P81-W1.log:132, …P80-W1.log:131). Both _data() caches are re-run here once. - C33's W1-n1-r2 parsed both C6a logs in a 3 s window. - Plus two × 40 single-point U3 calls, six (Lim) / (Sup) calls, and one cem43 per history. - Predicted ≈ 15–60 s. A kill parks the item; never raise the ceiling.

Tier. Smoke label, complex, -n 1, no solve. Class: lane 3 → chain step (closed form). Cost: ≈ 4.8 measured / 20 predicted min.

Traps already paid for. - Items 876's, 898's, 913's and 921's lists. - C33's closing logs hold its self-test table (a renamed copy of entry 52, header naming 20990101T000000Z_GEO-38-C6-3T.log, …C33-W1-n1-r2.log:59). Read the one block whose header names both real logs (read_c33_rows does). The -n 2 log …C33-W1-r2.log prints the real table twice (:194, :224), and read_c33_rows refuses it. Use …-n1-r2.log, as EX-193 did. - Normalisers: P75 / P80 / P81 are per deposited gel watt; C6a's SAR10g is per its own drive; P61 is per accepted watt. State s on every row (the 10-24 normaliser rule). - s from the .9e tokens, not the 7-digit ratio. The two differ in the 7th digit (≈ 3.6934990 against 3.693500e+00), so (K) bounds the comparison and never string-compares it. - The lattice is in the fixture frame; map it with p79._to_box (P80 did; lat_pts already carries it). The c* index is looked up by label. - Row 0 of every history is 0 exactly and never evaluated. Same-batch bytes (item 537): (Sym) compares the two c* columns of one L / SL batch, and the two u histories call by call. - cem43 is nonlinear in θ. Never scale a dose by s, and never call a cem43 per watt a lever. - The leak hook: if it flags a printed digit string, print fewer digits and re-run W1 (rule (i)). - Never import a fixture or a test_* name. Use -s.

Scope. Closed form; continuous sources; the unwalled six-face box (entries 59 / 60's geometry) for the three pictures; the uniform picture also in P75's 1D-reduced walled form; per accepted watt at 1.5 T and 3 T at each side's c*. Not claimed: - any entry-59 or entry-60 figure, or a ratio to them (C39); - which picture the clinical heating follows; - an eddy or end-weighted walled box; - a dose lever, a dose band, a compliance figure, a 10 g-averaged θ; - that 3.6935 is the clinical heating lever (it is the pictures' prediction).

Negative result. - A precondition, (M) or (K) red: the reader misreads C33's route or the logs. Stop, park on attempt/MAT-21-P83-*, BLOCKED. - (Sym) red: a picture is not mirror-even at these points, or a batch effect. Report both columns' max |Δ|, BLOCKED. - (Sup), (Lim), (Bq), (Ball), MAT-20's forms or (Cem) red: report the value, BLOCKED. - A control inside its band: a mislabelled comparand. Run W1 in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000, complex build, -n 1, container timeout -k 30 120, pytest -s. You are the executor: do not spawn agents and never background a window. On a red, park on attempt/MAT-21-P83-*, mark item 935 BLOCKED in the same commit, and report; never widen a band."
