docs.text:
Enumerated by the 11-11 weekly (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10 chain P, P88, lines 5124–5135, "now"). Serial on nothing. Family P88, attempt 1 of 4. Step number: §10 says MAT-21 step 47, but item 955 (P86) closed as step 47 (its Outcome above); this brief proposes step 48 and prefix MAT21-48 — the review confirms. No band, tolerance, done-when or target is set or moved; the brief supplies execution detail only. Independent of item 963 (P89): neither imports the other's module.

Reading of the step text (execution detail, target kept). 1. "P80's end-weighted picture at c* (the one that reproduces entry 52's shape)". The end-weighted picture is P81's (step 45, test_mat21_end_source_probe_points_closed_form.py, step 6's q = Q[1 − cos(πx/A)]); P80 is the eddy picture. P81's is the one whose x+0mm column rises toward the box ends as entry 52's does (0.0664 / 0.5035 against entry 52's 0.1040 / 0.6388, 20261109T180259Z_MAT-21-P81-W1.log; it does not reproduce the values). Its history per deposited watt at each c* is P83's _data()["sd"][side]["dep"]["n"] (= p81._data()["SL"][:, idx], test_mat21_field_strength_heating_closed_form.py:144–145). Both c* (1.5 T x-105mm dz-50mm, 3 T x+105mm dz+50mm) carry the same history: P83's (Sym) read 0 on rows 1–40 (20261110T103343Z_MAT-21-P83-W1.log:54–57). So "at c*" is one history, asserted equal on both. 2. θ(t) for P_dep W is P_dep·h(t) by the series' homogeneity (P83's (Sup) 0, :58). The dose is cem43(T_GRID, T_INF + P·h), with cem43 MAT-20's function, src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py:45 (r_above=0.5, r_below=0.25, t_ref=43.0, exact on the piecewise-linear interpolant, :5–15). At 100 W the hottest sample is T_INF + 100·0.00356031 ≈ 20.356 °C, so only the R = 0.25 branch is ever reached; the R = 0.5 branch is stated, not exercised (asserted as a precondition, printed). 3. "(Lim) the quadrature against the analytic antiderivative at B1_BAND". cem43 is the analytic antiderivative per linear segment (dose.py:8–15). The independent quadrature is MAT-20's per-segment adaptive _quad_dose (test_mat20_tuned_heating_dose.py:78, scipy.integrate.quad, epsrel=1e-13) as wrapped by _q_check_g (test_mat21_box_dt_duty125_dose_closed_form.py:131, which also returns the R-swap). (Lim) is _q_check_g's rel at each P, at B1_BAND (= 1e-12, test_imp4_pec_cylinder_closed_form.py:46) instead of its usual DOSE_BAR (1e-10). Backed: the same comparison read 4.833e-16 / 6.247e-16 / 6.442e-16 on P80 / P81 / P83's histories (…P80-W1.log:62, …P81-W1.log:55, …P83-W1.log:63). _quad_dose hard-codes LN_R = ln 0.25 (test_mat21_box_dose_closed_form.py:54), which is valid only below 43 °C: that is reading 2's precondition. 4. (N-lin) "differs from 10 by more than INTERIOR_BAND" is read literally: |r − 10| > INTERIOR_BAND (= 1e-2, test_mat13_transient_perfusion_sphere.py:64), r = excess(10 W)/excess(1 W). The relative form |r/10 − 1| is printed beside it and is not asserted (it is ≈ 1.5× the band, see Controls).

Code. New tests/validation/test_mat21_dose_nonlinear_power_closed_form.py, complex build (P83 imports P79 → P61 / C6 and C33), print prefix MAT21-48. No src/ edit; no landed module edited. Read every signature before use. Never import a fixture or a test_* name. - Holds (import closure, measured for this brief). P83 imports P79 (test_mat21_clinical_probe_reader.py:49–50, which imports P61's test_geo38_f_clinical_box_heating — held with entry 63 until 11-13 — and C6's test_geo38_f_clinical_box_loaded — entry 62's module, xxl 11-14) and C6 directly. So P79, P80, P81 and P83 are all inside the held closure: import them, never edit them. The new module is imported by no queued window. - Module objects: p83 (test_mat21_field_strength_heating_closed_form): _data() (keys sd → per side dep["n"], s, label), SIDES. p75: T_STAR. p80: _cem_bracket (:297). - By name: cem43 (fem_em_solver.thermal.dose); T_GRID, DOSE_BAR, LN_R (test_mat21_box_dose_closed_form); T_INF (test_mat21_box_closed_form); _q_check_g (duty125 module, :131); R_BELOW, T_REF (test_mat20_tuned_heating_dose.py:48–49); B1_BAND, INTERIOR_BAND (as P81 imports them). - Constants (hard-coded with their cites, P86's pattern): P_SET = (0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0) W (the step's); D0_CITED = 4.009592657894245e-11 s (20261020T190033Z_MAT-21-step15-W1-probe-dose-closed-form.log.gz:83); H_TSTAR = "0.00356031" (…P83-W1.log:81, …P81-W1.log:95); P83_DOSE = {"1.5T": ("4.010097e-11", "5.045885e-15"), "3T": ("4.011457e-11", "1.864127e-14")} (…P83-W1.log:88, :92, P83's .7g cem43 and .6e excess). - Histories: h = p83._data()["sd"]["1.5T"]["dep"]["n"] (41 rows, K per deposited watt); h₃ the 3 T one. D0 = cem43(T_GRID, np.full(T_GRID.size, T_INF)) — P83's exact expression (:421), so excess strings tie byte for byte. For each P: th = h * P, cem = cem43(T_GRID, T_INF + th), exc = cem - D0. - The linear term (printed comparand, exact on the interpolant): excess_lin(P) = P·ln 4·R_BELOW^(T_REF − T_INF)·np.trapezoid(h, T_GRID) — the first-order term of R^(43−T_INF−Ph) on the same piecewise-linear history (trapezoid is exact for a linear interpolant). The nonlinearity is excess/excess_lin − 1.

docs.text:
Enumerated by the 11-11 weekly (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10 chain P, P89, lines 5136–5147, "now"; the weekly's own pointer, line 4853: "the ≈ 9 % excess is the 3 T source's shape at c*, a question P89 poses"). Serial on nothing. Family P89, attempt 1 of 4. Step number: §10 says step 48; with P86 holding 47 this brief proposes step 49 and prefix MAT21-49 — the review confirms. No band, tolerance, done-when or target is set or moved. Independent of item 962 (P88): neither imports the other's module.

Reading of the step text (execution detail, target kept). 1. "C33's JSON strings, (K) re-read equal" — the premise is false as worded, and the route is the tracked log. - C33's JSON (/workspace/logs/geo38/c33-1p5t-3t.json, gitignored by .gitignore:82 /logs/) is side() per entry plus the four ratio strings (test_geo38_c33_field_strength_reader.py:112–131, :317–318). It carries no lattice: c*'s SAR10g, the normalisers and the B1 means only. - The 18 lattice SAR10g strings per side live on tracked paths: entry 52 20261103T080009Z_GEO-38-C6.log:12289–12306 and entry 58 20261109T080008Z_GEO-38-C6-3T.log:12238–12255. They are read through C33's own route, the ans:11 page's parse_c6_log loaded by c33._load_page() (P83's route, test_mat21_field_strength_heating_closed_form.py:129–132), never a new regex. This is the §9 digest's "every new step's reader … parses its tracked log". - (K) is that re-read: c33.check_side on each side, the 36 tokens re-formatted .9e equal, and the host C6a node JSONs (c6-node-193.5996.json, c6-node-44.0525.json, which do carry the lattice) through c33.custody_json — custody only: absent prints "absent", never a red. 2. "P80's 10 g-ball sources, one per lattice point". Each lattice point i carries a uniform source on the ball B_i of radius r = c6._a10() (0.013365 m, …P80-W1.log:47) at its box point (p80._lattice()), with strength ∝ its SAR10g. Per deposited watt, q_i = w_i/V_B with w_i = SAR_i/Σ_j SAR_j. ρ, P_acc and the drive amplitude cancel exactly. 3. The closed form (derived here; no src/ edit). analytical.py has no ball source in the Robin box, and its box series are even-only. The construction is the box heat kernel integrated over the ball, split in time at s₀ (Ewald-style): - θ_i(x, t) = (1/ρc)∫₀^{s₀} P∞(|x − p_i|; s) ds + (V_B/k)·Σ_modes F(√Λ r)·Φ(p_i)Φ(x)/𝒩·[e^{−αΛs₀} − e^{−αΛt}]/Λ, for t ≥ s₀. - Modes: per axis a, b both families — even cos(γs/L), γ tan γ = Bi (robin_slab_eigenvalues, analytical.py:1874), 𝒩 = L(γ + sin γ cos γ)/γ (:2179); odd sin(γs/L), γ cot γ = −Bi (robin_slab_odd_eigenvalues, :2307), 𝒩 = L(γ − sin γ cos γ)/γ (:2341). Axis c: even only, because every ball centre and both c* sit at c = 0 (P80 asserted max |c| 0), so every odd-c term carries sin 0 = 0. Λ = Σ_d (γ_d/L_d)². - The ball factor is exact: a product mode is a sum of plane waves with |k|² = Λ, and the ball mean of e^{ik·y} is e^{ik·p}·F(|k|r), F(u) = 3(sin u − u cos u)/u³ — the identity P81's _ball_mean_end uses (test_mat21_end_source_probe_points_closed_form.py:127–132). - The short-time piece neglects the walls. Every ball is ≥ 0.031635 m from a face, so the image factor is ≤ exp(−(2·0.031635)²/(4αs₀)) ≈ e^{−69.7} at s₀ = 100 s (printed). P∞ is the probability that a 3D Gaussian of variance σ² = 2αs about x lies in the ball: for d > 0, ½[erf((r−d)/(σ√2)) + erf((r+d)/(σ√2))] + (σ/(d√(2π)))[e^{−(r+d)²/(2σ²)} − e^{−(r−d)²/(2σ²)}]; at d = 0, erf(w) − (2/√π)w e^{−w²}, w = r/(σ√2). It is integrated by scipy.integrate.quad(…, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-13, limit=200) (_quad_dose's settings). - Truncation: per axis, keep γ/L up to α(γ/L)²s₀ ≥ 40. At s₀ = 100 s that is N = (180, 120, 30) per family (γ_N/L ≥ 1730 / 1780 / 2025 m⁻¹ against the 1670 m⁻¹ needed); the dropped tail is ≤ e^{−40}. - Contraction: with c = 0 everywhere the c-factor is 1/𝒩_c for every ball. So θ₂ = (V_B/k)·Σ_lmn T_lmn W_lm/𝒩_c,n, with W = A·diag(q)·Bᵀ and T = F(√Λ r)·e^{−αΛs₀}·(−expm1(−αΛ(t − s₀)))/Λ: one (2N_a)(2N_b)N_c tensor per (t, s₀). 4. "θ(c*, t*) per deposited watt at each field strength's own c*; the predicted 3 T / 1.5 T ratio printed as power share × shape part". SP = θ₃(c*₃)/θ₁.₅(c*₁.₅), both per deposited watt. Predicted lever = (s₃/s₁.₅)·SP, with s from the .9e tokens (P83's expression, :140). 5. (N-eq) "equal columns ⇒ the shape part is 1 (P83's case reproduced)" — read as mirror-equal. - The two c* are mirror images under (a, b) → (−a, −b) (C33 …C33-W1-n1-r2.log:131), and so are the lattice and the box. - Literally equal columns do not give 1: the 1.5 T column on both sides gives SP ≈ SAR₁.₅(x+105mm dz+50mm)/SAR₁.₅(x−105mm dz−50mm) = 1.349823646/1.378896513 = 0.978916 (…C6.log:12304, :12291), plus neighbour terms. This is printed. - The asserted control is the mirror-equal column (the 3 T weights := the 1.5 T weights at the mirrored label) and the flat column (all w = 1/18, P83's even-source case). Both must give SP = 1.

Code. New tests/validation/test_mat21_lattice_ball_superposition_closed_form.py, complex build (P80 imports P79 → P61 / C6; C33 uses mpi4py), print prefix MAT21-49. Never import a fixture or a test_* name. - Holds (import closure): P80 / P79 import P61's module (held with entry 63) and C6's (entry 62's); C33 imports neither. Import only, never edit. No queued window imports the new module. - Module objects: - c33: _load_page, find_log, check_side, custody_json, ENTRY58_GLOB, ENTRY52_NODE_PF, ENTRY58_NODE_PF, HOST_JSON_DIR. - p80: _lattice (:122, labels in C6 order, box points, off), C52_STAR. - c6: _a10, _lattice. - By name: robin_slab_eigenvalues, robin_slab_odd_eigenvalues; step 0's A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX, HALF, K, H, T_C, RHO_C as RHO_C_0; T_GRID (t* = T_GRID[-1]); B1_BAND, INTERIOR_BAND; scipy.special.erf, scipy.integrate.quad. - Logs: entry 52 = page.SOURCE_LOG; entry 58 = c33.find_log(c33.ENTRY58_GLOB), which must read "tracked". C39 = docs/testing/logs/20261111T103024Z_GEO-38-C39-W1.log: exactly one line matching ccw hotspot point theta per P_acc: (\S+) \| (\S+) \| (\S+)$ (:373, ratio token 4.042515e+00), and one each for ccw ball theta per P_acc (:372, 4.030354e+00) and cw hotspot point theta per P_acc (:384, 4.539718e+00). These are read for the printed reading only. - Constants (cited): P83_S = ("0.05285093", "0.1952049", "3.6935") (…P83-W1.log:75–77); C33_SAR_LEVER = "4.101440e+00" (…C33-W1-n1-r2.log:129); NEEDED_SP = "1.094495" (20261111T104011Z_EX-194.log:66); S0 = 100.0 s; N0 = (180, 120, 30).

Gates (asserted, bands imported; all collected, then asserted — item 668). - Preconditions: - 18 lattice points; labels equal c6._lattice() in order; every point inside the box at c = 0 within P80's 4ε bound; every ball inside (max_d(|p_d| + r − L_d) ≤ 0; P80 read −0.031635 m). - The c* labels from the two parses are x-105mm dz-50mm / x+105mm dz+50mm. - The mirror map is exact: for every lattice point, (−a, −b, 0) is a lattice point by float equality, and it maps c*₁.₅ to c*₃. - t* = T_GRID[-1] ≥ S0. - (K): - c33.check_side passes every check on each side (P83 read 8 / 8, …P83-W1.log:47–48). - The 36 SAR10g tokens re-format .9e equal (P80's (K-lat) form). - The host C6a node JSONs via c33.custody_json: present ⇒ 0 mismatches; absent ⇒ printed. C33's own JSON is named as lattice-free on the line. - (K-s): f"{s:.7g}" per side and f"{s₃/s₁.₅:.5g}" equal P83_S by string (P83's own format strings, :407, :409). - (Lim): the transient at t = 1000·T_C against the steady form, both sides at their c*, ≤ B1_BAND. The steady form is written as its own function: the same split, with T_ss = F·e^{−αΛs₀}/Λ. Predicted ≤ 1e-15 (αΛ_min·1000·T_C ≈ 700). - (Bq), the representation's two truncations, ≤ B1_BAND, on θ₁.₅(c*₁.₅, t*), θ₃(c*₃, t*) and SP: - (i) N0 → 2·N0 at s₀ = 100 s. - (ii) the split identity: s₀ = 100 s → 50 s at N = (250, 160, 40) (γ_N/L ≥ 2407 / 2379 / 2723 m⁻¹ against the 2362 m⁻¹ needed). - (ii) is the anchor: the short-time piece (free-space, independent of the modes) and the modal piece over [50, 100] s must agree. It tests the norms, the parities and the ball factor together. - Predicted (i) ≤ 1e-15 (tail ≤ e^{−40}) and (ii) ≤ 1e-13: quad epsrel 1e-13 on a piece that is ≈ 20 % of the self-term. Margin ≈ 10×; see Negative result.

Controls (asserted, factor 1 at the gate's own band; rule (e)). - (N-eq-m): the 3 T weights replaced by the mirrored 1.5 T weights ⇒ |SP − 1| ≤ 1e-12 (the step's number, = B1_BAND). Predicted ≤ 1e-15: sin(−x) = −sin x, and the odd-a × odd-b signs cancel pairwise. - (N-eq-u): flat weights on both sides ⇒ |SP − 1| ≤ B1_BAND. This is P83's even-source case reproduced. - (c-lit), printed only (predicted, no log backs it): the 1.5 T column on both sides at the two c*, SP ≈ 0.9789, range [0.977, 0.981] (reading 5). Ceiling: none posed.

Printed (🟡 record, no band, ≤ 7 digits; predictions from the cited log lines by this review's arithmetic, a miss outside a range disclosed, never red). - Per side: Σ SAR10g; w(c*) = SAR(c*)/Σ — predicted 0.08182573 (1.5 T) / 0.09035190 (3 T), ± 1e-6 — and the image factor e^{−69.7}. - θ(c*, t*) per deposited watt: the total, the self-ball term and the 17-ball neighbour sum, plus the short-time / modal split. - Predicted total ≈ 0.920 K/W, range [0.89, 0.94] at 1.5 T. Basis: the infinite-medium ball centre at t* is 0.7557 of r²/(2k), × q = 8182.6 W/m³; the Robin faces 45 mm away change it by ≈ 1e-3. - Predicted ≈ 1.016 K/W, range [0.98, 1.04] at 3 T. - Neighbour sum / total ≤ 1e-3 at both: the nearest ball is 100 mm away, against √(αt*) = 20.1 mm. - SP ≈ 1.1042, range [1.103, 1.106], beside the self-only quotient w₃(c*)/w₁.₅(c*) = 1.104199. Their difference is the neighbours' share. - The lever: - predicted 3 T / 1.5 T = share × SP ≈ 4.0784, range [4.074, 4.085]; - beside C39's 4.042515 (ccw point, :373), 4.030354 (ccw ball, :372) and 4.539718 (cw, :384, cw heated at ccw's c*); - beside P83's 3.6935 and C33's SAR lever 4.101440; - SP − 1 against the needed 0.094495 (EX-194 :66): the fraction of the ≈ 9 % the lattice carries, predicted ≈ 1.10, range [1.08, 1.13]. - The lattice-local reading, printed with its caveat: Σ_i (SAR_i/P_acc)·ρ·θ_i(c*) per accepted watt, 3 T over 1.5 T, predicted ≈ 4.1018 [4.100, 4.104] — C33's SAR lever plus neighbours. The balls do not deposit the box's power, so this reading is not per deposited watt. - The verdict line, printed: "lattice resolves the excess" if SP − 1 lies within ± 25 % of 0.094495; else "the excess lives below the lattice's 100 mm spacing" (or above it, if SP − 1 > 1.25 × 0.094495). The weekly reads it; no gate. - The normaliser line: per deposited watt of the 18-ball source; P_dep, P_box, P_acc never mixed; s from the .9e tokens.

Anchor (closed form, named with its function). The volume-mean rise ⟨θ⟩(t) of the six-face Robin box under two sources. - (a) Uniform q = P_dep/V: step 1's triple series, robin_box_transient_temperature (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py, used at tests/validation/test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:52–54), integrated over the box term by term. Its own antiderivative per axis is ∫cos(γs/L)ds/(2L) = sin γ/γ, so ⟨θ⟩_u(t) = (q/k)·Σ_lmn Π_d [c_d·sin γ_d/γ_d]·(1 − e^{−αΛt})/Λ, with c_d = 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) (_axis_data, :61–64), Λ = Σ_d (γ_d/L_d)², and even roots only (robin_slab_eigenvalues). - (b) P89′'s lattice at 1.5 T (degree 1, entry 52's weights p89._data()["w"]["1.5T"]). Only all-even modes survive the box mean, because every odd family integrates to 0. Per ball of power w: ⟨θ_i⟩(t) = (w_i/k)·Σ_even F(√r)·cos(γ_a p_a/L_a)cos(γ_b p_b/L_b)·Π_d c_d (sin γ_d/γ_d)·(1 − e^{−αΛt})/Λ, with F the ball factor (p89._F, test_mat21_lattice_ball_superposition_closed_form.py:148) and r = c6._a10(). This uses (2L sin γ/γ)/𝒩 = c_d with P89's 𝒩 (p89._axis, :154). The series converges absolutely (F ≈ u⁻², sin γ/γ ≈ 1/n), so no time split is needed. - (Bq-split), the P89′ cross-route: the same mean through P89's split at s₀ = 100 s equals s₀·Σw/(ρcV) (the free-space piece, exact to the image factor e^{−69.7}) plus the modal piece's [s₀, t] mean. Both routes agree ≤ B1_BAND.

Reading of the step text (execution detail, target kept). 1. "(Lim) at B1_BAND against the series' own antiderivative". Read as two asserted identities: - (Lim-a) the termwise antiderivative (sin γ/γ per axis) against 64-node Gauss–Legendre quadrature of the same cos modes per axis (separable, so cheap). Both sources, ≤ B1_BAND. - (Lim-∞) ⟨θ⟩ at 1000·T_C against its steady form (the (1 − e^{−αΛt}) factor dropped). Both sources, ≤ B1_BAND. The review may rule on a narrower reading. The weekly names only "the series' own antiderivative". 2. "(N-h): h → 0 gives P_dep·t*/(ρc·V_sub) to 1e-12". With h → 0 the first root γ₀ ≈ √Bi carries all the weight, and (1 − e^{−αΛ₀t})/Λ₀ → αt. The correction is ≈ αΛ₀t*/2 ≈ h·t*·Σ_d(1/L_d)/(2ρc) ≈ 0.010·h. Run at h = 1e-11 W/m²K (predicted residual ≈ 1e-13), both sources. Use −expm1 for 1 − e^{−x}, and check robin_slab_eigenvalues brackets γ₀ ≈ 2e-6 to relative 1e-9 (printed). - V_sub = 8·A·B·C = 0.024570 m³ from step 0's constants (:34). Then 1/(ρcV) = 9.737e-06 K/s/W (SPEC row 3, ans13_…/SPEC.md:100), and P_dep·t*/(ρcV) ≈ 2.7473e-02 K/W at t* = T_GRID[-1] = 2821.5 s. - (N-h) is a negative control with ceiling 1e-12 (the weekly's number, = B1_BAND). 3. "the number P87's print (entry 69's row 5) is read against". SPEC row 5 is ⟨θ⟩(t*) (SPEC.md:102). Entry 69's FEM source is the clinical SAR, not 18 balls. This step prints both closed forms with their ratio; it asserts no comparison with any FEM figure.

docs.title: §9 item 999 — 2026-11-15 (chain P / lane 3 closed form; re-pose of 991, attempt 2 of 4)
docs.text:
Re-pose of BLOCKED item 991 by the 2026-11-15 18:00 daily review under rule (6). MAT-21 step 51, family P91, attempt 2 of 4, print prefix MAT21-51. The target, every band (B1_BAND = 1e-12), the (N-h) ceiling (1e-12), h = 1e-11, the printed ranges and the done-when are item 991's, unchanged. Only three things change: the series form that the (Bq) gates and the records run on, the truncation N that the (N-h) control runs on, and one display line that item 991's own derivation corrects. Serial on nothing. Independent of item 997 (that item edits p89's _c39 reader, which this module does not import at runtime).

Review note (2026-11-15 18:00 daily; provisional, for the 11-16 weekly). R1: the corrected lattice normalisation (Π c_d / V per ball) that attempt 1 derived is accepted as a premise correction, not a target change. R2: (N-h) is fixed on the test side (N = (40, 40, 40), below the first bracket flip at root 53); no src/ edit, and the tiny-Bi bracket in robin_slab_eigenvalues is filed as a reading for the weekly, not a defect, because no wrong value is returned. R3: comparing against the direct sum at 2N₀ sizes N from the measured tail; B1_BAND and the (N-h) ceiling are unchanged. A re-pose keeps its family's count and is not a provisional step: chain P stays 0 of 6. Cost: ≈ 3.8 measured (lane-3 median, recomputed at this review).

Diagnosis of attempt 1 (from the code and W1; no new run).

  1. Why the direct [0, t*] series is algebraic. At an even root, γ sin γ = Bi cos γ gives sin γₙ ≈ ±Bi/γₙ for large n. So both factors are small:
  2. c_n = 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) ≈ 2Bi/γ²;
  3. the box mean sin γ/γ ≈ Bi/γ².

Then a_n = c_n·sin γₙ/γₙ ≤ 2Bi²/(γ³(γ − ½)), which is ∝ γ⁻⁴ and positive. Item 991's "sin γ/γ ≈ 1/n" was wrong.

Every mode with αΛt* ≫ 1 has a saturated time factor (1 − e^{−αΛt})/Λ → 1/Λ ≤ L_d²/γ_d². So the tail of the [0, t*] series is the steady series' tail: terms ∝ γ⁻⁶ per axis, and a tail ∝ N⁻⁵.

Item 991 posed no time split. Its claim of absolute convergence is true, but it does not reach 1e-12 at the brief's N.

Splitting off the steady part does not help. The 3D Robin-box steady mean Σ Π a_d/Λ has no elementary closed form; it is the algebraic series. The cure is a split in time at s₀. On [s₀, t*] every mode carries e^{−αΛs₀}, and the [0, s₀] piece takes a short-time closed form. P89 already does this for (b).

  1. The rigorous tail bound for (a), stated. All a_n > 0, Σ_n a_{d,n} = 1 (the box mean of 1), 1 − e^{−x} ≤ 1, and 1/Λ ≤ L_d²/γ_d². Together these give

T(N) = (1/(kV))·Σ_d Σ_{n>N_d} 2Bi_d² L_d² / (γ_n⁵(γ_n − ½)), γ_n ≥ (n − 1)π,

an upper bound on direct(∞) − direct(N) per deposited watt. Drafter arithmetic, relative to ⟨θ⟩_u:

N bound T(N) measured gap to the split value (40, 40, 40) 4.249e-08 4.214e-08 (80, 80, 80) 1.285e-09 1.282e-09 (360, 240, 60) 3.059e-12 3.055e-12

W1's 40 → 80 step was 4.086e-08, consistent with the first row. The bound is tight. Meeting B1_BAND on the direct route by construction would need N = (402, 284, 84), a 9.6M-entry tensor with a 77M-entry 2N rung. That is too large for smoke. So the direct route is not the gate route for (a).

  1. (N-h) crash: a fixture choice meeting a floating-point edge. It is not a wrong-answer src/ defect.
  2. Root i ≥ 2 of γ sin γ = Bi cos γ sits at (i − 1)π + δ with δ ≈ Bi/((i − 1)π).
  3. At Bi = 5.4e-12 and i = 167, δ ≈ 1.0e-14. That is below ½ ulp(522) ≈ 5.7e-14, so the root cannot be represented apart from the bracket endpoint lo = (i − 1)*np.pi.
  4. f(lo_fl) = (−1)^k(kπ·ε_k − Bi), where ε_k is lo's rounding offset (|ε_k| up to ≈ 2e-16·k). So the sign at lo flips once kπ·ε_k > Bi, and brentq raises.

  5. Measured on the host (numpy, (i − 1)*np.pi as analytical.py:1893 computes it), at h = 1e-11:

    axis L Bi first sign flip at i flips in i ≤ 180 0.325 m 5.417e-12 167 4 0.21 m 3.5e-12 84 11 0.045 m 7.5e-13 53 24

  6. Hence W1: the uniform source's 40 roots passed on every axis, and the lattice's (180, 120, 30) raised.

  7. The function's documented contract (one root per interval for Bi > 0) holds mathematically, and it fails loudly rather than returning a wrong root.
  8. At Bi ≈ 1e-12 the modes n ≥ 2 carry c_n ≈ 2Bi/γ² ≈ 1e-12, and in the time integral their contribution beyond n = 40 is ≈ 1e-16 relative. They need not be resolved past n = 40.
  9. The cheapest fix that keeps the target is therefore module-side: run (N-h) on N = (40, 40, 40) for both sources, below every first flip with margin 13 / 44 / 127 roots. A src/ hardening is posed only as the alternative in ruling R2.

Anchor (closed form, named with its function). Unchanged target: item 991's ⟨θ⟩(t*) under (a) and (b), now through these forms. - (a) Uniform, s₀-split. This rests on an exact product identity. The box survival S(x, τ) under unit initial temperature with Robin faces is Π_d S_d(x_d, τ). Its box mean is Π_d M_d(τ), with M_d(τ) = Σ_n a_{d,n} e^{−α(γ_n/L_d)²τ} (the module's even axis, robin_slab_eigenvalues). Duhamel then gives ⟨θ⟩_u(t) = (q/ρc)∫₀ᵗ Π_d M_d dτ. Split at s₀ = p89.S0 = 100 s:

⟨θ⟩u(t) = (q/ρc)·I_s + (q/k)·Σ{N₀} Π_d a_d · e^{−αΛs₀}·(−expm1(−αΛ(t − s₀)))/Λ.

The modal piece is the module's _tfac(…, s0=S0). I_s = ∫₀^{s₀} Π_d M_d^{sh}(τ) dτ.

M_d^{sh}(τ) = 1 − [erfcx(x) − 1 + 2x/√π]/Bi_d, with x = (h/k)√(ατ). This is the slab mean with each face treated as a semi-infinite Robin solid: surface temperature erfcx(x), with heat lost ∫hθ_s dτ. Its image correction is ≈ e^{−L_d²/(αs₀)} ≤ e^{−141} on the thinnest axis.

I_s is evaluated by 64-node Gauss–Legendre in u = √τ (dτ = 2u du) on [0, √s₀]. x ≤ 0.0632, so the integrand is analytic and its quadrature is exact to roundoff. Drafter: I_s ≈ 99.6540 s.

q = 1/V, so the result is per deposited watt. Modal exponents at N₀ = (180, 120, 30) are αk_N²s₀ = 43.0 / 45.5 / 58.8 (at N = 40 on the long axis it is only 2.04, so the split needs P89's N₀, not SERIES_TERMS). - (b) Lattice, s₀-split, P89's route as attempt 1 coded it. free = s₀Σw/(ρcV) (exact to the image factor e^{−69.7}), plus the module's mean_lattice(…, s0=S0). The display line is corrected, as attempt 1's docstring derived and as R1 asks the review to ratify:

⟨θ_i⟩ = (w_i/(kV))·Σ_even F(√Λ r)·Π_d cos(γ_d p_d/L_d)·Π_d c_d·(time factor).

This is Π c_d / V per ball, not Π c_d sin γ_d/γ_d. The sin γ/γ appears only after a further mean over the source position, which recovers (a). - (S-a), the seam (new identity at the same band, no new band). Per axis, |M_d^{sh}(s₀) − Σ_{n≤N₀_d} a_n e^{−αk_n²s₀}| ≤ B1_BAND, absolute (M ≈ 1). It tests the short-time closed form against the eigen-series where both are converged. Drafter: 2.2e-16 / 3.3e-16 / 2.2e-16.

Gates (asserted; all collected, then asserted). - Unchanged from attempt 1 (green in W1, code untouched): preconditions; even-axis custody; (Lim-a); (Lim-∞) on the direct form (both sides truncated alike); (Point); Π > 0. - (S-a) as above. Predicted ≤ 4e-16. - (Bq-N)(a): split(N₀) vs split(2N₀), relative, ≤ B1_BAND. Drafter: 1.4e-16 (0.02521149463867279 vs …672793). - (Bq-N)(b): split(N₀) vs split(2N₀), relative, ≤ B1_BAND. Predicted ≲ 1e-15: the tail is ≈ e^{−43} times c·F/Λ prefactors of 1e-11 or less. - (Bq-split)(b), item 991's cross-route kept: P89's split at N₀ vs the direct mean at 2N₀ = (360, 240, 60), ≤ B1_BAND. N is sized to the measured tail: W1's own values give |2.7130840381052967e-02 − 2.7130840381064007e-02| / ⟨θ⟩ = 4.07e-13, with the N₀ step at 1.58e-10. The code is unchanged, so the reading is bit-reproducible. Margin 2.46×. No (b) bound is claimed, because the ball factor's oscillation makes the (a)-style bound loose. - Printed only (not asserted): the (a) direct gaps to split(N₀) at (40, 40, 40) and (80, 80, 80), each beside T(N), with the flag "gap ≤ T". This checks the bound to within 1 % and must not become an assertion. Also print the N that T needs, (402, 284, 84), stated as not run.

Negative control (asserted, factor 1, ceiling computed). - (N-h) as in item 991: |⟨θ⟩/(P_dep t*/(ρcV)) − 1| ≤ 1e-12 at h = 1e-11 (never raised), both sources, on the direct route, on N_h = (40, 40, 40) for both. - It stays on the direct route because the short-time form is ill-conditioned at Bi ≈ 1e-12: erfcx(x) − 1 + 2x/√π ≈ x², with x ≈ 6e-14, cancels to noise. There the direct tail ∝ Bi² is negligible. - Predicted (a): 1.014e-13, which is hAt*/(2ρcV) = 1.015e-13 (drafter). Predicted (b): range [0, 1.2e-13]. The balls lose less than the uniform source, and root-ulp noise in c_n for n ≥ 2 is ≲ 3e-14. - Ceiling arithmetic: the reachable floor is ≈ 1e-13, so the 1e-12 ceiling has ≈ 10× margin. A contraction blind to h would read exactly 0 at every h. At step 0's h = 10 the same ratio reads the W1 surface fractions 0.082302 / 0.012437, a separation of ≈ 8e11 / ≈ 1e11 between the two h. γ₀'s brentq precision (xtol 1e-15, so relative ≈ 4e-10) contributes ≈ 1e-22. - Print per axis γ₀, √Bi, γ₀²/Bi − 1 (the small-Bi asymptote γ₀² ≈ Bi(1 − Bi/3), expected ≈ −Bi/3 plus the root's ≈ 1e-9) and the residual/Bi as attempt 1 did. Also print "N_h below first bracket flip i = 167 / 84 / 53 (h = 1e-11)".

Predicted, all inside item 991's ranges as W1 already was: - ⟨θ⟩_u(t*) 0.02521149 K/W (split 0.025211494639; W1 direct 0.02521149358); - ⟨θ⟩_lat(t*) 0.02713084 K/W; - ratio 1.076130; - surface fractions 0.082302 / 0.012437; - I_s and its ratio to s₀; - the normaliser line, unchanged.

The W1 log is already on main. - Edit only that module: - add m_short(L, tau, h=H) (scipy.special.erfcx), i_short(s0) (GL64 in √τ), mean_uniform_split(t, n=N_L, s0=p89.S0), the (S-a) gate, and the T(N) print; - re-point (Bq-N)(a)/(b) and the two records to the split routes; - change (Bq-split)'s direct comparand from l0 (N₀) to l1 (2N₀); - set N_H = N_U in test_negative_control_small_h (pass n=N_H to both mean_uniform and mean_lattice); - add the docstring sentences (the diagnosis, the product identity, the corrected lattice line, citing this item). - No src/ edit. docs.title: §9 item 646 — 2026-10-25 (§9 rule (5) lane 3, MAT-3 step 1b: a two-pole Cole–Cole medium, α > 0, on TH-6's plane wave)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-25 18:00 daily review (lane-3 fact sheet). Lane 3 lists MAT-3 by name. The anchor is the closed-form plane wave k = k₀√ε̂(ω) (the same as TH-6's and step 1's), with ε̂ the Cole–Cole sum (Cole & Cole 1941, as cited in src/fem_em_solver/materials/dispersion.py). The band is TH-6's 5 %, imported. Nothing here sets or moves a band, tolerance, record, Done-when or target. Why: step 1's FEM gate runs one Debye pole (α = 0), so no FEM run has exercised a broadened pole (α > 0) or more than one pole. Those are the cases Gabriel tissues use, and the evaluator's (jωτ)^(1−α) polar branch (dispersion.py:110–113) has only been tested by numpy identities. The parameters are synthetic, as step 1's were, so the step needs no table.

The medium (fixed by this brief; the executor re-derives the predictions in W0). ColeColeMaterial(epsilon_inf=4.0, poles=((50.0, 1/(2π·100 MHz), 0.30), (4000.0, 1/(2π·1 MHz), 0.35)), sigma_ionic=0.2). This is a muscle-like shape: a γ-like pole near 100 MHz and a large β-like pole near 1 MHz, both broadened. Predictions from the formula, computed by this review with the standard library:

f ε̂ α_k (Np/m) β_k (rad/m) Debye-reduced (α_n → 0) α_k miss wrong-f α_k miss 63.87 MHz 181.505 − 283.983j 11.8044 21.5541 17.15 % — 127.74 MHz 118.420 − 182.618j 18.8581 34.7047 19.91 % 29.77 % (ε̂(63.87) frozen, solved at 127.74)

λ at 127.74 MHz is 2π/34.70 ≈ 0.181 m. At 24³ on the 0.1 m box that is ≈ 43 cells per wavelength; step 1 had ≈ 61 at β = 24.4.

Anchors (asserted, TH-6's imported 5 % band BAND from step 1's module): - (Ev) complex_permittivity(f) equals an independent standard-library evaluation of ε∞ + Σ Δεₙ/(1 + (jωτₙ)^(1−αₙ)) − jσ/(ωε₀), written in the test with cmath and (1j*w*tau)**(1-alpha) (principal branch, which is the evaluator's polar form for ωτ > 0), to ≤ 1e-12 relative at both frequencies. Then step 1's _truth cross-checks: _wavenumber / _analytic_alpha_beta from TH-6's module at the frozen (σ_eff, ε′) equal k₀√ε̂ to 1e-12 / 1e-10. - (i) 127.74 MHz, 12³ → 24³: rel L2 decreasing, rate > 0.9, 24³ rel L2 < BAND, α_k and β_k within BAND at 24³. - (ii) 63.87 MHz, 24³: α_k and β_k within BAND.

Negative controls (asserted, 16³, each a self-consistent solve; ceilings computed above): - (a′) Debye-reduced: the same Δε, τ and σ with every αₙ = 0 (ColeColeMaterial.debye(4.0, poles=((50.0, τ₁), (4000.0, τ₂)), sigma_ionic=0.2)), solved at 127.74 MHz, misses the Cole–Cole α_k by > BAND. The closed-form ceiling is 19.91 %, ≈ 4× the band. This is the control that a broadening-blind evaluator (α ignored) would fail. - (b′) wrong frequency: ε̂(63.87 MHz) frozen and solved at 127.74 MHz misses α_k by > BAND (ceiling 29.77 %). - The β_k misses of both controls are printed only, as step 1 does.

Route — a new module, nothing edited. tests/validation/test_mat3_cole_cole_plane_wave.py, modelled on tests/validation/test_mat3_debye_plane_wave.py. Import by name from it: F_HIGH, F_LOW, BAND. From tests/validation/test_lossy_plane_wave.py import MU_R, _analytic_alpha_beta, _solve_plane_wave, _wavenumber. From fem_em_solver.materials import ColeColeMaterial. Write the module's own _truth(f, material) and _solve(n, f, material, material_f=None) taking the material as an argument; do not reuse step 1's, which close over DEBYE. Never edit step 1's module, TH-6's, or dispersion.py.

Windows. - W0 (smoke, -n 1, complex): the (Ev) node alone, plus printing the table above (ε̂, α_k, β_k and both ceilings). No mesh. Assert the two ceilings > 2 × BAND before any FEM window, so a control that cannot miss is caught for free. - W1 (standard, -n 2, complex, timeout -k 30 180), after docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-3-step1b-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && cd /workspace && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_mat3_cole_cole_plane_wave.py tests/validation/test_mat3_debye_plane_wave.py -v -s --tb=short'". Over 180 s is a kill: park, never raise the timeout.

The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped.

Traps already paid for. - (jωτ)^(1−α) must be the principal branch with arg = π(1−α)/2. A (w*tau)**(1-alpha) * 1j**(1-alpha) spelling is the same. A (1j*w*tau)**(-(alpha-1)) sign slip conjugates the pole, and (Ev) is there to catch it. - e^{+jωt}: the ionic term is −jσ/(ωε₀), and Im k < 0 on the decaying wave (step 1's _truth asserts k.imag < 0). - ufl.max_value and ordering comparisons on complex operands do not compile (OPS-22). The material enters only through HomogeneousMaterial, so no new UFL is needed. - assemble_scalar is rank-local, so reduce before asserting. pytest captures prints without -s. - Never pipe the harness command, and never delete a log.

docs.text:
MAT-5 step 3: σ(T) fed back on P1's fixture, Phase 8 subgoal (8d) (implementer; heavy by ceiling, -n 2, complex; ≈ 23 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min; depends on nothing). It is the first step of the family, so this is attempt 1 of 4.

P1's fixture. It is MAT-15 step 1, §10 chain P1 (docs/planning/plan-archive.md:36414–36419; tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py). The EM side is ANS-2's 10 MHz loaded F-small birdcage on the 0.0025 m phantom rung: 199 920 / 58 866 cells, a σ = 800 S/m wire, and saline phantom σ₀ = SALINE_SIGMA 0.5 S/m, εᵣ 78 (test_lossy_sphere_fullwave.py:92–93). The thermal side is the tag-3 submesh with Robin cooling on every exterior facet: gel K_GEL 0.6, H_GEL 10, T_INF 20 (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:82–84), Bi = 0.5. The normalisation is G = 1 W / P₁. This item uses drive k = 0 (P1) only. The C4 rotation is already MAT-15's and is not re-bought here.

Formulation (pinned here). The coupling is a steady Picard fixed point. A transient trajectory with σ(T(t)) would need one EM solve per time step, which is out of reach. Let θ = T − 20, let Π₀ be the DG0 interpolant on the sub (step 2's t_dg0.interpolate), and let S be solve_steady_conduction(sub, ft, k=K_GEL, h=H_GEL, t_inf=T_INF, robin_tag=ROBIN_TAG, degree=1). The map is Φ(θ) = S[G·½σ(θ)|E(σ(θ))|²], with σ(θ) = σ₀[1 + α Π₀θ] on tag 3 only. The law is LinearTemperatureConductivity(sigma_ref=SALINE_SIGMA, alpha_per_k=ALPHA, t_ref=T_INF), with α = ALPHA 0.02 /K imported from tests/materials/test_mat5_step2_lumped_root.py:54 (an input, not a material claim). E is re-solved on every iterate through P1's own lumped-sheet path, _solve_driven(sweep, "P1") (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:142). G is fixed once, from iterate 1 (σ ≡ σ₀): never renormalise per iterate, because a per-iterate G = 1/P_diss removes the feedback being measured. θ₀ = 0, N = 8 iterates, no relaxation. The loop lives in the test, as in step 2: thermal/steady.py's Picard routine has no per-iterate hook.

Code. - (1) Additive knob, unset-identical. Add TimeHarmonicSolver.solve(..., sigma_field_hook=None) in src/fem_em_solver/core/time_harmonic.py:393. When the hook is not None, it is called as sigma_field_hook(sigma_field) immediately after build_material_fields (:468–475) and before bilinear_form (:490). It mutates the parent DG0 σ in place, so fields.sigma_field (:749) is the field that was solved and that mean_sar reads. With None no line executes, so the assembled forms are the gated ones. The docstring cites this item. - (2) Add the same keyword to the test helper _solve_driven(sweep, driven_port_id, degree=None, sigma_field_hook=None), passed through to solver.solve. Every existing caller passes nothing. - (3) New tests/solver/test_sigma_field_hook.py, built on test_time_harmonic_smoke.py's _smoke_mesh(0.03, comm): SIGMA 0.7, 127.74 MHz, an axial drive on tag 1. It has three cases: - (a) no hook against an identity hook (each cell rewritten with its own value): np.array_equal on the owned E coefficients; - (b) a doubling hook: fields.sigma_field reads exactly 2 × 0.7 on every owned cell; - (c) the same doubling hook moves ‖E‖ by > 1e-6 relative. This is a control, predicted O(1e-1) and printed. - (4) New tests/validation/test_mat5_coil_driven_sigma_feedback.py, with two module-scoped fixtures, alpha0 (W1) and coupled (W2). Each builds build_four_port_sweep(phantom_resolution=PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG, build_only=True) (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:516–529; P1's mesh, without the 4-port sweep's solves). It imports the following: - _tag_submesh, _cell_average_dg0_tag, _cn, _e_prime, P1_RECORD_W, K_GEL, H_GEL, T_INF from P1's module; - _robin_tags, _to_sub, _allsum, _say, ROBIN_TAG, B_BAND, C_BAND from MAT-10; - _sub_to_parent, L0_BAND, D_BAND, S_BAND from step 2 (test_mat5_em_coupled_sphere.py:104,107,108,117); - E_BAND from MAT-12. The σ write is sigma_field_hook=lambda sf: _sub_to_parent(sf, sig_sub, parent_ids). It goes cell → dof through both dofmaps, never dof = cell. The source is step 1's G·½σ|E|² DG0 cell average on tag 3, transferred by _to_sub.

Anchors (asserted). - (R0a) α = 0, in-run: the hook path equals P1's path. Compare _solve_driven(sweep, "P1") with no hook against the same call with a hook writing σ ≡ σ₀ through _sub_to_parent. The checks are |P_diss,hook/P_diss − 1| and ‖q_h,hook − q_h‖{L2(sub)}/‖q_h‖ ≤ L0_BAND 1e-9. Predicted: 0.0, because the matrix is identical and the solve is in-process. - (R0b) α = 0 reproduces P1's records, at REPRO_BAND 1e-9 (new constant, relative). The band is above ½ ulp of every compared print (13 digits, ≤ 1e-13 relative). It is also ≈ 190× above the measured cross-run spread of P₁ over six runs: 5.503204728583e-08 … 612e-08, ≤ 5.3e-12 (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1925, 20261002T112729Z_EX-79-mat15-regate.log:1925, 20261004T141433Z_ANS-9-step1a-mat15-regate.log:1925). Complex MUMPS at -n 2 is not bit-reproducible across processes (OPS-43, known-issues 2026-09-10), so no cross-run comparison is bitwise. The records: - P₁ against P1_RECORD_W 5.503204728588e-08 (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:97); - CN N = 40 through P1's _cn on iterate 1's q_h: (E′)'s stored 7.657997570402e-01 W and surface 2.342002429598e-01 W (…123309Z…W1.log:1930, new constants P1_E_STORED_W, P1_E_SURFACE_W; the other two runs read 7.657997570404 / 405e-01, ≤ 4e-13); - mean θ(t*) 1.153314 K (:1929). It is printed to 6 decimals, so it is compared at ½ ulp = 5e-7 K absolute, never tighter; - V_sub against V_SUB_RECORD_M3 at P1's V_BAND 1e-10 (:96,98). - (R0c) α = 0 map: the residual vanishes. Two Picard iterates with α = 0 give ‖θ₂ − θ₁‖/‖θ₁‖ ≤ 1e-12. Predicted 0.0: the map is constant, and the in-run solve is identical. - (D0) The hook touches only the phantom. Rank-reduced max |σ_hooked − σ_built| over non-tag-3 owned cells = 0 exactly. This covers the conductor's 800 S/m and the air's 0. - (K) Contraction against the linearised prediction (§10: within 10 %). δ_k = θ_k − θ{k−1} on the sub (P1), and the signed Picard ratio is ρ_k = ⟨δ_{k+1}, δ_k⟩/⟨δ_k, δ_k⟩ in L2(sub), rank-reduced. The gate is |ρ₄/μ_pred − 1| ≤ 0.10. ρ₄ = ⟨δ₅, δ₄⟩/‖δ₄‖², chosen early enough that ‖δ₅‖ stays ≫ solver noise even at μ ≈ 0.01. Every ρ_k and the surface-mean increment ratio (step 2's metric) are printed. - What μ_pred is. It is the dominant eigenvalue of the Jacobian of Φ at the fixed point, with E re-solved: J v = S[G·(½·σ₀α Π₀v·|E*|² + σ*·Re(E*·conj δE[σ₀α Π₀v]))], where δE is the field response to the conductivity perturbation. With E frozen, J reduces to S[α σ₀ G ½|E*|² Π₀v], whose eigenvalue is ≈ α·θ̄ — step 1's (mR/λ₁)² generalised. The δE term is why it must be computed and not quoted. - How μ_pred is computed. By finite-difference J-vector products on the same mesh at the base θ_b = θ₇: Jv ≈ [Φ(θ_b + εv) − θ₈]/ε, with θ₈ = Φ(θ₇) from the Picard run. v is L2-normalised so that εv has RMS 1e-2 K. The truncation is O(αε) ≈ 2e-4, and the round-off ≈ 1e-12·6 K/1e-2 ≈ 6e-10. Power iteration runs from v₀ ≡ 1 (not the Picard direction), M = 5 steps (5 EM + 5 Robin solves), with μ_j = ⟨Jv_j, v_j⟩/⟨v_j, v_j⟩ and μ_pred = μ₅. - (K-conv) |μ₅/μ₄ − 1| ≤ 1e-2, predicted ≤ 1e-3. - (M0) |μ_pred| ≥ 5e-3. This is the floor that makes (K) a measurement and not noise. - (F) The fixed point converged: ‖δ₈‖/‖θ₈‖ ≤ S_BAND 1e-3. Predicted ≈ μ⁷, below 1e-6. - Energy identity at the fixed point (iterate 8), at the imported bands: - (E*) |∮h θ₈ dS − G·P_diss,8|/(G·P_diss,8) ≤ C_BAND 1e-9. This is EM-deposited power against convected power, with P_diss from mean_sar(…, sigma=fields.sigma_field, subdomain_ids=PHANTOM_CELL_TAG); - (B′) ∫_sub q_h dV = G·P_diss,8 ≤ B_BAND 1e-10; - (C′) convected_power = source_power ≤ C_BAND; - (D′) the σ transfer moment ∫σ x·x dV, parent tag 3 against sub, ≤ D_BAND 1e-10.

Printed (predicted). - μ_pred in [+0.03, +0.14]. The estimate: a 1 W steady state has surface-mean θ = 1/(h·∮dS) = 4.83 K and θ̄ ≈ 5–6.5 K, so the frozen-E factor μ_E ≈ α·θ̄ ≈ 0.10–0.13. The eddy part of E is σ-independent at a/δ ≈ 0.13, while the conservative part goes as 1/σ, so it scales μ by c ∈ [0.3, 1.05]. - ρ₁ … ρ₇. - The steady α = 0 state, a new record: θ̄, θ_s and max θ. - θ̄₈/θ̄₁ − 1, predicted ≈ μ/(1 − μ) ≈ 3–16 %. - σ̄₈, P_diss,8/P₁, the EM seconds per solve and peak RSS summed over ranks.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (N1) frozen σ₀, asserted. Feeding σ(T₀) on every iterate is the α = 0 map, so its contraction factor is exactly 0, which (R0c) asserts to ≤ 1e-12. Its miss of (K) is therefore |0 − μ_pred|/|μ_pred| = 1.000 exactly. That is 10× the 10 % band, and it is the ceiling for any map that carries no feedback. In W2 the separation is carried by (M0): |μ_pred| ≥ 5e-3 makes the frozen ratio's miss ≥ 1.0 relative. - (N2) frozen-|E| prediction, predicted and printed, not asserted. μ_E is a thermal-only power iteration at θ_b using E₈: J_E v = S[α σ₀ G ½|E₈|² Π₀v], M = 5, under 1 s each. Its separation |μ_E/μ_pred − 1| is the δE share, predicted 0–50 %. No ceiling can be computed before the run, so it is not a gate. If it lands inside 10 %, the journal says that (K) cannot tell a re-solved E from a frozen one on this fixture. - (N3) the hook's own control: W0's doubling hook moves E by > 1e-6, asserted.

Windows (complex; foreground; Bash timeout: 660000; container timeout -k 30 590 on heavy windows). - First, two checks. pgrep -c python3 in the container must read 0. Then run the orphan sweep as one bare call: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-5-step3-cache-sweep "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /root/.cache/fenics && for c in libffcx_*.c; do s=\${c%.c}; ls \$s.*.so >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo orphan \$s; rm -f \$s.c \$s.c.cached \$s.o; }; done; echo sweep done'" - W0, the knob (standard; predicted ≤ 60 s; the smoke fixture is 1 405 cells). It runs at -n 1 because the (a) bitwise check is defined there (OPS-43): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-5-step3-W0-hook "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 170 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/solver/test_sigma_field_hook.py tests/solver/test_time_harmonic_smoke.py::test_time_harmonic_smoke_solve_conserves_real_power -s -v --tb=short'" - W0b, the core closed-form re-gate (added by the 18:00 review, binding — rule (c)). The hook edits core/time_harmonic.py, which every EM gate imports, so TH-6's lossy plane-wave module re-runs green through the harness in the same slot, after the edit and before W1: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh MAT-5-step3-W0b-th6 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_lossy_plane_wave.py -s -v --tb=short'". Traps. - G is fixed from iterate 1. A per-iterate normalisation silently zeroes the coupling. - σ goes on tag 3 only, through _sub_to_parent, so the conductor's 800 S/m is never touched ((D0)). docs.title: MAT-8 — Finite-wire correction to the Dodd–Deeds closed form
docs.text: Finite-wire correction to the Dodd–Deeds closed form — eq. (1) of utils/dodd_deeds.py evaluated for a filament; the fixture is a 5 mm wire whose cross-section spans lift-off 17.5–22.5 mm and radius 37.5–42.5 mm, a second-order-in-r/a (≈ 0.06) modelling term nobody has quantified and the floor under any sub-0.5% ΔR claim (ANS-1 adjudication, 2026-09-02) | ✅ (scoped 2026-09-02 weekly review; smoke, closed form only, no solve. Add coil_impedance_change_finite_wire(f, a, h, σ, r_wire) averaging eq. (1) over the uniform-current disc (2-D quadrature in the wire cross-section, mutual kernel already in the module). Anchors: (i) r_wire → 0 recovers the filament value to 1e-8 relative (asserted, three radii 1e-4/1e-5/1e-6 m); (ii) the perfect-conductor limit of the corrected form equals the disc-averaged image mutual inductance from utils/analytical.py to 1e-6 (the same constant-pinning check step 1 used); (iii) the correction at the fixture's r_wire = 0.0025 is printed and recorded, ungated, beside the FEM ΔR's 1.58% / 0.28% — the reading everyone wants is whether it is 0.1% or 0.5%. Negative control: the correction changes sign of the ΔX term's second derivative … no — keep it simple: the correction vanishes for h ≫ r_wire faster than (r/a)² (assert monotone decay across three lift-offs). Cost < 30 s. Scope: a closed-form term and a record; no gate re-registers on it until MAT-6 step 11 lands. Negative result: a limit not recovering is a bug in the quadrature, not physics) — ✅ 2026-09-02 (07:30 slot). coil_impedance_change_finite_wire + image_limit_inductance_change_finite_wire added to utils/dodd_deeds.py (purely additive, 198 lines, nothing existing modified); 7 asserts in tests/validation/test_dodd_deeds_finite_wire.py. The kernel factorises — the generalised eq. (1) is separable in source and observation filament, so the double disc average is one 2-D fixed Gauss–Legendre polar rule applied twice (ΔZ = jωπμ₀∫Γ(α)F(α)²dα), never a 4-D quadrature. Measured (20260902T123618Z_MAT-8.log:42–87, 7 passed, Status 0, 4 s — smoke by footer): r_wire = 0 reproduces the filament form to 1.785e-16; (i) r→0 residuals 2.2222e-06 / 2.2222e-08 / 2.2222e-10 at r = 1e-4/1e-5/1e-6 with decade ratios 100.0001 / 100.0002; GL 16×16 vs 24×24 9.819e-15; (ii) PEC limit vs the 4-D elliptic disc-averaged image mutual 5.7833e-08 (ΔL −1.9786839059e-08 vs −1.9786840203e-08 H) with spurious-loss ratio 5.78e-08. (iii) The ungated record, MAT-6 fixture (10 MHz, a = 0.04, h = 0.02, σ = 100, r_wire = 0.0025, r/a = 0.0625): ΔR 3.22596150e-01 → 3.22967899e-01 Ω, correction +0.115237%; ΔX −6.15867486e-01 → −6.16759345e-01 Ω, +0.144814%. So the answer to "0.1% or 0.5%" is 0.115% on ΔR — negligible against the 1.58% production discrepancy but ≈ 41% of the 0.2829% step-8 slab-refined one, which MAT-6 step 11 must account for. Two scoping deviations, both forced by measurement and neither a loosened bound. (1) Anchor (i) as scoped is arithmetically impossible: the r→0 residual is the leading finite-wire term and scales as exactly r² (ratios above), so a 1e-8 bound at r = 1e-4 would require the very correction this chunk computes to be absent; the plan's bound is asserted at the tightest radius (r = 1e-6, 2.2222e-10) plus the second-order rate, which is strictly stronger than a single tolerance. (2) The scoped negative control's premise is false — the correction does not decay with lift-off, it rises monotonically (1.152e-3 → 1.946e-3 across h = 20…640 mm) to the closed-form limit r_wire²/(2a²) = 1.953125e-03: the coupling's lift-off dependence vanishes, but the wire's own mean-square-radius shift is a property of the loop, not of the half-space. Replaced by asserting monotone increase, every value below the closed form, monotone gap closure, and agreement to 0.38% at h = 640 mm — a closed-form anchor where the scoped control was only a monotonicity check. Both deviations are documented verbatim in the test docstrings with log filenames (MAG-10/MAG-15 precedent) and are the review's to ratify. Regression 20260902T123643Z_MAT-8.log: 14 passed, 3 skipped with test_dodd_deeds_impedance.py (the 3 are complex-only FEM tests), Status 0, 4 s. Scope held: no gate re-registers, no band moves, MAT-6 stays ✅ at 1.58%, ANS-1 untouched. Audited 2026-09-02 10:30 review — auditor PASS on all eight checks: the record log's Commit: is the closing commit's parent, 15 of 15 digits traced to 20260902T123618Z_MAT-8.log:42–91 (the review itself re-read :71–72, +0.115237%), the dodd_deeds.py diff is + lines only, anchors (i)/(ii) are asserts at test_dodd_deeds_finite_wire.py:101,130,165–166, and the 4 s footer sits inside the declared smoke ceiling. Both scoping deviations are ratified: an r² residual cannot meet 1e-8 at r = 1e-4 by arithmetic, and a bound at the tightest radius plus the asserted second-order rate is stronger than the single tolerance; and a control whose premise the measurement refutes is correctly replaced by the closed-form limit r_wire²/(2a²) it actually converges to — a sharper anchor, not a loosened one. One correction to the slot's journal: the sign. Step 8's slab-refined FEM reads −0.2829% — below the filament form — and the finite-wire term raises the closed form by 0.115%, so against the corrected form the refined discrepancy is ≈ −0.40%, not "nearer 0.17%"; the 10 MHz h → 0 bracket shifts to ≈ [−2.26%, −1.02%]. MAT-6 step 11's framing is annotated accordingly. The module docstring's "Tier: standard" is corrected to smoke in this review's commit.

docs.title: MAT-9 — Steady heat conduction with a volumetric source and a convective boundary
docs.text: Steady heat conduction with a volumetric source and a convective boundary — Phase 8 step 1, gel regime (§9 rule (5) lane 3; opened by the 2026-09-28 18:00 daily review under lane 3's closed-form licence — the weekly ratifies or re-homes it, dashboard). fem_em_solver.thermal.steady: −∇·(k∇T) = Q in Ω, −k ∂ₙT = h(T − T∞) on ∂Ω, Lagrange P1/P2, real build. Done-when, step 1: on a homogeneous ball, T = T∞ + QR/(3h) + Q(R² − r²)/(6k) (Incropera, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, §3.5 / App. C; Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids, ch. IX — the executor pins equation numbers in the docstring) at interior relative L2 ≤ 1 %, P1 L2 rate ≥ 1.7 on a ratio-2 whole-ball ladder, and ∫Q dV = ∮h(T − T∞) dS to ≤ 1e-9, each with a control. Step 2: transient (the sphere's eigen-series or a 1-D Green's function). docs.title: OPS-26 — Systematic dolfinx-0.11 migration completeness sweep
docs.text: Systematic dolfinx-0.11 migration completeness sweep — re-run OPS-17's "observed in a completed run" census on the 0.11 image and statically sweep src/ for un-migrated call sites. Two silently-broken gates have already been found by examples rather than by the upgrade's own re-gate (TH-9 cavity, OPS-24; straight-wire h-refinement, red on main, found 2026-08-25 by mag:6); a third is likelier than not. Commissioned 2026-08-25 by operator directive, interactive session — queue at the next review. Queued 2026-08-25 10:30 review: step 1 is §9 item 3; step 2 held until step 1's site list lands. Step 1 ✅ 2026-08-25, 15:00 slot — src/tests clean at 434 call sites / 29 APIs, negative control binding and passing, two survivors filed in scripts/probes/; step 2 (execution census) is now unblocked. Step 2 leg (a) DONE 2026-08-27 (four consecutive slots, 19:30 → 00:00) — the seven cheap roots at 184 / 189 observed (182 green, 2 red), 5 deferred, every deferral with a substantive reason and 182 + 2 + 5 = 189; two reds and one rank-dependent deadlock filed in known-issues (all three carry the 0.11 "overlapping facets" string on different generators — owner GEO-23, commissioned by the 03:00 review), one dead module filed. The fix that unstuck tests/solver (0 → 47/51 in ≈220 s) was one command per module; leg (b) adopts it from the start. Step 2 stays 🟡 on leg (b) (§9 item 1). Step 2 leg (b) PARTIAL 2026-08-27 (04:30 slot) — denominator re-derived at 289 / 63 modules (validation 272/59, ports 17/4); 22 observed (19 green, 3 red), 267 deferred, tests/ports complete at 17/17, tests/validation at 5/272. New defect class found (*finding 12**): tests/ports/test_port_orientation_sensitivity.py is red because OPS-14's rank-safety comm.allgather outgrew its _DummyComm double — not a 0.11 break, and invisible to step 1's static sweep by construction. The owed materials complex conversion failed onto a fifth GEO-23 "overlapping facets" site, the second rank-dependent one; leg (a)'s 184/189 is unchanged with that name's deferral reason upgraded. Two known-issues entries filed. Leg (c) owns the ≈267-name tests/validation remainder.* Step 2 leg (b) PARTIAL, second slot 2026-08-27 (06:00) — 139 / 289 observed (136 green, 3 red), 150 deferred; tests/validation 5 → 122 of 272, this slot's 117 names all green, twenty-seven module-per-command runs, no batching, no red, no no-footer deferral, no exit 124, 2 028 s. Finding 15: grep -L complex tests/validation/test_*.py returns 6 of 59 — 53 modules are complex-gated, so the real build scores them as runtime skips, which is the structural reason attempt 1 banked 5 names; running the complex build for the 53 and the real build for the 6 banked 117 in one slot at the cost of one zero-compute grep, and all 6 real-build modules are now green, so the remainder is entirely complex work. Finding 16: cost is concentrated, not spread — gap-voltage 483 s + circular-loop 350 s are 41% of the slot for 20% of its names — and thirteen 0.11 prices are banked for leg (c). Finding 17: test_circular_loop.py, which stopped OPS-17 (b2) attempts 1–2 with the JIT failure that commissioned OPS-22, is 3 passed in 348.74s complex — the fixture fix holds on 0.11. Leg (c) owns the remaining 150 names over 28 modules (coil_loading_* 58, dodd_deeds_* 38, birdcage 32, straight-wire 7, a 13-name cheap remainder, the one complex-only skip). Step 2 leg (c) PARTIAL 2026-08-27 (07:30 slot) — 188 / 289 observed (184 green, 4 red), 101 deferred; tests/validation 122 → 171 of 272, fourteen module-per-command runs, 1 874 s. The birdcage PORT-9/PORT-11 block is complete at 32/32 green for 593 s (18.5 s/name, the census's best rate — priced blocks before unpriced cheap tails is what bought the slot 49 names). Finding 18 — leg (b)'s build classifier is unsound and its failure mode is invisible to the fail-closed control: grep -L complex misfiled the real-build magnetostatics module test_straight_wire.py as complex-gated on a comment at line 94, and running it in the complex build produced a footered Status-1 red (TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'complex' and 'float', 3 failed / 4 passed, 192 s) indistinguishable from a genuine red; in the real build the same module is 7 passed, Status 0, 314 s. Sound classifier, now used: grep the actual gate (complex_mode|requires_complex|is_complex|skipif). Finding 19 (red, filed): leg (b)'s owed complex conversion of test_geometry_floor_discriminator.py lands on a genuine red — it asserts the pre-OPS-18 128 MHz record 1.8260% and measures OPS-18's 1.7686% (3.14% > 1%); a stale constant, not a TH-10 finding. Finding 20: test_helmholtz_v2.py, the OPS-17 (b2) attempt-2 hang, is 1 passed in 1.24s in the real build — the hang was a finding-18-class build-gate artifact. Finding 21: test_port_gap_voltage_padding.py, the OPS-17 (b2) formal deferral, re-priced not inherited — Status 124 at 400 s with zero PASSED/FAILED lines printed, i.e. it completed none of its 2 tests in the window; deferral upgraded from inherited to measured. Leg (d) owns the remaining 101 names over 16 modules: coil_loading_* 58, dodd_deeds_* 38, test_port_systematics_composition.py 3, and finding 21's 2. Step 2 leg (d) PARTIAL 2026-08-27 (09:00 slot) — 207 / 289 observed (202 green, 5 red), 82 deferred; tests/validation 171 → 190 of 272, four module-per-command runs, 704 s, three footered (Status 0/0/1) and one Status 124. Finding 23 (red, filed): test_coil_loading_larmor_mesh_cache.py::test_the_cached_rung_is_the_priced_mesh asserts the exact 0.7.2-era cell count 2 807 309 and 0.11's gmsh meshes 2 808 204 — +0.032%, a mesher-version drift against an equality record, with the module's other 4 names green in the same run. That is the third site of the class leg (c)'s finding 19 named (test_geometry_floor_discriminator.py) and GEO-16 first showed: records made on 0.7.2 and not swept when OPS-18 re-recorded. The class, not the constant, is the deliverable — a review should commission one sweep over all exact-equality records rather than three one-constant fixes. Finding 24: the real-build route for larmor_mesh_cache is real and cheap — OPS-17 (b2) priced it at 445.55 s complex, this slot ran it real at 219 s (2.03×), and its 4 environment skips are all complex-only tests outside the census roots, so a gate-classifier "not complex-gated" verdict (finding 18's rule) is worth half the window on this module. Finding 25: test_coil_loading_larmor_third_rung.py did not reproduce its OPS-17 (b2) record — recorded 11 passed / 174.86 s / exit 0 at -n 8 with TH11_STEP5_RUNG=fine, this slot Status 124 at 300 s with only the module's first (non-solving) test out, deferred — no footer. The likely cause is ordering: in attempt 8 mesh_cache ran immediately before it and populated the rung's on-disk cache, so 174.86 s is a warm-cache price, not the module's. Leg (e) should run mesh_cache first and third_rung second in the same slot, at -k 30 500. Rate note (finding 22 confirmed): the two priced dodd_deeds modules returned 14 names for 184 s = 13 s/name, the census's best rate to date, against 219 s for 5 names on the unpriced-in-this-build mesh_cache. Leg (e) owns the remaining 82 names over 13 modules: coil_loading_* 53 (of which degree2's 14 are the TH-12 structural defer and third_rung's 7 need the cache ordering), dodd_deeds_* 24 over 5 modules (all ≈400 s single-fixture files, widths in the leg-(c) price table), test_port_systematics_composition.py 3, test_port_gap_voltage_padding.py 2. Queued as leg (e) by the 2026-08-27 10:30 review (§9 item 1); the three stale-record reds are OPS-27, finding 12's test double is OPS-28. Step 2 leg (e) PARTIAL 2026-08-27 (12:00 slot) — 214 / 289 observed (208 green, 6 red), 75 deferred; tests/validation 190 → 197 of 272, five compute windows, 1 853 s, three footered (Status 1/1/1) and two Status 124. Finding 25 CONFIRMED and the ordering remedy works: mesh_cache real first (262 s, its 4 green + the filed finding-23 red reproduced verbatim), then third_rung complex -n 8 fine against the warm cache — which footered at 304 s, where the same command cold had been Status 124 at 301 s. The recorded 174.86 s was indeed a warm-cache price; the module's own cold price is ≥ 500 s. Finding 27 — the trap list's "sweep 0-byte FFCx stubs first" is not optional, and skipping it cost this slot a 329 s window. The first warm third_rung attempt returned a footered Status 1 with all 7 census names in ERROR, every one RuntimeError: Failed JIT compilation of form: JIT compilation timed out, probably due to a failed previous compile … libffcx_forms_1ea5a4c22c3fbbdfad7ef834d249519203ba0bb6.c. The cache held exactly one 0-byte .c, timestamped 14:07 — i.e. created by leg (d)'s own 300 s kill of this very module five hours earlier. One rm and the identical command produced 1 failed, 17 passed. This is the failure mode the fail-closed control cannot see (compare finding 18): a poisoned stub yields a footered run whose names are ERROR, not absent, so a census that trusted the footer would have recorded 7 spurious reds. Rule, now mandatory: sweep find /root/.cache/fenics -name '*.c' -size 0 before the first window of every slot, and again after any exit-124 window, because a killed window poisons the cache for the next one. Finding 28 (red, filed, the fourth stale-record site): third_rung::test_the_rung_is_inside_the_priced_ceiling asserts the exact 0.7.2 fine-rung count 417 914 and 0.11 meshes 418 888 — +0.233%, seven times the mesh_cache site's relative drift, same sign, with the module's other 6 names (both complex-power identities, the free-solve dissipation identity, and test_the_fine_rung_reproduces_step2s_recorded_deviation) green in the same run. So the rung's physics reproduces its TH-11 record while only its cell count does not. Note for OPS-27: its planned grep -rn '0\.7\.2' tests/ would not necessarily reach this constant — it was found by reading a red's assertion message, so the sweep clause should be widened to exact-equality mesh counts regardless of version tag. Finding 29 — two dodd_deeds prices from leg (c) did not hold on this image, both near-misses: reactance_combined_knobs -n 8 (recorded 421.90 s) was Status 124 at 521 s having printed one PASSED, and resistance_slab_resolution -n 2 (recorded 386.82 s) was Status 124 at 437 s having reached 100% of its progress bar on both ranks before dying in teardown/summary. Both are deferred — no footer by the fail-closed control despite the second one visibly finishing its tests — the control is working as designed, and the remedy is width, not interpretation: budget these two at ≥ 600 s (slab is worth ≈450 s + margin, knobs unknown above 520 s). No stub and no stray python3 was left by either kill. Leg (f) owns the remaining 75 names over 12 modules: dodd_deeds_* 24 over 5 (two of them now re-priced upward), coil_loading_* 46 (of which degree2's 14 remain the TH-12 structural defer), test_port_systematics_composition.py 3, test_port_gap_voltage_padding.py 2. Step 2 leg (f) PARTIAL 2026-08-27 (13:30 slot) — 255 / 289 observed (242 green, 13 red), 34 deferred; tests/validation 197 → 238 of 272, six compute windows, 2 314 s, five footered (Status 1 ×5) and one Status 124; 41 names banked, the census's best rate on the expensive tail. Finding 30 — the stale-record class collapses to shared meshes, and it re-shapes OPS-27: this slot's six reds are all of that class, and pooling them with legs (c)–(e) gives nine red names over eight modules carrying only FOUR distinct 0.7.2-era cell counts — 138 619 → 138 490 (*−0.093%) in richardson_ladder ×2 params, larmor_probe and transition_30mhz; 417 914 → 418 888 (+0.233%) in slab_resolution, larmor_resolution and third_rung; 697 401 → 697 926 (+0.075%) in combined_knobs; 2 807 309 → 2 808 204 (+0.032%) in mesh_cache. Two consequences: the unit of repair is the mesh, not the file (a per-file fix leaves siblings red; one re-record retires up to four names, so OPS-27 is four measurements and \~nine edits, not nine measurements), and the drift is per-mesh, not a global offset (it does not even share a sign, so no unmeasured record can be predicted from a measured one). Leg (e)'s note that grep -rn '0\.7\.2' tests/ is insufficient is confirmed twice over — none of the five new sites was reachable by version tag; all were found by reading a red's assertion message. The census is the sweep: OPS-27 should take its site list from finding 30's table, not re-derive it by grep. Finding 31 — item 1's own draw order is lossy and cost-relevant: richardson_ladder was budgeted as two commands / 800 s, but OPS-17 step 3j had already refuted the split in the journal (TH11_STEP4_RUNG selects the mesh, FREQ_MHZ=10,30 selects both parametrisations) — one command, all 14 names, 143 s; and the "unpriced" larmor_probe/transition_30mhz pair was priced in the journal at 137.18 s and reproduced at 137.35 s (+0.12%) for 12 names. Two zero-compute greps turned a budgeted 800 s + "unpriced" into 282 s for 26 of the slot's 41 names. Rule: grep attempts.md for the module name before sizing any window. Finding 32: finding 29's ≥ 1.5× sizing rule is validated — slab_resolution footered at 429.91 s (+11.1% over record) and combined_knobs at 568.26 s (+34.7%, the census's largest under-pri, which is why its 520 s and 615 s windows fell on opposite sides) — but reactance_box_truncation is not a pricing near-miss: at -n 8 / 600 s it died inside its firstalidation test wh no other name started, so it is deferred — measured, first test alone > 590 s at -n 8 and must not get a third -n 8 window without a by-name split or a width change (its first test is itself another cell-count equality, so finding 30 predicts a tenth red behind it). Finding 27's cache sweep was run before window 1 and again after the exit 124 — can both times, zero sty python3. Leg (g) owns the remaining 34*names over 6 modules, of which only 20 over 5 are reachable (degree2's 14 stay the TH-12 structural defer): the three untried dodd_deeds_* 15, test_port_systematics_composition.py 3, test_port_gap_voltage_padding.py 2 — one slot should finish the tail and write the chunk-level reconciliation.* Step 2 leg (g) PARTIAL 2026-08-27 (15:00 slot) — 264 / 289 observed (250 green, 14 red), 25 deferred; tests/validation 238 → 247 of 272, four compute windows, 1 606 s, three footered (Status 0/0/1) and one Status 124; 9 names banked, and the reachable tail is down to 9 names over 3 modules. The two PORT unknowns are now resolved in opposite directions: test_port_systematics_composition.py is 14 passed / 363.35 s (-n 2, +0.87% on its 20260821T034507Z record of 360.23 s) — its 3 census names green, and the PORT-10 batch-C killer is simply an expensive file, not a broken one. Finding 33 — test_port_gap_voltage_padding.py is a measured structural deferral, not a pricing miss, and it is now cited to two windows at the same width: at -n 2 / 590 s it printed collected 2 items and then the name of its first test and nothing else — Status 124, zero PASSED/FAILED lines, exactly as at 400 s (finding 21). Its gap_ports_padded fixture is scope="module", so a by-name split cannot help — it would pay the same setup twice — and the deferral reason is upgraded to deferred — measured, module fixture alone > 590 s at -n 2, two windows (400 s, 590 s). That makes it the same shape as box_truncation (finding 32) and a substantive reason for step 2's close criterion, not a not reached in slot. Finding 34 — finding 31's journal-grep rule paid a third time, and reactance_wire_resolution was never unpriced: item 1 budgets it as "record 491.96 s with 2 deselected, full file unpriced, ≥ 740 s" and therefore unrunnable in one foreground window, but the journal carries two disjoint -k halves from 2026-08-20 (pinned 242.68 s, projected or refinement 499.80 s) that together cover all 6 validation names. Run at those boundaries — with the environment root dropped and the second half selected by node id rather than -k "a or b" (the quoting trap) — the halves came in at 214.36 s (−11.7%) and 434.40 s (−13.1%), both under their records, and the file is complete at 6/6 in 649 s against a budgeted ≥ 740 s for one window that could not have run. Note the sign: this is the first module family to come in under its 0.7.2-era price, which is why finding 29's ≥ 1.5× rule must stay a sizing rule and never becomes a prediction. Finding 35 (red, filed) — a tenth stale-record name, a fifth mesh, and it has no sibling: wire_resolution::test_the_refinement_landed_on_the_wire_and_not_on_the_far_field asserts the exact 0.7.2 count 366 207 and 0.11 meshes 365 970 (*−0.0647%, the second negative drift), with the module's other 5 names green across the two halves. A zero-compute grep -rn '366207' tests/ finds only this site — so finding 30's "one re-record retires up to four names" is an upper bound and the value→module map is ragged (4, 3, 1, 1, 1); OPS-27 should size self as fi measurements, \~ten edits.inding 27's cache sweep ran before window 1 and again after the exit 124 — clean both times, zero stray python3. Leg (h) owns the remaining 25** nam over 4 modules, of which only 9 over 2** are reachable: klzzwxh:08 4 (journal-priced at 5598 s full file at -n 2, or two recorded -k halves of 271.08 s + 260.07 s — take t halves, the full file was 98.2% of its window) and box_truncation 5 (finding 32: -n 2 or a by-name split, never a third -n 8 window); degree2's 14 and gap_voltage_padding's 2 are both defers-with-reason and are not to be re-opened. Leg (h) should finish the tail and owes the chunk-level reconciliation.* Step 2 ✅ 2026-08-27 (16:30 slot, leg (h)) ⇒ chunk ✅. Final: 268 / 289 observed (254 green, 14 red), 21 deferred; tests/validation 247 → 251 of 272, tests/ports 17/17. Three windows, 1 166 s, two footered (Status 0/0) and one Status 124. reactance_box_size is 4/4 green on its two recorded -k halves (282.59 s + 289.44 s = 572 s, +4.2% / +11.3% on the 2026-08-20 record — finding 37: taking the halves was right, the full file's 559.58 s + 11% would have blown a 590 s window). Finding 36: reactance_box_truncation is a permanent measured deferral — Status 124 at both -n 8/600 s (leg (f)) and -n 2/590 s (this slot), each dying inside its first validation test; its projected_xlarge_box fixture is scope="module" and all five tests consume it, so width is not the constraint and a by-name split cannot help. It needs a smaller fixture, not a different selection — a MAT-6 pricing question, not a census one. Finding 30's predicted eleventh red sits behind that fixture and is pending, not falsified. Chunk-level reconciliation (written in attempts.md, 2026-08-27T22:20Z): repo-wide over both censuses, 478 collected → 452 observed (436 green, 16 red), 26 deferred (452 + 26 = 478), i.e. 94.6% of the repo's collected tests observed in a footered run on 0.11, with zero not reached in slot and zero deferred — no footer surviving. The seed list of four is green by name — test_convergence.py 1 passed / 141.51 s (its test_h_refinement_straight_wire, cited in this chunk's own rationale as red on main right now, PASSED; MAG-20 owns the band, but the gate executes), test_port_lumped_two_torus.py 5 passed / 90.97 s, test_cavity_resonances.py 3 passed / 5.59 s, test_birdcage_conductor_sizing.py PASSED in leg (a)'s 38-item run. The 16 reds are exactly three families with named owners: ten stale 0.7.2-era exact records over 8 modules but only 5 distinct meshes (OPS-27), three "overlapping facets" reds (five GEO-23 sites counting the dead test_cylindrical_domain.py module and the rank-divergent materials conversion — 10 + 3 + 3 = 16), and three test-double-drift names (OPS-28, finding 12 — invisible to step 1's static sweep by construction). The 26 deferrals are degree2 14 (TH-12 memory wall), box_truncation 5 (finding 36), gap_voltage_padding 2 (finding 33), leg (a)'s 5 (all GEO-23/filed) — every one a measured cost or a filed defect. No band was loosened and no red fixed in-slot across seven census slots. Answer to the operator's directive: the 0.11 transition worked; the three exception families are stale records (the physics reproduces), one gmsh boundary-mesh family, and one mock a prior chunk's rank-safety fix outgrew — OPS-18's §4 close stands, every §2 physics claim's gate was observed executing and passing on 0.11. Audited COMPLIANT 2026-08-27 18:00 review — all 18 leg (e)–(h) footers re-read (statuses and per-leg elapsed sums 1 853 / 2 314 / 1 606 / 1 166 s reproduce from the logs), 18 matching test-results.md rows, reconciliation arithmetic verified (268 + 21 = 289, 452 + 26 = 478, 16 = 10 + 3 + 3, 26 = 14 + 5 + 2 + 5); one wording defect corrected in this row (the reds-vs-sites conflation above). The §7 prose entry below narrates step 1 and leg (a) only — the leg (b)–(h) evidence lives in this row and attempts.md. | ✅

docs.title: OPS-27 — Re-record the 0.7.2-era exact records the OPS-18 re-record did not reach, version-tagged on the GEO-16 precedent, and sweep for siblings
docs.text: Re-record the 0.7.2-era exact records the OPS-18 re-record did not reach, version-tagged on the GEO-16 precedent, and sweep for siblings — two reds on main filed by the OPS-26 census: test_geometry_floor_discriminator.py RECORD_128_RELL2 = 0.01826 vs OPS-18's 1.7686% (leg (c) finding 19) and test_coil_loading_larmor_mesh_cache.py NCELLS_THIRD = 2 807 309 vs 0.11's 2 808 204 (leg (d) finding 23, +0.032% mesher drift); GEO-16's 79 534 → 79 070 was the first of the class. No band introduced; a grep -rn '0\.7\.2' tests/ sweep (11 files) tabulated for a third site. Commissioned 2026-08-27 10:30 review. Re-scoped 2026-08-27 18:00 review from the finished census: the class is ten names / eight modules / five meshes plus the relative-L2 pair, every 0.11 value already measured in a census log — split into step 1 (cheap half: geomfloor, the 138 619 family, mesh_cache; ≈ 570 s) and step 2 (expensive half: the 417 914 family, combined_knobs, wire_resolution; ≈ 1 440 s), independent; box_truncation's suspected sixth mesh pending on a cheaper fixture. Rubrics: §9 items 1 and 2. Step 1 ✅ 2026-08-27 (19:30 slot) — the cheap half landed exactly as ruled: RECORD_128_RELL2 0.01826 → 0.017686 / RECORD_128_SEPARATION 57.31 → 59.16, NCELLS_BASELINE 138_619 → 138_490, NCELLS_THIRD 2_807_309 → 2_808_204, every one an exact equality version-tagged with its 0.7.2 digit and its census log in-comment (GEO-16 precedent), no band anywhere and git diff -- src/ empty. All four anchors green from main in four foreground windows, 604 s total: geomfloor 12 passed / 46.45 s (Status 0, 49 s, -n 2 complex), richardson FREQ_MHZ=10,30 25 passed / 147.00 s where the census read 2 failed, 23 passed (Status 0, 149 s), probe + 30 MHz 23 passed / 149.09 s where the census read 2 failed, 21 passed (Status 0, 150 s), mesh_cache real 12 passed, 4 skipped / 254.75 s where the census read 1 failed, 11 passed, 4 skipped (Status 0, 256 s). Collected counts identical to the census runs (25 / 23 / 16), so exactly the six stale-record names flipped and no other name's status moved. Finding 38 — the 138 619 family is ONE constant, not four: richardson_ladder, transition_30mhz (and degree2) all import test_coil_loading_larmor_probe.NCELLS_BASELINE, so finding 30's "the unit of repair is the mesh, not the file" holds in its strongest form — one edit retired four reds, and a per-file sweep would have found nothing to edit in two of the three modules. Finding 39 — the 0.7.2 completeness grep is confirmed empty: grep -rn '0\.7\.2' tests/ returns 26 hits over 11 files and none is one of this chunk's sites; every hit is either an already-swept record carrying both digits or prose. The demotion to a completeness check was right. Finding 40 (scope note for step 2 / the review): the value greps surface prose copies of these meshes in modules outside either step's scope — 138 619 in test_coil_loading_degree2.py (×5), test_degree2_energy_mechanism.py, test_dodd_deeds_impedance.py (×2), test_dodd_deeds_projected_drive.py, test_dodd_deeds_reactance_box_size.py, test_dodd_deeds_reactance_box_truncation.py (×3), test_dodd_deeds_reactance_combined_knobs.py (×3), test_dodd_deeds_reactance_wire_resolution.py (×3), test_dodd_deeds_resistance_slab_resolution.py — and 417 914 in richardson_ladder (×3). None is asserted (the _dodd_deeds_ ones are growth-ratio denominators printed for scale, not records), so none was edited under this step's "five names, five files" scope; they are stale documentation and want a single prose sweep after step 2 lands, not an in-scope edit here. Step 2 ✅ 2026-08-27 (21:00 slot) ⇒ chunk ✅ — the expensive half landed as ruled: NCELLS_FINE 417_914 → 418_888 (slab_resolution, larmor_resolution), NCELLS_COMBINED 697_401 → 697_926 (combined_knobs), and the :268 literal 366_207 → 365_970 (wire_resolution); exact equalities, version-tagged, no band, git diff -- src/ empty. Three anchors green from main, 1 523 s, all Status 0: slab -n 2 16 passed / 479.37 s (census 1 failed, 15 passed), knobs -n 8 15 passed / 577.00 s (census 1 failed, 14 passed), wire-projected -n 2 by node id 4 passed / 459.44 s (census 1 failed, 3 passed); collected counts identical (16 / 15 / 4). Finding 41: third_rung:443 holds no constant — it imports NCELLS_FINE from larmor_resolution, so the rubric's five edits are four, and step 1's finding 38 (import aliases, not per-file records) repeats on a second family. Finding 42: combined_knobs reproduced inside its finding-32-widened 660 s window at 577.00 s (+1.5% on its census reading); all three anchors came in above their census elapsed (+11.5% / +1.5% / +5.8%), so the ≥ 1.5× rule stays a sizing rule. Finding 43: the negative control is name-and-status level only — an all-green run captures the prints the census log showed via failure capture. larmor_resolution and third_rung are edited but not re-run (same mesh value the slab run measured; third_rung is warm-cache-only 304 s at -n 8, finding 25) — their known-issues line is re-headed 🟡 "re-recorded, re-run owed to the next census". Retired: the leg (f) entry in full, the leg (g) wire_resolution entry. box_truncation's suspected sixth mesh stays pending, fixture not opened. Step 3 ✅ 2026-08-28 (16:30 slot) — the owed tail is closed. Both re-runs green from main in two foreground windows, 719 s, both Status 0 with identical rank streams: test_coil_loading_larmor_resolution.py -n 2 complex 17 passed / 424.32 s (20260828T213049Z_OPS-27-step3-larmor-resolution.log, 426 s) where the census read 1 failed, 16 passed; test_coil_loading_larmor_third_rung.py -n 8 complex TH11_STEP5_RUNG=fine 18 passed / 291.03 s (20260828T213807Z_OPS-27-step3-thirdrung.log, 293 s) where the destubbed census read 1 failed, 17 passed. Collected counts identical to the census runs (17 / 18), so exactly the two stale-record names flipped and no other name's status moved — the NCELLS_FINE == 418_888 equality and its imported alias (finding 41) are both executed green now, and both known-issues entries are RETIRED. Finding 44 — the cold price feared for third_rung does not exist on the record. Finding 25 inferred a "≥ 500 s cold" from a 300 s kill and a 304 s warm footer, and the rubric sized a 900 s window for it; the module returned at 291 s, below the warm figure, with larmor_resolution having run first as ruled. So this slot again measured a warm-fixture price and the cold price is still unmeasured — the ≥ 500 s number should not be carried forward as if it were a measurement. Finding 45 — the finding-40 prose sweep is not a mechanical substitution; three quarters of the copies must keep the 0.7.2 digit.
