docs.title: OPS-55 — evaluate_vector_field_parallel refuses equal-count point lists whose coordinates differ across ranks
docs.text: evaluate_vector_field_parallel refuses equal-count point lists whose coordinates differ across ranks — opened 2026-09-19 (interactive session, from an external code review; the same class as OPS-40, in the form its count guard cannot see). post/evaluation.py allgathers only n_points; each rank then locates and evaluates its own copy of the points and rank 0 scatters the hits by positional index, so with equal counts and different coordinates values[i] is the field at some other rank's row i, reported against rank 0's — all-valid mask, plausible numbers, no error; where two ranks both claim row i the last gathered wins. Latent, not live: a survey of the ≈58 calling files found every current caller passing identical points (the one site building points from rank-local mesh data, tests/validation/test_birdcage_b1_plus_closed_form.py:729–741, gathers and broadcasts first); the realistic trigger is a fixed-N rank-local list (unseeded np.random.rand(N, 3), mesh.geometry.x[:N]). Plan. (1) Validate, do not broadcast — broadcasting rank 0's points would hide a caller that still indexes the result against its own local points. Fold a digest into the existing collective: comm.allgather((n_points, hashlib.blake2b(points.tobytes()).digest())) — no extra round on the valid path. (2) Counts equal but digests differing is known on every rank, so the error path may use further collectives safely: bcast rank 0's points, each rank computes its first differing row and max abs deviation, allgather, and raise ValueError on every rank with the per-rank figures — the magnitude separates rank-local points (gross) from rank-dependent floating-point ordering (≈1e-16); the message says to broadcast the points from rank 0. The count-mismatch message and the shape check are unchanged. (3) Bitwise identity is the documented contract; a caller differing only in the last bit would begin to raise — none found, and that raise is correct. Done-when (§4): in tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py, at -n 1 and -n 2: equal counts with coordinates shifted by 0.01 * rank inside the unit cube raise on every rank (allgathered flags == [True] * size), the message naming each rank's first differing row and deviation, and at -n 1 the same construction does not raise (negative control); a pre-change control — the function at the pinned pre-change sha, git show into a scratch module under /logs/ as OPS-53 did — returns an all-valid mask on that input and values deviating from the closed form (x, 2y, 3z) at rank 0's points by the amount the shift predicts (quantitative: the defect was silent, and by how much); the existing identical-list test still green at < 1e-12. Standing rule (c): a representative -n 2 subset of existing callers (tests/post, tests/ports, one SAR test) unchanged, since a false raise on a valid caller is the one way this change can do harm. Out of scope: the shape check raises rank-locally (a bad shape on one rank would hang the rest) — reachable only from already-broken caller code. For a review to queue into §9; not queued by this session. Closed 2026-09-21 (11:00 UTC slot, §9 item 27): digest hashlib.blake2b(points.tobytes(), digest_size=16) folded into the existing allgather; mismatch path bcasts rank 0's points, allgathers (first differing row, max abs deviation) and raises on every rank. Measured at -n 2 (20260921T111743Z_OPS-55.log, 6 passed, 2 s): flags [True, True], message rank 0: first differing row -1, max abs deviation 0.000e+00; rank 1: first differing row 0, max abs deviation 1.000e-02; -n 1 negative control flags [False] (20260921T111745Z_OPS-55-n1.log, 6 passed, 2 s). Pre-change control, blob git show 14a0d71:src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py (= this commit's ^) into /workspace/logs/: all-valid mask, per-row deviation from (x, 2y, 3z) at rank 0's points [1.1e-16, 3.000000e-02 ×7] — exactly the predicted 0.03·rank for rows rank 1 located, silently (20260921T111730Z_OPS-55-prechange.log:50, asserted in-test to 1e-12). Rule (c) caller subset at -n 2: complex tests/post tests/ports tests/validation/test_lossy_sphere_sar.py 54 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped, 159 s — the two failures are exactly known-issues entry 3 (placeholder fakes, no call into this function), the skip is the env-gated pre-change test (20260921T111802Z_OPS-55-callers-complex.log:1203); real tests/post 14 passed / 25 skipped, 3 s (20260921T112042Z_OPS-55-callers-real.log). No caller was passing rank-local points. (20260921T111714Z_OPS-55-prechange.log is a docker-socket denial from a date &&-prefixed call, no run.) | ✅

docs.title: OPS-56 — Sweep-planner endpoint inclusion must not depend on the carrier frequency
docs.text: Sweep-planner endpoint inclusion must not depend on the carrier frequency — opened 2026-09-19 (interactive session, from an external code review; reproduced in plain numpy with the function's own logic). ports/sweep.py::_uniform_frequency_grid decides whether to append the requested endpoint with a default np.isclose, whose rtol = 1e-5 scales with the absolute frequency: at 128 MHz anything within ≈1.3 kHz of stop_hz (640 Hz at 64 MHz) counts as already present. Reproduced: (127.7000e6, 127.7009e6, 500) ends at 127.7005 MHz; (127.7000e6, 127.7012e6, 1e3) drops the endpoint; (64.0000e6, 64.0005e6, 1e3) returns a single point. kHz steps around a resonance are what refined_step_hz exists for and what birdcage tuning will ask of it; tests/ports/test_frequency_sweep_planner.py uses MHz spacing only, so nothing sees it. Two neighbours in the same function: non-finite inputs fail by accident (nan → ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer, inf → OverflowError), and plan_frequency_sweep de-duplicates the merged coarse+refined grid with np.unique, which merges only bitwise-equal floats — two points 1e-8 Hz apart both survive, and each is a full field solve. Plan. Validate start / stop / step finite (intended ValueErrors). Decide inclusion from the grid's own construction: n = floor(span/step + 1e-9); the endpoint is on-grid iff abs(span − n·step) <= 1e-9·step, in which case the last point is set to stop_hz exactly, otherwise stop_hz is appended. De-duplicate the merged grid with the same step-relative tolerance (the finest step in play) instead of np.unique. Tolerances are relative to the step, never to the carrier. Done-when (§4): unit tests asserting exact grids for the three reproduced cases (endpoint present, length as computed by hand), a nondivisible span, the float-noise case (0.1, 0.3, 0.1) → 3 points, an on-grid endpoint bitwise equal to stop_hz, a coarse/refined near-duplicate merging to one point, and the intended ValueError for each non-finite input; a pre-change control showing the three reproduced cases fail on the pinned pre-change sha; the two existing planner tests green unchanged. Pure numpy — no solve. For a review to queue into §9. Closed 2026-09-21 (§9 item 28, implementer): finite checks + step-relative inclusion (n = floor(span/step + 1e-9), on-grid iff |span − n·step| ≤ 1e-9·step ⇒ last point := stop_hz exactly, else appended) + _merge_frequency_grids de-duplicating at 1e-9 × the finest step in play. Pre-change control on the c1d167d blob (in /logs/): 3/3 reproduced cases fail — ends 127.7005 MHz, ends 127.7010 MHz, single point (64.0e6,). Committed module -n 1: 19 passed, 2 s — three cases hit their hand grids with stop_hz bitwise last; (0, 10, 3) → (0, 3, 6, 9, 10); (0.1, 0.3, 0.1) → 3 points ending bitwise 0.3; 63–65 MHz @ 0.1 MHz → 21 points ending bitwise 65e6; coarse/refined pair 6e-8 Hz apart merges (7 points, not 8); nan/±inf on each of start/stop/step raise the intended ValueError; the three pre-existing planner tests green unchanged (no caller of plan_frequency_sweep outside that test file, so no sweep record depended on the old rounding). Logs 20260921T112323Z_OPS-56.log (control), 20260921T112330Z_OPS-56.log (green). Audit 2026-09-23 03:00 review: auditor DEMOTE(2) — overruled, ✅ stands. The auditor could not grep four of the grids above out of the green log (the nondivisible span, the 0.3 float-noise case, the 21-point MHz grid, the 7-point merge) because the window printed nothing for them. They are the operands of exact-equality asserts — tests/ports/test_frequency_sweep_planner.py:101 (== (0.0, 3.0, 6.0, 9.0, 10.0)), :107–109, :114–115, :132–135 — whose PASSED lines are 20260921T112330Z_OPS-56.log:48–51. A passing exact equality is log evidence of its value. §4's elements (harness log, agent-executed, quantitative assertion, elapsed) are all met; the digits are cited to source + PASSED line, not to a print. | ✅

docs.title: OPS-57 — S ↔ Z conversions: let the solve report singularity; one impedance-to-S implementation
docs.text: S ↔ Z conversions: let the solve report singularity; one impedance-to-S implementation — opened 2026-09-19 (interactive session, from an external code review). ports/circuit.py tests singularity with abs(np.linalg.det(m)) == 0.0 at three sites (terminate's I − S_bb Γ at :138, s_to_z at :167, z_to_s at :185). A determinant is scale- and dimension-dependent — 1e-21 · I₁₆ has det == 0.0 exactly and condition number 1 — so the test can reject a perfectly conditioned matrix. Honest size: unreachable on this project's matrices (I − S has O(1) entries, Z + z0 I a diagonal ≥ z0), so this is a correctness-of-intent fix, not a live defect. The real weakness is the opposite one: == 0.0 catches only exactly singular matrices, which np.linalg.solve already refuses (LinAlgError: Singular matrix), so the line is a second factorisation that adds a message and no protection. Separately, ports/sparameters.py::sparameters_from_impedance is the same formula as z_to_s with an explicit np.linalg.inv, a non-finite check z_to_s lacks, and a looser z0 check. Plan. (1) Drop the three determinant tests; wrap each solve in try / except np.linalg.LinAlgError and raise ValueError with the existing message text. (2) Add the non-finite input check to s_to_z / z_to_s. (3) sparameters_from_impedance keeps its signature and docstring and delegates to z_to_s (check the import direction first — no cycle). No conditioning threshold: a near-open-circuit S legitimately has a huge Z, and a cut-off would be an invented tolerance. Done-when (§4): unit tests — round trip z_to_s(s_to_z(S)) to ≤ 1e-12 on a 16-port matrix scaled so its determinant underflows (the pre-change control: the pinned pre-change sha raises on it); an exactly singular I − S still raises ValueError with the same message at all three sites; sparameters_from_impedance and z_to_s agree to ≤ 1e-14 on a random passive Z. Standing rule (c): inv → solve moves S in the last bits, so tests/ports and the PORT validation gates that consume sparameters_from_impedance are re-run at -n 2 and must be green with no tolerance touched — a gate that fails on a last-bit change is a finding about that gate, reported, not loosened. For a review to queue into §9. | ✅ 2026-09-21 (11:00 UTC slot, §9 item 29) — the three det == 0.0 tests replaced by try/except np.linalg.LinAlgError → ValueError with the unchanged messages; s_to_z/z_to_s refuse non-finite input; sparameters_from_impedance keeps its signature/validation and delegates to z_to_s (circuit.py imports only numpy — no cycle). tests/unit/test_ops57_sz_conversions.py (smoke, -n 2, 22 passed with the PORT-20/PORT-15 unit modules, 3 s, 20260921T112537Z_OPS-57.log): 16-port round trip at z0 = 1e-21 Ω, max|Δ| = 1.877e-16 ≤ 1e-12 with cond(Z + z0 I) = 3.944 and |det| = 0 — the pre-change control (the removed guard fires on that matrix) asserted; exactly singular matrices raise the same message at all three sites; sparameters_from_impedance vs z_to_s 0.000e+00 ≤ 1e-14. Rule (c), complex, -n 2, no tolerance touched: test_port_package_sparameters.py 18 passed / 194 s (20260921T112548Z_OPS-57.log; the one red is tests/environment/test_scikit_rf_version.py, the known-issues OPS-60 deliberate entry) — ‖S − z_to_s(Z)‖/‖S‖ = 0, σ_max 0.8613568944353246 vs record (miss 4.353e-10, band 1e-6), symmetry 3.112130867e-05 (miss 1.867e-11, band 5e-7); PORT-9 gate test_port_birdcage_four_port.py 5 passed / 37 s (20260921T112912Z_OPS-57.log) — ‖S − Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ 1.078765433e-14 (was 1.044255156e-14: the predicted last-bit move), ‖Z − Zᵀ‖/‖Z‖ 8.814400604e-05 and σ_max 0.999992805 and class spreads 0.0553/0.0353/0.0214 % digit-identical. PORT-20 step 2's 1e-12 residual is now a same-implementation check; its docstring names the unit closed form as the anchor.

docs.title: OPS-58 — Private-leak check: commit messages, fail-closed on inspection errors, "skipped" is not "clean", and a positive control
docs.text: Private-leak check: commit messages, fail-closed on inspection errors, "skipped" is not "clean", and a positive control — opened 2026-09-19 (interactive session, from an external code review, which framed these correctly as limits of the mechanism, not evidence of a leak). (a) CLAUDE.md forbids AED figures in commit messages, but check_private_leak.py runs as pre-commit, which never sees the message. (b) staged_additions() and tracked_lines() swallow every exception and yield nothing, so a failing git diff reads as a clean pass; collect() does the same for an unreadable secret file. (published_digits() failing is the safe direction — nothing subtracted — and stays.) (c) With no raw exports present the script returns 0 silently, so the CI private-leak job, which can never hold the exports, reads as a pass while checking nothing. (d) The checker has no test, and its own docstring records that it once passed its planted figure. Plan. --message-file <path> mode (comment lines stripped), installed by install_git_hooks.sh as a commit-msg hook beside pre-commit; --audit additionally scans git log --format=%B. Inspection errors propagate → exit 2 with could not inspect: …. No reference data → print SKIPPED: no reference data on this machine; nothing was checked (exit 0), distinct from clean: …. ROOT / secret globs overridable so a script-style test beside test_tier_guard.py can build a scratch git repo with synthetic secrets. Done-when (§4): that test asserts exit codes exactly — planted figure staged → 1; planted figure in the message → 1; a truncated spelling of it → 1; clean → 0 with clean:; no reference data → 0 with SKIPPED; broken git → 2 — plus the pre-change control (the pinned pre-change script passes the message plant and the broken-git case); the CI private-leak job runs the same test, which becomes the one part of that job that tests something on a runner; --audit on this clone still reports clean (the count of figures printed, never a figure). Operator step after it lands: re-run scripts/testing/install_git_hooks.sh once — .git/hooks is untracked and not agent-writable (dashboard Waiting-on-you). What stays unfixed, deliberately: matching needs ≥ 8 significant digits; a figure rounded to 3–4 digits in prose, or transformed into a ratio or percentage, is invisible to any digit matcher that is not also drowning in false positives. The hook is a copy-paste net; the written rule remains the control. Closed 2026-09-22 — all eight exit-code cases plus the pre-change controls assert exactly, 24/24 (20260922T040113Z_OPS-58.log, 3 s, smoke host-side). --audit on this clone reported one match (2026-09-21); the operator ruled it a false positive — a shared geometric input the repo already publishes in plain text in its own SPEC.md, echoed back by the export, not an AED result — so no history rewrite. A narrow shared-input allowlist now suppresses exactly that site: an entry keys on (tracked path, JSON key present on the line, exact value) and carries its reason plus the tracked public source that publishes it; the value is computed from its published closed form, never written out, so an AED output cannot be entered at all. Suppression is never silent — the count and the site are printed on every run. Negative controls gate it: a synthetic AED output beside the allowlisted site is still flagged, and the same value in a different file, or under a different key in the same file, is still flagged. --audit now clean: with 1 shared-input match suppressed (20260922T040116Z_OPS-58-audit.log, 8 s). Operator step still open: re-run scripts/testing/install_git_hooks.sh once. Audit 2026-09-23 03:00 review: PASS (24/24 at 20260922T040113Z_OPS-58.log:92, clean: + suppression count at …040116Z_OPS-58-audit.log:34, both reds on ancestors). Tier note: both closing windows were wrapped in the standard timeout -k 30 180 while this row says smoke; measured 3 s / 8 s fit either — the tier word stays smoke. | ✅

docs.title: OPS-60 — scikit-rf in the image, pinned
docs.text: scikit-rf in the image, pinned — the circuit engine PORT-23 gates against the raw layer (operator directive 2026-09-20: use a vetted circuit solver, netlist prepared in our code) | ✅ 2026-09-23 (04:30 slot, §9 item 33): green on the ordinary fem-em-solver service — [OPS-60] skrf=2.1.0 file=/dolfinx-env/lib/python3.12/site-packages/skrf/__init__.py PASSED on both ranks (20260923T093017Z_OPS-60.log:76–77, :153–154), whole tests/environment 12 passed per rank (:146, :223), dolfinx 0.11.0.post0 complex128 (:68), Status 0, 39 s, -n 2; no recreate was needed. Negative control on record: ModuleNotFoundError on the pre-rebuild image (20260921T093041Z_OPS-60.log:48). Known-issues 2026-09-21 DELIBERATE and 2026-09-23 NOT-A-RED entries retired; PORT-23 unblocked. Audit 2026-09-25 (03:00 review): auditor DEMOTE(8) on the tier word, overruled — ✅ stands. Every §4 element is present and traced 8/8 (20260923T093017Z_OPS-60.log:3,12,76,146,153,223,226–227; red baseline on 9eb1e39, the pin commit's parent, 20260921T093041Z_OPS-60.log:3,48,55; the assert tests/environment/test_scikit_rf_version.py:40 untouched since f3fcdeb). Exact version equality is §4-quantitative on the OPS-18 / OPS-25 precedent (a documented reference value with a discriminating control). The defect is the label: a "smoke" row whose closing window ran the whole tests/environment suite under timeout -k 30 60 for 39 s — the window the 09-23 review's §9 item 33 wrote verbatim. Tier column re-labelled standard, the precedent of the 09-23 OPS-57 / OPS-58 tier notes. History: **2026-09-21 (04:30 slot): Dockerfile pin scikit-rf==2.1.0 (newest on PyPI, read in-container by pip index versions, 20260921T093027Z_OPS-60-version-probe.log:34) and the test landed; the negative control fails as predicted on the current image — ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'skrf' (20260921T093041Z_OPS-60.log:48, 1 s, -n 1). ✅ owed to the operator's rebuild: the same test green on the rebuilt image (known-issues 2026-09-21). 2026-09-23: the operator rebuilt the image at ≈21:10 local 2026-09-22 and reports import skrf → 2.1.0 host-side, but two attempts to run the gate (interactive session 02:13 UTC, 20260923T021343Z_OPS-60.log; subagent immediately after) both died on permission denied ... unix:///var/run/docker.sock before entering the container — neither is a test result (known-issues 2026-09-23). The chunk stays 🟡 pending one harness-logged run from a session with docker-socket access; nothing in the repo needs to change for it. 2026-09-23 03:00 review: the rebuilt image carries the pin — the 02:00 xl window (same fem-em-solver:latest image, service recreated before the window) ran this test green on every rank, [OPS-60] skrf=2.1.0 (20260923T070007Z_ANS-4-step3f.log:271–283), dolfinx 0.11.0.post0 unchanged (:287), congruent-cut cell records reproduced exactly (no mesher drift from the rebuild). ✅ is left to §9 item 33, which runs the test on the ordinary fem-em-solver service every slot uses — a container not recreated after the build still runs the old image. Step 1: add scikit-rf==<latest release at execution, pinned> to docker/Dockerfile's pip block beside pyvista, and a tests/environment/test_scikit_rf_version.py that imports skrf, prints skrf.__version__ and asserts it equals the pin (the OPS-25 pattern). The image rebuild is the operator's (docker compose build, outside the sandbox); the slot edits the Dockerfile and the test, runs the test to show it fails on the current image (import error = the negative control), journals, and marks PORT-23 PENDING PREREQUISITE → READY only after the operator's rebuilt image passes it. Code (probe scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py only; additive; disclosed). - FREQ_SET_O2 = {"f05x_o2_f10": (0.010, 2), "f05x_o2_f128": (0.128, 2)}, beside FREQ_SET (:671). FREQ_SET itself is not edited. - New o2-configs mode. A new function mirroring freq_configs (:679–704) with the same checks on f05x.json: - checks: Model.Mesh, four ports with Attributes [21]…[24], all +Z, Order == 1, Freq == [0.064]; - writes f05x_o2_f10.json and f05x_o2_f128.json only (Order 2, Freq set, Output "postpro_<name>"); - asserts neither file exists (never overwrite). - New read --exact-strip-o2 mode. - Lift the per-run (P) block of read_exact_strip_set (:735–786) into _p_check(name, path, tag), returning (s, ident, fails) and printing with the caller's tag. read_exact_strip_set calls it with its existing [OPS-61 1d W5] tag, so its output stays byte-identical. W5 proves that. - The new function runs _p_check on each present FREQ_SET_O2 run, and on f05x_o2 as the 64 MHz tie. - It imports the two record constants from tests.validation.test_ans4_exact_strip_records. The probe already puts REPO on sys.path (:59–61) and already imports tests.validation.* in this mode family. - Class means use the probe's _circulant_classes, as ours_means does (:724–732). - It never reads z_matrix_ohm, the aed key or any file under docs/private/ / aed_results/. - Dispatch: two new sys.argv branches beside :837–846. export, read, read --exact-strip, flip-config, freq-configs and read --exact-strip-set keep their behaviour.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - (P) on Palace f05x_o2_f10 and f05x_o2_f128, item 159's set, as read_exact_strip_set applies it: - reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND (test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86); - σ_max ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, and every column power ≤ 1 + 1e-9; - every S-class spread ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:121); - pooled ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR × the worst (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:129,173). - Palace log check (executor, journalled). Each of W2 / W3 shows: - 117 206 elements; - Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on attributes 21–24; - ND (p = 2): 753062; - ω/2π = 1.000e-02 / 1.280e-01 GHz; - every GMRES solver converged line (four per run; Linear.MaxIts is 100). - W5 (regression of the lift): read --exact-strip-set reproduces 20261003T110728Z_OPS-61-item194-W5-read.log's (P) lines and order-2 readings digit for digit.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (C2″) Order-mismatch separation, predicted ≥ 25×, printed. Per class: |ours p1 (ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P1_RECORDS[k]) − Palace o2| / |ours p2 (…_S_P2_X1[k]) − Palace o2|. - The numerator is predicted to be our own p2-vs-p1 move: 1.98 / 0.43 / 0.72 % at 10 MHz, 5.85 / 4.50 / 7.22 % at 128 MHz (…item192-W3-p2.log:2222,2224). - The denominator is predicted ≤ 1e-6. 64 MHz measured 2.4e8–4.7e8× (item 194 W5). - The ceiling is set by the denominator's round-off, so ≥ 25× is ≥ 10⁶× under what the 64 MHz case showed. - The 10 MHz adjacent class (0.43 %) is the least separated numerator. It still clears 25× unless the matched gap exceeds 1.7e-4. - (T) 64 MHz tie, predicted ≤ 1e-6 relative per class, printed. ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["64"] vs postpro_f05x_o2. A miss means the record is not Palace's discrete system: stop and report, and do not read 10 / 128. - (P)'s power to discriminate was shown on this mesh by item 159's flip: 200.0204 % spreads against the 0.5 % band, the sign-flip ceiling, 400×. It is not re-run.

Predictions (written first, printed). - Price, from item 194 W4 (20261003T110249Z_OPS-61-item194-W4-palace-o2.log:110,164–336,341–351). o2 at 64 MHz: Palace total 265.6 s. - Fixed ≈ 85 s: setup 48.1, estimation ≈ 33, the rest ≈ 4. - Iteration-bound ≈ 180 s: linear solve, preconditioner and coarse solve over 4 × 37 GMRES iterations, i.e. ≈ 4.87 s per iteration-of-four. - Peak 6.1 G. - Iterations scale with frequency as at order 1: 16–17 at 10 MHz, 31–32 at 64, 53–55 at 128 (item 194 W2 / F10b W2 / item 194 W3). The o2/o1 ratio at 64 MHz is 1.17. - ⇒ o2 10 MHz ≈ 19 iterations (15–25), Palace total ≈ 180 s (160–210). - ⇒ o2 128 MHz ≈ 63 iterations (55–75), Palace total ≈ 390 s (350–450). - Peak 6.1–6.5 G on both, against the 128 G service limit. - (P): spreads ≲ 0.15 % (o2 64 MHz: 0.0371 / 0.0248 / 0.0500 %); reciprocity ≈ 1e-10; σ_max < 1. - Ours p2 vs Palace o2 at 10 and 128 MHz: 0.0000 % per class (≤ 1e-6), the 64 MHz result. - Palace o2 vs Palace o1 (postpro_f05x_f10 / _f128) equals ours p2 vs p1 to the printed digit: 1.9821 / 0.4323 / 0.7216 % (10 MHz) and 5.8471 / 4.5018 / 7.2217 % (128 MHz).

Windows (bare, whole, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; -np ≤ 12; Palace v0.18.1, image fem-em-palace:0.18.1, compose profile palace). - Pre-check (not a harness call): ls logs/ops61/. - If f05x_o2_f10.json or f05x_o2_f128.json already exists, stop: never overwrite. Report it. - If postpro_f05x_o2/ is missing, (T) is "not measured"; continue. - W1 (≈ 2 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item229-W1-o2cfg "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py o2-configs'" - W2, 10 MHz o2: the price probe. Predicted 160–210 s: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item229-W2-palace-o2-f10 "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/ops61 && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 f05x_o2_f10.json'" - Price gate (binding, after W2). Read W2's Total (Elapsed Time Report) T₁₀ and its iteration count n₁₀. - The box factor is r = T₁₀ / (85 + 4.87 × n₁₀) (≈ 178 s at n₁₀ = 19). The projected 128 MHz total is r × 450 s, the upper prediction. - Run W3 iff r × 450 ≤ 540 s, i.e. r ≤ 1.2 (T₁₀ ≤ ≈ 215 s at 19 iterations). Print r, n₁₀ and the projection in the journal. - T₁₀ > 215 s ⇒ do not run W3. 128 MHz o2 is "not measured — price". W4 / W5 still run, and the item lands the 10 MHz half as a record. - W3, 128 MHz o2. Predicted 350–450 s on a normal box. The same command with f05x_o2_f128.json, labelled OPS-61-item229-W3-palace-o2-f128. After any kill, check docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps for a lingering fem-em-palace container before W4. - W4 (≈ 3 s), the new read; the probe's last window together with W5: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item229-W4-read "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py read --exact-strip-o2'" - W5 (≈ 3 s), the regression of the lift: item 194's W5 command verbatim, labelled OPS-61-item229-W5-regress-read. No probe edit after W4 starts.

Traps. - Never overwrite f05x*.json, flipx.json, f1 / f05 / flip, any existing postpro_*, or ours_f05x_p*.json. - freq-configs asserts its outputs do not exist, so do not re-run it. Item 194's files are present and it would fail. - An abort on a port set not aligned with the axes is a finding: never change Direction, Order, MaxIts or Tol in-slot. - A GMRES … did not converge line is a finding, not a retry: report the iteration count, and treat that run's S as not measured. - Compare S classes only; never read Palace's z_matrix_ohm or the aed key. - Palace's postpro_* and the configs are gitignored under logs/, so nothing new is tracked. The harness logs under docs/testing/logs/ are. - Record row and journal carry relative gaps and identity readings only, plus Palace's own numbers in full (version, config, mesh cited). No absolute S₁₁ / Z_in claim, and no Palace figure set against an AED one in any tracked file. Never open docs/private/, aed_results/ or COMPARISON_private.md. - Status 124 on W2 or W3: the price is the finding. Never lengthen the timeout or raise -np in-slot (no measured -np 12 Palace point exists).

Scope. Covered: Palace order 2 at 10 / 128 MHz on the exact strip mesh, its (P) set, and ours-vs-Palace from the tracked records. Not covered: - our degree-2 (F) / (G) at 10 / 128 MHz, re-solved (item 192 asserted them); - the PEC / copper hole columns (F22, step 2); - ANS-7's lumped RLC; - the private (a) / (b) / (c) reading, which is the weekly's; - any h-statement: one mesh, two orders; - src/ and any band.

Status it can move. - The OPS-61 row records step 1e. No glyph: 🟡 stays. - The row's §2-facing sentence can become "ours matches Palace to 0.0000 % at matched order in every class at 10 / 64 / 128 MHz, both orders". That holds only if W2 and W3 both land and every printed matched gap is ≤ 1e-6. - Rule (j): the Done-when names step 1c only. The review adds a step-1e sentence in its commit.

Negative result. - Palace aborts, or a log lacks 117 206 elements / Rs 43.75 Ω/sq / ND 753 062: record verbatim, open a known-issues entry, BLOCKED (rule (d)). - (P) red on either run: report every identity's number, park, BLOCKED. Never widen. - (T) misses ≤ 1e-6: the record and Palace's mesh have parted. Report the per-class gap and BLOCKED. Do not print 10 / 128 against the record. - Matched gap at 10 or 128 MHz ≫ 1e-6 with (T) green: a reading, not a failure. Print it; the review reads it. It would be the first frequency-dependent disagreement between the two codes. - W5 not reproducing item 194's digits: the lift moved the old mode. Revert the probe, BLOCKED. - Price gate trips: a partial record (10 MHz only). Not BLOCKED; the review re-queues 128 MHz at a quiet hour. - No PREDICTED RED line.

Outcome (2026-10-04 16:30 CDT slot): DONE — step 1e recorded, no glyph. The probe gained FREQ_SET_O2, o2-configs and read --exact-strip-o2. The (P) block of read_exact_strip_set was lifted into _p_check(name, path, tag). Pre-check: neither o2 config existed and postpro_f05x_o2/ was present. freq-configs was not re-run. Windows, all Status 0: W1 20261004T213348Z_OPS-61-item229-W1-o2cfg.log (0 s), W2 20261004T213356Z_OPS-61-item229-W2-palace-o2-f10.log (213 s), W3 20261004T213741Z_OPS-61-item229-W3-palace-o2-f128.log (351 s), W4 20261004T214342Z_OPS-61-item229-W4-read.log (3 s), W5 20261004T214346Z_OPS-61-item229-W5-regress-read.log (2 s). The probe was last edited before W1. Palace is v0.18.1, configs logs/ops61/f05x_o2_f{10,128}.json, mesh ops61_ans4_x1_strip.msh. - Palace log check: W2 and W3 each show 117 206 elements (:68), Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on attributes 21–24 (:79–82), ND (p = 2): 753062 (:110) and ω/2π = 1.000e-02 / 1.280e-01 GHz. Each has four GMRES solver converged lines: 26 iterations at 10 MHz (W2 :153,194,235,276) and 55 at 128 MHz (W3 :182,252,322,392). No line reports a failure to converge. - Price gate: T₁₀ = 211.423 s Palace total (W2 :307), n₁₀ = 26. Both are just above prediction: 15–25 iterations and 160–210 s. r = 211.423 / (85 + 4.87 × 26) = 0.999, and the projection is r × 450 = 449.6 s ≤ 540 s, so W3 ran. W3 measured 349.3 s Palace total (:423) at 55 iterations, against a prediction of 350–450 s and 55–75 iterations. Peak was 6.0 G and 6.3 G, against a prediction of 6.1–6.5 G. - (P), W4: f05x_o2_f10 reciprocity 1.390e-10, σ_max 0.999995411583, spreads 0.0963 / 0.0270 / 0.0619 %, separation 99.51×. f05x_o2_f128 reciprocity 3.261e-11, σ_max 0.999307666282, spreads 0.0167 / 0.0319 / 0.0329 %, separation 1834.92×. Column powers are ≤ 0.8835. The predicted ceiling of spreads ≲ 0.15 % held. f05x_o2 was re-checked green, with numbers identical to item 194. - (T) 64 MHz tie: ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["64"] vs postpro_f05x_o2 reads 2.464e-10 / 9.668e-11 / 9.883e-11, against a prediction of ≤ 1e-6. GREEN. - Ours p2 record vs Palace o2, matched order: 0.0000 % in every class. At 10 MHz the gaps are 2.542e-10 / 9.997e-11 / 6.236e-11; at 128 MHz they are 9.930e-11 / 8.685e-11 / 1.495e-10. That is the record's 10-digit rounding, and the frequency-dependent disagreement is nil. - C2″ (predicted ≥ 25×): ours p1 record vs Palace o2 reads 1.9923 / 0.4335 / 0.7239 % at 10 MHz and 5.6659 / 4.6653 / 7.7237 % at 128 MHz. Separations are 7.836e7 / 4.336e7 / 1.161e8× and 5.706e8 / 5.371e8 / 5.167e8×. - Palace o2 vs Palace o1 reads 1.9821 / 0.4323 / 0.7216 % (10 MHz) and 5.8471 / 4.5018 / 7.2217 % (128 MHz). That equals ours p2 vs p1 to the printed digit, as predicted. - W5: the output section is byte-identical to 20261003T110728Z_OPS-61-item194-W5-read.log (a diff of the two output sections is empty), so the lift did not move the old mode. - For the review: at both orders and all three frequencies, ours and Palace solve the same discrete system on this mesh. The §2-facing sentence the brief licences now holds. Still one mesh: this is not an h-statement.

docs.title: §9 item 234 — 2026-10-04 (chain F22)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-04 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain F22 as the 2026-10-03 weekly wrote it ("a Gmsh export of ANS-6's exact hole mesh and Palace's PEC column on it at 64 MHz, order 1 (order 2 after F19). Target: Palace. The first Palace run on a hole mesh — a capability probe, red is a record"). F19's 64 MHz degree-2 record has landed (item 226), so the order-2 leg runs here behind a price gate. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target moves. The sheets-and-κ ruling (§9, 2026-10-02) binds: exact CAD rectangles, κ off.

OPS-61 step 2a (§10 F22): the exact-rectangle hole mesh exported to Gmsh 2.2, and Palace's PEC column on it at 64 MHz. Palace's own (P) identities are asserted. Ours is set against Palace per class from our tracked records on the same mesh at matched order, printed. Ours needs no new solve. - Executor: implementer. Probe only (scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py); no test module, no src/. - Tier: heavy. Export and read at -n 1 in the complex container; Palace at -np 8. - Class: chain step (solve), measured median ≈ 23 min. - Cost: ≈ 23 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 10 code + W1 ≈ 1 + W2 / W3 ≈ 1 + W4 ≈ 3–5 + W5 / W6 < 1 + ≈ 5 spare). - Depends on: nothing. Every input is on main or on disk: - the hole route with exact rectangles: _sheets_build(True, as_hole=True, leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION), the call th14._build_ladder makes (tests/validation/test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:313; item 193); - ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD = 80 798 (tests/validation/test_ans6_exact_strip.py:100); - ours, degree 1: ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1["64"]["pec"] (:119–121; -n 2, 20261003T095650Z_ANS-6-item193-W2-solve.log:3096, reproduced to 10 digits by item 193 W3 and items 216 / 226 W0); - ours, degree 2: ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P2["64"]["pec"] (:154–156; -n 8, 20261004T184757Z_ANS-6-item226-W2a-p2-64-sweeps.log:1256–1257, reproduced by W2b); - logs/ops61/f05x.json as the config template, and logs/ops61/postpro_f05x/ for one printed cross-fixture line.

What "the PEC column" is on our side, and how it maps to Palace. - Our PEC column is TH-15 step 3's fixture verbatim: _problem(..., pec_facet_tags=None) pins every exterior facet (test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:339). On the hole mesh those are the outer box faces and the cavity wall, facet tag 401 (BIRDCAGE_CONDUCTOR_SURFACE_TAG, src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:266). The coil is a hole: there are no conductor cells (tag 1 absent, test_birdcage_conductor_hole.py (iv)). - Palace's equivalent is Boundaries.PEC.Attributes = [1, 401], with the box written as attribute 1 (EXTERIOR_TAG, probe :67) and the wall as attribute 401. - Why step 1a's writer cannot be reused as is. export() writes every exterior_facet_indices triangle as attribute 1 (:205–208). On a hole mesh that set includes the wall. So the wall would be PEC by accident, and the 0.3072 m² exterior anchor (:241–245, :374–376) would fail. The split is th14._outer_box_tags (:133): box = exterior ∖ 401, with a reduced census (exterior, cavity, cavity_exterior, outer, tag_collision). - Every exterior triangle carries an attribute. Palace applies its natural condition (PMC, n × H = 0) to any exterior boundary with no listed BC. An unlisted wall is therefore a silent magnetic wall, not a conductor. That is exactly control (K′) below, run on purpose. - Ports. th14._build_ports (:185) is the construction our PEC column was solved with. Its returned tags_f holds exactly N_i, the 0.007 × 0.008 SPEC rectangle (item 193 (M2)). The export writes N_i as 20 + i. The template's four LumpedPort entries are unchanged: Attributes [20+i], R 50 Ω (REFERENCE_IMPEDANCE_OHM = TERMINATED_PORT_IMPEDANCE_OHM, test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:125), +Z. So Palace reads Rs = 50 · 0.007 / 0.008 = 43.75 Ω/sq, as on f05x. F_i ∖ N_i is not written, because no BC reads it (f05x's 30 + i triangles were inert). - Materials are built from the mesh's own cell tags: phantom (σ = 0.5, εᵣ = 78) plus every other tag as air. Never list CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG, which is absent from a hole mesh. Whether Palace aborts on a material attribute it cannot find is unmeasured, so do not test it.

Code (probe only; additive; disclosed). - Constants beside FREQ_SET_O2 (:679): - HOLE_MESH_NAME = "ops61_ans6_x1_hole_strip.msh"; - HOLE_WALL_ATTR = BIRDCAGE_CONDUCTOR_SURFACE_TAG (imported, never restated); - HOLE_SET = {"h05x_pec": ([EXTERIOR_TAG, HOLE_WALL_ATTR], 1), "h05x_pmc": ([EXTERIOR_TAG], 1), "h05x_pec_o2": ([EXTERIOR_TAG, HOLE_WALL_ATTR], 2)}, mapping name to (PEC attributes, Order). - New export_hole_pec(), dispatched by export --hole-pec. This is a new function. export() is not edited and not lifted: the only way to regression-run it is export --exact-strip, which rewrites F10a's strip mesh and f05x.json without an existence check. 1. assert comm.size == 1. Then check logs/ops61/ and assert that HOLE_MESH_NAME and the three HOLE_SET JSONs do not exist (never overwrite). Load f05x.json and check it as o2_configs does (:866–876): Model.Mesh, four ports with Attributes [21]…[24], all +Z, Order == 1, Freq == [0.064]. 2. Build _sheets_build(True, as_hole=True, leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION). Then create_connectivity(fdim, tdim) and create_entity_permutations(), as _build_ladder does (:313–317). 3. outer_tags, census = th14._outer_box_tags(msh, facet_tags, comm) and tags_f, _defs, specs = th14._build_ports(msh, cell_tags, comm). 4. Write the triangle blocks with step 1a's entities_to_geometry pattern (:196–202): box → 1, facet_tags.find(401) → 401, N_i → 20 + i. Write the tets with step 1a's reorientation and Gmsh 2.2 writer, copied (:250–283). Assert no tet is untagged. 5. Write three configs from the f05x.json template, changing only these keys: Model.Mesh → HOLE_MESH_NAME; Domains.Materials → as above; Boundaries.PEC.Attributes → the HOLE_SET list; Solver.Order; Problem.Output → postpro_<name>. Print each config's Boundaries and Domains blocks. 6. Anchors (E1)–(E5) below are asserted after writing, as step 1a does, so a failure still leaves the artefacts to inspect. - New read_hole_pec(), dispatched by read --hole-pec. - It runs _p_check(name, path, "[OPS-61 2a W5]") (:714) on h05x_pec (required) and on h05x_pec_o2 if present. It does the same on h05x_pmc but prints only: the PMC wall is a control, not a fixture. - It imports the two ours records and ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P1_RECORDS from tests. Class means come from _circulant_classes, as read_exact_strip_o2's means does (:914–915). - If the gitignored logs/ans6_exact/ans6_exact_p1.json is present, it also prints the 64 MHz PEC 4×4's entry-level max|ΔS| and σ_max beside Palace's, labelled "gitignored source, printed only". - It never reads z_matrix_ohm, the aed key or any file under docs/private/ / aed_results/. - Dispatch: two new sys.argv branches beside :992–1005, plus a docstring paragraph. Every existing mode keeps its behaviour, which W6 proves.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - Export, W1: - (E1) tets = ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD exactly (as step 1b's export asserted its record). - (E2) CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG is absent from the cell tags, and the phantom tag is present. - (E3) census: cavity_exterior == cavity > 0 (the wall is all exterior), outer == exterior − cavity, tag_collision == 0. - (E4) box (attribute 1) area = EXTERIOR_AREA_M2 0.3072 within EXTERIOR_AREA_BAND (:70–71). - (E5) for each port: the numpy area of N_i, and the spec's sheet_width_m and gap_height_m, equal SPEC_AREA_M2 / SPEC_WIDTH_M / SPEC_HEIGHT_M (test_ans4_exact_strip_records.py:131–133) within STRIP_BAND, relative, as (M2) applies it. - Printed only: the wall's triangle count and area, with the area's ratio to diag["conductor_cavity_cad"]["area_m2"] (an inscribed triangulation of tori and cylinders, so a little under 1), and the N_i facet count per port. - (P), W5: item 159's set via _p_check, on h05x_pec and on h05x_pec_o2 if run: - reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND; - σ_max ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, and every column power ≤ 1 + 1e-9; - every S-class spread ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND; - pooled ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR × the worst. - Palace log check (executor, journalled). W2 / W4 each show: - 80 798 elements, and the bounding box ±0.12 / ±0.12 / ±0.10 m; - Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on attributes 21–24; - Configuring Dirichlet PEC BC at attributes: listing 1 and 401 (W3: 1 only); - ND (p = 1): 111946 (W2 / W3) or ND (p = 2): 570332 (W4). These are our degree-1 / degree-2 unknown counts on this mesh (…item193-W2-solve.log:3089; item 226). Palace counts every edge, as f05x's 140 460 = its edge count showed (20261002T021838Z_OPS-61-F10b-W2-palace-f05x.log:66,110). A free geometry check; - ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz; - four GMRES solver converged lines (Linear.MaxIts 100).

Ours against Palace (printed, never gated). A same-mesh, same-order record of ours exists. Its band is not imported, though: STEP3A_RECORD_RTOL is a re-recording band for our own code, not a cross-solver one. So the readings are printed, as item 229 printed its own. - (T1) ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1["64"]["pec"] vs Palace h05x_pec, |Δ mean|/|mean| per class. Predicted ≤ 1e-6 ("0.0000 %"), because the same discrete system is solved. The record's 10-digit rounding sets the floor near 1e-10. - (T2) if W4 runs: ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P2["64"]["pec"] vs h05x_pec_o2, predicted ≤ 1e-6. - (C3) Palace h05x_pec vs Palace postpro_f05x (σ = 800 solid, sibling mesh) per class, beside the same move between ours' two records (ANS6_…_P1["64"]["pec"] vs means(ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P1_RECORDS["64"])). Predicted equal to the printed digit. This is the conductor-model move as each code sees it. Prints "absent" without postpro_f05x/.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (K′) The wall attribute reaches Palace's operator — floor asserted, size predicted (item 159 (K)'s pattern). h05x_pmc drops 401 from PEC, which makes the coil wall Palace's natural PMC wall: the broken export, run on purpose. - Asserted: every class mean moves from h05x_pec by > KNOB_REACHES_THE_SOLVE (test_port21_feed_sensitivity.py:156, imported). - Predicted, printed: ≥ 10 % on at least one class, because a magnetic wall where the current path was conducting rewrites the coil. No ours-PMC record exists, so the size is not banded. - The read also prints h05x_pmc's own (P) readings, never asserted. - (C2‴) Order-mismatch separation — predicted ≥ 25×, printed (item 229's C2″ on this fixture). Per class: |ours p2 − Palace o1| / |ours p1 − Palace o1|. If W4 ran, the reverse is also printed: |ours p1 − Palace o2| / |ours p2 − Palace o2|. - The numerator is predicted to be our own PEC p1-to-p2 move at 64 MHz, computed from the two tracked records: ≈ 4.35 / 1.67 / 3.11 % (item 226's (N3) Cu move, 4.35 / 1.67 / 3.11 %). - The denominator is (T1), predicted ≤ 1e-6. So the predicted separation is ≥ 1.6e4×, and ≥ 25× is the item-229 bar. The ceiling is set by the record's rounding. - (P)'s power to discriminate was shown by item 159's flip (200.0204 % spreads against the band). It is not re-run.

Predictions (written first, printed). - W1: hole mesh ≈ 20–25 s at -n 1 (item 226 P: 23.30 / 22.49 s); window 45–90 s. Box 0.3072 to ≈ 1e-16. N_i facet count equal on all four ports. - W2 (o1, PEC): Palace total 15–30 s (f05x 23.35 s on 140 460 ND; this mesh 111 946); peak ≈ 1.3–1.9 G. GMRES iterations printed, not predicted (a PEC hole changes the operator; f05x 31–32). - W3 (o1, PMC): the same price. - (P): spreads ≲ 0.15 %, reciprocity ≈ 1e-10, σ_max < 1. - W4 (o2): f05x's o2 / o1 ratio was 265.6 / 23.35 = 11.4 (item 194 W4, item 159 W2). That projects 11.4 × T₁, ≈ 170–340 s; peak 4–6 G.

Windows (bare, whole, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; -np ≤ 12; Palace v0.18.1, image fem-em-palace:0.18.1, compose profile palace). - Pre-check (not a harness call): ls logs/ops61/. - If ops61_ans6_x1_hole_strip.msh or any h05x_*.json exists, stop and report: never overwrite. - If f05x.json is missing, run item 159's W0 export verbatim first, relabelled OPS-61-item234-W0-export. - W1 (≈ 45–90 s), the export:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item234-W1-export-hole "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py export --hole-pec'" - W2 (≈ 15–30 s), PEC column, order 1:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item234-W2-palace-hole-pec "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/ops61 && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 h05x_pec.json'" - W3 (≈ 15–30 s), the (K′) control: W2's command with h05x_pmc.json, labelled OPS-61-item234-W3-palace-hole-pmc. - Price gate (binding, after W2). Read W2's Total (Elapsed Time Report) T₁ and its iteration count. - Run W4 iff 11.4 × T₁ ≤ 450 s, i.e. T₁ ≤ 39.5 s. Print T₁, the iterations and the projection in the journal. - Otherwise order 2 is "not measured — price". W5 / W6 still run, and the item lands the order-1 half. - W4, order 2: W2's command with h05x_pec_o2.json, labelled OPS-61-item234-W4-palace-hole-pec-o2. After any kill, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps to look for a lingering fem-em-palace container before W5. - W5 (≈ 3 s), the new read; together with W6, the probe's last window:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item234-W5-read "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py read --hole-pec'" - W6 (≈ 3 s), the dispatch regression: item 229's W4 command verbatim (20261004T214342Z_OPS-61-item229-W4-read.log:12), labelled OPS-61-item234-W6-regress-read. Its output section must diff empty against that log's. No probe edit after W1 starts.

Traps. - Never run export or export --exact-strip. They rewrite step 1a's / F10a's mesh and configs without an existence check. Do not re-run flip-config, freq-configs or o2-configs, which assert that their outputs do not exist and would fail. - The first as_hole build in this probe runs at -n 1 (the probe asserts it). A gmsh failure deadlocks wider runs. - Palace on a hole mesh is untried. An abort is the finding: record the MFEM / Palace message verbatim. Never change Direction, attributes, Order, MaxIts or Tol in-slot. A GMRES … did not converge line is a finding, not a retry: that run's S is "not measured". - Write the wall as its own attribute. Folding it into attribute 1 passes the PEC tie but fails (E4) and voids (K′). - cell_tags.values and facet sets are rank-local. The export is serial by assertion; _outer_box_tags and _build_ports reduce internally. - Compare S classes only. Never read Palace's z_matrix_ohm or the aed key. - The record widths differ: P1 is -n 2, P2 is -n 8. Both are κ off. Never re-register a record from Palace. - Palace's postpro_*, the configs and the mesh are gitignored under logs/. The harness logs under docs/testing/logs/ are tracked. - Record row and journal: identity readings and relative gaps, plus Palace's own numbers in full (version, config, mesh cited). No absolute S₁₁ / Z_in claim, and no Palace figure set against an AED one in any tracked file. Never open docs/private/, aed_results/ or COMPARISON_private.md. - Status 124: the price is the finding. Never lengthen a timeout or raise -np in-slot.

Scope. Covered: the exact-rectangle hole mesh as a Gmsh 2.2 export with box / wall / port attributes; Palace's PEC column on it at 64 MHz, order 1, plus order 2 if the gate allows; its (P) set; ours vs Palace from the tracked records; the PMC-wall control. Not covered: - the copper column: Palace's finite-conductivity / impedance boundary on 401 against our Leontovich term. That is step 2's other half, for the weekly to enumerate; - 10 / 128 MHz; - the F-human rung; - any h-statement (one mesh); - the private (a) / (b) / (c) reading; - ans:6's tracked artefacts; - src/ and any band.

Status it can move. - The OPS-61 row gains a "step 2a record (F22, §9 item 234)" sentence: Palace's first hole-mesh run, (P) readings, and the matched-order (T1) / (T2) per class. No glyph: 🟡 stays. The row's Done-when names step 1c only, and step 2 is "at closure". - Rule (j), proposed Done-when sentence for the review: "Step 2a is done when Palace -np 8 solves the exported exact hole mesh's PEC column at 64 MHz, order 1 (80 798 elements, PEC on attributes 1 and 401, Rs 43.75 Ω/sq), its 4×4 meets item 159's (P) set at the imported bands, the PMC-wall control moves every class mean by more than KNOB_REACHES_THE_SOLVE, and ours-vs-Palace per class is printed against ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1['64']['pec']." - If (T1) prints ≤ 1e-6, the §2 / CLAUDE.md Palace clause ("matches ours to 0.0000 % at matched order") can extend to the PEC hole route. That is the weekly's call. - §10 F22 completes, and the copper half becomes enumerable.

Negative result (no PREDICTED RED: line; any red stops the slot). - (E1)–(E5) red: the exported mesh is not the solved mesh. Stop before any Palace window, park on attempt/*, BLOCKED (rule (d)). If (E1) alone is red, the mesher moved: open a known-issues entry. Re-recording under (1*) is record-reconciler's job, not this item's. - Palace aborts on h05x_pec, or the W2 log lacks 80 798 elements / Rs 43.75 / PEC on 1 and 401: this is the capability finding — "red is a record". Record the message verbatim in the journal, open a known-issues entry ("Palace v0.18.1 on the exported hole mesh: "), park the probe on attempt/* and mark the item BLOCKED (implementer-run.md step 4). The review writes the finding into the row as a record. - (P) red: report every identity's number, park, BLOCKED. Never widen. Our (G) is green on this mesh at degree 1 (item 193), so this would be the first identity-level disagreement between the codes. - (K′) red (the PMC wall moves S by ≤ 1e-6): attribute 401 is not reaching Palace's operator, so the PEC tie would be unexplained. Park, BLOCKED. - W6 not byte-identical: the dispatch edit moved an old mode. Revert the probe, BLOCKED. - (T1) or (T2) ≫ 1e-6 with (P) and (K′) green: a reading, not a failure. The item lands DONE as a record, and the review reads it. It would be the first disagreement between the codes. The ports, phantom and box were already shown to agree on f05x, so it would point at the PEC hole boundary. - W3 aborts or fails to converge: (K′) "not measured". (C2‴) still carries the control; journal it and continue to W5. - Price gate trips: a partial record (order 1 only). Not BLOCKED; the review re-queues order 2.

docs.title: §9 item 241 — 2026-10-05 (chain F23, daily provisional)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §9 rule (6), a provisional next step on live chain F. Item 234's outcome said "the copper (impedance-boundary) half is now enumerable" (docs/testing/attempts.md, entry "2026-10-05 02:26 UTC", "Hypothesis for next"). Chain F's Palace steps carry "Target: Palace" (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10, F21 / F22). This item sets no target, and it moves no band, tolerance or Done-when. The sheets-and-κ ruling (§9, 2026-10-02) binds: exact CAD rectangles, κ off.

OPS-61 step 2b (§10 F23): Palace's copper column on the exact hole mesh at 64 MHz. Item 234's export is reused unchanged. Attribute 401 (the conductor wall) carries Palace's finite-conductivity boundary for copper, σ = 5.8e7 S/m. The run is order 1, plus order 2 behind a price gate. Palace's own (P) identities are asserted. The comparison with ours on the same mesh at matched order comes from ours' tracked copper records and is printed. Ours needs no new solve. - Executor: implementer. Probe only (scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py); no test module, no src/. - Tier: heavy. Configs and the read run at -n 1 in the complex container; Palace runs at -np 8. - Class: chain step (solve), measured median ≈ 16 min (the 2026-10-04 18:00 restock, PROJECT_PLAN.md:3875). - Cost: ≈ 16 measured / ≈ 35 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 8 code + W1 < 1 + W2 < 1 + W3 / W4 ≈ 1 + W5 ≈ 3–6 + W6 / W7 < 1 + ≈ 5 spare. - Depends on: nothing. Every input is on main or on disk: - item 234's artefacts in the gitignored logs/ops61/: ops61_ans6_x1_hole_strip.msh (80 798 tets, box = attribute 1, wall = 401, N_i = 20 + i), h05x_pec.json as the template, and postpro_h05x_pec/port-S.csv (plus postpro_h05x_pec_o2/port-S.csv) as the PEC column; - ours, degree 1: ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1["64"]["cu"] and ["pec"] (tests/validation/test_ans6_exact_strip.py:116–121; -n 2, 20261003T095650Z_ANS-6-item193-W2-solve.log:3091–3101); - ours, degree 2: ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P2["64"]["cu"] and ["pec"] (:152–157; -n 8, 20261004T184757Z_ANS-6-item226-W2a-p2-64-sweeps.log:1256–1257); - th14.COPPER_SIGMA = 5.8e7 and th14.SIGMA_LADDER (tests/validation/test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:109, :111), th14.FREQUENCIES_HZ["64"] (:107, = FREQUENCY_64_HZ), and surface_resistance_ohm (src/fem_em_solver/core/cavity.py:543).

Our Leontovich term, and the Palace equivalent. - Ours. The copper column is th14._build_ladder's σ loop (test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:345–353). It runs on imp_problem, which pins only the outer box (OUTER_BOX_TAG, the exterior minus 401). The wall is left unpinned and given _leontovich_term (:160–171): γ ∮ (n × u)·(n × v̄) ds(401), with γ = jωμ₀/Z_s. This is Jin §5.8.3's third-kind condition, the same as core/boundary_terms.py:13–30. - Our Z_s = (1 + j)·R_s, where R_s = surface_resistance_ohm(ω, σ) = √(ωμ₀/(2σ)) (cavity.py:543–546; ω in rad/s; μ₀ = 4π·10⁻⁷, utils/constants.py:6). - The equivalence. δ = √(2/(ωμ₀μ_rσ)), so 1/(σδ) = √(ωμ₀/(2σ)) = R_s identically, and Z_s = (1 + j)/(σδ). - At 64 MHz, copper (ω = 2π·64.0e6 = 4.0212e8 rad/s): δ = 8.2607e-6 m, R_s = 2.087161e-3 Ω, Z_s = 2.087161e-3 (1 + j) Ω. Ours logged exactly this value: sigma = 5.8e+07 S/m: Z_s = 2.087161e-03(1+j) ohm (…item193-W2-solve.log:2911). - The (K2) control at σ = 5.8e11: R_s = 2.087161e-5 Ω, which is 100× smaller (:2926). - Palace's keyword. It is not confirmed from any file in the repo. No probe-written config uses it; the resolved JSON Palace writes (postpro_h05x_pec/h05x_pec_resolved.json) echoes only the blocks a config used; and the image ships no schema. docker/palace.Dockerfile copies only /opt/palace plus examples/. The 2026-10-03 daily notes that "Palace's lumped RLC and conductivity boundaries have never run here" (docs/planning/reviews/2026-10-03-daily.md:93). - Palace's documentation (v0.18 config reference) describes a Boundaries.Conductivity array with entries {"Attributes", "Conductivity" [S/m], "Permeability" (μ_r, default 1), optional "Thickness"}. It implements the thick-conductor Z_s = (1 + j)/(σδ) above. That is the keyword this item uses. - Boundaries.Impedance (Rs / Ls / Cs) is not used. Whether Palace combines those in series or in parallel is unverified, so an equivalent Rs / Ls pair cannot be written down with confidence. - W2 confirms the keyword by file, or the item stops BLOCKED with the reading. - The Palace configs. Copy h05x_pec.json and change only these keys: - Boundaries.PEC.Attributes → [1]; - add Boundaries.Conductivity = [{"Attributes": [401], "Conductivity": σ, "Permeability": 1.0}]. Never write Thickness or External: the thick limit is Leontovich's; - Solver.Order; - Problem.Output → postpro_<name>. - Attribute 401 goes in exactly one boundary block. Every exterior triangle still carries a BC, so Palace's PMC fallback warning must not appear (item 234 W3 shows what that warning looks like: 20261005T021915Z_OPS-61-item234-W3-palace-hole-pmc.log:52–56).

Code (probe only; additive; disclosed). - New cu_configs(), dispatched by cu-configs. 1. assert comm.size == 1 (or no MPI import at all). 2. Assert that none of h05x_cu.json, h05x_cu_o2.json, h05x_cu11.json exists (never overwrite). 3. Load h05x_pec.json and check it the way o2_configs checks its template (:892–904): Model.Mesh == HOLE_MESH_NAME, four ports with Attributes [21]…[24], all +Z, Order == 1, Freq == [0.064], and PEC.Attributes == [EXTERIOR_TAG, _hole_wall_attr()]. 4. Write three configs with CU_SET = {"h05x_cu": (COPPER_SIGMA, 1), "h05x_cu_o2": (COPPER_SIGMA, 2), "h05x_cu11": (SIGMA_LADDER[-1], 1)}, mapping name to (σ, Order). Both σ values are imported, never restated. 5. Print each config's Boundaries block. 6. Then assert (Z) below, reading σ, μ_r and Freq back from each written JSON. - New read_hole_cu(), dispatched by read --hole-cu. - It reuses _p_check (:742), _identities (:418) and the rel / means idioms of read_hole_pec (:1260–1273). - It prints each run's postpro_<name>/<name>_resolved.json Boundaries.Conductivity block, which is file evidence of the keyword and of the defaults Palace filled in. - If the gitignored logs/ans6_exact/ans6_exact_p1.json is present, it prints the entry-level max|ΔS| and σ_max of ours' 64 MHz cu 4×4 against h05x_cu, labelled "gitignored source, printed only". - It never reads z_matrix_ohm, the aed key, docs/private/ or aed_results/. - Dispatch: two new sys.argv branches beside :1389–1392, plus a docstring paragraph. export --hole-pec, read --hole-pec and every older mode keep their behaviour, which W7 proves.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - (Z), W1: the surface-impedance tie, pure arithmetic. - For each CU_SET config: |Z_ours − Z_doc| / |Z_ours| ≤ STRIP_BAND (tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58, imported), applied as a relative tie the way item 234's (E5) applies it. - Z_ours = (1 + j)·surface_resistance_ohm(2π·th14.FREQUENCIES_HZ["64"], σ_json). - Z_doc = (1 + j)/(σ_json·δ), with δ = √(2/(ω_json·μ₀·μ_r,json·σ_json)) and ω_json = 2π·Freq_json·1e9. - Also asserted exactly: σ_json == COPPER_SIGMA (or SIGMA_LADDER[-1]), μ_r,json == 1.0, and 2π·Freq_json·1e9 equal to 2π·FREQUENCY_64_HZ within the same band. - Printed: δ, R_s, and |Z_s| beside ours' logged 2.087161e-03(1+j) (…item193-W2-solve.log:2911). Also printed: the size of the CODATA-μ₀ variant (2.7e-10 relative), which Palace might use internally. It sits under the band, so a μ₀ convention cannot trip (Z). - Palace log check (executor, journalled), W3 / W5: - 80 798 elements and the bounding box ±0.12 / ±0.12 / ±0.10 m; - Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on attributes 21–24; - Configuring Dirichlet PEC BC at attributes: listing 1 only; - a Robin / conductivity configuration line listing 401, quoted verbatim, with any σ or δ Palace prints compared against W1's printed values to the printed digits; - no "no associated boundary condition … PMC assumed" warning; - ND (p = 1): 111946 (W3 / W4) or ND (p = 2): 570332 (W5), as in item 234; - ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz; - four GMRES solver converged lines. - (P), W6: item 159's set via _p_check, on h05x_cu (required) and on h05x_cu_o2 if it ran: reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND; σ_max ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE and every column power ≤ 1 + 1e-9; every S-class spread ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND; pooled ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR × the worst. Ours against Palace (printed, never gated — Target: Palace, as F22). STEP3A_RECORD_RTOL is a re-recording band for our own code, not a cross-solver one. So no band is imported for these readings. - (T3) ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P1["64"]["cu"] vs Palace h05x_cu, |Δ mean|/|mean| per class. Predicted ≤ 1e-6, if Palace's conductivity boundary is the same discrete term. Note the ceiling: if the two boundary models differed entirely, (T3) could not exceed ours' own copper-vs-PEC move (below), which is ≤ 6.4e-4. So (T3) alone is weak evidence, and (T3m) is the discriminating reading. - (T3m) The copper move, as each code sees it. Per class, Δ_Pal = mean(h05x_cu) − mean(h05x_pec) and Δ_ours = P1 cu − P1 pec (complex). Print |Δ_Pal − Δ_ours| / |Δ_ours| and arg(Δ_Pal/Δ_ours). Predicted ≤ 1e-3 and |arg| < 0.1°. - Ours' moves are 6.420e-4 / 2.811e-4 / 4.861e-4 relative (computed from :116–121). - The floor is set by the 10-digit record rounding and item 234's (T1) PEC tie (≤ 1.3e-10, 20261005T022223Z_OPS-61-item234-W5-read.log:48). Both are about 1e-6 of a move this size. - A conjugated or 1/σ-scaled Palace impedance would show as a phase or magnitude miss here. - (T4) If W5 runs: (T3) and (T3m) at order 2, against P2["64"]["cu"] / ["pec"] and h05x_cu_o2 / h05x_pec_o2. Ours' order-2 moves are 6.330e-4 / 2.866e-4 / 4.947e-4. - (C2⁗) Order-mismatch separation — predicted ≥ 25×, printed (item 229's bar). Per class: |ours P2 cu − Palace h05x_cu| / |ours P1 cu − Palace h05x_cu|. The numerator is predicted to be ours' copper p1-to-p2 move, 4.35 / 1.67 / 3.11 % (computed from the records).

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (K1) The σ boundary reaches Palace's operator — floor asserted, size predicted. - Asserted: every class mean of h05x_cu moves from h05x_pec by > KNOB_REACHES_THE_SOLVE (tests/validation/test_port21_feed_sensitivity.py:156, imported). - Backing: the same comparison on the same mesh, measured by ours. The class-mean moves are 6.42e-4 / 2.81e-4 / 4.86e-4 (records :116–121), and the entry-level max|S_σ − S_PEC| is 4.243e-4 / 1.285e-4 / 1.869e-4 (…item193-W2-solve.log:2918). The floor sits ≥ 280× below the smallest of them. - The size is (T3m), predicted only. - A Palace that silently ignored the block, or treated 401 as PEC, reads ≤ 1e-10 (item 234's (T1) floor). - (K3) Loss direction — asserted: σ_max(h05x_cu) < σ_max(h05x_pec). - Backing: ours on the same mesh at 64 MHz, degree 1. Copper is 0.999851545100 (…item193-W2-solve.log:2917) and PEC is 0.999904317474 (…item234-W5-read.log:65), a gap of 5.3e-5. Ours' σ ladder rises monotonically toward PEC: 0.999868053 at 5.8e9 and 0.999900690 at 5.8e11 (:2924, :2931). - A wall with a sign error (active rather than lossy) would put σ_max above PEC's. - Predicted, printed: Palace's copper σ_max equal to ours' 0.999851545 to ≈ 1e-9. - (K2) σ scaling — predicted, printed. h05x_cu11 (σ = 5.8e11) vs h05x_pec, per class move, and the ratio (K1) / (K2). - Predicted ≈ 100 (Z_s ∝ σ^(−1/2); the Leontovich perturbation is linear at this small Z_s). - Comparand: ours' measured entry-level ratio on this fixture, 4.243e-4 / 4.250e-6 = 99.83, with 99.83 and 99.79 for the other two classes (…item193-W2-solve.log:2918, :2932). - A Palace σ that never reached the operator reads ≈ 1, and a Z ∝ 1/σ reads ≈ 1e4. - It is not asserted: Palace has no prior measurement on this comparison. The (K2) run's own (P) is printed only. - (P)'s power to discriminate was shown by item 159's flip (200.0204 % spreads). It is not re-run.

Predictions (written first, printed). - W1: < 5 s.
