OPS-61 step 1f: Palace order 2 on ANS-4's exact-strip h = 0.0075 rung at 10 MHz, against our degree-2 record of that rung. Our side is not re-solved. It is read from xl entry 27's tracked log. - Executor: implementer. Probe only (scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py); no test module, no src/. - Tier: heavy. Export and read run at -n 1 in the complex container; Palace runs at -np 8 (the only width Palace has been measured at here). Class: chain step (solve), ≈ 12 measured min (18:00 restock table, PROJECT_PLAN.md grep "| chain solve |"). - Time: ≈ 55 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + W1 ≈ 2.5 + W2–W5 ≈ 4 × 4 (range 3.5–7 each) + W6 / W7 < 1 + ≈ 5 spare. - Depends on: nothing. Inputs on disk (checked 2026-10-13) or tracked: - logs/ops61/f05x_o2_f10.json (the ×1 order-2 10 MHz config, item 229) and logs/ops61/postpro_f05x_o2_f10/port-S.csv; - ours at h = 0.0075, degree 2, κ off, 10 MHz: the 10-digit S lines docs/testing/logs/20261005T070009Z_ANS-4-step6b.log:3702–3706 (header :3702, S_1k … S_4k at :3703–3706), σ_max 0.999995526884 at :3707, cells 282 198 and 1 822 094 degree-2 unknowns at :2167 / :3700; - ours at ×1, degree 2: ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["10"] (tests/validation/test_ans4_exact_strip_records.py:233).

Why the window is split four ways (the price, and the binding ceiling). - The weekly's ≈ 800 s is for one Palace command with all four excitations. That is inside the heavy tier's 1200 s with 1.5× margin. The binding ceiling is not 1200 s, though. A slot's harness call is a foreground Bash call capped at 660 s. PROJECT_PLAN.md:952 says so, and §5.1's standing caution at PROJECT_PLAN.md:2231 is that ≈ 480 s is the safe container ceiling for a foreground slot. So no single slot command can hold an 800 s Palace run. - Item 229's breakdown of the ×1 order-2 10 MHz run (20261004T213356Z_OPS-61-item229-W2-palace-o2-f10.log:296–308, 753 062 unknowns, four excitations at 26 GMRES iterations each, Total 211.4 s): - Setup 46.7 s, paid once; - Linear Solve + Preconditioner + Coarse Solve 126.8 s, i.e. ≈ 31.7 s per excitation; - Estimation 33.2 s, i.e. ≈ 8.3 s per excitation. - Scaled to the rung (1 822 094 / 753 062 = 2.42× unknowns): - Setup ≈ 113–192 s (2.42^1.0 to 2.42^1.6; it includes the coarse factorisation); - ≈ 77–97 s per excitation (linear in unknowns, with 0–25 % more iterations on the finer mesh); - ≈ 20 s estimation per excitation. - All four excitations in one command: ≈ 500–700 s. That is over the slot ceiling. - One excitation per command: ≈ 215–400 s, central ≈ 245 s. Peak memory ≈ 14–22 G against the service's 128 G. - So the window is split. W1 is the mesh export (our container, ≈ 90–150 s). W2–W5 are four Palace commands, each exciting one port with the other three as passive 50 Ω loads. W6 is the read. No command exceeds 590 s, and the item's whole compute is ≈ 17–29 min. Palace's factorisation is repeated four times. That costs ≈ 3 × Setup, the price of fitting the slot. It is disclosed, not hidden.

Code (probe only; additive; disclosed). - Constants, beside HOLE_MESH_NAME (:705): - H0075_RES = 0.0075; - H0075_MESH_NAME = "ops61_ans4_h0075_strip.msh"; - H0075_CELL_RECORD = 282198, a literal with provenance 20261005T070009Z_ANS-4-step6b.log:2167, :3700. No tracked constant holds this count; entry 27's (F′) asserted only "> 1.02 × 117 206". - H0075_SET = {f"f05x_h0075_o2_f10_e{k}": k for k in (1, 2, 3, 4)}. - New export_exact_strip_h0075(), dispatched by export --exact-strip-h0075. A new function. export() is neither edited nor lifted. Its only regression run is export --exact-strip, which rewrites F10a's ×1 strip mesh and f05x.json without an existence check. 1. Assert comm.size == 1. Assert that H0075_MESH_NAME and the four H0075_SET JSONs do not exist (never overwrite). 2. Load f05x_o2_f10.json and check it the way o2_configs checks its template: Model.Mesh == STRIP_MESH_NAME, four ports with Attributes [21]…[24] all +Z and R 50, Solver.Order == 2, Freq == [0.010]. 3. Build _build(np.zeros(LEG_COUNT), resolution=H0075_RES, leg_sheet_strip_fraction=GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION) (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_leg_offset.py:107–113). This is the build test_ans4_exact_strip_records.exact_rungs passes under FEM_EM_ANS4_EXACT_RESOLUTION=0.0075. Assert ncells == H0075_CELL_RECORD before anything is written. 4. The sheet steps, the N_i strip selection, the triangle and tet blocks and the Gmsh 2.2 writer are copied from export(exact_strip=True) (:143–383), with a provenance comment (commit and line span). Never call the function itself. 5. Write four configs from the template, changing only: - Model.Mesh → H0075_MESH_NAME; - Excitation → true on port k and false on the other three (R 50 Ω stays on all four); - Problem.Output → postpro_<name>. 6. Then assert (E1)–(E4) below. As in step 1b, a failure still leaves the artefacts to inspect. - New read_exact_strip_h0075(), dispatched by read --exact-strip-h0075. - It reads each present postpro_f05x_h0075_o2_f10_e{k}/port-S.csv with _read_port_s (:400). It asserts the column it keeps is labelled S[i][k] for the excited port k. If Palace labels a single excitation S[i][1], the read keeps that column by position and prints the labelling as a reading. - It assembles the 4×4. A new _p_check_s(name, s, tag) copies _p_check's (:752) assertions onto a matrix. _p_check is not edited. - It parses ours from the tracked log. Find the header [ANS-4 step5] 10 MHz kappa-off S (10 digits): and take the next four S_ik = lines. Strip any leading PASSED (pytest output is interleaved, :3703), and read the four complex tokens per line with the regex [+-]\d\.\d+e[+-]\d+[+-]\d\.\d+e[+-]\d+j. Open the log with gzip if only ….log.gz exists, since rotation may compress it. - It never reads z_matrix_ohm, the aed key, docs/private/ or aed_results/. - Dispatch: two new sys.argv branches beside :1693–1714, plus a docstring paragraph. Every existing mode keeps its behaviour, which W7 proves.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - Export, W1: - (E1) tets == H0075_CELL_RECORD (282 198) exactly. - (E2) exterior (attribute 1) area == EXTERIOR_AREA_M2 0.3072 within EXTERIOR_AREA_BAND (probe :89–90). - (E3) for each port, N_i area == SPEC_AREA_M2 and A/h == SPEC_WIDTH_M, within STRIP_BAND relative (tests/validation/test_ans4_exact_strip_records.py:131–133; tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58). - (E4) N_i ⊂ F_i, as step 1b's (A3). - (Tie) the parse, W6: the parsed 4×4's σ_max equals the log's printed 0.999995526884 (:3707) within 1e-9 absolute. This is a parse check, not a physics band. The 10-digit rounding moves each entry by ≤ 5e-11, so it moves σ_max by ≤ ‖ΔS‖_F ≈ 3e-10. A wrong block misses by ≥ 1.7e-4 (the 64 MHz block's σ_max is 0.999823496773, :3713). A miss means the wrong block was parsed: stop. - (P), W6, on Palace's assembled 4×4 (item 159's set, as _p_check applies it): - ‖S − Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND (tests/validation/test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86); - σax ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, and every column power 1 + 1e-9 (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:129); - every S-class spread ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:121); - pooled ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR × the worst (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:173). - Reciprocity here is a real cross-window check: S_ij and S_ji come from two different Palace commands. - Palace log check (executor, journalled), W2–W5: - 282 198 elements, and the bounding box ±0.12 / ±0.12 / ±0.10 m; - Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on attributes 21–24; - PEC on 1 only; - ω/2π = 1.000e-02 GHz; - exactly one excited port, k; - one GMRES solver converged line; - ND (p = 2) printed. It is predicted to equal our 1 822 094: on the hole mesh the two counts matched, 570 332. A mismatch is a reading, not a stop.

Ours against Palace (printed, never gated — OPS-61's precedent). - No cross-solver band exists. Items 159 / 194 / 229 / 234 / 241 printed the matched-order gap and predicted ≤ 1e-6. STEP3A_RECORD_RTOL (tests/validation/test_ans4_resolution_ladder.py:198) is a re-recording band for our own code, not a cross-solver one (item 234). "0.0000 %" in the §2 wording is the .4f % print, i.e. < 5e-7. - (T5) Per class and per entry, |Palace o2 − ours p2|/|ours p2| on the rung. Predicted ≤ 1e-6 in every class, with the 10-digit log rounding as the floor (≈ 1e-10). Printed as "x.xxxx %" and in e-notation. - (C-h) Palace o2 at h = 0.0075 against Palace o2 at ×1 (postpro_f05x_o2_f10), per class, printed beside ours' h-move 0.2527 / 0.0447 / 0.1375 % (20261005T070009Z_ANS-4-step6b.log:3726). Predicted equal to the printed digit: both codes see the same h-move.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (C2-h) Mesh-mismatch separation — predicted, printed. Per class: |ours ×1 p2 (ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["10"]) − Palace o2 h| / |ours h p2 − Palace o2 h|. The numerator is predicted to be the h-move above, 2.5e-3 / 4.5e-4 / 1.4e-3. The denominator is (T5), ≤ 1e-6. So the predicted separation is ≥ 447× on the weakest (adjacent) class, against item 229's ≥ 25× bar. The ceiling is set by the denominator's rounding floor: ≈ 4.5e-4 / 2.5e-10 ≈ 1.8e6×. - (P)'s power to discriminate was shown by item 159's flip: 200.0204 % spreads against the 0.5 % band, the sign-flip ceiling, 400×. It is not re-run. - A wrong rung reads as a mesh-move-sized gap. If the export built ×1 by mistake, (E1) fails first. If it built some other rung, (T5) prints the h-move (≈ 2.5e-3), not ≤ 1e-6.

Predictions (written first, printed). - W1: mesh ≈ 60–110 s at -n 1 (×1 strip 26.4 s; GEO-29 measured 281 728 cells at 0.0075 without the strip, so the cost scales ≈ 2.4×). Window 90–150 s. Box area 0.3072 to ≈ 1e-16; N_i 5.6e-5 to ≤ 2e-15. - W2–W5, each: - Palace Total ≈ 245 s (215–400); - GMRES 26–33 iterations (×1 26); - peak 14–22 G. - (P): reciprocity ≈ 1e-10. Spreads ≲ 0.1 % (ours on the rung: Z-class spreads 0.0346 / 0.0166 / 0.0168 %, :3707). σ_max 0.999995527 ± 1e-9. - (T5) ≤ 1e-6; (C-h) equal to ours' h-move to the printed digit.

Price readout and the 64 / 128 MHz decision (pre-registered; printed by W6 from the four W2–W5 logs). - Let T_e be the Palace Total and S the Setup line of the excitation-k run (Elapsed Time Report, Avg column). Let n₁₀ be that run's iteration count. - The projected single-excitation total at frequency f is S + (T_e − S) × r_f, with r₆₄ = 37 / 26 = 1.423 and r₁₂₈ = 55 / 26 = 2.115. These are the ×1 order-2 iteration ratios: item 194 W4 (37) and item 229 W2 / W3 (26 / 55). - The projected four-excitation single-command total is S + 4 (T_e − S) r_f. It is printed for the 10-14 weekly's xl entry. - Rule: if max_k projected T_e(128) ≤ 450 s (590 / 450 = 1.31× margin), then 64 / 128 MHz are heavy, as four single-excitation windows per frequency, and the next review writes that item. Otherwise they are an xl cost probe written by the 10-14 weekly. Print the rule's inputs and outcome.

Windows (bare, whole, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; -np ≤ 12; Palace v0.18.1, image fem-em-palace:0.18.1, compose profile palace, one-shot run --rm containers as every OPS-61 Palace window has used — no up / down). Never two heavy windows at once. No probe edit after W1 starts (rule (i)). - Pre-check (not a harness call): docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps shows fem-em-solver Up, and ls logs/ops61/: - stop and report if ops61_ans4_h0075_strip.msh, any f05x_h0075_*.json or any postpro_f05x_h0075_* exists; - f05x_o2_f10.json and postpro_f05x_o2_f10/port-S.csv must be present. - W1 (≈ 90–150 s), the export:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item418-W1-export-h0075 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 400 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py export --exact-strip-h0075'" - W2 (≈ 245 s, ≤ 590), excitation 1, the price probe:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item418-W2-palace-h0075-e1 "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/ops61 && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 f05x_h0075_o2_f10_e1.json'" - Price gate (binding, after W2). Read W2's Palace Total T₁. - Run W3–W5 iff T₁ ≤ 450 s. Print T₁, Setup, the iterations and the projection in the journal. - Otherwise columns 2–4 are "not measured — price". W6 still runs on column 1: it prints (T5) per entry of column 1 only, and (P) is "not measured". The item lands as a partial record, not BLOCKED, and the review re-queues or prices it. - W3 / W4 / W5: W2's command with …_e2.json / …_e3.json / …_e4.json, labelled OPS-61-item418-W3-palace-h0075-e2 / -W4-…-e3 / -W5-…-e4. - Minute gate: if W5 cannot start by minute 50, stop launching. The postpro_* directories are durable and gitignored, so the next slot runs the missing excitations with no edit and then W6. Commit what landed, marked "partial; columns k… pending" (rule (d)). - After any kill, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps and look for a lingering fem-em-palace run container before the next window. - W6 (≈ 3 s), the read:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item418-W6-read "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py read --exact-strip-h0075'" - W7 (≈ 3 s), the dispatch regression: item 241's W6 command verbatim (20261005T093623Z_OPS-61-item241-W6-read.log:12), labelled OPS-61-item418-W7-regress-read. Its output section must diff empty against that log's.

Traps already paid for. - Never run export, export --exact-strip or export --hole-pec. The first two rewrite meshes and configs without an existence check; the third asserts that item 234's outputs are absent. Never re-run flip-config, freq-configs, o2-configs or cu-configs; each asserts its outputs are absent. - The first 0.0075 export runs at -n 1 (the function asserts it). A gmsh failure deadlocks wider runs. - A slot command is capped at 660 s. Never put two excitations in one Palace command, and never raise -np (no -np 12 Palace point exists) or lengthen a timeout in-slot. A Status 124 is the price finding: record it and run no further e-window. - Docker socket. Every harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative (bash_guard.py). An executor that loses the docker socket mid-item stops and reports. - Orphans. After any killed window, check before anything else: for the solver container, docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0; for Palace, docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps must show no lingering fem-em-palace container. - An abort on a port set that is not aligned with the axes is a finding: never change Direction, Order, MaxIts, Tol or attributes in-slot. A GMRES … did not converge line is a finding, not a retry: that column is "not measured". - Parse trap: line :3703 starts with PASSED, and other S_1k blocks exist earlier in the log (:2498 …). Anchor the parse on the 10 MHz κ-off header only. (Tie) catches a wrong block. - Compare S only. Never read Palace's z_matrix_ohm or the aed key. Never re-register a record from Palace. - Record row and journal carry Palace's numbers in full (version 0.18.1, the four configs, the mesh) beside ours and their gaps (§5.4 (i)–(iii)). No Palace figure is ever set against an AED one in a tracked file. Never open docs/private/, aed_results/ or COMPARISON_private.md.

Scope. Covered: Palace order 2 at 10 MHz on the exported h = 0.0075 exact-strip rung; its (P) set on a 4×4 assembled from single excitations; the matched-order gaps against entry 27's record; the measured price and the 64 / 128 MHz decision. Not covered: - 64 / 128 MHz; - Palace order 1 on the rung; - the h = 0.005 rung; - any h-statement for Palace; - the copper / hole columns; - the private reading; - src/ and any band.

Status it can move. - The OPS-61 row (✅ 2026-10-05) gains a "step 1f record (F34, §9 item 418)" sentence: Palace on a second mesh, (P), and (T5) per class. No glyph change. - Rule (j): the row's Done-when is step 1c's and is met. A record sentence needs no amendment. - If (T5) ≤ 1e-6 in every class, the §2 / CLAUDE.md Palace clause ("matches ours to 0.0000 % at matched order") may extend to "on two rungs (×1, h = 0.0075)". That is the weekly's call. - §10 F34's price question is answered by the pre-registered rule above.

Negative result (no PREDICTED RED: line; any red stops the slot). - (E1) red: the export is not entry 27's mesh. Stop before any Palace window, park on attempt/*, BLOCKED (rule (d)). Open a known-issues entry only if the count moved on an unchanged image; a re-record is record-reconciler's, under (1*). - (E2)–(E4) red: the strip did not reach the mesh at this resolution. Report spans and facet counts, park, BLOCKED. - Palace aborts, or a W2–W5 log lacks 282 198 elements / Rs 43.75 Ω/sq: record verbatim, open a known-issues entry, BLOCKED. - (Tie) red: a parse bug. Fix it once in-slot, before W6 is re-run; still red, BLOCKED. - (P) red: report every identity's number, park, BLOCKED. Never widen. - (T5) ≫ 1e-6 with (P) and (Tie) green: a reading, not a failure. The item lands DONE as a record, and the review reads it. It would be the first matched-order disagreement between the codes on a refined mesh. - W7 not diff-empty: the dispatch edit moved an old mode. Revert the probe, BLOCKED. - Price gate trips: a partial record. Not BLOCKED.

Outcome (2026-10-13, 07:30 slot, DONE — record): every anchor green first time, nothing killed. (E1) 282 198 tets exact; (E2) exterior 0.3072 m² to 5.6e-17; (E3) each N_i 44 triangles, area / A/h to ≤ 8.9e-16 relative; (E4) N_i ⊂ F_i. W2–W5 Palace logs: 282 198 elements, Rs 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on 21–24, PEC on 1, 1.000e-02 GHz, one excited port each, one GMRES converged line each (25 iterations), ND (p = 2): 1822094 = ours; Total / Setup (Avg) 146.2 / 34.2, 143.5 / 33.6, 143.4 / 33.5, 144.5 / 33.9 s, peak ≈ 14.4 G — under the predicted 215–400 s, price gate passed (T₁ 146.2 ≤ 450). W6: (Tie) σ_max 0.999995526892 vs printed 0.999995526884, |Δ| 8.4e-12; each excitation wrote its own S[i][k] column; (P) PASS — reciprocity 1.525e-11, σ_max 0.999995526884, spreads self 0.0374 / adjacent 0.0173 / opposite 0.0161 %, column powers 0.813217154401 / 0.813253013484 / 0.812988621828 / 0.813196344670, pooled 9.5104 % = 253.98× the worst; (T5) per class self 1.917e-10 / adjacent 1.861e-11 / opposite 7.373e-11 ("0.0000 %"), per entry 1.8e-11 … 2.7e-10; (C-h) Palace's own h-move 0.2527 / 0.0447 / 0.1375 % = ours to the printed digit; (C2-h) separation 1.315e7 / 2.403e7 / 1.862e7× (the adjacent numerator is 2.112e-4 absolute = the brief's 4.5e-4 relative × |S| ≈ 0.47). Price readout: projected single-excitation 189.8–193.7 s at 64 MHz, 265.9–271.3 s at 128 MHz; four-excitation single command 658.7–672.1 / 962.8–982.5 s; rule: max_k T_e(128) 271.3 ≤ 450 s ⇒ 64 / 128 MHz heavy, four single-excitation windows per frequency. W7 output section diff-empty against item 241's W6. Disclosed gap: the module-docstring dispatch paragraph and usage: string were not added (rule (i) forbade the edit after W1 started); the new functions carry their own docstrings. Logs 20261013T123326Z_OPS-61-item418-W1-export-h0075.log, …123438Z_…-W2-palace-h0075-e1.log, …123719Z_…-W3-palace-h0075-e2.log, …123955Z_…-W4-palace-h0075-e3.log, …124228Z_…-W5-palace-h0075-e4.log, …124505Z_OPS-61-item418-W6-read.log, …124517Z_OPS-61-item418-W7-regress-read.log.

docs.title: §9 item 420 — 2026-10-13 (§10 chain T39; lane 1 → heavy)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-13 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain T, T39 (PROJECT_PLAN.md, grep "T39 (lane 1 → heavy)"), quoted, not changed: "Palace twin of the ESR-tuned F-small at degree 2, one frequency: OPS-61's hole-route configuration with the four gap sheets as unexcited Palace lumped elements (R = 0.2 Ω in series with C_in) and the feed as the lumped port, at 64.000 MHz; target: S at the tuned node against T26's at OPS-61's matched-order band; the price is the readout. Serial on nothing."

The rulings that apply: - the capacitor-ESR ruling (§9, PROJECT_PLAN.md grep "Binding ruling — capacitor ESR (operator, 2026-10-06"), (i)–(iii); - the sheets-and-κ ruling (exact rectangles, κ off); - the Palace directive (§5.4 (i)–(v)).

No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved.

What "the four gap sheets as unexcited lumped elements" means against our T26. Our T26 Route A (item 311; tests/validation/test_ans7_exact_strip.py:2401–2417) works like this: - Port 1 (the feed) is the bare 50 Ω port. - P2–P4 carry series-RC sheets series_rlc_impedance(f, r_ohm=0.2, c_f=C_in(r)) (src/fem_em_solver/ports/lumped.py:138). - The feed's own (r + C) branch is added in parallel in post-processing: Z_in = 1/(1/Z_bare + 1/(r + 1/(jωC))), as in ruling 311-Q5 and _z_branch (:2223).

So the twin is: - Palace port 1 = LumpedPort R 50 Ω, excited; - Palace ports 2–4 = LumpedPort, Excitation: false, carrying the gap impedance; - the comparand is the bare S11 at port 1, our S11_A.

The feed branch is circuit post-processing on both sides. It enters T40, not this item. The mesh is item 234's ops61_ans6_x1_hole_strip.msh (80 798 tets). That is the mesh ANS-7's _exact_geo builds: the same _sheets_build(True, as_hole=True, leg_sheet_strip_fraction=…) call (test_ans7_exact_strip.py:409–425), and ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_HOLE_CELL_RECORD = 80 798 (tests/validation/test_ans6_exact_strip.py:112) equals T26's printed cells (20261012T094112Z_ANS-7-item395-W0-esr64.log:2137). The copper wall is item 241's Boundaries.Conductivity, which matched our Leontovich term to ≤ 2.6e-10.

Does Palace's lumped element do series R–C? Not confirmed by any file in the repo. - What is confirmed: Palace v0.18.1's resolved LumpedPort block carries R, L, C, Rs, Ls, Cs (defaults 0.0) and Excitation (logs/ops61/postpro_h05x_cu_o2/h05x_cu_o2_resolved.json, gitignored; the tracked echo is docs/testing/logs/20261005T093211Z_OPS-61-item241-W2-palace-keyword.log:103–151). The keys exist. - What is not confirmed: how Palace combines them. The image ships no schema (docker/palace.Dockerfile copies /opt/palace and examples/ only). The drafter's reading of Palace's public documentation is that a lumped port's R, L, C form a parallel RLC (Y = 1/R + 1/(jωL) + jωC), as HFSS's Lumped RLC does (ESR ruling (iii)). - The brief does not rely on that reading. It discriminates in-run (control (K-short) below). The exact single-frequency series → parallel map is ESR ruling (iii)'s: - Q = 1/(ωCr), R_p = r(1 + Q²), C_p = C·Q²/(1 + Q²), with C = C_in(r), r = 0.2 Ω, ω = 2π·64.000 MHz; - then 1/(1/R_p + jωC_p) = r + 1/(jωC) exactly at that ω. - Values (drafter's arithmetic from T26_C_IN_R_X1 = 6.359301781809668e-11 F, test_ans7_exact_strip.py:2184): Q = 195.52429426, R_p = 7 646.14993 Ω, C_p = 6.35913544e-11 F (C_p/C − 1 = −2.6157e-5). Palace's sheet values are R_p·w/l ≈ 6.690e+03 Ω/sq and C_p·l/w ≈ 7.268e-11 F/sq (w = 7 mm, l = 8 mm, as Rs = 50 · 7/8 = 43.75 Ω/sq on f05x). The identity's residual in double precision is 3.6e-16 relative. - Entering 0.2 Ω as Palace's R would short the gap if the convention is parallel (ruling (iii)): |Z| 0.2 Ω against the series branch's 39.1 Ω. That misread is run on purpose as the control.

OPS-61 step 3a: Palace order 2 on the exported hole mesh at 64.000 MHz, port 1 excited at 50 Ω, ports 2–4 carrying the ESR-tuned capacitors, against our T26 Route A S11. - Executor: implementer. Probe only (scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py); no test module, no src/. - Tier: heavy. Configs and the read run at -n 1 in the complex container; Palace runs at -np 8. Class: chain step (solve), ≈ 12 measured. - Time: ≈ 40 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + W1 / W2 < 1 + W3–W5 ≈ 3 × 1.5 (1–2.2 each) + W6 / W7 < 1 + ≈ 5 spare. - Depends on: nothing. Inputs on disk (checked 2026-10-13) or tracked: - logs/ops61/ops61_ans6_x1_hole_strip.msh and h05x_cu_o2.json (item 241); - logs/ans7_exact/tune_p2.json (c_in = C_in(0)) and tune_p2_esr0.2.json (c_in_r); - ours' S11_A at (r, C_in(r)), 64.0 MHz: −2.392625126044e-01+9.637828488809e-01j (20261012T094112Z_ANS-7-item395-W0-esr64.log:2128; 12 digits; the latest window that rewrote item 311's ESR files); - ours' lossless S11_A at C_in(0), 64.0 MHz: −2.404062978868e-01+9.685876774136e-01j (20261011T093544Z_ANS-7-item311-W1-cin64-lossless.log:2055; C_in(0) 6.359009101426113e-11 F at :2058).

Code (probe only; additive; disclosed). - New ans7_configs(), dispatched by ans7-configs. 1. Assert comm.size == 1. 2. Assert none of t39_esr.json, t39_lossless.json, t39_short.json exists (never overwrite). 3. Load h05x_cu_o2.json and check it as cu_configs checks its template: - Model.Mesh == HOLE_MESH_NAME; - four ports, Attributes [21]…[24], all +Z, R 50; - Order == 2, Freq == [0.064]; - PEC.Attributes == [1]; - Conductivity σ == COPPER_SIGMA on [401]. 4. Import T26_C_IN_R_X1 from tests.validation.test_ans7_exact_strip (a module import, never a test_* name). Assert it equals tune_p2_esr0.2.json["c_in_r"] bit for bit (pure quantity). Assert tune_p2.json["c_in"] equals the literal 6.359009101426113e-11 (…item311-W1-cin64-lossless.log:2058) bit for bit. 5. Write three configs from the template, changing only the keys named. In every config, port 1 keeps R 50 with Excitation: true, and ports 2–4 get Excitation: false and R removed unless stated. Problem.Output → postpro_<name>. - t39_esr: ports 2–4 R = R_p and C = C_p from the map at 64.000 MHz. - t39_lossless: ports 2–4 C = C_in(0), no R. This tie is convention-free: a pure C is the same in series or in parallel. - t39_short: ports 2–4 R = 0.2 and C = C_in(r). This is ruling (iii)'s misread, the control. 6. Then assert (Z) below, reading R, C and Freq back from each written JSON. Print each config's Boundaries.LumpedPort block. - New read_ans7_esr(), dispatched by read --ans7-esr. - It reads each present postpro_t39_*/port-S.csv with _read_port_s (:400) and keeps S[1][1] only. Palace's S[i][1] for i = 2–4 are referenced to impedances that are not ours' 50 Ω and are never compared. - It prints each run's resolved LumpedPort block, which is file evidence of the keys and defaults Palace filled in. - It prints the readings below. - It never reads z_matrix_ohm, the aed key, docs/private/ or aed_results/. - Dispatch: two new sys.argv branches beside :1693–1714. Every existing mode keeps its behaviour, which W7 proves.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - (Z), W1: the map's own identity, pure numpy. For t39_esr, |Z_par − Z_ser| / |Z_ser| ≤ STRIP_BAND (1e-9, tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58), applied as item 241's (Z) applied it. - Z_par = 1/(1/R_json + jω_json C_json) and Z_ser = series_rlc_impedance(64.0e6, r_ohm=0.2, c_f=T26_C_IN_R_X1), with ω_json = 2π·Freq_json·1e9. - Also asserted: 2π·Freq_json·1e9 equals 2π·TUNE_TARGET_HZ (test_ans7_exact_strip.py:928) within the same band. - Printed (not asserted): R_p, C_p, Q, the residual (predicted ≈ 4e-16), and the short config's |Z| 0.2000 Ω beside the series 39.105 Ω. - (F) the mesh: each W3–W5 Palace log shows: - 80 798 elements, and the bounding box ±0.12 / ±0.12 / ±0.10 m; - Configuring Robin finite conductivity BC on 401 with σ = 5.800e+07, and Dirichlet PEC on 1 only; - ND (p = 2): 570332; - ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz; - one excitation, one GMRES solver converged line; - port 1 Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq; - for ports 2–4, whatever surface R / C line Palace prints, quoted verbatim and compared with the predicted 6.690e+03 Ω/sq and 7.268e-11 F/sq (t39_esr), 1.750e-01 Ω/sq (t39_short) to the printed digits. Executor-journalled, as items 234 / 241's log checks.

Ours against Palace (printed, never gated — OPS-61's precedent). No cross-solver band exists: items 159 / 194 / 229 / 234 / 241 all printed and predicted ≤ 1e-6. STEP3A_RECORD_RTOL is our own re-recording band (item 234), and the §2 "0.0000 %" is the .4f % print, < 5e-7. If the review wants T39's "at OPS-61's matched-order band" asserted, it must name the band (Q1 below); this brief does not choose one. - (T6) the tuned node: |S11_Pal(t39_esr) − S11_A| / |S11_A|, against …item395-W0-esr64.log:2128. Predicted ≤ 1e-6 if Palace's lumped R ‖ C is parallel: same discrete system, map exact at 64.000 MHz, floor ≈ 1e-12 from the 12-digit print, GMRES Tol 1e-10. - (T6-0) the C path alone: |S11_Pal(t39_lossless) − S11_A,lossless| / |S11_A,lossless| against …item311-W1-cin64-lossless.log:2055. Predicted ≤ 1e-6, whatever the R convention. - Printed beside them: |S11| of each run; the Z_bare each implies through _ANS7._z_from_s11; Palace Total and iterations per run.

Negative controls (rule (e); every factor predicted, since Palace has never run a lumped R / C here). - (K-short), the convention discriminator and the misread control. |S11_Pal(t39_short) − S11_A| / |S11_A|. - If the convention is parallel, it is predicted ≥ 5e-2, in [5e-2, 2.0]: three gaps at 0.2 Ω instead of 39 Ω rewrite the coil. - The ceiling is (1 + |S11_A|)/|S11_A| = 2.007 (|S11_A| = 0.99303). - Exactly one of (T6) / (K-short) is predicted to read ≤ 1e-6: (T6) if Palace is parallel, (K-short) if Palace is series. Printed as the "convention reading": parallel / series / neither. - (K-esr) r reaches the operator: |S11_Pal(t39_esr) − S11_Pal(t39_lossless)| / |S11_Pal(t39_lossless)|, printed beside ours' same move. Ours' move comes from the two 12-digit S11_A lines above: ≈ 4.9e-3, the drafter's arithmetic. The executor recomputes it and prints it. - Predicted equal to ours to ≤ 1e-6 relative. - A Palace that dropped R (or a typo key) reads ≈ 1e-10 here.

Predictions (written first, printed). - W1: < 5 s; (Z) ≈ 4e-16. - W3–W5, each: - Palace Total ≈ 70 s (60–130). Item 241 W5's breakdown, hole mesh, order 2, four excitations, 175.95 s (20261005T093309Z_OPS-61-item241-W5-palace-hole-cu-o2.log:312–327): Setup 30.6 s once, 29.7 s iterative and 5.8 s estimation per excitation, so one excitation ≈ 69 s. - GMRES 30–80 iterations. The tuned node may slow convergence; MaxIts is 100. - Peak 3–4.6 G. - (T6), (T6-0): ≤ 1e-6. (K-short): in [5e-2, 2.0]. Convention reading: parallel. - The price readout for T40: t39_esr's Palace Total, predicted ≤ 120 s.

Windows (bare, whole, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; -np ≤ 12; Palace v0.18.1, image fem-em-palace:0.18.1, compose profile palace, one-shot run --rm as every OPS-61 Palace window). Never two heavy windows at once. No probe edit after W1 starts (rule (i)). - Pre-check (not a harness call): docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps shows fem-em-solver Up, and ls logs/ops61/ logs/ans7_exact/: - stop and report if any t39_*.json or postpro_t39_* exists; - h05x_cu_o2.json, the hole mesh, tune_p2.json and tune_p2_esr0.2.json must be present. Never re-create one. - W1 (< 10 s), configs and (Z):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item420-W1-ans7-configs "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py ans7-configs'" - W2 (smoke, ≤ 30 s), the keyword check, item 241 W2's shape:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item420-W2-palace-dryrun "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/ops61 && timeout -k 10 25 palace -dry-run t39_esr.json'"

It must print "No errors detected". A configuration-time rejection of R / C on an unexcited LumpedPort is the capability finding (negative result below). - W3 (≈ 70 s), t39_esr:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item420-W3-palace-t39-esr "docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile palace run --rm -T fem-em-palace bash -lc 'cd /workspace/logs/ops61 && timeout -k 30 590 palace -np 8 t39_esr.json'" - W4 / W5: W3's command with t39_lossless.json / t39_short.json, labelled OPS-61-item420-W4-palace-t39-lossless / OPS-61-item420-W5-palace-t39-short. After any kill, run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps and look for a lingering fem-em-palace container before the next window. - W6 (≈ 3 s), the read:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-61-item420-W6-read "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 300 mpiexec -n 1 python3 scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py read --ans7-esr'" - W7 (≈ 3 s), the dispatch regression: item 241's W6 command verbatim (20261005T093623Z_OPS-61-item241-W6-read.log:12), labelled OPS-61-item420-W7-regress-read. Its output section must diff empty against that log's.

Traps already paid for. - Never enter 0.2 Ω as a parallel R (ESR ruling (iii)), except in the labelled t39_short control. - The map is single-frequency. R_p and C_p are exact at 64.000 MHz only. R_p follows 1/f² away from it (ruling (iii)), so never reuse t39_esr's values at another frequency. That is T40's trap. - The feed's (r + C) branch is post-processing, not a Palace element. Putting a capacitor on port 1 would make Palace's S11 a different quantity from ours' S11_A (ruling 311-Q5 applies in T40's read). - Compare S[1][1] only. S[i][1] for i ≥ 2 are referenced to Palace's port impedances, not ours' 50 Ω. Never read Palace's z_matrix_ohm or the aed key. - Never run export, export --exact-strip or export --hole-pec, and never re-run flip-config, freq-configs, o2-configs or cu-configs. - Lumped R / C in Palace is untried here. An abort is the finding: record the MFEM / Palace message verbatim. Never change Direction, attributes, Order, MaxIts, Tol or a key name in-slot. A GMRES … did not converge line is a finding, not a retry: that run's S is "not measured". - Docker socket and orphans: every harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative, and an executor that loses the socket stops and reports. After any killed window: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0, and docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml ps must show no lingering fem-em-palace. Never lengthen a timeout or raise -np. - Record row and journal: Palace's numbers in full (v0.18.1, the three configs, the mesh) beside ours, and the gaps. No Palace figure set against an AED one in a tracked file, and no AED ESR case exists to tempt it. Never open docs/private/, aed_results/ or COMPARISON_private.md.

Scope. Covered: - the bare S11 at the ESR-tuned node at 64.000 MHz, order 2, on the ×1 hole mesh, Cu; - the lossless C-path tie; - the convention reading and the misread control; - the price.

Not covered: - f₀, R_in, Q (T40); - 127.74 MHz; - the h = 0.01 rung; - order 1; - any AED reading; - a measured ESR; - src/ and any band.

Status it can move. - The OPS-61 row (✅) gains a "step 3a record (T39, §9 item 420)" sentence: Palace's first lumped R / C run, the convention reading, and (T6) / (T6-0). - The ANS-7 row gains "T39 (item 420, record): Palace twin of the ESR-tuned node at matched order". It holds 🟡: its Done-when is Q's h-statement (T30 / F31 / T41), which this does not write. - Rule (j): both rows read; no mismatch. - T40 (item 421) becomes runnable or is returned to the weekly by its own first step.

Negative result (no PREDICTED RED: line; any red stops the slot). - (Z) red: a config wrote the wrong R, C or Freq. Stop before any Palace window, revert the probe, BLOCKED (rule (d)). - W2 rejects the config, or W3 aborts at configuration: the capability finding. Record verbatim, and open a known-issues entry ("Palace v0.18.1 LumpedPort R / C on an unexcited port: "). Park the probe on attempt/* and mark BLOCKED. Unblock: the review re-poses on Palace's Boundaries.Impedance (Rs / Ls / Cs), with its series / parallel convention confirmed first. - (F) red (wrong element count, PEC on 401, PMC-fallback warning): the export is not the solved mesh. Park, BLOCKED. - Convention reading "series" ((K-short) ≤ 1e-6, (T6) ≫): a finding about Palace's convention, not a failure. The item lands DONE as a record and journals it. T40's config route switches to (r, C_in(r)) directly at each frequency (item 421's step 0 reads it). - Convention reading "neither" with (T6-0) ≤ 1e-6: the C path agrees and the R path matches neither convention. That is a reading for the review. Land DONE as a record, and item 421 stops at its step 0. - (T6-0) ≫ 1e-6: the C path or the port geometry disagrees on a convention-free quantity, the first lumped-element disagreement between the codes. Land DONE as a record with a known-issues entry; item 421 stops at its step 0. - W7 not diff-empty: revert the probe, BLOCKED.

Question for the review. (Q1) T39's target says "at OPS-61's matched-order band". No such constant exists, and every OPS-61 precedent printed the gap. The brief prints (T6) / (T6-0) against the ≤ 1e-6 prediction and asserts only (Z). Registering a cross-solver band (for example 5e-7, the "0.0000 %" print threshold) is the review's or the weekly's call, not the slot's.

The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Run every window in the foreground with timeout: 660000, container timeout -k 30; never two heavy windows at once. Probe only — no src/, no test module; never enter 0.2 Ω as a parallel R outside t39_short; never open docs/private/ or aed_results/."

Outcome (2026-10-13, 09:00 slot, DONE — record; no glyph): every anchor and control green first run, nothing killed. The probe gained T39_* constants, _t39_map, ans7_configs() (ans7-configs) and read_ans7_esr() (read --ans7-esr), additive; last edited before W1 (14:02:18 UTC). Palace v0.18.1, configs logs/ops61/t39_{esr,lossless,short}.json, mesh ops61_ans6_x1_hole_strip.msh. - W1 (Z): |Z_par − Z_ser|/|Z_ser| 3.634e-16 ≤ STRIP_BAND; |dω|/ω 1.482e-16; Q 195.52429426, R_p 7 646.14992955 Ω, C_p 6.3591354418e-11 F (C_p/C − 1 −2.6157e-5); T26_C_IN_R_X1 = tune_p2_esr0.2.json c_in_r and tune_p2.json c_in = 6.359009101426113e-11 bit for bit; the short control's |Z| 0.2000 Ω vs series 39.105 Ω (printed). - W2: Dry-run: No errors detected in configuration file "t39_esr.json"; the resolved block carries R_p / C_p on ports 2–4 with Excitation: false. - (F), W3–W5 (executor-journalled): 80 798 elements; box (±1.200e-01, ±1.200e-01, ±1.000e-01) m; 401: σ = 5.800e+07 S/m; Dirichlet PEC on 1 only; ND (p = 2): 570332; ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz; one excitation (index 1 on 21); port 1 Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq. Ports 2–4 verbatim: t39_esr Rs = 6.690e+03 Ω/sq, Cs = 7.268e-11 F/sq (predicted 6.690e+03 / 7.268e-11, equal); t39_lossless Cs = 7.267e-11 F/sq (C_in(0)·8/7 = 7.2674e-11); t39_short Rs = 1.750e-01 Ω/sq, Cs = 7.268e-11 F/sq (predicted 1.750e-01, equal). Circuit lines Index = 2: R = 7.646e+03 Ω, C = 6.359e-11 F etc. GMRES 34 / 35 / 33 iterations; Palace Total 51.765 / 53.164 / 51.132 s (log Avg; palace.json 51.778 / 53.176 / 51.143 s); peak 4.2–4.3 G; harness 53 / 55 / 53 s. - W6 (printed, none asserted): S11_Pal(t39_esr) −2.392625129e-01+9.637828488e-01j, |S11| 0.993037728250; (T6) 2.569e-10; (T6-0) 2.565e-10; (K-short) 1.437e-01 (S11 −9.9427e-02+9.9207e-01j, Z_bare +0.1348+45.24j Ω, in [5e-2, 2.0]); (K-esr) Palace 4.949105e-03 = ours 4.949105e-03, |ratio − 1| 1.994e-9; convention reading: parallel — Palace v0.18.1's LumpedPort R, C form R ‖ C, as HFSS's Lumped RLC (ESR ruling (iii)). Z_bare(t39_esr) +0.2815019608+39.10426459j Ω vs ours +0.2815019607+39.10426460j Ω. - Price readout for T40: t39_esr Palace Total 51.8 s ≤ 120 s per frequency — item 421 runs heavy. - W7: item 241's W6 command, output section diff-empty (41 = 41 lines, 0 diff lines). - Logs 20261013T140218Z_OPS-61-item420-W1-ans7-configs.log, …140228Z_…-W2-palace-dryrun.log, …140240Z_…-W3-palace-t39-esr.log, …140343Z_…-W4-palace-t39-lossless.log, …140447Z_…-W5-palace-t39-short.log, …140547Z_…-W6-read.log, …140556Z_…-W7-regress-read.log. - Disclosed gap (as item 418): the module-docstring dispatch paragraph and usage: string were not extended (rule (i)); the new functions carry their own docstrings.

docs.title: §9 item 421 — 2026-10-13 (§10 chain T40; lane 1 → heavy; depends on item 420)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-13 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain T, T40 (PROJECT_PLAN.md, grep "T40. Palace's driven sweep"), quoted, not changed: "Palace's driven sweep on T39's configuration — T26's five nodes; f₀ and R_in / Q read as ours are; target: f₀ within T26's zero resolution, Q within the 5 % the copper contribution is quoted at (the Q clause's public external check while F31 settles its h). Heavy if T39 reads ≤ 120 s per frequency, else the 10-14 weekly tiers it. Serial on T39." The ESR ruling (iii), the sheets-and-κ ruling and the Palace directive apply. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved.

Step 0 (first, before any code or window): the tier gate and the convention gate. 1. Read item 420's W3 log (…OPS-61-item420-W3-palace-t39-esr.log), the Elapsed Time Report Total, Avg column: T₄₂₀. 2. If T₄₂₀ > 120 s: stop. No code, no window. Mark item 421 BLOCKED with "tier returned to the 10-14 weekly (T₄₂₀ = … s > 120 s per frequency; §10 T40)" (rule (d)), journal it, and take the next item. 3. If item 420 did not land, or its convention reading is "neither", or (T6-0) read ≫ 1e-6: stop the same way, with that reason. 4. Otherwise the route follows item 420's convention reading. - Parallel: each frequency gets its own map (R_p(f), C_p(f)) at C_in(r). - Series: each frequency gets (R = 0.2, C = C_in(r)) directly. Under that convention one Palace multi-point sweep would be exact, but the brief still runs one point per window, for the price.

Why three frequencies, not five (a deviation from the §10 letter; the review rules — Q1 below). - T26 has no five-node set. Its Route A, the in-model quantity this twin reproduces, is read at the three tune points 63.9 / 64.0 / 64.1 MHz (TUNE_MHZ, test_ans7_exact_strip.py:929) through parallel_rows (ans:7, 07_tuned_copper_birdcage_driven_sweep.py:238–262). Its Route B uses item 196's seven ×1 nodes, not five. Item 214's five nodes are the h = 0.01 rung's. - parallel_rows reads f₀, R_in and Q from the bracketing pair alone (the − → + crossing interval and its linear interpolants). Points outside (63.9, 64.1) cannot change a row. - Five nodes 1.3 MHz apart (item 214's spacing) would interpolate Im Y_in across ≈ 3 half-power bandwidths (f₀/Q ≈ 0.39 MHz), against a band of 1.287e-5 (≈ 824 Hz). That is unreadable by construction. - So "read as ours are" means T26's triple. Item 420 supplies 64.000 MHz; this item adds 63.9 and 64.1.

OPS-61 step 3b: Palace order 2 at 63.9 and 64.1 MHz on T39's configuration, and with item 420's 64.000 MHz run, Palace's f₀, R_in and Q at the ESR-tuned node read through parallel_rows, against T26's Route A rows. - Executor: implementer. Probe only; no test module, no src/. - Tier: heavy. Configs and the read run at -n 1; Palace runs at -np 8. Class: chain step (solve), ≈ 12 measured. - Time: ≈ 30 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 6 code + W1 < 1 + W2 / W3 ≈ 2 × 1.2–2 (from T₄₂₀) + W4 / W5 < 1 + ≈ 5 spare. - Depends on: item 420, through step 0.

Code (probe only; additive; disclosed). - New ans7_sweep_configs(), dispatched by ans7-sweep-configs. - It writes t40_esr_f63.9.json and t40_esr_f64.1.json from t39_esr.json, changing only: - Freq → [0.0639] / [0.0641]; - ports 2–4 R / C, from the map at that frequency (parallel route) or (0.2, C_in(r)) (series route); - Problem.Output. - It asserts neither file exists. - It asserts (Z′) per config, reading the JSON back. - New read_ans7_sweep(), dispatched by read --ans7-sweep. 1. Take S11 at 63.9 / 64.0 / 64.1 from postpro_t40_esr_f63.9, postpro_t39_esr, postpro_t40_esr_f64.1 (_read_port_s, S[1][1] only). 2. Form Z_bare = _ANS7._z_from_s11(S11), then Z_in = 1/(1/Z_bare + 1/_z_branch(ω, C_in(r), 0.2)). The feed carries r too (ruling 311-Q5). Import _z_branch and parallel_rows from tests.validation.test_ans7_exact_strip; never a test_* name. 3. Read rows = parallel_rows([63.9e6, 64.0e6, 64.1e6], Z_in). 4. Print the per-point S11 ties against ours' S11_A at 63.9 / 64.1 (20261012T094112Z_ANS-7-item395-W0-esr64.log:2127, :2129). Each is predicted ≤ 1e-6.

Covered: Palace's bare S11, f₀, R_in and Q at the 127.74 MHz ESR-tuned F-small node on the h = 0.01 exact-rectangle hole mesh, degree 2, Cu, read as T38 reads them; the lossless C-path tie on the rung at 127.74 MHz; Palace's own ×1 → 0.01 move at 127.74 MHz beside ours'. Not covered: - an h-statement for Q (T41's, from F31 + T30); - the two-frequency ratio reading (Q(r)-move / Q₀-move 0.4525 against 0.2915), which is the 10-17 weekly's; - the h = 0.005 rung, whose C_F Route B twin is the weekly's to tier (item 444 (Q1)); - Route B rows (T38's :2209); - order 1; AED; a measured ESR; - an absolute tuned C, f₀, R_in or Q claim beyond "Palace = ours at matched order on one refined rung at 127.74 MHz"; - src/ and any band.

Status it can move. - The ANS-7 row's Q clause gains "T44 (item 448, record, provisional): Palace at matched order on the h = 0.01 rung reads f₀ within T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION and Q within T40's 5 % of T38's rows at 127.74 MHz, and its own ×1 → 0.01 Q move equals ours (−0.852 %)". With T43 that gives both Larmor frequencies. A record for T41. No glyph: the Done-when is Q's h-statement (T41). Rule (j): read; no mismatch. - The OPS-61 row (✅) gains a "step 3e record (T44)" clause. - §10 T44 recorded DONE (provisional; the weekly ratifies or reverts).

Negative result (no PREDICTED RED: line; nothing here is expected red; any red stops the slot). - (E1′) red: the file on disk is not item 444's rung mesh. Stop before any Palace window, revert the probe, park on attempt/*, BLOCKED (rule (d)). Never re-export in-slot; the review decides. - (Z′) / (Z0) red, or a W1 bit-equality / f_hz assert red: the wrong C, map or directory. Stop before any Palace window, revert the probe, BLOCKED. - A W2–W5 log lacking 140 270 elements, σ = 5.800e+07 on 401, PEC on 1 only, or the right ω/2π: park, BLOCKED. - (C1) red: report Palace's Im Y_in triple; park, BLOCKED; the review reads it against (T6′). - (f₀) or (Q) red with (C1) green: a disagreement on the external check on the refined rung at 127.74 MHz. Report the gaps, (T6′) and (C-h), open a known-issues entry, park, BLOCKED. Never widen, re-map or change r. - (f₀) green against T22P_ZERO_RESOLUTION but red against T21P_ZERO_RESOLUTION: not predicted (gaps ≈ 1e-10). If it happens, BLOCKED as above, and the band question goes to the weekly with the number (ruling 2026-10-13 10:30 (3)). - (T6′) ≫ 1e-6, or (C-h) ≠ ours' move beyond ≈ 1e-8 on Q, with (f₀) / (Q) green: a reading, not a failure. DONE as a record with a known-issues entry: the codes agree on T40's targets but not at matched order on the rung, so T41 cannot cite this item as "the discretisation's" at 127.74 MHz. - (T6-0‴) ≫ 1e-6: a convention-free disagreement on the rung. DONE as a record with a known-issues entry (item 420's disposition); (f₀) / (Q) are still read. - W7 or W8 not diff-empty: revert the probe, BLOCKED. - Price gate trips: a partial record, not BLOCKED.

Questions for the review / weekly. - (Q1) T44 is chain T's third rule (6) step since the 10-12 weekly, the last one allowed; no further provisional chain-T step can be written before the weekly. - (Q2) If T44 lands green, both Larmor frequencies carry a matched-order Palace twin on the h = 0.01 rung. Whether T41 then needs Palace at h = 0.005 (item 444 (Q1)) or can write "unconverged, the discretisation's" from these two records is the weekly's ruling.

Spawn line: "Use the implementer agent to execute OPS-61 §9 item 448 per docs/planning/chunks/OPS-61.md (read the latest Review ruling paragraph first). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Run every window in the foreground with timeout: 660000, container timeout -k 30; configs and the read at -n 1, Palace at -np 8. Reuse item 444's ops61_ans6_h0010_hole_strip.msh (never re-export). One frequency per Palace window, each with its own map; C_in(r, h) = 1.5288749690061608e-11 F from logs/ans7_exact/t127.74/ (never a ×1 or 64 MHz literal); the lossless config's Freq set to 127.74 MHz. The price gate after W2 binds. Probe only — no src/, no test module; never run an export or older *-configs mode; never overwrite t39_* / t40_* / t42_* / t43_*; never open docs/private/ or aed_results/."

docs.title: §9 item 454 — 2026-10-14 (§10 chain F37, daily — provisional; chain step, solve)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-14 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §9 rule (6) (PROJECT_PLAN.md, grep "Rule (6), the chain-extension licence"): the next numbered step of live §10 chain F toward its remaining subgoal (the copper-loss rung and the public tables, PROJECT_PLAN.md grep "Chain F — closed on the h-statement"), tagged (daily, 2026-10-14 — provisional); the weekly ratifies or reverts. It is chain F's second rule (6) step since the 10-12 weekly (F36 = item 437 the first). F37 (provisional): OPS-61 step 2a / 2b's ×1-hole Palace twin (items 234 / 241) moved onto F26's copper-loss h-rung — ANS-6 step 5b's h = 0.0075 exact hole mesh (xl entry 31, docs/testing/logs/20261012T070009Z_ANS-6-step5b.log) — exactly as F34 (items 418 / 434 / 435) moved step 1's strip twin onto the 0.0075 strip rung. Target: F34's, imported, not new — our identities (P) asserted on Palace's 4×4 at the imported bands; the per-class matched-order gap to entry 31's degree-2 class means printed beside the ≤ 1e-6 precedent (no cross-solver band exists: 2026-10-13 rulings (1) / (4)); Palace's own ×1 → 0.0075 move printed beside ours (C-h); the rung's Cu − PEC move (step 2b's (T3m) analogue) printed. The Palace directive (§5.4 (i)–(v)), the sheets-and-κ ruling (exact rectangles, κ off) and the 2026-10-13 rulings bind. No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved.

Split (the price forces it; derivation under "Price"). Both columns need 4 excitations × 2 conductor models = eight single-excitation Palace windows plus a fresh export. That is ≈ 57 predicted min, past the minute-50 gate. This item is the copper half, because the copper-loss rung is the chain's subject. It writes the shared code for both columns (as item 434 wrote item 435's) and runs Cu only. The PEC half (four windows, no probe edit) is the 2026-10-15 03:00 review's to queue; its shape is in (Q1) below. No second item number is drawn here.

OPS-61 step 2c (§10 F37, Cu half): export the h = 0.0075 exact-rectangle hole mesh, then Palace order 2 with Boundaries.Conductivity (σ = 5.8e7 S/m) on wall 401 at 64 MHz, one excitation per window, against entry 31's degree-2 copper 4×4. Ours is not re-solved: it is read from entry 31's tracked log. - Executor: implementer. Probe only (scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py); no test module, no src/. - Tier: heavy. Export, configs and read run at -n 1 in the complex container; Palace runs at -np 8 (the only width Palace has been measured at here). Class: chain step (solve), ≈ 8 measured min (the 10:30 restock's class median). - Time: ≈ 48 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 15 code + W1 ≈ 1.5 (60–90 s) + W2 < 1 + W3–W6 4 × ≈ 2.4 (140 s central, 115–180 s each) + W7–W9 < 1 + ≈ 5 spare. - Depends on: nothing. Inputs on disk (checked read-only 2026-10-14) or tracked: - logs/ops61/h05x_cu_o2.json and h05x_pec_o2.json (the ×1 hole order-2 configs, items 241 / 234; templates, never overwritten); - postpro_h05x_cu_o2/port-S.csv and postpro_h05x_pec_o2/port-S.csv (Palace ×1 order 2, four excitations each). - Absent, as required: ops61_ans6_h0075_hole_strip.msh, any h05x_h0075_*.json, any postpro_h05x_h0075_*.

What exists on our side (the comparand; not re-solved). Entry 31, 20261012T070009Z_ANS-6-step5b.log: -n 16 xl, degree 2, κ off, 64 MHz only, Status 0. Ledger row "ANS-6-step5b" in docs/testing/xl-ledger.md. Line numbers below are into this log. - Mesh. :2093 reads hole flag on: cells=226904 build 51.53 s. :3101 reads hole mesh 226904 cells, mesh 52.0 s, -n 16; census {'exterior': 40212, 'cavity': 27352, 'cavity_exterior': 27352, 'outer': 12860, 'tag_collision': 0}. :3102 and :4587 give 1 538 030 degree-2 unknowns. The mesh is th14._build_ladder's call _sheets_build(True, as_hole=True, resolution=0.0075, leg_sheet_strip_fraction=float(GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION)) (tests/validation/test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:310–314; knob FEM_EM_EXACT_ANS6_RESOLUTION, tests/validation/test_ans6_exact_strip.py:189, forwarded at :491–500). - PEC 4×4, 10 digits: :4556–4559 (rows S_PEC_1k = … S_PEC_4k =), under the header :4555 [TH-14 step2] f = 6.400000e+07 Hz: PEC sweep 250.2 s, …. - Cu 4×4, 10 digits: :4561–4564 (rows S_1k = … S_4k =), under the header :4560 sigma = 5.8e+07 S/m: Z_s = 2.087161e-03(1+j) ohm, sweep 260.4 s. That is the same Z_s as item 241's (Z) tie, which read 0.0. σ_max 0.999904939998 at :4565. - Class means, 10 digits: Cu at :4589, PEC at :4590. - Cu − PEC relative gap per class: 0.0615 / 0.0279 / 0.0479 % (:4592). - Ours' ×1 → 0.0075 move: Cu 0.1206 / 0.0506 / 0.1091 % (:4593) and PEC 0.1193 / 0.0501 / 0.1081 % (:4594). Both are against ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P2["64"] (tests/validation/test_ans6_exact_strip.py:163–169, -n 8). - σ ladder on the rung (rising, the (K3′) backing): 0.999904939998 (Cu, :4565) < 0.999905161481 (5.8e9, :4572) < 0.999908196413 (5.8e11, :4579). The PEC-limit max|dS| is 4.139e-06 (:4580). - No tracked constant holds the rung's class means or its cell count. grep -rn 'h0075\|0p0075\|STEP5B\|226904' tests/ finds none for the hole route. test_ans6_exact_strip.py asserts only cells > KNOB_CELL_FACTOR × 80 798 (:448, :769). So the comparand is the tracked log, as item 418 read entry 27's.

Price (from measurement; F34's rule). The non-Setup Palace cost per (ND unknown × GMRES iteration) is measured on three fixtures: - ×1 hole Cu o2: (175.950 − 30.604) / 4 = 36.3 s per excitation at 30–31 iterations on 570 332 ND, i.e. 2.10e-6 s (20261005T093309Z_OPS-61-item241-W5-palace-hole-cu-o2.log:318, :327, iterations :161–296). - 0.0075 strip, 64 MHz, e1: 185.767 − 32.911 = 152.9 s at 43 iterations on 1 822 094 ND, i.e. 1.95e-6 s (20261013T170207Z_OPS-61-item434-W2-palace-h0075-f64-e1.log:101, :159, :181, :190). - h = 0.01 hole, single excitation: 94.502 − 16.631 = 77.9 s at 40 iterations on 968 016 ND, i.e. 2.01e-6 s (item 444 W3).

Scaled to the 0.0075 hole (1 538 030 ND, predicted equal to ours, as on every prior mesh): - Iterations: 30–31 at ×1 hole. On the strip, ×1 → 0.0075 raised 37 → 43 (×1.16), so ≈ 35 here (bracket 30–45). - Per excitation, non-Setup: 1 538 030 × 35 × 2.05e-6 ≈ 110 s (90–145). - Setup: 16.6 s at 968 k ND and 32.9 s at 1.82 M ND, so ≈ 25–35 s. - One excitation per command: ≈ 140 s (115–180). Peak ≈ 12.5 G (11–16 G; 14.8 G × 0.844 from item 434), against the service's 128 G. - All four excitations in one command: ≈ 470 s (390–615). That is above F34's 450 s rule and §5.1's ≈ 480 s safe foreground ceiling, so this item runs one excitation per window. The cost is ≈ 3 × Setup (≈ 90 s), disclosed. - Both columns: the PEC column is ≈ 0.91× Cu (×1 hole: 160.575 vs 175.950 s, 20261005T021936Z_OPS-61-item234-W4-palace-hole-pec-o2.log:324), so ≈ 9 more minutes. With the export and the code, that is ≈ 57 min, which fails the minute-50 gate. Hence the split above. - Export: the rung mesh built in 51.53 s at -n 16 (gmsh is serial on rank 0; :2093). Item 418's 0.0075 strip export took 56.77 s at -n 1 (window 61 s, 20261013T123326Z_OPS-61-item418-W1-export-h0075.log:1862, :1867), and item 444's h = 0.01 hole export took 32.70 s (window 37 s). So W1 ≈ 55–75 s, window 60–90 s. Every window is ≪ the 590 s container timeout and the 1 200 s heavy ceiling.

Code (probe only; additive; disclosed; written once, covering both columns). - Pre-check for the code: grep -n "hole-h0075" scripts/probes/ops61_step1a_palace_ans4.py. If it is dispatched, make no probe edit. - Constants beside T44_*, each with its log-line provenance comment: - H0075_HOLE_MESH_NAME = "ops61_ans6_h0075_hole_strip.msh"; - H0075_HOLE_CELL_RECORD = 226904, a literal (:2093, :3101, :4587; no tracked constant holds it); - H0075_HOLE_ND_P2 = 1538030 (:3102; a predicted Palace reading, not an anchor); - H0075_HOLE_SETS = {col: {f"h05x_h0075_{col}_o2_e{k}": k for k in (1, 2, 3, 4)} for col in ("cu", "pec")}; - H0075_HOLE_TEMPLATES = {"cu": "h05x_cu_o2.json", "pec": "h05x_pec_o2.json"}; - H0075_HOLE_OURS_LOG (the entry 31 log path); - H0075_HOLE_OURS, per column: - the header prefix ("sigma = 5.8e+07 S/m: Z_s =" for Cu, "[TH-14 step2] f = 6.400000e+07 Hz: PEC sweep" for PEC); - the row label ("S_" / "S_PEC_"); - the 10-digit class means (:4589 / :4590); - the printed σ_max (Cu 0.999904939998; PEC None, since it is not printed at 10 digits); - the h-move (:4593 / :4594); - the Palace ×1 output (postpro_h05x_cu_o2 / postpro_h05x_pec_o2); - H0075_HOLE_CU_PEC_GAP_OURS = {"self": 6.15e-4, "adjacent": 2.79e-4, "opposite": 4.79e-4} (:4592).

H0075_RES, H0075_TIE_BAND, HOLE_MESH_NAME, T43_GLOBAL_TAGS and _hole_wall_attr() are reused, not copied. - New export_hole_h0075(), dispatched by export --hole-h0075. A copy of export_hole_h001 (:3595–3792; provenance comment with commit and span) that writes the mesh only. export_hole_h001 is neither edited nor called. Changes from that function: - resolution=float(H0075_RES), H0075_HOLE_MESH_NAME, H0075_HOLE_CELL_RECORD, and the tag [OPS-61 2c W1]; - drop assert H001_RES == H_RES; - (E6) reads the cell-tag set from h05x_cu_o2.json's Domains.Materials, the template actually used, instead of t39_esr.json, and also asserts it equals T43_GLOBAL_TAGS; - print the tet and element counts, never the file's byte size (the private-leak hook trap, items 434 / 435).

Like its source, it asserts comm.size == 1, asserts the mesh is absent, and asserts ncells == 226 904 before anything is written. - New hole_h0075_configs(col), dispatched by hole-h0075-configs --cu / --pec. 1. Assert -n 1 (or no MPI). Assert the four H0075_HOLE_SETS[col] JSONs do not exist. 2. (E1′) Parse H0075_HOLE_MESH_NAME's $Elements type-4 count and assert it == 226 904 before any write (item 434's parse; print the count only). 3. Load H0075_HOLE_TEMPLATES[col] and check it: - Model.Mesh == HOLE_MESH_NAME; - four ports, Attributes [21]…[24], +Z, R 50, Excitation 1…4; - Order == 2, Freq == [0.064]; - Cu: PEC.Attributes == [1] and Conductivity == [{"Attributes": [401], "Conductivity": th14.COPPER_SIGMA, "Permeability": 1.0}], with no Thickness / External key; - PEC: PEC.Attributes == [1, 401] and no Conductivity key. 4. Write four configs, changing only Model.Mesh → H0075_HOLE_MESH_NAME, each port's Excitation → true on k and false on the other three (item 418's single-excitation form), and Problem.Output → postpro_<name>. 5. Read each config back and assert the template diff is exactly those keys. This carries item 241's (Z) tie over unchanged (σ, μ_r and Freq are untouched; (Z) read 0.0, 20261005T093201Z_OPS-61-item241-W1-cu-configs.log). - New _ours_hole_rung_s(log, header_prefix, label). A copy of _ours_rung_s (:2268–2288) with two changes: the header is matched by startswith on the stripped line (exactly one match asserted), and the row prefix is f"{label}{k}k =". _ours_rung_s asserts S_{k}k = and cannot parse the S_PEC_ block; it is not edited. Leading PASSED runs are stripped as before, and a .log.gz is opened if rotation compressed the log. - New read_hole_h0075(col), dispatched by read --hole-h0075 --cu / --pec. A copy of read_exact_strip_h0075_freq (:2291–2402, provenance comment) with the hole set, ours' block, the ×1 Palace output and ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P2["64"][col] substituted. Its additions: - (Tie) on the class means (and on σ_max for Cu); - ours' and Palace's _class_spread printed side by side; - (K1′) / (K3′) in --cu mode, against ours' parsed PEC 4×4; - in --pec mode, if all four Cu columns are present, Palace-internal (K1) / (K3) and (T3m-h) (below); - the price section reading *_OPS-61-item*-W*-palace-hole-h0075-{col}-e*.log and printing measured Total / Setup / iterations / peak beside this brief's 115–180 s.

read_exact_strip_h0075_freq, read_hole_cu and read_hole_pec are not edited. It never reads z_matrix_ohm, the aed key, docs/private/ or aed_results/. - Dispatch: five new exact-list sys.argv branches, first in __main__ as items 436 / 444 / 448 placed theirs. Every existing mode keeps its behaviour, which W8 / W9 prove.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported, never restated). - Export, W1: - (E1) tets == 226 904, asserted before the write and again parsed from the written file. - (E2)–(E5) as export_hole_pec's: - no CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG, and the phantom tag is present; - the census holds cavity_exterior == cavity > 0, outer == exterior − cavity and tag_collision == 0 (predicted 40 212 / 27 352 / 12 860, as :3101); - box area == EXTERIOR_AREA_M2 within EXTERIOR_AREA_BAND; - per port, the N_i area / width / height == SPEC_AREA_M2 / SPEC_WIDTH_M / SPEC_HEIGHT_M within STRIP_BAND (tests/validation/test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58). These are the exact rectangles at the rung, which is the precondition of the sheets-and-κ ruling. - (E6) the cell-tag set equals h05x_cu_o2.json's Materials set, which equals T43_GLOBAL_TAGS. - (E1′), W2: the type-4 count parsed from the file == 226 904. - (Tie), W7: a parse check, not a physics band. - The parsed Cu 4×4's σ_max equals 0.999904939998 (:4565), and its class means equal :4589, each within H0075_TIE_BAND 1e-9 absolute. - The parsed PEC 4×4's class means equal :4590 within the same band. - A wrong block misses by much more. Cu against the 5.8e9 block differs by ≈ 3.7e-4 on self (:4566 / :4573), and Cu against PEC by ≥ 1.2e-4 (adjacent). - (P), W7, on Palace's assembled Cu 4×4 (_p_check_s, item 418's): - ‖S − Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND (tests/validation/test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86); - σ_max ≤ 1 + PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE, and every column power ≤ 1 + 1e-9 (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:129); - every S-class spread ≤ ADJACENT_SPREAD_BAND (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:121); - pooled ≥ POOLED_SEPARATION_FLOOR × the worst (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:173). - Reciprocity is cross-window: S_ij and S_ji come from two Palace commands. - Palace log check (executor, journalled), W3–W6: - 226 904 elements, and the bounding box ±0.12 / ±0.12 / ±0.10 m; - Rs = 4.375e+01 Ω/sq on 21–24; - Configuring Dirichlet PEC BC at attributes: listing 1 only; - Configuring Robin finite conductivity BC at attributes: / 401: σ = 5.800e+07 S/m, quoted verbatim (item 241 W3's form, 20261005T093223Z_OPS-61-item241-W3-palace-hole-cu.log:78–79); - no PMC-fallback warning; - ω/2π = 6.400e-02 GHz; - exactly one excited port, k; - one GMRES solver converged line; - ND (p = 2): 1538030 predicted (= ours; a mismatch is a reading, not a red).

Ours against Palace (printed, never gated — 2026-10-13 rulings (1) / (4)). - (T5-Cu) per class and per entry, |Palace o2 Cu h − ours p2 Cu h|/|ours|. Predicted ≤ 1e-6. The measured precedents are item 241 (T4) 1.6–2.0e-10 on the ×1 hole Cu and items 434 / 435 ≤ 1.3e-10 on the strip rung. The floor is the 10-digit print, ≈ 1e-10. Ours is -n 16; Palace is -np 8. - (C-h-Cu) Palace o2 Cu at h = 0.0075 against Palace o2 Cu at ×1 (postpro_h05x_cu_o2), per class, printed beside ours' 0.1206 / 0.0506 / 0.1091 % (:4593). Predicted equal to the printed digit (items 434 / 435 / 437 measured exactly that on the strip rungs). Palace ×1 Cu o2 equals our ×1 record to ≤ 2.0e-10 (item 241 (T4)), so both codes start from the same point. - Ours' and Palace's _class_spread per class, side by side. Predicted equal to the printed digit (the two 4×4s tie entrywise). The xl log's :4565 spreads (0.0009 / 0.0013 / 0.0006 %) use th14's definition, not _class_spread; item 241's prediction miss was exactly this. Never compare across the two definitions. - Palace Total, Setup, iterations and peak per window, beside 115–180 s.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (K1′) The conductivity boundary reaches Palace's operator — floor asserted, size predicted. - Asserted: per class, |Palace Cu h − ours PEC h| / |ours PEC h| > KNOB_REACHES_THE_SOLVE (1e-6, tests/validation/test_port21_feed_sensitivity.py:156, imported). - Same-fixture prior: ours' Cu − PEC gap on this mesh is 6.15e-4 / 2.79e-4 / 4.79e-4 (:4592), ≥ 279× above the floor. Palace's PEC equals ours to ≤ 2.2e-10 at ×1 (item 234 (T1)). - Printed: the separation |Palace Cu − ours PEC| / |Palace Cu − ours Cu|. Predicted ≥ 279× if (T5-Cu) ≤ 1e-6, central ≈ 3e6×. - A Palace that treated 401 as PEC reads ≈ 1e-10 here. A wall left out of every block reads ≥ 100 % (item 234's (K′)), and the PMC-fallback warning shows first. - (K3′) Loss direction — asserted: σ_max(Palace Cu h) < σ_max(ours PEC h). The read computes the latter from :4556–4559 and prints it. - Same-fixture prior: ours' σ ladder on the rung rises monotonically toward PEC (:4565 < :4572 < :4579). - Predicted margin ≥ 3.3e-6 (0.999908196 − 0.999904940), against a ≈ 1e-9 tie. - A wall with a sign error (active, not lossy) puts σ_max above PEC's. - (C2-h) Mesh-mismatch separation — predicted, printed (no prior Palace measurement on this mesh). - Per class: |ours ×1 p2 Cu (ANS6_EXACT_STRIP_CLASS_MEANS_P2["64"]["cu"]) − Palace Cu h| / |ours h p2 Cu − Palace Cu h|. - The numerator ≈ the h-move. The weakest class is adjacent, 5.06e-4 relative (≈ 2.3e-4 absolute). - Predicted ≥ 506× against item 229's ≥ 25× bar, central ≈ 5e6×. docs.title: OPS-62 — The ANS-4 ladder's refinement guard counts unknowns, not cells
docs.text: The ANS-4 ladder's refinement guard counts unknowns, not cells — opened and executed 2026-09-22 (interactive session, operator-instructed, out of band: it was not queued through §9, and §9 was deliberately left untouched). Defect: tests/validation/test_ans4_resolution_ladder.py::test_every_finer_rung_actually_refines asserted finer["cells"] > coarser["cells"] between consecutive rungs. That is the wrong invariant for step 2d's h:degree ladder, which refines in h and p: a p-rung holds the mesh fixed on purpose. Evidence: the 2026-09-22 XL window (20260922T070007Z_ANS-4-step3e.log, Status 1) ran the pre-registered FEM_EM_ANS4_STEP2_RUNGSPEC="0.015:1 0.015:2 0.0075:2 0.005:2" at 64 MHz; rungs 1 and 2 are the same mesh at degree 1 then degree 2, so the guard read resolution 0.015 gave 116085 cells, not more than 0.015's 116085 (:8802–8805, 8812) while the discretisation actually went ≈139 302 → ≈742 944 unknowns (:2452, 4542). All four rungs completed and produced Z/S; the PORT-11 gates, the record-rung check and the readout all passed — one spurious red on an otherwise usable window. Internal inconsistency, not a judgement call: the same file's stop rule is already stated in unknowns (STOP_ABOVE_DOFS, "cells mean different things at different orders"), through _estimated_dofs(cells, degree); only the guard was never updated when the ladder gained p-rungs. Fix: _refinement_measure(rung) = _estimated_dofs(rung["cells"], rung["degree"]) (the rung dicts have carried degree since _four_port_rung gained it) and a pure _check_refines(rungs) returning the offending consecutive pairs; the guard asserts that list is empty. Strictly stronger, not loosened — no tolerance, no >=, no equal-cells exemption: an inert h keyword still gives identical meshes at fixed degree ⇒ identical unknowns ⇒ still caught, and an inert or backwards degree knob, which a cell count cannot see, is caught too. Cells stay in the printed [ANS-4 step2] refinement: line (now cells and unknowns, rank 0 only); the failure message names the rung pair, both degrees and both unknown counts. Controls (§4, smoke, -n 2, complex, 20260922T165511Z_OPS-62.log, Status 0, 7 s): test_refinement_check_controls, 1 passed in 1.3 s on both ranks, on synthetic rung dicts, no solve — four identical rungs ⇒ 3 failures caught; a p-rung (116 085 cells, degree 1 → 2) ⇒ clean, with the measure asserted at exactly 139 302 → 742 944; an h-rung ⇒ clean; the real 3e ladder shape with that window's measured cell counts (116 085 / 116 085 / 281 728 / 592 744) ⇒ clean, i.e. the fix would have let that window through; a degree drop at fixed h ⇒ caught; equal unknowns across a pair (1 600×1.2 == 300×6.4) ⇒ caught; and the strength case — cells 100 000 → 200 000 with degree 2 → 1, which the old cell guard passed and the new one catches. The module still collects: 6 tests in 2.5 s. Nothing else touched — no ladder data, no _estimated_dofs, no STOP_ABOVE_DOFS, no PORT-11 band, no other test. Whether ANS-4 step 3e is re-run is the next 03:00 review's call — this chunk did not touch xl-queue.d/, xl-pending.md or xl-ledger.md, and implementers never commission a window. Audit 2026-09-23 03:00 review: PASS. Correction from the same review's log-pathologist reading: the 3e window had two reds, not one — the second is the deliberate pre-rebuild OPS-60 skrf red (20260922T070007Z_ANS-4-step3e.log:8892–8895, :8969–8970), not physics either; ruled not re-run, and 3f (09-23) ran 18 / 18 green under this guard (20260923T070007Z_ANS-4-step3f.log:4923–4924). | ✅

docs.title: §9 item 384 — 2026-10-11 (weekly flag 8, OPS-66 step 2; ops/docs, lane 1)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-11 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

Licence. The 2026-10-10 weekly's flag 8 (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10, "Flagged for the 2026-10-11 03:00 daily review", item 8): "rotate_plan_archive.py chunks: a state line beginning with the glyph is doubled — OPS-66-class tool fix (strip a leading glyph), lane 1."

Home. The chunks subcommand was built by OPS-46 (✅ 2026-09-12; docs/planning/chunks/OPS-46.md) and extended by OPS-47 (--narratives). The weekly named the class OPS-66 (rotation-tool defects the weekly finds), so the brief lives here as OPS-66 step 2. The review may instead open a new row (next free OPS-71); the brief is unchanged either way. No band, Done-when or target is set or moved.

The defect (read on 510f41f9). _replacement builds the status cell as f" {parsed['title']} | {parsed['glyph']} {state} {dw}" (scripts/maintenance/rotate_plan_archive.py:428–431). parsed['glyph'] is the row's current glyph (_parse_row, :401–405). A spec state line written from the row's last ruling usually opens with that glyph ("✅ 2026-10-05 …"), so the cell becomes "✅ ✅ 2026-10-05 …". The 2026-10-10 weekly's run hit it on all twelve rows (docs/testing/logs/20261011T020900Z_WEEKLY-ROTATE-CHUNKS.log:35–46) and de-duplicated them by hand in 397b69d0 (its commit message: "the tool's prepended glyph de-duplicated by hand on all twelve"). The spec file itself was not kept. The script's last commit is 15bdce61ca16199c6b1f3e947b6f13ad020e6ed8 (2026-10-01).

The fix (≈ 10 lines; the docstring at :29–47 gains one sentence). - In _replacement, or in a helper _strip_leading_glyph(cid, state, glyph) called from rotate_chunks before _check_state, state.lstrip() is tested against GLYPHS (:351): - (i) If it opens with the row's own glyph, remove that glyph and the whitespace after it. - (ii) If it opens with a different member of GLYPHS, raise RowError(f"{cid}: state line opens with {g} but the row's status is {glyph}; the rotation never changes a status"). - (iii) Otherwise, unchanged. - (ii) goes beyond the weekly's letter ("strip a leading glyph") and is the review's to accept. The reason: a strip-any rule would silently drop a status the reviewer typed, and the tool's contract is a verbatim move ("never edits a line it moves", :23). If the review declines (ii), the leading glyph is stripped whatever it is, and test (G3) asserts the row's glyph survives. - _check_state's digit and sentence checks run on the stripped state, so their behaviour is unchanged (a glyph carries no digit and no sentence stop).

Test: new tests/unit/test_rotate_chunks_glyph.py. It loads the tool with _load / importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, as tests/unit/test_rotate_known_issues_entries.py:68–75 does, and uses git -c safe.directory=… (:78–89). Every fixture is synthetic and written under tmp_path: a minimal plan with a ## 7. heading, a | ID | Title | Status | Tier | table, and two rows ZZ-1 (✅) and ZZ-2 (🟡) whose history carries the digit runs the state lines use, closed by a ## 8. heading. The chunks dir is empty under tmp_path, and every spec is written by the test.

Anchors (asserted, exact). - (G1) Glyph-led state. Spec === ZZ-1 / ✅ 2026-10-10 state. through rotate_chunks(spec, plan, chunks_dir, dry_run=False, date="2026-10-11"): rc 0, and the row's new status cell begins | ✅ 2026-10-10 state. with exactly one ✅ between the title/status boundary and *History:. - (G2) No-glyph state, unchanged behaviour, byte for byte. Spec === ZZ-2 / state without a glyph 2026. (digits present in the row), with and without a Done-when: line, run once through the new tool and once through the pinned pre-change tool on identical fixture copies: plan bytes, chunk-file bytes and --dry-run stdout are all equal. The same equality holds on a --census run. - (G3) Mismatched glyph (as ruled). Spec === ZZ-1 / 🟡 2026-10-10 state. on the ✅ row: rc 1, REFUSED: ZZ-1: state line opens with 🟡 … printed, plan bytes unchanged, no chunk file created. If the review declines (ii): rc 0 and the cell opens ✅ 2026-10-10. - (G4) The variation-selector glyph. A ⚠️ row (U+26A0 U+FE0F, as in GLYPHS) with state ⚠️ 2026-10-10 x. → exactly one ⚠️.

Negative control (rule (e)): the pinned pre-change tool, never HEAD:. - git show 15bdce61ca16199c6b1f3e947b6f13ad020e6ed8:scripts/maintenance/rotate_plan_archive.py goes into the gitignored /workspace/logs/ops66-step2-control/ (OPS-66 step 1's idiom). That is the file's last commit before the fix, i.e. the fix commit's ^ version. - Run on the (G1) fixture, it writes ✅ ✅ 2026-10-10 (two glyphs). Asserted as a binary: old = 2, new = 1. - It is backed by the same comparison on real data: the weekly's twelve doubled rows (…WEEKLY-ROTATE-CHUNKS.log, 397b69d0). - A control that copied HEAD: would go stale the moment the fix lands. That trap cost OPS-43 (a) a window (rubric item 4).

Printed only (real-data replay, no assertion). - Inputs: git show 38aa4afd:PROJECT_PLAN.md (397b69d0^, the pre-rotation plan) and a spec reconstructed from 397b69d0:PROJECT_PLAN.md. The reconstruction takes each row's state = the row glyph + the text up to **Done-when:** or *History:, and the Done-when line from the same row. It covers the nine rows whose titles were not hand-condensed: OPS-70, GEO-36, MAT-15, WF-1, WF-10, WF-12, WF-15, WF-16 and WF-17 (MAT-20, WF-8 and EX-89 were, per the commit message). - Run into a tmp_path plan and chunks dir. Print, per row, whether the new tool's row equals 397b69d0's row byte for byte, and the old tool's doubled-glyph count. - Predicted: 9 / 9 equal, and old doubled = 9. A mismatch is a reading (another hand edit in 397b69d0), never a red.

Window. Smoke. Foreground; the harness call is the whole Bash command, bare; Bash timeout: 660000; -s. No MPI and no complex build (OPS-66 step 1's W1 ran this way, 8 passed, 2 s; outcome above).

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh OPS-66-s2-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_rotate_chunks_glyph.py tests/unit/test_rotate_known_issues_entries.py -s -v --tb=short'"

Cost. ≈ M measured / ≈ 25 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 8 code + W1 ≈ 0.1 + journal). Class: ops/docs (median 3, carried; this one carries code). Depends on nothing.

Traps already paid for. - Pin <sha>, never HEAD:. - git in the container needs -c safe.directory=/workspace. - No pipe or filter in the harness command; -s always. - No hard-coded live line numbers in the test. - No edit after W1 (rule (i)). - Never path-checkout a record file. - The scratch copy goes under gitignored /workspace/logs/, never tests/.

Scope. Covered: the chunks replacement's leading glyph. Not covered: --narratives, --census output (beyond (G2)'s equality), the attempts / known-issues / history / plan modes, the title derivation (the three hand-condensed titles are a separate question for the weekly), and weekly-review.md.

Park on attempt/OPS-66-s2-* and mark item 384 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). - (G2) unequal → the fix touched the no-glyph path: report the first differing byte. - The control does not double → the pinned tool is not the defective one: report the sha. - The step 1 module red → a regression in the shared loader: report it.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. OPS-66 stays ✅: its Done-when is the known-issues entry pattern, met 2026-10-01. The row gains one sentence: "Step 2 (§9 item 384, 2026-10-11): chunks strips a state line's leading row glyph (refuses a different one); the pinned pre-change tool doubles it, the new one does not; no-glyph output byte-identical (…_OPS-66-s2-W1.log)." The weekly's flag 8 is discharged, and its next chunks rotation needs no hand de-duplication; the weekly confirms on that run. No rule (j) amendment, as no glyph moves. If the review opens OPS-71 instead, that row's Done-when is (G1), (G2) and the control asserted ⇒ ✅.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Execute §9 item 384 — OPS-66 step 2 (weekly flag 8) — per docs/planning/chunks/OPS-66.md §9 item 384. Read the brief and any review rulings beneath it first. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a window; run pytest with -s. Pin the control to 15bdce61ca16199c6b1f3e947b6f13ad020e6ed8, never HEAD:. Never run the tool against the live PROJECT_PLAN.md or docs/planning/chunks/. You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command string. On a red, park on attempt/OPS-66-s2-*, mark item 384 BLOCKED in the same commit, and report."

Outcome (2026-10-12, 22:30 CDT slot fourth item, implementer): DONE. Fix as drafted, (ii) included (no review ruling declined it): _strip_leading_glyph called from rotate_chunks before _check_state; docstring gains one sentence. W1 20261012T035822Z_OPS-66-s2-W1.log (Status 1, 2 s): the new module 7 passed — (G1) new cell ✅ 2026-10-10 state., one ✅; control (pinned 15bdce61) ✅ ✅ 2026-10-10 state. — binary old 2 / new 1; (G2) plan / chunk / --dry-run / --census byte-identical without and with Done-when: (430 / 112 / 201 / 455 B and 472 / 112 / 244 / 455 B); (G3) rc 1, REFUSED: ZZ-1: state line opens with 🟡 but the row's status is ✅; the rotation never changes a status, plan unchanged, no chunk file; (G4) ⚠️ old 2 / new 1. The one red is not this item's: step 1's test_a2_old_subset_of_new_and_difference_is_exactly_the_four fails identically on clean main fc95e41b with the fix stashed (20261012T035840Z_OPS-66-s2-W0-main.log, 1 failed / 7 passed) — the archive now carries three later undated RETIRED headings (ANS-7 2026-10-06, WF-17 2026-10-08, OPS-69 2026-10-08) that A2's archive ⊆ FOUR never anticipated. docs.text:
Executor: implementer. Tier: smoke, one harness window (-n 1, no MPI). Cost: ≈ 5 measured / 25 predicted min. This uses the ops / docs class (uncalibrated, n = 4): 25 predicted × the 03:00 → 10:30 interval's measured / predicted ratio of 0.18 (52 / 285).
