Never build. - Never delete a log.

Scope boundary. Step 1 re-gates every tests/package/ module, plus tests/post/test_wf8_figures.py, at its degree-1 / non-degree-2 nodes on one HEAD. It does not re-run: - the degree-2 legs (WF-15 lossy W2a / W2b, temperature degree-2, WF-16 four-port / sweep / SAR / B1 at -n 8, WF-17 first-study degree-2). These are step 2 below, not queued by this item; - upstream validation modules (MAT-4, MAT-10, MAT-17, MAT-18), which are not edited by the seven commits; - any xl / xxl window.

A green step 1 says the 2026-10-08 edits did not regress any degree-1 / API / CLI / installed-package gate. It says nothing new about the degree-2 records. No band, record or §2 sentence moves. No WF-* glyph changes: all are ✅ already.

Negative result. - Any red assertion is a regression on the final tree. Report it and stop the slot, with no in-slot fix, not even a one-line one. Record: - the node, its reading against its band, its last green log, and git log --oneline <that log's commit>..H -- src/fem_em_solver/study.py src/fem_em_solver/cli.py; - a known-issues entry (OPS-70: <node> red on H); - a dated §7 note on the owning chunk's row and on OPS-70; - §9 item 335 marked BLOCKED (rule (d)).

Commit the red log, which is the evidence. Nothing is parked, because there is no code change. - A comparator gone blind (a control reading 0 or at its band) is reported the same way. - A window killed by its timeout is a price finding, not a regression. Check for orphans, sweep the cache, record the elapsed, mark the remainder step 1b BLOCKED-on-time, and do not re-run at a larger timeout. - A log Commit: ≠ H voids that window: re-run it.

There are no PREDICTED RED: lines: every assertion is expected green, and a red anywhere stops the slot.

The WF-13 step 4, WF-15 step 4, WF-16 steps 4 / 5 / 7 and WF-17 step 3 records each gain a final-tree log, cited on their §7 rows' history lines without a glyph change. - Any red: a known-issues entry plus a §7 note as above. The owning record is contested until a fix chunk re-gates it. - Step 1b (time-parked): OPS-70 stays ⬜ with the green subset recorded.

docs.title: §9 item 665 — 2026-10-27 (§10 lane 1, OPS-72: the migration sweep's cost; lane-1 revalidation)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-27 03:00 daily review from the §7 row's Done-when (PROJECT_PLAN.md OPS-72), unchanged. No band, gate or scope moves: the checker's roots (src, tests, examples, scripts) and every assertion in tests/environment/test_dolfinx_api_migration.py stay as they are.

The cost, measured (the before). tests/environment at -n 1: 3 passed in 144.42 s (20261026T021500Z_MAT-3-step1b-envprice.log; known-issues 2026-10-26, :31–39). Per test: test_negative_control_detects_reverted_migrations 78.76 s (a baseline sweep of src + tests plus a sweep of the temp copy), test_no_unmigrated_call_sites 39.01 s (a third sweep of src + tests), test_filed_survivors_outside_the_gated_roots_are_unchanged 26.63 s (examples + scripts, then scripts/probes). The checker is loaded by importlib in a module fixture (test_dolfinx_api_migration.py:79–85), and nothing in it or the checker mentions MPI, so every rank runs all of it. The last five W-env windows measured 102–120 s (test-results.md:5462–5493).

Anchor (the Done-when's measurements, asserted by the windows' own verdicts). - (V) Every tests/environment verdict unchanged: the same test IDs, all passing, at -n 1 and -n 2, counted per rank by token. - (N) The planted negative control still detects: status=pass and applied=6 (:121–124, unedited). - (R) The checker's CLI RESULT: line byte-identical on a clean tree before and after the change: python3 scripts/testing/check_dolfinx_api_migration.py (default --roots src tests, :778) run once on the parent commit and once on the change, each line pasted into the outcome, compared by cmp or string equality in the outcome note. - (T) The full tests/environment ≤ 60 s by the harness footer at -n 1 and at -n 2.

Negative control. The before run is the control: 144.42 s at -n 1, ≈ 2.4× the 60 s bar. A change that only moves the sweep to rank 0 cannot meet (T) at -n 1, because one rank still does three src + tests sweeps there. So the route has to remove duplicated work, not just ranks.

Route (in order; stop at the first stage that meets (T)). 1. Profile, no edit (W0): one checker.sweep(["src", "tests"], REPO_ROOT) under cProfile at -n 1, top 15 cumulative entries printed. That shows whether the time is parsing, signature resolution or I/O. Paste the top 5 lines into the outcome. 2. One sweep per root set per session, on rank 0. Add a module-scoped fixture that computes the src + tests report once on rank 0 and broadcasts it (MPI.COMM_WORLD.bcast; SweepReport / Finding are dataclasses, check_dolfinx_api_migration.py:90–103; check they pickle). Then test_no_unmigrated_call_sites reads it, and negative_control takes it as its baseline through a new keyword-only argument baseline: SweepReport | None = None (default None keeps the CLI path byte-identical). Rank 0 runs the negative control and the survivors sweep and broadcasts (status, captured_output) / the reports. Each rank asserts on the same broadcast values, so the verdicts stay per rank. 3. Only if 1–2 do not reach 60 s: memoise the expensive resolution that the profile names (e.g. one signature lookup per distinct API rather than per call site), as an internal cache inside the checker. The RESULT: line (R) is the proof that it changed nothing.

Do not narrow what any sweep reaches (the Done-when's "skips nothing it checked before"): the negative control still sweeps the whole temp copy, and the file / call-site / API floors stay. If stage 3 is still over 60 s, stop: report the measurement and leave the row ⬜ with the stage-by-stage times. Narrowing the control's scope is the weekly's call.

Windows (bare harness calls, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; real build is fine, since tests/environment runs either way, but use the complex image as every W-env has: source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1): - W0 OPS-72-W0-profile (-n 1, timeout -k 30 300): python3 -c running the profile of route step 1 inside the container, with PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace. It is a measurement, not a pytest run, so it does not trip the pytest-routing guard; keep it one bare harness call. - W-rb OPS-72-W-rb (-n 1, timeout -k 30 120): the CLI on the parent commit's checker (git show HEAD:scripts/testing/check_dolfinx_api_migration.py > /workspace/logs/ops72-checker-before.py from the host first; then run that copy with --roots src tests in the container). Its RESULT: line is (R)'s before. - W1 OPS-72-W1-n1 (-n 1, timeout -k 30 300): python3 -m pytest tests/environment -v --tb=short --durations=5, the W-env command verbatim (20261027T003839Z_WF-15-s8-Wenv.log:12). - W2 OPS-72-W2-n2 (-n 2, timeout -k 30 300): mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment -v --tb=short --durations=5. - W-ra OPS-72-W-ra (-n 1, timeout -k 30 120): the CLI on the changed checker, --roots src tests. Its RESULT: line must equal W-rb's.

Executor: implementer. Tier: smoke (target), -n 1 / -n 2, the before run is standard. Class: lane-1 revalidation (the weekly placed OPS-72 on lane 1). Cost: ≈ 6.0 measured / 30 predicted slot-minutes. Depends on: nothing. Family: OPS-72 step 1, attempt 1 of 4.

Traps already paid for. - bash_guard.py denies pytest runs that bypass the harness and any harness call that is not a bare whole command. W-rb's host-side git show … > is its own Bash call, never chained to the harness call. - A string pgrep -f "python3 -m pytest" is denied by the guard; pgrep -c python3 in the container is the check. - Count pytest verdicts per rank by token. In a 2-rank stream a trailing PASSED can be the other rank's. - capsys captures only the calling rank's stdout. Under route step 2 the non-root ranks must assert on the broadcast output string, not on capsys. - A collective call (bcast) inside a test that one rank skips deadlocks the window. Every rank must reach every bcast; keep them in fixtures, not in branches.

Scope. The cost of tests/environment. Not claimed: any change to what the sweep checks, its roots, its floors or the negative control's six reversions; any other environment test.

Negative result. (V), (N) or (R) red ⇒ the change altered the gate: revert it, park on attempt/OPS-72-*, BLOCKED. (T) over 60 s with (V)/(N)/(R) green ⇒ land the stages that are green as an improvement, record each window's footer, keep the row ⬜ and known-issues 2026-10-26 open with the new measurement, and the environment-first ruling keeps binding. No PREDICTED RED: line.

Status it can move. OPS-72 ⬜ → ✅ when (V), (N), (R) and (T) are all green; known-issues 2026-10-26 retires in the same commit; the environment-first ruling is then lifted by the next daily review (not by the slot). Otherwise the row records the measured time.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim, if delegated). "Execute §9 item 665 — OPS-72 — per docs/planning/chunks/OPS-72.md "§9 item 665". The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Never edit an assertion, floor or reversion in tests/environment/test_dolfinx_api_migration.py; the checker's CLI default stays byte-identical. Spawned executors run every window foreground with Bash timeout: 660000."

Outcome (2026-10-27, 07:30 CDT slot, implementer, no spawn) — ✅, all four green; route steps 2 and 3 both landed. - W0 profile (20261027T124634Z_OPS-72-W0-profile.log:63–70, one src + tests sweep under cProfile, 108.10 s profiled): sweep 108.097 cum; sweep_file (582 calls) 99.120; ast.walk (22 716 788 calls) 87.526; iter_child_nodes 59.279; enclosing_bindings (1 998 calls) 52.423 — a full re-walk of every scope's subtree per call site. Parsing and signature resolution are not the cost; tree walking is. - Change. Checker (internal only): scope_map stores each scope's set of contained node ids, built by one walk per scope, and enclosing_bindings tests membership, giving the same set union. sweep_file walks its tree once and reuses the list for its four passes (the tree is never mutated, so the order is the same). negative_control gains keyword-only baseline: SweepReport | None = None; None (the CLI) sweeps as before. Gate module: three module fixtures compute the src + tests report, the control's (status, stdout) and the examples + scripts / scripts/probes reports on rank 0 and bcast them. Every rank asserts on the broadcast values, so capsys is gone from the control test. No assertion, floor, root or reversion is edited. - (R) W-rb (parent checker, 20261027T124558Z_OPS-72-W-rb.log:56) and W-ra (changed, …124919Z_OPS-72-W-ra.log) print the identical line RESULT: files=582 calls=1471 apis=39 methods=17 violations=0 uncheckable=0 shadowed=0 (string-equal; CLI 28 s → 16 s). - (V) W1 -n 1 (the W-env command verbatim, no -s): 12 passed. The sorted ID PASSED list cmp-identical to 20261027T003839Z_WF-15-s8-Wenv.log's. W2 -n 2 (with -s, rule (g)): 24 PASSED tokens = 12 per rank, 0 FAILED / ERROR, two 12 passed summaries. - (N) test_negative_control_detects_reverted_migrations PASSED on every rank at both widths, so status == 0, "status=pass" in out and "applied=6" in out held on the broadcast output. The control still sweeps the whole temp copy. - (T) Footers: W1 44.90 s (12 passed, 22 warnings in 44.90s, harness elapsed 46 s); W2 44.73 s / 44.66 s per rank (harness elapsed 46 s). The before was 144.42 s (MAT-3 envprice) / 119.34 s (last W-env). Setup times at -n 1: control 18.27 s, src + tests sweep 15.77 s, ungated 10.14 s. - Not done here: lifting the environment-first ruling (the next daily's).

docs.text:
PASS on §4, with the tier re-declared from smoke to standard by measurement; no demotion (auditor, re-cited by the review). The harness logs exist with Status 0 and an elapsed time. The verification was executed by the slot, and the asserted gates are unchanged in tests/environment/test_dolfinx_api_migration.py:131–195. - Timing. 20261027T124941Z_OPS-72-W1-n1.log:114 reads 12 passed … in 44.90s, with harness elapsed 46 s at :118. 20261027T125038Z_OPS-72-W2-n2.log:145 and :154 read 12 passed per rank (44.66 s / 44.73 s), 24 PASSED tokens. - (R). …124558Z_OPS-72-W-rb.log:56 and …124919Z_OPS-72-W-ra.log:56 print string-equal RESULT: lines (re-read with cmp). - Tier. docs.title: OPS-73 — a retention-safe reader for tests that read a dated harness log
docs.text:
History file for the §7 OPS-73 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-01 10:30 daily review under §9 rule (5) lane 1 (an open known-issues entry a slot can execute), from WF-13 step 13's Wreg (§9 item 715).

  • The defect. Retention compresses a cited log at 7 days (retention-policy.md §1). A test that reads docs/testing/logs/<stamp>.log by its plain name then raises FileNotFoundError. test_wf13_s11_fh2_row_is_its_log went red that way after the 11-01 sweep (20261101T133249Z_WF-13-s13-Wreg.log:7669). It passes on a decompressed copy (20261101T133621Z_WF-13-s13-Wfh2.log). main is red on this node until this lands.
  • What the 10:30 review swept. Of 538 dated logs cited anywhere in tests/, 484 exist only as .gz, 38 are gone and 16 are plain. Most citations are comments. Matching module constants named *LOG* to a run-time read, with no gzip in the module, finds three modules: tests/package/test_wf13_estimate_f_human_d2.py (ENTRY41_LOG), tests/unit/test_ans8_v3_d2_block.py (H30_LOG), tests/validation/test_wf10_lattice_d2.py (D1_TABLE_LOG, D1_PPH_LOG, H18_LOG). That sweep does not see a name built at run time (_log("…")), so the slot repeats it for that form. None of the 38 absent logs is named by a matching constant, but the same limit applies.

Done-when. tests/log_records.py::read_log_text exists and is the only route those modules use; test_wf13_s11_fh2_row_is_its_log passes on main with no plain .log present; (H) and (A) below asserted; the known-issues entry retired in the same commit.

docs.title: §9 item 724 — 2026-11-01 (lane 1, known-issues 2026-11-01)
docs.text:
Anchor. (H) read_log_text(path) returns the identical text for a plain file and for a .log.gz of the same bytes. (A) with neither present it raises FileNotFoundError naming both paths. (Node) test_wf13_s11_fh2_row_is_its_log passes on both ranks with docs/testing/logs/20261022T070008Z_WF-10-step4-H28.log absent and .gz present, asserted in the window by a printed ls, not a decompressed copy.

Negative control. In the unit test, a bare Path.read_text on a .gz-only path raises FileNotFoundError, so the test really is on the state that was red. W0 runs the node before the edit and shows the red once: keep that log.

Execution. - New tests/log_records.py: read_log_text(path, errors="replace"), as tests/package/test_wf13_estimate_f_clinical_d2.py::_log_lines and tests/unit/test_ans4_ans6_palace_sections.py:162–164 already do it. Do not move those modules; they work. - New tests/unit/test_log_records.py. - Route the three modules through it: test_wf13_estimate_f_human_d2.py:119, test_ans8_v3_d2_block.py:129 and :176, test_wf10_lattice_d2.py:109, :319, :342. Change only the read. parse_table(path) reads fh.read().splitlines(), and read_log_text(path).splitlines() is the same. - Re-sweep: grep tests/ for reads of a name built at run time from docs/testing/logs (_log(, LOG_DIR, LOGS /). Each module on the known-issues list (test_ans4_h_table.py, test_ans7_verdict_section.py, test_ans7_palace_section.py, test_ans4_ans6_palace_sections.py, test_ans8_v3_record_rows.py, test_arch1_u76_palace_outputs.py, test_wf10_f_human_four_port_sar10g.py, test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py) is either fixed the same way or named in the outcome with why it needs nothing (several already fall back; test_ans8_v3_record_rows.py:118 reads JSON).

Tier, ranks, wall clock. Standard, -n 2, complex, timeout -k 30 170. W0 (red node, pre-edit) ≈ 10 s. W1 the new unit test ≈ 3 s. Wreg: the three modules, plus any the re-sweep changes, ≈ 60 s; test_wf13 alone took 161 s in its full Wreg, so run the named node and the changed reads, not the whole family. Wenv ≈ 49 s. Class: ops / docs. Cost: ≈ 5.6 measured / 20 predicted min. Depends on: nothing.

Traps already paid for. Never gunzip a record in docs/testing/logs/ to get green; item 715's temporary copy was removed in the same window and is not the fix. The bash guard refuses shell text that pipes pytest. Count verdicts per rank by token. Modules whose solve knob is unset skip their solve nodes, which is correct here, because the reads under test are not in those nodes; say which nodes ran.

Scope. Reads of records. Not claimed: any change to retention, to a record, or to a value read. No log is regenerated.

Negative result. A module that reads a log that is gone (not .gz): do not regenerate it and do not skip the test. File a known-issues entry naming the module and the log, and leave that node as it stands. No PREDICTED RED: line beyond W0's, which is the pre-edit reproduction, not a gate.

Status it can move. §7 OPS-73 ⬜ → ✅; the known-issues 2026-11-01 entry retires in the same commit; main green on test_wf13_s11_fh2_row_is_its_log.

Outcome 2026-11-01 (12:00 slot, item 724): DONE, run inline, no executor spawned. New tests/log_records.py (read_log_text, plus resolve_log_path and glob_log_paths, which the brief did not name and the re-sweep needed) and tests/unit/test_log_records.py. W0 reproduced the red on both ranks with only the .gz listed (20261101T182028Z_OPS-73-W0.log:35, :65, :68, :85, Status 1, kept). W1: 9 passed per rank, covering (H), (A), the bare-read control and the glob (20261101T182228Z_OPS-73-W1.log:81, :84). (Node): test_wf13_s11_fh2_row_is_its_log passes on both ranks, the window's ls listing only the .gz (20261101T182231Z_OPS-73-Wreg.log:35, :69, :73). That window's own footer reads 1 failed, 9 passed, 4 skipped per rank, Status 1: the one red is test_ans8_v3_d2_block at (R2), :102, ahead of any log read, a page-versus-render defect from H35 (704025e6). It is a new known-issues entry, not fixed here. test_ans4_h_table.py passed at -n 1 (20261101T182310Z_OPS-73-Wreg-h.log:87), after a first red kept in 20261101T182235Z_OPS-73-Wreg-h.log: the numbers file records each log's listed name, so a resolved .gz name broke (X). Wenv 12 passed. Re-sweep, run-time names. Fixed the same way: test_ans4_h_table.py (:119–120 and H_TABLE_LOGS name logs that exist only as .gz, so it would have been red on main, and it was not on the review's list), test_ans8_v3_record_rows.py (_log(…) into the example's plain-only node_log_readings, and the glob at :378), plus test_wf10_lattice_d2.py's _d2_log glob and the read at :285. Need nothing: test_ans7_verdict_section.py, test_ans7_palace_section.py, test_ans4_ans6_palace_sections.py, test_arch1_u76_palace_outputs.py and test_wf7_f_human_ring_matrix.py already fall back; test_wf10_f_human_four_port_sar10g.py only cites a log in a comment; test_helmholtz_magnitude.py and probe_wf6_sheet_facet_census.py too. Skipped, so their edited reads have not executed: test_wf10_h27_degree2_lattice (FEM_EM_WF10_H27) and the three knob-gated record nodes of test_ans8_v3_record_rows.py, which read gitignored JSON; parse_table itself ran through the .gz in K1. docs.text:

docs.title: OPS-76 — femem run on a swept file with no tune.at_hz ends in an uncaught ValueError
docs.text:
History file for the §7 OPS-76 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-02 03:00 daily review, lane 1, from item 744's disclosure (WF-17 U114) and the known-issues entry of the same date.

The defect. _run_load_result (src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py:2034) refuses a bad tune.at_hz by field, but not a missing one. A multi-frequency load_result: with no tune.at_hz reaches Study.tune (study.py:1232), which raises a plain ValueError. cli.py:209 catches only StudyConfigError, so femem run ends in a traceback instead of the rc 2 by-field refusal that item 730's three refusals give. The page says the API raises ValueError; it says nothing false about the CLI, but the CLI's route is the one the user meets.

Done-when. femem run on that file exits 2 and prints the field tune.at_hz, on every rank's return code, with no output written and no solve; the API's ValueError naming at_hz is unchanged; the known-issues entry is retired in the same commit.

docs.text:

docs.title: OPS-77 — how close a 1e-12 cross-solve gate sits to the known MUMPS drift
docs.text:
History file for the §7 OPS-77 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-02 03:00 daily review, lane 1, from OPS-74's disclosure and known-issues' OPS-43 observation.

The question. Known-issues' 2026-09-10 observation records that solves are not bit-reproducible, with a drift of up to ≈ 4.5e-11 on a lossy fixture at -n 2 (MAT-1 probe, its second-fixture row), and states that any solve-output record tighter than ≈ 5e-11 is exposed. Since then IDENTITY_BAND = 1e-12 has been used across two separate solves: the WF-15 / EX-167 (S) gate, a Study against the direct build. OPS-74 read that (S) at 1.295e-15 and then 6.598e-14 with no code change, ≈ 51 ×, and EX-172's 10 MHz C_mode moved rel ≈ 1.4e-13 between windows. Those are the same phenomenon the observation names, so they need no new diagnosis. What nobody has measured is the distribution on this gate: whether it is 1e-14 noise that clears the band forever, or a tail that will fail one window in N for no reason.

Done-when. A table of every recorded (S) reading on the fixture, plus two new identical windows, with the largest read against IDENTITY_BAND; the known-issues observation gains the row; the weekly is told which branch below fired.

docs.title: §9 item 755 — 2026-11-02 (lane 1, known-issues; OPS-74's disclosure)
docs.text:
Why. Red gates that are noise cost slots and teach people to distrust reds. The rule stands regardless: a band is never loosened to swallow this. The measurement only tells the weekly whether the gate's design needs its attention, as OPS-43 (d)'s did.

Anchor. IDENTITY_BAND 1e-12, imported, on (S) in each window, asserted by the example's own gate. New: scripts/testing/read_s_identity_record.py, stdlib only, reading each listed log through the .gz-safe route and printing log, value, multiple of the band.

Records to read, no solve. Every EX-167* log, the EX-167-close log and every WF-15-s10*, WF-15-s11* log carrying an (S) line. Grep first and list what you found. Each reading is one sample of the same comparison; say which share a process.

docs.title: OPS-78 — which identity gates compare two separate solves
docs.text:
History file for the §7 OPS-78 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-02 10:30 daily review, lane 1, from OPS-77's tail branch and known-issues' OPS-43 observation.

The question. OPS-77 measured one gate on one fixture and found a tail: (S) reached 0.115 × IDENTITY_BAND, and WF-16's four-port (I) landed at 1.004e-13 on another fixture, so the reading is not the rod's alone. The weekly decides tonight whether the gate's design changes, and it cannot decide that from one gate. The name IDENTITY_BAND appears on 147 lines in 27 files. Most uses compare a quantity with itself on a shared route, where the floor is 0.000e+00 (OPS-77's control), and are not exposed. Nobody has listed the ones that compare two separate factorisations.

Done-when. A table of every use site of a band ≤ 1e-11 on a solve output, classified shared route / separate solve / not a solve output, with the count checked against grep; for each separate-solve gate, its largest recorded read and its headroom; the observation gains the row; no band moved.

docs.text:
Why. A red that is noise costs a slot and teaches people to distrust reds. This gives the weekly the whole exposed set. A band is never loosened to swallow this, and this item proposes no band.

Anchor. How to classify. Read the call: two factorisations in one window on the same operator are a separate solve; one solve read twice is a shared route. For each separate-solve gate, read the largest recorded value through tests.log_records.read_log_text or the .gz-safe route in scripts/testing/read_s_identity_record.py, extended with a pattern list if that is the shortest way. By the brief's rule, "two factorisations in one window on the same operator are a separate solve", mri:38 lands in "separate solve"; the brief requires "shared route". mri:37 lands where required. The call: examples/mri/38_implant_rod_on_a_sweep.py:100 runs solve_sweep, and :107 runs a new Study(...).solve(comm) per frequency. _study_solve_sweep (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:1092, :1114) and _study_solve_ports (:777, :799) each call geom.build(comm) and then run_n_port_sparameter_sweep with no solver handed across, and the example's own docstring says each "builds its own mesh" (:8). reuse_factorization shares a factor among the drives of one sweep, not between the two calls. docs.title: Review ruling 2026-11-02 18:00 — the control was wrong, not the rule
docs.text:
The brief's rule stands; the required label for mri:38 flips. The slot stopped correctly, and its reading of the call is confirmed here (examples/mri/38_implant_rod_on_a_sweep.py:100, :107). The error was the 10:30 review's: it took 0.000e+00 for proof of one solve read twice, and OPS-77 had written the same premise.

Why the rule stands. The census exists to list what the drift can reach. Known-issues' OPS-43 observation localises that drift after assembly, in the factor or solve, with the A / b fingerprints identical. So a gate is exposed by repeating a factorisation, whether or not a given pair of solves happened to drift. A zero read is a read inside the exposed class, not a different class. OPS-43's own tally at -n 2 was 2 drifted of 34 on another fixture, so most pairs there read bit-identical.

What stays open, and is not claimed. mri:37 read non-zero 5 of 5 and mri:38 zero 6 of 6, which is more of a split than an intermittent drift alone suggests. mri:37's two sides come from different builders and mri:38's from one, but WF-17 s25 (P=Y), two Study routes, reads non-zero. So the census records the builder as a column and draws no conclusion from it. No cause is claimed, and this review does not assert that mri:38 can drift.

Done-when unchanged. Only "How to classify" and the negative control change. OPS-77's line and known-issues' row are corrected by this review.

The question. _loss_power_w (tests/validation/test_port_drive_superposition.py:205–221), which _exact_shares uses, integrates ½σ|E|² over PHANTOM_CELL_TAG (3) and CONDUCTOR_CELL_TAG (1) only. On I41's kept-rod build that left out tag 403's loss, and (P) read 2.882e-06 against 1e-6 (20261103T195044Z_GEO-36-I57-diag-W1.log:1919–1942). The entry's Scope says "the callers have not been audited for this", and its Resolves-with names that audit beside the weekly's call on widening the helper. This item is the audit, and nothing else. At HEAD b29c4f77, grep -rnw '_exact_shares\|_loss_power_w' tests src examples scripts returns 46 lines in 16 files. src/fem_em_solver/ports/shares.py mentions the name in its docstring only (:4).

Done-when. A table of every grep -rnw line for the two names, each classified as one of: definition, import, prose/docstring, or a call. Each call is classified on the mesh it runs on: - (U) unaffected: the only lossy volume cells are tags 3 and 1. This covers hole builds, where tag 402 is a facet. - (K) kept lossy cells outside 3 and 1: for example keep_cells=True with tag 403 mapped to a lossy material. It is marked two-tag if the gate's (P) uses the helper's sum, or all-cells if the caller sums over all cells. - (?) undecided by code reading.

Traps already paid for. - grep -w counts _ as a word character. A wrapper named, say, _exact_shares_all is therefore not in the count, while a call through a module attribute (_pd._loss_power_w) is. A wrapper found that way is listed and classified too, with the difference from grep named. - An import alias (from … import _exact_shares as _es) hides later calls from the grep. Follow every alias and list its calls under the import line. - The tag a kept body carries is the builder's, not the caller's. build_four_port_sweep's material map has no tag 403 (I41 W1b, test_imp3_tip_q_entry48_def.py:13–17). A kept body whose map omits 403 takes the default material, so read what that default's σ is before classifying it (U). - Do not edit the helper in passing. Other modules import it (the entry's own instruction).

Scope. This is an exposure list. Not claimed: any re-run, any (P) re-read, a band, a fix, or the weekly's widening decision. The known-issues entry stays open. Entries leave only with the commit that fixes them.

Negative result. If a (K) two-tag call is found on a gated (P) other than the known one, it is the finding: name it in the entry's Scope with file:line and the log of its last green run, and change nothing. If the controls split, report and stop. No PREDICTED RED: line.

Completeness identity. Each line is classified exactly once. _exact_shares: 1 definition + 8 imports + 10 prose + 16 calls = 35. _loss_power_w: 2 definitions + 1 import + 4 prose + 4 calls = 11. In total, 3 definitions + 9 imports + 14 prose + 20 calls = 46, with 0 unclassified.

The rule's two facts, cited once. build_four_port_sweep gives lossy material to tags 1 and 3 only, and every other tag gets the default σ = 0 (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:472–485). docs.text:
The guard branch applies. The case object the helper receives carries its material map. build_four_port_sweep returns "problem", a TimeHarmonicProblem with .material and .material_map, in both its return dicts (tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:469–487, :521, :625).

One premise in the weekly's text is corrected, as execution detail; the target is kept. Every kept-cell (K) caller in OPS-80's table writes a lossy tag 403 into that same map, then reaches _exact_shares through _rb._arm (test_imp3_rod_birdcage.py:329): - _arm_rod._wrapped sets 403 to σ_wire (test_imp3_tip_q_entry48_def.py:111). Its all-cells (P) gate reads _exact_shares' p_src and sheet_field_total, and its asserted control reads the two-tag p_vol. - _arm_with_403._wrapped sets 403 to the gel (test_imp3_rod_heating_matched.py:115). _gel_seen and examples/implants/15_rod_heating_matched_phantom.py both go through it.

An unconditional raise would therefore turn test_imp3_tip_q_entry48_def.py, I41 and imp:15 red. That contradicts the target's "the existing callers' gates unchanged". So: - The guard raises by default. - The case dict may carry an explicit acknowledgment key. Exactly the two _wrapped functions set it, each with its reason.

The ring-quadrature route builds a sweep with no "problem" key (test_port_drive_superposition.py:1326). The guard skips it, and the docstring says so. The acknowledgment is named in the dashboard for the 11-07 weekly to ratify or revert.

docs.title: OPS-83 — the (S2-tip) comparand's form on a rough DG0 source: a stub measurement that separates the two readings
docs.text:
History file for the §7 OPS-83 row (OPS-46). Opened by the 2026-11-06 03:00 daily review (lane 1, known-issues diagnosis) from the known-issues entry of the same date: xl entry 55's (S2-tip) red, which WF-15 step 14 / U127 met first. The weekly re-poses the gate; this chunk only measures.

Why. Two windows have failed the same assertion on field-derived sources, and the gel twin of entry 55 misses it too. The global (S2) on those runs is green. The gate is |ρc·⟨θ¹⟩_B/(Δt₁·⟨q⟩_B) − 1| ≤ S2_BAND. One reading is that the comparand has the wrong form: one BE step from rest gives ρc·θ¹/Δt₁ → M⁻¹b as Δt → 0, the consistent-mass L2 projection Πq of the DG0 q onto P1, and Πq keeps the domain mean but not a ball mean. The other reading is physics the gate is meant to catch. Under the form reading, (i) the gap needs a rough source, (ii) it does not scale with Δt₁, and (iii) it vanishes against ⟨Πq⟩_B. U127's Δt₁/10 control already saw (ii) (log-pathologist, 2026-11-06). The pathologist named this measurement as the cheap check.

Neither U127's mesh (its Study route lives only on attempt/WF-15-s14-20261105T212843Z) nor entry 55's (xl) can be read in a slot. I41's matched pair can: it is on main, it carries the rod and its gel twin on one mesh family with the same tip balls (TIPS, 1 g), and its last window ran 310 s at -n 2 (20261105T183330Z_OPS-81-W2-i41.log:3772, :3798).

docs.title: OPS-85 — an exercising node for the _tuned_quadrature_temperature gradient refusal
docs.text:
History file for the §7 OPS-85 row (OPS-46). Its Outcome (docs/planning/chunks/WF-1.md:3590) says: "(3) The _tuned_quadrature_temperature gradient refusal is in src but has no node that exercises it, because reaching it needs a tuned Study."

The refusal. src/fem_em_solver/study.py:3396–3397, inside _tuned_quadrature_temperature (:3378):

if transient.initial_gradient_k_per_m is not None:  # `WF-1` step 28 (§9 item 830)
    raise ValueError("initial_gradient_k_per_m is defined on a ThermalBoxGeometry only")

The same message also stands at :1659 (the EM sphere, _study_temperature) and :2139 (_study_transient_temperature). The route, read against the code (no run). A tuned two-port Study needs no mesh to reach the check: - Study.temperature is _study_temperature (:1734). - Its first branch takes excitation._temperature_port_study (:1625–1629). - TwoPortQuadratureDrive._temperature_port_study (:3030–3035) calls _tuned_quadrature_temperature. - The function checks cooling (:3392), transient (:3394) and the gradient (:3396) before _tuned_result(study, comm) (:3412). Traps already paid for. - A complex-build refusal is never asserted through fem.form inside pytest.raises: ArityMismatch is a BaseException, raised on rank 0 alone, and the peer hangs to the ceiling (item 849, §9 rulings). (Ref) g = 10.0 and (Ctl-g0) g = 0.0 each raise ValueError with the exact message from the frame _tuned_quadrature_temperature (printed line 3534 — the site moved from :3396 with item 878's study.py edit), _tuned_result calls 0, builder calls 0, on both ranks. W1 (complex, -n 2): 20261108T152052Z_OPS-85-W1.log, 8 passed per rank (test_complex_mode.py 4, this module 3, WF-16's (K0) 1), 3 s, [capture] rc=0. The auditor traced every claim to 20261108T152052Z_OPS-85-W1.log (per-rank verdict tokens :63, :65, :66, :69, :70, :72; 8 passed twice :79, :82; [capture] rc=0 :83; Status 0, 3 s :85–88) and 20261108T152105Z_OPS-85-W-real.log (5 passed / 3 skipped twice :77, :80; Status 0 :83–86). Each is falsifiable: delete the refusal, change the message, move it, or make it truthy, and an assert fails. They meet §4's quantitative clause in its operative sense, though not by a literal match to its bullet list (closed form, rate, conservation / reciprocity identity). No earlier closure rested on a refusal alone (OPS-81 paired its refusal contract with reproduced records), so this sets a precedent, which the 11-09 weekly ratifies or reverts; if reverted, the row returns to 🟡. docs.text: Phase-6 ring-rung solve probe — the first solve on the 32-ring-port high-pass layout (mesh:9, 265 621 cells, GEO-20/EX-35) | ✅ (steps 1, 2 and 3 all closed; a step 4 is a review's to scope) step 3 ✅ 2026-09-04, 17:00 slot — the full 32×32 exists, and it is reciprocal / passive / C16 × mirror symmetric on the first attempt; every one of the six anchors green, no band moved, widened or renamed anywhere in the step. Three foreground windows through the harness, complex build, FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, tests/environment first, the half selected by FEM_EM_RING_SWEEP_HALF alone (never a -k): window A (bottom, -n 8, timeout -k 30 600) 12 passed, 6 skipped in 271.93s, Status 0, 274 s (20260904T170452Z_PORT-13.log:10940, 11398–11399); window B (top, same) 18 passed in 268.86s, Status 0, 271 s (20260904T170934Z_PORT-13.log:10882, 11340–11341) — B also ran the assembly gates, bottom.npz being on disk by then; window C (assembly, -n 2, no solve, smoke, timeout -k 30 120) 17 passed, 1 skipped in 23.47s, Status 0, 25 s (20260904T171419Z_PORT-13.log:183, 262–263), every digit identical to window B's at a different rank count. Both windows meshed 270 728 cells at ratio 1.000000 of RING_LONGITUDINAL_SCALED_CELL_RECORD and their measured azimuth tables agree at 0.000e+00 ° — the halves are one fixture built twice in two processes, which is what makes anchor (i) a mesh-reproducibility reading as well as an extraction one (:77). Price: window A 158.87 s of solve over 16 drives (min 9.18, max 10.61 s), 246.75 s wall; window B 156.25 s (min 8.88, max 10.41), 243.76 s wall; summed ru_maxrss 6.771 / 6.649 GiB against the 128 G cap; the 600 s stop rule was not approached (20260904T170452Z_PORT-13.log:10731, 20260904T170934Z_PORT-13.log:10731). Anchor (i), reciprocity of the 32×32 at the unmoved imported 1e-3: ‖S − Sᵀ‖_F/‖S‖_F = **5.446798e-13**, ‖S‖_F = 5.414671 (against the item's predicted √(32 × 0.916) = 5.41); the in-run negative control — one cached column × CONTROL_COLUMN_SCALE 1.01, the PORT-9 leg (d2) per-column normalisation class — moves it to 2.496159e-03 = 2.496× the band, matching the item's computed ≈ 2.5× ceiling to three digits and clearing the locally defined MATRIX_CONTROL_MARGIN = 2.0 bar (:83–84). Anchor (ii), passivity on the matrix, σ_max(S) ≤ 1 via np.linalg.norm(S, 2): 0.999999452, margin +5.48e-07 — passive, and tight, exactly as the 0.957 column norms predicted; the reading is a measurement, not a record, and it did not land in the (1, 1+1e-2] band the negative result reserved for the accounting offset (:87–89). Anchor (iii), the C16 × mirror class identity over the 18 classes built from the measured azimuths and measured ring membership (2 relations × 9 separations of 22.5°, all 1024 entries classified, every pair landing on a class to better than AZIMUTH_MATCH_DEG): every class inside the unmoved 5%, worst 0.4426% on the same-ring 0-step class (the 32 diagonal entries, max |S_38,38| = 4.315637e-02 vs min |S_29,29| = 4.296576e-02); the mirror class (other ring, 0 steps) reads mean |S| = 8.948395e-01 at 0.0462% spread over its 32 entries, and the 14 classes at ≥ 3 steps all sit at 6.12–6.13e-02 within 0.06% — the far-field floor the rung's 32 terminations impose (:92–113). Anchor (iv), the tie to the audited step: the four step-2 columns' Σ_i|S_ij|² reproduce 0.915817419 / 0.915956086 / 0.915816510 / 0.915944997 at 1.2e-10 … 3.1e-10 relative against the rtol 1e-6 bar — two decades tighter than the OPS-34 precedent, so the additive refactor and the two-window split moved nothing (:114–118). Anchor (v) above; anchor (vi), all 32 power residuals inside the imported, unmoved 1e-2: 9.330979e-03 … 9.680804e-03, spread 3.498e-04, worst P37 at 0.968× the band (:80) — 32 drives agreeing on the 0.97-of-band offset is the 03:00 ruling's own prediction made visible, and no new band was created for it. Code: new module tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py; the step-2 module gained the additive plain helper _build_ring_context() holding the fixture body verbatim (nothing renamed, nothing removed) and step 2's 19 tests re-ran green in the same slot — 19 passed in 143.21s, Status 0, 145 s at -n 8, with its own digits unchanged to the digit (4×4 reciprocity 2.485653e-13, control 7.045018e-03 = 7.045×, worst mirror pair P20/P36 at 0.0308%) (20260904T171451Z_PORT-13.log:10802–10803, 10866, 10943, 11401–11402). The two .npz caches live in the gitignored output/port13_ring_columns/ and are not committed; window C skips with a message on a clean tree. Not claimed: no σ_max record, no absolute accuracy, no tuning, resonance or mode spectrum, no §2 claim beyond the one clause added there. ~~Step 3 scoped 2026-09-04 10:30 review (§9 item 1) — the full 32×32, sized off step 1's slower price, not step 2's.~~ Step 2's footer projects 32 drives at 292 s of solve at that load, but step 1 measured 27.96 s/solve on the same fixture (895 s), and a window is sized for the price that has already happened: so two solve windows of 16 drives each (the bottom ring P17–P32, then the top ring P33–P48), each rebuilding the deterministic mesh (ratio 1.000000 in every window so far) and caching its 16 columns to the gitignored output/port13_ring_columns/ (np.savez on rank 0 after a barrier; currents are already reduced), then one assembly window with no solve. Per solve window at -n 8: mesh 69–106 s + 16 × (9.1–28.0) s + 16 current extractions ⇒ 215–560 s, timeout -k 30 600; a window past 600 s is the finding. The half is selected by an environment variable (FEM_EM_RING_SWEEP_HALF=bottom|top), never a -k expression. New module tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py; the step-2 module gains one additive plain helper, _build_ring_context(), holding the fixture body so the fixture, the new module and ports:11 call one function (rename nothing; step 2's 19 tests re-run green in the same slot). Anchors (asserted in the assembly window, every band imported and unmoved): (i) reciprocity of the 32×32 at RECIPROCITY_BAND 1e-3 — the two halves come from two separately built meshes, so this one is a mesh-reproducibility reading as well as an extraction one; (ii) passivity on the full matrix, σ_max(S) ≤ 1 (PORT-9's gate; the column norms are 0.957, so the margin is small and a reading in (1, 1 + 1e-2] is the accounting residual's own size — see the negative result); (iii) the C16 × mirror class identity: |S_ij| grouped by (same/other ring, azimuth separation 0…8 steps) from the measured azimuths and ring, 18 classes, each class spread ≤ OPPOSITE_SPREAD_BAND 5% (step 2 measured the mirror class at 0.0308%); (iv) the four step-2 columns' Σ_i|S_ij|² reproducing 0.915817419 / 0.915956086 / 0.915816510 / 0.915944997 (20260904T093638Z_PORT-13.log:10797–10800) at rtol 1e-6 (same -n 8, the OPS-34 scatter precedent) — the tie to the audited step; (v) both halves' cell counts equal and equal to RING_LONGITUDINAL_SCALED_CELL_RECORD, both azimuth tables equal to 1e-9°. Negative control, ceiling first: scale one cached column by CONTROL_COLUMN_SCALE 1.01 — ‖S‖_F ≈ √(32 × 0.916) = 5.41, a 1% scale on a 0.957-norm column moves ‖S − Sᵀ‖_F by ≈ 0.01 × 0.957 × √2 = 0.0135, so the ratio moves ≈ 2.5e-3 = 2.5× the band; assert ≥ 2× (5× is not reachable on 32 columns, and step 2's 7× was the 4-column arithmetic). Scope: the 32×32 and its three identities on one fixture at 10 MHz, degree 1 — no σ_max record, no tuning, no resonance, no mode spectrum, no §2 claim beyond "the 32×32 exists and is reciprocal / passive / C16-symmetric to the stated digits". Negative result: reciprocity or a class spread outside its band, or σ_max > 1 + 1e-2, is a known-issues entry with the matrix's |S| printed — the first network-level defect on this rung; σ_max ∈ (1, 1 + 1e-2] is a known-issues entry naming the 0.97-of-band accounting offset as the suspect, band not widened, gate not loosened; a solve window past 600 s is journaled with the per-solve price and the item is re-rung by the next review at 8 drives per window. step 2 ✅ 2026-09-04, 04:30 slot — the ring column became a 4×4 sub-block; all four anchors green on the first run, the control at 7.045× the band. tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_ring_column.py extended in place (nothing renamed; step 1's three tests keep passing on the P17 column), one heavy window at -n 8, complex build, FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, tests/environment first, timeout -k 30 600: 19 passed in 147.24s, Status 0, 149 s (20260904T093638Z_PORT-13.log:10943, 11401–11402) — half the 600 s window and a third of the ≈ 430 s estimate, the box being lighter than at 05:05 (the same fixture meshed in 69.74 s against step 1's 106.07, and one solve took 9.12 s against 27.96). Same mesh, same 270 728 cells at ratio 1.000000, same port spec; four drives over the one mesh — P17, its measured z-mirror P33 (both 11.250°, opposite rings) and step 1's two measured opposites P25 / P41 (191.250°) — every port terminated at Z_p = z0 = 50 Ω, 1 V on the driven one, solve wall times 9.12 / 11.68 / 9.94 / 10.07 s, four-drive total 40.82 s, summed ru_maxrss 6.571 GiB against the 128 G cap (:10715, :10758). Column j of S is read straight off the matched-termination drive, S_ij = (V_i − z0 I_i)/V_src, one expression for the diagonal and the off-diagonals both (asserted to 1e-12 against −2z0I_i/V_src + δ_ij in the structural test); no Z is formed. Anchor (iii), reciprocity of the 4×4 at the unmoved imported 1e-3: ‖S₄ − S₄ᵀ‖_F/‖S₄‖_F = **4.118219e-13** — machine-level, as a Galerkin discretisation of a reciprocal medium should be (the discrete operator is complex-symmetric and all 32 port functionals are the same object on both sides), so this gate tests column extraction, not mesh error; the in-run negative control is what gives it teeth — scaling the measured P17 column by 1.01, the (d2) per-column normalisation defect class, moves the ratio to 7.045018e-03 = 7.045× the band, matching the item's computed ≈ 7.0e-3 ceiling to two digits and clearing the pre-stated 5× bar (:10781–10795). Anchor (iv), column passivity Σ_i|S_ij|² ≤ 1: 0.915817419 / 0.915956086 / 0.915816510 / 0.915944997 on P17 / P25 / P33 / P41 — margins +8.4183 / +8.4044 / +8.4183 / +8.4055 %, right on the ≈ 0.92 the item projected from step 1's printed currents (:10796–10801). Anchor (v), the top/bottom mirror identity |S_{σ(i),33}| vs |S_{i,17}| over all 32 pairs at the unmoved 5%: worst pair P20/P36 at 0.0308 % (next 0.0303 % at P36/P17), 163× inside the band, on two independently solved columns — the one identity the second solve buys (:10806–10839). Anchor (vi), step 1's power accounting re-asserted per column at the unmoved imported 1e-2: residuals 9.679798e-03 / 9.680187e-03 / 9.680020e-03 / 9.680343e-03 (0.968× the band, margins +3.20e-04), each with WF-6's conductor-blind control at 4.14× the band (:10843–10854). The four residuals agree to 6 digits across four different drives, which is the ruling's own prediction made visible: the 0.97-of-band reading is a drive-independent term-accounting offset, not noise and not an h-effect — no band was moved, widened or renamed anywhere in this step. Not claimed: the 32×32 (step 3 — a 32-drive sweep now projects to 292 s of solve time at this load, plus one mesh, so it may fit a single window without column caching, but that is a review's call from this footer), no C16 class gate, no σ_max on a full matrix, no tuning or resonance claim, no §2 claim beyond §2's one-column sentence. ~~Step 2 scoped 2026-09-04 03:00 review (§9 item 1) — not the 32×32.~~ Four drives over one mesh (P17, its top-ring partner P33, the two opposites P25 / P41), column j of S read directly from the matched-termination drive as S_ij = (V_i − z0 I_i)/V_src without forming Z (leg (d2)'s defect lived in the Z assembly, and four columns cannot be inverted); anchors: reciprocity of the 4×4 sub-block at the unmoved 1e-3 RECIPROCITY_BAND, column passivity Σ_i \|S_ij\|² ≤ 1 (the P17 column projects to ≈ 0.92 from step 1's printed currents), the top/bottom mirror identity between the P17 and P33 columns at the unmoved 5%, and step 1's power accounting re-asserted per column at 1e-2. Negative control: one column scaled by 1.01 (the per-column normalisation defect class) must move the sub-block reciprocity by ≥ 5× the band — ceiling from step 1's column: ‖S₄‖_F ≈ 1.79 with the 0.893 mirror couplings, so 1% on one column gives ≈ 7.0e-3 = 7×; 5× is the assertable bar. Cost ≈ 430 s at -n 8 (330 s window + 3 × 28 s), timeout -k 30 600. Ruling on step 1's 0.97-of-band residual: no new band — 9.68e-3 on 270 728 cells sits where WF-6 step 1's 9.80e-3 sits on 116 085, a term-accounting reading rather than an h-effect; a column crossing 1e-2 is a known-issues entry, not a wider band. Step 3 (the 32×32, column caching across windows) is scoped from step 2's four-solve footer. step 1 ✅ 2026-09-04, 00:00 slot — the first field on the 16-leg / 32-ring-port longitudinal fixture, both anchors green on the first run. New module tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_ring_column.py, one solve, complex build, FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1, tests/environment first, -n 8, timeout -k 30 570: 14 passed in 325.27s, Status 0, 329 s (20260904T050538Z_PORT-13.log). Fixture: 270 728 cells at ratio 1.000000 of RING_LONGITUDINAL_SCALED_CELL_RECORD (imported, not restated), orientation 'longitudinal', mesh 106.07 s, 32 ring ports, P17 (bottom ring, 11.250°) driven at 1 V, every other port terminated at Z_p = z0 = 50 Ω as PORT-9 leg (d) terminates them, 10 MHz, degree 1 (:10714). Port spec as pre-registered: h = ring_port_gap_chord_m = 8.008718871e-03 m (arc 8.0e-03), w = A/h from the reconstructed sheet = 1.000000000e-02 m at a C32 spread of 2.255e-15 (:10716). Anchor (i), the WF-6 step 1 three-way power accounting at the imported, unmoved 1e-2: supplied ½Re(V_src I*) = 5.078728668e-03 W against phantom 9.180375767e-09 (0.0002%) + conductor 1.612862046e-04 (3.1757%) + the 32 sheets' ½|I|²Re Z_p 4.868272216e-03 (95.8561%) — residual 9.679798e-03, INSIDE (0.97 of the band; WF-6 step 1's own reading was 9.80e-3, so this fixture sits where that one does), with WF-6's free in-run negative control at 4.143700e-02 = 4.14× the band when the conductor term is dropped (:10750–10756). Anchor (ii): the two ports diametrically opposite P17 — P25 and P41, both at 191.250°, found from the measured sheet azimuths — read V = −3.057655713e-02+1.781654553e-03j and −3.057233042e-02+1.888893716e-03j V, a complex spread of 0.3504% (magnitude-only 0.0072%) against the pre-registered 5% PORT-9 C4-class band (:10760–10763); the full 32-vector of V = V_src − I·Z_p and per-port I is printed at :10717–10749 for step 2. PRICE (the deliverable): one solve 27.96 s wall at -n 8 — 6.4–13× under the item's ≈ 3–6 min prediction, the whole run being mesh-bound — summed ru_maxrss 5.732 GiB against the 128 G cap, stop rule 900 s not approached (:10715). Step 2's 32 solves project to 895 s of solve time plus one 106 s mesh, i.e. ≈17 min of compute — over the 20-minute per-command rule only if run as one command, so step 2 is a review's to scope (no 32×32, C16 gate, tuning or resonance claim is made or implied here). ~~⬜~~ UNBLOCKED 2026-09-03 18:00 review — GEO-26 step 2 landed RING_LONGITUDINAL_SCALED_CELL_RECORD = 270 728 on main (1ad8ba3, identical at -n 2 and -n 12, all 32 longitudinal sheets exact) and the review ruled the rung's bistable terminal triangulation acceptable for the port model (the sheet is exact; the terminal-area covariance is a record, GEO-26 step 3's). Step 1 runs as re-scoped below with the two pre-registered edits: the in-run cell-count control is 270 728 (the longitudinal mesh, not EX-35's 265 621), and the port spec names h = ring_port_gap_chord_m and w = A/h from the reconstructed sheet. Queued as §9 item 4, independent of item 3. ~~🚫~~ BLOCKED 2026-09-03 (22:30 implementer slot) — the GEO-20 ring sheets are transverse mid-sections, so the lumped-sheet port model has no h. Step 1 assumes the 32 ring ports can be terminated "as PORT-9 leg (d) terminates them". They cannot: PORT-9's route (ports/lumped.py) needs a longitudinal sheet spanning the gap along the drive direction — R_s = Z_p·w/h, I = (1/R_s)∫E·ĥ dS / h, E_src = V_src/h — which is what GEO-16/GEO-18 emit for a leg gap (the box's longitudinal mid-plane, dx·dz, h_bbox/dz − 1 < 1e-9). io/mesh.py emits the ring gap's transverse mid-section at phi = phi_c instead (ring_port_sheet_area_m2 = box_width², ring_sheet_of_ordinal normal = phi_hat). Measured (-n 2, standard, 29 s, 20260903T033437Z_PORT-13.log:6956–6967, 4-leg ring rung at its 110 786-cell record, ratio 1.000000): every one of the 8 ring sheets spans ≤ 1.43e-17 m along its own phi_hat and exactly 1.000000000000 w along û and ẑ (w = 1.000000000e-02 m), area 1.000000000000 w² — so h = 0 to machine precision, w = A/h is undefined, and E·ĥ is the H(curl)-discontinuous normal trace on an interior facet. No solve was attempted and no price was taken. Resolves with a GEO-20 step that emits a longitudinal ring sheet (the radial-û/phi rectangle spanning the gap arc, h = ring_gap_length, w = box_width) — src/ work on birdcage_port_domain, a review's ruling, not an in-slot fix; step 1 is unexecutable until then. Test parked on attempt/PORT-13-20260903T033437Z (30756cf). Ruled 2026-09-03 03:00 review — a log-pathologist read the claim SUPPORTED on the digits (:6959–6966, largest φ̂ extent P9 1.428955e-17 m; footer Status 0 / 29 s at :6976–6977) and on the construction (the four sheet corners are built at one φ_c, io/mesh.py:3713–3721, and the test derives φ̂ from the ordinal alone, so the reading is a consistency check of a known-transverse emission, not circular), with one clause corrected: the lumped route would not raise on this sheet — gap_height_m is caller-supplied (ports/lumped.py:148,322) and nothing in ports/ derives h from the mesh — a solve would run and integrate the normal trace of an H(curl) field on an interior facet, which is not a defined quantity. The blocker is therefore a well-posedness gap, and it stands. Nothing in the log speaks to 16 legs (the "same code path" appeal is an argument, not a measurement) — GEO-26 step 2 emits the new sheet there and measures it. Disposition: GEO-26 opened (§9 item 1) with the parked module as its negative control (cherry-picked onto main; the branch is deleted in that commit). Step 1 re-opens, unchanged in scope, when GEO-26 step 2's 16-leg longitudinal record exists, with two edits a review makes then: the cell-count control becomes that record (not EX-35's 265 621, which is the transverse mesh), and the port spec names h = ring_port_gap_chord_m and w = A/h from the reconstructed sheet exactly as test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:286–287 derives them for legs. (commissioned 2026-08-30 02:15 weekly review; the ruling text was lost with that session — only the dashboard's one-line summary survived. Re-scoped 2026-09-02 weekly review — queueable as step 1. One single-port solve on mesh:9 (16 legs, 32 ring-gap lumped-sheet ports, 265 621 cells, the EX-35 mesh reproduced at 0.000e+00 as the in-run control) at 10 MHz, degree 1, -n 8, port P1 driven at 1 V with every other port terminated as PORT-9 leg (d) terminates them. Anchors: (i) the three-way power accounting WF-6 step 1 gate (i) uses — supplied vs dissipated + stored — inside the same 1e-2 band; (ii) the open-circuit ring-port voltages on the 31 undriven ports read as a C16 pattern: the two ports diametrically opposite P1 agree to the C4-class spread PORT-9 measured (≤ 5%), asserted, and the full 32-vector is printed for step 2. Cost: priced from PORT-11 step 1 (116 085 cells, ≈ 25 s/solve at -n 2) scaled by 2.3× cells and the MUMPS fill growth MAT-6 step 10a measured (1.69× flops per 1.28× cells) ⇒ ≈ 3–6 min at -n 8; ceiling timeout -k 30 1200, stop rule 900 s (an overrun is the finding — journal, do not raise). Memory: report peak RSS against the 128 G cap. Scope: one solve, one identity, one price — no 32×32, no C16 gate, no tuning, no resonance claim; a full S-matrix is 32 solves and is step 2, scoped by a review from step 1's price. Negative result: a power-accounting miss or an overrun goes to known-issues with the price; nothing else moves. Pre-queued 2026-09-03 10:30 review as §9 item 5, serial on GEO-26 step 2 (item 1) and saying so: the slot that reaches it skips it if RING_LONGITUDINAL_SCALED_CELL_RECORD is not on main; the two pre-registered edits — the cell-count control = that record, h = ring_port_gap_chord_m and w = A/h from the reconstructed sheet — are written into the item. Status stays 🚫 until that slot lands)

docs.text:
PORT-14 — lumped RLC sheets (HFSS Lumped RLC) 🟡 (step 1 executed 2026-09-05, 21:00 implementer slot — the code lands, the gate does not close. series_rlc_impedance and a complex Z_p on the sheet, plus src/fem_em_solver/ports/circuit.py::reduce_terminated_ports, are in and solve; the 50 Ω baseline reproduces PORT-9 on the run's own mesh (‖S−Sᵀ‖/‖S‖ = 1.464324816e-14, σ_max = 0.999992805); the reduction identity reads 1.595580e-03 (C = 100 pF), 3.370512e-03 (L = 1 µH), 7.249519e-04 (R = 200 Ω) against the pre-stated 1e-3, i.e. the lumped sheet is single-mode to 3.4e-03, not 1e-3. Band not widened, per §9 item 2's negative-result protocol; known-issues 🟡, test deliberately red on main. The ceiling-first Γ = 0 control passes with room (Δ = 0.322 / 0.325 / 0.211, misses 0.322 / 0.327 / 0.212 = 200–330× the band), so the gate is resolving the termination. The residual tracks |Γ|, not the element type — the hypothesis a step 1b would test is sheet/interior-width resolution, not the complex arithmetic. 20260905T020428Z_PORT-14.log, heavy tier by ceiling, -n 2, 105 s, 13 solves on one 116 085-cell mesh.) (feature ladder A2, operator directive 2026-09-04; serial on nothing; TH-17 is serial on it.) The PORT-9 sheet term carries Z_p = 50 Ω; let it carry Z_p(ω) = R + jωL + 1/(jωC) per sheet, so a capacitor in a ring gap is a boundary condition rather than a circuit afterthought. Gate (an algebraic identity, no closed form needed): the field-solved S-matrix with port k terminated in Z_p equals the circuit reduction of the 50 Ω S-matrix by that termination (S' = S_aa + S_ab Γ (I − S_bb Γ)⁻¹ S_ba, Γ the termination's reflection coefficient) to ≤ 1e-3 on the 4-leg fixture at 10 and 64 MHz, for a capacitor, an inductor and a resistor each. That is also PORT-15's gate seen from the field side, which is why the two are one lineage. Standard tier.

  • Step 1b (the |Γ| ordering, measured on resolution; scoped 2026-09-05 03:00 review, §9 item 4). The slot's hypothesis — the residual tracks |Γ| (1.6e-3 and 3.4e-3 at |Γ| = 1, 7.2e-4 at |Γ| = 0.6), i.e. total reflection re-excites the sheet's non-single-mode content — predicts that the residual falls with sheet resolution and is indifferent to the element type. Measure it on the L = 1 µH case (the worst) and the C = 100 pF case, on two refined rungs of the same fixture: conductor_resolution × 0.75 and × 0.5 through an additive conductor_resolution=None keyword on tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets.py::_build (the WF-6 step 3f₀ phantom_resolution precedent — None leaves every gate's mesh bit-identical, and test_port_birdcage_four_port.py is re-run green in the same slot as its gate). Per rung: the 50 Ω 4×4 (4 solves) with the imported reciprocity / passivity asserts, then the two terminated 3×3s (6 solves), residuals printed beside the 116 085-cell record with the cell count. Pre-registered readings: monotone decrease on both cases is the hypothesis confirmed and step 2 (64 MHz) is queued on the finer rung; flat or rising residuals refute it and the next suspect is the sheet law's sheet_width_m (the area-based effective width, lumped.py:353) — a PORT-14 step 1c, not a band change. REDUCTION_BAND stays 1e-3 either way; the row stays 🟡; nothing is asserted on the residuals in this step. Heavy by ceiling.
  • Step 1b executed 2026-09-05, 09:00 implementer slot — the hypothesis is REFUTED, and the refutation names the next suspect. Two refined rungs, one window each, band untouched, row still 🟡. The residual is not monotone in sheet resolution:
conductor_resolution cells sheet_width_m per port C = 100 pF L = 1 µH ×1 (step 1's record) 116 085 7.294123600e-03 ×4 1.595580e-03 3.370512e-03 ×0.75 161 695 6.884098695e-03 / 7.649794837e-03 alternating 4.187955e-03 (×2.6247) 8.875487e-03 (×2.6333) ×0.6 209 604 7.674817764e-03 ×4 1.490415e-03 (×0.9341) 3.144877e-03 (×0.9331)

The least-squares t is a closed-form projection, Γ_eff = t/(1 + S₁₁t), and Z_eff = z0(1 + Γ_eff)/(1 − Γ_eff).
