docs.title: §9 item 187 — 2026-10-02 (lane 1)
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only Plan agent and reviewed by the 2026-10-02 18:00 daily review.

This is the sphere half (7a) of the 09-30 weekly's last-step target for POST-1. 7b — the same residuals on the loaded birdcage as a C4-gated record — reuses 187's extraction, is serial on it, and is not written. - Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy (W1 carries a ≈ 195 s POST-8 re-gate; the item's own module is standard). -n 2 / -n 4, complex, plus one real-build window. - Cost: ≈ 4 measured / ≈ 35 predicted min. Depends on: nothing.

Code (rule (c), additive, disclosed). In src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py: - Add a keyword-only candidate_cells=None (local cell indices) to point_owner_cells and to evaluate_vector_field_parallel. - It is valid only with owner="lowest_original_cell"; anything else raises ValueError before any collective. - Candidates are the owned cells ∩ the set; the tie-break is unchanged. - candidate_cells is None joins the OPS-40/55 allgather key. - With None, both functions are byte-identical. - A point with no candidate on its side returns valid=False.

Modules. - (K) tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py (both builds). On create_unit_cube(4,4,4) at the face point (0.5, 0.3, 0.6), restricted to cells with centroid x < 0.5 and then x > 0.5, each call returns the min of a DG0 original_cell_index field over the incident set on that side, with imaginary part 0. - tests/post/test_post1_one_sided_interface_sphere.py (complex_only). - Imports _series, _mesh_and_solve, SPHERE_TAG, RESOLUTIONS_64 and RESOLUTIONS_128 from tests/validation/test_lossy_sphere_fullwave.py (unedited). - Rungs: RESOLUTIONS_64 + RESOLUTIONS_128[-1] (5 866 / 17 667 / 55 241 cells), 64 MHz, degree 1, fields.e_complex. Air is tag 2 (io/mesh.py:2251). - Interface points: on each rank, every face of an owned tag-1 cell whose three vertices satisfy ||v| − a| ≤ 1e-9·a. - The vertices are sorted lexicographically; the centroid p is their mean. - n_f is from the cross product of the sorted vertices, oriented so n_f·p > 0. - The points are allgathered and sorted by (inside cell's original_cell_index, sorted coordinates), so the array is bitwise identical on all ranks. - E⁻, E⁺: the owner rule restricted to cell_tags.find(1) / find(2). - Series values: S⁻ = internal_field(p); S⁺ = incident_field(p) + scattered_field(p). - Residuals: - R_n = ‖ε_c E⁻·n_f − E⁺·n_f‖₂ / ‖E⁺·n_f‖₂; - e∓ = ‖E∓ − S∓‖₂ / ‖S∓‖₂ over all three components.

Asserted. - (S0) Premise, closed form only. At p̂ = a·p/|p|, both of these are ≤ 1e-9: - ‖(ε_c S⁻ − S⁺)·r̂‖/‖S⁺·r̂‖; - ‖r̂×(S⁻ − S⁺)‖/‖S⁺‖.

Predicted ≤ 1e-12: each series term matches termwise. - (X0a) F = 2V − 4 exactly. F is the number of interface faces and V the number of distinct surface vertices (a closed genus-0 surface). - (X0b) Every point has exactly one owned containing cell of tag 1 and one of tag 2, counted globally with Allreduce SUM. - (X1) max |n_f×(E⁻ − E⁺)| ≤ 1e-10·max|E⁺|. The N1curl tangential trace is continuous, so this proves the two calls read the two cells of the same face. - (C) R_n, e⁻ and e⁺ each strictly decrease over the three rungs (TH-10's "decreasing rung to rung" precedent). - The levels are a record, predicted in [0.01, 0.30] at the finest rung. - The pairwise rates are printed, predicted ≈ 1. - (B) The legacy owner=None route for both sides gives R_n = |ε_c − 1| (160.155 at 64 MHz) to 1e-12 relative.

Controls (rule (e)). - (B) is algebraic, and asserted above. - The separation |ε_c − 1|/R_n is predicted ≥ 500× and printed, not asserted. - Printed beside R_n: - the σ-blind residual (εᵣ in place of ε_c), predicted 0.874; - the conjugated convention (ε_c*), predicted 1.748 — TH-10's 173.8 % signature; - the fraction of points where the legacy route lands on the tag-1 side, predicted ≈ 0.5.

Windows. Bare, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000.

Basis: the TH-10 module ran five solves in 21 s (20260822T123746Z_OPS-18-step3-th10-rerun.log), and POST-8 step 2's W1 took 195 s. - W1 (-n 2, ≈ 270 s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh POST-1-step7a-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_ANS_SKIP_PRIVATE=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py tests/validation/test_post8_owner_rule_ans2.py tests/post/test_post1_one_sided_interface_sphere.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W2 (-n 4, ≈ 60 s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh POST-1-step7a-W2 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 4 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py tests/post/test_post1_one_sided_interface_sphere.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W3 (real, ≈ 50 s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh POST-1-step7a-W3-real "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py -v -s --tb=short'"

After W2, print the R_n difference between -n 2 and -n 4 as a record (predicted ≤ 1e-9).

Traps: - Never total_field for S±. It switches on r < a, and each centroid sits inside by the chord sagitta. - Point lists must be bitwise equal on every rank, or OPS-55 raises. Build from sorted vertices, and never round. - cell_tags.values is rank-local; candidates are owned cells only. - A face point found on one side only is a collision-tolerance finding. Print it, and never tune the 1e-9. - The POST-8 re-gate loads ans:2 without main() (item 177's precedent). No slot opens docs/private/ or aed_results/. - Rule (i): no edit after W1 without re-running it. - Harness hygiene: -s, no -k, no pipes. After a kill, run pgrep -c python3 in the container first. - File overlap: item 188 imports from post/evaluation.py but does not edit it. The two items are independent.

Scope. 7a only: degree 1, 64 MHz, pointwise interface residuals. No peak, SAR, birdcage or ✅ claim, and no band on the levels.

Negative result. Report and stop; never loosen a bound. - (S0) red: a known-issues entry against LossySphereSeries (the TH-10 records are implicated). - (X0a) / (X0b) red: a mesh or extraction finding. Park and mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). - (X1), (K) or a re-gate red: revert src/ and park. - (C) red: record the levels on the row, mark BLOCKED, and the review rules. - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Status it can move. The §7 POST-1 state line gains "7a done" and stays 🟡 (or a known-issues entry if red). 7b becomes writable.

Outcome — DONE 2026-10-03 (21:00 CDT slot, executor implementer). Every asserted check green; nothing edited after W1 (rule (i)). - Windows: W1 20261003T020316Z_POST-1-step7a-W1.log (-n 2, 215 s, 27 passed, 1 skipped — the pre-existing test_prechange_control_was_silent; POST-8 ans:2 re-gate green); W2 20261003T020658Z_POST-1-step7a-W2.log (-n 4, 67 s, 16 passed); W3 20261003T020808Z_POST-1-step7a-W3-real.log (real, -n 2, 53 s, 20 passed, 5 skipped). A smoke dev run precedes them: 20261003T020248Z_POST-1-step7a-dev.log. - (K): the face point resolves to cell 223 (x < 0.5) and 232 (x > 0.5), each the oracle minimum on its side; the unrestricted rule gives 223. Same at -n 2, -n 4 and real. - (S0): normal 5.5e-16 … 6.1e-16, tangential 2.8e-16 … 2.9e-16 (bound 1e-9). - (X0a): F / V = 494 / 249, 1104 / 554, 2496 / 1250 — F = 2V − 4 exact. (X0b): one tag-1 and one tag-2 cell per point on every rung. - (X1): 2.3e-15, 3.8e-15, 5.8e-15 (bound 1e-10). - (C), a record (5 866 / 17 667 / 55 241 cells): R_n 0.5007 / 0.2821 / 0.1778; e⁻ 0.0718 / 0.0366 / 0.0202; e⁺ 0.2810 / 0.1900 / 0.1328. All strictly decreasing, finest-rung levels inside the predicted [0.01, 0.30]. Pairwise rates: R_n 1.414, 1.142; e⁻ 1.658, 1.473; e⁺ 0.963, 0.886. - (B): legacy R_n = |ε_c − 1| = 160.155313 to ≤ 3.5e-16. - -n 2 vs -n 4 R_n (record): 2.2e-13, 4.8e-13, 2.1e-12. - Controls (printed): separation 319.9× / 567.8× / 900.8× (finest meets the predicted ≥ 500×); σ-blind 0.893 / 0.876 / 0.873 (predicted 0.874); legacy tag-1 fraction 0.478 / 0.488 / 0.506. The ε_c* control misses its prediction: 2.153 / 1.974 / 1.889 against the predicted 1.748 (+8 % at the finest rung). It still separates from R_n by ≈ 10×, but TH-10's 173.8 % signature value is not reproduced. Under rule (e) this is reported, not decided; the review rules. - Code (rule (c), disclosed): candidate_cells=None keyword on point_owner_cells / evaluate_vector_field_parallel in post/evaluation.py, per the brief's letter. New: tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py, tests/post/test_post1_one_sided_interface_sphere.py.

docs.title: §9 item 203 — 2026-10-03 (lane 1)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-03 03:00 daily review; the review reviewed it.

This is 7b, the birdcage half of the 09-30 weekly's last-step target ("the same residuals on the loaded birdcage as a C4-gated record"). It reuses 7a's one-sided extraction (candidate_cells, item 187) unchanged. - Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy (W1 is predicted at 170–260 s, above the standard ceiling). -n 2 (W1) and -n 4 (W2), complex only. No real-build window: no src/ change. - Class: lane-1 revalidation (measured median 8 min). Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 40 predicted min. Depends on: nothing (7a is done).

Fixture. The loaded F-small four-leg gapped birdcage on the 1 g rung at 64 MHz, degree 1: - build_four_port_sweep(frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_64_HZ, phantom_resolution=PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG, build_only=True), then four _solve_driven(sweep, pid) (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:142). build_only + _solve_driven is test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:321's idiom. If it raises on a missing key, use POST-8 step 2's full-sweep case construction (test_post8_owner_rule_ans2.py:114–148) with the frequency keyword added. Edit no helper. - Why this rung. C4 gates already run on it: MAT-15's 10 g pairs (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:50–51, :390). IMP-3 W2 solved it at 64 MHz (20261002T170843Z_IMP-3-step1-W2.log:1918, 199 920 cells; build 38.7 s, sweep 21.3 s at -n 4, :3809). Its 58 866 tag-3 cells (h ≈ 2.5 mm) give ≈ 7 700 interface faces. The default mesh has 537 tag-3 cells (test_birdcage_phantom_resolution.py:64, ≈ 1.5 cm), which is too few for a quadrant-level reading. - The band, imported and never restated: C4_COVARIANCE_BAND = 5 % (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:120). It is the band the 64 MHz field gate (test_birdcage_b1_larmor.py:69–83), the coil-driven SAR integral gate (test_birdcage_sar_integral.py:117–121) and MAT-15 import.

Module tests/validation/test_post1_one_sided_interface_birdcage.py (complex_only). Nothing under src/. - Imported, never restated: - C4_COVARIANCE_BAND and _solve_driven (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py); - PARTITION_EPS_M and PARTITION_RTOL (test_birdcage_sar_integral.py:142, :149); - QUADRATURE_STEP_DEG and _port_index (test_birdcage_b1_quadrature.py); - ONE_GRAM_RUNG_CELL_RECORD, ONE_GRAM_RUNG_PHANTOM_CELL_RECORD and PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG (test_birdcage_sar_1g_rung.py:114–126); - PHANTOM_CELL_TAG (test_port_birdcage_lumped_column.py:101; air is tag 2 per its comment at :96–99, so define AIR_CELL_TAG = 2 citing it); - PHANTOM_RADIUS and PHANTOM_HEIGHT (test_birdcage_port_tags.py:28–29; the phantom is centred on the origin with axis z); - _phantom_sigma_range and PHANTOM_SIGMA_RTOL (test_birdcage_sar_map.py:239, :201); - _series, FREQUENCY_64_HZ and SALINE_SIGMA (test_lossy_sphere_fullwave.py). Take ε_c = _series(FREQUENCY_64_HZ).epsilon_c, exactly 7a's convention. - CAD_AREA_M2 (test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:99, printed only). - Drive order: sorted sheet ids, with k from _port_index (P1 at 360° is k = 0). The rotation sense is imported from test_birdcage_sar_integral.py:337–345: drive k+1 at Rx equals drive k at x, so P_{j+1}^{(k+1)} = P_j^{(k)}. - Interface faces (partition-free, rank-safe): - On each rank, take every face of an owned tag-3 cell whose three vertices are all on the lateral surface (‖(x, y)‖ − R ≤ 1e-9·R in absolute value, |z| ≤ (H/2)(1 + 1e-9)) or all on one cap (||z| − H/2| ≤ 1e-9·H/2, ‖(x, y)‖ ≤ R(1 + 1e-9)). Apply the test per face, never per vertex. - Store each face's lexicographically sorted vertices, and orient n_f outward: n_f·(p − c) > 0, where c is the tag-3 cell's centroid. - Allgather the faces and lexsort them on the nine sorted coordinates, as at test_post1_one_sided_interface_sphere.py:107–111. Drop every face that appears twice: those are interior chords between two tag-3 cells with all three vertices on the surface. An interface face has exactly one tag-3 cell, so it appears exactly once. Print the dropped count (predicted 0–30). - Points: three per face at barycentric (2/3, 1/6, 1/6) and its permutations, all interior to the face. This rule is exact for the quadratic |·|² of a degree-1 N1curl trace. The array is bitwise identical on every rank (OPS-55). - E⁻, E⁺: evaluate_vector_field_parallel(e, pts, comm, owner="lowest_original_cell", candidate_cells=cell_tags.find(3)) for E⁻, and the same with find(2) for E⁺. The legacy route is the default owner=None, read once. - Residual integrals per drive k, with quadrant weights w_j as a numpy twin of _quadrant_weight (test_birdcage_sar_integral.py:207–220, same PARTITION_EPS_M): - r = ε_c E⁻·n_f − E⁺·n_f; - N_j^{(k)} = Σ_f (A_f/3) Σ_q w_j(x_q)|r(x_q)|²; - D_j^{(k)} = the same sum with |E⁺·n_f|²; - N^{(k)} = Σ_f (A_f/3) Σ_q |r|², and R_n^{(k)} = √(N^{(k)}/D^{(k)}).

Asserted. - (A0) Global cells == ONE_GRAM_RUNG_CELL_RECORD (199 920) and tag-3 cells == ONE_GRAM_RUNG_PHANTOM_CELL_RECORD (58 866), exactly, both reduced. The four sheets sit on the 90° grid (_port_index), and f = FREQUENCY_64_HZ. - (A1) The phantom σ is uniform at SALINE_SIGMA to PHANTOM_SIGMA_RTOL (_phantom_sigma_range, reduced). |ε_c − 1| is printed beside 7a's 160.155313. - (X0a) F = 2V − 4 exactly over the kept faces: the phantom is a closed genus-0 cylinder. V is counted as distinct input_global_indices, as in 7a. - (X0b) Every point has exactly one owned containing cell of tag 3, one of tag 2, and two in total, counted globally with Allreduce SUM (7a's _side_counts, plus the total). Both one-sided calls return valid everywhere. - (X0c) Σ A_f equals MAT-15's ∮ds on the same mesh, 2.072479761e-02 m² (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1926), to 1e-8 relative. It is a second route to the same facet set; store it as a module constant with that provenance. Print the deviation from CAD_AREA_M2. - (X1) Per drive, max |n_f×(E⁻ − E⁺)| ≤ 1e-10·max|E⁺| (7a measured ≤ 5.8e-15). - (P) Partition: |Σ_j N_j^{(k)} − N^{(k)}| ≤ PARTITION_RTOL·N^{(k)}, and likewise for D, for all four drives. - (B) The legacy route gives R_n = |ε_c − 1| to 1e-12 relative for every drive. This is algebraic: both sides read the same cell. 7a measured ≤ 3.5e-16. - (G1) The C4 gate on whole-interface residuals: the four cyclic pairs |N^{(k+1)} − N^{(k)}|/N^{(k)} are each ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. The whole surface is its own C4 image. Predicted ≤ 2 %. - (G2) The C4 gate on the residual map at quadrant resolution: the sixteen cyclic pairs |N_{j+1}^{(k+1)} − N_j^{(k)}|/N_j^{(k)} (k, j = 0…3, indices mod 4) are each ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, one parametrised test per pair so that a miss names its (k, j). Predicted in [0.3 %, 8 %]. The upper end is above the band; see Negative result.

Records (printed, no band): - R_n^{(k)} per drive, predicted in [0.05, 0.6] (7a's sphere: 0.50 → 0.18 over three rungs); - the 4 × 4 tables N_j^{(k)}, D_j^{(k)} and quadrant R_n; - F, V, the number of points; - elapsed time for the build, each solve, the extraction and the window; - the D-pair table: the same sixteen pairings on D, predicted ≤ 1 % (test_birdcage_sar_integral.py:172–185, which measured 0.2–1.5 % on the coarse mesh); - the single-drive mirror |N_{k+1}^{(k)} − N_{k−1}^{(k)}|/N_{k−1}^{(k)}, predicted ≤ the band; - P1–P4 phantom power ½∫σ|E|² dx(3) beside IMP-3 W2's 1.530006187e-06 / 1.527879591e-06 / 1.527774714e-06 / 1.528062711e-06 W (…IMP-3-step1-W2.log:3802–3805; a different solve path, built= + sweep keep_fields), predicted ≤ 1e-6 relative.

Why the gate is at quadrant resolution, not pointwise (a deviation from the 03:00 design letter, for the review). A pointwise residual map read against its rotated image is ill-posed on this fixture. The mesh is not C4-congruent: c4_congruent_sheets binds only the port sheets (io/mesh.py:3748). So a rotated face point is neither a face point nor on the faceted surface, and one of the two one-sided reads would be invalid. The fixture's own history also prices the pointwise construction: the pointwise SAR C4 identities missed this same 5 % band by 25–41 % (test_birdcage_sar_map.py:24–32). The same solves met it as cell integrals at ≤ 1.52 % (test_birdcage_sar_integral.py:172–185). R_n is itself a cell-level discretisation error. The smooth partition makes w_{j+1}(x) = w_j(R⁻¹x) exact, so (G2) is the rotated map at the finest resolution where the identity is exact on a non-congruent mesh. - Printed only: a nearest-face pointwise reading, for the record. For each face f of drive k, take the face g whose centroid is nearest R^{−k}p_f, by brute force on rank 0 in row chunks (no scipy dependency). Print the median and 90th percentile of |ρ_g^{(0)} − ρ_f^{(k)}|/ρ_f^{(k)} (ρ = the face's mean |r|²) and the median match distance divided by h. Predicted median ≥ 10 % (the pointwise floor).

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (B) is asserted (algebraic, above). Its separation |ε_c − 1|/R_n^{(k)} is predicted ≥ 250× and printed. Ceiling: the separation is 160.155/R_n by construction, so it is whatever R_n allows: 267× at R_n = 0.6 and 900× at 7a's finest sphere level. - The mis-rotated pairing, predicted and printed: |N_{j+2}^{(k+1)} − N_j^{(k)}|/N_j^{(k)}, i.e. the 180° image read where the 90° one belongs (test_birdcage_sar_integral.py:345's control, on N). There is no prior measurement on N, so it is not asserted. Print per k its mean, its ratio to the (G2) mean, and the ceiling: under C4 the control reads drive k's own adjacent-quadrant contrast |N_{j+1}^{(k)} − N_j^{(k)}|/N_j^{(k)}, so it cannot exceed max_j N_j^{(k)}/min_j N_j^{(k)} − 1. Print that bound per drive. Predicted: control in [10 %, 150 %] and ratio ≥ 3×, never above the printed bound. - Trap: never use the wrong-sense pairing (j − 1) as a control. Under C4 it maps to N_{j−2}^{(k)} vs N_j^{(k)}, and for j = k+1 that is the mirror pair N_{k−1}^{(k)} = N_{k+1}^{(k)}, which the symmetry makes equal. The control would sit inside the band by construction on a quarter of its pairs. - Printed beside R_n, 7a's two sign sentinels: - σ-blind (εᵣ for ε_c): predicted [0.80, 0.95]. The leading order is |σ/ωε₀|/|ε_c| = 140.43/160.64 = 0.874; 7a measured 0.873–0.893. - the conjugated ε_c*: predicted [1.6, 2.4]. The leading order is 1.748; 7a measured 1.889–2.153, which missed its point prediction, so this is a range. - The legacy route's tag-3 fraction is predicted ≈ 0.5.

Rank invariance (W2). - At -n 2, rank 0 writes /workspace/logs/post1/step7b-n2.npz (gitignored) with the sorted face-vertex array, F, V, Σ A_f, N, D and R_n, then Barrier. At -n 4 the module loads it; if it is missing, pytest.fail and never recompute. - (W0), asserted: the face-vertex array is bitwise equal, and F and V are equal. Mesh coordinates do not depend on the partition. - Printed: max relative N, D and R_n difference, predicted ≤ 1e-8. N is a difference of two O(1) normal fields, so the ≈ 2e-10 solve drift POST-8 3a measured across widths is amplified ≈ 1/R_n.

Windows. Bare, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000, in order W1 → W2.

Basis: MAT-15 W1 on this rung at -n 2 took mesh + rung 61.3 s and EM 142.6 s (20261001T123309Z_MAT-15-step1-W1.log:1924, :1954). POST-8 3a's W1 / W2 took 272 / 231 s on the same mesh. The extraction is 12 evaluator calls on ≈ 23 000 points. - W1 (-n 2, predicted 170–260 s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh POST-1-step7b-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py tests/validation/test_post1_one_sided_interface_birdcage.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W2 (-n 4, predicted 140–240 s):

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh POST-1-step7b-W2 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 4 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_post1_one_sided_interface_birdcage.py -v -s --tb=short'" - A smoke dev run before W1 is allowed, as 7a did (…POST-1-step7a-dev.log). Rule (i) still binds W1.

Traps: - The face test is per face, not per vertex. A face with one rim, one lateral and one cap-interior vertex is an interior face. Faces seen twice are chords: drop them. Never tune the 1e-9 surface tolerance. A point found on one side only is a collision-tolerance finding: print it. - Point lists must be bitwise equal on every rank (OPS-55): build from sorted vertex coordinates and never round. - Rank-local data: cell_tags.values / .find are rank-local, and the candidates are owned ∩ the set (the evaluator does this). Every face sum is built from the allgathered global arrays, so do not reduce it again. The phantom-power assemble_scalar is rank-local: allreduce it. - Complex build: w_j is numpy, so there is no UFL comparison. If any UFL form carries SpatialCoordinate, pin quadrature_degree (POST-5), and never use ufl.max_value or <= on complex operands (OPS-22). - ε_c comes from _series(...).epsilon_c, never re-typed. The conjugate sentinel is the sign check. - A killed compile leaves an orphan .c: run the rubric's cache sweep (daily-review.md:426) only when pgrep -c python3 in the container reads 0. - Harness hygiene: -s, no -k, no pipes. The harness call is the whole Bash command. After a kill, run pgrep -c python3 first. - Rule (i): an edit after W1 means W1 and W2 re-run. - Private data: nothing here touches examples/ansys_benchmarks/. At R_n ≈ 1, N measures the local discretisation error of the normal trace, not the interface physics. - The red sits in fixed space. Every red (G2) pair is in absolute columns j = 0 / 1, for every k. Each drive's own-quadrant N, the dominant entry, reads 7.64 / 6.75 / 7.64 / 7.86e-2: quadrant 1 is ≈ 12 % lower whatever the drive. - On a mesh that is C4-congruent only on the port sheets (io/mesh.py:3748), a discretisation error inherits the mesh's quadrant differences. docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 03:00 daily review; the review reviewed it.

This is 7b′, the 10-03 weekly's re-pose of 7b (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4451–4456): "the same one-sided residuals on TH-16's mirror-built F-small mesh, where the D2 images exist cell for cell, gating the D2 image pairs at the brief's imported band; the C4 statement is dropped, not loosened". It is attempt 2 of 4 in the 7b family (attempt 1 is item 203, ruled above). - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard (W1 predicted 75–130 s). -n 2 (W1) and -n 4 (W2), complex only. There is no real-build window, because nothing under src/ changes. - Class: lane-1 revalidation (measured median 8 min). Cost: ≈ 8 measured / ≈ 30 predicted min. Depends on: nothing (7a is done; TH-16 is ✅).

Fixture: TH-16 step 3c's mirror-built full mesh (tests/validation/test_th16_quarter_birdcage.py). The module imports that file's helpers and edits nothing in it. - Mesh. Build the quarter with _build(True, symmetry_quadrant=True) (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheets.py:80): 36 034 cells, mesh 6.90 s, rung 8.09 s at -n 2 (20260930T093451Z_TH-16-step3c-W1.log:934). - Mirror. Gather, mirror and distribute exactly as full does (test_th16_quarter_birdcage.py:514–598): _gather_owned (:234); _mirror_by_index across axis 1, then axis 0 (:255, :518–519); _distribute (test_th16_symmetry_plane_driven.py:145); cell tags through distribute_entity_data + meshtags_from_entities (:528–539). This gives 144 136 cells and 26 253 vertices, built in 1.03 s; per-tag cells 1:50 624, 2:87 016, 3:1 256, 102:2 704, 201:2 536 (…W1.log:990–991). The phantom is tag 3, with 1 256 cells (≈ 1.1 cm). - Port sheets: the whole cut-plane box face, not the narrowed sheet (a deviation from TH-16's letter, for the review). - TH-16 narrows each quarter sheet to GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION 0.5 (:318–327). That is a sub-sheet triangulated out of a box, which the 2026-10-02 binding ruling forbids in new fixtures. - The exact-strip knob refuses symmetry_quadrant (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:4266–4271). - So the quarter sheets are the un-narrowed faces _owned_exterior_on_plane(msh, cells, SHEET_PLANE_AXIS[p], KEPT_HALF[p]) (:154, :306). Each is the whole CAD face of the port box on the cut plane, 50 / 56 facets (SHEET_FACET_RECORD, :109). The box is 10 mm wide against the 12 mm leg (test_birdcage_port_tags.py:24,30). This whole-mid-plane sheet has been solved before: it is PORT step 2's own sheet, the f = 1.0 control (test_port_lumped_narrowed_sheet.py:127–131). - Width is w = A/h with κ off. Copy :304–317 and :328–341 and omit :318–327. - The mesh is unchanged, and the D2 symmetry holds with either sheet. This item reads no port quantity. - Full-mesh sheets 211–214 come from the midpoint match at :565–598: P1 = P1q; P2 = P2q; P3 = P1q flipped on axis 0; P4 = P2q flipped on axis 1 (FULL_SHEETS, :134; SHEET_PLANE_AXIS :140). - Solve. The problem is as at :603–617 (all exterior PEC; conductor SIGMA_WIRE_S_PER_M; tag 3 at SALINE_SIGMA / SALINE_EPSILON_R). Two changes: frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_64_HZ, and the sweep is run_n_port_sparameter_sweep(problem, defs, lumped_sheet_ports=specs, lumped_sheet_facet_tags=tags_s, degree=1, keep_fields=True) (ports/sparameters.py:310,325). The specs are as at :618–641, with interior=True and FULL_Z0_OHM. Drive k's field is result.fields[f"P{k+1}"].e_complex, and its σ is .sigma_field. - Code by path. Land the parked module with git checkout attempt/POST-1-step7b-20261003T141500Z -- tests/validation/test_post1_one_sided_interface_birdcage.py. It is code that main has never had. Never check out its log or test-results.md by path. - Re-target in place. Keep _FACES, _BARY, _w, _interface_faces, _side_counts, the per-drive extraction loop and its sentinels, and the (X0a) / (X0b) / (X1) / (P) / (B) / (W0) tests. - Delete: build_four_port_sweep, the 1 g records in (A0), (X0c) with MAT15_SURFACE_AREA_M2, IMP3_W2_PHANTOM_POWER_W, _rotz and the nearest-face reading, and the (G1) / (G2) C4 tests. - Docstring: 7b′. Say that the 7b version is at cbd32287. - New npz path: /workspace/logs/post1/step7b2-n2.npz.

The D2 image map (derived; mesh and drives). - Port positions. The quarter keeps x, y ≥ 0. P1q lies in y = 0, so it is at θ = 0; P2q lies in x = 0, so it is at θ = 90°. P3 is the axis-0 flip of P1 (θ = 180°) and P4 the axis-1 flip of P2 (θ = 270°). So drive k = (port number − 1) sits at θ_k = kπ/2, the same centring as _w's θ_j = jπ/2. - The three maps (indices mod 4): - σ_x, the mirror x → −x: P1 ↔ P3, P2 and P4 fixed; k ↦ 2 − k, j ↦ 2 − j, since c_j(M_x p) = c_{2−j}(p) in _w. - σ_y, the mirror y → −y: P2 ↔ P4, P1 and P3 fixed; k ↦ −k, j ↦ −j. - σ_π = σ_xσ_y: k ↦ k + 2, j ↦ j + 2. - Why the residual is invariant. Every drive is ẑ-directed (:375, :637), and ẑ is invariant under both mirrors, so the image of drive k is drive σk with the same sign. E is a polar vector, so the image field is M·E(Mx). The image face's outward normal is M n_f, so E·n is invariant. Hence |r|² at Mx under drive σk equals |r|² at x under drive k. - The cell-for-cell premise is TH-16's measurement. On this mesh the S-level D2 pairs read S₁₁/S₃₃ 1.491e-13, S₂₂/S₄₄ 9.769e-13 and adjacent 1.663e-13 (…W1.log:946–947,1021–1022). - No face is its own image. A self-image would need three collinear vertices, so every orbit has 4 faces and F ≡ 0 (mod 4).

Imported, never restated. - The band: C4_COVARIANCE_BAND = 5 % (test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:120), the band item 203 imported (its brief, above). It is used here on D2 pairs only. - From TH-16: MIDPOINT_MATCH_TOL_M (:132), PLANE_TOL, QUARTER_CELL_RECORD, FULL_CELL_RECORD, SHEET_FACET_RECORD, SHEET_AREA_RTOL and FULL_SHEETS / FULL_SHEET_TAG / SHEET_TAG / KEPT_HALF / SHEET_PLANE_AXIS / SHEET_TRANSVERSE_AXIS. - EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (test_birdcage_symmetry_quadrant.py:47). - LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND and PASSIVITY_SIGMA_TOLERANCE (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:165). - _class_means is not needed. Copy TH-16's d2 dict lines (:659–664) verbatim. - Everything else as in the parked module: _series, FREQUENCY_64_HZ, SALINE_SIGMA, PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, PHANTOM_RADIUS / PHANTOM_HEIGHT (the same 0.03 / 0.08 m that _build passes), PARTITION_EPS_M / PARTITION_RTOL, _phantom_sigma_range / PHANTOM_SIGMA_RTOL, CAD_AREA_M2 (printed). For _phantom_sigma_range, pass {"mesh": msh, "cell_tags": cells} as the sweep argument.

Asserted. - (M0) The mesh is TH-16's, as test_mirror_build_conforms (:758–768) with the sheet record swapped: - quarter cells == QUARTER_CELL_RECORD; - full cells == FULL_CELL_RECORD; vertices == builder count; - per-tag cells ×4 exactly; |V_f/(4V_q) − 1| ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL; zero owned exterior facets on either plane; - un-narrowed quarter sheets == SHEET_FACET_RECORD; full sheets 50 / 56 / 50 / 56 owned facets, with dS areas equal to the quarter's at SHEET_AREA_RTOL; - sheet k's mean midpoint on the predicted side: P1 x > 0, P2 y > 0, P3 x < 0, P4 y < 0. - (A1) The tag-3 σ is uniform at SALINE_SIGMA to PHANTOM_SIGMA_RTOL over 1 256 cells (reduced). f = FREQUENCY_64_HZ. - (I3) The drives are D2 images. S_f's pairs S₁₁/S₃₃, S₂₂/S₄₄ and the adjacent spread are each ≤ LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. Predicted ≤ 1e-11 (1.5e-13 … 9.8e-13 at 10 MHz with the narrowed sheet, above). (I1) reciprocity and (I2) σ_max are printed. - (X0a) F = 2V − 4 exactly. (X0b) One owned tag-3 cell, one tag-2 cell and two in total per point (Allreduce), and every one-sided read is valid. (X1) max |n_f×(E⁻ − E⁺)| ≤ 1e-10·max|E⁺| per drive. (P) The partition identity at PARTITION_RTOL. (B) The legacy route gives |ε_c − 1| to 1e-12. All five are item 203's, unchanged. - (M1) The face set is D2-closed. For σ ∈ {σ_x, σ_y}, every face's image centroid has exactly one face centroid within MIDPOINT_MATCH_TOL_M. - The map is a fixed-point-free involution. - Matched areas agree to EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, and so do matched normals (n_g = M n_f, absolute on unit vectors). - The matching is brute force on every rank: the arrays are allgathered and identical, and F ≈ 600. - (G1′) Whole-interface D2 pairs. |N^{(σk)} − N^{(k)}|/N^{(k)} ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND for (σ_x, k = 0, 2) and (σ_y, k = 1, 3), 4 readings (σ_π gives the same pairs). - (G2′) Quadrant D2 pairs. For each σ ∈ {σ_x, σ_y, σ_π} and each (k, j) with (σk, σj) ≠ (k, j): |N_{σj}^{(σk)} − N_j^{(k)}|/N_j^{(k)} ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. That is 12 + 12 + 16 = 40 parametrised readings, each naming (σ, k, j). They include the single-drive mirrors (σ_y on k = 0 is N₁⁽⁰⁾ against N₃⁽⁰⁾), which read 12.98 / 0.72 / 15.10 / 0.55 % on the non-mirror 1 g mesh (20261003T140719Z_POST-1-step7b-dev.log:1897–1900; a different mesh, so context only). - (G3′) Face-level D2 pairs (pointwise). For σ ∈ {σ_x, σ_y} and each k: max_f |ρ_{σf}^{(σk)} − ρ_f^{(k)}|/ρ_f^{(k)} ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND, with ρ the face mean of |r|². That is 8 readings. Also print min ρ_f / mean ρ. - Predictions for (G1′) – (G3′): ≤ 1e-9 for the integrals and ≤ 1e-7 face-wise. Basis: the D2 identity is exact on this mesh up to solve round-off. TH-16 (I3) measured ≤ 9.8e-13, and -n 2 in-process solves differ by ≈ 2e-12 (MAT-5 W1, ruled 2026-10-05). |ε_c| ≈ 160 amplifies E⁻'s noise in r. - The band is ≈ 1e7 above the prediction. Reporting rule (not a band): any reading above 1e-8 is journaled as unexplained, even when green.

Records (printed, no band). - R_n per drive, predicted [0.8, 1.5]: 7b read ≈ 1.0 at h ≈ 2.5 mm, and this phantom is coarser. - The N_j^{(k)}, D_j^{(k)} and quadrant R_n tables, and the same D2 pairs on D. - F (predicted [400, 900], ≡ 0 mod 4), V and the number of points. - Σ A_f against CAD_AREA_M2. - Phantom power per drive through mean_sar (reduced), with its σ pairs. - S_f. - Elapsed: quarter build, mirror build, sweep, extraction, window. - The dropped C4 statement, as a record only: item 203's (G1) / (G2) C4 pairings on this mesh. They are never gated and never read as a field finding: this is the mesh's own C4 contrast. Predicted 0–20 %.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (B) is asserted (algebraic: both sides read one cell). 7b measured ≤ 1.775e-16 (…POST-1-step7b-dev.log:1861–1873). Its separation |ε_c − 1|/R_n is predicted 100–200× and printed. Ceiling: 160.155/R_n by construction, so ≈ 160× at R_n ≈ 1. - (N1) The half-mapped pairing, predicted and printed: map the quadrant but not the drive, only on drives σ moves. - Under σ_x: k ∈ {0, 2}, j ∈ {0, 2}. Under σ_y: k ∈ {1, 3}, j ∈ {1, 3}. - The reading is |N_{σj}^{(k)} − N_j^{(k)}|/N_j^{(k)}, the driven quadrant against the opposite one. - Predicted [50 %, 400 %], from 7b's own-to-opposite ratios on the 1 g mesh: 0.733 / 2.743 at k = 0 through 0.769 / 3.330 at k = 3 (N table above). - Ceiling per drive: max_j N_j^{(k)}/min_j N_j^{(k)} − 1, printed. The reading cannot exceed it. - Separation over (G2′)'s max: predicted ≥ 1e6×, printed. - Trap: never take the half-mapped pairing on a drive σ fixes (σ_y on k = 0). That is the identity, and it sits inside the band by construction. This is the D2 analogue of item 203's wrong-sense trap. - (N2) The face-level half-mapped pairing ρ_{σf}^{(k)} against ρ_f^{(k)}, on drives σ moves: median and p90 printed, predicted median ≥ 10 % (7b's nearest-face C4 median read 68.8–70.0 %). - Item 203's sentinels, printed: - σ-blind, predicted [0.95, 1.10] (7b 1.001–1.009, :1862–1874); - ε_c*, predicted [1.6, 2.6] (7b 2.297–2.323); - the legacy tag-3 fraction, ≈ 0.5.

docs.title: POST-10 — The point-owner rule on a create_submesh mesh: key submesh cells by their parent's original cell index
docs.text: Item briefs and execution history (operator directive 2026-10-01). The §7 row is the status of record.

docs.title: §9 item 254 — 2026-10-05 (lane 1, known-issues "Resolves with")
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 10:30 daily review; the review reviews it.

POST-10 step 1: make owner="lowest_original_cell" work on a create_submesh mesh by keying each submesh cell with its parent cell's original index. This is the "Resolves with" of the known-issues entry 2026-10-04 — 🟡 OPEN (ANS-9 step 1a, §9 item 218) — evaluate_vector_field_parallel(owner="lowest_original_cell") raises RuntimeError: Mixed topology unsupported. on a create_submesh mesh (docs/testing/known-issues.md:1372–1379): "A post/evaluation.py fix mapping submesh cells to parent original indices (a POST step, not yet opened), or a documented restriction." It is a lane-1 item (§9 rule (5): "open known-issues entries whose own 'Resolves with' a slot can execute", PROJECT_PLAN.md:3742–3743). - Executor: implementer. One src/ change and one new test module. No solve, no meshing beyond create_unit_cube. - Tier: standard, three windows: W1 real build -n 2, W2 complex -n 4, W3 complex -n 1. Each runs timeout -k 30 180. - Class: lane 1, ≈ 7 measured min (class median). Predicted ≈ 40 min: 15 fixed, ≈ 15 code (≈ 40 lines in src/, ≈ 220 in the test), three windows of ≈ 1 min each, and the remainder for the journal and the known-issues retirement. - Depends on nothing. - Not a ⚠️ subsystem. No POST row in §7 carries ⚠️. POST-8, whose rule this extends, is 🟡 and its rule has gates (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2567–2575). So §9's no-new-features rule (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3651) does not bind.

What raises, read off the code and the log. - point_owner_cells keys the rule with original = _original_cell_index(mesh) (src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py:92). That reads mesh.topology.original_cell_index (:19–28). - On a create_submesh mesh, DolfinX 0.11.0.post0 (the image's version, 20261003T020658Z_POST-1-step7a-W2.log:97) raises RuntimeError: Mixed topology unsupported. from dolfinx/mesh.py:268 (20261004T142026Z_ANS-9-step1a-W1.log:1949–1977). A submesh carries no original cell index. - The raise is symmetric today. It comes after evaluate_vector_field_parallel's key allgather (:216) and before point_owner_cells' first collective (:114), and every rank's submesh topology refuses alike. So it does not hang, but the fix must keep it that way. - The submesh does not reference its parent. No zero-argument fix exists, so the caller must pass the map. Every submesh site in the repo already holds it: parent_ids = emap.sub_topology_to_topology(np.arange(n_sub, dtype=np.int32), False) over owned + ghost sub cells (tests/validation/test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:74–88, re-used as _sphere_submesh by MAT-12 / MAT-14 / MAT-19 / MAT-5, and as _tag_submesh in tests/validation/test_mat15_coil_driven_heating_phantom.py:105–120). This idiom is green on 0.11. - Why the rule's meaning survives. On the parent, the original cell index is the mesher's order, not the partition's (POST-8 step 2, docs/planning/chunks/POST-8.md:28). Its restriction to the kept cells is injective. Over all ranks, the owned sub cells are exactly the kept cells, each counted once. So "lowest parent original index among the submesh cells containing the point" is one deterministic cell at every width. It is the same cell the parent's one-sided rule picks with candidate_cells = keep (POST-1 step 7a, :70–74). The argument does not need submesh and parent ownership to coincide, so that is printed, not asserted.

Code (src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py only). - New keyword parent=None on point_owner_cells and evaluate_vector_field_parallel. It takes None or (parent_mesh, parent_cells). parent_cells gives the parent-local cell index of every local (owned + ghost) cell of mesh, i.e. exactly the parent_ids above. Keys become _original_cell_index(parent_mesh)[parent_cells], and nothing else in the rule changes: same owned-only candidates, same candidate_cells mask, same Allreduce MIN, same claim check. - One helper replaces the bare read at :92, collectively checked. Compute the keys or a local error. The errors are: original_cell_index raised and parent is None; parent_cells has length ≠ size_local + num_ghosts; or parent_cells holds an index outside [0, parent n_local). Then one allreduce of a status code runs, and the helper raises on every rank if any rank failed. - A missing index raises RuntimeError. Its message names create_submesh, parent=(parent_mesh, parent_cells) and POST-10, and chains the DolfinX error. - Malformed parent_cells raises ValueError. - This adds one integer collective to the existing owner path. It moves no value. - In evaluate_vector_field_parallel: - parent is valid only with owner="lowest_original_cell". Otherwise raise ValueError before any collective, mirroring candidate_cells (:188–192). - parent is None joins the OPS-40/55 key, which becomes (owner, candidate_cells is None, parent is None) (:216–218). The mismatch message at :252–257 mentions it, and keeps the substrings "owner" and "collective" that K5 asserts (tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py:212). - Docstrings for both functions gain the keyword. OWNER_RULES does not change. post/__init__.py exports nothing new. - With parent=None on a mesh that has an original index, the output must be bitwise unchanged. The regression modules below show it. - No helper that builds parent_cells (scope). The three test copies of the idiom stay as they are. - Comment-only edit, same commit: src/fem_em_solver/thermal/probe.py:9–13 cites the entry as live. Re-point it: "raises on create_submesh meshes unless parent= is given (POST-10)". The ball average stays integral-based, and MAT-19's code does not change.

Test: new tests/post/test_submesh_owner_rule.py, runs in both builds (as test_point_owner_rule.py does). - Fixture. The parent is create_unit_cube(comm, 4, 4, 4): 384 cells, the POST-8 K fixture (tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py:52–53). - Kept cells. keep is every local cell (owned + ghost) whose midpoint has x < 0.75, from dmesh.compute_midpoints(msh, 3, np.arange(n_local, dtype=np.int32)). A tet midpoint never lies on the grid plane x = 0.75, so the split is geometric and the same at every width. - The submesh is sub, emap, _, _ = dmesh.create_submesh(msh, 3, keep), with parent_cells taken from the idiom verbatim (test_mat10_sar_to_heat_sphere.py:82–88). - Points (POINTS, shape (6, 3), identical on every rank): - P0 interior (0.13, 0.27, 0.61). - P1 on the facet plane x = 0.5: (0.5, 0.3, 0.6). - P2 on the interior vertex: (0.5, 0.5, 0.5). P0–P2 are POST-8's three points. - P3 on the submesh-boundary facet: (0.75, 0.3, 0.6). - P4 on the submesh-boundary vertex: (0.75, 0.5, 0.5). - P5 outside the submesh: (0.9, 0.3, 0.6). - Planted fields. - Parent: a scalar DG0 holding _original(msh) on owned cells, then x.scatter_forward() (K3's idiom, :135–142). - Submesh: a scalar DG0 holding _original(msh)[parent_cells[c]] on owned sub cells, then scatter_forward(). - Submesh: an N1curl degree-1 field interpolating A_VEC + B_VEC × x (K2's field and constants, :46–47, :124–128). N1curl represents it exactly. - Oracle. The geometric oracle independent of DolfinX's collision search (test_point_owner_rule.py:62–82, BARY_TOL = 1e-12) computes each point's incident set of parent original indices, restricted to kept cells. It allgathers each owned parent cell's original index, its four vertices and its keep flag. Rank 0 decides and broadcasts.

Anchors (asserted at every width). - (S0) Fixture identity (arithmetic). - The submesh size_global is 288 (= 6 · 4³ · 3/4: three of four x-slabs). - len(parent_cells) == sub size_local + num_ghosts. - The kept cells' parent original indices are unique across ranks and their count is 288. - Printed: the fraction of owned sub cells whose parent is owned on the same rank (predicted 1.0, not asserted; the rule does not need it). - (K) Closed form against the oracle. - point_owner_cells(sub, POINTS, comm, parent=(msh, parent_cells))[0] equals min(oracle keep-set) exactly (integers) at P0–P4, and −1 at P5. - Through evaluate_vector_field_parallel(..., owner="lowest_original_cell", parent=...), the submesh DG0 value equals float(min) with imaginary part 0, P0–P4 are valid, and P5 is invalid. - Each point has exactly one claiming rank (K3's claims check, :178–180). - (I) The identity with the parent's one-sided rule. - The owner arrays are equal as integers: submesh rule with parent= vs point_owner_cells(msh, POINTS, comm, candidate_cells=keep). - values and valid are bitwise equal (np.array_equal, band 0): submesh DG0 under the rule with parent= vs parent DG0 under owner="lowest_original_cell", candidate_cells=keep. - DG0's basis is 1, so the value is the dof itself, copied from the same parent array. No round-off band applies. - (N) N1curl closed form on the submesh under the rule. max |eval − (A + B × p)| ≤ CLOSED_FORM_TOL = 1e-12 at P0–P4. - Define the constant with POST-8's citation comment, as test_point_owner_rule.py:44–45 does ("the guard module's bound, test_evaluation_collective_guard.py:83"). - (N) shows the chosen sub cell is evaluated correctly. It does not depend on which cell is chosen. - (W) Partition independence. - (K) and (I) are asserted at -n 1, -n 2 and -n 4, so the owner integers equal the same oracle minimum at every width. - Within each run, owner_original, the DG0 and N1curl values are bitwise equal on every rank (_bitwise_equal_across_ranks, :84–86). - Print the owner integers at every width so the three logs can be diffed by eye.

Negative controls (rule (e): labels as stated; ceiling first). - (C1) Discrimination, asserted (arithmetic). At P1, P2 and P4 the oracle keep-set has ≥ 2 members, with max − min ≥ 1. - Ceiling: the most any wrong-cell choice can be separated from the rule is exactly that set's max − min. It is an integer ≥ 1 against (K) / (I)'s band of 0, so the fixture cannot be blind to a different owner. - Predicted, printed only: set sizes 2 / 24 / ≈ 12 at P1 / P2 / P4, and 1 at P3. P1 and P2 lie inside the kept region, so their keep-sets are POST-8's measured incident sets on the same cube (20261003T020808Z_POST-1-step7a-W3-real.log:104–106): P0 {217}; P1 {223, 232}, separation 9; P2 24 cells, min 126 / max 257, separation 131. Predicted rule owners: P0 217, P1 223, P2 126. They are a prediction, not a band: (K) asserts the oracle's own minimum. - (C2) The restriction is explicit, asserted. The submesh call with owner="lowest_original_cell" and no parent raises RuntimeError on every rank, at every width. - The flags are allgathered as K5 does (:192–212). The message contains parent= and create_submesh. - A silent fallback to submesh-local numbering fails here. - (C3) Asserted. parent= with owner=None raises ValueError before any collective (the candidate_cells analogue, tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py:135–141). - (C4) Asserted. parent_cells[:-1], one entry short, raises ValueError on every rank (allgathered flags). It must not hang. - (C5) The naive fix, printed and predicted, not asserted. Key each submesh cell by sub.topology.index_map(3).local_to_global instead of the parent map: Allreduce MIN, then allgather (key, DG0 value) pairs. Print the DG0 value that key selects at P1, P2 and P4 beside the rule's value. - Predicted: differs from the rule at ≥ 1 point at ≥ 1 width. The index-map global number is partition-dependent (POST-8.md:28). - Not asserted, because nothing forces a disagreement on this fixture. - Printed only: at P3 / P4, the unrestricted parent owner (point_owner_cells(msh, POINTS)), beside the submesh owner. It shows whether the parent's rule would pick a cell on the x > 0.75 side.

Regression (rule (c)), same windows, must be green and unedited. - tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py covers the legacy owner=None path and the OPS-40/55 key. - tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py covers K0–K6, the unrestricted rule and the mismatch message. - tests/post/test_one_sided_owner_rule.py covers candidate_cells. - tests/post/test_post1_one_sided_interface_sphere.py covers the complex-build gmsh one-sided gate. - Not re-run, with reason: tests/validation/test_post8_owner_rule_ans2.py, test_post8_step3a_averaged_row1.py, test_post1_one_sided_interface_birdcage.py and test_imp3_palace_fields.py. They call the same rule with parent=None. Their value path is the one the four modules above exercise. The ANS-2 module alone is a 590 s-ceiling heavy window (20261002T200654Z_POST-8-step2-W2.log, 191 s with it). - Name them in the journal as untouched.

Windows (foreground, Bash timeout: 660000; each harness call is the whole Bash command, bare and repo-relative; -s; no pipes; no -k selection; tests/environment first).

docs.text:
Why. The entry's "What this affects" table lists 11 P1 interpolation sites in examples/ as of 2026-08-12, ten of them fed by a non-conforming source (N1curl / DG). The census is now 138 examples, and grep -rn '"Lagrange", 1\|("CG", 1\|("P", 1' examples --include=*.py finds ≈ 82 constructions (this review's count; the executor re-counts). The anchor (a census identity, measured). A probe script scripts/probes/post4_p1_site_census.py (new, stdlib only, no dolfinx import) walks examples/**/*.py, finds every functionspace(…, ("Lagrange"|"CG"|"P", 1 …)) construction, and prints one row per site: file:line, and the name of the function that is interpolated into it on the following .interpolate( call when one exists in the same function body. The executor then classifies each row by reading the code, into exactly one of: - (N) source is N1curl / RT / any ufl curl of one; - (D) source is DG of any degree; - (C) source is conforming (Lagrange of any degree, a numpy/analytic expression) — safe by construction; - (U) cannot tell from the file (say why).

and, orthogonally, (x) export only, or (e) the interpolant is evaluated, sampled, integrated or asserted on.

Asserted by the script (window 1): (i) the 08-12 table's ten file paths each still exist or are named as removed / moved, with their current line; (ii) the row count equals the independent grep -c total printed in the same window (the negative control — a parser that misses a spelling shows here). Deliverable. Traps already paid for. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. No docker call is needed. Never delete a log. Write ≈, never a tilde, in the entry. Negative result. If the parser's count and the grep count differ, report both and the missing spellings, commit the probe and log, and stop without the sub-section (rule (d): mark item 607 BLOCKED). If an (N)/(D)-sourced (e) site is found whose printout a guide quotes as a number, that is the finding: list it in the sub-section and in the journal's "Hypothesis for next", nothing more.

No PREDICTED RED: line.

docs.title: Narrative — moved verbatim from PROJECT_PLAN.md §7 (OPS-47)
docs.text:
POST-6 — arbitrary multi-port drive superposition (HFSS Edit Sources) ⬜ (feature ladder A1 — the first item of the ladder, operator directive 2026-09-04, §9 item 5; serial on nothing.) Why. Quadrature drive is the MRI excitation and every B₁⁺/SAR quantity in §1 step 3 is defined under it. WF-6 step 2 built it once, for four ports at fixed e^{∓jkπ/2}, inside a test module; EX-39 shows it. Nothing package-level takes N stored single-drive solves and a complex weight vector, which is what a tuned 32-port drive (PORT-15) and any asymmetric drive need.

  • Step 1. ports.superpose_drives(sweep_result, weights) → the combined E (and B via post.magnetic_flux_density_from_e), the combined port voltages/currents, and the combined accepted power. Gates, all identities: (i) the four-port quadrature weights reproduce WF-6 step 2's C4-invariance and mirror digits verbatim (imported, never restated); (ii) linearity — the superposed port voltages equal the weighted sums of the single-drive ones to 1e-12; (iii) power — P_acc = wᴴ(I − SᴴS)w from the S-matrix equals the volume loss integral of the superposed field to ≤ 1e-3 (the first drive-level power identity). Standard tier on the 116 085-cell 4-leg mesh. Review 2026-09-05 (03:00), two rulings on the slot's disclosures. (a) Ratified: anchor (i)'s pre-registered rtol 1e-6 against STEP2_IDENTITY_RECORDS was arithmetically unreachable — the records are four-significant-digit literals (0.9818e-2), so even a bit-identical re-run agrees with them only to ±5.1e-5 — and the substituted pair (literals at the imported CG1_RECORD_RTOL = 1e-3, package-vs-fixture path equality at 1e-12, measured 1.2e-15) is strictly tighter on the quantity that carries the information. Not a loosening; the 1e-6 was the queueing review's error. (b) The denominator hypothesis is arithmetic on the log, adopted as the working diagnosis, not as a finding: WF-6 step 1's single-drive accounting misses by 9.795751e-03 × 6.856240413e-03 W = 6.716e-05 W absolute (20260831T033704Z_WF-6-step2.log:4684–4688); supplied − sheets is 5.154401e-04 W, so that same absolute gap is 13.0% of the single-drive accepted power, and the superposed drive reads 3.511e-04 W absolute on 3.014e-03 W = 11.6% — the same fraction within the cross-term share. Whether the S-derived P_acc equals supplied − sheets per drive is the one thing not measured; that is an identity of the power-wave definition at z0 = Re Z_p and is step 1b's assertion.
  • Step 1b (the denominator, measured in-run; queued 2026-09-05 03:00 review as §9 item 2). In the existing module, for each single drive k: P_acc,k = ½|a_k|² (1 − Σ_i |S_ik|²) from the assembled 4×4 beside the fixture's supplied − sheets accounting, asserted equal at rtol 1e-6 (the power-wave identity; both are already computed in the module, test_port_drive_superposition.py:248 and the _power_waves route); then the single-drive form of identity (iii) P_acc,k vs ½∫σ|E_k|², printed with its residual, and the ratio (superposed residual) / (mean single-drive residual) printed. Gate: the rtol 1e-6 identity only. Disposition rule, pre-stated: if it holds and the four single-drive residuals read ≈ 13%, the drive-level red is the fixture's ≈1% accounting offset against a 13× smaller denominator — the next review re-points POWER_BALANCE_BAND's drive-level use to supplied (or opens a chunk for the 1% offset itself), and the test stays red until it does; if the identity fails, the S-matrix's power-wave normalisation disagrees with the sheet accounting — known-issues entry with both numbers, stop. Executed 2026-09-05, 06:00 implementer slot — the identity holds at machine precision. tests/validation/test_port_drive_superposition.py only, three new tests on the existing superposition_case fixture, no new solve; 20260905T110305Z_POST-6.log, 1 failed, 21 passed … 102.66s (:2034), Elapsed 104 s (:2112), heavy by ceiling (timeout -k 30 600), -n 2, complex. The one failure is the deliberate step-1 red test_the_drive_level_power_identity_closes, untouched. (1b-i) green: P_acc,k = ½|a_k|²(1 − Σ_i|S_ik|²) equals supplied_k − Σ_i sheets_ik to 1.683e-15 / 0.000e+00 / 1.679e-15 / 0.000e+00 for P1–P4 against the pre-registered 1e-6 (:1924–1939) — the power-wave normalisation and the sheet accounting are one number, so "the two accountings disagree" is excluded and the 11.6% is not a normalisation story. (1b-ii) green: the superposed ccw P_acc reproduces 3.014424803e-03 W at rtol 1e-9 — same solves, same path. Printed, not asserted: the four |P_acc,k − P_vol,k|/P_acc,k read 1.303004e-01 / 1.302723e-01 / 1.300031e-01 / 1.302052e-01, mean 1.301952e-01, and the superposed 1.164806e-01 is 0.8947× that mean (:1940) — the four-port drive misses slightly less than its own single drives, so the superposition adds nothing. Negative control, ceiling first: deleting S_kk from drive k's column misses by 7.659732e-01 / 7.656687e-01 / 7.634896e-01 / 7.652279e-01, each equal to the closed form |S_kk|²/(1 − Σ_i|S_ik|²) computed from the assembled 4×4 before the assertion, against a claimed floor of 1e-3 (1000× the band); nothing above the computed value claimed. The disposition rule fires as written: the identity held and the four residuals read ≈ 13%, so the drive-level red is the fixture's ≈1%-of-supplied accounting offset read against a 13× smaller denominator. POWER_BALANCE_BAND was not touched in-slot and the test stays red; the next review is the actor. What step 1b does not settle: the ≈6.7e-05 W absolute gap common to every drive is still unexplained — it is 0.98% of supplied and 13.0% of accepted, and candidate (b) "a real un-accounted loss channel" survives at that same absolute size. Known-issues entry carries both. Review 2026-09-05 10:30 — the disposition is held for the 2026-09-06 weekly, with a recommendation. The 03:00 review listed this decision for the weekly explicitly ("a decision the dailies cannot make") before step 1b ran, and step 1b's result sharpens rather than removes the reason: re-pointing the drive-level band at supplied makes the test a restatement of WF-6 step 1's single-drive gate (0.98% of supplied, already green) and gates nothing about the superposition, whose own contribution step 1b measured at 0.8947× the single-drive mean. The recommendation this review records: (a) re-scope the drive-level test to the relative identity the data actually supports — the superposed residual against the mean single-drive residual, both computed in-run, ratio asserted ≤ 1 + CG1_RECORD_RTOL-class slack (measured 0.8947; a superposition that adds power error is what it would catch); (b) the 6.7e-05 W absolute gap becomes its own chunk with a mechanism list (sheet-loss vs volume-integral double count in the gap cells; Poynting flux through the outer wall under the natural BC; the _loss_power_w quadrature on DG0 σ) — POST-5's three-term identity is the instrument, and a fixed-h gap that is 0.98% of supplied on every drive is a systematic, not noise. The test stays red and POWER_BALANCE_BAND stays 1e-2 until the weekly rules; the known-issues entry leaves with that commit.
  • Step 2. The same on PORT-13's 32-ring-port fixture with the 16-fold quadrature weights; the C16 invariance of |B₁⁺| is the gate.
  • Done-when (§4). Both steps asserted; WF-6 step 3 and WF-7 are re-pointed to consume this entry point rather than their own sums.

docs.title: §9 item 177 — 2026-10-02 (lane 1; the 09-30 weekly's sampling rule)
docs.text:
Outcome (2026-10-02 15:00 slot): DONE — the rule implemented opt-in and gated at -n 1 / 2 / 4. All four windows Status 0, one tree.

  • Code: post.evaluation.point_owner_cells (owned candidates, int64 Allreduce(MIN) on original_cell_index, Allreduce(SUM) claim guard) and the keyword-only owner=None | "lowest_original_cell" on evaluate_vector_field_parallel; owner rides the OPS-40/55 allgather key; the legacy path is untouched (guard module 6 passed / 1 skipped at every width; C1a reproduces both logged CG1 rows).
  • Windows: W1 -n 2 20261002T200331Z_POST-8-step2-W1.log (195 s; 23 passed / 1 skipped); W2 -n 4 20261002T200654Z_POST-8-step2-W2.log (191 s); W3 -n 1 20261002T201013Z_POST-8-step2-W3.log (228 s); W4 real build 20261002T201406Z_POST-8-step2-W4-real.log (49 s; 17 passed / 5 skipped). git status --porcelain examples/ empty after W4.
  • K0: original_cell_index is an int64 ndarray covering owned + ghost cells in 0.11 (shape (223,) at -n 2, 191 owned + 32 ghosts); owned part unique, 384 = size_global. K1 / K2: CG1 ≤ 8.9e-16, N1curl ≤ 2.2e-15 (≤ 1e-12). K3: oracle incident sets 1 / 2 / 24 (vertex prediction 24 met); the rule returns the minimum 217 / 223 / 126 at all three widths, imaginary part 0. K4, K5, K6 green (K5 raises on every rank at -n 2 / 4, does not at -n 1). CK2: the legacy DG0 value at the vertex is in the incident set and is 126 (= min) at -n 2, 128 at -n 4, 131 at -n 1; at the facet 232 ≠ min at -n 4 — the legacy path's partition dependence shown on the known answer.
  • A0: 199 920 cells at every width; P1 phantom power rel 4.91e-12 / 8.93e-13 / 1.07e-11 (-n 2 / 4 / 1). A1: one owned containing cell per point at every width. A2 (the gate): max rel vs STEP1_N1CURL_SAR 1.37e-10 / 6.55e-11 / 3.03e-10 (≤ 1e-9). A3: owner-rank eval bitwise and all ranks bitwise at every width.
  • Cross-width record (not asserted): pairwise max relative difference of the 16 SARs: -n 2 vs -n 4 1.33e-10, -n 2 vs -n 1 1.66e-10, -n 4 vs -n 1 2.98e-10, all at P3 / −y (the smallest-magnitude entry class, 7.48e-9 W/kg). The printed prediction ≤ 1e-11 is missed (a negative result on a prediction, rule (e)); the asserted bound ≤ 2e-9 holds. The owner cell is the same (original index 150135 / 162464 / 142550 / 169932 at every width), so this is the solve's own width-dependent round-off at ≈ 1e-10 (P1 phantom power also moves 1e-11 across widths), not sampling.
  • C1a: 8.89e-11 (-n 2) / 5.89e-10 (-n 4) ≤ 1e-9. C1b: min |rel| vs the other width 0.1293 / 0.1485 ≥ 0.10. C1c (-n 1, printed): P1 CG1 row −3.43 / +87.8 / −4.30 / +29.8 % from the -n 2 row and −20.2 / +8.82 / −16.7 / +12.5 % from the -n 4 row (prediction ≥ 1 % from each: met). C1d: P1 +x CG1 / raw 0.881 (-n 2), 1.066 (-n 4; step 1's reading), 0.851 (-n 1). C2: owner local_to_global 85735 / 68816 / 194905 at +x for -n 2 / 4 / 1 while original_cell_index stays 150135 — even -n 1 renumbers, so local_to_global is not the input order at any width.

Drafted by a read-only Plan agent and reviewed by the 2026-10-02 10:30 daily review.

POST-8 step 2 puts the 09-30 weekly's sampling rule into the point-evaluation path, as an opt-in keyword on post.evaluation.evaluate_vector_field_parallel. The rule is gated on ans:2's named points at -n 1, -n 2 and -n 4. It also gets a known answer on a shared vertex and facet, and the CG1 route serves as the negative control. - Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy, since each ans:2 window is ≈ 2–5 min, above the 180 s standard tier. - Builds: complex, plus one cheap real-build window. - Cost: ≈ 4 measured (lane-1 median) / ≈ 50 predicted min. - Depends on: nothing; step 1 landed on 0b00091 (item 54).

The rule as ruled (§10, 09-30 weekly): "Raw point evaluation takes a deterministic owner (lowest global cell index among the cells containing the point), gated width-invariant to 1e-9 at -n 1 / 2 / 4; public comparison rows quote cell or mass averages."

Which global cell index: mesh.topology.original_cell_index, never index_map(tdim).local_to_global. - The original index is the cell's position in the input array given to create_mesh. Every birdcage mesh goes through _model_to_mesh (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:12), so that position is set by the gmsh mesh and not by the partition. - The index-map global number depends on the partition. Step 1 measured it: the same +x cell, carrying the same E digits, is global cell 85735 at -n 2 and 68816 at -n 4 (20260927T112115Z_POST-8-step1-n2.log:1918, 20260927T112501Z_POST-8-step1-n4.log:1920). The probe used local_to_global (scripts/probes/post8_pointwise_partition.py:102); do not copy that line.

Code (a src/ change; rule (c) disclosure; additive only). In src/fem_em_solver/post/evaluation.py: - New public point_owner_cells(mesh, points, comm). It returns owner_original (int64[N], identical on every rank, −1 for a point outside the mesh) and owner_local_cell (int32[N]; the local cell on the owning rank, −1 elsewhere). 1. bb_tree → compute_collisions_points → compute_colliding_cells (the existing calls, :99–101). 2. Keep only owned candidates (c < size_local). 3. local_min = the minimum original_cell_index over those, with sentinel np.iinfo(np.int64).max. 4. Reduce with the buffer-form comm.Allreduce(local_min, global_min, op=MPI.MIN). 5. The rank whose local_min == global_min != sentinel owns the point. 6. Defensive: an Allreduce(SUM) of claim counts above 1 raises on every rank. - New keyword-only owner=None on evaluate_vector_field_parallel. - The accepted values are None (the legacy path, byte for byte) and "lowest_original_cell". Anything else raises ValueError before any collective. - Under the rule, each owning rank calls function.eval only on its owned points, in the owner cell. The existing gather / scatter / bcast (:120–135) is unchanged. - owner joins the OPS-40/55 key. The (n_points, digest) allgather becomes (n_points, digest, owner), so a rank-mismatched owner raises on every rank instead of hanging. - The default stays the legacy path. Every existing caller therefore stays digit-identical by construction: ≈ 30 test modules, core/solvers.py:763, post/sar.py:354, ports/gap_voltage.py:289, and the examples. Flipping the default is adoption, which is step 3. - Export point_owner_cells from src/fem_em_solver/post/__init__.py (additive).

Module 1: tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py — a known answer, cheap, run in both builds. - Fixture: create_unit_cube(comm, 4, 4, 4), with three points: interior (0.13, 0.27, 0.61), the hex-face plane (0.5, 0.3, 0.6), and the interior vertex (0.5, 0.5, 0.5). - Oracle, independent of DolfinX collision: allgather each owned cell's original index and its four vertices. Rank 0 takes the incident set at barycentrics ≥ −1e-12 and broadcasts it. - Asserted: - (K0) original_cell_index (the owned part, allgathered) is unique, and its count equals size_global. Print its type and shape: the 0.11 API may return a per-cell-type list, in which case take [0]. - (K1) CG1 (x, 2y, 3z) under the rule meets its closed form to ≤ 1e-12 at all three points (the guard module's bound, tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py:83). - (K2) N1curl a + b × x, with a = (1, −2, 0.5) and b = (0.3, 0.1, −0.2), meets its closed form to ≤ 1e-12. - (K3) The tie-break. A DG0 scalar holds original_cell_index in each cell (owned and ghost, then scatter_forward). Under the rule, each point returns exactly the minimum over the oracle's incident set, with imaginary part 0 in complex. The oracle count is 1 at the interior point and ≥ 2 at the facet and vertex points. - (K4) Every rank holds bitwise-equal values. - (K5) If rank 0 passes owner=None while the others pass the rule, every rank raises. At -n 1 the same construction does not raise (the control). - (K6) An unknown owner string raises ValueError. - Controls: - (CK1, asserted by construction once K3's count is ≥ 2 with distinct indices): the incident set's maximum ≠ its minimum at the vertex and facet points. - (CK2): the legacy value at the vertex is a member of the incident set (asserted). That it differs from the minimum at some width is predicted and printed only. - Printed: the incident-set sizes (predicted 24 at the vertex, not asserted) and the rule's three answers. The slot compares those answers across W1–W3.

Module 2: tests/validation/test_post8_owner_rule_ans2.py — complex_only, one module-scoped fixture, width taken from comm.size. - Fixture: - sweep = build_four_port_sweep(phantom_resolution=PHANTOM_RESOLUTION_1G_RUNG), imported directly from tests.validation.test_port_birdcage_four_port and tests.validation.test_birdcage_sar_1g_rung. - _solve_driven(sweep, pid) for P1…P4, with the pids as _build_mass_averaged derives them (tests/validation/test_birdcage_sar_mass_averaged.py:232, 239–249), but without its 21 ball integrals. - Load ans:2's script by importlib, as the probe does (post8_pointwise_partition.py:77–82). Assert not ans2.RESOLUTION_OVERRIDDEN. - Use only ans2._pointwise_sar and ans2._phantom_power; never main(). - Import LOGGED_P1_ROW, LOGGED_P1_SOURCE, TRACKED_P1_POWER_W, ROW_RTOL and POWER_RTOL from the probe; never restate them. - Named points: (±CENTRE_RADIUS_M, 0, 0) and (0, ±CENTRE_RADIUS_M, 0), in ans:2's order (02_birdcage_coil_driven_sar_10MHz.py:747–755). - Anchors (asserted): - (A0) Cells == ONE_GRAM_RUNG_CELL_RECORD 199 920 exactly (n2 log :1901, n4 log :1903). P1 phantom power is within POWER_RTOL 1e-9 of TRACKED_P1_POWER_W; measured 4.80e-12 / 6.62e-14 (:1913 / :1915). - (A1) Each named point has exactly one owned containing cell globally (Allreduce SUM == 1; n2 log :1916 / 1930 / 1944 / 1958). - (A2) The gate. The 16 raw N1curl SARs σ|E|²/(2ρ) (with SALINE_SIGMA and PHANTOM_RHO_KG_PER_M3, as _pointwise_sar uses them), taken from evaluate_vector_field_parallel(e_complex, points, comm, owner="lowest_original_cell"), each lie within 1e-9 relative of STEP1_N1CURL_SAR. That record is restated with its log citation: - Each entry is the mean of the -n 2 print (n2 log :1917–1965) and the -n 4 print (n4 log :1919–1967). The two prints agree in 8 of 16 entries and differ by one unit in the 10th figure in the other 8. - Comparand budget ≤ 5e-10. Predicted measured ≤ 5e-10 at every width. - The -n 2 values (+x / +y / −x / −y): - P1: 5.514140460e-07, 8.056036637e-09, 6.147781056e-08, 1.000625322e-08; - P2: 5.413193615e-09, 5.365427637e-07, 7.538407567e-09, 6.062393526e-08; - P3: 6.887651145e-08, 7.937373888e-09, 5.038331027e-07, 7.475028492e-09; - P4: 9.595073748e-09, 6.651644441e-08, 9.294666807e-09, 4.980486020e-07. - Print with .17e: the 16 SARs and the E components, each point's owner original_cell_index and its local_to_global. - After W3 the slot records the pairwise maximum relative difference across the three logs, predicted ≤ 1e-11, as a record that is not asserted. Each window's assertion bounds that pairwise difference at ≤ 2e-9 through the common comparand; the docstring says so. - (A3) On the owning rank the rule's value equals e_complex.eval(x, [owner_local_cell]) bitwise, and every rank holds the same 16 values bitwise. - Negative control, the CG1 route (ans2._pointwise_sar on the same solves, which interpolates to CG1 and then uses the default owner=None): - (C1a, asserted, at -n 2 / -n 4 only): the P1 CG1 row reproduces LOGGED_P1_ROW[width] to ROW_RTOL 1e-9; measured 8.94e-11 / 4.95e-10 (n2 :1907, n4 :1909). This is also the check that the default path did not move. - (C1b, asserted, at -n 2 / -n 4): the same row against the other width's logged row has minimum |rel| ≥ 0.10. Measured −17.35 / −42.04 / −12.93 / −13.36 % (n2 :1908) and +20.99 / +72.54 / +14.85 / +15.42 % (n4 :1910). The minimum is 0.1293, i.e. 1.29e8× the 1e-9 the rule is held to. - (C1c, predicted, printed, -n 1): no logged -n 1 CG1 row exists. Print it beside both logged rows; predicted ≥ 1 % from each. - (C1d, printed): the CG1 / raw ratio per (point, drive). Step 1 read 0.881 / 1.066 at P1 +x. - (C2, predicted, printed): the owner's local_to_global differs across widths, while its original_cell_index does not.

Windows. Foreground, Bash timeout: 660000, each harness call bare and whole, pytest -s, no pytest -k selection, no pipes. Run W1 → W4 in that order. - Basis: step 1's 213 s (-n 2) and 174 s (-n 4) windows (n2 :2016, n4 :2018). Those included the 21 ball integrals this module skips. The driven solves take ≈ 17–21 s each and the mesh 36 s. - W1 (-n 2), predicted ≈ 170 s:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh POST-8-step2-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py tests/validation/test_post8_owner_rule_ans2.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W2 (-n 4), predicted ≈ 140 s: the same command with -n 4, labelled POST-8-step2-W2. - W3 (-n 1), unmeasured, predicted ≈ 260 s: the same command with -n 1, labelled POST-8-step2-W3. - W4, the real-build re-gate under rule (c), predicted ≈ 30 s:

scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh POST-8-step2-W4-real "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py tests/post/test_point_owner_rule.py -v -s --tb=short'" - tests/post/test_evaluation_collective_guard.py is evaluation.py's pre-existing gate (OPS-40/55; 6 passed / 1 skipped complex, 20260921T111802Z_OPS-55-callers-complex.log:260–272). - After W4, run git status --porcelain examples/ as its own call. It must be empty.

Traps: - Use the buffer-form Allreduce on int64 with MPI.MIN. The lowercase allreduce compares objects. Never decide ownership rank-locally. - Filter to owned cells: create_unit_cube ghosts by default, and bb_tree may include ghost cells. - Read original_cell_index's shape in-container (K0 prints it). - The rule is collective, which is why owner rides the digest allgather. Raise on every rank (OPS-40). - Loading ans:2 also loads EX-34's script and patches build_four_port_sweep inside the mass-averaged module. Import the builder directly, and never call ans2.main(): it writes metrics.json, COMPARISON.md and the private comparison. - cell_tags.values and assemble_scalar are rank-local. _phantom_power → mean_sar already reduces, so do not re-sum. - Use the complex build. The DG0 index field is complex there: compare .real and assert .imag == 0. - Rule (i): no edit to either module after its last window. Rule (g): -s. - A W3 kill at 590 s is not a result. Run pgrep -c python3 first, and never lengthen the timeout. - If the oracle's incident set disagrees with DolfinX's at the vertex, print both: that is a collision-tolerance finding. Never tune the 1e-12.

Scope (step 3, not queued here): - adoption at the census sites (ans:2's _pointwise_sar, post/sar.py:354, phantom_fields.py:163 and the 18 heuristic candidates); - flipping the default; - classifying the census; - re-issuing ans:2's Row 1 as a cell or mass average; - re-reading the 09-26 ANS-2 "within 6.3 %", which keeps its -n 4-only caveat.

No band moves, and no integral is touched.

Status it can move: - §7 POST-8 stays 🟡. Its state line gains "step 2 done: the rule implemented opt-in and gated at -n 1 / 2 / 4", and step 3 becomes queueable. - The 2026-09-27 known-issues entry (known-issues.md:573–576) stays OPEN; its "Verified at" row gains step 2's reading. - The review that queues step 3 (which writes "→ ✅") amends the Done-when under rule (j) to name -n 1 / 2 / 4 and the averaged public Row 1.

Negative result: report and stop, never widen a bound. - (A2) misses at -n 2 / -n 4 with A0 / A1 green: step 1's reading is contradicted. Annotate the known-issues Cause row, park on attempt/*, and mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)). - (A2) misses at -n 1 only: record it and mark BLOCKED with W1 / W2 green; the weekly re-poses the -n 1 clause. - (A0) or (A1) fails: the mesh depends on the width. Open a new known-issues entry and stop. - K1–K3 red: revert src/ and park. - The guard module or W4 red: the legacy path moved. Revert src/ and stop. - C1a fails: the fixture drifted. Report it and stop. - W3 killed: W1 / W2 stand. Mark BLOCKED, with the unblock condition "re-brief -n 1 on P1 only". - There is no PREDICTED RED line.

The rule is asserted to be a bitwise no-op at single-incidence probes and width-invariant at -n 1 / 2 / 4, and the edited modules plus their downstream gates are re-run green. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: - W1: heavy by ceiling (-n 2, 400 s), predicted ≈ 110 s. docs.text:

At -n 1, coil-phantom (R) is printed only. - This is an identity on the same solve, not a band, and it is the only valid test of "the record moved": the docstring digits predate the 0.11 image (see "The sites"). The edited module's printed metric is set beside the docstring record for information only. - (R) can be red only at a multi-incidence probe whose owner cell differs from the legacy cell at that width. - (O) Coil-phantom only. - At -n 2, rank 0 writes /workspace/logs/post8/step3b-ii-t2-n2.npz (gitignored) with the 27 + 1 owner original indices (the probes plus V), n_incident, and the 27 owner-path b_dg0 samples, then Barrier. - At -n 4 / -n 1 the module loads it, with pytest.fail if it is missing, never a recompute. Predicted: ≤ 1e-6. No band is set on it. - (V) The lexicographically smallest vertex of centerline probe 0's owner cell (the pattern of t1's _vertex_v, on b_dg0's mesh), with its coordinates shared by Allreduce SUM.

Negative controls. - (N0), asserted (rule (e)): at V, n_incident ≥ N0_MIN_INCIDENT (4), and max/min |B_dg0| over V's incident cells > 1 + N0_SPREAD_FLOOR. The values come from each rank's _owned_incident_cells evaluated in-cell, then allgather. - This shows a cell choice at a shared vertex moves the DG0 sample, so (O) has teeth. - Predicted, printed: > 1.01. Degree-1 curl A is cell-wise constant, and the module docstring's 3.03× CG1 swing is that jump averaged. - (N1), printed: the legacy cell at V against the owner, at every width.

Prediction for (S) / (R), printed, not asserted. The centerline jump ratio scatters 0.341 % across widths, and the mirror metric 0.022 % (:99–102). Both are ≥ 10⁴ × the LU floor. Windows. Each runs in the foreground with Bash timeout: 660000 and -s, and each harness call is the whole bare Bash command. Before each window, docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 must read 0. Traps already paid for. - Rule (i): an edit after W1 starts means W1–W4 again. - Use -s and container timeout -k 30. A kill is not a result: run pgrep -c python3 first, then at 0 run the rubric cache sweep as POST-8-step3b-ii-t2-cache-sweep. New known-issues entry. - (N0) red: the item parks for a re-pose. - Status 124: not a result; park with the measured time.
