docs.title: §9 item 277 — 2026-10-06 (lane 2, TH-5 step 2a)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-06 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §9 rule (5) lane 2, the weekly's enumerated target (PROJECT_PLAN §10, "Lane 1 and lane 2, targets for the daily": "TH-5 2a / 2b as re-posed 09-30"); the re-pose is in docs/planning/plan-archive.md (grep step 2 — re-posed in two parts). No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved here. The [0.3, 0.7] band and the sign clause are the weekly's; every other number is imported by name or labelled predicted.

TH-5 step 2a — the first-order ABC on PORT-1's two-torus box: a banked negative. Three solves at PORT-1's 3b-xi paddings W = 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.12 m, with the PEC wall replaced by the first-order ABC (Jin 3e §9.2 (9.44) at s = 1; plane-wave reflection (9.48); the curved-boundary form §9.1.2 (9.21); this file's 1b-0 Γ_sph). At 10 MHz the box sits at k₀·half-width ≈ 0.022–0.035 (k₀ = 0.20958 rad/m), where |Γ_sph| = 1/√(1 + 4x⁴) ≈ 1 − 2e-6. There the ABC is a reflector, equal to the natural (magnetic) wall to O(k₀R). The sphere model's static reaction fields (+2 under PEC, −1 under a magnetic wall; entry step-2 note) predict that the box term flips sign and halves. The item measures that, and banks the entry's original "≥ 5× fall" as unreachable.

  • Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy (one window ≈ 5–6 min, over standard's 180 s), complex build, -n 2 (PORT-1 / GEO-4's width). Class: lane-2 solve. Cost: ≈ 7 measured (the weekly's lane median) / ≈ 40 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + W1 ≈ 6 + W2 ≈ 1 + ≈ 6 spare. If W1 is not green by minute 40, park (rule (d)).
  • Depends on: nothing. Attempt: 1 of 4. No src/ edit: the ABC term exists (fem_em_solver.core.boundary_terms.first_order_abc_term, step 1a), and the solver takes it through TimeHarmonicSolver.solve(extra_bilinear_terms=…) (core/time_harmonic.py:400, 556–559, PORT-9's hook). No re-gate under rule (c).

Settled from the code (read before designing). - The box term, as the entry defines it. The §7 entry's step 2 says "the box term D∞", and its step-2 note says "the box term would flip sign and about halve". Both mean B(W) = deficit(W) − D∞, where D∞ is the free-exponent extrapolated box-free deficit. Read here (for the review to ratify): the weekly's "|D∞^ABC| / |D∞^PEC|" is the ratio of box terms, r(W) = |B^ABC(W)| / |B^PEC(W)|, and the sphere model's 0.5 is that ratio. Under the same model the extrapolated box-free deficits would agree (ratio ≈ 1), so the literal reading contradicts its own 0.5. - PEC leg: no new solve beyond the premise. PORT1_PADDING_RUNGS_M (0.08, 0.10, 0.12) / PORT1_PADDING_DEFICITS_PP (−8.0324, −5.0256, −3.2733) and _free_exponent_fit (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:436–440) give D∞ = +1.6934077797 pp, p = 1.6574 (GEO-4 (A0), bitwise the probe, docs/planning/chunks/GEO-4.md:11). Hence B^PEC = −9.7258 / −6.7190 / −4.9667 pp at the three rungs. The common reference is D∞^PEC: the mesh, drive and discretisation are shared per rung, so the discretisation part of the deficit cancels in B. - Fixture. MeshGenerator.two_torus_domain returns (msh, cell_tags, facet_tags), and facet tag 1 is the outer boundary (io/mesh.py:1353–1354). Deficit = 100·(Im Z₂₁ / ωM₁₂ − 1) on one driven column (tag 1), as in GEO-4's gate_deficits_pp (tests/validation/test_geo4_box_padding_heuristic.py:236–249). The reaction is Z = −∫_tag E·J / (I_d I_t) (test_port_reaction_impedance.py:227–239). - _solve_reaction_z hard-codes boundary_condition="pec_zero_tangential_a" and takes no surface terms (test_port_reaction_impedance.py:261–317). Do not add a kwarg to it: that edits PORT-1's gated module and buys its re-gate. Instead, copy its mesh / current / solve / _reaction lines into the new module as _solve_z_column(padding, wall) with wall ∈ {"pec", "natural", "abc"}, where "abc" = boundary_condition="natural" plus extra_bilinear_terms=[first_order_abc_term(msh, facet_tags, 1, OMEGA)]. Import the constants (MAJOR_RADIUS, MINOR_RADIUS, SEPARATION, H_FAR, H_WIRE, CURRENT_A, TORUS_TAGS, OMEGA, FREQUENCY_HZ), _azimuthal_current_density, _tag_volume, _reaction and mutual_inductance. Skip the step-2f energy bookkeeping. - The volume form's scaling matches the ABC term's. The solver assembles (1/μᵣ)∫∇×u·∇×v̄ − k₀²∫ε_c u·v̄ with load −jωμ₀∫J′·v̄ (time_harmonic.py:520–549). That is the convention boundary_terms.py:3–10 assumes (γ = +jk₀).

New test module tests/validation/test_th5_abc_two_torus.py (tests only). One module-scoped fixture runs five solves: PEC at 0.08 m (premise), ABC at 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.12 m, and natural at 0.08 m (control). @complex_only on every solve node.

Anchors (asserted). - (P0) Premise. The copied solver at W = 0.08 m under PEC reproduces GEO-4's 0.11-image rung −8.0404 pp within P0_BAND_PP (0.05 pp, imported from test_geo4_box_padding_heuristic.py). This proves the copy is the fixture. - (S) Sign (the weekly's clause). B^ABC(W) = deficit^ABC(W) − D∞^PEC > 0 at all three rungs, against B^PEC(W) < 0. Predicted ≈ +4.86 / +3.36 / +2.48 pp. - (R) Ratio (the weekly's band). |B^ABC(W)| / |B^PEC(W)| ∈ [0.3, 0.7] at all three rungs; the sphere model gives 0.5. Predicted ABC deficits (r = 0.5): +6.556 / +5.053 / +4.177 pp. The band maps to [4.611, 8.501] / [3.709, 6.397] / [3.183, 5.170] pp. - (E) The ABC term is in the matrix (sign asserted). Under ABC, Re Z₁₁ > 0 (the boundary absorbs). Under PEC, |Re Z₂₁| ≤ 1e-9·|Z₂₁| (PORT-1's structural-zero test, IDENTITY_TOLERANCE). - Printed beside it, not asserted: the Galerkin power identity Re Z₁₁·I₁² = ∮_{tag 1}|n × E_h|² ds / η₀. It is the imaginary part of the weak form at v = E_h; ∫_tag E·J = ∫E·J′ still holds under the ABC because n × ∇q = 0 for q ∈ CG1 ∩ H¹₀. Relative residual predicted ≤ 1e-6. - Re Z₁₁ itself is predicted at ≈ 1e-4–5e-3 Ω and printed: the free-space loop R_rad of 9.7e-7 Ω times the near-field factor ≈ 1 + 1/(k₀R)² ≈ 800–2 000. Here the ABC acts as a resistive η₀ wall on the near field.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) PEC in the ABC's place — asserted. A broken ABC run that leaves the Dirichlet set on, or drops the term into a PEC solve, returns the PEC deficit. (S) separates the two by |B^ABC − B^PEC| ≈ 14.6 pp at 0.08 m (predicted), against a rung precision of 5e-5 pp. Asserted through (S) and (P0) on the same mesh. - (c2) Conjugated γ — asserted via (E). γ = −jk₀ makes the boundary a source and gives Re Z₁₁ < 0 (the 1b trap: |Γ(z = −1)| = 19.76). (E)'s sign catches it. - (c3) Natural wall at 0.08 m — predicted, printed only. |deficit^ABC − deficit^NAT| is predicted ≤ 0.05·|B^PEC(0.08)| ≈ 0.5 pp (expected ≈ (k₀R)²·|B| ≈ 0.01 pp). It shows that the ABC is the magnetic wall here. It is not step 2b's combination and gates nothing.

Printed (not asserted). - Cell counts per rung (0.08 m: 119 533 on the 0.11 image, GEO-4.md:13), per-solve seconds, and the complex Z₂₁ and Z₁₁. - The free-exponent fit through the three ABC deficits (_free_exponent_fit): D∞^ABC, p^ABC, and |D∞^ABC − D∞^PEC|, predicted ≈ 0 under the sphere model. The fit may fail if the ABC ladder is not monotone; if so, print the failure. - The entry's original bar, |B^ABC| ≤ |B^PEC|/5. (R)'s lower bound 0.3 > 0.2 makes it false by construction: that is the banked negative.

Windows. Foreground; each harness call bare and whole; Bash timeout: 660000; -s; node IDs only, never -k; tests/environment first; no pipe or redirect (the window is under 10 min, so no durable capture). - W1 (heavy). Predicted ≈ 330 s, bracket 250–450 s: environment ≈ 45 s plus five mesh-and-solves. The rung costs come from GEO-4 at 43 / ≈ 52 / ≈ 70 s for the 0.08 / 0.10–0.11 / 0.12–0.14 m rungs (20261003T035018Z_GEO-4-W1.log: 226 s for three solves). scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh TH-5-step2a-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_th5_abc_two_torus.py -v -s --tb=short'" - W2 (real build: collection and skips, ≈ 15 s). scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh TH-5-step2a-W2 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 1 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_th5_abc_two_torus.py -v -s --tb=short'"

Traps already paid for. - Signed deficits and signed box terms (GEO-4). Never compose relative percents. C is negative in the commissioning convention. (S) is on signed B; (R) is on magnitudes. - project_source stays at its default, True (CG1 ∩ H¹₀, pinned exterior): the projection every PEC rung was measured with. "matched" would unpin the exterior under the natural mode and change the drive between the walls. - A conjugated γ is a source (boundary_terms.py:10–11). Use first_order_abc_term as it is; never re-derive γ. - The ABC needs boundary_condition="natural". Under PEC the Dirichlet rows overwrite it silently (c1). - Rank-safety. Allreduce every assemble_scalar (the reaction and the ∮|n × E|² integral). Take global counts via index_map(…).size_global. Print on rank 0. - Complex build. No ufl.max_value and no ordering on complex operands. The boundary integral is ufl.inner(ufl.cross(n, E), ufl.cross(n, E)), with the real part taken after the allreduce. Pin metadata={"quadrature_degree": …} on any SpatialCoordinate-bearing facet integral (POST-5). - A kill at 590 s is not a result. Run pgrep -c python3 in the container first, and sweep orphan .c files only when it reads 0. Never lengthen the timeout or change -n. Status 124 is a finding. - Rule (i): no edit to the new module after its last green window. Write ≈, never ~, in tracked Markdown.

Scope. - Covered: one fixture (PORT-1's two-torus, d = 0.04 m, 10 MHz, degree 1, -n 2), with the first-order ABC on the whole outer box at three paddings. - Not this item: step 2b (the ⅓ PEC + ⅔ natural mixed wall, its weights and its ≤ |B^PEC| / 5 gate); the §2.1 boundary-model line; any second-order ABC or PML; any birdcage or open-boundary figure; any statement about larger boxes (k₀R ≳ π belongs to 1b). PORT-1's ✅ and GEO-4's heuristic are untouched.

Status it can move. No glyph: TH-5 stays 🟡. Its Done-when as re-posed 09-30 is ✅ on 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b and the §2.1 line. On green, the §7 row gains a step-2a record sentence (the B^ABC signs and r(W) at three rungs, the fit's D∞^ABC, elapsed time). The §10 lane-2 entry marks 2a DONE, and 2b becomes the lane's next step with the measured ratio beside the sphere model's.

Negative result. In every case: report the measurement, park on attempt/TH-5-step2a-*, mark item 277 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)), and journal it in attempts.md. No band moves. - (P0) red: the copied solver is not the fixture. Stop before reading (S) / (R). - (E) red (Re Z₁₁ ≤ 0 under ABC): the term did not enter a, or entered with the wrong sign. Stop: this is a code defect, not a physics reading. - (S) red (B^ABC < 0 at any rung) with (E) green: the box does not behave as a magnetic wall. That contradicts 1b-0's closed form at x → 0; a finding for the weekly. - (R) red with (S) green: the cube departs from the sphere model, recorded as that (the weekly's own disposition in the plan-archive re-pose). The measured r(W) goes into the §7 row as the 2a record. The weekly decides whether 2a stands closed on the record, and re-derives 2b's weights from it. - W1 killed or over 450 s: BLOCKED without a result. The review shrinks the case (drop (c3), or split the rungs over two windows).

No PREDICTED RED: line. The asserted clauses (P0, S, R, E) are all predicted green. The banked negative is the original ≥ 5× bar, which is printed and never asserted.

Outcome (2026-10-07 00:00 slot, attempt 1 of 4): 🚫 BLOCKED — (R) red with (S) green. (P0) −8.0404 pp (|Δ| 0.0080); (E) Re Z₁₁ > 0 at all rungs; (S) B^ABC +4.7133 / +2.3965 / +1.1256 pp; (R) r(W) = 0.4846 / 0.3567 / 0.2266 against [0.3, 0.7], red at 0.12 m. 20261007T052330Z_TH-5-step2a-W1.log (313.7 s) on attempt/TH-5-step2a-20261007T052330Z. Recorded in the §7 row; the weekly rules on 2a and on 2b's weights.

docs.title: §9 item 290 — 2026-10-06 (lane 2)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-06 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §9 rule (5) lane 2, the weekly's enumerated target (PROJECT_PLAN §10, "Lane 1 and lane 2, targets for the daily": "TH-5 2a / 2b as re-posed 09-30"); the re-pose text is in docs/planning/plan-archive.md (grep step 2 — re-posed in two parts): "2b (the mixed wall): the ⅓ PEC + ⅔ natural-wall combination, weights from the sphere model's +2 / −1 reaction fields and stated before the run — asserted, its box term ≤ |D∞^PEC| / 5 at the smallest padding; red ⇒ the cube's weights differ, a record." No band, tolerance, Done-when or validation target is set or moved here. The ⅓ / ⅔ weights and the ÷ 5 bar are the weekly's; every other number is imported by name or labelled predicted.

TH-5 step 2b — the mixed wall on PORT-1's two-torus box. Two solves at PORT-1's smallest 3b-xi padding W = 0.08 m (PEC, the premise; natural, the measurement), and two printed natural rungs at 0.10 / 0.12 m. The mixed impedance is the post-solve combination Z^mix = ⅓ Z^PEC + ⅔ Z^NAT (the §7 entry's "mixed average", PROJECT_PLAN §7 TH-5 entry, step-2 note ≈ line 2441). It is not a boundary condition and not a face split.

  • Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy (W1 predicted ≈ 230 s, above standard's 180 s), complex build, -n 2 (PORT-1 / GEO-4's width). Class: lane-2 solve. Cost: ≈ 7 measured (lane-2 median) / ≈ 35 predicted min: 15 fixed + ≈ 10 code + W1 ≈ 4 + W2 ≈ 1 + ≈ 5 spare. If W1 is not green by minute 40, park (rule (d)).
  • Depends on: nothing. Step 2b carries its own premise (P0) and its own natural solve; it does not need item 277's ABC term or its result. Code source, deterministic: if tests/validation/test_th5_abc_two_torus.py is on main with _solve_z_column(padding, wall), import it (no edit to that module, rule (i)); otherwise write the copy item 277's brief specifies (this file, §9 item 277, "Settled from the code", the _solve_z_column bullet), restricted to wall ∈ {"pec", "natural"}, into the new module. Either path is proven to be the fixture by (P0). Its effect on the glyph needs 277 (see "Status it can move"). Attempt: 1 of 4. No src/ edit; no re-gate under rule (c).

The anchor — the sphere model's reaction weights (stated before the run). Take a magnetic dipole m at the centre of a sphere of radius R, quasi-static (k₀R ≈ 0.03–0.04 here; 1b-0's |Γ_sph| = 1/√(1 + 4x⁴) → 1). The uniform interior reaction field that cancels B_r at r = R (PEC) is −2m/(4πR³); the one that cancels H_θ (magnetic / natural wall) is +m/(4πR³). For a general l-pole the two coefficients are (l + 1)/l and −1 (interior potential C r^l P_l against the source A r^{−(l+1)} P_l, with ∂_r Φ = 0 vs Φ = 0 at R). Hence on the l = 1 term B^NAT = −½ B^PEC (the §7 entry's "+2/R³ under PEC and −1/R³ under a magnetic wall", ≈ line 2435), and the weights wPEC = ⅓, w_NAT = ⅔ (2w_PE − wAT = 0, w_PEC + w_NAT = 1) cancelt. The residual for l ≥ 2 is (1 − l)/(3l) of each pole's PEC term. The loops sit ±d/2 = ±0.02 m off-centre and a/R ≈ 0.36, so a residual of a few percent of |B^PEC| is expected, plus the cube's departure from a sphere, which has no closed form. Dipole-field form: Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics 3e §5.6 — from memory, not held in the repo; the derivation above is two lines, and the executor may check it in numpy beside the run (printed only).

Settled from the code and the records (read before designing). - Deficit and box term, as item 277 defines them (the 03:00 review's ruling on item 277: the weekly's "D∞" ratio is a ratio of box terms). d^X(W) = 100·(Im Z₂₁^X / ωM₁₂ − 1) pp on one driven column (tag 1), GEO-4's gate_deficits_pp form (tests/validation/test_geo4_box_padding_heuristic.py:236–249). B^X(W) = d^X(W) − D∞, with D∞ = D∞^PEC = +1.6934077797 pp from _free_exponent_fit(PORT1_PADDING_RUNGS_M, PORT1_PADDING_DEFICITS_PP) (src/fem_em_solver/io/mesh.py:436–440; GEO-4 (A0)). Because the weights sum to 1, B^mix = ⅓ B^PEC + ⅔ B^NAT = d^mix − D∞, and d^mix is the deficit of Z^mix (the same ωM₁₂ denominator, so linear). - The bar, read as 277 reads D∞: |B^mix(0.08)| ≤ |B^PEC(0.08)| / 5, with both from this window's solves. Predicted B^PEC(0.08) = −8.0404 − 1.6934 = −9.7338 pp (20261003T035018Z_GEO-4-W1.log:294; GEO-4 (C1) measured 9.7338), so the bar is ≈ 1.947 pp. Algebra: B^mix = B^PEC(⅓ − ⅔r) with r = |B^NAT| / |B^PEC|, so the bar is met iff r ∈ [0.2, 0.8]; item 277's (R) band [0.3, 0.7] lies inside it. Literal reading, printed only: |D∞^PEC| / 5 = 0.3387 pp, met iff r ∈ [0.448, 0.552] (a question for the review). - Fixture. MeshGenerator.two_torus_domain returns (msh, cell_tags, facet_tags); facet tag 1 is the outer boundary (io/mesh.py:1353–1354). The natural wall is boundary_condition="natural" with no surface term: no Dirichlet rows, no extra_bilinear_terms. Constants and helpers come from tests/validation/test_port_reaction_impedance.py (MAJOR_RADIUS 0.04, SEPARATION 0.04, H_FAR 0.03, FREQUENCY_HZ 10 MHz, OMEGA, TORUS_TAGS, CURRENT_A, _azimuthal_current_density, _reaction, mutual_inductance, IDENTITY_TOLERANCE = 1e-9 at :192). _solve_reaction_z hard-codes PEC (:316): do not add a kwarg to it (that edits PORT-1's gated module). - One mesh per padding, both walls on it. At 0.08 m build the mesh once and solve PEC and natural on it, so the discretisation part of the deficit is shared and cancels in B.

New test module tests/validation/test_th5_mixed_wall_two_torus.py (tests only). Constants at module top, before any solve: W_PEC = 1.0 / 3.0, W_NAT = 2.0 / 3.0, MIX_BAR_DIVISOR = 5.0 (the weekly's). One module-scoped fixture runs four solves: PEC and natural at 0.08 m, and natural at 0.10 and 0.12 m. @complex_only on every solve node.

Anchors (asserted). - (P0) Premise. The PEC solve at 0.08 m reproduces P0_RUNG_PP (−8.0324 pp) within P0_BAND_PP (0.05 pp), both imported from test_geo4_box_padding_heuristic.py. This is exactly GEO-4's premise (measured there: −8.0404, |Δ| 0.0080). - (E) Lossless identity. Under both walls |Re Z₂₁| ≤ IDENTITY_TOLERANCE·|Z₂₁|. There is no loss term, so the system is real up to the j of the load; GEO-4 printed Re Z = 0.000000e+00 under PEC (:290). - (S) Sign flip of the natural wall. B^NAT(0.08) > 0 against B^PEC(0.08) < 0. Predicted d^NAT(0.08) ≈ +6.56 pp at r = 0.5 (range +3.64 … +9.48 for r ∈ [0.2, 0.8]). - (M) The weekly's gate. |B^mix(0.08)| ≤ |B^PEC(0.08)| / MIX_BAR_DIVISOR. Predicted ≈ 0 (sphere model), and ≤ ≈ 1.3 pp across 277's band; the bar is ≈ 1.947 pp.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) Wall not switched — asserted via (S). A run that leaves the Dirichlet set on returns d^NAT = d^PEC bitwise and B^mix = B^PEC, missing (M) by exactly 5× (the ceiling, by construction). (S) separates the two by |B^NAT − B^PEC| ≈ 14.6 pp (predicted) against a rung precision of ≈ 5e-5 pp. Also assert that d^NAT(0.08) and d^PEC(0.08) differ by more than P0_BAND_PP. - (c2) Swapped weights — asserted, conditional on (M) green. ⅔ PEC + ⅓ NAT gives B^swap = B^PEC(⅔ − ⅓r); assert |B^swap(0.08)| > the bar. Ceiling computed: |B^swap| / bar = 5(⅔ − ⅓r) = 2.5 at r = 0.5, and 3.0 … 2.0 across r ∈ [0.2, 0.8]. So any r that passes (M) makes (c2) miss by ≥ 2.0×: the weights discriminate, not any mixture passes. Equal weights (½, ½) miss by only 1.25× at r = 0.5: printed, not asserted.

Printed (not asserted). - Cell counts per rung (0.08 m: 119 533 on the 0.11 image), per-solve seconds, complex Z₂₁ and Z₁₁ per wall, and the reaction/energy residual per solve. - r_NAT(W) and B^mix(W) at 0.10 / 0.12 m against B^PEC from the fit (−6.7190 / −4.9667 pp; labelled fit-referenced, since no PEC solve runs there). - The weights that would zero B^mix on this cube, w_PEC* = r/(1 + r), beside ⅓; and the literal-reading margin, |B^mix| against 0.3387 pp. - If item 277 has landed: its (c3) natural deficit at 0.08 m beside this one (it should agree to print precision: same code, same mesh recipe).

Windows. The PML design constants below (thickness, grading order, the two design reflections) are the item's fixture parameters, stated before the run. The read the bar is applied to is a question for the review (For the review, 1), because at step 1a's own read the bar sits under that read's floor.

The anchor in Jin (cited from the converted text; the equation bodies are not in it). INDEX.md lists only section titles, and states that equations are placeholders [eq (n)] numbered as in print (docs/references/jin-fem-3e/INDEX.md:3–6). The PML is §9.6, 09_absorbing-boundary-conditions.md:761–1209: - §9.6.1 (9.133) (:877–881): the metal-backed PML with a constant stretch s = s′ − js″. Its reflection is "reduced systematically by increasing the value of s″L", with |R| = exp(−2κ₂ s″ L cosθ) (the form the prose describes, assuming κ₂ is real). - §9.6.4 (9.165) (:1039–1043): the polynomial profile of s_z across N layers, "where m can be 0, 1, 2, or 3", with δ_max "the maximum loss tangent" (:1047). - (9.166) / (9.167) (:1045–1049): Jin's discrete R^TM / R^TE of the N-layer PML, computed by the 1D FEM of §3.4. They are not closed forms. - §9.6.2 (9.152)–(9.154) (:961–973): the anisotropic absorber Λ. - §9.6.3 (9.157) (:993–995): the FE vector wave equation with Λ. - :1027 is the item's premise: "Although the PML interface is reflectionless in the continuum space, this is not the case in the discretized space [41]."

The graded closed form is (9.133) with s″L replaced by its integral over (9.165)'s profile. For s(ξ) = 1 − j s″_max (ξ/d)^m on 0 < ξ < d, PEC-backed, e^{+jωt}, θ = 0:

docs.title: §9 item 644 — 2026-10-25 (§9 rule (5) lane 2, TH-5 step 3c: the graded PML's angular law at 45°, on the closed leg)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-25 18:00 daily review (fact sheet: the step 3b module, the Γ_c function and the angle table). Lane 2's anchor is a closed form (Jin 3e, cited below) at an imported band; no band, tolerance, record or Done-when is set or moved. Step 3b's own scope said "one angle … Not closed: other angles or a sweep in θ" (:593 of this file).

Why 45° and why the closed leg. At step 3b's absorbing design (R(0) = R_ABSORB = 1e-6), |Γ_c(θ)| = R(0)^{cos θ} sits below PML_REFLECTION_BAR (1e-4) at every angle under 60° (5.7e-5 at 45°, 6.4e-6 at 30°), so a run returning Γ = 0 would pass (the trap step 3 named: "at R_ABSORB, Γ_c is invisible under the discretisation term", :465). On step 3's closed leg (R_CLOSED = 1e-3, S_CLOSED, test_th5_pml_reflection.py:59, :61), |Γ_c(45°)| = (1e-3)^{0.7071} ≈ 7.6e-3 = 76× the bar, and its phase −2k₀ cos θ d (d = 1.5 λ₀) is not a multiple of π, so Γ_c is complex. 30° is excluded: TE20 is exactly at cut-off on that guide (k_c2 = 2k₀ sin 30° = k₀). 75° is excluded: (Cabc)'s ceiling there is 21, under CABC_RATIO_BAR, and λ_g = 3.9 m is 4× the 1 m fit window. 45° is clean: a = λ₀/√2 ≈ 0.707 m, β = k₀/√2 ≈ 4.443 rad/m, λ_g ≈ 1.414 m, TE20 evanescent (k_c2 = 2√2 π > k₀).

The anchor. pml_reflection_pec_backed(S_CLOSED, PML_D, PML_M, K0, cos_theta=cos 45°) (src/fem_em_solver/core/boundary_terms.py:107–119): Γ_c = −e^{−2jk₀ cos θ d}·exp(−2k₀ cos θ s_max d/(m + 1)), Jin 3e §9.6.1 eq. (9.133) integrated over the §9.6.4 profile (9.165) — the same citation as step 3b (the operator's print-copy check, dashboard item 0, still stands). Asserted: - (Gc45) | |Γ_c(45°)| / |Γ_c(0)|^{cos 45°} − 1 | ≤ IDENTITY_TOLERANCE (imported from test_port_reaction_impedance, as step 3b does), and | |Γ_c(45°)| − R_CLOSED^{cos 45°} | ≤ 1e-12·R_CLOSED^{cos 45°}. - (B45) degree 2, λ₀/40, PML at S_CLOSED, read at k_fit (step 3b's read, β scanned ±5e-3 relative, 21 points, scan_interior asserted): |Γ_h − Γ_c(45°)| ≤ PML_REFLECTION_BAR.

The negative control (asserted, ceiling computed). (Law) the normal-incidence law — the reflection a PML that ignored the angle would give on this leg, Γ_c(cos θ = 1) = −e^{−2jk₀d}·R_CLOSED = −1e-3 (d = 1.5 λ₀) — misses: |Γ_h − Γ_c(cos θ = 1)| > 10 × PML_REFLECTION_BAR. Ceiling: |Γ_c(45°) − Γ_c(0)| ≥ 7.6e-3 − 1e-3 = 6.6e-3 = 66× the bar, so the 10× bar has ≥ 6.6× margin. Also printed (not asserted): the 60° law on this leg, |Γ_h − Γ_c(cos 60°)| (|Γ_c(60°)| = 3.16e-2). (Cabc) is printed only: at 45° on the closed leg its ceiling is |Γ_ABC|/|Γ_c| = 0.1716/7.6e-3 ≈ 22.6, under CABC_RATIO_BAR by construction — the step-3b control does not transfer to this leg, and the brief does not pretend it does. docs.text: Binds over the brief above. docs.title: §9 item 256 — 2026-10-05 (chain U5)
docs.text:
Outcome: ✅ DONE 2026-10-06 00:41Z (19:30 CDT slot, attempt 1). Five windows green on first run; no in-slot fix. Execution record at the end of this file.

Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-05 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain U5 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4739–4741), a weekly-enumerated step (§9 rule (4)). It is serial on U4, and U4 is met: WF-16 ✅ (ee9be842), WF-15 ✅ (4239ba88). The WF-1 §7 row (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2876) has no Done-when, and the 10-03 weekly left it for the daily to write ("the daily writes the Done-when at rubric grain"). The Done-when under "Status it can move" below is that text. The review copies it into the row in its own commit (rule (j)). No band, tolerance, record or validation target moves. Every band below is imported by name from the file:line cited, and none is set here.

WF-1 step 1: a thin YAML layer over Study, and a femem console script. femem run <file>.yaml parses a YAML study file into the same Study object that WF-15 / WF-16 build in Python. It solves the study and writes the outputs: a JSON summary, plus a Touchstone file for a port study. - Two committed files drive the two gated fixtures at degree 1, -n 2, to the records those chunks already assert. - Three malformed files fail with a named field. - The installed console script refuses the same three. - Executor: implementer. - What it adds: - two new src/ modules (YAML loader, CLI) plus a __main__.py; - one additive [project.scripts] table in pyproject.toml; - three __all__ exports; - two new test modules and seven YAML files; - the registry and snapshot entries. - What it does not touch: study.py, any existing gate module, helper or record. - Tier: W1 standard (180 s); W2 heavy by ceiling (400 s, the ceiling WF-16 W1 had on the same fixture at the same width); W3 / W4 the WF-14 / WF-13 windows verbatim; W5 smoke (installed console script, real build). - Ranks: -n 2 for every solve window, which is the width of both records. Complex build for W1 / W2. - Class: chain step (solve, degree 1 only). Measured median ≈ 9 min (the 10-05 restock table). - Cost: ≈ 50 min predicted: - 15 fixed + ≈ 25 code; - windows ≈ 1.7 + 2.5 + 0.1 + 0.6 + 0.5 min; - ≈ 5 spare. - Depends on: nothing open. Nothing named cli, femem, load_study or StudyConfigError exists in src/. pyproject.toml has no [project.scripts] (read 2026-10-05). pyyaml is both a declared dependency (pyproject.toml) and installed in the image (docker/Dockerfile:15). - Shared files. Items 259 / 260 may also edit src/fem_em_solver/__init__.py, tests/package/public_surface.txt and tests/package/validation_envelope.toml. Make every change there by edit, adding lines only. On a rebase, keep both sides (both sets of names, both sets of tables). This item does not edit study.py, so 259 / 260's study.py edits cannot conflict with it.

Settled from the code (read before designing). - The Python-built comparands, imported and not rebuilt by hand: - Sphere: tests/package/test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere.py, _study(degree=1) (:111–119) on GEOMETRY (:98–104). That is σ 0.57 / εᵣ 78 (_material_057, :107), QuasiStaticSphereField(e0=E0), frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_HZ and density_kg_m3=RHO_KG_M3. - Birdcage: Study(FourPortBirdcageGeometry.f_small(), GelledSalinePhantomMaterial(SALINE_SIGMA, SALINE_EPSILON_R, FREQUENCY_64_HZ), LumpedPortDrive(), frequency_hz=FREQUENCY_64_HZ, degree=1), which is test_wf16_study_four_port.py:139–145. - The records and bands: - Sphere: MAT4_DEG1_RECORD 8.291558128e-08 and MAT4_DEG1_PRINT "8.291558e-08" (test_wf15…:87–88), L0_BAND 1e-9 (test_mat5_em_coupled_sphere.py:104), and MAT4_BAND (test_phantom_material_model.py:222). - Birdcage: ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P1_RECORDS["64"] / ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_S_P2_X1["64"] and ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH (test_ans4_exact_strip_records.py), LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:165), ANCHOR_TOL / FREQ_ATOL_HZ (tests/io/test_touchstone_skrf_crosscheck.py:51–52), and the PORT-11 bands and helpers exactly as test_wf16…:73–89 imports them. - What WF-15 / WF-16 measured on these comparisons today: - Sphere, -n 2, degree 1: (I) Study against direct, in-process, 0.000e+00; (R1) 6.222e-11; (R2) the string matched (20261005T170210Z_WF-15-r2-W1-deg1.log). - Birdcage, -n 2, degree 1: (R1) 9.557e-11 against P1; (T1) 6.873e-14; (T2) 9.557e-11; (I) in-process 9.110e-16; (c1) cross-degree 0.0491; (c2) P1↔P2 swap 0.2492 (20261005T202623Z_WF-16-W1-deg1.log). - Degree 2 at -n 8 (20261005T203015Z_WF-16-W2-deg2.log) is not re-run here (Scope). - "Bit-identical" cannot mean bitwise solver output. WF-16's in-process Study-against-direct read 9.110e-16, not 0. -n 2 MUMPS is also not bitwise across processes (known-issues.md:69, OPS-43; SOLVE_FLOOR_RECORD at known-issues.md:81). The reading is WF-15's rule-(j) reading (PROJECT_PLAN.md:2890): - bitwise up to the solve: the YAML-built Study's spec equals the Python-built one field by field, with floats compared by float.hex, and the DG0 material fields assembled from it are equal; - the solve outputs within the imported bands: SAR at L0_BAND; S and the Touchstone file at LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND; - plus the registered records the U3 / U4 tests already assert.

The Done-when states this as "(read by the 2026-10-05 18:00 review, rule (j); the weekly ratifies)". - The JSON round trip is exact. json.dump writes a Python float by repr, and json.load reads it back to the same double. So the summary file's SAR and S equal the in-memory values bitwise, and the test may compare the file's numbers with == where it says so. - PyYAML's float resolver (YAML 1.1) needs a dot and a signed exponent. Measured on the host's PyYAML 6.0.1, yaml.safe_load gives: - 64.0e6 → str and 1e-9 → str; - 6.4e+07, 64000000.0 and 0.5700000000000001 → float; - 78 → int and true → bool; - for a: 1\na: 2 → {'a': 2}: the duplicate key is dropped silently.

The container's pyyaml is unpinned, so the test prints yaml.__version__. - The literals the good files carry. The files write each float as its Python repr: - repr(0.01 / 10.0) is 0.001 and repr(0.01 / 5.0) is 0.002, both == the decimal literals (host arithmetic, 2026-10-05); - repr(64.0e6) is 64000000.0; - repr(np.nextafter(0.57, 1)) is 0.5700000000000001.

(K) checks every bit, so a hand-typed literal that is one ULP off fails there, in the parse node, before any solve. - The material frequency is the study's. GelledSalinePhantomMaterial(sigma, epsilon_r, frequency_hz, mu_r=1.0) is a frozen dataclass (materials/phantom.py:21–40). The YAML material section has no frequency key: the loader passes study.frequency_hz. A mismatch would raise at core/time_harmonic.py:462–465, and that is not one of the three gated failures. - femem will not be on PATH in the dev container. The image's pip install -e . (docker/Dockerfile:36) predates the entry point, so in-container windows call fem_em_solver.cli.main([...]) in-process. The console script is exercised only in WF-13's fresh venv. That venv's pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation . (scripts/package/wf13_setup.sh:84) builds a wheel from the copied pyproject.toml and does install [project.scripts]. Never pip install into the live container.

Code. - (1) New src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py with three public names: - StudyConfigError(ValueError), with attributes .field (the dotted path, e.g. "geometry.sphere_raduis") and .source (the file path). Its message is f"{source}: {field}: {reason}", so the field name appears in str(exc). - load_study(path) -> Study. It parses with a yaml.SafeLoader subclass whose construct_mapping raises StudyConfigError on a duplicate key. Never use yaml.load. import yaml happens inside the function, so import fem_em_solver does not import yaml. - run_study_file(path, *, output_dir=None, comm=MPI.COMM_WORLD) -> StudyRun. It calls load_study, then study.solve(comm), then writes the outputs. StudyRun (study, result, summary dict, written paths) is a dataclass and is not exported, as PortStudyResult was not. - Schema v0. Units are SI and given by the key name; a unit string is a type error. - femem (int, must be 1; required). - study: frequency_hz (number, required), degree (int in {1, 2}, optional, default 2, the Study's own default), density_kg_m3 (number, optional, default the Study's). - geometry: kind (required). - sphere_in_box: sphere_radius, box_half_width, resolution_sphere, resolution_far (numbers, required), sphere_tag (int, optional). - four_port_birdcage: preset: f_small (optional), plus any FourPortBirdcageGeometry field name as an override. A list is converted to a tuple for port_box_size. Any other key, including width_correction_kappa, is an unknown key. - material: either preset (low / mid / high, which goes through Study's own string route) or sigma + epsilon_r (+ optional mu_r), building GelledSalinePhantomMaterial(sigma, epsilon_r, study.frequency_hz, mu_r). Both forms at once is an error on material. - excitation: kind (required). - quasi_static_sphere_field: e0 (optional). - lumped_port_drive: z0_ohm, port_impedance_ohm (optional numbers), drive_voltage_v (optional: a number or a [re, im] pair). - outputs (optional): directory. - Numbers. A number field accepts int or float, converted by float(). It rejects bool (it is an int subclass) and str. The str message names the YAML-1.1 trap: "YAML reads 64.0e6 as a string; write 6.4e+07 or 64000000.0". - Validation order is fixed, and the first error raises: - at top level: the version, then unknown top-level keys, then missing required sections; - then section by section in the order study → geometry → material → excitation → outputs; - within a section: unknown keys, then missing required keys, then types and values. - No solver code, no mesh before the parse completes, and no import from tests/. A StudyConfigError is raised identically on every rank, because every rank parses the same file. There is no collective before it. - Outputs. run_study_file resolves output_dir as the argument, else outputs.directory, else ./femem_out/<stem>. After every reduction, rank 0 creates it and writes summary.json. Then comm.Barrier(), and every rank returns. The summary holds: - femem 1, source (absolute path), sha256 of the file, family, degree, frequency_hz, ranks, cells, elapsed_s; - sphere: the mean_sar dict with every value float()-ed; - ports: s_matrix and z_matrix as nested [re, im] pairs, and touchstone (the filename).

For a port study it calls `result.write_touchstone(<output_dir>/<stem>.s4p)` (`study.py:405–421`, rank 0 plus `Barrier`).
  • (2) New src/fem_em_solver/cli.py. It defines main(argv=None) -> int with argparse subcommands:
  • run <file> [--output-dir DIR] calls run_study_file and returns 0;
  • check <file> calls load_study only and prints, on rank 0, one line per spec field (family, degree, frequency, the material's σ / εᵣ, the excitation kind). It returns 0.

Behaviour: - A StudyConfigError prints femem: error: <message> to stderr on rank 0 and returns 2 on every rank. - main returns an exit code and never calls sys.exit. The console-script wrapper does that. - (3) New src/fem_em_solver/__main__.py: import sys; from .cli import main; sys.exit(main()). It is not exercised by a window, so it is disclosed as unexercised. - (4) pyproject.toml: add one table, [project.scripts] with femem = "fem_em_solver.cli:main". Nothing else changes. - (5) src/fem_em_solver/__init__.py: import StudyConfigError, load_study and run_study_file from .study_yaml, and append them to __all__ (30 → 33). cli is not imported by __init__. - (6) tests/package/public_surface.txt: add the three names, keeping the sort order: StudyConfigError after Study, load_study before load_touchstone, run_study_file after run_single_port_excitation_case. - (7) tests/package/validation_envelope.toml: - add [names.StudyConfigError] (the malformed node and the installed node), [names.load_study] (the good-file and malformed nodes) and [names.run_study_file] (the two CLI nodes); - append test_wf1_cli_sphere_reproduces_wf15 to [names.Study]; - node IDs only, no number (WF-14 (N)). - (8) Seven YAML files under tests/package/wf1/: - sphere_mat4.yaml: femem: 1; study: {frequency_hz: 64000000.0, degree: 1, density_kg_m3: 1000.0}; geometry: {kind: sphere_in_box, sphere_radius: 0.01, box_half_width: 0.02, resolution_sphere: 0.001, resolution_far: 0.002, sphere_tag: 1}; material: {sigma: 0.57, epsilon_r: 78.0}; excitation: {kind: quasi_static_sphere_field, e0: 1.0}. - f_small_four_port.yaml: femem: 1; study: {frequency_hz: 64000000.0, degree: 1}; geometry: {kind: four_port_birdcage, preset: f_small}; material: {sigma: 0.5, epsilon_r: 78.0}; excitation: {kind: lumped_port_drive}. - control_sigma_ulp.yaml: sphere_mat4.yaml with sigma: 0.5700000000000001 and no other change. - malformed_unknown_key.yaml: sphere_mat4.yaml with sphere_radius misspelled sphere_raduis. Expected .field = geometry.sphere_raduis. - malformed_wrong_type.yaml: sphere_mat4.yaml with frequency_hz: 64.0e6, which YAML reads as a str. Expected .field = study.frequency_hz. - malformed_missing_section.yaml: f_small_four_port.yaml with no excitation: section. Expected .field = excitation. - malformed_duplicate_key.yaml: sphere_mat4.yaml with sigma given twice (0.57, then 0.75). Expected .field = material.sigma. This is the loader's guard, printed and asserted in the parse node, and not one of the row's three.

Each file has a one-line comment header citing this item. Each malformed file differs from its parent in exactly the one stated place. - (9) New tests/package/test_wf1_study_yaml.py. @complex_only goes on the two solve nodes, so WF-14's real-build collection imports the module cleanly. - Imports from test_wf15… / test_wf16…: helpers and constants only, namely _study, GEOMETRY, _closed, _record, _rel and the constants. Never a test_* function or a fixture (deg1, leg): an imported test name is collected again in this module. - Helper _spec_diff(a, b) -> list[str]. It returns the dotted names that differ between two Study objects. It walks geometry, material and excitation dataclass fields plus frequency_hz, degree and density_kg_m3. It compares type() first, then floats by float.hex, complex numbers by the hex of their real and imaginary parts, tuples elementwise, and everything else by ==. - Nodes: - test_wf1_good_files_build_the_python_studies (no solve; (K), (Deg), (c1) parse half, duplicate key); - test_wf1_malformed_files_name_their_field (no solve; (X)); - test_wf1_cli_sphere_reproduces_wf15 (W1); - test_wf1_cli_f_small_reproduces_wf16 (W2). - Width guard on both solve nodes, asserted and never skipped: MPI.COMM_WORLD.size == ANS4_EXACT_STRIP_RECORD_RANK_WIDTH (2). - Output paths. Each CLI node first has rank 0 delete /workspace/logs/wf1/<stem>/ if it exists, then Barrier; /logs/ is gitignored, .gitignore:82. It then calls cli.main(["run", <file>, "--output-dir", "/workspace/logs/wf1/<stem>"]) in-process and reads summary.json on every rank after main returns. A stale summary therefore cannot pass for a fresh one. - (10) New tests/package/test_wf1_installed_cli.py. It uses stdlib only (subprocess, sys, pathlib), with no import from tests/ and none of fem_em_solver. It is skipped unless WF13_INSTALLED_CHECK=1, and it locates femem at Path(sys.prefix) / "bin" / "femem". Node: test_wf1_installed_femem_refuses_the_malformed_files (W5, (X′)).

Anchors (asserted). - (K) The YAML builds the Python Study, bitwise and field by field (no solve). - _spec_diff(load_study("sphere_mat4.yaml"), _study(degree=1)) == []. - _spec_diff(load_study("f_small_four_port.yaml"), <the WF-16 Python Study at degree=1>) == []. - The preset route: the sphere mapping with material: {preset: mid}, built through the private mapping entry point that load_study uses (no extra file), gives _spec_diff(..., _study(material="mid", degree=1)) == []. - Print each list, and the float.hex of geometry.resolution_sphere / resolution_far / study.frequency_hz on both sides. - (Deg) Degree 2 when omitted, structurally. Both good mappings with study.degree deleted give .degree == 2. Exact. - (X) Three malformed files fail with a named field (no solve). For each malformed file: - load_study raises StudyConfigError, not a bare KeyError, TypeError or YAML error; - exc.field == the expected dotted path above, and that path in str(exc); - cli.main(["run", <file>, "--output-dir", "/workspace/logs/wf1/malformed"]) returns 2 on every rank (allreduced MPI.MIN == MPI.MAX == 2), and the output directory does not exist afterwards, which shows the parse fails before any mesh or write. - The three .field values are pairwise distinct. - Duplicate key (printed and asserted, beside the three): malformed_duplicate_key.yaml raises StudyConfigError with .field == "material.sigma". - (U) Upstream identity through the CLI's own parse, sphere (W1). - DG0 σ / εᵣ / μᵣ come from build_material_fields / build_mu_r_field, built on the Python Study's solved mesh / cell_tags once with load_study(file).material as phantom_material and once with _study(degree=1).material, both with phantom_tag=SPHERE_TAG and the same background. - Each reads max |Δ| == 0.0 with 0 differing on owned dofs, using _dg0_owned_diff (test_phantom_material_model.py, as WF-15 imports it). - (S) The CLI's outputs are the run's. Two implementation choices to disclose. - Duplicate-key guard. The loader is a yaml.SafeLoader subclass whose construct_mapping refuses a repeated key. To name the field by its dotted path, it composes the node tree first, then constructs it, and maps the offending mapping node back to its path. It reads material.sigma on the guard file. - Order inside geometry / excitation. kind is checked first (missing, then unknown value), because the allowed key set depends on it. Unknown keys, missing keys and types follow in the briefed order. A geometry.kind / excitation.kind mismatch (a sphere driven by ports, or the reverse) is refused as excitation.kind. Negative controls (rule (e)). - (N1) the PEC column — asserted, backed. The YAML Cu summary's SAR10g(P1, origin) misses the PEC Study B's by > REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL, and the same for |B₁⁺|(P1, origin). Backing: item 388's W1 printed both columns of this comparison on this fixture at this point and drive — SAR 2.408073397e-06 vs 2.409072917e-06 W/kg, |B₁⁺| 1.833178311e-08 vs 1.833834143e-08 T (20261012T033238Z_WF-16-s11-W1.log:2694–2695), a relative gap of 4.151e-04 (SAR) and 3.578e-04 (|B₁⁺|), so ≈ 415× and ≈ 358× the band; the factors are printed. The ceiling is that physical Cu-vs-PEC gap itself; a 1× bar is reachable with more than two decades of margin. This is the control that separates "the YAML file's conductor reached the field route" from a PEC-walled field. (Item 388's backing pair was Python-vs-Python; here the Cu side is the YAML Study, equal to the Python one by (I-SAR). The review may relabel it predicted, as it might have 388's (N1); the assertion would then be dropped and the factors printed.) - (N2) surface-blind identity — asserted, backed. The kept-field residual with P_surf omitted is ≥ BLIND_FACTOR × DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (= 1e-5). Backing: 3.1559e-04 = 315.6× on the same kept-field route, fixture and drive (…W1.log:2718); the ceiling is P_surf / P_src ≈ 3.16e-04, so ≈ 316× is the most this fixture can show and the 10× bar holds with ≈ 32× margin; the factor is printed. - (X=)'s control is deterministic, asserted: the malformed file's mapping (_mapping) with geometry.as_hole set to True parses through _study_from_mapping to a Study with _spec_diff against load_study(CU_SAR_FILE) of [] (the refusal is that one bit's alone), and with outputs deleted it still raises at conductor (the refusal is the conductor's, not the outputs').

Windows. Foreground. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Bash timeout: 660000 on every window; pytest with -s; tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py first on the path; node IDs, never -k. Every window is under 10 min, so no durable capture. Before W1: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. Windows run serially, never beside another heavy window. - W0 — the no-mesh node (standard; predicted 20–40 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s8-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_copper_sar_b1.py::test_wf1_s8_parse_and_refusal_parity -v -s --tb=short'". - W1 — the module (heavy by ceiling; predicted 140–190 s, ≤ 250 s at the 1.32× box reading): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s8-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 400 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_copper_sar_b1.py -v -s --tb=short'". Price, from item 388's W1 (…W1.log:2691, 99 s for three builds): four builds of the 80 798-cell hole mesh at ≈ 30 s each (mesh 23.2 s + sweep 6.3–6.7 s) — run_study_file's solve() and field route, Study A's and Study B's field routes ≈ 120 s; 4 + 4 + 1 balls and three CG1 projections ≈ 12 s (item 388: two balls and two projections with evaluation 4.8 s, :2696); identity 0.4 s; start-up, test_complex_mode.py and the no-mesh node ≈ 15 s ⇒ ≈ 150 s. - Wgen / Wval / Wapi / Wdoc (the registry lines move the API pages and docs/guide/validation.md; commit both): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s8-Wgen "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 python3 scripts/docs/generate_api_reference.py --out docs/guide/api'" (2 s, 20261011T214232Z_WF-16-s9a-Wgen.log:12); then scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s8-Wval "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/docs/generate_validation_page.py --out docs/guide/validation.md'" (20261012T034338Z_WF-14-s2-W0-gen.log:12); then scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s8-Wapi "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 170 python3 -m pytest tests/package/test_wf14_validation_envelope.py tests/package/test_wf17_api_reference.py tests/package/test_wf14_validation_page.py -v -s --tb=short'" (22 passed, 14 s, 20261012T034345Z_WF-14-s2-W1-page.log:12, :220); then scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s8-Wdoc "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/testing/check_example_doc_references.py --docs-root docs/guide --check-links'" (0 dead; 20261011T214244Z_WF-16-s9a-Wdoc.log:12). - No rule (c) re-gate: no src/ file changes. The executor confirms git diff --stat main -- src/ is empty before the commit and says so. If the module shows a defect in src/, it is a finding — known-issues, park — not an in-slot fix.

Traps already paid for. - Two REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOLs exist: tests/validation/test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py:171 (1e-6, the one 382b / 390b import) and tests/validation/test_port19_factor_reuse.py:82 (1e-12). Import the first by its full module path. - The stub is function-scoped. The parity node uses the monkeypatch fixture (restored after the node) and never requests runs; a module-scoped stub would hand {"mesh": None} to the fixture's builds. _conductor_setup runs after build and before the problem, which is why the stub needs only "mesh" (item 388 trap). - One field build per Study. run_study_file already populated run.study.fields_result through _sar_summary; the API re-read must reuse it (asserted by identity). Never clear fields_result or _b1_cg1, never build a fresh Study for (iii) / (B2′) — that is a third ≈ 30 s build and a different comparison. - PyYAML 1.1 floats need a dot (0.0, 10.0, 58000000.0; WF-1 step 1); false is a bool, 0 an int (refused at geometry.as_hole, step 4). - Every sar / b1_plus_at call is collective on both ranks (item 227's deadlock); points and centres identical on every rank; point evaluation only inside b1_plus_at (evaluate_vector_field_parallel). cell_tags.values and assemble_scalar are rank-local — _kept_identity reduces each power. rc is rank-local — _rc_all. - Never import a test_* name or a module-scope solving fixture; helpers and constants only. Scope. One fixture (the F-small exact-rectangle copper hole mesh, 80 798 cells, κ off, strip_fraction = GATED_WIDTH_FRACTION), 64 MHz, degree 1, -n 2, LeontovichWall(COPPER_SIGMA), one point (the origin), four drives. Not claimed: any SAR or |B₁⁺| value on copper as a physical figure (per 1 V records, compared with themselves through two front ends); the {ring_radius_m} centre form on the hole route; the PEC-hole YAML file with outputs (its Study is reached only as the Python control B); femem run with a solve through cli.main or the installed console script on this file (the CLI is exercised on the refusal only); degree 2; other frequencies or widths; F-human (items 390a / 390b); a C4 statement at the origin; any AED statement.

What a negative result means. Report and stop; park on attempt/WF-1-step8-<UTC>, mark item 394 BLOCKED with its unblock condition in the same commit (rule (d)), journal in docs/testing/attempts.md. (K) red — the parse moved: a study_yaml finding, known-issues, never a test edit to match. (X=) red on the YAML side — the refusal order or text moved; on the Python side — item 388's fix regressed: known-issues, stop. (K1) / (S=Y) red with (R) green — the YAML Study's field route does not carry the conductor although the parse does: a defect against item 388's fix, known-issues, never a widened band. (I-SAR) / (I-B) red with (K), (S=Y) and (iii) / (B2′) green — two equal Study specs give different fields across builds: print per-drive residuals, known-issues, never re-band. (iii) / (B2′) red — the summary is not the API's value on its own Study: a run_study_file finding. (P) red with (N2) green — kept-field accounting; (N2) or (N1) inside its bar — the YAML field carries no wall term (the conductor did not reach the field route): stop, known-issues. A Wapi red after Wgen / Wval — regenerate once after a rebase, else park. No PREDICTED RED: line: a red anywhere stops the slot.

Status it can move. - §7 WF-1 row: stays ✅ (rule (j): its Done-when is step 1's, which this item does not touch). On green the row's history gains one step-8 record clause, exact text from the review's return, of the form "Step-8 record (§9 item 394, U44, provisional): outputs.sar / outputs.b1_plus with a leontovich conductor on the F-small hole Study return the Python copper Study's field-route 10 g SAR and |B₁⁺| at the origin within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (max / over four drives), the YAML field route equals its solve() to (LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND), the kept field's copper identity closes at (DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL); a solid-route leontovich file refuses at conductor as Study.sar / b1_plus_at / solve() refuse (as_hole), with no mesh". - §10 chain U: U44 marked DONE (provisional until the next weekly ratifies). - WF-16.md, item 388's Scope: the "YAML conductor + outputs.sar / outputs.b1_plus combination … untested" clause is answered by this record (a pointer line under item 388's outcome; the clause itself is not edited). The WF-16 row does not move. - WF-14's registry gains the seven node IDs; no known-issues entry is filed on green. No §2 sentence moves.

Executor spawn prompt (verbatim). "Execute §9 item 394 — WF-1 step 8 (§10 U44, provisional: copper SAR / |B₁⁺| through the YAML front end, and solid-route refusal parity) — per docs/planning/chunks/WF-1.md §9 item 394. Pass timeout: 660000 on every Bash call that runs a window; run pytest with -s. Write the two YAML files and the test module, then run W0, W1, Wgen, Wval, Wapi, Wdoc in order, foreground. Before W1 run docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 and require 0. If W1 has not started by minute 35, park. No edit to the test module, the YAML files or the registry after the window that closes on them. Never delete a log. You are the executor — do not spawn agents, never background a harness window. If the docker socket is denied, stop and report the exact command string. On a red, park on attempt/WF-1-step8-*, mark item 394 BLOCKED in the same commit, and report."

Review ruling 2026-10-12 03:00 (daily) on the item 394 draft, and on items 390a / 390b. (Q1) Agreed: item 388's printed SAR / |B₁⁺| values stay printed beside the YAML values, never asserted (that would register a record under rule (6)). (Q2) REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL accepted, as 382b / 390b. (Q4) Refusal parity as drafted — same ValueError family, the as_hole token in both messages, no mesh built on either side — accepted; it is a parity of outcome, not of call site, and the brief says so. docs.title: §9 item 401 — 2026-10-12 (WF-1 step 9: femem check prints the parsed geometry kind; lane 1, ops)
docs.text:
Written by the 2026-10-12 10:30 daily review, from item 390a's finding (1).

What. cli.py:158 labels every study that is not a sphere four_port_birdcage. Edit (src/fem_em_solver/cli.py only, the check branch). Print the parsed geometry.kind, the same kind that study_yaml._load(path) returns and run_study_file writes. Take it from _load, or from a small public wrapper in study_yaml that returns (study, kind) if the slot prefers not to import a private name; disclose which. Nothing else changes: not the other five printed lines, the return codes or the StudyConfigError path. study_yaml.py gains at most that wrapper. The parse and solve paths are not touched.

Anchors (new tests/package/test_wf1_check_family.py, -n 2, no mesh, no solve). - (F) Take every tracked YAML under tests/package/wf1/ that is not malformed (glob *.yaml, exclude malformed_*; print the list, ≥ 10 files). For each, cli.main(["check", f]) returns 0 on every rank, and its printed family: line (captured on rank 0 with capsys) equals study_yaml._load(f)[1]. Print each pair. - (F-h) Three literals, the letter of the known-issues entry: - f_human_tuned_copper.yaml prints family: f_human_birdcage; - sphere_mat4.yaml prints sphere_in_box; - f_small_four_port.yaml prints four_port_birdcage. - (U) For sphere_mat4.yaml and f_small_four_port.yaml, the other five lines of check's output are unchanged. Compare them against the output of the pinned pre-change cli.py (b01dc790, never HEAD:). The host writes that copy under the gitignored logs/ with a plain git show b01dc790:src/fem_em_solver/cli.py > logs/cli_b01dc790.py, and the test loads it by path. Loaded that way, the copy's relative imports need its package context. If that does not work cleanly, compare against the five lines printed in 20261012T123618Z_WF-1-s7a-W0.log and the RG logs of item 390a instead, and say which.

Negative control (asserted; backed by the measurement above, the same comparison on the same file). The pre-change check on f_human_tuned_copper.yaml printed family: four_port_birdcage (…WF-1-s7a-W0.log:68), which differs from _load(...)[1]. Assert that this logged line differs from the string (F) now prints. Without this control, (F) could pass on a file set that never reaches the bug.

Re-gates (standing rule (c): the pre-existing gates on the edited module). These modules call cli.main(["check", …]): - tests/package/test_wf1_study_yaml.py - tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_sar_b1.py - tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_probes.py - tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_f_human.py

Grep cli.main under tests/package/ and add any others, plus test_wf13_launch_helper.py, which asserts s["family"]. Run them in one -n 2 window at standard tier, skipping and naming any that is solve-gated behind an opt-in variable. If item 390a's W9 window exercises the installed console script, re-run it too.

Registry. This item adds no WF-14 registry line, so (Q3)'s page windows are not owed. If the slot does add one, it runs Wgen / Wval / Wapi / Wdoc as item 394 did.

src/ edits (every touched existing function is named for rule (c)). - study.py, the hook. - TwoPortQuadratureDrive gains _temperature_port_study(study, cooling, *, transient, balls, window_s, sense="ccw", comm) beside its _sar_port_study / _b1_plus_port_study hooks (the existing pattern). These are new lines. - _study_temperature gains two inserted lines at its top: hook = getattr(self.excitation, "_temperature_port_study", None) and if hook is not None: return hook(self, cooling, transient=…, balls=…, window_s=…). - Its signature gains keyword-only balls=None, window_s=None. When they are not None on a non-tuned Study, it raises ValueError before any mesh. - Every existing statement is unchanged. _refuse_f_human stays for the solid route. - study.py, the branch body — P17's route, lifted with provenance comments (test_mat15_f_human_tuned_heating.py at 59809ba7, line spans named), never imported: 1. res = _tuned_result(study, comm), so the field is reused and there is no second solve. 2. The source: q = cooling.source_scale × the DG0 average of ½σ|E_sense|² over PHANTOM_CELL_TAG, through _dg0_cell_average then _dg0_to_submesh. The scale is applied after the average (ruling 361-4: one compiled form). 3. Robin on every exterior submesh facet (_exterior_robin_tags). 4. solve_transient_conduction(sub, ft, k, rho_c, q, h, t_inf, t_init=t_inf, robin_tag, dt=transient.dt_s, n_steps=transient.n_steps, theta=transient.theta, startup_half_steps=transient.startup_half_steps, degree=cooling.degree, snapshot_steps=tuple(range(n_steps + 1))). 5. Per snapshot: the volume mean ⟨θ⟩ₙ and, per ball centre, θ̄ₙ through P17's indicator forms, with radius averaging_ball_radius(mass_kg=mass_g·1e-3, rho=study.density_kg_m3) and SAR_QUADRATURE_DEGREE. 6. Per series, running_average(times, series, window=window_s) → (peak, t_max). - study.py, the result. A new non-exported TunedTemperatureResult carrying times_s, volume_mean_k, balls (centre, radius, volume, theta_k), six_minute (peak, t_max per series), source_power_w (∫q), max_balance_residual, cells, n_sub, sense, cooling and transient. - Collectives. Every ball assembly and reduction is collective on every rank. Never guard a collective with "owns phantom cells" (item 227; MAT-19 D4's empty ranks). - study_yaml.py. - _parse_thermal's F-human elif (:477–479) no longer refuses outright. It calls a new _parse_thermal_f_human(sec, source) that returns a private _FHumanThermal(cooling, transient, balls, window_s, sense). The keys: - k_w_per_m_k, h_w_per_m2_k, t_inf_c, source_scale; - transient: {dt_s, n_steps, rho_c_j_per_m3_k, theta?, startup_half_steps?} — required; - balls: {mass_g, centres: [[x, y, z], …]} — required; - window_s — optional; omitted means the API default, never a loader default (the (Deg) rule); - sense — optional, ccw / cw. - A section without transient raises at field thermal with "f_human_birdcage needs thermal.transient (a transient Study)". This mirrors 390a's "two_port_quadrature needs a conductor ⇒ conductor" rule, and it keeps 390a's mutation assertion green unedited. A malformed key inside transient or balls raises at its dotted field. Order inside the section as everywhere: unknown keys, missing, types, values. - _parse_mapping carries the result in the cooling slot of its return tuple for F-human only. Every caller (_study_from_mapping, _load, load_study, run_study_file) is updated in the same diff (item 295's rule). - run_study_file's F-human branch gains, after the existing S / SAR / B lines and before the write: if fh_thermal is not None: thermal = study.temperature(...). It then writes summary["temperature"] = {"sense", "times_s", "volume_mean_k", "balls": [{"centre", "radius_m", "volume_m3", "theta_k"}], "six_minute": {...}, "source_power_w", "max_balance_residual", "source_scale"}. The series is the summary, and the bundle writes it. StudyRun.thermal is set. - The four-port and sphere branches are untouched. - Name no artifact-shaped token in any docstring (item 274's trap). - Not touched: cli.py, __init__.py, public_surface.txt. No new public name, since TunedTemperatureResult is returned, not exported.

Licence: §9 rule (6), a provisional next step on live chain U (Phase 9, 9a), after U53 (§9 item 472, WF-16 step 12, 24088335) and U54 (§9 item 473, WF-17 step 6). Target: reproduction plus an identity. No band, tolerance, record, Done-when or validation target is set or moved; every band is imported by name. Anchors: WF-12 step 3's H12c C_mode 1.181185799070e-10 F at REDUCTION_BAND (the comparand item 472 already reproduced through the API), and summary = API at EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL. The sheets-and-κ ruling (2026-10-02) binds. The capacitor-ESR ruling is not engaged (the read is lossless, study.py:1027–1029). Item 442 (this file) and item 472 (WF-16.md) are the templates.

Owner. WF-1 owns femem run's tune: section: item 442 is WF-1 step 11 and this file holds its brief (:1108); WF-17 owns the guide pages (step 6, item 473, is a page) and EX-115 is the example of item 442's route. This is WF-1 step 12.

Finding at drafting (code reading): the YAML route cannot reach the ring read today. A src/ change is needed, src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py only; study.py is untouched. Three walls, in parse order: - Excitation. _EXCITATION_FOR["f_human_birdcage"] = "two_port_quadrature" (study_yaml.py:119–124); _parse_excitation refuses any other kind at excitation.kind (:361–367). Item 472's Study needs LumpedPortDrive(). - Tune. _parse_tune refuses every non-four-port geometry at tune (:724–727). - Run. run_study_file's F-human branch (:1061–1094) reads drive.c_in_f, result.s_node, result.y_in, which are the TwoPortQuadratureDrive result's attributes. A LumpedPortDrive F-human Study returns a PortStudyResult (study.py:574, through _study_solve_ports, :609, (S1) of item 472 at :619–622). That branch would raise AttributeError after the solve. - Nothing else is missing. Study.tune already dispatches the F-human LumpedPortDrive Study to _study_tune_ring (study.py:1033–1034). _tune_summary (study_yaml.py:996–1005) is geometry-blind: z_k is serialised by length, so the ring read's 9 entries serialise as the four-port's 4 do. PortStudyResult.write_touchstone takes any port count (ports/touchstone.py:15–18, .s{n}p).

Pinned refusals the change must keep (found at drafting). - tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_f_human.py:223 (item 390a): f_human_tuned_copper.yaml with only excitation.kind set to lumped_port_drive (so c_in_f / esr_ohm remain) must still name excitation.kind. Admitting the kind and falling through to the four-port _unknown check would name excitation.c_in_f and turn that gate red. The drafter's design keeps it green with no test edit (E1b below). The alternative is to re-point that row's expected field to excitation.c_in_f, which edits a pinned assertion; the drafter does not propose it, and the review rules if E1b is declined. - tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_tune.py:132–136 (item 442): tune on f_human_tuned_copper.yaml (quadrature) names tune. It stays so (E2 admits f_human_birdcage only with a LumpedPortDrive). - malformed_quadrature_on_four_port.yaml → excitation.kind (test_wf1_yaml_f_human.py:70): unchanged (E1 widens only the F-human row).

The change — study_yaml.py only, ≈ 35 lines. Existing-line edits are E1, E2, E3 and two docstrings, so standing rule (c) applies: disclose them, and re-run the pre-existing gates (RG1, RG2, and W0's re-gate modules). - (E1) _parse_excitation's mismatch test (:361) admits one more pair: kind == "lumped_port_drive" and geometry_kind == "f_human_birdcage". Every other pair refuses as now, message unchanged. - (E1b) Additive, in the same function, before the LumpedPortDrive _unknown (:376): on an f_human_birdcage, if the section carries any of c_in_f, esr_ohm, feeds (the quadrature keys), raise StudyConfigError(source, "excitation.kind", "lumped_port_drive takes no c_in_f / esr_ohm / feeds (two_port_quadrature's keys); …"). A user who switched the kind but kept quadrature keys is told at the kind; item 390a's :223 row stays green unedited. - (E2) _parse_tune(sec, geometry_kind, source, excitation=None): admitted on a four_port_birdcage (as now) or on an f_human_birdcage whose excitation is a LumpedPortDrive; anything else refuses at tune (message names both admitted forms). k handling unchanged. - (E3) _parse_mapping's call (:792) passes excitation. - (E4) Additive refusals in _parse_mapping, each placed at its section's place in the fixed validation order: on an f_human_birdcage + LumpedPortDrive, a thermal: section raises at thermal (after the cooling line), and outputs.sar / outputs.b1_plus raise at outputs.sar / outputs.b1_plus (after the outputs line). Reason: those routes are the two_port_quadrature per-sense routes (Study.sar / b1_plus_at / temperature refuse an F-human LumpedPortDrive Study, study.py:526–530); without E4 they would fail after the solve. - (E5) Additive branch in run_study_file, between the four-port branch and the quadrature F-human branch: elif isinstance(study.geometry, FHumanBirdcageGeometry) and isinstance(study.excitation, LumpedPortDrive): writing cells, the .s32p Touchstone, s_matrix, z_matrix and touchstone exactly as the four-port branch's :1047–1054, then if "tune" in outputs: summary["tune"] = _tune_summary(study, outputs["tune"], comm). Neither neighbouring branch gains or loses a line. - Docstrings: the module's tune bullet (:66–70) and the excitation lines gain the F-human lumped_port_drive form; run_study_file's docstring (:1014–1016) says the quadrature route writes no Touchstone and the lumped_port_drive route writes <stem>.s32p. Wgen regenerates the API page. - Never: change _load's 4-tuple; add a Study.__init__ keyword; touch study.py; pass κ; admit an F-human lumped_port_drive file without as_hole: true and a leontovich conductor (both refusals exist: :279–283 and :773–778, unchanged).

WF-1 step 12: femem run (run_study_file) with a top-level tune: {k: 1} on the copper F-human hole lumped_port_drive YAML at degree 1, -n 8, solves once; summary["tune"] equals the same Study's Study.tune(k=1) and reproduces WF-12 step 3's H12c C_mode within REDUCTION_BAND; k = 2 misses. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: heavy, -n 8 (the comparand's width, item 472's W1), complex. W0 / RG1 / RG2 -n 2. - Class: chain step (solve), median ≈ 10.5 measured. - Cost: ≈ 45 predicted min = 15 fixed + ≈ 12 code (≈ 35 src lines, module ≈ 200 lines, one YAML, registry lines, one guide bullet) + W0 ≈ 0.5 + RG1 ≈ 0.3 + RG2 ≈ 1.5 + W1 ≈ 4–5 + Wgen / Wval / Wapi / Wdoc ≈ 1 + ≈ 7 row / journal / spare. If the src/ change and W0 / RG1 / RG2 are not green by minute 30, or W1 has not started by minute 35, park (rule (d)). - Depends on: nothing open. Reads logs/wf12/h12c-cu-s32-a2.npz through NPZ_PATH (tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root.py:50); absent ⇒ stop, BLOCKED, never re-solve. Never beside another heavy window. Anchors (asserted; bands imported). - (K) Parse, no mesh. Every geometry's build monkeypatched to raise (as test_wf1_yaml_tune.py:80–85). _spec_diff(load_study(FILE), _study()) == [] (item 472's Python Study: FHumanBirdcageGeometry(as_hole=True), saline, LumpedPortDrive(), LeontovichWall(COPPER_SIGMA), 64 MHz, degree 1); parsed outputs == {"tune": {"k": 1}}, type(k) is int; tune: {} → {"tune": {}}. - (X) Refusals, no mesh, each naming its field. On mapping variants of FILE: tune: {k: 3} → tune.k; excitation.c_in_f added → excitation.kind (E1b); thermal: added (item 390a's _add_thermal values) → thermal; outputs.sar (one literal centre) → outputs.sar; outputs.b1_plus → outputs.b1_plus; as_hole: false → geometry.as_hole; conductor removed → conductor. On f_human_tuned_copper.yaml + tune: {k: 1} → tune (unchanged). cli.main(["check", FILE]) rc (0, 0) via _rc_all, rank 0 prints family: f_human_birdcage. Zero build calls. - (R0) Fixture tie. summary["cells"] == HOLE_CELL_RECORD (369 387); _residual(S_run[p][:, p], s32_npz) ≤ REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL with p the name map to the npz order (item 472's construction, test_wf16_study_tune_f_human_copper.py:242–259); len(summary["s_matrix"]) == 32; summary["touchstone"] == FILE.stem + ".s32p" and the file exists (rank 0, broadcast). Predicted ≤ 1e-10 (item 472 measured 1.632e-12 on the same build route, …213534Z_WF-16-s12-W1.log:7346). - (I=) Summary = API, one solve. |summary["tune"]["c_mode_farad"] / api1.c_mode_farad − 1| ≤ EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL; the same for off_diagonal_residual; len(z_k) == 9 and every real / imaginary part within EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL of api1.z_k's; JSON read-back equal to the in-memory summary; k == 1, frequency_hz == 64e6. Printed beside: float.hex equality (predicted equal: same self.result, same arithmetic, item 442's (I=) reading). - (a) The comparand. |summary C / WF12_STEP3_C_MODE_CU_F − 1| ≤ REDUCTION_BAND. Predicted ≤ 1e-9 (item 472: −3.545e-13 through the API on the same fixture and width). Printed beside: the gap to item 472's measured C.

Negative control (rule (e)). - (c1) The mode index — asserted. t2 = _tune_summary(run.study, {"k": 2}, comm); assert run.study.result is res0 and |t2["c_mode_farad"] / WF12_STEP3_C_MODE_CU_F − 1| > REDUCTION_BAND. Backing: the same comparison, fixture and width measured −0.3327259 (332.7× the band) through the API (…213534Z_WF-16-s12-W1.log:7380) and 0.332726 in step 3 (20261006T170222Z_WF-12-step3-a2-W1.log:6397). Predicted −33.27 %. Ceiling: the assertion is one-sided (> band), so no ceiling binds. - Printed only: WF12_STEP3_K2_SEPARATION beside (c1)'s gap.

Windows. Foreground, in the order W0, RG1, RG2, pgrep, W1, Wgen, Wval, Wapi, Wdoc. The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. Bash timeout: 660000; pytest with -s; node IDs, never -k; tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py first. Run W0 only after every edit (rule (i)). - W0 (no mesh, -n 2; the new parse node plus the rule-(c) parse re-gates: item 442's parse node, test_wf1_check_family.py (the new good file joins its glob), item 390a's and 431a's no-mesh modules (E1 / E1b / E4 sit in their path; their Run-0 fake nodes cover the untouched quadrature branch), and item 473's page module (the guide bullet)): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s12-W0 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 180 mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_tune_f_human.py::test_wf1_s12_parse_and_refusals tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_tune.py::test_wf1_s11_tune_parse_and_refusals tests/package/test_wf1_check_family.py tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_f_human.py tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_f_human_thermal.py tests/package/test_wf17_tuning_yaml_page.py -v -s --tb=short'" - RG1 (rule (c): every [names.load_study] node): item 442's RG1 command verbatim (this file, item 442 "Windows", 20261014T110438Z_WF-1-s11-RG1.log:12), label WF-1-s12-RG1; the review rules): item 390b's -n 8 quadrature solve (20261012T125631Z_WF-1-s7b-W1.log, 243 s): no line of the quadrature branch moves and W0's Run-0 fakes exercise it. - Before W1: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T fem-em-solver pgrep -c python3 reads 0. - W1 (heavy, -n 8; predicted 200–260 s, ≤ 345 s at the box's 1.32×): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-1-s12-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_WF1_S12=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_tune_f_human.py -s -v --tb=short'" - Price: item 472's W1 on this Study, mesh and width: 203.4 s, mesh 106.5 s, sweep 93.4 s, 9.765 GiB summed (20261015T213534Z_WF-16-s12-W1.log:7343–7344). Wval's node count is the count before the item plus 5 (229 + 5 = 234 if nothing else landed; print it). Wdoc reads 0 dead. - git diff --stat main -- src/ shows src/fem_em_solver/study_yaml.py only. Traps already paid for. - degree: 1 in the YAML. The Study default is 2; a degree-2 copper F-human solve at -n 8 was killed at 590 s (item 472's trap list). (K) catches a missing degree. - YAML floats: write 64000000.0 and 58000000.0, never 64.0e6 (_YAML_FLOAT_HINT, study_yaml.py:115). - femem prints on rank 0 only: read check's stdout on rank 0 and reduce rc through _rc_all; never assert a print on every rank. - -k a or b splits into stray argv inside the quoted container command: node IDs only. - Registry nodes added ⇒ API pages and docs/guide/validation.md regenerated and committed, Wgen / Wval / Wapi / Wdoc in the slot (ruling Q3 of 2026-10-12; item 472 did the same). - Rank-local values: cells and S come through the Study's reduced paths; the Touchstone exists on rank 0 only — broadcast the existence bool. - The npz is a fixture input, not the comparand; (a)'s comparand is step 3's :6366. - Never TwoPortQuadratureDrive for the read (its tune refuses; item 442's (X) row pins it at parse). - Never float.hex across builds (item 442 ruling, :1290); here the identity is the same Study, asserted at EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL, hex printed. - Rule (i): no edit to study_yaml.py, the module, the YAML or the registry after the window that closes on them; a src edit after W0 means W0, RG1, RG2 again. - Status 124 / a kill: pgrep -c python3 first; at 0 only, the rubric orphan-stem sweep, label WF-1-s12-cache-sweep. Never raise a timeout or change -n. - Write ≈, never a tilde. No AED number.

Scope. Covered: k = 1 C_mode from a study file's tune: section on the copper (Leontovich, σ = 5.8e7 S/m) F-human hole, κ off, degree 1, 64 MHz, -n 8, one solve, equal to the same Study's tune() and to WF-12 step 3's H12c reading; run_study_file is femem run's call (cli.py, run → run_study_file). Not claimed: the installed console script or --ranks on this file (not run); degree 2; an h-statement; a tuned f₀, Q, R_in, match, C_in or resonance; ESR; the .s32p or s_matrix as validated quantities beyond (R0)'s tie; SAR / |B₁⁺| / thermal on the lumped_port_drive F-human file (refused, E4); the PEC or solid σ = 800 F-human from YAML (still refused); --estimate (item 480's rc 2 stands); AED.

What a negative result means. Report and stop. Park on attempt/WF-1-step12-<UTC>, mark item 484 BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)), journal it. - (K) / (X) red: a parse defect. Fix in-slot inside study_yaml.py only and re-run W0 (rule-(i) clock restarts). - W0's re-gate modules, RG1 or RG2 red: the edit changed more than the new route. Revert and stop; the review rules. Never edit a pinned row to fit. - (R0) red: the YAML-built Study is not item 472's on the same build route; print the worst column and the cell count, file nothing new until the review rules. - (I=) red: _tune_summary / the JSON loses the ring read. A defect in this item's src; no band move. - (a) red with (R0) and (I=) green: custody of the comparand; print item 472's C beside and report. - (c1) inside the band: a blind comparator. Stop. - W1 status 124: not a result; park with the measured time.

No PREDICTED RED: line. A red anywhere stops the slot.

; src: study_yaml.py only (rule (c), re-gates green)". - §10 U56 marked DONE (provisional until the weekly ratifies). - WF-14: five nodes; API pages and validation.md regenerated. - WF-17: step 6's page loses a statement this item falsifies (one bullet, re-gated in W0). - For the weekly: an EX-115 F-human companion (the 32-port tune: from a file) becomes openable once U56 is ratified; not opened here.

docs.text:
Queued, with three rulings. - The src/ change is licensed under ruling (c): study_yaml.py only, E1–E5 as briefed (≈ 35 lines), disclosed in the commit. Any other src/ file in the diff parks the item. - E1b, not the re-point. Item 390a's pinned row (tests/package/test_wf1_yaml_f_human.py:223) stays unedited and green. An existing assertion is never re-pointed to admit a new feature. - Item 390b's -n 8 F-human YAML solve is re-run in this slot, by its node ID (never a -k a or b expression). The change touches the F-human run branch, and ruling (c) requires a touched path's pre-existing gate to be re-run green in the same slot. The brief's "not re-run, disclosed" is overruled. Two heavy windows never run at once: W1 first, then 390b. If both are not green by minute 40, park on attempt/WF-1-s12-*, BLOCKED in the same commit.

Chain U's provisional count is now 1 of 3. The weekly ratifies or reverts.

The only ESR key in the schema is two_port_quadrature's esr_ohm (F-human non-feed gaps, :428–432), and E1b refuses it on any other route (:383–391). - Run. Even if parsed, run_study_file's four-port branch (:1089–1103) would fail after the solve: CapacitorStudyResult.write_touchstone raises NotImplementedError (study.py:743–744) and its z_matrix is None (study.py:833), which _pairs cannot serialise. - The API needs nothing. CapacitorSheets(c_f, esr_ohm=0.0, on=…, drive=LumpedPortDrive()) (study.py:690–731) dispatches through _study_solve_ports' hook (:614–617) to _study_solve_capacitor_sheets (:747–847), which refuses an F-human geometry, on outside P1…P{leg_count} and an on that leaves no port before any mesh (:755–766). PyYAML's SafeLoader reads a bare on key as the boolean True (on / off / yes / no are YAML 1.1 booleans). A YAML key spelled like the API field (on: [P2, P3, P4]) would reach the parser as {True: [...]} and _unknown would name excitation.True. The schema key is therefore sheets (it maps to CapacitorSheets.on), and a True key in the section is refused with a message naming excitation.on and the fix. Disclosed; question 1 for the review.

The change — study_yaml.py only, ≈ 50 lines. write sheets: [...]"; - _unknown(sec, ("kind", "c_f", "esr_ohm", "sheets"), …); _missing(sec, ("c_f", "sheets"), …); - c_f: _number, finite and > 0, else at excitation.c_f; - esr_ohm: optional, _number, finite and ≥ 0, else at excitation.esr_ohm;
