docs.title: §9 item 491 — 2026-10-15 (§10 chain H27; chain step)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-15 18:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain H, weekly-enumerated (§9 rule (4)), quoted, not changed: "H27 (heavy, -n 8). The 10 g lattice at degree 2 — after entry 35: the 18-point z_c lattice under the two-port drive at degree 2 from the saved -d2 node record, the per-point d1 → d2 move printed beside H18's spread; the mirror gate asserted at C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. Serial on entry 35 (its record on disk)" (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4771–4775). No band, tolerance, record, Done-when or target is set or moved; every band is imported by name.

Drafter's finding: the -d2 node record cannot give the lattice, but entry 35's log already holds it. - The record has no field in it. The builder writes s_node, w, y_in, partitions, p_rc_node, times_s and degree (tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:576–583). A 10 g ball needs E (mass_averaged_sar(fields[key], …), test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py:305). So to compute the lattice from the record, the slot would have to run the build plus a degree-2 factorising node pair again. - That re-solve does not fit a slot. Entry 32 measured the degree-2 F-human (2 570 024 unknowns) at -n 16: build 122.0 s, factorising solve 273.1 s, 89.31 GiB memory.peak (20261013T070008Z_WF-12-step4-H16.log:6534, :6651, :7810). At -n 8 the prediction is ≈ 120 s build + ≈ 400–650 s factorisation, ≈ 89–106 GiB, plus 39 unpriced degree-2 balls. A foreground slot window has to return inside the 660 s Bash ceiling (≈ 590 s container-side; see item 367a's pricing). A degree-2 re-solve at -n 8 therefore does not fit a heavy slot, and this brief never runs one. - What is on disk instead. Entry 35's command runs test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py at FEM_EM_WF10_DEGREE=2 with FEM_EM_WF10_STEP2_SAR=1 (docs/testing/xl-pending.md:1781). That module prints every ball's ccw and cw(M) SAR10g to 9 significant digits (:380–384). It also prints and asserts (iii-a) / (iii-b) at C4_COVARIANCE_BAND in the window (:448–449), and prints the z_c-row spread (:394–397). - So H27 is post-processing only. It parses entry 35's degree-2 table and the degree-1 table of item 359 (same mesh, same 0.015 m phantom, same root). It re-derives the mirror gate from the parsed degree-2 table and asserts it at C4_COVARIANCE_BAND. It prints the per-point d1 → d2 move beside H18's spread. Re-tiered by measurement (rule (4)): smoke, -n 1, numpy and regex, no dolfinx solve. The weekly's "heavy, -n 8" assumed a re-solve.

WF-10 H27: the 18-point 10 g lattice at degree 2, read from entry 35's window, its mirror gate re-derived, and the per-point d1 → d2 move recorded. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: smoke, -n 1, complex image (the module imports tests.validation siblings), W0 then W1. - Class: chain step (post-processing), median ≈ 23 measured min. Cost: ≈ 23 measured / ≈ 35 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + W0 ≈ 0.5 + W1 ≈ 0.5 + ≈ 7 commit / journal / spare). If W1 has not started by minute 40, park. - Depends on xl entry 35 (Friday 2026-10-16 02:00, docs/testing/xl-queue.d/20261016-WF-10-step4-H20.env). This item is queued tonight; any slot before entry 35's log exists skips it and takes the next item. Before any code, the slot runs a first check. All four conditions below must hold; if any fails, mark the item BLOCKED ("entry 35 has not landed a green degree-2 lattice") and stop. Never run entry 35's modules in-slot, and never fall back to a degree-1 file. 1. The record exists: logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437-d2.json on the host (in the container it is /workspace/logs/wf10/h9p-node-118.2437-d2.json; JSON_DIR is test_wf10_f_human_copper_esr_root.py:51, the -d2 name is test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py:135). It reads "degree": 2, and its mtime is 2026-10-16. 2. The window log exists: exactly one docs/testing/logs/20261016T*_WF-10-step4-H20.log (the launcher's *_${SAFE_CHUNK}.log, scripts/automation/xl-run.sh:199; expected ≈ 20261016T0700xxZ). 3. The window passed: its footer reads - Status: 0 and its last capture line is [capture] rc=0 (entry 32's footer shape, …H16.log:7811, :7814). Both test_wf10_step2_tuned_b1_quadrature and test_wf10_step2_tuned_sar10g read PASSED. The docs/testing/xl-ledger.md row for 2026-10-16 WF-10-step4-H20 carries Status 0 if the review has filled it in. 4. The full lattice ran: the log has [WF-10 step2s] ccw 10 g table (18 points) with no REDUCED. - If condition 4 fails only because of REDUCED (the first degree-2 ball took > FIRST_BALL_STOP_S = 25 s): run the item on the 12 z_c points. Name them as the pre-registered STOP subset, which is prefix-independent (_lattice docstring, :64–68). Print "REDUCED (12 of 18)" and leave the dz = ±50 mm move unrecorded. The 18-point degree-2 lattice then goes back to the weekly as an xl ask. - If entry 35 is red, or its log is missing or footerless: BLOCKED in the same commit, and the 10-17 weekly reads entry 35. - Family: WF-10 H27 (degree-2 lattice), attempt 1 of 4.

(1) Anchor — the feed-bisector mirror identity on the degree-2 lattice, re-derived and asserted. - (R1) Reproduction. The module parses the degree-2 table (18 labels, ccw and cw(M)). It recomputes (iii-b) = _relative_l2(sar_m, sar_c, mask) (tests/validation/test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:600) and (iii-a) at the logged c*. Each must equal the in-window printed value within the print rounding: |Δ| ≤ 6e-7 absolute (the window prints .4f %, i.e. ±5e-7). The z_c-row spread per radius must also match the printed .4f % values within 6e-7. ASSERTED. - (M2) The gate. Recomputed (iii-a) ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND and (iii-b) ≤ C4_COVARIANCE_BAND (5 %, test_birdcage_b1_plus_map.py:120, imported by name). ASSERTED; never re-band. Predicted: (iii-a) 0.3–3 %, (iii-b) 0.5–3 % (d1 0.6413 / 1.2789 %). - (K1) Coding control on known data, run first in W0. The same parser and recomputation on the degree-1 table (docs/testing/logs/20261010T171705Z_WF-10-step2s-W1.log:6353–6375) must reproduce (iii-b) 1.2789 % and the spreads 16.7267 / 20.9986 / 18.6041 % to ≤ 6e-7. The drafter checked this with a stdlib re-computation at drafting: 0.0127886 and 0.167267 / 0.209986 / 0.186041. ASSERTED. - Label identity. The 18 degree-2 labels equal the degree-1 labels in order, and the degree-2 c* ball coordinates equal the _lattice(az17, z_c) point for its label to 1e-3 mm (the printed .3f). The az₁₇ and z_c values come from the same mesh, so both tables index the same points. ASSERTED.

(2) Negative control — the mirror gate without the sense flip. - A comparator that forgets that the feed-bisector reflection swaps ccw ↔ cw compares ccw at a point with ccw at its image. On the z_c rows the image of row az₁₇+0 is row az₁₇+90, and 180 ↔ 270 (test_wf10_step2_sar_lattice_coding, :205–209). - Measured at degree 1 from the same log at drafting: the no-flip rel L2 over the 12 z_c points is 17.93 %, against 1.47 % with the flip. - Assert no-flip > C4_COVARIANCE_BAND at degree 2. Predicted [10, 30] %. - Ceiling: this control measures the two-port drive's row anisotropy, which H24 identified (verdict "drive anisotropy", item 422). It is therefore bounded by roughly the z_c spread, and the most separation the degree-1 data show is 17.93 / 5 = 3.6×. No factor bar is set; the assertion is "> band" only.

(3) Tier, ranks, wall clock. - W0 (-n 1, smoke): (K1) plus (L0)-style parser tests on the degree-1 log only. - W1 (-n 1, smoke): the degree-2 parse, (R1), (M2), the control and the move table. Both windows are a regex over two ≈ 8 000-line logs, ≈ 1–3 s each, timeout -k 30 30. - No mesh, no solve, and no mpiexec -n 8. The weekly's -n 8 was a solve price (see the finding above). - Window shape: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-10-H27-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_WF10_H27=1 timeout -k 30 30 python3 -m pytest tests/validation/test_wf10_lattice_d2.py -v -s --tb=short'" This is a bare whole Bash command, foreground, with timeout: 660000. The knob name is the drafter's; the implementer may rename it.

Readout (printed, rule (e); a record, not a gate). - Per-point d1 → d2 move: ccw and cw(M) for each of the 18 points, as d2/d1 − 1, with max |move| and RMS. - The d2 z_c spread per radius, printed beside three references: item 359's 16.7 / 21.0 / 18.6 % (d1, 0.015 m), H18's 14.1 / 17.2 / 18.2 % (d1, 0.0075 m, 20261011T125304Z_WF-10-step3b-W3.log), and H24's four-port 3.21 / 4.27 / 0.78 %. - c*: whether it moved, and SAR10g(c*) d1 → d2. - Predicted: per-point moves 0.5–8 % (entry 32's S moves 2.3–6.9 %); d2 spread 12–22 % per radius, i.e. the anisotropy persists; c* unchanged (r = 45 mm, z_c, az₁₇). - The reading for the weekly: is the per-point order move small beside the drive-anisotropy spread and beside H18's resolution move (−2.6 / −3.8 / −0.4 percentage points)? The 5 % quoting rule is entry 35's (on SAR10g(c*) and mean |B₁⁺|), and this item does not restate or apply it.

(4) Traps already paid for. - The wrong degree-1 table. Difference against item 359's 0.015 m table (…171705Z_WF-10-step2s-W1.log), never H18's 0.0075 m table (367b W3). That is a different phantom mesh, and its spread is printed beside, never differenced. - 16-rank output. The table is printed under comm.rank == 0 (:377), but say(...) ball lines and pytest's PASSED appear once per rank. Parse the [WF-10 step2s] r= table rows only, and assert exactly 18 (or 12 if REDUCED). - Filter after the fact. Never pipe or grep inside the harness command, because the footer then records the pipe's status. - Do not edit the step 2 modules. test_wf10_f_human_tuned_b1_sar.py and test_wf10_f_human_tuned_sar10g.py must not change: entry 39 and H25 read them. Import _lattice, C4_COVARIANCE_BAND and _relative_l2 by name, and lazily (function-local). - No re-solve. Never call build_tuned_quadrature. docs.title: §9 item 175 — 2026-10-02 (chain H, H12b′ — daily provisional, rule (6))
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only Plan agent and reviewed by the 2026-10-02 10:30 daily review. Licence: §9 rule (6), "(daily, 2026-10-02 — provisional)". This is chain H's first provisional step of three; the weekly ratifies or reverts it.

WF-12 step 2′ runs H8a's C-sweep construction on H12b's copper fixture. - Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy, -n 8, complex. - Windows: W1 builds the κ-corrected Cu 32×32 and solves two anchor points; W2 solves the remaining points. - Cost: ≈ 11 measured (chain-solve median) / ≈ 60 predicted min. - Depends on: nothing. H12b landed (6c870ee1, item 169), and H8a's code is on main (a53e1002; tests/validation/test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py:292–650). Neither attempt/WF-10-* branch is used. - Family: a new family, WF-12 step 2′, attempt 1 of 4. It is not a re-pose of H8b: WF-10 step 1d stays at 3 of 4, and nothing here re-runs it. - What the weekly reads from it: does the identity residual that went red on σ = 800 fall under 1e-3 on copper near C_mode? If so, the conductor model was the cause and H12c is worth posing. If it tracks σ = 800's curve, the sheet / κ is the cause. No band moves.

Configuration: H8a's, not H8b's. - P17 and P21 (4 slots on, same ring) sit in 50 Ω, and the other 30 ring gaps carry C. - The σ = 800 comparand at C_mode in this configuration is 3.486500e-03 (20261001T110957Z_WF-10-step1c-W2.log:10647). - H8b's 2.399e-03 (C on all 32 gaps, feeds at Z_th; 20261001T140319Z_WF-10-step1d-W1.log:10658) is printed beside it, but it is not the comparand.

Code: tests only. No src/, and no edit to test_wf12_f_human_copper_matrix.py or test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py. - New module: tests/validation/test_wf12_f_human_copper_c_sweep.py::test_wf12_step2p_copper_c_sweep. - FEM_EM_WF12_STEP2P=1 runs W1; adding FEM_EM_WF12_STEP2P_W2=1 runs W2. - The npz is /workspace/logs/wf12/h12b-prime-held-s32.npz (gitignored), with H8a's keys: s32, kappa, order, cells, meas_tuned, r_tuned, cond_tuned, meas_mode, r_mode, cond_mode. - Fixture: _build_f_human(comm, as_hole=True) (test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py:64), unchanged. - Copper wall: as H12b builds it — z_s = (1+1j)·surface_resistance_ohm(omega, COPPER_SIGMA), wall = _leontovich_term(msh, built["facets"], z_s, omega) (test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:160). - Drive helper: a module-level local copy of H12b's closure _drive (test_wf12_f_human_copper_matrix.py:170–217), with provenance noted in a comment. - It takes specs as an argument. - partition=False skips the volume, surface and sheet power forms. - keep_e=True returns e for κ before del fields. - The wall term goes first in every factorising call's bilinear list. - Imports, inside the function only: underscore helpers and constants, never a test_* name. - From H8a's module: _respec, _circuit_currents, _k1_shares, _circuit_scan, _rule_points, _entrywise_rel, C_TUNED_F, C_MODE_F, SCAN_POINTS, NEGATIVE_CONTROL_FACTOR, QUADRATURE_SLOT_OFFSET, ANTI_MODE_C_PF. - From H12b's module: HOLE_CELL_RECORD, P17_P_SRC_RECORD_W, P17_P_SURF_RECORD_W, COPPER_SIGMA, BLIND_FACTOR. - From test_wf12_f_human_hole.py: _census_checks, _owned_census, _rss_gib. - σ = 800 literals, entered with their log lines from …step1c-W2.log (residual and cond at :10642–10647):

Point C Residual cond C_tuned C_TUNED_F 6.992446e-04 4.608715 on_lo 7.569773860279e-11 (:10625) 2.016987e-03 23.12163 off1 8.834726608692e-11 (:10629) 3.576879e-03 12.51408 on_hi 1.050184374462e-10 (:10633) 6.106169e-03 21.35226 off2 1.130093729141e-10 (:10637) 3.513256e-03 18.61198 C_mode C_MODE_F 3.486500e-03 18.56031

Also enter H8b's 2.399380e-03 (…step1d-W1.log:10658) and the σ = 800 slope +1.0332 (:10650).

W1 sequence: 1. Build, then run (A0) and (iv). 2. Drive P17 at uncorrected widths, all 32 sheets at 50 Ω, Cu, factorising. This is H12b's P17 drive and also H8a's κ column. Run (R), (P) and NEG on it, then κ = terminal_form_deficit(...)["pooled"]. 3. Build the κ-corrected 32×32 in H8a's order, [P17, P21] then the others by number: 1 factorising + 31 held, partition=False. 4. Run the circuit tuning sweep (tuning_sweep / select_c_tuned, terminated 2…31) and the 2 001-point _circuit_scan on [C_TUNED_F, C_MODE_F]. 5. Solve the in-model pairs at C_TUNED_F and C_MODE_F. In each pair P17 factorises (wall + 30 sheets at Z_C + 2 feeds at 50 Ω, all κ-corrected) and P21 is held. 6. Rank 0 saves the npz, then Barrier.

W2 sequence: 1. Load the npz. If it is missing, pytest.fail; W2 never recomputes it. 2. Build, and assert that the cells and order equal the npz. 3. Re-solve the guard pair at C_TUNED_F. 4. Solve pairs at the four σ = 800 rule C values (on_lo, off1, on_hi, off2). 5. Print copper's own _rule_points from W2's scan. If copper's on_lo or on_hi differs from σ = 800's by more than 0.5 % in C, also solve it — but only if the projection build + (1 + n_points) × guard_pair_s + 50 is ≤ 540 s. Otherwise print "deferred, projection X s". 6. Print the reading table.

Anchors (asserted; every band imported): - (A0) Hole cells 369 387 (20261002T094751Z_WF-12-step2-W2.log:6352) within CELL_COUNT_BAND 0.01 (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_sheet_prerequisite.py:57). (iv) is as in H12b (_census_checks, reduced). - (R) The uncorrected P17 Cu drive reproduces H12b's P_src 6.916352890e-03 W and P_surf 8.551752204e-07 W, each within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL 1e-6 (test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py:171). Measured 2.1e-11 / 1.5e-11 at :6387. S_driven(P17) is printed beside 0.383271+0.391623j (:6411). - (P) On that drive, P_src = ΣP_sheet + P_phantom + P_(Ω∖phantom) + P_surf within DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL 1e-6 (test_birdcage_power_identity.py:227). Measured 2.42e-13 (:6353). - (M) The κ-corrected Cu 32×32: reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND 1e-3 (test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py:86) and σ_max ≤ MATRIX_PASSIVITY_CEILING 1.0 (test_port_birdcage_ring_matrix.py:150). - (C) At every solved C, the circuit 2×2 and the in-model 2×2 each have reciprocity ≤ RECIPROCITY_BAND and max column Σ|S|² ≤ COLUMN_PASSIVITY_CEILING (H8a's checks, test_wf10_f_human_tuned_circuit.py:632–650). - (A3, W2) The guard MEAS at C_TUNED_F equals W1's npz meas_tuned entrywise within LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND 1e-9 (test_port_birdcage_four_port.py:165). σ = 800 precedent: 3.8e-13 (…step1c-W2.log:10624). - The per-C identity residual is not asserted. It is the record, printed exactly as H8a printed it: _residual(meas, pred), i.e. ‖MEAS − PRED‖ / ‖PRED‖.

Negative controls (rule (e)): - Asserted: on the uncorrected P17 drive, the identity with P_surf dropped misses by ≥ BLIND_FACTOR 10× DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. This is the same comparison on the same fixture, measured at 123.6× (…step2-W2.log:6353). The ceiling is ≈ 124× (= P_surf / P_src). - Binary: (A0) separates the hole route from the solid σ = 800 route (507 266 cells). - Predicted, printed: the 0.5·C_TUNED_F circuit prediction against MEAS at C_TUNED_F is ≥ 10× REDUCTION_BAND. σ = 800 measured 1364× (…step1c-W1.log:10843). Copper is unmeasured, so this is not asserted; predicted range [300×, 3000×]. - Printed, not asserted: the two circuit routes. - Column 0 of tuned_input's reduced 2×2 against the current route S_i0 = δ_i0 − 2·z0·I_i, with cond(I − S₃₂) and cond(I + S₃₂) beside it. σ = 800 precedent 9.1e-15 (…step1d-W1.log:10654). - CURRENT_ROUTE_CONVERSION_BAND 1e-12 may be too tight for copper's 1 − σ_max = 6.66e-6. Do not import S_VS_Z_ROUTE_RTOL: its module's importorskip("skrf") would skip this test.

Printed against predictions written first: - κ_Cu beside σ = 800's 4.590991e-03 (…step1c-W1.log:10611): predicted [2.3e-3, 9.2e-3]. - κ-corrected Cu 32×32: reciprocity ≈ 1e-14; 1 − σ_max in [1e-7, 1e-4]. - Copper select_c_tuned beside 19.7327 pF: predicted [17, 23] pF. - Copper cond maxima beside 75.70 / 105.02 pF: predicted ±5 %. - The per-C residual r_Cu(C), beside r_800(C) and ρ = r_Cu / r_800 at the six shared C, with residual/cond, the circuit k = ±1 shares and the log-log slopes. - Prediction: "tracks". ρ in [0.5, 2] at every point; r_Cu(C_MODE_F) in [1.7e-3, 7e-3]; slope +1.03 ± 0.3. A slope ≈ +1 in C (∝ 1/|Z_C|) points at the C sheets, which copper leaves unchanged. - Confidence is low, because the gap neighbourhood is meshed differently on the hole route. - The pre-registered reading rule (printed only): - "conductor": r_Cu(C_MODE_F) ≤ 1e-3 and ρ ≤ 0.5 at all five C ≥ 75 pF. - "tracks": 0.5 ≤ ρ ≤ 2 at all six points and |slope_Cu − 1.03| ≤ 0.3. - "mixed": anything else. - Also print the H8b-configuration estimate 0.688 × r_Cu(C_MODE_F), labelled "assumed transfer, not measured". - If /workspace/logs/wf10/h8a-held-s32.npz exists, print ‖S_Cu − S_800‖_F / ‖S_800‖_F. Its absence is not a failure. - The price per pair and per window, and the RSS per rank and summed: predicted pair [35, 55] s, summed RSS ≤ 13 GiB.

Windows. Bash timeout: 660000, foreground. Each harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, never chained or piped. Run with -s. Copy §5.1's durable-capture idiom, trailing ; exit $rc kept. - Measured basis: - build 107.2 s (…step2-W2.log:6352); - a Cu factorising drive, 31.89 s solve + 2.08 s post (:6353); - a held drive, ≈ 0.5 s + 2–3 s post (:6354–6385); - pytest overhead ≈ 48 s; - σ = 800 in-model pairs, 35.76–50.16 s (…step1c-W2.log:10620–10637). - W1: predicted pytest [370, 480] s.

Traps: - The wall term goes first in every factorising call. - Never hold a factor across a C point or across the κ change. Each pair's P17 is held=False, and only P21 is held. A held Cu factor solves a different load without complaint (PORT-19). - Use ctx["solver"] as built. pec_facet_tags=None would pin the cavity. - At C points read only the two feeds' S column. The 5e-5 wall band is still the 10-03 weekly's to ratify.

Write a known-issues entry, park, BLOCKED. - W2 (A3) miss or a missing npz: stop. - W1 Status 124 or > 540 s: the readout is the price. BLOCKED; the review decides the split. - "mixed": report the table and stop. Never refit or re-classify in-slot. - There is no PREDICTED RED line. r_Cu(C_MODE_F) is predicted above 1e-3, but it is printed, not asserted.

docs.title: §9 item 215 — 2026-10-04 (chain H14)
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-04 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

WF-12 step 2″ (§10 H14): are F-human's 32 ring-gap sheets exact? Each meshed sheet is checked against its CAD rectangle at STRIP_BAND, on the copper hole mesh WF-12 uses. The in-run κ is printed as a diagnostic on one degree-1 Cu drive. Target: CAD identity. - Executor: implementer. Tier: heavy, -n 8, complex, one window. Class: chain step (solve), measured median ≈ 18 min. - Cost: ≈ 18 measured / ≈ 35 predicted min (15 fixed + ≈ 15 code + W1 ≈ 4–5 min). - Depends on: nothing. - Family: WF-12 step 2″, attempt 1 of 4.

Already measured on this fixture (read by the drafter; the review should weigh it before spending the slot). Both halves of H14 already have a reading, on the same 369 387-cell hole mesh, the same P17 drive and the same uncorrected widths. - Sheet area. WF-12 step 1 (i) asserted the 32 meshed areas against chord × w = 1.716154044e-02 × 1.000000000e-02 m². Worst case P23, rel 2.220e-15, at SHEET_AREA_BAND 1e-9, which is numerically STRIP_BAND (20261002T020254Z_WF-12-step1-W1b.log:16559). - CAD side. The generator reports 1 OCC surface per sheet, area 1.716154044e-04 (20261002T094751Z_WF-12-step2-W2.log:222, …W1b.log:45). That fits io/mesh.py:4925–4971: a plane surface whose four edges lie on the gap box's radial caps and z faces, i.e. ruling (i)'s "longitudinal ring sheets". - κ. κ_Cu = 4.534948e-03 on the uncorrected Cu P17 drive (20261002T183158Z_WF-12-step2p-W1.log:6357), against σ = 800's 4.590991e-03 and 4.45–5.07e-3 over all 32 σ = 800 drives (20260928T093759Z_POST-7-step1-W1.log:10636). The ruling's exact F-small rectangles read ≈ 1.6e-5 / 1.8e-5. - So the predicted outcome is "areas exact, κ ≈ 4.5e-3". H14's rule does not name that cell: "larger ⇒ rebuild on exact rectangles" would rebuild sheets that are already exact OCC rectangles. Ruling (ii)'s own clause covers it: "a non-zero κ on an exact sheet is a reading, not a correction". - An untested hypothesis, printed only: κ here measures how non-uniform E·ĥ is across a w = 10 mm sheet. That sheet spans the 8 mm tube plus 1 mm clearance either side (io/mesh.py:3885, box width = 2·r_minor + 2·clearance), with circular π r² terminals (ring_terminal_area_m2). That is field shape, not sheet geometry. - What the slot adds over the citations: the full rectangle census below (extents, planarity, width), the per-sheet κ, and both in one logged window.

Code (tests only, no src/, no edit to any existing module). - New module: tests/validation/test_wf12_f_human_sheet_census.py::test_wf12_step2pp_sheet_census. It is complex_only, selected by FEM_EM_WF12_STEP2PP=1, and skips otherwise. - Fixture: _build_f_human(comm, as_hole=True) (test_wf7_f_human_b1_quadrature.py:64), unchanged. The layout comes from built["diag"]["ring_port_layout"]: ring_port_sheet_longitudinal_area_m2, ring_port_gap_chord_m, ring_port_box_width_m, ring_gap_length_m (the arc), ring_gap_z_m. - Imports, inside the function only. Underscore helpers and constants, never a test_* name. - STRIP_BAND (test_ops61_exact_strip_ports.py:58). - DEGENERATE_EXTENT_M, _sheet_extent_along (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_ring_sheet_orientation.py:133, 276). - _interface_area_or_zero (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_port_terminals.py:100, reduced). - _ring_gap_frame (tests/mesh/test_birdcage_ring_gaps_scaleup.py), SHEET_IFACE, _ring_ports. - HOLE_CELL_RECORD, P17_P_SRC_RECORD_W, P17_P_SURF_RECORD_W, COPPER_SIGMA, BLIND_FACTOR (test_wf12_f_human_copper_matrix.py). - _drive and S_DRIVEN_H12B (test_wf12_f_human_copper_c_sweep.py:114, 55). - _census_checks, _owned_census, _rss_gib (test_wf12_f_human_hole.py). - _leontovich_term (test_th14_birdcage_copper.py:160), surface_resistance_ohm, terminal_form_deficit. - Every band comes from these imports. - New helper: a module-local _sheet_span(msh, tags, tag, axis, comm) -> (lo, hi), which is _sheet_extent_along (:276–296) returning both reduced ends. Use it for the centre prints. - Sequence: 1. Build. Run (A0) and (iv) as in test_wf12_f_human_copper_c_sweep.py:274–287. 2. Run the sheet census on every one of the 32 sheets (S1–S4). 3. Solve the Cu P17 drive: _drive(ctx, built, list(ctx["specs"]), "P17", held=False, wall_term=wall, z_s=z_s, partition=True, keep_e=True). This is item 175 W1's block (:356–380): uncorrected widths, all 32 sheets at 50 Ω. 4. Run (R), (P) and NEG on that drive. 5. Call terminal_form_deficit(msh, ctx["tags_f"], d["sheets"], d["e"], comm) and print pooled and every per_sheet value, then del d["e"]. 6. Print the branch line.

Anchors (asserted; bands imported). - (A0) Hole cells 369 387 within CELL_COUNT_BAND; (iv) census none; outer census as in H12b. - The CAD-rectangle identity, per sheet i, with φ̂_i from _ring_gap_frame(i, 16) (it returns (phi_hat, centre)) and û_i the unit xy direction of centre (= (cos φ_c, sin φ_c, 0), the sheet normal at io/mesh.py:4952). Use only the direction: centre's magnitude and z are built from the module's F-small RING_RADIUS / LEG_SPACING (test_birdcage_ring_gaps_scaleup.py:150–155), not F-human's, so R and z come from the layout. All four checks are reduced over ranks. - (S1) |A / zzwxh:0534 − 1| < STRIP_BAND. - (S2) The extent along φ̂ equs ring_port_gap_chord_m, and the extent along ẑ equals ring_port_box_width_m, each within STRIP_BAND. - (S3)** Planarity: the extent along û_i is < klzxh:0539 (1e-12 m). - (S4)** T width the port model receives, A / chord (klwxh:0540's sheet_width_m), equals ring_port_box_width_m within STRIP_BAND. - WhyS1)–(S3) together prove an exact rectangle: th put a planar sheet inside a chord × w rectangle with area chord × w. That means it fills the rectangle, with no ragged edge and no hole. - Printed:** thcentre along û (against R) and ong ẑ (against ±ring_gap_z_m) from _sheet_span; facet count per sheet; the generator's CAD line. - On the drive: - (R) P_src and P_surf against H12b's records within REUSE_REPRODUCTION_RTOL (measured 2.1e-11 / 1.5e-11); - (P) the full partition within DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL (measured 2.4e-13); - S_driven(P17) printed beside S_DRIVEN_H12B. - κ is not asserted (ruling (ii)). It is the diagnostic H14 reads.

Negative controls (rule (e)). - Asserted (arithmetic): the same meshed areas against the arc rectangle ring_gap_length_m × w must miss by ≥ 1e3 × STRIP_BAND. - Predicted chord/arc − 1 = tan α/α − 1 = 1.090e-3 (α = g/2R = 0.0571429, g = 0.0171429 m, R = 0.15 m). That is also the ceiling, ≈ 1.09e6 × the band, and the 1e3 bar sits 1090× under it. - It shows the band resolves the chord-versus-arc distinction the generator itself names (io/mesh.py:3941–3946). - Asserted: on the drive, dropping P_surf misses (P) by ≥ BLIND_FACTOR (10) × DISCRETE_IDENTITY_RTOL. Measured 123.6×, ceiling ≈ 124×. - Binary: (A0) separates the hole route from the solid σ = 800 route (507 266 cells). - Predicted, printed, never asserted: - pooled κ = 4.534948e-03, range [4.50e-3, 4.57e-3] (the identical drive; deterministic); - the driven sheet's per-sheet κ and the 31 terminated sheets' spread, range [1e-3, 2e-2] (low confidence, never measured per sheet); - the branch line will read "S1–S4 green, κ > 1e-4: a cell H14's rule does not name — the review decides".

Branch line (printed verbatim, the slot acts on none of it). - κ ≤ 1e-4 with S1–S4 green ⇒ "sheets exact; H12c proceeds". - κ > 1e-4 with any of S1–S4 red ⇒ "ragged; GEO rebuild branch". - κ > 1e-4 with S1–S4 green ⇒ "exact sheets, κ a reading (ruling (ii)); rule cell unnamed".

Tier and window. Bash timeout: 660000, foreground, the harness call bare and whole. - Measured basis: - H12a W2 is the same build plus one Cu drive with the partition: 199 s wall, build 109.1 s, factor plus solve 39.2 s, summed RSS 9.62 GiB, pytest overhead ≈ 48 s (20261002T020713Z_WF-12-step1-W2.log). - Item 175 W1: P17 43.28 s + 5.08 s post, κ eval 4.44 s (…step2p-W1.log:6354–6357); hole builds 107–170 s. - The census is ≈ 4 reductions × 32 sheets, < 15 s. - Predicted: [200, 300] s wall, ≤ 11 GiB. - W1: scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-12-step2pp-W1 "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_WF12_STEP2PP=1 timeout -k 30 590 mpiexec -n 8 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_wf12_f_human_sheet_census.py::test_wf12_step2pp_sheet_census -v -s --tb=short > /workspace/logs/wf12-step2pp-w1-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/wf12-step2pp-w1-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/wf12-step2pp-w1-raw.log; exit \$rc'". That is the §5.1 idiom as H12a W2 / item 175 used it, with the trailing ; exit $rc kept. - No rule (a) / (c) re-gate applies: no existing module, helper or src/ file is edited.

Traps. - Rank-local geometry. Facet areas and node extents are rank-local. Use _interface_area_or_zero and _sheet_extent_along / _sheet_span, which reduce, never probe_two_torus_conductor_hole._facet_area; H12a used that only at -n 1. - No facet integral with SpatialCoordinate. Centres and planarity come from node coordinates, not facet integrals; any new facet form pins quadrature_degree. - The solver as built. Use ctx["solver"] as built: pec_facet_tags=(OUTER_BOX_TAG,), because None would pin the cavity. The wall term goes first in the factorising call; _drive already does this. - κ needs the field. Compute κ before del d["e"], with d["sheets"] exactly as solved, then del the field. - Imports. Do not import from test_port23_skrf_route_b.py: its importorskip would skip the test. Import no test_* name either, because pytest would collect it twice. - Status 124 is the finding. Run pgrep -c python3 in the container, then the cache sweep. Never lengthen the timeout. No module edit after W1 starts (rule (i)).

Scope. Degree 1, 64 MHz, one Cu drive, this one hole fixture. Not covered: - C_mode (H12c); - any rebuild of the F-human generator — the slot never rebuilds the generator, whichever way the branch reads. A rebuild is its own GEO step, queued by the review; - applying κ; - degree 2, AED, any band.

The decision between H12c and a GEO step is the review's to queue next, not the slot's.

Status it can move. - The §7 WF-12 row records step 2″ as a record: no glyph move, Done-when unchanged. - §10 H14 is answered. Either H12c becomes queueable, or a GEO rebuild step is opened by the review. In the predicted unnamed cell, the review or weekly re-poses H14's rule with the census in hand. - Entry 29's decision rule reads "with H14's sheet census" (xl-pending.md:1513). This is that census.

Negative result. - (A0), (iv), (R) or (P) red: the fixture moved. Stop, park on attempt/, mark BLOCKED (rule (d)). - Any of (S1)–(S4) red: a sheet-geometry finding. That is H14's rebuild branch, measured. Report the per-sheet table, write a known-issues entry, and stop. The rebuild is not attempted in-slot. - The arc control below its bar: the band cannot resolve the geometry. Stop and report. - κ in any range: report it. Never apply it, never band it. - There is no PREDICTED RED line. Nothing asserted is predicted red; the predicted κ > 1e-4 is a printed diagnostic.

Review disposition of §9 item 215 (2026-10-04 03:00 daily review): WITHDRAWN, not queued. The drafter found both halves of H14 already measured on this fixture, and the review re-read the lines. (a) CAD identity: on the 369 387-cell copper hole mesh, the 32 ring sheets equal chord × w to a worst 2.220e-15 at STRIP_BAND 1e-9, and the generator reports one OCC face per sheet (20261002T020254Z_WF-12-step1-W1b.log:16559, cells :6176). (b) κ: κ_Cu = 4.534948e-03 on the same mesh (20261002T183158Z_WF-12-step2p-W1.log:6357, (A0) cells :6352), against σ = 800's 4.590991e-03. So the sheets are exact and κ is ≫ 1e-4. H14's rule reads "κ ≤ 1e-4 ⇒ exact, H12c proceeds; larger ⇒ rebuild the generator on exact rectangles", which presumes κ measures sheet raggedness. On F-human that premise fails: the sheets are already exact, and per ruling (ii) a non-zero κ on an exact sheet is a reading, not a correction. An untested candidate: the 10 mm sheet is wider than the 8 mm conductor tube, so E is uneven across it. A slot would re-measure the same two numbers and act on neither branch. Whether H12c proceeds is the weekly's call (named in the dashboard). No band or target is moved.

What the build environment is (read from the repo; the slot confirms in W1's prints). - pyproject.toml exists. Its backend is setuptools.build_meta (requires setuptools>=61, wheel), with packages.find where = ["src"]. src/fem_em_solver/ holds only .py files, so no package data is needed. - src/sitecustomize.py is a top-level module, not a package, so pip install . does not install it (expected, see the traps). - docker/Dockerfile is FROM dolfinx/dolfinx:v0.11.0 plus pip install of gmsh, pyvista, scikit-rf, meshio, pytest, … and finally pip install -e .. The image's python3 is itself a venv, /dolfinx-env: the OPS-60 record reads skrf from /dolfinx-env/lib/python3.12/site-packages. DolfinX itself lives outside any site-packages, at /usr/local/dolfinx-{real,complex}/lib/python3.12/dist-packages. It is reached only through the PYTHONPATH the compose file and the mode wrappers set. - Network: an in-container pip index versions worked on 2026-09-21 (20260921T093027Z_OPS-60-version-probe.log:34), but this item does not depend on it. It does not see /dolfinx-env's site-packages (numpy, mpi4py, gmsh, pytest, setuptools), and dolfinx is outside every site-packages anyway. --system-site-packages alone fails at import numpy or import dolfinx, which is what the stack .pth is for. WF-13 step 2: Study.estimate() — a resource estimate before a solve (9c). docs.title: §9 item 432 — 2026-10-13 (§10 chain U47; chain step, (9c))
docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-13 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Licence: §10 chain U, "U47 (9c). The exit-gate rehearsal, our half: inside the container, pip install . into a scratch prefix outside /workspace/src, then femem run on the F-small gel YAML from a directory outside the repo with no PYTHONPATH, reproducing MAT4_DEG1_RECORD at its band; the installed version and the public-surface snapshot asserted. Standard. Serial on nothing. (The operator's own run from the docs alone is the exit gate.)" (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4787–4792), weekly-enumerated (§9 rule (4)). No band, tolerance, Done-when, record or validation target is set or moved; every record and band is imported by name.

Two readings for the review (rule (e): reported, decided provisionally here so the item can run). 1. "The F-small gel YAML" versus MAT4_DEG1_RECORD. - MAT4_DEG1_RECORD (tests/package/test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere.py:87) is the lossy gel sphere's SAR, and the committed YAML that reproduces it is tests/package/wf1/sphere_mat4.yaml (σ 0.57 S/m, ε_r 78, sphere_in_box). - The F-small file f_small_four_port.yaml reproduces P1 (an S-matrix), never MAT4_DEG1_RECORD. - The brief reads the step by its named record: the sphere file. The F-small installed solve is already item 293's record (20261007T050226Z_WF-1-s2-W2-installed-f-small.log). - If the weekly meant the F-small file, the anchor is P1 at LEG_D0_REPRODUCTION_BAND. That is item 293 W2's window plus this item's (V) / (S), and only the review can choose it. 2. "A scratch prefix". pip install --prefix=<dir> without a PYTHONPATH is not importable, which contradicts "no PYTHONPATH". - The brief reads the prefix as WF-13 step 1's fresh virtual environment /tmp/wf13/venv: sys.prefix outside /workspace, built by scripts/package/wf13_setup.sh real from a /tmp/wf13/pkg copy. - It is the same route items 220, 293 and 294 closed on.

Build backend and network (checked as asked). - pyproject.toml:1–3 declares setuptools.build_meta (requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]). - docker/Dockerfile installs neither explicitly. Its pip block (:8–27) has no setuptools or wheel line, and :52 is pip install -e .. - setuptools comes from the base image's /dolfinx-env. Version 82.0.1 was printed by wf13_setup.sh's probe on the current image as recently as 20261012T172921Z_WF-1-s9-W9-installed-femem.log:50. setuptools ≥ 70.1 builds wheels without the separate wheel package, and the build has succeeded on every wf13_setup.sh real run since 20261005T022512Z_WF-13-W1.log:60–66 ("Successfully built … installed fem-em-solver-0.1.0"). - The install is already --no-index --no-deps --no-build-isolation (wf13_setup.sh, item 220), so the container's lack of network does not matter. - So the backend check is the setup script's own probe, inside W1. It exits 3 with "NEGATIVE RESULT 1" if setuptools is absent. That outcome stops the item (BLOCKED; known-issues; the unblock is the operator's — add setuptools>=61 to the Dockerfile pip block and rebuild). No separate first item is needed.

WF-13 step 5: the exit-gate rehearsal, our half — the installed package, run from outside the repo with no PYTHONPATH, reproduces MAT4_DEG1_RECORD, and its version and public surface are asserted from the install. - Executor: implementer. - Tier: standard by prediction (≈ 45–75 s); heavy by ceiling, since the inner timeouts sum to 335 s, like item 293. -n 2 for the solve (the record's width); complex. - Class: chain step (solve), median 12 measured min. Cost: ≈ 35 predicted — 15 fixed + ≈ 12 code + W1 ≈ 1.2 + pages / W2 ≈ 0.8 + ≈ 6 spare. - Depends on: nothing. No src/ edit. - Prices: the installed sphere run took 28 s whole (20261010T023356Z_OPS-70-W19-installed-sphere.log) and 41 s (20261007T050136Z_WF-1-s2-W1-installed-sphere.log). The venv-side pytest took ≈ 5 s in item 220.

What is new against items 220 / 293 / 294. Item 293 already ran the installed femem run on this file from /tmp/wf13/run/u18. This step adds three things: - (V) the installed version, asserted three ways from the venv; - (S) the public surface, asserted from the installed package against the committed snapshot; - a rehearsal directory that holds only what an outside user would have: the YAML, plus the two files (V) / (S) read.

Code (tests and window only). - New tests/package/test_wf13_installed_surface.py (venv side). It imports only stdlib, pytest and, inside the node, fem_em_solver, so it runs from the copy in the rehearsal directory, as test_wf1_installed_cli.py does. It is skipped unless WF13_INSTALLED_CHECK=1. It reads WF13_REHEARSAL_DIR, which holds copies of public_surface.txt and pyproject.toml. - (L) fem_em_solver.__file__ is under sys.prefix and not under /workspace; PYTHONPATH is unset; the cwd is outside /workspace; PETSc.ScalarType is complex128 (the sitecustomize guard, item 220). - (V) importlib.metadata.version("fem-em-solver") == fem_em_solver.__version__ == tomllib.load(pyproject)["project"]["version"]. The pure helper _version_violations(meta, attr, toml) returns a list. - (S) sorted(set(fem_em_solver.__all__)) equals the snapshot's non-blank lines, and every name resolves by getattr. The pure helper _surface_violations(surface, snapshot) is the shape of WF-14's (tests/package/test_wf14_validation_envelope.py:86–100), restated in stdlib because the venv cannot import tests/. Its provenance comment names the source. - On green, rank 0 writes out/installed.json with version, file, n_names and snapshot_sha256. - Two control nodes always run (no install needed): (c1) and (c3) below. - New tests/package/test_wf13_exit_rehearsal.py (repo side, read-only on the outputs, as test_wf1_installed_solve.py). - It locates the outputs by WF13_REHEARSAL_OUT and FAILS, never skips, on a missing summary or installed.json. - Its docstring's first paragraph backticks only WF-13, WF-1 and WF-15. - Imports (names only; never a test_*): MAT4_DEG1_RECORD, MAT4_DEG1_PRINT, _closed (tests/package/test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere.py:87–88, as test_wf1_installed_solve.py imports them); WF15_DEG2_RECORD, SPHERE_FILE (tests/package/test_wf1_study_yaml.py:99, :87); L0_BAND (tests/validation/test_mat5_em_coupled_sphere.py:104, 1e-9); MAT4_BAND (tests/materials/test_phantom_material_model.py:222, as test_wf1_installed_solve.py imports it). - Registry (lines added only): the repo-side node goes under [names.run_study_file]. The venv-side module is not registered, because it is skipped in ordinary collection.

Anchors (asserted). - (L) / (V) / (S) — venv side, as above. The repo-side node also asserts installed.json["version"] == fem_em_solver.__version__ (repo import) and installed.json["snapshot_sha256"] equal to the sha256 of tests/package/public_surface.txt, so the rehearsal checked the committed snapshot and not a stale copy. - (P) provenance. summary["source"] == "/tmp/wf13/run/u47/sphere_mat4.yaml"; its sha256 equals SPHERE_FILE's; ranks == 2, degree == 1, family == "sphere_in_box". /tmp/wf13/venv/bin/femem's first line is #!/tmp/wf13/venv/bin/python (item 293's (P)). - (R) the record. summary["mean_sar"]["mean_sar_w_per_kg"] is within L0_BAND of MAT4_DEG1_RECORD; its .6e string == MAT4_DEG1_PRINT; and it is within MAT4_BAND of the closed form _closed. Priors on the same route and file: 5.909e-11 (item 293) and 1.042e-10 / 6.222e-11 at N = 1 / 2 (item 294).

Negative controls (rule (e)). - (c1) planted surface name — asserted by construction. _surface_violations(snapshot + ["_wf13_planted"], snapshot) reports exactly not in snapshot: _wf13_planted. A checker that read nothing would pass a drifted surface; this shows it cannot. - (c2) degree confusion — asserted, backed. |SAR / WF15_DEG2_RECORD − 1| > L0_BAND. Same comparison, same file, installed route: 3.4937 % (20261007T050136Z_WF-1-s2-W1-installed-sphere.log; first read at 20261006T003504Z_WF-1-W1-parse-sphere.log:288). That is a separation of 3.5e7× the band, and no ceiling binds. - (c3) planted version — asserted by construction. _version_violations("0.0.0", attr, toml) reports exactly the metadata mismatch.

Window (one bare harness call, foreground, Bash timeout: 660000). The harness call is the whole Bash command: bare, repo-relative, nothing chained or piped. -s; node IDs; no $ in the command. - scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-13-s5-W1-rehearsal "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'timeout -k 10 50 bash /workspace/scripts/package/wf13_setup.sh real && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && timeout -k 10 15 bash /workspace/scripts/package/wf13_setup.sh complex && mkdir -p /tmp/wf13/run/u47/out && cp /workspace/tests/package/wf1/sphere_mat4.yaml /workspace/tests/package/public_surface.txt /workspace/pyproject.toml /workspace/tests/package/test_wf13_installed_surface.py /tmp/wf13/run/u47/ && cd /tmp/wf13/run/u47 && env -u PYTHONPATH FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 timeout -k 30 120 mpiexec -n 2 /tmp/wf13/venv/bin/femem run sphere_mat4.yaml --output-dir /tmp/wf13/run/u47/out/sphere && env -u PYTHONPATH WF13_INSTALLED_CHECK=1 WF13_REHEARSAL_DIR=/tmp/wf13/run/u47 timeout -k 10 60 /tmp/wf13/venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider test_wf13_installed_surface.py -v -s --tb=short && cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 WF13_REHEARSAL_OUT=/tmp/wf13/run/u47 timeout -k 30 90 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/package/test_wf13_exit_rehearsal.py -s -v --tb=short'" - W2, WF-14 + pages (the registry gains a node, so the API pages and docs/guide/validation.md move; the §9 "Every item" bullet): item 394's four commands verbatim (docs/planning/chunks/WF-1.md, item 394 "Windows"), labelled WF-13-s5-Wgen / -Wval / -Wapi / -Wdoc. Commit the regenerated pages. - No rule (c) re-gate: no src/ file changes. Confirm git diff --stat main -- src/ is empty and say so.

Traps already paid for. - env -u PYTHONPATH sits on each venv line itself. MPICH's hydra forwards the environment. The complex-mode source re-sets PYTHONPATH, which is why wf13_setup.sh complex regenerates the stack .pth after it (item 220). - The venv-of-a-venv. --system-site-packages alone does not reach /dolfinx-env; the stack .pth does (item 220). An ImportError for an image package means the .pth is incomplete: the window is not a result. - sitecustomize.py is not installed. Without the build-filtered .pth, complex mode can silently hand back the real dolfinx. (L)'s PETSc.ScalarType clause is the guard. - pip prints "Not uninstalling fem-em-solver … outside environment" for the image's editable install. That reading was taken from source and never run. Ruling (4) said it "gets no known-issues entry until a window shows it", and named it a lane-1 follow-on. docs/testing/known-issues.md has no entry for it today: there is no estimate, thermal_ball or sphere_tag hit among the open entries. No band, tolerance, Done-when or target is set or moved here. This item is WF-13 step 9 (steps 1–8 are used; step 8 is item 480).

The prediction (drafter's source reading at b8679d22, not run). femem run --estimate tests/package/wf1/thermal_ball_duty_a.yaml should go through these steps: 1. cli.main → _estimate (src/fem_em_solver/cli.py:175) → load_study, which returns a Study on a ThermalBallGeometry with material = None and frequency_hz = None (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:114–132). 2. study.estimate(comm) (cli.py:108) → _study_estimate (study.py:1667). 3. _refuse_f_human passes (:1674). The geometry is not four-port, so the else branch runs, and self.geometry.build(comm) builds the ball mesh (:1680; MeshGenerator.ball_domain, 151 548 cells at resolution: 0.005, item 500's W1a). 4. While Python evaluates the keyword arguments of TimeHarmonicProblem(…), phantom_tag=self.geometry.sphere_tag (study.py:1687) raises AttributeError: 'ThermalBallGeometry' object has no attribute 'sphere_tag'. The frozen dataclass has the fields radius / resolution / wall and the property outer_radius (:1319–1334). 5. _estimate catches (ValueError, TypeError) only (cli.py:109), and main catches StudyConfigError only (:178). So the exception escapes, with a traceback on both ranks (the build is collective, and both ranks fail at the same statement after it, so there is no hang) and status 1.

The earlier keyword arguments (frequency_hz=None, phantom_material=None) are only evaluated, not used, before :1687. The prediction does not depend on the build (real or complex). It is labelled predicted until W0 shows it.

Why the fix goes in study.py, not cli.py (drafter's choice, for the review). Item 480 widened the CLI handler because the API already had a designed refusal (WF-16 step 8's TypeError). Only the exit path was wrong. Here the API has no refusal at all. The crash is an unguarded attribute read after a wasted mesh build, and a direct Study.estimate caller gets the same raw AttributeError. Catching AttributeError in _estimate has three problems: - it would turn every future programming error inside the estimator into a polite rc 2; - the mesh would still be built before the refusal; - the API would still crash.

So the narrowest fix is a pre-mesh refusal in the API, written in _refuse_f_human's style (study.py:526–530) and with the exception type that Study.solve already uses for a thermal-only Study (TypeError, study.py:171–172). Item 480's handler then delivers the CLI contract unchanged ("returns 2 on every rank", cli.py:96–101; module docstring :9–13). The result is no cli.py edit.

Item 507's slot journal asked whether sar / b1_plus / tune on a thermal-only Study refuse cleanly. A read-only drafter answered from source at 9e2dbe7f; nothing was run, so this is no record and moves no status. Its reading: - API. sar, b1_plus, b1_plus_at, tune, solve, solve_sweep and mean_sar each raise TypeError before any mesh: study.py:1875–1880, :1937–1941, :1971, :1040–1044, :171–172, :928–929 and :201–205. - probe cannot run on a thermal-only Study at all: it calls temperature(cooling) without a transient, which refuses at :1446–1447, before the build. That is a design gap, not a crash. - CLI. The thermal-ball YAML refuses tune: and outputs.sar / b1_plus / probes at parse (study_yaml.py:570, :845), so the CLI never reaches the methods. The constructor also drops frequency_hz / conductor silently on a thermal geometry.

No observe-then-fix item exists: there is no crash after a mesh and no CLI path to anchor on. A guard on the three helpers, or a transient pass-through for probe, would be a design choice, so it is the weekly's to pose if it wants one.

docs.title: §9 item 525 — 2026-10-18 (§10 U55b, PRICE_TABLE row for the F-human thermal YAML; lane 1)
docs.text:
Drafted by a read-only agent for the 2026-10-18 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it. Code read on d94320db; nothing was run.

Licence. §10 chain U, U55b (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4846–4847), lane 1 (:4905): "The PRICE_TABLE row for the F-human thermal YAML from item 431b's log, --estimate inside ×2. Standard. Serial on nothing." No band, tolerance, Done-when or target is set or moved. BRACKET (×2) is tests/package/test_wf13_study_estimate.py:31. This would be WF-13 step 10 (steps 1–9 are used; step 9 is item 507).

Recommendation: do not queue; return U55b to the 2026-10-19 weekly with two questions. As enumerated, the item cannot reach its own anchor, and none of the four blocks below is a lane-1 fix. Each was checked against main:

  1. The estimator refuses this file before it reads any row. _study_estimate calls _refuse_f_human(self, "estimate") as its first statement (src/fem_em_solver/study.py:1681; helper :526–530, TypeError, "S-parameters only"). The F-human thermal YAML is an f_human_birdcage (tests/package/wf1/f_human_tuned_copper_thermal.yaml:7). So femem run --estimate on it exits rc 2 through item 480's handler whatever PRICE_TABLE holds.
  2. The refusal is pinned twice: by WF-16 step 8 (tests/package/test_wf16_study_f_human.py:155–156, inside test_wf16_f_human_w0_kwargs_tags_refusals, :126) and by item 480's rc-2 node (tests/package/test_wf13_cli_estimate_f_human.py, on the sibling f_human_tuned_copper.yaml).
  3. The 2026-10-15 03:00 ruling returned exactly this question to the weekly: "whether Study.estimate should price an F-human Study at all" (this file, item 474, :504–506, ruling :515). The 10-17 weekly enumerated U55b, but its block carries no ruling that lifts the refusal: a grep of PROJECT_PLAN.md for refus / PRICE_TABLE / step 8 past :4000 hits only :4691 (a GEO-38 modelling note), :4846 (U55b itself) and :4951 (the pace line naming "the installed estimator's refusals" as landed work).
  4. Lifting the refusal also needs an F-human branch in _study_estimate. Today only the four-port and sphere branches exist (:1683–1700), and the sphere branch would mis-build an F-human Study (phantom_tag=self.geometry.sphere_tag, :1695).
  5. Item 431b's log carries no row. A row is fitted only if it has unknowns and, for memory, peak_gib (study.py:1660–1662). 20261014T020254Z_WF-1-s10b-W1.log (-n 8, :12) prints cells 369 387 (:6283), the mesh wall time 98.23 s (:6281) and the window, 147 s (:6365). A grep for GiB, unknowns, ru_maxrss and dofs in it finds nothing. A row needs a measuring window first, as items 471a / 479 needed (their Wm). That window is -n 8 on the 369 387-cell mesh, heavy by ceiling, and it is not a lane-1 window. Item 472's W1 printed 9.765 GiB summed on the same mesh at -n 8 (docs/planning/chunks/WF-1.md:1362), but for the 32-drive lumped_port_drive sweep: a different route and RHS count, so not 431b's row.
  6. "Price" is undefined for a thermal run. _predict fits one EM factorisation: memory a·N^b and time·ranks = c·N^e (study.py:1653–1671; n_rhs is not priced, :1656–1658). 431b's 147 s is ≈ 98 s of mesh, the two-port EM solve and a CN transient, of which _predict models only the middle term. Item 474 named the choice (:502, :506): price the EM factorisation only (then seconds is the EM solve time, which the log must print separately), or price mesh + EM + transient (which needs a time model _predict does not have).
  7. "Inside ×2" would be true by construction. A row taken from the file's own log sits inside the fit that prices that file. Item 479's ruling labelled the same construction a record, not a gate (:550). The predictive reading is the leave-one-out one, with the row excluded. At degree 1, the fit's rows are P1 / P3 / T49 at ≤ 140 460 unknowns (study.py:1617–1619). The F-human Study at degree 1 has an N of the order of its edge count: H26a's degree-2 count is 2E + 2F = 2 570 024 (docs/planning/chunks/WF-10.md:1237), so E is several times 10⁵. That is roughly an order of magnitude past the largest degree-1 row, an extrapolation and not a ×2 statement.

The same block applies to U61 (PROJECT_PLAN.md:4873–4875, --estimate on the degree-2 F-human file): it, too, meets _refuse_f_human first.

Questions for the 10-19 weekly (no target changed here). - (Q1) Lift WF-16 step 8's refusal for estimate only? That would turn test_wf16_study_f_human.py:155–156 and item 480's node into dated records, re-posed in the lifting item. - (Q2) What a thermal F-human price means: the EM factorisation only, or mesh + EM + transient.

Re-pose, if the weekly answers Q1 yes and Q2 "EM factorisation only" (drafted for it, not queued). U55b′, WF-13 step 10, chain step (solve), heavy, -n 8, complex; ≈ 18 measured / ≈ 50 predicted min. - (Wm) 431b's W1 command (20261014T020254Z_WF-1-s10b-W1.log:12) under a new label, before any edit, with report_peak_rss (collective) and the N1curl count at degree 1 printed. That is 471a's Wm shape. Predicted 150–220 s. - The F-human branch in _study_estimate: build the hole mesh, form N1curl at self.degree with no form or assembly, and use n_rhs = 2. That needs the refusal lifted and item 480's node re-pointed, disclosed. - The row "FH1" (degree 1, -n 8, cells 369 387, N and GiB from Wm, seconds = Wm's EM solve time, never the 147 s window). - Anchors: (U7) N exact against Wm; (E) inside BRACKET, by construction (item 479's label); the leave-one-out P1 / P3 / T49 price printed beside, never asserted; (D2) the degree-2 estimate unmoved at EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL (20261008T200148Z_WF-13-s4-W1.log:212). - Re-gates: item 479's RG1–RG4 and WF-4's presets (debug / dev). - Controls: FH1's N ×1.1 moves the price by more than EXACT_IDENTITY_RTOL; a table without FH1 prices the file outside ×2. That second control is predicted, because no prior measurement exists, so it is printed and never asserted.

If the review queues anyway (not recommended). The only runnable content is a W0 that observes femem run --estimate tests/package/wf1/f_human_tuned_copper_thermal.yaml exiting rc 2 (item 507's W0 shape: python3 -m fem_em_solver run --estimate …, complex, -n 2, timeout -k 30 60). docs.text:
Drafted by a general-purpose agent for the 2026-10-04 03:00 daily review; the review reviews it.

WF-14 step 1: the validation envelope. A committed registry maps every public name to the gate test nodes that cover it. A test asserts three things: the surface is fully registered, every registered node is one pytest --collect-only finds, and a snapshot of the surface fails on a planted unregistered addition. - Executor: implementer. Tier: standard ceiling, -n 1, real build, no mpiexec. The row says "smoke by prediction"; the window is predicted at 15–40 s, and collection imports dolfinx and gmsh, so the window is registered at the standard ceiling and its tier word is re-labelled on measurement (the OPS-60 precedent). Class: chain step, no solve. The class median is ≈ 11 min, borrowed. - Cost: ≈ 11 measured / ≈ 45 predicted min. That is 15 fixed + ≈ 15 for mapping 25 names by grep + ≈ 10 code + one or two windows of ≈ 1 min + spare. - Depends on nothing. It shares the new tests/package/ directory with item 220; the two do not conflict.

The public surface, defined concretely. - The surface is fem_em_solver.__all__: 25 names, src/fem_em_solver/__init__.py:41–67. It is the only surface the package declares at the top level, and the one a study script imports from. - From core: LinearSolveDiagnostics, MagnetostaticProblem, MagnetostaticSolver, classify_residual_trend, HomogeneousMaterial, TimeHarmonicBoundaryCondition, TimeHarmonicFields, TimeHarmonicProblem, TimeHarmonicSolver, build_material_fields, build_mu_r_field, normalize_boundary_condition. - From materials: GelledSalinePhantomMaterial. - From ports: twelve port, sweep and Touchstone names. - Not in v0's surface, said so in the registry header: the sub-package __all__ lists, which hold ≈ 99 more quoted names by line count (core 19, io 8, materials 3, ports 45, post 18, thermal 6; coils and utils declare none). The review may widen the surface to the qualified union (≈ 124 entries), which roughly triples the mapping cost. Widening is a target choice, so it is the review's, not the slot's.

Code (no src/ change). - Registry: tests/package/validation_envelope.toml (read with stdlib tomllib, Python 3.12). It is test metadata, so it lives beside the tests. Shipping it as package data is (9c) / (9d) follow-on. - Format. A header comment, then one table per name: toml # WF-14: public name -> gate test nodes. Node IDs only — no band, record or # tolerance is restated here (§7 WF-14 Done-when). Surface = fem_em_solver.__all__. [names.TimeHarmonicSolver] nodes = ["tests/validation/test_lossy_plane_wave.py::test_lossy_plane_wave_matches_closed_form"] - Node IDs are relative to /workspace (pytest's rootdir), function-level. A parametrised node may be named without its […] suffix, and then it matches any collected id + "[". - Mapping guide: prefer the closing gate of the chunk that gated the name. Leads from grep: - TimeHarmonicSolver / TimeHarmonicProblem / HomogeneousMaterial → TH-6; - MagnetostaticSolver → MAG-14 (tests/validation/test_helmholtz_magnitude.py); - LinearSolveDiagnostics / classify_residual_trend → tests/solver/test_convergence_diagnostics.py (it is reached via last_solve_diagnostics, never named in a test); - normalize_boundary_condition / TimeHarmonicBoundaryCondition → tests/solver/test_boundary_condition_selection.py; - validate_required_port_tags_exist → tests/ports/test_port_definition.py; - plan_frequency_sweep → tests/ports/test_frequency_sweep_planner.py; - run_placeholder_port_coupling_case → tests/ports/test_sparameter_assembly.py (its only reference); - PortVoltageCurrentEstimate → tests/validation/test_port_lumped_sheet_sweep.py; - the S-parameter names → PORT-9 / PORT-11's gate nodes. - Snapshot: tests/package/public_surface.txt, one name per line, sorted. - Test: tests/package/test_wf14_validation_envelope.py. - Pure checkers: - _surface_violations(surface, snapshot, registry) -> list[str], naming each of: not in the snapshot, in the snapshot but gone, no registry entry, a registry entry for no surface name, and an entry with an empty nodes; - _node_violations(registry, collected_ids) -> list[str]. - Collection, by the robust route. A module-scoped fixture runs one subprocess, sys.executable -c <script> <out.json> <files…>, with cwd /workspace and the union of the registry's files as arguments. - The script calls pytest.main(["--collect-only", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", *files], plugins=[C()]), where C.pytest_collection_finish(session) records [i.nodeid for i in session.items]. It dumps {"rc", "ids"} as JSON (to tmp_path). - Why this route. It never parses verbosity-dependent text: pyproject.toml's addopts carries -v, so -q nets to verbosity 0 and prints a tree, not node IDs. And it never nests pytest.main inside the running session, where conftest and plugin re-registration and importlib-mode module reuse are fragile. - Child environment: strip PMI_*, HYDRA_*, MPIR_*, OMPI_* and PMIX_* from it (belt and braces; see the traps). - Tests: - test_surface_matches_snapshot: sorted(set(fem_em_solver.__all__)) == snapshot, with every name resolved by getattr. - test_every_public_name_has_an_entry: _surface_violations == []. - test_every_entry_names_a_collectable_node: the subprocess rc == 0, and _node_violations == []. - test_registry_restates_no_number: every table's only key is nodes, every value is a str, and none parses as a float. This enforces the Done-when's last sentence. - The two controls below. - Printed, never asserted: per name, whether any named node's file mentions the name textually. Predicted 24 / 25; LinearSolveDiagnostics is the exception.

Anchors (asserted). These are identities, which is the row's letter: - (S) the surface equals the snapshot; - (R) the registry keys equal the surface; - (C) every registry node is among the collected IDs, with collection rc == 0; - (N) the registry holds no number.

Negative controls (rule (e): both are asserted by construction, as planted controls with no prior measurement needed). - (c1) Planted unregistered name (the row's control). Run _surface_violations(surface + ["_wf14_planted_name"], snapshot, registry), and also the real path: monkeypatch.setattr(fem_em_solver, "__all__", [*fem_em_solver.__all__, "_wf14_planted_name"]) plus monkeypatch.setattr(fem_em_solver, "_wf14_planted_name", object(), raising=False), then the snapshot check. It must report exactly the planted name, both as not in the snapshot and as having no entry. - (c2) Planted uncollectable node. The child must run with cwd /workspace so that ini file and rootdir apply. Node IDs are then rootdir-relative. - Collection imports every named module. A module that fails to import in the real build is (C) red with rc 2. Print the child's stdout on failure, which -s shows. complex_only modules import fine in real mode (they use skipif). - Never list a probe_*.py: python_files = test_*.py, so it never collects. - Run hygiene: PYTHONPATH carries :/workspace; rule (i) applies (no edit after the last window).

Report it; do not edit __init__.py in-slot. - A control that passes (it reports no violation): the checker is blind. Stop and report. - A collection hang: it is killed at the ceiling and is not a result. Run pgrep -c python3 first, then re-run once with the environment strip verified, then BLOCKED.

There is no PREDICTED RED line.

Inputs, checked on 510f41f9. - tests/package/validation_envelope.toml: 41 [names.*] entries = 41 lines of tests/package/public_surface.txt; 106 distinct node IDs over 36 modules; all function-level (no Class::method). - The registry's own Done-when forbids any non-nodes key: test_registry_restates_no_number asserts set(entry) == {"nodes"} (tests/package/test_wf14_validation_envelope.py:200–212). The chunk IDs and bands are therefore derived by the generator from the test sources. Nothing is added to the TOML. - Docstring census (drafter's grep). - 28 of 36 modules name a backticked §7 ID in the docstring's first paragraph. - 7 carry only pre-plan letter labels: "(chunk D5)" tests/io/test_touchstone_export.py; "C2" tests/materials/test_phantom_material_model.py; "D4" tests/ports/test_frequency_sweep_planner.py; "E1" tests/ports/test_port_definition.py; "E4/D3" tests/ports/test_sparameter_assembly.py; plus tests/solver/test_boundary_condition_selection.py and tests/solver/test_convergence_diagnostics.py, which carry no ID. - No §7 row is named D5 / C2 / E1 (grep of ^| \[A-E][0-9]`→ 0). -tests/validation/test_helmholtz_magnitude.pynamesMAG-14` in its second paragraph.

Code. - New scripts/docs/generate_validation_page.py. It loads generate_api_reference.py by importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, as test_wf17_api_reference.py:62–66 does, and reuses its public_names, load_registry and REPO_ROOT. It writes one file, docs/guide/validation.md, never into docs/guide/api/: that tree's generate() deletes stale header-bearing *.md (generate_api_reference.py:169–171), and its (N) / (G) globs api/*.md. CLI: --out, --check (exit 1 on any byte difference), as in main() at :189–205. - Chunk IDs per node. - Take the backticked IDs matching `([A-Z]+-\d+)` in the node module's docstring. Use the first paragraph; for a module whose first paragraph has none, the whole docstring. - For a module with none, use an explicit CHUNK_OVERRIDES: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] in the script, one line per module with a # comment citing the §7 row or the test-results line the implementer read to attribute it. Expected ≈ 7 entries, as above. Never guess: a module the implementer cannot attribute from the plan gets no override, and the generator then fails on it (below). That is a finding: report it and stop. - Every derived ID must exist as a §7 row (^| \` |inPROJECT_PLAN.md); otherwise the generator raises naming it. - **Bands per node.** - Useastonly, never import a test module (they carry knobs and import dolfinx). Collect everyName/Attribute.attrin the node function's body that matches^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]_(BAND|RTOL|ATOL|TOLERANCE|FLOOR|CEILING)$. - Resolve each through the module's top-levelAssign/AnnAssign, or onefrom X import NAMEhop to X's top-level assignment. - RenderNAME = whenast.literal_evalsucceeds on the right-hand side; otherwiseNAME (computed). Give the defining file as a relative link and **no line number** (line numbers churn). - A node whose body names none renders "— (structural / inline; see node)". That is printed and counted, never an error: bands asserted inside fixtures or helpers are not traced in v0, and the page says so in one sentence. - **Page.** - Aheader and one intro paragraph: the registry is the source; "listed" ≠ "green today", as on the API pages. - Then, inpublic_names()order, one### section: a link toapi/.md; gating chunk IDs (sorted, de-duplicated, plain code text, **no links** intodocs/planning/); and a table| Node | Chunk | Bands |per registry node in registry order, with the node's file linked relative todocs/guide/. - No timestamps, host, commit or absolute path.\nendings, writtennewline="\n". - **Generator refusals** (exit 1, message naming the offender, nothing written): - (F1) a name inallwith no registry entry; - (F2) a node whose module yields no §7 ID; - (F3) a derived ID with no §7 row. - **New testtests/package/test_wf14_validation_page.py.** It loads the script by spec, and imports_surface,_load_registry,_COLLECT_SCRIPT,_STRIP_PREFIXES,node_violationsfromtest_wf14_validation_envelopeandrun_checkerfromtests.unit.test_doc_reference_exit_codes, astest_wf17_api_reference.py:44–52does. It imports names only, nevertest`.

Anchors (asserted; all exact). - (N) The page's ### names == _surface() == registry keys, each exactly once; each links api/<Name>.md once. - (E) Per name, the page's node list == the registry's, in registry order (parsed as parse_page_nodes does). - (G) The committed page is byte-identical to a fresh generate(tmp), and two generations are identical (WF-17 (G)'s pattern). - (I) Every chunk ID on the page is a §7 row. - (B) Every rendered band name resolves to a top-level assignment in the linked file. None is a factor. - (c1) Planted unregistered entry point. monkeypatch fem_em_solver.__all__ plus the attribute with _wf14_planted_name (PLANTED_NAME, test_wf14_validation_envelope.py:45). The generator raises / main returns 1, naming exactly that name. Bash timeout: 660000; -s. - W0 (generate, ≈ 2 s): scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh WF-14-s2-W0-gen "docker compose exec -T fem-em-solver bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace timeout -k 30 60 python3 scripts/docs/generate_validation_page.py --out docs/guide/validation.md'" - W1 (≈ 10–20 s).
