docs.title: Retention policy — logs, journals, and repo hygiene
docs.text:
Adopted 2026-09-03. This document says what the repo keeps, for how long, and who removes the rest. It exists because harness logs were arriving at about forty a day and the tracked log volume passed 110 MB in August 2026; the journals that cite them had passed 70 000 lines between them.

The mechanical half of this policy is scripts/maintenance/housekeeping.py (--report is read-only, --apply performs the sweep, --check exits non-zero when a budget is exceeded). The preventive half is the filter built into scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh. Nothing in this policy edits a log's contents after it is written, rewrites git history, or removes a log that a closure cites.

docs.title: 1. Artifact classes and retention
docs.text:
Ages are measured from the UTC timestamp in the log's filename (YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ_<chunk>.log), not from mtime, so a checkout on another machine reaches the same verdict.

Class What it is Compress Delete Gating log Cited by basename from PROJECT_PLAN.md, docs/planning/plan-archive.md, docs/testing/known-issues.md, any examples/**/*.md, docs/validation/**/*.md, docs/ports/**/*.md, or pinned in docs/testing/retention-keep.txt at 7 days never Non-gating log Every other file in docs/testing/logs/ — failed attempts, reruns, probes, dry runs, smoke checks whose only citation is attempts.md or the test-results.md index at 7 days at 14 days Index (docs/testing/test-results.md) One row per harness run, append-only never never — it is the record that a deleted log once existed Journals (attempts.md, known-issues.md, PROJECT_PLAN.md) Narrative of record rotated to the *-archive.md files by the weekly review, on the line thresholds in §3 never Probe scripts (scripts/probes/) One-off measurement scripts — flagged by the sweep when their chunk ID no longer appears in PROJECT_PLAN.md; removal is a review decision, never automatic

Why citation defines "gating": §4 of the plan makes a chunk ✅ only on an executed, logged, quantitative assertion, and the auditor and log-pathologist agents re-read those logs to overrule a status. Anything the plan, the archive, known-issues, or an example guide points at is therefore evidence and is kept. attempts.md cites every run it journals, including the ones that went nowhere, so it does not confer gating status; the journal entry itself is the surviving summary of a deleted log.

Compression keeps the basename and appends .gz, so every existing citation still matches on a substring search. Readers use zcat or gzip -dc; the Read tool does not open .gz files.

Deleted logs leave three traces: the test-results.md row, the attempts.md entry, and git history. A citation that resolves to a missing file should be read as "expired under this policy on the 14-day rule", and if that log turns out to matter, restore it from history and add its basename to retention-keep.txt.

docs.title: 2. Prevention — the harness filter
docs.text:
run_and_log.sh post-processes each log once the command exits. Runs of consecutive gmsh mesh-optimisation progress lines (ImproveMesh, SwapImprove, SplitImprove, N swaps performed, Total badness, a < quality < b, and the like) collapse to one line reporting how many were elided. Nothing else is touched: pytest output, tracebacks, the set -x command echo, timing lines, and gmsh's node/element counts all survive verbatim. The ## Exit footer records the elided count so a reader knows the log was filtered. Set FEM_LOG_FILTER=0 to disable it for a run whose raw mesher chatter is the object of study.

Rationale: the largest logs on main were ≈1.9 MB each, and about nine lines in ten were this chatter; the filter removes the growth at source rather than paying for it in the sweep.

docs.title: 3. Budgets and tripwires
docs.text:
The sweep reports these; --check fails when any is exceeded (gating-log volume is reported for information only, per the operator's 2026-09-03 decision), which is the signal for the daily review to raise a "Housekeeping over budget" item in the dashboard's Waiting-on-you section.

Metric Ceiling Tracked non-gating log volume 25 MB — gating logs are exempt: they are closure evidence, never deleted, and grow with every closure (≈ 60 MB on 2026-09-03), so their size is reported but never a breach Loose git objects (git count-objects -v size) 50 MiB → git gc on --apply docs/testing/attempts.md 6 000 lines → rotate at the next weekly review docs/testing/known-issues.md 6 000 lines → rotate at the next weekly review PROJECT_PLAN.md 9 000 lines → compress closed §7 narratives per the weekly-review carve-out

docs.title: 4. Cadence and ownership
docs.text:
• Every harness run: the filter (§2). No agent action.
  • Weekly sweep: scripts/automation/housekeeping.sh, cron Sunday 01:45 local (scripts/automation/crontab), runs housekeeping.py --apply and commits chore(housekeeping): weekly sweep YYYY-MM-DD. No Claude session is involved: the sweep is mechanical, skips on a dirty tree or off main, and shares the automation flock. What it can only flag (orphan probes, over-budget journals) lands in docs/testing/housekeeping.md for the next daily review; nobody widens the deletion set by hand.
  • Weekly review: journal rotation on the §3 thresholds, as already specified in docs/automation/weekly-review.md.
  • Daily review: reads --check, escalates an over-budget state.

docs.title: 5. What the sweep never does
docs.text:
• Delete a gating log, whatever its age.
  • Modify a log's contents (compression is byte-preserving).
  • Rewrite history, git filter-*, or force-push.
  • Delete a probe script, an example, or a journal line.
  • Run compute of any kind.

docs.title: Test Tolerance Policy
docs.text: Solver/validation thresholds are centralized in tests/tolerances.py.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• Prevent ad-hoc numeric literals from drifting across files.
  • Keep coarse-mesh, VPS-safe expectations explicit and reviewable.
  • Make future tightening/loosening a single-file change.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Current shared constants cover:

  • nontrivial field magnitude floors
  • ratio denominator safety floor
  • centerline smoothness bounds
  • symmetry absolute/relative sanity bounds

When adding or changing thresholds in tests/solver or tests/validation, prefer importing from tests.tolerances and update rationale in that module.

docs.title: MRI Birdcage + Phantom v1 Acceptance Checklist
docs.text:
This checklist defines minimum evidence required to declare v1 achieved for the coil + phantom workflow.

Status guidance: - Mark item PASS only when linked logs/artifacts are present and criteria are met. - Mark BLOCKED when a required prerequisite test cannot run (for example, environment unavailable). - Keep this file aligned with PROJECT_PLAN.md §7. - Chunk IDs below are legacy (B1, C2, D3, …). Resolve them via the mapping table in PROJECT_PLAN.md §8.

v1 is not currently attainable. Sections covering field plausibility and S-parameter sanity depend on TH-1 (a real time-harmonic formulation) and PORT-1 (port quantities derived from the solved field). Until those land, the underlying numbers are placeholder-derived and no evidence gathered against them can support a v1 signoff. See PROJECT_PLAN.md §2.

docs.title: Required chunk evidence
docs.text:
• B1 — Parametric birdcage geometry generator
  • B2 — Port-face geometry robustness checks
  • B3 — Phantom placement presets
  • B4 — Air-box and boundary sizing heuristics
  • B5 — Region-specific mesh resolution policy
  • B6 — Geometry sanity report utility

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Human logs show required mesh tags are present with non-zero counts (conductor, air, phantom, required port_* tags).
  • Human logs show no overlap/placement failures for centered and off-center phantom presets.
  • Human logs include domain sizing diagnostics and no unhandled undersized-domain failures.
  • Human logs include geometry sanity report output with expected sections and actionable warnings.

docs.title: Required artifacts/logs
docs.text:
• docs/testing/test-results.md rows for chunks B1..B6 with successful exit.
  • Corresponding docs/testing/logs/*_B1.log .. *_B6.log entries.

docs.title: Required chunk evidence
docs.text:
• C1 — Time-harmonic API hardening
  • C2 — Phantom material model expansion
  • C3 — Boundary-condition option set
  • C4 — Interface-aware field extraction reliability
  • C5 — Energy/consistency diagnostics
  • C6 — Convergence/conditioning diagnostics
  • E3 — Quick-look phantom metrics report

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Logs report finite, non-trivial phantom field metrics (no NaN/Inf in reported diagnostics).
  • Material presets and frequency hooks execute without invalid-parameter failures.
  • Boundary-condition selection is explicit and reflected in diagnostics.
  • Consistency metrics and solve-health summaries are emitted and numerically finite.
  • Quick-look report emits status (OK or WARN) with finite |E| and |B| summaries.

docs.title: Required artifacts/logs
docs.text:
• docs/testing/test-results.md rows for C1..C6 and E3 with successful exit.
  • Corresponding docs/testing/logs/*_C1.log .. *_C6.log and *_E3.log files.
  • Quick-look artifacts from example run (mri_coil_phantom_quicklook.json, mri_coil_phantom_quicklook.md).

docs.title: Required chunk evidence
docs.text:
• D1 — Calibration checklist to executable checks bridge
  • D2 — Multi-port drive/termination consistency checks
  • D3 — S-matrix reciprocity/passivity sanity metrics
  • D4 — Frequency sweep orchestration utility
  • D5 — Touchstone metadata completeness + parser cross-check
  • D6 — Port-orientation sensitivity tests

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Port ordering/orientation/area checks are enforced and diagnostics reference calibration checklist.
  • Logs show deterministic driven/passive port setup diagnostics.
  • Reciprocity/passivity sanity metrics are emitted; suspicious cases produce warnings (not silent failure).
  • Sweep planner produces deterministic, ordered frequency grids.
  • Touchstone export includes metadata (port_order, z0_ohm, frequency_points_hz) and loader cross-check catches mismatches.
  • Orientation sensitivity logs confirm expected sign-convention behavior when a port is flipped.

docs.title: Required artifacts/logs
docs.text:
• docs/testing/test-results.md rows for D1..D6 (successful exits for acceptance; blocked chunks must be resolved before signoff).
  • Corresponding docs/testing/logs/*_D1.log .. *_D6.log files.
  • At least one reviewed Touchstone output (.sNp) with metadata lines preserved.

docs.title: Required chunk evidence
docs.text:
• E1 — Harden MRI example CLI/config
  • E2 — Reproducible output bundle manifest
  • E4 — Scenario presets (debug/dev/benchmark-lite)

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Example CLI help exposes expected control flags and exits cleanly.
  • Manifest file is produced and contains at least: commit hash, key parameters, and artifact list.
  • Preset selection is explicit in logs and effective parameter choices are printed.
  • A debug preset run completes and produces expected output references.

docs.title: Required artifacts/logs
docs.text:
• docs/testing/test-results.md rows for E1, E2, and E4 with successful exit.
  • Corresponding docs/testing/logs/*_E1.log, *_E2.log, *_E4.log files.
  • Manifest artifact (mri_coil_phantom_manifest.json).

docs.title: 5) Signoff gate (v1 achieved)
docs.text:
Mark v1 achieved only when all statements below are true:

  • [ ] No required chunk in sections 1-4 is in 🚫 BLOCKED state.
  • [ ] Every required chunk has a logged result with successful exit in docs/testing/test-results.md.
  • [ ] Required artifact files are present and referenced by logs.
  • [ ] Any WARN-level diagnostics are reviewed and accepted as non-blocking with notes recorded in PROJECT_PLAN.md §7.

The fem-em-solver-xl compose service (profile xl, 512 G limit) exists for one run per 7 days, commissioned only by the weekly planning review, which names the chunk and its pre-registered readout. The bash guard (scripts/automation/hooks/bash_guard.py) reads the most recent date in this table and denies any XL command inside 7 days of it; run_and_log.sh appends the row automatically when a harness command targets the XL service. Fill in the last four columns by hand from the log after the run, and commit the row with the log.

docs.title: XL / XXL pending windows — pre-registered by the weekly, queued by the daily
docs.text:
Why this file exists (operator directive 2026-09-13). XL and XXL windows are cron scripts with no Claude session — the only compute in the project that costs no tokens — but only the weekly review may commission one, the queue files hold one item each, and the weekly runs at most twice a week (once a week during the 2026-09-13 … 09-26 wind-down). Left as it was, at most one of the three budgeted XL windows and, some weeks, no XXL window would run. This file splits the role: the weekly decides (it pre-registers entries here — tier, chunk and step, the exact command, the measured price, the readout and the decision rule) and the daily review is the clerk (daily-review.md step 6b: it copies every READY entry of a tier into its own file in docs/testing/<tier>-queue.d/ verbatim, up to the tier's budget — a FIFO the launcher drains one window per night, 2026-09-15). An interactive operator session may do either.

Backlog floor and daily licence (operator directive 2026-09-15). The daily review keeps ≥ 4 xl and ≥ 1 xxl entries ahead (READY or QUEUED for a future night), reports the count on the dashboard, and when short may write entries itself in two classes only — priced-family variants of an already-measured case (same script and mesh; frequency, degree, drive/port set, rank count or one env knob varied) and cost probes (first window on an unpriced case, readout = the price). Each such entry names its licence class. Everything else is the weekly's.

Budget, as the clerk reads it. xl: fewer than six rows with a non-zero Elapsed in the trailing 7 days of docs/testing/xl-ledger.md (nightly Sun–Fri, operator directive 2026-09-13) (killed and 0-second rows are uncharged, §5.1). xxl: no such row in the trailing 7 days of docs/testing/xxl-ledger.md. The next run date is the next 02:00 for the tier (xl Sun–Fri, xxl Saturday) after the budget opens.

Status words. READY — prerequisite landed, command final. PENDING PREREQUISITE — names the item that must land first (an ordinary §9 item). QUEUED <date> for <run date> — copied into <tier>-queue.d/. RUN <log> — the launcher consumed the queue file; the review that finds the ledger row marks it and the weekly interprets it. Entries are never edited after QUEUED except to add the run status; a changed command is a new entry.

docs.title: 1. xxl — WF-7 step 0b: the F-human rung at degree 2, one drive, 64 MHz
docs.text:
Status: RUN 20260919T070008Z_WF-7-step0b.log — both legs rc 0, Status 0, 673 s, memory.peak 106.1 GiB; degree 2 is 3 256 418 unknowns, 347.56 s, 107.9 GiB summed; |S₂ − S₁| / |S₁| = 5.50 % from the two printed S_driven values (ledger row 2026-09-19; marked by the 2026-09-19 03:00 review; the weekly of 2026-09-19 reads it against the decision rule below — branch (c) is excluded, and the F-small 64 MHz moves it is compared with are 6.51 / 2.60 / 4.11 %, entry 4's "Why"). (Was QUEUED 2026-09-13 (operator, interactive) for Saturday 2026-09-19 02:00 — moved to docs/testing/xxl-queue.d/20260919-WF-7-step0b.env 2026-09-15 when the queue became a directory; consumed by the launcher.)

Prerequisite: scripts/probes/wf7_step0_f_human_cost.py gained the FEM_EM_WF7_DEGREE knob (this commit; unset or 1 is byte-identical to step 0). Landed.

What runs: the step-0 probe twice in one window against fem-em-solver-xxl at -n 16: degree 1 first (the control — step 0's solve at -n 8 read 607 039 unknowns, 37 s, 10.93 GiB summed; the same mesh at -n 16 re-reads S_driven), then degree 2. Durable capture, both rcs recorded, memory.peak printed, [capture] rc= last.

Price, predicted (not measured at this order and scale — that is the point): degree 2 on the 507 266-cell rung is ≈ 3.2 M unknowns. From ANS-4 step 2d's measured point (3.79 M unknowns, 290.2 GiB peak, ≈ 1 400 s per drive before factor reuse, -n 16) scaled at memory ∝ N^1.35 and time ∝ N^1.8: ≈ 235 GiB, ≈ 17 min; the probe prints its own brackets 150–350 GiB and 10–60 min and says INSIDE / OUTSIDE. Timeouts 1 500 s + 27 000 s inside the 28 800 s window; 754 GiB limit.

Readout (record, 🧪 — nothing asserted beyond the imported cell band): S_driven at degree 1 and degree 2 on the same F-human mesh, and |S₂ − S₁| / |S₁| — the human-scale order sensitivity, which nobody has measured; plus the degree-2 price (unknowns, solve time, ru_maxrss per rank, summed, memory.peak), banked in xxl-ledger.md.

Decision rule, pre-registered for the 2026-09-19 weekly: compare the F-human degree-1 → 2 move with F-small's own move at 64 MHz (ANS-4 step 2b, our figures). (a) F-human's move is in the same class or larger ⇒ a human-scale S quoted at degree 1 carries that error, degree 2 is the production order at human scale, and this window is its price. (b) Much smaller (an order of magnitude) ⇒ degree 1 suffices at human scale for S, and the human-scale sweep stays an ordinary heavy-tier job. (c) The degree-2 run does not finish or exceeds the box ⇒ the price is the finding; TH-16 (symmetry planes) moves up. Either way no band moves and no absolute claim is made.

docs.title: 2. xl — ANS-4 step 3: the 64 MHz order-matched rung (weekly 2026-09-13, §10)
docs.text:
Status: RUN 20260916T070008Z_ANS-4-step3.log — 16 passed, Status 0, 1658 s, memory.peak 280.8 GiB (ledger row 2026-09-16; marked by the 2026-09-16 03:00 review; the weekly of 2026-09-19 interprets it against the decision rule below). Before that PENDING PREREQUISITE — ANS-4 step 3a. 3a landed on main 2026-09-14, 04:30 slot. The knob reaches the solve, and the flag-off control reproduced 2a″ at its -n 8 record width, not -n 2 (OPS-41). Marking this entry READY is the next daily review's job.)

Prerequisite (an ordinary §9 item, standard tier, tests only): tests/validation/test_ans4_resolution_ladder.py is hard-wired to FREQUENCY_128_HZ (two sites). Step 3a adds an env knob FEM_EM_ANS4_FREQUENCY_HZ (default 128e6; unset is bit-identical) and proves it with the flag-off control — the 0.015:1 rung reproduces step 2a″'s recorded digits — through the harness at -n 2. No band, no record.

Budget: open — three charged rows in the trailing 7 days (09-09 ×2, 09-10) against six. The gate is 3a: the first daily review after 3a lands on main queues this for the next 02:00 (3a queued Monday 09-14 and landed that morning ⇒ the Wednesday 09-16 03:00 review queues it for Thursday 2026-09-17 02:00; Tuesday has no review).

Command (final once 3a lands; the knob name above is the contract):

XL_CHUNK="ANS-4-step3"
XL_COMMAND="docker compose --profile xl exec -T fem-em-solver-xl bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && mkdir -p /workspace/logs && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_SOLVER_PROGRESS=2 FEM_EM_ANS4_FREQUENCY_HZ=64e6 FEM_EM_ANS4_STEP2_RUNGSPEC=\"0.015:1 0.005:2\" timeout -k 60 14400 mpiexec -n 16 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_ans4_resolution_ladder.py -v -s --tb=short > /workspace/logs/ans4-step3-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[XL] memory.peak bytes:\" >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3-raw.log; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3-raw.log; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/ans4-step3-raw.log; exit \$rc'"

Price, measured: step 2d ran this mesh and order at 128 MHz — 592 744 cells, 3.79 M unknowns, 290.2 GiB peak, 5 653 s for four drives before factor reuse. With one factorisation and three back-substitutions (PORT-19) the window is predicted 2 000–3 000 s; memory the same.

Readout and decision rule: as pre-registered by the 2026-09-13 weekly (§10): public — the three C4 classes at 64 MHz at degree 2 against the degree-1 record, every imported PORT-11 gate on the rung; private (docs/private/) — the miss against the AED First Order column. A miss in the same class as the 128 MHz order-matched residual ⇒ the 64 MHz AGREE stands on evidence and its "by mechanism" qualifier is dropped; a materially larger miss ⇒ a frequency-dependent feed-model systematic re-opens as a known-issues entry and a PORT systematics chunk.

docs.title: 3. xl — ANS-4 step 3b: the 128 MHz degree-2 rung on the C4-congruent cut (daily licence: priced-family variant, 2026-09-16 review)
docs.text:
Status: RUN 20260917T070008Z_ANS-4-step3b.log — 15 passed / 1 skipped (the -n 16 record-width skip this entry predicted), Status 0, 1539 s, memory.peak 273.1 GiB, 592 550 cells at h = 0.005 under the cut (ledger row 2026-09-17; marked by the 2026-09-18 03:00 review; the weekly of 2026-09-19 interprets it against the decision rule below). (Was QUEUED 2026-09-16 for Thursday 2026-09-17 02:00 — docs/testing/xl-queue.d/20260917-ANS-4-step3b.env, consumed by the launcher.)

Licence class: priced-family variant of the ANS-4-step3 (2026-09-16) and ANS-4-step2d (2026-09-10) ledger rows — the same module, the same RUNGSPEC="0.015:1 0.005:2", the same generator; one named env knob varied: FEM_EM_ANS4_STEP2_C4_CONGRUENT=1 (GEO-32's congruent port-sheet cut, off in both priced rows). The frequency is the module default (128 MHz, knob unset). The cut changes the mesh by construction (116 118 vs 116 085 cells at the ×1 rung, +0.03 %; the h = 0.005 count under the cut is unmeasured and is part of the readout).

Why (the §10 question it answers): the 128 MHz AGREE was banked on step 2d's degree-2 rung with the cut off, while the degree-1 record it is compared against (2a″) has the cut on, and GEO-32 showed the cut carries the whole degree-1 read-back spread. This window gives the order-matched 4×4 on the same cut as the degree-1 record — apples to apples — and shows whether the degree-2 class spreads (0.1985 / 0.1715 / 0.1946 % at 64 MHz, 3× the degree-1 rung's) are the cut too.

Command:

XL_CHUNK="ANS-4-step3b"
XL_COMMAND="docker compose --profile xl exec -T fem-em-solver-xl bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && mkdir -p /workspace/logs && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_SOLVER_PROGRESS=2 FEM_EM_ANS4_STEP2_C4_CONGRUENT=1 FEM_EM_ANS4_STEP2_RUNGSPEC=\"0.015:1 0.005:2\" timeout -k 60 14400 mpiexec -n 16 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_ans4_resolution_ladder.py -v -s --tb=short > /workspace/logs/ans4-step3b-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[XL] memory.peak bytes:\" >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3b-raw.log; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3b-raw.log; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3b-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/ans4-step3b-raw.log; exit \$rc'"

Price, inherited from the family (scaling stated): ANS-4-step3 ran this RUNGSPEC at -n 16 in 1658 s with memory.peak 280.8 GiB (592 744 cells, 3.79 M unknowns, four drives 1476.9 s); step 2d's same rung read 290.2 GiB. A direct solver's cost is set by the mesh and order, not the frequency, and the cut moves the cell count by ≈0.03 %, so the prediction is 1 500–2 500 s, 270–300 GiB; if the congruent cut at h = 0.005 meshes materially differently, the cell count printed at [ANS-4 step2d] rung h=0.005 degree 2 (c4_congruent_sheets=on) is the first reading. Timeout 14 400 s inside the 4 h window; 512 GiB limit.

Readout (record, nothing asserted beyond the module's imported gates): public — the degree-2 4×4 at 128 MHz on the congruent cut, its class spreads beside step 2d's (cut off), and the degree 1 → 2 move on the same cut (the ×1 rung in this window against the 2a″ record, which the module prints); private (docs/private/) — the miss against the AED First Order column beside step 2d's. Decision rule for the 09-19 weekly: classes within their own step-2d spread of step 2d's ⇒ the cut is not a degree-2 systematic and the 128 MHz AGREE stands as written; a class move larger than the spread ⇒ the cut is a named systematic of the order-matched rung and GEO-32's 🧪 row gains the degree-2 reading. No band moves. The module's 128 MHz record assert (test_the_frequency_knob_reaches_the_solve) is skipped at -n 16 by design (OPS-41) — the ×1 digits are printed.

The 10 MHz point says whether the order sensitivity itself is frequency-dependent the way the miss was: a small move at 10 MHz means the 10 MHz AGREE was non-accidental at degree 1 and the Larmor misses were order; a move of the same size means order matters everywhere and the 10 MHz agreement was at a degree-1 point that happened to sit inside AED's band.

XL_CHUNK="ANS-4-step3c"
XL_COMMAND="docker compose --profile xl exec -T fem-em-solver-xl bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && mkdir -p /workspace/logs && PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_SOLVER_PROGRESS=2 FEM_EM_ANS4_FREQUENCY_HZ=10e6 FEM_EM_ANS4_STEP2_RUNGSPEC=\"0.015:1 0.005:2\" timeout -k 60 14400 mpiexec -n 16 python3 -m pytest tests/environment tests/validation/test_ans4_resolution_ladder.py -v -s --tb=short > /workspace/logs/ans4-step3c-raw.log 2>&1; rc=\$?; echo \"[XL] memory.peak bytes:\" >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3c-raw.log; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3c-raw.log; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> /workspace/logs/ans4-step3c-raw.log; cat /workspace/logs/ans4-step3c-raw.log; exit \$rc'"

Price, inherited: ANS-4-step3 — 1658 s, 280.8 GiB at -n 16 on this exact mesh; frequency does not change the factorisation's size, so the prediction is 1 500–2 000 s, 270–290 GiB.

Readout (record): public — the degree-2 4×4 at 10 MHz, the imported PORT-9 gates on the rung, and the degree 1 → 2 move on the driven column (the ×1 rung's 10 MHz 4×4 is PORT-9 leg (d)'s, reproduced by ANS-4 run1 to 1.2e-10); private — the miss against the AED 10 MHz columns beside the degree-1 one. Decision rule for the weekly: a 10 MHz move an order of magnitude below the Larmor moves ⇒ the frequency trend is an order-sensitivity trend, and the 10 MHz AGREE stands at either order; a move in the same class ⇒ the degree-1 10 MHz AGREE is re-read as coincidental and ANS-4's row says so. The module's off-128 MHz knob assert (every class moves > 1e-2 from the 128 MHz record) is the only frequency-dependent gate and holds trivially at 10 MHz.

Status: READ 2026-11-02 (weekly) — the first branch: C_in(F-clinical-3T, d1) exists, 44.0615 pF by the bracketing pair on P33 (1, +1j) at the grid's 0.28 pF resolution (44.0505–44.0897 across the four series), every gate green; an internal tuning statement at degree 1, no absolute or external claim. The 3 T twin's C5 / C6 are posed at it (C21's body tonight; entry 58 the window, at entry 57's refined node). The sign reading — C_mode 43.9719 pF 0.20 % below the root here, the 1.5 T root 0.73 % below its C_mode — is C26's (the reader with and without r on both twins), not a window. Entry 57 kept. Full text PROJECT_PLAN §10. Was: RUN 20261101T080008Z_GEO-38-C16.log (marked by the 2026-11-01 03:00 review): 5 passed, 5 skipped on all 16 ranks, Status 0, 1 738 s, 39.39 GiB; every gate green; one − → + crossing on all four series inside [43.9719, 44.2500] pF, P33 (1, +1j) 44.061525 pF by the bracketing pair (ledger row). The decision rule is the 11-02 weekly's to read; its first branch reads as firing. Entry 57 refines the bracket. Was: QUEUED, re-dated 2026-10-30 (18:00 review) for Sunday 2026-11-01 02:00 — docs/testing/xl-queue.d/20261101-GEO-38-C16.env, the same file renamed, its text unchanged: the host was down at 02:00 on 10-29 and 10-30, so the file was never consumed. Sunday is the next xl night (Saturday is xxl). Trailing-7-day count on 11-01 (cutoff 10-26): 10-26, 10-27, 10-28 = three, four with it. Was: QUEUED 2026-10-28 (03:00 review) for Thursday 2026-10-29 02:00 — docs/testing/xl-queue.d/20261029-GEO-38-C16.env (the command below, copied verbatim with the Write tool). Both prerequisites MET: (ii) entry 47 green (10-27, every gate, 20261027T070008Z_GEO-38-C11.log; its 64×64 at logs/geo38/c11-cu-s64-d1-128mhz.npz, C12's C11_SAVE_PATH) and C15 DONE (§9 item 655; c15-c-mode-d1-128mhz.json, C_mode 43.9719 pF). Grid (8 nodes, written by this review): 42.7000, 43.2000, 43.4500, 43.6000, 43.7400, 43.9719, 44.2500, 44.7000 pF — C15's centre and seven nodes from −2.9 % to +1.7 % of it, densest where entry 51 put the 1.5 T root (0.73 % below its C_mode), spacing 0.34–1.14 %. Every node's printed .12e capacitance was checked against the private-leak guard's reference set before queueing (none informative except the centre, which is clear), because entry 51's log was held on its own node line (see entry 51). Re-priced from entries 46 / 51 (same module family, -n 16): 1.5 T node pairs 196–223 s on U₁ 1 525 193 ⇒ ≈ 0.91× on U₁ 1 425 765 ≈ 180–205 s per node; t_b 376.9 s (entry 47, this mesh); Z50 pair ≈ 175–185 s ⇒ predicted ≈ 2 050–2 300 s, 40–50 GiB; readout brackets window [1 200, 5 400] s, memory.peak [25, 90] GiB. Trailing-7-day count on 10-29: 10-23, 25, 26, 27, 28 = five, six with it. Was: PENDING PREREQUISITE — (i) MET 2026-10-22 (§9 item 595, C12: tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_3t_esr_root.py, knobs FEM_EM_GEO38_C12 = build / 1, FEM_EM_GEO38_C12_NODES_PF, degree unset ⇒ 1; build-only green at -n 2: census 64, U₁ 1 425 765); (ii) entry 47 green (Tuesday 10-27) and C15 (the 3 T C_mode(k = 1) from entry 47's saved 64×64 through C10's reader — §10 chain C, a lane-1 slot step the 10-27 03:00 review queues; its JSON is this entry's grid centre). The 10-28 03:00 review, reading entry 47 and C15, writes the command with a fixed 6–8-node grid (≤ 4 decimals in pF) around C15's prediction, -n 16, marks READY, and queues it into xl-queue.d/20261029-GEO-38-C16.env (trailing-7-day count on 10-29: 10-25, 26, 27, 28, 29 = five). If either prerequisite is missing by then, 10-29 goes unspent or to a priced-family variant (step 6b rule 4).

Why: chain C's step 4 on the 3 T twin — the first tuning statement at 128 MHz on a clinical fixture, by the route that found F-human's root (H17 / H26) and F-clinical-1.5T's (entry 46).

Price (to be read from entries 46 and 47): one degree-1 factorisation per node on U₁ 1 425 765 (0.935× entry 46's unknowns ⇒ ≈ 0.91× its per-node time at exponent 1.433) plus the Z50 pair, 6–8 nodes ⇒ predicted (6–8) × t_node + t_b; memory ≈ entry 47's peak. Re-priced by the READY review from entry 46's measured per-node time. Timeout 14 400 s; 512 GiB limit.

Readout (H26a's root-finding route asserted at its imported bands — (A0), the port census 64 and U₁, (Z50) and (P50) on the Z50 pair, NEG, (P_RC) at each node): C_in(F-clinical-3T, d1) beside C15's circuit prediction, the sign and size of Im Y_in at each node, per-node time and RSS; the node JSON saved under the gitignored /workspace/logs/geo38/.

Decision rule (pre-registered; the first weekly after the window reads it): one − → + crossing of Im Y_in inside the grid's own resolution ⇒ C_in(F-clinical-3T, d1) exists and the 3 T twin's C5 / C6 are posed at it; no crossing ⇒ a known-issues entry and one re-centre from the measured slopes before any second window; a gate red ⇒ a known-issues entry on the clinical-scale ESR sheet at 128 MHz. No band moves.

Command (entry 51's durable-capture shape with C12's module and knobs, written 2026-10-28 03:00 review; the clerk copied it verbatim):

XL_CHUNK="GEO-38-C16"
XL_COMMAND="docker compose --profile xl exec -T fem-em-solver-xl bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && mkdir -p /workspace/logs /workspace/logs/geo38 && R=/workspace/logs/geo38-c16-raw.log && { echo [orphans-before]; pgrep -c python3; true; } > \$R 2>&1; PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_SOLVER_PROGRESS=2 FEM_EM_GEO38_C12=1 FEM_EM_GEO38_C12_NODES_PF=42.7000,43.2000,43.4500,43.6000,43.7400,43.9719,44.2500,44.7000 timeout -k 60 14400 mpiexec -n 16 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_3t_esr_root.py -v -s --tb=short >> \$R 2>&1; rc=\$?; { echo [orphans-after]; pgrep -c python3; true; } >> \$R 2>&1; echo \"[XL] memory.peak bytes:\" >> \$R; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak >> \$R; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> \$R; cat \$R; exit \$rc'"

No XL_OUTPUTS: the node JSONs (logs/geo38/c12-node-<pF>-128mhz.json) are gitignored. Not exercised before: C12's 1 branch has never run (item 595 stopped at build-only); it composes C4a's _run_nodes, which ran green in entries 46 and 51.

docs.title: 50. xxl (Saturday 2026-10-31) — GEO-38 C5a: one degree-2 node on F-clinical-1.5T — the degree-2 cost probe, -n 16 (weekly 2026-10-24, §10 chain C5a; cost probe, priced from entry 32's F-human degree-2 column and entry 40's exponent)
docs.text:
Status: READ 2026-10-31 (weekly) — the first branch: the clinical degree-2 column is priced. Tier ruled (the rule's letter plus the memory clause it did not write): a root grid runs on xl at ≤ 3 nodes per window (entry 53's shape); an OOM on xl moves the family to xxl at the same ≤ 3 nodes with no xl re-run; the column set (entry 54) and any root-node column set (C19) are xxl. Entries 53 and 54 kept as written. (Z50) is not an asserted gate at degree 2 — the Readout below is read against the module's asserts. Full text PROJECT_PLAN §10. Was: RUN 2026-10-31 20261031T070008Z_GEO-38-C5a.log — Status 0, 6 315 s, 472.42 GiB memory.peak (xxl-ledger.md row, 10:30 review): every asserted gate green; the clinical degree-2 column is priced. The first branch reads as firing; node pair 3 056.9 s is under 1 h, so the rule's tier reads xl, at 92 % of its memory limit. The 10-31 weekly rules. Im Y_in is +5.389409e-02 S at the degree-1 root, so on degree-1's shape the degree-2 root lies below it (entries 53, 54; this one node alone gives a sign, not a root). (Z50) is printed only at degree 2 (module :678), so "(Z50)" in the Readout below is not one of the gates this window asserts, the correction entry 39 had and this entry never got; read "every gate green" against the module's asserts. Was: QUEUED 2026-10-30 (18:00 review) for Saturday 2026-10-31 02:00 — docs/testing/xxl-queue.d/20261031-GEO-38-C5a.env. Node 193.5996 pF (entry 51's crossing 193.599624 at four decimals; the fallback does not apply, entry 51 ran green). The 10-29 03:00 review named for this never ran (outage, journal §1), and the night is still ahead, so this review wrote it. The node's printed forms were checked against the private-leak guard's reference set before queueing, clear. xxl trailing-7-day count on 10-31: nothing since 10-24. Was: PENDING PREREQUISITE — re-conditioned 2026-10-26 by the weekly: the node is entry 51's refined crossing (Wednesday 10-28; the 10-28 03:00 review reads it), fallback 193.5178 pF (entry 46's interpolation) if entry 51 is red or killed. The 10-29 03:00 review writes the node into the command, marks READY and queues it into xxl-queue.d/20261031-GEO-38-C5a.env. Entry 46 was read first branch (every gate green, one crossing), so the "red on a gate" clause does not fire. Was: PENDING PREREQUISITE — entry 46's reading (Monday 10-26 02:00 → the 10-26 weekly / 10-27 03:00 review). (i) MET 2026-10-20 (§9 item 561, C4a: tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_esr_root.py, knobs FEM_EM_GEO38_C4 = build / 1, FEM_EM_GEO38_C4_NODES_PF, FEM_EM_GEO38_C4_DEGREE; build-only at -n 2 asserted U₂ = 2E + 2F = 7 885 674). (ii) the node: C_in(F-clinical, d1) if entry 46 finds a crossing, else C10's 195.0265 pF — one node only. The 10-27 03:00 review writes the node into the command, marks READY and queues it into xxl-queue.d/20261031-GEO-38-C5a.env (the xxl trailing-7-day count on 10-31 is one: nothing since 10-24). If entry 46 is red on a gate (not merely "no crossing"), 10-31 is not spent on this entry.

Why: the operator's ladder step (5) — degree 2 on xl / xxl, priced by step 1 — has no measured degree-2 price on the clinical fixture; the 10-21 weekly's re-read (the module's 1 061 s / 231–405 GiB used F-human's exponent 0.84; at the measured 1.433 the degree-2 column is ≈ 1 774 s, xxl-only) is a projection. One degree-2 factorisation with the Z50 pair on it is the smallest window that measures it, and it runs on the route C5 proper will use.

Price (measured in the family; scaling stated): entry 32 — one degree-2 copper column on F-human (2 570 024 unknowns) at -n 16: 514 s window, build 122.0 s, factorising drive 287.1 s, memory.peak 89.31 GiB (20261013T070008Z_WF-12-step4-H16.log). This fixture has 7 885 674 degree-2 unknowns (3.07×); with the factorisation's time scaling N^1.5–2.0 and memory N^1.2–1.5 the drive is 1 550–2 700 s and 340–480 GiB, the build gmsh-serial ≈ 350 s (entry 44), the Z50 pair two solves on one factorisation (≤ 60 s) ⇒ predicted 1 900–3 100 s, 340–480 GiB; readout brackets window [1 200, 7 200] s, memory.peak [200, 700] GiB. Timeout 14 400 s; 754 GiB limit. Killed or OOM ⇒ the last flushed phase line (build / assembly / factorisation) is the lower bound and the price is recorded as "above N GiB at 16 ranks"; the step returns to the weekly (a rank-count or quarter-symmetry route is then the question, TH-20's precedent).

Readout (record; C4a's gates asserted at their imported bands at the one node — (A0), census 64, U₂ 7 885 674 exact, (Z50), (P50), NEG, (P_RC)): Im Y_in at the node at degree 2 beside entry 46's degree-1 value at the same capacitance (the order move of the admittance, printed); build / assembly / factorisation / solve times, RSS per rank and summed, memory.peak — the price is the readout.

Decision rule (pre-registered; the first weekly after the window reads it): every gate green ⇒ the clinical degree-2 column is priced; C5 proper (the degree-2 root grid, then the degree-2 column set) is tiered from it — xxl if a node costs > 1 h, otherwise xl; a gate red ⇒ a known-issues entry (the first degree-2 red on the clinical fixture), price as a record; killed / OOM ⇒ as above. No band moves.

Command (entry 46's durable-capture shape with C4a's module and knobs on the xxl profile and service; the 2026-10-30 18:00 review filled the node and copied it verbatim):

XL_CHUNK="GEO-38-C5a"
XL_COMMAND="docker compose --profile xxl exec -T fem-em-solver-xxl bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && mkdir -p /workspace/logs /workspace/logs/geo38 && R=/workspace/logs/geo38-c5a-xxl-raw.log && { echo [orphans-before]; pgrep -c python3; true; } > \$R 2>&1; PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_SOLVER_PROGRESS=2 FEM_EM_GEO38_C4=1 FEM_EM_GEO38_C4_NODES_PF=\"193.5996\" FEM_EM_GEO38_C4_DEGREE=2 timeout -k 60 14400 mpiexec -n 16 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_esr_root.py -v -s --tb=short >> \$R 2>&1; rc=\$?; { echo [orphans-after]; pgrep -c python3; true; } >> \$R 2>&1; echo \"[XL] memory.peak bytes:\" >> \$R; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak >> \$R; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> \$R; cat \$R; exit \$rc'"

No XL_OUTPUTS: the node JSON is gitignored.

docs.title: 51. xl (Wednesday 2026-10-28) — GEO-38 C4r: entry 46's root bracket refined to 0.25 pF on F-clinical-1.5T, degree 1, -n 16 (daily 2026-10-26 03:00, step 6b rule 4 — priced-family variant of entry 46, one named knob varied: FEM_EM_GEO38_C4_NODES_PF)
docs.text:
Status: READ 2026-10-31 (weekly) — branch 1: C_in(F-clinical-1.5T, d1) = 193.5996 pF at 0.25 pF resolution is the record; entry 46's 193.5178 sat 0.042 % low (Im Y_in convex across the old bracket), so on every root grid from tonight the bracketing pair's interpolation is the reading, never a multi-point linear fit. The 193.5996 node in entries 48 / 50 / 52 is ratified. The held log is the operator's to land. Full text PROJECT_PLAN §10. Was: RUN 2026-10-28 20261028T070008Z_GEO-38-C4r.log — held by the private-leak guard in the gitignored logs/leak-held/ (a false match on one input-echo line, :13037; the operator rules on landing it). Status 0, 1452 s, 48.49 GiB, every gate green; P33 (1, +1j) crosses once in [193.50, 193.75] at 193.599624 pF ⇒ branch 1 (ledger row; log-pathologist, COUNTABLE). Entry 50's node is written from it on 10-29. Was: KEPT 2026-10-26 (weekly): not withdrawn — the root's precision is inherited by entries 50 / C5 / C6, and the family is priced; the refined crossing is entry 50's node (entry 50's status). The decision rule's first bullet is read with that: entry 50's node is written on 10-29 from this window, not on 10-27 from entry 46. Was: QUEUED 2026-10-26 (03:00 review) for Wednesday 2026-10-28 02:00 — docs/testing/xl-queue.d/20261028-GEO-38-C4r.env (copied verbatim from the command below with the Write tool). The 10-26 weekly may withdraw it by deleting that file before 10-28 02:00; if it does, the night goes unspent. Written under the daily's variant licence because entry 48 cannot run (its =1 branch is a stub, entry 48's status) and the 10-28 night would otherwise idle. Trailing-7-day count on 10-28 (cutoff 10-22): 10-22, 23, 25, 26, 27 = five charged, six with it.

Why: chain C4's question is C_in(F-clinical, d1), and entry 46 answered it on its coarsest low interval. The crossing lies between 192.5000 and 194.0000 pF (1.5 pF ≈ 0.77 %, one node below it), and the interpolated 193.517801 pF rests on two points (20261026T070008Z_GEO-38-C4.log:14152). Entry 50 (C5a, xxl 10-31) takes C_in(d1) as its degree-2 node, and C5 / C6 are posed at it. So the root's precision is what the next three windows inherit. Four nodes inside the bracket read the crossing at 0.25 pF (≈ 0.13 %) and show whether Im Y_in is linear across it. This window poses no new physics, no new fixture and no band.

Price (measured in the family; scaling stated): entry 46 on the same mesh, module and -n 16: t_b 357.7 s, Z50 pair 203.3 s, node pairs 196.3–214.5 s (:14156), memory.peak 49.07 GiB (:14211). Four nodes plus the Z50 pair is ≈ 358 + 203 + 4 × 205 ⇒ predicted ≈ 1 350–1 450 s, 45–55 GiB; readout brackets window [800, 3 600] s, memory.peak [30, 90] GiB. Timeout 14 400 s; 512 GiB limit.

Grid (4 nodes, ≤ 4 decimals in pF, none equal to an entry-46 node, so no entry-46 node JSON is overwritten): 193.0000, 193.2500, 193.5000, 193.7500.

Readout (record; C4a's gates asserted at their imported bands, as in entry 46: (A0), census 64, U₁ 1 525 193, (Z50), (P50), NEG on the Z50 pair, (P_RC) at each node): - Im Y_in at each node on all four series (P33 / P41 × (1, ±1j)). - The module's interpolated root on the recorded series. Beside it, entry 46's 193.517801 pF, and the root from a linear fit through the six points 192.5000 … 194.0000 (entry 46's two plus these four), computed by the reading review from the node JSONs. - Whether either counter-handed series crosses in [193.0, 193.75]. - Per-node times and memory.peak.

Decision rule (pre-registered; the first weekly after the window reads it): - Every gate green and one crossing inside [193.0, 193.75] ⇒ C_in(F-clinical, d1) is recorded at this grid's resolution, beside entry 46's interpolation. Entry 50's node is written on 10-27 from entry 46, before this window runs. The 10-28 weekly reads the two values against each other. - Every gate green and the crossing outside [193.0, 193.75] (that is, in [192.5, 193.0] or [193.75, 194.0]) ⇒ entry 46's interpolation is off by more than 0.25 pF. The bracket is recorded, and no second window is bought. - A gate red where entry 46's was green ⇒ a known-issues entry on the module's reproducibility at -n 16.

No band moves.

XL_COMMAND="docker compose --profile xl exec -T fem-em-solver-xl bash -lc 'cd /workspace && source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode && mkdir -p /workspace/logs /workspace/logs/geo38 && R=/workspace/logs/geo38-c4r-raw.log && { echo [orphans-before]; pgrep -c python3; true; } > \$R 2>&1; PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src:/workspace FEM_EM_REQUIRE_COMPLEX=1 FEM_EM_SOLVER_PROGRESS=2 FEM_EM_GEO38_C4=1 FEM_EM_GEO38_C4_NODES_PF=193.0000,193.2500,193.5000,193.7500 timeout -k 60 14400 mpiexec -n 16 python3 -m pytest tests/environment/test_complex_mode.py tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_esr_root.py -v -s --tb=short >> \$R 2>&1; rc=\$?; { echo [orphans-after]; pgrep -c python3; true; } >> \$R 2>&1; echo \"[XL] memory.peak bytes:\" >> \$R; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak >> \$R; echo \"[capture] rc=\$rc\" >> \$R; cat \$R; exit \$rc'"

docs.title: 52. xl (Tuesday 2026-11-03; was Sunday 11-01, which entry 49 takes after the outage) — GEO-38 C6: the ASTM-box-loaded F-clinical-1.5T under the two-port drive at the degree-1 root, no rod — |B₁⁺| and the located 10 g hotspot, -n 8 (weekly 2026-10-26, §10 chain C6; entry 45's family — the same mesh with the rod mapped to gel)
docs.text:
Status: RUN 20261103T080009Z_GEO-38-C6.log (2026-11-03 02:00, 868 s, Status 0; ledger row filled by the 2026-11-03 03:00 review; the 11-04 weekly reads it and poses C7 and prices entries 58 / 59). Ratified 2026-10-31 (weekly): the sense (the target is mean |B₁⁺|_ccw, ccw = (1, −1j); the body runs the lattice under ccw and prints the (1, +1j) ball at c* — "(1, +1j)" in the 10-26 text was the label of the series the root was read on), the 10-28 18:00 daily's 18-point lattice, and the coverage identity on tags (3, 403) with no conductor limit. The command and node stand. QUEUED 2026-10-31 (03:00 review) for Tuesday 2026-11-03 02:00 — docs/testing/xl-queue.d/20261103-GEO-38-C6.env, the command below copied verbatim (both lines matched against this file, bash -n clean). Trailing-7-day count on 11-03, cutoff 10-28: 10-28, 11-01, 11-02 = three, four with it. §9 item 701 (C6a‴) DONE 2026-10-31, 04:30 slot: _run_box ran end to end on stubs at -n 1 / -n 2 (20261031T093245Z_GEO-38-C6a-W0b-r4.log), so this file stands and the first-run risk narrows to _drive and the factorisation. Was: READY (2026-10-30 19:30 slot, §9 item 694 landed: the 1 branch is composed, K1–K7 green, 20261031T003506Z_GEO-38-C6a-W0b-r3.log). The command below is written and final. Two wording points for the 10-31 weekly (GEO-38.md "Review ruling 2026-10-30 18:00"): the lattice runs under ccw = (1, −1j), the weekly's "(1, +1j)" printed beside it at c*, because "(1, +1j)" and "|B₁⁺|_ccw" are opposite senses on this pair; coverage (i) runs on the gel as tags (3, 403), with no conductor limit on the ball. Was: PENDING PREREQUISITE — (2026-10-30, §9 item 693: the module and its build branch landed, but its 1 branch still raises NotImplementedError, so (i)'s readouts are not composed and a command written today would stop at once; (ii) met. Not READY until a step composes them.) (i) §10 C6a (a slot step, no solve → standard, build-only at -n 2): a module tests/validation/test_geo38_f_clinical_box_loaded.py (knob FEM_EM_GEO38_C6 = build / 1, the node knob as I36b's) that takes I36b's arm R — GEO-36 step 8's rod-in-ASTM-box mesh (1 217 025 cells, U₁ 1 606 744) with tag 403 mapped to gel, I41's route — under the (1, +1j) quadrature drive on P33 / P41 with r = 0.2 Ω on all 64 gaps, and composes WF-10 step 4's readouts on the box: mean |B₁⁺|cw over theox's 18-point lattice, the located 10 g hotspot (mass_averaged_sar on the box's balls), the coverage identity (i); (ii) I36b landed** (the arm-R route it imports). **The first review after both land writes the command in entry 45's shape with the module and knob at -n 8,arks READY and queues it into xl-queue.d/20261101-GEO-38-C6.env** (the Sunday night; trailing-7-day count on 11-01: 10-27, 28, 29, 30 = four, five with it). If either prerequisite is missing by the 10-31 18:00 review, the 11-01 night goes to a priced-family variant under the daily's licence or unspent, and this entry waits.

Why: chain C's step 6 — the ASTM box loaded, |B₁⁺|, 1 g / 10 g SAR, a located hotspot — on the fixture the 2026-10-14 directive names for all new human-scale work, at the root entry 46 found; the first clinical-scale safety quantity, and the fixture C7 (the ANS case) is posed on. The rod-in-box mesh is reused because its box is the ASTM load (I33 placed it as the standard places it); mapping the rod to gel is I41's gated route, so no new mesh is bought.

Price (measured in the family; scaling stated): entry 45 on the same mesh at -n 8: t_b 458.2 s, one factorising column 277.8 s, held 2.06 s, 41.76 GiB; entry 41's SAR / |B₁⁺| post-processing on F-human (369 387 cells) 82.4 s. One factorisation with two held columns plus the box's lattice and balls ⇒ predicted ≈ 850–1 000 s, 42–50 GiB; readout brackets window [600, 2 400] s, memory.peak [30, 120] GiB. Timeout 14 400 s; 512 GiB limit.

Im Y_in at 193.5996 pF is positive on all four readings, so on degree-1's shape the root lies below the node, as on F-human (entry 39). Entry 50 gave a sign and no degree-2 slope.

Grid (3 nodes, ≤ 4 decimals in pF): 184.5000, 185.7500, 187.0000. Written from logs/geo38/c4-node-193.5996-d2.json against the degree-1 node JSONs. Each degree-2 reading sits just above the degree-1 reading at 201.0000 pF. Linear extrapolation from the two top degree-1 nodes puts them at an equivalent degree-1 capacitance of 201.28–201.55 pF. That is a move of −7.68 to −7.95 pF (≈ −4.0 %). The translated root is 185.65–185.92 pF, and the proportional reading gives 185.96–186.21 pF. Entry 39's same one-point reading bracketed F-human's root (115.49 translated, 115.55 proportional, 115.52 found). The log-pathologist ruling on entry 50 (journal §4) narrows and shifts that: the degree-1 secants fall from 9.5e-3 to 5.2e-3 S/pF going up in C, so the linear reading is biased low, and a quadratic through 197, 198.5 and 201 pF gives translated roots of 185.55–185.83 pF. Re Y on the crossing series maps to ≈ 202.0 pF, which implies ≈ 185.2 pF, with loss differences unseparated. The estimates therefore span ≈ 185.2–186.2 pF. Here the move is ≈ 3× F-human's in pF and n = 1 is the only precedent, so this is an estimate, not a prediction with a band. The risk is lopsided: the root falls below 185 pF on a slope only 7–9 % low, and the high side needs ≈ +20 %. A first grid of 185 / 186 / 187 pF was dropped for that reason. This grid leaves ≈ 0.7 pF below and ≈ 0.8 pF above the span. A 1.25 pF spacing costs little, because the secant is good to ≈ 0.08 pF at 1.5 pF (entries 46 and 51) and a refinement follows anyway. The nodes' printed .4f and .12e forms were checked against the private-leak guard's reference set before queueing: clear.

Why three nodes and not C5's full grid. Entry 50's node pair is 3 056.9 s, so 3 nodes fit an xl window and 8 fit an xxl one only with ≈ 7.7 h of its 8 h. Three bracket the estimate and measure the degree-2 slope, which entry 50's one node cannot, and a refinement is then a priced variant.

Price (measured in the family; scaling stated): entry 50 on the same mesh, module, degree and -n 16: build 341.8 s, Z50 pair 2 892.1 s, node pair 3 056.9 s, memory.peak 472.42 GiB (20261031T070008Z_GEO-38-C5a.log:12595, :12650). This window has four factorisations to entry 50's two, and the budget tracks MUMPS INFOG(19), which varied with the node (482 667 and 498 030 MB in entry 50, :12482 for the second; 7.5 % max / min in entry 39). The 512 GiB limit leaves ≈ 540.5 GB of INFOG(19), +8.5 % over the top draw, or +5.4 % if the Z50 pair carried the peak, against a family max / mean of +3.7–3.8 %. It probably fits; that is not proven, and an OOM is covered by the decision rule. Timeout 14 400 s, the xl ceiling, which is a 14 % margin; factorisations spread 7 % in entry 50 (2 524.98 / 2 700.21 s, :12285, :12506). 512 GiB limit, 92 % used in entry 50.

Runs past the 04:30 slot. This will be the first window to overlap a slot. OPS-54's row says it queues nothing until a measured window has overlapped one; a window's Python imports resolve at start, so the exposure is late imports only. The reading review says whether the overlap showed anything.

Decision rule (pre-registered; the first weekly after the window reads it): - Every gate green and one − → + crossing on P33 (1, +1j) inside [184.5, 187.0] ⇒ C_in(F-clinical, d2) is recorded at this grid's resolution, as a record, and a 0.25 pF refinement (entry 51's pattern) or the column set is posed at it. P41 (1, +1j) and P33 (1, −1j) never cross at degree 1 on any of the 12 nodes, so "none" on those two matches degree 1; F-human's "all four cross" is not the expected outcome here. - Every gate green and no crossing on P33 (1, +1j) inside the grid ⇒ the extrapolation is off by more than ≈ 1 pF. docs.title: Harness logs: a representative subset
docs.text:
Every verification run in this project goes through scripts/testing/run_and_log.sh, which writes one log recording the commit, environment, exact command, full output, exit status and elapsed time. The private development repository holds about 4,700 of them (about 74 MB). This public snapshot keeps 67:

  • every log cited in PROJECT_PLAN.md §2.1 ("Validated, with the number that licenses it"), so each headline validation claim can be traced to the run that produced it;
  • the oversight logs: the private-data leak audits (OPS-46, OPS-47, OPS-58, LEAK-CHECK-*) and the MAT-6 step 10 runs, where a plain timeout failed to stop an MPI job and led to the mandatory timeout -k 30 rule (see AI_WORKFLOW.md).

Logs are gzipped; read them with zcat or zless. Elsewhere in the plan, the chunk files, the attempt journal and test-results.md, log names are cited that are not included here. Those citations are records of runs in the private repository. Tooling that checks every cited log exists (the doc-reference census) will report them as missing in this snapshot.

docs.title: XL / XXL queue directories
docs.text:
xl-queue.d/ and xxl-queue.d/ are the FIFO queues scripts/automation/xl-run.sh reads at 02:00 (operator directive 2026-09-15). Each *.env file holds one window in the XL_CHUNK / XL_COMMAND format of the legacy <tier>-queue.env (still honoured first when non-empty). Files run in lexical order, so name them <intended run date>-<chunk>.env; the launcher checks the ledger budget before taking a file, runs the first valid one, and deletes it afterwards whether the window succeeded or failed. Entries are copied verbatim from xl-pending.md by the daily review (daily-review.md step 6b), the weekly, or the operator — never authored here.

Optional XL_OUTPUTS (OPS-64, 2026-09-28): space-separated repo-relative paths the window writes into the tree that belong in its commit. The launcher refuses the entry before the window (queue and ledger untouched) if a declared path is absolute, outside the repo, or gitignored, and stages the declared paths that exist after it. An undeclared tree output is left uncommitted and makes the next window and the next slot stop on a dirty tree, so a pre-registered entry that writes into the tree must declare it. Output under the gitignored /logs/ (the usual raw-log route) needs no declaration. The launcher also records the container's python3 count before and after every window in a ## Launcher section of the committed harness log, so an entry no longer needs its own [orphans-before] / [orphans-after] lines.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Validate that the FEM magnetostatic solver reproduces the analytic on-axis field of a Helmholtz coil pair, quantitatively.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Validated to 0.04% against the closed-form solution (2026-07-27).

An earlier version of this page concluded "Phase 1 Helmholtz validation is complete" on the strength of a uniformity check alone (CV < 1%). Uniformity is a necessary but far weaker condition than agreement with an analytic magnitude — a solver can produce a beautifully uniform field of entirely the wrong strength. The quantitative comparison below is what actually closes this.

docs.title: Geometry and setup
docs.text:
• Coil model: two torus wire volumes
  • Major radius R: 0.02 m
  • Minor radius a: 0.005 m
  • Coil separation: 0.02 m (Helmholtz spacing, equal to R)
  • Mesh generator: MeshGenerator.two_torus_domain(...)
  • Material: mu = MU_0
  • Current: azimuthal current density in both torus volumes, unit magnitude, so the current per loop is I = |J| * pi * a^2

docs.title: Quantitative validation
docs.text:
mpiexec -n 8 python3 examples/magnetostatics/04_helmholtz_analytic_comparison.py \
  --major-radius 0.02 --minor-radius 0.005 \
  --air-padding 0.08 --far-resolution 0.010 --resolutions 0.003 --points 21

Reference: the filamentary on-axis Helmholtz field,

B_z(z) = sum_i  mu_0 * I * R^2 / (2 * (R^2 + (z - z_i)^2)^{3/2})

Result (log docs/testing/logs/20260727T171928Z_MAG-4.log, 127k cells, 26 s):

Metric Value Centre B_z, FEM 3.529697e-09 T Centre B_z, analytic 3.531057e-09 T Centre relative error 0.04% Mean on-axis relative error 0.83% Central uniformity CV 0.003%

This clears the project's <5% MVP criterion by two orders of magnitude.

docs.title: The air box dominates accuracy — not mesh resolution
docs.text:
The single most important result from this validation is why it initially disagreed. At the historical domain size the error was 20.5% and did not improve across a 7x refinement (10k → 70k cells). It is not a discretization error.

The outer boundary carries the natural condition n x (mu^-1 curl A) = 0, i.e. n x H = 0. That is a perfect magnetic conductor: it mirrors flux back into the domain and inflates the on-axis field. two_torus_domain originally hardcoded box_half = R + 3a, tying the air gap to the wire radius, so making the wire thinner shrank the air box. That inverted trend — a thinner wire giving worse agreement, 43.7% at a = 0.003 versus 20.5% at a = 0.005 — is what identified the boundary as the cause.

Air padding Cells Centre error 0.5 R 40k 20.42% 1 R 51k 7.43% 2 R 76k 1.73% 4 R 163k 0.01%

Two independent convergence studies confirm the result is real rather than error cancellation — boundary error falls monotonically with domain size, and discretization error falls monotonically with h:

Wire h at 4R padding Cells Centre error Mean error 0.004 89k 0.11% 1.07% 0.003 127k 0.04% 0.84% 0.002 228k 0.05% 0.51%

Use air_padding >= 2 * major_radius for any free-space comparison. Pair it with wire_resolution/far_resolution graded sizing, or cost becomes prohibitive: grading gives ≈76k cells where a uniform mesh of equivalent wire fidelity needs ≈626k.

docs.title: Uniformity check
docs.text:
tests/validation/test_helmholtz_v2.py remains as a cheap regression guard:

mpiexec -n 2 python3 -m pytest tests/validation/test_helmholtz_v2.py -v
  • Evaluate Bz on axis for z in [-0.1R, +0.1R]
  • Require CV = std(Bz)/|mean(Bz)| < 1%

Note this test previously located sample points with a per-rank collision search asserting len(links) > 0, which passed at 1–4 ranks and failed at 8. It now uses post.evaluation.evaluate_vector_field_parallel.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The magnetostatic formulation in core/solvers.py — the N1curl weak form ∫ mu^-1 (curl A)·(curl v) dx = ∫ J·v dx with gauge penalty — reproduces the closed-form Helmholtz field to 0.04%. This is the project's one quantitatively validated component and the foundation the time-harmonic work (TH-1) builds on.

Caveat for higher order: N1curl degree 2 was measured on the straight-wire fixture and diverged (2724% error at h = 0.003), which points at the gauge-penalty formulation rather than element order. Do not raise the element degree without re-validating.
